# Explanation of the Frontispiece.

Our highly-enlightened author, Jacob Böhme, begins his theosophy <note>original: "Theosophiam," referring to divine wisdom or the study of the nature of God.</note> with GOD; and considers Him either as He is in Himself, above and outside of Nature and Creation, as an incomprehensible **Nothing** and an unfathomable **Abyss** <term>Ungrund: Böhme’s term for the absolute, "groundless" state of God before any creation or manifestation—a void that is simultaneously a potential for everything.</term>, which can be known by no creature; because in such a respect one can name neither names nor properties, nor anything of GOD. This **Nothing** and this **Abyss** we have represented in a wide round circle.

Or otherwise he considers GOD as He has expressed Himself in Nature and Creation, and revealed Himself therein, conceiving a delight and a will to lead Himself out of His Abyss into a Ground, and out of His eternal Nothing into Something. This delight of GOD toward revelation is the beginning and ground of all life and being; which we have depicted in the center-point of the large circle, with the image of a heart and a core, from which all life and being is birthed. In the heart we have a † <note>The cross symbol.</note>, signifying the **birth of the cross**, where every life ignites itself in the cross, and drives itself in the form of a cross upwards, downwards, and across. Yet the impulse of Divine delight and will is nonetheless a most simple act <note>original: "Actus."</note>, without form, figure, or property, without an "upwards" or "downwards." By us, however—who are but piecework <note>A reference to 1 Corinthians 13:9; meaning humans can only understand things in fragments or parts.</note> and cannot grasp GOD in such simplicity—it cannot be considered otherwise than piece by piece. Thus, we attribute the desiring and working will, or the driving delight toward Nature and Creation, to GOD the Father; the working will, which satisfies the delight and desire with eternal pleasure, we attribute to GOD the Son; that working will which reveals the satisfied and fulfilled will of GOD, we attribute to the Holy Spirit, who proceeds from the Father and the Son. The revelation itself, through which the Triune GOD becomes manifest in such a threefold property of working, we call **PRINCIPLES** <note>original: "PRINCIPIA."</note>. Because each of the three properties of working has its certain limit <note>original: "Terminum."</note>, enclosure, and boundary, we call it a World. These three Principles or Worlds we have prefigured by three smaller circles enclosed within the large one; and each opens itself out from the other from a sphere <note>original: "Sphæra."</note> and central ground.

The first Principle, or the revelation of GOD according to the property of the Father, consisting in three shapes or forms of working (as in desiring and attracting, driving and ascending, sharpening and igniting), we have figured in the lowest circle. Its center and core, because of the three properties, is represented in a Δ <note>The Greek letter Delta, used here as the alchemical and symbolic character for fire.</note>, as the character of fire. The seven fire-sparks standing upon it signify the seven source-spirits <term>Quell-Geister: The seven fundamental qualities or forces of nature in Böhme's system that "flow" or "spring" forth to create reality.</term> or forms of working. The enclosure of such workings and to each...

# Explanation of the Frontispiece.

Our highly-enlightened author, **Jacob Böhme**, begins his Theosophy <note>original: *Theosophiam*, meaning "divine wisdom"</note> from **God**; and considers Him either as He is in Himself, above and beyond nature and creature, as an incomprehensible **Nothing** and unfathomable **Abyss** <note>original: *Ungrund*, a central term in Böhme’s thought referring to the absolute, "groundless" state of God before creation or differentiation</note>, which can be known by no creature; for in such a respect, one can name neither name nor qualities, nor anything of **God**. This **Nothing** and this **Abyss** we have represented in a wide, round Circle.

Or else, he considers **God** as He has expressed Himself in nature and creature, and revealed Himself therein—conceiving a delight and a will to lead Himself out of His Abyss into a Ground, and from His eternal Nothing into Something. This delight of **God** toward revelation is the beginning and ground of all life and being; which we have depicted in the center-point of the large circle, with the image of a heart and core, from which all life and being originates. In the heart we have a †, indicating the Cross-birth <note>A pivotal Böhmean concept where the "dark fire" of nature breaks through into the "light fire" of the spiritual realm, forming the shape of a cross</note>, where every life ignites itself in the cross and, in the form of a cross, drives itself upward and downward and across. However, the impulse of Divine delight and will is nonetheless a most simple act <note>original: *Actus*</note>, without form, figure, or quality, without an "above" or a "below." But by us—who are fragmentary beings and cannot grasp **God** in such simplicity—it can be considered in no other way than piece by piece. Thus, we attribute the desiring and active will, or the driving delight toward nature and creature, to **God** the Father; the active will that satisfies the delight and desire with eternal pleasure, we attribute to **God** the Son; that active will which reveals the satisfied and fulfilled will of **God**, we attribute to the **Holy Spirit**, who proceeds from the Father and the Son. The revelation itself, whereby the Triune **God** becomes manifest as acting in such a threefold quality, we call **Principles** <note>original: *Principia*</note>. Because each of the three qualities of acting has its certain limit <note>original: *Terminum*, a boundary or end-point</note>, enclosure, and dividing-goal, we call it a **World**. These three Principles or Worlds we have prefigured through three smaller circles enclosed within the large one; and which open out from one another from a sphere <note>original: *Sphæra*</note> and central ground.

The first Principle, or the revelation of **God** according to the quality of the Father, consisting in three shapes or forms of acting (as in desiring and attracting, driving and ascending, sharpening and igniting), we have figured in the bottommost circle. Its center and core, because of the three qualities, is represented in a Δ <note>The Greek letter Delta or a triangle, which in alchemy represents the element of fire</note>, as the character of fire. The seven fire-sparks standing upon it signify the seven source-spirits <note>original: *Quell-Geister*, also translated as "fountain-spirits," the seven fundamental forces that Böhme believes construct all reality</note> or forms of acting. <meta>This page continues the explanation of the frontispiece, moving from the "Abyss" of God to the first three distinct "Principles" or realms of existence in Jacob Böhme’s complex cosmology. It describes the transition from a dark, consuming fire to the light of divine love, and finally to the mixed reality of our physical world.</meta>

This driving property of life’s ignition is called the **Fire-World**. And because this ignition has its boundary <note>original: *Scheide-Ziel*, a dividing point or limit</note> and does not reach the revelation of **GOD**, it is called the **dark Fire-World**. In this world, **GOD** is revealed not as the highest Good and Love, but as an angry, jealous **GOD**, as an eternal glow and a consuming fire.

The second **Principle** <note>original: *Principium*, one of the three fundamental realities in Böhme’s system</note>, or the revelation of **GOD** according to the property of the **Son**, we have depicted in the upper circle. Its center is the **Spring-Well** <note>original: *Quell-Brunn*, a fountain-like source</note> of Divine Gentleness, represented by a $\nabla$ <note>the alchemical symbol for water</note>, the character of water. In the $\Delta$ <note>the alchemical symbol for fire</note> below it, with seven flames of fire, the fire is presented as it is pacified in the fire-flash from the dark world through the boundary; with its seven **Source-Spirits** <note>original: *Quell-Geister*, the seven fundamental forces that Böhme believed built all reality</note> it gives birth to the **Water-Source**, and in that—as if in an unburnable oil and balsam—it becomes a light, in which **GOD** is revealed in the lovely name **JESUS** as the highest Good and Love. Above such a **Balance** <note>original: *Temperatur*, a state where opposing qualities like fire and water are perfectly harmonized</note> of the properties of fire and water, the **Holy Spirit** hovers in the form of a dove, as if in its **Heaven** <note>original: *Schammajim*, Hebrew for "heavens"</note>, full of the majesty, brilliance, and glory of **GOD**. This poured-out brilliance of glory is embraced and reflected by the Principle of Light, whereby the **Mirror of Wisdom** is opened, in which the bright-flaming spirits of **GOD** behold wonders and ceaselessly glorify Him for them; this is represented by the image of the eyes. Therefore, this Principle is called the **Light-World**, and also the **Angelic World**, because the angels were contained in this Principle as fire-sparks of **GOD'S** omnipotence and were revealed as creatures; they also function <note>original: *qualificiren*, to act according to their inner quality</note> therein as long as they incline their will out of the power of fire and place it into the **Spring-Well** of the gentleness and love of **GOD** in the name **JESUS**. However, after an entire kingdom of angels turned their will away from this little **Spring-Well** and placed it into their own fire-power, the **Creative Word** <note>original: *Fiat*, the Latin "let it be"</note> of the dark Principle seized them, and the wrath of **GOD** shaped each one according to the impression of his ignited will; they are then bound in such forms, as if in eternal prison, with chains of darkness, as vessels of the wrath of **GOD**, in which **GOD** has been revealed as an angry and jealous **GOD**.

The third **Principle**, or the revelation of **GOD** according to the property of the **Holy Spirit**, consists of both properties—fire and light—as they have proceeded from the balance <note>original: *Temperatur*</note> and stand in a constant struggle according to all the forms of their **Source-Spirits**. Thus, **GOD** is revealed simultaneously in light and darkness, love and wrath, heat and cold, life and death; and such is this visible world. This revelation is attributed to the **Holy Spirit**, not indeed as if the **Holy Spirit** actually reveals such a conflict, but just as the **Holy Spirit** proceeds from the **Father** and the **Son**, so the third Principle has proceeded from the property of the **Father** and the **Son**, as if from the dark **Fire-World** and from the bright **Light-World**. The reason, however, for such a revelation of both Principles is the Fall of the Angels, who turned away from gentleness and ignited their kingdom with wrath, placing it out of the balance <note>original: *Temperatur*, the state of perfect harmony where no quality dominates another</note> and into such conflict. When **GOD** moved again according to both Principles in His almighty Word, separating light and darkness, and brought forth all creatures—each according to its indwelling form—and, dividing His work into six days, contained eternity within a period of time, then this was revealed as its own world. We have depicted this in the middle circle, of which one half consists of the upper circle and the other half of the lower circle; the line in the middle signifies the boundary <note>original: *Scheide-Ziel*, a dividing point</note> of both Principles, where fire and light are birthed and also separated.

We have represented the "source-quality" <term>Quall: a term Böhme used to describe the agonizing, vibrating, and driving quality of inner life or energy</term> or the drive of **GOD'S** working will, according to the property of this Principle, in the image of a tree. For as soon as life is awakened in the heart and core, it either drives downward and takes root in the dark Principle—whose **Source-Spirits** <term>Quell-Geister: the seven fundamental forces that Böhme believed built all reality</term> drive toward the ignition of fire-life, according to the shape of their property, such as harsh, stern, bitter, fierce, anxious, dark, and fiery—or it drives upward through the **Cross-Birth** <note>original: *Creutz-Geburt*, the spiritual transformation or "flash" where the dark fire is transformed into light, symbolized by the cross</note>, reaching toward the growth, the flower, the crown, and the fruit. 

When the growth driven through the cross reaches the paradisiacal source of light, where the Source-Spirits exist in perfect balance <note>original: *Temperatur*</note>, then **GOD** is revealed therein in paradisiacal majesty, radiance, sweetness, gentleness, and love; it is then rightly called the **Tree of Life**. The trunk of this tree rises from the fire-root of the dark Principle through this visible world, where light and darkness—and all their Source-Spirits—stand in powerful conflict, and the stars and elements well up as harsh, stern, fierce, and fiery. This "welling" reaches all the way to the **†** <note>the symbol for the Cross</note>, where the kingdom of this world separates from the Kingdom of **GOD** and the World of Light. 

Now, when the angels of darkness blow up the fire-life in the root according to their monstrous images, and drive the Source-Spirits of the dark power too harshly, fiercely, and sharply, the fire-source becomes too fierce and too harsh. It is unable to reach the source of gentleness by "sinking down" <note>original: *Ersincken*, a mystical term for the soul's humble surrender or descent into the depths of God</note> into the Cross-Birth; instead, it wells up in its own harsh fire-power and prefers to sprout below the Cross. It greens, blooms, and brings forth fruit in the kingdom of this world, according to that property toward which the stars and elements, through their harsh influence, drive and draw the fire-source in the trunk. 

And so the growth, which in the paradisiacal source is called the **Tree of Life**, becomes here a **Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil**. To this tree belongs everything that does not sprout forth in the Kingdom of **GOD** by being driven through the **†**, dying to all self-interest through humble sinking and **releasement** <term>Gelassenheit: a key mystical concept meaning the total surrender of the individual's self-will to God</term>. Even if it otherwise possesses a fine appearance, it is nonetheless nothing but a fleeting glimmer of this world and its glory, sprouted from the "source-quality" of self-love. The image of Man, whom **GOD** created according to His likeness and in His own image, and brought forth as an extract <note>original: *Extract*, meaning a distillation or microcosm containing all parts of the whole</note> from all three Principles; so that with his will he might penetrate from the realm of this world into the Kingdom of **GOD**, yet soothe the fire-source <term>Feuer-Quell: the intense, driving energy of the first principle, associated with God's "wrath" or raw power</term> through the gentleness of **JESUS**, and might elevate himself and all creatures into the harmony <term>Temperatur: the state of perfect balance where no single quality dominates another</term> of the property of the Paradisiacal source. In this way, the fire would then be swallowed up in the light, the wrath in love, and desire in pleasure, and **GOD** would be revealed in man—and through man in all creatures—as the highest good, life, light, and love. He was meant to strive toward such a source and bring forth fruit into the Kingdom of **GOD**, so that he, as an angel of **GOD**, might possess the throne of Lucifer and fill that kingdom with another angelic host. However, he was pulled by all three principles, and there arose within him the struggle of great temptation, whereupon he turned his desire away from the source of gentleness and introduced his longing into the realm of this world. Meanwhile, from the dark world, the false fire-desire rose up in the form of a serpent, which leaned against the tree beneath the † <note>The symbol of the Cross, often used in these diagrams to mark the point of transformation</note> and infected man with its poison of evil lust.

All of this is to be noted from the figure, where Man is depicted raising his head above the Cross, standing with his heart and life-source between both Principles—the Kingdom of **GOD** and this world—pointing with his right hand toward the Tree of Life, but with his left toward the Tree of Knowledge, and thus deliberating which of the two he should surrender and dedicate himself to. Furthermore, [one sees] how his lower body, formed from the slime of the earth <note>original: *Limo der Erden*, a reference to the "dust of the ground" in Genesis 2:7</note>, stood in this principle, and how the source of this principle—animalistic lust—was awakened by the serpent and the impulse of the Tree of Knowledge, so that he inclined his desire and hunger toward the tree and ate of the forbidden fruit. [It shows] how such food surged and operated within him, so that he died to the Kingdom of **GOD** and awoke to the kingdom of this world, wherein he found himself in the greatest misery: naked and bare, in hunger and thirst, in heat and cold, in internal anguish, and in external, indescribable lamentation. It also shows how **GOD** came to his aid through grace and gave him the Serpent-Crusher <term>Schlangen-Treter: a traditional title for Christ, the "seed of the woman" who would bruise the serpent's head</term> as a promise. This hero, in the fullness of time, would enter into his struggle, break through the gates of the deep and the powers of darkness, and set man's fire-desire free from all lust of the world and the flesh. Through the Cross and death, He would lead him back into the Kingdom of **GOD**, so that man, dying again to the kingdom of this world, might turn green and break forth again in Paradise. All of this is revealed point by point <note>original: *von Punct zu Punct*</note> in this treatise, in fitting order for the inclined reader, with the testimonies of the highly enlightened **JACOB BÖHME**. # Preface
### By the Author of these sublime Writings/
->To the<-
### Truth-loving and impartial Reader.

The author of these writings wishes the kind reader, who is eager for salvation, the living obedience of faith for a fundamental knowledge, and active love for the actual possession of Wisdom <note>In this context, "Wisdom" refers to "Sophia," a central figure in Böhme’s mysticism representing the divine mirror or the feminine aspect of God’s wisdom</note>, from the Father of Light and from the Source of Truth, which is in Christ JESUS.

->§. 1.<-

We present here to the God-loving reader—as a soul-healing guide on how one may arrive at a true and unerring knowledge of GOD and of oneself—an extract <note>original: *Ausbund*, meaning a choice selection or a quintessential collection</note> of the writings of the highly-illuminated Jacob Böhme, otherwise called the Teutonic Philosopher <note>original: *Philosophus Teutonicus*</note>, in such a form and order as has been requested for many years by the lovers of this excellent Theosophical Study <note>original: *Studii Theosophici*</note>. In doing so, we have deemed it unavoidably necessary to prevent the kind reader, with a faithful heart as far as we are able, from certain prejudices that might encounter him regarding both the author's testimonies and this present arrangement; therefore, we remind him with a short preface: 1. What moved us to arrange and publish these high writings in such an order. 2. How the kind reader should view such an arrangement and accept it with benefit.

§. 2. Regarding the motivation: it has been about 12 years since we—according to the measure of our knowledge at that time, and prompted by much internal and external occasion—published our first treatise on the 12 Articles of the Christian Creed, under the title: **Depiction of the Hidden Man of the Heart.** This writing, contrary to our expectation, found its way among many earnest lovers of the Theosophical Study and the writings of the late "Teutonicus," after they found therein much similarity and agreement with the testimonies of this highly-illuminated author, and therefore sought to confer with me about this in Christian friendship. However, because at that time I had not read these high writings of the late Jacob Böhme, except for the treatise *On the Incarnation of Christ*, and saw neither the means nor the opportunity to acquire them, all the works of the late man were sent to me from distant lands through the special direction of GOD and the arrangement of a faithful patron and benefactor; and I was faithfully and earnestly directed toward this high study.

§. 3. Regarding the theological matters and testimonies, I found in them a singular harmony with the guidance GOD was then providing to my soul. The doctrine of repentance, the instruction on prayer, the powerful convictions of the Spirit toward a humble obedience of faith, as well as the entire foundation of Rebirth <term>Wiedergebuhrt: the spiritual process of internal transformation and the restoration of the divine image in man</term>, of redemption, justification, and sanctification of the poor sinner before GOD through Jesus Christ, were to me like golden nails <note>An idiom suggesting firm, unshakeable anchors of truth</note> for the fastening of what was occurring in my soul. However, regarding the mysteries of the Theosophical Study—how the invisible eternal Godhead introduced itself into Nature and Creature, and therein became active and manifest according to the 3 Principles <term>Drey Principien: Böhme’s system of the dark fire-world, the light world, and the external world of nature</term> and the 7 Properties of Nature <term>7. Eigenschafften der Natur: the seven formative qualities through which all things are created and sustained</term>—I could at that time in no way fundamentally recognize or grasp such things, though I read day and night with great desire and often repeated what I had read. Indeed, through meditation and sharp reflection, it became darker and darker to me the longer I tried, so that for a time I had to lay these writings aside and be content with my understanding at that time. In the meantime, the leading hand of GOD led me into another school, wherein I was given many a difficult lesson to learn, and many and various trials and temptations came over me—sometimes from the cares of physical sustenance, sometimes from flesh and blood,

<meta>This page continues the preface, shifting from the general introduction of Jacob Böhme’s work to a specific explanation of the "Image of Man" (the microcosm) and the cosmic struggle between the Three Principles. The image of Man, whom God created in His likeness as His image, and brought forth as an extract <note>Böhme views man as a "microcosm" or a small summary containing all the elements of the entire universe (the "macrocosm").</note> from all three principles: so that with his will, he might penetrate from the kingdom of this world into the Kingdom of God, while soothing the source of fire in the gentleness of JESUS. In this way, he might elevate himself and all creatures into the harmony <note>original: *Temperatur*, referring to the alchemical and mystical state of "Temperamentum," where all opposing qualities are perfectly balanced and no longer in conflict.</note> of the quality of the Paradisiacal source. Thus, the fire would be swallowed up in the light, the wrath in love, and the desire in delight, and God would be revealed in man—and through man in all creatures—as the highest Good, Life, Light, and Love. 

Man was meant to strive toward such a source and bring forth fruit into the Kingdom of God, so that as an angel of God, he might occupy the throne of Lucifer and fill that kingdom with another angelic host. However, he was drawn by all three principles, and there arose within him the conflict of great temptation, as he then turned his desire away from the source of gentleness and introduced his longing into the kingdom of this world. Meanwhile, from the dark world, the false fire-desire rose up in the form of a serpent, which placed itself against the tree beneath the † <note>The symbol of the Cross, often used in these texts to represent the intersection of the divine and earthly dimensions.</note> and infected man with its poison of evil lust. 

All of this is to be noted from the figure where man is depicted: raising his head above the Cross; standing with his heart and life-source between both principles of the Kingdom of God and of this world; pointing with his right hand toward the Tree of Life, but with his left toward the Tree of Knowledge; and thus deliberating to which of the two he should surrender and devote himself. 

Furthermore, one sees how his lower body, formed from the clay <note>original: *Limo*, from the Latin *limus*, referring to the dust or "slime" of the earth from which Adam was made.</note> of the earth, stood in this earthly principle. It shows how the source of this principle—namely, animalistic lust—was awakened by the serpent and the impulse of the Tree of Knowledge, such that he inclined his desire and hunger toward the tree and ate of the forbidden fruit. As such food surged and operated within him, he died to the Kingdom of God and woke to the kingdom of this world. In this state, he found himself in the highest misery: naked and bare, in hunger and thirst, in heat and cold, in internal anguish, and in external, indescribable sorrow. 

Yet, it also shows how God came to his aid out of grace and, through His powerful Word, gave him the promise of the Serpent-Crusher <note>original: *Schlangen-Treter*, a reference to Genesis 3:15, interpreted as Christ who would bruise the head of the serpent.</note>. In the fullness of time, as a mighty hero, this Crusher would enter into man’s struggle, break through the gates of the deep and the powers of darkness, and set man’s fire-desire free from all lust of the world and the flesh. Through the Cross and death, He would lead man back into the Kingdom of God, so that man, dying again to the kingdom of this world, could once more turn green and burst forth in Paradise. 

All of this is opened to the kind reader in this treatise, point by point, with the testimonies of the highly-illuminated JACOB BÖHME, arranged in a fitting order. For the thorough realization of this, we heartily wish every faithful seeker and warrior a right earnestness, true humility, living faith, and active love, through zealous prayer and intercession.

# Preface
## By the Author of these High Writings,
->To the<-
## Truth-loving and Impartial Reader.

The author of these writings wishes the kind reader, who is eager for salvation, a living obedience of faith for fundamental knowledge, and an active love for the actual possession of wisdom, from the Father of Light and from the Source of Truth, which is in Christ JESUS.

->§. 1.<-

We present here to the God-loving reader, as a healing guide on how he may attain a true and unerring knowledge of GOD and of himself, an exemplary collection of the writings of the highly enlightened Jacob Böhme <note>Jacob Böhme (1575–1624) was a German mystic and theologian whose work deeply influenced Western esotericism.</note>, otherwise called the *Teutonic Philosopher* <note>original: "Philosophus Teutonicus." This was a common title for Böhme, marking him as a profound thinker writing in the German (Teutonic) vernacular rather than academic Latin.</note>, in such a form and order as has been requested for many years by the lovers of this excellent <term>Theosophical study</term> <note>In Böhme’s context, "Theosophy" refers to "divine wisdom"—a direct, mystical understanding of God and the nature of the universe.</note>. In doing so, we have deemed it unavoidably necessary to prevent the kind reader, with a faithful heart and as much as is within our power, from any prejudices he might encounter—both regarding the author's testimonies and this present arrangement—and therefore to remind him with a short preface: 1. What moved us to arrange and publish these high writings in such an order. 2. How the kind reader should view this arrangement of ours and accept it with benefit.

§. 2. Regarding the motivation: it has been over twelve years since we—according to the measure of our knowledge at that time and due to much internal and external occasion—published our first treatise on the twelve articles of the Christian Creed, under the title: **Illustration of the Hidden Man of the Heart.** This writing, contrary to our expectations, found its way among many earnest lovers of the Theosophical study and the writings of the late *Teutonic Philosopher*, after they found in it much similarity and agreement with the testimonies of this highly enlightened author, and for that reason sought to confer with me about it in Christian friendship. However, because at that time I had not read these high writings of the late Jacob Böhme, except for the treatise *On the Incarnation of Christ*, and saw neither the means nor the opportunity to acquire them, all the works of the blessed man were sent to me from distant lands through the special direction of GOD and the arrangement of a faithful patron and benefactor, and I was faithfully and earnestly directed to this high study.

§. 3. Regarding the theological matters and testimonies, I found in them a singular harmony with the way GOD was leading my soul at that time. The doctrine of repentance, the instructions for prayer, the powerful convictions of the Spirit toward a humble obedience of faith, as well as the entire foundation of <term>Rebirth</term>, of redemption, justification, and sanctification of the poor sinner before GOD through JESUS Christ, were to me like golden nails to fasten that which was occurring in my soul. But as for the mysteries of the Theosophical study—how the invisible, eternal Godhead introduced itself into nature and creation, and therein became active and manifest, according to the <term>Three Principles</term> <note>Böhme’s "Three Principles" describe the transition from the "Abyss" (Ungrund) into the dark world (fire/desire), the light world (love/spirit), and the physical world (the manifestation of both).</note> and the <term>Seven Properties of Nature</term> <note>Böhme describes seven "Source-Spirits" or qualities (such as contraction, expansion, and circulation) that drive the unfolding of all existence.</note>—I could not at that time recognize or grasp such things fundamentally in any way, even though I read day and night with great desire and frequently repeated what I had read. Indeed, through meditation and sharp reflection, it became darker and darker to me the longer I tried, so that for a time I had to set these writings aside and content myself with my understanding at that time. Meanwhile, the guiding hand of GOD led me into another school, in which I was given many a difficult lesson to learn, and many and various trials and temptations came upon me—sometimes from the worries of sustenance, sometimes from flesh and blood,

The Image of Man, whom God created in His likeness and in His own image, was brought forth as an extract from all three <term>Principles</term> <note>In Böhme’s cosmology, the Three Principles are the dark fire-world of God's wrath, the light-world of God's love, and the physical, visible world.</note>. This was done so that he might, by his own will, press out from the kingdom of this world into the Kingdom of God, thereby soothing the source of fire within the gentleness of Jesus. He was intended to elevate himself and all creatures into the balanced temperament of the <term>Paradisiacal Source</term> <note>Böhme uses "source" (Quell) to describe an active, bubbling spring of spiritual energy or quality.</note>, so that the fire might be swallowed up in the light, the wrath in love, and desire in delight. Thus, God would be revealed in man—and through man in all creatures—as the highest good: life, light, and love. 

Man was meant to strive toward such a source and bring forth fruit into the Kingdom of God, so that as an angel of God he might possess the throne of Lucifer and fill that kingdom with another angelic host. However, he was pulled by all three principles, and within him arose the conflict of great temptation. He then turned his desire away from the source of gentleness and led his longing into the kingdom of this world. Meanwhile, from the dark world, the false fire-desire rose up in the form of a serpent, which placed itself at the tree beneath the † <note>The cross (†) here symbolizes the spiritual axis or the promise of Christ's eventual sacrifice, contrasting with the Tree of Knowledge.</note> and infected man with the poison of evil lust.

All of this can be observed in the figure where man is depicted, raising his head above the Cross, standing with his heart and life-source between both principles of the Kingdom of God and of this world. With his right hand he points toward the Tree of Life, but with his left toward the Tree of Knowledge, thus deliberating to which of the two he should surrender and devote himself. 

Furthermore, we see how his lower body, formed from the <term>clay of the earth</term> <note>original: "Limo der Erden," from the Latin *limus*, meaning mud or slime.</note>, stood in this principle, and how the source of this principle—as animal lust—was awakened by the serpent and the impulse of the Tree of Knowledge. Man leaned his desire and hunger toward the tree and ate of the forbidden fruit; this food then surged and operated within him so that he died to the Kingdom of God and woke up to the kingdom of this world. In this state, he found himself in the highest misery: naked and bare, in hunger and thirst, in heat and cold, in inward anguish, and in outward, indescribable lamentation. 

We also see how God came to his aid out of grace and, through His powerful Word, gave him the promise of the <term>Crusher of the Serpent</term> <note>original: "Schlangen-Treter." A reference to Genesis 3:15, interpreted as Christ who would defeat the devil.</note>. This Promised One, in the fullness of time, would step into the conflict as a mighty hero, break through the gates of the deep and the powers of darkness, and set man's fire-desire free from all lust of the world and the flesh. Through the Cross and death, He would lead man back into the Kingdom of God, so that man, dying again to the kingdom of this world, could once more turn green and break forth in Paradise.

All of this is opened to the kind reader in this treatise point by point <note>original: "von Punct zu Punct"</note>, in proper order, alongside the testimonies of the highly enlightened Jacob Böhme. For a fundamental understanding of this, we heartily wish every faithful seeker and warrior true earnestness, sincere humility, living faith, and active love in zealous prayer and intercession.

# Preface
## Of the Author of these sublime Writings
->To the<-
### Truth-loving and impartial Reader.

The author of these writings wishes the kind reader, who is eager for his own salvation, a living obedience of faith for a grounded knowledge, and an active love for the actual possession of wisdom, from the Father of Light and from the Source of Truth, which is in Christ JESUS.

->§. 1.<-

We present here to the God-loving reader, as a healing instruction on how he may attain a true and unerring knowledge of GOD and of himself, a choice collection of the writings of the highly-enlightened Jacob Böhme, otherwise called the <note>original: "Philosophus Teutonicus"</note> *Teutonic Philosopher*. These are presented in such a form and order as has been desired for many years by the lovers of these excellent <note>original: "Studii Theosophici"</note> *Theosophical Studies*. In doing so, we have deemed it unavoidably necessary to steer the kind reader away—with a faithful heart and as much as is within our power—from certain prejudices he might encounter regarding both the author's testimonies and this present arrangement. For this reason, we provide this short preface to remind him: 1. What moved us to arrange and publish these high writings in such an order. 2. How the kind reader should view and profitably receive this arrangement of ours.

§. 2. Concerning the motivating cause: it has been well over 12 years since we—according to the measure of our understanding at that time, and prompted by much internal and external occasion—published our first treatise on the 12 articles of the Christian confession of faith, under the title: **Depiction of the Hidden Person of the Heart.** This writing, contrary to our expectations, found its way among many earnest lovers of theosophical studies and the writings of the late *Teutonicus* <note>Refers to Böhme, the "Teutonic" or German philosopher.</note>. They found in it much similarity and agreement with the testimonies of this highly-enlightened author and therefore sought to confer with me about it in Christian friendship. However, because at that time I had not read these sublime writings of the late Jacob Böhme (except for the treatise on the Incarnation of Christ), and saw neither the means nor the opportunity to acquire them, all the works of that blessed man were sent to me from distant lands through the special direction of GOD and the provision of a faithful patron and benefactor. Thus, I was faithfully and earnestly directed toward this high study.

§. 3. Regarding the theological matters and testimonies, I found in them a singular harmony with GOD’S leadings of my soul at that time. The doctrine of repentance, the instruction on prayer, the powerful convictions of the Spirit toward a humble obedience of faith, as well as the entire foundation of <term>Rebirth</term> <note>In Böhme's thought, "Wiedergebuhrt" (Rebirth) is not a metaphor but a literal spiritual process where the soul is transformed back into its original divine state.</note>, redemption, justification, and the sanctification of the poor sinner before GOD through JESUS Christ, were to me like golden nails for the fastening of what was occurring in my soul. But as for the mysteries of theosophical study—how the invisible, eternal Godhead introduced itself into nature and creature, and became active and manifest therein according to the 7 <term>Principles</term> and the 7 <term>Properties of Nature</term> <note>These represent the stages of manifestation from the divine "Nothing" into the physical "Something," moving from dark desire to light and expression.</note>—I could by no means fundamentally recognize or grasp such things at that time, though I read with great desire day and night and often repeated what I had read. Indeed, through meditation and sharp reflection, it became darker and darker the longer I tried, so that for a time I had to lay these writings aside and be content with my understanding at that time. In the meantime, the guiding hand of GOD led me into another school, wherein I was given many a difficult lesson to learn; many and various trials and temptations also came upon me, now from worries about sustenance, now from flesh and blood,

<meta>This page continues the author's personal narrative regarding his spiritual crisis and his eventual discovery of Jacob Böhme’s writings. He explains the transformative effect these works had on him and begins to analyze why Böhme's style is so difficult for the average reader or scholar to understand.</meta>

...sometimes by the spirit of this world, sometimes by heavy inner temptations, divine abandonment, terrifying anxieties, and such strongly persistent powers of darkness that it often seemed as if hell had opened its jaws with all its might and properties to swallow me up, both bodily and spiritually. I do not wish to provide a list or a lengthy report of these things here. My intention is only to let the kind reader understand how it pleased the **Wisdom of GOD** <note>In Böhme’s theology, 'Wisdom' (or Sophia) is the divine mirror or feminine principle through which God is revealed.</note> to prepare me in her school through much inner suffering and many hard trials, so that I might more thoroughly recognize her high mysteries. For through such hard trials, the **star of my reason** <note>original: "Gestirn meiner Vernunfft"; a term referring to the natural human intellect as influenced by the earthly or astral realm.</note> was somewhat weakened, the **veil of the flesh** was torn, and the heart was purified more and more from foreign fire, so that the **Spirit of JESUS Christ**, like a bright **morning star**, began to announce a new day and to awaken the **life of JESUS** in great joy of faith. But because the life of JESUS often still had many a struggle with **selfhood** <note>original: "Selbstheit"; the ego-driven will that operates independently of God.</note>, both in the will and in the reason, the light still had great alternation with the power of darkness, and the little fountain of divine love was often hindered by external circumstances, and thereby the clear mirror of wisdom was troubled.

->§. 4.<-

Although the fire of Divine Omnipotence was always driving me, and the Spirit of JESUS blew so powerfully to work out of the **Mystery** <note>original: "Mysterio"; the hidden, unmanifested ground of God's being.</note>, the light was nevertheless darkened again at times. In this state, I devoted myself to reading the writings of the highly enlightened **Jacob Böhme**. Whatever else came into my hands, I found next to Holy Scripture nowhere else but in these a similar strengthening taste, and such agreement in everything I could grasp. What years ago I was unable to achieve with all my meditating, reading, and self-torment now opened itself to me of its own accord as clearly as bright day. Beyond this, I found such an earnest inner drive to devote myself to this study that at first I held it to be a temptation, as it often occurred to me as if I were being worked upon, driven, and prompted by a foreign spirit that did not rise from the fire of my own heart. Therefore, I often earnestly prayed to God that if such a strong driving of the mind originated from anything other than His will and fire of love, His faithfulness toward me would not let me work toward a foreign growth. However, as often as I tried to lead the spirit of my will into something else, it would occupy itself with nothing else; indeed, it seemed as if the spirit of the **blessed author** <note>Refers to the deceased Jacob Böhme.</note> also wished to encourage me in turn.

->§. 5.<-

In such an inner drive, I devoted myself with much earnestness and great joy to this high study. I read, re-read, tasted, and tested this spirit in all sorts of ways; and as harsh, sharp, strict, and rough as it seemed to me in the beginning, so lovely, sweet, and pleasant was the noble fruit. I spent two whole years in great earnestness, and in this so earnest study, I had various heavy trials from without and within. Although the study was interrupted thereby now and then, I nevertheless found afterward that the **little pearl-tree** <note>A poetic metaphor used by Böhme for the growth of the divine seed or "new man" within the soul.</note> nonetheless had a drive toward growth and revelation. So that my work might also bring me benefit in times of need, I began to briefly compose my understanding into a **memorial** <note>A personal record or summary intended to aid memory and further study.</note>. I investigated, above all things, the reasons why the writings of this highly enlightened man fall so hard for beginners of this study to grasp. I then found reasons, partly on the side of the writings and partly on the side of the reader.

->§. 6.<-

The writings themselves are composed just as they flowed into the pen of the blessed author, who originally wrote them for himself as a memorial. When the burning fire drove him so quickly, his hand and pen hurried after the impulse, so that it often fell like a **cloudburst** <note>original: "Platz-Regen"; a sudden, heavy downpour of rain.</note> which hits whatever it hits; and if it had been possible to grasp and write everything, the foundation would likely have been laid three times deeper. But that could not be; therefore, more than one book was made, and indeed always deeper, so that what could not be seized in one might be found in the other. This was then the reason that the author often began to treat one matter and, in the meantime, wandered completely away from it onto another subject, whereby in many places the connection and link between truths was broken, and countless repetitions of the same and very same testimonies were presented. Also: that the blessed author used many foreign ways of speaking in his writings and cites many **Latin** and **German** words in a completely different sense than is customary in those languages. He was not born into the schools of this world, so he did not bind himself to their **school-wisdom** <note>Formal academic or theological training.</note>, but used words and **terms** <note>original: "Terminos"</note> as he deemed most convenient according to his understanding.

->§. 7.<-

The causes on the part of the reader are primarily because the reader is usually so **misinformed** <note>original: "verbildet"; literally "mis-formed" or wrongly educated by the world's systems.</note> that he searches more for his own meaning than for the author’s meaning in the writings; just as no people reach the author’s meaning less than those from the **school of this world**, who have no further intention than to either adorn themselves with foreign feathers and to scratch out and chatter after the author’s excellent testimonies, or to blaspheme that which they do not grasp with their coarse understanding, as the writings of the learned are full of such blasphemies. Many an otherwise more faithful mind, when searching these writings with much earnestness, still looks first—according to the perverse school-way—for an empty image or, as they call it, a clear concept and **ideal knowledge** <note>Theoretical or abstract knowledge as opposed to practical, spiritual experience.</note> of the matter, and neglects to [bring] the will of the soul to a true **obedience**...

<meta>This page continues the author's explanation of how human reason often fails to grasp divine mysteries. He transitions into his personal method for studying Jacob Böhme’s works, emphasizing humility, prayer, and the gradual discovery of spiritual truth.</meta>

...to bow in obedience, which is indeed the only key to unlocking this **treasure-chest of Divine Mysteries**. Since they then try to bring everything into comprehension through sharp meditation, speculation, and reflection, and by grasping the modes of speech according to the **scholastic sense** <note>original: "Schul-Sinn"; referring to formal academic or theological training rather than spiritual intuition.</note>, they imagine nothing but pure **chimeras and monsters of vain wisdom** in their fantasy.

§. 8. Since it has now pleased **Divine Wisdom**, in the manner described above, to awaken such a fire in my soul through the hidden power of her inward-working Spirit, and to lead the spirit of my mind into this high study with such a strongly persistent drive, I have—following the guidance of the Spirit of Grace, along with diligent prayer and persistence in the Spirit—endeavored above all things to clear away all **obstacles** <note>original: "obstacula"</note> or hindrances that might make the light and the truth of these writings foreign to me. For this reason, I set aside all my own images, concepts, previous knowledge, and intellectual powers for a time, and indeed fashioned my spirit as the author requires of a simple reader. I approached this study in a holy awe, like an incoming apprentice, and truly began at the **A.B.C.** <note>The author refers to learning the basic spiritual "alphabet" or fundamental principles of Böhme’s mystical system.</note> I first sought out the clearest testimonies, diligently contemplated them, and very sharply tested whatever was unknown to me regarding repentance, prayer, faith, and **rebirth**, until I found the actual taste of them. Thereafter, I proceeded to the spelling and composing of the testimonies into such an order and form that I might most easily come to a proper understanding; there I found such a concise connection of Divine Truths in these writings that each was the key to the concept of the other, and in the beginning one could see and recognize the end. Furthermore, I took special care to form nothing in my mind unless it was well-tested by the **will-spirit** <note>original: "Willen-Geist"; the faculty of the soul that directs intention and desire toward God.</note>, so that the spirit would not be burdened with anything beyond comprehension, or whereby some **Turba** <term>Turba: a term used by Jacob Böhme to describe a state of spiritual disturbance, chaos, or the "uproar" of the wrathful nature and divine wrath.</term> might arise in the mind, which could have caused a dizziness—as has happened to many earnest seekers, and likely to myself in the beginning. Finally, I guarded against haste, especially where the fire within was in too strong a drive, so that the spirit did not search too high or too deep all at once, but rather contented itself with how the truths opened themselves one after the other. Thus, I gradually came upon the **blessed field** in which this treasure lay hidden, where I did not cease to dig through earnest persistence in prayer and trust, until the **pearl** was found, for which I thank GOD in eternity, because through it many a hard knot has been untied for me, and many a dark mist driven out of my mind.

§. 9. Since this **pearl**, where it truly has its effect and birth, cannot hide the radiance of its glorious properties, but seeks to awaken its drive in others through its rays, I was encouraged by the Spirit of Wisdom—partly inwardly, and partly outwardly through other lovers of wisdom—to give the salvation-seeking reader an instruction on how he also should seek and find, just as I have sought and finally was found by her. There I found in myself a frankness to further increase this **talent** <note>A reference to the biblical Parable of the Talents (Matthew 25), regarding the responsibility to use God-given gifts for spiritual growth.</note>, just as I myself have been increased by the noble spirit of such excellent knowledge. Because the author himself already testified in his time to a great desire, and found it good, that finally only one [work] should be made out of all his writings, and all the others be put away, because the plurality—on account of the readers' hasty comprehension—causes only strife and adversity, especially among those who do not know how to distinguish the Spirit which speaks such a wondrous language; for reason often thinks it is contrary to her, and yet in the depth it is not contrary. Although I do not wish to present myself as the man who has hit upon everything according to the wish of the lovers [of wisdom]: nevertheless, it seems to me high time that someone begins to place the light—which until now, in view of the great multitude of men, has been seen by few but remains hidden under a **bushel** <note>A reference to Matthew 5:15: "Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick."</note> among most—upon a **candlestick**, and to put this precious **pound** <note>original: "Pfund"; another reference to the biblical parable of the minas/talents (Luke 19:13).</note> out for interest. If there is someone who can then bring it higher and present it even more radiantly than has been done here, he always retains his freedom; and it would give me a special joy to see such a jewel shining in its most glorious **lustre** <note>original: "lustre"; brilliance or splendor.</note> and in the most perfect radiance of its majesty, by whomever it might be presented. For as I believe that in this school, or in this study, no **Doctors** and **Masters** <note>original: "Doctores und Magistri"</note> are created who have fully studied **Theosophy** <term>Theosophy: "Divine Wisdom"; the mystical study of God's nature and the mysteries of creation.</term> and **Philosophy** and have perfectly recognized GOD in nature, but rather that here we are all still students who, even when they have come far and have grasped a good concept of the matter for themselves, can nonetheless bring nothing more to others than the **rudiments** <note>original: "Rudimenta"; the basic or first principles.</note> and the coarsest beginnings: so I will also here in this my work give myself out as no more than a **fellow-student**, even though I have endured many a school-trial in the years of my pilgrimage, and have found what I possess of this study to be proven in many tests. # Author’s Preface.

...soon by the spirit of this world, soon by heavy internal temptations, divine abandonment, terrifying anxieties, and such strongly persistent powers of darkness, that it often seemed as if hell had opened its maw with all its power according to its ancient nature to swallow me up, both bodily and spiritually. I do not wish to set down a list of these things here, nor to provide an extensive account. My intention is only to give the kind reader to understand how it pleased the **Wisdom of GOD** to prepare me in her school through much inner suffering and many hard trials, so that I might more fundamentally recognize her high mysteries. For through such hard trials, the **star of my reason** <note>A metaphor for human intellect, which the author believes must be dimmed to allow divine light to shine.</note> was somewhat weakened, the **veil of the flesh** torn, and the heart purified more and more from foreign fire, so that the **Spirit of JESUS Christ**, like a bright **morning star**, began to announce a new day and to awaken the **life of JESUS** in great joy of faith. But because the life of JESUS often still had many a struggle with **selfhood** <note>original: "Selbstheit"; refers to the ego-driven will that resists divine alignment.</note>, both in the will and in the reason, the light still experienced great fluctuation from the power of darkness, and the little fountain of Divine Love was often hindered by external circumstances, and thereby the clear mirror of Wisdom was clouded.

§. 4. Although the fire of **Divine Omnipotence** was always driving, and the **Spirit of JESUS** blew so powerfully to work out of the **Mystery** <note>original: "Mysterio"; the hidden depth of God's nature.</note>, nevertheless the light was sometimes obscured again. In this state, I devoted myself to reading the writings of the highly enlightened **Jacob Böhme** <note>original: "Jacob Böhms"; Böhme (1575–1624) was a German mystic whose complex works on the nature of God and the soul deeply influenced later Pietism and philosophy.</note>. Whatever else came into my hands, I found next to the **Holy Scripture** nowhere else but in these a similar strengthening taste, and such agreement in everything I could grasp. That which I was unable to achieve years ago with all my meditating, reading, and agonizing, now opened itself to me as clear as day. Moreover, I found such an earnest drive from within to devote myself to this study that I initially held it for a temptation, as it often occurred to me that I was being worked upon, driven, and impelled by a foreign spirit that did not rise from my heart's fire. Therefore, I often earnestly prayed to **GOD** that if such a strong driving of the mind originated from anything other than His will and fire of love, His faithfulness toward me would not allow me to labor upon a foreign growth. However, as often as I tried to lead my will-spirit into something else, it would concern itself with nothing else; indeed, it seemed as if the spirit of the late Author <note>referring to Jacob Böhme</note> wished to animate me in turn.

§. 5. With such an inner drive, I devoted myself with much earnestness and great joy to this high study. I read, re-read, tasted, and tested this spirit in all sorts of ways; and as harsh, sharp, strict, and rough as it appeared to me in the beginning, so lovely, sweet, and pleasant was the noble fruit to me. I spent two whole years in great earnestness, and in this so earnest study I had various heavy trials from without and within. Although the study was interrupted thereby now and then, I nevertheless found afterward that the **little pearl-tree** <note>original: "Perlen-Bäumlein"; a common metaphor in Böhme’s work representing the growth of Christ within the soul.</note> nonetheless had an impulse toward growth and revelation. So that my work might also be of use to me in times of need, I began to briefly compose my recognition into a **memorial** <note>original: "Memorial"; a record or notebook of spiritual insights.</note>. I investigated, above all things, the reasons why the writings of this highly enlightened man are so difficult for beginners of this study to grasp. I then found reasons partly on the side of the writings, and partly on the side of the reader.

§. 6. The writings themselves are composed just as they flowed into the pen of the late Author, as he initially wrote them for himself as a memorial. When the burning fire drove so quickly within him, his hand and pen hurried after the impulse; thus it often fell like a **cloudburst** <note>original: "Platz-Regen"</note> that hits whatever it hits. If it had been possible to grasp and write everything, the foundation would likely have been laid three times deeper. But that could not be; therefore, more than one book was made, and indeed ever deeper, so that what could not be seized in one might be found in another. This was then the reason why the Author often began to treat a matter and meanwhile moved entirely away from it, falling into another subject; whereby in many places, partly the connection and linking of truths was broken, and partly innumerable repetitions of the same and identical testimonies were presented. Likewise: that the late Author used many foreign modes of speech in his writings and cites many **Latin and German words** in a completely different sense than is customary in those languages. He was not born into the schools of this world, so he did not bind himself to their **school-wisdom**, but used the words and **terms** <note>original: "Terminos"</note> as he considered most convenient according to his recognition.

§. 7. The causes on the side of the reader are primarily because the reader is commonly so misinformed that he searches more for his own meaning in the writings than for the Author's. Indeed, no people achieve the Author's meaning less than those who are from the **school of this world** <note>A critique of academic theologians who prioritize intellectual logic over spiritual experience.</note> and have no further intention than either to adorn themselves with foreign feathers and to inquire after and chatter about the Author’s excellent testimonies, or to blaspheme that which they cannot grasp with their coarse understanding—as the writings of the learned are full of such blasphemies. Many an otherwise true-minded soul, when searching these writings with much earnestness, still looks first—according to the perverse school-fashion—for an empty image or, as they call it, a clear concept and **ideal recognition** of the matter, and neglects to bring the will of the soul to a true

For just as a true prophet is like the flower of a plant, which reveals the properties of the whole plant through its shape, color, scent, and power, so this divine man of wonders was the flower of the departed seventeenth century. This flower, in the power of the Spirit and the Word, foretold what fruits the plant has brought forth from that time until our own. Thus, the late author predicted—in such detail that we may easily perceive the present and near future from the past—the heavy and <term>Thirty Years' War in Germany<note>A devastating series of conflicts in Central Europe (1618–1648).</note></term> which followed immediately after his death, the subsequent invasion of the Turks, as well as the resulting plague along with other terrifying judgments.

**§. 11.** Or do we not see how the <term>Turba<note>original: Latin "Turba." In Böhme’s thought, this refers to the spirit of disruption or the "stirrer" that awakens the wrath of God within nature or the soul, leading to chaos and destruction.</note></term> in our present century stands in a complete outbreak throughout all of Europe? How the properties of GOD’s fierce wrath are in a terrifying ignition, driving both the secular and the so-called spiritual governance toward the final goal of total ruin? There, the harsh, severe, and attractive properties of kings, princes, and authorities suck the sweat and blood—indeed, the very marrow and sap—from the bones of their subjects, so that many kingdoms and principalities are like an exhausted and emaciated <term>skeleton<note>original: Latin "sceleto."</note></term>. There, the power of darkness in its harsh form hardens the souls of men, and the cold fire constricts hearts into mere hard, rocky cliffs. There, the bitter <term>quality<note>original: "Qualität." Used here in Böhme's sense as a fundamental driving force or "source-property" of being.</note></term> rising up in the kingdom of wrath drives one king over another, one prince, count, nobleman, citizen, peasant—even one beggar over another—to exalt himself with all cunning and violence (from which arises all indescribable pomp, pride, bitterness, and hostility in secular government and civil life). Alongside this, it inflates the souls of men in such a way that most, like winged angels from the dark world, fly out over one another in spiritual pride, and rise so high in their own <term>qualification<note>original: "Qualificirung." The process by which a soul or spirit takes on a specific nature or "quality."</note></term> by their own fire-power that they eventually burn their wings and fall to the earth like poor earthworms—and some even go into the abyss of hell—and yet, in the kingdom of <term>Fantasy<note>original: Latin "Phantasiæ." For Böhme, this is a realm of false imagination and self-delusion divorced from divine reality.</note></term> with Lucifer, their suzerain, they seek to overwhelm everything with fierce fire-power. Much could be said of the poisonous envy and burning wrath, which is the ignition of hellish fire in secular and spiritual governance, all of which our late author foretold as clearly as if he were personally living through our present times himself. Especially noteworthy are the magnificent reminders and earnest warnings which Heavenly Wisdom has presented to her lovers through this sanctified instrument: namely, how a faithful soldier of Jesus Christ must break through the power of darkness by a living power of faith, and fight his way through all inner and outer powers of malice, and through all cunning and powerful temptations, so that he may keep the faith and attain the noble <term>Pearl-Wreath<note>original: "Perlen-Kranz." A symbol of the soul’s spiritual victory and its mystical union with Sophia (Divine Wisdom).</note></term> from the Virgin. For truly, today's struggle—not only against flesh and blood, but also against the powers of darkness and the spiritual forces of malice—is no small thing. On one side, <term>Stellar Reason<note>original: "gestirnte Vernunfft." Böhme’s term for human intellect that is limited to the physical, "astral" world and lacks divine enlightenment.</note></term> has placed its falsely-celebrated art upon the highest peak under a false appearance of heavenly wisdom, to which the godless <term>Descartes<note>original: Latin "Cartesius" (René Descartes). The author critiques Cartesian rationalism as a path toward secularism.</note></term> with his empty <term>philosophy<note>original: Latin "Philosophia."</note></term> has given great help and guidance. Under the pretext of cleansing human understanding of prejudices and eradicating all <term>superstition<note>original: "Superstition."</note></term> from churches and schools through his philosophy, he has opened a high and wide gate so that <term>Atheism<note>original: "Atheismus."</note></term>, <term>Spinozism<note>original: "Spinosismus." Referring to the philosophy of Baruch Spinoza, often accused of pantheism or atheism in this period.</note></term>, and <term>Naturalism<note>original: "Naturalismus." The belief that only natural laws and forces operate in the world, excluding the supernatural.</note></term>, with their whole...

...continuance of all profanity in teaching and life has gained free entry into churches and schools. In these schools, new philosophers, masters, and doctors are continually hatched; so many have already emerged that, like a swarm of locusts, they cover the land and, like a dark cloud, fog all the brilliance of wisdom in the consciences of men. By many, the entire Gospel history is viewed as a seventeen-hundred-year-old fable; the miracles of Christ are held to be mere parables; the mouth of Truth is mocked; and all earnest following of Christ, the taking up of His cross and tribulation, along with the denial of self and the killing of one's own lusts, is regarded as foolishness and slandered. Because, amidst this corruption of the world, the spirit of a truly rational man always searches, asks after wisdom, and wishes to recognize the ground and cause of all things—yet is easily led astray from the truth toward a vain delusion of wisdom by the aforementioned writings filled with empty chatter—we have wished to present to such deep-searching minds, instead of false <note>original: "philosophia"</note> philosophy, the writings of our highly-enlightened <term>Teutonic Philosopher<note>Philosophus Teutonicus: A title for Jakob Böhme (1575–1624), suggesting his role as a divinely inspired sage for the German-speaking world.</note></term>, wherein one is instructed to recognize GOD in all of nature and in all creatures, and to thoroughly conceive, understand, and distinguish the beginning and end of all things, their cause, birth, the kindling of life, growth, decline, <term>putrefaction<note>The process of decay or decomposition, which Böhme viewed as a necessary stage for spiritual or natural transformation.</note></term>, and change, <note>original: "ab ovo"</note> from the very beginning, as the saying goes.

§. 12. On the other hand, we see how the ignited <term>Turba<note>In Böhme’s terminology, the "Turba" is the spirit of disruption, confusion, or divine wrath that breaks forth when a thing loses its proper balance or divine order.</note></term> occasionally blows out a wind of new doctrine and vain opinions, as well as various spirits, whereby souls—otherwise eager for their salvation—are led away from Christ, the living rock of their salvation, and are driven about from one heap of sand to another. What new <note>original: "Motus"</note> movements have we not experienced? How do we not hear from all places in our entire Europe: "Look here! Look, there is Christ!"? What has not been written, shouted, and proclaimed under the great banner: *Thus speaks the LORD of Hosts / the LORD / LORD*: which shortly thereafter was called into doubt again by the prophets themselves, and even retracted as fraud and <note>original: "Phantasia"</note> fantasy? What an alarm was raised by a new <term>Economy<note>original: "Oeconomia." Refers to a proposed new social or religious order, likely alluding to radical pietist or millenarian movements of the time.</note></term>, to which everyone was invited under the name of the Holy Spirit, yet after long driving, moving, and speaking, the growth in many broke forth into "fruits of the flesh"? All of this our <term>blessed author<note>Jakob Böhme.</note></term> foretold; he revealed the growth of our presumed Zion at its deepest root and gave many faithful reminders of how we might well distinguish these dangerous times—what is flesh and spirit, and what the property and birth of each may be—to test them exactly and recognize every rising spirit (under whatever name, power, or appearance it may be) in the kindling of its life. Thus, all those who faithfully follow the loyal admonition of the Wisdom of GOD in this instrument [Böhme] receive a singular gift and power to distinguish these times and the spirits rising within them; and when they have searched the growth in its inner root and know its <note>original: "Qualificirung"</note> quality, they are not easily driven about by every wind, nor deluded by every appearance of truth.

§. 13. These are, therefore, the primary reasons why we first searched the writings of the late author for ourselves, and then presented them here for the benefit of others, arranged in the following order. It has been most fittingly divided into 4 main parts. In the **first part**, we have brought into a proper order the author's teachings, testimonies, and reminders regarding repentance, prayer, faith, and the <term>New Birth<note>Die neue Geburt: Böhme’s core doctrine that a human must undergo a radical internal transformation to return to the divine image.</note></term> as the sole key to the true and fundamental knowledge of the Great Mystery.

In the **2nd part**, we have given the kind reader instructions to unlock the <term>Great Mystery<note>original: "Mysterium Magnum." The ground of all being or the "chaos" out of which the Triune God manifests the world.</note></term> and to open all gates to the revelation of the Triune GOD in the flesh: specifically, how the Triune GOD introduced Himself into nature and the creature, and how He became manifest and active therein, according to the seven <term>Source-Spirits<note>original: "Quell-Geister." The seven foundational qualities or forces of Böhme's divine and natural cosmology.</note></term> of nature: First as a gracious and loving GOD, the highest good, life, light, and love, according to the **2nd Principle**, following the property of the Holy Light-World and the angelic, paradisical world: then also as a just and jealous GOD, and as a consuming fire, according to the **1st Principle**, following the property of the dark world and of hell.

In the **3rd part**, we have composed the author's doctrine of how the Triune GOD became manifest according to the **third Principle**, according to love and wrath, light and darkness, in the creation of this visible world and each and every one of its creatures, but especially of Man: here we have given guidance for the fundamental knowledge of how the Triune GOD created man through His almighty Word, and became manifest and active in him according to all 3 Principles and all seven properties of nature: Namely, 1. in the state of perfection, 2. in the state of his temptation, 3. in his Fall; and how, after the Fall occurred, GOD became manifest in man as an angry and jealous GOD, but again in the Word of promise as a gracious and merciful GOD. We have further opened the mystery of the propagation of man according to soul and body, and thereby refuted the error of predestination from the author’s treatise on the <term>Election of Grace<note>original: "Gnaden-Wahl." Böhme's work arguing against strict Calvinist predestination, emphasizing God's universal desire for salvation.</note></term>. We should have gone further here and presented the revelation...

### Author’s Preface.

...revelation and various <term>economies<note>Original: "Oeconomien oder Haushaltungen." These terms refer to the different stages or "divine stewardships" of God's plan throughout history.</note></term> of GOD under the administration of the Covenant of Grace. This includes how God revealed Himself to the patriarchs, both according to His strict justice in the <term>Line of Cain<note>In Böhme’s thought, the lineage of Cain represents the "dark world" and the "wrathful" side of nature, contrasted with the "light world" of the godly line.</note></term>, wherein the dark world and its properties flourished, and according to His grace and love in the Line of the Covenant. This line runs from Seth to Enoch, from Enoch to Noah, from Noah to Abraham, from Abraham to Moses, and from Moses to CHRIST. However, because explaining these circumstances properly and presenting all the wonders of God’s wrath and grace would require a massive volume—and since the author himself has already presented these wonders in a concise order according to the guidance of Scripture in his <term>*Mysterium Magnum*<note>Latin for "The Great Mystery," one of Böhme's most famous works, which provides an esoteric commentary on the Book of Genesis.</note></term>—we have chosen to pass over them here. We direct the interested reader to that work, until perhaps God’s providence gives us more opportunity to present those matters in a question-and-answer format and add them to this volume.

In the fourth part, we have revealed the revelation of GOD in Christ JESUS as the economy of the New Covenant. Here we have shown how the Covenant of Grace reached its goal in the Word of promise of the <term>Serpent-Crusher<note>Original: "Schlangen-Treter." A reference to Genesis 3:15, interpreted as Christ, who defeats the "serpent" of evil.</note></term>, and how Christ, the Son of GOD and the eternal Word of the Father, took on human nature in Mary. We have explained in detail how the Word became flesh and how GOD was revealed in the flesh; how Christ lived, taught, suffered, was crucified, died, was buried, rose again, and ascended to heaven to sit at the right hand of God’s majesty; and how He accomplished everything and carried out the entire work of redemption. Furthermore, we show how we should accept the work of redemption with true faith, how we are reborn in Christ, attain a new humanity, die to the "old man" and his lusts and desires, and walk in a new life through the power of Jesus Christ. In short: how we may become conformed to the image of Christ. We have also shown the true ground of the Holy Sacraments of Baptism and the Lord’s Supper, adhering strictly to the author’s own testimony and presenting it for impartial examination. Finally, we have included the author’s prophetic testimonies concerning the Fall of Babylon, the downfall of the Antichrist’s kingdom, and the future <term>Lily-Time<note>Original: "Lilien-Zeit." A Böhmean prophecy of a coming age of spiritual peace and enlightenment on Earth before the end of the world.</note></term>, as well as the state of souls after death and the Last Judgment, with which we bring the fourth part to a close.

Since many materials remained which belong to Philosophy and Astrology, or <term>Natural Magic<note>Original: "Magiæ Naturali." In the 17th century, this referred to the study of the hidden powers of nature rather than sorcery.</note></term>—such as the <term>Signature of All Things<note>Original: "Signatura Rerum." Böhme’s theory that every creature and object bears an external "sign" of its internal spiritual essence.</note></term>, the four complexions of man, the origin of diseases, and true medicine; also the mineral kingdom and the <term>Philosophical Work<note>Original: "philosophischen Werck." A common term for the "Great Work" of alchemy—the transformation of base matter into spiritual gold.</note></term>—we have added these separately in an appendix. This is to give the reader more cause for further investigation and more revelation beyond what our blessed author has already presented.

§. 14. The blessed author often presented one and the same matter with different parables, and frequent repetitions are found in his writings, which can often become tedious for a beginning reader. For this reason, we have first gathered all the <term>parallel passages<note>Original: "Loca Parallela."</note></term> together and printed the clearest among them. If anything remained in one or the other that was not found in the printed version, we saved it and inserted it fittingly in another place. In this way, we hope the gracious reader will find here a pithy extract and a choice selection of all the author’s testimonies. We have also endeavored to stay strictly within the author’s boundaries and not exceed his goals in any subject. We have left the pearl itself exactly as it is, changing nothing; we have only set it in such a form that its ornament, luster, and preciousness might be best recognized and revealed to the dim-sighted and the weak. Just as a goldsmith sets a diamond or gemstone in a form that allows its brilliance to play most magnificently and shine into the eyes, we have not *made* the pearl, but *found* it. We do not present it here as our own work, but as God’s gift, and we offer it to our neighbor in the form that seemed to us to shine most gloriously. We do not doubt that an honest heart will recognize our kind intentions in this study. Should anyone become eager to search these mysteries thoroughly, let them set their desire with true earnestness through prayer and faith into the source of the new life, in Jesus Christ, until the new birth is kindled in them and the Spirit of Jesus Christ becomes the driving force. Then they will have the key to unlock this excellent treasure-chest of wisdom. Without this key, everything remains sealed to them; but through it, the noble **Pearl-Tree** will break forth and bloom, in which they, along with us, will have unspeakable joy in time and eternity. Amen.

->Given in Amsterdam / in the days of Pentecost / 1715.<-
