<meta>This page continues the editorial introduction, moving from a summary of the book's contents to a defense of the author’s (Jacob Böhme's) character. It cites respected Lutheran theologians and provides cautionary tales of those who suffered divine judgment for attacking Böhme's works.</meta>

### Author’s Preface.

->* * *<-

Because the old testimonies, given by two Doctors of Theology at Wittenberg—namely Meisner and Gebhard—regarding the blessed Author’s <term>writings<note>The "Author" refers to Jacob Böhme (1575–1624), the German mystic and shoemaker whose complex, visionary writings often drew accusations of heresy.</note></term>, are being denied by today’s world: namely, that the former said: "He would not take the whole world and help condemn the man"; while the other is said to have answered him: "My dear colleague, I would not either; who knows what lies behind it? How can we judge what we have not grasped, nor can grasp, whether it be right or wrong, black or white? May God convert the man if he errs, and preserve us in His divine truth," etc. Therefore, we add here the judgment and counsel of the famous orthodox theologian, <term>Dr. Philipp Jacob Spener<note>Spener (1635–1705) was the "Father of Pietism," a movement within Lutheranism that emphasized personal piety and "living faith" over rigid dogma. His defense of Böhme was significant for the author’s legitimacy.</note></term>, which he gave concerning our godly Author and his writings, and which can be read in his treatise titled *The Freedom of Believers*, Chapter 6, 22, page 96: "Meanwhile, I heartily wish that God would awaken people who are not only learned and may possess what belongs to the understanding of such an author (which I do not consider enough), but who also have from Him a sufficient gift for the <term>discernment of spirits<note>A biblical concept (1 Corinthians 12:10) referring to the supernatural ability to distinguish between divine, human, or demonic influences in a person's speech or writing.</note></term>, who might thoroughly investigate the Author, precisely see what his opinion is in all matters, and then both test him according to God’s Word themselves and make his testing easier for others; so that one might finally see what one has in him, whether a wandering spirit or a good teacher, so as not to sin against him on one side or the other. Therefore, though I do not like to see many disputes in the Church, I would nevertheless not be displeased to see something written for and against this Author by various people for a while." <margin>Thus far this honest-minded theologian.</margin> With whom we agree insofar as the first part—the testing—is concerned, and we wish from our hearts that God would awaken faithful and experienced witnesses who, according to their inner sanctified "sense of smell" and "taste," and a healthy judgment in holy awe before God, may well investigate and distinguish everything, and give a pure and undaunted testimony to the clear truth. This, however, will not be settled by writing "pro or contra," but can only be attained through earnest prayer, living faith, joyful obedience, and a true sanctification in the Spirit of wisdom and truth: of which we wish to remind the reader.

->* * * * * *<-

Furthermore, we add several remarkable examples, cited by this same Dr. Spener, as an earnest warning to those who—in a godless manner—blaspheme our highly-enlightened Author and his precious gifts of grace and writings (which they neither grasp nor understand in the least), and condemn them with all sorts of improper, shameful, and mocking names. Just recently, such a blasphemous writing of "impartial truth" was published, in which, alongside other highly-esteemed men of God who have already lain under the earth for some hundreds of years and whose divine testimonies are a great blessing to many thousands of lovers of truth, our holy Author is also attacked in a blasphemous way. The aforementioned remarkable examples can be read in Dr. Ph. J. Spener’s treatise titled *Rescue of the Just Cause of Future Hope against Dr. A. Pfeiffer*, printed in duodecimo in Frankfurt, 1696, pages 260, §. 9, to page 293. After <term>M. J. G. Holtzhausen<note>Johann Georg Holtzhausen, a critic of the Pietists and Böhme.</note></term> in Frankfurt had presumed to refute Jacob Böhme’s writings in public print and violently contest his person and spirit—and had repeatedly reinforced this against Johann Mathäi (alias Zimmermann), who opposed him—it happened shortly thereafter that this Holtzhausen was visited by God with <term>consumption<note>Original: "Schwindsucht," an old term for tuberculosis.</note></term> and a terrible anguish of conscience. He died from this a few weeks later in the year 1693, publicly confessing that, because of his accusations against J. B., he found himself charged with the <term>sin against the Holy Spirit<note>In Christian theology, the "unforgivable sin" (Matthew 12:31), here interpreted as willfully attributing the work of the Holy Spirit to the devil.</note></term>, and that he had sinned grievously by undertaking the judgment and condemnation of J. B.’s writings, rather than refraining entirely from his person and spirit; for his judgment had been convicted by Böhme's booklet *The Way to Christ*. On account of this, he was violently accused and terrified in his conscience day and night, and driven to publicly retract everything. "I found," he said on page 264, "so much good in *The Way to Christ* that my heart began to tremble as to whether I had done the man wrong with my hard judgment, and whether I had not even committed the sin against the Holy Spirit by considering and reviling the spirit from which he wrote as a lying spirit, and that in public writings." He made this retraction in a missive to Dr. Spener, with the request to publish it, as all this can be seen and read in detail in the aforementioned treatise. Likewise, this same Dr. Spener recounts in this treatise on page 319, and in his *The Freedom of the Children of God against Dr. Meyer* on page 94, of a Superintendent named Zeller, who, after giving a sermon and blaspheming against Böhme, was "struck by the hand of God" and was plagued with terrifying hellish anguish until his end.

### Author’s Preface.

...revelation and the various <term>economies<note>From the Greek "oikonomia," referring to the different "households" or eras of God’s management of human history.</note></term> or households of GOD, under the administration of the Covenant of Grace: namely, how GOD was revealed in the Fathers—both according to His strict justice in the <term>Line of Cain<note>original: "Linea Cains"</note></term>, wherein the dark world and its properties operated and flourished, and according to Grace and Love in the Line of the Covenant, from Seth to Enoch, from Enoch to Noah, from Noah to Abraham, from Abraham to Moses, and from Moses to CHRIST. However, because revealing such matters with the proper detail and presenting all the wonders of GOD’s wrath and grace would require a large book—and since the Author himself presented these wonders according to the guidance of Scripture in a concise order in his <term>Great Mystery<note>original: "Mysterio Magno"; Böhme's massive commentary on Genesis, explaining the spiritual origins of the universe.</note></term>—we have chosen to pass over it here. We wish to direct the kind reader there until perhaps GOD’s providence gives us more opportunity to present those matters in question-and-answer form and add them here.

In the fourth part, we have revealed the revelation of GOD in Christ JESUS as the economy of the New Covenant. There, we have shown how the Covenant of Grace reached its goal in the word of promise of the <term>Bruiser of the Serpent<note>A reference to the prophecy in Genesis 3:15, interpreted as the first promise of the Messiah.</note></term>, and how Christ, the Son of GOD and the eternal Word of the Father, took on human nature in Mary. We have detailed how the Word became flesh and GOD was revealed in the flesh; how Christ lived in the flesh, taught, suffered, was crucified, died, was buried, rose again, and ascended into heaven, seating Himself at the right hand of the Majesty of GOD; and how He accomplished everything and carried out the entire work of redemption. Furthermore, we show how we should accept the work of redemption with true faith, how we are <term>born again<note>original: "wiedergebohren"; a central theme for Böhme, referring to a literal internal transformation rather than just a legal status.</note></term> in Christ, obtain a new humanity, die to the old man and his lusts and desires, and walk in a new life through the power of Jesus Christ. In short: how we may become conformed to Christ. We have also shown the true foundation of the Holy Sacraments, Baptism and the Lord’s Supper, in which we have adhered strictly to the Author's testimony and presented it for impartial examination. Finally, we have also cited the Author's prophetic testimonies concerning the Fall of Babylon, the downfall of the Antichristian kingdom, the coming <term>Lily-Time<note>original: "Lilien-Zeit"; Böhme's term for a future golden age of spiritual peace and clarity before the end of the world.</note></term>, as well as the state of souls after death and the Last Judgment, thereby bringing the fourth part to a close.

However, since many subjects remained that belong to Philosophy and Astrology, or <term>Natural Magic<note>In the 17th century, "Natural Magic" referred to the study of the hidden powers of nature and the divine signatures within the physical world, not sorcery.</note></term>—such as the *Signature of All Things*, the four complexions of man, the origin of diseases, and true medicine; likewise, the mineral kingdom and the <term>Philosophical Work<note>A reference to alchemy, which Böhme used as a metaphor for the spiritual purification of the soul.</note></term>—we have added these separately in an Appendix, to give the reader more cause for further investigation and a broader opening beyond what our late Author presented.

§. 14. The late Author often presented one and the same matter with various parables, and frequent repetitions are often found in his writings, which can often become tedious for a beginning reader. Therefore, we have first gathered all <term>Parallel Passages<note>original: "Loca Parallela"</note></term> and printed the clearest among them. If anything remained in one or another passage that was not found in the printed version, we saved it and inserted it appropriately in another place, so that, hopefully, the kind reader will have here a pithy extract and a choice selection of each and every one of the Author's testimonies. We have also endeavored to remain strictly within the Author’s boundaries and not go beyond his goal in any matter. We have left the pearl as it is in itself and changed nothing in it; we have only set it in such a form so that it might be best recognized and revealed in its beauty, radiance, and preciousness to the dim-sighted and the weak. Just as a goldsmith is accustomed to setting a diamond or gemstone in such a form through which its brilliance can play most magnificently and shine into the eyes: thus, we have not *made* the pearl, but *found* it. We do not present it here as our work, but as GOD’s gift, and we set it before our neighbor in such a form as it appeared to us to shine most magnificently. We do not doubt for a moment that an honest-minded heart will recognize our kind intention in this study. If anyone should thereby become eager to search these mysteries thoroughly, let him set his desire with right earnestness through prayer and faith into the source of the new life, in Jesus Christ, until the new birth is ignited in him and the Spirit of Jesus Christ becomes the driving force. Then he will have the **Key** to unlock this excellent treasure-chest of wisdom; without which key, everything remains sealed to him, but through which the noble **Pearl-Tree** will break forth and bloom for him, in which he will have unspeakable joy with us in time and eternity. Amen.

->Given in Amsterdam / in the days of Pentecost / 1715.<-

Because the old testimonies, given by two <term>Doctors of Theology<note>original: "Doctores Theologiæ"</note></term> at Wittenberg—namely Meisnerus and Gebhardus—concerning the writings of the late Author, are being denied by today's world: specifically where the former said: *He would not take the whole world if it meant helping to condemn the man*; while the other is said to have answered him: *My dear colleague, neither would I / who knows what lies behind it / how can we judge / what we have not grasped / nor can grasp / whether it is right or wrong / black or white / may GOD convert the man / if he errs / and keep us in His divine truth / etc.* Therefore, we add here the judgment and counsel of the famous Orthodox Theologian, Dr. Philip Jacob Spener, which he gave regarding our godly Author and his writings, and which can be read in his treatise titled: **The Freedom of Believers, Chapter 6, 22. p. m. 96.** "In the meantime, I heartily wish that GOD would raise up people who are not only learned and possess what is required to understand such an author (which I do not consider sufficient), but who also have from Him an adequate gift for <term>discerning the spirits<note>original: "Geister zu unterscheiden"; a spiritual gift mentioned in 1 Corinthians 12:10 to distinguish divine inspiration from other sources.</note></term>; people who would thoroughly investigate the Author and see exactly what his opinion is in all matters, and then test him according to GOD’s Word themselves, as well as making his examination easier for others. This is so that one might finally see what one has in him: an **errant spirit or a good teacher**, so as not to sin against him on one side or the other. Therefore, although I do not like to see many disputes in the Church, I would nevertheless not be displeased to see people write <term>for and against<note>original: "pro und contra"</note></term> this Author for a while." <margin>Thus far this honest-minded theologian.</margin> We agree with him in so far as the first part—the examination—is concerned, and heartily wish that GOD would raise up faithful and experienced witnesses who, according to their inner sanctified "scent" and "taste" and a healthy judgment, might investigate and distinguish everything in holy awe before GOD, and give a pure and fearless testimony to the clear truth. This, however, will not be settled by writing *for* or *against*, but can only be obtained through earnest prayer, living faith, joyful obedience, and true sanctification in the Spirit of Wisdom and Truth: of which we wish to remind the reader.

We further add several remarkable examples, which this same Dr. Spener cites as a serious warning to those who—in a godless manner—blaspheme our highly-enlightened Author and his precious gifts of grace and writings (which they neither grasp nor understand in the slightest) and condemn him with all sorts of improper, shameful, and mocking names. He said (on page 264): "I found so much good in *The Way to Christ* that my heart began to tremble, wondering if I had done the man wrong with my harsh judgment, and whether I had even committed the Sin against the Holy Spirit by considering and reviling the spirit from which he wrote as a lying spirit, and doing so in public writings." He made this retraction in a missive to Dr. Spener, with the request to publish it, as all of this can be seen and read in detail in the aforementioned treatise. This same Dr. Spener also recounts in this treatise (page 319) and in his *Freedom of the Children of GOD against Dr. Meyer* (page 94) of a superintendent named Zeller who, after delivering a sermon and blasphemy against Böhme, was "touched by the hand of GOD" and was plagued by terrifying hellish anguish until his end.

**§. 2.** The content of this preface is a critique or examination of two types of people who stand in direct opposition to one another. Some hold the Author, **Jacob Böhme**, in such high regard that, according to these excessive admirers, nothing short of **canonization** and **infallibility** would be equal to the greatness of his merits. Others, on the contrary, curse him as a devilish heretic, or despise him as a vain <term>spirit-driven fanatic<note>original: "Geist-Treiber"; a derogatory term for someone perceived as being driven by false spiritual inspirations or "enthusiasm."</note></term> who is deranged in his brain. This is done to such an extent that no one dare confess a tolerable opinion of this Author before them without being suspected of all manner of godlessness. Indeed, some are found who, having spent barely a few hours reading these writings, are judged as if they had spent their time on nothing but foolish pranks and filth, to their own folly and pure madness.

**§. 3.** Furthermore, I will gladly confess that I have ventured far into the investigation of these two mightily-clashing parties; nonetheless, I deny that anyone can rightfully accuse me of wrongdoing. Rather, this great difference of opinion provides a fair occasion for a certainly moderate and laudable curiosity to investigate the matter itself, and to research how it lies hidden in its innermost depths. For it was indeed the lot of our Savior Himself that, just as He was held by some to be the Son of GOD, He was held by others to be one who possessed a devil.

**§. 4.** To those who consider the Author **infallible**, and who so highly **esteem** and admire his writings, More seeks to excuse himself.

**§. 5.** He then continues to speak of the others, who curse Jacob Böhme as a devilish man, or despise him as a poor and lowly writer. For the spirit that manifests itself in his writings is so far from being a devilish spirit that it is, rather, a particularly **Christian spirit**. This is evident because he emphasizes nothing so often as humility, love, gentleness, and brotherly love; likewise, nothing so much as a perfect submission to the will of GOD, a perfect renunciation of ourselves, the denial of this world and all the vanities of this present life, in the full hope of those unspeakable joys which we shall share with all **holy souls** and angels in **Paradise**. ->So much from the preface of the treatise, **A Critique of the Teutonic Philosophy.** <note>original: "Philosophia Teutonica Censura."</note> And in the treatise itself / §. 2. he gives the following testimony of our author:<-

I confess indeed / that I had no small aversion in my mind toward reading this obscure author / but the rich veins of moral and divine testimony found here and there within him / have so wonderfully refreshed me / and so occupied my mind / that the disgust I feared has been changed into pure delight and pleasure. There is in his writings such a simple and innocent spirit / which so powerfully drives us to perform that to which we are chiefly obligated / touching the mind so strongly and mightily / and insinuating and pressing itself into the soul with such a wholesome and unaffected loveliness / that I now certainly cease to wonder / that people whose excellent gifts of understanding are joined with a love for the fear of God and virtue / are drawn to a godly obligation and high esteem for the writings of this holy man: And I am not without a strong suspicion / that something greater than the human lies hidden therein; yes, at times not without a **presumption** <note>original: "Præsumption"; here meaning a strong assumption or intuitive belief.</note> / that everything is infallibly inspired / primarily because the author himself so often and so reliably declares / that he wrote from such a ground of divine inspiration. Moreover, I confess once more / that I believe / there was no knavish deceit in this man / but that he spoke what he recognized from the bottom of his heart.

---

Thus far **Henry More** <note>Henricus Morus (1614–1687), a prominent Cambridge Platonist who initially admired Böhme but later became more critical.</note>, the famous English philosopher, whose testimony might better be called an **Apologia** <note>A formal defense of a position or person.</note> and protective writing / than a **Critique** <note>original: "Censura."</note> of our author and his writings. These are More’s own words, which we have translated from the Latin language. With what grounds, however, one thing or another in J. B.’s writings is critiqued and blamed by him, that an impartial reader may judge for himself. Some wish to assert that this More, who was formerly a great **Cartesian** <note>A follower of the philosophy of René Descartes, which emphasized reason and dualism.</note>, changed his sentiment after reading the writings of J. B. / and he may have undertaken such a **Critique** / partly to make the writings more widely known / and partly, as a highly learned man, to prevent any suspicion of heresy / and to avoid having the reputation / that such a critic and mighty philosopher had learned something from such a humble instrument in philosophy. Just as today / among theologians as well as philosophers / many, out of ambition, most despise and reject those very writings from which they have gathered their greatest and best knowledge / only so that they may more boldly bring to light as their own that which they have secretly stolen.

<summary>This page concludes the preface by citing Henry More's glowing, if cautious, praise for Jacob Böhme’s spiritual sincerity and divine inspiration. The editor suggests that even More's criticisms were likely a strategic move to protect his own academic reputation while secretly drawing from Böhme's "Teutonic Philosophy."</summary>

# CLAVICULA
### Or
## Small Key/
#### By which the earnest seeker is given instruction / to find the right sense and understanding of the most prominent unusual modes of speech / terms and words / and to more deeply open the author’s <note>The author refers to Jacob Böhme.</note> foundation. Compiled according to the order of the alphabet.

->**A.**<-

**A.** The first and most prominent letter of the alphabet and of all languages; it issues forth from the heart in total freedom, without form and without any obstruction, neither of the throat, nor the tongue, nor the teeth, nor the lips. This vowel and tone signifies the free, image-less, and form-less working <term>Will of God</term> <note>Böhme often describes God's initial state as a "Will" seeking to manifest itself.</note> for the revelation of the eternal, hidden Godhead: From this A, as the first beginning, all other letters of the alphabet proceed, both in speaking and in writing.

**Abyss** <note>original: "Abgrund"</note> / see **Groundless** <note>original: "Ungrund"; Böhme's term for the nothingness or "Great Mystery" that precedes all creation.</note>.

**Adonai** <note>original Hebrew: "Lord"</note>, is what the author calls the first movement of the eternal, unfathomable unity toward the opening or revelation of the single Godhead into the multiplicity of innumerable creatures. Now, because this first movement arises from an eternal freedom of the will, without the urge or moving cause of a higher power, the author’s meaning is entirely in agreement with the understanding of the Hebrew text, where the word **Adonai** is translated to mean a sovereign and free-commanding Lord who has no higher power above him.

**Eternity** <note>original: "Æternitæt"</note> refers to such an eternity in which God has revealed Himself in a specific way to the rational creature. Thus, the revelation of GOD under the Law is called one eternity; the revelation of GOD in the Son is called another eternity.

**Ether** <note>original: "Æther"</note> is what the author calls not so much the air or the visible sky, but rather the womb and container from which every spirit is conceived, and to which it ascends again when it is dissolved. The schools <note>Referring to the Scholastic academic tradition.</note> call it a <term>Centrum</term> <note>Latin: "Center"</note>, a resting point; the author sometimes calls it a <term>sedem</term> <note>Latin: "seat" or "throne"</note>, a seat-place. Just as the sea is a seat-place and gathering of the waters: so every spirit or creature has its own Ether.

<column-break/>

**Alchemy** <note>original: "Alchymia"</note> is the name of the **Art of Separation**, through which the Alchemist or artist separates the pure from the impure, dissolves the blessing from the curse, and love from the wrath, and brings the good to its proper perfection.

**Alphabet** properly refers to those forms and figures through which a word is spoken or written, such as a, b, c. Such figures or letters are either **Vowels** <note>original: "Vocales"</note> or **Consonants** <note>original: "Consonantes"</note>. **Vowels** are certain voices that come from the heart and sound like air driven into a pipe, such as: ***a***, which is a free tone without form; ***e***, a somewhat narrower tone where the will draws the throat together a little; ***i***, a narrow tone where the will-spirit draws the throat tight and drives the tone in the breath out from the inner ignition of life or will through the narrow throat; ***o***, a free resonance of the will, but is shaped into a circle by the lips of the mouth; just as the mouth figures itself when the tone sounds as a ***u***. **Consonants** are forms, figures, and images in which the resonance of the working will captures itself for revelation, much like air driven into the various pipes of an organ.

**Alphabet of the Language of Nature** <note>original: "Natur-Sprach"</note> is the common name for all creatures of the heavens and the earth, which are actually nothing other than certain forms and figures through which GOD speaks His almighty Word and reveals His otherwise hidden will, in love and wrath, according as the Will of GOD drives and works within them. Thus the whole world, together with all creatures, is [the Language of Nature]

### Clavicula, or a Small Key to Unusual Modes of Speech.

natures of heaven and earth are an ever-echoing Word, which is spoken for ever and ever, and a book sealed with seven seals; he who has the power to unlock them can read and recognize the otherwise hidden Will of God in such a book, and therein behold God with wonder. In every creature, he perceives a character and letter of Divine Revelation; from its form, image, connection, and fellowship with others, he makes syllables; from syllables, words; and from words, whole sentences and speeches, through which he recognizes God’s active Will. But in particular, the **Alphabet of the Language of Nature** <note>original: "Natur-Sprach"; Böhme believed that before the Fall, Adam spoke a language that perfectly expressed the inner essence of all things.</note> is the form, figure, and image of a sound, through which every creature—and most of all man—makes manifest and gives to be understood the inner property and working of his will. For just as a breath of air arises from the lighting of a fire, so a spirit proceeds from every working of the will; and the more effective the will is, the more the spirit drives toward revelation. Whatever property, form, and impression the will has, the spirit is also active in that form, and in turn shapes the instruments for speaking, such as the throat, tongue, teeth, lips, and mouth. Just as a resonance or sound is formed in speaking by the throat, tongue, etc., so too did the ancients form and shape their letters in the beginning; from this, the first art of writing arose, as can still be noticed to some extent in the degenerated and distorted Hebrew style of writing and other Oriental languages, though that does not strictly belong here.

**Alphabet- or Letter-Spirits**; the author calls these the inwardly working spirits of the will, which are contained within a certain form, image, and property. Thus, he who knows the spirits of the letters in their driving, working, echoing, and speaking, also knows the inner centers, beginnings, and roots of the ignition of a will. For as the will has a form in the mind, so a spirit rises up; and as the spirit is formed and has an impression, so it also makes for itself a form and image in speaking, which the inner hearing distinguishes.

**Anatomicus** <note>Latin: "Anatomist"</note> is one who, according to his art, dissects the dead corpse of a human or animal, and from this intends to learn the ground and mystery of nature; such an art is called *Anatomia* <note>Anatomy</note>.

**Animalic** <note>original: "Animalisch"</note> usually means "beastly," from *Animal* <note>Latin: "a beast/animal"</note>. However, in the book *Aurora*, the author takes the word from *Anima* <note>Latin: "the soul"</note>, and with it actually designates a spirit that rises out of a fire-soul, and seeks to ignite such a life as that from which it arose. Thus, the animal spirit of Lucifer is one rising out of the ignited fire of the wrath of God, in order to ignite such a fire of wrath in the Godhead and in all creatures.

<column-break/>

(14)

**Antimony** <note>original: "Antimonium"</note> is a mineral, which is commonly called stibnite <note>original: "Spieß-Glaß"</note>.

**Apologia** <note>Greek/Latin: "Apology"</note> is a written defense that a defendant puts forth for his accountability.

**Aquaster**, from *Aqua* <note>Latin: "water"</note> and *Astrum* <note>Latin: "star"</note>, is that property in the working cause through which an essence, or *Materia Universalis* <note>universal matter</note>—which is otherwise neither dry nor wet, neither hot nor cold—is terminated into water. Such an Aquaster is either divine, being a working cause such that God, who in and of Himself is neither this nor that, nevertheless becomes manifest to the ignited and thirsty as a living water. Or it is a heavenly Aquaster, through which the pure element flows together like a spiritual water, and the volatile parts of the essence are bound into the form and figure of water. There is also an Aquaster of this visible world, which has made the essence of the pure element into water and bound it in such a property; just as another property of the working cause coagulates the same essence into sulfur or earth.

**Arcanum** <note>Latin: "secret/mystery"</note> refers to a hidden mystery that lies concealed in a secure container, as in a chest, and may not be unlocked except by a proper key.

**Archæus** <note>A Paracelsian term for the "inner alchemist" or vital force.</note> refers to the working Word, or cause, in every creature, through which everything is formed according to the creature’s impression and property. Each *Principium* <note>Latin: "Principle"</note> has its Archæus, which grasps, orders, and digests the universal essence, tincture, or Spirit of God according to the property of that Principle. Thus, the Archæus in a snake orders the power of the sun into a venomous life, and in a thistle into the thistle-green, but in a lamb into a gentle life of joy, and in a lily into a pleasant, lovely scent. Physicians <note>original: "Medici"</note> use the word for that power and property in the stomach through which all consumed food is digested, and each kind of juice is guided and distributed to its proper place in the body.

**Artista** <note>Latin: "Artist"</note> refers to an experienced practitioner of an art, in particular a great lover of chemical sciences <note>i.e., an alchemist</note>.

**Ascendant**, strictly speaking, the part of the *Primi Mobilis* <note>Latin: "First Mover," referring to the outermost celestial sphere</note> rising *pro tempore* <note>for the time being</note>, the *Horoscopus* <note>Horoscope</note>, or the...

### Clavicula, or a Small Key to Unusual Modes of Speech.

B 3

the **rising degree of the Ecliptic** <note>original: "Gradus Eclipticæ Oriens"</note>; but metonymically <note>A figure of speech where a thing is called by the name of something associated with it.</note> it refers to the resulting qualification of every earthly subject <note>original: "Sublunar Subjecti," referring to beings existing below the moon, i.e., on Earth.</note> drawing its first breath. Because the **First Mover** <note>original: "Primum Mobile," the outermost sphere of the heavens in classical astronomy, which provides motion to all others.</note> never stands still for a moment, the **Ascendants** are also in constant change; one person's Ascendant is either with, against, above, or below another’s; and of equal diversity is the influence on all sides. That toward which one is naturally inclined, another is naturally disinclined: the former always holds a secret dominion over the latter, and the latter serves the former without any apparent reason. These various Ascendants are spirits that spring from the ignition of the starry fire within visible nature. They have their dominion in the air and are rooted in the stars. Just as the stars are diverse, so too are the Ascendants of various kinds, both in their longing and drive, as well as in their rising and elevation; they are, as it were, an imitation which temporal nature brings forth, drives, and moves through its stars, just as eternal nature brings forth the spirits of the world of darkness and the world of light, whose wonders these Ascendants mimic and play out. However, they have no fixity or permanence, but are changeable and fleeting, because they have sprouted from a changeable root in the stars.

**Star** <note>original: "Astrum"</note> is properly the name for a constellation, but according to the author’s meaning, it is manifold: one belongs to eternal nature, by which we are primarily to understand the seven forms of nature—divine in God, angelic in angels, and hellish in devils. The other "star" belongs to temporal nature, namely the seven forms for the revelation of God’s will in this visible world: such a "star" is either starry, or of the four elements, vegetable, animal, or mineral, through which the constellation arises. Thus, neither in heaven, nor in hell, nor in this world, is there a single creature that does not have such a "star."

**Astral** is the name for everything that is effected and ignited by any "star" <note>original: "Astro"</note>.

**Astrologer, Astronomer** is the name for such a wise man who fundamentally recognizes the "star" and inner property of every creature, and who well understands the constellation of every creature—visible and invisible, earthly and heavenly—and also distinguishes their procreation and birth, their working, and that which they produce. Such knowledge is called **Astronomy.**

**Aurora** means the "Morning Glow"; the author gives this name to his first treatise because the light was then beginning to rise for him, preceding the sun, so that while writing this book, he had not yet reached the highest degree of true knowledge.

<column-break/>

->B.<-

**Merciful** <note>original: "Barmherzig"</note> means for the author the same as **warm-hearted** <note>original: "warmherzig"</note>. **Warm** is a very tempered fire, whose fierce hunger is pacified so that it no longer burns and consumes, but rather, like the warmth of a mother, awakens life and also nurtures and maintains the life it has awakened. Hence the word **Barm** in the Old Saxon language means as much as a ferment or sourdough that awakens a whole mass and brings it into digestion <note>Böhme uses "digestion" in an alchemical sense, meaning a process of maturation or transformation.</note>. **Heart** means as much as a powerful drawing and longing of love, so that **Merciful** <note>Barm-herzig</note> refers to the great fountain-spring of God's warming and attracting love, or the omnipotence of the Father in the Son, through which all things are awakened into life and maintained therein; this agrees entirely with both the Hebrew and Greek root words, which signify the rumbling of the inward parts or the active warmth of the heart. The reader should reflect further on this.

**Lightning-Flash** <note>original: "Blitz"</note> is what the author calls the desire and longing that rises from the ignition of a will, with a very rapid drive, in order to reach the light and revelation in gentleness. Just as a flash from the ignition of the will flashes through the eyes and enters into that which the will desires—as can be judged by an angry or amorous face. The author calls such a rising power a "flash" because of its speed, like lightning in thunder, when the sulfurous parts ignite in an instant through the rapid, contracting movement and penetrate everything with their flash. The flash is either sincere, straight, and strong, or squinting—that is, false, crooked, bent, and flashing crosswise.

->C.<-

**Kabbalah** <note>original: "Cabala"</note> is a fundamental science and knowledge through which the wise man recognizes hidden mysteries. Such knowledge is either Divine—where the Divine Kabbalist, through the Eye of Wisdom, fundamentally recognizes all inner shapes, forms, figures, images, qualifications, ways of life, union, and fellowship of a spirit, angel, or soul, and how and why God has revealed Himself thus in each of them—or it is an Intellectual Kabbalah, where the wise man recognizes each and every creature of this world, along with its property, qualification, and nature, from its outer image, signature, resonance, and sound.

(17)

### Clavicula, or a Small Key to Unusual Modes of Speech.

recognizes language and tone, and also knows what GOD intended to signify through them. Thus, the wise Cabalist <note>A practitioner of the Kabbalah; here, Böhme refers to someone who can read the "signatures" or secret meanings God placed within the natural world.</note> knows all the letters and figures in the great Book of Nature, assembles syllables and words from their fellowship, and therefrom reads and contemplates the hidden will of GOD, as He has made Himself manifest in nature and the creature. This study is the most excellent of all, but requires a very secluded and humble heart that is discreet and does not "talk out of school" <note>An idiom meaning to reveal secrets or sacred knowledge to the uninitiated.</note>. There is also a literal Kabbalah, where the literalist brings out a hidden sense from the figures, images, compositions, and permutations of the letters; this Kabbalah is the least significant and most uncertain among Jews and Christians.

**Cagastric/Cagastrum**, from *kakia* <note>original Greek: κακία, meaning "badness" or "vice"</note> and *astron* <note>original Greek: ἄστρον, meaning "star"</note>, refers to astral malignancy, or as Paul says, *the spiritual wickedness in the heavenly places* <note>original Greek: ἡ πονηρία ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις (Ephesians 6:12)</note>. The author uses these words to signify an effect and bearing of the Fire-Spirit according to a false and monstrous image and property toward an outgrowth; here, the spirit—ignited with a false image of desire—drives and labors to give birth to a body according to such an image of its desire, from the property of the ignited star <note>original Latin: "Astri"</note>. Thus the author calls Eve a Cagastric person, because she was formed out of Adam’s animal desire and was born as a monster out of the quintessence of his body, which had been infected by the ignition of the stars.

**Chaos** is what the school-scholars call a mixed mass of many materials and properties. The author understands by this a Matrix <note>A womb or source of origin.</note> in which the seed does not yet lie in its green state, but only in its *potentiality for being* <note>original Latin: "potentia ad esse"</note>, and in the possibility of revelation and birth: just as the seed for a bird lies in an egg, from which a bird can develop according to every form, shape, color, property, and way of life, just like the bird from which the egg came. Such a Chaos is either divine—and is the will of GOD, in which heaven and earth, angels and humans, together with all creatures, lay hidden before that same will became active for revelation—or it is a Chaos of eternal nature, in which all seeds for the Angelic world according to love and wrath were hidden, which thereafter came into being and were revealed through eternal nature. So also there is a Chaos of temporal nature or this visible world, which is that from which GOD, through His almighty Word, brought forth heaven and earth, the four elements, air, water, earth, trees, plants, stars, fish, birds, animals, and even man himself.

<column-break/>

**Center** <note>original Latin: "Centrum"</note> refers to the innermost ground, beginning, and end of every life, where the beginning contains the end and the end contains the beginning again; the first beginning and the first movement toward life, and also the highest goal of that same life. For example: a tree grows from a small kernel or seed; as soon as that same seed is awakened and ignited, and begins to stir in the innermost heart, it labors from the Center as its beginning until it reaches its Center or final goal—namely, a tree that again bears such seed, according to all the properties of the one from which the first seed was born. And when it reaches its Center and goal, in that same seed, when it enters the earth, such a Center begins once more to drive and labor from the beginning into that same goal. Thus, it is called:

**Center of Nature** <note>original Latin: "Centrum Naturæ"</note> the first beginning, the first movement in the first seed toward nature, and also the highest goal and boundary <note>original Latin: "Terminus"</note> of nature, wherein there is again a beginning to nature and the ignition of such a life. The Center of Nature is twofold: one toward fire, and one toward light. The Center or beginning toward fire, and its goal, is the first active and driving power toward the ignition of fire, and its goal is the ignition of life itself, in the middlemost seat <note>original Latin: "Sede"</note> or in the heart of nature, as the fourth form of nature <note>In Böhme’s system, the "fourth form" is the "Fire-Flash" or "Lightning," the turning point where the dark, contracting qualities of nature transform into light.</note>. The Light-Center takes its beginning from the goal of the Fire-Center, namely from the ignition of life, and works and drives toward its goal, namely toward the essence and the satisfaction of the fire-desire and the fire-life; in which goal the Center or a beginning to the fire-life is once again awakened and ignited. Since nature is twofold, namely eternal and temporal, so also is its Center. Thus, Center of Nature refers to the beginning and the end of nature.

**Coagulation** is the effect of the harsh <note>original: "herben," referring to the first of Böhme's seven properties of nature, which is a contracting, "sour" force.</note> form and property of nature, through which a thin watery essence is drawn together, curdles, and a volatile thing is bound. Such a curdled, thickened, contracted, and bound essence is called a Coagulum.

**Compacting** <note>original: "Compactiren"</note> / to strictly draw something together, to grasp it, and pack it together through the harsh property.

**Compacted Tongue.** See *Tongue*.

**Concordance** <note>original: "Concordanz"</note> refers to an agreement and union to act.

<meta>This page continues the "Clavicula" or glossary of Jacob Böhme’s specialized terminology, proceeding through definitions of "Corpus" (Body) and the alphabetical sections for D and E. (19 20)
->Clavicula, or a Small Key to Unusual Modes of Speech.<-

When Mars and Venus stand in a constellation or operation in the firmament, they awaken Mars and Venus in all creatures; then, in all beings, each according to its kind, Mars and Venus drive and labor toward a birth. Thus, there is a constellation <note>Böhme uses "constellation" not just for stars, but for the harmonious alignment of different spiritual "worlds."</note> between the Angelic Light-World, the dark Fire-World, and this visible earthly world—between the stars in the firmament and the "stars" (inner drives) in all creatures.

**Corpus, Corporis** <note>Latin: "Body, of a Body"</note>, a body; such is either visible and composed of parts so that it can be measured in length, breadth, and depth; or invisible and heavenly, which, though it has its limits, cannot be measured, like the subtlest air. Thus, the Angelic Light-Bodies are from the pure holy element, in the highest simplicity, subtle and transparent. The Author also speaks of a Divine **Corpus** or Body. It is true that GOD, in and of Himself—as He is and what He is, outside of nature and creation—is a most pure and holy Spirit who has no body. However, when the Author speaks of the Divine Body, he understands this to be GOD as He has introduced Himself into nature and the creature, **by way of emanation** <note>original Latin: "per modum emanationis"</note>, in the manner of an outflowing. Just as the sun flows out with its rays, that which has flowed out is just as much GOD Himself as He who flows out; for because GOD is a most simple Being, nothing can flow out of GOD that is not itself GOD. Now, let the Author understand by this "outflowed thing" the Body of GOD, which is like a breath, respiration, and Spirit of the Almighty, wherein GOD always flows out, and which He always breathes out, and wherein He lives, dwells, and works in all and through all—which also, in such a body, may not be measured, restricted, included, or excluded. Although this body is not necessary to the **Being** <note>original Latin: "Esse"</note> of GOD, it is necessary for the **revelation** of GOD. This is not at all strange, as Holy Scripture itself speaks of GOD as if He had a body—eyes, ears, nose, mouth, hands, feet, heart, entrails, and the like. Also, all kinds of bodily actions are attributed to GOD, which belong to GOD in a God-becoming way much more properly than to man in a human way; for man himself is only an image and likeness of GOD. Thus, Holy Scripture itself testifies that—take note—*the whole fullness of the Godhead dwells bodily in Christ.*

### D.

**Thin as a Nothing** <note>original German: "Dünne als ein Nichts"</note> is the name for everything that cannot be grasped, seen, felt, distinguished, or divided, like the thin air.

<column-break/>

### E.

**Egest** <note>likely from the Latin "egesta," meaning things carried out or excreted</note> is a matter which is separated and expelled as something foreign or adverse, like the dregs and yeast cast out from beer and wine, or an excrement that is excreted and cast off during digestion.

**Element** is what the Author calls the "first matter" from which a body is generated and born; in its innermost ground, it is nothing but a pure breath, respiration, and outflow of the Spirit, which is gently drawn together, dried, and subtly (yet incomprehensibly) bound. However, when Lucifer ignited the holy pure element of his kingdom with GOD’S wrath and corrupted it, he burnt the holy pure element and partially contracted it into hard stony rocks. In the Creation, however, when Good and Evil came into separation, the holy pure element became manifest in four elements according to the four forms of nature: Fire according to the fourth form, then Air, Water, and Earth.

**Ens** <note>Latin: "Being" or "Essence"</note> is what the Author calls not a matter or substance, but the **Being** <note>original Latin: "Esse"</note> of a thing; not the outward essence or element, but the life, the working, the "greening," and the driving within a being. Thus, every **Principle** <note>Böhme's term for the three fundamental realms: Fire/Wrath, Light/Love, and the Outward World.</note> has its own **Ens** or **Esse**. Thus, there is a "Wrath-Ens" or **Being** that lives and drives in the fallen angels; and a "Light-Love-and-Joy-Ens" wherein the holy angels live and exist. Likewise, there is a **Being** and life according to the property of this world, which is sidereal, elemental, vegetable, mineral, animal, and in its highest perfection, a "Paradisiacal Ens."

**Entalic** is the name for everything that has a strong life, drive, and "greening" within itself.

**Sensible and Findable** <note>original German: "Empfindlich und findlich"</note> is said of GOD, who in Himself is "insensible"—that is, unfathomable, invisible, and so deeply hidden that He may not be known nor found, like a Nothing. But since GOD introduced Himself from His **Groundless** <note>original German: "Ungrund," the abyss of the divine before manifestation</note> into a Ground, from the Nothing into Something, He has become visible, manifest, sensible, and findable—understand this: to the eyes of the sanctified understanding.

**Essentia** <note>Latin: "Essence"</note> does not mean here an outward essence or substance, but the first beginning of a working cause for the ignition of life; essentially "eating" or "drawing" <note>Böhme connects the Latin "Essentia" to the German "Essen" (to eat), implying that existence is a process of consuming or "pulling in" spiritual hunger.</note>.

**Esch or Elch** is called Fire in the Hebrew language <note>Hebrew: אֵשׁ (Esh)</note>, hence the word "ash," likewise a "forge" <note>original German: "Esse"</note>. Thus, "Essences" are the first powers to work, which powers...

# Clavicula, or a Small Key to Unusual Modes of Speech.
<meta>catchword: GOD</meta>

**Powers** <note>original: "Kräffte"</note> consist of a "pulling" according to the astringent quality, and a "driving" according to the bitter quality; from the interaction of both, **Essences** are born within the "anguish" <note>Böhme uses "anguish" (Angst) to describe the tension or compression of forces before they break through into life or light.</note>.

**The Fifth Essence** <note>original: "Essentia quinta"; often called the Quintessence in alchemy</note> is the first active cause within the highest balance of properties, through which the most noble life is born and ignited—namely, the pulling, driving, flourishing, and living according to the Second Principle and the quality of Paradise.

**Essential** <note>original: "Essentialisch"</note> refers to that which possesses such powers to pull, to drive, and to ignite a fire-life.

**Evestrum**, from the Greek <note>original: "$\epsilon \upsilon$ and $\alpha \sigma \tau \rho \circ \nu$" (eu and astron)</note>, means astral goodness; it is the opposite <note>original: "Contrarium"</note> of **Cagastrum** <note>a term for the corruptive influence of the stars or a "bad" astral birth</note>, which is explained in its proper place. Good stars <note>original: "Astra"</note>, spirits, and souls are so qualified that they take nothing else as the object of their constantly active intelligence, contemplation, and proclamation than the wonder-works of **GOD**, and they concern themselves solely with performing and promoting **GOD’S** honor, praise, and service. In contrast, the wicked have inwardly assumed an entirely different quality; they seek to awaken external images through their fantasy, in which they express, paint, and mirror their own selves according to their inner lust. Just as Lucifer, following the desire and drive of his ignited star-spirits, made an image for himself and mirrored himself in self-complacency within his own likeness—in which monstrous image he raised himself above the image of **GOD**—so too did Adam. He turned his heart away from the Heavenly Virgin <note>In Böhme’s thought, the "Heavenly Sophia" or Wisdom</note> and created an image in his imagination according to his lust. His star <note>original: "Astrum"</note> worked upon this ignited image and drove it until he had such a model and mirror before him as was his desire. This image may well be called **Evestrum** and **Cagastrum**, a birth made from the stars; especially since Scripture calls woman not the image of **GOD**, but the image or reflection of man.

->F.<-

**Fiat** <note>Latin: "Let it be"</note> is the active word of **GOD** for creation and revelation. It is active in nature and the creature; for **GOD** speaks the word even now for the preservation and constant propagation of creatures, the same word He spoke in the first creation. As it was then in its working and creating, so it remains. It is actually a small Latin word and means "Let it be"; however, this word creates in all creatures according to the specific quality of each creature.

**Figure** is an image or form by which one creature is distinguished from another. This is either internal, called **Idea** <note>original: "Idea"</note>, a "thought-image"; or external, which is the form of a thing.

**Fixed** <note>original: "Fix"</note> refers to everything that remains constant in fire and is neither driven away nor consumed by fire.

<column-break/>

->G.<-

**Spirit** <note>original: "Geist"</note> refers to a rising will, or a longing and desire that goes forth from an ignition of life, just as air goes out from fire and breath from life. This spirit has within itself a desire and longing to ignite such a life in something else, identical to the life from which it proceeds. Thus, the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son as a breath and inhalation in the desire to awaken and ignite the life of the Father and Son in every creature.

**The Spirit of this World** proceeds from the general ignition of fire and life of this entire visible world and all its creatures, longing and desiring to ignite and maintain such a life—according to the quality of this world—in all creatures, including those endowed with understanding.

**The Spirit of the Stars** rises from the source of the stars and elements, and possesses within itself the sharpness and harsh longing of the stars.

**The Soul-Spirit** rises from the fire-source of the soul in a powerful longing and desire for the Light.

**The Will-Spirit** is a rising longing and hungry desire of the ignited and active will. Just as the will has an internal source, and as one "quality of nature" holds the upper hand within it, so too the spirit has a hunger and longing of the same nature.

**Genius** <note>Latin term for a guiding spirit</note> refers to the pure image of **GOD** in its activity, drive, life, and essence according to the quality of the Light-World.

->I.<-

**I**, a vowel letter, is formed by the spirit from the heart through the constricted throat, like a tone thrust out of a narrow flute. It signifies the most inward, tightly encompassing love that drives out from the heart.

**Jah** <note>A shortened form of the Hebrew name for God, Yahweh</note> signifies the Spirit of **GOD** as it rises from the heart and Center of eternal freedom toward revelation, and drives out from the confinement back toward freedom. For **J** is the spirit and breath from the innermost Center of love, and **ah** is the spirit in the highest, image-less and formless freedom.

**Ja** <note>German: "Yes"</note> signifies the outflowing, giving will of **GOD**...

# Clavicula, or a Small Key to Unusual Modes of Speech.
->C<-

**GOD'S** "No" signifies the encompassing, attracting, and restraining will of **GOD**, and is as much as "out" and "in": so all things exist and consist in the **Yes** and **No**.

**Idea** refers to a pleasing mental image <note>original: "Denck-Bild"</note> of a thing, in which the mind takes delight before it is expressed from the heart through the Word and brought forth. The Author plays very charmingly and wonderfully with this meaningful little word according to the basis of the "Language of Nature."

**Jehovah** is the highest name above all names of **GOD**. In its perfect sense, it remains unutterable to this day, both in the understanding and on the tongue; it is actually pronounced by no one except **Jehoschuah** <note>The Hebrew form of the name Jesus</note>, who is exalted above all the heavens of heavens and sits at the right hand of Majesty. In this name, the vowels and all five sounding letters are, as it were, a single Holy Breath or Spirit, so that whoever fundamentally knows and understands this name might unlock and reveal everything hidden. The Author calls this name the **Tetragrammaton** <note>Greek for "four-lettered name"</note> because, contrary to the custom of Hebrew root words, it is written with four letters; see Tetragrammaton.

**Iliaster**, from the Greek words for matter and star <note>original: "$\dot{\upsilon}\lambda\eta$" (hyle) and "$\alpha\sigma\tau\rho\text{ov}$" (astron)</note>, refers to Astral Matter: the constellation working within matter, or the source-spirit; a beginning of the Divine Will toward manifestation according to the Second Principle, which is Love.

**Iliastric** refers to that in which the source-spirits—acting as the Star <note>original: "Astrum"</note> of the Divine Will according to the quality of the Second Principle—become active and driving toward manifestation; such as angels and paradisiacal creatures.

**To Imagine** <note>original: "Imaginiren"</note> means to introduce one's desire into something through Magic, and therein to awaken and ignite the longing and the drive of the will, so that the one imagining, as it were, goes out of himself and seeks his life in that which he imagines. Therefore, that into which the imagination enters must have the necessary qualities to catch such a fire and receive such a life.

**Imagination** is as much as a magical longing and the driving effect of a will into something that it forms in its mind, in which it has either pleasure or aversion; the former awakens and ignites a fire of Love, the latter a fire of Wrath.

**Impression** is a very strong imprint of a certain image, which, as it were, dries together and gives shape to the "harsh" quality, so that the form and image hold firmly together and do not easily dissolve again.

**To Imprint** <note>original: "Imprimiren"</note> means to imagine and press something firmly into the mind. **To Impress** <note>original: "Impressen"</note> means to force something in very strongly.

<column-break/>

**Incantation** <note>original: "Incantatio"</note> refers to a conjuration or enchantment which is introduced into something through certain words in a song-like manner.

**To Infect** <note>original: "Inficiren"</note> means to apply oneself to something, just as a fire applies itself to wood for burning, or as the sun applies itself to a plant for growth and driving; it is also how one person applies himself to another in love or wrath.

**To Inqualize** <note>original: "Inqualiren"</note>; that is, to work with an equal quality. For example, when the sun in the firmament awakens the solar tincture in a creature and thereby influences and drives it; or when one person awakens love or wrath in another, and thus works in and with him.

**Inqualization** <note>original: "Inqualirung"</note> refers to such a union for the purpose of a shared effect.

**Jovial** refers to that which works according to the quality of the planet Jupiter, or rather its source-spirit.

**The Philosophers' Stone** <note>original: "Lapis Philosophorum"</note>, the so-called stone of the wise.

**The Cornerstone** <note>original: "Lapis Angularis"</note>, the cornerstone Christ.

**Larva** <note>Latin for mask or ghost</note>, a false and monstrous image through which a creature disguises itself.

**Limbus**, as if derived from the word for "loin" <note>original: "Lumbus"</note>, the hip; it signifies the quality of masculinity or the fire-power of life. When the Author uses this word regarding **GOD** and the Spirit, he understands it as nothing other than the working will of **GOD** according to the property of the Father, for the birthing of the Son in nature. In this sense, it is placed in opposition to the **Matrix** <note>the female "womb" or origin-point</note>, the birther. When it is used of humans or animals, it means the male faculty of generating <note>original: "facultas generandi mascula"</note>, the masculine quality and power to procreate; sometimes even the male member itself. Just as the word for "hip" <note>original: "Lumbus"</note> is often used in Holy Scripture for masculinity. Genesis 24 and 33.

**Limus** <note>Latin for mud or slime</note>, a clay, loam, or viscous slime; it is used for the seed and the Quintessence of a being, of minerals, vegetables, and animals. Because of their "harsh" quality, these are similar to a viscous, coagulated, and dry slime or loam; nature binds the otherwise volatile, subtle powers through this viscous quality so they do not fly away.

**Jehovah** is the highest name above all names of God; in its perfect sense, it has been unutterable until now, both in the intellect and on the tongue, and is truly pronounced by no one except **Jehoshua** <note>original: "Jehoschuah", referring to Jesus</note>, who is exalted above all the heavens of heavens and sits at the right hand of Majesty. **Imagination** is as much as a magical craving and the driving effect of a will into something that it has formed in its mind, and in which it has either pleasure or aversion; the former awakens and ignites a fire of love, the latter a fire of wrath.

**Impression** is a very strong imprint of a certain image, which the harsh property <note>original: "herbe Eigenschafft"</note> dries together and figures, so that the form and image hold fast together and do not easily dissolve again.

### M.

**Macrocosmus** <note>The Great World</note> is the whole visible world, heaven and earth, along with everything therein.

**Microcosmus** means the small world, which is man; the author often calls the large world *Major mundus* and the small one *Minor mundus*. <note>Latin: "Greater world" and "Lesser world"</note>

**Magia** <note>Magic</note> is the outgoing and attracting desire of the working will; it approaches that into which it has set itself, and works so that it may awaken and kindle a life in someone according to its property and impression. Thus, **Divine Magia** <note>original: "Magia Divina"</note> is the almighty desire of the working will of GOD, for the awakening, kindling, working, and revelation of the Divine life in all things, but especially in man, according to the property of the Son, as the second Principle. According to the property of the first Principle, when separated from the other, it is called the dark **Magia**, where the will, kindled by the fire of the wrath of GOD, goes out in a severe, harsh, burning, fierce craving, to kindle the wrath of GOD where the will attaches itself through desire.

**Magia Naturalis** <note>Natural Magic</note> is the sharp attracting and kindling effect of the human will, whereby the earnest lover sets his serious desire into the things of eternal or temporal nature, and attaches himself to them, awakens them according to their centers in their root, and thus kindles his life therein, either according to love or wrath. This Magic in its right and orderly use is a natural working of the will; but if it is misused in self-centeredness and malice, it is a false Magic; the author calls it **Nigromantia** <note>original: "Nigromantia", meaning necromancy or black magic</note>, the black art, sorcery.

**Magus** means a wise man who has the power to introduce his will into a creature, angel, human, or whatever it may be, and to kindle therein a life according to his pleasure, delight, and property. Whoever seeks to kindle the life of GOD in his

<column-break/>

neighbor or another creature, according to the property of the second Principle toward light, love, joy, praise of GOD, peace, and contentment, and is able to do so, he is a **Divine Magus** <note>original: "Magus Divinus"</note>. But he who awakens in his neighbor or in a creature the dark fire-life, insatiable greed, abominable pride, fierce envy, wrath, enmity, revenge, and unrest, he is rightly called a dark **Magus**, a sorcerer and black-artist. It is well to note that the stronger the fire-will is in a person or a creature, the more powerful he is in Magic; and whatever property *predominates* in the will, such is also the Magic of the will.

**Magnet** refers to every sharp-attracting power in a creature: just as the magnet attracts iron because it has the property of iron within itself, and its hunger and desire are set toward iron; so every creature has within itself a magnet, an attracting and desiring power, according to such an essence wherein the hunger finds such food for which it hungers.

**Magnetisch** <note>Magnetic</note> refers to everything that is strong, powerful, and effective in such attracting power and desire.

**Majestät** <note>Majesty</note> here does not mean so much a royal highness and dignity, or title, as it does the luster, radiance, and glory which shines forth from the revelation of the Divine Majesty in the creature. When the author uses this word of an angel or human, it is understood as the perfection of Divine revelation according to the property of the second Principle, where the property of the light in the human or angel reaches its highest degree and crown, just as the sun, among all stars, has the noblest tincture <note>In alchemy, a "tincture" is a spiritualized substance that can transform and color other things</note> and the highest majesty and radiance.

**Mercurius** <note>Mercury</note> refers to the life-spirit which, bound and fettered by the harsh property, seeks to be free from its enclosure. It is the ground of all motion and all life and being. The author uses this name for the Son of GOD, as he is born from the Father into nature and the creature, and becomes active, moving and driving everything with the life of GOD. So also Mercury is the sixth planet, and likewise the sixth source-spirit <note>original: "Quell-Geist"</note> in nature, the first cause of the senses and understanding, sound and resonance; it is also called quicksilver.

**Mercurialisch** <note>Mercurial</note> refers to that in which the driving and volatile Mercury predominates and is active.

**Matrix** <note>The Womb or Mother</note> refers to the bearer of every life and Principle; it is set in opposition to the **Limbus** <note>The formative "seed" or spiritual "extract" of a thing</note>, the power of fire, and has within itself a receiving and passive water-like property.

-># Clavicula, or a Small Key to Unusual Modes of Speech.<-
->### C 2<-
<meta>Catchword: curi-</meta>

**Mars** refers to the fiery property of nature in all creatures; among the stars, it is the planet nearest above the Sun, and among minerals, it is called **Iron**.

**Mens** <note>Latin: "Mind"</note> is the word for sense, mind, or understanding in the Latin language; however, the author uses it to mean a "subject" or a vessel for the *Entis* <note>The "Ens" or essential being</note>, representing the eternal life, being, and activity of a thing. According to the spirit, *Mens* is a vessel for the Will, wherein the source-spirits are active in a spiritual manner, much like thoughts within a mind. According to the body, however, *Mens* is an essence in which the *Ens* or *Esse in actu* <note>Latin: "Being in action"</note>—that is, the actual working or grasping—exists.

**Mental** refers to everything in which there is a "being in action" <note>original: "esse in actu"</note>, driving and working. See also: **Tongue**. <note>The author likely refers to the "Language of Nature" or "Sound."</note>

**Menstruum** is what the chemists call the moisture in which they cook their elixir, whether it be its own inherent fluid or another liquid poured over it.

**Mesch** <note>Likely related to "mischung" or mixture; a "mash"</note> refers to a mixed mass and material in which the four elements are blended and mingled together, yet not truly united. From this word **Mesch** comes the word **Mensch** <note>German: "Human"</note>; he is so named because he has deviated from the balanced temperament of his properties, and his soul and body have fallen into a mixed state.

**Millenarium** refers to the thousand-year kingdom of Christ described in the Revelation of John, which was not sufficiently known to our author. <note>The editor suggests Böhme did not fully articulate this specific eschatological concept.</note>

**Minerals** refers to all kinds of ores and the works of the mine.

**Moder** <note>Smolder or decay</note> refers to the fire that glimmers in secret and exists in a powerful "hunger" before it catches the air and reaches the light.

**Monstrum** <note>Monster or omen</note> is a foreign image into which a creature reshapes and changes itself, abandoning its first image in which it was formed and grasped by GOD. This is like man, who shamed the image of GOD and, first through false desire, made his mind—and thereafter also his body—monstrous.

**Mummies** refers to the flesh of deceased human bodies that has been preserved by strong spices and balsam and is used as medicine.

**Mysterium** <note>Mystery</note> refers to everything that is still hidden and has not yet been carried out or made manifest, just as an image lies hidden within a tree before the artist carves and forms it.

**Mysterium Magnum** <note>Latin: "The Great Mystery"</note> is the darkness and the chaos in which everything—heaven and earth, along with all creatures—lay hidden before they became manifest. Just as all of a man's thoughts lie within his mind and are not carried out or revealed until they become a "work," so too does everything lie within the *Mysterium Magnum* materially and formally, in potential, as a possibility for revelation. Now, just as one thought proceeds from another, so one mystery proceeds from the *Mysterium Magnum* toward revelation: **Day unto day uttereth speech, and night unto night sheweth knowledge. Psalm 19.**

<column-break/>

### N.

**Nature** is not taken here to mean a mere quality, kind, or form of living, as it is commonly used, but rather for a Mother or a power of birthing (from the Latin *a Nascendo* <note>"from being born"</note>), through which all births are brought forth. Such Nature, as a workshop of birthing and a field in which births grow, is twofold: the eternal Nature and the temporal Nature. The temporal is within the eternal, and the eternal within the temporal, like day within night and night within day.

**Necrolic** refers to the way in which the forms or source-spirits labor toward the fire as their goal within the dark "chamber of anguish," before the kindling of the fire.

**Necromanticè** refers to the way the source-spirits qualify or work as they labor toward the light during the kindling, yet do not actually reach the light.

**Nutrimentum**, a means of nourishment.

### P.

**Paradise** refers, according to the Greek language, to a revelation, transfiguration, *Ostentatio*, or *Demonstratio* <note>A display or demonstration</note>. Thus, Paradise does not actually mean the Garden of Eden in which Adam was placed, but rather the greening, driving, working, and transfiguration of the pure heavenly **Tincture**, where the powers and juices of the angelic world break through the coarse, hard, dark earth and purify and clarify it. This Paradisiacal greening began in the Garden of Eden, and that was actually why Adam was created into the kingdom of this world: to introduce the heavenly Tincture into the entire visible world, so that all its creatures might be clarified, "tinctured," and brought back into a Paradisiacal state. Thus, Paradise would rise up in the whole world, and the clarity of GOD would work through the power of the darkness, so that the whole world would become an angelic kingdom and a pleasure-garden of GOD, as it was before Lucifer’s fall.

**Particular** is what the author calls a special Tincture through which this or that disease specifically is cur... <note>The word is cut off, continuing to the next page as "cured."</note>

**Pearl** is what the author calls the heavenly maiden Sophia <note>Sophia is the Greek word for Wisdom, personified in Böhme’s thought as the divine mirror or the "bride" of the soul.</note>, or the Light and holy Oil of Divine Gentleness and Love. In this, the fire-soul—sinking away from its own fiery power—attains its highest clarity, joy, and delight, where the fire is swallowed up in light, anguish into joy, movement into rest, and hunger into perfect fullness.

**Pearl-tree** is what the newly-born person is called, in whom the Divine Tincture <note>The "Tincture" is a transformative spiritual essence that "colors" or changes the soul's nature.</note> drives, reaching its crown, flowers, and fruits, within which the seed of the new birth is once again contained. Everything that is planted, grafted, or joined into such a Pearl-tree dies to its natural impulse and henceforth grows according to the nature of the Pearl-tree.

**Pearl-Wreath** or **Crown** is the firm assurance of the new humanity and of the union and marriage with Sophia, where the impulse of Divine Life reaches its highest limit and goal of perfection. And though it may be obscured by the power of darkness, it nevertheless does not wither, but reaches its full stability and ripeness.

**Gate** <note>original: "Porten"</note> is what the author calls a disclosure and opening of a mystery for the recognition of truth, and for the entrance out of darkness into the light. Thus, every Principle <note>original: "Principium"</note>, life, and world—indeed, every creature—has its gates, and every gate has its key for the disclosure of the Wisdom of God hidden therein, and for the true recognition of its nature.

**Primas, Primus** <note>Latin: "The First"</note> is used to describe a source-spirit or a property of nature which has the upper hand in its struggle.

**Principle** <note>original: "Principium"</note> does not mean to our author so much the "first beginning" or "foundation," but rather a property and kind of drive—the first ignition of a life in a specific manner. According to the general understanding, the author recognizes a single active Principle <note>original: "Principium agens"</note>, or working cause and beginning, and such a Principle is the active Will of God for the revelation of the triune Godhead. When he speaks of three principles, he does not mean three beginnings or three working causes (as the academic scholars <note>original: "Schul-Gelehrten"</note> accuse him), but three different modes of operation through which the single active Principle or working cause is effective, where none is the other, and where each has its own goal.

**Torment** <note>original: "Quaal." Böhme famously puns on the German "Qual" (torment/pain) and the Latin "Qualitas" (quality).</note> means as much as "quality" <note>original: "qualitas"</note>: a property and a way of working.

**Qualifying** <note>original: "Qualificiren"</note> is quality in action <note>original: "qualitas in actu"</note>: the working of the Will according to a particular kind and property.

**Agony** <note>original: "Quahl"</note> means as much as a pain and plague.

**Welling-up** <note>original: "Quallung"</note> is a strong boiling and drive of the Will; the Will in action <note>original: "Voluntas in actu"</note>.

**R.** is the character of the driving fire, according to its harsh property. For when a fire ignites in wood or flammable sulfur, it begins to rattle or snarl, much like a rattling wheel.

**Quick** or **Rash** <note>original: "Rasch oder Rås"</note> is the sharpness and the first drive and craving to work where life ignites. it is the opposite of the word "mute"—much like a seed-corn is "mute" before it is cast into the earth, having life in potential <note>original: "in potentia"</note> or capacity, but not in action <note>original: "in actu"</note>. But when it is cast into the earth, the life is awakened to drive according to its property, and is then called "quick" or "rash."

It takes its origin and root from the harsh, stern, contracting property of the working cause. It is the opposite of Mercury <note>original: "Mercurio"</note>, which is the root and first beginning of all life, stirring, and movement.

**Salt-Spirit** is the craving that rises from a fire-ignition in a harsh, sharp, attracting property, in order to turn a universal matter <note>original: "universal Materiam"</note>—which otherwise is neither this nor that—into a salt, and to give it boundaries.

**Salitter, Salt-Niter** <note>original: "Sal Nitri"</note> is what the author calls the first root, mother, and ground for the ignition of fire, in which first the life and afterward the body of a thing is born. It is the same as the First Matter <note>original: "Materia prima"</note>. This Salitter is divine—namely, the first ground in which the life of God is born in a creature.
