# Clavicula or Small Key to Unusual Ways of Speaking.

### C 3
<meta>catchword: Mine-</meta>

a substance in which the source-spirits <note>Böhme’s "Quell-Geister" are the seven fundamental forces or "qualities" that drive all of existence.</note> are active in a heavenly manner, kindling a heavenly life, just as in the angelic world and its creatures. There is also a hellish Salitter <note>Salitter is a term Böhme coined, likely derived from "Salpeter" (saltpeter), to describe the foundational matter or "divine earth" of a realm.</note>, a mother in which the fire of God’s wrath is kindled. Lucifer awakened and ignited this Salitter in his kingdom, and thereby burnt everything. There is also a Salitter of this visible world, a root from which the stars in the firmament are born, driven, and grown. Furthermore, every element—fire, air, water, earth—has *its own particular Salitter*. Just as the Salitter in the air, water, earth, etc., has its own birth, property, and effect, so the Divine Salitter or Balsam has its birth in a divine way, the Angelic in an angelic way, and the hellish in a hellish way; it is the first root and the material ground for the kindling of such a life.

**Salnitric Shock** <note>original: "Salnitrischer Schrack"</note> is a metaphor for a sudden and rapid ignition of fire, such as is seen in thunder and gunpowder, where the <term>Acidum</term> <note>Latin: "acid" or "sharpness"</note> or sharpness in the nitre ignites, and the harshness—within which the volatile Mercury and Sulfur-spirit are bound—bursts its bond, causing a sudden movement from which the "Shock" arises. The author uses this to describe the sudden ignition of fire in every action and impulse toward revelation, and in every sudden kindling of life.

**Saturn** <note>original: "Saturnus"</note> is used by the author not only for the planet Saturn or for lead, but when speaking of the source-spirits of nature, he understands it as the first, the harsh form and property <note>In Böhme’s system, Saturn represents the "astringent" or "contracting" quality that gives things form and hardness.</note>.

**Sharpness** <note>original: "Schärff"</note> is used by the author to describe the strong effect of a source-spirit, such as a sharp salt-spirit, a sharp Mercury, or a sharp sulfur-spirit; the author uses it especially for the first form of nature: the harsh, stern, and sharply-attractive property.

**Shadow** <note>original: "Schatten"</note> refers to an image and figure that exists in form, but not in <term>esse</term> <note>Latin: "being" or "essence"</note>, <term>in actu</term> <note>Latin: "in actuality"</note>, or in life and action. He also uses it for a body where life was once inside but has since withered and gone out, like the dry slough or skin of a snake. Thus, Lucifer as an angel is now only a shadow, in which the angelic life and greening have died; instead, he is a dragon in which the hellish life and the wrath of God flourish. Likewise, our "old Adam" <note>A biblical reference to the fallen, sinful nature of humanity.</note> stands in the shadow if we kill the lusts and desires of the flesh, set our will into the life of God, and become new human beings.

<column-break/>

**Scientz** <note>This is Böhme’s specific use of a word sounding like "science," but derived from "scire" (to know) and "sentire" (to feel/perceive).</note> does not mean "knowledge" here, but a pulling <term>Ens</term> <note>Latin: "essence" or "entity"</note>, a harsh pulling property in its being, impulse, and action. Thus, every creature has within itself a "Scientz"—a hunger and craving for a substance into which it can introduce its essence, being, life, and existence.

**Sensus** <note>Latin: "sense"</note> does not mean a physical sense to the author, such as sight or hearing, but rather an ideal concept and understanding of a thing. When the will accepts this concept, the will is then formed and becomes active according to it; thus, that which was previously only in <term>sensu</term> <note>Latin: "in thought/sense"</note> enters into <term>esse</term>—into life, drive, and action, according to either love or wrath.

**Sensual** <note>original: "Sensualisch"</note> refers to everything that exists in images, thoughts, and in the understanding before the will drives and works toward revelation. See "Jung" <note>Likely a cross-reference to the entry for "Youth" or "Virgin."</note>.

**Separator** is the active Word which digests and separates everything in the inner ground, ordering each thing into its proper place and principle.

**Sedes** <note>Latin: "seat" or "throne"</note> refers to the place and position that belongs to each thing.

**Signatura** <note>Latin: "signature"</note> means form, shape, sound, noise, color, and all identifying marks by which one can distinguish the property of a thing.

**Signatura Rerum** <note>Latin: "The Signature of Things"</note> refers to the designation of things, from which one can recognize the inner nature, property, power, and effect of every thing.

**Sophia** <note>Greek: "Wisdom"</note> means to the author: 1. The mirror of the mind, in which God has conceived all ideas and images which He has brought forth and made manifest through the Word. 2. Sophia also refers to the Heavenly Virgin who marries the new, reborn person; this marriage is nothing other than the fire-soul uniting with the water of life, the gentleness, and the oil of the Holy Spirit. In this, the fire finds a light, the anguish finds joy, and the hunger finds eternal satisfaction, wherein God becomes manifest as in His highest kingdom of joy. Therefore, the author nowhere understands Sophia as a "fourth person" <note>Böhme was often accused of heresy for suggesting Wisdom was a fourth member of the Trinity; here the editor defends him.</note> of the Trinity, as he is accused. Sophia is not a person; a person, whether an angel or a soul, becomes manifest, glorious, and full of joy *within* Sophia. Just as a dark fire becomes light in oil, so a fire-soul becomes a spirit in and with Sophia. And Sophia becomes a person in a new human being or holy angel, just as the oil becomes a light in the fire, and as God is a person in Christ.

**Sol** <note>Latin: "Sun"</note> refers to the sun, not only in the firmament, but everything that has the property of the sun: in the Angelic world in an angelic way, in the sidereal <note>Relating to the stars and the physical cosmos.</note> world in a sidereal way, in the...

<meta>This page continues the alphabetical glossary of Jacob Böhme’s specialized vocabulary, picking up mid-sentence from the previous page's discussion of "Salitter." It moves from the letter S into the letter T, covering fundamental theosophical concepts like the "Teutonic Philosopher," the "Tincture," and the "Turba."</meta>

# Clavicula or Little Key to Unusual Ways of Speaking.

[...in a] mineral manner in a mineral way, and it is the heart and the core in all things. <note>This fragment completes the definition of "Salitter" from the previous page, explaining how the divine substance manifests within the physical mineral kingdom.</note>

**Species** means a particular form and kind of a thing.

**Spiritus** [means] a spirit.

**To Speculate** <note>original: "Speculiren"</note> signifies for the author not a mere rationalizing or intellectual "shadow-fencing," but a sharp imagining—the act of introducing one's primary will into something. By this process, the subject of one's speculation is ignited by the quality of that will, so that the will becomes active within it. Just as sun-rays are concentrated by a burning-glass and directed toward a flammable object, so did Lucifer "speculate." He concentrated the out-flowing powers of GOD through his own harsh, strictly-contracting qualities, and thereby set his entire kingdom on fire. In this same way, Lucifer and humanity still speculate today, igniting everything they apply themselves to according to their own inner quality.

**Substance** <note>original: "Substantz"</note> here does not mean an independent self-subsistence, but is understood as a tangible and massive being or matter. Something "substantial," core-like, and solid is contrasted here with a thin, flowing, and volatile matter, such as thin air.

**Sulphur** signifies sulfur, fire, salt, or the "food of the fire." The author calls every balsamic, oily matter that is capable of catching fire "Sulfur." When he uses this term in relation to GOD, he understands it as what the Scripture calls "Balsam" or the "Oil of the Holy Spirit."

**Sydus** or **Sidus** <note>Latin: "constellation" or "star"</note> means a constellation in the firmament.

**Sidereal** <note>original: "Syderisch"</note> refers to whatever depends on such a constellation or belongs to it.

### T.

**Temperature** <note>original: "Temperatur"</note> means an equal operation of the two principles or qualities, where the fire is not stronger or sharper than the water is toward the light; where the drive and movement do not exceed the goal; and where hunger and desire are no more severe than the food provided. Instead, everything remains in its proper measure, limit, and weight.

**To Temper** <note>original: "Temperiren"</note> means to soothe something that pulls or drives too sharply, bringing it back into its proper measure and order.

**Temperamentum** <note>Latin: "temperament" or "proportion"</note> means moderation: the right, well-ordered measure and weight that holds all the active source-spirits <note>original: "Quell-Geister"</note> in their proper order, so that no single one exerts power over the others.

**Ternarius Sanctus** <note>Latin: "Holy Ternary" or "Holy Triad"</note> [means] the Holy Three-Number [the Trinity]. The author calls everything a *Ternarius Sanctus* in which the

<column-break/>

Father begets his beloved Son, and the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son, glorifying them both. Thus, the World of Light, all angels, Paradise, and man in his state of perfection are each a *Ternarium Sanctum*, because the Holy Trinity has been made manifest within them as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

**Teutonic Philosopher** <note>original: "Teutonicus Philosophus"</note> means the "German Knower of Nature." This is how the late Jacob Böhme <note>J. B.</note> was titled by the scholars of his time.

**Teutonic Theosophy** <note>original: "Teutonica Theosophia"</note> refers to our author’s grounded knowledge and teaching concerning GOD: His nature, qualities, operation, and revelation within the creature.

**Thesaurinella** <note>Latin diminutive: "Little Treasury"</note> [means] a very secret, hidden treasure that is little-regarded by others, but highly valued by the one who knows it.

**Tincture** <note>original: "Tinctura"</note> here does not mean a chemical extract or a solvent <note>original: "Menstruum"</note> that has drawn the virtue, power, and color out of a substance into itself. Instead, it is understood as an *active power*. The author calls it a "spirit-water," which in its ground is neither pure spirit nor pure water, but a middle-thing between spirit and being (or body). Through the Tincture, the spirit works within the being or body; for the spirit is active, driving, shining, gleaming, greening, and blooming within the Tincture. 
The Tincture is of many kinds: Divine, Angelic, Heavenly, Hellish, Paradisiacal, Earthly, Fiery, Watery, Masculine, Feminine, Vegetable, and Mineral. Furthermore, it can be solar, lunar, martial, veneric, mercurial, jovial <note>Referring to the seven planetary influences: Sun, Moon, Mars, Venus, Mercury, Jupiter.</note>. Just as the Tincture in earthly things has a birth, operation, drive, and quality in an earthly way, so the Divine/Angelic Tincture has a birth in a divine way. It resembles a very penetrating, volatile spirit-water that is not sufficiently bound by harsh qualities or "cold fire," but hovers and drives like a subtle air.

**Turba** <note>Latin: "turmoil," "crowd," or "disturbance"</note> is an ignition of the source-spirits, arising from a conflict of qualities—between fire and light, love and wrath—where fire and wrath gain the upper hand. it is the opposite of "Temperature." This *Turba* is a powerful fire-trial within a spirit or body; like a strongly-driving ferment, it attacks everything it touches and consumes everything of a "foreign" quality within that spirit or body. It casts out all impurity and finally extinguishes itself once it finds nothing more to oppose it.

**Turba Magna** <note>Latin: "Great Turmoil"</note> is a general ignition of the wrath of GOD in the whole world, or in a nation...

<keywords>Jacob Böhme, Tincture, Turba, Teutonic Philosopher, Speculation, Ternarius Sanctus, Theosophy, alchemy, spiritual qualities</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the alphabetical glossary of Jacob Böhme’s specialized vocabulary, picking up mid-entry from the previous page's definition of "Turba." This term refers to the destructive or "disturbing" power of divine wrath when it is provoked out of its natural balance.</meta>

...people, kingdom, or city, where the wrath of GOD first ignites within the person, and then through the person into the elements, so that everything that does not stand in its proper quality is consumed and broken. Depending on how a quality is ignited in an object <note>original: "Vorwurff"</note>, the **Turba** <note>Latin: "commotion" or "disturbance." In Böhme's thought, it is the spirit of destruction that breaks things apart so they can return to their source.</note> works accordingly; it hardens one, melts another; one thing becomes black through it, another white; one is burned, the other becomes clearer and pure.

**Turba in man** is either of the soul or of the body. In the soul, the fire of God’s wrath is ignited by all kinds of unrighteousness: greed, tyranny, envy, murder, anger, lusts of the flesh, unruly passions, etc. In the body, it is an ignition of nature—sickness, pain, suffering, and finally death.

The **ground and root of the Turba** is the elevation of the fire-power above the goal of gentleness. All sins arise from the elevation and fire-ignition of the will, when desire enters into something and attaches itself to it. In this, God’s wrath ignites, and the fire rules over the water: such as temporal goods, lusts of the flesh, etc. When the will enters into these, it is as if fire is set to straw.

### V.

**The Word of the Lord** <note>original Latin: "Verbum Dominus"</note> is the Word that was in the beginning with GOD, being God himself, as He speaks Himself into nature and the creature and becomes active within them.

**The Word of the Lord** <note>original Latin: "Verbum Domini"</note> is the word that has been spoken by the Speaking Word, and is still spoken at all times. <note>Böhme distinguishes between the internal, eternal "Speaking Word" (God's essence) and the "Spoken Word" (manifested creation).</note>

**Vegetable** <note>original: "Vegetabilisch"</note> refers to everything that belongs to the kingdom of growths: plants, herbs, shrubs, trees, and their kind, nature, and quality.

**Venus** is the name of the fifth form of nature, called Love. Thus there is a divine *Venus*, an angelic one, a hellish one, and a planet; and when the author speaks of metals, he understands it as either copper or the quality of copper.

**Venereal** <note>original: "Venerisch"</note> is used for things carnal, lustful, lewd, unchaste, and inclined toward fleshly mixing.

**Vulcan** <note>original: "Vulcanus"</note> is the active, working, and driving fire in every single thing. He is properly called the god of fire, or the causer of all ignition of fire.

**The Groundless** <note>original: "Ungrund"</note> is what the author calls the eternal, infinite Godhead that surpasses all understanding, without beginning or end, primarily as it is considered in and of itself, outside of nature and creation. It is set in opposition to the "Ground"—which is sensitivity, findability, or something in which GOD has become manifest.

**Universal** is that which has no **limit** <note>original: "Terminum"</note>, but from which one can make whatever one wishes; it applies itself to all things and works upon each according to its quality. It is used in reference to **Medicine** and the **Universal Tincture**, otherwise called the **Philosopher’s Stone** <note>original: "Lapis Philosophorum"</note>, which dyes <note>The term "tingiret" (to tincture/dye) refers to the alchemical process of transformation.</note> **animals, plants,** as well as **minerals**, driving them into their perfection. It is the opposite of the **Particular** <note>Meaning a substance that only works on specific things.</note>.

<column-break/>

### W.

**Wonders** <note>original: "Wunder"</note> are not always called **miracles** <note>original: "Miracula"</note> by the author, but rather something that has swung itself upward from the hidden into revelation. Thus, every **Principle** has its wonders: the wonders of Hell are the evil spirits, as are all works and vessels of the wrath of GOD; the wonders of Light are the holy angels and souls; the wonders of this world are the creatures of this world.

### Z.

**Tongue or Speech** is either **sensual**, that is, speaking internally within the understanding, such as **logical reasonings** <note>original: "Ratiocinia"</note>, deliberations, and contemplations of the mind.

**Mental Tongues** are those where thoughts begin to become active in the will and drive toward expression, like driving lusts and desires.

**Compacted Tongue** <note>original: "Compactirte Zung"</note> is when thoughts are packed and contained in the word as if in forms and figures.

# Foreword concerning the Author and his sublime writings.

...retaining such prophecy and warning along with the image of the man in his mind, and being unable to forget it, he became more earnest and attentive in all his actions from then on. As a result, the aforementioned spiritual outcry and Sabbath-Day <note>This refers to a period of spiritual peace or "rest" in God following a period of inner struggle.</note> followed shortly thereafter. Once he had returned to himself, he increasingly set aside the desires of foolish youth and diligently attended church. Alongside reading the Holy Bible, he regularly made use of the preached Word and the most venerable Sacraments. He was driven by a Divine Zeal, so much so that he could not bear to hear shameful words or foolish talk—especially blasphemous speech and curses. He even had to rebuke and punish his own master <note>Böhme was an apprentice shoemaker at the time.</note> for such behavior. Thus, out of love for true godliness and virtue, he applied himself to an honorable and secluded life, renouncing all extravagance and bad company. Because this was entirely contrary to worldly customs, he was persecuted with mocking scorn, laughter, and words of disgrace, and finally dismissed by his own master (who could not tolerate such a "house-prophet") to wander elsewhere.

In the meantime, having supported himself as a faithful laborer by his own hands and the sweat of his brow, he was seized a second time by the Divine Light at the beginning of the 17th century—namely in the year 1600, in the 25th year of his age. Through his starry soul-spirit, and by a sudden glance at a tin vessel <note>This refers to Böhme’s famous illumination while looking at a polished pewter dish, where the reflection of the sun triggered a mystical vision of the universe.</note> (as a lovely Jovial <note>original: "Jovialischen." In alchemy, tin is the metal of Jupiter; Böhme uses this to describe a joyful, balanced spiritual clarity.</note> sheen), he was led into the innermost ground or center of secret nature. Somewhat doubtful and seeking to shake such supposed fantasies from his mind, he went out into the greenery at Görlitz, before the Neisse Gate <note>original: "Neysthore"</note> (where he had his dwelling by the bridge). Yet, he felt this received vision all the more strongly and clearly the longer he walked, so that—

<column-break/>

—through the depicted signatures <note>The "Signatures" are the outward marks or forms of things that reveal their inner spiritual essence.</note> or figures, lines, and colors, he was able to see, as it were, into the heart and the innermost nature of all creatures (just as this discovered ground is sufficiently explained and contained in his little book *The Signature of All Things* <note>original Latin title: "de Signatura Rerum"</note>). He was overwhelmed with great joy, but remained silent, praising GOD, attending to his household affairs and the upbringing of his children, and interacting with everyone in a peaceful and friendly manner. Concerning this light he had received, he shared little or nothing of his inner walk with GOD and Nature with anyone. But according to the secretly working holy counsel and will of GOD, ten years later, in 1610, he was touched by GOD for a third time through the overshadowing of the Holy Spirit, and was graced and strengthened with new light and insight. So that he might not let such great grace slip from his memory, nor resist such a holy and comfort-rich teacher, he began to write in the year 1612 (though only for himself), provided with meager means and no books other than the Holy Bible. This was his first book, **The Morning Glow at the Sunrise** (later named **AURORA** by Dr. Balthasar Walter). Although he eventually entrusted it to a well-known nobleman who had happened to find it with him, he did so only at great request and merely for reading; he did not wish for it to come to the light of day, much less be printed. However, out of a great desire for such hidden depths, that nobleman immediately divided the manuscript and had it copied quite hastily, day and night, by various scribes and by his own hand. Thus it became known to one person and then another, until it finally reached the Chief Pastor in Görlitz, Gregorius Richter. He, following common or perverted academic custom, and without sufficient examination or understanding, immediately began to attack it with public blasphemy from the pulpit—

# Foreword concerning the Author and his sublime writings.

...condemned from the pulpit <note>original: "Predigt-Stuhle"; the text begins mid-word from the previous page</note> in the highest degree. This was repeated and driven forward so often and for so long with personal insults and excommunications of the innocent author, until finally the City Council of Görlitz itself made inquiries. They summoned Jacob Böhme, as their citizen, before them, kept the book in safekeeping at the Town Hall, and warned the author to "stick to his last" <note>This is a play on the idiom "Shoemaker, stick to your last," meaning he should focus on his trade and stop writing books.</note> and leave book-writing alone. The details of this process are found elsewhere, particularly regarding the improper zeal of this untimely judge <note>A reference to Gregorius Richter, the primary pastor in Görlitz who led the persecution against Böhme.</note> and the great gentleness and humility of the blessed J.B., alongside other highly significant testimonies from the Electoral Saxon theologians. These are contained in a missive attached here by Dr. Cornelius Weißner, a famous physician and chemist. The *autographum*, or Jacob Böhme’s own manuscript of that book <note>The "Aurora," his first work.</note>, after remaining in the Council's custody for twenty-seven years, was presented on November 26, Anno 1641, by Dr. Paul Scipio, the Mayor there, to the Electoral Saxon House Marshal in Dresden, Mr. Georg Pflug (a well-disposed patron of our J.B.), when he came to Görlitz. From his hand, it was further sent through H.P.H. to Abraham Willems von Beyerland, citizen and merchant in Amsterdam.

Following this, the holy and patient man kept a complete Sabbath for a full seven years out of obedience to his authorities, and wrote nothing during that time. But when he was strengthened and awakened by further experiences—namely, the fourth movement <note>Böhme described his spiritual development in stages or "movements" of divine influence.</note> of the Foundation laid within him—and was urgently exhorted by the seeking and persistence of several God-fearing men who understood Nature not to bury such a high and precious talent or pledge, but to invest it well for the honor and benefit of GOD and His community, he took up the pen again in the name of GOD.

In this regard, it should be remembered that the *Forty Questions concerning the Soul* were posed with singular and high deliberation by the physician and chemist <term>Dr. Balthasar Walter</term> <note>A widely traveled scholar from Silesia who became one of Böhme's most important early supporters.</note> from Great Glogau in Silesia, who was very well-traveled and experienced in Europe, Africa, and Asia. These were translated into the Latin language by the noble and highly-learned Mr. Johannes Angelius Werdenhagen, a legal scholar and Princely Counselor of Lüneburg, and printed in Amsterdam in the year 1632 under the title *Psychologia Vera* <note>Latin: "True Psychology."</note>, dedicated to ten distinguished politicians in 18-mo format; subsequently, in the year 1650, it was printed in German in the same place in 12-mo. The aforementioned and esteemed Dr. Balthasar Walter (who later died in Paris and made the writings of the *Teutonicus* <note>Latin: "The German," referring to Böhme.</note> known to and left them with distinguished people there and elsewhere) testified repeatedly and on many occasions that during his many and far-reaching travels—especially when he spent a total of six years in Arabia, Syria, and Egypt—he searched with great and diligent industry for the true hidden wisdom (which is otherwise called <term>Kabbalah</term>, <term>Magic</term>, <term>Alchemy</term>, or also, in its right understanding, <term>Theosophy</term>). He found it here and there in pieces and mixed with other things, but nowhere so perfectly high and deeply grounded as with this simple man and rejected cornerstone <note>A biblical allusion to Christ, suggesting Böhme was an overlooked source of divine truth.</note> (not without great offense and annoyance to the dialectical school-scholars and metaphysical "church-lights"). And Dr. B. Walter behaved toward our *Theodidacto* <note>Greek/Latin: "One taught by God."</note>—whom he called *Teutonicum Philosophum* <note>Latin: "The German Philosopher," a title that became Böhme's most famous epithet.</note> (perhaps after the old

<column-break/>

canon Johannes Teutonicus, or to distinguish between nations, and because of the excellent gift of such writings composed in High German)—very strictly in his diet and all his actions. He did not well perceive that Jacob Böhme, by contrast, was more free- and gentle-spirited, or <term>indifferent</term> <note>In this context, "indifferent" means impartial or not bound by rigid external religious forms.</note>, and without self-willed affectation. For indeed, mere art and nature—without the holy light of favor and grace—is always more external, sharp, partisan, and legalistic than internal, sweet, mild, universal, and Evangelical. Therefore, the gifts of the Spirit, according to the distinction of their original ground and first origin, as well as by their fruits and offspring, are to be distinguished fairly and thoughtfully. One should appropriately assign and share with each person what is theirs (according to whether they are a limb of the body or a vessel and tool in the house), and not (as happens in <term>Babel</term> <note>Böhme's term for the confused, squabbling state of institutional churches.</note>) shave everything with the same comb or strike everything over the same last. One should not immediately pervert and condemn whatever does not harmonize perfectly or one-sidedly with everything else, as is found very thoroughly and understandably explained in these writings of our *Teutonicus*.

Furthermore, it is especially to be noted that our blessed *Teutonicus* did not learn those Latin <term>Terminos</term> and technical words which he used (especially in his later writings) from himself or from reading foreign books, but from the written and oral acquaintance he maintained with learned people, especially physicians, chemists, and philosophers. As I have heard from him many times, he earnestly wished that he had at least learned the Latin language (about which <term>Maximilian I</term> <note>The Holy Roman Emperor (1459–1519).</note> also complained). For he felt he could not fully express the many wondrous things hovering before his eyes in his German mother-tongue...

In the friendship-albums of good friends, he commonly wrote the following rhymes:

When in the year 1624 / he was with us in Silesia for several weeks / and alongside other edifying conversations regarding the blessed knowledge of God and His Son / especially from the light of secret and manifest nature / he simultaneously prepared the *Three Tables of Divine Revelation* (addressed to John Sigmund von Schweinitz / and me, A. "...take me into your Kingdom!" But when it was barely 6 o'clock in the morning, he took leave of his wife and son, blessed them, and then spoke: "Now I depart for Paradise!" He asked his son to turn him over, sighed deeply, and fell asleep. Thus, he departed from this world in peace, very gently and quietly. After this, the mortal remains of our late Jacob Böhme <note>The text uses the initials J. B., referring to Jacob Böhme (1575–1624), the German mystic and cobbler.</note> were properly cleansed and shrouded, subsequently placed in a coffin, and buried there in Görlitz in the "God’s Acre" <note>original: "Gottes-Acker"; a traditional German term for a cemetery, suggesting a field where the body is "sown" to be raised later.</note> with the usual bells and singing. ->2. Question: But how can one be certain that J. B. is the actual, true author of these sublime writings?<-

**Answer:** Should there be anyone who might take offense at either the simple person or the highly venerable gift of the author, and might suspect that someone else was "under the covers" <note>A common idiom meaning "acting in secret."</note> hiding under such a name to chatter something new and unknown to a curious world—or perhaps even to bring forth some old, damned heresy and dreamed-up devilry from the abyss (which is not uncommon among current dream-addicted world-fantasists, especially those Aristotelian school-quarrelers <note>Referring to the Scholastic academics who relied on Aristotelian logic rather than mystical experience.</note> and young, fashionable "lords of the temple")—let such a person be faithfully warned for the sake of God and His eternal, remaining truth. Let him be sufficiently informed not to allow himself to be taken in by such completely groundless thoughts and slanderous blasphemies, nor be turned away from the truth. For it has thus pleased God, according to His wise counsel and will, to choose not what is high, what is powerful, what is noble, what is wise, what is rich, or what is "something," etc., but what is lowly, what is weak, what is ignoble, what is foolish, what is poor and nothing in the eyes

<column-break/>

of the world, so that He may put to shame what is high and mighty. For God resists the proud and casts the mighty from their seats; He raises the poor out of the mire, and to the humble He gives such and other grace. The secret of the Lord is among those who fear Him, and He lets them know His covenant. Or does the Almighty not have the power to do what He wishes with His own? Do you, proud Pharisee, envious High Priest, and know-it-all scribe, look sour and squint-eyed because the Lord our merciful God and Father is so pious and kind toward His children? Then go hence, and in your anger and pride, bite off your own tongue out of heartache and gnashing teeth; tear and devour your own earthly and godless heart with grimness and hellish misery from your body. Thus one may recognize that your birth is from the old serpent and vengeful hell, and all your art is from the proud Lucifer and the angry dragon-devil, but by no means from God, in Christ and His Holy Spirit and the word of grace and truth. Or should it not be necessary, in these current highly dangerous times of a devastated and destroyed Christianity, that God finally look into it and speak with "other lips" <note>A reference to Isaiah 28:11, suggesting God will speak through unexpected, non-clerical messengers when the leaders fail.</note> to these misled peoples and their blind guides? For all flesh corrupts its way before the Lord, and especially the Evil One—in his sham-holy and false lights, which are called spiritual and Christian but are recognized as fleshly and un-Christian—has most elegantly and artistically covered everything. And yet, under such masks, he has awakened and stretched out the fiery blood-sword and hellish sword of vengeance, setting one brother against another (especially among Christians and those who call themselves Evangelical). I shall not zealot further upon this, but rather leave the general revelation and very painful experience to those who love God.

...caused, as the diligent and impartial reader of these writings (if he deems them worthy) will more and more experience to his satisfaction, and not without special, fruit-bearing edification in true, unvarnished <note>original: "ungefürnisten"; meaning pure or sincere Christianity, not covered with a "varnish" of hypocrisy or external ritual.</note> Christianity.

However, certain things are contained herein—especially concerning previously unknown mysteries and hidden things of the Divine and human, heavenly and earthly, angelic and devilish **birth, nature, and property**—which may not be immediately understood and grasped by everyone. One must leave this to the Spirit of God in His own school, and for this time, until one thing or another might be better recognized in a future unfolding and revealed to those who are worthy. For God, according to His eternal wisdom, does not reveal everything so soon, all at once, or in a single moment, but gives and illuminates His holy light and knowledge from time to time. In this, it should be well observed that in such God-inspired writings, the common "pagan" academic style of examining and judging will not suffice. This refers to how one otherwise presumes to master and criticize the mouth and hand of the Holy Spirit Himself in Holy Scripture, according to the godless and spiritless Aristotle's sharp **Logic** <note>original Latin: "Dialectica"</note>, talkative **Rhetoric** <note>original Latin: "Rhetorica"</note>, and absurd **Metaphysics** <note>original Latin: "Metaphysica"</note>, acting in an overly clever, overly wise, and even blasphemous manner. Or the lazy Jew of the living Word? Or the foolish Greek of the Spirit of eternal wisdom (which he has neither seen, nor heard, nor understood)? What judgment can they pass that is consistent with God, Nature, Scripture, or Faith? None at all. Instead, it requires a very different school, birth, and testing—namely, Divine revelation and the renewal in the spirit of the mind (as the light of hidden grace and truth

<column-break/>

**Jesus Christ** <note>original Latin abbreviation: "J. C."</note> with the opening of the Kingdom of God, together with the sight and foretaste of the powers of the world to come, and the eternal Word of God in us). The author of these glorious writings speaks and points this out very clearly and extensively here and there.

->3. Question: How did this simple, ordinary man reach such an uncommonly high knowledge of God?<-

Answer: He himself testifies to it thus: "When (he says) I looked upon the great deep of this world, as well as the sun and stars, and the clouds, rain, and snow, and considered in my spirit the whole creation of this world; therein I found in all things good and evil, love and wrath—in the irrational creatures, such as wood, stones, earth, and elements, as well as in humans and animals. Additionally, I considered the little spark <note>original: "Füncklein"; a common mystical term for the soul's inner point of contact with God.</note> of man, what he might be esteemed by God in comparison to this great work of Heaven and Earth. But because I found that in all things there was evil and good—in the elements as well as in the creatures—and that in this world it went as well for the ungodly as for the pious, and even that the barbaric nations possessed the best lands and that fortune favored them even more than the pious: I became therefore entirely melancholy and highly troubled. No Scripture could comfort me, though I was quite well acquainted with it. In this, the Devil surely was not idle, for he often drummed "pagan" thoughts into me, which I will here keep silent. But when, in such tribulation, I earnestly raised my spirit (for I understood little or nothing of what it was) into God, as if in a great storm, and my whole heart and mind, together with all other thoughts and will, enclosed themselves therein, wrestling without ceasing with the love and mercy of God, and..."

# Foreword regarding the Author and his sublime Writings.

->E 2<-

...not to let go, unless he then blessed me—that is: unless he then enlightened me with his Holy Spirit, so that I might understand his will and be rid of my sadness—then the Spirit broke through. But as I stormed so hard against GOD and all the gates of hell in my established zeal, as if more of my powers were at hand, intending to risk my life for it (which certainly would not have been in my power without the assistance of the Spirit of GOD), immediately after several hard storms, my spirit broke through the gates of hell into the innermost birth of the Godhead, and was embraced there with love, as a bridegroom embraces his dear bride. 

But what kind of triumphing there was in the spirit, I cannot write or speak of; it can be compared to nothing except that where life is born in the midst of death, and it compares to the resurrection from the dead. In this light, my spirit immediately saw through everything, and recognized GOD in all creatures, in herb and grass alike—who he is, and how he is, and what his will is. Also, in this light, my will immediately grew with a great urge to describe the **essence of GOD**. 

Because I could not immediately grasp the deep births of GOD in their essence and comprehend them in my reason, it was delayed a good twelve years before the right understanding was given to me. And it happened as it does with a young tree that one plants in the earth: at first it is young and tender, and has a friendly appearance, especially when it begins to grow well, but it does not bear fruit immediately; and even if it blossoms, the blossoms fall off; many a cold wind, frost, and snow also pass over it before it grows up and bears fruit. So it also happened to this spirit; the first fire was only a seed, but not an ever-persistent light; since that time, many a cold wind has passed over it,

<column-break/>

but the will has not been extinguished. This tree has also often tested itself to see if it might bear fruit, and showed itself with blossoming, but the blossom was knocked off the tree until this day; now it stands in its first fruit in growth.

From this light I now have my knowledge, as well as my will and urge, and I will write this knowledge according to my gifts and let GOD rule; even if I should hereby anger the world, the devil, and all the gates of hell, I will see what GOD intends by it. For I am much too weak to recognize His purpose; although the spirit gives some things that are future to be known in the light, I am much too weak according to the **outward man** <note>The "outward man" refers to the physical, earthly personality as opposed to the inner, spiritual self.</note> to grasp such a thing.

The **animal spirit** <term>Animal spirit: Derived from the Latin *anima* (soul), this refers to the soul-spirit or the animating principle that "inter-qualifies" or works in harmony with the divine.</term>, which **inter-qualifies** <term>Inter-qualifies (inqualiret): A term Böhme uses to describe how different forces, spirits, or qualities (Qualitäten) flow into and operate within one another.</term> with GOD, understands it well; the **beastly body** <note>original: "thierische Leib"; refers to the lower, biological, and mortal nature of man that lacks spiritual perception.</note>, however, only gets a glimpse of it, just as when lightning flashes. For thus the innermost birth of the soul presents itself when it tears through the gates of hell in the elevation of the Holy Spirit, as if through the outermost birth, which however soon closes again; then the **wrath of GOD** bolts the firmament and keeps it captive in his power. 

At that point, the knowledge of the outward man is gone, and he goes about in his sorrowful and anxious birth like a pregnant woman in labor, who would always gladly give birth and yet cannot, but is always in anguish. So it goes with the beastly body too: once it has tasted the sweetness, it always hungers and thirsts for it. But the devil in GOD’s wrath resists excellently, and a man in such a course must always stand in anxious birth, and it is nothing but fighting and fencing in his births. I have written this not for my own praise, but for the reader's comfort, in case he might desire to [walk] on my narrow path with [me]...

...to wander with me / so that he might not soon despair / when the gates of hell / and the wrath of GOD meet him / and confront him. 4. **Question:** What moved the highly enlightened author to write down this high knowledge?

**Answer:** I cannot hide from you / (he writes,) the simple child’s path / that I walk in Christ / for I cannot write of myself in any other way than as a child / who knows or understands nothing / and has never learned anything / except only this / which the Lord wishes to know within me / according to the measure / by which he reveals himself in me. For I never desired to know anything of the Divine Mystery <note>original: "Mysterio"</note> / much less understood / how I might seek or find it / nor did I know anything of it / as is the way of laypeople in their simplicity. I sought only the heart of Jesus Christ / to hide myself therein from the fierce wrath of GOD / and the attacks of the devil / and I earnestly prayed to GOD for his Holy Spirit and grace / that he might bless and lead me in him / and take from me / that which turns me away from him / and to surrender myself entirely to him / so that I might live not according to my own / but his will / and that he alone might lead me / and I might be his child in his Son Jesus Christ.

In such earnest seeking and desire / in which I suffered violent setbacks / but would rather have risked my life / than go out from it and cease / the gate was opened to me / so that in a quarter of an hour I saw and knew more / than if I had been for many years in high

<column-break/>

schools <note>universities</note> / at which I greatly wondered / and knew not / how it happened to me / whereupon my heart overflowed into the praise of GOD. For I saw and recognized the **Being of all beings** / the Ground and the Abyss <term>Ungrund: Böhme’s term for the absolute, undifferentiated nothingness or "groundless" state from which God and the universe originate</term> / likewise the birth of the Holy Trinity / the origin and the primal state of this world / and of all creatures / through the Divine Wisdom. I recognized and saw in myself three worlds / as 1. the Divine / Angelic or Paradisiacal: And then 2. the dark world / as the origin of nature toward fire: And 3. this outer visible world / as a creature and offspring / or as a spoken being / from the two inner spiritual worlds. I saw and recognized the whole being in evil and good / how one originated from the other / and how the mother of the procreatress was / so that I not only greatly wondered / but also rejoiced. And it fell so strongly into my mind / to write this down as a record <note>original: "Memorial"</note> / although I could only grasp it with great difficulty in my outer man / and put it to the pen; I had to begin working immediately in this very great mystery / like a child / who goes to school. Inwardly I saw it well / as in a great depth / for I saw through it as into a Chaos <note>original: "Chaos"; here meaning a primordial state where all things are present but not yet distinct</note>, where everything lies within / but its unfolding was impossible for me. But it opened itself in me from time to time / as in a plant: Although I went about with it for 12 years / and was pregnant with it in myself / and found a violent drive within me / before I could bring it into the exterior / until it afterwards fell upon me like a downpour / whatever it hits / it hits. So it went with me / whatever I could grasp to bring into the exterior / that I wrote down. Although the sun shone for me afterwards for a considerable time / but not always constantly; when it hid itself / then I could also hardly understand my own work / and this for the reason / so that man may recognize / that knowledge is not his / but GOD’s.

# Foreword regarding the Author and his sublime Writings.
<sig>E 3</sig>
<meta>catchword: not</meta>

...that GOD knows in the soul of man what and how He wills. I intended to keep such writings of mine with me for my entire life, and to give them to no one: But it came to pass through the providence of the Most High that I entrusted something of them to a person, through whom it became public without my prior knowledge. Consequently, my first book, *Aurora* <note>original: "Aurora," Latin for "The Daybreak," Böhme's first major work written in 1612</note>, was taken from me. and because strange things were revealed therein, which were not immediately comprehensible to the human mind, I had to endure much from those who are wise only in their own reason. I did not see that same first book for three years, thinking it was long dead and gone, until copies were sent to me by learned people, exhorting me to reveal my talent. My outward reason did not want to do this at all, since it had already suffered so much. Thus, my reason was very weak and timid, for at the same time the Light of Grace was withdrawn from me for a considerable time and smoldered within me like a hidden fire, so that there was nothing but anguish in me—mockery from without, a fiery urge from within—and yet I could not grasp it, until the Most High came to my aid again with His breath and awakened a new life in me. There I attained a better style of writing, and also a deeper and more fundamental knowledge; I could bring everything better into the outward expression, as the book *Of the Threefold Life* through the three Principles <note>original: "3. Principia," referring to Böhme's cosmological system of the three "worlds" or forces that govern reality</note> demonstrates, and as the Divine Lover, should his heart be opened to it, will see.

Thus I have now written, not from human doctrine or science learned from books, but from my own book, which was opened within me. As the noble likeness of God—the book of the noble image (meaning the image of God)—was granted to me to read, and therein I found my study, like a child in its mother's house who sees what the father does and mimics him in its childhood play; I need no other book for it.

<column-break/>

My book has only three leaves; these are the three Principles of Eternity. Therein I can find everything that Moses and the Prophets, as well as Christ and the Apostles, have spoken. I can find the foundation of the world and all secrets therein—yet not I, but the Spirit of the Lord does it, according to the measure that He wills. For I have pleaded with Him many hundreds of times: if my knowledge might not serve His glory and the improvement of my brothers, He should take it from me and keep me only in His love. But I found that with my pleading, I only ignited the fire within me more intensely, and in such ignition and knowledge, I produced my writings. I did not intend to become known among such people as I see now; I still thought I was writing for myself, although the Spirit of God in secret showed my spirit enough of the purpose for which it was intended. Yet my outward reason was always the contrary, except at times when the Morning Star <note>A term Böhme uses for the dawning of spiritual enlightenment in the soul</note> rose; then reason was ignited along with it and danced as if it had grasped it, but it is far from it. God dwells in the noble image, and not in the spirit of the stars and elements; He possesses nothing but Himself in His own likeness. And although He possesses everything, since He indeed owns all things, nothing grasps Him except that which has sprung and come from Him, namely the soul in the likeness of God.

Therefore, all my writing is like that of a schoolboy going to school. God has led my soul into a wondrous school, and in truth, I can claim nothing for myself, as if my "I-hood" <note>original: "Ichheit," referring to the ego or the self-centered human personality</note> were anything or understood anything. No one should think more highly of me than what he sees here; for the work in my labor is not mine. I have it only according to the measure granted to me by the Lord; I am only His tool with which He does what He wills. This I report to you, my beloved sir, for your information, so that...

5. Question: Why did the late author publish his high writings?

Answer: How this came about we have heard in part in the cited testimony: Namely, he wrote in the beginning for himself as a memorial; but when his writing became known through God's providence, he then wrote for no other reason than out of the desire of true love toward the children of God. "That I," (he says,) "might delight myself as one with them; I am not concerned with any temporal goods or gifts, as Your Honor <note>original: "E. Gestr." (Euer Gestrengen), a formal address to a person of high social or administrative standing</note> has so kindly offered to me in service of love as to a stranger. Rather, it is for the hope of Israel <note>A biblical reference to the spiritual restoration of God's people and the realization of divine promises</note>, and so that I may be highly gladdened with God's children in that life to come; and then my labor, which I perform here in love toward them, will be well rewarded, when I thus rejoice with my brothers and everyone’s works shall follow them."

Therefore I am in earnest, since a spark of the noble pearl <note>A reference to the "Pearl of Great Price" from Matthew 13:45, symbolizing Divine Wisdom or the inward Christ-light</note> has also been given to me, and Christ faithfully warns us not to put it under the bench or bury it in the earth. We should also not fear too much those men who kill the body and can do nothing more, but rather fear Him who can destroy body and soul and cast them into hell.

And though in my time I shall not obtain great thanks from some, to whom their

<column-break/>

belly is dearer than the kingdom of heaven; yet my writings have their gifts and stand in their own time. For they have a truly precious, earnest birth and origin; and when I reflect upon my own slight, lowly, and simple person, I wonder even more than my adversary does. But because I recognize in power and light that it is a pure gift from God, who still gives me such a driving will to it, so that I must write what I see and recognize, I ought to be more obedient to God than to men, so that my bishopric <note>original: "Bisthum"; Böhme uses this biblically (Acts 1:20) to mean his spiritual office or duty to witness</note> be not taken from me again and given to another, which would surely cause me eternal regret. Since Your Honor has gained a desire to read the same—perhaps, as I certainly hope, by God's providence—then I will not hide it from Your Honor, since God the Most High has called Your Honor to the first work, to publish the same through His wonderful counsel. Where I thought the driver <note>original: "der Treiber," referring to Gregorius Richter, the pastor of Görlitz who persecuted Böhme and suppressed his first book, *Aurora*</note> had swallowed it, it sprouted as a green twig, entirely without my knowledge. And though I know nothing of myself as to what God will finally do, and His counsel is hidden from me, as is the way He wishes to go—I can also say nothing of myself—the driver might yet attribute it to me as an untimely pride, that I would thus wish to boast of my few gifts, which I nevertheless have from grace, and thus let the thoughts of my heart be seen for my own glory. 6. **Q.** But if the author wrote for himself alone as a memorial, why does he use the word **We** or **Us**, etc., when speaking of his person?

**Ans.** We speak (he says) thus, as if of many, and yet we mean that we write for ourself; all of which is hidden in God; for the fiery impulse <term>fiery impulse; Böhme’s term for the divine drive or inspiration that compels the soul to act or speak</term> desires it to be so, as if we spoke out of many and also before many, though I know nothing of it. Therefore, if it should happen that it were read, no one should regard it as a work of external reason; for it was made from the inner hidden man; accordingly, this hand has written without regard for any person; we therefore admonish the reader to enter into himself and behold himself in the inward man; thus we will be very sweet and dear to him, we say this without jest in all faithfulness.
<margin>The Threefold Life, chapter 6, sections 9, 10, 11.</margin>

That the author thus uses the word **We** and **Us** happened much more out of reverence and humility, so as not to attribute this high revelation to himself, as he expressly testifies: "Although it is indeed given and opened to me, it is nevertheless not of my understanding and own knowledge, but the knowledge stands in the Spirit of Christ, according to which the hand names itself twofold, as **Us**; for it speaks from two persons; for two persons do not say **I**, but **We**, and speak of two, like a Lord who speaks both of his person and of his kingdom. Thus God’s children and servants should also not say: 'Mine is the knowledge, mine is the understanding,' but give God the honor, and in their opening of the wonders of God, speak of two, as of the Giver and the Receiver:"

<column-break/>

"...therefore no one should understand our writing as if the hand were boasting and honoring itself according to human authority and dignity; although we are of dignity in Christ, we desire no honor or glory according to the external man, for the honor belongs to God."
<margin>Forty Questions, 30, sections 3, 4, 5.</margin>

7. **Q.** What then is actually the right main purpose why the author wrote so many books?

**Ans.** Our whole writing (he says) aims only at how we may seek, make, and finally find ourselves; how we must give birth so that we are one spirit with God; that God may be in us and we in God; that God’s Spirit of Love may be in us—both the willing and the doing—so that we may escape the torment of anxiety <term>Angst-Quaal; Böhme uses 'anguish' or 'torment' to describe the state of nature or the soul before it finds the light of God's love</term>. He himself has given the actual theme and ground of these writings to be understood in the beautiful preface to his first book, called: **The Aurora** <note>original: "Die Morgen-Röthe", Böhme's seminal first work, meaning "The Day-Spring" or "Dawn"</note>, sections 84-88.

"Now I have given this book the name: **The Root or Mother of Philosophy, Astrology, and Theology**: But so that you may know what this book treats of, understand: 1. Through **Philosophy** is treated the Divine power, what God is, and how in the being of God nature, stars, and elements are constituted, and from whence all things have their origin; how heaven and earth are constituted, as well as angels, men, and devils, plus heaven and hell, and everything that is creaturely; also what both qualities in nature are, from the true ground in the knowledge of the Spirit, in the impulse and surging of God."

"2. Through **Astrology** is treated the powers of nature, the stars and elements, how all creatures have come from them, and how they drive, govern, and work in everything, and how evil and good are wrought through them..."

# Preliminary Report on the Author and his High Writings.

[This is an] Image / for those / who sprout forth from the animal image with their own human image / which belongs in God's Kingdom / and who would gladly live and grow in the human image / in the true human [being]; who are often and much hindered by the contrary life / and thus remain stuck in the mixed life / and suffer in the birth of the holy life: For them we have written these writings / and tell them / that they should not consider it impossible to recognize / or to know such mysteries / and we give them this to contemplate in a parable: Suppose there were a life / that had grown out of all [other] lives / and was mixed; but another life grew [within it] / which / even though it grew out of all lives / was free from all the other lives / and yet also stood in all the **essences** <term>Essentien: the inner, spiritual "stuff" or fundamental qualities of a being</term> of the lives. That same other new life would be illuminated with the Light / and only within itself / so that it could see all the other lives. And behold / the other lives could not see nor grasp the new life. Thus it is with everyone / who is born again in and out of GOD / out of the mixed life / [both] evil and good.

That same new image born in the life of GOD / sees all natural lives / and nothing is foreign or difficult for it / for it sees only its root / out of which it has grown; just as we can recognize / how a beautiful flower grows out of the wild earth / which does not look like the earth / but declares with its beauty the potential of the earth / and how it is mixed with good and evil. So too is every person / who is born back into the true image of GOD / out of the animalistic / wild / earthly nature and property. For those / who are now in the growth / and are pushing toward the beautiful **Lilies** <note>The "Lily" is Böhme’s favorite symbol for the spiritual rebirth and the flourishing of the soul in the "Age of the Holy Spirit."</note> in the Kingdom of GOD / and stand in the birth / we have written this book / so that they may strengthen their essences therein / green forth in the life of GOD / and grow in the **Tree of Paradise** <note>A symbol of the interconnectedness of all believers who live within the divine life.</note> / and bear fruit; since all children of GOD / who grow in this tree / and each is a branch on the same tree / so we have wished to share our sap / scent / and essence with our fellow-branches in our tree / in which we all stand / and out of which we all grow / so that our Tree of Paradise would green forth / and we would rejoice among one another / and that each branch and twig would help cover the other from the storm / we give ourselves as children of this growth to be kindly considered in this book / and recommend ourselves to them in their love and growth.

->Preface in 6 Points.<-

10. **Question.** Is there not many a soul desiring salvation / who with all their diligence in reading and searching / still cannot grasp the Author's meaning?

**Answer.** It does not require much tormenting and heavy thinking in these deep writings / we write from another **Principle** <term>Principio: one of the foundational realms of existence; Böhme describes three—the dark world of fire, the light world of God, and the outward world of nature</term>; no reader understands us rightly in the ground [of their being] / unless their mind is born out of GOD; no **historical knowledge** <note>Böhme uses this term to refer to academic or factual learning that lacks spiritual experience.</note> should be sought in our writings / because just as it is impossible to see GOD with earthly eyes / so it is also not possible / that an unilluminated mind should grasp heavenly thoughts and senses / in the earthly vessel / it must only be grasped like with like. We do indeed carry the heavenly treasure in an earthly vessel / but a heavenly container must be hidden in the earthly [one] / otherwise the heavenly [treasure] will not be grasped or preserved. No one should think / that he will find the lilies of the heavenly growth with deep searching and thinking / if he does not enter through earnest repentance into the **new birth** / so that it grows in himself / otherwise it is only a **History** <note>A mere story or external account without inner reality.</note> / where his mind never experiences the ground / and yet he imagines / he has grasped it / but his mind makes it manifest / what spirit's child he is / for it stands written: *They shall be taught by GOD.*

...are [one] who returns again to the Father, then leave my book unread; it will otherwise go poorly for you. For the Grand Prince, Lucifer, will not rest from troubling you. In these writings, he stands before the children of GOD entirely naked and bare, for which he is ashamed like a person who is made a mockery before all people because of their misdeeds. **11. Question:** How should an earnest lover [of God] approach the work to achieve this healing knowledge?

**Answer:** Everything depends on the will and on earnestness; that the will enters into the **Magic** <term>Magia: For Böhme, this is not sorcery, but the "desire-will" or the spiritual force of attraction that pulls possibilities into actual existence.</term> (into the attractive desire and hunger); for eternity is magical. Everything has come into being <note>original: "zum Wesen kommen"</note> out of **Magic** (as the attractive power). Out of **Magic** arises **Philosophy**; this seeks and finds **Astrology**; this in turn seeks its maker and master, **Astronomy**.

->*Forty Questions on the Soul*, 1, paragraph 194, 195.<-

Therefore let the reader be warned not to ground himself with his will deeper into these very deep writings than he can grasp; he should always let himself be satisfied with what he can comprehend. For in comprehension he still stands within the **essential being** <term>Wesenheit: the actual substance or reality of a thing</term>; there he does not err, no matter how deep the Spirit might lead him, for much more is given to one than to another. This alone is the goal: that each person remains standing in humility toward GOD and surrenders himself to GOD, so that He may work the willing and the doing with him as He wills. When you do this, then you are as if dead within yourself, for you desire nothing but GOD’S will, and the will of GOD is your life. It goes into itself even unto the thousandth

<column-break/>

number, and searches the depths of the Deity with all wonders: He leads your will, surrendered to Him, into the Virgin of His Wisdom <note>The "Sophia" or Divine Wisdom, depicted as a feminine mirror of God’s glory.</note>, so that you may behold all wonders. But you should not **imagine** <term>imaginiren: to create mental constructs or false images from one's own ego</term> the wonders from Him; as soon as you do that, you step out of GOD’S will, which is eternal freedom, and are caught in your own **imagination**. Mark this: for every imagination creates **substantiality** <note>original: "Wesenheit"</note>. Within that you stand, and you must go out again, or you will not behold GOD.

Therefore Christ teaches us humility, love, purity of heart, and to be merciful; and He commands us to seek GOD’S will and surrender ourselves into it. For in GOD’S will we are capable of all things: it is not our own nature that shall do it, but GOD Himself opens within us, and He is our doing, if we work any wonders. For no human soul should say or think: "I will work wonders." No, that cannot be. For the wonders beyond outer nature proceed solely from the **Center** <note>original: "Centro"</note> of eternal nature, from the tenth number, which the creature cannot master. But if the soul is surrendered to GOD’S will, then GOD works wonders in the creature, for it is His pleasure to reveal Himself in the weak. For the strong man stares [fixedly] in his own will and will not surrender it to GOD; he trusts in his own wit. Thus his will is outside of GOD and can do nothing. And if he then speaks of GOD’S being and will out of himself, then he is an ignorant liar; for he does not speak from GOD’S Spirit and will, but from himself, from his delusion, in which there is vain doubt. From this arise the disputes of faith concerning Divine Science: when one seeks GOD in one’s own will and knowledge. Men want to find GOD in their own will, and He is not therein; for He dwells only and purely in the will that surrenders itself entirely with all reason and knowledge to Him. To that person He gives recognition and power to recognize His essence.

# Preliminary Report concerning the Author and his High Writings.

Also, these noble writings must be read through with patience; for their name is called: **The longer, the dearer; the more sought, the more found**; for it is impossible to grasp everything at once. The essence of GOD in the creature is like a wheel, where many wheels are made crosswise <note>original: "quäricht," meaning intersecting or transverse</note> above and below one another, and always turn together; there one indeed sees the wheel and is greatly amazed, and yet cannot learn nor grasp its turning all at once. Instead, the more one looks at the wheel, the more one learns of its form; and the more one learns, the greater delight one has in the wheel. For one always sees something more wonderful, and a person cannot see and learn enough; even though the spirit sees the wheel and wants to grasp its form in every place, it cannot do so sufficiently because of the wheel's turning. But when it comes around again, so that he sees his first form once more, he always learns something more, and becomes ever more favorable toward the wheel, and loves it.

<margin>Aurora, Chapter 21, Sections 61, 64.</margin>

**12. Quest. Whence does it come then, that those who are otherwise practiced in these writings, stumble in their understanding of them, and do not always agree?**

**Answer.** This is not to be wondered at, since we see that such happens even to the most godly themselves from the Holy Scripture. Every creature, in view of the others, is only piecework <term>piecework (Stückwerck): A reference to 1 Corinthians 13:9, "For we know in part." Böhme uses this to explain that human perception is always fragmentary compared to the divine whole.</term> and not a whole; therefore, it sees for itself only piecework. And even if we recognize much more of it, we may not, with our tongues, exalt and bring forth more than piecework. Therefore, one person here grasps this piece, and another grasps another piece of the whole, and thinks he has the whole; he also wants to persuade the other to believe that he has the whole. Thus, one always understands it differently than the other; according to how each is gifted with wisdom, so he grasps it, and so he interprets it. My

<column-break/>

writings will not be understood by everyone according to my meaning—no, perhaps not even by a single person—for everyone receives according to his gift, for [his own] improvement, one more than the other, according to how the Spirit has its property within him. For the Spirit of GOD is also often helpful to the spirits of men, if they are well-willing, and sees what the person wants, so that his good is not hindered, but that everywhere GOD’s wanting and will may be done. For the Spirit that is born out of the soul-fire from GOD’s gentleness <term>gentleness (Sanfftmuth): A technical term in Böhme's system referring to the "light-world" or the soothing, loving quality of God that tames the "fire" of the soul.</term> and essence, that is also the Holy Spirit; He dwells in the Divine property and takes His vision from the Divine property.

What is it now that is foreign in us, so that we cannot see GOD? If the world and the Devil are in GOD’s wrath, so that we do not see with GOD’s eyes, that is no hindrance. If someone now says, "I see nothing Divine," he may consider that his flesh and blood, with the Devil’s cunning, is a hindrance and a lid <note>original: "Deckel," meaning a cover or obstruction</note> to him; often, that he cannot see GOD because of his pride, for his own honor; and often, that he is filled and blinded with earthly malice. If he sat at Christ’s footsteps and walked in [Christ's] life, gave himself under the Cross of Christ, and desired only the entrance of Christ through Christ’s death and descent into hell to the Father—I think it would happen that he would see the Father and his Savior Christ, with the Holy Spirit. Should the Holy Spirit then be blind, if He dwells in the person? Or do I write this for my own glory? Not so, but as a measuring-rule <note>original: "Richt-Schnur," a plumb line or guiding principle</note> for the reader, that he may stand away from his own self-interest <note>original: "Eigenthum," meaning "own-ness" or the self-centered ego</note>, and go out from the way of blasphemy into a holy Divine essence, so that he also may see the wonders of GOD with Divine eyes; to the end that GOD’s will be done, for which purpose this pen has written so much, and not for the sake of own honor and the pleasure of this life, as the "driver" <note>The "driver" (Treiber) likely refers to a legalistic critic or a persecutor who lacks spiritual insight.</note> always scolds us—and yet he remains only the driver in the wrath of GOD, to whom we [turn] the back-

...would gladly grant the [Kingdom of Hea]ven, he might be freed from the Devil and earthly vanity: a craving which makes him blind.

Therefore, you dear children of God, who seek with many tears, let it be a matter of earnestness for you; our seeing and knowing is in God; He reveals to everyone in this world as much as He wills, as He knows is useful and good for them. For he who sees out of God must carry out God’s work; he shall and must practice, teach, speak, and do that which he sees, otherwise his sight will be taken from him. For this world is not worthy of God’s sight, but for the sake of the wonders and revelation of God, it is given to some to see, so that the name of God may be made manifest to the world; which will also be a testimony against all godless existence, which turns the truth into lies and despises the Holy Spirit. For we are not our own, but belong to Him whom we serve in His light. We know nothing of God; He Himself—God—is our knowledge and seeing. We are a nothing, so that He may be everything in us; we should be blind, deaf, and dumb, and know no life in ourselves, so that He may be our life and soul, and our work may be His. Our tongue shall not say, when we have done something good, "we have done this," but "the Lord has done this in us; may His name be highly praised." But what does this evil world do now? If someone said: "God has done this in me"—even if it is good—the world says: "You fool, you did that; God is not in you, you lie." Thus the Spirit of God must be their fool and liar. What is it then, or who speaks out of the blaspheming mouth? The Devil, who is an enemy of God, so that he may cover up God’s work, so that God’s Spirit may not be recognized, and he remains prince of this world until the Judgment.

Thus, when you see that the world strives against you, persecutes you, and blasphemes for the sake of God’s knowledge and name, then think that you have the black Devil before you; so you should bless, so that God’s kingdom may come to us,

<column-break/>

and break the Devil's sting, so that the person may be delivered from the Devil through your blessing and prayer; then you labor rightly in God’s vineyard, and hinder the Devil's kingdom, and bring forth fruit upon God’s table. For in love and gentleness out of the wrath of God, we are born anew; in love and gentleness we must bathe among the Devil's thorns, and strive against him in this world; for love is his poison, it is a fire of terror to him, where he cannot remain. If he knew of one little spark of love in him, he would cast it away, or burst apart so that he might be rid of it. Therefore love and gentleness <term>gentleness (Sanfftmuth): a key Böhmean virtue representing the yielding, "meek" quality of the Second Principle or Divine Light</term> are our sword; with them we can strive with the Devil and the world for the noble little crown under Christ's crown of thorns; for love is the fire of the **Second Principle** <note>original: "andern Principii." Böhme's cosmology describes three principles: the dark fire-world, the light world (this one), and the external world.</note>, it is God’s fire, which the Devil and the world hate: love has God’s eyes, and sees into God; and wrath has the eyes of grimness in the wrath of God, and sees into Hell, into torment, and into death.

<margin>Of the Incarnation <note>original: "Menschw." (Menschwerdung)</note>, Chapter 7, Sections 4, 5, 10.</margin>

**13. Quest. What may be the cause that no people blaspheme and mock these high writings more than the school-scholars and the wise ones of this world?**

**Answer.** Because our highly-enlightened man is taught not by the schools of this world, but by God; who was led into such uncommon knowledge not through his own searching and speculating, but through God’s Spirit and will. Our author gives to these scholars, as a faithful warning against mocking, the following reminder in the *Second Apology against Balthasar Tilke* <note>Balthasar Tilke was a contemporary critic who accused Böhme of heresy.</note>, section 52 to 61:

"Your imagining is a dead understanding of the **Mystery** <note>original: "Mysterio"</note>; if you are taught by God, then go with me to the **Center** <note>original: "Centrum"</note>, and I will prove it to you in all things in this world, yes, in your own selves. I will have nothing excepted where I will not [show] you the like—"

We are a nothing, so that He may be everything in us; we should be blind, deaf, and dumb, and know no life in ourselves, so that He may be our life and soul, and our work may be His. Our tongue should not say, "When we have done something good, we did that," but rather, "The Lord has done that in us; let His name be highly praised." But what does this evil world do now? If one said: "God has done this in me," even if it is good, the world says: "You fool, you did that yourself; God is not in you, you are lying." Thus, the Spirit of God must be their fool and liar. What is it then, or who speaks out of that blasphemous mouth? The devil, who is an enemy of God, so that he may cover up God’s work, so that God’s Spirit may not be recognized, and he may remain prince of this world until the Judgment.

So, when you see that the world strives against you, persecutes you, and blasphemes for the sake of God’s knowledge <term>Erkanntnis: a deep, experiential spiritual knowledge or realization</term> and His name's sake, then think that you have the black devil before you; so you should bless, so that God’s kingdom may come to us,

<column-break/>

and break the devil’s sting, so that through your blessing and prayer, man may be redeemed from the devil; thus you work rightly in God’s vineyard, and hinder the devil's kingdom, and bring forth fruit upon God’s table. For in love and gentleness <term>Sanfftmuth: a state of mildness, humility, and calm resignation</term> out of the wrath of God, we are born anew; in love and gentleness we must bathe in the devil’s thorns and strive against him in this world, for love is his poison; it is to him a fire of terror where he cannot remain. If he knew even a tiny spark of love within himself, he would cast it away or burst apart to be rid of it. Therefore, love and gentleness are our sword; with them we can strive with the devil and the world for the noble little wreath under Christ’s crown of thorns; for love is the fire of the second principle <term>Principium: Böhme’s term for the three fundamental realms of existence; the "Second Principle" is the world of Light and Love</term>; it is God's fire, which the devil and the world hate. Love has God’s eyes and sees into God, and wrath has the eyes of grimness in the anger of God and sees into hell, into torment, and into death.

<margin>*On the Incarnation of Christ*, chapter 7, paragraphs 4, 5, 10.</margin>

### 13. Question: What might be the cause that no people blaspheme and mock these high writings more than the school-scholars and the wise ones of this world?

**Answer:** Because our highly-enlightened man is taught not by the schools of this world, but by God; he was led into such uncommon knowledge <note>original: "Erkanntnis"</note> not through his own searching and speculating, but through God’s Spirit and will. Our author gives these scholars the following reminder in the *Second Apologia* <note>original: "Apologia," a formal defense or justification of his views</note> against Balthasar Tilke <note>A contemporary critic of Böhme who attacked his lack of formal theological training</note>, paragraphs 52 to 61, as a faithful warning against mocking:

> Your imagining is a dead understanding of the mystery <note>original: "Mysterio"</note>; if you are taught by God, then come with me to the center, and I will prove it to you in all things in this world, yes, in yourselves. I will have nothing excepted where I will not show you the likeness...

It frames the struggle between love and wrath as a spiritual battle where love acts as a "poison" to the devil.</summary>
