# Preliminary Report concerning the Author and his High Writings.

...[knowled]ge <note>original: "Erkanntnis"; the word begins on the previous page</note> of the **3 Principles** <term>3 Principles: Jacob Böhme’s foundational concept describing three realms: the dark fire-world (God's wrath), the light world (God's love), and the outer world (the physical universe)</term> to show. Cease from your blasphemy and become a child of the Wise, then it shall be shown to you; but I do not throw the **pearl** <note>A reference to Matthew 7:6, "neither cast ye your pearls before swine," implying that sacred truths should not be shared with those who will only mock them</note> before your feet; know this, not to any of you yet.

I do not have my knowledge from delusion or opinions, as you do, but I have a living knowledge in contemplation and sensibility; I need no **Doctor** <note>A reference to university-educated theologians</note> from the school of this world for it, for I have not learned it from them, but from **God's Spirit**; therefore, I fear nothing of your boasting and mocking.

Dear Lords and brothers in Christ, be students of the **Wisdom of God**: let no one say of himself that he understands it: We know nothing of God, what God is; God's Spirit must become the knowledge in us, otherwise our knowledge is only **Babel** <term>Babel: A term Böhme uses to describe the "confusion" of competing church dogmas and intellectualized religion without spiritual spirit</term>, a perpetual confusion, always teaching, and understanding nothing of the ground in the **Center** <note>original: "Centro"; the inner source or essence of being</note>. What does it matter if I spoke much of wisdom from the Scripture, and could even know the Bible by heart, and did not understand what the wise have spoken, from what spirit and knowledge, if I do not also have the same spirit that they had? How then will I understand them? Such knowledge does not belong to imagining and gathering a heap of verses for one's purpose: No saint or wise man has done that; but a living spirit from God, who may behold the **Mystery** <term>Mysterium: The hidden spiritual reality that underlies the physical world</term>, and walk in living knowledge. God’s Spirit must be in **Reason**, because Reason beholds God. It requires a humble, resigned heart

<column-break/>

for that, not a mocker who boasts <note>original: "rühmet"; the word begins as "rüh" on the previous column</note> in his reason that his reason is enlightened. It is nothing other than a **sidereal enlightenment** <term>Sidereal enlightenment: Intellectual knowledge derived from the "stars" or natural world, rather than the direct light of the Holy Spirit</term>, to be so sharp-witted.

If one is a child of God, let him seek brothers in the love of God, then I can trust him; but because he is a mocker, he goes about having put on the devil's **mask-caps** <note>original: "Larven-Kappen"; likely referring to the disguises of hypocrisy or false identity</note> and walks in pride; he is no Christian, but a **Mouth-Christian** <term>Mouth-Christian: One who claims faith with their mouth but lacks it in their heart or actions</term>, and a confused Babel, just as all such abusive and quarrelsome books are. If one shows the other the way of God in love, humility, and the fear of God, as belongs to children of God, then such contempt will not arise in the world, by which the simple layman is led astray, and becoming entirely ignorant, falls into blasphemy and contempt against his brother who is not of his opinion or religious name; and yet one is as blind as the other in religion (which outside of God’s essence and power is but a trifle and delusion). For true religion does not stand alone in external words in appearance, but in living deed and power, so that one fulfills the very thing he knows from the bottom of the heart, in love towards the other. It must come to the **doing**, or it is only a colored gloss, a **Historical Babel** <term>Historical Babel: Knowing the "history" or literal text of the Bible without experiencing its spiritual power</term>: Where God’s Spirit is not, there is no faith, nor any Christian; but where He is, there He works nothing but works of love, teaches and rebukes gently, and is not puffed up and mocking, like my **adversary** <note>original: "Gegensetzer"</note>.

->Answer<-

What he is; 2. From what or from whom he originates; 3. For what purpose he was created; and 4. What his office <note>original: "Amt"; in this context, it refers to one's spiritual duty, calling, or functional role in the divine order</note> is. All of this has been placed under his hands, so that through his senses and reason he can tame all such things and use and drive them according to his will as it pleases him. # Of the True Knowledge of God in General.

...the Devil goes about like a roaring lion, seeking those he may devour. Because we are in such terrible danger in this world, surrounded on all sides by enemies and walking quite insecurely on our pilgrimage—and moreover, because we carry the worst enemy within ourselves, whom we hide and do not wish to acknowledge, yet who is the most harmful guest of all, plunging us into God’s wrath. Indeed, he is the wrath of God himself, casting us into the eternal fire of wrath, into eternal, unquenchable pain. It is therefore absolutely necessary that we learn to know this enemy well: what he is, who he is, and how he is; how he entered into us; what his right and property within us are; as well as the Devil's right and access to us, and how he is befriended by our own enemy who dwells within us—how they are favorable and kind to one another, how they are both enemies of God, and how they are constantly lying in wait to ruin and murder us.

Furthermore, it is highly necessary for us to contemplate and learn to know ourselves for these great reasons: because we see and know that for the sake of our own enemy (who is God's enemy and ours, who dwells within us, and is even half of the person himself), we must die and decay. If this enemy becomes powerful within us, gains the upper hand, and becomes the master <note>original: "Primas"; the primary or governing part of a person's nature</note>, he plunges us into the abyss with all the devils, to dwell with them forever in eternal, unquenchable torment and pain in eternal darkness. Indeed, he plunges us into a house of desolation, into the eternal forgetting of all good, and into God's displeasure, so that God and all creatures become our eternal enemies.

We have even higher reasons to learn to know ourselves—how we are comprised of both good and evil—since we have the promise of eternal life: that if we overcome our own enemy together with the Devil, we shall be God's children and live in His kingdom with Him, and in Him among His holy angels in eternal joy, clarity, and splendor

<column-break/>

and well-being, in grace and gentleness, without any touch of evil, and even without any knowledge of evil, living eternally in God. To this end, we have the promise that if we have overcome our own enemy and buried him in the earth, we shall come forth again on the Last Day in a new body—in which there will be no torment—to live with God forever in perfect love, joy, delight, and blessedness. Also, we have the knowledge and science that we have within us the rational soul, which is in God's love and is immortal; and if she is not overcome by her opposite, but rather fights against her enemy like a spiritual knight, then God will stand by her with His Holy Spirit. He will enlighten her and make her strong to victory against all her enemies; He will fight for her, and in the overcoming of evil, He will glorify and crown her as a precious knight with the most beautiful heavenly crown (2 Timothy 4:7-8, Revelation 2:10).

### 2. Question: In what does the true knowledge of God and oneself actually consist?

**Answer:** The true knowledge of God and ourselves is not a historical knowledge <note>theoretical or academic learning based on reading rather than experience</note> of God—His nature, essence, name, attributes, and works—nor of man’s creation, fall, and redemption as it is taught in the schools and grasped by reason. Rather, it is a living and infallible acquaintance <note>original: "connoissance"</note>, just as a single sincere friend recognizes another as proven through many trials. External reason says: "How can a human in this world see into God, as if into another world, and say what God is? That cannot be; it must be an imagination with which a person tickles and deceives themselves." This is as far as external reason goes; it can explore no further so that it might rest. If I were still stuck in that same art <note>meaning the "art" of worldly logic or philosophy</note>, I would say the same. For he who sees nothing says: "There is nothing there." What he sees, he recognizes; he knows nothing more of anything than what is before his eyes. But I would ask the mocker and the entirely earthly man whether heaven is blind, as well as hell and God Himself? Is there also a "seeing" in the Divine world? Does the Spirit of God also see, both in the love-light-world and also in the fury in the wrath-world, at the Center? If he says: "There is a seeing within it," as is indeed true, then he may well take care that he does not more often see with the Devil’s eyes in his intended malice,

<column-break/>

since he fashions a thing in the imagination of his false malice for a long time before carrying it out, and sees beforehand how he can and will accomplish his villainy. If he can see the malice there beforehand, why does he not also see his reward beforehand? Oh no, the Devil sees with his eyes and covers up the punishment so that the man might complete the malice. If he drove out the Devil, he would see his great folly that the Devil had consecrated to him. The Devil lets him see the evil and lends him eyes for it, so that he sees the distant thing that is yet to happen, and he is thus blinded and does not know that he sees with the Devil’s eyes.

In the same way, the Saint sees with God’s eyes. What God sees before Him, the Spirit of God sees in the new rebirth <note>the spiritual transformation of a person</note> through the right human eyes, from the image of God; he is, in his essence, both a seeing and a doing. This does not happen in the "Old Adam" <note>the fallen, worldly nature of humanity</note>; this part must be a servant to it. He must put into action what the New Man sees in God. For Christ said: "The Son of Man does nothing except what he sees the Father do; that he also does." Thus the Son of Man has become our Head, into whom we have entered; He has become our body, and His Spirit is our spirit. Should we then be blind to God while in Christ? The Spirit of Christ sees through and in us what He wills, and what He wills, we see and know in Him. Outside of Him, we know nothing of God. He performs Divine works and sees what and when He wills—not when Adam wills, or when Adam would like to pour out his malice (to show himself off with pride). Oh no, there He hides Himself, and does not look within us into the joy-light in God, but into the Cross, into tribulation, into Christ’s suffering and death, persecution and shame, into great sadness. He looks into that, and lets the "old donkey" <note>a derogatory term for the stubborn, physical body or the unrefined ego</note> struggle and carry Christ’s cross; that is his office. But on the path through the death of Christ, the New Man sees into the angelic world <note>original: "englische Welt"; 'English' here is an archaic German form for 'angelic' (Engel)</note>; it is easy for him...

# On the True Knowledge of God in General.

...clearer and brighter to grasp than the earthly world; it happens naturally, not through imagination, but with seeing eyes—those eyes which are meant to possess the angelic world, namely the image-eyes of the soul. It is seen with the spirit that proceeds from the soul's fire; that same spirit looks into heaven and beholds God and eternity, and no other. This is also the noble image made after God’s likeness.

<margin>The Incarnation of Christ <note>original: "Menschw." refers to Böhme's work *Von der Menschwerdung Jesu Christi* (1620).</note>, Part 2, Chapter 7, Sections 1, 2, 3.</margin>

**3. Question:** How then may a soul hungry for salvation reach such living fellowship and acquaintance with God?

**Answer:** The only key to reaching the knowledge and fellowship of God is the knowledge and denial of oneself. However, the key to the knowledge of oneself is the knowledge of God. As much as we know ourselves, so much may we know God; as much as we deny ourselves, so much will we have fellowship with God. As much as we have fellowship with God, so much will we know ourselves. The more we open our eyes, the more we see the light of the sun; the more we see the light, the more our eyes will open, etc.

**4. Question:** Can a person reach no true knowledge of God and themselves through mere contemplation and reading of Holy Scripture?

**Answer:** To be sure, Holy Scripture is beyond contradiction a glorious means to true knowledge, like the bright air illuminated by the clarity of the sun, and a pure and undefiled mirror of wisdom. But whoever wants to see the light and look at themselves in the mirror must first have eyes to see. Because man is by nature blind, and is hidden and sealed away from himself with the seven seals <note>A reference to the Book of Revelation; here representing the various layers of human sin and worldly distraction that block spiritual sight.</note> of the wrath of God, he cannot truly recognize the Scripture, nor himself, nor God, unless he be born anew and follow the Lamb <note>Jesus Christ</note> who walks among the seven golden lampstands, who alone has the power to open the book and its seals. The person who truly wants to learn to know what they are cannot reach this through their own reason, but only in the true process of Christ—in a truly yielded soul <term>yieldedness: (German: *Gelassenheit*) a central mystical concept meaning the total surrender of one's own will to God</term> which leaves behind reason and

<column-break/>

its own cleverness of human selfhood <note>original: "Selbstheit"; the ego-driven nature that seeks its own gain rather than God's will</note> by turning away from the earthly path. Such a soul enters into the highest simplicity of Christ, in true humility under the cross of Christ, as Christ faithfully taught us when He said: *Unless you turn and become like children, and are born again of water and the Holy Spirit, you shall not see the kingdom of God.* For this, a true yieldedness and abandonment of human selfhood is required, so that the person turns entirely into their inward ground <note>the "Seelengrund" or the deepest, essential part of the soul where God dwells</note> and brings their selfhood to nothing. Through earnest repentance and with inward desire, they must turn from this worldly existence into God, dying to their own ability and will in the death of Christ, sinking into God’s mercy. In this way, they may be seized by the Holy Spirit within their own inward ground, so that the Spirit sees, wills, and acts through them as pleases God. The Spirit alone is the searcher in divine knowledge and the light of the soul, in which the soul beholds and recognizes God; in no other way can one reach divine and natural knowledge and contemplation. For the natural "reason-man" understands nothing of the mystery of the kingdom of God, because he is outside of God and not in Him. This is proven by the scholars of reason <note>theologians who study the Bible only as an academic or logical subject</note>, who argue about God's nature and will and yet do not recognize Him, for they do not hear God’s word within them. Everything is dead regarding God if it does not have the living voice and the divine hearing of the new birth in the essence of Christ within itself, so that the Spirit of God gives testimony to its outward hearing and teaching. Only in this inward seeing is God recognized and His essence understood, for which the outward, literal word is merely a form and a prepared instrument. True understanding, however, must enter into the literal word from the inward ground—from the living Word of God, which must first be opened within the person.

# Part I / Chapter 1.

Taste <note>In this mystical tradition, "taste" refers to a direct, sensory-like experience of God's presence, rather than just thinking about Him.</note> is more precious and lovely than all the joy of the world; and whoever receives it once values it higher than all the world’s goods; nothing is equal to it except the Godhead itself. Such a little crown is placed upon the one who seeks it with earnestness and surrenders themselves not to flesh and blood, but to His discipline and guidance.

->Epistle 10, sections 20, 21, 22, 24.<- <note>original: "Send-Br." refers to Jakob Böhme’s *Theosophic Epistles* (Sendbriefe).</note>

### 2. Question: In what, then, does the true knowledge of GOD and oneself actually consist?

**Answer:** The true knowledge of God and ourselves is not a "historical" knowledge <note>The author uses "historical knowledge" to mean "book learning" or knowing facts about God without actually knowing Him personally.</note> of God—His nature, essence, name, attributes, and works—nor of man’s creation, fall, and redemption as it is taught in schools and grasped by reason; rather, it is a living and infallible acquaintance, <term>connoissance</term> <note>original French: "acquaintance" or "knowledge."</note>, just as a single, sincere friend recognizes another as proven through many trials. Outer reason says: "How can a person in this world see into God as if into another world, and say what God is? That cannot be; it must be a fantasy with which a person tickles themselves and deceives themselves." This is as far as outer reason goes; it can explore no further so that it might rest. And if I were still stuck in that same art, I would say exactly the same. For he who sees nothing says: "There is nothing there." What he sees, he recognizes; he knows nothing more than what is before his eyes. But I would ask the mocker and the entirely earthly man: Is heaven blind, as well as hell and God Himself? Is there also a seeing in the Divine world? Does the Spirit of God also see, both in the Light-world of love and also in the "grimness" <note>The "Wrath-world" or "Grimness" (Grimm) is Böhme’s term for the dark, fire-principle of God's nature, separate from His light.</note> in the Wrath-world, in the Center? If he says there is a seeing within it—as is indeed true—then he should take care that he does not more often see with the devil's eyes in his intended malice,

<column-break/>

when he models a thing for a long time in his imagination of false malice in order to carry it out, and sees beforehand how he can and will accomplish his villainy. If he can see the malice there beforehand, does he not also see his reward <note>Likely referring to the "recompense" or punishment for sin.</note> beforehand? O no, the devil sees with his witnesses and covers up the punishment so that he may carry out the malice. If he were to drive out the devil, he would see his great foolishness which the devil had shown him. The devil lets him see the evil; he lends him eyes for it, so that he sees what is far off and yet to happen, and he is thus blinded and does not know that he sees with the devil’s eyes.

Thus, in the same way, the holy person sees with God’s eyes what is before God. That is what the Spirit of God sees in the new birth <note>The "new birth" (Wiedergeburt) is the spiritual transformation where the soul is re-awakened to God's light.</note>, through the right human eyes, out of the image of God; He is a seeing and also a doing for the person. Not for the old Adam <note>The "old Adam" refers to the fallen, selfish human nature that must be overcome.</note>; he must be a servant to it; he must carry into action what the new man sees in God. For Christ said: "The Son of Man does nothing except what he sees the Father doing; that he also does." Thus the Son of Man has become our brother, into whom we have entered; He has become our body, and His Spirit is our spirit. Should we then be blind to God in Christ? The Spirit of Christ sees through and in us what He wills; and what He wills, we see and know in Him. Outside of Him, we know nothing of God. He performs Divine works and sees what and when He wills, not when Adam wills. When Adam would like to pour out his malice (and show off his pride), O no, then He hides Himself and does not look within us into the Joy-Light in God, but into the Cross, into tribulation, into Christ’s suffering and death, persecution, shame, and great sadness. He looks into that and lets the "old donkey" <note>A common Pietist metaphor for the physical body or the stubborn, unrefined ego.</note> struggle and carry Christ’s Cross; that is his office. But on this path through the death of Christ, the new man sees into the angelic world; it is living to him.

# On the True Knowledge of GOD in General.

...clearer and more brightly to grasp than the earthly world; it happens naturally, not through imagination, but with seeing eyes—with those eyes that shall possess the angelic world, the image-eyes of the soul. It is with the spirit that proceeds from the soul’s fire; that same spirit sees into heaven, beholding God and eternity, and no other. That spirit is also the noble image, made according to God's likeness.

<margin>*On the Incarnation of Christ*, Part 2, Chapter 7, Sections 1, 2, 3.</margin> <note>original: "Menschw." refers to Jakob Böhme’s treatise *Von der Menschwerdung Jesu Christi*.</note>

### 3. Question: How then may a soul hungry for salvation attain such a living communion and acquaintance with God?

**Answer:** The only key to attaining the knowledge and communion of God is the knowledge and denial of oneself. However, the key to the knowledge of oneself is the knowledge of God. As much as we know ourselves, so much may we know God; as much as we deny ourselves, so much will we have communion with God. As much as we have communion with God, so much will we be renewed. The more we open our eyes, the more we see the light of the sun; the more we see the light, the more our eyes will open, and so on.

### 4. Question: Can a person reach a true knowledge of God and themselves through mere contemplation and the reading of Holy Scripture?

**Answer:** Holy Scripture is undoubtedly a glorious means to true knowledge, like the clear air illuminated by the brightness of the sun, and like a pure and stainless mirror of wisdom. But he who wishes to see the light and look at himself in the mirror must first have eyes to see. Because man is by nature blind, and is hidden and sealed from himself with the "seven seals of God’s wrath," he cannot truly recognize the Scripture, nor himself, nor God, unless he is born anew and follows the Lamb <note>A reference to Jesus Christ, often depicted as the Lamb of God in the Book of Revelation.</note> who walks among the seven golden lampstands—the only one who has the power to open the book and its seals. The person who wishes to learn to truly recognize what they are cannot reach this through their own reason, but only through the true "Process of Christ" <note>In this context, the "Process of Christ" refers to a spiritual journey where the believer mimics the life, suffering, death, and resurrection of Jesus within their own soul.</note> in a truly resigned soul, which leaves behind the reason and

<column-break/>

cleverness of "human selfhood" <note>term: <term>Selfhood</term> (German: *Selbstheit*). This refers to the ego-driven state of a person who is focused on their own will rather than God's will.</note> by turning away from the earthly path. Such a soul enters into the highest simplicity of Christ, in true humility under the Cross of Christ, as Christ faithfully taught us when He said: "Unless you turn and become as children, and are born anew of water and the Holy Spirit, you shall not see the kingdom of God." For this, a true resignation <term>Gelassenheit</term> <note>original: *Gelassenheit*. A central concept in German mysticism meaning a state of yieldedness, surrender, and letting go of one's own desires to be filled by God.</note> and an abandonment of human selfhood is required, so that the person turns entirely into their "inward ground" <note>term: <term>Inward Ground</term> (German: *inwendiger Grund*). The deepest, most essential part of the soul where God can be met directly.</note> and brings their selfhood to nothing. Through earnest repentance and with an inward desire, they must turn from this worldly essence toward God, dying to their own capacity and will in the death of Christ and sinking into God's mercy. Then they may be grasped by the Holy Spirit within their own inward ground, so that the Spirit sees, wills, and acts through them as pleases God. This Spirit alone is the searcher of Divine knowledge and the light of the soul, in which the soul beholds and knows God; in no other way can one attain Divine and natural knowledge and contemplation. For the natural "reason-man" understands nothing of the mystery of God's Kingdom, for he is outside of God and not in Him. This is proven by the "reason-scholars" <note>A critical term for theologians who study God only through intellectual logic rather than spiritual experience.</note> who argue about God's nature and will but do not recognize Him, for they do not hear God’s word within them. Everything is dead toward God if it does not have the living voice and the Divine hearing of the "new birth" within the Being of Christ, such that the Spirit of God bears witness to their outward hearing and teaching. In this inward seeing alone is God known and His nature understood; the outward, literal word is merely a form and a prepared instrument for this. But true understanding must flow from the inward ground—from the living Word of God, which must first be opened within the person—into the literal word.

<margin>Epistle 35, Sections 34, 5, 6, 7.</margin>
As long as this internal ground is not unlocked, a person cannot fundamentally understand the Holy Scriptures—not even their simplest points of doctrine—just as both ancient and modern experience testify. The Scribes and Pharisees had Moses and the Prophets; the utterances of God were entrusted to the Jews, but they had lost the key of knowledge—namely, the rebirth <note>original: "Wieder-Geburt"</note> and renewal of the Holy Spirit. They stood in a foreign image <note>meaning they were spiritually alienated from God's true nature</note>, so that they did not recognize the core of glory, the express image of the self-subsistent nature of God. Instead, they rejected and crucified Him as a deceiver. "You search the Scriptures," says our Savior to them, "and you think that you have eternal life in them; and it is they that testify of me; but you will not come to me that you may have life" (John 5). For no one should call himself a master, a discerner, or a knower of the Divine Being based on historical accounts alone, but rather from the Holy Spirit, who appears from a different center than the center of human life—appearing to the right and earnest seeker. Therefore, let us not be proud or secure, nor rely on human skill <note>original: "Kunst"; often used by Böhme to describe academic or artificial learning</note>, and much less on the letter; for His Spirit is hidden from us without God’s Spirit. We have God’s will clearly in Holy Scripture, but without God’s Spirit, we have only a tool and a dead word. It is God’s Spirit that first awakens the living word in us, so that we understand the letter and the written word. This is proven enough by the fact that those who are scholars of the letter <note>original: "Buchstaben-Gelehrte"</note> are not scholars taught by God; otherwise, they would not quarrel over Christ’s honor and teaching. 5. **Question:** Since Holy Scripture is so difficult to understand, has God therefore ordained the teaching and preaching office to announce and interpret God’s counsel to us?

**Answer:** If Holy Scripture were subject to any explanation according to one’s own [human] knowledge, it could be no true or infallible principle <note>original: "Principium"</note> or key; for that which seeks to unlock something sealed must not itself be sealed, but must be clear and manifest. If someone now wishes to be a doctor and master of Holy Scripture, he must himself be taught by God and have as his leader that same Spirit from which the Holy Scripture flowed. All teachers and preachers, in all sects and religious factions, appeal to the Holy Scripture and want to prove their articles of faith against one another; yet from this, nothing but strife and quarreling is born. One can hardly bring two or three of the scholars of human skill together who—even though they have sworn to the very same articles—are at one in their fundamental ground. On the other hand, if a thousand people taught by God, who are born in the spirit of Jesus Christ, were together—where each had a particular knowledge and gift in God—they would still all be united in the root of Christ, and each would desire only the love of God in Christ. Which disciple shall exalt himself over his master? If we are one body in Christ, why must one member quarrel with another over food? When the desiring mouth eats, all the members receive strength; every member has its task to reveal the wonders of God. We do not all carry one word, but one Spirit in Christ; to each is allotted his portion of what he should reveal in God, so that the great mysteries of God may become manifest, and the wonders that have been foreseen from eternity in His wisdom may come to...

In this matter, there are no doctors who have studied enough. No one has their own power to grasp anything in the depths of GOD or to teach others such things; rather, they are all only children and **ABC-students** <note>A term for absolute beginners or elementary pupils; Böhme uses this to emphasize that human intellect is useless without divine revelation.</note>. For the devil also has his **matrix** <note>original: "Matricem," meaning a womb or source of origin.</note>, and within it his children; they also speak from their mother's spirit: that of **false reason**. They are the ones who make conclusions, saying: "This is how we will believe, this is how we will understand the Scripture," and they create heavy dogmas and punishments for anyone who will not cling to their decrees, which they enforce with worldly power. Guard yourselves against them, you children of GOD; they speak from themselves and not from the Spirit of GOD. They do not have the childlike spirit of humility in obedience and love toward the Mother—much less toward her children—they who devour the children's bread and nourish themselves with deceit. Through them, the cup of GOD'S wrath is poured out, and yet they call themselves the little sheep of Christ.

O you wolves, where is your children's clothing? If you have learned the mysteries of GOD so well and "enough," then you are no longer children and students. If you live in the wonders of the Mother, in her humility and purity within GOD'S miraculous work, then we will believe you. Take off your proud coat and take us poor **ABC-students** into your lap with our Mother, and teach us the mother-tongue; then we shall live together as brothers. But what should one say of you? The Spirit of the Mother indicates that you are the proud Whore of Babylon, riding upon the dragon in the Revelation of JESUS Christ. There is your mirror.

**7. Question:** You surely would not reject the external means, such as teaching, preaching, reading, and contemplating GOD’S Word in Holy Scripture?

**Answer:** Daily experience teaches how far external means—without GOD’S Spirit—are helpful toward true knowledge; for despite all external teaching and hearing, one is and remains mute, deaf, and blind to the Kingdom of GOD.

For us humans in this world, it is of the greatest importance that we seek again what was lost. If we wish to seek it, we must not seek it outside of ourselves. We have no need for hypocrites and **ear-ticklers** <note>original: "Ohren-Zucker," literally "ear-sugarers"; those who say only what people want to hear.</note> who comfort us and promise us many "golden mountains" <note>An idiom meaning extravagant, empty promises.</note> just so that we follow them and make them look radiant. And if I sat and heard sermons all my life long, and heard preaching, singing, and ringing about the Kingdom of Heaven and the new **Rebirth** <note>term: "Wiedergeburt" (Regeneration); the spiritual transformation of the soul into a new, Christ-like nature.</note> and left it at that, I would still be the same as before. When one throws a stone into the water and pulls it out again, it is still just as hard a stone as it was before, and it keeps its shape. But when one throws it into the fire, then

9. Question: If one cannot attain the true knowledge of God from Holy Scripture, will it be achieved much less through the contemplation of nature and the creatures of this world?

Answer: As far as nature is concerned—that is, the creation of this visible world—it is certainly a glorious revelation of Divine Wisdom, in which God transfigures His wonders and omnipotence. However, Man, as the Microcosm <note>Original: *die kleine Welt*, the "little world." Mystics believed the human being was a miniature version of the entire universe.</note>, is the only key given the power to radically <note>Meaning "at the root" (Latin: *radicaliter*).</note> unlock the mysteries of God’s creatures and therein to behold, worship, and glorify God’s wisdom and power. But because Man has fallen from the Kingdom of God into the kingdom of darkness, the whole of nature and all creatures are sealed to him with the mighty seals of God’s wrath. Indeed, Man is closed and hidden to himself; until he can unlock himself, he must first begin within himself through the renewal of his mind and the new birth, which is the only key that passes through everything and to which nothing remains hidden, whose spirit searches all things, even the depths of God. For every thing that is to come into being consists of the Father’s nature, as Moses also testifies: that God the Father made all things through the Word "Let there be" <note>Latin: *Verbum Fiat*.</note>. Thus all creatures stand in the Father, for which reason He is called the Father of all beings, and we humans are His children. But with Adam, we have deviated from the power of the seventh spirit <note>In Böhme's system, the "seventh spirit" represents the completed, bodily form of divine manifestation.</note> and entered with our <term>Imagination<note>For Böhme, "Imagination" is the soul's creative focus or "in-forming" power that shapes its reality.</note></term> into the spirit of this world, which clothes us with corruptible flesh and blood and holds us prisoner. Thus we are in the power of the seven stars <note>The seven planets or astral influences.</note> or the seven stern spirits of the Father's nature, which bring their wonders to light within us. But where we depart with our <term>Imagination</term> from the kingdom of this world and from our captivity, and are born anew through Christ, we return again into the Center...

10. **Question:** What then is actually the ground and the cause / that all our diligence, trouble and labor, searching and reading in Holy Scripture and in nature, is not sufficient in and of itself without God’s light / to arrive at a salutary knowledge?

**Answer:** No life can stand in certainty / unless it remains in its **Center** <note>Original: *Centro*. The source or point of origin from which a being emerges.</note> / from which it has sprouted. Because the soul has sprouted from God's Word and Will / but has entered into its own lust and desire for **Self-Willing** <note>The act of the individual will separating itself from the Divine Will; the root of "the Fall" in Böhme’s thought.</note>: therefore, in such searching of the self-will, it cannot reach its first ground / from which it sprouted; it runs therefore now outside its ground in vain uncertainty / until it turns back again to its origin. All beginnings go out from the eternal One / as from the **Trinity** of God / through the out-breathing or speaking of the Unity of God /

<column-break/>

just as a spring flows from its source: through which outflow the Unity introduces itself into a **Self-Contemplation** <note>Original: *Selbst-Beschaulichkeit*. The process by which the undifferentiated Divine becomes aware of itself and takes form.</note> / a state of being found and sensed / toward its own forming and shaping. All visible and invisible beings / both spiritual and physical / have taken their origin in the out-breathing of Divine Power / and are a **Counter-image** <note>Original: *Gegen-Bild*. The created world is seen as a reflection or mirror of God's internal movements.</note> of the distinct will of God / and stand with their ground within it. For the beginning of all beings is nothing else / than an **imagination** <note>In this context, *Imagination* is the creative power that gives form to spirit; the "imaging forth" of the divine will.</note> of the outflowing will of God / which has introduced itself into distinctness / formality and figurativeness; therein lies the entire **Creation** / and every life stands in its own re-breathing / and counter-imaging likewise.

Because human life is an outflow and counter-image of Divine power / understanding and science / it is proper for the same to remain at its origin / or it loses Divine knowledge / power and science / and leads itself with its own **speculation** into its own centers / and into foreign formations / whereby its origin becomes darkened and foreign to it.

<margin>*Explanation of the Testament*, chapter 1, §. 2. 7.</margin>

The state of being focused on the ego rather than the divine source.</note> does / when it receives the **Light of Nature** as its own property / so that it may walk in its own governance through the intellect. Human logical reasoning unilluminated by divine spirit.</note> / stands caught and firmly bound in a heavy prison / namely in God’s wrath / as well as in earthly vanity / it is very dangerous for a man to carry the light of knowledge in selfhood / as his own...

Lucifer entered into the center of the fierce nature, into the **matrix** <term>Matrix: Here used to mean a spiritual womb or the formative source-structure of a specific nature.</term> of fire; and Adam entered into the earthly nature, into the matrix of the outer world, into the lust for both good and evil. This happened to both of them for these reasons: because they had the light of understanding shining within their selfhood, in which they could mirror and behold themselves. Through this, the spirit of selfhood entered into the **imagination** <note>In Böhme’s thought, "Imagination" is not just fantasy, but the soul's active power to "image" or form itself into a specific state through the focus of its will.</note> as a desire for the center, to elevate itself, to become great and powerful, and also to become more clever. Just as Lucifer sought the mother of fire in his center, thinking thereby to rule over God's love and all the angelic host; so too Adam desired to taste the mother—from which good and evil flow—within the essence, and he led his desire into it by his own will, so as to become clever and wise. Both of them, Lucifer and Adam, were caught in their false desire within the mother and broke themselves off from the **surrender** <note>Original: *Gelassenheit*. With the spirit of their will, they were caught by the desire in the mother, which immediately seized the government of nature. Thus, Lucifer remained standing in the fierce torment of fire, and that same fire became manifest in his will-spirit, whereby the creature, in its desire, became an enemy of the love and gentleness of God.

So too, Adam was immediately seized by the earthly mother (which is both good and evil) out of God’s love and wrath, and was created 

<column-break/>

into a being; immediately, earthly properties took over the government within him. From this it came to pass that heat and cold, and wrath and all false opposition and malice against God, became manifest and ruling within him. However, if they had not led the light of **knowledge** into their selfhood, then the mirror of knowledge in the center and the original state of the creature, as well as their own power, would not have become manifest to them, from which the imagination and lust arose. This same thing still brings danger today to the enlightened children of God: when the sun of the sweet sight of God's holiness shines upon many, from which life enters into triumph, Reason mirrors itself therein, and the will of selfhood enters into its own searching. It wants to test the **center** from which the light shines, and force itself into it through selfhood. From this, miserable pride and self-conceit arise, so that one's own Reason (which is after all only a looking-glass of the Eternal) thinks it is something more. It thinks that whatever it does, it is God's will doing it within her, that she is a prophetess; and yet she is only within herself, walking in her own desire. In this desire, the center of nature soon swings upward and enters into its own desire of falsehood against God, and then the will enters into a **conceit** <note>Original: *Dünckel*. A state of spiritual self-delusion or vanity where one mistakes their own thoughts for divine revelation.</note>. Then the **flattery-devil** <note>Original: *Schmeichel-Teufel*. A demonic influence that appeals to human vanity and spiritual pride.</note> approaches him, sifts the center of nature, and leads his false desire into it, so that the person becomes as if drunk in his selfhood. He persuades himself that he is being driven by God in this way; thereby the good original state, in which the light of God was shining in nature, is corrupted, and that same light of God departs from him. Then the external light of the outer nature remains shining in the creature; because his own selfhood forces itself into it, he thinks it is still the first light from God. He then searches through the "Mother"—the origin of life—which is the **Center** <term>Center: In Böhme's system, the "Center of Nature" (Centrum Naturae) refers to the internal spiritual engine or source of a being's life and drive.</term>, but it has become a dry and powerless place. The **Wrath of God**, as the Center of Nature, is entirely powerless, meager, and dry in its own self-property, and cannot come to rule according to the nature and property of its fierceness. Satan searches this place to see if he might find any gate open where he could enter with his desire and "sift" the soul so that it might exalt itself. And if the **Will-Spirit** of the creature now swings itself with the Light of Reason into the Center (as into selfhood) and enters into its own delusion, it departs from God's light once again. Now the devil finds an open gate to it, and a garnished house—the Light of Reason—for his dwelling. Thus, he takes the **seven forms** <note>Böhme taught that there are "Seven Qualities" or "Seven Forms" of nature that make up all reality; here, they are turned toward evil.</note> of life’s property to himself in selfhood, like hypocrites who have departed from God into selfhood. There he enters and sets his desire into the lust of selfhood, and 

<column-break/>

false imagination: where the Will-Spirit beholds itself in the forms of life’s properties, within the outer light. There it sinks into itself as if it were drunk; then the **Stars** <term>The Stars (Gestirne): Not just physical planets, but the "astral" or cosmic influences that Böhme believed shaped human personality and intellectual impulses.</term> seize it and lead their powerful **Constellation** into it, to seek the wonders of God there and to reveal themselves therein. For every creature longs for God. And although the Stars cannot grasp the Spirit of God, they much prefer a house of light in which they may delight themselves, rather than a locked house where they have no stability. Thus, this person goes about as if he had become drunk on the Stars; he grasps great and wondrous things and has a constant guide in the Stars. So the devil also notices exactly where a gate stands open for him, where he may ignite the Center of life, so that the Will-Spirit—in its own pride, in its conceit (or indeed in greed)—ascends on high. From this arises "own honor," so that the Will of Reason desires to be honored. For it thinks it possesses the **roast of salvation** <note>Original: *Braden des Heils*. A metaphorical way of saying the person thinks they have secured the "prize" or "substance" of spiritual success.</note> because it possesses the Light of Reason, and can judge the locked house, which God may well exclude. It thinks honor is now its due because it has reached this rational understanding, and it never realizes how the devil delights himself with his desire in the seven life-forms of the Center of Nature, and what ghastly errors he prepares. Out of this [false] understanding, the **false Babel** <note>Babel: For Böhme, "Babel" represents the confused state of organized, institutional religion that relies on human logic and dogma rather than the living Spirit of God.</note> was born in the Christian Church on earth, where men teach and govern with rational conclusions, and have placed upon it the "child of drunkenness" with selfhood and its own lust, well-adorned like a beautiful virgin. But the devil has moved into the seven life-forms of the Center as his lodging—that is, into the selfhood of one's own Reason—and constantly leads his will and desire into this garnished "virgin" adopted from the Stars. He is her **Beast**, upon which she [rides] in her own life-form...

## Chapter II.
### Of the true means of the living and salvific knowledge of GOD; and first, of Repentance.

->**1. Question.**<-

I now acknowledge before GOD and man that with all my wisdom and learning, which I acquired with so much effort and great expense in my own will, I find myself shamefully deceived. I have transformed myself into a bloated monster with vain knowledge, both of theological and philosophical things, defiled my soul with many sins, and been fooled by falsely-famed art, as well as all kinds of sinful intentions. How then may I now free myself from all the evil and lying powers of darkness, and arrive at the true knowledge of the living truth?

->**Answer.**<-

Because our whole heart, along with all powers—both of the understanding and the will—has broken away from GOD and His blessed fellowship, and is corrupted into error through self-opinion and self-will, no person can arrive at a true knowledge of GOD and themselves unless they turn back from their error and are born anew. Christus says: *Whoever does not leave houses, fields, money, goods, wife, children, brothers and sisters, and denies themselves, and follows me, is not my disciple or servant.* Also: *You must turn back and become as children, or be born anew of water and Spirit, otherwise you shall not see the kingdom of GOD.* This is not meant to suggest that one should run from wife and child, or from their calling and station, into a desolate wilderness and leave everything; rather, one must leave the Anti-Christ, such as **Mine-ness**, **Thine-ness**, and **I-ness** <term>I-ness (German: *Ichheit*): The state of being centered on the self or ego, which mystical writers saw as the root of all sin.</term>. Whoever wishes to arrive at Divine contemplation and sensitivity within themselves must kill the Anti-Christ in their soul and—

<column-break/>

—depart from all selfhood of the will, yes, from every creature <note>In this context, "creature" refers to anything created or worldly, as opposed to the Creator.</note>, and in the selfhood of the mind become the poorest creature, so that they no longer have anything as their own property, whatever station they may be in. And even if they were a king, yet their mind should leave all selfhood, and in their station—even in honors and temporal goods—regard themselves as nothing more than GOD’S servant, so that they should therein serve GOD and their brothers; and that all that they have, they do not have and possess by natural right as if it were their own, but that it belongs to their brothers and fellow members, and that GOD has appointed them as a steward and administrator <term>Steward (German: *Amtmann*): An official who manages an estate on behalf of a lord; here, a metaphor for how humans should manage worldly wealth for God.</term> over it, and think that they serve their Master therein, who would demand an account from them. Also, they must completely surrender their own will—which drives them to such possession of selfhood—to the suffering and dying in the death of Jesus Christ, and humbly ask GOD in right earnest **repentance** <term>Repentance (German: *Busse*): More than just saying sorry, this implies a total "turning around" or transformation of the mind.</term> and conversion that He would kill this evil will toward selfhood and temporal pleasure in the death of Jesus Christ, and lead the soul’s will into the true childhood of GOD; so that they no longer will or desire for themselves, but that GOD’S will becomes their willing and desiring in them, so that they die in their **I-ness** according to the soul’s will, and GOD in Christ becomes their life. They must immerse their will into the highest humility, into GOD’S mercy, and [offer] Him such a will in GOD’S promise of grace...

## Chapter II.
### On the True Means of the Living and Wholesome Knowledge of GOD; and first, on Repentance.

**1. Question.**

I now recognize before God and men that with all my wisdom and learning—which I acquired with so much effort and great expense through my own will—I find myself shamefully deceived. I have transformed myself into a bloated monster <note>original: "Monstro"; Latin for a distorted or unnatural thing.</note> through vain knowledge of both theological and philosophical matters; I have stained my soul with many sins and have been deluded by "falsely-famed art" <note>A reference to 1 Timothy 6:20, warning against "science falsely so called."</note> and all sorts of sinful intentions. How then may I now free myself from all the evil and lying powers of darkness and arrive at the true knowledge of the living truth?

**Answer.**

Because our entire heart, along with all its powers of both understanding and will, has broken away from God and His blessed communion, and has been corrupted into error through stubbornness and self-will, no man can arrive at a true knowledge of GOD and of himself unless he turns back from his error and is born anew. Christ says: *Whoever does not leave houses, fields, money, goods, wife, children, brothers, and sisters, and denies himself and follows me, he is not my disciple or servant.* Also: *You must turn back and become as children, or be born anew of water and spirit, otherwise you shall not see the kingdom of GOD.* This does not imply that one should run away from wife and child, or from one's calling and station, into a desolate wilderness and leave everything behind; rather, it refers to the "Anti-Christ" within—such as "Miness," "Thiness," and "I-ness" <note>original: "Meinheit / Deinheit / Ichheit"; these terms refer to the ego's possessiveness and self-centeredness.</note>. Whoever wishes to attain divine contemplation and sensitivity within himself must kill the "Anti-Christ" in his soul and

<column-break/>

depart from all selfhood of the will—indeed, from every created thing—and in the particularity of his spirit become the poorest creature, so that he no longer holds anything as his own property, no matter what station of life he is in. And even if he were a king, his mind should nevertheless leave all "selfhood" <note>original: "Eigenheit"; the state of being attached to things as "mine."</note> and, in his station, even amid honors and temporal goods, regard himself as nothing more than God’s servant, serving GOD and his brothers therein, for which God would demand an account from him. Furthermore, he must surrender his own will—which drives him toward such possession of selfhood—entirely to the suffering and dying in the death of JESUS Christ. He must humbly pray to GOD in true, earnest repentance and conversion, asking that He might kill this evil will toward selfhood and temporal pleasure through the death of JESUS Christ, and lead the soul’s will into the true status of a child of GOD. Thus, he should no longer want or desire for himself, but let GOD’S will become his wanting and desiring within him, so that he becomes dead in his "I-ness" according to the soul’s will, and GOD in Christ becomes his life. He must submerge <note>original: "vertauffen"; literally "baptize" or "drown."</note> his will into the highest humility, into GOD’S mercy, and [offer] Him such a will in GOD’S promise of grace...

Part I / Chapter 2.

...to draw from the **promise**, desiring in this hour to depart from all the selfhood <note>original: "Eigenheit"; referring to the selfish ego or the state of being attached to one's own will rather than God's.</note> of this world’s pleasure, and never to enter into it again—even if he should be considered the world’s fool for it—and to fully immerse himself in the deepest humility and unworthiness before GOD through **repentance** <term>Pœnitentz: Derived from the Latin *poenitentia*, this refers to the internal process of atonement and turning one's heart back to God.</term>. He must grasp the promise of grace within his soul and stand firm within it like a soldier before his enemy when life and limb are at stake. When this happens, his own will—acting as the **Antichrist** <note>In this context, the "Antichrist" is not just a historical figure, but the selfish "ego-will" that opposes the spirit of Christ within the human soul.</note>—is seized and put to death in the death of Christ. Immediately, his soul becomes like a new, simple child that has lost its natural cleverness of selfhood, and it begins to plead before GOD like a young child before its mother, placing its trust in whatever the mother chooses to give. And this is what Christ meant when he said: *You must turn back and become as children, and leave everything and follow me.* For Adam stepped away from God's will into a will of his own, and through his own desire, he introduced the serpent’s craving and the devil’s will into himself. Thus, he led himself and his life-companions—who stood in equal **harmony** <term>Concordantz: From the Latin *concordantia*, meaning a state of agreement or balanced harmony between different forces or elements.</term> within a single will, which was GOD’s—into a state of division. There, the properties of nature moved out of that harmony, each property into its own "selfhood" or selfish desire. From this, the lust for both Evil and Good arose within him; heat and cold immediately pressed upon him, and he died to the holy life that existed in that harmony—where he had lived in a single Element, and the four elements were held in equal balance within him. Regarding this, God said to him: *Do not eat of the tree of Good and Evil, or you shall die.* He meant the death of the Kingdom of Heaven, that beautiful angelic image, which immediately died into the false, introduced desire of the serpent. Now, it must and shall be born anew in the Spirit of Christ; thus, this false serpent-will must first die in the death of Christ through a true turning-about—

<column-break/>

—and out of this dying, Christ rises again within us in His Spirit, in that heavenly image that had died in Adam; thus the **inner man** is born anew in the Spirit of Christ.

This new spirit attains **Divine Contemplation** <note>original: "Göttlicher Beschaulichkeit"; a state of mystical vision or intuitive looking into the nature of God.</note> within itself and hears God’s Word; it possesses Divine understanding and sweetness, and may behold the **Great Mystery** <term>Mysterium Magnum: A central term in Böhme’s philosophy, referring to the "Great Mystery" or the chaotic "ground" from which all creation and spiritual reality manifest.</term> of divine and natural secrets within itself. And though the earthly flesh still clings to it in its inclinations, it does the spirit no harm. In this new birth, the spirit is like fine gold within a coarse stone; the coarseness of the stone cannot break the gold. For the spirit's true will has died to earthly cravings and desires to put the lust of the flesh to death every hour—and indeed does so without ceasing. For here, the **Seed of the Woman** <note>A biblical reference to Genesis 3:15; here representing the new man born in Christ.</note> treads upon the head of the serpent’s will in the flesh, which is the Antichrist.

<margin>
Epistle 31. §. 3. 12.
</margin>

**2. Question.** Is this not a difficult lesson for a mind that has broken itself off from the true life (which is from GOD) into its own selfhood, and thinks it may seek God’s face through **meditating, speculating, and discoursing** <note>These Latin-derived terms—*meditiren, speculiren, discurriren*—refer here to purely intellectual or academic study without the necessary spiritual "death of the self."</note>, rather than through the mortification of itself?

**Answer.** It is a difficult lesson, yet it is the *only* true lesson, without which all other knowledge and science is a pure **Babel** <note>Referring to the Tower of Babel; here meaning a confused, prideful, and false structure of human ideas.</note> and a fable. Therefore, dear soul, if you desire this way and wish to attain it with the noble Virgin in the **Pearl-tree** <note>A symbolic image used by Böhme to represent the growth of divine wisdom and the soul's blossoming in God's grace.</note>, you must use great earnestness. It must not be mere mouth-hypocrisy where the heart is far away; no, you will achieve nothing that way. You must gather your mind, along with all your senses and reason, entirely into one single will: that you wish to be converted and leave your abominations behind. You must set your mind upon GOD and His mercy with a certain confidence that you will attain it.

# On True Repentance.

And if the devil speaks within your sins, saying: "It cannot happen now; you are too great a sinner," do not let this terrify you. He is a liar and seeks to make your mind despondent. He pretends as if he were not there, yet he is present, resisting you like a vicious dog. You may know for certain that everything that enters your mind as doubt is nothing but his interference. For there are no more than two kingdoms that call out to you: one is the Kingdom of **GOD**, wherein **Christ** dwells and desires you; the other is the Kingdom of Hell, wherein the devil dwells, who also desires you. 

Now, a struggle for the poor soul takes place here, for she stands in the middle. **Christ** offers her the new garment, and the devil offers her the sin-garment. And as surely as you have a thought or an inclination toward **GOD**, desiring to enter into true repentance, just as surely is that thought not your own, but **GOD’s** love is luring you. The noble **Virgin** <note>original: "Jungfrau"; referring to Sophia or Divine Wisdom, a central figure in Böhme's mysticism who represents the mirror of God’s glory and the soul's true partner.</note> of **GOD** calls to you through it, telling you that you should simply come and not give up. 

And as surely as your great sins come to mind on this path and hold you back, so that at times your heart finds no comfort, just as surely is this the devil’s obstruction. He throws into your thoughts the idea that **GOD** will not hear you, that you are still in too many sins; he refuses to let comfort into the soul and covers it with the sinful kingdom of this world. But let nothing discourage you; he is your enemy. It is written: *Though your sins be red as blood, if you turn back, they shall be made white as snow, like wool.* Also: *As I live, I have no pleasure in the death of the poor sinner, but rather that he turn back and live, says the LORD God of Hosts* <term>Zebaoth: A Hebrew title for God, "Sabaoth," meaning "Lord of Hosts" or "Lord of Armies."</term>. You must remain steadfast with this resolved mind. Even if you receive no strength in your heart, and even if the devil strikes your tongue down so that you cannot pray to **GOD**, you must still sigh and yearn toward Him, and remain in this mindset, persisting like the **Canaanite woman** <note>A reference to the biblical story in Matthew 15, where a woman persistently begs Jesus for help even when he seems to ignore or rebuff her, illustrating the power of persistent faith.</note>—

<column-break/>

always persisting; the more you press on, the weaker the devil becomes. You must take the suffering, death, and **satisfaction** of **JESUS Christ** for yourself and wrap your soul in His promise, where **Christ** says: *My Father will give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him for it.* Also: *Ask, and you shall receive; seek, and you shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.* And the more powerfully you break out from the devil and your sins, the more powerfully the Kingdom of **GOD** breaks into you. 

You must simply not depart from this will until you obtain the **Jewel** <note>original: "Kleinod"; a term used to describe the precious treasure of spiritual rebirth or the presence of God within the soul.</note>, even if it lasts from day until night, and for many days thereafter. If your earnestness is great, then the Jewel you obtain in your victory will also be great. For what it is, no one knows except he who experiences it himself. It is a very dear guest when he moves into the soul; there is a most wonderful triumph, where the **Bridegroom** embraces his dear bride, and the song of praise of Paradise begins. 

Ah, the earthly body must tremble at this! Even if it does not know what is happening, all the limbs rejoice. Ah, what a beautiful knowledge the **Virgin of God’s Wisdom** brings with her! She makes a person learned, and even if he were otherwise mute, the soul is nonetheless crowned in **GOD’s** wonder-work. She must speak of His wonders; there is nothing but pure desire within her. The devil must retreat and becomes entirely faint and weary.

# Part I / Chapter 2.

To seek, to find, and to establish schools: it is all a trifle without **Divine Understanding**. Whatever **Reason** <note>original: "Vernunfft"; Böhme uses this to describe the limited, earthly intellect that cannot grasp spiritual truths on its own.</note> seeks in the arts of this world is nothing; she finds no more than this world—and even then, not even half of it. She wanders forever in her searching, and finally finds only pride and hypocrisy while she discovers worldly wisdom. Seek only the **Word** and **Heart of GOD**, which became man in the manger with the ox in the stable, in the dark night. If you find that, you find **Christ** as the **Word** in the **Father**, together with the **Father**, **Son**, and **Holy Spirit**, as well as eternal nature, the angelic world, and paradise. You will find your blind **Reason**, which has led you staggering for so long like a drunkard. You must not break your mind with lofty thoughts; you will not find the Ground <note>The "Ground" or "Ungrund" is a central concept in Böhme’s thought, referring to the absolute, fathomless depth of the Divine.</note> through high senses and poeticizing. Instead, simply yield your mind and senses, with all your **Reason**, into the love and mercy of **GOD**, so that you may be born from the **Word** and **Heart of GOD** in the **Center** <note>original: "Centro"; the inner spiritual core where the divine light breaks through.</note> of your life, that His light may shine into the light of your life, and that you may be one with Him. For **Jesus Christ**, the **Son of GOD**, the eternal **Word** in the **Father**—who is the radiance and the power of the light-filled eternity—must be born as a man within you if you wish to truly know **GOD**. Otherwise, you remain in the dark stable, merely searching and fumbling about. You look for **Christ** forever at the right hand of **GOD**, thinking He is far away from you; you try to force your mind beyond the stars to seek **GOD** there, just as the **Sophists** <note>A term Böhme uses for academic theologians who rely on book-learning rather than spiritual experience.</note> teach, who paint **GOD** as being far away in a distant heaven.

But just as the devil wishes to fly over the **Heart of GOD** in his fiery source-torment <note>original: "Quall"; a characteristic Böhme pun merging *Quelle* (source/fountain) and *Qual* (torment/agony) to describe the raw energy of nature.</note>, yet remains only in the four forms of eternal nature in the darkness: so it goes with blind **Reason**, which sits in darkness and seeks **GOD** in the darkness. If you wish to find Him, seek Him in His source-quality; it is everywhere, everything is full of **GOD**, and it shines in the darkness. In your dark heart is

<column-break/>

**GOD**, but in another **Principle** <note>original: "Princ."; Böhme's term for a fundamental state of existence or "world" (e.g., the world of darkness, light, or the physical world).</note>. Knock, and it shall be opened unto you. The **Holy Spirit of GOD** is the key in the **Center**. Depart from the desires of the flesh into a truly earnest **Repentance**, and place your will alone—with all **Reason** and senses—into the mercy of **GOD**. Then the **Word of GOD**, as His dear **Heart**, will take on a form within you. Then you will stand before the manger where **Jesus** was born; so bow down to the little Child and offer Him your heart, and **Christ** will be born in you. Only then must you go into the **Jordan**, and the **Holy Spirit** will baptize you; there heaven stands open to you, and the **Holy Spirit** hovers over you. But you must also go into the **Wilderness** and be tempted by the **devil**. (Understand this rightly: the **devil** will test himself against you, leading you deep into the wildernesses of the world, stepping into your fleshly heart before your soul to bolt it shut. It takes great **Earnestness** to shatter the **devil’s center**.) You will often not see **Christ**; the **devil** will deny Him to you, claiming He has not become man in you. For you stand there as a light in the **Center**, surrounded by darknesses, and you are a plant growing in the **Life of GOD** out of the dark, harsh nature. Therefore, fight for yourself; then look and stand firm, as **Christ** did. Do not act like **Adam**, who abandoned the longing of the Spirit for this world and led us into fleshly darkness. You must be persecuted, mocked, and scorned with **Christ** if you wish to soar in the wonders of **GOD**. And if you remain in Him, He remains in you; then you may seek what you will, and you shall find whatever your desire is. Otherwise, you seek in the Godhead in vain; and even if you bring your search to the highest point, you will find only this world. Let this be said to you as a warning.

->*The Threefold Life*, chapter 3, paragraphs 29–36.<-

**Answer.** My dear mind <note>original: "Gemüthe"; refers to the seat of one's emotions, thoughts, and will—the "inner disposition."</note>/ you think/ you are quite healthy/ but you are so very battered/ that you no longer feel your sickness/ yet you are subject to death nearly at hand/ how then can you judge yourself healthy?

Alas! my dear soul/ do not boast of your health/ you lie captured in heavy bonds/ in a dark dungeon/ you swim in deep water/ which reaches up to your mouth/ and you must always expect death; Moreover, the driver <note>The "driver" (Treiber) is a common Böhme image for the Devil or the driving force of the fallen world.</note> is behind you with a large troop of your worst enemies/ as he pulls you ever downward on his chains/ into the cruel depth/ into the abyss of hell/ and his troop keeps pushing after/ and they run around you on all sides/ barking and hunting/ as if they have the hind <note>original: "Hinde"; a female deer. Böhme uses this image to represent the soul being hunted by demonic forces.</note> which they chase after. So speaks **Reason**: Why do they do this? O my dear soul/ they have a great cause for it/ look/ you were their hind/ and you broke away from their garden: furthermore, you have become so strong/ that you have broken their garden fence/ and taken over their dwelling: moreover, you have made their food bitter/ so that they cannot eat it. You have broken their throne with your horns: furthermore, you have led a foreign army into their garden/ and used a foreign power/ to drive them out of their garden. And although they have you on their leash/ you set yourself against them/ as if you would break their kingdom. You tear their ropes into pieces/ and break their bonds/ and are a constant attacker of their kingdom; You are their worst enemy/ and they yours/ and even if you still went out of their garden/ they would yet be satisfied; But while you are inside/ the war lasts/ and has no end/ until the Old One <note>Likely referring to Death or God as the final judge who ends the earthly struggle.</note> comes/ who will separate you. If you are indeed in the rose garden/ as you think/ see to it/ that you are not on the devil's pasture/ and are his favorite hind/ which he fattens for a slaughter-feast/ for his food. Truly/ I tell you/ and it is no joke/ when I was at Jericho <note>Jericho is used here as a symbol for the fallen, material world, following the parable of the Good Samaritan.</note>/ there my dear companion <note>Böhme often refers to "Divine Wisdom" or the Holy Spirit as his "companion" in visions.</note> opened my eyes/ so that I saw/ and look/ a great race and multitude of people were among one another/ and one part was like beasts/ and one part as humans/ and there was a conflict among them/ and the abyss of hell was under them/ and the beasts did not see that/ but the humans were afraid/ and wanted to flee/ yet the devil would not allow them that/ for his garden had no doors/ and they broke his garden: Thus he had to guard the beasts/ so they would not also escape him. But the beasts/ who were also humans/ ate of his food/ and drank of his drink/ and he did nothing to them/ for he fattened them for his slaughter-feast: And there was a constant enmity between the true humans and the beast-humans <note>original: "Thier-Menschen"; those who live according to their animalistic desires rather than their divine spark.</note>. Or do you think/ it is not true/ what my dear companion showed me/ when he opened my eyes/ so that I saw? Look/ by Jerusalem we understand Paradise/ and by the road to Jericho/ the departure from Paradise into this world/ where this world then has us captured in its garden—

Also, the Devil is within it, who has bound us with **God’s Chain of Wrath** and leads the poor soul captive in the dark garden of flesh and blood, in his grim garden of wrath. Oh, how often he robs the poor soul of its beautiful garment of the **Knowledge of God**; how he tears the Word of God from its ears and heart, as Christ clearly says. If the soul then does not want what he wants, and insists on tearing itself out of his garden, he first throws his filth and uncleanness upon it; then he rouses all his hunting dogs, who must bark at it and cast nothing but mockery upon it. For he fattens them in **God’s wrath**, and they are merely his hunting dogs with which he hunts the **hind** (the poor soul which wants to escape him and storm his hellish kingdom). The [Devil] would be satisfied if only a few souls escaped him, though it would weaken rather than increase his kingdom; but because his kingdom is being broken thereby, he is not satisfied. For just as he hunts in his kingdom and catches the poor souls however he can, and pursues the poor souls through his servants with all vices, so he constantly sets a **mirror** before the soul, so that it should look at itself in its vices; he even tickles it with great promises of great honor, power, and authority. He sets the poor, despised **little flock** <note>original: "Häufflein"; refers to the small community of true believers who are often marginalized.</note> before it and says to the soul: "Why do you alone want to be the world's fool? Come along; I will give you the kingdom of this world to possess," just as he did to Christ.

Likewise, in the same case, when the soul has put on the **Kingdom of Heaven**, so that it stands in this dark valley in flesh and blood and sees the Devil's murders upon its brothers and sisters, it is also immediately armed by **God** to fight against the Devil and to reveal his **den of robbers**. For love for its neighbor also drives it to want to help increase its Kingdom of Heaven. Therefore it teaches and rebukes, and warns against sin, and teaches the way to the Kingdom of Heaven, which the outer, animalistic body indeed does not understand. It goes along like a coarse **donkey** and thinks with its astral and elementary mind: "Oh, what evil am I doing to myself, that I make myself the world's fool? What do I have from it but mockery? I am not even safe in my life because of it, and I deprive myself and my family of their daily bread and..."

Just as a mustard seed is sown / which is small and little / and afterwards a tree grows from it; so the Pearl grows in the soul / in the Virgin’s <note>In Böhme’s theology, the "Virgin" refers to Sophia, the personification of Divine Wisdom, rather than a physical person.</note> womb.

->To suffer need is a bitter guest.<-

Do not let the Devil sprinkle sugar over you / for though the kingdom of this world is made sugar-sweet for you / there is nothing but gall within it. Just think / that your poor soul is not at home in this world / nor even in your own flesh and blood; it must wander into another land. Therefore, do not let the Devil cover the soul with the foulness of the flesh. For it requires a very great earnestness to drive away the Devil / even though this does not lie within our own powers / if that precious Knight, JESUS Christ, did not stand by us.

Therefore, one should not be so bold as to mock the children of **GOD** / who stand in the struggle against the Devil; think / you must also face it / if not during your good, healthy days / then at your death. When the poor soul must depart from the body / it must enter the struggle; there is no other way / for it must leave the body out of the spirit of this world. Then, two gates stand open / namely the Kingdom of Heaven and the Kingdom of Hell / into one of them it must go; there is no other place or site outside of this world. If it is now so hard-captured in sins / and has always put off repentance until tomorrow / and is thus clothed in **GOD's** wrath / and has piled up nothing but mockery of God’s children / so that it is stuck in God's wrath up to its palate / and hangs only by a thread.

Oh, alas! how heavy that is! Think then / whether the soul must not bathe for a while in the mockery / which it inflicted upon the children of **GOD**? Will it then immediately reach the noble Virgin in

<column-break/>

the love and mercy of **GOD**? Where then remains the Pearl-tree / which is sown as a tiny mustard seed / and grows in delight as a laurel tree? Will its sap turn to greening / while the soul stands in the bath of wrath? Oh, it will not truly turn green in eternity! Therefore Christ said: They shall surpass one another in glory <note>original: "Klarheit," referring to the radiant brilliance of the resurrected body.</note> in the resurrection / like the sun, moon, and stars. What help to you then is the money and goods you had here / your honor and power? When all this leaves you / and you must depart from it? Where then is your mockery and contempt for the children of **GOD** / as well as your greed and envy / when you yourself must bathe in them with great harm and great need? Then you will have great shame before **GOD’s** angels / and all the devils will mock you / saying that you were an instrument <note>original: "wachse," likely meaning a growth or a tool/wax of God.</note> of **GOD** / and yet had no time for it / and are now such a meager little branch. Or how do you think / since your little branch is entirely withered / you must bathe eternally in **GOD’s** wrath? Then your human form will be taken from you / and you will be shaped like the most poisonous animals, worms, and snakes / all according to your will and deeds here. Then your deeds will stand eternally before your eyes as a figure in the **Tincture** <term>Tinctur: In Böhme's mystical alchemy, the spiritual essence or "coloring" that defines the true nature of a being.</term> / and they will gnaw at you / so that you think: Had you not done this or that / you could have come to **GOD’s** grace. Your mocking stands before your eyes / you are ashamed / so that you would not let even one good thought into your soul / for the Good is before you like an angel / and because of your great shame you dare not touch it with your mind / much less look upon it; instead, you must eternally swallow your own mockery along with all the blasphemies and sins / and you must despair eternally. Even if you think to escape through abstinence <note>original: "Abstinentz," here likely referring to a late or forced attempt at self-denial or fleeing the consequences.</note> / the light nevertheless strikes you down in great shame / and you fall only into your own consuming abyss.
