# Of True Repentance.

You reach out over the thrones of **GOD** yourself / and you are like one who stands upon a cliff / and desires to leap into an immeasurable chasm / and the deeper he looks into it / the deeper he falls into it. Thus your own sins / mockery, and vices in contempt of **GOD** / are your hellish fire / which gnaws at you eternally / as we say in the Word of Life.

Therefore, O dear soul / turn back / do not let the Devil catch you / pay no mind to the world’s mockery / all your mourning must be turned into great joy; Even if you do not have great honor / power, and wealth in this world / that helps you not at all / you do not know / if tomorrow is the day / when it will be your turn. Yet a morsel of bread tastes better to the needy man / than the best feast to the powerful; What advantage does the powerful have / other than that he sees much / and must torment himself with many things / and must in the end give an account of all his doing and housekeeping / of what kind of planter he has been in this world. He must give an account of all his servants / if he has led them with evil examples / and has offended them / so that they stepped onto the godless path; Then their poor souls will cry "Ah" and "Woe" eternally over their superiors: There everything stands in the figure in the tincture <note>In Böhme's alchemy-influenced theology, the "tincture" refers to the hidden spiritual essence or "color" that gives life and character to a being.</note>. Why then do you strive so hard for worldly honors / which perish? Strive rather for the pearl-tree <note>The "pearl-tree" represents the growth of Divine Wisdom and the spirit of Christ within the believer.</note> / which you take with you / and rejoice in its growth eternally.

<margin>The Three Principles of the Divine Essence, Chapter 24, paragraphs 6 & 30.</margin>

The more I want to fight against it / the worse it becomes / until the Devil finally presents a whole register of my sins to me / so that I become a horror and a loathing to myself / and would rather give up the hard struggle?

The origin <note>original: "Uhrstand." Böhme uses this to describe the primal foundation or "clock-state" from which all existence emerges.</note> from God the Father moves toward nature, and travels through nature to His heart, which is the end of nature; it dwells in the eternal, still freedom outside of nature, and within nature, as its own principle <note>original: "Principium." In Böhme’s theology, a "Principle" is one of the three fundamental ways God manifests: as dark fire/power, as light/love, or as the physical world.</note> within itself. Thus, the origin of nature has the other principle, from which beings now come that may be changed—but the principle of the heart of God cannot be changed. Therefore I say again, and it is the precious truth: everything that is carved and taught regarding the way to God, if it does not lead toward the gentleness of love and forward into the disposition of the will toward the heart of God, then it is all merely carving-work <note>original: "Schnitz-Werck." This refers to artificial human religious systems or intellectual constructs that lack the living spirit.</note> within the wonders of God. This is so that the great wonders may be brought to light which stood within the hidden seals; those carvers are merely workers in the wonders of God, laboring on the great building for God's glory, which will appear in those wonders when this time is changed, when all things return to the ether <note>original: "Æther." The divine, spiritual substance that remains when the material world passes away.</note>. I do not judge or condemn the eager seeker who seeks in blindness and does not know what he does, for he labors on the building of the great wonders of God; he will find his reward at the end, since he stands with the will to penetrate into God, even if he remains within the building.

So, when the building appears before God at the end of time, its master-builder will also appear before God. Or let us say this alone: does not the Scripture say in the Revelation of Jesus Christ that our works shall follow us, and that each shall reap what he has sown? Therefore, cease from reviling and slandering, and from your own delusions and striving regarding the ways to God; give yourselves up from the devil’s greed and pride into the ways of love, which stand in humility toward the heart of God: in Christ Jesus, who has opened again the hidden seals with which we were sealed into eternal death in Adam; thus you will be, through Christ, in

If you want to know how it is, see, I tell you in a parable: When you have pushed into wealth and power according to your heart’s desire, it is for you just as if you stood in deep water, where the water reaches up to your mouth, and there is no ground under your feet. Instead, you must swim with your hands and protect yourself; at one moment you are deep in the water, at another in the shallows, and yet you are always in great terror, waiting for the moment you might go under, where the water would sometimes enter your mouth, and you would always be expecting death.

In such a state, and no other, do you sit in your pleasures of the flesh; if you do not want to fight, you will not conquer, but you will be murdered in your soft bed. For man always has a powerful army before him that constantly fights against him; if he will not defend himself, he will be captured and slain. But how can one who swims in deep water defend himself well? He has enough to do just protecting himself from the water, and yet he is still stormed by the devils.

Oh, danger upon danger! Just as our King Christ says: *It is hard for a rich man to enter the Kingdom of Heaven; it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the Kingdom of Heaven,* Matthew 19:25, Mark 18:25 <note>The original text cites Mark 18, though the Gospel of Mark only contains 16 chapters; this likely refers to Mark 10:25.</note>. Instead, he must fight and struggle against himself, also against the devil and against all lusts of the flesh. Dear children, when we turn away from our reason <term>Reason (Vernunfft): Böhme uses this term to describe human logic and intellect when it operates independently of God's spirit.</term> and surrender ourselves to the will of God, so that He may create and do with us what He wills: when we place our trust in Him, then we enter into our true Father and are His children. Look at the birds under the heavens; they neither sow nor spin, nor do they gather into barns, yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not much better than they? O you of little faith!*

The soul knows that this garment of earthly flesh and blood is a foreign garment, in which she is heartily ashamed before God's face. Therefore, she is also doubtful of God's grace when she prays. She always thinks her sins are too many, that she cannot reach God's measure. The devil also inflicts such torment upon her; he always opens his smoke-vent <note>original: "Rauch-Loch." The devil always makes a stern judge out of God. Thus the poor soul holds back, enters into the spirit of this world, and seeks nourishment. She thinks God lets things go as they will; yes, quite well for those who build and trust in themselves! For the soul believes that when she is stuck in reason outside of God, she must accomplish things through her own worries; that there is no other way, that it must happen so, and that the hands must do it alone—or else by cunning, from which a great deal of evil arises.

The outer life consists of three parts: one is the <term>Governance of the Stars<note>original: *Sternen-Regiment*; the astrological and celestial influences on the physical world.</note></term>; the second is the element in four parts—namely the four forms of fire, air, water, and earth; the third is God’s governance, for the Spirit of God hovers upon the water, upon the <term>Capsule<note>original: *Capsula*; a protective shell or container.</note></term>, upon the Matrix.

### Part I / Chapter 2

...of his wondrous deeds. Each person has a calling in which he spends his time; before Him, they are all equal. However, the **Spirit of this World** has its highness, which it distributes by its power, just as the **Spirit of God** does in heaven; there too are great distinctions, all according to how the spirit or soul is clothed with Divine Power. Thus is His highness in heaven, as well as His beauty and clarity, but everything exists in one love. 

Each angel and soul finds joy in the strength and beauty of the other. Just as the flowers of the earth do not begrudge one another, even if one is more beautiful and powerful than the other, but stand friendly among each other, and each enjoys the strength of the other. And as a physician mixes various herbs together, in which each power yields its own virtue, and they all serve the sick: So too do we all please God, as long as we enter into His will; we all stand in His field. 

And just as thorns and thistles now grow from the earth, covering and tearing many a good herb and flower: So too is the godless man, who does not trust God but builds within himself, thinking: "I have my God in the chest <note>i.e., his money box or safe.</note>; I will be greedy and leave great treasures to my children, so that they may also sit in my honor." That is indeed the "best way" <note>Böhme is being sarcastic here about the worldly perspective.</note>, and yet it tears many a heart, so that it also becomes frivolous and thinks: "This is indeed the good way of fortune, that one has wealth, power, and honor—he truly has it good." 

And when one considers this, it happens to one as it does to the other, and yet the poor soul is lost thereby; for the rich man’s delicacies taste no better than the hungry man’s morsel of bread. Everywhere there is worry, sorrow, fear, sickness, and finally death. It is only shadow-boxing <note>original: *Spiegel-Fechten*; literally "mirror-fencing," meaning fighting an illusion or engaging in a pointless, imaginary struggle.</note> in this world; the powerful one sits in the governance of the spirit of this world, and he who fears God sits in the governance of Divine Power and Wisdom. The governance of this world ends with the body, and the governance in God's Spirit remains

<column-break/>

standing eternally. It is a completely miserable thing that man pursues that which would follow him if only he were still and pious. He runs after sorrow and worry, and yet they follow him on their own. He is as if he were always mad; he creates unrest for himself. If he were content, he would have rest. He places a "devouring worm" <note>A common 17th-century metaphor for a guilty conscience, referencing the biblical "worm that never dies."</note> in his heart that plagues him and makes for him an evil conscience that gnaws at him, and he is only a fool for it. For his goods belong to another, and the gnawing worm in his conscience he takes with him from this world; he considers that to be his treasure which gnaws at him eternally. Surely no greater folly can be found under the sun.

Since man is the most noble and rational creature in this world, he is also in spirit the greatest fool among all races, in that he hunts so hard for that which he does not even need himself. For to each one, his portion is allotted by the spirit of this world, if only he would be content. One man is another’s devil, tormenting the other, and it is all for a handful of earth or for stones, of which the earth has enough. Might this not be a wonder? Does not the fierce hellish spirit carry out his wonders according to his wish upon man, as the **Book of Revelation** witnesses, where one seal of wrath after another has opened, and men have become servants of wrath? They have willingly set out with blood and goods, and still thought they were doing God a service.

God wants to give you everything; He has given you everything; you had it by <term>Natural Right<note>original: *Natur-Recht*. In Böhme's view, this is the original dignity and dominion man held in his unfallen state.</note></term>. The sun and stars are yours; you are a lord over everything. Just let the foolish will go. # Of True Repentance.

**Humility.** Or do you think it is so good to dwell in wrath? See, when the light of your eyes breaks <note>i.e., at the moment of death.</note>, you will depart into the darkness and take your foolish torment with you, into which you have placed yourself here. Is the darkness then better than the eternal light? Just ask the night whether it is better than the day! Or do you think we are mad to speak thus? We speak what we see, and testify of what we know, and yet you are blind. You have been blinded by the **Harlot of Babylon** <note>In Böhme’s vocabulary, "Babel" or "the Harlot" refers to the corrupted, prideful, and divided institutional church and worldly systems.</note>, whom the **Avarice-Devil** has fathered while men were complacent, having grown weary of God’s Word and Spirit, as the Revelation of John testifies: *I will come to you and push away your candlestick.* And **Paul** says: *God will allow powerful errors to come, so that they will believe the spirits of lies, who speak lies in hypocrisy and error; they will cling to the devils.* But in the last days, says the **Prophet David**, the word of the Lord shall flourish like grass upon the earth. *Make the gates in the world high, and the doors wide, that the Lord may enter.* Who is the Lord? He is the **Hero in battle** <note>Original: "Held im Streit," referring to God as the champion of the soul against darkness.</note>. All swords and spears shall be made into plowshares and sickles, says the Prophet of God; and it shall come to pass, that whoever calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved. Therefore it is good to trust in God, even if the earthly body should always stick in the mud. It is but for a short time; and since no one knows which hour his time in this world is up, the judgment over his life follows immediately thereafter.

Therefore, leave off from **Greed**; it is the sole root of all evil and all folly. A greedy man is the greatest fool on earth, for he devours himself and creates unrest for himself, achieving nothing but evil: He does not know what kind of man it is who shall possess his wealth <note>i.e., he cannot know if his heirs will be worthy.</note>, and it is often shamefully swallowed up by harlots: While one has ruined his soul for it, another is merry with it in a different kind of folly. For it

<column-break/>

must all eventually come to fruition. But he who trusts God always has enough; he is satisfied with what he has. Thus, he is much richer than the fool who oppresses the wretched for the sake of money—money which cannot preserve his life from death and hell. The **Pious Man** collects a treasure for himself in heaven; he receives a new body in which there is no hunger, thirst, frost, nor heat, and he has peace in his conscience and will rejoice in his treasure eternally. And the **Greedy Fool** collects for himself an earthly treasure that remains for others, along with a bad conscience and a treasure in the abyss that will eternally gnaw and devour him. God’s blessing never forsakes anyone who earnestly trusts in God and lets go of that which does not wish to stay. God has wondrous ways by which He feeds and nourishes His children, like **Daniel** in the lions' den, and **Elijah** under the juniper tree, and the **Widow of Zarephath** during the famine. *He who trusts God has built well, in heaven and on earth.*

**9. Question:** I would gladly be satisfied with a dry crust of bread, if I could only be assured of it or earn it with the labor of my hands. But what shall I say? When I truly examine myself, everything within me swarms with sins and cares; I am like a barrel full of impurity where the slightest movement causes all the stench and refuse to rise. I see neither beginning nor end to my misery.

**Answer:** This is not at all unusual. As soon as the Devil perceives that the soul is in earnest, he stirs up nothing but riot and misery. Here the soul enters the state of the **Prodigal Son**, who became a swineherd; we have shamefully squandered our paternal inheritance with the husks of the Devil's and the world’s swine. ### Part I / Chapter 2.

...of His wonder-work: Everyone has a **vocation** <term>Beruff; a station, calling, or role in life</term> in which they spend their time; they are all equal before Him. Only the **spirit of this world** has its highness; it distributes this in its power, just as the Spirit of **GOD** does in Heaven. There too are great differences, depending on whether the spirit or soul is clothed with **Divine Power**. So too is His highness in Heaven, as well as His beauty and clarity, but all in one love. Every angel and soul finds joy in the power and beauty of the other. Just as the flowers of the earth do not envy one another—even if one is more beautiful and powerful than the other—but stand friendlily among each other, and each enjoys the power of the other. And just as a physician mixes many kinds of herbs together, in which each power yields its own virtue, and all serve the sick: so also do we all please **GOD**, provided we enter into His will; we all stand in His field.

And just as thorns and thistles now grow out of the earth, covering and tearing many a good herb and flower: so too is the **godless man**, who does not trust **GOD** but builds within himself and thinks: "I have my god in the money-chest <note>Original: 'Kasten'. This refers to a treasure chest or strongbox, implying that the miser's wealth has become his deity.</note>; I will be greedy and leave great treasures to my children so that they too may sit in my honor." This is indeed his "best way," yet with it he tears many a heart so that it also becomes frivolous and thinks: "This is surely the good way to fortune, that one has wealth, power, and honor; such a man has it good." 

But when one considers this, it goes for one as it does for the other, and yet the poor soul is lost by it. For the rich man’s delicacies do not taste better to him than a morsel of bread tastes to the hungry. Everywhere there is care, sorrow, fear, sickness, and finally death. It is only **shadow-boxing** <term>Spiegel-Fechten; literally 'mirror-fencing,' meaning a useless struggle against illusions or vanities</term> in this world. The powerful man sits in the **dominion** of the spirit of this world, but he who fears **GOD** sits in the dominion of Divine Power and Wisdom. The dominion of this world ends with the body, but the dominion in **GOD’S** Spirit remains

<column-break/>

standing eternally. It is a truly piteous thing that man pursues that which would pursue him if he were only still and pious. He runs after grief and sorrow, and yet these follow him of their own accord. He acts as if he were perpetually mad, creating unrest for himself; yet if he were content, he would have peace. He places a **consuming worm** <note>A reference to the biblical 'worm that never dies' (Mark 9:44), symbolizing the eternal gnawing of a guilty conscience.</note> in his heart which plagues him, and creates for himself an evil conscience that gnaws at him, and he is but a fool for it. For his goods belong to another, but the gnawing worm in his evil conscience he takes with him from this world; he holds that for his treasure which gnaws him eternally. Surely a greater folly cannot be found under the sun.

Since man is the noblest and most rational creature in this world, why is he such a great fool in his greed among all generations, hunting so hard after that which he does not even need? For to everyone their portion is allotted by the spirit of this world, if they would only be content. Thus, one man is the other’s devil, tormenting the other, and it is all for a handful of earth or for stones, of which the earth has enough anyway. Might this not be a wonder? Does the fierce, hellish spirit not accomplish his wonders upon man according to his desire, as the **Book of Revelation** testifies, where one **seal of wrath** after another has opened, and men have become servants of that wrath? They have willingly gone after blood and goods, and even thought they were doing **GOD** a service thereby.

O you blind man, how are you imprisoned in wrath? What are you doing, or who are you? Why do you let the devil lead you? Heaven and earth are yours; **GOD** wants to give you everything; He has given you everything; you had it by **Natural Right** <term>Natur-Recht; the inherent rights or state of man in the original divine order of nature</term>. The sun and stars are yours; you are a lord over all; only let go of that foolish will. Why do you give yourself over to greed and pride? For **GOD’S** kingdom stands in love.

<meta>This page continues Part I, Chapter 2, following the discussion on spiritual blindness and the "Harlot of Babylon." ### Part I / Chapter 2 ###

...and see how far we have stepped away from God’s righteousness and truth, as well as from brotherly love, and to examine our hearts well to see what they are inclined toward. When we do this, we will find within ourselves many hundreds of evil beasts, which we have set up in God’s place and honor as God; and we will then first see what abominable beasts were revealed in **Adam** through false desire, and why God said to Adam: *The Seed of the woman shall crush the head of the serpent* <note>original: "Des Weibes Saamen soll der Schlangen... den Kopf zertreten." This is a reference to Genesis 3:15, often called the "Protevangelium," or the first gospel promise.</note>, referring to these monstrous creatures.

For instance, we will first see in our desire the proud **Lucifer**, who has departed from Divine and brotherly humility, and who despises the members of his own body <note>By "members of his body," Böhme refers to fellow human beings, who should be seen as part of one collective spiritual body.</note>, and has set himself up over them as a god and lord; in him there is no Divine love, neither to love God nor his brothers.

Secondly, we will find a beast in our nature that is like a **greedy sow**, which draws everything to itself and wants to eat and possess it alone, and desires more than it needs, so that the proud Lucifer can boast and show himself to be a god over all things who can rule and have power and authority over his fellow elders. We will see how this proud Lucifer has broken himself off from the **Tree of Life** and from the growth of love, wanting to be his own tree; therefore, he has also withered away from God.

Thirdly, we will find the **poisonous, envious snake** in our nature, which stings all around like a venom—that is, envy—which begrudges anyone as much as it wants for itself; it stings and rides in other people's hearts, slanders them with words, and praises only the proud Lucifer within itself, calling its own falsehood an "Angel of God."

Fourthly, we will find the **fiery dragon** sitting in hellfire within our nature—that is, wrath—which, if it cannot get what it wants through greed and envy,

<column-break/>

wants to strike with its fists and take things by force; it is so mad that it almost bursts with malice, breaking apart in its own unrestrained wickedness, becoming a completely dry, dead tree that is fit only for the fire.

Fifthly, we will find many other beasts in our desire, according to how **Pride** loves and honors itself before God, and how **Greed** draws treasures to itself, and Pride parades around as if they were gods; thus, one person pulls the bread away from his brother, so that the brother must consume it in misery and tribulation with his oppressors.

When a person views himself in this **Mirror of Selfhood** and becomes aware of these evil beasts, he will truly realize—while considering the weak Adam here—that these desires were all planted in us together as a "Monster of the Serpent" through the Devil's introduction of them into our first parents.

All these beasts are damned and must die within us; and even if some lingering desire remains in our flesh, they must be completely killed in the soul, which is the inner ground. The inner image of the soul must be **tinctured** <term>Tincture: In alchemy, a substance that transforms base metals into gold; for Böhme, the "Tincture of Christ's Blood" is the spiritual force that transforms the "base" fallen nature of the soul back into its divine state.</term> once again through the true tincture in the blood of Christ, so that the qualities of the inner ground may live in truth again; otherwise, they cannot reach salvation within themselves.

Now, if a person recognizes this, he cannot get rid of the desires of his evil beasts in any other way than by immediately turning to the **Cross** with all his strength, with a completely firm will and purpose, intending to be an enemy to these "devil-beasts"—since they are only the Devil's servants. He must wish to turn back to his lost Fatherland, into childhood and unity, and see himself as nothing other than the **poor lost swineherd** <note>A reference to the Parable of the Prodigal Son (Luke 15), who was reduced to feeding swine before returning to his father.</note>; for that is indeed what he is, and nothing else or better; and he must immediately begin the turning-around of his soul...

# Of True Repentance #

...Father, in the highest humility of his unworthiness, as one who has shamefully squandered the bestowed inheritance of **Christ’s merit**, and enters into repentance. He should give his earnest will with all his strength to this: that from this hour forward he intends to repent and no longer love these evil beasts <note>Böhme uses "beasts" to represent the distorted desires and passions of the fallen human nature.</note>. But it must be in **earnest**; he must not think of a day, a week, or a year, but rather his mind should judge these beasts to the condemnation of death. He must no longer wish to love them, but hold them as enemies and desire to turn toward the grace of **GOD**. When this happens, I say truly, he may turn to earnest prayer in humility and ask for grace from God. And even if his heart speaks a loud "no," and the **Devil** says: "Wait a while; it is not good right now"; and when tomorrow comes, he says "tomorrow" again, and speaks to the **flesh**: "You must have this and that first; collect a treasure for yourself first so that you do not need the world, and only then enter into such a life"—even then, the mind must remain firm in its purpose and think: "These intrusive thoughts are my evil, hungry beasts; I will kill them and drown them in the blood of **Christ** in His love. Not one of them shall live for me any longer, for I want them no more. I am on the way to my old Father, who has sent His Son to me in my misery, who says: *Come unto me, all ye that labor and are heavy laden with sins, and I will give you rest.* <note>original: "Kommet alle zu mir her / die ihr mit Sünden beladen / und aber derselben mühselig seyd / ich will euch erquicken." A paraphrase of Matthew 11:28.</note> My Father will give the **Holy Spirit** to those who ask Him for it." He should impress this into his heart and come to the Father like the **Prodigal Son**. When the Father sees that the soul’s mind is directed toward Him and would gladly be converted but cannot do so on its own, He will immediately come to meet him. He will take the soul into the arms of His drawing power and lead it into the suffering and death of Christ. There, through earnest <term>penitence</term> <note>original Latin: "Pœnitenz." This refers to the active, internal process of remorse and spiritual discipline.</note> and repentance, the soul will die to the abominable beasts and rise from the death of Christ with a new will and a new, right, Divine desire. The soul begins to become a completely different person and will no longer value what it previously loved and held as its treasure; it will be as if he had it and yet did not have it, and he will hereafter regard himself in all his ability only as a servant of God. For as soon as he can overcome the proud **Lucifer** with his pride, the other evil beasts all become faint and weak together and lose their rule. Although they still live in the earthly flesh during this time, they are only like a donkey that must carry the sack, or like an evil dog on a chain; their power is broken. For when Christ rises, Lucifer must lie captive. And if one were truly in earnest, such a **jewel** <note>Böhme frequently uses the "jewel" or "pearl" (Kleinod) to describe the sudden, ecstatic realization of God's presence.</note> would follow that this pen cannot write of it here; only those know it who have been at the **Heavenly Wedding**, where the noble **Sophia** <note>Sophia is the Greek word for Wisdom. In Böhme's theology, she represents the "Eternal Bride" or the Divine Mirror, the feminine aspect of God with whom the human soul must be reunited.</note> is wedded to the soul. Of this, Christ says that there is such great joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, more than over ninety-nine righteous ones. This joy is also held in heaven for the person in this wedding—this is understood among our own.

# Part I / Chapter 2 #

...and see how far we have wandered from **God’s** righteousness and truth, as well as from brotherly love, and to examine our heart well to see what it is inclined toward. When we do this, we will find many hundreds of evil animals within us, which we have set in **God’s** place and honor as **God**. We will then see for the first time what ghastly beasts became manifest in **Adam** through false desire, and why **God** said to **Adam**: *The seed of the woman shall crush the serpent’s head* <note>A reference to Genesis 3:15, interpreted by Böhme as the spiritual power of Christ overcoming the "monstrous" nature of the fallen human ego.</note>, as the head of these monstrous beasts.

First, we will see in our desire the proud **Lucifer**, who has turned away from Divine and brotherly humility, despised the members of his own body, and set himself up as a God and Lord over them—he in whom there is no Divine love, neither to love **God** nor his brothers.

Secondly, we will find a beast in our own nature that is like a greedy sow, which draws everything to itself and wants to eat and possess alone, desiring more than it needs, so that the proud **Lucifer** can boast and show himself off as a "God over all being" who can rule and have power and authority over his fellow elders. We will see how this proud **Lucifer** has broken himself off from the Tree of Life and from the growth of Love, wanting to be his own tree; for this reason, he has withered away from **God**.

Thirdly, we will find the poisonous, envious serpent in our nature, which stings all around like a venom—that is, Envy—which grants no one as much as itself, which stings and rides in other people's hearts, slanders them with words, and praises only the proud **Lucifer** within itself, calling its own falsehood an Angel of **God**.

Fourthly, we will find the fiery dragon sitting in hellfire within our nature—that is, Wrath—which, if it cannot obtain what Greed and Envy desire,

<column-break/>

wants to strike with fists and take by force. It is so mad that it almost bursts from malice and breaks apart in its unbridled wickedness; it is an entirely dry, dead tree that is fit only for the fire.

Fifthly, we will find many other beasts in our desire: how Pride loves and honors itself before **God**, and draws Greed to itself as a treasure. Pride boasts as if it were a god, and thus pulls the bread away from its brother so that he must consume it in misery and tribulation with his oppressors.

When a person views himself in this mirror of selfhood and becomes aware of these evil beasts, he must truly acknowledge them. He must consider the weak **Adam** in this state and realize that all these desires were implanted together as a "monster of the serpent" through the **Devil’s** introduction of them into our first parents.

All these beasts are damned and must die within us. Even if some remnant of desire remains clinging to the flesh, they must be completely killed in the soul’s desire—that is, in the inner ground. The inner soul-image must be <term>tinctured</term> <note>Tincture: In Böhme’s mystical alchemy, this is the spiritual "medicine" or transformative power of Christ’s love that "colors" and transmutes the dark, base nature of the soul into divine light.</note> again through the true Tincture in the blood of **Christ**, so that the qualities of the inner ground live in the truth once more; otherwise, they cannot reach salvation within themselves.

Now, if a person recognizes this, he cannot get rid of the desires of his evil beasts in any other way than by immediately turning to the Cross with all his strength, with a very strict will and purpose. He must choose to be an enemy to these "devil-beasts"—since they are merely the **Devil's** servants—and desire to turn back toward his lost Fatherland, toward childhood and unity. He should see himself as nothing other than the poor, lost swine-herd <note>original: "Sau-Hirte." A reference to the Parable of the Prodigal Son (Luke 15), who reached his lowest point tending swine before returning to his father.</note>—for that is exactly what he is, and nothing else or better—and begin immediately with the turning of his soul...

<summary>Böhme identifies the "inner beasts" of the fallen soul (Pride/Lucifer, Greed/Sow, Envy/Serpent, and Wrath/Dragon) and explains that they must be transformed through the "Tincture" of Christ's blood. He calls for the reader to adopt the humility of the Prodigal Son to begin the process of returning to God.</summary>

# Chapter III.
### Of Prayer in the Practice of Repentance.

->**Question 1.**<-
Even though I often make a serious resolution to come before the Father like a prodigal son and to persist in heartfelt prayer for the forgiveness of sins, I am nonetheless immediately held back by unbelief and mistrust?

->**Answer.**<-
The true foundation of prayer consists of a sincere, pure desire to be redeemed from sin and to become a child of **GOD**. One should therefore consider well what prayer actually is. It is not like appearing before a worldly king or lord when one has offended him and asks for mercy while often thinking quite differently in one's heart. No, rather it is a "going out" of oneself, wherein a person surrenders to **GOD** with all their strength, with all that they are, and all that they possess. Indeed, with true prayer, he gives himself over to be the property of **GOD**. Like the prodigal son, he returns to the Father in his original fatherland and inheritance, from which Adam, our first father, led him away. He no longer has a natural right to heavenly goods; he lost them all with Adam's departure and consumed them through the devil’s dalliance <note>The original German "Bulerey" refers to an illicit or sinful love affair, here meaning the soul's unfaithful attachment to worldly vanity.</note> with vanity. Thus, he must now come to **GOD** in great humility and faith, in true hope for the grace **GOD** has offered in his son **Jesus Christ**, arriving like the prodigal son and considering himself unworthy of any heavenly goods by natural right. He must fall down before **GOD**, his eternal Father, and beg for the offered mercy in his son **Jesus Christ**, asking that He might yet accept him as a day-laborer and worker in His vineyard, and give him heavenly food and drink for his languishing, hungry, and thirsty soul, so that he might no longer have to eat the husks of

<column-break/>

vanity, lies, and falsehood with the devil’s swine, or live in unbelief without heavenly power. In his prayer, he must open his hungry and thirsty "soul-mouth" toward the grace and mercy of **GOD** with heartfelt sighing and a turning toward grace, surrendering himself entirely into the hands of **GOD’s** grace. Then he will immediately hear in his soul that **GOD** is coming to meet him with His grace, and that He is giving the grace offered in **Jesus Christ** into his soul. For the poor, hungry soul will powerfully and essentially <note>original: "wesentlich" — meaning "in substance" or "in reality," not just as an idea.</note> receive within itself that which it asks and desires from **GOD**: namely, the flesh and blood of **Jesus Christ**, which is offered as food to all hungry, repentant souls. He will feel within himself how the ancient Father of the prodigal son comes to meet the poor, turned-around, repentant soul, falling upon the "neck" of the soul's essence with His love, embracing it, kissing it, taking it into His arms, and speaking to it in the spirit: "This is my dear son; this is my dear soul, which I had lost! It was dead and has become alive again. Now slaughter the Lamb, **Jesus Christ**; <note>This is a mystical reference to the Eucharist and the sacrifice of Christ, paralleling the "fatted calf" from the biblical parable of the Prodigal Son (Luke 15).</note> she shall sit at the table with me in my joy, and eat with me from my prepared meal—from the true food of my son **Jesus Christ**—and shall rejoice with me eternally." There, the signet ring—the precious testament of the covenant of **GOD**—is placed back on the soul in the blood of **Jesus Christ**, and the soul is accepted again as a child of **GOD** through such a covenant and sealing. Every prayer that does not find and take this is cold and lukewarm, and is stuck in a husk of temporal, earthly things—that is to say: the soul is not approaching **GOD** with purity.

**2. Question:** If I then pray often and present my misery to **GOD**, why does it seem as though the sin in my flesh and my unbelief only grow more powerful, so that with my prayer I only ignite the **Wrath of GOD** all the more?

**Answer:** Behold, you poor wounded soul, you stand and pray: "O **GOD**, forgive me my sin, let Your wrath subside, and accept even me into Your grace." This is quite right; however, you do not understand how **GOD** accepts the poor sinner. You think it is as if you come before your local Prince, having forfeited your life, and you plead with him, and he forgives your misdeed out of mercy, so you are then "quiet" <note>original: *quiet*; meaning legally cleared or at peace regarding a debt</note>. But your sins still rebuke you to your face, and your heart accuses itself, saying you are still deserving of punishment. Behold, this is how you also come before **GOD**, and by this means, many hypocrites are born. You think **GOD** in His Being and Spirit takes your sin away from you. Do you not know what the Scripture says: *That all our works shall follow us*? If it happened that way, then **GOD** would have to move Himself for the sake of every person who calls upon Him and cast their sin away from them—and yet **GOD** has not moved Himself more than twice since eternity: once with the creation of the world and all creatures, and then secondly in the **Incarnation of Christ**; there, the heart of **GOD** was moved.

Behold, when **GOD** forgives your sin as you call upon Him, He takes nothing from you, nor does He descend from heav-

<column-break/>

-en down into you, for He has been in your soul from eternity, but in His **Principle** <note>original: *Principio*; refers to the underlying source or fundamental ground of existence</note>. Your soul only went out from Him, from His **Principle**—understand this as being from the holy will of the **Majesty**—into the **Wrath** <note>In this mystical context, "Wrath" (Zorn) is the dark, fiery foundation of nature that is separated from God's light.</note>. Now you were in the **Wrath** in eternal death, and the man **Christ**, who is **GOD** and man, has made a path through death and **Wrath** to the **Majesty of GOD**. You must only turn back and go through that same path—through the death of **Christ**, through the **Wrath** toward the **Majesty**. Then you will be received by the most beloved Angel <note>Likely referring to Christ's divine nature or the "Angel of Great Counsel"</note>, who never committed any sin. Nor will any sin be recognized in you, but only **GOD’s** wondrous deeds, which had to be revealed within the **Wrath**. For Love could not do this within the fire; she does not mingle with the fire, but shines through it.

Now, when you pray like this: "O **GOD**, forgive me," you are still constantly doubting because of your sin, wondering whether **GOD** will hear you and come into your heart. Behold, do not do that! For with your doubt, you despise the **Majesty**, and that is also a sin. Instead, gather all your sins, which are without number, into a heap, and come with your desiring soul boldly and in humility to **GOD**, and enter into **GOD**. Only turn your soul away from the will of this world and into **GOD’s** will; throw yourself with all your **Reason** and senses into **GOD’s** will. And even if your heart and the Devil say a loud "No," then strike your outer **Reason** dead, enter in by force, and remain standing. Do not look back, like **Lot's wife**, who turned back into a pillar of sulfur and salt, but stand firm. Let the Devil, as well as the spirit of this world and your heart with its flesh and blood, struggle and flail; give **Reason** no room. When it says: "You are not in **GOD**," then say: "No, I am in **GOD**; I am in heaven in Him, and I will never depart from Him through all eternity. The Devil may keep my sin, and the world the body, but I live in **GOD’s** will; His life...

Therefore, it is said: "Stand still, for the devil goes about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour." He comes every hour to the door of your heart and looks to see if he can get back in, for it is his favorite lodging. In hell he has no rest, but in the human soul he has joy and pleasure; he can reveal his malicious wonders there, so that after this life he may also have a game in which he delights, for hell and **GOD’s** wrath desire that.

4. **Question:** I would often gladly pour out my heart before **GOD** with words, but I am so hardened and so burdened that I can find no words?

**Answer:** We can speak with **GOD** without words. Words serve more to express ourselves in our own understanding than to bring our concerns before **GOD**. Nevertheless, prayer with words is very useful for a beginner and often brings great refreshment to the soul. If, however, a beginner is unable to express his concerns with words, he can use powerful prayer formulas, such as our author—as a well-practiced **supplicant** <note>original: "Bitter."</note>—presents most excellently even for beginners in the **Struggle of Repentance**, specifically for the true recognition and confession of our sins.

O great, unsearchable, holy **GOD**, **LORD** of all beings, you who have revealed yourself in **Christ Jesus**, out of great love toward us, with your **Holy Being** in our humanity. I, a poor, unworthy, sinful human, come before your revealed face in the humanity of **Jesus Christ**, even though I am not worthy to lift my eyes to you; and I plead before you and confess to you that I have become faithless and broken regarding your great love and grace which you have bestowed upon us. I have abandoned the covenant which you made with me out of pure grace through **Baptism**, in which you accepted me as a child and heir of eternal life; and I have led my desires into the **Vanity** <term>Eitelkeit: In this context, it refers to the empty, fleeting, and prideful nature of the material world.</term> of this world, and defiled my soul therewith, and made it entirely beast-like and earthly, so that my soul no longer even knows itself because of the **miry filth of sin**, and considers itself entirely a stranger before your face, one who is not worthy to desire your grace. I lie in the mud of sins and the vanity of my corrupted flesh, up to the very throat of my soul, and have only a tiny spark of the living breath left in me which desires your grace. I have become so dead to myself in vanity that I do not even dare to lift my eyes to you in this emptiness.

<column-break/>

O **GOD** in **Christ Jesus**, you who became man for the sake of poor sinners so that you might help them; to you I lament; to you I still have a spark of refuge in my soul. I have disregarded your hard-won inheritance, which you earned for us poor humans through your bitter death, and I have made myself a partaker in the inheritance of vanity in your Father’s wrath, in the curse of the earth, and am captured in sins and half-dead in your kingdom. I lie in a faint, far from your power, and grim death waits for me; the devil has poisoned me so that I do not know my **Savior**. I have become a wild branch on your tree and have consumed my inheritance from you with the **devil’s swine** <note>An allusion to the Prodigal Son in Luke 15.</note>. What shall I say before you, I who am not worthy of your grace?

# Part 1 / Chapter 3

...can only become firm if the soul, which forms itself toward **God** high above the stars, learns to recognize how **God** is present everywhere and in all things. Secondly, that it places a very earnest desire in **God’s** love and mercy, and thus prays more through its desire than through reason and the contemplation of things, for prayer is nothing other than an earnest desire for **God**. When a person finds such a desire and hunger within themselves that they would gladly perform **repentance** <term>Busse: A total change of mind and a turning of the heart back toward God.</term>, yet finds no "true remorse" <note>original: "Reue"</note> for the committed sin within—but nonetheless feels a hunger for remorse (as the poor imprisoned soul ever groans, fears, and must admit its guilt for sins before **God’s** judgment)—they can do no better than to gather their senses and mind <term>Gemüthe: The inner disposition, combining will, emotion, and intellect.</term> together with all reason into one. At that very hour—immediately in the first contemplation when they feel a longing for repentance—they should make a powerful resolution that they will enter into repentance this very hour and minute, and depart from the ungodly way. They must disregard all the world's power and honor, and if necessary, leave everything behind for the sake of true repentance and count it as nothing. And they should set before themselves such a hard and strict mind that they never wish to depart from it again, even if they should be considered the world’s fool for it. They must desire, with their mind, to go out from the beauty and pleasure of this world and enter patiently into the suffering and death of **Christ**, into and under His cross, and direct their entire hope toward the future life. They should now desire to enter into **Christ’s** vineyard in righteousness and truth, to do **God’s** will, and to begin and complete all their works in this world in **Christ’s** spirit and will. For the sake of **Christ’s** word and promise, in which He has promised us a heavenly reward, they should gladly suffer and bear all misfortune and the cross, so that they may only be counted among the fellowship of **Christ’s** children and be incorporated and united into His humanity through the blood of the Lamb, **Jesus Christ**.

<column-break/>

They should firmly imagine—wrapping their soul entirely within it—that through this resolution they will attain the love of **God** in **JESUS**, and that **God**, according to His faithful promise, will give them the noble jewel, the **Holy Spirit**, at their beginning. They should believe that they will be born anew within the humanity of **Christ** according to the Divine Essence, and that through **Christ**, their mind will be renewed in His divine power and their weak faith made strong. Also, that in their divine hunger, they shall receive **Christ’s** flesh and blood as food and drink within their soul’s desire (for which they hunger and thirst), drinking from the sweet well of **Jesus Christ**, the water of eternal life, according to **Christ’s** promise and true, strong assurance. They should also firmly imagine the great love of **God**: that **God** does not desire the death of the sinner, but wants him to turn back and live. They should remember how **Christ** so kindly calls poor sinners to Himself, how He wishes to refresh them, and that **God** sent His Son into the world for this reason: to seek and to save that which is lost—namely, the poor, repentant, returning sinner. For the sake of the poor sinner, **God** gave His Son unto death and let Him die for him in our assumed humanity. This they should firmly imagine: that **God** would much rather hear them and receive them into grace in **Christ JESUS** than they could ever come to Him. In the love of **Christ**, in the highly-precious name **JESUS**, **God** can will no evil; there is no more wrath in this name. Rather, it is the highest and deepest love and faithfulness, the supreme sweetness of the Godhead in the great name **JEHOVAH** <note>The Hebrew Tetragrammaton, here representing the majestic and eternal ground of God's being.</note>, which He has revealed in our corrupted and faded <note>original: "verblichenen," referring to the spiritual "death" or darkening of the divine image in the Fall.</note> humanity—specifically the heavenly part that faded in **Paradise** due to sin—and has therefore moved Himself according to His heart...

### Of Holy Prayer.
L 3
<meta>catchword: am;</meta>

...instilled His sweet love in us, so that the Father's wrath, which was ignited within us, might thereby be extinguished and transformed into love; all of which happened for the sake of the poor sinner, so that they might once again obtain an open gate of grace.

In such contemplation, one should firmly imagine that at this very hour and moment, they stand before the face of the **Holy Trinity**, and that **God** is truly present both within and outside of them, by virtue of the **Holy Scripture**, which says: *Am I not He who fills all things?* <note>original: "Bin nicht Ichs, der es alles erfüllet?" — Jeremiah 23:24</note> Likewise: *The word is near you, namely, in your mouth and heart.* <note>Romans 10:8</note> Likewise: *We will come to you and make our home within you.* <note>John 14:23</note> Likewise: *I will stay with you every day, until the end of the world.* <note>Matthew 28:20</note> Likewise: *The kingdom of God is within you.* <note>Luke 17:21</note>

Thus, one should certainly know and believe that they stand with their soul firmly before the face of **Jesus Christ**, before the **Holy Godhead**, and that their soul had previously turned its back to **God's** face; and that now, at this hour, they wish to turn the soul’s eyes and desires back toward **God**, coming to the Father with the poor, lost, and returning son. <note>A reference to the Parable of the Prodigal Son.</note>

->Of True **Repentance** <term>Busse: Not just a feeling of regret, but a total reorientation of one’s life toward the divine.</term> §. 12.<-

4. **Quest.** I would often gladly pour out my heart before **God** with words, but I am so hardened and so burdened that I can find no words?

**Ans.** We can speak with **God** without words. Words serve more to express things for our own understanding than to bring our concerns before **God**. Nevertheless, for a beginner, prayer with words is very useful and often brings great refreshment to the soul. If a beginner is unable to express their concerns with words, they can use powerful "prayer formulas" <note>Pre-written prayers meant to guide the heart's focus.</note>, such as those our author—as a well-practiced petitioner <note>original: "Bitter" — a supplicant or one who intercedes in prayer.</note>—vividly sets forth for beginners in the struggle of repentance, for the true recognition and confession of our sins.

> O great, unsearchable, holy **God**, **Lord** of all beings, You who have revealed Yourself in **Christ Jesus**, out of great love for us, with Your Holy Essence in our humanity.

<column-break/>

> I, a poor, unworthy, sinful human, come before Your revealed countenance in the humanity of **Jesus Christ**, though I am not worthy to lift my eyes to You; I plead before You and confess to You that I have become faithless and broken regarding Your great love and grace which You have bestowed upon us. I have abandoned the covenant which You made with me out of pure grace through **Baptism**, in which You accepted me as a child and heir of eternal life; and I have led my desires into the vanity <term>Eitelkeit: In this context, it refers to the fleeting, empty, and illusory nature of the material world.</term> of this world, besmirching my soul with it and making it entirely beastly and earthly, so that my soul no longer recognizes itself because of the "sin-sludge" <note>original: "Sünden-Schlamm"</note> and considers itself a complete stranger before Your face, unworthy of desiring Your grace. I lie in the sludge of sin and the vanity of my corrupted flesh, up to the very palate of my soul, and have only a tiny spark of the living breath left in me which desires Your grace. I have become so dead to myself in this vanity that I do not even dare to lift my eyes to You in this emptiness.
>
> O **God** in **Christ Jesus**, You who became human for the sake of poor sinners so that You might help them; to You I lament, to You I still have a spark of refuge in my soul. I have thought nothing of Your hard-won inheritance, which You earned for us poor humans through Your bitter death, and have instead partaken in the inheritance of vanity in Your Father’s wrath, in the curse of the earth; I am imprisoned in sin and half-dead in Your kingdom. I lie in a faint, deprived of Your strength, and grim death waits for me; the devil has poisoned me so that I do not know my **Savior**. I have become a wild branch on Your tree and have consumed my inheritance from You with the devil’s swine. What shall I say before You, I who am not worthy of Your grace?

5. **Q.** This excellent prayer expresses my whole heart and mind. Oh, that I had the power and spirit to speak such words with life! But it usually happens to me / as it did to the Canaanite woman <note>A reference to Matthew 15:22–28, where a woman persists in her request for healing despite being initially rebuffed and compared to a dog; it is a classic example of "tested faith."</note> / as if I were being turned away like an unworthy dog / and instead of composing myself in humility and faith / my heart is full of anguish, fear, and doubt?

**Ans.** It usually happens this way in such an undertaking / as if God would not hear / the heart remains without comfort / its sins and unworthiness still appear before its eyes / as if it were not worthy: the mind is / as if it were mute / the soul groans in the depths / the heart receives nothing / and perhaps cannot even pour out its confession before God / just as if its heart and soul were locked shut: the soul would gladly [speak] / but the flesh holds it captive / the Devil covers it tightly / and fashions the way of vanity before it again / and tickles it with the lust of the flesh / and says in the mind: "Wait a while / do this and that first / gather money first so that you do not need the world / then enter into a godly life / into repentance / there is time enough."

Oh, how many hundreds perish in such a beginning / if they enter back into vanity / and it happens to them / like a young graft <note>original: "Pfröpflein." A metaphor for the newly "grafted" spiritual life of a believer which is still fragile.</note> / that is broken off by the winds / or withered by the heat.

Listen, dear soul / if you wish to become a knight over death and hell in your Savior Christ / and if you wish that your young graft should become and grow into a tree in the Kingdom of Christ / then you must remain standing in your first earnest purpose: it costs your first paternal inheritance / and moreover your body and soul / whether you will be an angel in God / or a devil in hell. If you wish to be crowned / then you must fight / you must conquer in Christ / and not lie defeated beneath the Devil. Your purpose shall remain standing / you must not prefer temporal honor and goods over this. When the spirit of the flesh says: "Wait a while / it is not a pleasant time right now"; Then the soul must say: "Now is my time and hour / that I may enter again into my Fatherland / from which..."

6. **Qu.** I have often made such an earnest purpose firm for myself, yet when it came to the test of overcoming sin in flesh and blood, I was stormed by so many powers of malice that I soon fell back exhausted?

**Ans.** Even this should not drive us away from our purpose. All the more must a faithful warrior establish himself in **humility**. And though it seems that GOD casts you out like a filthy dog, then cast yourself out, and praise GOD in his holiness; thus you will meanwhile overcome the proud and high-flying dragon, the greedy wolf, and all evil poisonous animals through humility. In whatever state you may be, humility must stand at the front; otherwise, you will not attain her **marriage** <note>Likely referring to the "Mystical Marriage," the union of the soul with Divine Wisdom or Christ.</note>, although true humility is first born in her marriage; but your soul’s free will must stand like a knight. This I grasp for myself; let GOD's wrath now do with my sin what it will, and let the Devil rush over my soul in his constructed Robber-Castle however he wishes: no Devil, death, nor hell shall tear me from Your wounds. You foul Devil, you must be put to shame through me and leave your Robber-Castle; for I will sink it into the love of JESUS Christ, and then you may dwell therein if you can. Amen.

### Instruction in Temptation.

Kind reader, this is no joke. He who has not experienced it and considers it a joke is not yet judged; and even if it were saved for his final end—which is dangerous—he must still go through this judgment. O, happy is he who passes through it in early times, in his young years, before the Devil builds his Robber-Castle firm. Such a person can afterward become a laborer in Christ's vineyard and sow his seed in Christ's little garden; he will surely reap the fruits in his time. This judgment lasts a long time and many years for some, if they do not earnestly surrender themselves into Christ's armor when the judgment of **temptation** <note>original: "Anfechtung." This describes a state of intense spiritual trial or "assault" where the soul feels abandoned by God.</note> first admonishes them toward repentance. But he who comes of his own earnest purpose and intends to depart from the godless way, for him it is not so difficult and does not last long; though he must endure a knightly victory against the Devil, he is mightily assisted, and it turns out for his very best, so that when afterward the **Morning-Redness** <note>original: "Morgen-Röthe." A central concept in Böhme’s mysticism, symbolizing the dawning of divine light and the birth of the spirit within the soul.</note> in the soul begins—

### Warning to the Reader.

With good intentions, dear reader, I will not hide from you what has been earnestly shown to me here. If you are still comfortable in the vanity of the flesh and are not in earnest purpose on the way to the new rebirth <note>original: "Wiedergeburt." The process of spiritual regeneration or being "born again."</note>, intending to become a different person, then leave the words written above in this prayer unsaid; otherwise, they will become God’s judgment within you. You shall not misuse the Holy Name; be faithfully warned. These words belong to the thirsty soul; if it is truly in earnest, the soul will experience what they are.

# Chapter IV.

## Concerning true living Faith and its proper Fruits, namely: Concerning the earnest Imitation of JESUS Christ as the means to arrive at a true knowledge of GOD and of oneself.

->1. Question.<-
->What do you actually understand by true faith?<-

->Answer.<-

By "faith," we do not mean a historical science <note>original: "historische Wissenschafft." This refers to "head-knowledge"—knowing the facts of the Bible without experiencing a spiritual transformation.</note>, such that a person merely constructs articles of belief and clings to them, forcing his mind into the works of his reason. Rather, faith is one spirit with God. The Holy Spirit moves within the spirit of faith. Faith is a power of God, a spirit with God; it works in and with God; it is bound to nothing except

<column-break/>

right love, from which it draws its life’s power and strength. Just as light is free from the fire, even though it is always born out of the fire, and the fire’s torment <note>original: "Quall." In this mystical context, it refers to the burning quality or "source-spirit" of the fire.</note> cannot grasp the light; so faith is born out of the life-spirit as if from an ever-burning fire. Prayer is the fire-hunger <note>original: "Feuer-Hunger." A mystical term for the soul’s intense, consuming longing for God's essence.</note>, and faith is the spirit that goes out in the fire-hunger and desire, and grasps the essence for which it hungers and clothes itself with it, of which we will say more below.

# Part 1 / Chapter 4

**2. Question:** But how does faith give birth to true knowledge?

**Answer:** Just as a fire-spirit takes hold in oil and gives birth to a light: so too is faith a spirit from God; it proceeds from the soul into God and becomes luminous within God. For everything born in nature is enclosed within God’s will, and nothing can enter into God’s will unless it is first born out of God’s will. Thus, faith is a spirit from God’s will; therefore, it <term>interacts<note>The original term is "inqualiret," a word used by Jacob Boehme to describe how two things merge their qualities or "harmonize" in their inner nature.</note></term> with God’s will and reveals God to us with His light, when the spirit of the soul becomes free from all "selfhood" and rises into God in full <term>resignation<note>Original: "Gelassenheit." This is a central concept in German mysticism, referring to a state of yieldedness, letting go of the ego, and serene surrender to God.</note></term>.

Therefore, if we wish to attain true living knowledge, it is necessary that we withdraw our will, senses, and mind from all earthly things and turn them toward Christ’s suffering, death, and resurrection. We must continually crucify the <term>old Adam<note>A theological term for the fallen, sinful nature of humanity inherited from the biblical first man.</note></term> through the death of Christ, and always die to sin in the death and dying of Christ; and with Him, we must always rise again from the anguish of death as a "new man" and flourish in the life of God. This "flourishing" is nothing other than a transfiguration and revelation of God through Christ within us.

**3. Question:** I thought that if one had faith as small as a mustard seed, he could move mountains and reach a light where he would have pure peace and joy; but you speak to me of nothing but the cross, death, dying, and the like?

**Answer:** The true light drives out the darkness with all its power and all its works. Thus, the cross and suffering—even death and dying—are the proper test of true light and living knowledge. Where such a light is used rightly, there life is born in death, and joy is born out of anguish. The light of God opens itself; thus, that is precisely what true faith is in a person: that he dies to his "selfhood"—that is, his own desire—and leads his desire in all its beginnings and intentions into God’s will. He claims no action as his own but considers himself in all his doings only as God’s servant and minister, thinking that everything he does and intends, he does for God.

<column-break/>

Then, in such an intention, the Spirit leads him into true faithfulness and honesty toward his neighbor; for he thinks: I do not do my work for myself, but for my God, who has called and appointed me to it as a servant in His vineyard. He always listens for the voice of his Lord to hear what He commands him within himself, and what he should do; the Lord speaks in him and commands his actions. But "selfhood" does what the external reason wants, influenced by the stars; into this reason, the "flying-in" Devil introduces himself with his desire. Everything that selfhood does is outside of God’s will; it all happens in "fantasy," in which the wrath of God drives away His delight.

No work outside of God’s will can reach God’s kingdom; it is all merely useless "carving" <note>Original: "Schnitz-Werck." Used here to mean artificial, man-made efforts that lack organic spiritual life.</note> produced in the great toil of men. For nothing pleases God except what He Himself does through the will. For there is only one God in the essence of all essences, and everything that works with Him in that same essence is one spirit in Him. But whatever works in its own selfhood and its own will is outside of His governance, existing in itself. To be sure, it is within His almighty governance by which He rules all life, but not in the *Holy Divine Governance* within Himself; rather, it is in the Governance of Nature, in which He rules over both evil and good. Nothing is called "Divine" that does not move and work within God’s will.

"All plants," says Christ, "which my Father has not planted, shall be rooted out and burned in the fire." <note>A reference to Matthew 15:13.</note> All the works of man which he performs outside of God’s will shall all burn in the final fire of God and be given over to the wrath of God—as the abyss of darkness—for eternal "delight." <note>Here "delight" is used ironically to describe the grim satisfaction of divine justice or the consuming nature of the abyss.</note> For Christ says: "He who is not with me is against me, and he who does not gather with me scatters." <note>A reference to Matthew 12:30.</note> He who does not work and act in a resigned will, trusting in Him...

# On True Faith.

Therefore, all that happens through the conclusions of human <term>selfhood<note>German: "Selbstheit." A key term in Jacob Boehme’s mysticism, referring to the ego-driven nature that seeks its own will instead of God's.</note></term> in divine knowledge and will is nothing but fable and <term>Babel<note>Used here to signify spiritual confusion and the prideful attempt to reach God through human effort, referring to the biblical Tower of Babel.</note></term>. It is merely a work of the stars and the outer world, and it is not recognized by God as His work; rather, it is a game of the struggling wheel of nature, where good and evil wrestle with each other. What the good builds, the evil breaks, and what the evil builds, the good breaks. This is the great misery of wasted effort, which all belongs to the judgment of God, to the separation of the conflict.

Therefore, whoever works and builds much in such toil works only for the judgment of God: for there is nothing perfect or permanent; everything must pass into <term>putrefaction<note>Original: "Putrefaction." An alchemical term for the decomposition of matter, which mystical writers used to describe the necessary "decay" of the old self before a new spiritual life can arise.</note></term> and be separated. For what is wrought in God’s wrath is taken up by Him and kept in the <term>mystery<note>Original: "Mysterio." Referring to the hidden storehouse or the "Mysterium Magnum" where all things are recorded and preserved.</note></term> of His desire until the Day of Judgment, when evil and good shall be separated.

But if man now turns back, and departs from selfhood, and enters into God’s will, then the good that he wrought in selfhood will also be released from the evil that he wrought. For Isaiah says: *Though your sins be red as blood, if you turn back and repent, they shall become white as snow like wool.* For the evil is swallowed up in death within the wrath of God, and the good comes forth like a plant from the wild earth.

4. **Question:** Now I see how urgently necessary the path of <term>self-denial<note>Original: "Verläugnung." The act of renouncing one's own ego and desires to follow God.</note></term> is for true knowledge. But what is the closest and surest way of such following? For one often tends to delay oneself more than to progress through one's own well-meaning rules and practices.

**Answer:** We cannot better learn the nearest footsteps of Jesus than by surrendering ourselves in

<column-break/>

faithful obedience to the guiding and chastening hand of God. As soon as a soul makes a serious resolution to carefully tread the path of salvation, his evil nature becomes truly rebellious. The storm of hell begins immediately, and great unrest, persecution, and shame from the devil and the corrupt world come upon the outer, sinful man. There, the outer sinful man must allow himself to be judged by God’s strict justice in wrath, by the children of wrath, because another man lives within him who is not like the outer, mortal man. Thus, in Christ’s <term>process<note>Original: "Process." Referring to the sequence of Christ's life, suffering, and death as a blueprint or pattern for the believer's own spiritual development.</note></term>, man is sacrificed to the justice of God in wrath through contempt and mockery in his suffering and death, and becomes like the image of Christ.

<margin>Epistle 46, 26, 27.</margin>

5. **Question:** How then does faith lead us to such a living knowledge of God?

**Answer:** When the desire of faith proceeds into the spirit of our <term>mind<note>Original: "Gemüth." This encompasses the soul, disposition, and the inner emotional-intellectual core of a person.</note></term> and takes hold of its highest understanding, it draws the life of God into itself, which awakens the seed-grain of divine grace in the soul, and this drives toward a new growth and birth. The stronger and more powerful the faith, the stronger is the driving and growth of the **new birth**; and the stronger the new birth, the more glorious and living is the knowledge and the true vision of God. It is, however, quite impossible to write about this, for no one understands it except him who enters into it. He becomes a completely different person in his mind; he is taught by God and sees how all the activity in <term>history<note>Original: "Historia." Here used to mean knowledge based on outward reports, books, or tradition rather than internal, living experience.</note></term> without God’s Spirit is only a confused, Babylonic work from which strife and conflict arise in one’s own pride: for they only intend pride and their own exaltation, to delight themselves in the lusts of the flesh. All those who boast of a true knowledge of God outside of the new birth, and even presume to teach others, are indeed not servants of Christ, but of the **Antichrist**. They have sat themselves upon Christ’s throne but built it in this world.

# Part 1 / Chapter 4.

But Christ’s kingdom is not of this world, but stands in power; and there is no true knowledge in any person unless they are reborn in GOD out of their corrupted house of sin. In this rebirth, the <term>wrath<note>Original: "Grimm." In this context, it refers to the harsh, fiery quality of nature that has been separated from God’s light.</note></term> is transformed into love, and the person becomes a priest of GOD in the life of JESUS Christ, always seeking what is in heaven and within the wonders of GOD. The new man is hidden within the old, not belonging to this world, but dwelling in the <term>Holy Ternary<note>Original: "Ternario Sancto." A mystical term referring to the spiritual "body" or manifestation of the Holy Trinity.</note></term>, in the Holy Body of JESUS Christ—that is to say, in the power of His body.

6. **Question:** It is easy to understand that without a true spiritual rebirth, no one can have a certain and living knowledge; yet, can a person not grasp some knowledge of God through logic and rational conclusions—such as from the works of creation, proving that a GOD exists? *etc.*

**Answer:** All such knowledge is far from sufficient, nor is it enough for salvation. Christ says: **I am the vine, you are the branches; whoever abides in me will bring forth much fruit, for without me you can do nothing.** Likewise: **Whoever abides in me, and my words in him, brings forth much fruit.**

In this lies the entire foundation, and it is the single root to the fountain from which Divine understanding flows. There is no other foundation for true and right knowledge in the wisdom of GOD; no other seeking, studying, or researching helps. For every spirit searches only its own depths and that in which it is ignited. Even though a spirit may search within its own "ignition" or passion, it finds nothing more than a mere image of the thing, like a shadow or a dream. It cannot behold the <term>Essence<note>Original: "Wesen." Refers to the actual, living reality or "being" of God as opposed to a mere idea or description.</note></term>. If it wishes to behold the Essence, it must be *in* the Essence, and the Essence in it, so that it may be capable of it and see within the Essence itself. But since we have died to the Divine Essence in <term>Adam<note>Referring to the "Fall of Man," where the original human state of connection to God was lost.</note></term> and have become 

<column-break/>

blind and as strangers, there is no power of our own within us. In our <term>reason<note>Original: "Vernunfft." Used here to describe human intellectual logic, which the author argues is blind to spiritual reality.</note></term>, we know nothing of GOD but mere <term>histories<note>Original: "Historien." This refers to "head-knowledge"—knowing stories about God from books without experiencing His presence directly.</note></term>. We do not feel His power; we do not see His light, unless we turn back and become like children who know nothing, who allow themselves to be cared for and governed. And just as a child looks to its mother and longs for her, and she in turn nourishes and raises it, so must our reason be completely blinded, cast down, and dampened. Reason must throw itself with desire into GOD’s grace and love, disregarding the resistance of the external mind which says: **“It is not true; GOD is far away; you must recognize Him [intellectually]; you must research His will as He has revealed it.”** It is in this way, and no other, that reason wants to be known.

This is how the external, historical, and spiritless reason judges—the very reason that governs the entire world, except for a tiny "little flock" of the children of GOD. Christ said: **“You must abide in me, for without me you can do nothing; you can know nothing of GOD and research nothing true. For whoever comes to me, I will not cast out; with me, you will bring forth much fruit.”** For every branch grows upon its own tree and possesses the tree's sap, power, and character, and it brings forth fruit according to the tree's nature.

Thus, anyone who wishes to be taught by GOD and desires to have Divine knowledge must stand in the tree into which GOD has planted us through the spiritual rebirth. He must have the sap and power of that same tree; otherwise, he brings forth strange, wild fruits that do not have the taste of the good tree. We must become like a child who understands nothing but only knows its mother and longs for her. We must drink from the new milk of the Incarnation of Christ, so that we may partake of His flesh and spirit; His power and sap must become our sap and power—
