# On the True Faith.

...forth: We must become God's children through divine eating and drinking. Nicodemus said: "How can this happen, that a person can be born differently in their old age?" Yes, dear Nicodemus, and dear outer reason—how could it happen that Adam, who was indeed a perfect image of God, decayed in his perfection and became earthly? Did it not happen through **imagination**, in that he introduced his longing and desire into the outer starry and elemental kingdom? Since he was then immediately impregnated in his desire, longing, and imagination, he became earthly, whereby he fell into the sleep of outer **magic**.<note>original: "Magiæ." In this context, "magic" refers to the creative or shaping power of the will and desire.</note> **Note.** This is also how it happens with the **New Birth**: through imagination and earnest desire, we become pregnant with the Godhead again and receive the new body within the old. The new does not mix with the old, just as **gold**<term>gold<note>The original uses the alchemical symbol ☉. Here it represents the divine spirit hidden within the "stone" of the physical body.</note></term> in a stone is an entirely different thing, having a different spirit and **tincture**<term>tincture<note>A term from alchemy and theosophy referring to a spiritual essence or "dye" that can transform the quality of a substance.</note></term> than the coarse matter in the stone. So also is the new person within the old; the coarse stone knows nothing of the **gold**, and likewise, the earthly Adam knows nothing of the divine, heavenly Adam.

Therefore, there is a conflict within the person, and the person is at odds with themselves. The earthly Adam wants to see, feel, and taste, but he only receives a ray and a precursor from the inner person, though at times he tastes something—not essentially, but rather just as the sun’s light swallows the mournful darkness so that it seems as if no darkness were there anymore, while the darkness truly remains hidden in the light, which becomes manifest when the sun’s light withdraws.

Thus the new person often swallows the old in divine power, so that the old one thinks he has grasped the Godhead; but he is not capable of its essence. Instead, the Spirit of God passes through the old from the new, and when the Spirit returns to its **mystery**<note>original: "Mysterium." The hidden, underlying reality of God.</note>, the old person does not know what has happened to him, but seeks ways to God, searches

<column-break/>

for God’s purpose and will, and finds only trifles and opinions; he is zealous in his opinion and does not know what he is doing. He does not find the root, for he is neither capable nor worthy of it, as evidenced by his death and decay.

But the new person, who originates through **imagination** in earnest will and purpose, remains in the rest of Christ, in the tree that God the Father planted into the human soul—standing and turning green in the life of God—when He moved Himself for the second time according to His heart. This person grows in the power and the sap of God’s **essence**<note>original: "Wesenheit."</note> in God’s love; they receive divine knowledge and science, not according to the measure of the outer will (what the outer self wants to know), but according to the measure of the inner heaven.

The inner heaven ignites the outer, so that the understanding grasps and comprehends the outer. For with the outer world, God—who is a Spirit and also a Being—has revealed Himself in a likeness, so that the Spirit and Being might behold itself. And not only that, but also that the creature might behold and recognize God’s Being in the form; for no creature can behold God’s Being outside of itself. The Spirit beholds God in the essence and in the radiance of Majesty, and does so within itself and its own kind; for GOD is Himself the Spirit of all beings, but specifically understood as the Spirit of the heavenly ones. When we see the divine creature, we see an image from God’s Being, and when we see its will and deeds, we see God’s will and deeds.

Thus the new person is also born of God; what that person wills and does is God’s will and deed; their knowledge is God’s knowledge. For without God’s Spirit, we know nothing of God. The outer cannot behold the inner, but when the inner draws the outer into itself with a glance, the outer grasps the mirror of the inner as an indication that the outer world...

Therefore, understand us rightly as to what the **New Birth**<term>New Birth<note>original: "Wieder-Geburt." The outer, earthly, mortal man is not born anew in this lifetime—neither the outer flesh nor the outer part of the soul. The outer man, in both soul and flesh—meaning the outer part of the soul—possesses no divine will and understands nothing of God, just as the Scripture says: *The natural man perceives nothing of the Spirit of God,* etc. But the fire-breath of the inner world, once it is enlightened, does understand; it has its great groaning, lamenting, hungering, and thirsting after the **sweet fountain of Christ**. And this is the reason why the fiery soul cannot reach perfection during this life: it remains tied to the outer bond of vanity, through which the Devil constantly shoots his poisonous rays at it, sifting it so that it sometimes "bites" at his bait and becomes poisoned. Then the struggle begins within the whole man: the outer fleshly man lusts against the inner spiritual man, and the spiritual against the fleshly. One who has the outward appearance of holiness or intellectual "light" but lacks the inner substance of the "Pearl."</note></term> out of itself, regarding itself as divine even though the Pearl is gone. Many remain in this state and often perish.

8. **Question:** Since there is such great self-deception in man—that he takes his own **astral reason**<term>astral reason<note>original: "gestirnte Vernunft." The intellect influenced by the "stars" or the natural, fallen world, as opposed to divine wisdom.</note></term> for God's wisdom and its luster for true knowledge—tell me, how shall an untrained person thoroughly distinguish this in himself and others?

**Answer:** Man finds the most certain test of the truth of Divine knowledge and the **New Birth** nowhere more surely than in an impartial examination of his own will, desire, senses, and mind. For as soon as the growth of the **New Man** rises up, he also possesses his own sight. Just as the outer man sees the outer world, so also the new man sees the Divine world in which he dwells. For it is written: *The spirit of man, in the Spirit of Christ, searches all things, even the depths of the Godhead.* And although it does not depend on intellectual searching and soaring—if man wishes to search only within his reason—it depends instead on humble surrender, so that the soul desires nothing but God's love. As soon as the soul reaches that love, the joy-filled Spirit of God immediately leads the soul's image (or the **Likeness of God**) into the heavenly, Divine school of noble, precious knowledge. There she is taught more than in the schools of this world, for she studies in the school of **Divine Wisdom**. The Holy Spirit is her schoolmaster, and also her knowledge and understanding.

There is no knowledge of God where a creature might know or feel God except

<column-break/>

only in this: that the creature is *in* God, as a branch within the sap of the tree. If the spirit, with its will-spirit, is not directed into God but rather into the outer reason, it is blind to God. But if it earnestly desires God, it becomes pregnant with God's essence through its desire, and God's essence is given to it as its own property. Within this, the Spirit of God governs, and the person becomes a child of God, like a branch on a tree. If a man knows this branch of the **New Birth**, he also knows the eternal birth in God; his living, greening, and fruit-bearing is God's life, for he is God's own likeness and property. For the book in which all secrets are contained—the **Great Arcanum**<term>Great Arcanum<note>original: "grosse Arcanum." Latin for "Great Secret" or "Great Mystery," referring to the hidden inner workings of God and Nature.</note></term>—lies within him alone. The revealing of it belongs to the Spirit of God. But when the **Lily**<note>The lily is a symbol of the blossoming of the spiritual life and the purity of the New Birth.</note> of the New Birth greens forth from God's humanity, then the Spirit of God proceeds from the Lily out of its eternal origin and ground; that same Spirit seeks and finds all hidden things within the Divine Wisdom.

<margin>Theosophical Epistles 20. §. 3. 4. 5. 27. §. 54.</margin>

For just as a branch has the life within itself which the tree also has, so the **Regenerated** person has within himself God's Spirit and Essence, from which, through which, and to which all things live, move, and have their being.

Through this Spirit, he recognizes the structure of all nature, and through this key he can unlock all secrets—thoroughly distinguishing all their beginnings, births, pains, governance, life, and death. He has the power to look into all the wonders that are in nature; he can subdue the starry heaven, just as **Joshua** commanded the sun to stand still, and **Moses** commanded the sea to stand, and also commanded the darkness to come. He can tame and subdue the devils, provided he is in God and the Holy Spirit leads him in the ways of the soul.

<margin>See 40 Questions, 6.</margin>

# Of True Faith.

**N 3**

<meta>catchword: There-</meta>

From all of this, a reader who hungers for salvation will easily be able to see through what eyes our **highly enlightened author**<note>Referring to Jacob Böhme (1575–1624), the German mystic whose works this text introduces.</note> has seen, and from what spirit he has written these high mysteries; also what kind of spirit and eyes anyone must have who wishes to thoroughly understand these things, without which these writings would serve him more for offense and ruin. We have already reminded the reader sufficiently above, and remind him herewith: that whoever does not wish to enter into the knowledge of these high mysteries through this door of **earnest repentance**, **zealous prayer**, **living faith**, **active love**, and true <term>New Birth<note>original: "Wieder-Geburt." The core mystical process of spiritual transformation and the central theme of Böhme's "The Way to Christ."</note></term>, is regarded here as nothing other than a **thief and a murderer**<note>A reference to John 10:1: "He that entereth not by the door... the same is a thief and a robber."</note>; he will also, with all his meditating, speculating, discussing, and chattering, steal and rob nothing but empty opinions and vain science, without truth, spirit, and life, to his own judgment and ruin. Therefore, we have placed this first part forward to direct every earnest reader to the right door and true entrance into the **Palace of Divine Wisdom**, so that he may be found therein as a home-born, natural member of the household, and not as a foreign thief and murderer, a loose chatterer, a sophist, or a deceiver. We set here the author's faithful warning for everyone to consider well upon his conscience before GOD.

The Spirit, therefore, invites and summons all straying and Devil-seduced people to the school for this **Mirror**; there they shall look into the heart of the **Murderous Devil**. Whoever will not guard himself against his lies, even though he well can, for him there is no counsel either here or there: whoever wants to sow with him will also reap with him. In the **Center of the Flash**<note>original: "Centro des Blitzes." A Böhmean term referring to the sudden, transformative moment of divine revelation or the "lightning-bolt" of spiritual insight.</note> it is proven that the harvest is already quite white; there everyone will reap what he has sown.

Here I will lend out my entrusted **pound at interest**<note>A reference to the Parable of the Talents/Minae (Luke 19:11-27), where a servant is expected to trade and gain interest on the money entrusted to him by his master.</note>, as I have been commanded. Whoever now wants to profit and trade with me shall be free to do so, whether he be a **Christian, Jew, Turk, or Heathen**; it is all the same to me; my **Merchant House** shall stand open to everyone, and no one shall be defrauded or cheated, but shall be treated with justice.

There let everyone take heed how he trades, so that he may earn profit for his Lord; for I fear indeed that

<column-break/>

not every merchant will be suited for my wares, since they will be quite unknown to many, and not everyone will understand my language.

Therefore, I would have everyone warned to trade cautiously and not let himself imagine that he is rich and cannot become poor. Truly, I have wonderful wares for sale; not everyone will understand them.

Now, if someone were to blunder in according to his own clumsy way and fall into ruin, he may blame himself; he certainly needs a light in his heart so that his understanding and mind might be governed. Otherwise, let him not come to my **Merchant House**, or he deceives himself; for the wares that I have for sale are very noble and precious, and require a very sharp understanding. Therefore, look out for yourself, and do not climb into the heights where you see no ladder, or you will fall. But to me, **Jacob’s Ladder**<note>Genesis 28:10-19. Böhme uses this as a symbol for the mystical ascent through the levels of reality to reach God.</note> has been shown, upon which I have climbed even into Heaven and have received my wares, which I have for sale. If anyone now wants to climb after me, let him also see that he is not drunk, but he must be girded with the **Sword of the Spirit**.

For he must climb through a cruel depth; dizziness will often come into his head. Moreover, he must climb right through the **Kingdom of Hell**. What mockery and scorn he will have to suffer there, he will certainly experience. I have often had to experience it in this struggle with a sad heart; the sun has often gone out for me, but risen again—and the oftener it went out, the brighter and more beautiful it rose again. I do not write this for my own praise, but so that if it should go likewise for you, you do not entirely despair; for a very rigorous labor belongs to this, for whoever wants to fight with the Devil between Heaven and Hell, for he is a powerful prince.

# Part 1 / Chapter 4. Of True Faith.

Therefore, see to it / that you wear the **armor of the Spirit**<note>original: "Panzer des Geistes." This alludes to the "whole armor of God" described in Ephesians 6, suggesting that reading this book is a form of spiritual engagement.</note> / otherwise do not even come to my **marketplace**<note>original: "Kauff-Hauß." You must renounce the **devil and the world** / if you wish to fight / otherwise you will not conquer; but if you do not conquer / then leave my book in peace / and remain with your old ways / or you will receive a bad reward. Do not be deceived / **God is not mocked.**<note>Galatians 6:7.</note>

It is indeed a **narrow path** / that seeks to press through the **gates of hell** to God / it must suffer many a pressure and squeeze from the devil. For human flesh is very young and tender / and the devil is rough and hard / additionally dark / hot / bitter / sharp / and cold: these two fit poorly together.

<column-break/>

Therefore I would have the reader faithfully warned / as with a preface to these great mysteries / if he does not understand this matter / and yet would gladly understand it / that he should pray to God for His **Holy Spirit** / that He would enlighten him with the same.

Without the enlightenment of the Spirit, you will not understand this mystery / for there is a **strong fortress** in the spirit of man against it / which must first be unlocked; and no human can do that / for the Holy Spirit alone is the **key** to it.

Therefore / if you wish to have an open gate into the **Godhead** / then you must dwell in God's love. I have placed this here for your instruction.

->**Aurora**, chapter 13, §§ 14, 28.<-

Part 2 / Chapter 1.

# Chapter 1.
## Of GOD / what He is / and how a human being may know GOD.

In the first part, we have shown the reader who thirsts for salvation the safest and most excellent <note>The original "all-" is likely a fragment of "allerbeste" (best/most excellent).</note> gate for entering into a true, living knowledge of GOD and of oneself: Namely, that if one is in right earnest to change one’s mind and to practice the true obedience of faith, following JESUS, the Captain of our salvation, in the New Birth, and to surrender oneself to the service of Wisdom, we wish here to give further instruction on what and how one should practice in the House of Wisdom, in order to contemplate GOD’s wonders and to glorify Him in His life.

<column-break/>

**1. Question.**

I have a great desire to honor GOD holily, as a GOD, and also to prepare myself thoroughly so that GOD may open the wonders of His love and mercy in me, who am unworthy and miserable. Dear friend, please give me further instruction: how may I worthily know and glorify GOD?

->**Answer.**<-

When the Sun of Grace rises in the soul with its effective power, the soul rejoices and always desires to see GOD’s face in a creaturely way, just as Moses desired; it constantly thinks that GOD must be something formal <note>original: "Förmliches." Böhme uses this to describe something with a specific, limited shape or external appearance.</note>, imagining that it does not see GOD correctly, and wishes to know GOD in imagery. Creaturely imagery lies so heavily upon us in our departed self-will within the mind, that we can understand nowhere what GOD is, except that He Himself is the Abyss <term>Abgrund: A fundamental term in Böhme’s thought (often related to the *Ungrund*), referring to the "bottomless" or "foundationless" nature of God before any creation or form exists.</term> of all nature and creatures, as the Eternal One who dwells in nothing but Himself alone, and has no form nor anything else. And it would be right and good if we were not led into such figurative forms by the masters of the letter <note>The "masters of the letter" refers to scholars and theologians who rely on literal scriptural interpretation without inward spiritual experience.</note> when one teaches and speaks of the one GOD, as has happened until now—leading us into mere images within the essential will, as if the one GOD willed this or that, when He Himself is the only Will toward creature and nature, and the

<column-break/>

entire Creation lies solely and uniquely within the formation of His breathed-out Word-Will, and the differentiation of the single Will in its speaking is understood as the enclosure into nature.

If the pride of Lucifer could be torn from the hearts and eyes of the masters, then one would soon see God’s face. But the Babylonian Tower <note>A reference to the Tower of Babel, symbolizing the confusion of tongues and the prideful attempt of man-made theology to reach God through intellectual effort.</note>—where people want to ascend to GOD via stairs and opinions, into a specific heaven where GOD sits locked away—misses the true knowledge and understanding. Thus we are always asking: What is His name? Where is GOD? What does GOD want? Also: He wants good and evil; from which they make various decrees of Divine Purpose, just as a prince makes laws in his land. They have just as much understanding of GOD and His will as the pot understands of its potter.

It is to be lamented that we are thus led astray and the truth is given out in images; for when the Divine Power becomes clear and active with its luster in the inward ground of the soul, so that the human being resolves to leave the godless way and surrender to GOD, then the entire Trinity <note>original: "der ganze Dre..." The text likely intends "Dreifaltigkeit" (Trinity).</note> of GOD is present in the soul’s life and movement. This is the heaven where GOD dwells, opened within the soul; and that very place is there in the soul where the Father begets His Son, and where the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son.

<summary>This page defines God not as a physical form or a distant ruler, but as the formless Abyss and the Eternal One who is experienced internally within the soul's "House of Wisdom." It critiques "Babylonian" theology for trapping God in intellectual images and arbitrary laws.</summary>

# Of GOD in Himself.
D
<meta>catchword: sel-</meta>

For GOD requires no specific physical location; He also dwells in the abyss <term>Abgrund: Literally "without ground." In Böhme's thought, this refers to the primal void or the depth of the soul where God's presence is felt either as light or as consuming fire.</term> of godless souls—but to those souls, He is not graspable according to His love, but is instead manifest and graspable according to His wrath. For the eternal speaking of the Word (according to its incomprehensibility to nature and creaturely beings) becomes an image according to the will of the soul, of which the Scripture says: *With the holy you are holy, and with the perverse you are perverse.* <note>Original Latin context: Psalm 18:26-27. Böhme suggests God appears to us reflecting our own internal state.</note> Likewise: *Whatever kind of people they are, they have such a GOD.* For in the thrones of the holy angels, GOD is manifest in His love; but in the thrones of the devils, He is manifest in His fury, as darkness and painfulness—and yet He is only one single GOD and not two. According to the nature of painfulness, He wills painfulness; and according to love, He wills love. Just as a burning fire desires only resinous sulfur according to its own kind, while the light from the fire desires nothing but an open place where it may shine: it takes nothing, but gives itself for the joy of life; it only allows itself to be taken, and has no other will within itself than to give itself and to work good. Thus also GOD, according to His holiness, has no other will within Himself than that He wishes to manifest His power of love and radiance (in creaturely form), just as the sun manifests itself in a plant and tints it and makes it good—so it is also to be understood regarding GOD.

Therefore, it is all useless chatter and creaturely imagery when people ask: "What is GOD’s name?" Or when people say much about how "He wills this or that, evil or good," yet know nothing of the "Ground" <note>The "Ground" refers to the underlying source or foundation of existence.</note> to explain *how* He wills evil and good. This struggle over the letters of the law is truly the "confused tongue" at the high tower of the children of Nimrod in Babel, where one people does not understand the other; they bicker over the one GOD in whom we live and exist, through whom the kingdom of nature is made manifest and brought into figurative wonders.
<margin>Mysterium Magnum 60. §. 40. 48.</margin>

<column-break/>

**2. Question.** What then is GOD, actually?

**Answer.** I cannot describe the entire Godhead to you in a single circle, for it is immeasurable; yet to the spirit that is within GOD’s love, it is not incomprehensible. The spirit understands it well, but only piece by piece; therefore, grasp one thing after another, and you will see the whole.
<margin>Aurora 10. §. 26.</margin>

**3. Question.** If one can only recognize GOD piece by piece, as He has manifested Himself in the creaturely world, then, dear friend, where should one begin to seek and recognize GOD?

**Answer.** GOD is considered by us either as He is in and for Himself, outside and above nature and creatures, or how He has introduced Himself into nature and creatures and manifested Himself therein. GOD, as He is in Himself outside of nature and creatures, is the **eternal Unity**, the immeasurable single Good, which has nothing behind it or before it that might give it something or contribute to it, or that might move it. He is without any inclinations or specific properties, and without the origin of time He is only "One" within Himself—like a sheer purity without touch, which has no place or position anywhere, nor requires any for His dwelling. Instead, He is simultaneously outside the world and in the world, and is deeper than a thought can soar. Yes, even if one spoke numbers for 100,000 years regarding His greatness and depth, one would still not have begun to express His depth, for He is Infinity. Everything that can be counted and measured is "imagistic" <note>original: "bildlich." Referring to things that have a form or shape that the mind can visualize.</note>, but the Unity of GOD cannot be spoken, for it is through everything all at once.
<margin>Theosophical Questions 1. §. 1.</margin>

He is like an **eternal Nothing**, of which one can form no thought or image. He possesses nothing but Himself; He births Himself...

Himself from eternity to eternity within Himself. The Holy Scripture testifies that He dwells in a light where no one can come. The most secret beholders of God, in their high and deep knowledge and communion with God, have finally had to confess that God in Himself cannot be known otherwise than by negation <note>original: "per Negativam"</note>, that is: through that which He actually is not.

**4. Question: Does God then, in Himself, outside of Nature, have no attributes or names by which one might recognize Him in some measure?**

**Answer:** Here we wish to remind the reader that God in Himself (insofar as He is called God outside of Nature and creaturely existence) has no more than a single will, which is that He gives and begets Himself. The God JEHOVAH begets nothing but God, that is: He begets only Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, into the single Divine power and wisdom.

Just as the sun has only one single will, which is that it gives itself and, with its desire, penetrates and grows in all things, giving power to all life and energizing itself: so also, in the same way, God is outside of Nature and creaturely existence—the single Good that can or will give nothing but God, or the Good. Outside of Nature, He is the greatest gentleness and humility, wherein neither a will toward good nor evil inclination is sensed, for there is neither evil nor good before Him; He is Himself the single eternal Good, and a beginning of all good essence and will. It is also not possible that anything evil could penetrate into Him, insofar as He is that same single Good, for He is a "Nothing" to all things that come after Him. He is an actual, essential spiritual power within Himself, the most sublime and simplest humility and benevolence—namely: a feeling of Love, a tasting of Love, in the sense <note>original: "Sensu"</note> of sweet birthing, a well-disposed and willing hearing.

<column-break/>

For all the senses harmonize in concord, and there is nothing but the spiritual surge of the Holy Spirit's single wisdom. There one can [find] neither an angry God, nor a [biting] God; for within this there is no [cause] for anger, nor any cause [to harm], for He is the single Love itself, who leads and [gives] Love in the Trinity.

<margin>Election of Grace, ch. 1, §. 18-21.</margin>
Thus God, outside of Nature [and creation], has no name, but is called alone the [One] Good, the <term>Unground: "Ungrund" in the original German; it refers to the primal, bottomless abyss or the absolute "Nothing" from which God's will and all existence emerge.</term> and ground of all things. In Him no place is found, [therefore] no creature can name Him; for all names stand in the formed word, but God Himself is the root of all [things], without beginning or name.

<margin>Mysterium Magnum, ch. 60, §. 38.</margin>
In the Unground outside of Nature, it is [like] a stillness without essence; it has nothing that gives anything; it is an eternal [peace], and no equal; an Unground [without] beginning and end. There is also no [goal], no place, no seeking or finding. [It is] a will after which we should not [strive] or search, for it [disturbs]. By this same will, we understand the [inner] Ground of the Godhead, which has no [origin]; for it encompasses itself within itself, [where] we are rightfully silent, for it is [outside] Nature.

<margin>The Incarnation, part 2, ch. 1, §. 8.</margin>
If you now wish to know who, what, [and where] God is, then take away Nature and [the] creature; then God is everything. If you say: "[I] cannot," for if that should happen, then [I would be] a nothing. Therefore, I must model the [Godhead] for myself through images, because I [know] that within me is evil and good, as [in] the whole of creation.

Listen, my brother: God has [forbidden] making an image or likeness of Him. Therefore, the closest way [is] that the image of God within oneself sinks away from all [imagined] images, and all images [The...]

<meta>The previous page concluded with a description of God as an essential, non-manifested "Nothing" or "Goodness" that precedes all nature and will. # Of GOD in Himself.

...and abandon conflict within oneself / and despair of one’s own will / desiring, and opinion / and sink and trust oneself purely and alone into the eternal **One** / as into the pure, single love of God.

<margin>The Election of Grace, chapter 1, sections 28, 29.</margin>

5. **Question:** Is God, then, outside of Nature and creation as the eternal Nothing and the <term>Abyss</term> <note>original: "Ungrund"; in this context, it refers to the "groundless" or "unfathomable" source of all being that exists before manifestation</note>, something separated from the God who has revealed Himself in Nature and creation?

**Answer:** The sun in the sky, and the sun within the creatures, is just one and the same sun; it is of one property, one quality, power, and effect. In the same way, God outside of Nature and creation, and God in Nature and creation, is one single God, highly praised in eternity. But just as the sun works in a particular thing according to the idea and property of that particular <note>The author suggests that while the sun is one, its effect depends on what it shines upon—melting wax but hardening clay.</note>, so God works in Nature and creation according to the image and kind of the creature. In one that is adverse and hostile, He acts as an angry, jealous God; in one who is at one with God, as love and peace; in one who is humble, poor, and miserable, as a merciful God; in one who is repentant, as a gracious God; "holy among the holy / pure among the pure / upright among the upright / and perverse among the perverse." <note>This is a paraphrase of Psalm 18:25-26, expressing that God reflects the internal state of the person seeking Him.</note>

Just as we cannot grasp the light of the sun unless we have eyes that possess the sun’s own property so that we may see: so we cannot behold God—even though He is before us every moment and the Godhead is within us—unless we place our <term>imagination</term> <note>original: "Imagination"; here meaning the soul's ability to focus its internal desire and form its spiritual reality</note> and earnest will into God. Then God appears in the will and fills the mind, where we then feel God and see Him with our eyes. But if we place our will and imagination into wickedness, we receive the torment of hell in wrath, and the devil seizes our heart in the wrath of God.

<margin>The Threefold Life, chapter 2, sections 51, 52.</margin>

According to how a person's imagination is formed and set in love or in wrath, so God becomes manifest therein. For the pure Godhead is entirely present everywhere / in all places and ends. The birth of the Holy Trinity in one <term>Essence</term> <note>original: "Wesen"</note> is everywhere, and the angelic world reaches to all ends, wherever you might think, even in the middle of the earth, stones, and rocks. So too is hell / or the realm of wrath present everywhere in all places.

<margin>The Threefold Life, chapter 1, sections 50, 51.</margin>

Therefore / if you wish to contemplate a star, an animal, a herb, a stone, or any creature, you should not think that its Creator dwells somewhere far above the stars in a heaven; rather, He is in the creature itself.

When a person looks at the depths above the earth, he sees nothing but stars and watery clouds; then he thinks: "There must be another place where the Godhead shows itself with the heavenly and angelic <term>governance</term> <note>original: "Regiment"; the divine order or ruling power</note>." He simply wants to distinguish the depths, along with their governance, from the Godhead, for he sees nothing there but stars, and the governance between them is fire, air, and water. Then he thinks: "GOD made that out of His purpose from NOTHING; how could God be in that essence, or how could that be God Himself?" He always imagines it is just like a house, in which God rules and dwells with His Spirit; as if God could not be a God whose being consists in the power of this governance.

Many might well say: "What kind of God would that be, whose body, essence, and power stood in fire, air, water, and earth?" Behold, you incomprehensible man, I will show you the true ground of the Godhead: if this entire essence is not God, then you are not God’s image; if there is some foreign god elsewhere, then you have no part in him. For you are created out of this GOD, and you live in the same, and the same constantly gives you power, blessing, food, and drink from within Himself; also all your knowledge stands in this God, and when you die, you are buried in this God.

Now, if there were a foreign god who is outside of this one, who then will bring you back to life out of this God in whom you have decayed?

# Chapter II.
## Concerning the Revelation of GOD in general / how the eternal GOD has introduced Himself out of Nothing into Something / out of the Groundless into Ground / out of Unity into Multiplicity / and has revealed Himself therein.

**1. Question.**
**Of these high mysteries, the highly-enlightened Author <note>A reference to the mystic Jacob Böhme (1575–1624), whose complex writings this text seeks to explain.</note> has spoken so highly and deeply that it almost disturbs me: the more I read, the less I understand?**

**Answer.**
The Author did not recognize these high mysteries all at once / but rather like one who sees the dawn <note>original: "Morgen-Röthe," a reference to Böhme’s first work, *Aurora*.</note> out of the dark night / and thus proceeds with the rising of the sun in light and knowledge / until high noon / when he can distinguish everything much more clearly than in the dawn: as he recognized it, so has he presented it. Now, if someone wishes to reach the Author’s meaning / it can happen no more suitably than by first considering the very clearest and most distinct testimonies / and thereby bringing the darker passages to true understanding.

**2. Question. Who, then, is actually the one who reveals Himself?**
**Answer.** It is the eternal and infinite GOD, the unthinkable Groundless <term>Ungrund: Böhme’s term for the absolute, bottomless void or nothingness that precedes all existence and even God’s own self-manifestation.</term>, the alone-single ONE, and the most high NOTHING, dwelling in Himself / as the eternal, immeasurable freedom.

**3. Question. How then does this invisible God reveal Himself, so that He, the Groundless, may be known in the Ground / the Nothing in Something / and the Unity in Multiplicity?**
**Answer.** Because we are by nature so very deformed / we must and can speak of this so deep mystery in no other way than in images / until we finally become free of images / and 

<column-break/>

learn to know GOD / as He is / and what He is according to His highest name. Also, Holy Scripture itself points us in all places to images and parables / and speaks of God according to our deformed understanding. If we now speak of this high ground / the Author points us to our own mind <note>original: "Gemüthe," referring to the seat of the soul’s will, thoughts, and emotions.</note>. What our mind is, we do not grasp except from its powers / the understanding and the will. The understanding conceives a thought-image <note>original: "Denck-Bild"</note>; and the will draws it to itself / in order to lead the thought-image, which is there living and raw, into an essence and to reveal it. In this way, understand us concerning GOD in a Divine sense / when we speak of the Godhead with figurative and intelligible modes of speech. GOD is an eternal, thinking, and unsearchable mind; however, the thoughts of this mind are not like our thoughts / the one who thinks is God, the thought-image that God thinks is God, the will that draws the thought-image to itself / and reveals it through its working is God, the will that fulfills and satisfies the drawing desire and longing of the first will / is also God, the longing, power, and majesty that goes out from the fulfilled will / is God. For there is nothing in God that is not God Himself.

If the eternal mind did not exist / out of which the eternal will proceeds / then there would be no God. But as it is, there is the eternal mind / which gives birth to the eternal will / and the eternal will gives birth to the eternal heart / (which diminishes the desiring will /) the heart gives birth to the light / the light the power / and the power the spirit / and that is the almighty God / who is in a changeable will. ## Chapter II.
### Concerning the Revelation of GOD in general / how the eternal GOD has introduced Himself out of Nothing into Something / out of the Abyss <note>original: "Ungrund." A central concept in this philosophy, meaning the "groundless" or "bottomless" origin of God before any creation.</note> into a Ground / out of Unity into Multiplicity / and has revealed Himself therein.

**1. Question.**
Of these high mysteries the highly enlightened Author has spoken so highly and deeply / that it almost disturbs me: the more I read / the less I understand?

The Author did not recognize these high mysteries all at once / but like one / who beholds the morning glow out of the dark night / and thus proceeds with the sun’s rising in light and knowledge / until high noon / when he can distinguish everything much more clearly than in the morning glow: as he recognized it / so he also presented it. ### 4. Question: What then is GOD’S Will specifically?

**Answer.** There is one single God, and this one God also has one single Will. However, when we speak of God’s Will, we mean the working and revelation of God’s Will in nature and in the creature. In this respect, God has a Will to eternally birth Himself in His eternal, almighty, all-sufficient Deity—namely, to desire and love Himself, and to satisfy and fulfill Himself with His own well-pleasing. This Will of God is incomprehensible to us, and therefore the Author calls it a "Nothing" in regard to our perception. He calls it "thin," like the thin and incomprehensible air that we cannot grasp or feel with our hands. He also calls it an Abyss <note>original: "Ungrund." This refers to the "groundless" or "bottomless" state of the Divine before manifestation.</note>. For though this Will is active, such activity is not manifest to us; but if this Will becomes active in "Something," then we recognize God’s Will in that Something. Outside of that "Something," however, such a Will is hidden from us, incomprehensible, and mute.

We see and find / that every life is essential <note>original: "essentialisch," meaning it possesses a fundamental essence or substance.</note> / and then we find / that it stands in the Will / for the Will is the driving force of the Essences <term>Essences (Essentien): The fundamental spiritual forces or "qualities" that make up the reality of a thing.</term>. And we are to imagine it / as if a hidden fire lay in the Will / where the Will would always raise itself against the fire / and would want to awaken and ignite it. For we understand / that every Will / without the awakening of the fiery Essences / is a state of powerlessness / just as if it were mute without life / in which there is no feeling / understanding / nor being. For it is like only a shadow without substance / for it has no leader / but rather it sinks away / and lets

<column-break/>

itself be driven and led / like a dead being / as such can be perceived in a shadow / which is led without an essence.

Thus, a non-essential Will is a mute being without concept or life / and is yet a figure in the bottomless eternal Nothing / for it hangs upon corporeal things. Just as the Will without essence is mute and without substance / so it is a being and image according to the Essences / which is formed according to the Essences; for the Will's image is born out of the Essences.

Thus, the life of the Essences is the Will / and the Will / in which the figure of life stands / is the father of the Essences. No essence can arise without the Will; for in the Will, the desire is originated / in which the Essences originate. If then the eternal Will is an Abyss / to be regarded as an eternal Nothing / we then recognize it like a mirror / in which one sees one's own image / like a life / and yet it is not a life / but a figure of life and of the goal of life.

Thus, we recognize the eternal Abyss outside of nature / like a mirror. For it is like an eye / that sees / and yet carries nothing in its seeing / with which it could be something / for the seeing is without substance / it is not born out of substance / but out of the essential life. Thus, it is recognizable to us / that the eternal Abyss outside of nature is an eye / like an eye / in which nature lies hidden / like a hidden fire that does not burn / which is there / and is also not there. 5. **Question:** What then is the difference between the groundless Will / which is as a Nothing / and incomprehensible / and the Will through which GOD leads Himself out of the Nothing into Something and out of the Abyss into the Ground?

**Answer.** To Will [Wollen] actually means as much as to Well [Wallen] or to Gush [Quallen] <note>Böhme uses wordplay here to link the act of "willing" with the "welling up" or "flowing out" of a spring.</note> / that is, to constantly birth and flow out of oneself / and to constantly grasp, take in, and fulfill oneself again / which is then the infinite working and qualification of the eternal Abyss. Thus there is no further difference between the groundless and the flowing Will / than between the sea and the waters flowing out of it / which are also the sea / just like the sun / which wells up within itself / and the sun / which has that very same welling and gushing in the creatures.

# Chapter III.
### How the one GOD becomes manifest in the begetting and working of nature and creature as a triune GOD—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

-> 1. Question. <-
-> How is the doctrine of the triune GOD- <-
-> head to be understood? <-

-> Answer. <-

Because GOD is active in nature and creature as a Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, there is an irrefutable testimony that GOD begets and is born within Himself, desires and satisfies Himself, and also reveals Himself to Himself as a triune GOD. Herein consists the supreme omnipotence of GOD: that GOD eternally vivifies Himself; the highest perfection: to eternally fulfill His infinite, unfathomable desire with Himself. The highest wisdom: to eternally reveal and recognize Himself. Thus, the doctrine of the triune GODhead is such a high and unsearchable mystery that it cannot be grasped by the most magnificent human understanding. For this reason, not only the prophets but Christ and the Apostles themselves spoke very little of it, indicating that such a mystery should be honored more with silence by the holiest of men than taught with much talk and reasoning. It is therefore a terrible presumption that the <term>schoolmen [scholastics]<note>original: "Schul-Gelehrten." Refers to academic theologians who relied on logic and dogma rather than mystical experience.</note></term> drive this high mystery so hard—to the offense of the Jews and Turks—and entrust it to the smallest children as if it were the alphabet, pre-forming their minds with the <term>mental images [thought-pictures]<note>original: "Denck-Bildern."</note></term> of three persons in the GODhead without understanding.

It is well known where the word <term>Person<note>original: "Person." Derived from the Latin *persona*, meaning a mask worn by an actor.</note></term> has its origin: namely, from the <term>comedians [stage actors]<note>original: "Comödianten."</note></term> who, in their plays, represented and modeled something which they themselves were not in deed and truth. How very offensive and improper it is to use such a word for the invisible GODhead, a God-loving heart may judge. Indeed, our author <note>A reference to Jacob Böhme, the 17th-century mystic upon whose work this text is based.</note> himself often used the word "Person," but more out of habit than <term>approval<note>original: "Approbation."</note></term>, as he himself testifies.

We Christians say that GOD is threefold in essence; however, it is commonly said that GOD is threefold in persons, which is

<column-break/>

poorly understood by the ignorant. Some learned men understand GOD as a Person only in Christ, but otherwise as the eternally-begetting, active power that [is] everything together with all beings; everything takes its origin from Him.

<margin>Mysterium Magnum, Chapter 7.</margin>

2. Question: If a God-seeking heart desires to properly recognize the holy triune GODhead, how should it prepare itself for this?

Answer: Here I wish to have faithfully exhorted you that you let go of your <term>conceit [vanity]<note>original: "Dünckel." Intellectual pride or self-opinion.</note></term> and do not gape after lofty wisdom, nor be offended by the word of the author. For the word is not of his reason, but the impulse of the Spirit. See only that you have the Holy Spirit, who proceeds from GOD, within your own spirit; He will lead you into all truth and reveal Himself to you. Then, in His light and power, you will well understand the Holy Trinity and everything that is written hereafter.

<margin>Aurora, Chapter 3, Section 1.</margin>

3. Question: How does one recognize GOD the Father?

Answer: GOD the Father is recognized from that very power and working which He is in nature and creature. This power is the desiring, the attracting, as well as the driving and governing—for GOD's sake—in nature and creature. The working power is omnipotent to beget everything it wills and to bring it from <term>Nothing into Being [Essence]<note>original: "aus dem Nichts in Wesen." A central concept in Böhme's cosmogony where God manifests the world out of the "No-thing."</note></term>. It is recognized spiritually and intellectually (or understandably) in spirits, angels, and the souls of men; in visible creatures and earthly things, it is recognized visibly and bodily.

5. Qu. How does one recognize the Holy Spirit?
Ans. Just as one recognizes the <term>quality [property]<note>original: "Eigenschaft." In Böhme's thought, this refers to the specific characteristics or 'signatures' that define a being's nature.</note></term> of a plant by its scent and colors, so one recognizes the Holy Spirit; for His quality is a constant proceeding and revealing, birthing and communicating the powers of the Father and the Son.

The same <term>unfathomable [groundless]<note>original: "ungründliche." Derived from "Ungrund," referring to the absolute abyss or the "nothing" that exists before any nature or Godhead is formed.</note></term>, incomprehensible, un-natural, and un-creaturely Will—which is only one, and has nothing before it nor behind it; which in itself is only one; which is as a Nothing, and yet is Everything—is called and is the one GOD, who grasps and finds Himself within Himself, and begets God from God. Namely: the first unbeginning single Will, which is neither evil nor good, begets within itself the one eternal Good as a graspable Will, which is the Son of the unfathomable Will, and yet within the unbeginning Will, equally eternal. And this same second Will is the eternal sensitivity and findability of the first Will, where the Nothing finds itself as Something within itself; and the Unfindable—as the unfathomable Will—goes out through its eternally Found-One and leads itself into an eternal <term>contemplation [visibleness]<note>original: "Beschaulichkeit." This implies a state where God can be 'beheld' or mirrored back to Himself.</note></term> of itself.

Thus, the unfathomable Will is called the eternal Father, and the grasped, born Will of the <term>Abyss [Ungrund]<note>original: "Ungrund." This threefold Being in its

birth, in its self-contemplation of Wisdom, has ever been from eternity, and possesses within itself no other ground or place but itself. It is a single life, and a single Will without desire, and is neither thick nor thin, neither high nor deep; it is no space, nor does it possess within itself thickness or thinness, height or depth, nor space nor time nor place, but is through all in all, and yet to all as an incomprehensible Nothing.

Just as the sun’s radiance works in the whole world, in all and through all, and yet that same "all" can take nothing from the sun, but must suffer it and work with the sun’s power. In such a way is GOD considered—what He is outside of nature and creature in Himself, in a self-grasping <term>Chaos [Void]<note>original: "Chaos." # From God's Will toward Nature. 142

->Here I must now write in a parable:<- <note>original: "Gleichnis"; in Böhme’s writing, this refers to a symbolic analogy where the physical world reflects spiritual realities.</note>

In this place I will show you a parable in nature / showing how the Holy Being exists in the Holy **Trinity**. Look at the sky / it is a round sphere / and has neither beginning nor end / rather, the beginning and the end are everywhere / wherever you look upon it: even so is **God** in and above the heaven / having neither beginning nor end. Now look further at the circle of the stars / they signify the Father’s manifold power and wisdom / and they were also made out of the Father’s power and wisdom. Now, the heaven / the stars / and the entire depth between the stars / together with the earth / signify the Father / and the seven planets signify the seven spirits of **GOD** / or the Princes of the Angels / among whom Lord **Lucifer** was also one before his fall / all of whom were made out of the Father in the beginning of the creation of the angels / before the time of the world.

Now observe / the sun moves in the midst of the depth between the stars in the round circle / and it is the heart of the stars / and gives light and power to all stars / and tempers the power of all stars / so that everything becomes lovely and rich in joy. It also illuminates the heaven / the stars / and the depth above the earth / and works in all things / whatever is in this world / and is the king and the heart of all things of this world / and it truly signifies **God the Son**.

For just as the sun stands in the middle between the stars and the earth / and illuminates all powers / and is the light and heart of all powers / and all joy in this world / moreover, all beauty and loveliness exists in the sun’s light and power: so also the **Son of God** / within the Father / He is the heart in the Father / and shines in all powers of the Father / and His power is the moving, welling <note>original: "quallende"; Böhme uses this to describe a source that is both a "springing forth" and a "quality" of being.</note> joy in all the Father’s powers / and shines throughout the entire Father / just as the sun does in the entire world. If one could take away the earth / which signifies the house of misery or of hell / then the entire depth would be completely light in one place as in another: so also the entire depth in the Father is completely light in one place as in another / from the radiance of the **Son of God**. And just as the sun is a self-subsisting <note>original: "selbstständige"; meaning independent or existing in its own right.</note> creature / power or light / which does not shine out of all creatures / but into all creatures / and all creatures rejoice in its power: so also the Son in the Father is a self-subsisting person / and illuminates all power in the Father / and is the Father’s joy or heart in His center <note>original: "Centro"</note> or midst.

->Here note the great mystery of GOD.<-

The sun is born or made out of all the stars / and is the light taken from the whole of nature / and shines back into the whole nature of this world / and is bound with the other stars / as if it were one star with all the stars. So also the **Son of GOD** is always born from eternity out of all the powers of His Father / and not made / and is the heart and radiance out of all the powers of His heavenly Father / a self-subsisting person / the center <note>original: "Centrum"</note> / or in the depth the body <note>original: "Corpus"</note> of the radiance. For the Father’s power begets the Son from eternity to eternity forevermore; if the Father were to cease begetting / the Son would be no more / and if the Son no longer shone in the Father / then the Father would be a dark valley / for the Father’s power would not rise up from eternity to eternity / and the Divine Being could not consist. Thus the Father is the self-subsisting being of all powers / and the Son is the heart in the Father / who is always born out of all the powers of the Father / and who illuminates the Father’s powers in return. You must not think / that the Son is so mixed into the Father / that one cannot see or recognize His person; no / if that were so / then it would be...

### Concerning God the Holy Spirit.

**GOD** the Holy Spirit is the third person in the triumphant Holy Divinity, and proceeds from the Father and the Son; the Holy surging wellspring of joy <note>original: "Freuden-Quell"</note> in the Father, a lovely, gentle, and quiet rustling out of all the powers of the Father and the Son, as can be seen in the prophet Elijah at Mount Horeb (1 Kings 19:12) and on the Day of Pentecost with the Apostles of Christ (Acts 2).

But if one wishes to describe his person, substance, and quality from a true foundation, it must be represented in a parable <note>original: "Gleichnis"; a symbolic analogy where the physical world reflects the spiritual.</note>; for the Spirit cannot be written of, because he is not a creature, but the surging power of **GOD**. Now, look for a moment at the sun and the stars—the diverse and manifold stars, which are inexpressible and innumerable—they signify the Father. From these same stars, the sun came to be, for God made it from them; it signifies the Son of **GOD**. Now, from the sun and stars have come the four elements: Fire, Air, Water, Earth, as I will clearly prove hereafter when I write concerning the Creation.

<column-break/>

->Now observe:<-

**T**he three elements—Fire, Air, and Water—have three kinds of movement or qualification <note>original: "Qualificirung"; the specific way a substance acts or manifests its character.</note>, but only one body. See, the fire or heat raises itself up from the sun and stars, and from the heat the air raises itself, and from the air the water. And in this movement or qualification consists the life and spirit of all creatures, as well as everything that may be named in this world; and that signifies the Holy Spirit. Just as the three elements—Fire, Air, and Water—proceed from the sun and stars, and are one body within one another, and create the living movement and the spirit of all creatures in this world: so also the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son, and creates the living movement in all the powers of the Father. And just as the three elements surge in the "Depth" <note>original: "Tieffe"; a term for the vast, unformed space of the cosmos.</note> as an independent spirit, and create heat, cold, and clouds, and flow from the power of all stars—and all the powers of the sun and stars are in the three elements, as if they themselves were the sun and stars from which the life and spirit of all creatures comes and in which it consists: so the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son, and surges in the whole Father, and is the life and spirit of all powers in the whole Father.

->Here observe the deep mystery.<-

**A**ll the stars that are seen and not seen signify the power of **GOD** the Father; now, from these same stars the sun is born, which is the heart of all stars. Now, from all the stars, the power that is in each star proceeds into the Depth; now the sun’s power, heat, and radiance also go into the Depth, and in the Depth, the power of all stars is one thing with the sun’s radiance and heat—a moving surging, like a spirit or a matter—except that it does not have reason, for it is not the Holy Spirit, even though...

### Concerning the Holy Trinity.

When one speaks or writes of three persons in the Godhead, you must not think that there are therefore three Gods, where each rules and governs for himself like earthly kings on Earth. No, there is no such substance or being in **GOD**, for the Divine Being <term>Wesen: often translated as "essence" or "being," referring to the fundamental reality of a thing.</term> stands in power, and not in body or flesh. The Father is the entire Divine power from which all creatures have come, and has always been from eternity; he has no beginning nor end. The Son is in the Father, the Father's Heart or Light, and the Father begets the Son from eternity to eternity forevermore, and the Son's power and radiance shine back into the entire Father, just as the sun shines in the whole world. Now, the Son is a different person than the Father, but not outside of the Father, and

also no other **GOD** than the Father; his power, radiance, and omnipotence are no less than the entire Father. The Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son and is the third self-subsistent person in the Godhead. Just as the elements in this world proceed from the sun and stars and are the "moving spirit" in all things in this world, so also the Holy Spirit is the moving spirit in the entire Father, and proceeds from eternity to eternity evermore from the Father and the Son, and fills the entire Father; he is nothing smaller or greater than the Father and the Son; his weaving <note>original: "webende"; implies a continuous, active process of creation or maintenance, like weaving a fabric.</note> power is in the entire Father. All things in this world have come to be according to the likeness of this Trinity. You say there is but one single being in **GOD** and that **GOD** has no Son: Now open your eyes and look at yourself; a human being is made according to the likeness and out of the power of **GOD** in his Trinity. The animal, however, has arisen solely from the wild nature of this world; the stars and elements have given birth to the animals through their motion according to the will of **GOD**. Thus also does the spirit arise in birds and worms, and everything has its threefold source in the likeness of the Trinity in the Godhead. Thus, you also see the Trinity of the Godhead in wood and stones, as well as in herbs, leaves, and grass—except that these are all earthly. First is the power from which a thing becomes, whether it be wood, stone, or herb. Next, within the same, there is a sap; that is the heart of a thing. ## The IV. Chapter.
### Concerning the Wisdom and the Word of GOD, wherein the triune Godhead is revealed.

**1. Question.**
The visible things, wherein we can perceive the triune Godhead and its properties in all creatures, point us away from themselves toward the matter they represent to us; must we now consider and recognize this more closely in the spirit of our mind?

->**Answer.**<-

Just as we cannot grasp the sun and its inner birth and qualification itself, but judge it by its power and radiance: so we can recognize the triune Godhead best from its radiance and majesty, and from its effective power toward revelation. The former in the eternal Divine Wisdom <note>original: "Weißheit," often personified as Sophia</note>; the latter in the living, self-subsistent Word. Regarding Wisdom, we must consider: 1. who this Wisdom actually is, from where she originates, and what her property and effect are. 2. How the triune **GOD** becomes manifest in Wisdom, and how we may recognize such revelation.

<column-break/>

**2. Q. What, then, does the author actually understand by Wisdom?**

**Answer.** By this he actually understands that essence <note>original: "Wesen"</note> in which the triune **GOD** dwells, works, and becomes manifest; like the air, in which the sun has its radiance and shine, as if in its mirror; and like the breath, in which the inner spirit of life goes out and in, as in a vehicle <note>original: "Vehiculo oder Wagen"</note> or carriage, and harmonizes with the spirit of the great world, and strengthens itself from those properties which it has in the air. Thus Wisdom is the Divine Delight and the vehicle in which the triune **GOD** dwells, works, and is revealed. Just as the triune **GOD** is active in one creature in one way and in another differently, so Wisdom has one revelation in one and another revelation in another, and yet her birth or the lighting of her light is, in and of itself, exactly one and the same in each and every thing.

**3. Q. Does the author then not understand Wisdom or Sophia <note>The Greek name for Wisdom, often used as a proper name for the Divine Feminine in mystical thought.</note> to be a self-subsistent spirit?**

**Answer.** Everything that is from **GOD**, and is in **GOD**, is self-subsistent. But just as the radiance of the...

Now the Virgin is before **God**, and appropriates herself to the Spirit from whom the power goes out, from which she becomes the chaste Virgin of Wisdom; she is now **God’s** companion, for the honor and joy of **God**, who beholds herself in the eternal wonder of **God**,

and in that beholding she becomes longing for the wonder in the eternal Wisdom, which she yet is herself; and so she longs within herself, and her longing is the eternal **Essences**, which draw the Holy Power to themselves, and the harsh <note>original: "herbe," meaning astringent or sharp, a key quality in Böhme’s system representing the contracting force of nature.</note> **Fiat** creates it, so that it stands in Being; and she is a Virgin, and has born nothing, and also takes nothing into herself: her acceptability stands in the **Holy Spirit**, who goes out from **God**, and not back, and does not draw to himself, but wells <note>original: "wallet," describing the active, bubbling motion of divine power.</note> before **God**, and is the flower of the growth.

And that same Being is the eternal Element, wherein all **Essences** stand open in the Divine Power, and are visible, in which the beautiful and chaste Virgin of Divine Wisdom always beholds herself according to the number of infinity, from which come many thousand times thousand without end or number; and in that same beholding, as from the eternal Element, go forth colors, art, and virtue, and the growths of the **Lilies of God**, in which the Godhead always rejoices in the Virgin of Wisdom: And that same joy goes out from the eternal **Essences**, and is called **Paradise**, because of the sharpness of the births of the lovely fruit of the lilies into infinity, for then the essences of the lilies rise up in wonder, in many thousand times thousand without number, as you have a likeness in the blooming earth.

You dear soul, see, consider it, this is now **God** and his Kingdom of Heaven with the eternal Element and Paradise, and so it stands in the eternal source-testimony <note>original: "Uhrkund," a foundational record or primal evidence of reality.</note> from eternity to eternity. What joy now, delight...

### 2. Part / Chapter 4.

**The Mirror:** The Spirit is life / and the mirror is the revelation of life / otherwise the spirit would not recognize itself / for the mirror / as Wisdom / is its ground and container / it is that which the spirit has found / where the spirit finds itself within Wisdom. Wisdom is no being without the spirit / and the spirit is not revealed to itself without Wisdom / and one would be an Abyss <note>original: "Ungrund," a term Böhme uses to describe the absolute void or "nothingness" before God manifests into existence.</note> without the other.

Thus Wisdom / as the mirror of the spirit of the **Godhead** / is silent in itself / and is the body of the **Godhead** / as the spirit / in which the spirit dwells: It is a virgin matrix <note>original: "jungfräuliche Matrix," referring to the divine receptive space or womb from which all things are birthed.</note> / in which the spirit reveals itself / and is **God's** essence / like a holy divine sulfur <note>original: "Sulphur," an alchemical term used here to describe the active, fiery principle of life and manifestation.</note> / held within the imagination of the spirit / of the Abyss of eternity: And this mirror or sulfur is the eternal first beginning / and the eternal first end / and resembles an eye everywhere / through which the spirit sees / what it is within / and what it wishes to reveal.

This mirror or eye is without ground or goal / just as the spirit has no ground / except in this eye: It is entirely whole everywhere / undivided / as we recognize that the Abyss cannot be divided / for there is nothing to separate it / there is no movement outside of the spirit. Thus it is understandable to us / what the eternal spirit is in Wisdom / and what the eternal beginning and the eternal end are.

As we then recognize / that the eternal beginning in the Abyss is an eternal will in itself / whose origin no creature shall know: Yet it has been given to us to know and recognize in the spirit its ground / which it makes for itself / wherein it rests. For a will is as thin as a nothing / therefore it is desiring / it wants to be something / so that it may be manifest within itself / for the nothing causes the will / to be desiring / and the desire is an imagination <note>In Böhme’s vocabulary, "imagination" is the act of the will "imaging" or forming itself into a substantial state.</note> / where the will beholds itself in the mirror of Wisdom / it imagines out of the Abyss into itself / and

<column-break/>

makes for itself in the imagination a ground within itself / and impregnates itself with the imagination out of Wisdom / as from the virgin mirror / which is a mother without birthing / without will.

The impregnation does not happen in the mirror / but in the will / in the will's imagination. The mirror remains eternally a virgin without birthing / but the will is impregnated with the sight of the mirror. Thus we recognize the impregnation of the Father as the center <note>original: "Centrum"</note> of the spirit of eternity / where the eternal spirit always composes itself. # On the Revelation of God in Wisdom.

[Spoken forth] / as into the virginal mirror / and it opens the Word of Life in the mirror of Wisdom / so that the threefold essence of the **Godhead** becomes manifest in Wisdom.

Thus we recognize an eternal, groundless Divine Being / and therein three persons / where none is the other / such as the eternal Will / which is the one cause of all being / that is the first person. But he is not the being itself / but rather the cause of the being / and is free from the being / for he is the Abyss <note>original: "Ungrund"; in Böhme’s thought, this is the absolute void or "nothingness" that precedes existence.</note>: Nothing is before him / that could give him anything / but rather he gives himself / of which we have no knowledge. He is everything / yet also thus unified in himself / without being he is a "Nothing" / and in this unified Will originates the eternal beginning through imagination or desire / and in the desire the Will impregnates itself from the eye of Wisdom / which is with the Will in equal eternity / without ground and beginning / as mentioned above. This same impregnation is the ground of the Will and the essence of all beings / and is the Son of the Will / for the Will begets this Son from eternity to eternity forevermore / for he is his Heart / or his Word / as a sound or revelation of the Abyss of still eternity / and is the Mouth or Understanding of the Will / and is rightly called a different person than the Father / for he is the Father’s revelation / his ground and essence / for a Will is not a being / but the Will’s imagining creates being.

Thus the second person is the essence of the **Godhead** / understand (the essence of the Holy Trinity) the Mouth or Revelation of the essence of all beings / and the power of the life of all lives.

The third person is the Spirit / who goes forth with the comprehension of the Will through the imagination from the power of speaking / from the mouth of the Father into the eye / as into the mirror of Wisdom / he is indeed free from the Will and also from the Word: And although the Will gives him forth from the Word / yet he is free / like the air from the fire / as one sees then / that the air is the fire's spirit and life / yet is something other than the fire / though it is also given from the fire. And as one sees / that the air provides a living and weaving heaven / which is visible and moving: So also is the Holy Spirit the life of the **Godhead** / and another person than the Father and Son / he also carries out another office / he opens the Wisdom of **God** / so that the wonders appear / just as the air opens all life of this world / so that everything lives and grows. This is thus a short indication of the **Godhead** in the Abyss / how **God** dwells in himself / and is himself his own center of the birthing-mother <note>original: "Gebährerin," referring to the generative, creative principle within God.</note>.

<margin>Incarnation <note>original: "Menschw." referring to Böhme’s treatise "Von der Menschwerdung Christi" (On the Incarnation of Christ).</note> part 2. chapter 2. §. 9. 12. chapter 3. 1. 2. 3. 7.</margin>

->5. Question: Why does the author call Wisdom a Virgin?<-

Answer: Just as a sincere mirror presents everything in such an image without change / also without blemish or preference <note>original: "Annehmlichkeit," here meaning a subjective bias or personal attachment; the mirror reflects purely.</note>, whatever shines into the mirror: So is Wisdom a virginal mirror, which without preference, without blemish and without distortion presents and reveals everything to the understanding eye, how the triune **Godhead** plays within it.

I understand / that Wisdom is not the center or the opener / but rather **God's** Spirit. I understand it to speak in a parable thus / how the soul reveals itself in the body through the essence of the flesh / and the flesh would not have the power / if a living spirit were not within: So also is **God's** Wisdom the spoken essence / through which the power and the Spirit of **God** reveals itself in forms / understand in Divine forms and formations in wonders. She gives birth / but she is not the Divine Principle or the center of the birthing-mother / but rather the Mother / in whom the Father works. And therefore I call her a Virgin / because / she is the discipline and purity of **God** / and carries no desire behind her toward the fire / but her delight goes forward with the revelation of the **Godhead**.

Part 2 / Chapter 4.

She could give birth to nothing, if the Spirit of **God** did not work within her; and therefore she is not a "bearer" <note>In the sense of an active biological mother.</note> but rather the **mirror of the Godhead**. The Spirit of **God** gives birth within her; He is her life, she is His casket or body; she is the corporeality of the Holy Spirit. Within her lie the colors and virtues; for she is the **spoken-forth essence**, which the Father grasps from the **Chaos**—that is, from Himself, outside and before nature—into "nothingness." He leads it with desire toward nature, through the **eternal nature**, through the **first Principle**, through the fire of His power in the **second Principle**, out into the Divine power, in the light of Majesty. It is she whom the Father grasps again and again from eternity to eternity; she whom the Father, who is a fire and light, leads into His fire-life to the **Center** of His heart. She is the highest essence of the **Godhead**; without her **God** would not be manifest, but would be only a "Will." But through **Wisdom** He leads Himself into "Being," so that He is manifest to Himself. And she is called a **Virgin** for this reason: because she is in the **Marriage of God**, so that she gives birth without a "fire-life" <note>That is, without the consuming, destructive aspect of the first principle, the "wrath" or "fire."</note>; for in her the light, or the true Divine life, reveals itself. She is a Virgin of the discipline and purity of **God**, and yet is in marriage with **God**.

You clever school of the stars, if you understood the ground here, you would need no more books; everything lies within this. The **Philosopher's Stone** <term>A reference to the *Lapis Philosophorum*; in this context, it is not a physical substance but the spiritual "key" to all knowledge and transformation.</term> lies in this place. But first, take off your rough little coat <note>A metaphor for shedding earthly ego and materialist preconceptions.</note>; then you shall see it.

### 6. Question: Where does Wisdom dwell and exist?

**Answer:** She is and dwells through everything where **God** is and works. In and of herself, she is a **Universal** in respect to all of nature; but in respect to angels and humans, she is figured as a **Particular**, according to the qualities and image of the rational creature. We shall speak of this further below, when we discuss angels and humans.

<column-break/>

### 7. Question: What is the difference between Wisdom and the living, self-subsisting Word?

**Answer:** Between the **Word** and **Wisdom** there is no other difference than that which exists between the **Will**—which we represent in the mind <note>original: "Gemüth"; the deep-seated center of human thought, will, and emotion.</note> through thoughts and mental images—and the **Will** through which we reveal our thoughts in the word and carry out our understanding. The triune **God** beheld Himself in **Wisdom** as in a mirror, and from the sight of Himself, He conceived a desire to lead Himself into nature and the creature, and to reveal Himself therein. Through this working Will, the powers of the unified Divine quality introduced themselves into distinction. Just as a carpenter considers a building from the ground up in his mind, and forms a mental image of every piece, but afterward brings this into being through the work of his hands and reveals that which he had conceived in his mind: So has **God**, through His almighty **Word**, brought His will and pleasure into an actual effect, as He recognized and beheld it in **Wisdom**; and He revealed the most holy image of His self-subsistence, His beloved **Son**, in nature and the creature as the **eternal Word**, from which, through which, and to which all things are.

### 8. Question: What is the "WORD" actually called here?

**Answer:** The **Word** here means nothing other than the eternally working **Will** of the triune **God**, through which the triune **God** introduced Himself into nature and the creature, and revealed Himself therein. Therefore, John calls it the **Word**; in John 1 it stands:
> In the beginning was the **Word**, and the **Word** was with **God**, and **God** was the **Word**. The same was in the beginning with **God**. All things were made by Him, and without Him was not any thing made that was made.

The beginning of all beings was the **Word** as the **breathing-out of God**; and **God** has been the eternal One from eternity, and remains so in eternity. But the **Word** is the outflowing of the Divine Will or the Divine Knowledge. Just as the senses flow out from the mind, and yet the mind is but one: so also the eternal One was present in the outflowing of the Will. That is: In the beginning was the **WORD**.
