# Of the Revelation of God in Wisdom.

WORD; for the **Word**, as the outflow from the will of God, has been the eternal beginning and remains so eternally: For it is the revelation of the eternal One, by which and through which the Divine power is brought into a "knowledge of something." And by the **WORD**, we understand the revealed will of God; and by the word "God," we understand the hidden God, as the eternal **One**, from which the Word eternally springs.

Thus, the outflow of the Divine One is the **Word**, and yet it is God Himself as His own revelation. This outflow flows from God, and that which has flowed out is Wisdom—the beginning and cause of all powers, colors, virtues, and properties. From such a revelation of powers, in which the will of the eternal One beholds itself, there flows out the understanding and the knowledge of the **NOTHING** <note>original: "ICHTS." This is a term used by Böhme to describe a state that is not yet a "thing" but is no longer "nothing"; it is the "I" emerging from the "Naught."</note>, where the eternal will beholds itself in the **NOTHING** and introduces itself into a "longing" or "delight" within Wisdom, toward a likeness and image. And this same image is the **Great Mystery** <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"</note>, as the creator of all beings and creatures; for it is the **Separator** <note>The "Separator" is the divine dividing power that differentiates the unified will into specific, distinct qualities.</note> in the outflow of the will, which makes the will of the eternal One divisible. It is the quality of "separability" within the will, from which powers and properties arise. These same powers are, in turn, an outflow of themselves, where each power introduces itself into its own will, according to the virtue of that power. From this, the multiplicity of wills arises, and from this also the creaturely life of the eternal has taken its origin—such as angels and souls. Yet one cannot say that a "nature" or "creature" is yet understood here; rather, it is the eternal imagery of the Divine Word and Will, where the Spirit of God has played with itself in such a "counter-reflection" <note>original: "Gegenwurff"</note> within the powers of Wisdom, forming a likeness of itself.

Just as the mind of a human being, through the understanding and the senses, introduces itself into a counter-reflection of an image, and

<column-break/>

flows out with the same and captures it in a mental picture—which images are the thoughts of the mind, wherein the will of the mind works—and thus, through longing, captures itself in a "sharpness" or a "magnetic attraction," from which joy and sorrow arise: So too must we understand the eternal Mind of sensitivity. We see that the exit of the single will of God has introduced itself through the Word into "separability," and this separability has introduced itself into "acceptability" <note>The process of "taking in" or "assuming" a form.</note>, as into its own delight and desire for its self-revelation, moving from Unity into Multiplicity.

Desire is the ground and beginning of the nature of the "sensitivity" of the individual will; for within it, the separability of the Unity is brought into a state of "taking-in." From this, the divisions of the wills are brought into the sensitivity of a "Selfhood," in which the true creaturely, sensitive, angelic, and soulful life is understood. For the will of the eternal One is "unsensing" and without inclination toward anything, for it has nothing toward which it could incline, except within itself. Therefore, it leads itself out of itself and leads the outflow of its Unity into Multiplicity, and into the "taking-in" of Selfhood, as if into a place or a nature, from which properties arise. For every property has its own **Separator**, divider, and maker within itself, and is in itself entirely according to the property of the eternal Unity. Thus, the **Separator** of each will again leads properties out of itself, from which the infinite multiplicity arises, and through which the eternal One makes itself "sensing"—not according to the Unity, but according to the outflow of the Unity.

He is called God’s Light because the light is ignited in Him and takes its origin in Him. He is called the Radiance of God because He creates a radiance in the eternal quiet freedom, which originates from the sharpness of eternal nature, as was mentioned before. And this is the distinction: that the Father and Son are called two persons, and yet are only one God in one essence; for the Father is the generator of nature, and in Him it is born through His will out of desire; and His Heart separates itself from nature and is not encompassed by nature, and maintains a distinct center as Love, while the Father is Wrath. In the Father’s sharpness is fire, and in the Son’s sharpness is light; and yet they are in each other like fire and light.

10. **Q.** I understand to some extent the birth, the property, and the working of the Word, as well as the distinction between the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit; but what is meant by the "Beginning," in which the Word was, and is, and shall be?

**Ans.** The Beginning is nothing other than the first ground of the Divine Will for the revelation of unity and multiplicity within this ground; where the Father becomes longing to carry out His counsel and will, there the Son of God becomes active to fulfill the Father’s counsel and longing will, as the speaking Word, in which all beings stand with understanding, reason, and senses, taking their ground and beginning from it, as John says: **All things were made through the same, and without the same nothing was made that was made.** Here, my dear soul, consider where light and darkness come from, as well as joy and sorrow, love and enmity, also the kingdom of heaven and hell, good and evil, life and the enclosure of death. You say: God created these. Yes, rightly so; but why are you blind and do not recognize this, even though you are God’s **likeness** <note>original: "Gleichheit." # Chapter V.
## Concerning eternal Nature as the Revelation of God, according to the first Principle, in the Property of the Father.

Hitherto we have considered God as He introduces Himself into nature and creature and reveals Himself therein; it follows now to investigate the revelation through which God becomes manifest in nature and creature. This revelation is threefold, according to the properties of the One who reveals Himself—namely, the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—and is called the "Three Principles."

### 1. Question.
**What does the author actually mean by a "Principle"?**
->Answer.<-

By a "Principle," the author understands the very first beginning of life, where the Nothing becomes active in the Something, and the <term>Ungrund</term> becomes active in the ground, through which life and movement are ignited where otherwise no life exists. It is just as when one lights a candle or **wood** with fire; a life is awakened in the wood or candle that was otherwise [not present] in the wood...

### Of Eternal Nature.
<margin>R 3</margin>

Wood and candles, before they are lit, exist not in **actuality** <note>original Latin: *actu*; refers to something currently happening or existing in fact</note>, but in **potential** <note>original Latin: *potentia*; refers to the inherent capacity to become something</note>—not in the deed itself, but in the possibility.

2. **Question:** If there is truly only one **Active Principle** <note>original Latin: *Principium Agens*; the primary force that causes change</note>, why then does the author name three Principles?

**Answer:** There is but a single Active Principle, and that is the eternally-speaking Word of the triune God. However, this eternally-speaking Word is revealed in nature and in created beings through a threefold property. This Principle has only one Spirit, which is the life of the Principle, and it has only one Will, which is the fulfillment of eternity through the radiance of Majesty. Thus, by "Principle," the author actually means nothing other than a new birth and a new life that has a beginning and did not exist before. If we consider the matter in its highest and most supreme beginning, there is no more than one single Principle wherein an eternal life dwells, which is the eternal **Godhead** <term>GOttheit: the essential nature or essence of God, distinguished here from the individual persons of the Trinity</term>. This Godhead, however, is only revealed through three properties, which the author calls the Three Principles. These are not actually separate Principles, but rather the active properties of a single Principle. The first property is that of **Fire**; in this, God is revealed as a Father, and where this property has the upper hand, He is revealed as a jealous, wrathful God. The second property is that of **Light**, in which God is revealed as the Son, who fulfills the Father’s will with pleasure; where this property has the upper hand, there is light, love, life, joy, peace, and full contentment. The third Principle is the visible world, in which both properties of Divine Revelation—those of the Father and the Son—are dwelling and active, in the likeness of the property of the Holy Spirit, who proceeds from the Father and the Son.

One Principle dwells within the other, yet each retains its own property. There is no mixing of the **essence** <term>Essentz: the fundamental nature or "stuff" of a being</term>; rather, one receives the other through **Desire** <term>Begierde: in Böhme’s thought, this is the fundamental "pull" or attractive force that brings spiritual possibilities into physical existence</term>. The Light dwells in the Fire’s desire, so that the property of the Fire gives its desire into the Light, and the Light gives its desire into the Fire. Thus, they are one being and not two, yet they are two properties, where one is not the other, nor can they ever become so throughout eternity. Just as the property of the Spirit cannot be the Fire or the Light, yet it proceeds from the Fire and out of the Light; and it could not exist from the Fire or the Light

<column-break/>

alone. The fire alone could not produce it, nor could the light; rather, both produce it. It is the life of both, and there is only one being, but three properties, where none is the other—as can be seen in fire, light, and air.

In this way, you also understand the third Principle, which is and has these same properties: it also has fire, light, and spirit (which is air), and it is equal to the eternal being in all circumstances. But it has a beginning and proceeds from the Eternal. It is a revelation of the Eternal; it is not the Eternal itself, but it has become a "being" within the Desire. The Desire has revealed itself and led into a being that is like the Eternal.

->Six Points, chapter 2, sections 13, 14, 15<-

3. **Question:** To distinguish these properties or Principles more thoroughly and to recognize the effect of each, tell me: what is the "First Principle," and what is its effect and property?

**Answer:** We call the First Principle nothing other than that life which originates from the active will of God in nature through the Word, according to the property of the Father, for the revelation of His eternal omnipotence, justice, and wisdom. The author represents this life in the image of fire and ignition, as the first fundamental beginning of life.

4. **Question:** Why is this called the "First Principle"?

**Answer:** It is called the first, not because one exists in God earlier than the other—for in God there is no "before" or "after"—at the very point where God’s will becomes active as Fire, it also becomes active as Light. Rather, it is the first because it is awakened by the active will of God according to the property of the Father, which is to be considered prior to the will of God according to the property of the Son.

**Answer:** It is the eternal, almighty will of God, which God, in His unchangeable eternal counsel...

...[He] formed a resolution to lead Himself out of His **UNGROUND** <term>Ungrund: A central concept in this philosophy referring to the "groundless" or "abyssal" state of God before creation; a void that is neither light nor dark, but the source of both</term> and **NOTHINGNESS** into a **GROUND** and into **SOMETHING**, and to manifest His wonders. We call this will GOD, because nothing is in GOD that is not GOD Himself; we call Him FATHER, because this will acts according to the property of a father to bring forth and reveal Himself in Nature and Creature.

### 6. Question: What, then, does the Will of God the Father actually want?

**Answer:** The ungrounded <note>or "abyssal"</note> will of the Father—within which the Son is eternally born—wants nothing other than to bring forth His Son and Heart in Nature and Creature as the single center of His will. He desires that this Heart might be manifest in Nature and Creature, so that GOD might have His "play" <note>original: "Spiel"; a common mystical term for the creative activity of God</note> therein, according to the likeness of His will in the Unground of His eternal Godhead. For in the Unground there is no revelation, but rather an eternal Nothing; a stillness without essence, colors, or virtue. But within this Desire, colors, power, and virtue come to be; yet even then, it remains hidden within itself and would eternally never be manifest—for there would be no light, radiance, or majesty—but would instead be a triple spirit within itself, which would exist as a single essence without "torment" <term>Quaal: In this context, it refers to the "paining" or "laboring" quality of existence that leads to birth or manifestation</term>.

Thus we are to understand the essence of the deepest Godhead as it exists both within and outside of Nature. Furthermore, we see how the eternal will of the Godhead desires to reveal itself from its own ground in the light of majesty. Here we recognize the first will of the Father as it desires the Son and the light of majesty, and this occurs in two ways: first, the way toward the Center of the Word; and second, toward the light or revelation of the Word. We find that every desire is "attractive" <note>acting like a magnet</note>, even though in the Unground there is nothing that could be pulled. Therefore, the desire pulls itself, and "impregnates" the other will of the Father, which imagines <note>or "forms an image"</note> toward the light of majesty from the Center of His Word or Heart. Now the Heart is pregnant with Light, and the first will of Nature is

<column-break/>

pregnant; and yet, even so, nothing would be manifest if the Principle were not born. For it is our understanding that the Father brings forth the first Principle out of the first will as Nature, which reaches its highest perfection in Fire; and then He brings forth the second Principle, in and out of the other will, into the Word. He does this by desiring the revelation of the Word in the light of majesty, where the fire of the second Principle <note>original: "andern Principii"</note> is a fulfillment of the second will in the light of majesty. This manifests as Meekness, which is set in opposition to the fire of the first Principle and extinguishes its wrath <note>original: "Grimm"</note>. It places it into an essential being, such as eternal life, where the fire is hidden within the light and gives the light its power, strength, and might. Thus, together they form an eternal bond, and one would be nothing without the other.

### 7. Question: What then is the actual property of the active will of God the Father?

**Antw.** The property of this will is revealed to us primarily in three forms <note>original: "Gestalten"; also translated as "aspects" or "configurations"</note>: the will of God is desiring, the desire is attractive, and it is firmly sustaining and strictly binding. That which is now desired, attracted, and firmly grasped is GOD, who desires Himself out of eternal freedom and leads Himself into Nature. Now, Nature is narrow and strict, but GOD is infinite and immeasurable; therefore, that which is enclosed seeks to be free from its enclosure once again. Thus, it conceives a will toward freedom; this will becomes a longing, a rising, a driving, and a moving. The first form of the Father’s active will is the cause of all enclosure, nature, and essence. The second form is the cause of life, motion, driving, and growth. These two active forms of the Father’s property work the third within the "anguish" <note>original: "Angst"; meaning a state of contraction or tension</note>, in which the active will ignites itself, from which the fourth form arises—namely, the Fire.

Just as the active will of God, according to the property of the Father, has three forms—Desire, Motion, and the Igniting of Fire—so too the active will of God according to the property of the Son has another three forms. The Fire stands as the fourth in the middle, as it were, the "boundary-mark" <note>original: "Scheide-Ziel"</note> where the properties of the Father...

10. **Question:** What then are the actual effects of the desiring Will?

**Answer:** 1. The desiring Will is "harsh," <note>original: *herbe*—a key term in Böhme’s thought meaning astringent, contracting, or bitter-cold</note> which is to say, it is attracting and contracting for the purpose of enclosing the "Nothing" into "Something"; such an enclosure makes things thick, full, and dark. 2. The desiring Will is a cause of hardness, stability, and comprehensibility. 3. It is a cause of sharpness, severity, and roughness. 4. It is a cause of cold, acting as coagulation, contraction, and compression. 5. It is a cause of all essence or corporeality, and in the *Great Mystery* <note>original: *Mysterio Magno*—referring to the primordial state of all possibilities within God</note>, it is a mother of all salts and a root of nature. However, this is to be understood as Divine regarding God, spiritual regarding the spirit, and physical regarding physical things. Thus, when we speak of God, this form causes God to appear harsh, severe, sharp, and rough within the creature; in a spirit, this quality makes it greedy, avaricious, severe, hard, cold, and dry, etc.; in physical things, it creates salt, hardness, severity, roughness, cold, stone, bone, and darkness.
<margin>See *Of the Election of Grace*, ch. 3. § 3. *Mysterium Magnum* 6. 14. 21.</margin>

In this sense, it is easy to distinguish and grasp when the author teaches that the whole Godhead, in its most initial birth (understand this to be within Nature, not within itself), has in its kernel a very sharp and terrifying sharpness. In this state, the harsh quality is a very bitter, cold, hard, severe, and dark contraction—much like the cold of winter that contracts and hardens water. Such is the omnipotence of God in His desiring Will toward Nature.
<margin>See *Aurora* 13. 55. 57.</margin>

11. **Question:** What is the second form of the active Will of God in the Word toward Nature?

**Answer:** It is nothing other than the stirring and movement caused by the Divine Spirit of Life or *Mercurius* <term>Mercury: An alchemical term used here to represent the moving, communicative spirit of life and growth</term>, when it longs to be free from the enclosure and the contraction—much

as when the wide air longs for its freedom and its center again when it has been locked and compressed into a narrow barrel; it breaks loose with great force and would rather shatter the barrel. Or better yet, like a prickly spring <note>original: *stachlichten Feder*—likely referring to a tensioned metal spring or a quill under pressure</note> which is curved into itself, where the air in the air-holes is so compressed that it cannot expand because of the great hardness of the barb, and thus seeks to extend itself again with a powerful drive. In this form stands the "First Mover" <term>primum Mobile: The first moved thing, or the source of all motion in the universe</term> of the inner and outer world—spiritually in the inner, physically in the outer. This form is a root of the mercurial life; in living and growing things, and in rational creatures, it is the cause of fleeting senses and thoughts, of the life of the spirit, of "welling and boiling," <note>A Böhme-esque phrase describing the active, bubbling emergence of life-forces</note> or of the working and driving will. Within the "Temperature" <term>Temperature: A state of perfect balance or harmony between the conflicting qualities of nature</term> it works as significant joy in the light; but where it exits the Temperature, it is a cause of all fierce and angry passions, of ill-will, of all strife and adversity, of the torment of wrath and poison, and also of pride, the elevation and inflammation of the mind. In physical things, it acts as a stinging, volatile poison; it is dissolving, driving, sublimating, etc.

# Of Eternal Nature.

->M 3<-

If the will did not exist, everything would be a Nothing—neither darkness nor light. And since "Something" exists, it is the **Eternal Will**, which is harsh and desiring, namely, the wonders of creation. Now, because there is a desire, that desire draws into itself; and that which is drawn into the desire fills the will, so that the desire becomes full. For the will is as thin as a Nothing, but that which is drawn into the will makes it thick, and that is its darkness. Thus, the eternal desire stands in the darkness.

When the will draws to itself in desire, this drawing is a **sting of stirring** <note>original: *Stachel der Rügung*—the initial impulse of movement or agitation in the void</note>; for the will is as thin as a Nothing and as still as a Nothing. Since the will is an eternal desire, it draws into itself eternally; and though it has nothing to draw in, it draws itself and impregnates itself, so that darkness arises out of the Nothing. This drawing creates the sting of the first essences, so that there is a stirring and a manifestation of mobility.

Now, the will cannot endure this drawing and impregnation, for it wants to be free, yet it cannot, for it is desiring. Since it cannot become free, it enters into itself with the drawing and conceives within itself another will: to exit the darkness into itself. This other conceived will is the **Eternal Mind** <note>original: *Gemüthe*—the spiritual center of thought and feeling</note>, and it moves within itself like a sudden flash of lightning, shattering the darkness. It goes out within itself and dwells within itself, creating another Principle <note>original: *Principium*—one of Böhme's three fundamental states of being</note> of a different quality <note>original: *Quall*—Böhme uses this word to imply both a 'source' and a 'vibrational quality'</note>, for the sting of stirring remains in the darkness.

Thus, we must now speak of the forms in the harsh, dark nature, for nature manifests itself according to such properties and ways. We understand that the darkness longs for the light, which stands eternally opposite it, but in another Principle. For these two forms—the **harsh** and the **bitter-stinging**—are the foundation of all being, and the Eternal Will is the mother in whom they are born: and

<column-break/>

it is for us to understand that the **harshness** <note>original: *Herbigkeit*—astringency or contraction</note>, through the grasping of the will, always draws to itself, and this drawing is the sting of stirring, which the harshness cannot endure. For harshness desires the harsh, strict enclosure of death, but the stinging bitterness is the opener—and yet, in itself, it would be nothing without the will.

Now, because harshness draws so strictly, the sting (which is the harshness's own drawing) cannot endure it, but stirs all the more violently. And the harshness cannot endure this stirring either, for it desires the stillness of death. Thus, this is a chain and a bond that is perpetually self-made and has no maker.

Because this happens as swiftly as a passing thought, the sting desires to escape the harshness, yet it cannot, for the harshness gives birth to it and also holds it. Since it cannot go beyond itself, it begins to turn like a **wheel** <note>original: *Rad*—Böhme's concept of the 'Wheel of Nature,' a state of chaotic, circular motion</note> and thus shatters the drawn-in harshness, creating a constant confusion and mixing in which "breaking" or "woe" resides—though here there is no physical sensation, only the forms of nature. We understand "sensation" here, yet it is not physical, for there is no matter <note>original: *Materia*</note>; rather, it is the manifestation of the spirit or eternal nature within the Eternal Will. For the harsh desire draws and makes straight, while the bitterness shatters it in the turning wheel, so that a multiplicity of essences arises. It is like an absurdity, or as I might say in a parable, a confusion of eternal mobility, a cause of essences. The Eternal Will must suffer this within itself; therefore, it conceives another will to flee from this wheel, yet it cannot, for this is its own being. And since it cannot, and yet cannot abandon its eternal desire and longing, it continues to hold and draw to itself, so that essences are always being born—though apart from this desire, they are a Nothing. Since the will cannot be free, it falls...

...it falls into **anguish** <note>original: *Angst*—in Böhme's thought, this refers to a state of contraction and tension, the "narrowing" before an explosion of light</note> (to speak thus according to human understanding). The Will is the vessel; that which is contained within the Will creates the darkness; and the desire creates the **Essence** <note>original: *Essentia*—here meaning the fundamental attractive forces or "building blocks" of being</note>, which is to say, the attractive forces. And the counter-will creates the **wheel of the multiplication of essences**, so that within it no number can be found; rather, as the mobility is, so too is the quantity. Thus, these two forms are the eternal essences or the active pulling and driving forces, and the eternal bond that creates itself. For the Great Vastness without end desires narrowness and containment, wherein it may reveal itself; for in the vastness and stillness there would be no revelation. Thus, there must be a pulling-in and an enclosing, out of which the revelation may appear.

<margin>*The Threefold Life*, chapter 1, sections 25, 35.</margin>
13. **Quest.** But how can one say of God’s Will that it is bitter, fierce, hostile, poison, or a sting, as the author is accustomed to speak?

**Ans.** This is not to be understood as God’s Will in and of itself, but rather how the Will of God works within Nature and Creature at the beginning of life. By this, one can understand the great "Earnestness" of God, where God’s desiring Will is almighty, and His Will according to freedom is also almightily active; this cannot be understood by us except through such a likeness. For just as bitterness and stings are cutting, dividing, and dissolving, such is also the effect of God’s Will in this form.

<margin>See *Aurora*, chapter 10, sections 51, 55.</margin>
14. **Quest.** Which is the third form of the active Will of God according to the property of the Father?

**Ans.** The third form in **Science** <note>original: *Scientz*—from the Latin *scientia*, meaning the divine self-knowledge or the "knowing" power of the Will that organizes nature</note> is **Anguish**, which arises in the opposition of harshness and the stinging bitterness, as an **Ens** <note>term: *ens*—a philosophical term for a "being" or an "entity"</note> of feeling. It is the beginning of the Essence and of the Mind, a root of fire and of all painfulness, a hunger and thirst for freedom—that is, for the **Groundless** <note>term: *Ungrund*—the primordial "Abyss" or "Nothing" that exists before any created thing</note>. It is a revelation of the eternal groundless Will within "Science," where the Will introduces itself into a spiritual form.

<column-break/>

It is also a cause of dying, acting as the birth of death, yet here no death arises; instead, it is the beginning of **Natural Life**. It is the very root where God and Nature are distinguished—not as a separation, but because of the "temperature" <note>original: *Temperatur*—the perfect balance or mixture of qualities</note> within the Godhead, so that here the audible, sensory life arises, from which Creation took its origin. These three aforementioned forms—Harshness, Bitterness (or the Sting), and Anguish—are the first three in the "Science" of the One Will, which is called the Father of all beings. They take their ground and origin in "Science" out of the Trinity of the Godhead. This is not to be understood as them *being* God, but rather His revelation in His Word of power.

First, **Harshness**, which is the beginning of strength and might, acting as a foundation from which everything comes and originates; this is the Father’s property in the Word. Secondly, the **Bitter Sting**, as the beginning of life, has its origin in the Son’s property from the Word; for it is the cause of all forces and distinctions, as well as of speech, understanding, and the five senses. Thirdly, **Anguish**, which originates from the Holy Spirit’s property in the Word; for it is the cause of both fires—namely, the light-fire of Love and the painful fire of consumption. It is the true origin of the "found" creaturely life, and also of dying into joy or sorrow—the root of all life, out of the "Science" of the one eternal Will.

In Creation and in Natural Life, following the compaction of the world, these first three are called **Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury** <note>original: *Sal, Sulphur, und Mercurius*—the three fundamental alchemical principles representing stability (Salt), combustibility (Sulfur), and fluidity/spirit (Mercury)</note>. Here, the spirit-life has introduced itself into a visible, tangible matter. This matter is in all things: in living flesh and in the growth of the earth, both spiritually and corporally, nothing excluded. For all beings of this world stand within them, as is evident to the eyes and known to the experienced. For thus has the invisible, as the...

15. **Quest.** But how is such a turning wheel generated in this third form?

**Ans.** Understand us by way of parable / how in this third form the mighty wheel of birth is generated / which we here paint before your eyes for the sake of conceptual understanding / when the Will of God takes up a purpose / to introduce and reveal itself out of the Nothing into the Something; so this purpose of God is like a point / as a central ground, <image-desc>small circle symbol</image-desc>. The desiring Will of God / for the sake of enclosure is as it were a striking ray <image-desc>vertical line symbol</image-desc>, the Will according to freedom is ascending, <image-desc>upward arrow symbol</image-desc>. The hub / to which the spokes <note>original: *Radii*</note> or rims are made fast / so that they stand firm, joined into one another / is the sharp / strict / harsh pulling of the active Will. The rims are the sharp essences or forces / which are always generated out of the desiring and driving of the Will of God. That the wheel drives all around / and the rims turn / the cause is the property of the pulling and desiring / as well as of the driving-away and ascending Will. The Author speaks very clearly of this wheel.

### Part 2 / Chapter 5.

Just as if a wheel stood before you with seven wheels, one crafted inside the other, so that it could go in all directions—forward, backward, and sideways—without needing to turn around. And as it moved, one wheel in its turning would always give birth to the next, yet none would pass away, but all seven would be visible. And these seven wheels would always generate the hubs <note>original: *Naben*</note> in their center according to their turning, so that the hub would always remain free and without change, whether the wheels went forward, backward, sideways, upward, or downward. And the hub would always generate the spokes, so that in the turning they were always positioned rightly everywhere, and yet no spoke would pass away, but would always turn together with the others, moving wherever the wind turned it, without needing to turn itself around.

->Now mark what I inform you.<-

The seven wheels are the seven Spirits of GOD; they always give birth to one another, one after the other. It is like turning a wheel in which seven wheels are nested within each other, where one always turns differently than the others in its inner standing, yet the seven wheels are joined together like a round sphere. One would nonetheless see all seven wheels—the rotation of each one individually—as well as its entire structure with its *rims <note>original: *Fälgen*—the outer circular edges of a wheel</note>, spokes, and hubs. And the seven hubs in the center would be as one hub, which adapts itself everywhere in the turning; the wheels always generate these same hubs, and the hub always generates the spokes in all seven wheels. Yet no wheel would pass away, nor any hub, nor any rim or spoke; and that same wheel would have seven wheels, and yet be only one wheel, always moving forward to wherever the wind drove it.

<margin>* The rims also signify the spokes.</margin>

<column-break/>

->Now see.<-

The seven wheels within each other, where one always gives birth to the other and they move on all sides without any perishing or turning back—these are the seven Source-Spirits <note>original: *Quell-Geister*—the seven fundamental "qualities" or "fountain-spirits" of Böhme’s divine nature</note> of GOD the Father. In the seven wheels, they give birth to a hub in every wheel, and yet these are not seven hubs, but only one, which fits itself into all seven wheels.

And that is the Heart, or the innermost body <note>original: *Corpus*</note> of the wheels, in which the wheels rotate; and this signifies the Son of GOD. All seven Spirits of GOD the Father always give birth to Him within their circle, and He is the Son of all seven Spirits. They all "qualify" <note>original: *qualificiren*—Böhme’s term for the spirits interacting, blending, and operating together</note> in His light. He is in the midst of the birth and holds all seven Spirits of GOD, and they turn with Him in their birth in this manner. That is: whether they now rise upward or downward, backward or forward, or sideways, the Heart of GOD is always in the center and always adapts itself to each Source-Spirit. Thus there is one Heart of GOD, and not seven, which is always born of all seven Spirits; He is the Heart and Life of all seven Spirits.

Now the spokes, which are always born of the hubs and the wheels and which adapt themselves to all wheels in their rotation—along with their root, support, or the points <note>original: *Pflecken*</note> where they stand and from which they are born—these signify GOD the Holy Spirit. He proceeds from the Father and the Son, just as the spokes proceed from the hub and the wheel, and yet they also remain within the wheel.

Now, just as there are many spokes always turning with the wheel, so the Holy Spirit is the Master-Workman <note>original: *Werck-Meister*</note> in the wheel of GOD, and He forms and shapes everything within the whole of GOD.

Now the wheel has seven wheels within one another and one hub that fits into all seven wheels, and all seven wheels move upon the one hub. Thus, GOD is a single GOD with seven Source-Spirits within one another, where one always [gives birth to] the other...

### Now observe.

The wheel in its combined, embodied structure signifies the **astringent quality** <note>original: *herbe Qualität* — the contractive, "harsh" force that pulls spirit into matter</note>; this pulls the entire bodily being of the Godhood together and holds it, drying it so that it persists. And the sweet source-water is born from the circling or ascending of the spirits. For when the light is born in the heat, the astringent quality is startled by great joy, and this is like a settling down or becoming thin, and the hard bodily being sinks down like a gentleness. The shock <note>original: *Schrack* — a sudden flash or startle reflex</note> or vision of the light now rises in the astringent quality, quite gently and trembling; it is now bitter in the water, and the light dries it and makes it friendly and sweet. Within this resides life and joy, for the shock or flash now rises in all qualities, like the aforementioned wheel that turns itself; there all seven spirits rise into one another and give birth to themselves as if in a circle, and the light becomes shining in the midst of the seven spirits, and shines back into all the spirits, and therein all the spirits triumph and rejoice in the light.

Just as the seven wheels turn upon the single hub as upon their heart which holds them, and they hold the hub; so also the seven spirits give birth to the **Heart** <note>Böhme’s term for the Son of God, the second person of the Trinity</note>, and the Heart holds the seven spirits; and there, voices and the divine realm of joy, heartfelt loving, and kissing arise. For when the spirits surge into one another with their light, turning and ascending, life is always being born; for one spirit always gives its taste to the other—that is, it infects the other. Thus one tastes the other and feels the other, and in the sound one hears the other, and the sound or tone penetrates from all seven spirits toward the Heart, and rises in the Heart in the flash of

<column-break/>

light; there, voices and the joy-realm of the Son of GOD arise, and all seven spirits triumph and rejoice in the Heart of GOD, each in its own quality. For in the light, in the sweet source-water, all astringency and hardness, all bitterness and heat are softened, and there is nothing in the seven spirits but a lovely scent and a wonderful birthing, like a **Holy Play of God**. Their sharp birth, however, remains hidden like a kernel <note>original: *Kern* — the seed or essence</note>, for it is softened by the light and the sweet water. Just as a sour and bitter green apple is compelled by the sun to become lovely to eat, yet still retains all its qualities; so also the Godhood retains its qualities, but they wrestle quite gently, like a lovely play. This, then, is the true birth of the Godhood, which has been this way from eternity in all ends (wherever God has introduced Himself into nature and creature) and remains so into eternity.

**16. Question: What then is born in this Anguish-Torment?**

**Answer:** The **Anguish-Torment** <note>original: *Angst-Qual* — a technical term for the fourth property of nature where the tension of the first three properties reaches a breaking point</note> first gives birth to the **Sulphur** or **Balsam**, which then ignites. We ground ourselves in the deep sense of the mind and find that **Desire** <note>original: *Begehren*</note> is astringent and attractive; for it is the stern power—namely, not in one end but everywhere—[the power] to bring the wide into the narrow, and to manifest itself; for otherwise there would be nothing in the whole depth and nothing would appear, but it would be eternally still. So the Desire draws into itself; and since it has nothing but itself, that which is drawn in is the "pregnancy" of the Desire, making the Desire full. And since it is yet nothing but a darkness (for the drawn-in substance is thicker than the Will), it is the darkness of the "thin" Will; for the Will is thin as a "nothing" and entirely still, but the Desire makes it full. And the attraction in the Desire are the **Essences**, acting as a sting of sensitivity, which...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the "Seven Qualities of Nature." Having previously described the first two qualities—contraction (astringency) and the sting (bitterness/motion)—the text now explains how their collision creates the third quality: the "anguish" or "torment" that leads to the manifestation of fire and light. This section also bridges the gap between divine spiritual principles and the physical chemistry of the world (Salt, Mercury, and Sulfur).</meta>

### Of Eternal Nature

For two things are understood by the fire: the **freedom** outside of nature, and the **severity** of nature. You have an example of this in a stone from which one strikes fire: For when one strikes upon the sharpness of the stone, the bitter **sting** <note>original: *Stachel* — the second quality of nature, representing motion and friction</note> of nature sharpens itself and becomes enraged to the highest degree; then nature is burst asunder in that sharpness so that the freedom appears like a flash of lightning. And you can see that this is true by this: as soon as the freedom appears, it consumes the darkness, and therefore the sharpness of God the Father is a **consuming fire** <note>original: *verzehrend Feuer* — a biblical reference to Deuteronomy 4:24</note>. For as soon as the flash in that sharpness seizes upon something substantial, it consumes it instantly, so that no nature remains there anymore. And the reason the flash vanishes so quickly is that the sharpness cannot hold it; for it is free from nature and is only seen in the bursting asunder. We give you this to understand: that this freedom outside of nature is God the Father, and nature is born within him in such a way that he is the Almighty of nature, just as the human mind is over the senses; for everything has a single origin.

<margin>The Threefold Life 4. 12. 26.</margin>
Now, this is not to be understood as referring to God in and of himself, nor that there is literal sulfur in God; rather, it means that just as sulfur is produced in temporal, earthly nature, so a spiritual, heavenly **sulfur** <note>original: *Sulphur* — Böhme uses this alchemical term to describe the "oil" or "balsam" of life</note>—an oil and balsam—is produced in eternal nature. Just as the Holy Scripture speaks: for just as little as one might say that there is **salt, sulfur, and mercury** <note>original: *Sal, Sulphur und Mercurius* — the *Tria Prima* or three primary substances of alchemy</note> in God, one can also not say that he is earth, water, oil, or balsam, etc., even though the Holy Scripture is accustomed to speaking in this way.

**17. Question: What then is actually the effect of the third quality of the working Will of God in the property of the Father?**

**Answer:** In the **anguish-torment** <note>original: *Angst-Quall* — Böhme derives "Angst" from the Latin *angustus*, meaning "narrowness" or "constriction"</note> there is now born sensibility, or perception and finding, where God—who is otherwise incomprehensible and unsearchable to nature in eternal freedom—becomes manifest, perceptible, and findable. This sensibility arises from the ignition, and the ignition from the movement and the heavy driving and rubbing of the desiring, attracting, precipitating, and sublimating properties; there, each property penetrates the other, and each ignites the other, so that the **Will** <term>Will: the primal divine intent that precedes existence</term> recognizes where the suffering comes from. For if there were no sensibility, the Will would know nothing of properties, for it would be at one with itself; thus, the Will takes nature into itself by feeling the sharp movement within itself. This movement is in itself like a **turning wheel**—not that there is literally such a turning, but it is so within the properties; for the desire pulls inward, and the movement presses outward. Thus, in such anguish, the Will can go neither inward nor outward, and yet it is pulled both inward and outward; so it remains a "quality" <note>original: *Gestalt* — also meaning form or configuration</note> which wants to go both inward and outward—that is, upward and downward—and yet can go nowhere, but is an anguish and the true foundation of **Hell** and **God's wrath**, as this anguish stands in the dark, sharp movement.

<column-break/>

It is from this foundation that the **sulfur-spirit**, together with the matter of a sulfurous kind, arose in the creation of the world; this sulfur-spirit is the natural life of earthly and elemental creatures. The **wise pagans** <note>referring to ancient philosophers and alchemists like Hermes Trismegistus or Paracelsus</note> understood this foundation to some extent, for they said: "In sulfur, mercury, and salt consist all things in this world." By this, they did not only look at the material substance, but at the **spirit** from which the matter arises; for their foundation does not consist in literal salt, mercury, and sulfur—they do not mean that—but rather the spirit of such properties, in which everything consists that lives, grows, and exists in this world, whether it be spiritual or material. For by **salt**, they indicate the sharp magnetic desire of nature; and by **mercury**, they indicate the movement and separation of nature, through which every thing is marked and formed; and with **sulfur**, they have designated the sensitive, willing, wak-

## 2. Part / Chapter 5.

growing life is indicated. For in the Spirit of Sulfur lies the Oil, wherein the Fire-Life burns; and in the Oil lies the **Quintessence** <note>original: *Quinta Essentia* — the "fifth essence," a pure spiritual substance that alchemists believed was the underlying life-force of all matter</note>, as the sulfurous **Mercury** <note>original: *Mercurius* — representing the active, moving principle in nature</note>, the true life of nature, which is an outflow from the Word of Divine Power and Motion, wherein the foundation of Heaven is understood. And in the Quintessence lies the **Tincture** <note>original: *Tincktur* — the highest spiritual power that can transform or "tint" lower substances into higher ones</note>, as the Paradisiacal ground, the out-flowed Word of Divine Power, wherein the properties lie in equality. Thus, we understand the third property of nature, namely **Anguish** <note>original: *Angst* — the tension or "dread" caused by the first two properties (contraction and motion) rubbing against each other</note>, as the sharpness and painfulness of fire, as the burning and consuming; for when the Will is placed in such sharpness, it always desires to consume the cause of such sharpness, for it always presses back toward the Unity of God, as toward rest. And the Unity presses with its outflow toward this motion and sharpness, and is thus a perpetual joining together for the revelation of the Divine Will, just as one always finds a Heavenly element within the earthly in these three—Salt, Sulfur, and Oil—if one understands this rightly and meditates according to the Spirit. For in the sharpness lies the Soul of a thing, and in the motion lies the true life of the sensory kind, and in the Oil of the sulfur lies the powerful Spirit, which originates from the Tincture. Thus, a Heavenly element always lies hidden within the earthly, for the invisible spiritual world flowed out along with the creation.

The fourth property or form of eternal nature is the **Spiritual Fire**, wherein the Light, as the Unity, becomes manifest; for the luster of the fire originates from the out-flowed Unity, which has given itself into the natural desire; and the agony and burning of the fire, as the heat, originates from the sharp consumptiveness of the first three properties. This happens thus: The eternal Unity, which I elsewhere in several of my writings call the

<column-break/>

**Freedom**, is the gentle stillness and is lovely, like a gentle act of kindness; and one may not express what kind of gentleness exists in the Unity of God outside of nature. But the three properties leading to nature are sharp, painful, and terrifying. In these three painful properties stands the out-flowed Will, which has arisen through the Word or Divine Breathing, and the Unity also stands therein. Thus, the Will longs for the Unity, and the Unity longs for the sensibility—that is, for the fiery ground. Thus, one longs for the other, and when that happens (understand the longing), it is like a **crack** or a flash of lightning <note>original: *Schrack* — a sudden shock or "shriek" of light that occurs when the divine light meets the dark properties</note>, just as if one rubbed steel and stone together, or poured water into fire, to speak in a metaphor. In this glance, the Unity feels the sensibility, and the Will receives the gentle Unity; thus, the Unity becomes a luster of the fire, and the fire becomes a **Love-burning**, for it receives essence or power from the gentle Unity.

In such an ignition, the darkness of the **magnetic impression** <note>the first property of nature, which draws inward and creates density</note>, or simplicity, is permeated with the light, so that it is no longer recognized, though it remains eternally within itself in the Impression.

-> Clavis 49. 51. <-

This ignition of fire is now the fourth form of nature, or the effective Will of God according to the property of the Father. And here is the **parting-point** <note>original: *Scheide-Ziel*</note>, where light and darkness separate, each into a **Principle** <note>original: *Principium* — Böhme's term for a fundamental realm of existence (Dark, Light, or Outer world)</note>, where the Spirit of Life, or the encompassed Divine Mercury, ignites within the enclosure, dissolves the anguish, and a **crack** rises up; and in rising, it is caught and bound again by the harsh property, so that it is startled and sinks into the fire-power. From this sinking, the **sweet Spirit-water** is born, wherein the fire becomes a light, of which more shall be said below. This crack creates within the first three—the harsh, bitter, and anguish—the hostile, terrifying life of the **Wrath of God** <note>original: *Zorn Gottes*</note> according to the dark impression within itself; for where this ignition takes the upper hand in nature and the creature, there God is manifest as an angry, jealous God. But where the fire-crack sinks into the Spirit, there God is manifest as Light and Love.

So understand now the ignition of the fire correctly. It occurs through a **conjunction** <note>original: *Conjunction* — a joining together or alignment</note> of the first three properties within their enclosure in **Wrath** <note>original: *Grimm* — the harsh, severe, or fierce quality of nature's foundation</note>; and on the other hand, from the lovely freedom of the **Being** <note>original: *Entis* — the essence or substance</note> in the **Balance** <note>original: *Temperatur* — a state of perfect harmony or "tempering" where no single quality dominates</note>, where Love and Wrath enter into one another. For just as when one pours water into fire, there is a **shock** <note>original: *Schrack* — a sudden crack, tremor, or explosive flash caused by the meeting of opposites</note>; so also, when Love enters into the Wrath, a shock occurs. In Love, this shock is the beginning of the flash or the **radiance** <note>original: *Glast*</note>, where the singular Love makes itself perceptible as Majesty or as shining—as the beginning of the kingdom of joy, in the same way that light becomes visible in fire. Also, in Love is the beginning of the **separation of powers** <note>original: *Schiedlichkeit der Kräffte*</note>, so that the powers become expressive through the shock, from which the scent and taste of the different qualities arise; and in the first three properties, the painful nature of fire is understood. For:

1.  **Harshness** compresses and devours;
2.  **Bitterness** is the sting of woe;
3.  **Anguish** is now death, yet also the new fire-life.

For Anguish is the **Mother of Sulfur** <term>Sulfur: in Böhme’s alchemy, this represents the "burning" or "willing" spirit of life</term>, and the **Essence** <note>original: *Ens*</note> of Love gives to the Anguish—as the Mother of Sulfur—a refreshment unto new life, from which the luster of the fire originates. For we see that the light is gentle and the fire is painful: Thus we understand that the ground of the light originates from the Balance—that is, from the unification of the **Abyss** <note>original: *Ungrund* — the groundless "Nothing" or the divine mystery beyond existence</note> of the singular Love, which is called GOD—and the fire originates from the leading will in the Word, out of the **Active Knowledge** <note>original: *Scientz* — the internal "knowing" or formative power within nature</note> through the impression and introduction into the first three properties.

In the Light, the Kingdom of God is now understood as the Kingdom of Love; and in the Fire, God’s strength and omnipotence are understood as the spiritual life of the creatures; and in the Darkness, Death, Hell, and the Wrath of God—along with the anxious, poisonous life—are understood, as can be seen in the earth, stones, metals, and creatures of the external, created world. And I admonish the reader: do not understand this high, supernatural sense (where I speak of God and the **Birth**—

<column-break/>

—of the **Great Mystery** <note>original: *Mysterii Magni* — the "Mysterium Magnum," the chaotic "potential" from which God brings forth the universe</note>) in an earthly way; for I am only indicating the ground from which the earthly arose. Thus, I must often speak in a way that the reader may understand, so that he may reflect upon it and swing himself into the inner ground; for I must often give heavenly things earthly names for the sake of expressing how the earthly proceeded from them.

In the ignition of the fire lies the entire ground of all hidden secrets. For the shock of the ignition is called in nature **Salt-Nitre** <note>original: *Sal Nitri* — not common saltpeter, but a spiritual "lightning" or explosive force that shatters the darkness to reveal light</note>, as a root of all the foundations of the powers—a separation of nature, where the **Active Knowledge** <note>original: *Scientz*</note> divides itself into the infinite, and yet always remains thus in the shock, as a shock of separation within the essence. In the ignition of the fire (understood according to the inner, magical fire), the Spirit of God makes itself "weaving," in the manner that air originates from fire. For there originates the **One Element**, which in the external world has unfolded itself into four elements. Understand it thus: In the flash of fire and light, the separation occurs. The Spirit separates itself upward—understood as into the fiery Knowledge of the powers—for it proceeds out of the fire-shock as a new life, and yet it is not a "new" life, but has merely taken on nature in this way. And the **Essence** <note>original: *Ens*</note> of Love remains in the middle, standing as a center of the Spirit, and gives forth from itself an **Oil** (understand this spiritually), in which the light lives; for it is the Essence of fiery Love. From this fiery Essence of Love, the **Tincture** <note>original: *Tinctur* — the highest spiritualizing power</note> proceeds upward with the Spirit into the height, as the "spiritual water," the power of fire and light, whose name is **Virgin Sophia** <note>original: *Jungfrau Sophia* — Divine Wisdom personified</note>, as seen in the **4th Book of Esdras, chapter 1, verse 39** <note>original: *4. lib. Esdræ* — Böhme is referencing the apocryphal book 2 Esdras (4 Esdras in the Vulgate)</note>.

You dear wise ones, if only you knew her, it would be good for you; that same "little water" is true **Humility**, which is immediately transmuted with the **Balance** <note>original: *Temperatur*</note> and is drawn back in by the light; for it is the light’s soul according to Love, and the fire is the man, as the Father’s property, namely...

18. Question: How does such a shock <note>original: *Schrack* — a sudden tremor or explosive flash</note> occur in the ignition of the fire?

**Answer:** The harsh, severe property, which is a coldness, is terrified before the light and before the great gentleness, the free delight, and becomes within itself a shock of death; then the fierceness and cold property retreats into itself and shuts itself up as if dead, for in the shock the dark mind becomes substantial; it gathers itself into itself as its own, as a great fear of the light, or an enmity toward the light.

<margin>Mysterium Magnum 3, 26.</margin>

<column-break/>

19. Question: How then does the fire-flash go forth in the shock?

**Answer:** When the life-spirit of its fierce fire-power rises up in the anguish, it is immediately bound by the harsh, cold property, where then the fire of its fierceness sinks down and becomes, as it were, water. In this water, the ignited life-spirit becomes burning and shining like a fire in oil; for it has a sharp, attractive hunger and thirst, and the water is its refreshment and drink. Now, where the water is more powerful, or as powerful as the fire's strength, it results in an ignition of light; but where the harsh, severe quality retains the upper hand, the flash is extinguished, and the life-spirit is bound in the torment of the dark hells; thus, two principles separate here: one to the fire, and the other to the light.

In this shock or fire-ignition, two kingdoms separate, and yet they are only one; but they divide themselves in essence, source-torment <note>original: *Quall* — a term used by Böhme to combine the ideas of a 'source' (Quelle) and 'torment' (Qual)</note>, and will; they also become invisible to one another; neither perceives the other in its own source-torment, and yet they are from one original state; they also hang together, and one without the other would be nothing, and yet they both take their source-torment from one original state. Understand it thus: When the flash or shock arises, it is a single point, and in the glance it makes a triangle $\Delta$ or a cross $\oplus$; and this is the correct interpretation of the symbol. $\oplus$ is first the sharpness of all things, and the manifested God in Trinity. The triangle indicates the hidden God, as the Word or Divine Understanding, which is threefold in its eternal, beginningless birth, and yet only one in its revelation. In the fire- or light-world, this trinity reveals itself in the birth; not as if there were a place where such a figure stood: No, but the entire birth is thus: wherever the Divine fire reveals itself in something, it makes a triangle $\Delta$ in its ignition, which the children of men should well note—how life is also ignited in a triangle, signifying the Holy Trinity. And because the light of life was in the Word of the Deity, which...

...which was breathed into man (as John says in the 1st Chapter) but faded away from God in Paradise, so it had to be born again at the <term>T</term> <note>original: *T* — the letter T is used here as a symbol for the Cross or the "Tau," representing the sacrificial death and rebirth in Christ</note>.

### Explanation of the Character Above.

The upper cross signifies the unformed Word in <term>Trinity</term> <note>original: *Dreyfaltigkeit*</note> outside of all nature, and the character stands thus: <term>A</term> <note>original: *A* — likely representing the Alpha, the beginning or the "unformed" state of the divine will</note>. And this character signifies the formed Word <term>T</term>, as the angelic world. But the fact that the <term>Triangle</term> <note>original: *Dreyangel* — a Böhmean term for the Trinity as a geometric force</note> with the three straight points has transformed into such a <term>T</term>, wherein death was strangled, points us to the great love of God. This love from the Triangle has sunk itself back into our humanity, after we had deviated from the Triangle into the light of life. Therefore, the great Angle leads itself downward, signifying great humility, and also that we have lost the fiery angle that goes upward, which we possessed when we were God’s image and likeness. For this reason, the upper Angle has turned itself downward in the <term>Rebirth</term> <note>original: *Wieder-Geburt*</note> at the <term>T</term>, and no longer leads a point upward. This now points us to true <term>Yieldedness</term> <note>original: *Gelassenheit* — a central concept in German mysticism meaning the total surrender of the self-will to God</note> under the <term>T</term>, where we are born anew in the light through the spirit of Christ by the great humility of God. Now the will divides itself in the <term>Fire-shock</term> <note>original: *Feuer-Schrack* — the sudden, explosive moment of ignition where darkness is transformed into light</note> into two kingdoms, where each dwells within itself: the shock in the darkness is God’s wrath, and the shock in the re-capturing toward the free desire becomes the high-triumphant Divine kingdom of joy within that free desire. For thus the free desire becomes uplifting and is introduced into a struggling play of love; and thus it becomes tormenting and active. This is not to be understood as God having a beginning in this way, but rather it is the eternal beginning of the manifested God—how the Divine understanding reveals itself through power in distinctness and leads into kingdoms, which is an eternal birthing. We speak here only of how the invisible, imperceptible God leads and reveals Himself in perceptibility.

<column-break/>

Now, however, with the ignition of the fire, we are to understand two kinds of fire, two kinds of spirit, and two kinds of essence: namely, a love-fire in the free desire, which becomes substantial through the <term>Impression</term> <note>original: *Impression* — the "contracting" or "drawing in" of the divine desire to create form</note> or longing; and in the fire, spirit and essence separate, yet they are in one another just as spirit and body are one. And as the spirit is, so also is that same essence. And just as there is a holy, sweet essence and a holy, sweet spirit in the Impression of the free desire, so also in the dark Impression there is a harsh, stern, coarse, and bitter essence and spirit. As the essence is, so also is the mind of the understanding and the will within that essence. Although the Eternal is as something spiritual compared to Time, the true spirit is nevertheless much more subtle than that which it makes into a <term>Substance</term> <note>original: *Substanz*</note> in its capturing; for the true, understanding spirit first proceeds out of the substance, whereas before the substance it is only a will and not manifest to itself; for the will leads itself into substance and essence so that it may be manifest to itself.

Now we must consider the distinctness in the fire. When the fire ignites, the fire-flash or shock is <term>salnitrous</term> <note>original: *salnitrisch* — Böhme's term for the explosive, creative, and "salt-peter-like" quality of the divine flash of manifestation</note>, where all powers give themselves away from one another and go into division. There the eternal, single power of God reveals itself and divides into distinctness in properties, both spiritual and substantial, as can be seen in this world, where then the manifold salts originate. These entered into such matters with the <term>Creation</term> <note>original: *Schöpffung*</note>, which in eternity was only a spiritual essence, but with the beginning of time became coarse and hard.

From this eternal root also originate the manifold spirits, good and evil, as well as the manifold stars, together with the four <term>Elements</term> <note>original: *Elemente*</note>, and everything that lives and moves. But the division within itself is to be understood by us thus: when the flash rises, the separation goes out from the fire; the fire-shock is consuming, it seizes the captured essence...

## Part 2 / Chapter 5

...it [the fire] consumes both—that which is in the **free delight** <note>original: *freyen Lust* — Böhme uses "Lust" not in a carnal sense, but as a primal longing or divine joy</note> and that which is in the **roughness**—and devours it instantly. For here, in the fire, the **eternal will** (which is a <term>bottomless abyss</term> <note>original: *kein Grund* or *Ungrund* — the undifferentiated state of God before any "ground" or creation exists</note>) becomes revealed. Nothing of substance can endure before it; it swallows everything into its "Nothingness." And here lies the <term>origin</term> <note>original: *Urstand* — a fundamental Böhmean term for the primal source or "original standing" of a thing</note> of eternal death or perishability. 

Yet within this devouring lies the highest <term>Arcanum</term> <note>Latin: "secret" or "mystery" — in alchemy, a hidden transformative power</note> or secret: For the true, essential, living spirit and understanding proceed out of this perishability and make a new beginning. The first beginning belongs to God, who leads Himself from the Abyss into a "Ground" <note>the foundational reality</note> for His own contemplation. But this [new] beginning, which emerges again out of the devouring fire, is a **spiritual beginning** and yields three worlds: 

1. First, the **dark fire-world** in heat and cold, a total roughness without substance. 
2. The second world is the **spiritual light-world** or **angelic world**. 
3. And the third had its beginning along with **Time**. When God moved both inner worlds, He birthed and created this outer, visible world out of them into a form of time. 

Now, the division within the fire of perishability is to be understood thus: the powers that had made the first "impression" <note>the contraction of spirit into matter</note> substantial are, in the fire, led into spirituality.

**I.** From the **free delight** there goes forth a <term>spiritual Mystery</term> <note>original: *geistlich Mysterium*</note>. This is spiritual according to the Godhead and the eternal understanding; it is the angelic life and light, as well as the true human life and all that resembles it, for these are the powers of God. Therefore, the angels carry the great name of **GOD** within them, as do the upright humans who possess the divine power.

**II.** From the essence of the free delight, a **heavenly corporeality** emerges in the fire as an **oily power**. This is the body or essence of the "Understanding," in which the fire burns, and from which the shine or radiance arises.

<column-break/>

**III.** From the origin and the spiritual oil, there goes forth a **weaving delight**, like an element, and this is the **Divine Element**.

**IV.** From this element goes forth a **watery quality**, though here it is to be understood only spiritually. This is the **water** of which Christ speaks when He says He would give it to us to drink, and whoever drinks it, it would spring up in him as a fountain of eternal life. It is the "water above the firmament" of which Moses says that God separated it from the outer waters beneath the firmament. This watery and elemental quality proceeds from the essence of the **free delight** which is consumed in the fire; thus the **Word of Understanding**, which has now revealed itself in the fire, speaks these powers out of itself as a now living and weaving essence, and the angelic world is understood to be within this.

In the separation from the **dark quality**, through the "Speaking Word" in the division of the fire, there goes forth another <term>Principle</term> <note>original: *Principium* — a foundational source or beginning</note> or start of a different quality:

1. From the harsh, stern "impression" comes a **hellish** (from which Hell takes its name), thirsty, fierce torment. It is entirely rough, in the manner of cold or hard stones, a mind that is as terrifying as a flash of lightning.

2. Out of this fiery spirit in the darkness, there also goes forth an **oil**, but it is of a **poisonous quality**. For this is the evil <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: *Mercurius* — in Böhme’s system, Mercury represents the restless, vibrating life-force; here it is the "poisonous" version of that force</note> born from the sting in the anxious harshness.

3. The anguish also creates a **weaving mind** or spirit, similar to the Element, but entirely in a high-fierce, penetrating quality. In this, the great fiery power and the will in the **Wrath of God** (or the "Grimness of God") find their origin. This is what **Lucifer** desired to be and to rule within, and for that reason, he became a devil—as one spewed out from the fire of Love into the dark fire.

4. A **watery quality** also goes forth from this fierce quality through the devouring in the fire, as if from the first dark impression. However, it is much more a **poisonous source** in which the dark life burns.

# Of Eternal Nature.

## Z 3

But that I write of Oil and Water here, understand it thus: In the kindling of the fire within the **Flash** <note>original: *Schreck* — often translated as "terror" or "shock," this refers to the sudden, explosive moment when the dark desire meets the light's freedom, igniting a transformative flash</note>, both in the **Flash of Joy** in the free delight-being, and in the **Flash of Wrath** <note>original: *Grimmigkeit* — the fierce, biting quality of the dark fire</note> in the impression <note>the "drawing-in" or contraction</note> of the dark spirit-being—the substance which the first desire has coagulated or grasped is consumed in the **Fire-Flash**. That is, it dies to its "Selfhood" and is grasped into the single Spirit which has here revealed itself in the fire of wrath and in the light-fire of the joy-realm; and that Spirit now speaks it forth from itself again as two spiritual worlds. Thus, understand it rightly:

Out of the fiery quality, there now proceeds in the "breathing out" from the source of life: toward the free delight, it is **Holy and Joy-rich**; toward the darkness, it is **painful and fierce**. The fierceness and painful source is the root of the joy-realm, and the joy-realm is the root of the enmity of the dark fierceness; so that there is a **Contrarium** <note>Latin: "Opposite" or "Counter-force"</note>, through which the Good may be made manifest and it may be known what is good. And the substance that died in the fire—which the first desire in the free delight had coagulated and made dark—proceeds through the **Fire-Dying** as a **spiritual Oil**, which is the quality of the fire and light. And out of that mortification <note>the "killing" or dying-away of the self-will</note> comes a **Water** as a deadened, unfeeling being, serving as a housing for the Oil, wherein the fire-source or spirit conducts its life-regiment. This Water is the food of the fire-source, which it draws back into itself and swallows, thereby quenching the fire-source and leading it into the greatest **Gentleness** <note>original: *Sanfftmuth* — the meekness or sweetness characteristic of the light-world</note>. In this gentleness the life of great Love arises as the "good taste," so that the fire-source in the Oil, through the mortification in the water-source, becomes a humility and gentleness. For no fire-spirit can exist without the mortification of its own right, or its own essential sap; but the Water (which was previously a grasped being from the free delight, yet died in the fire) can transform the fire’s essence into a gentle desire.

<margin>*Mysterium Magnum*, chapter 4, sections 1 and 21.</margin>

<column-break/>

Understand it rightly: In the kindling of the fire, two wills part into two ways. One rises in **Wrath**, for the birthing of the fierce fire; the other imagines <note>Böhme uses "imagination" as a creative, shaping force of the will</note> toward the **Center of the Word**, and sinks down from the anguish—as if through a dying—into the free life. In this way, it brings a life out of the anguish-source with itself into freedom, so that the **eternal Abyss** <note>original: *Ungrund* — the bottomless "Nothing" out of which all begins</note> is recognized as a life, and out of the "Nothing" an eternal life comes to be.

Thus, as the first path of the will rises to the birth of fire, we recognize it as the **first nature**, as the Father’s nature in fierce wrath; and the other entrance of the will into freedom, into the **Center of the Heart**, we recognize as the **Divine Nature**, as the life in the Light, in the power of the Godhead. To search further regarding the other will of the eternal Father, who is called **GOD**: He desires the Light in the Center of His Heart, and the revelation of the **Trinity** in Wisdom. That same will is set or directed toward the Center of Nature, for out of Nature the luster of **Majesty** must originate. Thus, that same other will in the Word of Life has freedom within itself; and the "anguish-will" in the sharpness of nature desires that freedom, so that freedom might be revealed within the anguish of the fierce mind. From this arises the anguish: that the first will wants to be free from the dark bitterness, and Freedom desires revelation, for it cannot find itself within itself without sharpness or pain. For the will of Freedom, which is called **Father**, desires to reveal itself, and it cannot do that without qualities.

Therefore, he is a "desirer" of the qualities which originate in the anguish, in the essences within the fire, so that he may reveal his wonders, power, and colors with them—which cannot happen without Nature. Thus the first will, who is called Father and is Freedom itself, desires Nature; and Nature desires with—

# Of Eternal Nature

There is lamentation and misery, and a compassion, in which the Father’s will—which is nonetheless free—manifests itself in the **wrath** of nature, so that the wrath may be softened. But nevertheless, on one side, the **anxious wheel of wrath** remains for itself; for in the **shock** <note>original: *Schrack*—the sudden transition or "flash" from darkness to light</note> a killing occurs—though not a silent death, but rather a **deadly life**, which resembles the most evil essence, as if a **parting-water** <note>original: *Scheide-Wasser*—a historical term for nitric acid or aqua fortis, used to separate metals by dissolving them</note> or poison were within it. For such a thing must be if the **Center of Nature** <note>original: *Centrum Naturæ*</note> is to stand eternally. And on the other side, life proceeds out of death, and thus death must be a cause of life; otherwise, if there were no such poisonous, fierce **torment** <note>original: *Quall*—Boehme uses this term to mean both a painful torment and a "welling up" or source of energy</note>, the fire could not be brought forth, and there would be no fire-sharpness or essence; thus there would also be no light, and no life that could find itself.

The first will, which is called the **Father**, is thus found in the **Wonder**. And the other will, which is called the **Son**, is thus found in **Power**. From this, the **Realm of Joy** also originates; for if there were no woe, there would also be no Realm of Joy. This, however, is the Realm of Joy: that life is redeemed out of **anguish**, even though life only originates in this way. Therefore, creatures have poison for their life, such as **gall** <note>In historical medicine, gall or bile was seen as the source of heat and bitterness that drove movement and emotion</note>. The gall is the cause of movement, so that life may arise, for it causes the fire in the heart; and the true life is the fire, but it is not the *form* of life. From the **fire-life**, the true spirit first arises; it proceeds from the fire

<column-break/>

in the light; it is free from the fire, like the **air**, which, although it originates from the fire, is free from it. For the true spirit—or in man, the spirit that is born from the **soul-fire**—has its quality in the light of life that burns from the fire; for it arises out of death, it proceeds out of dying. The hostile torment has remained behind for it in the fire, and continues beneath the fire, in the cause of the fire, as in fierce death.

Thus, fierce death is a **root of life**. And here, you humans, consider your death, and also **Christ's death**, who has born us again out of dying through the fire of GOD. For out of dying, the free life is born; whatever can proceed from dying is redeemed from death and the fierce torment. This is now his Realm of Joy: that no fierce torment is in him any longer; it has remained behind for him in dying (in the dark world), and thus life out of death reaches **eternal freedom**, where there is no more fear or terror. For in life, the **shock** is broken. The true life is a power of joys, an **eternal well-being**; for there is no torment in it, but only a **desire**, which has all the qualities of the torment, and yet the torment cannot rise up within it to ignite its quality there, for such a thing only increases the light and the freedom.
