# Chapter VI.
## Concerning the Second Principle, namely, of the working Will of GOD in the Word according to the property of the Son in Light, Love, Joy, and Peace.

**1. Question.**

Broadly, I have grasped the author’s meaning regarding the two properties of the Will in the ignition of the fire: toward the fire, and toward the light; for further clarification, let us now search more thoroughly and deeply into the active Will toward the light, wherein the Second Principle <note>original: *II. Principio*—In Boehme's system, the Second Principle is the world of Light and Love, associated with the Son of God, emerging from the First Principle of Fire and Strength.</note> stands. Dear sir, how does the Second Principle—wherein the Son of GOD is manifested as Light, Love, Joy, etc.—follow out of the first?

**Antw.**

Now I will write of the other Principle, of the clear, pure Godhead, the Heart of GOD. As mentioned above: in the first Principle there is Harshness, Bitterness, and Fire; yet these are not three things, but one, and one gives birth to the other. Harshness <note>original: *Herbe*—also translated as Astringency; the contracting force that "pulls" reality into being.</note> is the first Father; he is strict, drawing everything sharply to himself, and that same drawing-in is the Sting and Bitterness. This Bitterness cannot endure the Harshness and will not allow itself to be held captive in death, but stings and rises up as a fierce essence, yet it cannot leave its seat. Then a terrifying Anxiety <note>original: *Aengstlichkeit*</note> arises which finds no rest, and the birth stands like a turning wheel, so hard, stinging, and breaking—like a madness—which the Harshness cannot endure. Instead, it draws itself in ever more and harder, as if one were rubbing stone and steel together, from which the glinting Fire-Flash <note>original: *Feuer-Blitz*</note> rises. When the Harshness beholds this flash, she is terrified and sinks back, as if dead or overcome. And when the Fire-Flash enters its mother, the Harshness, and finds her thus overcome and gentle, it is much more terrified, and in that overcome Harshness, it instantly becomes white and bright.

<column-break/>

Now, when the Harshness receives this bright white light into herself, she is so greatly terrified that she sinks back as if dead and overcome; she stretches herself out and becomes quite thin and vanquished. For her own source was dark and hard; now it is light and gentle. Therefore, she is truly as if put to death, and is now the Water-Spirit <note>original: *Wasser-Geist*—This represents the transformation of the "hard" spiritual state into a "fluid," receptive, and humble state.</note>.

Thus the birth receives an Essence <note>original: *Essentiam*</note>: from the Harshness it is sharp, and from the Light it is sweet and thinly expanding. And now, when the Fire-Flash enters its mother and finds her so thin, sweet, and light, it loses its right to its "Qualifying" <note>original: *Qualificirung*—Boehme’s term for the active interaction of spiritual properties or "qualities."</note>; it no longer rushes upward, no longer tears or rages, nor does it sting anymore. Instead, it remains in its mother and loses its fiery right; it trembles and rejoices in its mother. And in that same joy within the Water-Source, the lovely source of unfathomable Love rises up; this is the Second Principle which dawns there. For the entire birthing process now turns into a heartfelt Love, because the Harshness now loves the Light because it is so blissful and beautiful. Through that same lovely bliss, she becomes so sweet, friendly, and humble; and the Bitterness now loves the Harshness because she is no longer dark and so strictly drawing-in, but is sweet, mild, pure, and light. There the "Taste" begins, so that each tastes the other and interacts with great desire within the other, so that there is nothing there but pure loving.

Thus the Bitterness now rejoices in its mother and strengthens itself therein, and through great joy it rises through all the Essences and announces to the Second Principle that the dear child is born; then all the Essences take heed, and [rejoice] in the dear...

Although no human tongue may here exalt or recount this, nor search out this depth where there is neither number nor end, yet we have power to speak of it, as children speak of their father. But to search out the entire depth troubles us, for God himself knows no beginning or end within himself.

And if we now wish to speak of the **Holy Trinity**, we must first say: there is one GOD, and he is called the Father and Creator of all things, who is almighty and all in all, all is his, and all has come from him, in him, and out of him, and remains in him eternally. And then secondly we say: he is threefold in Persons, and has from eternity begotten out of himself his Son, who is his Heart, Light, and Love, and yet they are not two beings, but one. From this it is now clearly seen, both the birthing and the quality of the second **Principle** <note>In the theology of Jacob Böhme, a "Principle" is a fundamental realm of existence. The Second Principle is the realm of Light and Love.</note>, in which the Son of God becomes manifest, as the unique delight of the Father full of majesty, love, grace, light, truth, and wisdom. Since he, as the Heart of God, eternally fulfills the desiring will of the Father with eternal delight, surrendering himself in perfect obedience to the Father's almighty attraction, he pacifies the rising, powerfully driving, and moving **Mercury** <note>original: *Mercurium*—the third "Source-Spirit" in Böhme's system, representing motion, sound, and the vital force that can be either chaotic or harmonious.</note> with humility and gentleness, dissolving the source of anguish <note>original: *Angst-Quall*—a play on the words for "torment" and "source-spring."</note>, and eternally brings forth light out of darkness, water out of fire, freedom out of anguish, the kingdom of joy out of bitterness, and full satisfaction out of the desire and hunger of the Godhead.

### 2. Question: What is actually understood here by the Light?

**Answer:** By the Light is understood the dawning of Divine Majesty, luster, and glory, wherein the eternal invisible Godhead is made manifest to the rational creature.

If we wish to contemplate the eternal Divine birth—in the light of Majesty—in its Trinity, and then the human soul in its image, substance, and being, we can conceive of this no better through a likeness than by fire and light; this is a true likeness. The fire signifies the eternal nature, which eternally originates in the desire, in the eternal will, from eternity to eternity; where the eternal Will-Spirit, out of the eternal Nothing—as from the freedom of the Godhead—manifests itself with its outgoing into the desire, with nature, and divides into two worlds or Principles, as into darkness and light. There each world has its **Center** <note>original: *Centrum*—the focal point of a specific quality or power.</note> for its source-drive within itself, and yet there is no separating from one another, but one world is in the other; the light holds the darkness captive; but the darkness is a cause of the fire, and the fire a cause of the light, for in the harsh and

<column-break/>

stern darkness originate the **Essences** <note>original: *Essentien*—the spiritual "stuff" or fundamental qualities that make up a being.</note>, or the source-quality of fire and nature.

Now we see indeed in fire and light two kinds of quality and desire; and we also see how the fire burns from a dark being, which indicates the dark world dwelling within itself. The fire signifies the eternal nature in the Father's will, in the desire for manifestation: and the light signifies the eternal freedom outside of nature, which manifests nature in its being. The fire has within it the fierce essence of the dark world, and the light has within it the eternal freedom, as a gentle, quiet delight.

Now, however, freedom and gentleness would not be manifest without the fire, but would be a quiet Nothing; and the fire also would have no luster outside of freedom, and neither fire nor light would be anything without the desire, which is the Center for the birthing-mother, and contains within itself the **Fiat** <note>original: *Fiat*—the Latin word for "let it be done," referring to the creative command of the Word of God.</note> of the Word. And in the desire is born the eternal Word, or the understanding, and also the Mirror of Wisdom, as well as the Mirror of Wrath from the root of the dark Center. And we see further how the fire dwells in the light, and the light in the fire, and one does not grasp the other: the light is born in the fire, as if through dying, or out of the consuming of the self; it shines out of death, and sinks into death within itself, and creates in itself a different quality than the fire is, another Principle, where another life goes forth, such as gentleness and lovely delight, whereas in the fire there is only anguish and pain. For we see that the light is as a Nothing compared to the fire and its root; for it is incomprehensible, and indicates to us the eternal freedom outside of nature, as the Divine Being and the angelic world; and yet it is everything, for it is all power of all Essences from the fire, and from nature in the light, and is a life of understanding, also of reason and sensibility, whereas in the fire nothing but opposition of will is understood. For the forms of the fiery nature are hostile...

# On the Revelation of God in the Second Principle

U 2

...one another; for **Harshness**, **Bitterness**, and **Anguish** are against each other, which are the root of the fire. Within the Desire stands the harshness, and in the harshness is the "pulling" <note>original: *das Ziehen*—the contraction or attraction that Böhme sees as the first step of creation.</note>, where the Nothing is led into Something, and the Will shadows itself with that which is drawn in. From this, a darkness and shadowing arises in the Desire, from which the other Will arises out of the first Desire to go out from the darkness; and yet it is no fleeing from one another, but rather the other Will enters into itself—into the **Freedom**, outside of the Desire, in the darkness—and thus brings the property of nature with it. This same fiery property is the revelation of **Freedom** as the "Nothing" <note>Böhme uses "Nothing" (Nichts) to describe the state of God before any manifestation or "Something" exists.</note>. For thus the luster and shine arise; for in Freedom, the property brought along by the other Will is placed into the still, gentle delight, and out of that same property a **Love-Desire** becomes.

Thus, fire and light indicate to us in a parable the Divine Being, and also the soul with its image. The matter from which the fire burns indicates the form of eternal nature and the dark world; and the fire indicates the property of the Father. The luster of the fire indicates the freedom outside of nature: The shine or the light indicates the other world, as another **Principle**, which is born out of the first, as out of the Father’s property, just as the Son of God is born out of the Father. The power of the light-shine indicates the Heart of God, as the Divine Center, as well as the understanding, wit, and wisdom; for in the power of the light stands the true life. The twofold spirit, which originates in the fire with two kinds of source-torment <note>original: *Quall*—a word Böhme uses to pun on *Qual* (torment) and *Quelle* (source-spring). It refers to the "rising quality" of a thing.</note>, as heat and air, indicates to us in a parable the Spirit of God: The hot one indicates the wrath and grimness of God, according to the eternal nature of the dark world, according to the property of grimness; and the gentle-airy one indicates the property of the gentle light, in the **Love-Desire**, out of the source of the light. The gentleness of the light indicates to us in a parable—

<column-break/>

—the Divine Being, or the **Water of Eternal Life**, in which Paradise is understood, and in the fiery property, Heaven.

Now we see how every fire draws the air back to itself and burns in the power of the air. For where a fire can have no air, it goes out; for the air blows up the fire and leads the essence of the light back into the fire, as the gentleness of the light—understand the **Water-Mother** <note>original: *Wassers-Mutter*—the spiritual "substance" or divine materiality that cools the fire of God's wrath into the light of His love.</note>, from which the luster in the fire originates. For gentleness originates from the Freedom outside the fire’s nature, as in the "Nothing," and each longs for the other. The grimness of the fire or nature longs for gentleness; and the gentleness, as the Freedom or the Nothing, longs for the revelation which becomes manifest in nature.

Now we see how the light gives a very friendly, joy-filled spirit out of the fire’s source: this same friendly and lovely aspect or spirit originates out of the swallowed-up water-source of gentleness, as if out of Freedom. While the fire draws the gentle essence of the light into itself, this same swallowed-up gentle spirit goes out again through the grimness of death, through the "consumability," into the light, and carries the property of nature with it; just as we then recognize in the air that it is a power of all life, and yet it is not nature in itself, but rules as a mighty spirit in nature.

Thus, in this prototype, the Divine Being is understood, and also eternal nature. Out of which desire and essence the **Third Principle**, as the outer visible world, was born and created in the beginning into a substantial being, together with all creatures. For from the eternal Mother has come the beginning Mother; for where there is nothing, nothing becomes; but where something has indeed become, it has become out of the Eternal, which was without beginning, and is the likeness, image, and essence of the eternal.

### 2. Question: What is actually understood here by the "Light"?

**Answer.** By the Light is understood the outflow of Divine Majesty, luster, and glory, in which the eternal, invisible Godhead becomes manifest to the sentient creature.

If we wish to consider the eternal Divine birth—in the light of Majesty, in its Trinity, and then the soul of man in its image, substance, and essence—we can devise no better comparison than that of fire and light; this is a true likeness. Fire signifies the eternal nature, which forever originates in the desire, in the eternal will, from eternity to eternity; where the eternal Will-Spirit, out of the eternal **Nothing**—as if out of the **Freedom** <note>The "Nothing" or "Freedom" refers to the *Ungrund*, the absolute state of God before any creation or manifestation began.</note> of the Godhead—reveals itself through its outflow into desire within nature, and divides into two worlds or principles: darkness and light. There, each world has its own center of torment within itself, and yet there is no departing from one another; instead, one world is within the other. The light holds the darkness captive, but the darkness is a cause of the fire, and the fire is a cause of the light; for in the harsh and stern darkness, the essences—or the torment of the fire and of nature—originate.

<column-break/>

Now we see indeed two kinds of torment and desire in fire and light; and we also see how the fire burns out of a dark essence, which indicates the dark world dwelling within itself. The fire signifies the eternal nature in the Father’s will, in the desire for revelation; and the light signifies the eternal freedom outside of nature, which reveals nature within the essence. The fire has within itself the fierce essence of the dark world, and the light has within itself the eternal freedom as a gentle, still delight.

But now, the freedom and gentleness would not be manifest without the fire, but would be a still "Nothing"; and the fire would also have no luster without the freedom. Neither fire nor light would be anything without the Desire, which is the center of the birthing-mother and holds within itself the **Fiat** <note>original: *Fiat*—Latin for "let there be." And we see further how the fire dwells in the light, and the light in the fire, and one does not seize the other: The light is born in the fire, as if through dying, or out of its "consumability." It shines out of death and sinks into death within itself, and creates in itself a different torment than the fire is—another **Principle** <note>original: *Principium*</note> where another life goes forth, such as gentleness and lovely delight, whereas in the fire there is only anguish and pain. For we see that the light is like a "Nothing" compared to the fire and its root; for it is incomprehensible, and points us toward the eternal freedom outside of nature, as the Divine Being and the angelic world. Yet it is everything, for it is all the power of all essences from the fire and from nature within the light, and it is a life of the understanding, as well as of reason and sensibility, whereas in the fire nothing but "Counter-Will" is understood. GOD is in all being, but not all being grasps him: only that which has proceeded from his eternal being grasps him—understand this as that which is of his essence, which stands within him. Böhme uses this to describe the external, material world as a secondary result of internal spiritual processes.</note> of external nature, but in the internal, in himself. The brilliance of the fire signifies GOD the Father; the form of the fire signifies eternal nature; and the power of the light signifies the Heart of GOD, as the true Godhead. For it carries a different Center of a different source-quality than the fire—namely, as a love-desire and gentleness. And the proceeding Spirit from the brilliance of the fire into the power of the light—out of the light’s essence, which is swallowed up by the fire, as out of love and gentleness—truly signifies to us the Holy Spirit, who always proceeds from the Father and Son, in the Divine power and essence, just as the air proceeds from fire and light and rules within the light's essence.

The outer world is entirely a likeness of the inner world, for the inner world has revealed itself through the outer, by which one can understand what the invisible GOD is in secret. One must not think that GOD is absent from anything, or from any place or site; He fills everything, but in his **Principle** <note>original: "Principio." A fundamental realm or governing state of existence.</note>, as in the middle world, which He is himself.

Just as the light comes from the fire, so the Son of GOD—and through him all recognition, revelation, and wisdom—becomes manifest from the Father and out of the darkness. He is called Light because this work of the Son in the Word reveals that which the Father works in the Word. For just as the day swallows the night, and the light swallows the darkness, so the Son reveals and glorifies the Father; indeed, the entire fullness of the triune Godhead becomes manifest in the Son.

Here one understands how the Son is a different Person than the Father. For he is the Light-World, yet he dwells in the Father, and the Father generates him in his will. He is truly the Father’s love, as well as his wonder, counsel, and power; for the Father generates him in his **Imagination** <note>In Böhme’s thought, "Imagination" is the creative, formative power of the will to give shape to spirit.</note> within himself, and leads him through his own fire—as through the Principle—through death, so that the Son makes and is another world, or another Principle, within the Father, just as the Fire-World exists in the darkness. Thus you also understand how the Father's eternal Spirit divides itself into three worlds. Firstly, he is the outgoing from the imagination of the first will of the **Unground** <note>original: "Ungrund." The "groundless" or "abyssal" void that exists before any creation or even before God's self-manifestation.</note>, who is called Father, in that he opens up Wisdom through his outgoing, and dwells in Wisdom, wearing it as his garment of great wonders. And then, secondly, he is the cause of the drawing-in toward the essence of darkness, as toward the other world, and is the cause and the spirit of the origin of the **essential fire**; He is himself the source-quality in the anguish of the Principle, and also the firing world, as the great life. And then, thirdly, he is also himself the one who leads the power out of the fire in the "dying" of the Principle, where the power separates itself from the anguish and the dying, and goes into freedom, and dwells in freedom, and makes the Light-World; thus he is the flame of love in the Light-World. And here, in this place, the precious name of GOD the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit has its origin. For in the firing world, he is not called the Holy Spirit.

3. Question: It seems somewhat difficult for me to understand such ways of speaking about GOD?

Answer: For this reason, we have faithfully warned above in our first part that the reader should not seek our meaning in the wisdom of this world, but in the light of eternal nature. We wish to have him directed there, as if into the new birth in the life of Christ; otherwise, we are mute and unintelligible to him. Apart from this, he may as well leave our writings unmastered, or he will eat the food of the first **Center** <note>original: "Centri." Do not look upon the hand of this pen <note>The author is referring to himself as merely the instrument of the writing.</note>—it is capable of nothing—but rather look at the **Center** where the light shines forth. It does not shine from this hand alone, but upon the whole world, like an opened seal in the eternal Center. Everyone may reach for it; it is not only outside of him, but within him. It simply means to unlock and to blossom with Jesus Christ, and to produce a flower—to bring forth an angelic world out of this world.

4. Question: What then is actually understood by "Love," and how does it have a "birthing" <note>original: "Gebährung." This refers to the process of generation or how a spiritual quality is "brought forth" or manifested.</note>?

Answer: Lest we should be mute and unintelligible to you

<column-break/>

in this description—since the concept does not exist in the spirit of this world—we will show you the other three heavenly forms and how they are born. Within these, GOD, the Kingdom of Heaven, Paradise, and the angelic world are primarily understood, so that the reader might be brought to an understanding. It is not to be understood that the Godhead thus takes a beginning or a change—no—but I write in the manner in which one should learn to understand the Divine Being. For we cannot use angelic words; and even if we used them, everything in this world would still appear as a created thing, and to the earthly mind, it would appear earthly. For we are also no more than a **Particular** <note>A "particular" refers to a single, limited part of a greater whole.</note> out of the Whole, and cannot speak the Whole, but only in **Piecemeal** <note>original: "Stück-werck." A reference to 1 Corinthians 13:9: "For we know in part [Stückwerk], and we prophesy in part."</note>; the reader should consider this. For the Divine Mind in the heart of GOD is alone a Whole, and nothing else; for everything else stands in the **Essences** <note>original: "Essentien." In Böhme's thought, these are the spiritual "substances" or dynamic qualities that make up the inner reality of things.</note>, and GOD alone is free, and nothing else. Therefore, we speak in piecemeal, and grasp the Whole in the mind; for we have no tongue to express it, except as if on a ladder for the reader.

If we then wish to write or speak rightly of GOD, we must speak of the Light and of the Flame of Love; for therein GOD is understood. Therefore understand us: GOD the Father is in himself, but without a name; for in himself he is the light, bright, and clear eternity without **Being** <note>original: "Wesen." Böhme uses this to mean "substance" or "manifestation." In his purely abstract state, God is "beyond" substance.</note>, if we speak purely of the Light of GOD. But if he does not wish to be without Being, then we understand his Will, which he grasps into himself out of nothing, merely out of and in himself. And we understand in his Will the **Desire**, and in the Desire the **Center of the Birthing-Mother** <note>original: "Centrum der Gebährerin." # 2. Part / Chapter 6.

The Mother <note>original: "Gebährerin." In Böhme's mystical philosophy, this refers to the generative power or "matrix" of nature that "gives birth" to reality.</note> in her desire creates the attraction, so that there is an eternal darkness in which Nature is born, as mentioned before.

Now the eternal Mother, in her first longing, desires Freedom—understand this to mean GOD—and not the darkness within herself. For He <note>Böhme often shifts between referring to the generative principle as "it" or "her" and the divine will as "He."</note> does not want the darkness, but only the Word that creates within the longing of the Mother. And there can be no Mother without an attraction which impregnates itself within the Will; in this impregnation, the **Center** <note>original: "Centrum."</note> of Nature stands. And there would be no Word unless there were Nature, for the Word originates within Nature.

And so, we give you here a very high and precious understanding of how two Words are born in Nature: one in the first **Center** of the Mother, in stern wrath <note>original: "Grimmigkeit." This term describes the harsh, consuming, and rigorous quality of the divine fire before it becomes light.</note>, to express the stern power of the Mother of serious, bitter wrath in the fire. This is here called the Nature of GOD the Father, which He thus brings forth in His quiet delight, within the vessel of His Will, without touching the freedom of the Light. And the other Word, which He brings forth out of Nature, out of gentleness—understand this as the eternal freedom of the Light, which is called GOD—which is out of Nature, beholds the dark Nature. Indeed, it is within the fire of sharpness, as previously mentioned, but the bitterness sinks into its own dark right and loses its stern right. For the flash of light <note>original: "Blitz." Böhme uses the metaphor of a lightning flash to describe the moment the divine light breaks through the dark fire of nature.</note> makes the dark, stern power thin again, and a "growth" <note>original: "Gewächse." Böhme uses the metaphor of a plant or growing organism to describe the unfolding of spiritual life.</note> arises within it from the innumerable essences; and that is the power of the second **Center**. For in this rising up there is a Love-Desire, and the eternal Light catches the freedom outside of Nature, so that the freedom outside of Nature is kindled in this Love, and thus becomes a desiring Light in which the radiance arises. For outside of Nature there is no radiance, even though there is a light, quiet delight; rather, the radiance first originates from the sharpness. Now, however, in the rising up of Love, no sharpness is

perceptible; and though it is present, it is nevertheless only a birth of joys, and a true fulfillment of the first Will, which is GOD’s, which He places into the desire, and thus brings forth Nature, and out of Nature the growth of Love.

Thus the second Word, or growth of Love, dwells in the first Will and is its true fulfillment, which He desires. For it is gentle, lovely, and friendly, and it is the power and heart of the first Will, from which the eternal desire always stands in growth and will. And so the Light bursts the gates of darkness, and the Love-growth goes out from the dark Nature and dwells in the eternal silence of the Father, and is the Father's power, and is called His Son. For the Father brings Him forth out of His eternal Will, and herein the Father’s radiance becomes manifest—which otherwise, in the first Will in dark Nature, appears only in fire, but in the second **Center** in Love, it appears in the Light.

And here, Love and enmity are considered—how they stand against one another. For Love is the death of wrath, and with its glance it takes away the power of wrath. Here, one must rightly consider the power of GOD in Love and Anger. But that the Love-birth may be born is caused by the first Will out of the quiet delight; for the quiet and bright delight is without torment; it does not desire wrath, yet it still creates wrath. For if there were no wrath, there would be no sharpness; thus the second **Center** of Love could not be born, out of which the supernatural Light becomes shining—wherein the name of GOD the Father and the Son then originates.

For if the eternal freedom did not give birth to the essence of Nature, He would not be a Father, but a Nothing. But since He gives birth to the essence of Nature, the Begetter is called Father, from whom it is born. Thus the Light shines in the darkness,

->Understand this as it may be; here observe properly.<-

**First** there is the **harsh** <note>original: "herbe." This refers to the astringent, contracting force—the first property of nature that draws things together into a solid form.</note> **quality**, then the **sweet**, and then the **bitter**; the **sweet** is positioned in the middle, between the **harsh** and the **bitter**. Now, the **harsh** always creates hardness, cold, and darkness; and the **bitter** tears, drives, rages, and cuts asunder. These two qualities rub and drive against each other so hard, and surge so violently, that they give birth to **Heat**. In these two qualities, this heat is initially dark, like the heat trapped within a stone. When one takes a stone, or something else hard, and rubs it against wood, both things become heated. Now, this heat is merely a darkness, and there is no light within it; so it is also in the Divine Power. Now, the **harsh** and **bitter** qualities, without the **sweet water**, rub and drive each other so hard that they give birth to the **dark heat** and ignite it within themselves. And that, taken together, is the **Wrath of GOD**, the fountain and origin of the hellish fire, as can be seen in the case of **Lucifer**. He exalted himself and compressed himself so hard with his legions that the **sweet source-water**—in which the **Light** is kindled and in which **Love** rises—dried up within him. Therefore, he is now eternally a **harsh, hard, cold, bitter, hot, sour, and stinking source-fountain**; for when the **sweet quality** dried up within him, it became a dark, sour stench, a valley of misery, and a house of corruption and wretchedness.

->Now further into the depth.<-

**When** the **harsh** and **bitter** qualities rub against each other so hard that they give birth to heat, the **sweet quality**—the **sweet source-water**—is positioned in the middle between the

<column-break/>

**harsh** and the **bitter**. And the **heat** is born between the **harsh** and **bitter** qualities within the **sweet source-water**, produced by the **harsh** and **bitter** qualities. There, the **Light** kindles itself in the **heat** within the **sweet source-water**; that is the **beginning of life**, for the **harsh** and **bitter** qualities are the beginning and a cause of the **heat** and the **Light**. Thus, the **sweet source-water** becomes a shining **Light**, similar to the blue, bright sky. And that same bright **source-water** ignites the **harsh** and **bitter** qualities; and the **heat**—which is born of the **harsh** and **bitter** qualities in the **sweet water**—rises out of the **sweet source-water** through the **bitter** and **harsh** qualities. And it is in the **bitter** and **harsh** qualities that the **Light** first becomes dry, shining, mobile, and triumphant. And when the **Light** rises out of the **sweet source-water** in the **heat**, within the **bitter** and **harsh** qualities, then the **bitter** and **harsh** qualities taste the bright and **sweet water**. The **bitter quality** catches the taste of the **sweet water**, and in the **sweet water** is the **Light**, though at first only as a sky-blue color. At that moment, the **bitter quality** trembles and dissolves the hardness in the **harsh quality**, and the **Light** dries itself in the **harsh quality** and shines brighter—much brighter than the radiance of the sun. In this rising, the **harsh quality** becomes gentle, bright, thin, and lovely, and receives its **Life**, whose origin rises from the **heat** in the **sweet water**. And this is now the true **Source-Fountain of Love**.

# Part 2 / Chapter 6.

Through the hard driving of the **harsh** <note>original: "herben"; refers to the astringent, contracting force of nature</note> and **bitter** qualities, the **heat** is produced, which rises up in the **sweet quality** as if within wood. If you do not wish to believe this, open your eyes and go to a tree; look at it and reflect. First, you see the whole tree; take a knife and cut into it, and taste it as it is. First, you will taste the **harsh quality**, which draws your tongue together; now, this same quality also holds and draws together all the power of the tree. After that, you taste the **bitter quality**, which makes the tree movable <note>active or dynamic</note>, so that it grows, turns green, and gains its branches, leaves, and fruit. After that, you taste the **sweetness**, which is entirely gentle and sharp; for it receives its sharpness from the harsh and bitter qualities.

Now these three qualities would be dark and dead if the heat were not within them. But as soon as spring comes, and the sun reaches and warms the earth with its rays, the spirit in the heat becomes alive within the tree. Then the spirits of the tree begin to turn green, grow, and bloom. For the spirit rises up in the heat, and all the spirits rejoice within it and live within it, and there is a heartfelt love between them. The heat, however, is born through the power and drive of the harsh and bitter qualities in the **sweet water** <note>the "sweet water" represents the receptive, nourishing element of the divine essence</note>; but they must use the sun's heat for ignition, because the qualities in this world are half-dead and too weak—a condition for which King Lucifer is a cause, as you will find in the account of his fall and the creation of this world.

On the other hand, there is cause for great joy, for in its need, the spirit of man is enlightened and ignited by the **Holy Spirit**, just as the sun ignites the cold heat in a tree or herb, whereby the cold heat becomes alive.

There is nothing there but pure longing, desiring, and fulfilling, where one triumphs and rejoices in the other. When the light rises, one spirit sees the other; and when the **sweet source-water** passes through all the spirits in the light, one tastes the other. Then the spirits become alive, and the power of life penetrates through everything. In that same power, one smells the other, and through this sourcing and penetrating, one feels the other. It is nothing but a heartfelt loving and friendly seeing, smelling well, tasting well, and feeling love—a lovely kissing, eating and drinking from one another, and walking in love. This is the **lovely bride** who rejoices in her **bridegroom**; therein is love, joy, and delight; there is light and clarity; there is a lovely fragrance; there is a friendly and sweet taste. This fifth form contains all the powers of the Divine Wisdom within itself, and is the **center** <note>original: "Centrum"</note>, wherein God the Father reveals himself in his Son through the speaking Word. 5. **Question:** Which do you call the sixth form of the working will of God in the Word?

**Answer:** When the desiring, driving, ascending, fiery will of the Father is fulfilled, soothed, and satisfied by the perfect love-will of the Son, then such perfect fullness, love, and light awakens a joyful, moving, ascending **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurium"; here Böhme uses the alchemical name for the planet/metal to describe the principle of movement, sound, and communication</note> or spirit of life. This spirit affects all forms of nature with its powers of light and love, so that the lovely grace shines, drives, and desires through all forms. Here now arises the understanding or the distinction of things, the ground of the senses, thoughts, and also all movements of the mind and the affections.

<column-break/>

The will becomes triumphant and rich in joy within this, so that the child of light is born within it. Here the second center rises up in joy, where love is the fire of the center; and the love-desire of the first will draws the joy to itself, and the light shines out of that joy. Thus this precious holy birth remains upon the **Cross**; there the wheel of the essences turns in the Cross, and the joy, as the **source of fire** <note>original: "Feuer-Quelle"</note>, rises above itself, and the center holds it. Thus the newly born will goes out from there with power and wonder, and confirms the first will of the freedom of the Father with the center of the love-birth of the Son. For this birth is the Father's Word or Heart, which he speaks out of his essences, and the going-forth from the love is the Spirit of the Word, which forms the essences; and together they are the **Trinity** <note>original: "Dreyzahl"</note> in one being.

But when the center in the Word now rises up in the power of the light from love, then one form receives the other with very friendly desires. For the first will is desiring, and creates the center—as was mentioned before regarding the **wrath** <note>original: "Grimm"</note>—so also in love; and instead of ill-will, there is a pure taste and a delighting-to-have within. Then, when the wheel of the essences moves in the **sound** <note>original: "Schalle"</note>, the sixth form is born. For the **harshness** <note>original: "Herbigkeit"; the contracting, astringent quality</note> nevertheless retains its hard, strict power in the sharpness of love, but quite gently; and the sixth form creates voices, tones, and sounds, so that one essence hears the other in the resonance, and tastes it through the influence <note>original: "Infiiciren"</note> of the wheel's essences, and smells it in the desire of love, and feels it with the breaking through of the **welling source** <note>original: "Qualls"; a Böhmean term combining the ideas of "Qual" (torment/labor) and "Quelle" (source/spring)</note>, and sees it in the light. 6. **Question:** Why does the author call this life-spirit and its affecting, awakening property "Mercury"?

**Answer:** Just as the Mercury of the planets contains the properties of all other planets within itself—and whichever planet has the **predominance** <note>original Latin: "Prædominium"</note> or the upper hand, Mercury exerts its effect and property according to that time—likewise, just as the Mercury of the metals (as quicksilver) is a mixture of all metals and is therefore a tester, separator, and dissolver of them, yet is also volatile, driving, and very sensitive: so also is the life-spirit when it reaches the sixth form of the properties of God.

This 6th form of nature and of all beings also arises out of all the others, and becomes manifest in the fire through the light in the desire for love; it is the understanding, sound, and speech of nature, and everything that makes a sound, whether in living or unliving things. Its true origin is from the harsh desire or impression of the first, second, and third forms, from which movement and hardness arise. In the fire, the essence of **coagulation** <note>The process of spirit taking on solid form or substance</note> is consumed, and from that consumption such a spirit goes out, both according to the property of the light (in love) and in

<column-break/>

the darkness according to the property of hostile source-working and anxiety. And we are to understand this as follows: every spirit desires essence according to its own likeness. Now, however, no more than one spirit goes out from the fire (that is, a spiritual understanding; it is the revelation of the understanding of the **Groundless** <term>Ungrund</term> <note>The "Ungrund" is Böhme’s term for the absolute, unconditioned depth of God that exists before and beyond all created nature</note> or of God); it takes hold of itself in the desire for love again and forms itself into the properties of the powers. This "entering into one another" or **working within one another** <note>original: "inqualiren"</note> is the lovely taste of love. But that which is grasped in the desire for love—where the desire coagulates the powers again and introduces them into forms, as into a substantial spirit where the powers can move audibly—that is now the natural and creaturely understanding which was in the Word. As **John 1** says: *In him was life, and the life was the light of men.* <note>original: "In ihm war das Leben / und das Leben war das Licht der Menschen."</note>

This sound of hearing, seeing, feeling, tasting, and smelling is the true intelligible life. For when one power enters into another, it receives the other in sound; when they penetrate one another, one awakens the other and recognizes the other. In this recognition stands the true understanding, which is without number, measure, or ground, after the manner of the eternal Wisdom, as the "One" which is all. Therefore, a single will may draw from this well-spring if it has Divine light within itself, and may behold the infinity—from which beholding this pen has written. To the audible life or sound of the powers belong hardness and softness, thickness and thinness, and a movement; for without movement everything is still, and yet there can be no sounding without the **fire-essence**. For the fire first creates the sound within the hardness and softness. Now, there would also be no sound without a "grasping" or "vessel," therefore all forms belong to the sound: 1. 7. **Question:** What does the author understand by the **seventh form of nature**, or of the working will of God?

**Answer:** The seventh form is actually not so much a working form of the will of God as it is a birth, an end-point <note>original: "Terminus"</note>, and a final purpose, wherein the six forms reach their fulfillment. Therein they find the goal, rest, and pleasure of their workings, and go no further, but remain and operate within it as in a house and workshop; the author also calls it **God's Body**. It is true that, strictly speaking, God has no body except in the humanity of Christ; yet God has his own being or element, wherein he dwells as an infinite spirit in all things and works through all things. Such a being, body, element, breath, or inhalation of the Almighty is, because of its fixity, constancy, and incorruptibility, much more to be called a "body" than all other heavenly and earthly bodies.

We recognize that God in his own essence is no "being" <note>original: "Wesen," often translated as "substance" or "essence"</note>, but merely the power or the understanding toward being, as a bottomless <note>original: "ungründlicher," referring to the *Ungrund*, the "abyssal" or "groundless" state before creation</note> eternal will in which everything lies and which is itself everything, and yet is only One. However, it desires to reveal itself and to introduce itself into a spiritual being, which happens through the fire in the love-desire, by the power of the light. Thus, the true Divine Being (understand here the "being" and not the Spirit of God) is nothing other than the revealed understanding, or the formation of the powers, and it stands in

<column-break/>

the desire—that is, in the love-desire—where one power recognizes the other in taste, smell <note>original: "Ruche"</note>, feeling, seeing, and hearing, in the essence and the laboring source <note>original: "Quall," a term Böhme uses to describe the agonizing or vibrant emergence of a quality</note> of the property. From this, the great longing desire arises. In those properties, the revealed God is understood as in a fiery flame of love-desire, wherein is a pure pleasant tasting, pleasant smelling, lovely and friendly seeing, a joyful hearing, and a gentle well-being or feeling. And yet it is only a spiritual being, where only the powers—which have introduced themselves into properties through the impression and have been revealed through the fire in the light—wrestle in and with one another in a **play of love**, like a lovely song, or a birthing harmony, or a kingdom of joy. This is therefore only the being of the revealed Spirit of God, as the powerful, all-present Word reveals itself out of itself in its own self-generation, wherein the **play of Divine Wisdom** is understood. But if we wish to speak of heavenly or Divine substantiality, wherein the Divine powers again lead themselves into a formation—into an external degree—then we must say that the powers of the formed and revealed Word in their love-desire introduce themselves again into an external being, according to the property of all powers, wherein they can spend their play of love as if in a housing <note>or "casing"</note>; so that they have something with which and in which they may play with their wrestling love-play. And this is now understood in this way:

Just as a mineral power lies in the earth and is ignited by the sun, from which it begins to stir and labor <note>quallen</note> and becomes desiring of the sun's powers and draws them into itself; but in such desire it catches itself and forms itself into a body <note>original: "Corpus"</note>, like a root or similar thing, out of which (in that same hunger-desire) such a body or herb grows as the first power was. In the same way...

# Of the Revelation of God in the 2nd Principle <note>original: "Principio"; Böhme uses this term to describe the fundamental realms or "worlds" of existence: darkness, light, and the physical world.</note>

Powers through the striving Knowledge <note>original: "Scientz"; in Böhme's vocabulary, this refers to a divine science or the active, "striving" desire of the will to manifest itself</note>, (or desires and active powers of the Divine Will) introduced into creaturely forms and births, so that the Divine Wisdom might be revealed in the wonders of formation and in manifold life. For in the Balance <note>original: "Temperatur"; the state where all qualities exist in perfect harmony without conflict</note> no creature can be born, for it is the one God alone; but in the outpouring of Knowledge, of the one Will, as it divides itself into particulars, a creature may arise as an image of the formed Word.

<margin>The Election of Grace <note>original: "Gnaden-Wahl"</note> 3:40.</margin>

8. **Question:** What is further to be considered regarding these properties?

**Answer:** **I.** It is to be noted that the first and seventh properties are always counted as one, and also the second and sixth as one, as well as the third and fifth as one; the fourth is the dividing line <note>original: "Scheide-Ziel"</note> alone, for there are only three properties of nature, according to the revelation of the Trinity of God.

As the first, the **Desire**, is attributed to God the Father and is only a spirit, and in the seventh, the desire is substantial <note>or "essential"</note>.

The second is attributed to God the Son as the **Divine Power**; in the second number it is only a spirit, but in the sixth it is the understanding power.

The third is attributed to God the Holy Spirit according to his revelation; at the beginning of the third property it is only a **fire-spirit**, but in the fifth property, the great **Love** is revealed therein. Thus, the outflow of divine revelation according to the three properties is natural in the First Principle before the light, and spiritual in the Second Principle within the light.

These are therefore the seven properties in a single ground, all seven equally eternal without beginning; and none can be counted as the first, second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth, and last, for they are equally eternal without beginning, out of the Unity of God. One must only set this forth in a **figurative way** for the sake of understanding, how one is born from the other, for a greater comprehension of what the Creator is, and so that one can contemplate the life and essence of the visible world.

<column-break/>

<margin>The Key <note>original: "Clavis"</note> §. 75. 80.</margin>

**II.** These seven properties are in a single ground, and each has the form of all properties within itself; none can exist without the other. For instance, the spirit of life does not become bitter or prickly without the harsh, severe property, and this harshness can cause no ignition without the bitter one. Each has its power and its persistence in the other; therefore, each has an inclination toward the other, and one gives birth to the other, and multiplies itself in the Conjunction <note>original: "Conjunction"; the mystical joining or union of these forces</note> into the infinite. For where the harsh "Primary" <note>original: "Primas"; the dominant or leading property in a given moment</note> is, there it gives birth to a harsh bitterness, a harsh anxiety, a harsh fire, a harsh light, a harsh love, a harsh sound, and a harsh essence. Likewise: where the bitter "Primary" is, there is a bitter harshness, a bitter bitterness, a bitter anxiety, etc.

The birth of eternal nature is just as the **senses** are in man, where a sense is born from something and afterwards spreads into infinity. Or as the root of the tree gives birth to itself, and thereafter the trunk and many branches and limbs come from it; also from the single root many roots, and many branches and limbs; and everything comes from the first single root. Also note, as mentioned before, since nature stands in a sixfold form, so each form gives birth again from itself to a form according to the nature of its quality, which then has the quality and nature of all forms within itself. But note: The first form among the six gives birth only to a source <note>original: "Quell"</note> according to its own kind, according to the kind of that same source-spirit, and not according to the first mother of harshness, just as a branch in the tree gives birth to another twig from itself. For in every source-spirit <note>original: "Quell-Geiste"</note> there is only one center, in which the fire-source rises up, and from the fire-flash <note>original: "Feuer-Blitz"</note> comes the light, and in each source are the first six kinds of forms.

But note the depth in this analogy; I put it thus: The harsh source in the origin is the mother, from which the other five sources—bitterness, fire, love, sound, water—are born- <note>The text ends mid-word on "erboh-," likely "erbohren" or "born."</note>

It is like a glassy sea and is the **corporeality of the Divine Nature**, wherein all the forms of the whole of nature stand; and herein the seven spirits of God are manifest as burning torches.

# Chapter VII.
## Of the true eternal Nature / of the First Matter, or the Being of all beings / and the infinite, innumerable birth of the Being of all beings.

**1. Question.**
->What does the author actually understand by the eternal nature?<-

**Answer.**
Until now we have considered the Acting Principle <note>original: "Principium Agens"; the active, driving force of the Trinity</note>, which is the triune GOD—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—in the Word according to each and every property of their active Will, acting as the efficient cause <note>original: "causæ efficientis"; the primary source that brings an effect into being</note>, as well as each and every one of those figures and forms that are worked; now follows the material cause <note>original: "causa materialis"; the "stuff" or substance out of which something is made</note>, from which the active Will created and made all things manifest. Namely, the first Matter <note>original: "Prima Materia"</note>, as the Being of all beings <note>original: "Wesen aller Wesen"; for Böhme, "Wesen" refers to a spiritual substance or "essence-matter" rather than just abstract existence</note>. To recognize this thoroughly, we must investigate: 1. The Begetter <note>original: "Gebährerin"; literally 'the one who gives birth'</note>, or the source from which the first Matter is born. 2. The Matter, or the Being of all beings itself. 3. How the Being of all beings divides itself, and how the Acting Principle, according to its properties, brought forth so many kinds of matters out of the Being of all beings through its working.

**2. Question. What does the author actually understand by the Begetter?**

**Answer.** He understands by it the eternal nature, and especially the working of the Word, according to those three properties of the first principle, where the eternal, incomprehensible GOD—out of the Nothing of his incomprehensible Freedom—calls the things that are not, so that they are; that is, through his almighty Word, he works Something out of NOTHING.

**3. Question. My reason has often thought to itself, how did GOD bring forth the Essence, or the Matter of all things, out of the Nothing? Dear friend, if you can bring this to a thorough understanding for me, you will unlock a powerful gate of knowledge.**

**Answer.** We have briefly mentioned how the six Source-Spirits <note>original: "Quell-Geister"; the seven fundamental forces of existence in Böhme's system</note> give birth to the seventh, as the Body; and by this Body, we understand the Being of all beings.

<column-break/>

**4. Question. Does the author then understand by the word Being <note>original: "Wesen"</note> not what the schools understand by it; namely, Being <note>original: "Esse"</note>, the subsistence of GOD, the act of existing <note>original: "Existere"</note>?**

**Answer.** By the Being of GOD, he understands the substance of GOD in the eternal nature, through which GOD—who in himself is a pure, immeasurable Spirit—becomes as it were sensible, graspable, and active. Just as a pure, floating, volatile air or spirit cannot be sensed, recognized, or felt; but where it coagulates, becomes bound and thick, it becomes substantial, essential, sensible, graspable, and visible: So GOD, outside of Nature and Creature, is a pure Spirit without a body; but as he introduced himself into Nature and contained himself therein, he became, as it were, sensible, findable, substantial, and essential therein.

In GOD is everything / Power / Spirit and Life / but what is Being / that is not Spirit / but what sinks down from the fire / as into weakness / that is Being / for the spirit originates in the fire / and yet divides itself into two sources / one in the fire / and one in the sinking into the Freedom in the Light. This is called GOD / for it is gentle and lovely / and contains the Kingdom of Joy within itself / and the angelic world is understood in the sunken Freedom of the Essentiality. Concerning the Divine Essentiality / as of the Divine Corporeality / it is thus to be understood: The light gives gentleness as a love: Now the fire's anguish desires gentleness / so that it may quench its great thirst / for the fire is desiring / and the gentleness is giving / for it gives itself: Thus, in the desiring of gentleness, Being arises / as a substantial Essentiality / which has escaped from the wrath <note>original: "Grimm"; the harsh, consuming quality of the First Principle</note> / which gives its own life freely / that is corporeality / for it becomes substantial from the power in the gentleness / and is attracted and held by the harshness / as by the eternal "Let it be" <note>original: "Fiat"; the creative command of God</note> / and is therefore called Essentiality or Corporeality /

**5. Question.** What does the Author actually understand by the Salitter? <note>Salitter (or Salniter) is Böhme’s term for the "divine saltpeter"—the spiritual substance or "earth" of heaven, representing the potential for all material forms.</note>

**Answer.** The Salitter is, for the Author, nothing other than a condensed dry fire-water, a bound spirit and breath of GOD, which is gently drawn together and dried by the harsh property of the working Will. He calls this heavenly Divine Being or element *Salitter* because, in a spiritual heavenly way, it has such a birth and cause, just as earthly saltpeter <note>original: "Salitter"</note> in the air or in the earth has a birth and property.

The six source-spirits <note>original: "Quell-Geister"; the seven (here six active) fundamental qualities that drive all existence in Böhme's cosmology</note>, he says, rise up in full birth, according to the power and kind of each source-spirit; and when they have ascended, then their power is mingled together, and the hardness is dried up, and it is like the whole Being. This bodily drying I call, in this book, the Divine Salitter.

With the word Salitter, it is understood in this book how the second Principle greens out of the first from the eternal Center of Nature <note>original: "Centro Naturæ"</note>, just as the light from the fire; where two spirits are understood, namely 1. a hot one, and 2. an airy one; where in the air-life stands the true growing, and in the fire-life the cause of the quality.

<margin>Aurora <note>Böhme’s first book</note>, Chapter II, Section 47.</margin>

# Chapter VII.
## Concerning the true eternal Nature / concerning the First Matter <note>Latin: *Prima Materia*</note>, or the Being of all beings / and the infinite, innumerable birth of the Being of all beings.

**1. Question.**
->What does the Author actually understand by eternal nature?<-

->**Answer**<-

Hitherto we have considered the Acting Principle <note>Latin: *Principium Agens*</note>, which is the triune GOD—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—in the Word according to each and every property of their working Will, as the efficient cause <note>Latin: *causæ efficientis*</note>; as well as each and every one of those figures and forms to be worked. Now follows the material cause <note>Latin: *causa materialis*</note>, out of which the working Will has created and made manifest all things. Namely, the First Matter <note>Latin: *Prima Materia*</note>, as the Being of all beings. To recognize this fundamentally, we must research: 1. The Progenitress <note>original: "Gebährerin"; the feminine principle or "birth-giver" of nature</note>, or the source from which the First Matter is born. 2. The Matter, or the Being of all beings itself. 3. How the Being of all beings divides itself, and how the Acting Principle—according to its properties—brought forth so many kinds of matters from the Being of all beings through its working.

**2. Question. What does the Author actually understand by the Progenitress?**

**Answer.** By this he understands the eternal nature, and especially the working of the Word according to the three properties of the first Principle <note>The "first Principle" in Böhme's system is the "dark world" or the fiery foundation of God's power</note>, wherein the eternal, incomprehensible GOD, out of the "Nothing" of His incomprehensible freedom, calls the things that are not, so that they are; that is, through His almighty Word, He works "Something" out of the "NOTHING."

**3. Question. My reason has often thought to itself: how did GOD bring forth the Being, or the Matter of all things, out of Nothing? Dear friend, if you can bring this to a fundamental concept for me, you will unlock a powerful gateway of knowledge.**

**Answer.** We have briefly mentioned how the six Source-Spirits <note>original: "Quell-Geister"; the fundamental forces of nature in Böhmean cosmology</note> give birth to the seventh as the "Body," and by this Body we understand the Being of all beings.

<column-break/>

**4. Question. Does the Author then understand by the word "Being" <note>original: "Wesen"</note> what the Schools understand by it; namely, "to be" <note>Latin: *Esse*</note>, the subsistence of GOD, or "to exist" <note>Latin: *Existere*</note>?**

**Answer.** By the "Being of God" he understands the substance of GOD in eternal nature, through which GOD—who in Himself is a pure, immeasurable spirit—becomes, as it were, perceptible, comprehensible, and active. Just as pure, floating, volatile air or spirit may not be perceived, recognized, or felt, but where it is coagulated, bound, and thickened, it becomes substantial, essential, perceptible, comprehensible, and visible: even so is GOD, outside of nature and creature, a pure spirit without a body; but when He introduced Himself into nature, and grasped Himself therein, He became therein perceptible, findable, substantial, and essential.

In GOD all is power, spirit, and life; but that which is "Being" is not spirit. Rather, that which "sinks down" <note>original: "ersincket"; a technical term for spiritual energy cooling or condensing into substance</note> from the fire as if into a faintness—that is "Being." For the spirit originates in the fire, but divides into two sources: one in the fire, and one in the "sinking" into the freedom in the Light. This latter is called GOD, for it is gentle and lovely, and contains the realm of joy; and the angelic world is understood to be within this sunken freedom of beingness. Concerning the Divine Beingness, as the Divine Corporeality, we are to understand it thus: The light gives Gentleness as a love. Now, the fire's anguish desires Gentleness so that it may quench its great thirst; for the fire is desiring, and the Gentleness is giving, for it gives itself. Thus, in the desiring of Gentleness, "Being" arises as a substantial essence which has escaped from the Wrath <note>original: "Grimm"; the fierce, dark, or "angry" side of the divine fire</note> and which gives its own life freely. This is Bodiliness; for it becomes substantial from the power in the Gentleness, and is drawn together and held by the Harshness as if by the eternal *Fiat* <note>Latin: "Let it be done"; the creative command of God</note>, and is therefore called Beingness or Corporeality.

<summary>This page describes how God, a pure and intangible spirit, manifests as "Being" or "Corporeality" through a process of spiritual condensation. It explains that "Being" is the result of the fiery divine will desiring the "Gentleness" of the light, causing a substantial, divine matter to "sink" into existence.</summary>

**5. Question. What does the Author actually understand by the Salitter?**

**Answer.** For the Author, the **Salitter** is nothing other than a condensed, dry fire-water, a bound spirit and breath of GOD, which is gently condensed and dried by the harsh property of the working Will. He calls this heavenly Divine Being or element "Salitter" because, in a spiritual heavenly way, it has a birth and a cause similar to how earthly saltpeter <note>German: *Salitter*; Böhme uses the term for saltpeter to describe a divine "mineral" or chemical foundation of reality</note> in the air or in the earth has a birth and property.

The six **source-spirits** <note>German: *Quell-Geister*; the fundamental forces of Böhme's nature</note>, he says, arise in full birth, according to each source-spirit’s power and kind; and when they have ascended, their power is mingled into one another, and the hardness is dried, and it is like the whole Being. This bodily drying I call the **Divine Salitter** in this book.

With the word Salitter, it is understood in this book how the second Principle <note>the realm of light and love</note> greens out from the first Principle <note>the dark, fiery foundation</note> out of the eternal **Center of Nature** <note>Latin: *Centro Naturæ*</note>, just as light comes from fire; where two spirits are understood: 1. a hot one, and 2. an airy one, for in the airy life stands the true growth, and in the fire-life the cause of the quality.

<margin>Aurora, chapter 11, section 47.</margin>

In this Salitter now consists all corporeality, comprehensibility, and sensitivity; for a spirit by itself is raw <note>unrefined or formless</note> without a Being. For a spirit is raw without a body: Yet there is no understanding without a body, and also the spirit does not exist in itself without a body. For a form in the spirit is a hunger and a yearning desire, one form after another. For all things stand in the Will and are driven in the Will. For if I do not conceive a will to walk, then my body remains standing still; therefore my will carries me, and if I do not have a desire for a place, then there is also no will in me. But if I desire something, that is the will of the **essences**.

<column-break/>

Now the essences <note>the active powers or "inner being" of a thing</note> desire nothing but the preservation and building of the body; for the body is their food, and the whole **Being of all beings** is a constant hunger, a filling, and then a birthing again out of that which is filled, as one can see. Every form of the spirit desires the others in hunger, and when it gets them, another form arises from it; yet the first does not pass away, but the second forms itself within the first into a different source-working <note>German: *Quall*; Böhme’s term for the vibrant, sometimes painful activity of a quality</note>, and yet both keep each other, each its own property. Thus we have written of Nature in six forms, how each comes from the other, and how each is the cause of the other being born, yet each retains its property in the other. And though they now stand within one another in six forms, there is still no place of rest; instead, there is a constant desire of all six forms, like a great hunger, from which the Will is always born. And since there is nothing where rest might be, except the **quiet eternity**, and such a thing cannot be grasped or found in the wheel of the fiery essences; so hungry Nature seeks in its Mother—that is, in the desire of **harshness** <note>German: *Herbigkeit*; the astringent, contracting force that pulls things into being</note>—and the harshness catches the desire of the essences and holds it. Thus all the essences of hunger stand held in the harsh Mother, for she is their only rest, which she fills again with that which is in her, namely, with herself.

Herein stands the rule <note>government</note> of a spirit; for nature stands not only in seven forms, but from every desire a will may be born again, within which the essences stand again, but changeable according to the desire of that same will; and in this stands the omnipotence and the wonders, of which no number can be found, as you may see in the creation of the world. But if the eternal Being desires a certain goal and measure, against or beyond which...

The Author, following Holy Scripture, calls such a revelation **Paradise**, which fundamentally signifies a demonstration, an ostentation, a transfiguration, or a mirroring; just as a tree, when it stands in its full bloom, mirrors itself and reveals its inner clarity, majesty, and glory. In this Paradise, as the transfiguration and revelation according to the property of fire and light, we recognize God in His luster and majesty. The Divine Salitter is, as it were, the water-mirror, without which we could no more grasp Him with the eyes of understanding than we are able to gaze upon the sun in its full luster and shine with our physical eyes.

**6. Question. What is it, then, exactly, that causes such a luster in the Holy Element and Salitter, and gives such a shine?**

**Answer.** The **Tincture** <note>In alchemy, a substance capable of infused transformation; for Böhme, a spiritual "inner fire" or life-force</note>, or that breath and odor which goes out from the ignition of the Life of God in the Word, and causes the living, weaving, driving, and friction in the Salitter or Holy Element.

**7. Question. What does the Author actually understand by the Tincture?**

**Answer.** The Author does not understand the Tincture to be some kind of extract or liquid in which the color and virtue are drawn out of a substance. Rather, by the Tincture, the Author understands a driving, active power and virtue which rises up from the life-ignition of a spirit and drives toward light and being. But no spirit, as long as it is raw, can give birth to the Tincture, unless its fire-flash reaches a **temperature** <note>German: *Temperatur*; here meaning a perfect balance or harmony of conflicting qualities</note> in the life-ignition. Namely, it must sink down from its fire-power and, as if powerless, be coagulated and bound by the harsh property, to the degree that it also remains powerful enough to ascend. It must not be more powerful in its fire-driving than in its sinking and descending. Through the descending, the fire-spirit is bound into water, and through the ascending, the life-spirit becomes weaving in the water. From the water comes the body or the essence, which outside of the Tincture would be as a dead and useless thing, just as when the weaving and volatile air is bound by the harsh and cold property...

This [second] will has within it the sharpness of **Mercury** <note>original: *Mercurii*; Böhme uses the planetary/alchemical name for the "Life-Spirit" or the principle of motion and communication</note>, and when it breaks through the dark chamber of anguish of the harsh property and attains freedom, it causes the fire in the water—the rising spirit of life—to become shining in the sunken essence, creating a delight.

Every life, however high or lowly it may be, desires its mother from whom it originates and in whom it stands; as we can recognize that every life desires the best that is in its center, such as the Heart or the **Oil** <note>Latin: *Oleum*; the fuel for the spiritual fire</note> in which the fire burns and the life stands open, so that it is a life. That [Tincture] is a lovely delight and is the **Freedom** <note>German: *Freyheit*; Böhme’s term for the *Ungrund* or the divine stillness beyond nature</note> of nature; for nature stands in great anguish and constrains itself so hard with desire for freedom until it reaches it, and when it reaches it,

then nature is a sharpness in freedom and always wants to consume freedom into itself so that it might become entirely one with freedom, and yet it cannot. The more it rages and raises itself toward freedom, the greater the Tincture of freedom becomes. Thus nature remains a fire and freedom remains a light. What the Tincture builds, the fire consumes; for the Tincture creates essence, its center is soft and is a sinking, just as the fire is a rising.

But because the light, as the Tincture, creates essence in its sinking—so that it is an essence like water in the light, and yet not water, but such a spirit and active quality—the fire consumes that same essence into itself. From this, its wrath is extinguished, and it rises up in the essence and burns just like a fire in oil, and that is the true natural life of all creatures, and it is called Tincture.

Now, however, this life is fragile, for it begins and stands only in four forms: namely in Fire, Air, Water, and in the Essence, which is the Body. And we will explain one more thing to you regarding this Tincture-life, as you see it naturally: that from every fire an active quality <note>German: *Quall*</note> goes forth, namely Air. It is formed thus: when the fire violently consumes and draws the essence into itself, the essence also flees again with violence from the active quality of the fire; for it is so subtle that the fire cannot hold it. Thus there is a drawing-in and a fleeing-back, for the fire wants to have the fleeing thing back with violence, and it is a perpetual struggle.

Thus you see this—and it is quite open—how the Life-Fire lets the Air go from itself, for the Air also does not want to remain in the fire's quality, but flees with power; and the fire's quality always draws it back into itself. Thus the fire is blown up [ventilated], otherwise it would suffocate and become dark. For these reasons, it reaches for the essence as Air, for no active quality desires the confinement of death.

**8. Question: How many kinds of Tincture are there?**

**Answer:** As many as there are spirits of life and bodies, or weaving essences <note>original: "webende Wesenheiten"; refers to the active, living substances of things</note>, both in eternal and temporal nature—so many also are the kinds of Tincture. In the Divine life weaves a Divine one; in the dark fire-world, a fire-tincture; in the holy light-world, a light-tincture; in the angels, an angelic one; in the perfect human, a paradisiacal one; in fallen humans, an earthly and animal one; in the newborn <note>referring to the spiritually "born-again"</note>, a virginal and heavenly one; in the vegetables, herbs, and trees, a vegetative one; in metals, a mineral one; in the sun, a solar one; in Venus, a Venusian one; in Mars, a fiery one; in the elements, an elemental one—as in fire, fiery; in water, watery, etc. Every visible being has within itself an invisible one; the outward is only an instrument of the inward; the inward forms itself within the inward. Thus we understand such powers of the three growing spirits <note>referring to Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury</note> in different centers, and yet only in one body. The first and outward spirit is the coarse **Sulfur, Salt, and Mercury**; this is a being of the four elements or the stars, according to the stars' harsh property. This creates the body and imprints itself, or conceives itself into a being, or draws the inner from the spiritual **Separator** <term>Separator: The archetypal, spiritual organizing force that distinguishes and "separates" qualities into individual forms</term> to itself, as well as the elements from without, and coagulates itself with them. From this immediately occurs the **Signature** <term>Signature: The outward physical appearance or "mark" of a thing that reveals its inner spiritual character</term> or designation from the Separator; it forms the visible body according to the property of the greatest power of the **Spirit of the World** <note>original: "Spiritus Mundi"</note>, such as the constellation of the stars, or the property of the planets and the now ignited elements.

<column-break/>

The other spirit, which has its own center, lies in the **Oil of Sulfur**, which is called the **Fifth Essence** <note>original: "fünffte Essentz" or "Quinta Essentia"; the pure, refined essence of a substance</note>, as a root of the four elements. This is the softening and joy of the coarse, painful sulfur- and salt-spirit, and it takes its nourishment first from within, from the **Light of Nature**, as from the outflow of spiritual gentleness, from the inner spiritual fire and light. And secondly, it takes its nourishment from without, from the sun and from the subtle power of the **Spirit of the World**, and is the true cause of growing life, a joy of nature, just as the sun is in the elements.

The third spirit is the **Tincture**, as a reflection <note>original: "Gegen-Wurff"; literally a "counter-throw" or projection</note> of the Divine **Great Mystery** <note>original: "Mysterii Magni"</note>, where all powers lie within in equality, and it is rightly called Paradise or Divine Delight. It is a housing of Divine power, a housing of the eternal souls, from which all outward powers spring, in the way that air springs from fire. For the Tincture is nothing other than a spiritual fire and light, where fire and light are an essence of their own within. But because it also has its **Separator** within it—the outflowing will toward manifestation—it is the highest ground from which the first distinction of properties in the being of this world originates; and according to its own nature, it belongs to eternity. For its origin is the holy power of God, and it has its own center, as the innermost ground of the creature, which is indeed hidden from the mortal creature because humans carry a false will against it. From this arose the curse of the earth in the fall of man. However, this high, holy ground penetrates through all beings of this world from its own center and flows out into the outer powers, just as the sun flows into the elements. But the creature may not touch the center of this power, unless it happens through Divine permission, as occurs in the new **Rebirth** <note>original: "Wieder-Geburt"</note>.
