# Of Eternal Nature and the Essence of All Essences

<note>original: "3" (Signature mark for the printer)</note>

Such revelation is seen in all things of the living and the growing. All things stand in these three **Principles** <note>original: "Principiis"; refers to the three fundamental realms of existence in Böhme’s cosmology: the dark fire-world, the light-world, and the external world</note>, or beginnings. Take an example in a herb of the earth: it has its nourishment <note>original: "Nutrimentum"</note> from within and without—namely, from within from the earth, and from without from the sun and stars, through which the spirit of the earth <note>original: "Erden Spiritus"</note> forms itself together with the external. When the herb grows out, it happens in such power that the external **Separator** <term>Separator: An alchemical term for the internal "craftsman" or spirit that divides, organizes, and gives form to matter</term> in the **Sulfur, Salt, and Mercury** <note>The "tria prima" or three primary substances of alchemy representing soul, body, and spirit</note> marks or "signatures" itself from the outside in the herb, through its building and form. For the Separator is the movement and sensitivity of the herb, and it makes itself corporeal. Thus, when I see a herb standing there, I say with truth: This is an image of the Earth-Spirit, in which the upper powers rejoice and which they also consider their child, because the Earth-Spirit is one essence with the upper, external powers. And when the herb has grown up, it blooms; then, with the blossom, the oily spirit marks itself with beautiful colors; and with the lovely scent of the blossom, the **TINCTURE** marks itself as the third ground. One then understands that the internal, hidden spirit of the elements has opened itself and introduces itself into the formation of the fruit. For the earth would have no such scent, nor colors, nor such virtue, if the hidden power of the **Divine Outflow** <note>original: "Göttlicher Ausfluss"; the idea that all of creation is an "out-breathing" or flowing forth of God's internal power</note> did not reveal itself.

One can see this also in the metals, which externally are a coarse body <note>original: "Corpus"</note> of Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt, in which the growth resides; but in their internal ground they are a beautiful, clear body, in which the imagined light of nature shines from the Divine Outflow. In this brilliance <note>original: "Glast"</note> one understands the Tincture and great power—how the hidden power makes itself visible. One cannot say of such power that it is "elemental," just as the power of the blossom is not elemental. The elements are only a casing and a counter-object <note>original: "Gegen-Wurff"; something thrown against or mirrored</note> of the inner power, a cause for the movement of the Tincture. For the power goes out from the Tincture through the movement of the coarse, elemental spirit, and thereby leads itself into sensitivity, such as taste. For scent is nothing other than the sensitivity of the Tincture, through which the outflow of Divine power reveals itself and thus takes on sensitivity. The sharpness of the scent is indeed elemental, but the true power and virtue within the sharpness of the scent is the Tincture. For the movement is not the highest ground of the power, but rather that from which the cause of the movement comes.

<column-break/>

->*Contemplation* <note>original: "Beschaul." (referring to Böhme's work 'The Contemplative Life' or 'Of True Resignation')</note> *chapter 3, paragraphs 19 and 29.*<-

Because we are speaking here of the **Divine Tincture**, we must learn to recognize its ground from the workings of the Tincture in earthly things, such as minerals, vegetables <note>original: "Vegetabilien"; plants</note>, and animals <note>original: "Animalien"</note>. From this, we can judge what the Divine Tincture must be in its highest degree. If we examine the Tincture to see what it is in its highest degree, we find the **Spirit** <note>original: "Spiritum"</note>; for we cannot say that fire is the Tincture, nor is air. For fire is quite contrary to the Tincture, and air would suffocate it. It is entirely a lovely delight; its root, from which it is born, is the fire. But if I should name its right seat, where it sits, I can say nothing other than that it is between the three Principles—namely, God's Kingdom, Hell's Kingdom, and this World's Kingdom in the middle. It has none of these as its own property, and yet it is born of all three. It is like a special Principle, though it is not a Principle itself, but rather a bright, lovely delight. It is also not the Spirit itself, but the Spirit dwells in it, and it renovates the Spirit so that it is bright and seeing. Its right name is "Wonderful," and no one can name it except him to whom it is given; he names it only within himself, and not outside of himself. It has no place of rest in substance, and yet always rests in itself, giving power and beauty to all things, just as the sun's radiance gives power and beauty to all things in this world, and yet is not...

So you will say: This must be GOD? No / it is not GOD / but God’s friend. Christ says: My Father works / and I work also / but she works nothing / is imperceptible in a thing / and yet one can master and use her / especially in metals / where she can make pure gold out of iron and copper / if she is pure. She can make much out of a little / and yet also drives nothing. Her way is as subtle as human thoughts / and thoughts also arise from her.

# The VIII. Chapter.
## How the triune GOD revealed Himself from one into many.

# Of the Revelation of GOD out of One into Many.

Each form also has a particular inclination toward and into the others, and in their constellation or union, they generate and bring forth a third. Thus they work within the Essence in such a qualification; for example: The harsh and the bitter produce a bitter and severe desire; the first and the third a fierce desire; the first and the fourth a fiery desire; the first and the fifth a harsh, attractive love; the first and the sixth a hard, coarse tone and sound. Likewise, the second and the first produce a harsh bitterness and sharp sting; the second and the third a fierce sting; the second and the fourth a fiery, burning bitterness; the second and the fifth a bitter, driving love; the second and the sixth a fast, violent, penetrating sound, ring, and tone. Thus they make for themselves a body according to their qualification. In this way, the birth proceeds from one into many, and from many into the innumerable. Just as from a human <term>Mind: (Gemüthe) Not just the intellect, but the seat of all desires, emotions, and thoughts</term> arise the senses and thoughts, where one sense follows from another and one thought from another, into the innumerable: So, from one Sense and Thought of GOD have proceeded innumerable ideas, which the active Will of GOD has figured and substantially represented through His almighty Word in the Essence of all Essences.

2. Q. Could the triune GOD not have revealed all His omnipotence, wisdom, and virtue in a single creature, rather than spreading this revelation out into the innumerable?

Ans. There is no creature so small in which the triune GOD is not manifest in His eternally-speaking Word. For the Godhead desired to see the wonders of eternal nature—of the innumerable eternal <term>Essences: The spiritual "powers" or fundamental qualities that make up the inner nature of a thing</term>—in actual being. For all things that have come into

being have come out of the eternal birth-giver <note>likely referring to the "Mysterium Magnum" or the divine chaos from which all things are born</note>, not at different times, but all at once. However, at different times, the formation of the Being stood in the wrestling of the <term>Center: (Centri) The focal point of natural forces where the "will" of a thing is forged</term> in the figure or form, and was seen by the Heart of GOD in the light; which He finally created, and that is when Time began.

From this has become manifest the many kinds of variation of the Will in the essences, and the great wonders of GOD’s omnipotence. For if everything in nature were only a single will and a single being, there would be no distinction and no revelation.

If the hidden GOD—who is only a single being and will—had not led Himself out of Himself with His will, from the eternal science in <term>Balance: (Temperamento) A state of harmony where opposing forces are perfectly equilibrated</term> into the <term>Distinction: (Schiedlichkeit) The state of being separable or distinct; the "brokenness" required for individual existence</term> of the will; and if He had not introduced that same distinction into a comprehensibility for a natural and creaturely life; and if that same distinction in life did not stand in conflict—how then would the hidden Will of GOD (which in itself is only one) be revealed to Him? How can there be a knowledge of oneself in a single will?

But since there is a distinction in the single will, so that the distinction introduces itself into centers and a self-will—so that there is a self-will in that which is separated, and thus in a single will there arise unfathomable and innumerable wills, like branches from a tree: So we see and understand that in such distinction, each separated will introduces itself into its own form, and that the conflict of the wills is over the form—that one form in its partiality is not as the other—and yet they all stand in one ground. For a single will cannot break itself into pieces; just as the mind does not break into pieces when it divides itself into a bad and a good willing; rather, the outgoing of the <note>original: "Sensuum" (Latin for "of the senses")</note> senses only divides itself into a bad and a good willing, while the mind remains whole in itself, and suffers that a bad and a good willing arise and dwell within it.

## Part 2 / Chapter 8.

->**Thus speaks Reason:**<-

->What is the use or benefit of the fact that Evil must exist alongside Good?<-

->**Answer.**<-

Evil, or the reluctant <note>German: *Wider-Willige*. This refers to anything that resists or pushes back against the primary Will.</note> quality, causes the Good to act as a Will, pressing back toward its original state—toward God—so that the Good (the good Will) becomes full of desire. For a thing that is only good in itself and possesses no <term>Quality (Quall): Böhme’s word for the internal tension, pain, or "source-spirit" that gives a thing its active nature</term> desires nothing; it knows nothing better within or before itself for which it could long. In this way, we can also philosophize regarding the singular good Will of God and say that He could desire nothing within Himself, for He has nothing in or before Him that could give Him anything. Therefore, He leads Himself out of Himself into a <term>Differentiability (Schiedlichkeit): The state of being able to be divided or distinguished into different parts</term>, into **Centers**, so that an opposition arises in that which has flowed out. Thus, the Good becomes perceptible, active, and willing within the Evil—namely, it desires to separate itself from the Evil and return again into the singular Will of God. But because the outflow of the singular, eternal Will of God continually proceeds out of itself toward its own revelation, the Good (the Divine Power) also flows out from the eternal One with this same outflow and enters into the state of differentiability and into the **Centers** of multiplicity.

Thus, the perpetual outflow of the Will causes the Good within it to move; the Good then longs for the state of stillness and becomes desirous of pressing back into the Eternal. Through this act of "pressing back" into itself, the One becomes movable and desirous, and within such an operation lies perceptibility, knowledge, and the Will. God—insofar as He is called "God"—can will nothing but Himself, for He has nothing before or after Him that He can desire. However, if He does will something, that thing has flowed out of Him and is a <term>Counter-reflection (Gegen-Wurff): A mirror-image or "object" thrown back at the observer, allowing for self-perception</term> of Himself, in which the eternal Will desires something within its own "Something." Now, if this "Something" were only a single thing, the Will would have no way to accomplish anything within it. Therefore, the unfathomable Will divided itself in the beginning and enclosed itself within "Being," so that it might work within something—just as one sees an analogy in the human mind <note>German: *Gemüthe*. A central term for Böhme, referring to the seat of the soul, will, and disposition.</note>. If the mind did not flow out of itself, it would have no senses; and if it had no senses, it would have no knowledge of itself or of any other thing, and could achieve no accomplishment or operation. But the sensory outflow from the mind (which is a counter-reflection of the mind, in which the mind perceives itself) makes the mind "willing" or "desirous," so that the mind leads the senses into "Something"—as if into a center of **Selfhood** <note>German: *Ichheit*. The quality of being an individual "I".</note>—within which the mind works with the senses, and in that working, reveals and contemplates itself.

If, then, in these centers of the senses—in this counter-reflection of the mind—there were no <term>Contrary (Contrarium): A Latin term for opposite or opposing force</term>, then all the centers of the outflowing senses would be but one; in all the centers of the senses there would be only a single will that did only one thing. How then could the wonders and powers of Divine Wisdom be recognized and brought into form through the mind (which is an image of Divine Revelation)? But because a **Contrary** (such as Light and Darkness) exists within it, the contrary is itself resistant, and each quality causes the other to enter into desire—willing to strive against the others and to rule them. In this desire, the senses and the mind are led into a natural and creaturely "ground" toward a Will—namely, toward a mastery within its own "Something," using its own **Center** to rule over all other centers, as one sense of the mind rules over another. From this, strife and anxiety, as well as reluctance, originate in the mind. Consequently, the entire mind is caused to enter again into a "shattering" of the senses and of the "self-willing" of the senses (those natural centers), wanting to escape from the...

->To what end is it good or useful, that alongside the Good there must be an Evil?<-

->Answer.<-

Evil or the reluctant-will <note>German: *Wider-Willige*. This refers to a force of resistance or a "will-against" that pushes back against the primary impulse.</note> causes the Good to act as a Will, so that it presses back toward its original source, which is God, and so that the Good, as the good will, becomes desiring. For a thing that is only good in itself, and has no source-quality <term>Source-quality (Quall): A term coined by the author to describe the driving, often painful tension or "source-fountain" that gives a thing its active nature or "quality."</term>, desires nothing; for it knows nothing better within or before itself for which it could long. Thus we can also philosophize about the single good will of God and say that it can desire nothing in itself; for it has nothing in or before itself that could give it anything. Therefore, it leads itself out of itself into a state of diversity <note>German: *Schiedlichkeit*. The capacity for being distinguished or divided into different parts.</note>, into centers <note>German: *Centra*. Focal points or individual origins of life and consciousness.</note>, so that an opposition <note>German: *Widerwärtigkeit*. Literally "adversity" or "turning-against."</note> might arise in the outflow—that is, in that which has flowed out—so that the Good might become perceptible, active, and willing within the Evil. Specifically, the Good wills to separate itself from the Evil and return again into the single will of God. But because the outflow of the single eternal will of God always goes out of itself toward its own revelation, the Good—as the Divine power—also flows out from the eternal One with such an outflow, and enters into diversity and into the centers of multiplicity.

Thus the perpetual outflow of the will causes the Good within it to move; through this movement, the Good longs again for stillness and becomes desiring to press back into the Eternal. In such a pressing into itself, the One becomes movable and desiring, and in such activity consist perceptibility, knowledge, and the will. God—insofar as He is called "God"—can will nothing but Himself, for He has nothing before or after Him that He can will. But if He wills something, then that thing has flowed out from Him and is a reflection <term>Reflection (Gegen-Wurff): Literally a "counter-throw." In this philosophy, a spirit cannot know itself unless it projects itself onto a "mirror" or opposing object to see its own image.</term> of Himself, in which the eternal Will wills within its "Something." Now, if that "Something" were only one thing, the Will would have

If the mind did not flow out from itself, it would have no senses. If it had no senses, it would have no knowledge of itself, nor of any other thing, and could have no accomplishment or activity. How then could the wonders and powers of Divine Wisdom be known and brought into forms through the mind (which is an image of Divine Revelation)? But since a contrast—such as light and darkness—exists therein, the contrast itself is oppositional, and one property always causes the other, so that the one leads the other into desire, wanting to strive against the others and rule over them. In this desire, the senses and the mind are led into a natural and creaturely ground toward a willing—as toward a dominion in its "Something," as with its center over all other centers, like one sense of the mind over another. # Chapter IX.

## Of the Revelation of the Triune God, specifically according to the Second Principle, namely of the Light- and Angelic World and its Creatures.

### Connection.

We have hitherto considered the working cause of all things, as well as the eternal nature, out of which the triune God, through His almighty Word, brought forth all things in heaven and on earth; also how and why God has revealed Himself in such indescribable differentiation <term>Differentiation (Schiedlichkeit): The state of things being distinct, varied, and articulated rather than remaining one uniform, hidden essence.</term> of things. Now we follow by considering the works of God Himself, and the births which the triune God brought forth for the revelation of His infinite omnipotence and eternal Godhead. These births consist, according to the attributes of the triune God, in three principles <term>Principles (Principia): In Böhme’s thought, these are the three fundamental "worlds" or states of being: the dark fire-world, the light-world, and the physical world.</term>, and worlds or modes of life. According to the attribute of the Father, in the dark fire-world or hell, wherein God becomes manifest as an angry, jealous God, a consuming fire or eternal glow. According to the other Principle or attribute of the Son, in the light-world and its creatures, wherein God becomes manifest as a God and the highest Good: the light, the love, the life, the joy, and eternal pleasure. According to the third Principle, where God reveals Himself as fire and light, wrath and love, evil and good, and finally the "little world," namely, man in his threefold life, in which the triune God—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—is transfigured and made glorious.

**Question 1.**

Which, then, are the creatures wherein God has become manifest as an angry, jealous God, and as a consuming fire?

**Answer.**

The triune God, through His eternally-speaking Word, did not create any creatures *into* the dark world so that He might be revealed to a creature as an angry, jealous God; rather, God’s will was active in the Word according to all attributes of nature for the revelation of God as the highest Good, Light, and Love. For in the darkness, nothing—indeed, not even God Himself—is revealed *as* a God <note>The text suggests that "God" as a concept of goodness only exists in the light; in the dark, the same divine force is experienced only as raw, terrifying power.</note>. But that the angels who fell were caught in such a perverted will that God is revealed in them in no other way than as an angry, jealous God, and their light-world became a dark hell—this occurred through their willful disobedience and fall, when they turned their will away from the light, humility, gentleness, and love of God, and placed it into such fury and opposition, of which more below.

**2. Q.** Which, then, are the words of God that were first revealed?

**Ans.** It is the great and glorious light-world, in which God the Father transfigured His only-begotten Son, and through His almighty, eternally-speaking

<column-break/>

Word brought forth therein the great, innumerable host of the holy angels and light-spirits, and still brings forth the blessed souls and spirits of the perfectly righteous. Before we now proceed to the opening <note>The "opening" refers to the explanation or unfolding of the mystery.</note> of this angelic light-world, the reader is reminded above all else how he is to receive and understand this teaching of the blessed author <note>The "blessed author" refers to Jacob Böhme (1575–1624), the German mystic whose work this text summarizes and explains.</note>. Above all things, the reader must not mock the author’s conclusions <note>original: *Ausschliesse*. Refers to Böhme's specific spiritual deductions or insights.</note>; rather, if these things are too high for him, he should let them rest in their place. It cannot be denied that the ancients among the Jews, and later within a strayed Christianity, fabled much and varied things about angels out of superstition; from this, today’s sharp-witted reason has taken occasion to laugh at everything taught about angels, and to retort and twist what the Holy Scripture testifies of them with perverted interpretation—understanding what is said of angels merely as human messengers of God, and thus denying the existence <note>original Latin: *Existentiam*</note> or the being of angels. The blessed author warns the kind reader against such mocking of reason, saying that whoever wishes to grasp this high mystery can reach it no better than through a serious struggle of faith <note>German: *Glaubens-Kampff*.</note> and labor toward the new birth in Christ Jesus, just as the author himself reached such high knowledge through this single means. "When my spirit," he says, "intermingles with God <note>original: *inqvalIiret*. A Böhmean term meaning to harmoniously operate or "quality" alongside the divine essence.</note>, then it grasps it; but when it falls into sin, then the..."

### 3. Question: What does the author understand by the spirits?

**Answer:** Spirits are actually those powers which proceed from every ignition of fire and reveal the interaction of qualities <term>Interaction of qualities (Qualificirung): A term used by Böhme to describe how different divine or natural forces act upon and "qualify" one another.</term>; but here, by "spirits," we understand those independent minds <note>original: "Gemüther"</note> which have proceeded from the fire-ground of God’s omnipotence in the Word, as divine fire-sparks out of the great fire-ocean of eternal nature. Understand it by way of an analogy: Our sense and mind is a tiny spark and an actual ray of the immeasurable fire and light of the eternal Godhead. Whatever impulse and interaction we, as tiny sparks, possess and are capable of in our minds, the eternal God likewise effects and works in His mind in an unsearchable way. Now, our mind is a thinking being, and one thought-image <term>Thought-image (Denck-Bild): An idea or internal visualization that has the potential to become a reality.</term> always proceeds from another. Wherever a thought-image is in harmony with the will of our mind, so that the thought-image awakens a delight in the mind, the will immediately enters into it. Then the mind becomes active according to the kind and form of the thought-image, and the will becomes desirous to lead the thought-image into a being <note>into a being: into a state of substantive, objective existence.</note>, and works through all the properties of nature up to the seventh, in which the thought-image reaches its essence. Thus, Wisdom is a divine mirror of the mind, in which God eternally mirrors Himself through His divine wonder-eye of eternity, and forms Himself in countless thought-images. Now, as God has no thought-images or ideas that are not in harmony with the true God, God proceeds from eternal freedom into the thought-image, and His divine will becomes active in the thought-image, desiring to lead the thought-image into a being. The desiring will is attractive; that which is attracted wants to be free from the enclosure, and thus gives a movement from the enclosure of the will toward the enclosure, and the will toward freedom, through the movement in and out, gives birth to the essences or powers. These awaken the ignition; in the ignition, the two wills are separated: one, as the desiring one, goes back and constantly awakens the fire; the other, toward freedom, goes forward, rising up in the flash. And when it reaches freedom, it sinks down away from its severe fire-power. Through such sinking and entering into gentleness <note>original: "Sanfftmuth"</note>, the fire becomes water, and burns in the water as a light. In this light, the will finds the uni-

4. **Question.** What is the difference then between a spirit and an angel?

**Answer.** A spirit is "raw," without substance, in the manner of a *mind* <note>original: "Mentis"</note> and not of a *being* <note>original: "Entis"</note>; that is, a spirit, before it reaches the seventh form of nature, is like a thought-image or a thought that does not become substantial in *effect* <note>original: "Effect"</note> and through the working will. Instead, it hovers in the mind like an idea that a carpenter has conceived of a building; it is raw and without substance as long as the carpenter has not executed the building in its full form according to how he conceived it. In this way, the spirits are in the mind of God *in potential* <note>original: "in potentia," meaning as a possibility</note>, but not *in effect* <note>original: "in Effectu"</note> and in the *nature of things* <note>original: "rerum Natura"</note> as actual substance. But because God is almighty, wise, and true, He has no vain thoughts; rather, everything He perceives, He wills, and what He wills, He does. As soon as God beholds the thought-images in the wonder-eye of eternity, He leads them into substance; for every spirit from God has within itself a fiery will and a drive toward the light and revelation. For all spirits were created for the light; they are the essences of life—not from the corporeality of death, but from the center of the essences in the original state of the <term>Tincture</term> <note>The "Tincture" refers to the spiritual life-force or "dye" that brings the hidden qualities of God into visible, glorious manifestation.</note>, which reaches the freedom of God the Father, which is light and a delight of eternity, wherein the Word holds its government with the angelic world. They are all created from the sharpness of the glances in the wheel of essences, and they stand in freedom before the heart of God, and are the wonders in the pleasure of God which the heart of God beheld in the wonders of power. Therefore, He then set the will into the <term>Fiat</term> <note>Latin for "let it be done"; the creative command of God.</note> and the creation <note>original: "Schuff"</note>; and by the word "creation" we understand a distinction or "deciding" of the essences in the center in the harsh matrix <note>The "matrix" refers to the generative womb of nature from which forms emerge.</note>. For this reason, there is as great a difference among the spirits as there is a great difference in the will of the essences. As we have a

<column-break/>

likeness and example of this in the will of our own mind, from which so many kinds of thoughts spring, and where each thought again has a will toward the center; so that from a conceived thought a substance may become, as the person of understanding well knows. In such a way, all spirits were created out of the center of the eternal mind; therefore they are also eternal. For whatever is born out of the eternal mind is eternal. Before the *Fiat* or the active will of God for creation, the wheel of the eternal essences turned without substance in the "wonder"; but when God set the will into the *Fiat*, it moved into substance, and "Time" began, which did not exist before eternity.

Now, just as all the forms that can be established in nature stood in the matrix of the "birther" <note>The "birther" or "generatress" refers to the underlying creative power of nature (the Mother) before light brings it to order.</note> before the kindling of the light; when God had the will in the *Fiat* and wished to create spirits, it was no different than when God spoke to the "birther" of the <term>third Principle</term> <note>The "Third Principle" refers to our physical, material world, which follows the "First Principle" (darkness/fire) and "Second Principle" (light).</note> of this world: "Let there come forth all kinds of animals, birds, fish, and worms, each according to its kind." Understand: the body is according to the kind of each essence, and so is the substance in the body, which is its spirit; it is exactly the same with the high spirits. From the eternal matrix, all essences went out, which are without number. And as each form is a particular fountain-well of nature, spirits went out from each form and from each fountain-well according to the manifold essences and properties, each according to its kind; and the chief-princely government comes from the head-source, which is a cause of the multiplication within it, just as the mind is a cause of the senses.

->*The Threefold Life*, chapter 4, sections 29...37. See *Theosophical Questions* 5 and 6.<-

## 2. Part / Chapter 9.

...the Eternal was created into a corporeal spirit, which no reason can grasp and no sense can find, and it is not fundamentally understandable to us. For no spirit can find its own foundation; it may see its own depth down into the abyss, but it does not comprehend its Potter <note>original: "Töpffer." A biblical allusion (e.g., Isaiah 45:9) to God as the creator who shapes the "clay" of existence.</note>. It beholds Him and explores Him down into the abyss, yet it does not know the manner of its own making; that alone is hidden from it and nothing else. For a child knows its father and mother well, but it does not know how its father made it; it is even of as high a rank as its father, yet it is hidden from the child how it existed within the seed <note>original: "Saamen." In Böhme's thought, this refers to the latent spiritual potential before physical or substantial birth.</note>. And even if the child searches, it still does not know the time or the place, for it was in the seed, in the wonder, and in the life—a spirit within the wonder.

<margin>40. Fr. 1. 269. 271.</margin>
Thus, before the time of creation, the spirits were a mystery <note>original: "Mysterium"</note> and a hidden secret, like thoughts in the mind that have not yet been revealed through words or gestures.

We cannot speak of eternity in any other way than as a spirit, for everything was only spirit and yet has been born into substance <note>original: "Wesen"</note> from eternity. This happened through longing and desire. We cannot say at all that there was no substance in eternity, for no fire can exist without substance. Thus, there is no gentleness without the birthing of substance; for Gentleness gives birth to water, and the Fire swallows this into itself. The Fire makes one part of this into Heaven and the Firmament, and the other part into Sulphur <note>original: "Sulphur." In spiritual alchemy, Sulphur represents the active, combustible principle of the soul.</note>, in which the Fire-Spirit, with its essential wheel, creates a Mercury <note>original: "Mercurium." This represents the principle of movement, communication, and process.</note> and further awakens Vulcan <note>original: "Vulcanum." The principle of the "fire-striker" or the heat that initiates manifestation.</note> (that is, it strikes up the fire). Thus the third Spirit, which is Air, is born. There, the noble Tincture <note>original: "Tincture." A divine "dye" or spiritual essence that transforms and perfects base nature.</note> stands in the middle, like a glass with many colors, and it takes its origin from the Wisdom of God; for the colors originate from the source-quality <note>original: "Quall." A Böhme-specific term for a "fountain-spring" of sensation or energy.</note>. Every color stands with its essence in the gentleness of the water-source, except for black, which has its origin in the harsh, grim

<column-break/>

wrath <note>original: "Grimmigkeit." Often used to describe the dark, rigorous side of God's nature.</note>. They all receive their colors from the source-quality.

So now, one form after another flickers into being, and from the craving desire, one form becomes pregnant with the other, and one brings the other into substance. Thus, eternity stands in a perpetual Magic <note>original: "Magia"</note>, where nature is in a state of growing and wrestling. The fire consumes that substance and also gives it forth, and so it is an eternal bond. Only the light of the Majesty and the Trinity of God is unchanging, for the fire cannot seize it, and it dwells freely within itself. And yet, it is recognizable and findable to us that the light of Love is full of desire—namely, for the wonders and figures in Wisdom. In this desire, this world was recognized from eternity in the Wisdom, in the deep, hidden Magic of God, as its model. For the desire of Love searches in the Ground and the Abyss <note>original: "Grund und Ungrund." The "Ungrund" is the "baseless" or "abyssal" nothingness from which God's will emerges before all creation.</note>. There also, from eternity, the desire of Wrath and the harsh, strict source-torment of the Father’s nature and property mixed itself in. Thus, the image of angels and men was glimpsed from eternity in the Divine property, in God’s Wisdom—and just as well, the devils were glimpsed in the property of Wrath (though not in the holy, light-flaming property). But they were not yet in any image or substance; rather, they were there by their "kind," just as a thought spins itself in the deep mind and is led before the mind's own mirror, where the mind often beholds a thing that does not yet exist in substance.

Thus the two "birthers"—namely, Wrath in the fire, and then Love in the light—placed their model into the Wisdom. There, the heart of God lusted in Love to create this model into an angelic image out of Divine Substance, so that they were a likeness and image of the Godhead. They dwelt in the Wisdom of God to fulfill the pleasure of the Godhead and for the eternal joy of the Divine Kingdom of Joy. And this is how we are now to understand the Word: *Let there be* <note>original: "Verbum Fiat." The Latin command from Genesis: "The Word: Let it be done."</note>.

# Of the Revelation of God in the Light-World.

The *Fiat* <note>Latin: "Let it be." In this context, it refers to the creative command or the formative power of God.</note>, which grasped them and brought them into a substance and a corporeal being—for the will toward this image arose from eternity out of the Father, from the Father’s property in the Word or Heart of God, as His desiring will toward the creature and toward the revelation of the Deity. However, because He did not move from eternity until the creation of the angels, no creation took place until the angels' creation; the foundation and causes of which we are not meant to know. God has reserved for His own power how it came to be that God moved Himself, since He is nonetheless an unchangeable God; we should not search deeper here, for this would only confound us.

We have the power to speak only of the creation, for it is a work within the essence of God. We understand that the will of the Word or Heart of God grasped the harsh *Fiat* <note>original: "das herbe Fiat." In Böhme’s system, the "harsh" or "astringent" quality is the first property of nature, characterized by contraction and solidification.</note> in the center of the Father’s nature, with its seven spirits and forms of eternal nature, and [grasped] such things in the form of the Throne. There, the harsh *Fiat* stood not as a maker, but as a creator in the property of those essences, as in the great wonders of Wisdom: just as the figures had been seen from eternity in Wisdom, so they were now grasped with the *Fiat* in the will-spirit of God—not from foreign matter, but from God’s essence, from the Father’s nature. They were led by God’s will-spirit into the light of God’s majesty, where they were then children of God and children of God's majesty, created out of the Father's nature and property, and their will-spirit was directed into the Son’s nature and property. They were meant to, and were able to, eat of God’s love-essence in the light of majesty, whereby their fierce property <note>original: "grimme Eigenschaft." This refers to the "wrathful" or "dark" fire of the Father's side of nature, which must be mitigated by the Son's light/love.</note> from the Father’s nature was transformed into love and joy.

<margin>Incarnation, Part I, Chapter 2, Section 1, etc.</margin>

<column-break/>

6. Question: What, then, are the angels exactly?

Answer: According to my manner of speaking from Holy Scripture, the word *Angelus* <note>Latin: "angel."</note> means a messenger or an envoy. A messenger is sent from one to another, as a mediator between two who are separated from each other; and it is believable that the name "Angel" as a "messenger" was only given to those spirits after the fall of mankind. For while man still stood in communion with God, no messenger was necessary; but when man was separated from God through sin, they were used as mediators and messengers until the Great Angel of the Covenant <note>A traditional title for Christ.</note> came and united God and man in human nature through his bloody sacrifice of atonement. However, our author does not understand the word "Angel" in this sense; rather, he understands it through the *Angel* [hinge] <note>original: "Angel." A play on words between the German *Engel* (angel) and *Angel* (hinge/hook/fishing rod). Böhme uses this to describe the "turning point" where the divine eye focuses into a specific form.</note> $\Delta$ <note>The triangle symbol representing the Trinity.</note>, a hinge in which the Triune God reveals Himself as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. For this reason, Holy Scripture also calls the angels fiery flames <note>A reference to Psalm 104:4.</note>, whose signature is a $\Delta$; and "Eng-El" is as much as a narrow, small, enclosed, shaped God <note>original: "enger, kleiner, eingefasster, geformter GOtt." Böhme interprets the syllable "Eng" as "narrow" or "contracted," suggesting the angel is a localized, finite manifestation of the infinite Divine essence (El).</note>.

The Scripture says of God in Psalm 104: *You make your servants into winds, and your angels into flames of fire.* Within these words lies the entire understanding; for with the word "servants," the figurative *Idea* is understood as the spirit of the angels, arising from the breath or exhalation of Divine strength and power, out of the Holy Name of God. And the phrase "flames of fire" points to the central fire of eternal nature, in which the creature’s essence stands as the own-will of its own being.

### This is understood as follows:

The IDEA, or the image of God, was a form of the Divine Name within the unfolding Name of God, in which God has known all things from eternity as an imagination of the Divine Will, wherein the will of the *Ungrund* <note>original: "Ungrund." A central term in Böhme’s philosophy referring to the "groundless" or "abyssal" state of God before any manifestation or distinction.</note> formed itself into a shape, and yet it was not a creature, but only an IDEA—just as an image forms itself in a mirror—so the imagination of Divine power formed itself in the outflowing Name of God.

## 2. Part / Chapter 9.

The eternal was created into a corporeal spirit / which no reason can grasp / and no sense can find / and it is also not thoroughly known to us. ness <note>original: "Grimmigkeit." This refers to the dark, astringent, and wrathful property of nature.</note>. They all receive their colors from the source-well.

And it is now thus for us to remember the Word <note>original: "Verbum." The creative "Speaking" of God that brings the inner thoughts of Wisdom into actual existence.</note>

### Part 2 / Chapter 9

But when God wished to have such an **IDEA** <note>original: "IDEAM." Böhme uses the Latin term to refer to the eternal archetypes or patterns of things held in the divine mind before they are physically created.</note> within a living creature / as in its own will / He moved and divided the central fire of eternal nature / and so the **IDEA** became manifest in the fire / which happened through the breathing out, or the **Yes** <note>original: "Jah." In Böhme's linguistic mysticism, "Jah" represents the divine "Yes," the affirmative breath of God (derived from the first syllable of the Hebrew name "Yahweh").</note>. Thus the **No** <note>original: "Nein." The "No" represents the force of contraction, selfhood, and negation that allows a creature to have a separate identity from God.</note> / as the outpoured will of self-satisfaction / formed itself along with the out-breathed **Yes** / so that the creature might stand in its own will / which self-will is understood to be in the central fire / as in the properties belonging to fire / in which the creaturely life stands. For if that had not been / then Lucifer could not have broken himself away from the Good in his own will and fallen. Had he not possessed his own will / then God’s power must have fallen; but instead, the creature broke itself away from the Good / and wished to rule in the power and in the properties of the central fire / as in transformation and fantasy <note>In this context, "fantasy" refers to a state of self-delusion or a false reality created by the ego, rather than divine truth.</note> / into which he then entered. Therefore Christ called him a murderer and a liar from the beginning / and this because the **No** gained the government within him / so he is a vain liar.

The essence and being of the good angels is a power of the central fire / and of the central light / in which their image stands: But the **IDEA** within them is a figure of the Holy Name of God / as of the wonder-working Word.

And just as there are many and countless Divine names / so also there is a distinction among the **IDEAS** within them. Just as one power has a different effect than another / though they are indeed equal in God / yet they are distinct in the outflow / as in the Wisdom / for the sake of revelation and wonders: So also there is a distinction of the angelic **IDEA**, in the powers / and each one has a greater power and might than another / and also different virtues. Just as the stars in the firmament are distinct; so also are the angels / so that there might be a **Harmony** <note>original: "Harmonia."</note> / as a joy and knowledge of the Divine powers / for their foundation stands therein / they are made from the essence of both inner eternal central fires / their powers are the great outflowing names of God / all springing from the **YES** [Jah] / and led into the **NO** [Nein] / into the enclosure / so that the powers might become manifest / there had to be an opposition / in which there would be a distinction.

7. **Question:** How then did the spirits come from the **YES** of eternal freedom into the **NO** / as into a form and enclosure / so that they became manifest as angels?

**Answer:** Just as the thoughts of a human being become manifest through speaking / so also the angels were led into being and made manifest through the eternally-speaking Word of God. Those who then accepted the will were angels, for they placed their **imagination** <term>Imagination: In this mystical context, it refers to the soul's power to focus its desire and "form" its internal reality</term> into the will, into the Heart of God, and they ate of the **Word of the Lord** <note>original: "Verbo Domini"</note>. But those who set their imagination into the dark mind—like Lucifer, intending to fly out beyond the Godhead and gentleness in the power of fire, in the lightning-flash of fire, in the sharp power of God, and to be lord alone—they became devils, and they have this name because of their expulsion from the light; for when the **Fiat** created them, they were in the light, for the **Fiat** that created them stood in the light.

8. **Q.** How then did the spirits come into a being?

**Ans.** Every little grain of seed has within it an **Idea** <note>original: "Ideam." Böhme uses this to mean the eternal blueprint or archetype of a creature.</note> of that plant from which it originates; as soon as it comes into the earth, as into its mother, its inner property becomes active according to both centers: as the will toward the fire works through the harsh and bitter essences toward the ignition of life; once life is awakened therein, the essences of the will toward the fire descend and generate the root; the essences toward the light ascend and produce the plant. The former find the substance for their fire-hunger in the earth, and with that they clothe themselves for the ignition of life; and the latter have their food in the sun and draw its **power** <note>original: "Krafft"</note> to themselves for growth, out of the four elements. Thus the little grain of seed grows downward and upward and works through attraction, hungering and fasting above and below the earth, until it is a plant like that from which it originated, and until it reaches its limit and goal, having brought such a seed to perfection as it was itself.

<column-break/>

All and every spirit from GOD is an imperishable seed of His living Word. This seed has within it the **Idea** <note>original: "Ideam"</note> of the triune Godhead. The sower is the active will of the Father, who sows this seed out of His inwardness. The Matrix or earth is the holy pure element, in which fire and water stand in the highest **temperature** <note>In the 17th century, this meant a state of perfect balance or "temperament" between opposing forces</note>, and breathe out the holy element. The essences or driving powers are the **Tincture** <term>Tincture: A spiritual life-force or "dye" that transforms and ennobles the qualities of a being</term>; the sun is the speaking Word, which through its speaking unlocks both centers and awakens the fire-source and water-source to drive [growth], where the fire-source roots itself downward into eternal nature, according to the property of the Father; but the water-source drives upward through the **Tincture** into Paradise, beautifully greening and blooming forth, proceeding according to the property of the Holy Spirit, opening and communicating the inner qualification, just as a flower gives off its essences through its scent. Thus all the angels were created in the first **Principle** <term>Principle: One of the three fundamental "worlds" or states of being; here, the first refers to the eternal nature or "fire-world"</term>, formed and embodied by the willing Spirit in the true angelic and spiritual manner, and enlightened by the light of GOD, so that they should increase the Paradisiacal joy and should remain eternally. If they were to remain eternally, they had to be figured out of the indissoluble bond, out of the first **Principle**, and they were to look upon the Heart of God and eat of the **Word of the Lord** <note>original: "Verbo Domini"</note>, and this same food would keep them holy and make their image clear and bright, just as the Heart of God, in the rising of the second **Principle**, enlightens the Father as the first **Principle**, and there the Paradisiacal power rises up...

## Part 2 / Chapter 9

->**Power and Joy, Paradise and the Kingdom of Heaven.**<-

So it is also with the angels who remained in Paradise; they stand in the first Principle <term>Principle: "Principio" in the original, referring to the first aspect of God's self-manifestation, often associated with the father's fire or the ground of existence</term> within the unbreakable bond. Their food is the Divine Power; their imagination <note>In this context, "imagination" or "Einbildung" refers to the creative, formative power of the mind to shape reality</note> is the will of the Holy Trinity in the Godhead. The confirmation of their will, life, and deeds is the power of the Holy Spirit. Whatever the Spirit does in the birthing of Paradise, the angels rejoice in it, and they sing the song of praise of Paradise, of the lovely fruit and eternal birth. All their activity is an increase of heavenly joy and a delight of the Heart of God—a holy play in Paradise, a will of the eternal Father. To this end, God created them: so that He might be revealed and rejoice in His creatures, and the creatures in Him, so that in the center of multiplicity or eternal nature, within the eternal unbreakable bond, there might be an eternal, joy-filled game of love.

<margin>Principle 4. §. 67. 68. <note>A reference to Böhme’s work "The Three Principles of the Divine Essence"</note></margin>

9. **Question:** *Did God then create all the angels at once, or were some brought forth before the others?*

**Answer:** Just as the thoughts of a human being move swiftly before him and give birth to a thousand others in a single moment, so God, in His surging <note>original: "Wallen," describing the dynamic, bubbling movement of divine energy</note>, created the holy angels all at once—not from any foreign material, but from Himself, from His power and eternal wisdom. The philosophers held the opinion that God made the angels only from light; but they have erred. They are not made from light alone, but from all the powers of God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. These powers are lovely, joyful, and manifold, and yet they are all within one another like a single power. Just as the power of all the stars rules in the air, so it is in God; however, in God, every power reveals itself with its own particular effect.

<column-break/>

Afterward, there is a resonance <note>original: "Schall," meaning sound or vibration</note> in every power, and the resonance sounds according to the quality of each power; and therein stands the entire heavenly kingdom of joy. From this divine Salitter <term>Salitter: A term used by Jacob Böhme to describe the "divine saltpeter" or the fundamental spiritual substance of the heavenly realm</term> and Mercury <term>Mercury: "Mercurio" in the original, representing the alchemical principle of movement, sound, and vital spirit</term>, all angels were made—understand this as being from the body of nature. You might now ask: "How were they made or born, or what kind of form is that?" Truly, if I had an angelic tongue and you had an angelic understanding, we could speak quite finely of it; but as it is, only the spirit sees it, and the tongue cannot lift it up, for I have no other words than the words of this world. Yet, if only the Holy Spirit is in you, your soul will surely grasp it.

Behold, the entire Holy Trinity, with its surging, has figured together a body <note>original: "Corpus"</note> or image out of itself, like a little God—though not proceeding as forcefully as the entire Trinity, but to some extent according to the size of the creature. In God there is no beginning nor end, but the angels have a beginning and an end <note>meaning a boundary or individual definition, rather than a cessation of existence</note>, though not in a way that is measurable or graspable, for an angel can be great one moment and soon small. Their swift change is as fast as human thoughts. All qualities and powers are in an angel, just as they are in the entire Godhead. But you must understand this correctly: they are made from the Salitter and Mercury and figured together; that is, from the "Rising-Up" <note>original: "Auffgange," likely referring to the dawn or the emergence of light</note>. Behold a likeness: from the sun and stars, the elements go forth, and they create a living spirit in the "Salnitter" of the earth; the stars remain in their orbits, yet the spirit nevertheless receives the quality of the stars.

Now, however, the spirit is a distinct thing according to its composition, and has a substance like all the stars; and the stars are and remain a distinct thing as well, each one free for itself. But nonetheless, the quality of the stars rules in the spirit; yet the spirit can and may raise or lower itself within its qualities, or may [remain] in the...

...live under the influences of the stars <note>In Böhme’s cosmology, "stars" often refer to the internal spiritual forces or "astrums" that shape a being's character</note> as he wishes, for he is free; for he has received the qualities that he has within himself as his own property. And though he initially received them from the stars, they are now his own; just as when a mother has the seed within her—while she has it and it is a seed, it belongs to the mother. But when it becomes a child, it is no longer the property of the mother, but the child’s own property. And even though the child is in the mother’s house, and the mother nourishes it with her food, and the child could not live without the mother, still the body and the spirit, which are begotten from the mother’s seed, are its own property and it retains its physical right for itself.

The same holds true for the angels; they too were all formed together from the Divine Seed, but each now possesses their body <note>original: "Corpus"</note> for themselves. And even though they are in God’s house and eat the fruit of their Mother <note>Here, the "Mother" refers to the divine substance or "Salitter" from which they were created</note> from which they were made, their body is now their own property.

However, the quality outside of them or their body—that is, their Mother—is not their property, just as a mother is not the property of the child, nor is the mother’s food the property of the child; rather, the mother gives it out of love because she gave birth to the child.

She may also certainly cast the child out of her house if it will not obey her, and may withhold her food from it—which is exactly what happened to the principality of Lucifer.

Thus, God may withdraw His Divine Power, which is outside of the angels, whenever they rise up against Him. But when that happens, a spirit must languish and perish, just as when air—which is also his mother—is withdrawn from a human being, he must die; so also, the angels cannot live without their Mother.

10. **Question:** *How then does the triune God become active within the angels according to His properties and their forms?*

**Answer:** Just as the triune God is qualifying <note>original: "qualificirend"; this refers to the active, living interaction of different divine attributes or "qualities"</note> within Himself, so He is also active within an angel. First, there is the formed body, which is inseparable and also indestructible, and incomprehensible to human hands; for it is driven together out of the Divine Power, and that same power is so bound together that it can never be destroyed eternally. Just as little as anyone or anything can destroy the whole Godhead, so little can anything destroy an angel; for every angel is formed together out of all the powers of God—not with flesh and blood, but out of Divine Power. First, the body <note>original: "Corpus"</note> is from all the powers of the Father, and in those same powers is the Light of GOD the Son. Now the powers of the Father and the Son, which are creaturely <note>meaning: "existing as a created being"</note> within the angel, give birth to an understanding spirit, which rises up within the angel.

In the beginning, the powers of the Father give birth to a light, through which an angel sees into the whole Father, through which he can see the external power and working of GOD that is outside his body, and through which he can behold his fellow brothers, and also see and enjoy the glorious fruit of God, in which his joy consists. And that same light originally came from the Son of God into the powers of the Father, creaturely into the angelic body, and is the property of the body, which can be taken from him by nothing—unless he himself extinguishes it, as Lucifer did.

Now all the power that is in the entire angel gives birth to that same light. Just as God the Father gives birth to His Son in His heart, so the power of the angel also gives birth to its own son and heart within itself, and this in turn enlightens all the powers in the entire angel. **source-vein of the wrath of GOD.** For it is one of the seven spirits of GOD, in whose power the Divine Essence stands in the whole Divine Power and heavenly splendor. Now if it is ignited, it is a fierce source of wrath and a beginning of the hells, and also a torment and woe of the hellish fire, and also a quality of darkness; for the Divine Love, and also the Divine Light, is extinguished within it.

The **bitter quality** is the first spirit, from which life becomes active, from which mobility takes its origin, and is rightly called **HEART** <note>original: "COR," Latin for heart. But if it is elevated, moved, or ignited too much, it ignites the sweet and harsh qualities, and is like a tearing, stinging, and burning poison, just as when a person has a tearing pestilence-boil from which he cries "Ah!" and "Woe!"

This quality is in the Divine Power, when it is ignited, the spirit of the zealous and bitter wrath of GOD, which is unquenchable, as can be seen with the legions of Lucifer. Furthermore, when this quality is ignited, it is the bitter hellish fire that extinguishes the light, which makes a stench out of the sweet quality, a sharpness and tearing in the harsh, a hardness and coldness; in the sour it makes it thick and brittle <note>original: "rühricht und brüchicht," describing a decaying or dross-like state</note>, a stench, a misery, a house of mourning, a house of the darkness of death and the hells, an end of joys, which can no longer be thought of therein, for it can be stilled by nothing, and can be illuminated by nothing again; but the dark, harsh, stinking, sour, thick, bitter, fierce source ascends into all eternity.

11. Fr.

The fourth quality or the fourth fountain-spirit <term>Quell-Geist: Böhme’s term for the fundamental "flowing" forces that constitute the nature of God and the universe</term> in the Divine Power of GOD the Father is **heat**; it is the true beginning of life, and also the true spirit of life. The harsh, sour, and sweet qualities are the Salitter <term>Salitter: a term Böhme uses for the divine "salt-nitre," the fundamental substance or "matter" of the heavenly realm</term> which belongs to the body <note>original: "Corpus"</note>, from which the body is formed. For in the harsh quality stands the cold and the hardness, which is the contraction and drying; and in the sweet quality stands the water and the light or radiance, and the entire matter <note>original: "Materia"</note> of the body. And the bitter quality is the separation or forming; and the heat is the spirit, or the kindling of life, from which the spirit in the body arises, which wells up in the whole body and shines outside the body, and creates the living movement in all the qualities of the body.

However, one must look specifically at two things in all the qualities. When one looks at a body, one first sees the stock or kernel of all qualities, which is formed out of all qualities; for to the body belongs harsh, sour, sweet, bitter, and heat; these qualities are dried together and make the body or stock.

### The Great Mystery of the Spirit.

Now these qualities are mixed in the body as if they were all only one quality, and yet each quality wells up in its own power and goes out. Each quality goes out from itself into the others and stirs the others; that is, it infects <note>original: "inficiret"—in this context, it means to permeate or influence the nature of the other qualities</note> the others, from which the other qualities receive this will; that is, they approve the sharpness and spirit of this quality, whatever is in it, and they always mix together. Now the harsh quality with the sour always draws the other qualities together, and grasps and holds the body and dries it, for it dries all other powers and holds them all through its infection; and the sweet quality softens and moistens all the others, and tempers itself with all the o-

<column-break/>

thers; from this they become fine, lovely, and gentle. And the bitter quality makes all the others active and movable, and divides them into members, so that each member receives a fountain-well in the tempering of all powers, from which mobility arises. And the heat kindles all qualities, from which the light breaks forth in all qualities, so that one sees the other; for when the heat works in the sweet moisture, it gives birth to the light in all qualities, so that one sees the other. From this arise the senses and thoughts, so that one quality sees the other—which is also tempered in it and with itself—and approves it with its sharpness, so that it becomes one will, which rises in the body into the first fountain-well in the harsh quality. There the bitter quality in the heat penetrates through the harsh, and the sweet in the water lets it through gently; there the bitter in the heat drives through the sweet water out of the body, and makes for itself two open gates; these are the eyes, the first sensibility. Of this you have an example and image: look at this world, especially the earth, which is of the nature of all qualities, and in it all sorts of figures are formed.

Firstly, the harsh quality is in it, which draws the Salitter together and firms the earth, so that it is a body and does not break apart, and forms within it all sorts of bodies according to the nature of each quality, such as all sorts of stones and ores, and all sorts of roots according to the nature of each quality.

Now, when the same is formed, it lies there as a bodily, welling mobility, for it wells through and in the bitter quality in itself, as in its own formed body; but it has as yet no life for growth or spreading out without the heat, which is the spirit of nature. When the sun's heat shines upon the soil, then all formations of ore and herbs, roots, worms, and everything that is within the earth well up and grow.

### Part 2 / Chapter 9.

**11. Question: How is the Son of God, according to his properties, active and manifest in the spirit and body of an angel?**

**Answer:** He acts as the **wellspring** of all that is good, satisfying and filling the desiring will of the Father with his all-sufficient Godhead; he soothes and gladdens the driving and longing will with eternal freedom. For the holy angels were made into creatures out of God for this reason: so that they should praise, sing, ring out, rejoice, and increase the heavenly joy before God’s Heart—which is the **Son of GOD**. And where else would the Father appoint them but before the door of his Heart? Just as all the joy of a human being, which resides in the whole person, arises from the wellspring of the heart, so too in God does the great joy arise from the wellspring of his Heart. Therefore, he created the holy angels out of himself; they are like "little gods" according to the essence and qualities of the whole God, intended to play, praise, sing, and resonate within the Divine Power, and to increase the rising joy from the Heart of God.

The radiance and the power of the Son of GOD—or the Heart of GOD, which is the light or source of joys—takes its most beautiful and joy-filled origin in the midst of these kingdoms, and shines in and through all **angelic gates** <term>angelic gates: Böhme’s term for the various regions or "ports" of the heavenly realm inhabited by angelic choirs</term>. You must, however, understand exactly how this is meant; for when I speak in parables and compare the Son of GOD to the **sun** or to a **round sphere**, it is not meant to imply that he is a finite wellspring that one could measure, or whose depth, beginning, or end one could fathom. I only write in such parables so that the reader might come to the right understanding. For it is not the case that the Son of God should be born only in the midst of these angelic gates and not also outside the angelic gates. For the Father’s powers are everywhere, from which and out of which the Son is 

<column-break/>

born, and from which the Holy Spirit proceeds. How then could he be born only in the midst of this angelic gate? The fundamental truth and meaning is this: that the Holy Father, who is everything, has his most joy-filled and lovely qualities within these angelic gates, from which the most joy-filled and lovely Light, Word, Heart of powers, or wellspring is born. Therefore, he also created the holy angels in these places for his joy, honor, and glory.

It is indeed the same in one place as in another within the unsearchable eternity; but where there are no creatures, it is recognized by nothing except by the Spirit in its wonders. And this is the chosen **place of glory** <note>original: "Locus der Herrlichkeit"</note> of God, which God the Father has chosen within himself, where his Holy Word or Heart is born in the highest clarity, power, and triumphant joy. For mark this mystery: all light which is born out of the Father’s powers—which is the true wellspring of the Son of GOD—is also born in an angel and a holy human being, so that he triumphs in great joy within that same light and knowledge. How then could it not be born everywhere in the whole Father? Since his power is everything and everywhere, even where our heart and senses cannot reach. Now, where the Father is, there also is the Son and the Holy Spirit; for the Father everywhere begets the Son, his Holy Word, Power, Light, and Sound; and the Holy Spirit everywhere proceeds from the Father and the Son, both within all angelic gates and outside all angelic gates. When one compares the Son of God to the **sphere of the sun**, as I have often done in the preceding chapters, one speaks in natural parables; and I have had to write thus for the sake of the reader’s lack of understanding, so that in these natural things he might direct his mind

# Of the Revelation of GOD in the World of Light.
## Bb 2

...lift up the mind / and thus climb from one step to another / until it might enter into the high mysteries. But it is not meant / that the Son of GOD is a formed, composite image / like the sun. For if that were so / then the Son of GOD would have to have a beginning / and the Father would have had to have birthed him at a single moment; thus he would not now be an eternal / almighty Son of the Father / but he would be like a king / who still had a greater king over him / who had birthed him in time / and who had the power to change him. But it is not so / rather the Father births the Son everywhere out of all his powers / and the Holy Spirit goes out everywhere from the Father and the Son / and is one single GOD in one being with three distinct persons. Of this you have a parable in a precious gold-stone <note>original: "Gold-Steine"; likely an unrefined nugget of ore containing gold</note> / which is undivided. Firstly there is the **Matter** <note>original: "Materia"</note> / that is the Saltpeter <term>Saltpeter: in Böhme’s thought, this represents the raw, explosive "materia" or building blocks of nature</term> and Mercury <term>Mercury: the "quick" or living spirit that drives movement and growth</term> / which is the mother or the whole stone / which births the gold everywhere within the whole stone / and in the gold is the glorious power of the stone. Now the Saltpeter and Mercury signify the Father / the gold signifies the Son / the power signifies the Holy Spirit: in such a way is also the Trinity in the Holy Threefoldness / except that within it everything moves and goes forth.

One also finds in a gold-stone perhaps in one place a **point** / where more and more beautiful gold is inside / than in another / regardless / of the fact that there is gold in the whole stone: Just so is the **Place** <note>original: "Locus"</note> or location in the midst of the angelic gates a dear / beautiful / lovely place to the Father / where his Son and Heart is born most lovingly of all / and where the Holy Spirit goes forth most lovingly of all from the Father and the Son. Thus you have the true ground of this mystery / and you must not think / that the Son of GOD was birthed out of the Father at one single certain time / having a beginning / and now stands there like a king / and lets himself be worshipped. No / that would not be an eternal Son / but he would have a beginning / and would be beneath the Father / who had birthed him: He could also not be all-knowing / for he would not know / how it had been / before the Father had birthed him; rather the Son is always being born from eternity to eternity / and shines from eternity to eternity ever again into the Father’s powers / whereby the Father’s powers from eternity to eternity are always pregnant with the Son / and always birth him. From this arises the Holy Spirit from eternity to eternity evermore / and goes out from eternity to eternity always from the Father and the Son / and also has no beginning nor end. And this essence is not in one place of the Father alone / but everywhere in the whole Father / who has neither beginning nor end / where no creature can sense or think.

<column-break/>

->Aurora, Chapter 7. Sections 13, 23, 29, 35.<-

What kind of joy that must be, when the eternal Divine hunger reaches its eternal satisfaction and a perfect fullness, when the fierce, almighty, rising source-spirit <term>source-spirit: "Quell-Geist," one of the seven foundational qualities or "fountains" that drive the existence of nature and spirit</term> finds a complete rest, and the eternal heat finds an inexhaustible spring of **gentleness**, and thus the Father finds his beloved Son in nature and creature, in whom he has all his delight.

Since the sweet quality is a thin / lovely / sweet source-water / it softens the heat / and extinguishes the fire / so that there remains in the sweet source-fountain of the sweet water only the joy-filled light / and the heat is only a gentle—

### Part 2 / Chapter 9.

...gentle warming / just like in a human being / who is of a **sanguine temperament** <note>original: "sanguinischer Complexion." And when the sweet / light power of love comes to them / so that they taste of it / and receive their life / oh, then there is a friendly **welcoming** <note>original: "Beneveniren," from the Latin *bene venire*</note> and triumphing / a friendly welcome and great love / truly a friendly and gracious kissing and pleasant tasting. Oh, noble light and clarity / who can measure your beauty? How elegant is your love? How beautiful are your colors? Oh, and eternally / who can express this? 13. **Question:** How does the Son of God become active in an angel according to the sixth form of nature / namely according to the rising and joy-rich **Mercury** <term>Mercury: In Böhme's system, "Mercurius" is the spirit of motion, communication, and the "wheel" of nature.</term>?

This spirit takes

<column-break/>

its origin in the fire-flash / that is / in the bitter quality / and rises in the flash through the sweet water / wherein it softens itself / so that it becomes bright / and in the harsh quality it is captured / there it stirs all the spirits / from this stirring rises the **Sound** / in the flash stands its rising source / and in the sweet water in love stands its body or root. Now this Sound is the divine realm of joy / the triumphing / wherein the divine and gentle play of love rises in God / along with the forms / shapes and all kinds of figures. But you should know here / that this quality penetrates quite gently and lovably with its stirring through all the spirits / in the manner / that in a human heart a lovely and gentle fire of joy rises / wherein the **soulish spirit** <note>original: "animalische (seelische) Geist." When the soulish spirit is born in the center of the heart in the midst of the seven source-spirits / so that the will of the seven spirits is incorporated together / then the Sound leads it out to the Body / and is its chariot / upon which the spirit travels / and executes that which is resolved in the counsel of the seven spirits. For the Sound travels through the soulish spirit into the nature of God or into the **saltpeter** <term>Saltpeter: "Salitter," a divine-natural substance or "sap" that Böhme views as the fundamental material of the heavenly world.</term> of the seventh source-spirit in the divine power / which is its initial mother / and **acts within** <note>original: "inqualiret"</note> the same in the forming / and also in the distinction of the formation.

14. **Question:** What is then finally the ground / and the goal / toward which all the life- or source-spirits of God drive and work in the creation of an angel?

## Bb 3

within which also all beauty and joy arises; that is the true Spirit of Nature, indeed Nature itself, in which comprehensibility <note>The quality of being a tangible, graspable substance rather than an abstract spirit.</note> resides, and in which all creatures are formed, in heaven and on earth. Indeed, heaven itself is formed within it, and all naturality in God resides in this Spirit; if this Spirit were not, there would be neither angel nor human, and God would be an unfathomable being, consisting only in an unfathomable power.

<margin>Aurora 11, § 1.</margin>
Without this quality to work through, nothing—not even God himself—would have been revealed. The angels, however, are not formed solely from the seventh Spirit of Nature—like the transient creatures—but rather, when the Godhead moved toward the creation of the angels, the Godhead, with its entire substance and being, was incorporated into every circle where each angel was corporated together. (Understand both eternal principles <note>original: "Principia"</note>, both fire and light—and yet not as a source of fire, but essentially <note>Meaning as a substantial essence rather than a burning heat.</note>) and it became one body, and yet the Godhead remained on its throne <note>original: "Sede"</note> as before.

### Understand this correctly.

The body of the angel, or its comprehensibility, is from the seventh spirit; and the birth within that same body consists of the six source-spirits <term>Quell-Geister: the seven fundamental active qualities of nature in Böhme's system</term>; and the spirit or the heart which the six spirits generate in the middle center <note>original: "Centro"</note> of the body, within which the light rises, and from the light the soul-spirit <note>original: "animalische Geist," from the Latin "anima" meaning soul; refers to the living breath or life-force.</note>, which also intermingles <note>original: "inqualiret," meaning to work together or share qualities.</note> outside of the body <note>original: "Corpus"</note> with the Godhead—that signifies the Heart of God, from which the Holy Spirit proceeds. And it was also intermingled from the Heart of God into the body of the angel during the first corporate-joining; therefore, the angel’s governance now takes place in the mind just as the Godhead’s does.

And just as in the seventh Spirit of Nature of God—which arises from the other six—there does not reside the entire, perfect knowledge of the other six spirits (for it cannot search out their deep birth, in-

<column-break/>

-asmuch as they are its father and generate it out of themselves): So too, the entire, perfect knowledge of God does not reside in the angelic body, but rather in the spirit which is born in the heart, which proceeds from the light. This spirit intermingles with the Heart and Spirit of God, and within it resides the perfect knowledge of God. But the body cannot grasp that same soul-spirit, just as the seventh Spirit of Nature cannot grasp the deepest birth of God. For when the seventh Spirit of Nature is born, it is dried by the harsh quality and held as if by the father, and it cannot go back into the depth—that is, into the center of the heart where the Son is born and from which the Holy Spirit proceeds. Instead, it must remain still as a born body, and allow the source-veins—that is, the spirits—to intermingle and work within it according to their pleasure. For it is the house or property of the six spirits, which they ever build according to their pleasure, like a pleasure-garden <note>original: "Lust-Garten"</note> in which the master of the house sows all kinds of fruits according to his pleasure, and enjoys them.

Thus, the other six spirits always build this pleasure-garden and sow their fruit in it, and enjoy the same for the strengthening of their power and joys; and this is the garden in which the angels dwell and walk, and in which the heavenly fruit grows.

The wondrous proportion <note>original: "Proportz"</note>, however, which manifests in the plants and figures in this garden, arises through the intermingling and through the love-wrestling of the other spirits. For whichever spirit becomes the first <note>original: "Primus"</note> in the struggle, it forms the plants according to its kind; the others always help in this—at one moment it is one in one place, then the other, then the third, and so on.

Therefore, so many kinds of plants and figures arise, which is entirely unsearchable and incomprehensible to the bodily reason of the angels; but to the Soul... <note>The text cuts off mid-word "Animalischen" at the bottom of the column.</note>
