<margin>Aurora, Chapter 16, Sections 14, 20</margin>

15. **Question:** How is the Holy Spirit manifested in the creation, begetting, and animation of an angel?

**Answer:** Just as the property of the Holy Spirit in the triune Godhead is that he proceeds from the Father and the Son, and carries out the begetting of the Father and the birth of the Son: so he also proceeds from the Father and the Son within an angel, like a scent that comes from a flower and makes known the flower’s property, power, and virtue. Thus, through the working of the Holy Spirit, the spirit proceeds out of the angel; that same spirit rises up into God as a lovely scent and affects the eternal Godhead in all angels with its volatile essences <note>original: "volatitischen Essentien"; referring to the subtle, moving spiritual substances</note>. For he passes through all, he tests and adorns them all, and is likewise tested by all. This then causes the unspeakable harmony of the angels for the praise of God, and for love, peace, and joy, each within the other.

This is, briefly and summarily, the working of the triune God, both for the creation and begetting, as well as for the qualification <note>original: "Qualificirung"; the process by which a being is imbued with specific divine qualities or powers</note> of an angel, from which their original state and way of life may be known.

### Here note the foundation and highest mystery of the angels of God.

If you now wish to know where their love, humility, and friendliness come from—which rise up in their hearts—then note the following: Every angel is fashioned like the whole Godhead and is like a little god. For when God created the angels, He created them out of Himself. Now, God is in one place as He is in another; everywhere there is the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

In these three names and powers stand heaven and this world, and everything your heart can think of. Even if you were to close off a tiny circle that you could hardly see into, or that you could hardly distinguish, the whole divine power would still be within it. The Son of God is born within it, and the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and Son within it. If it is not in love, then it is in wrath, as it is writ-

<column-break/>

ten: *With the holy you are holy, and with the perverse you are perverse* (Psalm 18:26), referring to those who awaken the wrath of God upon themselves. This wrath also exists in all the spirits of God in the place where it is awakened. Conversely, where the love of God is awakened, it also stands in the full birth of the entire Godhead of that place. In this, there is no difference; the angels are created one like the other, all out of the divine <term>Salitter</term> <note>A term Böhme uses to describe the "divine saltpeter" or the fundamental substance/matter of the heavenly realm</note> of heavenly nature. The only difference between them is that, when God created them, each quality was positioned differently within the "great movement" in its highest birth or ascent. From this, it has come to pass that the angels are of many kinds of qualities and have many colors and beauties, and yet all come from God.

Now, every angel has all the qualities of God within him, but one is the strongest in him; he is named according to that quality and glorified in it. Now, just as the qualities in God always beget one another, rising up and loving one another from the heart, and one always receives its life from the other; and as the lightning flashes up in the "sweet water" in the heat, from which life and joy have their origin; so it is also in an angel. His internal birth is nothing other than the external birth outside of him in God. Just as the Son of God is born outside the angels in the central <term>Quell-Brunn</term> <note>literally "source-well" or "fountain-spring"; Böhme's term for the dynamic centers of divine energy</note> in the heat in the sweet water out of all seven spirits of God, and in turn enlightens all seven spirits of God, from which they have their life and joy; so too, in like manner, the Son of God is born within an angel in his central "source-well" of the heart, in the heat in the sweet water, and in turn enlightens all seven source-spirits of the angel. And just as the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son and forms, shapes, and loves everything; so also the Holy Spirit in the angel proceeds out to his fellow brothers, and loves them, and rejoices with them.

<summary>This page explains that angels are "little gods" created from God's own substance, mirroring the Trinity's internal processes through their own "source-spirits" and hearts. Böhme emphasizes that the Holy Spirit flows through angels like a scent from a flower, creating a harmonious and communal joy among all heavenly beings.</summary>

# Of the Revelation of GOD in the Light-World.

For there is no difference between the spirits of GOD and the angels, except only this: that the angels are creatures <note>In Böhme's thought, a "creature" is a finite, created being as opposed to the uncreated, eternal Godhead.</note>, and their bodily being has a beginning; however, the power from which they are created is GOD himself, and is from eternity and remains in eternity. For this reason, their agility is as swift as human thoughts; wherever they wish to be, they are there instantly; furthermore, they can be large or small, as they desire.

And that is the true essence of GOD in heaven—indeed, heaven itself. If your eyes were opened, you would clearly see it right here on earth at the place where you are. For if GOD can allow a human spirit to see this while it is still stuck in the body, and can reveal Himself to it in the flesh, then He can certainly do so outside of the flesh, if He wills.

O you house of sin of this world, how you are encompassed by hell and death! Wake up, the hour of your **new-birth** <note>original: "Wieder-Geburt"</note> is at hand; the day breaks; the **morning-redness** <note>original: "Morgen-Röthe"; a reference to the title of Böhme's first book, *Aurora*, symbolizing the dawning of divine wisdom.</note> reveals itself. O you dull and dead world, why do you demand signs? Your whole body is frozen; will you not wake from sleep? Behold, a great sign is given to you, but you sleep and see nothing; therefore, the LORD will give you a sign in his zeal <note>original: "Eifer"; can also mean "jealousy" or "wrathful passion."</note>, which you have awakened with your sins.

<margin>Aurora, Chapter 12, verses 40, 50.</margin>

But you should not think that the heavenly light in this world is entirely extinguished within the **source-spirits** <term>Quell-Geister: Böhme's term for the seven fundamental properties or powers that drive both divine and natural life.</term> of GOD. No, there is only a darkness, which we cannot grasp with our corrupted eyes. But if GOD takes away the darkness that hovers over the light, and if your eyes were opened, you would see even here in the place where you stand, sit, or lie in your chamber, the beautiful face of GOD and the entire heavenly gates. You would not first need to cast your eyes up into the sky, for it

<column-break/>

stands written: *The WORD is near you, namely on your lips and in your heart* (Deut. 30:14; Rom. 10:8). GOD is so near to you that the birth of the Holy Trinity also happens in your heart; all three persons are born in your heart: GOD the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. When I write here of the **center** or middle—that the fountain-well of the Divine Birth is in the middle—it does not mean that there is a special place in heaven, or a special **body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note>, where the fire of the Divine Life rises up and from which the seven spirits of GOD go out into the entire depth of the Father. Rather, I speak in a bodily, or angelic, or human way, for the sake of the reader's lack of understanding, according to the way the angelic creatures were formed and how it is in GOD everywhere.

For you can name no place, neither in heaven nor in this world, where the Divine Birth is not thus, whether it be within an angel and holy person, or outside of them. Wherever a source-spirit is stirred in the Divine Power—no matter where the place may be, except only in the devil and in all godless, damned people—there the fountain-well of the Divine Birth is already present. There are already all seven source-spirits of GOD, just as if you were to draw a spatial, creaturely circle and had the entire Godhead contained specifically within it, exactly as it is born in a creature; so it is also in the entire depth of the Father in all ends and in all things. And in such a way is GOD an almighty, all-knowing, all-seeing, all-hearing, all-smelling, all-tasting, all-feeling GOD, who is everywhere, and who tests the hearts and kidneys <note>An archaic biblical idiom referring to the innermost thoughts and emotions.</note> of the creatures. And in such a way are heaven and earth His, and in such a way must all devils, together with all godless people, be His eternal prisoners, and in the **Salitter** <term>Salitter: A term Böhme uses to describe the "divine saltpeter" or the fundamental spiritual substance of the heavenly world.</term> which they have corrupted and ignited in their **place** <note>original: "Loco"</note>...

16. **Question:** How are the angels distinguished from one another?

**Answer:** The eternal Unity, introducing itself out of the **Unground** <note>original: "Ungrund"; Böhme’s term for the absolute, undifferentiated divine abyss or "groundless" state before creation.</note> into the Ground, and out of the NOTHING into SOMETHING, became effective in the Word, according to those principles of Fire and Light, and according to those seven **source-spirits** <note>original: "Quell-Geistern"; the seven primary qualities or forces through which God manifests in nature.</note> of nature. Now, just as one source-spirit gains the upper hand in an angel during the birthing process, so also the angel has a qualification, a way of life and form, color, virtue, office, and the like; and although they indeed have their particular way of life, qualification, virtue, luster, glory, and governance, they are nevertheless altogether only a prepared instrument of the one Spirit of GOD in His joy, which He reveals through them; for He reveals Himself through them. Their substance and essence, insofar as they are a possession <note>original: "Eigenthum"; also implies a specific self-centered identity.</note> and are called creatures, is an enclosure of eternal nature, which stands without beginning in divine operation, for His self-revelation, in the **eternal Genitrix** <note>original: "ewigen Gebährerin"; the eternal birthing-power of nature.</note>. Understand that, as creatures, they are of the eternal nature of all seven forms, and in great diversity of powers, in the manner that the first three introduce and form themselves in nature into infinite differences; thus is their creaturely being also to be understood in many properties, each one in its own property. And we are primarily to understand seven high princely governments in three hierarchies, according to the fountain-spring of the seven pro-

<column-break/>

perties of nature, wherein each form of the eternal nature is then enclosed in a throne, as a government, within which the differences are understood, as well as the will of obedience toward the prince of the throne. They hold this in administration as creatures of divine gifts, where GOD has given them the essence (of which they are an image) for a possession, wherein they dwell, which is the holy spiritual power of the world, of the **Temperament** <note>original: "Temperatur"; the state of perfect balance between the conflicting qualities of nature.</note>. Their most inward ground, which originates from divine property from eternity, is the single will of the Unground into the Ground. Thus they originate, according to the beginning of nature, out of the **Science** <note>original: "Scientz"; from the Latin "scientia," used here to mean a proto-conscious urge, a "knowledge-seed," or a self-moving tendency of the will.</note> of the free will, out of which and in which free will GOD composed His Word. That same free will introduced itself into the birth of nature—as in the ignition of the first principle of fire—into distinctness; and out of that same distinctness in the origin of the fire, the angels were introduced in the free will (as a particular part of the bottomless free will) to turn themselves with the free will into the first or the second principle, and to reveal themselves there. Just as God Himself is free and is everything in that same free will, and introduces Himself in that same free will in nature—in fire, light, and darkness, in pain and torment, as well as in love and joy—so also the particular creature has the power to introduce itself out of the whole free will into a creaturely property, in the three hierarchies or principles, as they wish. For the "Science" may grasp and reveal itself in the three hierarchies in which it has power, just as the divine "Science" has introduced itself into essence and operation: one part in the fiery, according to the cold; the second in the fiery, according to the heat; the third in the fiery, according to the light; the fourth into the **fantasy** <note>original: "Phantasey"; used here to describe the "play" of nature's properties when they act in selfhood or disharmony, creating a sort of illusory reflection of the divine.</note>, as in a play of nature’s selfhood, where it plays with itself in inequality, in the properties.

<margin>On the Election of Grace, Chapter 4, verses 23, 26.</margin>

**17. Question:** How are they distinguished according to the three properties as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit?

**Answer.** When GOD the Almighty decided in His counsel that He wanted to make angels or creatures out of Himself, He made them out of His eternal power and wisdom, according to the form and manner of the Trinity in His Godhead, and according to the qualities in His Divine Being.

First, He made three Royal Regimes, according to the number of the Holy Trinity, and each kingdom had the order, power, and quality of the Divine Being. Here, lift up your mind and spirit into the depth of the Godhead, for here a door is opened. The *locus* <note>original: "Locus"; Latin for "place" or "location."</note> or place of this world—the depth of the earth and above the earth unto heaven, as well as the created heaven, which was made out of the midst of the water, which hovers above the stars, which we see with our eyes, whose depth we cannot fathom with our senses; this space, or all of it together, was a kingdom, and Lucifer was the king within it before his expulsion.

The other two kingdoms, namely Michael's and Uriel's, are above the created heaven and are equal to the first kingdom. These three kingdoms together encompass such a depth that no human number can reach, and it cannot be measured by anything. Yet you should know that these three kingdoms have a beginning and an end; but the GOD who made these three kingdoms out of Himself has no end. Nevertheless, outside of these three kingdoms is the power of the Holy Trinity, for GOD the Father has no end. But you should know this mystery: that in the midst of these three kingdoms, the Luster or the Son of GOD is born. And the three kingdoms are circular around the Son of GOD; none is the furthest, and also none is the nearest to the Son 

<column-break/>

of GOD; one is as near to the Son of GOD as the other.

From this fountain and out of all the powers of the Father, the Holy Spirit goes forth, together with the light and power of the Son of GOD, into and through all angelic kingdoms and outside all angelic kingdoms, which no angel nor man can search out. I have also not set out to think further, much less to write, but my revelation reaches unto the three kingdoms, like an angelic knowledge; however, not in my own reason or comprehension or perfection, like an angel, but piece-meal, only as long as the Spirit remains in me; beyond that, I do not recognize it. When He departs from me, I know nothing, except only of elemental and earthly things of this world; but the Spirit looks even into the depth of the Godhead.

<margin>Aurora, chapter 7, sections 4, 11.</margin>

**18. Question:** How are they distinguished according to the seven forms of nature?

**Answer.** There are seven spirits of GOD; all seven have moved, and the light within them has also moved, and the Spirit that goes out from the seven spirits of GOD has also moved. Now the Creator, according to His Trinity, also wanted to create three hosts <note>original: "Heere"; can mean armies or great multitudes of inhabitants.</note> not far from one another, but one next to the other like a circle. Now observe: just as the spirits were in their surging <note>original: "Wallen"; Böhme's term for the boiling, welling, or active movement of divine qualities.</note> or rising, so also the creatures became; in the midst of each host, the heart of each host was incorporated together, and from that an angelic king or Grand Prince was made. Just as the SON of GOD is born in the midst of the seven spirits of GOD, and is the life and heart of the seven spirits of GOD, so also an angelic king was created in the midst of his territory out of nature, or out of the natural heaven from the power of all seven source-spirits, and he was now the heart in a host, and possessed the quality of his entire host.

## 2. Part / Chapter 9.

...power or strength within himself, and was the most beautiful among them.

Just as the **SON OF GOD** is the heart and the life, and the strength of all seven spirits of **GOD**, so too is a King of the angels within his army.

Now, just as there are seven primary qualities within the Divine Power from which the Heart of **GOD** is born, so too were several mighty Prince-Angels created according to each main quality in every army. I do not know their exact number, but they are the commanders of the other angels alongside the King.

Here you should know that the angels are not all of one quality, nor are they all equal to one another in power and might. While every angel certainly has the power of all seven <term>Source-Spirits<note>original: "Quell-Geister"; the seven active principles or forces that Böhme believes constitute both God and nature.</note></term> within them, one quality is typically the strongest in each, and he is glorified according to that specific quality. For just as the <term>Salitter<note>original: "Salitter"; a unique term Böhme uses to describe the divine "substance" or the spiritual "soil" of the heavenly world from which things are formed.</note></term> was in each place at the time of creation, so the angel became; and according to the quality that is strongest in the angel, he is named and glorified. Just as every meadow-flower receives its color from its own quality and is named according to that quality, so it is with the Holy Angels. 

Some are strongest in the *harsh* quality, and these are light-brownish and closest to the cold. When the light of the **SON OF GOD** shines upon them, they appear entirely bright in their quality, like a brown lightning bolt. Some are of the *watery* quality, and these are light, like the holy heaven; and when the light shines upon them, it looks like a crystalline sea.

Some are strongest in the *bitter* quality, and these are like a precious green stone that flashes like lightning; and when the light shines upon them, it appears as a reddish-green, as if a <term>carbuncle<note>A historical term for a red gemstone, usually a garnet, thought to glow with its own internal fire.</note></term> were shining out of them, or as if life itself had its origin there.

<column-break/>

Some are of the *heat* quality, and these are the brightest of all, yellowish and reddish; and when the light shines upon them, it looks like the lightning of the **SON OF GOD**. Some are strongest in the *love* quality, and they are a sight rich in heavenly joys, entirely light; when the light shines upon them, they appear light blue—a lovely sight.

Some are strongest in the *sound* <note>original: "Thons"; in Böhme’s system, the Seventh Spirit is the "Sound" or "Tone," representing the harmony and physical manifestation of the other spirits.</note> quality, and these are also light; when the light shines upon them, it looks like a rising flash of lightning, as if something were about to raise itself up there.

Some are of the *whole nature*, acting as a general mixture; when the light shines upon them, they look like the holy heaven, which is formed out of all the spirits of **GOD**. The King, however, is the heart of all qualities and has his realm in the center like a fountain-spring, just as the sun stands in the midst of the planets and is a king of the stars and a heart of nature in this world; a <term>Cherubim<note>original: "Jerubin"; Böhme's variant of Cherubim.</note></term> or Angel-King is just as great.

And just as the other six planets alongside the sun are commanders and give their will to the sun so that it may rule and work within them, so all angels give their will to the King, and the Prince-Angels are in council with the King. But you should know here that they all share one *will of love* with one another; no one envies another for his form or beauty, for as it is among the spirits of **GOD**, so it is among them. Also, they all possess Divine joys simultaneously and enjoy heavenly food together; in this, there is no distinction, only in the colors and the strength of power is there a difference—but in perfection, there is none at all. For everyone has the power of all the spirits of **GOD** within them; therefore, when the light of **GOD** shines upon them, each angel's quality reveals itself through its color.

19. **Q.** We have so far seen the distinction of the angels in general; I would further like to hear what the three hierarchies of angels actually are, what they consist of, and how one is distinguished from the other?

**Ans.** Just as the Godhead is threefold in its essence—in that the outcome from the seven spirits of **GOD** shows and brings itself forth as threefold: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, one single **GOD**, in whom the entire Divine Power consists, along with everything that exists—and yet the three persons in the Godhead are not a separable essence, but are within one another: so it was in like form when **GOD** moved and created the angels. Then three distinct angels were created from the best core of nature, from the essence of the Trinity within the nature of **GOD**, and in such authority and power as the Trinity has within the seven spirits of **GOD**. For the Trinity of **GOD** rises up within the seven spirits of **GOD**, and is in turn the life and heart of all seven spirits. Thus also, the three angelic kings have each risen up in the nature of their **ARMY** or place, and each is a natural **LORD** of his place over the government of the angels; but the <term>Place<note>original: "Locum"</note></term> itself is retained by the Trinity of the Godhead, which is unchangeable, for itself, while the king retains the government of the angels.

Now, just as the Trinity of the Godhead is one single essence in all ends of the entire Father, and is bound together like the limbs in a human body, and all places are as one place (even if one place has a different task than another, just like a person's limbs), it is still one Body of **GOD**. So too are the three angelic kingdoms bound together with one another, and not each specifically separated; no angelic king may say: "This is my kingdom, no other king may enter here." Although it is indeed his initial natural hereditary kingdom, and remains his, yet all other kings and angels are his true natural brothers born of one Father, and they all inherit their Father's kingdom at the same time.

Just as the <term>Source-Spirits<note>original: "Quell-Geister"; the seven fundamental forces of Böhme's cosmology.</note></term> of **GOD** each have their natural seat of birth and keep their natural place for themselves, and yet with the other spirits are the one **GOD** (for if the others were not there, he would not be either, and one rises up in the other): so it is also with the primacy of the Holy Angels, and it has no other form than in **GOD**. Therefore, they all live in a friendly and peaceful way with one another in their Father's kingdom, like dear little brothers; there is no boundary to how far one may go or not.
<margin>Aurora 12. 71. 77.</margin>

20. **Q.** How then were the kings of the three hierarchies born?

**Ans.** The person or the <term>body<note>original: "Corpus"</note></term> of a king of the angels was born out of all the qualities and all the powers of his entire kingdom through the surging Spirit of **GOD**. Therefore he is king because his power reaches into all the angels of his entire kingdom, and he is their head and army-leader, the most beautiful and powerful <term>Cherub<note>original: "Jerubin"</note></term> or Throne-Angel: Lord Lucifer was also such a one before his fall.

### Of the Ground and the Mystery.

If one wishes to find the mystery and the deepest ground, one must with diligence look upon and consider the creation of this world, its government and order.

# Part 2 / Chapter 9.

...nature, as well as the qualities of the stars and elements. Although this is a corrupt and dual essence, and also not living or understanding, for it is only the corrupt <term>Saltpeter<note>original: "Salnitter"; for Boehme, this is the foundational "divine earth" or the basic matter of the spiritual and physical world.</note></term> and <term>Mercury<note>original: "Mercurius"; the active, communicative, and mobile force within nature.</note></term> in which King Lucifer once held house, within which there is both evil and good—though it is indeed the true power of **GOD**, which before its corruption was bright and pure, just as it is now in heaven.

These powers of the stars and elements were, after the horrific fall of Lucifer's kingdom, again set into such an order by the Creator as the kingdom of angels stood in Divine pomp before his fall. However, you should not think that the angelic kingdom and its creatures were turned around in a circle like the stars are now, which are only powers and are turned about because of the birth of this world. This birth stands in tormenting anxiety, in evil and good, in corruption and redemption, until the end of this <term>enumeration<note>likely referring to the pre-ordained count of generations or the unfolding of time.</note></term> or the Judgment Day.

->Now observe.<-

The Sun stands in the midst of the deep and is the light or heart of all the stars; for when the Saltpeter and Mercury were thin before the creation of the world in Lucifer's kingdom and <term>qualified<note>original: "qualificiret"; meaning the powers acted upon one another according to their specific qualities or characteristics.</note></term> with one another, **GOD** pulled the heart out from all the powers and made the Sun from it. Therefore, it is the brightest of all and illuminates all the stars in return; and all stars work in its power, and it itself possesses the power of all stars, and with its brilliance and heat, it ignites the power of all stars, and every star receives according to its power and kind from the Sun. The angelic kingdom is also arranged in this way: The Sun signifies the supreme Throne-Angel, the <term>Cherub<note>original: "Jerubin."</note></term> or King in an angelic kingdom, as Lord Lucifer also was one before his fall; he had his seat in the center or in the middle of his

<column-break/>

kingdom and ruled with his power in all his angels, just as the Sun rules in all the powers of this world—in the Saltpeter and Mercury, that is: in soft and hard, in sweet and sour, in bitter and harsh, in cold and heat, in air and water. As one then sees in winter, when it is so severely cold that the water turns to ice, the Sun nonetheless shines warm through all the cold, regardless of the fact that in the path through which its brilliance travels, snow and ice freeze. But I will show you the true mystery here: Behold, the Sun is the heart of all powers in this world and is fashioned from all the powers of the stars together, and it illuminates in return all the stars and all powers in this world, and all powers become active within its power. (Understand this <term>magically<note>original: "magisch"; here implying a spiritual or symbolic understanding of the underlying reality rather than a purely physical one.</note></term>, for it is a mirror or likeness of the eternal world.)

Just as the Father begets his Son—that is, his heart or light—out of all his powers, and that same light, which is the Son, begets life in all the powers of the Father, so that in that same light all kinds of growth, beauty, and joy arise within the Father's powers; so also is the kingdom of angels arranged, all according to the likeness and essence of **GOD**.

A <term>Cherub<note>original: "Jerubin."</note></term> or army leader of a kingdom of angels is a wellspring or heart of his entire kingdom, and was made from all the powers from which his angels were made, and he is the most powerful and brightest. ->21. Question: Which then is the first hierarchy?<-

The King truly bears this name, for he is embodied from the <term>Source-Spirits<note>original: "Quell-Geister"; the seven foundational qualities or "fountains" of divine power that form the basis of all existence.</note></term> like a kernel from them, and now stands there in the place of **GOD** the Father. Not in the sense that he *is* **GOD** the Father (who consists in the seven spirits of the entire Deep and is not a creature), but so that within Nature among the creatures, there might also be such a creature as **GOD** the Father is in the seven Source-Spirits, who may rule among the creatures. For when **GOD** made himself creaturely, he made himself creaturely according to his Trinity. Thus, the King or Grand-Prince Michael looks like **GOD** the Father in his <term>glorification<note>original: "Glorificirung"; the state of being filled with divine light and clarity.</note></term> or clarity, and is a King and Prince of **GOD** upon the Mountain of **GOD**, and has his office in the Deep in which he was created. That same circle or space in which he and his angels were created is his kingdom, and he is a dear son of **GOD** the Father in Nature—a creaturely son in whom the Father takes his joy. You must not compare him to the Heart or Light of **GOD** which is in the entire Father and which has neither beginning nor end, just like **GOD** the Father himself. **22. Question: Who then are the princes in this kingdom?**

Answer: Just as **GOD** reveals himself as a Father according to the seven properties of nature, so also in the kingdom of <term>Michael<note>original: "Michaëlis"; referring to the archangel Michael, who governs one of the three main angelic hierarchies in Böhme’s system.</note></term>—as the <term>hierarchy<note>original: "Hierarchia"; the structured order of angelic beings.</note></term> fashioned after the property of **GOD** the Father—there are seven prince-angels. In these princes, the seven <term>Source-Spirits<note>original: "Quell-Geister"; the seven foundational divine forces or qualities that drive all of creation.</note></term> of **GOD** reveal themselves according to the working of their forms; for in every prince and his princedom, one specific form is the <term>primary<note>original: "Primarius"; the dominant or chief quality.</note></term> element.

Behold, **GOD** is a **GOD** of order. Just as it happens within his own government in himself—that is, in his birth, and in his rising, surging, and being—so too is the order of the angels. Just as within him there are primarily seven qualities by which the entire Divine Being is driven, manifesting itself through these seven qualities into infinity (and yet the seven qualities are the first things within that infinity, through which the Divine birth exists eternally and unchangeably in its order); and just as in the midst of the seven spirits of **GOD** the Heart of Life is born, from which Divine joy rises, so too is the order of the angels.

The prince-angels are created according to the spirits of **GOD**, and the <term>Cherubim<note>original: "Jerubin"; Böhme uses this term to describe high-ranking angels who embody the "Heart" or "Center" of the divine order.</note></term> according to the Heart of **GOD**. As the Divine Being works, so also do the angels. Whichever quality rises within the Being of **GOD** and shows itself particularly in its working—such as in the rising of the Tone or the Divine working, wrestling, or struggling—that same angelic prince who is most strongly devoted to that quality also begins his <term>round-dance<note>original: "Reigen"; a traditional circle dance, here used to describe the harmonious, rhythmic movement and joy of the heavenly hosts.</note></term> with his legions, with singing, ringing, dancing, rejoicing, and

<column-break/>

jubilating. That is a heavenly <term>music<note>original: "Musica"</note></term>, for there everyone sings according to the voice of their specific quality. The prince leads the dance, just as a <term>Cantor<note>original: "Cantor"; a choir leader or song-master.</note></term> does with his students, and the King rejoices and jubilates with his angels to the honor of the great **GOD**, and for the increase of heavenly joys. This is within the Heart of **GOD** like a holy play, and they were created for this very purpose: for the joy and honor of **GOD**.

Now, when the heavenly music of the angels rises, then in the heavenly pomp and in the Divine <term>Salitter<note>original: "Salitter"; a term unique to Böhme referring to the "divine saltpeter" or the fundamental spiritual-material substance of the heavenly world.</note></term>, there rises all kinds of growth, all kinds of figures, and all kinds of colors, so that the Godhead shows itself in infinite and unsearchable ways, colors, forms, and joys. Whichever Source-Spirit in the Godhead happens to show itself particularly at that time—with its rising and its wrestling in love, as if it had become the primary one—that same prince-angel immediately begins his heavenly music with his devoted angels according to his quality, with singing, ringing, piping, and all kinds of heavenly art that rises within the spirits of **GOD**. But when the Center in the midst rises—that is, when the birth of the **SON OF GOD** shows itself particularly as a triumph—then the music and the joys of all three royal governments of the entire creation of all angels rise together. What kind of joy this must be, I leave for every soul to contemplate; I cannot grasp it in my corrupted nature, much less write of it. With this song, I <term>summon<note>original: "citire"; a legal or formal calling.</note></term> the reader into that life; there he will be in the middle of the dance himself, and only then will he give belief to this spirit. What he does not understand here, he shall have there in vision.

You should know that this was not "sucked from a stone" <note>An idiom meaning this knowledge was not invented or derived from dead, material things, but from living revelation.</note>, but rather when the flash rises in the Center, then the spirit stands and recognizes it. Therefore, take heed, and do not play too mockingly in this place, or you will be found a scorner before **GOD**, and it may well go for you as it did for King <term>Lucifer<note>The fallen angel who mocked the divine order.</note></term>.

# Regarding the Revelation of GOD in the Light-World.

**23. Question: What is the second <term>hierarchy<note>original: "Hierarchia"; in Böhme’s theology, the angelic world is divided into three vast kingdoms, each reflecting one of the three persons of the Holy Trinity.</note></term>?**
**Answer:** The kingdom of those angels in whom the Son of **GOD** is active according to the property of Light, for the revelation of his eternal <term>generation<note>original: "Gebährung"; refers to the ongoing, eternal process of the Son being born from the Father.</note></term> and his glory, which he had with the Father before the world began.

**24. Question: Who then is the King of this hierarchy?**
**Answer:** The fallen angel, who did not preserve his throne and royal seat, but was cast out from his royal throne and lost his angelic name. The Author calls him <term>Lucifer<note>Böhme frequently uses "folk etymologies" to explain spiritual truths; here he contrasts the Latin meaning with a German word-play.</note></term>, not so much according to the Latin meaning, "Morning Star," but according to the sense of the German way of speaking: <note>original: "quasi fern à luce"</note> "far from the light."

**25. Question: What was the nature of this King’s birth, reign, way of life, and glory?**
**Answer:** Just as Michael was created according to the quality, nature, and property of **GOD** the Father, so also was Lucifer created according to the quality, nature, and beauty of **GOD** the Son. He was bound to him in love, like a dear son or a heart, and his heart also stood in the <term>Center<note>original: "Centro"; the spiritual focal point or source of divine power.</note></term> of the light, as if he were **GOD** himself; and his beauty surpassed everything. For his "encompassing" or his most noble mother was the **SON OF GOD**; there he stood as a King or Prince of **GOD**. His territory, place, and space, along with his entire host—wherein he became a creature and which was his kingdom—is the created heaven and this world, in which we now dwell with our King **JESUS CHRIST**. For our King sits in Divine Omnipotence, just as King Lucifer once sat upon the royal throne of the cast-out Lucifer; and King Lucifer’s kingdom has now become His. Prince Lucifer, how does that taste to you?
Now, just as **GOD** the **FATHER** is bound to his **SON** with great love, so too was King Lucifer bound to King Michael with great love—

<column-break/>

—just like one heart or one **GOD**; for the <term>source-fountain<note>original: "Quell-Brunn"; the flowing, vitalizing energy of the Divine.</note></term> of the **SON OF GOD** reached right into Lucifer’s heart. However, the light that he had in his own body, he held as his own possession; and this light, as it shone, <term>in-qualified<note>original: "inqualiret"; a Böhmean term meaning to merge properties or operate together in a single nature.</note></term> or incorporated with the light of the **SON OF GOD** (which was outside of him) as one single thing. Although you were two distinct beings, you were still bound together like body and soul.
And just as the light of **GOD** reigns in all the powers of the Father, so did he also reign in all the angels as a mighty King of **GOD**, and he wore upon his head the most beautiful crown of heaven.

**26. Question: Who is the King of the third hierarchy?**
**Answer:** This gracious prince and king takes his name from the Light, or from the flash or the "outgoing" of the Light, which signifies **GOD** the **HOLY SPIRIT**. Just as the **HOLY SPIRIT** goes forth from the Light and forms and fashions everything, and rules in everything, so also is the power and grace of a <term>Jerubin<note>original: "Jerubin"; Böhme’s specific term for the angelic king of the third hierarchy, related to the Cherubim.</note></term>. He is the king and the heart of all his angels; that is, when his angels merely look upon him, they are <term>infected<note>original: "inficiret"; in this context, it means to be permeated or influenced by a spiritual will or quality, rather than a disease.</note></term> by the will of their king. Just as the will of the heart "infects" all the members of the body, so that the entire body does what the heart has decided—or as the **HOLY SPIRIT** rises up in the center of the heart and enlightens all the members in the whole body—so also the Jerubin, with his entire radiance and will, "infects" all his angels, so that they are all together like one body, and the King is the heart within it. Now, this magnificent and beautiful prince is formed according to the nature and quality of the Holy Spirit; he is indeed a magnificent and beautiful prince of **GOD**, and is bound in love with the other princes like a single heart.

## Part 2 / Chapter 9

These are now the three Princes of GOD in Heaven. When the Flash of Life—that is, the SON of GOD—rises in the middle circle within the Source-Spirits of GOD and shows himself as triumphant, then the Holy SPIRIT also rises triumphantly above himself. In this rising, the Holy Trinity also rises in the hearts of these three kings, and each triumphs according to his specific quality and nature. In this rising, the entire host of Heaven and all the angels become triumphant and full of joy, and there arises the beautiful hymn "We Praise Thee, O God" <note>original: "TE DEUM LAUDAMUS"</note>. In this rising of the heart, the <term>Mercury<note>In Böhme’s mystical chemistry, Mercury represents the active, moving, and expressive principle of the divine life.</note></term> in the heart is awakened, as well as in the entire <term>Salitter<note>A term Böhme adapted from "saltpeter" to describe the crystalline, divine matter or "spiritual earth" of the heavenly kingdom.</note></term> of Heaven; then, within the Godhead, there arises the wonderful and beautiful formation of Heaven in many kinds of colors and forms, and each spirit shows itself specifically in its own shape. I can compare it to nothing other than the most noble stones, such as Rubies, Emeralds, Beryls <note>original: "Delfin," possibly referring to a blue-green beryl or aquamarine</note>, Onyx, Sapphires, Diamonds, Jasper, Hyacinth, Amethyst, Beryl, Sardis, Carbuncles, and the like.

In such color and fashion, the natural Heaven of GOD reveals itself in the rising of the Spirits of GOD. When the light of the SON of GOD shines therein, it is like a bright sea of the colors of the stones listed above.

<margin>Aurora, Chapter 12, verses 108-115.</margin>

27. **Question: Are these kings and kingdoms then divided into certain borders, locations, and places?**

**Answer:** Here the spirit shows that wherever any angel is created, that same place <note>original: "Locus"</note> in the heavenly nature—within which and out of which he became a creature—is his own seat, which he possesses by Natural Right as long as he remains in the love of GOD. For it is the place <note>original: "Locus"</note> that he held from eternity before he became a creature; that same Salitter stood in the place from which he was formed. Therefore, that same seat remains his by Natural Right so long as he moves within the love of GOD. However, you should not think that GOD is thereby bound, such that He would not dare to drive him out of it if he were to behave differently than how GOD first created him. For as long as he remains in obedience and in love, the place is his by Natural Right; but if he elevates himself and ignites the place in the **Wrath-fire**, then he sets fire to his Father's house and becomes a source of opposition against the place <note>original: "Locum"</note> from which he was made, making two things out of that which was one before his elevation. When that happens, he keeps his bodily Natural Right for himself, and the place keeps its own right for itself; but if the creature (which has a beginning) wants to set itself against the First (which was before the creature and has no beginning) and wants to destroy the place <note>original: "Locum"</note>—which it did not make, but wherein it was created as a creature in love—and wants to turn that place into the Wrath-fire, then Love rightly spews out the Wrath-fire together with the creature.

From this, the laws in this world also arise; for when a son sets himself against the father and strikes the father, he has lost his paternal inheritance, and the father may thrust him out of the house. But while he is in obedience to the father, the father has no power to disinherit him.

This worldly law takes its origin from Heaven, just as many other worldly laws written in the Books of Moses also take their start and origin from the Divine Nature in Heaven; this I will clearly prove in its proper place from the true foundation in the Godhead.

28. **Question:** What colors do the angels have, and what is the form and stature of their bodies?

**Answer:** When the author attributes colors, bodily forms, limbs, and the like to the angels, it is to be understood more as a likeness <note>original: "Gleichnis," a parable or metaphorical comparison</note> than in a literal way. Color is a revelation of the **Tincture** <note>a term used here to mean the inner spiritual essence or "color of the soul"</note> and its inner qualification. Just as the property and power of the Tincture in a flower is recognized by its colors, through which its inner power and virtue are revealed: so too the author understands by "colors" those external identifying marks through which the inner power and virtue of an angel are made known. For example:

Those angels in whom the first quality, the "astringent" or "harsh" quality, predominates, are called **light-brownish**. This signifies a strong contraction, for the more something is squeezed together, the browner it becomes. Those in whom the moving and "bitter" quality predominates are called **green**; and if the fire shines within it, they are **red-greenish**, like a rainbow or a carbuncle <note>a deep red gemstone</note>, which signifies the fleeting, driving, and moving property of this angel. Where heat predominates, they are **yellow-reddish**; that is, heated, fiery, and powerful in rising. Where the sweet "Water-Source" has the upper hand, they are called **bright and transparent**, like the clear sky; by this is understood their radiance, transparency, purity, truth, gentleness, and humility. Where Love is the "Primas" <note>Latin: the primary or first quality</note>, they are **light blue**, because fire and water are tempered as red and light. Where the joy-rich **Mercurius** <note>here referring to the spiritual force of movement and expression</note> rules, they are like a rising flash of lightning with a rapid change of colors, such as bright, yellow, red, and green, signifying their speed and cheerfulness.

Concerning the bodily form and stature of the angels: just as a human is created in the likeness of GOD, so too are the angels. For they are the brothers of humanity, and in the Resurrection, humans will have no other image or likeness than the angels, as our King Christ himself testifies in Matthew 22:30. Furthermore, the angels here on earth have never revealed themselves to humans in any other form than the human shape.

### Part 2 / Chapter 9.

So also in angels and humans, the power of **Smell** rises up from all the powers of the body <term>Corpus: the physical or essential body</term> through the spirit, and goes out through the nose, and becomes imbued <note>original: "inficiret," meaning to be flavored or colored by external forces</note> with every scent. It then brings this through the nose as the **third Council** into the head, before the **Princely Throne**. There it is "approved" <note>judged or evaluated</note> to see whether it is a good scent, acceptable to its complexion <term>Complexion: the specific balance of bodily and spiritual temperaments</term>, or not. If it is good, it brings it to the **Mother** <note>The "Mother" refers to the heart or the formative source of life within the body</note> so that it may be put into action; if not, it is cast out. And this Council of Smell, which is born out of the Salniter <term>Salniter: a mystical term for the "divine saltpeter," the explosive, creative energy of God's nature</term>, is also mixed with Mercury <term>Mercurio: Mercury, representing the force of movement, sound, and communication</term>, and belongs to the heavenly realm of joy; it is a magnificent, lovely, and beautiful wellspring in GOD.

The **fourth Princely Council** is **Taste** upon the tongue. It also rises from all the powers of the body through the spirit into the tongue, for all the fountain-veins <term>Quell-Adern: the spiritual conduits of life-force</term> of the entire body lead into the tongue, and the tongue is the sharpness <note>The "Schärffe" or intensity that defines the distinct quality of a thing</note> or taste of all powers. Just as the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son and is the "sharpness" or approval of all powers—bringing everything that is good in His surging or His rising back into all the powers of the Father, from which the Father’s powers become "pregnant" again and forever give birth to the "Taste"—so it is here. But whatever is not good, the Holy Spirit spews out as an abomination, as it is written in the Revelation of John <note>original: "Apoc. 3, 16"</note>: *I will spew thee out of my mouth*. This is also how He spewed out the Great Prince Lucifer in his pride and corruption, for He could no longer "taste" that fiery, haughty, stinking quality. Thus it still goes for all haughty, stinking people.

O Human, let this be said to you, for the Spirit is earnestly jealous in this matter: leave off from pride, or it will go with you as it did with the devils. It is no joke; the time is very short; you will soon taste the hellish fire.

Now, just as the Holy Spirit approves all things, so also does the tongue; it approves every taste. And if it pleases the spirit, it brings it into the head before the other four Councils, before the Princely Throne. There it is approved to see if it is useful to the qualities of the body. And if it is good, it is brought into the Mother of the Heart, which gives it to all the veins or powers of the body; then the mouth and hands take hold of it. But if it is not good, the tongue spews it out before it even reaches the Princely Council. However, if it happens that it pleases the tongue and tastes well, yet does not serve the whole body, it is still rejected when it comes before the Council, and the tongue must spew it out and touch it no more.

<column-break/>

The **fifth Princely Council** is **Feeling** <note>Touch or sensation</note>. This fifth Council also rises from all the powers of the body in the spirit up into the head. For just as all powers proceed from GOD the Father and the Son into the Holy Spirit, and one "stirs" <note>original: "rüget," an archaic term meaning to touch, affect, or set in motion</note> the other, from which the "Sound" or Mercury arises, so that all powers ring out and move. Otherwise, if one did not stir the other, nothing would move. This stirring makes the Holy Spirit mobile, so that He rises up in all powers and stirs all the powers of the Father. Within this, the heavenly realm of joy or "triumphing" arises—as well as sounding, ringing, birthing, blooming, and growing. All of this has its rising from the fact that one power stirs another. For Christ says in the Gospel: *My Father worketh hitherto, and I work* <note>original: "Ich würcke/ und mein Vater würcket auch," John 5:17</note>. He means precisely this stirring or working: that all power proceeds from Him and gives birth to the Holy Spirit, and in the Holy Spirit all powers are already active from the proceeding of the Father. Therefore, the Holy Spirit surges and rises from eternity to eternity, and in turn ignites all the powers of the Father and makes them active, so that they are always "pregnant."

Even such a form does it have in angels and humans; for all powers in the body rise up, and one stirs the other; otherwise, the angel and human would feel nothing.

He sits in the head, in the brain of the human (and in the angel, in the power that takes the place of the brain), upon his Princely Throne, and he executes that which has been decided by the entire Princely Council.

30. Question: How can the angels speak?

Answer: Just as GOD speaks His almighty Word, so too do the angels speak as creatures. The entire Divine power of the Father speaks out—from all the qualities—the Word, which is the Son of GOD. Now, that same sound or Word which the Father speaks goes out from the Father’s **Salniter** <term>Salniter: the "divine saltpeter," representing the crackling, creative energy of God's nature</term> or powers, and from the Father’s **Mercury** <term>Mercurio: the force of movement, sound, and manifestation</term>, his resonance or tone. The Father speaks this out within Himself, and that Word is indeed the luster <note>original: "Glanz," or radiance</note> from all His powers. When it has been spoken, it no longer sticks within the Father’s powers, but rather it sounds and echoes throughout the entire Father, back into all the powers.

Now, this same Word that the Father speaks has such a "sharpness" <note>original: "Schärffe," meaning intensity or penetrating power</note> that the tone of the Word passes instantly through the entire depth of the Father, and this sharpness is the **Holy Spirit**. For the Word that is spoken remains as a luster or a magnificent mandate <term>Mandat: an official decree or command</term> before the King; but the sound that goes out through the Word carries out the Father’s mandate which He spoke through the Word. This is the birth of the **Holy Trinity**.

Now see: an angel and a human are also like this. The power in the whole body has all the qualities, just as they are in GOD the Father.

## Part 2 / Chapter 9.

Now, just as in GOD the Father all powers rise up from eternity to eternity, so too do all powers in the angel and the human rise up into the head; for they can rise no higher, since the being is only a creature that has a beginning and an end. And in the head is the **Divine Seat of Counsel**, and it signifies GOD the Father; and the five senses or **qualities** <note>original: "Qualitäten," referring to the essential properties or "source-springs" of a being</note> are the advisors. These receive their influences from the whole body and from all its powers. Now the five senses constantly hold counsel in the power of the whole body; and when the counsel is concluded, the unified judge speaks it out into his **center** <note>original: "Centrum"</note>, or into the middle of the body as a word—into the heart—for that is the source-fountain of all powers, from which it also takes its rising.

Now, there it stands in the heart as a self-sustaining person gathered from all powers, and it is a **Word**, and that signifies GOD the Son. Now it goes out from the heart into the mouth upon the tongue; the tongue is the sharpness and it sharpens the word so that it sounds, and it distinguishes it according to the five senses. From whichever quality the word takes its origin, it is pushed forth from the tongue in that same quality, and the power of distinction goes out from the tongue; and that signifies the **Holy Spirit**.

For just as the Holy Spirit goes forth from the Father and the Son, and distinguishes and sharpens everything, and carries out that which the Father speaks through the Word—so also the tongue sharpens and distinguishes that which the five senses in the head bring through the heart onto the tongue. And the spirit travels from the tongue through the **Mercury** <term>Mercurium: in this context, the principle of sound, vibration, and mechanical motion</term> or sound to the place determined by the counsel of the five senses, and carries it out.

31. Question: Shall the holy angels then also eat, and what is actually their food?

Answer: Their food is an attractive, grasping desire, from which their central fire receives **balm**,

<column-break/>

so that the hunger is satisfied in the food and does not wake up.

The mouth signifies that you are a non-almighty son of your Father, whether you are an angel or a human; for through the mouth you must grasp your Father's power into yourself if you wish to live. An angel must do this just as much as a human; and although he does not require the element of air in the same way a human does, he must nevertheless grasp the spirit into himself through the mouth, from which the air in this world originates. For in heaven there is no such air; rather, the qualities are entirely gentle and full of joy, like a lovely rustling, and the Holy Spirit is among all qualities in the **Salitter** <term>Salitter: a term used by the author to describe the divine, crystalline "earth-substance" or "salt of the spirit" that makes up the heavenly realm</term> and the Mercury. And an angel must also make use of this, otherwise he cannot be a moving creature; for he must also eat of the heavenly fruits through the mouth. You must not understand this in an earthly way, however; for an angel has no intestines, nor does he have flesh or bone, but he is joined together from Divine Power in a form and manner like a human, also with all limbs like a human. But the reproductive organs, as well as an exit from below, he does not have; nor does he need them.

For man only received his reproductive organs, and also his exit, in the miserable **Fall** <note>Referring to the biblical Fall of Man, which the author believes physically altered human anatomy</note>. An angel drives nothing away from himself except the Divine Power which he grasps with his mouth, with which he kindles his heart; and the heart kindles all the limbs. This same power he drives from himself again through the mouth when he speaks and praises GOD. But the heavenly fruits that he eats are not earthly; and though they are in form and shape like the earthly ones, they are nonetheless only Divine Power, and thus have such a lovely taste and scent that I can compare it to nothing in this world, for they taste and smell of the **Holy Trinity**.

# On the Revelation of GOD in the Light-World.

You should not think that these things are merely a symbol or a shadow: No, the Spirit shows brightly and clearly that in the heavenly splendor, within the heavenly **Salitter** <note>original: "Salniter." A term Böhme uses to describe the "divine earth" or the fundamental spiritual substance from which all things are formed.</note> and **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurio." In Böhme’s thought, this refers to the dynamic, moving spirit or the "voice" that gives form to the divine substance.</note>, there grow divine trees, shrubs, flowers, and many other things of which the things in this world are but a shadow. Just as the angels are real beings, so too are the plants and the fruits—all of them arising from Divine Power.

You must not compare the plants of heaven to those of this world at all; for in this world there are two **qualities** <note>the essential "source-springs" or properties of a thing</note>, one evil and one good, and much grows through the power of the evil quality—this does not grow in heaven. For heaven has only one form; nothing grows there that is not good. It was Lord Lucifer alone who made this world as it is. That is why Mother Eve was ashamed when she had eaten of that which was prepared by the evil quality; likewise, she was ashamed of her reproductive organs, which had been altered by that "apple-bite" <note>a reference to the Fall of Man in the Garden of Eden</note>.

Now, the angelic and heavenly fruit is not of such a substance; there are indeed certainly and truly all kinds of fruits in heaven, and not just symbols. The angels take them with their hands and eat them, just as we humans do, but they have no need for teeth, nor do they have any, for the fruit is of Divine Power.

Now, all of this—whatever an angel uses that is outside of himself for the building up of his life—is not his physical property by "natural right," but the heavenly Father gives it all to him out of love. Their **body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note> is indeed their own property, for GOD gave it to them as a possession; and whatever is given to someone as their own or as a possession belongs to them by natural right, and he who takes it back without a legal cause does not act rightly. GOD does not do this; therefore, an angel is an eternal, imperishable **creature** who exists for all eternity. But now, what use would the body be to him if GOD did not feed it? He would have no movement and would lie there like dead wood. Therefore, the angels are obedient to GOD and humble themselves before the mighty GOD, praising, honoring, glorifying, and exalting Him in His great wonders, and constantly singing of GOD’S holiness because He feeds them.

<column-break/>

->Aurora chapter 6. paragraphs 10, 19.<-

### 32. Question: How can fruits and food grow in heaven?

**Answer:** In the depth of the Father—which is the active Will of GOD according to the property of fire—there is something like a Divine **Salitter**, which I must of necessity compare to the earth. Before its corruption, the earth was such a Salitter, but not so hard, cold, bitter, sour, and dark; rather, it was like the depth or like heaven, entirely bright and pure, wherein all powers were good, beautiful, and heavenly. But Prince Lucifer corrupted it, as will be explained hereafter.

This heavenly Salitter—or the powers interacting within one another—gives birth to heavenly, joy-filled fruits and colors, all kinds of trees and shrubs, upon which grow the beautiful and lovely fruit of life: Also, in these powers, all kinds of flowers spring up with beautiful heavenly colors and scents. Their taste is varied, each according to its quality and kind, entirely holy, divine, and full of joy; for every quality bears its own fruit. Just as in this corrupted **murder-pit** <note>original: "Mord-Gruben," a term Böhme uses to describe the post-Fall world filled with strife and death</note> or dark valley of the earth there spring up all kinds of trees, shrubs, flowers, and fruits—as well as beautiful stones, silver, and gold within the earth—this is a shadow or pattern of the heavenly birth. Nature works with the greatest diligence upon the corrupted and dead earth so that she might give birth to a heavenly form and kind, but she gives birth to dead, dark, and hard fruits, which are no more than a shadow of the heavenly ones. Furthermore, they are entirely fierce, bitter, sour, harsh, hot, cold, hard, and evil, and there is hardly a good spark within them. Their juice and spirit are mixed with the hellish...

When I now write of trees, shrubs, and fruits, you must not understand it in an earthly way, as if belonging to this world, for that is not my meaning: that a dead, hard, wooden tree or stone exists in heaven within an earthly quality. No, rather my meaning is heavenly and spiritual, yet truly and literally so; I mean no other thing than what I set down in the letters.

In the **Divine Splendor** <note>original: "Göttlichen Pomp." Refers to the majestic manifestation or "procession" of God's glory in the spiritual realm.</note>, two things are primarily to be considered: first, the **Salitter** <note>original: "Salitter" or "Salniter." A term Böhme uses for the divine "soil" or the fundamental spiritual substance—the "salt" of the heavenly earth.</note> or the Divine Powers. These are a moving, surging power; in this same power, fruit grows and is born according to every quality and kind, such as heavenly trees and shrubs, which bear their fruit without ceasing, blooming beautifully and growing in Divine Power. This is so full of joy that I cannot speak or write of it; rather, I can only stammer about it like a child learning to speak, who cannot rightly name anything as the Spirit gives it to be known.

The other form of heaven in the **Divine Splendor** is **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurius." For Böhme, this represents the active, sounding, and communicative spirit that gives voice and movement to the divine substance.</note> or the **Sound**. Just as there is resonance within the Salitter of the earth—from which grow gold, silver, copper, iron, and the like, from which one can make all kinds of instruments for sound or for joy, such as bells, pipes, and everything that rings—so too is this same sound present in all **creatures** <note>original: "Creaturen." All created beings, whether spiritual or physical.</note> on earth; otherwise, everything would be silent.

Now, through this same Sound in heaven, all powers are proven, so that everything grows full of joy and brings itself forth quite elegantly. Just as the Divine Powers are many and varied, so also is the Sound or Mercury many and varied. When the powers rise up in GOD, one stirs the other and they surge into one another, in a constant mixing. Then, all kinds of colors emerge within them, and in those colors, all kinds of fruit grow; this rises up in the Salitter. And the Mercury or Sound also mingles and rises up in all the powers of the Father; then, tunes and sounds arise in the heavenly realm of joy. If you were to bring together many thousands of kinds of instruments and stringed music in this world, and tuned them all together in the most artistic way, and had the most skillful masters to play them, it would still be like a dog’s barking compared to the **Divine Sound and Music** <note>original: "Göttlichen Schall und Musica."</note> that rises from the Divine Sound from eternity to eternity.

<column-break/>

If you now wish to contemplate the heavenly **Divine Splendor** and glory—what it is like, what kind of vegetation, pleasure, or joy is there—then look with diligence upon this world: what kind of fruits and vegetation grow from the Salitter of the earth, from trees, shrubs, herbs, roots, flowers, oils, wine, grain, and everything that is there and that your heart can only search out. All of this is a prefigurement of the Divine Splendor. For earthly and corrupted nature, from the beginning of its creation until today, has always labored to bring forth the heavenly form, both in the earth and in humans and animals. One can see this quite well in how new arts emerge every year; this has lasted from the beginning until now. But nature has not been able to bring forth Divine power and **quality** <note>original: "Qualität." The essential source-property or "spring-power" of a thing.</note>; therefore, its fruit is half dead, corrupted, and impure.

You must not think that in the Divine Splendor animals, worms, or creatures of the flesh come forth as in this world. No, rather I mean only the wonderful **proportion** <note>original: "Proportz."</note>, power, and skill within them. Nature works with the highest diligence so that it might bring forth heavenly figures or forms in its power, as one then sees in humans, animals, birds, and worms, as well as in the plants of the earth—everything brings itself forth in the most artistic way—for nature would gladly be free from vanity.

# Of the Revelation of GOD in the Light-World.
Ee 2

The angels are purely formed powers of the Word of GOD: For the mind <term>Gemüthe: A central term in Böhme's thought, referring to the deep-seated disposition, soul, or "mind-complex" of a being.</term> of man is a counter-image of the eternal power of GOD. For all senses come from the mind, and from the senses come right thoughts, as a conclusion or imagination, from which the pleasure <note>original: "Lust" – in this context, it refers to a holy inclination or "delight" that moves toward manifestation.</note> arises; this pleasure enters into a substance, from which comes the sensible desire, and from that, the work arises. In the same way, GOD is the eternal mind, as the understanding; yet there would be no distinction within Him if He did not flow out from Himself. His outflowing consists of the powers—just like the senses in man—and these powers lead themselves into an imagination, wherein stands the angelic idea. This imagination leads itself into pleasure toward sensibility—that is **JAH** <note>The first half of the name of God (Yahweh), representing the divine "Yes" or affirmative light.</note>—and the pleasure leads itself into desire—that is the ground of one’s own delight, as the **No**—and the desire leads itself into properties, even unto the fire, from which the light springs. Thus, these same properties of desire are Divine thoughts, to be understood in two centers: as in **Yes** and **No**. The **JAH** is Divine, and the **No** is the selfhood of nature, as the sensibility of desire. This desire of sensibility has become a work, namely the angels; they are nothing else but the thoughts of GOD, according to love and wrath, acting as a revelation of His mind and will.

It is not that there are separate "thoughts" within GOD Himself, but rather in His flowed-out, desiring will, which introduces itself into fire and light for the sake of sensibility.

And just as a human being rules the world and all creatures with their thoughts, so GOD, as the eternal unity, rules all things through the works of the angels. Yet the power and the working belong to GOD alone; they are His instruments <note>original: "Werck-Zeuge" – literally "work-tools."</note> with which He delights and moves Himself, through which and with which He reveals the eternal powers and wonders, and leads them into a play of love. They are all together but strings in the great harmony of the Divine kingdom of joy, in the song and sound

<column-break/>

of the powers; and they are all together workers of the wonders of GOD, as the formers of the powers, of the Holy Names of GOD.

Just as we humans form the powers of the senses <note>original: "Sensuum"</note> in our mouths and make them formal, into audible words; so too is their work a pure formation of Divine powers and forms. For what they will and desire is brought into shape and form through their imagining; these are pure ideas, modeled after the way the Divine powers formed themselves into such ideas before the creation of the angels. And herein stands the holy Kabbalah <term>Cabala: Böhme refers here to the mystical tradition of understanding the hidden structures of creation through divine names and emanations.</term> of changes, and the great kingdom of joy, wherein the Divine wisdom and knowledge is built and formed through the spirits of the central fire and light. There is such a joy of recognition within it that, out of great joy and knowledge, they eternally bow and humble themselves before such majesty, so that the **No** <note>the spirit of self-centered negation or pride</note> does not gain the rule within them, and they are not robbed of such honor and glory.

->Theosophical Question 6. I. 11.<-

This is herewith the thorough opening of the great mystery of the revelation of the triune GOD in the Holy Angels. Whoever is reborn and renewed in the spirit to a new life will livingly recognize what it is when the almighty Father finds His all-sufficient pleasure—His beloved Son—within a creature. And on the contrary, what a terrible darkness, wrath, anguish, and torment arises in the creature where the Father seeks and demands His beloved Son but does not find Him, finding instead a monster, a dragon, a wolf, a dog, or the like. How this world and its inhabitants must have been a glorious kingdom of joy before the fall of Lucifer and man, when the Father recognized and perceived His sole pleasure and delight in all the angels. But oh, you noble guest, why have you departed from us? O grimness and glory, you are the cause: Alas, you poor blinded human! Why do you let the devil make your body and soul so dark and blind? O temporal goods and lust of this life, you blind whore, why do you dally with the hellish devil?

# The X. Chapter.

### Concerning the Revelation of GOD according to the First Principle, in which GOD is revealed as an angry, jealous GOD, as a consuming fire, and an eternal glow; concerning the Fall of Lucifer and his angels, their rejection, way of life, and activity in the abyss of Hell. The terrifying dark gate.

### Connection.

After we have considered in the preceding chapters how the triune GOD has revealed Himself in His eternally-speaking Word through the creation and animation of the Holy Angels, as light, love, life, joy, and eternal contentment—which life of love we call the Second Principle <note>The "Second Principle" in Böhmean theology refers to the realm of Light and Divine Love, distinct from the "First Principle" of raw, fiery power.</note>, in which GOD is holy among the holy, and among the pious is recognized as pious, gracious, kind, merciful, friendly, and as the highest Good. Now it follows to investigate how the triune GOD, who in Himself is nothing other than love, is revealed as an angry, jealous GOD, and as a consuming fire; there we shall see how the Holy GOD appears perverse to the perverse, and to the disobedient shows Himself as a terrifying, stern, just GOD, an eternal darkness, a consuming fire, and fierce glow.

->**1. Question.**<-
**Was GOD then not manifest according to the First Principle before the beginning of the creation of the angels?**

->**Answer.**<-

GOD is and remains one and the very same triune GOD, before, after, and in the fall of the Holy Angels, highly praised in eternity. But just as the night is not manifest in the day, nor the fire in the light, so also was He not manifest to the creature in the beginning as an angry GOD. For the fiery world stood as if swallowed up and hidden within the Light of GOD, in which the light of the Majesty alone ruled in itself. And yet we must not think that the fiery world did not exist; it did exist, but it was separated into its own principle and was not manifest in the Light of GOD’s Majesty, just as we can perceive this in fire and light: that the fire is indeed a cause of the light, and yet the light dwells in the fire, ungrasped by the fire, and carries a different quality <note>original: "Quall" — a technical term for Böhme, combining the meanings of "quality," "source," and "torment" or pulsing energy.</note> than the fire; for the fire is fierceness and consuming, and the light is gentleness, and from its power comes essentiality <note>original: "Wesenheit" — refers to the spiritual substance or "body" that emerges from the light.</note>, like water or

<column-break/>

Sulphur <note>original: "Sulphur" — used here not as the chemical element, but as an alchemical term for the "soul" or the flammable, desiring principle of a thing.</note> of a thing, which the fire draws into itself and uses for its strength and life, and is thus an eternal bond.

This fire and Divine Light indeed stood still in themselves from eternity, where each stood in its order in its own principle, and has neither ground nor beginning; for the fire has within itself its own form for its pulsing quality, such as the Desire, from which and in which all forms of nature are born, where each is a cause of the other, as has been reported in detail in the other writings. And we find in the Light of Nature <note>The "Light of Nature" refers to the innate capacity of the human mind to understand spiritual truths through the observation of the physical world.</note> how the fire in its own essence was like a harsh, desiring quality, a darkness in itself, which stood as if swallowed up in the Gentleness of GOD, where it was not qualitative but essential within itself, not ignitable; and though it burned, it was only perceptible within itself as its own principle. For from eternity there were only two principles: one in itself, the fiery world, and the other also in itself, the light-flaming world, though they

### 2. Question. How then has GOD become manifest as an angry, jealous GOD?

**Answer.** This revelation was caused by the Holy Angels, who turned away from the gentleness of GOD, alienated themselves from the life that is from GOD, and entered into an enmity against GOD. To recognize this thoroughly, we have to investigate: 1. Who the Holy Angels are who fell. 2. What caused them to fall away. 3. The fall itself with its circumstances. 4. What followed upon the fall.

### 3. Question. Which then are the angels who fell?

**Answer.** It is Lucifer with his whole hierarchy, according to which GOD transfigured and revealed Himself in the property of His Son. For Lucifer was born out before all angels, from the desire of GOD, according to the property of the Light-World: the triune GOD, forming and beholding Himself in the Mirror of Wisdom, recognized in this one [Lucifer] above others the image of His eternal Godhead: the Father had an earnest will to eternally and forever beget His indwelling Son in him, and the Son had an earnest will to fulfill the longing will of GOD the Father in this angel with eternal delight; so also the Holy Spirit was to go forth from the ignition of the Light and the gentle Love-source of the Father in the Son, like a lovely scent from a flower, which proclaims all the virtue of the flower and affects the Spirit of GOD, as it also applies to all the spirits of the Holy Angels. Thus Lucifer, the Throne-Angel, had his whole kingdom, the whole triune Godhead working bodily within him, and indeed in the very same way, according to the image and likeness, as the Son of GOD is born and worked by the Father: GOD was active in him just as outside him; he had life within himself, and was allowed...
