# Of the Revelation of GOD according to the 1st Principle

...he could draw the same from no other being; he should only have let God work purely and clearly in him, and in no way misform himself: he had a free will, and such a qualification of his will, such a desire, such a movement, impulse, ignition of fire, flash, light, majesty, joy, and pleasure, just like the Son of God—except that the birthing of God in an angel is not so incomprehensible, divine, or imperceptible, but is somewhat sharper, coarser, and more graspable than it is outside the angel in God Himself and His Groundless Abyss <note>original: "Ungrund." A central Böhmean term referring to the absolute void or "nothingness" before creation from which God emerges.</note>. Therefore, the Source-Spirits <note>original: "Quell-Geister." These are the seven fundamental qualities or forces of nature in Böhme's system that "well up" or "source" all existence.</note> that are in an angel and give birth to light and understanding are so bound with God that they should not qualify <note>original: "qualificiren." This refers to the way a being's inner qualities interact and express themselves.</note> otherwise, or higher, or more harshly than God Himself; rather, there should be one single way, since they are only a piece of the whole and not the whole itself. For God created them out of Himself so that they should qualify in such a form and manner as God Himself.

But now the Source-Spirits in Lucifer did not do this; rather, because they saw that they sat in the highest primacy, they moved themselves so harshly that the spirit which they brought forth became entirely fiery and rose up in the source-fountain of the heart like a proud maiden.

If the Source-Spirits had qualified in a fine, lovely way—as they did before they became creatures, while they were still together in God before the Creation—then they would have also given birth to a lovely and gentle son within themselves, who would have been like the Son of God. Then the light in Lucifer and the Son of God would have been one thing, an in-qualifying <note>original: "Inqualirung." This describes the dynamic, interpenetrating influence of different divine qualities upon one another.</note> or an infusing, a lovely embracing, heartening, and wrestling.

For the great light, which is the Heart of God, would have played quite gently and lovelily with the little light in Lucifer as if with a young son; for the little son in Lucifer was meant to be the dear little brother of the Heart of God. For such a purpose God the Father created the angels: so that just as He is manifold in His qualities and incomprehensible in the changes of His love-play, so also—

<column-break/>

—should the little spirits or the little lights of the angels (which are like the Son of God) play quite gently before the Heart of God in the great light, so that the joy in the Heart of God might be increased here, and there might thus be a holy play within God.

The seven spirits of nature in the angel were meant to play and rise up quite lovelily in God their Father, just as they had done before their creaturely existence, and to rejoice in their newborn son whom they had birthed from themselves, who is the light and understanding of their body. And that same light was meant to rise up quite gently in the Heart of God and rejoice in the light of God, like a child with its mother; there was to be heart-felt loving and friendly kissing, a truly gentle and lovely taste. In this, the sound should rise up and ring out with singing and chiming, praising and jubilating, and all qualities therein should rejoice, each spirit performing its divine work, just like God the Father Himself. For the seven spirits had perfect knowledge of this, since they were in-qualified with God the Father so that they could see, feel, taste, smell, and hear everything that God their Father made.

Thus Lucifer became qualifying according to the spirit, but his body was born thus:

When the Godhead moved toward Creation and wished to form creatures in His body, He did not ignite the Source-Spirits—otherwise they would surely burn eternally—but rather He moved Himself quite gently in the harsh quality. This harsh quality contracted and dried the divine Salitter <note>original: "Salitter." A term unique to Böhme, referring to the divine substance or the "sap" of the heavenly kingdom from which all things are formed.</note> so that it became a body; and the entire divine power of all seven Source-Spirits of that place or space, as far as the angel encompassed, was captured in that body and became the property of the body, which cannot or shall not be destroyed again.

Just as one quality always birthed another, and yet none passed away (as it is in the whole of God); so too the entire Body birthed itself in the Trinity, just as the Godhead births itself in the Trinity outside of the Body.

However, I must report here that Lucifer the King was incorporated from his entire kingdom as the Heart of the entire place or space, as far as his whole angelic host was created, and as far as the circle extended within which he and his angels became creatures—a space which God, before the time of creation, had enclosed within Himself to be the realm of a kingdom. This circle encompasses the created heaven and this world, as well as the depths of the earth and the entire circumference.

According to these qualities, his Source-Princes were created, who are his Royal counselors, as well as all his angels. Yet you should know that every angel has all seven spirits within himself, but one among the seven is the Principal.

4. **Q.** How long did Lucifer stand in such glory before his fall?

**Ans.** At the same hour that the royal body of Lucifer was incorporated, the light was also kindled within Lucifer. For as soon as his <term>Source-Spirits: The seven fundamental qualities—such as desire, mobility, and perception—that "well up" to form all existence</term> began to <note>original: "qualificiren." There he was an exceedingly beautiful prince and king, and most dear and pleasant to the Divine Being, and was received with great joys. Likewise, the spirit also proceeded from the heart into all the source-veins of the body and kindled all seven spirits; then the royal body was instantly glorified and stood there as a King of God in unsearchable clarity, which surpassed the entire host of heaven.

Now, in this bright and light-filled flash, the seven Source-Spirits were immediately ignited, as one ignites a fire; for they were startled by the terrible clarity of their spirit and, in that first flash or sight, quickly became high-triumphing, elevated, proud, and far too rich in joy, and they moved toward a higher birth. Yet if they had remained sitting in their seat and had continued to operate as they had done from eternity, the high light would have done them no harm. For they were not new spirits made from something else, but were the ancient spirits that had no beginning, who had been eternal in God, and they well knew the law of the Deity and of Nature—how they ought to surge.

->Aurora, Chapter 14, verses 4, 7.<-

5. **Q.** But what caused Lucifer to thus elevate himself?

**Ans.** Self-complacency and self-love, through which he beheld himself in great glory. For the <term>Tincture: An alchemical and mystical term used by Böhme to describe the vitalizing spiritual essence or "soul-blood" of a being</term> of friendly delight shone out of all things, and the Heart of God shone before them; into this they were meant to imagine <note>To "imagine" in Böhme's sense is to direct one's will and desire toward a specific goal, thereby giving it form.</note> and draw their will and power in the <note>original: "Verbo Domini." Latin for "Word of the Lord."</note>. But because they saw that the Word of the Lord in the Center was like a different birth out of the Center, and they were born from the essences of the Great Source-Well (which is the nature of eternity), they despised the humility from which love and light are born, and they wanted to rule in the fierce power over humility in the <term>Fire-Torment: The harsh, consuming aspect of spiritual fire when it is separated from the cooling light of love</term>; for the Fire's <term>Matrix: The spiritual "womb" or underlying structure from which qualities are produced</term> wanted to have the government. For we can recognize it no other way than that Lucifer was created in the fourth form of the Matrix <note>The "fourth form" in Böhme's system is the "Flash" or "Fire-crack," the turning point where darkness can become either light or a consuming fire.</note>, for there wrath and love stand against one another, and there is the struggle for victory, where the light overcomes the darkness and holds it captive. Also, God’s wrath and the zeal of eternal nature wanted to become creaturely as well and show forth its wonders; therefore, they were held in the source-well of their own nature and have kindled the Matrix of wrath, envy, and fierceness. That is now their eternal delight.

The Tincture became false in their conceived will, in that they wanted to rule over the humility of the Heart of God out of fierce pride, and were therefore cast from the upper Center into the lower as a death, where there is only vain darkness, and they cannot reach the light of GOD. For to the light of GOD belongs a state of humility, in which the desire of love [exists]...

[which] is born, which grasps the Heart of God. And that is not Lucifer; rather, it is sheer wrath, envy, and pride—always wanting to fly out beyond the Heart of God and to rule with harsh power. 6. **Q.** *Did God then not allow Lucifer to fall by a predetermined plan, so that God might reveal His justice and manifest Himself as a wrathful, zealous God?*

**Ans.** Lucifer’s fall did not come from God’s intentional design. Everything that originates from the eternal Will—as it arises from the great eternal <term>Mystery: The "Mysterium Magnum," or the unmanifested source of all potential existence</term> (such as angels and the souls of men)—stands in an equal balance between evil and good, possessing free will, just as God Himself does. Whichever desire the creature allows to rise up into its <term>operation: The German "qualificiren" refers to how a thing acts or feels according to its inner qualities</term>, and which desire then surpasses the others, that quality becomes the creature’s essence. It is just as a candle produces a fire from itself, and from the fire a wind (or air), which the fire then draws back into itself and yet gives forth again: and when this spirit has proceeded from the fire and light, it is free from that fire and light. Whatever quality it then adopts, that is what it becomes.

The first Mystery in which the creature stands is the all-encompassing Mystery, but the second—found in the outgoing spirit—is the creature's own property and a will of its own. For every angel has its own spirit, which is born out of its own Mystery, having its origin in eternity. Why then does that same spirit become a tempter of God, and tempt the Mystery, which then catches him in the <term>Fierceness: The "Grimm," representing the harsh, consuming, and wrathful aspect of the first principle of nature</term>, as happened to Lucifer? He had the pull toward God’s wrath and God’s love within him; why then does the spirit (born from both), which is the likeness of the Spirit of God, not remain in its seat in

<column-break/>

obedience, like a child before its mother in humility? You might say: "He cannot." But that is no valid reason. Every spirit stands in the place where it was created, in equal weight, and has its free will. It is one spirit with the all-encompassing eternal Spirit; yet it may draw for itself a delight within that all-encompassing eternal Spirit however it wills—whether in God’s love or God’s wrath. Whatever it directs its desire into, it receives the essence and quality of that thing within the great Mystery of all beings. This "birth" is manifest in God as both love and wrath; why should it not also be so in the creature, who was created as an image out of God’s essence and will, and out of His voice and <term>Resonance: The original "Halle" suggests a sound or echo; Böhme views creation as the "sounding" of the Divine Word</term>? Whichever quality of that resonance the creature awakens within itself, that same quality echoes through and governs the creature.

God's will toward the creature was but one—a general revelation of the Spirit, just as each was grasped in the quality of the eternal Mystery. Thus, Lucifer was grasped in a good, angelic quality; this is proven enough by the fact that he was an angel in heaven. But his own incorporated will-spirit swung itself into the <term>Fierce Mother: The dark, fundamental root of nature from which the "light" is born; it is the source of strength but also of wrath</term>, seeking to awaken that quality within himself and thereby be a lord over all creatures. Now, the will-spirit is free; it is the eternal origin; it does what it will.

Because the will-spirit—which originates from both love and wrath, from both eternal principles—gave itself over to the Fierceness, the Fierceness swung itself upward and into the seat of government. It rose out of the equal harmony into a state of inequality; thus, he had to be driven into his own "likeness" <note>This refers to being cast into the darkness that matched his internal state.</note>, and that is his fall; such also is the fall of all wicked people.

<margin>The Signature of All Things 16. 30. 34.</margin>

**Ans.** When fire and light once separate, there is a great enmity between them, just like water and fire.

[...they] are enemies, and neither desires the other anymore, for one is the death of the other; but because they are together in a growing life, in one ground, they love one another and stand together in great joy. So it is also to be thought of the Devil and of GOD: GOD desires the Devil no more, and the Devil also desires GOD no more (understand this as the gentleness, humility, love, and grace of GOD). But as for the question of why GOD did not prevent this in the movement <note>referring to the "movement" or agitation of the eternal "will" that led to the creation and the fall</note>? We say: GOD had given him His love and warned him, just as He warned Adam; but the central eternal <term>Fire-will: The harsh, consuming aspect of the divine nature that provides the energy for life but becomes "wrath" when separated from the Light</term>, as the Wrath of GOD, did not want it; it separated itself into its own kind within them.

Here one must distinguish between GOD’s love and wrath. They are both called GOD, but GOD, insofar as He is the eternal Good, is not the wrath; the wrath has another <term>Principle: One of the three fundamental "worlds" or states of being in Böhme's philosophy—the dark fire-world, the light-world, and the external world</term>. They are indeed one in the fire of love, but in the separation they are two. And because they are both eternal without beginning, they also have an eternal will, wherein neither can kill the other; instead, each remains in itself eternally. It is only a twofold power, and there are two centers, yet they originate from unity, from one ground.

Therefore, when I speak of GOD’s love, it is almighty, over all and in all; this happens according to the will of the **Yes**, as the Light; and if the **No** gives its will to it, then the **Yes** transforms the **No** into its power and love, and yet two central wills remain in each other, but in one ground, in one love and desire. Otherwise the wrathful GOD would not be almighty if Love alone held Him in her omnipotence—and since there is but one GOD, yet love would not be manifest, and no love would be recognized without the wrath.

Therefore, Love yields itself to the Wrath-fire, so that it may be a Love-fire; but if Wrath separates itself from Love into its

<column-break/>

own self-interest <note>original: "Annehmlichkeit," referring to the ego's desire to please itself rather than remain in the divine flow</note>, Love does not prevent this with force, otherwise it would follow that GOD would become divided against Himself.

Thus the **No**, as GOD’s wrath, went into a separation from love in the fallen angels, as into its own kingdom; and this is also a wonder and moreover good, so that the other angels might have a mirror, and so that the self-will might not exalt itself; also that there might be an eternal joy and praise of GOD, so that they do not live in such a fire-essence, but rather turn their desire all the more into GOD’s unity and remain in <term>Resignation: "Gelassenheit," the spiritual practice of surrendering the self-will to God</term> and humility, as in Divine harmony.

Now, when one speaks here of the will of GOD’s wrath—that it has broken away from love and wished to be formative <note>original: "bildlich," meaning to take on a distinct, self-determined form or image</note>—one must not understand this as being outside the creature. It was not a foreign will that was not also formative within the fallen angels; rather, it was the wrathful GOD within the formed creature, which was previously formative; otherwise their entire place would have been an apostasy. But that it is not so is proven by the fact that they were cast out of their throne.

One must not blame GOD for the fault of the fall, but only the formed power in the creature according to the **No**; this power threw it away and became a lie—not GOD, but the creature; not the unformed power of wrath, in which love burns, but the throne, according to self-interest and selfhood; and as their king and prince did, so also did all his legions.

For when GOD’s wrath hardens a creature, no foreign fury enters into it to harden it; rather, its own fury does this. Therefore a judgment may pass over it. Otherwise, if GOD forced it toward evil, no judgment could pass over it, for it would only be doing what GOD wanted. But as it is, it does what GOD does *not* want from it; therefore it falls into judgment.

### 8. Question: What did the Devil desire that caused him to turn away from GOD’S love?

**Answer:** He desired to be an artist <note>The German "Künstler" here implies a "crafter" or "manipulator" who wants to shape reality according to his own will rather than following the divine pattern.</note>; he saw the creation and understood its foundation. Therein he wanted to be a god of his own, to rule over all things with the central fire-power, and to form himself with all things—even to form himself into whatever shapes he chose, so that he might be what *he* wanted, and not what the Creator wanted. Even today, this is the greatest joy of the devils: that they can transform themselves and take on many kinds of images, and thus indulge in fantasy <note>In Böhme’s thought, "Phantasie" refers to a delusive, self-created reality separated from the truth of God.</note>.

He wanted to be a fool, and he has indeed become one; but he did not know how that would turn out once the light was extinguished for him. Similarly, Adam did not know what it would be like when he would feel heat and cold, or when the central fire and its harsh qualities would awaken within him, causing him to fall from equality <note>equilibrium or harmony</note> and lose the central light-fire; Adam did not know this either.

The Devil wanted to be a lord in the "No" <note>The "No" represents the principle of self-will, contraction, and darkness, as opposed to the "Yes" of divine expansion and love.</note> and to possess a different principle <note>The "Principles" are Böhme's terms for the different realms of existence: the dark fire-world, the light-world, and the physical world.</note> than the power of separation found in the foundation of figurative formation. He was not pleased by submission, but by highness; he despised humility, sweetness, love, and truth. He did not want to exist in Unity, but in Multiplicity. He wanted to work through his own name—as if through the central fire-power—and not through the Name of GOD belonging to his throne. He placed the "No" over the "Yes" (or the

<column-break/>

outflow of GOD). Thus he became an enemy of God and a liar and murderer of good formation and good powers; he desired to destroy what God’s activity was building, so that he might present his own activity and formation. He was pleased by the magical foundation of omnipotence, and he exalted this within himself. He contradicted the "Yes" because, in his own center, it is not an active fire-working. He saw that the "Yes"—as the outflow of Unity in the fire-center—led into a light and into active love; he therefore thought the fire-nature was stronger and greater than the gentleness of Unity, or the formed Names in the opening Unity. He intended to lead these Names through his own fire-power however he pleased, but God did not create him for such a will. 

Therefore, because he left God’s order, the Holy opening Name of God separated from him and remained in the Unity. Lucifer remained in the qualities of the central fire, dwelling within himself. He still stood in his princely throne <note>Referring to his original station as a high prince of angels before his fall.</note>, wherein the Holy Name of God had formed itself into a throne; yet he was no longer an angel, but a mask-image and a monster. For when the light was extinguished for him, the darkness and the cold sharpness of wrath became manifest within him, and he was immediately an enemy of God and of all the heavenly hosts.

->Theosophical Question 9. 2. 10. Theosophical Question 10. §. 1. 7.<-

# On the Revelation of GOD according to the First Principle

The **Fiat** <note>original: *Fiat*; the Latin creative command "Let there be," which Böhme treats as a shaping force</note> has entered into movement and revelation; and the Angelic Princes, along with their legions, were also seized from the qualities within the **Word Fiat** <note>original: *Verbo Fiat*</note>, from the very first **Center** <note>original: *Centro*</note>—where delight captures itself into a desire and introduces itself into Nature—unto the most outward revelation, each hierarchy within its own heaven or quality.

Because Lucifer, in his creation or the shaping of his qualities, was seized within the **Flash** <note>original: *Bliß*; the sudden ignition of light and consciousness</note> where the ignitable fire originates and where the light becomes manifest, he arose within himself as the most powerful prince. In the root of his creaturely origin, where the great **magical constellation** <note>original: *magische Gestirn*; referring to a spiritual configuration of powers</note> stood as the **Mystery** <note>original: *Mysterium*</note> of the foundation of all beings—though in a dark quality—it had now become mobile and full of desire. This magical constellation in the dark world also wished to be manifest and creaturely, and so it directed its powerful desire toward its prince and hierarch. 

And he, Lucifer, turned away from the Divine Light and originated within the fiery Mystery against the fire of the darkness. Thus, the magical constellation of the great Mystery of the dark world seized him; for his desire—which the **Fiat** had led through the fire into the light—turned back, wanting to be equal to the Creator of all beings and to change himself and his essence according to his own pleasure. Thus he despised the **Gentleness** <note>original: *Sanfftmuth*; the characteristic of the Second Principle or the World of Light</note> in the light, which is the **Second Principle** <note>original: *Principium*</note>. This light is born through the "dying" of the fire—where the wrath or the spiritual essence of the fierce, dark quality dies in the fire, and out of that dying of consumability, the Second Principle is born as the Holy Love-World of great gentleness and humility. 

Instead, he went back into the **First Principle**, into the **Magic of Nature** <note>original: *Magiam Naturæ*</note>, in the origin of eternal nature, and wanted to be an "artist" <note>The term *Künstler* implies a manipulative crafter who shapes reality by his own will</note> and an all-knower; he wanted to rule in and over the entire creation and be a co-shaper in all qualities. Thus the light was extinguished for him, for he turned his angelic essence—which stood in great 

<column-break/>

gentleness and in fiery love-desire—into the dark, fierce quality, making it entirely rough, harsh, cold, and fiercely fiery. In that very hour, the qualities of enmity arose within him. In the light, these could not be manifest; but when the light was extinguished, they became manifest, and he became a **Devil**, and was cast out of his own heaven of the Second Principle, out of the angelic world. Thus we recognize that his fall arose from within his own creaturely self.

<margin>*Mysterium Magnum* 17. 23. 30.</margin>

10. **Question:** Where then did Lucifer fall?

**Answer:** When he voluntarily broke away from God’s Love-Will, he fell into God’s **Wrath-Will**, as if into a consuming fire and an eternal glow. Within this, he is a revealer and a worker of the quality of the dark world—which, without him, was not manifest, but through him became active as a quality in its own right. Thus he is a creaturely prince of the dark hells, a truly powerful and terrifying lord in the dark **Principle**. 

Because he despised God's light, heart, and gentleness, and rules in the fierce power of fire—and because he despised the source of gentleness in which he had become such a glorious angel—everything departed from him. He lost God and the Kingdom of Heaven, all Paradisiacal wit, delight, and joy; he also immediately lost the **Image of God** and the confirmation of the Holy Spirit, and remained in the dark valley of the **Four Anguishes** <note>The four foundational "qualities" of Böhme's dark nature: contraction (harshness), expansion (bitterness), rotation (anguish), and the fire-crack</note> of the eternal origin. Whenever he raised his **imagination**, he ignited within himself the source or the **Fire-root**. But when the Fire-root sought the "water" <note>Symbolizing the cooling, soothing element of the Light-world</note> as the true mother of eternal nature, it found only harsh astringency, and the Mother in the anguish of death; and the bitter sting shaped the birth into a fierce, raging serpent, rising up most terrifyingly within itself—an eternal enmity in an unbreakable bond, a counter-will within itself, an eternal...

12. **Question:** What did the second source-spirit <note>original: *Quell-Geist*; one of the seven foundational forces of Böhme’s cosmos</note> do in the bitter quality?

**Answer:** The second source-spirit was the gentle and lovely movement, stirring, and longing for freedom. For this bitter spirit arises in the flash <note>original: *Blitz*; the moment of transition from darkness to light</note>, and is the mobility or root of life that forms the Word within the harsh quality, so that a thought or will arises in the Body <note>original: *Corpus*</note>. This quality is normally a source of joy and the First Mover <note>original: *Primum Mobile*</note> for ascending into the Heart of GOD.

In just such a way was the bitter quality also within Lucifer, and it had no cause for its elevation, nor any drive from anything else; rather, it followed the arrogant pride of the harsh quality, as its father. It also presumed that it wanted to rule in its own kind over the whole Godhead, and so it ignited itself in its elevation.

As it now helped to give birth to the soulish <gloss>animal</gloss> spirit in the Body, that same spirit became, in this species, a fierce, stinging, raging, ignited, gall-bitter, and tearing spirit—a true quality of hellish fire, an entirely fierce and hostile being. Now, whenever this spirit within the soulish spirit speculated <note>original: *speculirete*; meaning to project one's will or focus intensely into something</note> from the heart of Lucifer and his legions into the Godhead, <insert>speculated—that is, led its will into it, as into the Mother who gives birth,</insert> it was nothing other than a tearing, breaking, stinging, murdering, and poisonous burning. Of this, Christ says: *The devil is a liar and a murderer from the beginning, and has never remained in the truth,* John 8:44.

<column-break/>

Lucifer, however, believed he would thereby be above GOD; he thought no one could rule and govern as terrifyingly as he, and that everything should bow before him. He wanted to rule with his spirit throughout the entire Godhead as a king, governing everything with violence. Because he was the most beautiful, he also wanted to be the most powerful. But he saw and well knew the gentle and humble being in GOD his Father; he also knew well that it had stood in such Divine gentleness from eternity, and that he too should give birth in such Divine gentleness as a dear and obedient son. However, because he was now formed so beautifully and gloriously, like a king in nature, his beautiful form pricked his pride. He thought: "I am now GOD, and formed out of GOD; who shall prevail over me, or who shall change me? I will be lord myself, and rule with my sharpness in all things, and my Body shall be the image that people shall honor. I will prepare a new kingdom for myself, for the entire territory is mine; I alone am GOD and no other." And in his pride, he struck himself with darkness and blindness, making himself into a devil, which he must be and remain eternally.

13. **Question:** How then did such a terrifying ignition happen within Lucifer?

**Answer:** Heat is born between the bitter and the harsh qualities, and is conceived in the sweet water; it is both shining and glowing, and is the true fountain-spring of life. Now, where there is water, there is no fierce fire, but rather a lovely warming and a gentle qualifying <note>original: *qualificiren*; Böhme’s term for how the fundamental forces or "qualities" interact and operate</note>; but when the water dries up, the fire becomes burning, fierce, and "qualifying." Thus, Lord Lucifer also thought he would ignite his fire so that he could rule with force in the Divine Power through zeal; but he thought it should burn and also shine eternally. He did not know that if he dried the water and ignited that same dry water, the kernel—that is, the oil or heart of the water—would consume itself, and darkness would come from the light, and a sour stench from the water. For the oil or the fat in the water is born through gentleness or well-doing, and it is that same fat in which the light becomes shining. But if

<column-break/>

the fat is burned, the water becomes a sour stench and, moreover, completely dark.

This is also what happened to Lucifer’s pride: he triumphed for a little while with his ignited light, but when his light burned out, he became a black devil. He intended, however, to rule eternally in the burning light within the entire Divine Power as a completely terrifying GOD, and so he wrestled with his fire-spirit against the Salitter <term>Salitter: The fundamental spiritual-material substance of the divine realm, which Böhme compares to saltpeter</term> of GOD, intending to ignite the entire region of his kingdom. And he certainly achieved something, in that he made the Divine Powers burning, which is still evidenced by the sun and stars; also, the fire in the Salitter often ignites within the elements so that one thinks the "depth" is burning, which I will deal with in its proper place.

Now, in this quality, King Lucifer truly prepared the hellish bath for himself. He cannot say that GOD built and prepared the hellish quality for him, but rather he did it himself. Furthermore, he offended the Divinity and made a hellish bath out of the powers of GOD as his eternal dwelling.

For when he and all his angels ignited the source-spirit of fire within their bodies, the fat in the sweet water burned, and from the flash or the "terror-crack" <note>original: *Schracke*; the sudden, explosive transition in the birth of light</note>—which rises up fiercely in the birth of light—came a sour stench.

### 2. Part / Chapter 10.

Fire ignited instantly in the body <note>original: *Corpus*</note> and extinguished the lovely light within the animal spirit <term>animal spirit: Böhme’s term for the living, sensing breath of life—derived from the Latin *anima*—that animates a creature's form.</term>, and it became a fierce, devilish spirit, all according to the ignition and the will of the source-spirits <term>source-spirits: The seven fundamental properties of divine nature that Böhme believes work together to manifest all of existence.</term>. Now, this animal spirit was connected to the Godhead within nature and could interact <note>original: *inqualiren*; Böhme uses this to describe how different qualities or spirits influence and merge with one another.</note> with it as if they were one thing. This spirit then struck out from the bodies of the devils into the nature of God like a murderer and a thief, who desired to murder and rob everything and bring it under his power; he ignited all seven spirits in nature, and there was nothing but a harsh, bitter, fiery, and crashing, burning tearing and raging.

You should not think that the devil overcame the Godhead with such power. No; rather, he ignited the Wrath of God <note>In Böhme’s theology, the "Wrath" is a hidden, dark potential within God’s nature that only becomes a manifest, burning fire when it is provoked by pride or rebellion.</note>, which would have rested in secret for all eternity, and he made a murder-pit out of the Salitter <term>Salitter: The fundamental "divine saltpetre" or the holy, crystalline substance of the heavenly realm.</term> of God. For when one puts fire into straw, it burns. God did not become a devil because of this. Furthermore, the fire of God's wrath in nature does not reach the innermost core of the Heart, which is the Son of God—much less does it reach the hidden holiness of the Spirit. Instead, it reaches into the birth of the six source-spirits in the place <note>original: *Locum*</note> where the seventh is born. For in that place, or in that birth, Lord Lucifer became a creature, and his dominion reached no deeper. Had he remained in love, however, his animal spirit would have reached into the Center <note>original: *Centrum*</note> of the Heart of God, for love penetrates through the entire Godhead.

But when his love was extinguished, the animal spirit could no longer enter the Heart of God, and his undertaking was in vain. Instead, he raged and fumed in nature—that is, in the seventh source-spirit of God. But because the power of all seven spirits resided in this one, all seven were also infected by wrath, though only in their external and perceptible interaction <note>original: *Qualificirung*</note>. For the devil could not touch the Heart, nor could

<column-break/>

he touch the innermost birth of the source-spirits; for the glory of his seven spirits had already died in the first flash of the ignition and was immediately held captive in the first output of the animal spirit.

In this hour, King Lucifer prepared hell and eternal destruction for himself; it now exists in the outermost source-spirit of God’s nature, or in the outermost birth of this world. When nature ignited so terrifyingly, the house of joys became a house of misery; for the harsh quality was ignited in its own house, and it was now a completely hard, cold, and dark being, like the cold and hard winter. This contracted the Salitter and dried it out so that it became entirely rough, cold, and sharp, like stones. The heat was trapped within this and contracted along with it, being formed into a hard, cold, and dark substance.

When this happened, the light in nature was also extinguished in the outermost birth, and everything became completely dark and corrupted. The water became entirely cold and thick, and gathered in the crevices; there is the origin of the elementary water on earth.

For before the time of this world, the water was entirely thin, like the air; moreover, life was born within it—the life that is now so deadly and corrupted, and which thus tosses and flows.

Out of the lovely love that rose up in the flash of life, there came a fierce and bitter poison, a true murder-pit, a sting of death. Out of the tone <note>original: *Thon*; Böhme associates the sixth spirit with sound and speech. Here, he suggests that the harmony of heaven hardened into the clashing sounds of the material world.</note> came a hard pounding of stones, a house of misery.

In summary, everything was a completely dark and miserable being in the entire region, in the outermost birth of Lucifer’s kingdom.

Ques.** We have seen from where, to where, and in what manner Lucifer, the king in the second hierarchy <term>hierarchy: In Böhme’s cosmos, angels are organized into three great "kingdoms" or hierarchies, each corresponding to a person of the Trinity; Lucifer was the head of the hierarchy associated with the Son.</term>, fell; now we must also investigate how, through him, so many thousand times thousand angels were brought to such a terrible fall?

**Ans.** As the lord commanded, so also did his subjects. When he rose up and wanted to be God, his angels saw this too and all did as their lord, as if they wanted to storm the Godhead; for they were all subject to him, and he ruled in all his angels, for he was created out of the core of the Salitter <term>Salitter: A term Böhme uses for the "divine saltpetre," the holy, crystalline substance or "soil" of the heavenly realm from which all things are formed.</term> from which all his angels were created. He was the lord of all his angels; therefore, they all did as he did. They all wanted to sit in the primacy <note>original: *Primat*; meaning the highest or first rank of power</note> of the Godhead and, with their lord, rule powerfully in the whole region <note>original: *Revier*</note> over the entire Divine Power. They were all of one will, and they would not let that will be taken from them.

<margin>Aurora 14, § 33. 34.</margin>
Lucifer, as the Throne- and Prince-Angel, was a great wellspring, like the sun compared to the stars. From this wellspring, all his angels went forth in many thousand times thousand; for the Spirit beheld itself in the *Fiat* <term>Fiat: Latin for "let it be"; the creative command of God that condenses spiritual will into substantial form.</term>, according to the manner of the Eternal Wisdom. Just as many thoughts come from one single thought, so the essences <note>original: *Essentien*</note> went forth from the Prince-Angel and his qualifying <note>original: *Qualificirung*; refers to the way different qualities of spirit work together and influence one another</note>, and the Spirit created them with the *Fiat*, and that remained as something substantial. Therefore, every host that had gone forth from a wellspring gained a will in the wellspring that was their prince—just as the stars give a will into the power of the sun, and the sun rules in them all, and they also have their beginning in this way. They are all like the branches on a tree. As the trunk has a drive and sap, so also do the branches. If the trunk has a monstrous image, then the branches also have a deformity, all according to the property of each; for their properties are entirely different, all according to the foundation of the hellish essence, and they have their princely government among themselves, all according to the

**20. Ques.** How many kinds of devils are there then?

**Ans.** There are many kinds, for when these evildoers turned their will away from gentleness and placed it into the fire, the fire rose up, and all six source-spirits <term>source-spirits: The "Quell-Geister" are the seven foundational properties (such as sourness, bitterness, heat, and sound) that Böhme believes constitute both God's nature and the created world.</term> left the state of balance <note>original: *Temperatur*; the harmonious mixing of all qualities</note>. Each source-spirit sought primacy in the ignition, and whichever one gained the upper hand, that one formed the body <note>original: *Corpus*</note> of malice. It is not as if there is one who is not full of all the other malices, for just as no source-spirit can be born without the others, so also can no malice exist without the remaining types of malice; only in one, this property predominates, and in another, a different one.

According to the first property—the harsh, strictly-attracting fire-desire—the greed-devils are generated, who have an insatiable hunger to devour everything alone.

According to the second property—the violent fiery driving and rising—are the pride-devils, the winged, fierce spirits like flying dragons.

According to the third property are the envy-devils, who strictly constrict the harsh fire-desire within themselves and enclose the "mercury" <term>mercury: In Böhmean alchemy, "mercury" represents the bitter, mobile, and agonizing quality of life that seeks to manifest itself.</term> or bitter property so tightly that it twists in the Wheel of Anguish <term>Wheel of Anguish: The "Angst-Rad"; a state where the spiritual forces spin in a circle of inner torment because they cannot break through into the light.</term> and thus becomes fierce, poisonous, envious, hostile, and prickly: like gnawing worms, snakes, and toads.

According to the fourth property, the wrath-devils are born; for the harsh quality in them is like a burning mirror <note>original: *Brenn-Spiegel*</note> that concentrates the sun’s rays and sets everything on fire in an instant. Thus they constrict the life-spirits and essences together so that they ignite like a flash of lightning and immediately inflame everything they seize. This kind are the wrath-devils, and Lucifer’s personal bodyguard <note>original: *Leib-Regiment*</note>, the hellish dragons. Here also are generated the cunning lying-spirits; for when wrath cannot break out like a flash because of the strict power of the fire, the life-spirit twists itself, and the flash becomes poisonous, squinting, and crooked, seeking a thousand deceits.

According to the fifth property of dark magic, there are the impure lustful-devils <note>original: *Huren-Teufel*; literally "whore-devils," implying spiritual and carnal lechery</note>, who burn in impure desire and, in their imagination, the abominable—

21. **Ques.** Since the devils are of such different kinds, the question arises: Are they also at odds with one another?

**Ans.** In their "Head" <note>meaning their leadership or central source</note>, they all share one will, which is an absolute enmity against GOD in many forms. In this, no one hinders the other from eternally hating and cursing GOD, nor from mocking His gentleness, humility, and love. Just as each **Source-Spirit** sharpens and gives birth to the other, so too do the devils sharpen one another: the devils of greed sharpen the devils of pride; these sharpen the devils of envy; the envious sharpen the devils of wrath; and from these come the unclean devils of lust, lying, <term>etc.</term> Therefore Christ says that the kingdom of darkness is not divided against itself.

22. **Ques.** Did **Lucifer** then bring down no more than his own <term>hierarchy: One of the three great angelic kingdoms in Böhme's cosmology</term> to such a wretched fall?

**Ans.** He did indeed try with all his power and cunning to infect the other hierarchies; however, because they were separate wellsprings and had their own branches on a trunk that depended directly upon the Word of Life, he found no entrance there, not even the slightest. For they set their imagination and their will with all earnestness away from the dark power of fire—that is, from the wrath—and bowed themselves into humility and gentleness. The more Lucifer sought to ignite himself, the more they sank away from all fiery power; the more they sank, the more the little fountain of light opened, with which they could extinguish all the fiery arrows of the wicked one. And so there was a mighty struggle between them both, of which we read in the <term>Apocalypse, chapter 12: The Book of Revelation</term>.

# On the Revelation of GOD according to the First Principle

...or the most external birth in man / which is the fleshly birth / and which man built and fashioned for himself through the first <term>Fall of Desire: The initial turning of the human will away from God toward self-interest and earthly longing</term> / is the devil’s fortress of plunder and dwelling-place / where the devil, as if in a fortress, battles with the soul / and gives it many a hard blow to the head.

This birth of the flesh is not the soul's true dwelling-place / rather, she enters into it with her light in Divine power while in conflict / and they fight against the devil's murderous intent. In response, the devil shoots his poison at the <term>seven source-spirits: The seven foundational qualities or forces of nature that give birth to all life</term> / which give birth to the soul / intending to corrupt and ignite them / so that he may take the entire body as his own property.

Now, if the soul is to bring her light and knowledge into the human mind / she must fight and struggle very hard / and has a very narrow path to travel through; she is often struck to the ground by the devil / but she must stand like a <term>Knight: A spiritual warrior or champion</term> in the heat of battle. If she then triumphs / she has overcome the devil / but if the devil triumphs / the soul is taken captive.

But because the fleshly birth is not the soul's own house / and she cannot possess it as an inheritance / as the devil can / the struggle lasts as long as the house of flesh lasts: But when the house of flesh is destroyed / and the soul is still free, unconquered and uncaptured in her own house / then the struggle has an end / and the devil must yield eternally from this spirit.

Therefore, this is a very difficult point to understand / and can not be understood at all / except through this very struggle; even if I were to write many books about it / you would still understand nothing / unless your spirit stands in such a birth / and that knowledge is born within yourself / otherwise you can neither grasp nor believe it. ->25. Question: Why then is Lucifer called the Dragon?<-

Answer: A Dragon is a terrifying, fire-spewing, flying worm—a hideous monster—to indicate his poisonous, fierce fire-power, his soaring pride, and his terrifying distortion, through which he so shamefully corrupted the image of God within himself and made it monstrous.

->26. Question: Why is he called the Old Serpent?<-

Answer: A serpent is a worm that can coil, bend, turn, and crawl within itself. In the same way, Lucifer turned his upright desire away from God, turned back into his own beauty and glory, and thus twisted his <term>Mercury: The "Mercurium" or vital life-spirit that drives motion and growth</term>. Thus, he became fierce, poisonous, hostile, envious, and false in the fire. He sought to preserve his creaturely life—which nevertheless depends on God—not through the <term>Cross-Birth: Represented by the symbol †, the process of dying to the self-will to be reborn in the Light</term> (namely, through the humble sinking down of the fire-power and the upright entering into God's will), but through his <insert>own</insert> <note>original: "eigen"</note> ways. His rising flash of light is not upright, but squinting, false, deceitful, and poisonous. His tone and word are like the lightning within thunder; thus he is rightly called the ancient serpent, because he is the wellspring of all lies and falsehood, and an enemy of all faithfulness and truth.

# Concerning the Revelation of God according to the First Principle

### Section 27
**Question:** Why is he called Satan and the Devil?

**Answer:** He is called **Satan** because of his <term>Adversity: "Widerwärtigkeit," meaning a state of being contrary or opposed to the nature of God</term> and his hostility toward God. For whatever is called the Highest Good in God—Light, Love, Joy, Peace, and eternal delight—is in Satan found as darkness, hate, enmity, <term>Fierceness: "Grimm," the harsh, wrathful quality of nature without light</term>, poison, and an eternal hunger and thirst.

He is called **Devil** in good German. The syllable **Teu** has its origin in a tone and sound from the depths, such as one hears when calling into a deep chasm. **Fel** has its origin in the "Fall." Also, **Teuff** signifies the same as **Deep-El** <note>original: "Tieff El"</note>, meaning a "Deep God" or "Deep Angel," for he is an **Eng-El** <note>A pun on the German word "Engel" (angel). Böhme breaks it into "Eng," meaning narrow or constricted, and "El," referring to God. He suggests the fallen angel is "fallen deep, deep, deep into narrowness or anguish."</note> who has fallen into constriction. Others derive this word "Devil" from the Greek *Diabolus*, meaning a destroyer and scatterer of unity.

### Section 28
**Question:** In what then does the conflict between Michael and the Dragon actually consist, and how can one ever seize the other for a struggle, since there is such a mighty chasm between them?

**Answer:** Every creature has within itself a powerful pull and drive toward its Mother, from whom it was born. But if that which is born adopts other qualities and a different image than those which came from its Mother, then that very pull and inclination awakens an unceasing struggle and hostility. Lucifer and his angels were born from God, and their spirit had within it a pull and drive toward its <term>Original State: "Urstand," the primordial source or foundation of a being</term>. However, because they defiled their image, corrupted their qualities, and alienated themselves from the life of God, each is now to the other an unchangeable adversity and enmity.

You should know that between God and Lucifer there was no other distinction than that between parents and their children—and even much closer. For just as parents bear a child from their own body according to their image, and keep it in their house as a natural heir to the body and nourish it: just so close is the **Body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note> of Lucifer to the Godhead. For God bore him from His own body; therefore, He also made him the heir of His goods and granted him the entire **Place** <note>original: "Locum"</note> in which He created him as his possession. The spirit which is born in the **Center of the Heart** from all <term>Seven Source-Spirits: "Quell-Geister," the seven fundamental forces or "qualities" of Böhme’s divine nature (e.g., bitterness, heat, sound)</term> is

<column-break/>

also (because it is still in the body when it is born) **co-qualifying** <note>original: "inqualirend," meaning working or vibrating in harmony with the same qualities</note> with God as one essence, and there is no distinction.

When that same spirit, which is born in the body, looks at something through the eyes, or hears through the ears, or smells through the nose, it is already inside that thing and works within it as its own property. And if it pleases the spirit, it eats from it, infects itself with the thing, and wrestles with it, creating a <term>Temperance: "Temperantz," here meaning a mixture or balance of qualities</term>, no matter how far away that thing may be. As far as its original or initial kingdom in God reaches, that far can the spirit rule instantly, and it is held back by nothing. For it is and comprises the power, just as God the Holy Spirit does; and in this, there is no distinction at all between God the Holy Spirit and the spirit of the body—except only this: that the Holy Spirit of God is the entire fullness, while the spirit of the body is only a piece which penetrates through the entire fullness. Wherever it goes, it infects itself with that same place and rules in that same **Place** <note>original: "Loco"</note> together with God. For it is from God and in God, and cannot be restrained, except only by the seven Nature-Spirits of the body which birth the **soulish spirit** <note>original: "animalischer Geist"</note>; these have the bridle in hand and can birth it however they wish.

When the harsh quality—as the Father—forms the Word, or the Son, or Spirit, it stands captured in the Center of the Heart and is approved by the other spirits to see if it is good. Now, if it pleases the Fire, the Fire releases the lightning (in which the bitter spirit stands) through the sweet...

29. Question: How can the devil live, move, and exist outside of GOD?

Answer: Concerning his creaturely life, the devil can exist outside of GOD no more than any other angel. But just as a viper takes in the <term>sun’s influence: "Influentz," the celestial power or rays of the sun</term> to create a life of poison, so the devil seizes the Spirit of GOD within himself as pure hostility and poison. GOD is indeed within him, but according to His Love-Light, He is not manifest in the will and mind of the godless; only His <term>wrath: "Grimm," the fierce, dark side of nature</term> is manifest within him. The light he

<column-break/>

cannot reach; it is in him, but it is of no use to him; his essence cannot grasp it. He shrinks from it; it is only his torture and torment. He remains in death and in dying torment; he cannot break through, for nothing comes to his aid that he could hold onto to ground himself in GOD’s kingdom. Even if he were to travel for a thousand years into the abyss and the deep, he would still be in the darkness outside of GOD—and yet GOD is in him and helps him not. He does not even know Him; he only knows of Him and feels only His wrath.

## 2. Part / Chapter 10.

If he <note>Referring to the devil or the fallen will</note> seeks to drive their <term>Mercury: "Mercurium," the active, craft-like spirit within the soul</term> toward elevation and incite them to pride, they humble themselves all the more deeply and sink all the more away from all fire-power <note>Surrendering the "fire" of the self-willed ego</note>. If he seeks to infect them with fierce envy, they surrender themselves entirely, with all that they are, into God’s will of love, and open their innermost core to share themselves with all the saints. If he seeks to plant his fierce fire of wrath and inflame them in anger, they surrender all fire-power even more, so that the fountain of Divine gentleness flows more abundantly and dampens the dragon’s fire-flames. Thus, there is a constant struggle between GOD and the devil, between light and darkness, between heaven and hell, and between Lucifer and Michael.

The life of darkness is opposed to all life of the light; for darkness produces a fierce and hostile essence, while the life of light produces a love-essence. In the darkness, there is only a constant stabbing and breaking within the essence, where every form of the essence is hostile to the other—a contrary existence. Every form denies itself and says to the others that they are evil and contrary to it, and that they are the cause of its unrest and fierceness. Each one thinks within itself: "If only the other form were not there, you would have rest." Yet each one is evil and false; hence it follows that everything raised out of the dark, fierce property is deceitful and always lies to the other forms, claiming they are evil—yet it is itself the cause of it, making the others evil with its own poisonous infection.

Thus they all are, and lies are their truth. When they speak lies, they speak from their own forms and properties; and so are their creatures. Therefore Christ said: *The devil is a liar and a murderer from the beginning* <note>original: "Der Teufel ist ein Lügner und Mörder von Anfang"</note>. For every form desires to murder the other; yet there is no actual murdering, but rather the greater the conflict, the greater their "murder-life" becomes.

Therefore it is called an eternal death and enmity, where pure contrariety arises; for there is nothing that could abolish the struggle; there is nothing that could tame a single form. The more it is resisted, the

<column-break/>

greater the fierceness would become—just like a fire that is stirred, which only burns more fiercely. Thus, the fierce kingdom can be extinguished by nothing except purely by God’s light; through that light, it becomes entirely gentle, lovely, and full of joy. Yet that also cannot be <note>Meaning the darkness cannot be entirely converted into light without destroying the basis of existence</note>, for if the dark kingdom were to be completely ignited by the light, then the light would have no root for its nature and property. No fire could be born, and there would be no light, nor any omnipotence, but everything would be a nothingness.

Therefore, the realm of wrath must exist, for it is a cause of the fire-world and light-world, and everything belongs to God. But not everything is recognized or named as "God," because the dark world has a different property; and the light-world is also a cause of the fierce terror of the dark property. For the darkness is terrified before the light and stands in eternal dread because the light-world dwells within it; it trembles eternally before the light and yet cannot grasp it, but is thus only a cause of life and movement, and so everything must serve God's glory.

The life of darkness has many kinds of forms; it is not of one single property, as can be recognized by us in the creatures of this world, where one is more evil than the other, or exists in a different torment than another—yet all of them still live in the power and light of the sun, by which they are softened.

Should this sun go out, however, the depth would become fierce and prickly; then one would soon see the true property of the dark world, and how all creatures would become so poisonous and evil. For all life stands in <term>poison: "Gifft," which Böhme uses to mean both a literal toxin and the "sting" or "stimulus" that creates movement and life</term>, and the light alone resists the poison—yet the light is also the cause that the poison lives and does not waste away.

Therefore we recognize that the life of darkness is only a languishing poison, like a dying torment, and yet there is no actual dying there, for the light-world...

The world encounters the mirror of darkness, which causes the darkness to stand in eternal terror. The dark life is like a sudden shock, where the flash and the terror always rise up as if they wished to escape from life and break out; and from this arises pride—the fact that the devil always wishes to be above God. This is his very nature; his "life-figure" is shaped this way, and he cannot do otherwise, just as a poison rages and stings as if it wanted to tear itself out of a limb.

Thus is the life of darkness within itself; the poisonous essences create such a mind, and from that mind proceeds such a spirit of the will. Such a quality exists within it, and it stands primarily in seven forms, according to the center of nature with its Principle. Just as the life of joy stands in seven forms according to the laws of nature, so too does the life of sadness. That which gives joy in the light gives sadness in the darkness. Yet we must not think that the life of darkness sinks into a misery where it forgets itself in mourning. It is not a "mourning" in our sense; rather, what we on earth call sadness according to this quality is, in the darkness, considered power and joy according to the nature of darkness. For sadness is a thing that sinks away into death; but death and dying are the very life of the darkness, just as the agony of poison is its life. The greater the agony within the poison becomes, the stronger the "poison-life" becomes, as can be observed in the nature of external poisons.

We cannot say of the devil that he sits in sadness as if he were despondent; there is no despondency in him, but rather a constant will to further ignite the <term>poison-torment: "Gifft-Quall," a term implying both a source-spring (Quelle) and an agonizing torment (Qual)</term>, so that his fury might become greater. For this is his strength, from which he draws his will to soar above the thrones and set them ablaze.

<column-break/>

is terrified; for the Light is the true poison that plagues him. Because he has abandoned it, it now stands against him; he is greatly ashamed of this, for he is a misshapen angel in a foreign image. He would be content with his fierce torment if only the Light were not so near to him. Therefore, the shame in him is so great that he becomes reckless and ignites his poisonous torment even more, so that his form becomes ever more hideous, simply so that the Divine image might not be recognized in him. Thus, he only strives to rage and storm against God, as if he were something foreign, or a foreign power, or as if he possessed a foreign kingdom. Yet he is poor, and the dark kingdom is not his own; rather, he is merely a prisoner within it. It is God’s <term>Abyss: "Abgrund," the unfathomable foundation of all reality</term>, and he is but a creature within it. He wants to be lord there, but he is merely a trickster <note>original: "Gauckler," meaning a juggler, buffoon, or one who creates illusions.</note> with his own fury. Nevertheless, he must act as the quality of his nature dictates, and this serves as a wonder before the stern power of eternity. It is like a play through which the stern power accomplishes its work, so that a distinction can be made between what is evil or good, joy or sorrow; and so that the creatures in the world of Light have cause to humble themselves. Yet, God created no devil, nor did He create Lucifer for the dark world. This is the source of the enmity in Lucifer: that he was once an angel, and the Light is so near to him, yet he has become a rebel.

Otherwise, there is no "woe" in the creatures that were created naturally within the dark world, for they are of the fierce quality and know nothing of the Light. Fierceness is their strength and power, and hostility is their will and life. The more evil and hostile a creature is in the dark world, the greater is its power. Just as the mighty tyrants of this world often display their power through wickedness so that men must fear them, or as tame animals fear the wicked, fierce ones: so also does this quality function in the dark world.

## Part 2 / Chapter 10

<meta>catchword: Own</meta>

When we wish to rightly consider the nature of the dark world, we need only look at the malice and pride of this world; it is a prototype. For all malice, falsehood, pride, and greed have their roots in the dark world. These are the characteristics of the dark world, whether they are recognized in humans or in animals. For this world stands upon the foundation of the dark world; the dark world gives this world its essence, will, and nature. If the Good had not been created alongside it, there would be no other action or will in this world than that which is in the dark world. However, the Divine power and the light of the sun prevent this. Yet, it can be seen among humans and animals how there is a biting, an enmity, a striking, and a proud self-will, where each one wants to rule over the other, to strangle, devour, and elevate itself alone; also to suppress everything with cunning, wrath, malice, and falsehood, and to make oneself the lord.

Thus, the dark world also has a specific nature. Whatever all malicious people do in this world, in their malice and falsehood, the devils also do in the dark world; and what the poisonous, evil worms and animals do in their malice, the other creatures in the dark world also do. Although they are without such physical bodies, they nonetheless have such characteristics in their spiritual bodies; and though they indeed have bodies, they are according to the manner of spirit, such as the devils have.

The birth, being, essence, and dominion of the dark world consist primarily only in the first four forms of nature <term>The first four forms of nature: In Böhme's system, these are the "harsh" properties—contraction, friction, anxiety, and fire—which form the basis of material existence before being transformed by light.</term>, such as in the agony-source <note>original: "Angst-Quall." Böhme often uses "Quall" as a pun on "Qual" (torment) and "Quelle" (source/wellspring).</note>, in a very strong and powerful dominion where everything in the essence is as if resounding. For gentleness is an enmity to the wrathful power, and one is always against the other. Otherwise, if it were meant to be one, there would have to be only one kind of source-torment, and if there were only one will, the eternal wonders would not be revealed. But the manifold source-torments make the eternal wonders manifest; for eternity could not otherwise be revealed, nor come to be-

<column-break/>

ing, except through the ignition—as in the strict, harsh attraction in which the dark world stands, and in which the fire-world originates, as well as the light-world. It is all only a single Being, but it divides itself into three properties of the source-energies. No property is separated from the others; rather, each gives rise to the other, just as can be seen in fire and light, as well as in the matter from which the fire burns.

->Six Points cap. 9. §. 1. 20.<-

**31. Question: But what follows from this battle between Michael and the dragon?**

**Answer:** On Michael’s side, a glorious victory and triumph; and on Lucifer’s side, an eternal, shameful expulsion from heaven. Now the question arises: How did the expulsion of the dragon and his army happen? Where was he thrust, since he can be outside of GOD, who is nonetheless present everywhere?

**Answer:** The expulsion of the dragon was the false, turned-away, figurative will of "self-acceptability" <note>meaning: the desire to find satisfaction only in oneself rather than God</note>, in which turned-away will Lucifer and his angels formed themselves. The dragon is the hellish foundation, and the cast-out spirits are the naturally formed characteristics of that hellish foundation. For when they broke themselves off from the Holy Name of God—from the essence of God’s unity—and formed themselves entirely into the "No," as if into lies, they became such.

The expulsion happened through the Holy Power-Name of the throne he once held; he was thrust with his legions out of his throne, as if out of his dwelling, and was immediately enclosed by the darkness and seized by the wrath <note>original: "Grimm," referring here to the harsh, structural severity of nature without light.</note> of the hellish foundation. Thus, he is severed from God’s holiness and dwells under the firmament, and upon the earth between time and eternity, as a prince of darkness in the wrath of GOD. His princely dominion is in the heights, but in various places, as well as in the elements in all places, according to his nature and—

### Of the Revelation of God according to the First Principle

The nature of the four elements / according to their properties / for their properties are manifold / and they have dwellings in all four elements / each species among them in its own likeness. However, one should understand it correctly: They do not possess the elements according to their good properties / no / but only the flowed-out **wrath** <note>original: "Grimm." In Böhme's thought, "Grimm" refers to the harsh, contracting, and fiery quality of God's nature when separated from His light and love.</note> / from the eternal wrath of the hellish foundation.

For two kingdoms are always understood to be in the elements / one according to God’s poured-out **love** / and the other according to his **wrath**; thus they dwell only in the part of the wrath / and are enclosed in the eternal night / and may not touch the good powers of the elements; but what flows out of the wrath / and forms itself into being / therein they can indeed dwell / with which being **sorcery** is practiced. There are indeed some powers / in which the holy power of the <term>central light-fire<gloss>The inner spiritual source of life and illumination that originates from God's heart.</gloss></term> has flowed out / which are entirely contrary to the hellish foundation. But in most things, evil and good are together / and the good holds the evil captive / and penetrates it / so that they may have no success therein / unless the will of man changes it with his power / or it be changed through the <term>Turba Magna<gloss>Latin for "Great Turmoil" or "Great Disturbance." In this context, it refers to the breaking of the natural order or the awakening of the wrath-fire that leads to destruction.</gloss></term> / so that a movement of wrath comes into a thing / so that the movement of evil exceeds the good. Their dwelling is a gulf of lies / a maw of eternal perdition / a formation of the fantasy / with a false light / into which this gulf from the central fire through its **imagination** <note>Here, "imagination" is not just "make-believe," but the creative or formative power of the spirit to shape its own reality.</note> models a light / which stands upon no foundation / and does not touch God’s Majesty / which / if the name of God is broken therein / is extinguished / as is to be understood in the case of sorcery.

This flowed-out dragon / or vengeance of the hellish foundation / is not itself the central fire of eternal nature / but an attraction of itself / as an outflow from the fire. Just as smoke and fire are two beings / and yet come from one foundation / so he is only a being of wrath / like the smoke from the fire.

<column-break/>

Therefore he is entirely separated from GOD / as the smoke is from the fire / but receives power and strength from the central fire of eternal nature / for his life stands therein / but his will and desire resemble the smoke from the fire. For his natural fire in his creaturely essence is burning / but in God’s being it is a <term>Temperamentum<gloss>A Latin term meaning a "balanced temperament" or "attunement." The cause of the fire is transformed into the light / but in the maw of the dragon or the throat of the hellish foundation, the properties are manifest in their working.

The hellish foundation and the heavenly / are against each other like day and night / and are near to each other / but neither perceives the other / nor does either see the other in its essence. For what is a **burning of love** in God / is a **burning of wrath** in hell.

This hellish gulf also pours itself out to some extent in many places through the elements, especially in the earth / as well as in the upper kingdom / where pools of fire are then perceived / sometimes of great cold / and sometimes of great heat / especially in great wastes / and where there are clefts of the earth / wherein the highly-damned spirits dwell / as well as the highly-damned souls of men / at which the evil spirits themselves are terrified / for it is the burning hell. Otherwise, their true foundation is not yet entirely manifest / and they must still await a greater judgment / the sun and the water still hold their kingdom hidden / so that it may not become entirely manifest until the Day of Judgment / though in the properties within themselves it is manifest / therefore the devils also tremble before the Last Day.

They stand against one another like death and life; each lives and wills within itself, and both together are like a **Something** and a **Nothing**. <note>original: "Ichts und Nichts." Böhme uses the term "Ichts" (from 'Ich' or 'I') to describe a state of "something-ness" or "aught," representing the manifestation of being out of the "Nichts" or Nothingness.</note> God is a **Something** in the Light, and a **Nothing** in hell; for the eternal Unity is a Being and Power only in the Light, while the Lie is a Being and Power only in its own self-centeredness. This is why the devils endure such great mockery: they are so close to God, yet they cannot reach him. And that is also the source of their anxious torment.

32. *Question: Did God not then create a specific place in which he shut up Lucifer with his angels, just as a criminal is locked in a prison?*

**Answer:** Just as the pure Godhead is entirely present everywhere in all places, so too is hell and the kingdom of God's **wrath** <note>original: "Zorn." In Böhme's cosmology, the "Wrath" is the fiery, consuming quality of God's nature when it is not tempered by His Light and Love.</note> everywhere. Thus we urge you to consider most seriously: God did not specifically create a hell and a particular torment where he wished to plague his creatures, such as angels and humans. For he is not a God who wills the evil that he himself forbids; moreover, he allowed his Heart to become human specifically to help mankind out of the eternal, anxious torment. Thus we must rightly consider the earnest torment of the abyss, which is eternal.

Therefore, as soon as the devils departed from the Light of God and wished to rule in the power of fire over the gentleness of God’s Heart, they were instantly and momentarily in the abyss of hell and were held by it. No special torment was made for them; rather, they remained outside of God (understand this as being outside the <term>Light-Principle<gloss>The second of Böhme's three "principles," representing the realm of divine love, clarity, and the "Heart of God."</gloss></term>), within the four forms of eternal nature.

<margin>The Threefold Life 2:53, 54</margin>

So, wherever the devil travels with his angels, he is in hell; the closer he is to God, the deeper he is 

<column-break/>

in hell. Just as the hotter the sun shines, the more powerful the **poison-source** <note>original: "Gifft-Quall." This wordplay connects 'Qual' (torment) with 'Quelle' (source/spring). It suggests a nature that is a self-generating fountain of poison.</note> becomes within a snake. His own <term>Impression<gloss>The spiritual act of "drawing inward" or "compressing," which Böhme describes as the first movement of nature that creates darkness and density.</gloss></term> and false image, in which he takes up God's powers, is his dungeon and prison. Just as a person driven by an evil, gnawing conscience finds the whole world too narrow, so too the entire vastness of space is too narrow for the devil. And although the **place** <note>original: "Locus."</note> or location of this world was given to Lucifer as a kingdom—for he was created within it—he has now been cast out of place and position and dwells in the abyss. There, he can eternally reach no place in the angelic kingdoms, yet he is enclosed in his own kingdom in the abyss, where he must bear eternal mockery like a prisoner. It is like a criminal led into a dark hole, away from all the beings of this world, where he must go without the joy and pleasure of the world and bear the shame of his crime.

This is also how it is for the devils and all damned souls; they lie captured in the dark dungeon. They do not even desire to come out because of the great mockery of their own gruesome shapes and images. And no matter where they go, they eternally enjoy nothing good; there is no refreshment for them. Instead, they lie in hell like the dead, or like those eternally starved, parched, and thirsting, and are nothing but an evil source of poison. Everything within them is contrary; they have only a thirst for anxiety and malice. They consume that within themselves eternally and give birth to blasphemy against God. The more gruesome they can make their own appearance, the better they like it—just like foolish people on earth who always want to be the greatest fools, making themselves look hideous and finding joy in it. This is what they also do eternally in hell, for they began that game here on earth. Just as a tyrant finds joy when he can torment people and flaunt their sweat in foolish, strange clothing and gestures, acting like a fool: so too do the devils in hell.
