33. **Question:** What do the devil and his angels do in hell?

**Answer:** They ignite the wrath of GOD always and eternally, serving as a foundation for the constant labor and operation of eternal nature. They fall away from the love of GOD always and eternally, and place their will into the terrifying power of fire. With his harsh quality, he pulls and constricts everything together; he hardens and makes stubborn the spirits and minds. He turns the essence of bodies into hard stone and bone, and he is an insatiable greed. He drives toward pride, a lust for power, tyranny, and compulsion. In the kingdom of this world, the cruel storm-winds arise from the fountain of the kingdom of darkness. He poisons with fierce envy and ignites the wrath of GOD wherever he can possibly reach. He is the stoker <note>original: "Calefactor," a Latin term for one who tends a furnace or heater.</note> and the fire-sprite <note>original: "Feuer-Fax." In Böhme's time, a "Fax" or "Fatz" referred to a fool or a trickster; here it implies one who plays with the dangerous fire of the First Principle.</note> in both the visible and invisible, and in the great and small world.

Furthermore, just as the holy angels form all kinds of figures and reveal the wisdom of GOD within them through many types of growths, so Lucifer also behaves according to his fantasy and apes the almighty and wise Creator. All angels live in humility and are surrendered in the Spirit of GOD; they exist within the eternally-speaking Word of GOD like a well-tuned instrument in the harmony of the kingdom of heaven, whose master-builder and ruler is the Holy Spirit. The devil, however, has prepared for himself a frivolous game <note>original: "Kizel-Spiel," literally a "tickling-game," implying something superficial and stimulating rather than spiritually deep.</note> like a fool, where he can play pranks with his transformations and behave foolishly, introducing himself into strange figures and mocking the image of angelic simplicity and obedience. That was exactly what he wanted: to leave the harmony of the angelic choirs. For the Scripture says he was a murderer and a liar from the beginning; his pranks are vain, alien figures and lies which GOD did not introduce into him in form. He, however, introduces them into himself as forms; and because this runs contrary to his creation, they are lies and abominations. He was once an angel, but he denied his angelic

<column-break/>

form and obedience and entered into the abominations of his antics.
<margin>Mysterium Magnum <note>A major work by Böhme titled "The Great Mystery," an exposition on Genesis.</note> chapter 9, sections 18, 20.</margin>

Such things are recognizable enough in the fierce, poisonous animals, snakes, worms, and flying and crawling vermin; so many monsters in which the qualities of the dark world reveal themselves—such as wolves, bears, flying dragons, wild ravenous beasts, birds of prey, vermin, and even the shameful organs of reproduction, which are an abomination and a loathing before GOD. Yet, the wisdom of GOD has so wisely ordered everything through its omnipotence that often the most noble and best thing lies enclosed and hidden within the fiercest and most poisonous.

34. **Question:** Would such wonders of GOD then not have been revealed if Lucifer and his angels had not fallen and were not active and driving according to the quality of the dark world?

**Answer:** The foundation has existed from eternity, but not in such a revelation. For GOD'S wrath has indeed existed from eternity, but not *as* a wrath; rather, it was like fire lying hidden in wood or in a stone until it is awakened. The awakening, or the igniting, or the "throat of the dragon," took its beginning in the fall of Lucifer as a creature, when his own will—as the "No"—turned away from the "Yes" <note>original: "Jah." Böhme uses the "Yes" and "No" (Ja und Nein) to describe the dialectical tension in all things: the "Yes" is God's light and outgoing love, while the "No" is the self-centered, inward-pulling fire.</note>. But because such an awakened ground has sprung from the eternal foundation and possesses an eternal will, such a foundation cannot pass away. If it did, the creation would be entirely abolished, and eternal nature would be extinguished in its own pleasantness. If that were to happen, then knowledge and sensitivity would also be extinguished, as well as the realm of joy. This cannot be, for two eternal beginnings must exist within one another so that one may be recognized and felt in the other, and so that the holy angels and souls, along with all heavenly creatures, may praise GOD and rejoice in the Good—because they do not dwell in the Evil and do not have to *be* the Evil.
<margin>Theosophical Questions 14, sections 1, 4.</margin>

## 2. Part / Chapter 10.

<meta>catchword: Therefore</meta>

35. **Qu.** In such a manner, did GOD will evil? And is He a cause that moved Lucifer to his fall, so that His strict justice might be revealed?

**Ans.** We will hear more of this matter below; here it is to be considered generally: no thing is evil that remains in such a <term>concordance</term> <note>original: "Concordantz," referring to the harmonious agreement or "tuning" of all spiritual forces.</note>, for that which produces the very worst through its departure from the concordance, also produces the very best when within that same concordance. That which causes sorrow also causes joy when in a state of balance.

Therefore, no creature can accuse its Creator of having made it evil. Everything is "very good," but through its own self-exaltation and departure from balance, it becomes evil, leading itself out of the form of love and joy into a form of torment.

King Lucifer stood with his highest kingdom of joy at the beginning of his creation; but he departed from balance and raised himself out of the concordance into the cold, dark, fiery <term>generation</term> <note>original: "Gebährung," a central term for Böhme describing the perpetual "birthing" or unfolding of spiritual qualities.</note>, from which the hot, fiery generation originates. He departed from his order, from the <term>harmony</term> <note>original: "Harmonie."</note> in which GOD created him; he wished to be a lord over all. Therefore, he also entered into the strict dominion of fire and is now an instrument in that strict power of fire, upon which the all-present Spirit also strikes and echoes upon his instrument. But this is according to the quality of the fierce fire: just as the harmony is the form of life in every thing, so also is its echo or the sound of the eternal resonance within it—holy in the holy, and perverted in the perverted.

Everything must praise the Creator of all beings; the devils praise Him in the power of His fury, and the angels and humans praise Him in the power of His love.

The Being of all beings is only a single Being, but in its generation, it divides itself into two <term>principles</term> <note>original: "Principia," the foundational dimensions of reality (Light/Dark).</note>, such as light and darkness, joy and sorrow, evil and good, love and wrath, fire and light; and from these two eternal beginnings, it proceeds into the third beginning, which is the Creation, for its own play of love, according to the quality of the eternal desire of both.

<column-break/>

Therefore, every thing goes in its harmony and is driven by one single Spirit, who is in every thing according to that thing's own quality; and that is the clockwork of the great <term>mystery</term> <note>original: "Mysterii," referring to the *Mysterium Magnum* or the hidden chaos/source of all things.</note> of eternity in every principle, according to the principle's quality, and then according to the present form of the prepared instrument of that creature and in all these beginnings.

For everything that is temporal, death is the parting-goal where the evil may be broken. But that which arises from the eternal beginnings and enters into another figure while in its harmony and form of life, that departs from GOD's harmony—from the true order into which GOD created it—and is cast out from that same harmony into its own likeness, as a discordant play or sound within the great and beautiful, harmoniously-tuned symphony. For it is a contrary thing; it carries a different tone, sound, and will, and thus it is led into its own likeness.

And for this reason, Hell was given to the devil as a house and dwelling, because he led his form of life into GOD's wrath and into the fierce fire of eternal nature, so that he might be the instrument in the eternal fire of GOD; and thus the Spirit of Wrath strikes his instrument, and it must nevertheless stand to GOD's honor and wonder-working, being the play within the desire and quality of the fierce wrath.

The wrath and fury of GOD is now his joy—not that he trembles and mourns or lives in weakness; no, but rather in great strength and fiery power, like a mighty king and lord, but only within that same quality which he himself is: namely, in the first principle, in the dark world.

# On the Revelation of GOD according to the First <term>Principle</term> <note>original: "Princ." or "Principium." In Böhme's theosophy, a "Principle" is one of the three fundamental modes of existence: the dark-fire world (Father), the light-fire world (Son), and the external world (Spirit).</note>

Thus, in the same way, we are to recognize the angelic world as the second principle, where GOD’s light and clarity appear in all being, and the Divine resonance or voice rises up in all creatures within the great kingdom of joy. There, the Spirit creates from the Divine resonance a kingdom of joy and a great, everlasting desire for love within those same creatures and in all Divine angelic beings. Just as there is a trembling of agonizing torment in the painful fire, there is likewise a trembling of the kingdom of joy in the fire of love and light; it is a great exaltation of the voice of GOD, which thus creates a great revelation of the Divine kingdom of joy in the angels and similar creatures, such as the souls of men.

<margin>The Signature of All Things, chapter 16, §§ 7–16.</margin>

36. **Qu.** How is it actually to be understood when the author teaches that love and wrath, evil and good, flow and arise from one single ground?

**Ans.** Understand it well. In the original state of eternal nature, in the Father’s property within the great <term>Mystery</term> <note>original: "Mysterio." Refers to the *Mysterium Magnum*, the chaotic or unmanifested potential of all things before they are brought into being.</note> of all beings, it is entirely one. For in the angelic world there is also that very same single fire, but in a different quality—as a fire of love. To the devils and to hell, this is a fire of poison or wrath, for the fire of love is the death, dying, and enmity of the fire of wrath; it takes away the power of the <term>fierceness</term> <note>original: "Grimm." This term denotes the harsh, stern, and wrathful quality of the first principle (fire) when it is not tempered by the light of the second principle (love).</note>, and the fierceness does not want this and cannot allow it. For if there were no fierceness, there would be no fire, and also no light; if there were no eternal fierceness, there would also be no eternal joy. The fierceness transforms itself into joy within the light. The essence of the fierce fire according to the darkness dies away in the fierce fire, and from that same death, it rises up into the fire of light and love. Just as the light burns from the candle, and within the candle, the fire and the light are one thing.

<column-break/>

Thus also the great mystery of all being in eternity is in itself one thing, but in its unfolding and revelation it steps forth from eternity to eternity into two essences: as one evil and one good. What is evil to one thing is good to another. Hell is evil to the angels, for they were not created within it; but to the other, hellish creatures, it is good.

Thus also heaven is evil to the hellish creatures, for it is their poison and death, an eternal dying and an eternal prison. Therefore, there is an eternal enmity, and GOD is called a GOD alone according to the light of His love. He is indeed all things Himself, but according to the darkness He speaks: *I am an angry, jealous GOD, and a consuming fire.* <note>original: "Ich bin ein zorniger eiferiger GOTT / und ein verzehrend Feuer." A paraphrase of Exodus 20:5 and Hebrews 12:29.</note> Every creature should remain in its <term>place</term> <note>original: "Loco."</note> in which it was seized during its creation and formed into an image; it should not deviate from that harmony, or it becomes an enemy to the essence of all essences. In that case, hell is just as much an enemy to the devil—for he is a foreign guest within it, like a <term>perjurer</term> <note>original: "Meineidiger," referring to one who has broken a holy oath or covenant.</note> cast out of heaven. He wants to be a lord in a place where he was not created to be. The entire creation rebukes him as a perjured and fallen false spirit who has deviated from his order. Even nature, in its fierceness, is his enemy; though he is of that same property, he is nonetheless a stranger there who wants to be lord. Yet he has lost his kingdom and is only a housemate in the wrath of GOD. He who was too rich has become poor; he had everything when he stood in <term>humility</term> <note>original: "Demuth."</note>, and now he has nothing, and is moreover imprisoned in the abyss. That is his shame: that he is a King and yet gambled away his kingdom through <term>pride</term> <note>original: "Hoffart."</note>. The royal creature remains, but the rule is gone; from a King he has become an <term>executioner</term> <note>original: "Nachrichter."</note>. Whatever the wrath of GOD seizes, he is the judge of it.

35. **Qu.** In such a way, did GOD will evil, and is He a cause that moved Lucifer to his fall, so that His strict justice might be revealed?

**Ans.** We will hear more concerning this matter further below; here it is generally to be considered that no thing is evil that remains in such <term>Concordance</term> <note>original: "Concordantz." This refers to the state of "agreement" or "harmony" where all the conflicting forces of nature are balanced and unified.</note>; for that which creates the very worst through its departure from the Concordance, also creates the very best within that same Concordance. That which causes pain there, also causes joy within equality.

Therefore, no creature can accuse its Creator of having made it evil. Everything is very good, but through its own self-exaltation and departure from equality, it becomes evil, and leads itself out of the form of love and joy into a painful form.

King Lucifer stood with his highest kingdom of joy in the beginning of his creation, but he departed from equality and raised himself out of the Concordance into the cold, dark, fiery birth, from which the heated birth of fire originates. He departed from his order, from the <term>Harmony</term> <note>original: "Harmonie." Böhme often uses musical metaphors; the universe is a song or a piece of music where every creature is a note.</note> in which GOD created him; he wanted to be a lord over all. Thus he also entered into the strict fiery dominion and is now an instrument in the strict power of fire, upon which the all-present Spirit also strikes and echoes upon his instrument. But according to the property of the grim fire: just as the Harmony, as the form of life, is in every thing, so also is its echo or sound of the eternal resonance within it—holy in the holy ones, and perverted in the perverted.

Everything must praise the Creator of all beings; the devils praise Him in the power of the wrath, and the angels and humans praise Him in the power of love.

The Essence of all essences is but one single essence, but it divides itself in its birth into two <term>Principles</term> <note>original: "Principia." Fundamental modes of existence: the dark "Fire-world" and the "Light-world."</note>, as in light and darkness, in joy and sorrow, in evil and good-

<column-break/>

-ness, in love and wrath, in fire and light; and from these two eternal beginnings, into the third beginning, as in the Creation for His own play of love, according to the property of the eternal desire of both.

Thus every thing proceeds in its harmony and is driven by one single Spirit, which is in every thing according to the thing's property; and that is the <term>Clockwork</term> <note>original: "Uhr-Werck." A metaphor for the mechanical yet divinely-driven structure of the cosmos.</note> of the great <term>Mystery</term> <note>original: "Mysterii." The "Mysterium Magnum" or the hidden potential of God from which all things are manifested.</note> of eternity in every Principle, according to the property of the Principle, and then according to the inherent form of the prepared instrument of that creature, and in all these beginnings.

For all that is temporal, death is the parting-limit where the evil may be broken. But whatever arises from the eternal beginnings and enters into another figure in its harmony and life-form, that departs from God's harmony—from the true order into which GOD created it—and is cast out of that same harmony into its own likeness, as a discordant play or sound in the great and beautiful, harmonizing Harmony. For it is a contrary thing; it carries another tone, sound, and will, and thus it is led into its own likeness.

And for this reason, Hell was given to the devil as a house and dwelling, because he led the form of his life into GOD’s wrath and into the fiery grimness of eternal nature, so that he might be the instrument in the eternal fire of GOD; and thus the Spirit of Wrath strikes his instrument, and it must yet stand for GOD’s glory and wonder-work, being the play within the desire and property of the grim wrath.

The wrath and grimness of GOD is now his joy; not that he trembled or mourned or lived in weakness: No, but in great strength and fiery power, as a mighty king and lord—but only in that same property which he himself is, as in the first Principle in the dark world.

## Part 2, Chapter 10: On the Revelation of GOD according to the 1st <term>Principle</term> <note>Böhme defines the "First Principle" as the dark, fiery foundation of all existence—the "wrath" of God that exists before and beneath the light of the "Second Principle."</note>

<meta>Dd 2</meta>

37. **Qu.** Is there then any hope that the fallen angels shall one day be restored to their former glory and blessedness?

**Ans.** Our author gives us very little hope for this; and although nowadays some hold such an opinion—seeking to prove it partly from Holy Scripture and partly from other reasons—all these arguments are found insufficient to establish this as a certainty. Holy Scripture begins its testimony with the restoration of that kingdom from which the fallen angels were cast out, and in whose place God ordered and appointed another king and another host, namely, mankind. Regarding the fall, return, and restoration of the fallen angels, it says little or nothing. It is even more surprising that some lovers of our author’s writings seek to prove such opinions from the author himself, even though the blessed author was quite distant from these views, and his principles in general cannot possibly be reconciled with them. For according to the author’s fundamental principles, the fallen angel and his followers become all the more fierce, poisonous, adverse, and monstrous the more God would act upon them with His gentleness, grace, light, love, and peace. Indeed, the author casts him as a <term>fire-stoker</term> <note>original: "Feuer-Fax." An archaic term for one who tends or plays with fire.</note> and a <term>steward of the furnace</term> <note>original: "Calefactor." Latin for one who provides heat or tends a fire.</note>, who constantly blows upon the fire of the dark world to open the wonders of God in temporal and eternal nature.

This, then, is the revelation of God according to the property of the dark world, in which God proves Himself—within those angels who have fallen—as an angry, jealous God; and therein is recognized God’s strict justice, enmity, adversity, hatred, zeal, vengeance, and eternal damnation.

37. **Question:** Is there then any hope that the fallen angels shall eventually be restored to their former glory and blessedness?

**Answer:** Our author gives us very little hope for this; and although some people nowadays are of such an opinion—seeking to prove it partly from the Holy Scriptures and partly from other reasons—all those arguments are found to be insufficient to establish such a thing as certain. The Holy Scriptures begin their testimony with the restoration of that very kingdom from which the fallen angels were expelled, and in whose place GOD has ordained and appointed another king and another host, namely, mankind. Of the fall, recovery, and restoration of the fallen angels, it says little or nothing. It is all the more surprising that some admirers of the

# Chapter 1.
## Concerning the Work of the Creation of this Visible World in General.

We have previously considered how the triune GOD—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—has revealed Himself in and through His eternally-speaking Word. According to the Second <term>Principle</term> <note>In Böhme's philosophy, the "Second Principle" is the realm of divine Light, Love, and the "Son" of God.</note>, as the most glorious Light, eternal Love and Gentleness, the highest Good and infinite fullness and pleasure in the World of Light and all the Angels of GOD; and according to the First <term>Principle</term> <note>The "First Principle" represents the fiery, dark, and powerful foundation of God's nature—His "wrath" or "sternness" when viewed without the light of His love.</note>, as an angry, jealous GOD, as an eternal glow, and a consuming fire. Now it follows that we also examine how the triune GOD has become manifest in the Third Principle in this visible world and all its creatures, through which one recognizes the eternal omnipotence, wisdom, and goodness of GOD, and the almighty power of His eternal Godhead in love and wrath, in light and darkness, in good and evil.

**1. Question.**
What is the very best and truest key to thoroughly unlock and open this great <term>Mystery of Godliness</term> <note>original: "Geheimnis der Gottseligkeit." This refers to the hidden spiritual truths regarding God's relationship with the created world.</note>—namely, how GOD has become manifest in the kingdom of this visible world?

**Answer.**

There is no better or truer key to such a high mystery than the true <term>Rebirth</term> <note>original: "Wiedergeburt." A central theme in Böhme’s thought: the idea that a person must undergo an internal spiritual transformation to perceive the truth of God.</note> and newest creation of a chosen, believing soul. For every spirit sees no further than into its "mother," from which it has its origin and in which it arises; for it is impossible for any spirit, by its own natural power, to see into another Principle and behold it, unless it be born again within it.

The natural man, however (whom the <term>Matrix</term> <note>original: "Matrix." For Böhme, this refers to the "womb" or the formative medium of the physical world that holds the human soul in its fallen state.</note> of this world has captured in his fall), has a natural spirit that hovers between two Principles—the Divine and the Hellish—and stands in both gateways. Into whichever Principle he falls, there he is born again, either to the Kingdom of Heaven or the Kingdom of Hell, and yet in this [present] time he is able to behold neither. He is, in his substance and whole being, a twofold man; for his soul, in its own substance, is from the First Principle, which from eternity has no ground or beginning, and the

<column-break/>

soul was, in the time of the creation of man in Paradise or the Kingdom of Heaven, truly "corporized" after the manner of a spirit through the <term>Fiat</term> <note>original: "Fiat." Referring to the divine creative command "Let there be" (Latin: *fiat*), which Böhme interprets as an active, attractive force of God's will.</note>. But it remained stood inseparably with the first power, which is from eternity in the first root, and was illuminated through the Second Principle (as the Heart of GOD). Thus, standing in Paradise, it was breathed into the Matrix of the Third Principle—into the starry and elemental man—by the wafting Spirit of GOD. The soul understands (as far as the Light of GOD shines within it) the foundation of Heaven, as well as the elements and also of Hell. For if the Light is in it, then it is born in all three Principles, though it is only a spark thereof, and not the great Wellspring, which is GOD Himself.

Therefore Christ also says: *If you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you may say to the mountain: Cast yourself into the sea, and it shall happen.* And in this power, through the Word and GOD's power, men have raised the dead and made the sick whole. They could not have done this otherwise, had they not stood in the power of all three Principles.

For the created spirit of man, which is from the Matrix of this world, rules in the power of the Light—understand: through the power of the Second Principle—over and in the power of the starry and elemental spirit, everything

But in Adam's case, we lost this great power when we vacated Paradise and wandered into the third <term>Principle</term> <note>In Böhme’s thought, the "Third Principle" is the material, visible world we inhabit.</note>, into the <term>Matrix</term> <note>original: "Matrix." Therefore, we still have knowledge only as if in a glint <note>original: "Glast" — a shimmer or reflection of light.</note>, and we see the eternal birth as if through a dark mirror.

Since we now float so powerlessly in all three births, the Paradisiacal gate is so often darkened for us, and the Devil so often pulls us toward the hellish gate; likewise, the elements and the <term>Sidereal Gate</term> <note>The "Sidereal" refers to the stars and the astral influences that Böhme believed governed the physical body and outward mind.</note> cover us and make us so bloated that we often float in the entire matrix as if deaf, dumb, or half-dead. It has seen everything and sees everything in the Light of GOD; it is not at all something distant or inscrutable. For the eternal birth, which remains hidden in the human <term>Center</term> <note>The spiritual core of a person where the divine light can be found.</note>, does nothing new; it recognizes, works, and does exactly what it has done from eternity, working toward light and darkness, and laboring in great anxieties. Therefore, if you wish to be a <term>Philosopher</term> <note>A "philosopher of nature" who seeks the spiritual truth behind physical reality.</note> and a student of nature, and to explore God’s being in nature—how all this is constituted—then ask GOD for His Holy Spirit, that He might enlighten you with the same.

For in your flesh and blood you cannot grasp such things; even if you read of them, they will be but a mist or darkness before your eyes. Only in the Holy Spirit—who is in GOD and also in all of nature, from which all things have come—can you search even into the entire body of GOD, which is nature, as well as into the Holy Trinity. For the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Holy Trinity and reigns in the entire body of GOD—that is, in all of nature.

Just as the spirit of a human reigns within the entire body in all the veins and fills the whole person, so also the Holy Spirit fills all of nature and is the heart of nature, reigning in the good qualities in all things. If you now have the same Spirit within you, so that He enlightens and fills your spirit, then you will understand what is written hereafter. But if not, it will happen to you as it did to the wise heathens <note>A term used for ancient Greek and Roman philosophers who relied on human reason alone rather than spiritual revelation.</note>, who became infatuated with creation and wanted to explore it through their own reason; they came in their searching before God’s face, yet could not see it, and were stone-blind in the knowledge of GOD.

Hitherto we have considered how the triune GOD—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—has revealed Himself in and through His eternally-speaking Word. Just as the spirit of a man rules in the whole body and in all the veins, filling the whole man, so also the Holy Spirit fills all of nature and is the Heart of nature, ruling in the good qualities in all things. If you now have Him within you, so that He enlightens and fills your spirit, then you will understand what is written hereafter. But if not, it will happen to you as it did to the wise heathens, who lost themselves in the creation and wanted to explore it through their own reason; they came in their thoughts <note>original: "Tichten"; meaning their mental constructions or poetic imaginings.</note> even before God’s face, and yet could not see Him, and were stone-blind in the knowledge of God.

### Part 3 / Chapter 1

**5. Qu.** But does our author not set himself too high, when he claims to understand and describe the mysteries of creation even more clearly and in greater detail than Moses—who, after all, spoke with GOD face to face and inquired of all the mysteries of the world’s creation directly from GOD?

**Ans.** Our highly-enlightened author strongly doubts that the dear man Moses was the actual author of the book of Creation <note>The book of Genesis.</note>. He says: **it is written in a quite unwise and simple manner**, though it contains an excellent understanding within it. Without doubt, the Holy Spirit did not wish to reveal these things so that the Devil would not know all the secrets of creation and misuse them through his instruments for false <term>magic</term> <note>In Böhme's thought, "magic" is the act of bringing spirit into form; "false magic" is the manipulation of the material world for selfish or diabolical ends.</note>. And it is likely to be presumed that the creation was not described in writing before the Deluge <note>The Great Flood of Noah.</note>, but was carried from one generation to another as a "dark word" in the memory, until after the Deluge, when the world began to live in an **Epicurean** <note>In this context, "Epicurean" refers to a life focused on material pleasure and the denial of divine involvement in the world, rather than the specific Greek school of philosophy.</note> manner again. When the Holy Fathers saw this, they described the creation so that it would not be forgotten, and so that the Epicurean world might have a mirror in the creation to see that there is a GOD, and that the essence of this world has not stood this way from eternity; thus they might have a mirror in it and learn to fear that hidden GOD.

This was also the primary instruction and teaching of the Patriarchs, both after and before the Deluge: they directed humanity toward the creation, just as the entire Book of Job does.

They did indeed honor and worship the sun and stars as gods, but they did not recognize how they were created or how they came to be, or from what they were made. For they should have thought that they must have come from something, and that the thing which created them must be greater and older than the stars. Furthermore, they had the earth and stones as an **example** <note>original: "Exempel"</note> that these things must have come from something, as well as humans and all **creatures** <note>original: "Creaturen"</note> on earth. All of this proves to them that a more powerful force is present in these things, which created all of this in such a manner.

Truly, why should I write much of the blindness of the heathens, since our **Doctors** <note>Academic theologians and scholars.</note> in their **crowned little hats** <note>A mocking reference to the academic biretta or doctoral cap, suggesting that their formal titles do not equal true spiritual insight.</note> are just as blind. They know, indeed, that there is a GOD who created all this; but they do not know *where* that GOD is or *how* He is. When they want to write of GOD, they seek Him outside of this world in a heaven alone, as if He were an image to be compared to something. They admit, of course, that this GOD governs everything in this world by a Spirit, but they insist His bodily presence is strictly many thousands of miles away in a heaven. Very well, you Doctors, if you are right, then give an answer to the Spirit; I will ask you a little something:

What do you suppose stood in place of this world before the time of the world? Or from what do you suppose the earth

-># Of the Creator of all Things<-

Kk 3

...of fire and light, of love and wrath, of good and evil; therefore our author calls it the **third <term>Principle<note>In Böhme’s thought, a "Principle" is a fundamental realm of existence. The first is the dark fire-world (wrath), the second is the light-world (love), and the third is this visible, material world.</note></term>**, because it has its birth from those two invisible principles, fire and light. As the ancient sages also taught: *Everything that is in one world is also in the other*, but according to the nature and property of the world in which a thing exists. That very thing which is in the dark fire-world is also in the angelic light-world; in the former according to the property and <term>quality<note>original: "Quall." Böhme uses this word to imply both a "source" (Quelle) and a "torment" or "vibrant activity" (Qual).</note></term> of wrath and darkness, but in the latter according to the property and quality of light and love. What lives, moves, and exists in these two worlds invisibly and in a spiritual, heavenly, and hidden way, also lives and moves in this visible world in a visible, comprehensible, <term>astral<note>original: "siderische." Referring to the influence of the stars and the cosmic spirit.</note></term>, and earthly way. Thus, heaven on earth is earthly, and the earth in heaven is heavenly; the stars are in the earth in an earthly manner, and all creatures of the earth are in heaven in an astral manner. What lives in the air according to the manner and property of air, lives in the water according to the property of water.

This visible world, says our author, has sprouted from those aforementioned spiritual worlds as an outflowing of the Divine Power, and is an <term>object<note>original: "Objectum oder Gegen-Wurff." A "throwing-against" or a mirror-image reflection of the internal reality.</note></term> of the spiritual world. The spiritual world is the inward ground of the visible world; the visible world stands within the spiritual. This visible world is nothing other than an outflowing of the seven properties; for it arose out of the six working properties, and in the seventh—as in Paradise—it stands at rest. This is the eternal Sabbath, in which the working of Divine Power rests.

<margin>Clavis § 81. 82.</margin>

Thus we can clearly contemplate the hidden spiritual world by looking at the visible world; for we see that in the depths of the world, fire, air, and water are continually being born, and that there is no rest or ceasing of such birth, and it has been so from the beginning of this world. Yet, in the outer world, we can find no cause for what this "ground" or foundation might be. Instead, human reason says: "GOD created it so," and stops there. This is true in itself, but reason does not know the Creator, who creates without ceasing as the true <term>Master-Builder<note>original: "Archæus." A term from alchemy and Paracelsian medicine referring to the vital internal force or "inner chemist" that directs growth and life.</note></term> or <term>Divider<note>original: "Separator." The force that distinguishes and separates different qualities from the primal unity.</note></term>. This Creator is an outflowing from the invisible world, as the expressed Word of GOD, which I indicate with the term of the **fiery Mercury**. For what the invisible world is in a spiritual working (where light and darkness are among one another), the visible world is in a substantial working. Those powers understood in the expressed Word within the inward spiritual world are also understood in the visible world in the stars and elements, but in a different principle of a holy kind.

<column-break/>

The four elements flow out of the *Archæus* <note>Master-Builder</note> of the inner ground, as from the four properties of eternal nature. At the beginning of time, they were breathed out from the inner ground and placed into their own active being and life. Therefore, the outer world is called a principle, a <term>subject<note>original: "Subjectum." Used here in the sense of a vessel or a platform upon which the inner world acts.</note></term> of the inner world, an instrument of the inner spiritual Master, which Master is GOD’S Word and Power. And just as the inner Divine world contains within itself an intelligent life from the outflowing of Divine Knowledge (in which the angels and souls are understood), so too the outer world contains a rational life within itself. This life stands in the out-flowed powers of the inner world, though this outer life has no higher understanding than that in which it stands—namely, in the stars and in the elements.

<margin>Clavis 96. 99.</margin>

**2. Question: Who then is actually the highest and most noble working cause of the creation of this visible world, the heavens and the earth, together with everything therein?**

**Answer:** Moses calls the Creator **ELOHIM** <note>original: "ÆLOHIM." Translated here as "mighty Lord."</note>, which actually signifies a mighty Lord.

### 3. Part / Chapter 2.

Lord, who has the power and sovereign authority to do all things. The ancient Hebrews understand this to mean the **ANGELS**, saying that this visible world was made by the **ANGELS**. However, along with our author, we understand this to be the eternally-speaking, true, self-subsisting Word of God, from which, through which, and to which all things are, as seen in Colossians 1:16–17.

**3. Question: What then is actually to be understood by the WORD of GOD?**

**Answer:** Our author uses the "WORD" in a threefold sense. First, the speaking Word, which the Scripture calls <note>original: "$\lambda o \gamma o \varsigma$"</note> **Logos**, the mind and understanding of God, God Himself, of whom John testifies: **In the beginning was the Word / and the Word was with God / and God was the Word / John 1:1.** The author calls this word the "speaking word," or the active cause of all things.

Secondly, "Word" also refers to that outgoing power through which the working or speaking Word brought forth all things. And this Word is the speaking and working itself. The author calls it the **FIAT** <note>Latin: "Let it be."</note>.

Thirdly, it is also the "spoken word," or that work which God made and created through the speaking and working of His Word—such as the heavens, the earth, and all that is within them. All of this is a compacted, grasped, and formed Word of God.

**4. Question: But why does God call Himself the WORD?**

**Answer:** Just as an upright person reveals themselves to another who does not know their mind or heart through words, and thus brings forth their heart, mind, and thoughts into the one to whom they wish to reveal themselves: so God has brought forth and revealed the depths of His heart in and through His eternally-speaking Word.

And just as the human mind, in understanding, introduces itself through the senses into an <term>object<note>original: "Gegen-Wurff." This is a Böhmean term for a "counter-throw" or a reflection/mirror through which the invisible will can perceive itself.</note></term> of an image, and flows out with those senses, capturing itself in images (which are the thoughts of the mind), wherein the will of the mind works and thus captures itself with desire into a sharpness—as if in a magnetic attraction—from which joy and sorrow originate: so too must we recognize regarding the eternal mind of sensitivity, that

<column-break/>

the outflow of the single will of God has introduced itself through the Word into <term>differentiation<note>original: "Schiedlichkeit." The process by which the unified divine essence divides into distinct, individual qualities and forms.</note></term>. This differentiation has introduced itself into "acceptability," as its own pleasure and desire for its own self-revelation, moving from Unity into Multiplicity.

From this eternal working of sensitivity and sensuality—since this same working has introduced itself from eternity into Nature and into properties—the visible world with all its host has sprung forth and been brought into a creaturely state. For the eternity of such working into fire, light, and darkness has led itself into an object <note>original: "Gegen-Wurff"</note> within the visible world. It has ordained the **Separator** <note>In Böhme's thought, the "Separator" is the cosmic "steward of nature" or "artificer" that differentiates the divine powers into specific material forms.</note> in all the powers of the outflowed essence, through desire, to be an officer of nature, by which the eternal will governs, makes, forms, and builds all things.

Thus we can by no means say that God's essence is something distant that possesses or occupies a particular place or location; for the abyss of nature and the creature is God Himself. The visible world with its host and creatures is nothing other than the outflowed Word, which has introduced itself into properties. Where there are properties, a self-will has arisen, and with the "acceptability" of the will, creaturely life has arisen. In the beginning of this world, this life introduced itself into an "acceptability" as a creaturely foundation, which the **Separator** has decided according to its property and brought into a self-willing according to that form. Thus, with this self-willing, such desire and essence arose as the "body" of every "acceptability" out of its own likeness and property. Through this, the **Separator** has signed and made himself visible, as can be recognized in all life.

<margin>Contemplative [Life], chapter 3, section 14.</margin>
From this, it is to be seen how the general, unfathomable, and unsearchable will of God has expressed and revealed itself through His eternally-speaking Word in the work of creation, as in the spoken word.

# Of the Creator of All Things.

5. **Question:** Now Reason asks: Why and for what purpose has the Creator made such a revelation?

**Answer:** There is no other cause than that the spiritual world should lead itself into a visible, figurative form, so that the inner powers might become figurative and formal. For this to happen, the spiritual essence had to enter into a material ground, within which it could form and fashion itself; and such a separation had to occur, so that the distinct parts <note>The "separated" or "individualized" elements of creation.</note> would always yearn for their first ground—the inner for the outer, and the outer for the inner.

<margin>Clavis 115 <note>Referencing Jacob Böhme’s work *Clavis*, or *The Key*.</note></margin>

Thus the wonders, which from eternity were seen in Wisdom without having actual substance, had to come into substance, and thus be revealed in time according to the forms of nature. For God is threefold in persons and wished to move Himself three times, according to the attribute of each Person, and no more in eternity. First, the <term>Center of Nature</term> <note>original: "Centrum des Vaters Natur." The foundational, driving force of the Father's aspect in the creative process.</note> moved toward the creation of the angels, and onward to this world. Secondly, the Son’s nature moved, when the Heart of God became man—and that will never happen again in eternity; and even if it does happen <note>i.e., through spiritual rebirth in others</note>, it happens through that same single Man who is God, through many and in many. Thirdly, at the end of the world, the Holy Spirit's nature will move, when the world shall return to the <term>Ether</term> <note>A term for the refined, spiritual state of the universe after its purification.</note> and the dead shall rise. Thus the Holy Spirit will be the Mover, who will place all the great wonders that have occurred in this world into the eternal essence, for God's honor and wondrous deeds, and for the joy of the creatures; and He will be the eternal Mover of the creatures, such as angels and men, for through Him, Paradise—which we lost here—shall flourish again. Know, therefore, that the great wonders of the world, which had to happen, lie in our path.

<column-break/>

This world is a great wonder, and would never have been recognized by the angels in the Wisdom of God <note>referring to God's "Sophia" or mirror of ideas</note> alone. Therefore, the Father's nature moved toward the creation of substance, so that the great wonders would be revealed; and then they shall be recognized in eternity by angels and men—all that God held within His power. And the image of the Trinity—the Eternal Virgin, who stood in the <term>Holy Ternary</term> <note>original: "Ternario Sancto." A Böhmean term for the spiritual corporeality or the "holy earth" of the heavenly realm.</note>, in the eternal Wisdom, in the essence, as a figure—would never have been recognized by the angels in eternity, had the Heart of God not become man. There the angels saw the radiance of Majesty in a living image, in which the entire Trinity was enclosed.

Thus the <term>Center of Nature</term> <note>original: "Centrum Naturæ."</note> would also never have been revealed to the angels in eternity, much less the governance of the Holy Spirit, had this world with its stars and elements not been created. Thus the angels recognize the eternal essence with all its forms through this world, and we humans do as well; and for this reason, God created the image of the Trinity—as man—into this world, so that he should reveal all wonders and should recognize the eternal God.

<margin>Threefold Life 7. §. 21. 25. <note>Referencing Böhme’s *The Threefold Life of Man*.</note></margin>

From this we see how God raised up the <term>Third Principle</term> <note>The material, visible world.</note> so that He might be revealed through the material world. For since He had created the angels and spirits in the <term>Second Principle</term> <note>The Paradisiacal or Light world.</note>, they understood in the <term>Third Principle</term> the eternal birth, as well as the wisdom and omnipotence of God, in which they could mirror themselves and place their <term>imagination</term> <note>In this context, "imagination" refers to the focused creative or spiritual desire of a being.</note> into the Heart of God; in which form they remain in Paradise and as angels. This the devils did not do; instead, they intended to rise up in the <term>Matrix</term> <note>original: "Matrix." The generative source or "womb" of nature.</note> and rule with great power over Paradise and all angelic realms. Therefore they fell out of Paradise and were driven from their place into a narrowness, so that the <term>Matrix</term> of this world now holds them captive.

6. **Question:** Would God then not have revealed Himself according to the third <term>Principle</term> <note>original: "Principio." In the author's system, the "third principle" refers to the visible, material world.</note>, and not created this visible world, if Lucifer had not been created?

**Answer:** When God moved toward creation in the first <term>Matrix</term> <note>original: "Matrix." However, the Matrix stood entirely hidden with its dark, harsh, bitter, and fiery law; for the Light of God had preserved it bright and blissful from eternity. But when God moved toward creation, it became manifest.

Now, when God created mighty prince-angels, great and in the place of the fourth property in the Matrix—where the source of fire originates—they did not remain steadfast. They did not project their imagination forward into the fifth property, in which the offspring of Paradise stands; instead, they raised their imagination back into themselves and formed a will in the Matrix to rule in the fire over Paradise and the Light of God. For the fiery Matrix, as the abyss of hell, also moved strongly during creation; from this, Lucifer, the Grand Prince, drew his will and remained within it, intending to be a great and terrible lord himself in his entire place.

Thus the Devil moved the Matrix, and the fiery property moved the Devil, for it also wished to be creaturely <note>To have a distinct, individual existence as a created being.</note>, like all properties in the Matrix. Yet this runs contrary to the fifth property in the Matrix, where the lovely source of love rises in the gentle and bright light, in which the second Principle stands eternally.

When this storm occurred during creation in the first Principle, the Matrix stood considerably and greatly ignited,

<column-break/>

and every property in the Matrix was active. But because wrath and fierceness arose there, and this place could not remain in Paradise, God moved this place even more intensely within the Matrix, which became even more ignited. This became the Devil’s bath, and the fourth property stood in the flash of fire, which looked back into the Mother <note>The primal source or Matrix.</note> and found the Spirit of God in the process of formation. At that moment, it lost its fierce law in great joy, becoming white, bright, and clear. And in this place stands the <term>Fiat</term> <note>original: "Fiat." Latin for "Let it be"—the creative command of God described in Genesis.</note>, through which God created Heaven and Earth. For before the Fiat, the third Principle was not manifest, but only Paradise in the place of this world.

But when God saw that the Grand Prince Lucifer wanted to rule in the power of fire in the Matrix of this place, He closed off the fifth property in the Matrix of Paradise from him; for it was extinguished in its incorporeal form, and also externally. For when the Matrix became thin, dead, and overcome again by the rising light, it became materially water, as we see now. And in that same ignition before the light of the Sun—while the Matrix still stood in harsh wrath—the Matrix contracted the workings within the water-spirit, from which rocks and stones were formed, as well as the dark earth, which before the time of creation had been only a dust. In this hour, the third Principle arose: the fiery heaven in the fifth property of the Matrix through the Fiat, which God the Father spoke through His Heart or Son. This occurred through and in the outgoing of His Spirit, which hovered there over the Matrix and formed the fiery heaven in the fifth property of the Matrix, just as the precious Moses clearly writes of it. For the Matrix is, in its origin, the water-spirit in the first property; and when it became material in the place of this world, the Spirit hovered upon the waters in the heavenly Matrix.

The spirit of coarseness <note>original: "Grobheit." This refers to the density of physical matter compared to the subtlety of the spirit.</note> is in the life of poison, in which Lucifer is a prince of this world; however, the Heavenly realm holds the torment of poison and coarseness captive. Just as an angry, zealous person ignites his body with his wrath, so that it becomes dark, weak, trembling, tearing, stinging, and breaking, and his blood becomes coarse, thick, burnt, and tartaric <note>original: "tartarisch." In early modern chemistry and mysticism, this refers to the hard, stony sediment (tartar) found in wine casks, symbolizing spiritual impurity or hardening.</note>: so too did Lucifer corrupt his habitation, so that the qualities in his body and his kingdom rose up against the Right of Eternity. Through such elevation, the "qualification" <note>The way properties interact and manifest.</note> departed from its balanced temperament within the matter or essence of the body, and thus became partly water, and partly dark earth, hard stones, bones, and metals.

7. Question: We have now seen the single true working cause of the creation of this world, and also what Lucifer did therein and still does: does it now follow that we should also consider the working itself, or the Speaking, through which the eternally-speaking Word created the world?

Answer: We noted above how two Centers open themselves out of the single Will of GOD. The one, according to the property of Fire—the Will of GOD working therein—is called FATHER. The other, according to the property of Light—the Will of GOD working therein—is called SON. As soon as Lucifer elevated the first Center of the Fire-Matrix above the Light, all the subtle, pure, transparent matter or essence became coarse, dark, and hard. Depending on which property held the upper hand within that essence, that same essence took upon itself the working of the Word according to that property. Just as the sun is active in every creature and essence according to the property and form in which that essence is shaped—where it makes some things thin, some thick, some soft, some hard, some dry, and some wet with one and the same working power—so too does the Word work in each and every matter, essence, and creature. In one, the Fire (and therein the Wrath of GOD) has the upper hand and becomes manifest; in another, the Water (and therein the Light and Love of GOD) prevails.

<column-break/>

8. Question: Why does the author call such working power of GOD in his writings "FIAT"?

Answer: Our blessed author <note>Referring to Jacob Böhme (1575–1624), the German mystic whose work this text explains.</note> possessed such a treasure and richness of wisdom and knowledge that he was not always able to express himself with sufficient emphasis using our common ways of speaking. Therefore, he often made use of such little words that were somewhat uncommon. It seems that the Wisdom of GOD held its holy play within this simple, unlearned instrument <note>Böhme was a simple shoemaker by trade, often called an "unlearned instrument" of God.</note>, as the author took a particular liking to certain Latin terms and words, among which is this *Fiat*. In the Latin language, this means "Let it be" or "Let it happen." However, it is to be explained by us more according to "Natural Language" <note>original: "Natur-Sprach" or "Etymologia Naturali." The mystical belief that the very sounds and mouth-shapes of words reveal the hidden nature of the things they name.</note> than according to artificial grammar or the vain art of speech.

According to the Language of Nature, we first have the formation of the **F** in speaking. This letter is formed by a joining of the lower lips and the upper teeth, while the tongue nestles against the lower teeth. When the mouth stands in such a figure for speaking, the sound <note>original: "Hall."</note> goes out from the Depth, through the narrowly-contracted throat, and passes over the compacted tongue and through the shaped mouth as an **I**, whose signature among the Hebrews is <term>י</term> <note>The Hebrew letter Yod.</note> where the narrow throat is figured like a pipe.

This **I** is the Divine Mercury <note>original: "Mercurius." In this context, it refers to the spiritual principle of movement, sound, and life-force.</note> and Life-Spirit, proceeding from the active and desiring Will of GOD toward revelation. The gathering of the lower and upper lips and the narrowness of the mouth of GOD—through which the Mercury and sound rise from the Depth and are driven through—signifies the harsh, contracting, enclosing, and coagulating property of the Will of GOD toward revelation, according to the property of Light and Love; for from such "qualification" the two highest names, **Jehovah** and **JESUS**, take their origin.

Furthermore, the **I** is the signature of Unity among the Latins; but among the Hebrews, it signifies the Crown-Number **X** (10), where the Unity leads itself from the *Unground* into the *Ground* <note>The "Unground" (Ungrund) is Böhme's term for the absolute, undifferentiated nothingness/everything of God before creation; the "Ground" is the beginning of manifestation.</note>, through all the numbers of three-times-three, until it reaches its limit <note>original: "Terminum."</note> and Crown, namely the <term>†</term> <note>The cross, often used to symbolize the number ten or the intersection of dimensions.</note>, beyond which number one may not count, but begins again at Unity according to the custom of all nations. Thus we are to understand how the Spirit of GOD goes out from the Depth through the strict and narrow gates of the dark world, and carries out the hidden Will of GOD from Unity into the highest number through the properties of the ignition of Fire. ### 3rd Part / Chapter 2.

When the depth comes through the narrowness into freedom, as if into a revelation, it expands widely; the tongue becomes loose, the lips part from the lower teeth, the mouth opens, and the throat widens, so that the spirit from the depth echoes quite freely without any hindrance or shaping. This sound is called A. This is the first letter, and it presses forth from the heart; it has no specific "nature," but rather we clearly understand within it the longing of the eternal Will out of nature, in which nature is birthed—which has existed from eternity. For the Will desires the heart, and the heart desires the Will. It is Father and Son, and the power that proceeds from them is the Spirit of eternal life. Now, just as the A is born from the heart as from the eternal Will, and pushes out from the Will, so the entire alphabet with twenty-four numbers <note>The early modern German alphabet often counted 24 letters, frequently omitting J and U or treating them as variants of I and V.</note> follows from the A.

->Threefold Life 16. 44. 45.<-

The signature <note>In this context, "signature" refers to the spiritual essence or "brand" imprinted on a thing that reveals its inner character.</note> of the A among the Hebrews is א <note>Aleph</note>, where Father and Son, fire and water, are united through the eternal bond of unity into a single being. Among the Europeans, the signature is XX as <term>fire</term> <note>original: "Feuer"</note> and v, just as one births the other and one grasps the other, XX. Now this A, as the free Spirit proceeding from the heart of God toward revelation, is held back by the harsh and severe quality, and is grasped by the active Will of the Father with the tongue against the teeth, and is called At. This signifies the encompassing quality through which the active and speaking Word encompasses the Spirit of freedom. For the T in Latin, and the ת <note>Tav</note> in Hebrew, likewise designate such a compaction and enclosure of the sound and of Mercurius <note>original: "Mercurii." In alchemy and mysticism, Mercury represents the principle of sound, movement, and communication.</note>. Although the severe quality of the Word is very sharp in drawing together and tightening, holding the Spirit fast with the tongue against the teeth, it cannot bind the Spirit so tightly that a subtle H, breath, or spirit does not follow after the T.

We have wished to give this to the reader in our own words with all the details, to make it more clearly understood, so that he may recognize how the author uses this little word *Fiat* <note>Latin: "Let it be done."</note> in a far deeper sense and with far more emphasis than is perceived by the unlearned. And our modern "school-foxes" <note>original: "Schulfüchse." A derogatory term for pedantic academics who focus on rote learning over spiritual insight.</note> with their bare grammar should rather hide themselves in shame before the deep knowledge of the language of nature, instead of mocking this enlightened man of God in their lack of understanding; for Natural Etymology <note>original: "Etymologia Naturalis." The study of how sounds naturally correspond to the essence of things.</note> has a far firmer foundation than grammatical derivations, which rest upon a presumed "positive" <note>An arbitrary human convention rather than a natural law.</note> and then fall silent.

9. Question: Reason is accustomed to object here that, in such a way, the Hebrew language should express the true sense according to nature better than the Latin, and thus the little word יהי <note>Hebrew: "Yehi" (Let there be)</note> should come closer to the meaning of the Spirit than the Latin *Fiat*, since there is a great difference in the sound, formation, shaping, and signature?

Answer: No one should think that when God created the world, He spoke in the Hebrew language with expressed words, saying: *Let there be* <note>original: "JEHI FIAT"</note>; rather, when it says "GOD spoke," one understands the working of His almighty Word. Furthermore, it is not to be believed that the Hebrew language was spoken in ancient times, or written with such characters, exactly as we speak and write it today; rather, it is likely that it—just like all other languages in our times—has deviated greatly from its first foundation. Who would believe that Adam, after the Fall, possessed such an excellent sound and pronounced words as exactly as before the Fall, when the qualities within him stood in perfect balance <note>original: "Temperatur." The harmonious blending of spiritual forces.</note> and he spoke with an angelic and magical wonder-tongue whatever he spoke? Who would further believe that the Hebrew language remained so uncorrupted among the Hebrews during the general confusion of tongues, since they, just like all other peoples, deviated from the true service of God and became vain in their imaginings? Indeed, we have living experience of how languages change with the nations from one century to another, because the qualities are in a constant struggle, and now this one, now that one, gains the upper hand within a people. The ancient Germans would likely no longer understand our modern German language, and we Germans have difficulty grasping the old Saxon language. Therefore, no language is more emphatic, constant, or proper than the <term>Language of Nature</term> <note>original: "Natur-Sprache." The idea that there is a lost, universal language where words perfectly match the essence of the objects they describe.</note>, and the Spirit of Wisdom is not bound to any words or modes of speech in its instruments. For the Spirit gives each thing a name according to how it stands within itself at its birth, and as it formed itself in the beginning during creation; thus our mouth also forms it, according to how it was born out of the eternal Being and came into existence.

10. **Question:** Why, then, does the author everywhere call the working or speaking of the Word the "harsh, severe, sharp FIAT"?

**Answer:** Because the *Fiat* is properly the desire, the attraction, and the grasping of the Will of God according to both properties of fire and light, where these two centers exist in a powerful hunger to be revealed—especially since Lucifer ignited the dark world even more and sharpened its hunger even more powerfully.

In God, this world existed before time, but without substance. Now Lucifer, the Grand Prince, awakened and ignited the wrath and the fire from the center of nature, which had never been known in eternity; for he wished to rule over God in the power of fire, and thus the fire-torment became his dwelling. And here we understand the severe *Fiat* as the Mother of Nature, the harshness and hardness that was ignited in its severe power. From the center of nature, it contracted the essence of the wrathful matrix <note>original: "Matricis"</note> out of the innumerable essences. From this came earth and stone, and also metals; for the center was sulfur, mercury, and salt <note>These are the three "paracelsian" principles believed to be the base of all matter.</note>, and was only one spirit. But in the severe *Fiat*, through the harsh, wrathful attraction, it became hard—turning into stones, metals, and earth—all according to the essences of each form. Everything became material; what before time was only a fine dust in the nature of the dark, wrathful essence, all became coarse, thick, and hard through that attraction.

# Chapter III.
## Concerning the Creation of Heaven and Earth in the Beginning.

We have considered the working cause of creation and the revelation of this world—namely, the eternally-speaking, self-subsisting Word, GOD. We have also examined the speaking and working itself in the little word *Fiat* <note>original: "Fiat", Latin for "Let there be"</note>. Now follows the investigation of the "spoken word," or that which God brought forth through His almighty Word, from the words:

### In the beginning God created heaven and earth.

**1. Question.**
-> What then is called the Beginning? <-

**Answer.**

GOD Himself, as He leads Himself out of the eternal, beginningless **Groundless** <note>The "Ungrund" (Groundless) is a central concept in the mysticism of Jacob Böhme, referring to the absolute, undifferentiated abyss of the Divine before any manifestation or creation.</note> into a **Ground**, and as He is revealed from the incomprehensible **NOTHING** of eternal freedom and unity into the **SOMETHING** <note>original: "ICHTS". A wordplay on "Nichts" (Nothing); it signifies the emergence of being, ego, or manifestation.</note>. It is not as if God had a beginning for Himself, but rather His revelation has a beginning.

This world (says the author) makes a beginning; God in the **Trinity** <note>original: "Drey-Zahl", literally "Three-number"</note> is the beginning; and so also the world makes an end. That is eternity, and that is also GOD. For before this world, God alone was from eternity; but that we do not comprehend such a thing is because there is no "concept" in God. For where there is a concept, there is a beginning and an end; therefore we are enclosed in darkness so that we may labor and reveal GOD (which revelation has a beginning and an end).
<margin>Threefold Life 6. 47.</margin>

If the unfathomable, uncreated God, as the eternal **ONE**, no longer spoke His Word and the speaking ceased, then there would be no more understanding, reason, or senses, nor nature or creature, and all creatures would be an eternal Nothing. For all life originates from the "breathing out" of the eternal One, as if from the Groundless. There can be no formality in the eternal One according to which or out of which something came to be.

<column-break/>

For if there had been a form for a figure, there would have to have been a cause again from which the form had arisen, and God would not be a single God who is without ground, time, and place. For everything that has a beginning is grounded; but what has no beginning is without ground and form. All beginnings go out from the eternal One, whereby the eternal One introduces itself into a self-contemplation, sensitivity, and findability for its own self-movement and forming.

All visible and invisible beings, spiritual and corporeal, have taken their origin in the breathing out of the eternal One and stand with their ground within it. For the beginning of all beings is nothing other than an **imagination** <note>In this context, "imagination" refers to a creative, formative power of the divine will to visualize and then manifest reality.</note> of the Groundless, that the same introduces itself through its own desire into an imagination, models and forms it, and grasps the figurativeness, and breathes it out from the eternal One for its self-contemplation. This breathing is the eternal Word of the groundless Godhead, as a speaking of the Groundless into a Ground, of the un-essential into an essential, in which the entire creation took its beginning with the speaking—as in the differentiation of the speech—and still takes it continually.
<margin>Testaments ch. 1. 2. 6.</margin>

# Concerning the Beginning of Creation.

<margin>Beginning.</margin> Eternal things take their beginning from the single Will of God for the revelation of Himself, and the bringing forth from the **Groundless** <note>The "Ungrund" refers to the absolute, undifferentiated abyss of the Divine before manifestation.</note> into a **Ground**; temporal things, however, originate from the eternal and are an image and character [imprint] of the eternal. The visible world is a mirror of the invisible spiritual world. The spiritual world is a mirror of **Wisdom**; Wisdom is a mirror of the Godhead. Thus, each world is the beginning of the other.

Three **Principles** <note>original: "Principia", Latin for primary sources or origins</note> give birth to themselves in the Essence of all Essences, where each is the cause of the other; within these, one also understands a three-fold life, as three distinctions of Divine revelation.

First, the true Godhead in itself in **Trinity**, in the **Science** <note>original: "Scientz", from the Latin *scientia*; here meaning the inner knowledge, awareness, or potentiality of the Divine</note> of the Groundless in a single will, where God gives birth to God. Namely, the single will that leads itself into the Trinity is not a "Principle," for there is nothing before it; thus, it can have no beginning from anything, but is itself its own beginning: the **Nothing** and also its **Something**.

But in the **Word** of the single Divine power—where the single Science of the birth of the Trinity breathes itself out—there originates the beginning of the **first Principle** <note>original: "Principii"</note>. And yet, this is not in the ground of the **Speaking** (as the Trinity), but in the grasping [formulation] of distinction, where distinction encompasses itself in nature toward sensitivity and mobility. There, sensitivity divides into two essences: into the **Wrath** (according to the impression in the darkness) into a cold, painful fire wherein heat originates. There one understands the first Principle in the **Fire-Root**, which is the center of nature.

And the **second Principle** is understood in the separation of the fire, where the Divine Science separates itself in the fire into the **Light**. There, it has introduced itself into nature and essence for the revelation of the Divine kingdom of joy, where the Word of powers stands in an actual birthing, where the **Mind** <note>original: "Mens", Latin for mind or soul</note> works into the **Being** <note>original: "Ens", Latin for essence or being</note>. There is the separation between two Principles, where God—according to the

The **third Principle** is understood in the seven days of work, where the seven properties of nature introduced themselves into the seventh into an essence for tangibility [comprehensibility]. This essence is in itself holy, pure, and good, and is called the eternal, uncreated heaven, as the dwelling place of God, or the Kingdom of God; likewise <note>original: "item"</note> Paradise, the pure element, the Divine **Being** <note>original: "Ens"</note>, or whatever one might call it according to its property.

This same single essence of the Divine working, which has ever been from eternity, God has grasped and moved with the Science of His groundless will, and encompassed it into the Word of His speaking. He spoke it out of the first Principle of the painful dark fire-world and out of the holy light-flaming love-world, as a pre-modeling of the inner spiritual world.

# Of the Beginning of Creation.

...just as it has formed and shaped itself from eternity within the Wisdom / so too is it formed in a particular life / for the glory and joy of the Holy Spirit / in the Word of life within itself.

And therefore God, in the eternal **Science** <note>The inner awareness or "knowingness" of the divine</note> of the eternal unfathomable Will / created angels out of both fires / namely, from the fire of Nature and from the fire of Love / although the fire of Love cannot produce a creature [on its own] / but rather it dwells within the creature / and fills it / as the sun fills the world / or nature / in the time of the world / so that the Holy Spirit might thus have a play of joy within itself.

<margin>Grace 4. 6. 20. <note>Likely a reference to Böhme’s work "On the Election of Grace"</note></margin>

**2. Question: Can the "Beginning" then also be understood as a beginning of time?**

**Answer:** The beginning of this visible world is actually the first movement of the working Word / toward the revelation of God according to the third **Principle** <note>The physical/material realm</note>. This movement occurred / when the Prince Michael fought with the Dragon / and the Dragon was cast out from heaven onto the earth. Whereby the earth became waste and void / of which we will speak in its proper place.

**3. Question: What does the author actually mean by the word "Creation"?**

**Answer:** By the word "Creation" <note>original: "Schaffen"</note> the author does not mean so much / bringing something out of nothing / or out of a "non-being" <note>original: "non ente"</note>; just as the word **"Created"** <note>original: "Barah" (Hebrew: בָּרָא)</note> in the Hebrew language has no such meaning / as could be proven with many scriptural passages / which even today’s theologians do not deny. Human **Reason** says that God made this world out of nothing. **Response:** There was indeed no substance or matter for it that was outwardly tangible, but there was such a form within the eternal power and the **Will**. The creation of this world occurred through an awakening of the **Will-Spirit**: The inner Will, which otherwise stands within itself, stirred its own nature—acting as the **Center** <note>original: "Centrum," the focal point of divine or natural energy</note>, which is that which desires out of itself—and as the **Light**, which presses outward from that Center. Thus, the Center grasped a substance out of itself through its own **Desire**. That is, it grasped or fashioned a substance for itself within its own **Imagination** <note>In Böhme’s thought, "Imagination" is the creative power of the mind or spirit to give form to desire</note>, in the longing, and also seized the substance of the Light along with it.

The **Elements** <note>original: "Elementa"</note>, which are the four forms appearing in the essence, were cast out from the **Holy Ternary** <note>original: "Ternario Sancto," referring to the divine triad or the sacred three-fold nature of God</note> into the external world. There is no mixing in the **Essence** <note>original: "Essenz"</note>; rather, one receives the other in desire, and the Light dwells in the fire's desire. It is not the Eternal itself, but rather it has become an essence within the eternal desire. The desire has revealed itself and led into an essence, just like the Eternal.

The Heaven where God dwells is everywhere, in all places, even in the middle of the earth. He encompasses Hell where the devils dwell; there is nothing outside of God. When your spirit lays hold of the **innermost birth** <note>the deepest, spiritual layer of reality where God is present</note> of God and penetrates through the sidereal <note>the astral or star-influenced layer of nature</note> and the fleshly births, then it is already in Heaven. THAT the place <note>original: "Locus"</note> of this world, in its innermost birth, inter-operates <note>original: "inqualiret," a Böhmean term meaning to share qualities or act in union</note> with the Heaven above us, and is one Heart, one Essence, one Will, one GOD, all in all. That is to say: the outermost birth of this world cannot grasp the outermost birth of the Heaven above this world, for they are like life and death to one another, or like a man and a stone to one another.

Therefore, there is a firm closure between the outermost birth of the upper Heaven and this world; for the **firmament** <note>original: "Feste," referring to the biblical barrier between the waters or realms</note> between them is **Death**, which rules at all ends in the outermost birth of this world. And for this reason, we cannot see the angels in our outermost birth, and the angels also cannot dwell with us in the outermost birth of this world—yet in the **innermost** birth, they do dwell with us. And when we fight with the Devil, they intercept his blows in the innermost birth and are the protection of holy souls. Thus, we cannot see or grasp the angels, because the outermost birth of their bodies is incomprehensible to the outermost birth of this world.

But now the Holy Spirit also rules in the second birth and helps to bring forth the third, Holy birth.
