### Part 3, Chapter 3.

...does not consist in freedom, but remains in the torment of that which it has awakened or made within itself; understand this as being from the Center of Nature <note>original Latin: "Centro Naturæ"</note>, based on what it has introduced into the will of freedom. Thus, that one thing will be a torment to it, a gnawing or a repugnance that it has birthed for itself out of its own nature. By this, it has darkened its own freedom so that the light cannot shine through; that shall be its darkness. For where the will is dark, there the being of the will—acting as its body—is also dark; and where the will is in torment, there the body is also in torment. For this reason, the children of the Light of freedom are separated from the children of darkness in the agony of torment, each into their own Principle <note>original: "Principium"</note>.

Thus, we further give you to understand that every Principle brings forth its own life according to its property; but the Fire is the dividing line that satisfies the two eternal Principles, namely Darkness and Light. To the Darkness, the fire gives its sting and its woe; and to the Light, it gives its sensitivity and its life.

In the same way, the third Principle <note>the physical, material world</note> also has two properties: heat and cold. Heat is the principle that gives its sting and woe to the cold, while to the light it gives life and sensitivity. The light, in turn, gives its essence to the fire so that it may be joined with it in a friendly way. The cold also gives its property and essence to the fire, but the fire breaks it apart and turns its essence into death and dying. Therefore, there is always an enmity between heat and cold, and they never become one. Yet, through this enmity, they achieve this: that life must flourish through death. For from heat and cold comes the growth of the third Principle (in which we live externally). From the cold comes fruit from the earth, as well as the bodies of all creatures and the substance within the elements; from the heat, out of their strife, comes the life into the bodies of all creatures

<column-break/>

and plants, just as in the depth of the elements it provides the Spirit of the Great World <note>the "Spiritus Mundi," or the soul of the physical universe</note> in various figures. For where the cold creates substance, the heat creates a spirit within it. Thus, all of existence is in a struggle, so that the wonders of the eternal world may be revealed within fragility, and that the eternal model in the Wisdom of God may be expressed in figures. These models shall stand eternally in the eternal Magic <note>original: "Magia"</note> and Mystery <note>original: "Mysterio"</note> as God's wonders, for the joy of angels and men—not as physical substance, but in the Magic and Mystery as a shadow of the essence, so that it may be eternally known what God has wrought and what He is able to do.

For after the breaking of this world, only the Eternal remains in essence: eternal spirits with the eternal substance of their bodies, along with the wonders performed here, which stand magically in their figures. By these, the spirits shall recognize God’s wondrous deeds and power.

6. **Question:** What kind of being, substance, and matter is the innermost birth or the Heaven that was created by GOD in the beginning?

**Answer:** This Heaven is called *Schammajim* <note>original: "Schammajim"; a Hebrew word for the Heavens</note> by the ancient Hebrews, from *aesch* and *maiim* <note>original: "æsch und maiim"; Hebrew for 'fire' and 'water'</note>, Fire and Water, or *Schammah-Maiim*, meaning "there is water." It is actually nothing other than a spiritual water. Our contemporary philosophers call it the proximate matter <note>original: "materia proxima"</note>, the matter of the first Element, and it is actually the best kernel, the marrow, the root, and the mother of all matter. In and of itself, it is universal, without any limit <note>original: "Terminum"</note>, from which every source-spirit <note>original: "Quell-Geist"; in Böhme’s thought, these are the seven active qualities or "fountain-spirits" of divine nature</note> can shape, limit, and specify its own particular form. If the "harsh" quality predominates within it, then gemstones, diamonds, crystals, and salts are formed from it. If the "bitter" quality is the primary one, then it is like a volatile, penetrating spiritual water. If the "fire" is the master, it becomes so volatile and driving that it is like a subtle, highly exalted spirit that does not become tangible or bodily, but flies in the air like a subtle dust. If "gentleness" gains the upper hand, this is the glassy sea, and the middle or the kernel of the waters, from which GOD made the lower or coarser heavens through His almighty Word. It is the single element from which the other four elements flowed forth as a sunken essence, according to the four qualities of nature. In itself, it is neither hot nor cold, neither dry nor wet; it is the weaving or the life of the inner heaven, the true angelic life according to the creature. It is the first divine revelation of nature out of the fire; when the qualities of the eternal nature work within it, it is called Paradise.

<margin>Mysterium Magnum <note>The Great Mystery, Böhme's commentary on Genesis</note> chapter 10, verse 49.</margin>

7. **Question:** What then is actually the Earth, which GOD created in the beginning?

**Answer:** The Earth, which GOD created through His almighty Word in the beginning, is nothing other than a gently contracted, subtly coagulated and dry Heaven. Everything that is mercurial, volatile, and thin in Heaven is fixed, tangible, and thick in the Earth. By "Heaven" we are

<column-break/>

to understand the operation of the seven source-spirits of nature, which work and operate within one another in a friendly manner, and through their working they give birth to the seventh as their body, in which they take shape. This body resembles a crystal and dry water, which is why contemporary philosophers maintain that the Earth was a transparent star before it was cursed by GOD and corrupted by Adam. Our author calls this Earth the *Salitter* <note>Salitter: a term Böhme used to describe the "divine salt" or the fundamental substance of the divine realm; not to be confused with common saltpeter</note>. This Salitter is a purely generative <note>original: "spermatischer"; meaning seed-like or full of potential</note> ground, where every being longs for the other—the upper for the lower, the lower for the upper. The former pours out the heavenly seed with great power; the seed is accepted by the Earth with great desire, and from this grow purely heavenly fruits and figures, which were the delightful food of the angels. The ancients called the qualities of this Earth Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury <note>original: "Sal, Sulphur und Mercurius"; the "Three Principles" of alchemy representing stability, combustibility, and volatility</note>. The Earth is universal in itself, pure and virginal, being neither this nor that. But if the "harsh" quality predominates, it brings forth this Earth as Salt; if the "bitter" quality has the upper hand, it brings forth Mercury or the water-spirit; and if the "anguish-quality," it brings forth Sulfur. Within this ground also lie the four elements, and they are not separated from it as something special; they are only the revelation of such a spiritual ground, like a casing for the spirit, in which the spirit works in a heavenly way as if in its own body.

This visible world with all its host and being is nothing other than a counter-reflection <note>original: "Gegen-Wurff"; a projection or mirror image</note> of the spiritual world, which is hidden within this material, elemental world, just as the tincture <note>tincture: the spiritual essence or "soul" of a substance in alchemy</note> is hidden in herbs and metals. And just as the tincture, with its virtue and its outflow, forms and makes itself visible in all things—so that one can see and recognize by the shape, as well as the colors and smell, what kind of "Separator" <note>separator: the divine or natural agent that divides and organizes chaos into specific forms</note> or outflow of the Divine Will has flowed out of the Great Mystery <note>original: "Mysterio Magno"</note>—so too can one recognize the inner ground from which it sprang by looking at the visible world, the sun, stars, elements, creatures, or all created things.

For no thing or essence of a thing has come to its place from afar; rather, its ground is in the very place where it grows. The elements have their cause within themselves, from which they spring; likewise also have...

Through and in all three births in this world, He is present in all spaces and places. He grasps, holds, and sustains everything as the newborn Son of the Father, possessing the power and sitting upon the throne of the once great and mighty—but now cast out, cursed, and damned—King Lucifer, the devil.

Therefore, child of man, do not be so fearful and discouraged when, in your zeal and earnestness, you sow your seeds of tears.

<column-break/>

You do not sow them on earth, but in heaven. For in your sidereal birth you sow, and in the animal <note>original: "animalischen"; refers to the physical, sensory life of the body</note> birth you reap, and in the kingdom of heaven you possess and enjoy the fruit. Because you live in this birth of conflict, you must bow down and let the devil ride upon you; but as hard as he strikes you, you strike him back just as hard, provided you defend yourself. For when you struggle against him, you stir up his fire of wrath and destroy his nest—it is then like a great riot, as if you were fighting a mighty battle against him.

And even if your body suffers some pain, he suffers much worse. When he is overcome, he roars like a lion whose cubs have been stolen, for the grimness and wrath of GOD torment him. But if you welcome him into your "inn" <note>the "inn" or "lodging" refers to the human soul or heart</note>, he becomes fat and lewd, and in time, he overcomes you.

Thus you have a true description of heaven. Even if you cannot grasp it with your reason, I can grasp it quite well. Yet, think about it reasonably: what is GOD? In this world, you see nothing but the "Depth," within which are the stars and the birth of the elements. Would you then say that GOD is not there? Dear friend, what was in that place before the time of this world? If you say "nothing," you speak without reason; you must say that GOD was there, otherwise nothing would have come to be. If GOD was there then, who has pushed Him away or overcome Him so that He is no longer there? But if GOD is there, then He is surely in His heaven, and moreover, in His Trinity. The devil, however, has ignited the "bath of wrath," which is why the earth and stones—and the elements as well—have become so volatile, and so cold, bitter, and hot, and have murdered the outermost birth.

->*Aurora*, Chapter 19, paragraphs 23, 44.<-

Just as man, through sin, corrupted his paradisical body and [took on] a gross, animal...

# On the Beginning of Creation

...have <note>Completing the word "haben" from the previous page</note> put on a tangible body of animal flesh and blood—the body of death—in which the sidereal <term>sidereal: referring to the "astral" or "starry" influence that shapes physical life</term> birth is active.

6. **Question:** What then is the innermost birth or the Heaven, which was created by GOD in the beginning, in terms of its essence, substance, and matter?

**Answer:** This Heaven is called *Schammajim* <note>original: "Schammajim" from Hebrew שמים (Shamayim)</note> by the ancient Hebrews, from *Esh* <note>original: "Æsch" (Fire)</note> and *Mayim* <note>original: "Maiim" (Water)</note>, or *Schammah-Maiim*—which means "there is water." It is actually nothing other than a spiritual water. Our contemporary philosophers call it the *materia proxima* <note>original: "materia proxima," meaning the "nearest matter" or the immediate substance of things</note>, the matter of the first element, and it is actually the best kernel, the marrow, the root, and the mother of all matter. In and of itself, it is universal, without any limit; from it, every source-spirit <term>source-spirit: "Quell-Geist" in German; the primary formative forces or qualities of nature</term> can shape, limit, and specify its own particular form. If the "harsh" quality predominates within it, then gemstones, diamonds, crystals, and salts are formed from it. If the "bitter" quality is primary, it is like a volatile, penetrating spiritual water. If the fire is the master, it becomes so volatile and driving that it is like a subtle, highly exalted spirit that does not become tangible or bodily, but flies in the air like a subtle dust. If gentleness gains the upper hand, this is the "glassy sea" and the center or kernel of the waters, from which GOD made the lower or coarser heavens through His almighty Word. It is the single element from which the other four elements flowed out as a "sunken" essence, according to the four properties of nature. In itself, it is neither hot nor cold, neither dry nor wet; it is the weaving or the life of the inner heaven—the true angelic <note>original: "englische," which in this context means "angelic" rather than "English"</note> life according to the creaturely state. It is the first divine revelation of nature out of the fire; when the properties of eternal nature work within it, it is called Paradise.

<margin>Mysterium Magnum, Chapter 10, verse 49.</margin>

7. **Question:** What then is actually the Earth, which GOD created in the beginning?

**Answer:** The Earth, which GOD created through His almighty Word in the beginning, is nothing other than a gently contracted, subtly coagulated and dried Heaven. Everything that is mercurial, volatile, and thin in Heaven is fixed, tangible, and thick in the Earth. By "Heaven," one is

<column-break/>

to understand the qualifying of the six source-spirits of nature, which work and qualify in one another in a friendly manner, and through their working, they give birth to the seventh as their body, in which they take their shape. This body resembles a crystal and dry water; therefore, contemporary philosophers also maintain that the Earth was a transparent star before it was cursed by GOD and corrupted by Adam. Our author calls this Earth the *Salitter* <term>Salitter: Böhme’s term for the divine-natural substance or "sap" of the universe, a spiritual saltpeter</term>. This *Salitter* is a purely spermatic ground, where every essence longs for the other: the upper for the lower, the lower for the upper. The upper pours out the heavenly seed with great power; the seed is received by the Earth with great desire, and from it arise purely heavenly fruits and figures, which were the joyful food of the angels. The ancients called the properties of this Earth Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury <note>original: "Sal, Sulphur und Mercurius," the three principles of alchemy</note>. The Earth is universal in itself, pure and virginal, neither this nor that. But if the harsh quality predominates, it gives birth to this Earth as Salt; if the bitter quality has the upper hand, it produces Mercury or the Water-spirit; and if the "anguish-source" <note>original: "Angst-Quall"</note> predominates, it produces Sulfur. In this ground also lie the four elements, and they are not separated from it as something distinct; they are only the revelation of such a spiritual ground, like a casing for the spirit, in which the spirit works in a heavenly way as if in its own body.

This visible world, with all its host and essence, is nothing else but a counter-projection <note>original: "Gegen-Wurff," a reflection or shadow-image</note> of the spiritual world, which is hidden within this material, elemental world, just as the Tincture <term>Tincture: the inner spiritual essence or life-force that gives things their quality and color</term> is hidden in herbs and metals. And just as the Tincture, with its virtue and its outflow, shapes itself and makes itself visible in all things—so that one can see and recognize by the shape, as well as the colors and scent, what kind of "Separator" <note>The force that distinguishes and separates qualities</note> or outflow of the Divine Will has flowed out of the *Mysterium Magnum* <note>The "Great Mystery" or the unmanifested source of all existence</note>—so also one can recognize the inner ground from which it sprang by looking at the visible world: the sun, stars, elements, creatures, and all created things.

For no thing or essence of a thing has come to its place from afar; rather, its ground is in the very place where it grows. The elements have their cause within themselves, from which they spring. So also...

### Part 3 / Chapter 3

...have <note>Completing the word "haben" from the previous page</note> the stars their chaos <note>original: "Chaos"; in this context, the primordial, unformed state of matter or the "atmosphere" unique to a celestial body</note> within themselves, in which they stand.

The elements are nothing other than a figurative, moving essence of the invisible, unmoving one: Likewise, the stars are an outflow of the properties of the spiritual world, according to the distinction of the <term>Separator: original Latin "Separatoris"; the divine agent or force that divides the unified source into distinct things</term>, whose foundation is the **WORD** or the distinguishing will of **GOD**.

The essence and movement of the elements is Fire, Air, Water, and Earth; within them are thick and thin, wet and dry, hard and soft. These are composed into one being—not that each has a separate origin and beginning, but they all come from a single foundation. And the very place they come from is everywhere. One need only consider how in each place a greater ignition occurred according to one property more than another; from this, the movement became greater and the matter in such form and essence became more abundant than in another place—as can be understood from the materials of the Earth, as well as the Water and the Air, and how a distinction exists at each pole and in every place upon the Earth. From this also comes the difference in customs and virtues, as well as in governments, order, and creatures.

The separation of these properties all arose out of the <term>Great Mystery: original Latin "Mysterio Magno"; the primordial source or "chaos" from which all creation emerges</term> through the single movement of the powers of all beings. This occurred when the single will of all beings moved at once and led out of imperceptibility into the perceptibility and distinctness of powers, making the eternal power active and willing, so that in every power an "opposite-projection" <note>original: "Gegen-Wurff"; Böhme's term for a reflection or an objectified counter-image of the divine will</note>—as an individual desire—arose. This same individual desire in the opposite-projection of the powers led itself out again into an opposite-projection; through this, the desire of such an outflow became sharp, harsh, and coarse, and it coagulated and turned into matter. And as the outflow of the inner powers from Light and

<column-break/>

Darkness, from sharpness and gentleness, or from a fiery or light-like nature; so too did the materials become. The further the outflow of a power extended, the more external and coarse the matter became; for one opposite-projection proceeded from the next, until finally reaching the coarse Earth. But we must rightly complete and indicate the foundation of such philosophy: where "Hard" and "Soft" took their foundation, which we recognize in the metals. For every material that is hard—such as metals and stones, as well as wood, herbs, and the like—has within itself a truly noble <term>Tincture: original Latin "Tinctur"; the spiritual essence or "coloring" power that gives a substance its life and quality</term> and a high spirit of power, as can also be recognized in the bones of creatures. The noblest tincture according to the power of the Light—the greatest sweetness—lies in the marrow of the bones, whereas in the blood there lies only a fiery tincture, such as in <term>Sulfur</term>, <term>Salt</term>, and <term>Mercury</term> <note>These three substances—Sulfur, Salt, and Mercury—were known in alchemy as the "Tria Prima," the three primary principles of all matter</note>. This is understood as follows:

**GOD** is the eternal One, as the greatest gentleness, insofar as He is within Himself, outside of His movement and revelation. But His movement—in which He is called a **God** in <term>Trinity: original "Dreyfaltigkeit"</term>, as a triune being, where one speaks of Three and yet only of One, and where He is called the eternal Power and Word—this is the precious and highest foundation. One should reflect on how the Divine Will encloses itself into a place of "Selfhood" as power, and works within itself, yet through its working it goes out and makes for itself an "opposite-projection"—which is <term>Wisdom: original "Weißheit"</term>—through which the foundation and origin of all beings has sprung. Likewise, know this: everything that is soft, gentle, and thin in the essence of this world is out-flowing and self-giving. Its foundation and origin is according to the Unity of Eternity, for the Unity evermore flows out from itself—just as one understands no perceptibility or pain in the essence of "thinness," such as Water and Air, which that essence is solely within itself.

# Of the Beginning of Creation.

But whatever is hard and compressed—such as bones, wood, herbs, metals, fire, earth, stones, and similar materials—within these lies the image of Divine Power and Movement. It locks itself away with its <term>Separator: original Latin "Separatore"; the internal agent or "divider" that directs the outflow of divine energy into specific physical forms</term>, (as the outflow of Divine Desire) like a noble jewel or spark of Divine Power, protected from coarseness. It is hard and fiery for this reason: it has its foundation in Divine Incomprehensibility, where the eternal One ever introduces itself into a foundation of the Trinity to move the powers. Yet, it closes itself off against the outflow—that is, against the introduction of nature's own self-will—and works through nature with the power of Unity.

This is also how we must understand the noble <term>Tincture: in alchemical philosophy, the spiritual essence or "soul" of a substance that gives it its virtues</term>; where it is most noble, it is most tightly locked away within hardness. For within it, Unity exists in a state of mobility, as a sensitivity of operation, which is why it hides itself. But in thinness <note>meaning subtle or fluid substances</note>, it does not exist in such sensitivity, but is equal to all things; just as water and air are equal to all things and are in all things. But the "dry water" is the true <note>original: "Perlen-Grund"; literally "pearl-foundation," referring to the crystalline, pure essence found at the heart of matter</note> foundation of pearls, wherein the subtle power of the operation of Unity lies in the center. We indicate this to our own who are worthy of it: do not occupy yourselves with seeking the mystery in what is soft and lacks a fiery nature. Thus, understand this mystery:

<column-break/>

That the soft and the thin originated from the Unity and its outflow from the <term>Great Mystery: original Latin "Mysterio Magno"; the primordial "womb" or chaos from which all things were created</term>, and are closest to the Unity. Conversely, the noblest foundation of Divine Revelation in power and operation lies within the fiery hardness; it is a "dry unity," serving as a <note>original: "Temperamentum"; a balanced state where opposing qualities are perfectly harmonized</note> temperament, wherein the distinctiveness of all powers is again contained. For where the powers lie within the distinctiveness of the will, there the will is divided, and there is no great power in that thing because the Tincture is too volatile. Physicians should take good note of this: that they should not look to spirits of strong scent, etc.

->See <note>original Latin: "Beschau l. c. 3. 34. 48."; likely a citation for *loco citato* (in the place cited), referring to another part of the author's work</note><-

From which it can be seen how, from this single universal earth, a thousand kinds of materials and plants come forth.

**8. Question:** Are then Heaven and Earth, which God created in the beginning, not distinguished <note>original: "localiter"; by location or physical space</note> spatially, that is, according to place and certain boundaries?

**Answer:** This Heaven operates according to the property of the six <term>Source-Spirits: original German "Quell-Geister"; the seven fundamental qualities of divine nature that produce all existence</term> in a spiritual, masculine, and fiery manner, which is why it is called Heaven. The Earth is the seventh; this one is born from the six and receives the seed-powers of Heaven like a mother. It contains the qualification of the six Source-Spirits within itself; these always give birth to the seventh. Heaven gives birth to the Earth, and the Earth to the Heaven; neither is outside the other or without the other. Thus, they are not distinguished <note>original: "localiter"</note> spatially, but <note>original: "formaliter"; in their form or essential nature</note> formally. Heaven is a volatile Earth, and the Earth is, so to speak, a fixed Heaven.

# Chapter IV.
## How the Earth, which GOD created in the Beginning, became formless and empty. Likewise: Concerning the darkness over the face of the deep, and concerning the spirit hovering over the waters, from Genesis 1, verse 2.

->**1. Question.**<-
How did it happen then, that the earth, which GOD created in the beginning, became <term>formless and empty: original German "öde und leer"; the traditional phrasing for the state of the world before the light was brought forth</term>?

->**Answer.**<-
We have already partially mentioned this above—namely, through the fall of Lucifer. As soon as this magnificent angel turned his <term>Imagination: the creative power of the will and mind</term> away from the gentleness and humility of GOD, the <term>Source-Spirits: original "Quell-Geister"; the seven foundational divine forces that flow through all of nature</term> of his being rose up in such a way that his entire <note>original Latin: "Corpus"</note> body, and consequently his entire kingdom, was altered and inflamed. This can be seen in an angry person: the fire rises in their gall, the blood ignites, and then it strikes through all their limbs so that their entire body trembles, their face turns pale, the eyes grow rigid with venom and fury, and their sound and speech echo with thundering, snapping, and crashing. In this same way, Lucifer corrupted his kingdom.

->**2. Question. In what does such a mighty and great corruption actually consist?**<-

**Answer.** To reveal this with more detail, we must investigate: 1. how the earth was in the beginning before Lucifer’s fall, and 2. how it became through Lucifer’s fall. Our author shows both points very thoroughly in *Aurora*, chapter 17, dealing with the lamentable and miserable condition of corrupted nature and the origin of the four elements in place of the Holy Government of GOD.

"Although," he says, "GOD is an eternal, almighty Ruler whom no one can withstand, nature has now received a strange government through its ignition—one that did not exist before the times of <term>Wrath: the "dark" or "fiery" side of God's power that manifests when nature is out of balance</term>. For before the times of wrath, the six Source-Spirits birthed the seventh Nature-Spirit in the <note>original Latin: "Loco"</note> place of this world in a complete and lovely way, just as happens now in heaven, and not a single spark of wrath had risen within it." Furthermore, everything 

<column-break/>

within it was entirely light, and yet it needed no other light; rather, the fountain-spring of the Heart of GOD illuminated everything. It was a light in all things, shining everywhere, indissoluble and unstoppable. For nature was then entirely <note>original: "dünne"; meaning subtle, spiritualized, or non-dense</note> thin, and everything consisted only in Power, existing in a truly lovely <term>Temperance: a state of perfect balance and harmony between opposing forces</term>. But as soon as the struggle in nature began with the proud devils, then in the seventh Nature-Spirit—in the <note>original: "Revier"; meaning territory or district</note> region of Lucifer, which is the place of this world—everything took on a different form and operation. For nature then received a double source, and every outermost birth in nature was ignited in the fire of wrath—a fire which is now called the WRATH OF GOD, or the burning hell.

To understand this requires the innermost sense, located where the light is born in the heart; only this sense perceives it, while the outer man does not understand it.

See, when Lucifer and his host awakened the fire of wrath in the nature of GOD—so that GOD was moved to anger in nature within the place of Lucifer—the outermost birth in nature took on a different quality: entirely fierce, harsh, cold, hot, bitter, and sour. The surging spirit, which previously had functioned with fine gentleness in nature, became quite violent and terrifying in its outermost birth. Because of its upheaval, this is now called "the Wind" or the element of Air in this outermost birth.

For when the seven spirits ignited in their outermost birth, they gave birth to a—

...such a hard-surging spirit: Thus also the sweet water—which before the times of wrath was entirely thin and <term>intangible: original German "unbegreifflich"; meaning spiritual or non-physical</term>—became entirely thick and substantial. The harsh quality became very sharp and cold-fiery, for it acquired a severe contraction similar to salt.

For the salt-water or salt, which is still found in the earth today, has its origin and descent from the first ignition of the harsh quality. The stones also have their beginning and origin from this, as does the earth. ### Now the question arises:
### How then did a tangible son come from an intangible mother?

You have a likeness of this in how the earth and stones came from intangibility. Look, the depth between heaven and earth is also intangible, yet the qualities of the elements nevertheless produce a living and tangible flesh within it at various times, such as locusts, flies, and worms.

This is caused by the severe contractions of the qualities, in which life then immediately gives birth to itself within that contracted Salitter. For when heat ignites the harsh quality, life arises, because the bitter quality—which is the origin of life—moves itself.

In the same manner, the earth and stones also have their origin; for when

the Salitter ignited in nature, everything became entirely rough, thick, and dark, like a thick, dark mist, which the harsh quality dried out with its coldness. Because of this, another creation of light had to follow; otherwise, the earth would be an eternal, insoluble death. Now, however, she brings forth her fruit by the power and ignition of the created light.

You cannot grasp or understand this better than by looking at your own body. Through the first fall of Adam, with all its birth, skill, and will, the body has become such a house as the <term>location of this world: original Latin "Loco dieser Welt"; referring to the physical universe as a specific "place" or dimension</term> has become.

First, you have the animal flesh; it became so through the "lustful bite" <note>A reference to Adam eating the forbidden fruit</note>, for it is the house of corruption.

When Adam was made from the corrupted Salitter of the earth—that is, from the seed or <note>original Latin: "Massa"</note> mass which the Creator drew from the corrupted earth—he was not at first such a flesh. Otherwise, his body would have been created mortal. Instead, he had an <term>angelic power-body: original German "englischen Krafft-Leib"; "englisch" here means angelic, not the English language</term>. In this body, he was meant to exist eternally and eat of angelic fruit, which grew for him in Paradise before his fall, before the LORD cursed the earth.

### Part 3 / Chapter 4

But because the seed or the <term>mass: original German "Massa"; refers to the raw substance or "clay" from which humanity was formed</term> from which Adam was made was somewhat infected with the devil’s corrupt craving, Adam lusted after his mother—that is, he desired to eat from the fruit of the corrupted earth. This earth had become evil in its external <term>tangibility: original German "Begreifflichkeit"; the state of being solid, physical, or "graspable" as opposed to spiritual</term> and had become so harshly tangible within the <term>wrath-fire: the dark, fierce, or "angry" aspect of divine nature that provides the energy for material existence</term>. But because Adam’s spirit lusted after such fruit, which was like the corrupted earth, Nature also fashioned a tree for him that was like the corrupted earth. For Adam was the heart within Nature; therefore, his <term>animal spirit: the vital, breathing soul-power that connects the mind to the physical body</term> also helped to form this tree from which he wished to eat.

But when the devil saw that this lust was in Adam, he confidently struck at the <term>Salitter: the fundamental divine "sap" or essence of nature</term> within Adam, infecting the Salitter from which Adam was made even more severely. Then it was time for the Creator to build him a woman, who afterwards put the sin into action and ate from the false fruit. Otherwise, had Adam eaten from the tree before the woman was made from him, it would have gone even worse. But because this requires a very high and deep description for which much space is needed, look for it under the "Fall of Adam," where you will find it described in detail. I now return to the comparison I intended.

Now, when Adam ate of the fruit that was both evil and good, he soon acquired such a body. The fruit was corrupt and tangible—just as all fruits on earth are today—and Adam and Eve immediately acquired such a fleshly and tangible body. But the flesh is not the whole human being, for this flesh cannot hold or grasp the <term>Godhead: the essential nature or essence of God</term>; otherwise, the flesh would not be mortal and subject to decay. For Christ says in John 6:63: <note>original: "Der Geist ist das Leben / das Fleisch ist kein nütze."</note> *The Spirit is life; the flesh is of no use.* This flesh cannot inherit the kingdom of heaven; rather, it is only a seed sown into the earth, from which an intangible body will grow again, just as

<column-break/>

the first one was before the Fall. The spirit, however, is the eternal life which <term>works within the qualities: original German "inqualiret"; a term describing how the spirit harmonizes or interacts with the fundamental forces of nature</term> with God, and grasps the inner Godhead within Nature.

Now, just as man is corrupted in his external self and is, by his fleshly birth, within the wrath of God—and even an enemy of God—and yet is only a single person and not two; so, conversely, in his spiritual birth, he is a child and heir of God who rules and lives with God, working within the innermost birth of God. This is also how the <note>original: "Locus"; Latin for "place" or "location"</note> place of this world has now become.

The external tangibility in the whole nature of this world and all things that are within it all stand in the wrath-fire of God. For it became so through the "ignition" of Nature; and Lord Lucifer with his angels now has his dwelling in that same external birth which stands in the wrath-fire. But the Godhead is not divided from the external birth so that there would be two separate things in this world; otherwise, man would have no HOPE, nor would this world stand within the power and love of God. Rather, the Godhead is hidden within the external birth and has the <term>winnowing shovel: a biblical metaphor (Matthew 3:12) for the tool used to separate grain from chaff</term> in hand; He will one day throw the chaff and the ignited Salitter into a heap and withdraw His inner birth from it, giving such things to Lord Lucifer and his followers as an eternal house.

In the meantime, Lord Lucifer must lie captive in the outermost birth in the nature of this world, within the ignited wrath-fire. Within it, he has great power and can reach into the hearts of all creatures with his animal spirit in the outermost birth which stands in the wrath-fire; therefore, the soul of man must constantly fight and struggle with the devil, etc.

3. Question: It is easy to understand from what has been said that the Earth became so corrupted in the essence or angelic bodies of Lucifer and his angels; but how did the entire Earth and the whole kingdom fall into such devastation? This is not so easy to understand.

Answer: To understand this well and thoroughly, one must distinguish the threefold birth in nature. Behold, the innermost and deepest birth stands in the center and is the <term>Heart of the Deity: In this system, this refers to the Second Person of the Trinity (the Son/Light) who acts as the organizing center of divine life</term>, which is born from the <term>source-spirits: original: "Quell-Geister"; the seven fundamental forces or "qualities" of God that flow like a fountain to create reality</term> of God. This birth is the Light, which—although born from the source-spirits—cannot be grasped by any source-spirit on its own. Rather, each source-spirit grasps only its own designated place within the Light; but all seven spirits together grasp the entire Light, for they are the father of the Light.

Likewise, the source-spirits of man do not entirely grasp the innermost birth of the Deity, which stands in the Light; rather, each source-spirit reaches into the Heart of God with its animal birth and <term>dwells: original: "inqualiret"; a term describing how different forces or spirits work together and influence one another within a single space</term> in that same place with Him. And that is the hidden birth in nature, which no human can grasp through his own reason or skill; rather, only the soul of man—which stands in the Light of God—grasps it, while others do not.

### The second birth in nature is the seven spirits of nature.

This birth is more intelligible and graspable, but still only to the "children of this mystery." The peasant does not understand it, though he sees, smells, tastes, hears, and feels it; yet he looks upon it and does not know what its essence is.

Now, these are the spirits in which all things stand, both in heaven and in this world, and from them the third and outermost spirit is born, in which corruption resides.

But this spirit, or this birth, has seven species: such as harsh, sweet, bitter, and heat; these four give birth to <term>tangibility: original: "Begreifflichkeit"; the state of being physical, solid, or "graspable" to the senses</term> in the third birth. The fifth spirit is Love, which arises from the Light of Life and gives birth to sensibility and reason. The sixth spirit is Tone [or Sound], which gives birth to resonance and joy, and is the rising source through all spirits.

In these six now stand the spirit of life, and the will or the reason and thoughts of all creatures, as well as all arts and changes, including forms and shapings—everything that stands in the spirit in <term>unfathomability: original: "Unbegreifflichkeit"; the state of being spiritual or non-physical</term>.

The seventh spirit is Nature, in which the bodily essence of all six spirits stands; for the other six give birth to the seventh. In this spirit stands the bodily essence of angels, devils, and men; it is a mother to the other six spirits, in which they give birth to themselves, and in which they also give birth to the Light, which is the Heart of God.

### Concerning the third birth.

Now, the third birth is the <term>physical world: original: "Begreifflichkeit der Natur"; literally "the tangibility of nature"</term>. Before the time of God’s wrath, this was thin, lovely, and bright, so that the source-spirits could see through everything. There were neither stones nor earth in it, nor did it need such a light <note>Meaning the physical sun</note> as it does now; rather, the Light was born everywhere in the center, and everything stood in the Light. But when King Lucifer was created, he awakened the <term>wrath of God: the dark, fire-like energy that becomes destructive when separated from the Light</term> in this third birth; for the bodies of the angels are [born] in this third ge- <note>This word is cut off by the page break; it likely completes as "Geburt" (birth).</note>

The core of the matter lies here: gold, silver, precious stones, and all bright ores have their origin in the Light, which shone before the times of wrath in the outermost birth in nature—that is, in the seventh spirit of nature. Because every human being is like the entire house of this world, his own source-spirits also love the "core" or the very best parts of this corrupted nature, and they use these things for their protection and defense. 4. Question: But how does it happen that the corruption in the earth is so varied—some parts hard, some soft, some black, some red, white, etc.—when the earth was one and the same in the beginning?

Answer: When Lucifer ignited his body <note>original: "Corpus"</note> and kingdom with such fierce fire-power, all his source-spirits became active in that fire of wrath. Now, as the Matrix <note>the "womb" or fundamental mother-substance of nature</note> was so greatly ignited and moved, and Lord Lucifer wanted to rule in the

<column-break/>

fire, the harsh, dark Matrix contracted. This caused the entire workings of the "out-birth" <note>the physical manifestation resulting from spiritual processes</note> to become earth, stones, metals, sulfur, and salt. Thus, Prince Lucifer's kingdom was locked away from him; he remained in the inner center, imprisoned in the outer. But the reason such things could be worked within the Matrix comes from the power that was already inside her; for a stone is nothing other than water, Mercury, Salt, and Sulfur, in which an Oil is hidden.

Now, the birth of the Matrix has such a form in its eternal essence and the birth of life: first, it is harsh, strict, and hard, which is the origin of cold. This harshness attracts itself and sharpens the cold; in its pulling together, it creates the "bitter sting." This sting pricks and rages, and cannot endure the hard contraction. It becomes anxious, like a mad insanity; it rises up and rages, becoming like a spirit of sulfur.

In this state of grimness, within the watery, harsh mother, the harsh and bitter earth, sulfur, and salt were born—this happened before the ignition of the Sun in the "intelligent" Matrix. The reason a separation occurred there is that the birth stood in great distress and desired separation. For bitterness cannot agree with harshness, and yet Mother and Son are members of one another. It must be so, otherwise nothing would exist; for this is the eternal bond and the evidence of life.

Furthermore, as the bitterness thus rages in the harsh mother, rising up and becoming anxious, it turns into a "squinting flash" <note>original: "schielenden Blitz"; Böhme's term for the first sharp, flickering breakthrough of light or fire within the darkness</note> that is quite terrifying. In this state, Mercury <note>the spirit of movement and communication in nature</note>—or "poison"—is born in the Matrix. For when the Matrix beholds this fire-flash in her dark, harsh form, she is terrified and is "killed" in her hard, harsh right <note>her natural state or "law" of being</note>. And at this place in the Matrix are born death, poison, falling, and breaking—as well as the noble life within Mercury and the rising of the Third Principle <note>the material world of the four elements</note>.

The movement of the three births lasted six days and nights, during which all seven spirits of GOD stood in full, moving birth, as did the Heart of the spirits. During this time, the **Salitter** of the earth turned six times in the "Great Wheel"—which wheel consists of the seven source-spirits of GOD—and in every revolution, a specific creation was born according to the source-spirits present.

This Fifth Essence, possessing a sulfurous <note>original: "sulphurischer"; referring to the expansive, light-seeking quality in Böhme's spiritual chemistry</note> property, drew the fire to itself and became radiant within it—not only in one place, but in the entire depth, wherever such a property existed in the mass. For with the Word, when GOD said: *Let there be light*, the essence of being moved into the property of light—not only in the earth, but also in the whole depth of power. Through this becoming light, the devil's power was entirely withdrawn from his being; for here the light shone in the newly awakened power within the darkness, which the Prince of Wrath <note>Lucifer</note> could not comprehend, and it was of no use to him, for it was the light of nature; that is of no use to him.

For the first movement of the Word, when the light of nature ignited in the essence, is the joy of the creation; it opened itself through the other days across all properties of nature. There, one may call each property a "heaven," for each has and brings its own special working within itself into the others. Every day, one property moved and revealed itself, and therein a special work became manifest.

...the clarity of the same, for in the day that which was otherwise hidden in the night becomes manifest. This Day proceeds through all other days until the seventh, wherein it finds its center and reaches its completion, because the seventh day has no night or alternation. It thus gives to the second, third, fourth, fifth, and sixth days their power for revelation, just as the sun gives the planets power for their luster and shine. Our author explains this according to the fundamental rules of his **Natural Language** <note>original: "Natur-Sprache"; the mystical belief that the sounds of words reveal the true essence and "signature" of the things they name</note>, speaking thus of the Day and of the Night.

The writer Moses writes that GOD divided the light from the darkness, and called the light Day, and the darkness Night; then from evening and morning the first day came to be. Because these words "evening and morning" run entirely contrary to **philosophy and reason**, it is to be held that Moses is not the original author of them; rather, they were brought to him by his ancestors, who reckoned all six days of creation into one course, and kept the creation of Adam only in a dark word and passed it to their descendants. For evening and morning did not exist before the time of the sun and stars, which were first certainly and truly created on the fourth day—which I will then prove from certain grounds during the creation of the sun and stars.

But Day and Night did exist, which I will here explain according to my recognition; you may here open the eyes of your spirit wide once again if you wish to understand it; if not, you will remain blind.

Just as this great work has remained hidden within humanity until this date, now (Praise be to GOD) it finally wants to become **DAY**: for the **MORNING GLOW** <note>original: "MORGEN-ROTHE" or *Aurora*; the title of Böhme's first major work, symbolizing the dawn of divine wisdom</note> is breaking; the "Breaker-through" of the innermost birth shows himself with his red, green, and white banners in the outermost birth upon the rainbow.

->Note,<-
->Now you might say:<-

### How then could there have been Day and Night, and not also Morning and Evening?

Morning and evening exist only upon the earth under the moon, and take their origin from the light of the sun; it makes **EVENING** and **MORNING**, and also the external **DAY**, and also the external dark **NIGHT**; everyone knows this. However, at that time there were not two kinds of creation of EVENING and MORNING; rather, once EVENING and MORNING began, they remained in their course until now.

### Of the Day.

The word **DAY** <note>original: "TAG"; Böhme is analyzing the phonetic mechanics of the German word to show how the "spirit" of the day is formed in the mouth</note> forms itself in the heart, and travels forward to the mouth, and travels through the street of the **harsh and bitter quality** <note>original: "herben und bittern Qualität"; two of Böhme's seven foundational properties of nature</note>, yet it does not wake the harsh and bitter quality; instead, it goes strongly through its location (which is at the back of the palate above the tongue) and comes forth quite gently, incomprehensible to the harsh and bitter quality. But when it comes forward onto the tongue, the tongue closes the mouth against the upper palate; but when the spirit strikes against the teeth and wants to get out, the tongue opens the mouth and wants to get out before the word, and makes a leap of joy out of the mouth. But when the word breaks through, the mouth opens wide inside, and the word takes hold of itself with its sound behind the harsh and bitter quality once more, and wakes the same up like a lazy sleeper in the darkness, and suddenly drives out to the mouth.

Then the **harsh quality** tugs afterward like a sleepy person being woken from sleep; but the **bitter spirit**, which proceeds from the lightning-flash of fire, remains lying down and hears nothing, nor does it move at all.

### Text. Gen. I. v. 3. <note>The author cites verse 3, but the passage he quotes is actually Genesis 1:6–8, concerning the second day of creation.</note>

**And God said, let there be an expansion in the midst of the waters, and let it divide between water and water. And God made an expansion, and divided the waters under the expansion, and the waters above the expansion / and it happened so, and God called the expansion Heaven, and there was evening, and there was morning, the second day.**

->4. Question: What does the second day’s work of God actually consist of?<-

Answer: The second day’s work consists of the expansion, which God brought forth through His almighty Word, to divide from the midst of the waters between water and water: through which division God, as it were, locked and bolted away the fierce fire which <term>Lucifer</term> <note>In Böhme’s theology, Lucifer’s fall ignited the "wrathful" fire of nature, which God had to subdue to make the physical world habitable.</note> awakened, so that it might not break through further and consume the whole world.

->5. Question: What then is actually called the firmament or expansion?<-

Answer: This expansion is nothing other than an ever-working and dividing power of GOD, and a strong lock, whereby the inner and outer birth—the upper, fiery, heavenly, volatile, spirit-rich waters—are divided from the lower, deadened, coarse, <term>phlegmatic</term> <note>Meaning sluggish, cold, or heavy; here referring to the dense physical matter of the material world.</note> waters.

If one wishes to rightly consider how God divided the water under the firmament from the water above the firmament / then very great things are to be found here. For the water that rests upon the earth / that is indeed a corrupted and deadly essence like the earth / and also belongs to the <term>outermost birth</term> <note>The physical, material realm which Böhme considers to be in a state of spiritual "death" or "stagnation" compared to the divine realm.</note>, which stands in death with its tangibility / just like the earth and stones. Not with the

<column-break/>

intention / that it is entirely cast out by God / for the heart within it still belongs to the <term>sidereal birth</term> <note>original: "Siderischen Geburt"; the astral or celestial realm that mediates between the divine spirit and physical matter.</note>, from which the holy birth is born. However, death stands in the outermost birth / therefore the tangible water has been divided from the intangible.

->Now you say: How is that?<-

See / the water in the deep above the earth / which <term>inqualifies</term> <note>original: "inqualiret"; a term Böhme uses to describe how different qualities or forces intermingle and operate within one another.</note> with the elements of air and fire / that is the water of the sidereal birth / in which the sidereal life stands / and in which the Holy Spirit primarily moves / and through which the third and innermost birth is brought forth, which is incomprehensible to the <term>wrath of God</term> <note>The "wrath" refers to the harsh, dark, and fiery principle of nature; Böhme believes the spiritual "upper" water is protected from this harshness.</note> therein: This same water is also like air before our eyes.

But that water, air, and fire are truly within one another in the deep above the earth / every sensible person can see and understand. For you often see the entire deep quite bright and clear / and in a quarter of an hour it is covered with water-clouds. That is / when the stars from above / and the water on the earth from below ignite it / then water is immediately birthed / which would likely not happen / if the wrath in the sidereal birth were not also present.

->The Gates of the Godhead.<-

### Now mark here the hidden mystery of God.

When you look into the Deep above the Earth, you must not say: "The gates of God are not here, where God dwells in His holiness." No, no, do not think such a thing; rather, the entire Holy Trinity—GOD the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—dwells in the Center beneath the firmament of Heaven, and that same firmament cannot contain Him. Indeed, everything is one single Body—the outermost birth and the innermost, along with the firmament of Heaven, as well as the sidereal <note>Sidereal refers to the "starry" realm—the influence of the planets and stars on the physical world.</note> birth within it, in which the Wrath of God is also active <term>qualifies</term> <note>original: "qualificiret." Böhme uses this to mean forces working or flavoring one another.</note>; yet they stand against one another, much like the governance within a human being.

The flesh signifies first of all the outermost birth, which is the house of death. The second birth in man is the sidereal, in which life stands, and where Love and Wrath struggle with one another; and this is as far as a person knows themselves, for the sidereal birth brings forth life in the outermost birth—that is, in the dead flesh.

The third birth is born between the sidereal and the outermost, and this is called the animate <note>original: "animalische." From the Latin 'anima' for soul; refers to the living, breathing soul rather than "animal" in the modern sense.</note> or the Soul; it is as large as the whole man. This birth the external man does not know or comprehend, nor does the sidereal man comprehend it; rather, each source-spirit <term>Quell-Geist</term> <note>Böhme’s term for the fundamental divine forces or "fountains" that flow through all existence.</note> only comprehends its own inherent root, which signifies HEAVEN. And this same animate man must press through the firmament of heaven to God and live with God; otherwise, the whole man cannot come to God in Heaven.

For every person who desires to be saved must be, in their internal births, just as the entire Godhead is with all three births in this world. A person cannot be entirely pure without wrath and sin, for the births in the Deep of this world are also not entirely pure before the heart of God, as seen in Job 15:15; <note>original: "Behold, God puts no trust in his saints; yea, the heavens are not clean in his sight."</note> rather, Love and Wrath always struggle with one another, which is why God calls Himself a wrathful, jealous GOD in Exodus 20:5 and Deuteronomy 5:9.

Now, just as man is in the governance of his births, so too is the entire Body of God in this world; however, in the "water" stands the gentle life. First, in the external Body of God in this world, there is the frozen, harsh, bitter, and fiery death, in which the tangible water is also frozen and dead. And therein now lies the darkness, wherein King Lucifer with his angels, as well as all fleshly, godless people, lie imprisoned even while in their living bodies, as do the departed spirits of damned people.

The Heart of GOD can neither see, hear, feel, smell, nor comprehend this birth; it is a fool, which King Lucifer has prepared in such a way through his pride. The second birth is the sidereal—you must understand this as the life of the seven source-spirits—wherein Love and Wrath now stand against each other. Within this stands the "Upper Water," which is a Spirit of Life; and within or between this is the firmament of Heaven, which is made from the midst of the water.

This birth now penetrates through the external, frozen birth through death, and brings forth the sidereal life in death—that is, in the frozen earth, water, and flesh of animals and humans, as well as birds, fish, and worms. And the devil can reach halfway into this birth, as far as the Wrath extends, but no deeper; that is the extent of his dwelling, and no deeper. Therefore, the devil cannot know how the other part has a root in this birth.

And man, in his knowledge of the world, has come this far since his Fall. The other root, which is called Heaven, the Spirit has kept hidden from man until now, so that the devil might not learn of it from man and scatter poison into it before man's very eyes.

### 3. Part / Chapter 5.

Therefore, wherever you stand, walk, or lie, if your spirit only **interacts** <note>original: "inqualiret." A term Böhme uses to describe how different qualities or spirits work together, blend, or influence one another.</note> with God, then in that part of yourself you are in Heaven, and your soul is in God. For this reason, Christ also says: "My sheep are in my hands, and no one shall pluck them out of my hand" (John 10:28).

Likewise, you see how, according to the part of you that is in Wrath, you are always in Hell among all the devils. If your eyes were only opened, you would see wonders; but you stand between Heaven and Hell and can see neither, walking upon a very narrow bridge. At certain hours, several people have been "carried away" according to the **sidereal spirit** <note>The "sidereal spirit" refers to the part of the human soul influenced by the stars and the cosmic arrangement of the universe.</note> (as it is called), and they immediately recognized the gates of Heaven and Hell. They even pointed out how many a person dwells in Hell while still in their living body. These people were indeed mocked, but with great lack of understanding, for that is truly how it is. At the proper place, I will also describe in detail the nature of their condition.

However, I will prove here through the **Language of Nature** <note>The "Language of Nature" is a concept where the physical sound and formation of words reveal the true essence and spiritual quality of the things they name.</note> that there is a twofold birth within water. This is the very language of all Nature, but not everyone can understand it, for it is a **mystery** <note>original: "Mysterium."</note> which has been granted to me by the grace of God, through the Spirit who takes delight in me.

->Now observe.<-

The word **WASSER** <note>Water.</note> pushes out from the heart and closes the teeth, and it passes over the harsh and bitter quality without stirring them. It travels out through the teeth, and the tongue joins with the spirit, helping to hiss, and **interacts** with

the spirit; the spirit goes quite powerfully out through the teeth. But when the spirit is mostly out, then the harsh and bitter spirit first rouses itself and **interacts** only afterward with the word; yet it remains sitting in its **seat** <note>original: "Sede."</note> and tugs powerfully afterward in the syllable **SER**.

The fact that the spirit gathers itself in the heart and travels forth, closing the teeth and hissing with the tongue through the teeth, signifies that the Heart of God has moved and has made a conclusion around itself with His Spirit, which is the **Firmament of Heaven** <note>original: "Beste des Himmels." Just as the teeth close and the spirit goes through the teeth, so also the Spirit goes from the Heart into the **sidereal birth**. But the fact that the harsh and bitter quality only wakes up afterward and forms itself at the end of the word signifies that while it is all one body, Heaven and the Holy Spirit, together with the Heart of God, have their own **seat** <note>original: "Sedem."</note> for themselves. Neither the Devil nor the Wrath can grasp the Holy Spirit or Heaven. # Of the first Day-Work of God.

<sig>Pp 3</sig>

...once the Holy Spirit has built a church and temple for him, and [the enemy] has destroyed it in wrath, and clings behind the Word like an enemy who does not want a temple of God built in his land, lest his kingdom be diminished.

<margin>Aurora, Chapter 20, Sections 39, 75, 86, 97</margin>

6. **Question:** Are the waters above the firmament and under the firmament not **distinct by location** <note>original Latin: "localiter." Böhme is asking if they are physically separated by distance or altitude.</note>, since one is above and not below, and the other is below and not above?

**Answer:** "Below" and "above" are not to be understood as a physical place in which each type of water is locked away. Rather, it refers to the **degrees of birth** <note>In Böhme’s theology, a "birth" is the process by which a spiritual quality or physical reality comes into existence.</note>, where one is active and the other passive; one is spirit-rich, the other spirit-less; one is fiery, living, and moving, the other is dull and mute. The upper is called **Heaven**, for it is the spirit-rich, Holy **Crystalline Water**, which can be excluded from nowhere and included nowhere, for this spirit-water is alive. The lower, as material water, is mute and unfeeling, and is as if dead compared to the living, for it sinks down. The **Firmament** <term>Veste: often translated as the "expanse" or "vault of heaven" in Genesis, Böhme treats it as a spiritual boundary or "closure."</term> is the partition between the upper and the lower, the living and the mortal (or lifeless), between the spirit-rich and the mute, between Time and Eternity.

That God calls it Heaven and makes a distinction between the waters is to be understood thus: Heaven is in the world, but the world is not in Heaven. The water above the firmament is in Heaven, and that below the firmament is the outer, material water.

Here one should understand the difference between the holy and the external element of water. The water above the firmament is spiritual in the birth of the holy element; and the water below the firmament is mortal, for it is caught in the **dark impression** <note>A term for the densifying, hardening force of "wrath" or "matter" in Böhme’s system that makes things solid and heavy.</note>; the curse is within it, as is the awakened **vanity** <note>Reference to the biblical "vanity" or futility of the fallen world.</note>—and yet, one water is not without the other.

When I look at the outer water, I must also say: the water above the firmament is here too, within the water under the firmament, but the firmament is the means and the

<column-break/>

partition within it between Time and Eternity, so that one is not the other. With the outer eyes of this world, I see only the water under the firmament; but the water above the firmament is that which God in Christ has established for the **Baptism of Rebirth**, after the Word of the power of God moved within it.

Now the outer water is the instrument of the inner, and the inner water is understood [through it], for it is the moving Spirit in the Word that governs the inner water in Baptism. Dear Christians, let this be told to you: it is the true foundation.

But when Moses says that God created the firmament and called it Heaven, that is the most inward mystery, which the earthly man can understand nothing of. Understanding is found solely in the power of the water above the firmament—as if in Heaven, or as I might put it, in the Spirit of God. If He awakens Himself in a person, in that water above the firmament (which faded in Adam's life), that person can see through [to the truth]; otherwise, there is no understanding here, but all is mute.

The creation of Heaven is understood as how the **Speaking Word** <note>The divine "Logos" or voice of God that brings the universe into being.</note> grasped the revealed powers of the spiritual world, wherein it is manifest and also works and governs. Secondly, it is understood as the revealed powers of the outer world, which the Spirit grasped from the **four-elementary being** <note>The physical world composed of Earth, Air, Fire, and Water.</note> and enclosed in the outer firmament, so that the Devil, as the **Prince of Wrath**, might not seize them—through which he would want to work with the inner water—so that the powers of Eternity work through the powers of Time. Just as the sun shines through the water, and the water does not grasp the sun but only feels it; or as a fire glows through iron, and the iron remains iron: so too is the outer heaven, which is passive, while the inner works through it and draws an external fruit out of the external, while the inner heaven lies hidden within it in the firmament, just as God...

<summary>Böhme explains that the "waters above and below the firmament" are not physically separated but represent spiritual and material dimensions existing simultaneously. He identifies the "waters above" as the spiritual foundation of baptism and the hidden "heaven" that remains inaccessible to the unawakened earthly mind.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the Second Day of creation, specifically the separation of the spiritual and material realms. Böhme is transitioning from the definition of the "Firmament" to how the "Source of Water" and the "Fiery Heaven" interact to produce physical life.</meta>

### 3. Part / Chapter 5.

God is hidden in time. Through the second **Day-Work** <note>The second day of creation (Genesis 1:6-8).</note>, we are to understand the revelation of the inner heavenly and outer heavenly essence as the revelation of the **Source of Water**. Understand this as the essence of the **seven properties** <note>In Böhme’s system, these are the seven fundamental qualities or 'forms' of nature that drive all existence.</note>, which acts as the corporeality or the **operation** <term>Gewürck: The active process by which spiritual forces manifest into physical effects.</term> of the other six properties. In the outer world, the soul or spirit of the outer world works and rules within it. This same operation in the outermost heaven is attributed to the **Moon**; for it is the revelation of the Moon’s property—not the physical star itself, which was only created on the fourth Day-Work to be a ruler in the outer realm—but rather that same property within the mute outer life, as seen in growing things.

<margin>Mysterium Magnum 12, 23, 30.</margin>
From this, we see clearly what the **water above the firmament** is: namely, the great **Sea of Fire**, which has its effect in each and every creature and is a cause of all life and movement, for it passes through everything. In the **vegetable kingdom**, it is the **Tincture** <term>Tinctur: A spiritual essence or "dye" that imparts life, color, and specific qualities to matter.</term> and the driving force in all plants. In the **mineral kingdom**, it is called the **Sulfur of the Philosophers** <note>original: "Sulphur Philosophorum." Not common chemical sulfur, but the alchemical principle of the soul and combustible energy within matter.</note>, in which **Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury** <note>The three "paracelsian" principles believed to be the building blocks of all physical things.</note> have the root of their life. In the **animal kingdom**, the water above the firmament is in the blood and is the **Radical Moisture** <note>original: "Humidum Radicale." The fundamental life-fluid or vital sap thought to sustain an organism's life-force.</note>, the spirit-rich **Fire-Water**.

It is the life that burns in the blood like fire in an oil, for the noble **Tincture** resides therein. Thus, we find Heaven in all things; the upper is the life and governance of the lower. It ignites the lower, by which the lower becomes stirred and active. The lower, in turn, is the body and "wife" of the upper; the lower cannot become the upper, and the upper cannot become the lower. Thus it is evident how the fiery heaven—from which the stars were afterwards born—exists (of which more will be said below). Or, to put it better for the dear reader: the **Quintessence** <term>Quinta Essentia: The "fifth essence" or purest spiritual element underlying the four physical elements.</term>, or the fifth form in the birth, is distinguished from the **watery matrix** <term>Matrix: A womb-like source or "mother" substance from which specific realities are birthed.</term>; otherwise, the birthing of stones and earth would never have ceased if the fiery nature had not been distinguished. But since the eternal Being, as **GOD**, wished to reveal—

<column-break/>

—himself in the **dark matrix** and make something out of nothing, He distinguished the ignited power and made the matrix bright and pure.

Thus the matrix now stands incomprehensible and yearns for the fiery nature, and the fiery nature yearns for the matrix. For the **Spirit of God**, which is the **Spirit of Gentleness**, mirrors itself in the **watery matrix**, and the matrix receives power from Him. Thus, there is a constant will to birth and to work; all of nature stands in great longing and anguish, always willing to birth the **Divine Power**, because **GOD** and **Paradise** stand hidden within it. However, nature gives birth according to its own kind and its own ability.

Now, when **GOD** had distinguished the matrix with its fiery form and wished to reveal Himself with this world, He placed the **Fiat** <term>Fiat: Latin for "Let it be done." Böhme treats this as the creative "word" or "will" that shapes matter.</term> into the matrix and spoke from Himself: "Let there come forth herbs, grass, trees, and animals, each according to its kind." The speaking was the **Heart**, or the power of the eternal Father; but the Spirit, who held the *Fiat*, went out from the eternal Father in the power of the Heart of GOD with the Will. That Will was the *Fiat*, and it created the power of the offspring in the **Third Principle** <term>Third Principle: In Böhme’s cosmology, the third principle is the visible, material world produced by the interaction of the first two spiritual principles.</term> materially, visibly, and tangibly, each according to its **Essence** <note>original: "Essentia."</note>. As the power was, so also was its body. For then the fiery matrix (or the stars) gave its power to the *Fiat*, and the watery matrix with the elements received the power, became pregnant, and gave birth—each element producing its own creatures from itself, and each form in the fiery and watery nature producing from itself. Yet they did not become separate beings; only the creatures were divided, each according to its kind, according to the eternal power which rose up as **longing through desire** <note>The interaction of 'Sehnen' (longing) and 'Lust' (delight or desire) is the mechanism by which spiritual desire condenses into material reality.</note> and became the **Third Principle**, which had not existed before time.

# Of God’s First Day-Work.

Thus the starry heaven rules in all creatures as its own property; it is the husband, and the **Matrix** <term>Matrix: In Böhme's thought, this refers to a "womb" or "mother-substance"—the receptive, feminine principle of nature that brings forth form.</term>, or watery form, is his wife, whom he always impregnates. The Matrix is the bearer; she gives birth to the child that the heaven makes. And it is so, that the created heaven exists in the **Third Principle** <note>Böhme divides reality into three 'Principles': 1. The dark fire-world (the source of power), 2. The light world (divine love), and 3. The visible, material world.</note>, from which the elements proceed—namely, the watery Matrix, from which the visible water was born and is still continually born in longing. Therefore Moses writes correctly: God created the heaven out of the midst of the water. But here you must understand this as being from the eternal watery Matrix, which is only a spirit, within which are Paradise and the Holy Heaven as the Divine Power. The dark Matrix in its hunger lusted after this power, and from that lust the visible Matrix of the elements was formed, out of which all beings that exist were created through the **Fiat** <note>original: "Fiat." Latin for "let it be done," the creative command of God.</note> by the eternal Spirit of God.

For every form in the Matrix has its creatures, both visible and invisible to human eyes, some of which are to us only like a figurative spirit. For example, the fire has invisible spirits and creatures that our material eyes cannot see. In the air, too, there are invisible spirits which we do not see because the air is immaterial, and so are its spirits. In the water there are material creatures, but they are not visible to us <note>Böhme likely refers here to elemental spirits or "undines," rather than common fish.</note> because they are not made of fire and air; they are of a different quality and are hidden from the airy and fiery beings unless they choose to reveal themselves.

Thus, just as fire, air, water, and earth lie together in a single chest, and the four are only one thing and yet four distinct parts—and none is able to grasp or hold the other—and if one of the four is "fixed" or dominant in a creature, that creature cannot hide itself from that element. Rather, it stands openly within it, visible and graspable to that specific spirit, while remaining ungraspable to the other 

<column-break/>

elemental spirits. For all things have become "Something" out of "Nothing," and every creature has the **Center** <note>original: "Centrum."</note> or the circle of its life-birth within itself. Now, just as the elements lie hidden within one another in one Mother, and none grasps the other even though they are members of one another, so too are the created beings hidden and invisible to one another. For each sees only into its own Mother which is fixed within it; the material being sees the material being, but does not see the immaterial being—the spirits in fire and air. Just as the body does not see the soul that dwells within it, or as the Third Principle does not grasp the other Principle in which God is; and even though it is *in* God, there is a "birth" (a threshold of existence) between them. This is the same as with the soul-spirit of man and the elemental spirit in man, where one is the chest and container of the other, as you will find in the account of the creation of man.

<margin>Principle 7. §. 30. 37.</margin>

Thus we understand what the outer heaven is: namely, the powers or the containment of the water. The Word or the Power that began with the world’s beginning—that same Word which "created"—is still creating today. It still continually creates the heaven out of the midst of the waters, and still continually separates the Holy Water above the firmament from the water below the firmament; and the Holy Heaven still continually hovers within the **Creation** <note>original: "Schuff." Here used as a noun meaning the state of being created or the fabric of the cosmos.</note> or the created heaven, etc.

In such a turning, the sharp separation began and was completed; also, the ungraspable gulf was made between life and death, wrath and love, between the upper spirit-rich realm and the lower mute realm.
