### Part 3 / Chapter 5

God is hidden within time. Through the second "Day-Work" <note>German: *Tag-Werck*, referring to the stages of creation in Genesis.</note>, we are to understand the revelation of the inner heavenly and outer heavenly essence, as the revelation of the "Water-Source." Understand this as the essence of the seven properties—the "corporeality" or the "weaving" <note>German: *Gewürck*, meaning the active, formative processing of nature.</note> of the other six properties—where, in the outer world, the soul or the spirit of the outer world works and rules within. This same weaving is attributed to the outermost heaven near the moon, for it is the revelation of the "Lunar" property—not of the physical star itself, which was only created as a ruler in the outer world on the fourth day, but rather that same property within the silent outer life, as seen in growing things.

<margin>Mysterium Magnum 12. 23. 30.</margin>
From this we see clearly what the "water above the firmament" <note>original: *Wasser über der Veste*; a reference to Genesis 1:7.</note> is: namely, the great "Fire-Ocean," which has its effect in each and every creature and is a cause of all life and movement, for it passes through everything. In the vegetable kingdom, it is the **Tincture** <term>Tincture: A spiritual essence or "inner light" that gives things their specific quality, color, and medicinal power.</term> and the driving force in all plants. In the mineral kingdom, it is called the **Philosophers' Sulfur** <note>original: *Sulphur Philosophorum*. In alchemy, this is the active, combustible principle of growth and soul.</note>, in which **Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury** <term>Sal, Sulphur, and Mercurius: The "Tria Prima," or three primary substances of alchemy representing the body, soul, and spirit of all matter.</term> have their root of life. In the animal kingdom, this "water above the firmament" is found in the blood and is the **Radical Moisture** <note>original: *Humidum Radicale*; in historical medicine, the vital fluid that maintains life-heat and prevents the body from drying out.</note>, the spirit-rich fire-water.

It is the life that burns in the blood like fire in an oil, for within it stands the noble Tincture. Thus we find heaven in all things; the upper is the life and rule of the lower—it ignites the lower, by which the lower becomes active and works. The lower, conversely, is the body and "wife" of the upper. The lower cannot become the upper, and the upper cannot become the lower. Thus it is evident how the fiery heaven exists, from which the stars were later born (about which more shall be said below). Or to put it better for the dear reader: The **Fifth Essence** <note>original: *Quinta Essentia*. The quintessence, or the purest, most spiritual element that permeates the four physical elements.</note>, or the fifth form in the birth, is distinguished from the "watery Matrix." Otherwise, the bearing of stones and earth would never have ceased if the fiery nature had not been distinguished. But since the eternal Being, as GOD, wished to reveal—

<column-break/>

—himself in the dark **Matrix** <term>Matrix: In Böhme's philosophy, the "womb" or receptive principle of nature that gives birth to form.</term>, and make something out of nothing, He distinguished the ignited power and made the Matrix bright and pure.

Now the Matrix stands in an incomprehensible state and longs for the fiery nature, and the fiery nature longs for the Matrix; for the Spirit of God, which is the Spirit of gentleness, mirrors itself in the watery Matrix, and the Matrix receives power from Him. Thus there is a constant will to give birth and to work, and all of nature stands in great longing and "anxiety" <note>German: *Aengsten*, here used in the sense of the labor pains or the high-tension "squeeze" of nature striving to produce life.</note>, always willing to give birth to the Divine Power, because God and Paradise stand hidden within it; yet she gives birth according to her own kind and her own ability.

When God had distinguished the Matrix with its fiery form and wished to reveal Himself through this world, He placed the **Fiat** <note>original: *Fiat*. Latin for "let it be done," the creative command of God.</note> into the Matrix and spoke out of Himself: "Let there come forth herbs, grass, trees, animals, each according to its kind." The "Speaking" was the Heart or the power of the eternal Father; but the Spirit, who held the Fiat, went out from the eternal Father in the power of God's Heart with the Will. That Will was the Fiat, and it created the power of the "out-birth" in the **Third Principle** <term>Third Principle: The visible, material world, which Böhme sees as the third stage of God’s self-manifestation (following the dark world and the light world).</term> materially, visibly, and tangibly, each according to its essence. As the power was, so also became its body. For there the fiery Matrix, or the constellation of stars, gave its power to the Fiat, and the watery Matrix with the elements received that power, became pregnant, and gave birth—each element its own creatures from within itself, and each form in the fiery and watery nature from within itself. Yet it did not become a separate being; only the creatures became divided, each according to its kind, according to the eternal power, which rose up in longing through "delight" <note>German: *Lust*, implying a divine desire or the "play" of God’s wisdom.</note> and became the Third Principle, which did not exist before time began.

# Regarding the First Day-Work of God.

->(The Second Day of Creation)<-

Thus the starry heaven rules in all creatures as if in its own property; it is the Husband, and the **Matrix** <term>Matrix: Latin for "womb"; in this context, it refers to the feminine, receptive, and formative principle of nature that gives birth to material forms.</term>, or the watery form, is his Wife, whom he is always impregnating. And the Matrix is the Mother who gives birth to the child that the heaven creates. Know that the created heaven in the **Third Principle** <note>original: "Principio"; refering to the third of Böhme's three realms of existence: the material world. The first is the dark world of fire, and the second is the light world of holiness.</note>, from which the elements proceed—namely the watery Matrix—is where the visible water was born and is still being born in longing. Therefore, Moses writes correctly: "God created the heaven out of the midst of the waters." But here you must understand: it was created out of the eternal watery Matrix, which is only a Spirit, within which Paradise and the Holy Heaven exist as the Divine Power. The dark Matrix hungers after this power, and from that hunger the visible Matrix of the elements was formed, out of which the **Fiat** <note>original: "Fiat"; Latin for "let it be," the creative command of God described in Genesis.</note> and the eternal Spirit of God created the "essence of all essences" that currently exist.

For every form in the Matrix has its creatures, both visible and invisible to human eyes, some of which are like figurative spirits compared to us. For example, in the element of Fire there are invisible spirits and creatures that our material eyes cannot see. In the Air, there are also invisible spirits which we do not see because the air is non-material; thus, its spirits are likewise non-material. In the Water, there are material creatures, but they are not visible to us <note>The author refers here to spiritual entities or elemental beings associated with water, rather than physical fish.</note> because they are not made of fire and air; they are of a different quality and are hidden from the airy and fiery beings unless they choose to reveal themselves.

Thus, just as Fire, Air, Water, and Earth lie within a single chest, and the four are only one thing yet remain four distinct parts—and none can grasp or hold the other—so it is with creatures. If one of the four elements is "fixed" or dominant in a creature, that creature cannot hide from it but stands openly within it, visible and graspable to that specific spirit, yet incomprehensible to the other elemental spirits.

<column-break/>

For all things have come from Nothing into Something, and every creature has the **Center** <note>original: "Centrum"; the spiritual core or point of origin within a being.</note> or the "Circle of the Life-Birth" within itself. Now, just as the elements lie hidden within one another in one Mother, and none grasps the other even though it is the other's limb, so too are the created beings hidden and invisible to one another. For each one sees only into its own "Mother" which is fixed within it; the material being sees the material being, but does not see the non-material being—the spirits in fire and air. Just as the body does not see the soul that dwells within it, or as the **Third Principle** <note>The physical world.</note> does not grasp the other realm in which God is; and even though the world is *in* God, there is a "birth" <note>A threshold, state, or vibrational boundary.</note> between them, just as there is between the soul-spirit of man and the elemental spirit in man—even though one is the chest and container of the other, as you will find in the account of the creation of man.

<margin>Principle 7. Sections 30, 37.</margin>

Thus we understand what the outer heaven is: namely, the powers or the vessel of the water. The Word or the Power that began at the world's beginning—that same "Creating Word"—is still at work today; it is still constantly creating the heaven out of the midst of the waters, and it still constantly separates the Holy Water above the firmament from the water beneath the firmament, and the Holy Heaven still hovers within the "Created Heaven," etc.

**7th Question:** How then did evening and morning become the second day?

In this turning, the "sharp separation" began and was completed; also, the "incomprehensible gulf" was made between life and death, wrath and love, and between the upper spirit-rich realm and the lower mute realm.

### Of the third Day-Work of God,
#### Namely, how God has revealed Himself in the Earth and its growths.

->Text. Genesis 1:7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12.<-

And God said: Let the waters under the heavens gather into one place, and let the dry land appear, and it was so. And God called the dry land Earth, and the gathering of the waters He called Sea, and God saw that it was good, and said: Let the earth bring forth herbs and grass that seed themselves, and fruitful trees, where each bears fruit according to its kind, and has its own seed within itself upon the earth, and it happened so. And the earth brought forth grass and herbs that seed themselves, each according to its kind, and trees that bore fruit and had their own seed within themselves, each according to its kind, and God saw that it was good. Then out of evening and morning came the third day.

Now the Mighty One has lost his dominion, he who was a king and a great prince; for the essence of wrath was captured in the light of nature, and he along with it. Thus he lies imprisoned in darkness between time and eternity until the Judgment of God.

In the third day-work, the sulphuric, mercurial, and salty <note>original: "sulphurische, mercurialische und salzische"; Böhme uses these three alchemical principles to represent the soul, spirit, and body (or the three forces of nature).</note> life was opened out of the Center into the properties of the external world out of the "anguish"—and yet no anguish is understood until the point of fire, but only an unfeeling, driving life, like a growth. For the flash of fire arises out of the anguish, as if from the third form of nature, and that same flash is the Salnitrous Terror <term>Salnitrous Terror: Böhme's term "Salnitrische Schrack" refers to a sudden, explosive discharge of energy (like lightning or gunpowder) that triggers the separation of qualities and the beginning of material form.</term> which distinguishes the powers in the properties; that was moved in the third day-work. Then the properties opened themselves and went out in the Salnitrous Terror, each one out of itself, which then grasped the impression back into itself and made it corporeal in the water. From this, trees, herbs, and grass have risen and gone out; every property is pressing outward in the Salniter...

...become, and has revealed itself with a fruit; where one then sees how the property of the dark world has powerfully forced itself in with the outer power; for this reason, some herbs and growths are poisonous and evil, for the earth has gone into a compaction out of both inner worlds <note>Böhme refers to the "light" and "dark" worlds that exist within the divine essence.</note>.

Now Mars has the rule of the first hour of the day on Tuesday, which day is the third in creation; and this salnitric <term>salnitric: derived from "Salitter," referring to a divine-chemical saltpeter or the explosive, expansive force in nature</term> fire-crack is precisely the property of Mars. Just as he is fierce and fiery, so too is this property in Sulphur <note>original: "Sulphur"; in Böhme’s alchemy, Sulphur represents the active, burning substance of the soul or heart of a thing.</note>, where we then understand the salnitric crack as the poisonous Mars, who is the cause of movement and stirring, and the sting in the first impression in eternal nature, as in the dark world. On the third Day-Work, God moved the third property of nature, namely the Sulphur-source <note>original: "Schwefel-Quall"</note>, in which the fire ignited; and in the fire-crack is the division of powers, where each property has become manifest in itself. So God spoke: Let the earth bring forth grass, herbs, and trees; that is nothing else than that He moved the spoken Word of powers in the properties, so the properties felt the light of nature within themselves, from which they became hungry, and *impressed* themselves—that is, grasped and compacted or coagulated. Because the light of nature has now found itself in a sensitivity, and nature is in the sweet light, the "realm of joy" <note>original: "Freudenreich"</note> has thereby risen up in the coagulation, as the breaking-forth or growth; for all growth stands in the light and water; when the light penetrates the Sulphur and the water-source, then Mars leaps up for great joy in the Sulphur. This opening began on the third day and lasts until the end of the world. On the first day, the earth was waste and empty, for the possibility for growth was not yet opened. Here the earth is moved, and the properties opened, and

<column-break/>

not only the earth, but the whole depth in the center <note>original: "Centro"</note> of the outer nature made itself external, and yet also remained internal.

Thus God made no new earth, but He awakened a new life in the earth through the Word, which from this day forward until now is always in speaking and working, in order to bring forth foliage and grass, trees and fruits. **Answer:** We have already partially provided an opening on this subject above. Therefore, when Reason asks: To what end did the Creator make such a revelation? The answer is: There is no other cause than that the spiritual world might thereby bring itself into a visible, figurative form, so that the inner powers would become pictorial and formal. Should this happen, the spiritual essence had to introduce itself into a material ground, within which it could form and fashion itself; and such a separation had to occur so that the divided state would always long for its first ground—the inner for the outer, and the outer for the inner.

So it is also with the four elements, which inwardly are only a single ground; here, each must long for the other, and desire the other, and seek the inner ground in the other. For there is no thing in this world's essence wherein there does not stand a fashioned form according to the inner spiritual world—either according to the grimness of the inner ground, or according to the good power. # Of the First Day-Work of God.

<note>Though the header mentions the "First Day," the content focuses on the internal mechanics of the "Source-Spirits" and the Archaeus, concepts Böhme uses to explain the Third Day of Creation when the earth brought forth life.</note>

the lower Archaeus <term>Archaeus</term> <note>a term borrowed from Paracelsian alchemy, referring to the hidden "master craftsman" or vital force within nature that directs growth and form</note> of the earth draws the upper, subtle Archaeus from the stars <note>original: "Gestirn"</note> into itself; then this enclosed foundation yearns back toward its origin in the upper Archaeus. In this outward striving, the growth of metals, herbs, and trees arises. For the Archaeus of the earth becomes so full of joy that it tastes and feels its original foundation within itself once more, and in such joy all things grow out of the earth. Likewise, growth exists in living creatures as a constant conjunction <note>original: "Conjunction", a union or marriage of forces</note> of the heavenly and the earthly, wherein the Divine Power works along with them, as can be recognized in the tincture <term>Tincture</term> <note>the inner spiritual essence or "color" of a thing's soul</note> of growing things, as if in their innermost foundation.

<margin>Key <note>original: "Clav." refers to Böhme's work 'Clavis' or 'The Key'</note> 105. 112.</margin>
Thus, whoever sees a beautiful green meadow has before them a true, living likeness <note>original: "Contrafey"</note> of the angelic world. But as to what kind of drive exists in the earth, and how the seven source-spirits <note>original: "Quell-Geister", the seven fundamental forces of Böhme's cosmos</note> of God still stand in a constant wrestling to bring forth paradisiacal plants and fruits from the earth, our author reveals this excellently: "Behold," he says, "the earth stands in its birthing process just like the entire Godhead, and there is no difference at all, except for the corruption in the wrath <note>the 'wrath' refers to the harsh, contracting quality of nature that became dominant after the Fall</note>, wherein tangibility <note>original: "Begreifflichkeit"</note> stands; that alone is the difference and the death between God and the earth."

You should know that all seven spirits of God are in the earth and give birth just as in heaven; for the earth is in God, and God has never died. However, the outermost birth is dead, wherein the wrath rests, and it is reserved for King Lucifer as a house of death and darkness, and as an eternal prison.

### Of the Seven Spirits of God and Their Working in the Earth.

Afterward, there is the **bitter spirit**, which arises in the flash of fire, also within the matter <note>original: "Materia"</note> or mass; it cannot endure being imprisoned in that which is dried out, but rather it rubs itself against the harsh spirit in the dried mass until it ignites the fire. When this happens, the bitter spirit is terrified and gains its life.

In the earth—apart from herbs or metals—you can perceive or find nothing but the harsh, the bitter, and water. But the water therein is **sweet**, which is entirely contrary to the other two. But life does not yet exist in the choking of these three; rather, they are a dark valley and are three things that never agree with one another, but there is an eternal choking among them. From this, mobility takes its origin; also God’s wrath, which rests in secret, takes its origin from this; likewise, the origin of the devil, death, and hell arose from this, as you can read earlier regarding the Fall of the Devil.

The first three—the **harsh**, **sweet**, and **bitter**—belong to the formation of the **Body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note>, and within them stand mobility and the physical frame. These now possess "graspability" <note>the quality of being tangible or material</note> and are the birth of the outermost nature.

Now, if the first three were not congealed in death so that they could ignite the Heat, you would soon see a bright heavenly body and would clearly see where **GOD** is.

These three qualities of the outermost birth—in which the **wrath-fire** stands—are not rejected all the way to the innermost core, but rather only the external tangible body and the external hellish torment within it.

From these magnificent testimonies of the author, we see what the growing life actually consists of, and also upon what ground the earth brings forth such many-fold kinds of plants.

**11. Question:** Was it then only the vegetable kingdom of plants that was awakened and revealed on the third day?

**Answer:** God, through His almighty Word, moved not only the **surface** <note>original: "Superficiem"</note> or the upper part of the earth, but also the **viscera** <note>original: "Viscera," meaning the internal organs or depths</note> and innermost parts, and awakened all powers to a driving and growing, each according to its kind, when God said: "Let it appear or be revealed." By "the dry land," He understands not only the upper parts, but also the depths of the earth, such as the minerals and metals.

**12. Question:** What kind of drive or impulse does the mineral kingdom—such as metal and ores—then have in the bowels of the earth?

**Answer:** Before the fall of Lucifer and the ignition of **wrath** <note>original: "Zorns Anzündung"</note>, the mineral kingdom was in the highest perfection and had its growth and birth just like the trees, flowers, herbs, and grass; as Moses himself testifies, that in Paradise there were gold and precious stones. The writings of the prophets and the Revelation of John are full of such testimonies. However, after Lucifer ignited the wrath of God in the earth, this tender growth of gold and precious stones was, as is easy to imagine, burnt and corrupted. Where the **Tincture** <term>Tinctur</term> <note>In alchemy, the "Tincture" is the spiritual essence or life-force that gives matter its color and quality</note>, and **Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury** <note>original: "Sal, Sulphur und Mercurius," the three primary principles of all matter in Böhme’s alchemy</note> were at their most noble, they became the most poisonous and the most corrupted; there, the noble, gentle life was locked away in fierce and harsh death. Now, when God moved the earth through His almighty Word and awakened life in the deepest grounds and the very hardest stones, the ores and metals—gold, silver, tin, iron, copper, indeed every stone and grain of sand—attained a growing and driving, a birthing and working within the earth, just like the plants above the earth.

Concerning the properties, birth, growth, purification, and use of metals, we shall reveal more of the author’s meaning and understanding in an appendix. This, then, is the revelation of God and the working of His almighty Word in the earth, in the creation of each and every earthly growth—foliage and grass—and also the minerals, precious stones, and metals; this revelation is called the Third Day.

The entire house of this world, which stands in a visible and tangible essence, is the old house of GOD or the old body, which stood in heavenly clarity before the time of the **Wrath** <note>In Böhme’s theology, "Wrath" (Zorn) is the dark, fiery principle of nature when it is separated from God’s Light.</note>. But when the Devil awakened the wrath within it, it became a house of darkness and death. For that reason, the Holy Birth of GOD separated itself as a special body from the wrath and made the Firmament of Hea-

<column-break/>

-ven between Love and Wrath, so that the **Star-Birth** <note>original: "Sternen-Geburt"; the generation of the stars and their influences.</note> stands in the middle. Understand this: with its external tangibility and visibility, it stands in the wrath of death; but with the new birth rising within it—which stands in the middle **Seat** <note>original Latin: "Sede"; meaning position or throne.</note>, where the conclusion of Heaven is—it stands in the **Meekness** <note>original: "Sanfftmuth"; Böhme's term for the light-principle or the gentle quality of God’s love.</note> of life.

For the Meekness surges against the Wrath, and the Wrath against the Meekness, and thus there are two distinct kingdoms in the single body of this world. But because the Love and Meekness of GOD did not want to leave the body or **Location** <term>Locum</term> <note>original Latin: "Locum"; the physical space or place occupied by the world.</note> of this ignited world of wrath in eternal anger and shame, He birthed the entire old body of this world once again into a proper form as a body in which life governed according to a Divine manner. Though it was within the ignited wrath, it still had to persist according to the Right of the Godhead, so that a new body could be born from it, which would consist in holiness and purity for eternity. For such reasons, a final Day of Separation has also been appointed in GOD, when Love and Wrath shall separate from one another.

Now, when you look at the stars and the deep together with the earth, you see nothing with your physical eyes but the old body in angry death; you cannot see Heaven with your physical eyes. For the blue sphere that you see on high is not Heaven, but rather it is only the old body, which is rightly called "corrupt nature."

However, the fact that it appears as if there were a blue sphere above the stars, whereby the **Location** <term>Locum</term> of this world is closed off from the Holy Heaven—as men have thought until now—is not so. Rather, it is the **Upper Water** <note>original: "Ober-Wasser"; a reference to the waters above the firmament mentioned in Genesis 1:7.</note> of nature, which is much brighter than the water under the moon; when the sun shines through the depth, it appears just like a light blue.

3. **Quest.** Has then the author not taught concerning the stars just as the rules of today's **Astrology** <term>Astrologia</term> <note>Referring to the professional and mathematical study of celestial bodies in the 17th century.</note> require, especially since more certainty has been found through the help of telescopes regarding the size, situation, course, etc., of the stars?

**Ans.** The learned and highly experienced masters of the **art of the stars** <note>original: "Stern-Kunst"; Astrology.</note> have come so high and deep in their understanding that they know the course and effect of the stars, what their conjunctions and the infecting and breaking through of their powers mean and bring with them, and how wind, rain, snow, and heat are stirred up thereby; also good and evil, luck and misfortune, even life and death, and all the dealings of this world. This is indeed the right foundation, which I recognize in the spirit to be so; but their knowledge stands only in the **house of death** <note>original: "Hause des Todes"; Böhme's term for the material world perceived only by the senses, which is transitory and separated from its eternal source.</note>, in external comprehensibility, and in the observation of the eyes of the body, and the root of this tree has remained hidden from them until now. It is also not my intention that I would want to write of the tree's branches and overturn their knowledge; nor do I build upon their ground, but let their knowledge sit in its seat, since I have not studied it. Instead, I write in the spirit as a servant of his LORD, concerning the whole tree's trunk, branches, and fruit—as a laborious servant of his Lord, seeking to expose the whole tree of this world. I do not do this with the intention of bringing something new onto the scene, for I have no command for that; rather, my knowledge stands in this birth of the stars, in the midst where life is born and breaks through death, and where the surging spirit arises and breaks through, and in its impulse and surging I also write.

<column-break/>

I also know full well that the **children of the flesh** <note>original: "Kinder des Fleisches"; those who prioritize physical comfort and worldly logic over spiritual truth.</note> will mock me and say that I should attend to my professional calling and leave these things alone, and rather take care of the diligent work that fills the belly for me and mine, and let those philosophize who have studied it and are called to do so.

With this temptation, the Devil has also given me many a blow and instilled such things in me myself, so that I have often ventured to omit this writing, but my intention became too heavy for me. For when I thought of the belly and resolved within myself to omit this undertaking, then the **gate of heaven** was bolted shut in my knowledge. At that time my soul was in anguish, as if it were captured by the Devil, whereby **reason** <note>original: "Vernunfft"; in Böhme’s view, human logic is limited and "dead" unless illuminated by God.</note> received many a blow, as if the body should perish; and the spirit did not let up until it broke through the **dead reason** again and burst open the gates of darkness and took its seat in its place again, through which it then always received new life and power. Through this I then understand that the spirit must be proven through the **cross and tribulation**; likewise, I have not lacked for bodily temptation, but have always had to stand in the struggle, so greatly was the Devil against it.

But because I perceive that my eternal salvation depends upon it, and that by my ceasing, the **gate of light** would be closed to me—which is yet the fortress of my heaven, in which my soul hides from the storm of the Devil, which I have nonetheless conquered with great effort and many a hard storm through the love of GOD, through the breakthrough of my Redeemer and King **JESUS CHRIST**—therefore I will let GOD rule and take my fleshly reason captive. And I have chosen for myself the gates of the knowledge of light, and will [follow] the spirit's impulse and...

# Part 3 / Chapter 6.

How deep or far the **place** <term>Locus</term> <note>original: "Locus"; referring to the physical location or spatial extent of the universe.</note> of this world might be, no man knows. Although many **natural philosophers** <term>Physici</term> or **astrologers** <term>Astrologi</term> have presumed to measure the depth with their compasses, their measurements are but a fable—a measurement of mere perception, much like someone trying to catch the wind.

The true heaven, however, is everywhere in this present time until the Last Day; and the house of wrath, belonging to hell and death, is also everywhere in this world until the Last Day. But the dwelling of the devils is currently from the moon down to and within the earth, in deep caverns and caves, especially where there are desolate and wild wildernesses, and where the earth is very stony and bitter. Their royal government, however, is in the depths within the four ends of the **equinoctial circle** <note>The celestial equator; Böhme suggests the spiritual "government" of fallen spirits is anchored in these astronomical coordinates.</note>, about which I will write in another place. But here, I wish to show you how the body of this world came to be, how it still stands now, and how it is governed within.

The entire body of this world is like a human body; for in its outermost circle, it is enclosed by the stars or the manifested forces of nature, and within that body, the seven spirits of nature govern, with the heart of nature standing in the center. The general stars, however, are the wondrous **proportion** or variation of GOD; for when GOD created the stars, He created them from the rising of infinity, out of the old, now-ignited body of GOD. For just as the seven **source-spirits** <term>Quell-Geister</term> <note>Böhme’s term for the seven fundamental qualities or "fountain-spirits" that drive all of existence (e.g., astringency, sweetness, bitterness, etc.).</note> of GOD had, before the time of wrath, given birth to infinite varieties through their rising and **interacting** <note>original: "Inficiren"; Böhme uses this to mean the way qualities influence and penetrate one another.</note>, from which so many kinds of forms and heavenly growths emerged: so also did Holy GOD shape His old body of this corrupted nature into as many various powers as had ever stood in birth within His holiness.

### Understand this high matter correctly.

Every star has a particular property, which you can also see in the beauty or the blooming of the earth. The Creator rebuilt and brought the old, ignited body back to life in so many various powers so that, through this old life now held in **wrath** <note>Böhme views the material world as a mixture of God’s love and His "wrath" (the harsh, fiery aspect of nature).</note>, a new life might be born again within it through the "enclosure" of heaven. This was so the new life would have all the power and effect that the old life had before the times of wrath, and so that it could **inter-operate** <note>original: "inqualiren"; a term Böhme coined to describe how different spiritual qualities work together as one essence.</note> with the pure Divinity outside of this world, being one Holy GOD with the Divinity beyond this world. Furthermore, this new birth was blooming at the time of creation, had man not corrupted it—through which nature was corrupted even further, and GOD cursed the field.

<column-break/>

Because man reached for the fruit of the old body, the fruit of the new body now remains hidden in his "heaven" <note>His internal spiritual realm.</note>; man must now look upon it with a new body, for he cannot enjoy it with the natural body. I long to eat of it, yet I cannot reach it, for heaven is the barrier between the old and the new body. Therefore, I must do without until the next life, and give my animal body "apples of wrath" from Mother Eve to eat.

### 5. Question: What then is the "constellation" or "star-system" actually called in Divine Magic?
<term>Magia Divina</term> <note>Divine Magic; in this context, it refers to the supernatural power through which God brings the hidden, spiritual world into visible form.</note>

**Answer:** The constellation in Divine Magic is the source-well of the eternal mind of the **Abyss** <term>Ungrund</term> <note>The "Unground" or "Abyss" is Böhme’s term for the absolute, groundless nothingness that exists before God manifests Himself.</note>, from which nature and all beings have arisen. That such a constellation exists within the Divine Nature and its birth is testified by Holy Scripture itself, which calls GOD a **Sun**, and calls the Son of GOD the **Bright Morning Star**—called **Venus** by the **Astrologers** <term>Astrologis</term>—and **Lucifer** <note>In Böhme’s symbolic language, Lucifer was the highest angel before his fall; the name means "Light-Bringer," and here it refers to the original, uncorrupted light-force.</note>. This constellation is called a "constellation" with the highest ground of truth because it is the true source of fire and light from which all physical stars take their origin. However, this constellation of the Divine Nature stands in the Divine **Heavens** <note>original: "Schammajim"; the Hebrew word for heavens.</note> or the sea of fire and water in heaven and in the innermost birth, in the highest **balance** <term>Temperatur</term> <note>A state of perfect harmonic proportion where no single quality dominates another.</note>. In a word, they are nothing other than the seven **source-spirits** <note>The "Seven Qualities" or "Fountain Spirits" that Böhme describes as the building blocks of both God’s nature and the universe.</note> of GOD, and their many and varied powers and revelations. How these source-spirits stand in a struggle and working within the Divine Nature, and how the constellation in Divine Magic brings itself forth, is taught in detail by the Author in *Aurora*, Chapter 23, verses 15 to 73. Because we have already provided some opening on this above, we have passed over it here so as not to lead the reader away from our main **subject** <term>Propos</term>.

### 6. Question: What kind of constellation is in the Angelic Light-World?

**Answer:** The constellation in the **Angelic World** <note>original: "Englischen Welt"; here meaning the world of angels, not the nation of England.</note> is nothing other than a revelation of the qualification of GOD according to the seven forms of eternal nature. For as the essence of GOD shows itself in its birth, so too do the angels. Whatever power becomes **primary** <term>Primus</term> <note>The dominant or first-acting force.</note> in the birth of GOD at any time—rejoicing and rising from the heart of GOD in the Holy Spirit—that power also becomes primary in the Angelic Kingdom; and what is primary in the Angelic realm also becomes primary in the **sidereal** <note>The physical world of the stars.</note> realm and in all creatures. That such a constellation exists in the Angelic world is testified by Holy Scripture itself, which calls the angels "stars"; for most theologians understand that which is written in Isaiah 13:10 regarding the stars, Orion, the sun, and the moon, to refer to the Angelic rather than the sidereal constellation. Compare also what is written in Job 9:7, 8, and 9. Indeed, John in his Revelation calls the angels of the seven churches "stars" in express words.

Thus the ancient wise men taught how every creature of this visible world has its own

<column-break/>

angel and its own star; but especially every human being. Thus, just as eternal nature has its birth in GOD, in an angel, and in the "depth" of this world, so too is there such a birth of the constellation within the creatures—whether in humans, plants, animals, or metals. This is precisely the ground and foundation of true **Magic** <term>Magia</term> and of all working influence, as well as the **constellation** of all three worlds. For just as the angels are nothing but figures and properties that shape for us the inner birth, will, and thoughts of the invisible Deity: so the stars in the firmament, through their birth, constellation, and working, give us to understand the birth of the Angelic world.

If one wishes to discover the mysteries and the deepest ground, one must with diligence look upon and consider the creation of this world, its government and order, as well as the qualities of the stars and elements.

The Creator, after the gruesome fall of Lucifer’s kingdom, re-ordered these powers of the stars and elements into the same arrangement that the kingdom of Lucifer and his angels held in Divine **splendor** <note>original: "Pomp"; referring to the magnificent display of divine glory.</note> before the fall. This does not mean the angels turned around in a **planetary wheel** like the stars—which are merely powers and are turned around in this way because of the birth of this world. This birth and movement exists in a **tormenting anguish** <note>A Böhmean term for the restless tension in the material world.</note>, in evil and good, in corruption and redemption, until the end of this **reckoning** <term>Enumeration</term>. Just as the sun is an **essence** <term>Extract</term>—the light and heart of all the stars—and is therefore the most luminous and illuminates all stars in return, and all stars work back into its power, and it itself possesses the power of all stars, etc.: So also is a **Throne-Angel** <note>A high-ranking angel in the celestial hierarchy.</note>; he is, as mentioned above, the heart, the core, and an essence of the entire Angelic kingdom. And just as a Throne-Angel has his birth in an angelic way, so the Son of GOD has His birth in a Divine way: Thus is each one the revelation of the other.

# Part 3 / Chapter 6.

7. **Question:** Now we come to our intended purpose, dear friend; what then is actually the "constellation" <note>original: "Gestirn"; refers not just to stars, but to the entire governing system of the heavens and their influence.</note> of this visible world?

**Answer:** The constellation of this visible world is nothing other than an exhaled power of the inner spiritual world of Fire and Light. As for its material, it is made of the **Mercury** <term>Mercurio</term> <note>In Böhme's chemistry of the soul, Mercury represents the "word" or the vibrating, moving power of nature.</note> and the **Salitter** <term>Salitter</term> <note>A term unique to Böhme, referring to the divine substance or the "living sap" of the heavenly world, similar to saltpeter but spiritual in nature.</note> of the created heaven—or **Heavens** <note>original: "Schammajim"; the Hebrew word for the heavens.</note>. According to its form, it is a model and imprint of the stars of the invisible worlds, through which the great Mind of Divine Wisdom has revealed its wonder-working powers and qualities; playing with itself, it is a likeness of the inner birthing of GOD, both according to Fire and Light, and all their wondrous shapes and figures.

Thus, the stars are nothing other than a power of the seven **Source-Spirits** <term>Quell-Geister</term> <note>The seven fundamental qualities or "fountain-spirits" that Böhme believes constitute the nature of God and the universe.</note> of GOD. For when the wrath of GOD was ignited by the devils in this world, the whole house of this world—in its nature or outermost birth—became frozen as if in death, from which the earth and stones originated. But when that same hard "rubbish" was driven together into a single lump, the deep became clearer, yet remained entirely dark, for the light within it had died out in the wrath. But now, the "body of GOD" in this world could not remain in death; rather, GOD moved Himself with His seven Source-Spirits toward a new birth.

Then GOD would lock the devil into the house of darkness in a narrow cave, and ignite the whole house again in His light, except for the cave of the devil.

What had that same space in GOD sinned, that it should stand in eternal shame? Nothing; it would have been an injustice. ### Part 3 / Chapter 6.

...distinction between the eternal love and the **newly born love**; rather, that the newly born love reaches into the Essence that has existed from eternity, and also persists for itself into eternity.

Thus, the newly born love—which has risen from the **water of life** into the light among the stars and throughout the entire body of this world—is so closely bound to the eternal, unbeginning love that they are one heart and one spirit, which carries and maintains everything. In this ignition of the light within the stars and elements, the birth of nature did not transform entirely into **Holy Gentleness**, as it was before the time of the wrath, such that the birth of nature would now be entirely holy and pure; no, rather it stands in its sharpest, strictest, and most anxious birth, where the **wrath of God** greens without ceasing, like the fires of hell.

For if nature, with its sharp birth, had been entirely transformed into love according to heavenly law, then the devils would once again be in the holy seat of God. You can also see and understand this quite clearly in the cruel heat and cold, as well as in the poison of bitterness and sourness in this world, all of which resides in the **sidereal birth** <note>The "sidereal birth" refers to the influences and movements of the stars upon the physical world</note> wherein the devils lie imprisoned.

The stars are only the ignition of the "great house" <note>The "great house" is a metaphor for the physical universe</note>; for the entire house is frozen in death, just like the earth. The outermost birth is dead and frozen, like the bark upon a tree. But the **sidereal birth** is the body where the life rises within. In its own body, it is quite sharp; but the new birth, which rises in the **water of life** and penetrates through death, makes it gentle. It cannot, however, change the "kernel" of the sharp birth; instead, it is born out of it and keeps its holy life for itself, penetrating through the wrathful death—and the wrathful death cannot grasp it. This love and wrath are now indeed one body, but the water of

<column-break/>

life is the heaven of distinction between them. Thus, love does not take or grasp the wrath into itself, and neither does the wrath grasp the love. Instead, love rises in the **water of life** and draws the power into itself from the first and strict birth (the power which is in the light, born out of the wrath), so that the new body is born out of the old. For the old body, which stands in the strict birth, belongs to the devil's house, and the new body belongs to the kingdom of Christ.

<margin>Aurora 24. 14. 29. §. 40. 49.</margin>
From this we see quite clearly how the inner divine and angelic constellation <note>original: "Gestirn"</note>—following the property of fire and light—became manifest in the outer constellation as if in a model. It possesses the same manner of qualifying as the **sidereal constellation**; just as the former was born, so too does the latter bring itself forth.

8. **Question:** Can you not bring the birth of the stars to my understanding better through natural parables?

**Answer:** When you light a candle or a piece of wood, you see within it the entire process of birth, just like the Creation. As soon as the fire ignites the candle, everything that was within the candle opens up, and each thing dissolves according to its property: Fire, Air, Water, Oil, Earth, Ash, <term>etc.</term> Likewise, through the working of the living Word of God, the otherwise dead and frozen body of this world was ignited. In such an ignition, everything that was compacted in the **Chaos** opened up, each according to its kind. The **Sulfur** <note>original: "Sulphur"</note> caught the fire; the fire bore the air; the air, the water; the water, the earth; and each separates into its own **Ether** <note>original: "Æther"</note> and becomes manifest therein.

Here one understands quite fundamentally how the separation in the fire of eternal nature has manifested itself with a formal shape in the visible essence of the outer world. For in the ignition of the fire in the **salnitrous flash** <note>original: "salnitrischer Schracke," a term describing the sudden, explosive movement of spiritual forces into physical reality</note>, two essences separate: a watery one from the perishability in the fire. When the fire consumes the rough **welling quality** <note>original: "Quall," a term referring to the active, surging forces or "source-qualities" of nature</note> of the **Impression** <note>The "Impression" refers to the spiritual contraction that forms matter</note>, a great gentleness proceeds from that consumption; this gentleness has "died" to the fire, is beyond feeling, and provides the welling of the water.

Secondly, the **fiery source-quality** <term>Quall: Böhme’s term for a "source-spring" or "quality" that can also imply "torment" or "laboring power."</term> separates itself—namely, those properties of the fiery quality which have now become agonizing and sensible through the ignition of the fire—into its own Principle. This fiery quality could not persist if it did not swallow the water back into itself, by which it strengthens itself; from this arises the **Salnitric terror** <note>original: "Salnitrische Schrack." This refers to a sudden, explosive flash like saltpeter (gunpowder), representing the moment life or consciousness is sparked from the friction of forces.</note>, wherein the "wrath" is startled before the essence of the water’s gentleness. From this, sensation arises, as well as the radiance of the fire. For that which is swallowed from the water into the fire is resolved into a **spiritual oil**, in which the fire shines; and from this oil comes the **air**, acting as the weaving spirit of the fire, which has become mobile within the fire.

Air is nothing other than the **moving life**, where the **speaking Word** <note>The "speaking Word" refers to the divine creative command acting through the forces of nature.</note> expresses itself through nature, through the powers of nature, through the fire in the oil of the nature of light, and in the source of the water. It is the life of the fire, yet it has "died" to the fire and is nonetheless made manifest by the fire; it is the life of nature according to the property of gentleness. Thus, with the ignition of the fire in the light of the fire (which is the light of nature), we are to understand four properties: a fiery, an airy, and an oily one (in which the light is manifest), and a watery one. These all originally arise from the first "desire toward nature," as the **free pleasure** introduces itself into a desire and a nature; they all express themselves through the fire into a moving life, and yet it is not a conscious life, but only properties belonging to the true life. The **conscious life** is the "out-breathed" Word that reveals itself through these properties. These properties are impressed in the creative command, that is, in the **Word "Let there be"** <note>original: "Verbo Fiat"</note>, and have entered into an essence. From this, a **Sulfur of Saltpeter** <note>original: "Sulphur Salnitri"</note> has come to be; that is, a magical constellation of stars, in the manner and way of the human mind, which also has its true origin therein.

This salnitric and sulfuric property has been carried out from the work of the third day, as

What nature is within itself in a tiny spark, the entire constellation of stars is in its great circle; and what nature is in its secrecy and hiddenness, the constellation is in an open, working essence. This is to be understood thus: every single star has the property of all stars within it, but hidden within its nature, and is manifest in only one single property. Otherwise, if the whole of nature were manifest in every single thing, then all things and beings would be only one thing and essence. It is an echo from God’s love and wrath, from the dark and light worlds. And note this well to understand it rightly: in every element lies an entire constellation of stars. 9. **Question:** What then does the Author actually understand by the "constellation" or "starry heavens"?

**Answer:** Nothing other than the **revelation of God** according to fire and light, as it brings itself forth in the entire visible world and in every creature within it. For in all places where **Mercury** and **Salitter** <term>Salitter: A term used by Böhme for the divine "sap" or saltpeter-like explosive force within nature that powers growth and life.</term>, fire and water come together, they bring forth an **Astrum** <note>original: "Astrum" — a Latin term for a star or celestial influence.</note>: divine in God, angelic in the angels, heavenly in the heavens, and earthly on the earth. Indeed, as mentioned above, one is the revelation and likeness of the other; without this likeness, God Himself would be invisible and incomprehensible to the understanding. In particular, however, the constellation refers to the lights which God created on the fourth day of creation in the depths of the heavens.

<column-break/>

10. **Question:** From whence do the many kinds of stars in the heavens arise?

**Answer:** Just as the **seven Source-Spirits** <note>original: "Quell-Geister" — Böhme's fundamental qualities of nature: Sourness, Sweetness, Bitterness, Heat, Love, Sound, and Substance.</note> of God had, before the time of wrath, born themselves into us through their rising and infecting <note>Meaning their mutual influence and blending</note>, from which so many figures and growths have since emerged; so too did the Holy God shape His "old body" of this corrupted nature into as many various powers as had ever stood in the birth within Holiness. Every star has its own property, just like the plants, trees, flowers, and herbs of the blooming earth; the birds of the air, the fish of the sea, and all the various creatures. Even human beings themselves each have a special figure, image, and property. These stars in the depths are now divided into **planets** and **fixed stars**. The King of both is the **Sun**. The planets are the bodies and houses of the seven Source-Spirits of God. The fixed stars are the forms and figures of the various births of the Source-Spirits. The planets are, as it were, the **vowels**; the fixed stars, however, are the **consonants**. These form, figure, and shape the **spoken Word** in the "Great Book" of this world. The vowels and consonants make syllables, the syllables make words, the words make a speech and a sentence; and thus God's almighty Word speaks out the **formed Word**, through which God reveals His Holy Will.

The entire constellation is nothing other than the external **Spoken Word** in sound. It is the instrument through which the Holy, Eternally-Speaking Word speaks and forms itself externally. It is like a great harmony of unfathomably many voices, from all kinds of instruments, playing before the Holy God. For they are nothing but powers that move into one another with their working, from which a sound rings out in the **essence**. This same sound is captured by the **Desire**—acting as the *Fiat*—which makes it substantial. That substance is a "spirit of the stars," which the elements take into themselves, coagulating and brooding over it just as a hen broods over her eggs. For its radiance or shine has a degree, a deep origin, just as the outer world is manifest within itself. The wise pagans noticed this and honored the sun as God, because the true God, who dwells in himself beyond all nature, was not known to them.

11. **Question:** Which then is the most glorious and greatest light that God has created?

**Answer:** The most glorious wonder of the entire visible great world is the sun. Moses writes that God said: Let there be lights in the firmament of heaven to divide the day and the night, and let them be for signs, seasons, days, and years; and let them be lights in the firmament of heaven to shine upon the earth; and it was so. And God made two great lights: a greater light to rule the day, and a lesser light to rule the night, along with the stars. And God set them in the firmament of heaven to shine upon the earth, and to rule over the day and the night, and to divide the light from the darkness.

### Part 3 / Chapter 6.

Although Moses wrote correctly that they [the stars] shall rule day and night, and also distinguish between light and darkness, and create seasons, years, and days, this is not yet sufficiently understood by the eager reader; for one finds a very high thing in the **power** <term>power: "Krafft" in the original, referring to the inherent virtue, energy, or "operating force" within a thing.</term> and authority of the stars: how all life, growth, colors, and virtues—thick and thin, small and large, good and evil—proceed from their power. Because of this, the wise heathens were also beguiled and honored them as GOD. Therefore, I wish to write something of their **origin** <note>original: "Urkund" — meaning the primordial record, source, or testimony of their beginning.</note>, as far as is permitted to me at this time, for the sake of the seekers who desire the pearls. But for the swine and other wild "beast-men," I have written nothing; they who trample the pearls into the muck and mock and despise the spirit of knowledge. They may expect the first world's flood of fire; and if they will not bear the **angelic image**, then they must bear the image of lions and dragons, as well as of evil worms and beasts. If they will not let themselves be advised so that GOD might help them, they must then experience for themselves whether the Scripture of prophecy will prove to be a lie.

The Evangelist John writes of the origin of the wise ones and the creatures of this world in such a high and correct manner as is found in no other writing in the Bible: *In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with GOD, and GOD was the Word; the same was in the beginning with GOD. All things were made through the same, and without the same nothing was made that was made. In him was life, and the life was the light of men, and the light shone in the darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it.* <note>John 1:1–5</note>

See what John says: In the beginning of creation, and before the times of the world, the Word existed, and the Word was GOD, and in the Word was the light that shone in the darkness, and the darkness could not grasp it.

<column-break/>

Here one understands clearly: firstly, how the eternal light is GOD; and understands secondly, how it has its eternal origin in the eternal power; and understands thirdly, how it is the eternal Word that shines in the darkness. Since that same Word has created all things in all places, it has also been in all places, for without it, nothing was made.

Now, that same Word had no **material** <note>original: "Materia"</note> from which it made anything; rather, it created all things out of the darkness and brought them into the light so that they might appear and exist. For in him was life, and he gave life into the creatures, and the creature is from his power, and the power became material, and the light shines within it, but the material power cannot grasp it, for it is in the darkness. But because the material power cannot grasp the light that shines from eternity in the darkness, GOD has given it another light that arose from the power—namely the **sun**, which shines in the creature so that the creature may be in the light and be manifest.

For firstly, just as the Godhead is the power and light of Paradise in the **second Principle** <term>second Principle: In this cosmological system, the Second Principle is the world of Light/Paradise, while the First is the world of Fire/Darkness and the Third is the physical world.</term>; so the sun is the power and light of this material world in the **third Principle**. And secondly, just as the Godhead shines in the eternal darkness in the **first Principle**; so the sun shines in the darkness in the third Principle. And thirdly, just as the Godhead is the eternal power and the spirit of eternal life; so the sun is the power and the spirit in the fragile [material] life.

Now, a spirit is nothing other than an ascending will, and in the will is the **anguish** <note>original: "Aengstlichkeit" — a technical term in this philosophy referring to the "contraction" or "labor pains" of nature as it strives toward birth.</note> for birth, and in the anguish, the fire is born, and in the fire, the light; and from the light, the will becomes friendly, lovely, mild, and sweet; and in the sweet will, the power is born, and out of the power, the kingdom and the glory are born. Thus the light retains the...

# Of the Revelation of GOD on the fourth Day.

Power / where that is extinguished / there ends the **force** <term>force: "Krafft" in the original, referring to the inherent energy or "operating virtue" of a thing.</term> and glory / and also the kingdom.

GOD / who is the eternal light / is the eternal Will / he shines in the darkness / and the darkness has seized the Will / and in the same Will / which the darkness has seized / there arises **anxiety** <note>original: "Aengstlichkeit" — in this context, it refers to a state of constriction or creative tension, like the pressure before a birth.</note> / and in the harsh anxiety the fire / and in the fire the light / and out of the light the force / and out of the force the kingdom. Now from the fire became the stars / and further the sun / and from the force the heavens / and the kingdom is GOD’s. All of this was together in the first Will in the creation. Then GOD separated the fiery will from the mild light-will / and called the fiery one "stars" / and the mild one "heaven" / according to the force of each.

The Sun is the **goddess** <note>In German, the word for Sun ("die Sonne") is feminine. The author personifies the Sun as a ruling feminine power within the physical world.</note> in the **third principle** <term>third principle: "tertium principium," the material world of the four elements produced by the interaction of light and darkness.</term> in the created world / understand this to be in the material force / which has gone out from the darkness in the anxiety of the Will / in the manner and way of the eternal birth. For when the **Fiat** <note>Latin: "Let it be done," the creative command of God.</note> of God placed itself into the darkness / the darkness received the Will of GOD / and became pregnant unto birth / the Will creates the harshness / the attraction and the stirring of attraction toward mobility / it creates the bitterness / the bitterness creates the woe / and the woe creates the anxiety / and the anxiety creates the rubbing, breaking, and rising. Now the harshness cannot endure the rubbing / and pulls itself together much harder / and the bitterness or the attraction cannot be held / but breaks and stabs so hard in the pulling / until it awakens the heat / in which the **flash** <note>original: "Blitz" — a sudden discharge of spiritual energy.</note> arises / and from the flash the dark harshness is terrified / and in the **terror** <note>original: "Schrack" — a central concept in this theology, representing the moment of sudden transformation or "shock" when fire turns to light.</note> the fire ignites / and in the fire the light. Now there would be no light there / if the terror did not happen in the harshness / but would remain only fire; but the terror in the harshness from the fire / kills the hard harshness / so that it sinks down to the bottom like dregs / and becomes as if dead and gentle /

<column-break/>

and when the flash beholds itself in the harshness / it is much more terrified / in that it finds the mother so mild and half-killed in a faint. In this terror its fiery right becomes white / gentle and mild / and is the ignition of the light / where the fire is transformed into a **white hell** <note>original: "weisse Hölle" — a paradoxical term used by the author to describe the luminous, white-hot center of divine fire or the clarified state of the light-world.</note>. In such a manner did the Sun arise in the *Fiat*.

12. **Question.** Reveal to me the birth of the Sun and its ignition somewhat more thoroughly / especially regarding its **matter** <note>original: "Materia."</note> from which it burns / and its **form and figure** <note>original: "Forma und Figur."</note> through which it reveals itself and shines?

**Answer.** When GOD had brought the body of this world into a proper **form** <note>original: "Formam."</note> in two days / and made the heaven as a distinction between love and wrath / then on the third day the love pressed through the heaven / through the wrath / then the old body in death stirred at once / and experienced anxiety toward birth / for love is hot / it ignited the fire-source / which rubbed itself in the harsh and cold quality of frozen death / until the harsh quality on the third day grew hot / from which then the harsh earth was made movable. For everything stood in the **fire-terror** until the fourth day / when the light of the Sun ignited / then the whole body was in the anxiety of birth / like a woman in labor. The harsh quality had been the encompasser / and the encloser of life / in it the heat now labored / which was ignited through the love of GOD / and pressed out through the harsh quality as through a dead body / but the heat kept its seat in the center point of the body / and pressed through. But as the light of the Sun now ignited / the nearest circle around the Sun stood in the fire-terror / for the Sun or the light became shining in the water / and the bitterness out of the water rose up with it in the fire-terror; But the light was hurrying so swiftly after / and seized the fire-terror / there it remained standing like a prisoner / and became physical.

3. Part / Chapter 6.

But because the heat in the middle point of the body was so powerfully great / it pushed out so far from itself / and opened the chamber of death before the kindling of the light so wide / that she (the Sun) is the greatest star. But as soon as the light kindled in the heat / the heated place was immediately captured in the light / and the **body** <term>body: "Corpus" in the original Latin, referring to the physical mass or substance of the star.</term> of the Sun could not become any larger / for the light softened the heat / there the body of the Sun remained standing in the middle as a heart / for the light is the heart of nature / and not the heat.

### Here, however, you must take special note.

As far as the middle point has kindled itself / so large is the Sun / for the SUN is nothing else / than a kindled point in the body of nature. You must not think / that there is perhaps some other power involved / than what is everywhere in the entire depth of the body.

If the love of GOD through his heaven wanted to kindle the entire body of this world through the heat / it would be as bright everywhere / as in the Sun. Now, if the great heat could be taken from the Sun / it would be one light with GOD: but because the same cannot be in this time / it remains a king and regent in the old corrupted and kindled body of nature / and the clear Godhead remains hidden in the gentle heaven. But the light of the gentleness of the Sun **interacts** <note>original: "inqualiret" — a term used by Böhme to describe how different qualities or forces work together and influence one another.</note> with the pure Godhead / but the heat cannot grasp the light / therefore the place of the Sun also remains in the body of the wrath of God / and you must not worship the Sun or honor it as God / for its place or body cannot grasp the water of life / because of its **fierceness** <note>original: "Grimmigkeit" — refers to the harsh, consuming, or "wrathful" quality of fire/heat in Böhme's system.</note>.
<margin>Aurora, chapters 25, 29—41.</margin>

From which it is to be seen / that the Sun is made of no other material / than precisely from the very purest **sulfur** <term>sulfur: in alchemy, the "Sulphur" principle represents the soul, the combustible element, and the source of light and heat.</term> in the **salitter** <term>salitter: a term unique to Jacob Böhme, referring to the divine "saltpeter" or the foundational substance of the spiritual and physical world from which all qualities grow.</term>, which sulfur, oil, and balsam in the whole of nature was the most noble, subtle, and pure, which kindled itself first.

13. Question: At what place was the Sun born?

Answer: The place / where the Sun is / is such a place / as any place you might choose above the earth. If GOD willed to kindle the light through the heat / the entire world would be nothing but such a Sun / for that same power / in which the Sun stands / is everywhere / and before the time of wrath it was as bright everywhere in the place of this world / as the Sun is / but not so unbearably. For the heat was not as great as in the Sun / therefore the light was also quite gentle / and because of the cruel fierceness of the Sun / the Sun is distinguished from the gentleness of GOD. Therefore one must not say / the Sun is an open gate of the light of GOD / but she is like the light in the human eye / where the place of the eye also belongs to the body / but the light is distinguished from the body. And although it arises through the heat in the water of the body / yet it is a distinct thing / which the body cannot grasp. Such a distinction also exists between God the Father and the Son.

Thus on the fourth day in the **anxiety-birth** <note>referring to the cosmic tension or "labor pains" of creation described on the previous page.</note> of this world, the Sun rose in the middle point of this world / and stands still in her eternal bodily place / for she cannot take herself from one place / and set herself in another. For she is the only natural light of this world / and outside of her there is no more true light in the house of death: And although it seems / as if the other stars also shone brightly / yet it is nothing / rather they all take their brilliance from the Sun.
<margin>Aurora, 25, 63—67.</margin>

This sulfur or fire-salt, oil, and balsam of the heavenly **salitter**, from which the Sun burns and shines, is in all places; for before the fall of Lucifer and the kindling of this world, the entire depth was full of **heavens** <note>original: "Schamajim" — the Hebrew word for heavens.</note>, in which the **tincture** <term>tincture: the spiritual essence or "color" that brings life and perfection to matter.</term> was born, which is why this entire world was transparent and light, which the ancient sages, and after them **Descartes** <note>original: "Cartesius."</note>, also recognized.

14. **Question:** Does the sun then not have its course around the earth, just as we see that it rises at one end in the morning and sets at the other end in the evening?

**Answer:** The sun has its own royal place <note>original: "Locum"</note> for itself / and does not deviate from its place / where it was first created / as some think / that it runs around the earth day and night / as even some astrologers write / and some have even dared to measure how wide its circumference might be. This opinion is incorrect / rather the earth turns itself / and runs with the other planets as if in a wheel / around the sun / the earth does not remain standing in one place / but runs around the sun once in a year / as do the other planets beneath the sun / except Saturn and Jupiter cannot do so <insert>in a single year</insert> because of their wide circuit and great height / since they stand high above the sun.

<margin>Aurora 25: 60, 61</margin>
The six planets run around the sun / as around their heart / and give power to it / and fetch power in the sun. So also life winds itself around the heart / and presses into the heart / then the spirit-life presses toward the soul / which burns out of the heart / out of the heart’s tincture <term>tincture: in Böhme’s alchemy, this is the subtle medicinal or spiritual essence that transmits life and light</term> / as a light / and into that they wind themselves / and one always drives the other forward / and the form is like a turning wheel / for the life of the spirit is thus from its origin. Those who say that the sun runs forth / they speak as the blind do of color / and have never yet recognized the Center of Nature <note>original: "Centrum Naturæ"</note> / although one should not blame them / for it has been reserved / until the Seal of the Sun has opened at the sound of the seventh trumpet <note>A reference to the Book of Revelation; Böhme believes he is living in a time of final spiritual disclosure</note>. Take note / it is no joke or boast / it applies to you all / or you will die blind / for which GOD is innocent.

The world has been one-eyed since the Fall of Adam / for it had lived with its knowledge under the six seals / understand under the six planets; But the seventh seal is opening / then you shall see with the eyes of the Sun <note>original: "Solis"</note>. We speak here of what we recognize and see: So understand us rightly / we wish to ease the difficult concept for you.

<margin>Threefold Life 9: 99, 100, 101</margin>
Thus our author has seen into the mystery of the sun’s stillness / and the earth’s, as well as the planets’ course around the sun, even before the times of the great Descartes <note>original: "Cartesii"</note>, and demonstrated the same with much better and more solid reasons, rightly from nature.

15. **Question:** What power and effect does the sun then have upon the rest of the stars and all creatures?

**Answer:** Just as the Son and the Heart of GOD is active in the divine world, and the throne-angels in the angelic world. And therefore this world is recognized as its own principle <term>principle: "Principium" — a fundamental realm of existence, in this case, the third or material world</term> / because it has its own nature-god; compared thus / as namely the sun / and yet the light of the Godhead truly shines through everything / through and through. The light of the sun takes essence from GOD’S fire / and GOD’S fire from GOD’S light. Thus the light of the sun gives that same power to the elements / these give it to the creatures / also to the plants of the earth / and everything / that is of good quality / thus receives GOD’S power for a vision / through the mirror of wisdom / from which it has its growth and life. ### 3. Part / Chapter 6. 563, 564

GOD stands present to all being / but not all being receives him in His essence <note>original: "Essentz"</note>. Rather, it is like a mirror reflecting the power of the Sun; for the Sun arises from the eighth number <note>The "eighth number" in Böhmean theosophy refers to the eternal world beyond the seven properties of nature</note>. Its root / from which it receives its shine / is the eternal fire / but its body <note>original: "Corpus"</note> stands in this world. Its desire is directed entirely into this world / therefore it shines into the world; but its first root stands in the first world / in the fire of GOD. This world gives substance to its desire / and it gives its power to substance / and thus fills all being of this world / just as GOD’S light fills the Divine Light-World; and if GOD’S fire burned no longer / the Sun would be extinguished and also the Divine Light-World. For God’s fire gives essence to both, and is a principle <note>original: "Principium"</note> of them both. And if the dark world were not / these two would also not be; for the dark world provides the causes for God’s fire. Thus also must the three worlds be within one another / for nothing may exist without a ground. For the Dark-World is the ground of nature / and the eternal unfathomable will / which is called the Father / is the ground of the dark world / as mentioned before / and the Light-World is hidden in the dark / and also this world in the Light-World. It is to be understood thus: That this world is enclosed in the wrath of God as if in death; for the wrath greens in the being of this world / were that not so / the being of this world might well perceive GOD’S light. Thus this world receives only a glimmer <note>original: "Glast"</note> with the Sun’s power from GOD. The Sun is not GOD’S light / for it does not shine entirely in Divine essence / but in elemental essence. But it has GOD’S fire for its root / yet is filled with the being of this world; for it is desiring as a magical craving / and receives into its imagination and craving the power of the stars and elements / and from the same it also shines. Although GOD’S fire is the root / it nevertheless does not belong to GOD’S kingdom. And

For the light and the power of this world is contrary to him / he does not go with his will into the property of the light / for he also cannot. He stands with his back against the light of the Sun / in his figure and property; therefore the Sun-light is of no use to him / and everything that grows in the Sun’s power / that makes itself own to the Sun / he treats as an enemy; his will does not like to enter into it.

16. **Question:** So much has been spoken of the Sun’s power and effect in general, does it now follow to reveal such effects in particular?

**Answer:** The Sun consists of fire and light, so it also works according to both principles, of fire and light, that is: it burns, heats, enlightens, and shines. Its effect in and of itself is universal / but it becomes particular in the object <note>original: "Vorwurf," referring to the thing receiving the light</note> into which it works, and such effects are innumerable, and indescribable. According to the first form of nature <note>Böhme’s seven properties of nature describe how reality manifests from spiritual desire into physical form</note> it makes dry, hard, stern. According to the second, it dissolves, melts, drives, and makes thin. According to the third it is enclosing, essential, igniting. According to the fourth it brings forth the fire, out of the fire the lightning, and in the sinking down of the lightning the water-source: as the fire now works in the water, it brings forth the light, luster, and majesty. According to the fifth form it is gentle, lovely, warming. According to the sixth gentle, moving, rejoicing. In the seventh it makes everything bodily and substantial / and seeks to bring everything to a perfect maturity <note>original: "Maturität"</note>: As is especially to be seen in precious stones and those things where the solar tincture <term>tincture: the vital, transformative essence of a substance</term> predominates.

Because now nothing is under the sun where the Sun’s tincture is not within, and where it does not have its qualification, therefore the Sun infects and applies itself to all things, and as a property in a thing has the upper hand, according to such figure and form the Sun also becomes active. It is the Mother and the Center, from which the life and growth of all things has its beginning. Therefore every thing yearns for the Sun, for it is the tincturing of all beings, the planets, stars, metals, plants, animals, etc. Just as the Sun’s power and rays unlock the mystery <note>original: "Mysterium"</note> of the outer world/
