[of]fen <note>This completes the word "offen" (open) from the previous page's catchword "so."</note> / so that creatures and plants proceed from it: Thus also, on the other hand, the Mystery <note>original: "Mysterium"</note> of the outer world is a cause in which the Sun's rays unfold and ignite. If the Great Mystery <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"</note>—consisting of Sulphur, Salt, and Mercury <note>The "Tria Prima" or three primary principles of Böhmean alchemy: Sulphur (the soul/fire), Salt (the body/substance), and Mercury (the spirit/movement)</note> of a spiritual type and property / did not lie in the Spirit of the World <note>original: "Spiritu Mundi"</note> / as in the Science <note>original: "Scientz"; here meaning the latent potential or "knowing" will within nature</note> of the stars' properties / which is a Fifth Essence <note>original: "Quinta Essentia"</note> over the four elements: then the Sun’s rays could not be revealed. But because the Sun is nobler / and one degree deeper in nature / than the Mystery of the outer world / namely / than the Spirit of the World / in Sulphur, Salt, and Mercury / in the Fifth Essence of the stars; it therefore penetrates into the outer Mystery / and ignites that / and also herewith itself / so that its rays become fiery / for otherwise they would not be fiery without the Science in the Mystery of this world. And just as the Sun now leads its desire vehemently into the Science, into the Mystery, as into these first three / namely Salt, Sulphur, and Mercury / to ignite and reveal itself in them: so also the Science leads its desire out of the Fifth Essence of the stars / through these first three / as Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt / just as vehemently toward the Sun / as its Nature-God / which is a soul of the Great Mystery in the outer Elemental world / as a likeness of the inner hidden GOD. One also sees / how the stars are so greedy and hungry for the Sun’s power / that they lead their Science and desire / in a magnetic fashion within the Spirit of the World / into the first three principles / and draw the Sun’s power into themselves; conversely, the Sun also powerfully penetrates into them / to receive their Science: therefore they have their shine from the Sun’s power / so that they in turn cast their ignited power / as a fruit / into the four elements / and thus qualify in one another / and each one is the other's revelation / as well as power and life / as well as the other's breaking / so that one property does not rise up above all the others.

Thus has the Highest spoken it into a likeness according to his own Being / out of his eternally-speaking Word / out of the eternal Great Mystery (which is entirely spiritual) into a Time / and represented the Eternal / in a Time / with a figure / in which all creaturely life originates / and also therein conducts its governance; except for the angels / and eternal spirits / as well as the right inner soul of the true human; these have their origin from the eternal beginning-less Science or Nature / as shall be mentioned hereafter.

### Concerning the Planets in General.

**17. Question: How were the remaining planets born on the firmament and in nature?**

**Answer:** Just as the six source-spirits <term>Source-Spirits: The seven fundamental qualities (the seventh being the "house") of Böhmean nature that generate all reality.</term> are born in the Godhead, and the Throne-Princes in the Light-World, so also the six remaining planets were born from the Sun, according to the manner and law of that impression and image which the Salitter <term>Salitter: A term Böhme used to describe the divine "substance" or "soil" of heaven, which became harsh or corrupted in the fallen kingdom of Lucifer.</term> of the kingdom of Lucifer had within itself, and according to the property of the working of GOD, in the creative Word or Fiat <note>The "Let there be" command of God</note>, which became active according to the properties of Fire and Light. According to the property of Fire, as Harshness, Bitterness, and Anguish—Salt, Sulphur, and Mercury—were born Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars, above the Sun; according to the property of Light, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon <note>original: "Luna"</note>, were born below the Sun. But the Sun, as the King, remains in the middle, for it is the center <note>original: "Centrum"</note> and the mother, from whom the other stars, as children, have gone forth. Our highly-enlightened author compares the birth of the stars to the birth of a human: the Sun is the heart, where the life ignites; Mars the gall, as the property of fire; Jupiter the brain; and Saturn the skull, etc.

# Of the Revelation of God on the Fourth Day.

By the power of the hidden heaven, Nature could not rest, but labored in the anguish of birth <note>In Böhme’s thought, "anguish" (Aengstlichkeit) refers to a creative, contracting tension or pressure required for birth.</note>; and from the spirit of sharpness, she brought forth the harsh, cold, and severe son or star, Saturn. For the spirit of heat could not ignite itself—from which the light, and from the light through the water, love and gentleness arise—instead, it was a birth of severe, cold, and earnest fierce wrath <note>original: "Grimmigkeit." For Böhme, this refers to the harsh, raw power of nature before it is softened by divine light.</note>. He is a desiccator, a destroyer, and an enemy of gentleness, who brings forth the hard bones within creatures. 

SATURN, however, is not bound to his place <note>original: "Locum"</note> like the Sun; for he is not a bodily location in the space of the deep, but rather a son born out of the chamber of death, out of the ignited, hard, and cold anguish. He is merely a house-companion in the space wherein he runs his course. For he possesses his own bodily property, like a child once it is born from its mother.

Just as the Sun is the heart of life and a cause of the spirits of nature, so Saturn is the heart and a cause of all bodies and formation within the earth and upon the earth, as well as in the entire body of this world.

And just as in man the skull <note>original: "Hirn-Schaale," literally brain-shell.</note> is an encloser and a sealer of the brain, wherein thoughts are born, so the Saturnine power is an encloser, a desiccator, and a keeper of all corporeality and tangibility. And just as the planet Jupiter is an opener and bearer of gentleness, standing between the fierce Mars and the severe Saturn, and brings forth gentleness and wisdom in creatures: so also the life and the sense of all creatures is born between these two qualities—especially the new body of this world, as well as the new man, about which you will find more in the description of man.

In the animal kingdom, he is the cause of all corporeality, hardness, legs, bones, and skulls. In the mineral kingdom, he is called Lead; his property, however, is found not only in lead but in all metals, for he is the cause of all hardness. If Saturn were not, all metals would be like a running <term>Mercury</term> or quicksilver, and all stones would be like water. The Solar <term>Tincture</term> <note>The spiritual essence or "soul" of the sun's light.</note>, grasped and enclosed by Saturn, creates a magnificent brilliance, as seen in gemstones, which are transparent, clarified minerals and harder than all other stones. Through these two stars and their constellation, according to the property of the Light-World, the great Crystal Sea is generated, of which Revelation speaks, and the gemstones of the New Jerusalem.

# Of the Revelation of GOD on the Fourth Day.

Through the power of the hidden heavens, Nature could not remain at rest but labored toward birth; from the spirit of sharpness <note>The "spirit of sharpness" refers to the astringent, contracting quality in Böhme’s theosophy that draws things together into a solid form.</note>, she brought forth the bitter, cold, and severe son or star, **Saturn**. Just as the Sun is the heart of life and a cause of the Nature-spirits, so Saturn is the heart and a cause of all bodies and formation in the Earth and upon the Earth, as well as in the entire body of this world.

And just as in man the skull is an encloser and a shutter of the brain, wherein thoughts are born, so the Saturnian power is an encloser, dryer, and sustainer of all corporeality and tangibility. And just as the planet Jupiter is an opener and bringer-forth of gentleness—standing between the grim Mars and the severe Saturn, and bringing forth gentleness and wisdom in the creatures—so also the life and the sense of all creatures is born between these two qualities; especially the new body of this world, as well as the new man, concerning which you will find more in the description of Man.

<margin>Aurora 26. 14.</margin>

From this we now see clearly what kind of birthing, power, and effect Saturn has, both in the sidereal <note>pertaining to the stars</note> heaven and in all of Nature. In the vegetable kingdom, he is a cause of all saps, as well as the external tangibility of wood; the harder it is, the more alkaline saltiness is found in the ashes. In the animal kingdom, he is a cause of all hardness: toughness, bones, skeletal structures, and skulls. In the mineral kingdom, he is called **Lead**; his property, however, is found not only in lead but in all metals, for he is the cause of all hardness. If Saturn were not, all metals would be like a running **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurio," referring to liquid quicksilver.</note> or quicksilver, and all stones would be like water. The Solar Tincture <note>The "Tincture" is the spiritual "dye" or essence that gives a substance its noble qualities, such as the color and value of gold.</note>, when captured and enclosed by Saturn, creates a magnificent brilliance, as can be seen in precious stones, which are transparent, clarified minerals and harder than all other stones. Their body is nothing other than a pure water that has been drawn together into a crystal and hardened by Saturn's power, and fixed by the Sun's heat so that it may not be dissolved again. Through these two stars <note>original: "Astra"</note> and their constellation, according to the property of the Light-World, the great **Crystal Sea** is generated, of which Revelation speaks, as well as the gemstones of the New Jerusalem.

### 21. Question: Where does Venus have her seat, and what is her office and effect?

If Mars did not so greatly permeate Venus with his poisonous life and fire-power, Venus would shine in pure chastity and glory like gold. Because every planet has the property of all planets within itself, all planets also possess the properties of Venus; otherwise, they could not exist. Venus gives all the fiery planets drink from her fountain: from this fountain, **Mercury** and the **Moon** <note>original: "Luna"</note> also flow. According to the spirit, she is the Love-desire; but according to the essence or body, she is water—which water, in the metals, provides the noble **Body of the Sun** <note>original: "Corpus Solis." In alchemy, this refers to Gold, the most perfect metal.</note>.

### Of the Planet Mercury, and his Origin, Quality, and Operation.

**23. Question: What kind of planet is Mercury?**

**Answer:** Mercury is the sixth planet, wherein the sixth form of nature has made its quality manifest in the deep above the earth: he is born from the Sun, according to the quality of the water, as a sinking-away of the fire-power. When Venus has drawn the power from the Sun, she retains the Sulfur, Balsam, Oil, and Fat; the watery part, however, becomes sinking beneath the oily and sulfurous.

Because Mercury now takes his power from Venus, he is therefore so merry / he likes to speak of all the wisdom of nature; He is a nimble, quick awakener of the seed / which Venus gives him / for he wants to awaken the body / and because he knows much / he wants to wander into everything / and gives languages to the body / and awakens it / gives it his own / especially into the brain / and into the womb <note>original: "Matricem"</note> of the seed.

What Jupiter is according to the quality of fire, that is Mercury according to the quality of water; and just as Jupiter stands between Saturn and Mars as a mediator, so Mercury stands between Venus and the Moon, which is why he also has the signature <note>original: "Signatur"</note> of both as ☿. He is very driving and volatile, he divides, separates, and makes thin where he has the upper hand. According to the wrath- and anger-quality he is a thief and murderer, a volatile consuming poison; according to the love-quality, he curbs and hinders the harsh power of Saturn, especially in the Moon.

In the Vegetable Kingdom he leads the volatile fire- and life-spirits in his power: he is the first who awakens in the kindling of the fire,

### Of the Planet Luna or Moon.

24. **Question:** Which then is the seventh planet?

**Answer:** The seventh planet, according to the seven properties of nature, is called the **Moon** <note>original: "Luna"</note>. Just as the seventh property is a body and essence, an enclosure and dwelling-house for the other six source-spirits, so too is Luna a mixed body <note>original: "Corpus"</note> made of all the other planets. Its qualifying and birth is either heavenly and internal, or external and earthly. Internally and heavenlily, the Moon is not only in the firmament but also in all things of a Solar property; for the Moon is from the Sun, as the woman is from the man. Therefore, its growths in minerals <note>original: "Minera"</note>, in herbs, and in animals are the noblest after the Sun, because its qualifying—both in its star and in all creatures—comes closest to the Sun. Indeed, it is internally Sun; therefore its hunger and desire are for the Sun, from which it also takes its luster. Its outer body is a confluence of the essence of all planets; Mercury is its nearest neighbor, who

<column-break/>

makes Luna so volatile and inconstant, and its luster so water-colored and pale.

What Mercury takes from the other planets, he cannot keep for himself, but lets it sink beneath him into Luna. For instance, Venus gives it balsam and sulfur; Mars gives it the fiery spirit of life; Saturn captures the outer body of Luna; therefore, it is a mixed body made of all. It is the "maggot-sack" <note>original: "Maden-Sack." A Böhmean term for the physical body as a vessel of corruptible matter and various conflicting influences.</note> of the planetary body; it receives everything that Mercury fills into it; it holds everything and does not let it sink; it receives everything and makes the whole image like an animal. It is corporality; in it, Venus curdles and stands always in fear of a fall because of the Earth, which stands beneath it. For it feels the Wrath <note>original: "Zorn" or "Grimm," the harsh quality of the first principle of nature.</note> in the Earth; therefore, it is afraid and lets nothing sink, but runs and hurries as if it were volatile. It is false, for it desires both the Upper and the Lower; it hypocritically aligns with the Center of the Earth and also with the Center of the Sun. It is of a feminine quality and has its heart or innermost being in the Sun, just as the woman has her heart in the man; it also receives all masculine planets, *etc.* From this, it is easy to consider what Luna is in the creatures of the earth, in animals, herbs, and minerals.

But the spirit of the soul—if it be turned around so that it sees into the interior with its own eyes, and into the exterior with the eyes of this world—that spirit understands it. For that is the vision in Ezekiel <note>A reference to the biblical vision of the "wheel within a wheel" in Ezekiel 1:15-21</note>, of the Spirit with the internal and external eyes, where the Spirit goes straight forward, and wherever it goes.

Although the wise Magi <note>original: "Magi"; high practitioners of spiritual wisdom or alchemy</note> and Mathematicians <note>original: "Mathematici"; here meaning astronomers and geometricians</note> have made a Sphere <note>original: "Sphæram"</note> and drafted the wheel, it is still not enough. It is indeed a way for those who do not understand to contemplate the Great Mystery <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"; the source of all things</note>, but the wheel has a far more subtle understanding and cannot be made with a compass in such a way. For it moves inward toward the Heart of the Sun <note>original: "Solis"</note>, and outward toward the figure of the essence: It drives above itself and beneath itself. For the Spirit of the Tincture <note>original: "Tinctur-Geist"; the spiritual life-force that gives quality and color to matter</note>, as the true fire-life, drives upward into the freedom of God, yet it desires the spirit of essence, which drives downward; for without that, the fire-life does not persist.

Thus the fire-spirit turns itself around, as if onto its side, and reaches always for

<column-break/>

the spirit of essence, and the spirit of essence flees from the fire. But because it is born out of the fire-life and cannot be separated from it, it is rotated with the fire-spirit. For when the fire-spirit turns to the right and crosswise, reaching for the spirit of essence, the spirit of essence also turns crosswise, and up from below on the other side; this creates a turning, and each hurries after the other. For the essence flees from fire and yet comes out of the fire, just as you see how air goes out of fire, and from the air comes water, which is the essence <note>original: "Wesenheit"; the substantial or material aspect of spiritual reality</note>.

Thus the fire, which is an anguish <note>original: "Angst"; Böhme uses this to mean a state of constriction or tension that produces motion</note>, desires gentleness and the freedom outside of the torment, and reaches for the spring of water. And the gentleness, as the spring of water, desires a body so that it might be free and hidden from the fire; and so the fire always hurries after the water, and the water flees from the fire. For if the fire went out at the top and the water went out at the bottom, there would be a wide separation, and in each would be death and a nothingness. But because the fire bows toward the water and refreshes itself therein, it retains its life and can again give forth the spirit-air from itself, so that life persists.

Thus we point out the Great Mystery <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"</note> to you, so that you shall learn to understand how far you should go, and where your number and end is. For the fire is the eighth number, after the seven spirits of nature, and is a cause of the seven spirits. Now, no creature persists in the fire, for the fire consumes the essence in which the natural life stands. But now the fire makes the Tincture, and a double one at that: one reaching inward toward eternal freedom, toward the still gentleness without essence; and the other reaching outward toward the external essence, as if toward the Oil <note>original: "Oleo"</note> which is out of the water, which is of Venus <note>original: "Venere"; representing the principle of love, beauty, and desire</note>, in which its external luster and shine arises.

### Part 3 / Chapter 6

And within the inner <term>Tincture</term> <note>The "Tincture" is Böhme’s term for a spiritual essence or catalyst that transforms a substance or state—similar to how a dye changes cloth or a medicine heals the body.</note>, in the desire for eternal freedom, the Majesty of freedom arises.

Thus, understand us rightly: fire holds the number eight, and the inner Tincture holds the number nine. This is as far as we should go, for the number ten is the eternal fire of GOD, and it holds the **Cross** in the middle of its birth; this divides the center of eternal nature into two kingdoms, which we have mentioned before. And whichever creature wishes to travel through, it passes through the Kingdom of GOD and back into the outermost, out of GOD and outside of this world, into the center of the fire—as if into an eternal darkness where the fire is black and there is an everlasting hunger.

The igniting of the fire-light stands alone beneath the Cross in gentleness, in the number nine; that is one number. The number ten is a double-count <note>original: "zwey Gezahl"; likely referring to the two digits of 10 or the dual nature of the tenth state</note>, which belongs to the angels and humans—but they are not to reach further into the center of the Cross. Instead, they must stand there before the Cross of the **Number Three** <note>The Trinity</note> and sink their minds down into the Tincture of humility, back into the number nine, and look forward into the tenth. But they must do so with a fearful mind, not drawing a will or intending to go into the tenth number, which is the center of the Fire of GOD. Rather, they should eternally rejoice greatly before the tenth number and sing before it with their song of praise: *Holy, Holy, Holy is our GOD, the Lord of Sabaoth* <note>original: "HErr Zebaoth"; a Hebrew title for God meaning "Lord of Hosts"</note>. This very song is the food of the Divine Fire, from which wonders, the Paradisiacal Element, and heavenly essence go forth into the Divine Essences. This stands before the Trinity like a Virgin of the eternal wit of GOD, and that is GOD’s **Wisdom**. For in Wisdom, the essence of all Divine Essences appears, for which we here have no more tongue nor pen to write. You see the hundredth number of the Virgins of Wisdom, and also the thousandth number of the Crown of Majesty. However, you should not search further into the tenth number to explore the abyss therein; otherwise, you go outside of GOD, like **Lucifer**, who wanted to be Creator in the tenth number and sought the fire of the eternal record <note>original: "Urkundes"; here meaning the primal source or original testimony of existence</note>, and there within he must remain eternally as if in death, in darkness. Therefore, let the reader be warned not to ground themselves further in these very deep writings, nor to swing their will deeper than they can grasp.

26. **Question:** But how does the course of the stars create specific times, days, and years?

**Answer:** Before the fall of Lucifer and the creation of this visible world, there was no specific time, day, or year; rather, the Wheel of Eternal Nature moved according to the right of the seven <term>Source-Spirits</term> <note>Böhme’s "Quell-Geister" are the seven fundamental qualities or forces that drive all of existence.</note> of GOD in free delight without material substance. For the Source-Spirits stood in <term>Temperament</term> <note>original: "Temperatur"; meaning a state of perfect balance and harmony where no single quality dominates the others.</note>; each qualified without any ill-will in free delight and opened its character according to its inner form, just as fire gives birth to the inner air from itself. But as soon as Lucifer ignited the <term>Salitter</term> <note>A term Böhme uses for the fundamental "divine salt" or spiritual matter of a kingdom.</note> of his kingdom with his wrath, the Source-Spirits left their Temperament, and each worked by igniting itself quite contrarily, wanting to rule over the others in its own self-interest. Through such a mighty struggle, the essence divided itself according to the two principles of fire and light into two properties: into darkness and light. Darkness worked with its Source-Spirits to make everything cold, harsh, rough, coarse, and opaque. The other spirit was ignited with bitter wrath, where the spirit of life became a poisonous, hostile, fierce sting that raged and stormed, yet was bound by the harshness and locked and bolted in the hard bodies, whereby darkness arose. The light, however, worked with its Source-Spirits to become free from the darkness and anxiety; thus, both properties stand in an unceasing wrestling match. Whichever gains the upper hand becomes manifest in the world: the darkness swallows the light and is called Night; the light, shining and working in the darkness...

# On the Revelation of GOD on the Fourth Day.
Uu 3

...dispels the darkness, and reveals itself; such a revelation is called **Day**. Thus, eternity has contained itself within a time according to both principles, those of fire and light.

The night is a revelation of eternity according to the property of the dark fire-world. The day is a revelation according to the light-world. Eternity dwells within time, just as GOD dwells in nature, and the soul in the body. Darkness alone without light, and light alone without darkness, cannot open up time; rather, the wrestling and the struggle between light and darkness create change. If it were always night, then the night would be nothing other than a dark eternity; and if it were always day, then the day would be nothing other than a bright, shining joy of eternity. But the alternation causes eternity to take a temporal beginning, from which beginning time—like a wound-up clockwork <note>The "clockwork" or "watch-work" (Uhr-Werck) was a popular 17th-century metaphor for a universe governed by divine laws and mechanical precision.</note> driven by inner craving and desire—runs toward freedom, as its center and end in eternity. The first <term>source-spirit</term> <note>original: "Quell-Geist." In Böhme's system, these are the seven fundamental qualities or forces that power all of existence.</note> of nature creates the casing and the clockwork. The second creates the <term>First Mover</term> <note>original: "Primum Mobile." The outermost sphere of the heavens in classical astronomy which carries the other spheres along with it.</note>, and the ignition of fire brings the movement into a constant action and drive, until time once again reaches the boundary of eternity.

<margin>See *Threefold Life*, chapter 6, sections 43, 64, 65, 66.</margin>
Thus the stars are signs and provide specific times, for they are the essences and powers of the seven forms of nature. From each form, another form emerges, all because of the wrestling wheel of nature; therefore, there are so many of them beyond our ability to count. But because they have a certain number, we know that they must return into the <term>ether</term> <note>The subtle substance believed to fill the space of the universe.</note>; for in the eternal center there is no number, but rather the omnipotence in its outflow is without number. For whatever can be counted and grasped is not eternal, because it has a beginning and an end. Just as we then recognize that the spirit of man has no beginning or end, and cannot be counted. This we understand in the "constellation" of our own mind, from which the senses emerge, which are without number; for from one sense, more other senses may emerge than there are stars in the firmament, wherein we highly acknowledge our salvation and greatly rejoice that we know such things.

<column-break/>

Thus we see how time comes from eternity, and eternity is within time, as if enclosed in a constant drive toward the eternal freedom of its center, from which the course of all visible nature, and especially of the stars, arises. This course has been measured out by Wisdom in measure, goal, and weight, so that not a single minute or point is missing in this great clockwork. It opens to us morning and evening, noon and midnight; it shows us days, weeks, months, years, centuries, and entire <term>eons</term> <note>original: "Æones." Great cycles of time or "terminirten Ewigkeiten" (finite eternities).</note>. Each day has twenty-four hours and is divided into morning and evening, day and night: each part has six hours, wherein each of the six source-spirits has one hour in the wrestling to reveal the day according to the property of light, and the night according to the property of darkness. These twenty-four hours are, as it were, the twenty-four letters through which the eternally-speaking Word—as if through a clock hand—reveals eternity and its secret qualities. If the earth now turns itself three hundred and sixty-five times, it has completed its entire course, and this course around the great center of the sun makes one year.

->27. Question: How can the stars, which stand so high above the earth, work upon the earth and its interior?<-

**Answer:** The effect happens through the <term>constellation</term> <note>In Böhme’s thought, a "constellation" is not just a group of stars, but the spiritual resonance or "alignment" between celestial forces and the internal spirit of a living creature.</note>, which the spirit of the stars awakens and works within the creatures. For just as there is a constellation above in the firmament, there is also a constellation within the earth; and every constellation has a sharp, attractive craving, the lower for the upper, and the upper for the lower. The spirit that goes out from the upper constellation has the property of all stars within itself and, through the ignition of fire, awakens the spirit in the lower constellation. Whatever <term>starry influence</term> <note>original: "Astrum."</note> predominates in the upper constellation, the star-spirit is active or effective according to that property; and wherever a creature has such a starry influence within itself, that same influence is awakened, thus forming a constellation. For example: when Saturn predominates in the upper constellation, he awakens "Saturn," or the harsh, strict quality, in all creatures—especially sharpening this property in those in whom he holds predominance. So do Jupiter, Mars, Venus, etc. The Sun, however, is Universal, and is received by all creatures with great hunger, but by each according to its own image and impression. Thus the entire constellation is both above and below...

### 3. Part / Chap. 6.

...and everywhere in all three principles, there are pure forces which merge with one another in their effect, resulting in the resonance of the Essence; (Like a great harmony of many voices from all kinds of instruments playing before Holy GOD; the stars of the invisible world resonate into the visible, and the visible stars of the world above resonate into those below.) For the Desire, as the <term>Fiat</term> <note>original: "Fiat." Latin for "let it be"; the creative command of God that gives form to thought.</note>, grasps that same resonance and makes it substantial. This substance is a spirit of the stars, which the elements take into themselves, coagulate, and hatch—just as a hen hatches eggs. From this comes the true life of reason in all creatures; and thus the <term>Sidereal Spirit</term> <note>original: "Siderische Geist." The astral or celestial influence that Böhme believed governed the physical and mental disposition of all living beings.</note> is hatched and coagulated in all creatures.
> Myst. Mag. 11. 26. 27.

So understand us correctly: from the sun and stars come the elements, and in the <term>saltpeter</term> <note>original: "Salniter." In Böhme’s unique chemistry, this refers to a volatile, generative energy within the earth that acts as a bridge between heavenly light and physical matter.</note> of the earth they create a living spirit. The stars remain in their orbit, yet the spirit nonetheless acquires the quality of the stars. Now, this spirit, by its composition, is a distinct thing and has a substance like all stars; and the stars are and remain a distinct thing, each free for itself. Nevertheless, the quality of the stars rules in the spirit; but the spirit may raise or lower itself in its qualities, or live in the influences of the stars as it wishes, for it is free. It has received its qualities as its own property; and although it initially received them from the stars, they are now its own. It is just as when a mother has the seed within her; while she has it and it is a seed, it belongs to the mother. But when it becomes a child, it is no longer the property of the mother but of the child, even though the child is still in the mother’s womb and could not live without the mother. The child still retains its bodily right for itself. It is the same with the Sidereal Spirit. This spirit is a "strenuous longing" <note>original: "strenge Sucht." A driving, intensive force or craving that defines the nature's character.</note>—that is, it contains the property of all stars within itself,

<column-break/>

and applies itself to all things according to each thing's own <term>astro</term> <note>Its specific star-sign or internal celestial blueprint.</note> and constellation, and this harmony or equal effect is called a Constellation.

28. **Question:** What does the author understand by the Elements?

**Answer:** What is commonly understood by them, namely Fire, Air, Water, and Earth. Just as the stars are active, attracting, driving, warming, and shining according to the property of Fire, so the Elements are passive, sinking, tangible, thick, and congealing according to the property of Water. The stars dwell and act in the elements like the soul in the body, so that a whole heaven of stars lies within each element. To understand this in detail, we will investigate:

First, what is the active cause and the source-well of the four elements?

Second, why four elements have come forth from a single source-well?

Third, what are their qualifications and effects?

Fourth, how they exist in a struggle and a wrestling, and must one day be dissolved from their distinct properties and reunited once more.

The active cause is the eternally-speaking Word which, as mentioned above, became active after the ignition of the wrath, according to the distinction of properties. The source-well and <term>primary matter</term> <note>original: "Materia Primigenia." The original, unformed substance from which all things are made.</note> is the pure Divine Element, the Divine Heaven and Earth, born from the six source-spirits of eternal nature, wherein the eternal wisdom of GOD sees itself infinitely, and in which all wonders, colors, art, and virtue arose in the beginning, as mentioned above.

29. **Question:** How has this one Element divided itself into four parts?

**Answer:** We have already partly reported on this above. Behold, when <term>Lucifer</term> <note>The fallen angel whose pride, in Böhme's theology, corrupted the original harmony of nature and turned its qualities into harsh, opposing forces.</note> with his host awakened the wrath-fire in the nature of GOD, so that GOD became angry in nature in the "Place of Lucifer," the outermost birth in nature acquired a completely different quality. The properties of the dark world arose, quite fierce, cold, harsh, hot, bitter, and sour. The surging spirit, which previously had its gentle quality in nature, became quite lifting and terrifying in its outermost birth—which we now call the element of Air, and because of its rising, the Wind.

30. **Question:** How is it to be understood that one element always gives birth to another, and that each one longs for the next?

**Answer:** Just as in the Paradisiacal <term>Principle</term> <note>original: "Principio." ### Part 3 / Chapter 6

<meta>Catchword: Heat</meta>

And the earth and stones had their beginning with the fierce attraction <note>original: "Anziehen." Böhme refers to a spiritual contraction or "drawing-in" that causes density.</note> at the fall of Lucifer; when the harshness stood so severely in its elevating attraction, this drawing-in extinguished the Light again in the third <term>Principle</term> <note>The physical world or the realm of nature.</note>.

<margin>Principles 7, 9, 13.</margin>
Thus the four **elements** originated from the four properties of eternal nature: the earth and its coarseness from the dark desire—wherein the six other properties became material along with it, as can be seen in the metals, though the dark desire has coagulated them all. The air originates from the movement of the magnetic impression, through the fire in the scattered <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: "Mercurio." In Böhme's alchemy, Mercury represents the "word" or the principle of movement, sound, and liquidity.</note>, from which the water comes. The water is the scattered Mercury where the fiery nature is killed <note>meaning its heat is dampened or neutralized.</note>. The water is the feminine part of the fiery Mercury, in which he works; from this, heat and cold, as well as thickness and thinness, are in conflict. The fire originates from the spiritual fire of the inner ground. The cold is understood as the magnetic sharpness, which is the true root of the fire.

<margin>Table of Principles 52, 53, 54, 55.</margin>
All these four elements are born out of the incessant struggle that exists between wrath and love, light and darkness, good and evil.

These two qualities are in this world in all powers—in stars and elements, as well as in all creatures—intermingled as one thing: and no creature exists in the flesh in this natural life unless it possesses both qualities within itself.

At this point, one must consider what the word "Quality" means or is. Quality is the mobility—the "welling up" <note>Böhme uses a wordplay here: "Qualität" (quality) and "quallen" (to well up or gush). He views a quality as an active, driving force rather than a static trait.</note> or driving of a thing—such as heat, which burns, consumes, and drives everything that enters it which is not of its own property. Conversely, it illuminates and warms everything that is cold, wet, and dark, and makes the soft hard. It has, however, two species <note>original: "Species." Types or aspects.</note> within itself: namely, the light

<column-break/>

and the fierceness <note>original: "Grimmigkeit." Can also be translated as wrath, severity, or fury.</note>, which are to be noted. The light, or the heart of the heat, is in itself a lovely, joy-filled sight, a power of life, an illumination and vision of a thing that is far off; it is a piece or source of the heavenly kingdom of joy. For it makes everything in this world living and mobile; all flesh, as well as trees, leaves, and grass, grows in this world by the power of the light and has its life therein, as in the "Good." Conversely, heat has within itself fierceness, so that it burns, consumes, and destroys; this same fierceness wells up, drives, and elevates itself in the light, and makes the light mobile. They wrestle and struggle with one another in their twofold source as one thing: it is indeed one thing, but it has a twofold source. The light exists in GOD without heat, but in nature it does not; for in nature all qualities are within one another as one quality—after the manner in which GOD is all, and how everything comes from him and goes out from him. GOD is the heart or the fountain-spring of nature; everything stems from him. Now heat rules in all powers in nature and warms everything, and is a source in all things; otherwise, if that were not so, the water would be much too cold, the earth would freeze solid, and there would be no air. The heat rules in everything—in trees, herbs, and grass—and makes the water mobile, so that through the water’s source, herbs and grass grow out of the earth. Therefore it is called a "quality," because it wells up in all things and elevates everything. But the light within the heat gives power to all qualities, so that everything becomes lovely and full of bliss. Heat without the light is of no use to the other qualities, but is a destruction of the good, an evil source, for it destroys everything in the fierceness of the heat. Thus, the light in the heat is a living fountain-spring into which the Holy Spirit enters—but not into the fierceness. The heat...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the "Fourth Day" of creation, moving from the formation of the celestial bodies and the four elements to a deeper exploration of how "Heat" and "Cold" act as the fundamental forces (or "qualities") that govern all physical life. It explains the dual nature of these forces—both life-giving and destructive.</meta>

Heat, however, makes the light mobile, so that it wells up and drives, as is seen in winter; then the light of the sun is likewise upon the earth, but the sun’s heat-rays cannot reach the ground, and therefore no fruit grows.

### Of the Qualification <note>original: "Qualificirung." For Böhme, a "quality" is an active, "welling" power (from the German words *Qual*, meaning agony or labor, and *Quelle*, meaning source or well-spring).</note> of Cold.

Cold is also a quality, just like heat; it qualifies in all creatures that have come out of nature, and in everything that moves within it: in humans, animals, birds, fish, worms, leaves, and grass. It is set in opposition to heat and works within it as if it were one thing, but it resists the fierceness of the heat and stills it. It also has two types <note>original Latin: "Species."</note> within itself that are to be noted: namely, that it softens the heat and makes everything fine and lovely; in this way, it is a quality of life in all creatures, for no creature can exist without cold, as it is a welling, driving mobility in all things. The other type is fierceness <note>original: "Grimmigkeit." Often translated as "wrath," it refers to the harsh, destructive side of nature.</note>; for if it gains the upper hand, it presses everything down and destroys everything, just like heat. No life can exist within it if the heat does not resist it. The fierceness of cold is a destruction of all life and a house of death, just as the fierceness of heat is.

### Of the Qualification of Air and Water.

Air has its origin from heat and cold, for heat and cold drive powerfully away from themselves and fill everything; from this comes a living and weaving movement. But when the cold softens the heat, then the quality of both becomes thin, and the bitter quality <note>The "bitter quality" is Böhme’s third property of nature: the principle of friction, tension, and the "sting" that causes movement.</note> draws it together so that it becomes droplets. Air, however, has its origin and greatest movement from heat, and water from cold. Now these two qualities constantly wrestle with one another; heat consumes the water, and cold constrains the air. Now, the air is a cause and

<column-break/>

spirit of all life and all movement in this world, whether it be in the flesh or in all that grows out of the earth; thus everything has its life from the air, and nothing that is in this world and moves can exist without the air.

Water also wells up in all living and weaving things in this world; in the water consists the body of all things, and in the air the spirit, whether in the flesh or in the plants from the earth. Both of these come from heat and cold and work together as one thing. Now, however, in these two qualities there are also two special types <note>original Latin: "Species."</note> to be noted: namely, the living and the deadly effect. Air is a living quality when it is gentle in a thing; the Holy Spirit rules in the gentleness of the air, and all creatures are joyful within it. But it also has fierceness within itself, so that it kills and destroys through its cruel elevation <note>Referring to storms or the "rising up" of the wrathful properties of nature.</note>. Yet the qualification takes its origin from this fierce elevation, so that it wells and drives in all things, from which life has its origin and stands; therefore, both must be present in this life.

Water also has a fierce, deadly source within itself, for it kills and consumes; moreover, everything living and weaving must rot and perish in water. Thus, heat and cold are a cause and origin of water and air, in which everything works and stands; all life and mobility stands within them.

The bitter quality is the heart in all life, just as it draws the water together in the air and also disperses it so that it becomes distinct. It is the same in all creatures, as well as in the plants of the earth; for leaves and grass have their green color from the bitter quality. If the bitter quality dwells gently in a creature, then it is a heart or joy in the same, for it sifts out all other evil influences and is a beginning or cause of joy or laughter.

<meta>This page continues the exposition of the various "Qualities" or driving forces of nature. The previous page discussed Heat, Cold, and Air; this page explores the "Bitter," "Sweet," "Sour," and "Harsh" (or Salty) qualities, detailing both their life-giving and destructive aspects.</meta>

For when it <note>The "it" refers to the Bitter Quality, which Böhme considers the source of mobility and sensitivity.</note> is moved, it makes a creature tremble and full of joy, and lifts up the same with the whole body; for it is like a glimpse of the heavenly kingdom of joy, an elevation of the spirit, a spirit and power in all plants out of the earth, a mother of life. The Holy Spirit wells and drives powerfully in this quality, for it is a piece of the heavenly kingdom of joy, as I will prove hereafter. But it also has another type <note>original: "Species."</note> within itself, namely fierceness <note>original: "Grimmigkeit." For Böhme, this represents the harsh, wrathful, or destructive side of nature.</note>, which is a true house of death, a corruption of all that is good, a corruption and consumption of life in the flesh. For when it raises itself too much in a creature and ignites in heat, it separates flesh and spirit, and the creature must die the death; for it wells up and ignites the element of Fire, in which no flesh can survive in such great heat and bitterness. But when it ignites in the element of Water and becomes welling <note>original: "quellend." Böhme uses this word to imply both a spring of water and a surging power.</note> therein, it brings the flesh into days of sickness and infirmity, and finally into death.

The **sweet quality** is set in opposition to the bitter and is a gracious, lovely quality, a refreshment of life, a softening of the fierceness; it makes everything lovely and friendly in all creatures; it makes the plants out of the earth fragrant and tasty, with beautiful yellow, white, and reddish colors. It is a glimpse and source of gentleness, a delight of the heavenly kingdom of joy, a house of the Holy Spirit, a qualification of love and mercy, a joy of life. Conversely, it also has a fierce source, a source of death and destruction within itself; for when it is ignited in the bitter quality within the element of Water, it gives birth to sickness and swollen pestilence and the corruption of the flesh. But when it is ignited in heat and bitterness, it infects the element of Air, from which is born the swift, flying pestilence and sudden death.

<column-break/>

->**Of the Sour Quality.**<-

The **sour quality** is set in opposition to the bitter and the sweet, and it tempers <term>Temperantz: the balancing of opposing forces to reach a stable state.</term> everything finely; it is a refreshment and a quenching when the bitter and sweet qualities rise too high; it is a desire in the taste, a delight of life, a welling joy in all things, a desire, longing, and delight of the kingdom of joy, a quiet delight of the spirit; such things it tempers in all living and welling things. But it also has within it a source of evil and destruction; for if it raises itself too high, or wells up too much in a thing so that it ignites, it gives birth to sadness, melancholy <note>original: "Melancholey."</note>, a stench in the water, becoming rotted and brittle, a forgetfulness of all good, a sadness of life, a house of death, a beginning of sadness, and an end of joys.

->**Of the Harsh or Salty Quality.**<-

The **salty quality** is a good tempering in the bitter, sweet, and sour, and makes everything finely lovely; it prevents the rising of the bitter quality, as well as the sweet and the sour, so that they do not ignite. It is a sharp quality, a delight of the taste, a source of life and of joys. Conversely, it also has within it fierceness and destruction; when it is ignited in the fire, it gives birth to a hard, tearing, stony nature, a fierce torment, a destruction of life; from this the Stone <note>original: "der Stein." Refers to kidney or bladder stones, which Böhme views as a physical manifestation of a spiritual "hardening."</note> grows in the flesh, from which the flesh suffers great martyrdom. But when it is ignited in the water, it gives birth in the flesh to evil scabs, ulcers, the French disease <note>original: "Franzosen," a common historical term for syphilis.</note>, the itch, and leprosy; it is a house of mourning for death, a misery, and a forgetfulness of all good.

In Böhme’s alchemical language, Saltpeter represents a volatile, explosive, and highly energetic spiritual-physical force that triggers change.</note>, it ignites itself. # The VII. Chapter.
## Concerning the fifth Day-Work of GOD, namely: Of the Creation of the Fish and Birds. Likewise: Of the Creation of the four-footed and creeping Animals on the sixth Day.

**1. Question.**
How did the fifth Day-Work of GOD, namely the creation of the fish and birds, follow upon the fourth Day-Work, which was the creation of the stars and elements?

**Answer.**
When GOD had opened the stars and the four elements as a weaving life / wherein the upper constellations granted the diversity within that weaving life / and stirred the four stars <note>Böhme refers to the "four stars" as the spiritual drivers behind the four elements of fire, air, water, and earth.</note> within the four elements; then he led forth the echo or resonance from the essence of all stars and elements, through the movement of his speaking word in the Word "Let it be" <note>original: "Verbo Fiat." The creative command of God that manifests spiritual ideas into physical forms.</note> / as the power of that same life / which was free from anguish / and he seized it through the Word "Let it be," and spoke that same life into forms with the holy eternally-speaking Word through the "Let it be," according to the properties of the stars in the spiritual body <note>original: "corpore."</note>, in which the "Let it be" or the Desire drew the elements to itself according to the outward being / as a body. ### Part 3 / Chapter 7.
<meta>catchword: 2. Es.</meta>

Male and female. When the spirit of the stars—or the spirit in the fire-form—mixed itself through its own longing with the watery spirit, two genders emerged from one single Essence <term>Essentia: The fundamental "being" or spiritual substance of a thing.</term>. One gender followed the Limbus <term>Limbus: The primordial "extract" or seed-matter, here associated with the fiery, masculine principle.</term> in a fiery form; the other followed the Aquaster <term>Aquaster: A term for the watery, astral spirit of nature, associated here with the feminine principle.</term> in a watery form. Yet they were mixed in such a way that they were equal in body. Thus, the male was qualified according to the Limbus or fire-form, and the female according to the Aquaster or watery form. Because of this, there is now a violent desire in all creatures: the spirit of the male seeks the "dear child" <note>The "child" refers to the lost unity or the spark of Paradise that was divided during the separation of the sexes.</note> in the female, and the female seeks it in the male. For the unreasoning part of the body in these irrational creatures does not know what it does; the body would not move so violently toward procreation, nor would it know anything of impregnation, if not for this. Rather, its spirit is so inflamed after the "Child of Love" that it seeks that Love—which is actually Paradise—but it cannot grasp it. Instead, it only creates a seed, within which the center for birth is found once again. And such is the original record of both sexes and their propagation. But they do not reach the Paradisiacal Child of Love; rather, it remains a fierce hunger. Thus, procreation proceeds with great earnestness.

Now, as I write that the stars rule in all animals and creatures, and that every creature received the spirit of the stars at creation and still stands under that same government, the simple man will not want to believe it—though the Doctor <note>Likely referring to a learned physician or scholar of the era.</note> knows it well. I point such a person to experience. Look: a male and female produce young, and often do so; though they come from one body, they do not all have the same nature, color, virtue, or physical shape. This is all caused by the changing of the stars. For when the seed is sown, the Carver <note>Böhme uses "Schnitzer" (carver/sculptor) as a metaphor for the celestial influences that "carve" the shape and character of a fetus.</note> makes an image out of it as he wills, according to the first Es-

<column-break/>

sence <note>original: "Essentia"</note>. He cannot change that essence, but he gives it the spirit within that essence according to his power—with its habits and senses, colors and gestures—exactly as he is, and as the constellation is in its essence (whether for evil or good) at the time it draws its breath from the air. Whether it is inclined to bite, push, or strike, or toward gentleness: everything is as the heavens are at that moment; so too shall be the animal’s spirit and will.

# Concerning the Revelation of God on the Fifth Day.
Yy 2
<meta>catchword: The</meta>

2. **Q.** But where does the terrifying wrath in animals come from? Indeed, why did God create some very harmful, predatory, and poisonous animals, arming them, as it were, for robbery, murder, stinging, biting, poisoning, and destruction—not to mention the disgusting worms, snakes, toads, and the harmful pests in the air, the earth, and the waters?

**Ans.** When Lucifer rebelled and ignited his source-spirits <note>original: "Quell-Geister"; these are the seven foundational qualities of nature in Böhme's philosophy.</note>, the animal spirit in the clay went out from all the bodies of Lucifer’s angels into the Salitter <term>Salitter: A term used to describe the divine "sap" or fundamental substance of the universe, which can be either holy or "ignited" with wrath.</term> of God, like a fiery serpent and dragon. Now, when God performed the creation of this world after the fall of Lucifer, everything was created out of that same Salitter in which Lucifer had resided. Consequently, the creatures of this world had to be created from that same Salitter; they formed themselves into good or evil according to the nature of the ignited qualities. Whichever animal had the strongest fire, or bitter, or harsh quality, it also became a bitter, harsh, hot, and fierce animal, according to whichever quality was primary <note>original: "Primas"</note>. This is the origin of the wild and evil animals in the world; and thus the Dragon <note>A reference to the fallen Lucifer.</note> formed all kinds of fiery and poisonous shapes and images, and impressed them into the Salitter.
<margin>Aurora, chapter 15, verses 76-79.</margin>

In this way, the inner Divine Word expressed itself through the outer spoken word in every science <term>Scientz: Not "science" in the modern sense, but a latent power, or the "self-knowledge" of a specific quality or force.</term>, out of the fiery property of the powers, into a creaturely life. These are the creatures on earth, in the water, and in the air—the birds—every creature coming out of its own "science," out of good and evil, according to the property of all three Principles <note>The three Principles are the Dark World (wrath), the Light World (love), and the Outward World (nature).</note>. Each is an image or likeness of the inner ground—from the Kingdom of Fantasy <term>Phantasey: In this context, it refers to a realm of chaotic, self-willed images or "play" that lacks the divine light.</term> as much as from the original good life. One can see this before one's eyes: that there are good and evil creatures. For example, poisonous animals and worms exist according to the center of the nature of darkness, from the power of the fierce property; these only desire to dwell in the dark, such as those that live in holes and

<column-break/>

hide from the sun. On the other hand, one also finds many creatures with which the Spirit of the World <note>original: "Spiritus Mundi"</note> has formed itself out of the Kingdom of Fantasy, such as apes and similar animals and birds, which only play pranks and plague and disturb other creatures. Thus, one is the enemy of the other, and everything strives against one another, in the same way that the three Principles play with one another in their powers. In this way, God has brought that same "play" before Him into a living, creaturely being through the Spirit of the World in his science. Just as one also finds good, friendly creatures in imitation of the angelic world—where the Spirit of the World has formed itself into the good, spoken powers, which are the tame animals and birds—even so, many evil animals (as evil properties) mingle among the tame ones, having been caught in mixed properties. In every animal's food and dwelling place, one sees where it has come from; for every creature desires to dwell in its "mother" <note>Here, "mother" refers to the specific elemental source or spiritual quality from which the animal originated.</note> and longs for her, as is clearly visible. The Spirit of the World, from which all outer creatures come according to the spirit, is enclosed within a time, a goal, and a measure of how long it shall last. It is like a clockwork <note>original: "Uhr-Werck"</note> made from the stars and elements, within which the highest God dwells and uses this clockwork as His tool. He has enclosed His "making" within it; it runs freely on its own and gives birth according to its minutes, as one might compare it. All things lie within it—what has happened in the world and what is yet to happen. It is God's purpose toward the creature and in the creature, wherein He governs everything with this regime of nature.
<margin>Concerning Grace, chapter 5, sections 20, 21.</margin>

Thus, in all living creatures we see nothing but images, both of the angelic world of love and also of the dark world of wrath (the Kingdom of Fantasy), through which both the good and also the fallen angels revealed their figures, thoughts, and fantasies.

# Chapter VIII.
## Concerning the Revelation of GOD on the Sixth Day, according to the Sixth Form of Nature, namely: Concerning the Creation of Man.

->1. Question.<-

What must a person search for if they wish to attain a true and thorough knowledge of how GOD created man?

->Answer.<-

A person cannot arrive at such knowledge in any way other than through the new birth; no amount of book-reading, studying, or meditating helps. Our author says: I have searched through the writings of many masters, hoping to find the pearls from the foundation of man, but I could not find that for which my soul hungered. I also found completely contradictory opinions; furthermore, I found some who forbid me from searching—I do not know on what ground or understanding, other than that a blind man does not begrudge the sighted his eyes. With all of this, my soul became quite restless within me, and suffered labor pains like a woman in birth, yet nothing was discovered until I followed the words of CHRIST, who says: *You must be born again if you wish to see the Kingdom of GOD.* <note>John 3:3</note> This initially locked up my heart, as I presumed it could not happen in this world, but only upon my departure from this world. Then my soul first labored for the birth, desiring to taste the pearl, and gave itself much more vehemently to the path of birth until at last it attained a jewel. Following this, I will now write as a memorial for myself and as a light for the seeker, for Christ says: *No one lights a candle and puts it under a bench or a bushel, but sets it on a table, so that all who are in the room may see it.* <note>Matthew 5:15</note> And for that purpose, he gives the seeker the

<column-break/>

pearl, so that he should share it with the poor for their health/well-being, as he has quite earnestly commanded.

Indeed, Moses writes: GOD made man from a clod of earth, etc. That is almost everyone's opinion, and I too would not have known how that was to be understood: I would not have learned it from Moses, nor from the glosses <note>original: "Glossen"; marginal commentaries or interpretations of scripture</note> that have been made upon it, and the veil would have remained before my eyes, albeit in great sorrow. But when I found the pearl, I looked Moses in the face and found that Moses had written correctly, but I had not understood it correctly. For GOD also spoke thus to Adam and Eve after the Fall: *You are earth, and to earth you shall return.* And if I had not considered the Limbus <term>Limbus: In Böhme's thought, this refers to the "essential extract" or the spiritual-physical substance of the divine world from which the material world was condensed.</term> out of which the earth was made, I would have remained just as blinded. That same Limbus now shows me the foundation of what Adam was before the Fall and after the Fall. For no such earth or such flesh as we now carry can exist in the light of GOD; therefore, Christ also said: *No one ascends to heaven except the Son of Man, who came from heaven and who is in heaven.* <note>John 3:13</note> Thus our flesh before the Fall was heavenly, made from the heavenly Limbus; but when disobedience came—to give birth to oneself in another center <note>original: "Centro"; the focal point of desire or existence</note> in the lust of this world—it became earthly. For with the earthly bite of the apple in the Garden of Eden, the earthly kingdom began, and immediately the Mother of the Great World <note>The Macrocosm or external Nature.</note> began to exert her power over the Small World <note>The Microcosm or Man.</note> and made out of it an animal-like kind in appearance and also in essence.

Now, how such a thing came to pass, a thorough report follows; therein you can look into the heart of the old and new man—provided you are born again from GOD and possess the pearl; if not, you will hardly see the old Adam here, and you will not behold the new at all.

The veil of Moses <note>A reference to 2 Corinthians 3, signifying spiritual blindness to divine truth</note> must go, and you must look Moses in the face, if you wish to see the new man; and without the pearl, you cannot take that veil away, and you will not know Adam as he was before his fall. 2. **Qu.** How is the creation of man to be viewed and considered?

**Ans.** The creation of man is just like the creation of both the angelic and the visible world: For just as this principle of this world is all together only one body; so also is GOD / the Kingdom of Heaven / Angels / Man and Paradise, with all heavenly, Divine being and attributes, all only one body, which together is called GOD / Majesty and Eternity. <column-break/>

the light of that same body, and the Holy Spirit is its air and spirit of life; but the creatures have their own spirit of life from within themselves: For every angel and man is just like the whole of GOD.

He also has within himself the Trinity <note>original: "Drey-Zahl"</note>, and the Holy Spirit also goes out within him, just as you see in the likeness of a glowing iron. The iron signifies the creature; the fire within it signifies the Godhead; the heat of the iron signifies the creature's own spirit; the air coming from the heat, which has no torment, signifies the Holy Spirit. Thus, we give you these high things to recognize in great enough simplicity: If anyone wishes to remain blind, may GOD help him; and we can thus present to you with a true foundation what man was before the fall, and what he became in the fall, and what he becomes again in the new rebirth, and what he will be after this life. For we know what he is in death and in life, and we also know what he is in hell; and this not from our own wit—as if it were greater than that of all the living—but in the Mother's womb, in the Mother's spirit <note>referring to "Sophia" or Divine Wisdom</note>. I am dead, and as a nothing, as I speak and write thus; and I do not write from myself, but from the Mother, from her knowledge and longing; and yet I live, just like all men, in anxiety, toil, and labor, in fear and terror, in temptation like all men: For I also wear Adam's hide <note>original: "Adams Pelz"; a reference to the "coats of skins" in Genesis 3:21, signifying the mortal, physical body</note>, and I live in the hope of Israel.

### Part 3 / Chapter 8.

The essence is like a human, and this world is also like a human; Eternity gives birth to nothing other than its own likeness: For there is nothing else within it, and it is unchangeable, otherwise it would perish or become something else, which is impossible.

As you now see and feel that man is, so also is Eternity: Consider the body and soul, in good and evil, in joy and sorrow, in light and darkness, in power and weakness, in life and death. Heaven, earth, stones, and elements are all within man, as is the Trinity <note>original: "Drey-Zahl," literally "Three-Number," referring to the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit</note> of the Godhead, and nothing can be named that is not within man. All creatures are in man, both those of this world and those of the angelic world; we are all, with the entire essence of all essences, only one body with many members, where each member is again a whole, and each member has its own special purpose.

Thus, man himself is the **Book of the Three Principles** <note>In the author's system, these are the three realms of existence: the dark fire-world (wrath), the light-world (love), and the outer physical world</note>, like three pages, written and engraved through and through by the finger of GOD. Then, man sees GOD his Creator constantly creating, GOD his Redeemer incessantly redeeming, and GOD the Holy Spirit incessantly proceeding from the Father and the Son, applying Himself to the sanctification and perfection of man. He sees the Father eternally begetting His beloved Son; he sees the Son eternally fulfilling the Father's will with eternal pleasure; he sees the Holy Spirit eternally proceeding from the Father and the Son, descending upon the new man in the form of a dove.

O great GOD! What is man, and the son of man, that You so accept him? Let us investigate this great wonder of GOD with holy awe and examine, first, the occasion and the motivating cause of why GOD created man. Secondly, the creation itself. Thirdly, the work that GOD created—namely, man in the state of his highest perfection.

Therefore GOD said: **Let us make man, an image that is like us, who shall rule over all animals and creatures on earth. And GOD created man in His image, yes, in the image of GOD He created him.**

6. **Question:** Who then is actually the Creator of man, who spoke and said: "let us make man"?

**Answer:** It is the Triune God, who introduced Himself into nature and the creature, and placed His will into the act of creation. This Triune God delighted in a perfect likeness of Himself; this delight <note>The German *Lust* here implies a joyful desire or longing</note> arose in the Heart, as the Son of God, and thus the Will of the Father became active and desiring within the Heart of the Son, to create into a physical being that of which the one God had an Idea and a delight. Because God’s Will is almighty in its operation, He moved through His almighty Word in all three Principles <term>Principles; in Böhme’s thought, these are the three "worlds" or dimensions of reality: the dark fire-world, the light love-world, and the visible material world</term>, and extracted the seed or Quintessence <term>Quintessence; the "fifth essence," representing the purest, most concentrated power of all elements combined</term> within eternal and visible nature, through His eternal Word, out of all Principles.

Indeed, God in and for Himself is free and without physical substance or desire, for His delight is only majesty and freedom; but the Center of Nature <note>original: "Centrum Naturæ"</note> upon the cross <note>A reference to the structural intersection of the divine forces</note> desired the image that was seen in the Virgin <note>Sophia, or Divine Wisdom</note>, where the Spirit of God goes forth into Wisdom, where Wisdom causes substantiality to arise whenever God’s Will is active within it.

God desired to make another image in place of Lucifer, who had ruined his kingdom and ignited the substance in his location <note>original: "Loco"</note>, from which earth and stones were formed and he was cast out. Thus, the third corporeality and the third Principle began with the kingdom of this world. Therefore, God created another image according to His likeness in this place. However, if it were to be God’s likeness according to all three Principles, it had to be taken from all three, and from all the substance of this place or this depth, as far as the *Fiat* <note>The "Let there be" or creative command of God</note> had given itself into the ethers for creation along with Lucifer’s princely throne. For man came to take Lucifer’s place, and from this originates the great envy of the devils—that they do not grant man this honor, but instead lead him always down the evil, corrupted path so that they might increase their own kingdom. They do this in defiance of gentleness, which is God’s love; yet they imagine—because they live in the wrath of strong power—that they are higher than God’s Spirit in love and gentleness.

<column-break/>

<margin>*On the Incarnation of Christ*, Part 1, Chapter 3, Section 12.</margin>
In these points lies the author’s deep foundation of humanity, which is well worth investigating.

Understand the Will-Spirit of God: as the Holy Spirit took hold of the twofold *Fiat*, in two Principles—the inner in the Angelic world, and then the outer in this external world—and created man <note>The author makes a pun here: "Mensch" (man) is linked to "mischen" (to mix)</note> as a **Note: mixed person.** For he was meant to be an image according to the inner and outer world, but was intended to rule over the outer world through the inner quality <note>of the Angelic Divine Life</note>; thus he was God’s likeness. *Ibid.* Section 13.

For God had not yet found an image and likeness among all that He had made in which He took His full pleasure and Divine delight. Therefore, His Heart burned in Divine love-desire to make an image and likeness on the sixth day, in which He might clarify and reveal Himself according to all three Principles, as if in a single mirror. In such an Ideal-delight and desire, the Will-Spirit of God went forth and became active through His almighty Word in all three worlds, in order to create and extract such an image and likeness. Just as the harsh *Fiat* in reproduction draws together from all members and parts of the male and female body the essences and powers—which the harsh *Fiat* crafts and turns into a clay <note>original: "Limo" or "Limus", referring to the "dust of the ground" in Genesis</note>, also shaping it according to the Idea and image of that from which they were drawn, which clay rises and grows as a seed in its proper matrix—so, in a sense befitting God, the love-desire of God as the *Fiat* became active in the entire body of the Deity according to all three Principles, and in each and every one of its creatures. From all of them, He extracted the Quintessence and the noblest powers: from eternal nature, from the Light-world, from stars and elements, trees and plants, fish and birds, four-footed and creeping animals, so that there would be no single creature in the entire body of the Deity [that was not represented in man].

### 7. Question: In what does the Image of God actually consist?

**Answer:** Man is, as it were, the sum and a small extract of the entire world. Just as God has proceeded from the One into the many and the innumerable, so He proceeds back again from the many and the innumerable into a Unity. Therefore, God in man is the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last.

It is then asked: what is God’s image? Look upon and contemplate the Godhead, and you will find it. For God is not an animal-like man; rather, man was intended to be an image and also a likeness of God in which God dwelt. Now, God is a spirit, and in Him are all three Principles; and He wished to make such an image that would have all three Principles within itself, which is truly a likeness of God. And "He created him"—here we must understand Moses correctly: that God created him and did not merely "make" him out of a lump of earth. The Limbus <term>Limbus; in Böhme’s alchemy, the celestial "slime" or spiritual substance from which the world and man were formed</term> from which He created him is the Matrix of the Earth, and the earth was born out of it. The matter <note>original: "Materia"</note> from which He created him was a mass <note>original: "Massa"</note>, a Quintessence of the stars and elements, which immediately became earthly when man awakened the earthly center and at that hour belonged to the earth and to fragility.

But the mass was from the heavenly Matrix, which is the root of the offspring or the earthly. The heavenly center was meant to remain fixed, and the earthly should not have been awakened. In such power, he [man] was a lord over the stars and elements; every creature would have feared him, and he would have been unbreakable. He had the power and property of all

<column-break/>

creatures within him, for his power was from the power of understanding. Now, he had to possess all three Principles if he was to be God’s likeness: first, the source of darkness; second, the source of light; and third, the source of this world. Yet he was not meant to live and operate <note>original: "qualificiren" – to be defined by or interact with certain properties</note> in all three, but only in one—the Paradisiacal one—in which his life arose. To prove that this is certainly so, it is written: *And God breathed into him the living breath, and man became a living soul.* All other creatures, which had come forth from the fragile Limbus through the Fiat <term>Fiat; Latin for "Let it be done," the creative word of God</term>, had their spirit awakened in their center by the Will in the Fiat; the spirit of each creature proceeded from its own essence and property, and thereafter interacted <note>original: "inqualirete"</note> with the spirit of the great world, the stars, and the elements.

And that was not meant to be so in man. His spirit was not to interact with the spirit of the stars and elements; two Principles—the darkness and the spirit of the air—were meant to stand still in such a being. Therefore, He breathed into him the living breath. Understand this as God’s breath—that is, the Paradisiacal breath or spirit, the Holy Spirit—which was meant to be the breath of the soul in the soul’s center. The spirit that proceeded from the Limbus, or the Quintessence of the stars, was meant to be powerful over the Quintessence of this world. For man existed in one essence and was only one man whom God so created; he could have lived eternally. Even if God had brought the stars back into their ether and pulled the Matrix of the elements along with the elements back into nothingness, man would still have remained. For this purpose, he had the Paradisiacal center within himself and could have given birth out of his own will, awakening the center, and thus given birth to an angelic host into Paradise without distress or anxiety, and without tearing <note>A reference to birth without the pain or physical rupture associated with the Fall</note>. And such a man...

# 3. Part / Chapter 8.

He had to be man if he were to remain in Paradise and be eternally unshaken. For Paradise is holy, so man also had to be holy: For within holiness stands the Divine Power and Paradise.

**8. Question:** Because man is made from all three principles, and is thus a perfect image of God, but we currently exist in imperfection, God's image in such perfection is not comprehensible to us, but only in fragments: Are we now to consider such fragments according to the three principles in which God has revealed Himself, as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit?

**Answer:** Man consists of body, soul, and spirit. Each Principle <term>Principles; the three dimensions of reality in Böhme's thought: the dark fire-world (1st), the light-world (2nd), and the material world (3rd)</term> has its property in man’s soul and body. And just as there is a qualification <note>The way specific qualities or forces interact to produce a state of being</note> in soul and body, so also a spirit goes forth. Thus, just as the triune Godhead lives, works, and qualifies in the whole great world, so also Father, Son, and Holy Spirit qualify in man, both in his creation and also in his preservation and enlivening. According to the innermost birth, man has within himself a Divine life; according to the light-world, a paradisical and angelic one; according to the dark world, a hellish and devilish one; according to the property of the stars, a sidereal one; according to the earth, an earthly, vegetable, and also animal one. Whichever way of life awakens in man, according to that property the man is either an angel, or a devil, or an animal. And as he has a longing and a will, so also God is revealed in him, either as an angry, jealous God, or as Love. The triune God becomes active in the Word for the creation of man, according to both principles, the fire- and light-world. The Father conceives a will to introduce Himself into humanity and to reveal Himself therein; the Son conceives a will to fulfill the will of GOD the Father with delight as the fullness of the Godhead. The former will is active according to the property of the dark world as the first Principle, and from that originates the fire-soul; the latter, however, is active according to the property of the light-world as the second Principle, and from that originates the light-soul.

The soul’s essence with its image can be understood by looking at a beautiful flower growing out of the earth, or by considering fire and light: Just as one sees how the earth is a center but has no life; rather, it is essential, and out of it grows a beautiful flower which does not look like the earth, nor does it have its smell or taste, much less its shape—and yet the earth is the flower’s mother.

So also was the soul perceived out of the eternal **Center of Nature** <note>original: Centrum Naturæ</note>, out of the eternal Essence, through the **Word "Let there be"** <note>original: Verbo Fiat</note> in the will of God, and held in that "Let there be"; so that it appeared as a **Fire-Eye** and a likeness of the **First Principle** <note>original: Principii</note> in a created form and essence.
