### Part 3 / Chapter 8

The soul's beautiful image is also caught in the dark harshness and infected with the bitter wrath. Now this same wrath has become a **Turba** <term>Turba; Latin for "uproar" or "disturbance." In Böhme's thought, it is the destructive force that breaks down divine order when the soul turns away from God</term> which possesses the image and destroys the likeness of God. For in God there is Love, Light, and Gentleness; but in this image there is darkness, harshness, and bitterness, and its essential torment is a fire arising from the wrathful essences. Therefore, as long as this image stands in such torment and form within the darkness, it does not belong in the Kingdom of God.

You have a further analogy of the soul in fire: The soul is an essential fire, and the flash of the fire creates the life within it. The soul is like a sphere of fire or an eye of fire. Now, the burning fire in the torment represents the **First Principle** <term>First Principle; The foundational "fire-world" of God’s power and potential wrath, which provides the energy for all existence</term>, and the life—though the fire is not the life itself, but rather the spirit of torment that arises in the anguish of the fire. The "air" that goes out from the fire is the true spirit of the fire-life, which constantly fans the fire so that it burns. Now the fire gives off a glow and light from the torment, which dwells within the torment and shines out from it; yet the torment does not grasp the light. This signifies the **Second Principle** <term>Second Principle; The realm of Light, Love, and the Godhead that originates from, but transcends, the fire</term> in which the Godhead resides; for one recognizes that the true power is in the light, and not in the fire. The fire only provides the "essences" <note>the raw materials or energetic qualities</note> to the light, and the life or light provides the gentleness and substance, like water. 

Now we understand that in the light there is a gentle life without torment; and though there *is* torment there, it is imperceptible, acting only as a desire for pleasure or love. We recognize that same "torment" then as a **Tincture** <term>Tincture; A mystical substance or spiritual "dye" that transforms and beautifies nature, turning the "torment" of growth into the "bloom" of life</term>, in which growth and flowering arise; yet the fire is the cause of it, and gentleness is the cause of the substance. For the light that desires love draws toward itself and holds fast so that it becomes a "being"; but the fire-desire consumes the substance.

Thus we must also remember regarding the soul: what the soul encounters purely alone in the **Center** <note>original: Centro; the inward spiritual focal point</note>

<column-break/>

is an essential fire in the **Eye of Eternity**. But now, that same eye is a desiring thing, namely as a figure and image according to God’s Wisdom. Thus the **Majesty** <note>The "Majesty" refers to the radiant glory of God's light</note> of God inflames the image within the essential fire, provided that the essential fire brings its desire into the Majesty. But where it does not, the image is raw and naked outside of God, and the **Tincture** becomes false; for the image stands in the Tincture and originates in the Tincture in the light, not in the torment of the fire—just as the Heart or Word of God takes its origin in the light of the Majesty within the Father’s eternal Fire-Tincture. So it is with the soul's image. 

The image indeed dwells in the fire of the soul, just as light dwells in fire; but it has a different **Principle**, just as the light is a different "torment" <note>here Böhme implies a "mode of feeling" or "state of being"</note> than the fire. Thus the true image of God dwells in the light of the soul-fire, which light the fiery soul must draw from God’s fountain of love in the Majesty through its imagination and self-surrender. If the soul does not do this, but instead imagines into itself, into its own wrathful forms toward the torment of fire, and not into the fountain of love in the light of God, then its own torment of severity, harshness, and bitterness arises and becomes the **Turba** of the divine image, swallowing the likeness of God into the wrath.

This section explores how the "imagination" or focused desire of the human heart acts as a creative force, shaping the soul into either a divine or a bestial likeness.</meta>

# On the Revelation of God in the Creation of Man

...self-will enters into greed, pride, or whatever else the heart’s will throws itself into. Such a likeness is formed by the **Fiat** <term>Fiat; Latin for "let it be." In Böhme’s thought, this is the active, formative power of God’s Word that "solidifies" spiritual desires into a specific shape or "image."</term> of the soul, though it happens by virtue of the **Third Principle** <term>Third Principle; The physical world and the cosmic forces of the stars and elements that govern material life.</term>, according to the spirit of the stars and the elements. Because the soul's will throws itself into the kingdom of this world, the external realm now has the power to introduce its **imagination** <term>Imagination; Not merely "fantasy," but the magical power of the soul to "image" or "form" itself into what it desires.</term> into the inner principle. And if the inner **Fiat** beholds this in the soul's fire, the soul becomes pregnant with it and holds onto it.

Now the soul possesses a bestial likeness according to the third principle, and this cannot be broken in all eternity unless the soul departs again with its will from the pleasure of earthliness and presses back into the Love of God. Only then does it regain the image of God. This can only happen during this life, because the soul stands essentially in its **Ether** <term>Ether; Here referring to the soul's formative spiritual environment or "breath" during its growth phase on earth.</term>, in the growth of its own tree; after this life, such a change may not occur.

Thus, we give you to understand what the soul, spirit, image, and **Turba** <term>Turba; Latin for "uproar" or "disturbance." It is the destructive force that shatters the divine image when the soul becomes dominated by wrath or earthly desire.</term> are: The soul dwells within itself and is an essential fire, and its image stands within itself—in its imagination, in its light—so long as it clings to God. If it does not, it stands in the anxiety and the fierce wrath of darkness and is a **larva** <note>original: "Larva"; Here used in the Latin sense of a "ghost," "mask," or "specter."</note> or image of the devils. Its **Turba**, which breaks the divine image, is the essential fierceness, and it occurs through imagination or false love and self-conceit. Therefore, everything depends upon the imagination: whatever a person lets into their desire, that is what the image becomes. And it is highly necessary for a human to constantly struggle against earthly reason in flesh and blood, to make the will-spirit of God’s mercy and love their own, and to constantly throw themselves into God’s will. They must not regard earthly goods or pleasure as their treasure or place their desire therein, for that destroys the noble image. For

<column-break/>

it is a **Turba** of the image of God and introduces bestial qualities into that image. In summary, Christ says: **Where your treasure is, there is your heart**, and according to this, God will judge the hidden things of humanity and separate the pure from the impure, giving the false over to the fire-trumpet <note>original: "Feuer-Tuba"; referring to the trumpet of the Last Judgment that sounds the end of the world.</note> to be swallowed up, while leading the holy—those who have entered into God—into His kingdom.

Thus the soul is in itself a strict, magical source of fire and a breath which has stood from eternity within itself in the eternal **Magia** <term>Magia; The "Great Magic" or the creative potentiality of God that brings something out of nothing.</term> of God. However, in creation, it was breathed forth by the eternally-working Word, qualifying in the rising fire-flash of the harsh **Fiat**, or the desiring, attractive will of God in the Word, according to the Father's property, and thus became active as its own being. The soul is therefore a pure, image-less fire, an awakened hunger and fire-desire of the **Triune** <note>original: "Drey-einigen"</note> God. Whatever this hunger and fire-desire now grasps—be it a divine, heavenly, or earthly essence—that same thing burns in the soul, just as oil-wood or similar things burn in a fire. If the fire-hunger of the soul is led into the holy, pure element and the essence of God (as the oil of the Holy Spirit), then this fire burns, qualifies, and works according to the property of this divine essence, bringing forth a divine life, light, and love. But if the soul’s fire-hunger is led into something earthly, tangible, fleshly, and bestial, then the soul burns in that as well and awakens an earthly, bestial, and fleshly life. If, however, the soul-fire seizes the property of hell and qualifies therein, it burns like a dark, fierce soot without light or majesty, and produces a poisonous, **arsenical** <note>original: "Arsenicalischen"; used here to mean "toxic," "corrosive," or "bitterly painful."</note>, biting, dark smoke; it lives then in a hellish manner, just as the devils live.

The soul's essences are from the **Center of Nature** <note>original: "Centro Naturæ"</note>, from the fire, with all the forms of nature. All three principles lie within it: everything that God has and can do, and what God is in His **Trinity** <note>original: "Drey-Zahl"</note>, that the soul is in its essence, like a branch from the power of a tree. Its being is created heavenly, out of the heavenly divine essence. But its will is free: either to sink into itself and...

<summary>This page explains that the human soul is an "essential fire" whose shape is determined by the "imagination" or focus of its desire. Depending on whether the soul desires God, the world, or wrath, it transforms into a divine, bestial, or demonic image.</summary>

### Part 3 / Chapter 8

...its beautiful **image** <term>Bildnis; In Böhme's theology, the "image" is the spiritual blueprint or true form of a being as God intended it.</term> is also imprisoned in dark harshness and infected with bitter **wrath** <term>Grimm; Often translated as "fury" or "wrath," it refers to the harsh, contracting, and agonizing quality of nature when it is separated from God’s light.</term>. Now that same wrath has become a **Turba** <note>original: "Turba"; A Latin term Böhme uses to describe a "disturber" or a spiritual storm that shatters the harmony of the soul and destroys its divine likeness.</note> that possesses the image and destroys the **likeness of God**. For in God there is love, light, and gentleness; but in this image, there is darkness, harshness, and bitterness, and its essential **torment** <note>original: "Quaal"; Böhme frequently plays on the linguistic connection between "Qual" (pain/torment) and "Quelle" (source/wellspring). Here it refers to the agonizing tension of the soul's raw energies.</note> is fire from the fierce **essences** <term>Essentien; The fundamental spiritual building blocks or "active powers" that make up a being's nature.</term>. Thus, as long as this image stands in such torment and form within the darkness, it does not belong in the Kingdom of God.

You have a further parable of the soul in the nature of fire: The soul is an essential fire, and the flash of that fire creates the life within it. The soul resembles a globe of fire or an "eye of fire." Now, the burning fire in its torment signifies the **First Principle** <term>First Principium; The dark, fiery foundation of all existence, which represents God's "strength" or "anger" before it is transformed by the light of the Son.</term>. Life itself, however, is not the fire, but rather the spirit of torment that arises in the anguish of the fire; that which goes out from the fire like an air is the true spirit of the fire’s life, which constantly blows upon the fire to keep it burning. Now, the fire gives off a shine and a light out of its torment, which dwells within the torment and shines forth from it—yet the torment does not comprehend the light. This signifies the **Second Principle** <term>Second Principium; The realm of Light, Love, and the Divine Majesty.</term> in which the Godhead dwells. For one recognizes that the power is in the light, and not in the fire. The fire only provides the "essences" to the light, while the life or the light provides gentleness and substantiality, like water. Now we understand that in the light there is a gentle life without torment; and though torment is present there, it is imperceptible—it is only a desire for joy or love. We then recognize that same torment as a **tincture** <term>Tinctur; A spiritual "dye" or transformative power that brings forth growth and the "bloom" of life.</term> in which growth and blossoming arise. The fire is the cause of this, but gentleness is the cause of its substance. For the love-desiring light draws substance to itself and holds it so that it becomes a "being"; but the fire-desire consumes that substance.

We must also remember the soul in this way: what the soul encounters purely on its own in its **Center** <term>Centro; The innermost point of origin for a soul's existence.</term>

<column-break/>

is an essential fire in the eye of eternity. However, that same eye is a desiring thing, namely a figure and image according to the Wisdom of God. The image stands within its desire—within its **imagination** <term>Imagination; For Böhme, this is not "fantasy," but a creative, magical power of the will that literally "images" or forms the soul's substance.</term>—for the **Word: Let it be** <note>original: "Verbum Fiat"; The creative command of God that "solidifies" spiritual desires into permanent forms.</note> has seized it, so that it should be a likeness according to the eternal Wisdom of God in which God dwells. Within this likeness, He may reveal through His Spirit what has eternally existed in His divine counsel.

Thus, the Majesty of God inflames the image within the essential fire, provided that the essential fire directs its desire into that Majesty. But where it does not, the image remains raw and naked outside of God, and its **tincture** becomes false. For the image stands in the tincture and has its origin in the tincture of light, not in the torment of the fire—just as the Heart or Word of God takes its origin in the light of Majesty within the Father's eternal fire-tincture. So it is with the image of the soul. The image certainly dwells in the soul’s fire, just as light dwells in fire, but it possesses a different **Principle**, just as light is a different kind of "torment" (or quality) than fire. Thus, the true image of God dwells in the light of the soul-fire. The fiery soul must draw this light from the "Wellspring of God’s Love" in His Majesty through its imagination and **surrender** <note>original: "Einergebung"; A central Böhme concept meaning the total yielding of the self-will to God's will.</note>. If the soul fails to do this, and instead imagines into itself—into its own fierce forms of fire-torment—rather than into the Wellspring of Love in God’s light, then its own torment of severity, harshness, and bitterness will arise. This becomes the **Turba** (the disturber) of God's image and swallows the likeness of God into the wrath.

Now, the harsh **Fiat** (the creative "Let it be") shapes an image in the soul’s fiery essences according to the soul's own imagination. Whatever the essential fire of the soul desires is formed into the soul as earthly figures, into which the soul's...

### 3. Part / Chapter 8.

...to regard itself as nothing / but rather to grow green like a branch from the tree and eat from God's love; or to rise up in its own will / in the fire / and to be its own tree: and from whatever it eats / from that it receives its substance / as the body of the creature. 11. **Question:** So much has been said of the fire-soul and her property on her own; but what is understood by the **light-soul**, in which the true **image of God** actually consists?

**Answer:** Note: because the soul is created through the working Word, out of the center of eternal nature, according to the property of the Father, as a magical **fire-source**; but the Father's will and desire is actually nothing other than to beget his beloved Son; so also the soul had this **idea** and impression within herself, to lead her magical fire-hunger into the Heart of God. However, she cannot proceed further in her **qualification** <note>Böhme uses "qualifying" or "qualification" to describe the way a thing acts, feels, or exists according to its inner qualities.</note> than to the flash of life, from which she has her origin. Now, when the soul sinks into the power of her own fire in her qualification, then the Heart and Son of God opens, and the little fountain of Divine **gentleness** <note>original: "Sanfftmuth"</note> wells up with the waters of life, which the soul draws in with powerful fire-desire, and therein qualifies. The water-source yields itself to the fire-source, and the fire-source ignites the water-source, and the fire in the water becomes a single light in the Lord. The fire-soul does not lose her essence, but just as the fire in the light, the day in the night, and hunger in food is as it were swallowed up, so the fire-soul becomes in the light-soul so magnificent, majestic, shining, lovely, friendly, and contented, that her fire-hunger, sting, wrath, and fire-power is not manifest; just as fire glows through an iron, and the iron appears as pure fire, although it is and remains iron; thus the Spirit of God dwells as a light in the soul, and shines through the soul, yet the soul does not become the Spirit, nor the Spirit the soul.

<column-break/>

In this now consists actually the true **image of God**, in which the soul may see God, namely in the fountain of life and the Heart of God. She is not by nature that same fountain; she only provides the fire for the revelation of this fountain, but the fountain is understood in the light, as in the gentleness of the light. So the soul's magical fire-source could also not be ignited, so that a glimmer of light might arise in the soul's fire, if the Divine love-desire, as the **Essence of love** <note>original: "Liebe Ens"</note>, did not yield itself into the soul-fire. The **essence** <note>original: "Ens"</note> of the Heart of God yields itself into the soul's fire-source; the soul-fire eats that into its fiery essence, by which the life of **fierceness** <note>original: "Grimmigkeit"</note> dies away, and the beautiful light is born from it.

The three forms of the dark fire-soul draw the **tincture** <note>A "tincture" in alchemy and Böhme's thought is a spiritualizing or transforming power that changes the quality of a substance.</note> from the fire and light into themselves, namely the **Virgin Sophia** <note>The "Virgin Sophia" represents Divine Wisdom, the feminine aspect of God’s mirror, and the true bride of the soul.</note>; she is their food, namely the greatest gentleness, the well-doing, and well-tasting; that takes hold in the desire of the three fire-forms into one essence: That essence is the

By the power of the properties of the soul, one arises out of the other, and each is always the mirror and eye of the other, through which the wonders are recognized and propagated. For in the abyss <note>original: "Abgrund"; refers to the "Ungrund" or the nothingness before creation.</note> there is nothing, but in the **Magic** <term>Magia: Böhme uses this term to describe the divine, supernatural power of the will that brings something out of nothing.</term> there is everything. Every mirror is a **center** <note>original: "Centrum"</note>, and yet it is its own center; for the first delight, longing, and desire give birth to it. It is the model of the first, for when I seek the foundation from the beginning of all being, I find the **Eye**, which is **GOD**. This is a desiring will of eternity; it enters into itself and seeks the abyss within itself. He is in nothing, but rather He is the mirror of the abyss and seeks Himself, and finds Himself, and that which is found seeks again for a model in which it can seek, find, and see itself. And this continues until the number ten, then the last finds the first again within itself, and thus the last is the model and mirror of the first, and the first is that of the last. It is like an eternal bond and stands in the will, in desiring, seeking, and finding, and within this being the **Great Mystery** <term>Mysterium Magnum: The "Great Mystery," the chaotic or potential state from which all distinct forms of life and matter emerge.</term> is enclosed.

But now the center, in its desiring, wishes to have a fulfillment in which it may rest; otherwise, everything would stand in anxious torment. The desire draws the "middle" out of all the forms so that it may fulfill its hunger, so that it may stand within itself in perfection and joy. Thus, out of the anguish, a **Love** is formed—a fulfillment of the torment—and this middle is **Sulfur** <term>Sulphur: In Böhme’s alchemy, this is not the chemical element, but the "soul" or inner power of a substance that contains both light and energy.</term>, with which the spirit in the will delights itself. For Sulfur has two forms within it: power and light. And together, this is the being born out of all the forms; it is **Matter**, essence, corporality, the Body of GOD, the Flesh of Christ, heavenly, and is the entire fulfillment of the Spirit in the **O** <note>The letter "O" represents the divine heart or the closed circle of eternity.</note>. It is the rest and revelation of the Godhead and stands in the **Virgin of Wisdom** <note>referring to Sophia, the divine mirror or the feminine principle of God's wisdom.</note>. The **Cross** is its goal, and it is the essentiality which goes through death by sinking down, as mentioned above, where the wrath remains in death, and it remains still as a death or a nothingness; and the life greens forth out of it in another **Principle** <note>original: "Principio"</note>.

<column-break/>

It is not the **Principle** alone; the Principle is born within it. In it, all the mirrors of the **Magic** are revealed, along with the wonders of the Mother <note>original: "Gebährerin"; the creative, birthing power of nature.</note>. She holds the **Great Mystery**, and out of her, the Spirit opens the wonders of eternity. The Spirit gives her the essences, for she is the food for his hunger. She is a being of wonders without number or end, and she also has no beginning. For the Spirit, in its desiring, begins her from eternity and remains in eternity. She is a body of the **Trinity** <note>original: "Drey-Zahl"</note> which is called **GOD**, and a body of the angels; so that the Spirit stands in an image, otherwise He would not be recognized.

Thus He knows Himself in the image and seeks the best **Magic**, and what He seeks, He finds, and he eats that, and thereby gives the Body of GOD His will, so that there is a unity in the holy Principle. For in the will of the corporal spirit, the wonders arise; these the Spirit of eternity grasps as the **Holy Spirit**. Thus it is a sound and a song from the eternal wonders, for the will of the corporal spirit is therein. And in this **seventh form** <note>The seventh property of nature, which Böhme calls "Essentiality" or "The Kingdom," where all the other forms find rest.</note>, the joy of the Godhead is increased and made perfect, for it is a fulfillment of the eternal desire and is the eternal food.

Since, however, all beings originate from **Fire**, we wish to present the **Great Mystery** clearly to you and show you **Paradise** well. If anyone wishes to be blind, he has been told and it has been revealed to him; let him go his way with **Babel** <note>Böhme’s term for the confused, worldly church and spiritual ignorance.</note>. You know that all life stands in fire and water, and the essence is its body, and the body is from the power of the spirit. For it is the spirit's food, and the spirit is in turn the body's food, and is the highest and greatest **nutriment** <note>original: "Nutriment"</note> within itself. For the external would not sustain it if the true life were not within itself.

So now, the **Fire** is the first cause of life, and the **Light** is the second cause, and the **Spirit** is the third cause, and yet it is one being which shuts itself into a body.

# Of the Revelation of GOD in the Creation of Mankind.

Since the soul has a certain qualification <note>original: "Qualificirung"; here meaning a specific set of active powers or qualities.</note>, it also begets a body. The fire-soul, within the light and heart of **GOD**, begets a holy, heavenly being and a pure heavenly body. But the fire-soul that directs its desire into the kingdom of this world begets an elementary and earthly body.

Thus Adam had a twofold body: one created from the inner element <note>In Böhme’s thought, the "inner element" is the pure, spiritual quintessence from which the four physical elements originate.</note>, where the inner element and heaven lie within alongside the heavenly essences—created in part by the inner **Fiat** <note>original: "Fiat"; Latin for "let it be," referring to God's creative command.</note>; and secondly, he was created out of the four elements of outer nature and from the stars by the outer **Fiat**. For in the matrix of the earth, these things stood within one another; Paradise was therein, and the body was also created into Paradise. Understand this rightly: he possessed both Divine and earthly essence, but the earthly was within the Divine, as if swallowed up or made powerless. The essence or matter from which the body was made or created was a mass, a water and a fire, containing the essence of both Principles <note>The "Principles" refer to the dark/fire world and the light/love world.</note>; although the first Principle also lay therein, it was not active. Each principle was meant to remain in its own seat and not mix, just as it happens in **GOD**; had it remained so, man would have been a complete likeness of **GOD'S** being.

<margin>Incarnation of Christ p. 1. c. 3. §. 3. == 15. <note>original: "Menschw."; abbreviation for Von der Menschwerdung Jesu Christi.</note></margin>
15. **Question:** What then is specifically to be understood by the inner heavenly and spiritual body?

**Answer:** The essence, working, and properties of the inner body are nothing other than a sinking down <note>original: "Ersincken"; Böhme's term for spirit condensing or subsiding into a more substantial form.</note> of that very spirit from which the soul itself is born. Every property of the soul also possesses a bodily property; for instance, the fiery property of the soul has a body from the inner constellation of the dark and fire-world, which is a spiritual body. And the light-property of the soul has a spiritual, oily, and watery body, in which the two properties of the highest Tincture <note>original: "Tinctur"; an alchemical term for the spiritual essence that transforms and perfects matter.</note> of fire and light reveal the luster and ornament of colors, wonders, and virtues of the Divine Wisdom.

<margin>Mysterium Magnum 15. 29. 30.</margin>
The Creator of this body is the **Fiat**, or the speaking and working of the Word, according to the property of fire and light that is active in the soul,

<column-break/>

in the manner of a spirit according to the six source-spirits <note>original: "Quell-Geister"; the seven foundational forces or "qualities" of nature in Böhme's system.</note> of nature leading toward the seventh, which is the body. The matter of this body is the pure, Holy Element. In **GOD**, everything is power, spirit, and life; the spirit originates in the fire, and as it sinks down from its fire-power, the fire becomes water. For water is nothing other than a sunken, powerless, extinguished fire-breath. This fire-breath is dried and drawn together by the harsh, cold desire of the **Fiat**, and from this arises a being and a tangibility, and it is called "body" because it is an extinguished and sunken spirit-water, coagulated by the cold, harsh **Fiat**, and rendered as it were powerless, without life, so that it had to be animated by a spirit and a life. The form and figure of this body is entirely according to the soul's fire- and light-shape: the pure virginal image of **GOD**. In this inner man are figured and formed all the likenesses of the invisible fire- and light-world, all thrones, princes, angels, and creatures of the angelic world—especially of that throne in which **Lucifer** was king. This body was majestic, bright, shining, transparent, of all kinds of colors and wonders, which played within it as if in pure precious stones, crystal, and diamonds. It is penetrating, fleeting, and full of spirit, confined to no place and enclosed in none. His eyes were like flames of fire and had their brilliance from within, in the birth of the light. His hands were the instruments of his power; his feet were swift, like the wings of the morning-redness <note>original: "Morgen-Röthe"; often translated as "Aurora," a central symbol of spiritual awakening for Böhme.</note>; his food grew within his body as in a pleasure-garden of **GOD**. His little fountain had an abundance of water; his mouth was the gentle, attractive desire of the will toward the light and an opening for the praise of **GOD**. His speech was a lovely resounding and echoing of the source-spirits, and all his nerves were like a tuned stringed instrument, where the essences stood in a harmony <note>original: "Harmonia".</note>. This inner man, then, was the true image of **GOD**, according to the likeness in which **GOD** revealed Himself in the angelic world, according to the property of fire and light. But because **GOD**, after the fall of **Lucifer**, also revealed Himself in this visible world, man also had to become an image of **GOD** according to the likeness of **GOD’S** revelation in this visible world and all its creatures, so that he might rule over everything.

### Part 3 / Chapter 8

created an unbreakable life; thus, we can in no way say of the coarse, fleshly image that this coarse, earthly property is the Image of **GOD** which can possess the holy world. For it is not of the same essence and being, of which Christ says in John chapter 6: "The Spirit gives life; the flesh counts for nothing." <note>original: "Der Geist ist das Leben / das Fleisch ist kein nütze"; referring to John 6:63.</note> Likewise, "flesh and blood shall not inherit the kingdom of heaven." And yet, the true body lies within this animal-like, coarse property, just as gold lies within a coarse stone. Everything about man that is earthly is animalistic and fragile, and is not truly "Man." Although **GOD** created an external body for man from the <term>clay</term> <note>original: "Limo"; from the Latin 'limus,' referring to the mud or dust of the earth from which Adam was formed.</note> of the earth, we are not to regard it as it currently exists. For the true human body, according to the inner world, is a spiritual <term>Sulphur</term>, a spiritual <term>Mercurius</term>, and a spiritual <term>Salz</term> <note>These are the 'Tria Prima' or Three Principles. In Böhme’s thought, Sulphur represents the internal fire or soul-will, Mercury represents movement and communication, and Salt represents the physical or substantial form.</note>; every property of the soul has a bodily or substantial counterpart within itself. **GOD** created such a body just as the soul was in its essence—as it existed in the expressed Word of the understanding—and breathed the soul into the understanding. Thus, the outer "sulphuric" body is by no means the coarse animal that passes away and does not return. The right and true body, which lies hidden within the coarseness, is to be considered a spiritual body in contrast to that coarseness. It is indeed within flesh and blood, but was created in a "fixed," enduring state.

Through Adam’s desire <note>original: "Lust"; referring to the wandering of Adam's desire away from God toward the earthly world.</note>, this coarseness became manifest through his <term>Imagination</term> <note>In Böhme’s terminology, 'Imagination' is the power of the mind to 'form' or 'image' its desires into reality.</note>. The true outer body is a property of sulphur, mercury, and salt—a pure, essential power according to the nature of the soul. Whatever the soul is in spirit, that the true human body is in substance: a housing for the soul. All properties of the inner holy body, together with the outer ones, were (in the first man) directed into a single <term>Harmony</term>. None lived according to its own selfish desire, but all surrendered their desire to the soul, in which the Divine Light was manifest, as in the holy heaven. The Light shone

<column-break/>

through all properties and created a balanced <term>Temperance</term> among them. All properties surrendered their desire into the Light, as into **GOD’s** revealed sweetness, which penetrated through all properties. In this penetration, they were all <term>tinctured</term> <note>original: "tingiret"; from alchemy, meaning to be infused or transformed by a higher essence.</note> with sweet love, so that between them there was nothing but pure delight and the desire for love.

The inner holy bodiliness, made of the pure element, penetrated through the four elements and held the <term>clay</term> of the earth (as the outer sulphuric body) within itself, as if swallowed up. Although it was truly present, it was there in the same way that darkness dwells within the light: its darkness cannot become manifest before the light. But if the light is extinguished, then the darkness is revealed. Thus, the inner man held the outer man captive within himself and penetrated him, just as fire makes iron glow—so that one thinks it is pure fire—but if the fire goes out, the black, dark iron becomes visible.

So also was the first man when he stood in his "fixity" <note>original: "Fixheit"; a state of spiritual stability and permanence.</note> in Paradise, in the same way that "time" is before **GOD** and **GOD** is in time, yet neither is the other, and yet they are not separately divided. Just as time is a "play" before **GOD**, so also was the outer life of man a play before the inner Holy Man, who was the true Image of **GOD**. The outer spirit and body were before the inner as a wonder of Divine Revelation—according to the worlds of fire, darkness, and light—a mirror of the great omnipotence and omniscience of **GOD**. The inner man was given to the outer as its ruler.

Just as **GOD** plays with the time of the outer world before Himself, so also should the inner divine man play with the revealed wonders of **GOD** in this world. He was to reveal the Divine Wisdom in every creature, each according to its property, as well as in the earth, in stones, and in metals, in which there is also a twofold be<meta>catchword: be (Wesen / being)</meta>

# On the Revelation of GOD in the Creation of Man.

Essence lies / as from the origin of the dark **Fire-world** / and then from the origin of the holy **Light-world**. All this was given to him for his play: He possessed the knowledge of all <term>Tinctures</term> <note>original: "Tincturen"; in Böhmean alchemy, a Tincture is the spiritual power that penetrates and transforms matter, like a soul or life-force.</note> / everything was under him: He ruled in heaven and earth / and in all elements, as well as in all the stars: And that was because the Divine Power was manifest in him / neither heat nor cold pressed upon him. Just as a Tincture penetrates a body and preserves it from sickness / and as the sun’s warmth preserves the body from cold / so also the highest Tincture of Divine Fire and Light / as the holy power of the inner spiritual body / penetrated through the outer body of flesh and blood / and took all outer elementary properties / as well as the <term>clay</term> <note>original: "Limum"; from the Latin 'limus,' referring to the 'dust of the ground' from Genesis.</note> of the earth into its preservation or protection. For in the body of the inner and outer man there was a <term>Temperament</term> <note>original: "Temperantz"; a state of perfect balance where no single element dominates another.</note>; thus nothing that was outside the body could destroy or attack this balance; just as gold withstands the fire / and as a Tincture penetrates everything and yields to nothing: So too was man subject to no thing / but only to the one **GOD** / who dwells through him / and was manifest in him with the power of the holy Essence: and that was an Image and Likeness of **GOD** / in whom the Spirit of **God** dwelt.

Reason will understand us poorly / and say: I speak of two kinds of men; But I say no / I speak only of a Single one / who is a likeness after **GOD** / according to the manifested **GOD** / according to the expressed formed Word of the Divine Power / of the Divine Understanding. Just as in **GOD** all things are in Essence / and yet He Himself is not that same Essence / and yet He rules the Essence / each essence according to its property: So also the inner spiritual man is an image of the formed Word of the Divine Power; and the outer is an image of the inner / as an

instrument of the inner. As we then see / that the Will is the master in every undertaking / and see further / how the inner has divine will and desire: But the outer has only an animal one / which only became so through the Fall. The whole man is only a single man / but his property lies in special <term>degrees</term> <note>original: "Gradibus"; stages or levels of being.</note> according to the inner and outer heavens / as according to Divine Revelation / through the seven properties of nature.

18. **Question.** What then is actually to be understood by the **Fifth Essence** or the best part of the earth?

**Answer.** Just as all seeds are a **Fifth Essence** and the **extract** from the body out of which they have grown, resembling also a <term>thickened</term> <note>original: "coagulirten"</note> spirit-water or a tough slime, therein lies the <term>Creative Command</term> <note>original: "Fiat"; from the Latin for "let it be," representing the active, shaping word of God</note>, the **Matter**, and the **Form** to become such a thing again as the body was from which the seed came. Thus this earth is a kernel and **Fifth Essence**, an **extract** of the whole visible world; in this **Fifth Essence** is the harsh **Creative Command**, the working word. The **Matter** is an **extract** from each and every thing—from the upper and lower creatures. The **Form** is shaped entirely according to the whole great visible world, so that in the kingdom of stars there is no spark so small, in the vegetable kingdom no blade of grass so humble, and in the animal kingdom no beast or worm so lowly, from which the harsh **Creative Command** has not drawn its **Fifth Essence**, kernel, and marrow, and from it made the body of **Man**.

Thus man is an **extract** of everything, and a **perfection** out of everything. For out of this great clockwork / as from the upper and the lower / where everything lies within one another / man was created in the image of **GOD** / for **Moses** says / the **LORD** spoke: **Let us make man / an image after us / who shall rule over all creatures on earth / over the beasts / birds / fish / and over all the earth / and the worms / that crawl upon the earth.** Now, if men are to rule over all these / then they must also be from the very same ground / and moreover from the best power thereof; for no thing rules deeper than its mother is / from which it comes / unless it be <term>transformed</term> <note>original: "transmutiret"</note> into something better / then it also rules in that better thing / and no further than its own ground reaches.

19. **Question.** Was the earth and the <term>Salitter</term> <note>original: "Salitter"; a Böhmean term for the divine "sap" or "saltpeter" of the earth, representing its creative potential</note>, from which Adam was taken, not then infected by the wrath of Lucifer?

But the Mass was held in the firmament of Heaven so that it did not congeal. For as the Heart of GOD looked upon the Mass with His hot love, the Oil in the Mass—which rose out of the water through the fire, from which the Light rises, and from which the Spirit of Love, the Heart of GOD, rises—became pregnant with a young son. That was the seed of love, for one love received the other; the love of the Mass received the love from the gaze of the Heart of GOD, and was thereby infected <note>In the sense of being "infused" or "seeded"</note> and became pregnant. And that is the birth of the soul; according to this son, man is GOD’s image.

The Source-Spirits in the Mass could not, however, be ignited by the soul immediately, for the soul stood only as a seed in the Mass, hidden with the Heart of God in His Heaven, until the Creator breathed upon the Mass. Then the Source-Spirits also ignited the soul, and then body and soul lived at once. 18. Question: What then is actually to be understood by the Fifth Essence or the best of the earth?

Answer: Just as all seeds are a Fifth Essence, and the extract from the body from which they have grown, they also resemble a coagulated <term>Spirit-Water</term> <note>original: "Geist-Wasser"</note>, or a viscous slime; within it lies the <term>Fiat</term> <note>Latin: "Let there be"; the creative word of God.</note>, the <term>Matter</term> <note>original: "Materia"</note>, and the Form to again become such a thing as the body was from which the seed came. Thus, this earth is a kernel and Fifth Essence, an extract of the whole visible world. In this Fifth Essence is the harsh *Fiat*, the working Word. The Matter is an extract from each and every thing, the upper and lower creatures; the Form is indeed figured after the whole great visible world, according to the figure of each and every property. Thus, in the Starry Kingdom there is no spark so small, in the Vegetable Kingdom no blade of grass so lowly, and in the Animal Kingdom no beast or worm so insignificant, from which the harsh *Fiat* has not drawn its Fifth Essence, kernel, and marrow, and from it made the outer body of man.

Thus man is an extract from everything, and a perfection of everything. For out of this great clockwork—as from the Upper and the Lower, where everything lies within one another—man was created in the **Image of GOD**. For Moses says: the LORD spoke: **Let us make man, an image after us, who shall rule over all creatures on earth, over the beasts, birds, fish, and over all the earth and creeping things that crawl upon the earth.** Now, if men are to rule over all these, they must also be of the same ground, and moreover of the best power of the same; for no thing rules deeper than its mother is from which it comes, unless it be transmuted into a better thing, then it also rules in that better thing, and no further than its ground is.

<column-break/>

Further Moses says: **GOD made man from the clod of earth, and breathed into him the living breath; then man became a living soul.** Here we are not to understand that GOD stood there in a personal, creaturely way like a man and took a lump of earth and made a body out of it; no, that is not it. Rather, the Word of GOD, as the Speaking (<term>Fiat</term>), was active in all properties (in the <term>Spirit of the World</term> <note>Latin original: "Spiritu Mundi"</note>, and in the Being of the earth from the Spirit of the World), and spoke a life into all essences—namely the *Fiat*, which is the desire of the Word in <term>potentiality</term> <note>original: "Scientz"; here referring to the divine imaginative power or proto-knowledge.</note>. This was in the eternally-seen model of man, which had stood in Wisdom, and it drew the Being of all properties of the earth, and whatever may be therein, into a mass; that was a Fifth Essence from the four elements, in which lay the <term>Tincture</term> <note>original: "Tincktur"; the spiritual essence or "soul" of a substance.</note> of all powers from all three principles, as well as the property of the whole creation of all creatures, as the essence of all essences from which all creatures had arisen.

For, understand it rightly: the earthly creatures of time are made with the <term>Body</term> <note>Latin original: "Corpore"</note> from the four elements, but the body of man is from the <term>Balance</term> <note>original: "Temperatur"; a state where all elements are in perfect harmony without conflict.</note>, where all four elements lie within one another in one essence, from which earth, stones, and metals, along with all earthly creatures, have their origin. Indeed, from the <term>Slime</term> <note>Latin original: "Limo"; referring to the "dust" or "mud" of Genesis 2:7.</note> of the earth, but not from the coarseness of the enclosed essence of division in the properties (where each property has taken itself into a special essence of earth, stones, and metals), but from the Fifth Essence, wherein the four elements lie within the Balance, where neither heat nor cold was manifest, but they were all in equal weight. For if man was to rule over all creatures, he must indeed have the higher power, as the highest Being of the creature, within himself, from which the creatures are one degree more external, or lower (or as...

# On the Revelation of GOD in the Creation of Man.

Yet we should not think that animal properties were meant to be creaturely or manifest within man; rather, the <term>Being</term> <note>original: "Ens"</note> of all creatures lay within the human Being, in the <term>Balance</term> <note>original: "Temperatur"; in Böhme’s thought, this is the state where all qualities are in perfect harmony, rather than one dominating the others.</note>. Man is an image of the entire creation of all three <term>Principles</term> <note>Böhme's "Three Principles" are the dark world of fire/will, the light world of love/majesty, and the visible world of nature.</note>, not only in the Being of the outer nature of the stars and four elements—as the created world—but also from the Being of the inner spiritual world, from Divine Essence. For the holy Word, in its Being, included itself within the spoken Word; namely, as the heaven included itself within the essence of the outer world, as well as the "greening" within the essence of the inner world, such as Paradise; the holy element was within the surging government.

In summary, the human <term>Body</term> <note>Latin original: "Corpus"</note> is a <term>Slime</term> <note>Latin original: "Limus"; referring to the "dust of the ground" in Genesis 2:7, viewed here as a refined extract.</note> out of the essence of all essences; otherwise, it could not be called a likeness of GOD, or an image of GOD. The invisible GOD, who has introduced Himself from eternity into Essence, and also with this world into time, has modeled Himself with the human image, out of all essences into a creaturely image, as a figure of the invisible Being. To this end, He did not give him the creaturely animal life from the "science" of the creature—for that life had to remain undivided in the Balance—but He breathed into him the living breath, as the true intelligible life in the Word of Divine Power; that is, He breathed into him the true soul of all three Principles in the Balance.

That was the seed of love, for one love received the other; the love of the Mass received the love from the gaze of the Heart of GOD, and was thereby infected and became pregnant: and that is the birth of the soul. According to this son, man is the image of GOD.

Moses calls the material from which Adam was made "Red Earth," because it possessed a solar quality and was a highly refined <term>Quintessence</term> <note>The "fifth essence," a substance more pure than the four physical elements (earth, water, air, fire).</note> extracted from all earth. Just as gold is a highly exalted form of earth, and the sun is the heart and core of all the stars, so too in this "Red Earth," the <term>Tincture</term> <note>A spiritual life-force or "essence" that gives quality and color to matter.</note> was most noble, and refined to the highest and richest degree.

### 20. Question: What kind of shape and image did the first man have?

**Answer:** It is very remarkable; regarding the first *inner* man, it is written: *And GOD created man in His own image, in the image of GOD created He him.* But regarding the *outer* man, it is written: *GOD formed the dust of the man from the Red Earth.* The outer man had no form other than the likeness of the inner man; his image was a <term>Replica</term> <note>original: "Contrafayt"; a portrait or exact representation.</note> of the entire world: heaven and earth, stars and elements, birds, fish, four-footed and creeping animals—everything was represented here. Beyond this, he also contained both male and female forms within himself, for both Tinctures were in him, which we shall discuss hereafter. The author demonstrates in great detail that man is, for example, a complete imprint of the stars and the entire depth of the heavens.

<column-break/>

"Take," he says, "an analogy from a man, who is made according to the image or likeness of GOD, as it is written in Moses, Genesis 1:27."

The interior or hollow space in a person's body represents the "Deep" <note>The vast space or vacuum of the universe.</note> between the stars and the earth. The entire body, with everything in it, signifies heaven and earth. The **flesh** signifies the earth and is also made of earth. The **blood** signifies the water and is also from water. The **breath** signifies the air and is also the air. The **bladder** <note>The author likely refers to the lungs or the thoracic cavity here, as he links it to air and breathing.</note>, in which the air operates, signifies the Deep between the stars and the earth, in which fire, air, and water operate in an elemental way; warmth, air, and water also operate in the bladder just as they do in the Deep above the earth. The **veins** signify the power-channels of the stars, and they truly are the power-channels of the stars, for the stars with their power rule in the veins and drive the person into their particular form. The **entrails** or intestines signify the working or "consumption" of the stars: everything that has come from their power, which they themselves have made, they consume again, and it remains within their power. Thus, the intestines are also the consumption of everything the person puts into them—everything that has grown from the power of the stars. The **heart** in man signifies heat or the element of **fire**, and it is indeed heat, for heat has its origin in the heart for the entire body. The **bladder** signifies the element of **air**, and air also rules within it. The **liver** signifies the element of **water** and is water, for from the liver comes the blood into the whole body and all the limbs; the liver is the mother of the blood. The **lungs** signify the **earth** and possess the same quality. The **feet** signify "near and far," for in GOD, near and far are one thing; a person can reach both near and far through their feet, but wherever they may be, in nature they are neither near nor far, for in God it is...

# Of the Revelation of GOD in the Creation of Man.

...one thing. The hands signify the **omnipotence of GOD**; for just as GOD can change everything in nature and make from it what He wills, so also can man with his hands change everything that has grown or come out of nature, and make from it with his hands what he wills. He rules with his hands the work and essence of all nature, and they rightly signify the omnipotence of GOD.

->Now note further here.<-

The whole body up to the neck signifies and is the round circle of the circulation of the stars, as well as the depth between the stars, wherein the planets and elements rule. The flesh signifies the earth, which is solidified and has no mobility: so also the flesh has in itself no reason, understanding, or mobility; rather, it is moved by the power of the stars, which rule in the flesh and veins. So also the earth would bring forth no fruit, nor would any metal grow therein—neither gold, silver, copper, iron, nor stone—if the stars did not work therein; not even a tiny blade of grass would grow from it <unclear>without</unclear> the working of the stars. The head signifies the heaven; it has grown together with the veins and "power-passages" of the body, and all powers go from the head and brain into the body, into the source-veins of the flesh.

But now, heaven is a lovely hall of joy, in which all powers are present, as in all of nature—in stars and elements—but not in such a harsh, driving, and agonizing way. For every power of heaven has only one <term>species</term> <note>original: "Species"; here meaning a specific type, form, or appearance of divine power.</note> or form of power: bright and quite gently welling, not evil and good mixed together as in the stars and elements, but pure and clear. It is made from the center of the waters, but it does not <term>qualify</term> <note>original: "qualificiren"; a technical term in Böhme’s writing meaning to operate, interact, or manifest specific qualities.</note> in the same way as the water in the elements, for the <term>wrath</term> <note>original: "Grimmigkeit"; referring to the harsh, bitter, or "dark" side of nature's forces.</note> is not

<column-break/>

therein. But nonetheless, heaven belongs to nature, for the stars and elements have their origin and power from heaven. For heaven is the **heart of the water**. Just as in all creatures, as well as in all that exists in this world, water is its heart, and nothing exists without water—whether it be in the flesh or outside the flesh, in the plants of the earth, or in metal and stones—so in all things, water is the core or the heart.

Thus, heaven is the heart in nature, in which all powers are, just as they are in the stars and elements; it is a soft and gentle material of all powers, just like the brain in the head of man. Now heaven, with its power, ignites the stars and elements so that they well up and drive; so also is the head of man like heaven. Just as in heaven all powers are gentle and lovely, and moreover full of joy and "qualify" [interact], so in the head or brain of man, all powers are gentle and full of joy. And just as heaven has a conclusion or <term>firmament</term> <note>original: "Schluß oder Festung"; literally a 'closure' or 'fortress,' referring to the boundary of the celestial sphere.</note> above the stars, yet all powers go out from heaven into the stars; so the brain has a conclusion or firmament for the body, and yet all powers go out from the brain into the body and into the whole man. The head has within itself the five senses, namely seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting, and feeling, in which the stars and elements interact, and therein arises the **sidereal star-spirit** or nature-spirit in men and animals. In these, evil and good well up, for it is a house of the stars. The stars take such power from heaven that they can make a living and moving spirit in the flesh of men and animals. The movement of heaven makes the stars mobile; so also the head makes the body mobile. Here, now open the eyes of your spirit, and behold GOD, your Creator.

### Part 3 / Chapter 8.

Just as man’s outer body has a form and nature according to the properties of the stars and elements, so too does he contain within himself a likeness of the vegetable kingdom, of trees and plants. His nerves and tendons are like the growths of the earth, with roots, trunks, branches, and all their outer parts; the muscles are like leaves. The bones were not so hard in the beginning, but transparent, and stood like veins of gold and silver in the earth; they were an essence of pure power. Likewise, he also had a nature like the animal kingdom, though in a very pure and holy degree, as was fitting for the image of GOD, and so he also had an outer form. However, our author describes this outer form more by what it was *not* than what it *was*. That Adam had a different form before the Fall than after the Fall we see from the fact that, after his Fall, he no longer recognized himself; therefore he was ashamed of his monstrous form and hid himself behind the trees in the garden. For he saw himself as having an animal-like form, and he immediately received animal-like members for reproduction, which the <term>Fiat</term> <note>original: "Fiat"; the divine command "Let there be," here acting as a creative force.</note> in the third principle created for him through the spirit of the great world. No one should imagine that man had animal-like members for reproduction before his Fall, but rather heavenly ones. He also had no intestines, for such stench and filth as a human has in the body does not belong in the Holy Trinity in Paradise, but in the earth, which must return to its <term>Ether</term> <note>original: "Æther"; the refined element or spiritual atmosphere.</note>. Man was created immortal and moreover holy, like the angels; and although he was made from the <term>Limbus</term> <note>original: "Limbo"; in this context, the spiritual-material "extract" or "mud" of the universe from which Adam was formed.</note>, he was nonetheless pure.

The Trinity, with all three principles, desired to have a complete likeness in essence and property, according to the "Being of all beings"; and this desire to have the same was awakened in God’s heart as a great wonder. This awakening was the harsh <term>Fiat</term>, acting as a longing attraction; it pulled from everything into one, and it became an image according to the likeness of GOD—according to heaven and this world, and also according to the world of wrath. The entire <term>Fiat</term> in the **Word of the Lord** <note>original: "Verbo Domini"</note>, from the kingdom of GOD and of wrath; (thus the soul is a breath of GOD awakened and breathed out according to all three principles from the heart of GOD). Therefore, nothing is higher than the soul, and there is nothing that can break it, for everything is beneath it and within it; it is a child of the entire Being of all beings. Thus was it created.

# On the Revelation of GOD in the Creation of Man.

Man is a living soul. Now, the breath and Spirit of GOD is a threefold source-quality: In the first <term>Principle</term> <note>original: "Principio"; Böhme’s term for the fundamental realms of reality.</note>, it is a fire-breath or spirit, which is the true cause of life and stands in the Father’s quality, as in the center of wrathful nature. In the second Principle is GOD's breath or Spirit, the light-flaming Spirit of Love, which is the true Spirit of the actual Godhead and is called GOD the Holy Spirit. And in the third Principle, as in the likeness of GOD, GOD's breath is the air-spirit, upon which the Holy Spirit travels, as David says: *The Lord travels upon the wings of the wind.* And Moses says: *The Spirit of GOD hovers upon the water* [Genesis 1:2], upon the <term>capsule</term> <note>original: "Capſulâ"; referring here to the atmospheric container or the 'shell' of the physical elements.</note> where the air originates. Now, the whole of GOD breathed and introduced this threefold spirit from all three principles into the created image; first, the fire-spirit, which He introduced from within—not through the nose, but into the heart, into the twofold <term>tincture</term> <note>original: "Tinctur"; a spiritual essence or transformative quality that "colors" or gives character to a being.</note> of the inner and outer blood. Although the outer was not yet recognized but remained a mystery, the inner was active and had two tinctures: the first from the fire, the second from the light. This fire-spirit is the true essential soul, for it possesses the <term>Center of Nature</term> <note>original: "Centrum Naturæ"; the core driving force of existence.</note> with its four forms of fire-power. It strikes up its own fire and itself makes the wheel of essences, as was reported at length in the second and third books. And you should know that the essential soul-fire is not the true image according to the Godhead: it is no image, but a magical, everlasting fire; it never had a beginning, nor will it have an end. Understand that GOD introduced the eternal, beginningless fire—which from eternity existed within itself in the eternal <term>Magic</term> <note>original: "Magia"; the divine, creative will.</note> as the will of GOD, in the desire of eternal nature, as an eternal center of the birthing mother—because this image was meant to be a likeness of Him. Secondly, along with the essential soul-fire,

<column-break/>

the Holy Spirit introduced the light-flaming Spirit of Love from out of Himself, specifically in the second Principle, wherein the Godhead is understood. This was not breathed in through the nose, but just as fire and light cling together and are one, yet exist in two qualities [Quallen], so the good Spirit of Love was introduced into his heart along with the essential fire-spirit. Each quality brought its own tincture with it, as its own life; and in the tincture of love, the true spirit is understood, which is the image of GOD. This spirit is a likeness of the clear, true Godhead and looks like the whole man, filling the whole man, but within its own Principle.

The soul, when considered purely on its own, is a fire-eye or a fire-mirror in which the Godhead has revealed itself according to the first Principle (that is, according to nature); for it is a creature, yet created in no likeness. But its image, which it brings forth out of its fire-eye into a light, that is the true creature for whose sake GOD became man and led it back out of the wrath of eternal nature into the <term>Holy Ternary</term> <note>original: "Ternarium Sanctum"; the holy realm of the Trinity’s manifestation.</note>. We must further understand the soul and its image in this way: they are indeed one spirit together, but the soul is a hungry fire and must have substance [Wesenheit], otherwise it becomes a hungry, dark valley, as the devils have become. Thus the soul produces fire and life, and the gentleness of the image produces love and heavenly substance. In this way, the soul-fire is softened and filled with love, for the image has water from GOD's well, which springs into eternal life; this is love and gentleness, and it takes it from GOD’s majesty. This can be seen in a lit fire: how the fire has a wrathful quality [Quall] and the light has a gentle, lovely quality; and just as in the depths of this world water is produced from light and air, so it is here as well.

### Part 3 / Chapter 8.

source-quality <note>original: "Quaal"; Böhme uses this term to describe both a "source-spring" and the inner "tension" or "vibration" that constitutes a thing's nature.</note>, like the air, was also simultaneously breathed into the human nose. He also had neither male nor female shape or form, for he was both and possessed both **tinctures** <term>tincture</term> <note>original: "Tincturen"; in Böhme’s thought, these are the spiritual essences of fire (male/soul) and light (female/spirit) which must be balanced.</note>, those of the soul and the spirit, of fire and light. He was a chaste **virgin** in pure love; he loved and impregnated himself through **Imagination** <note>This refers to a creative, spiritual power of the mind, not mere fantasy.</note>: thus was his reproduction intended to be. He was a lord over stars and elements, a likeness of GOD. Just as GOD dwells within the stars and elements and nothing can seize Him, for He rules over all: so too was man created. Earthly source-quality was not fully active in him; he did indeed possess the spirit of the air, but heat and cold were not to touch him, for God’s essentiality permeated everything. Just as Paradise permeated the earth and bloomed, so the heavenly essentiality bloomed in the outer being of his body and outer spirit. In GOD, all things are possible, even what appears strange to us in this earthly life.

Fourthly, through the introduction of his beautiful heavenly image into the Spirit of GOD, Adam received the **living Word of GOD**. That was the food for his soul and his image. This same living word was surrounded by the **Divine Virgin of Wisdom**.

Question: But because the third <term>Principle</term> <note>original: "Principium"; the third of Böhme's three cosmic realms, specifically the physical, visible world.</note> of this world was infected by the wrath of Lucifer, the spirit of this world carried the source-quality of that wrath with it. Why then did GOD breathe such a thing into man?

Answer: Man had to be an image according to GOD’s likeness in all three Principles; and as he had a body from the third Principle, so he also had to have a spirit from this Principle. Every spirit without a body is raw and does not know itself. Now, every spirit desires a body, both for food and for delight. Since GOD had created the third Principle as a **mirror of the Godhead** before the soul existed, this mirror was already attached to the Eternal, for it was born of the eternal wonders and thus created. Therefore, the third Principle did not want to let the soul go free, because it too was created from GOD’S wonders and stood in the beginning as a figure in God’s Wisdom. Because it was material, it desired also to have a material likeness in the soul; and it stirred the spirit within the <term>Fiat</term> <note>The divine command 'Let there be' (Latin), viewed here as a creative force or 'word' that shapes reality.</note>. This became a human: a raw earth made of fire and water. And the heavenly Matrix also longed for the soul and wanted it to bear her image; and during the creation of the body, she seized her own *Fiat* and created before the earthly *Fiat* could. This was the first; for out of the center of the Word, the *Fiat* went forth with the Word; thus the third Principle was created into the other.

The Virgin of Wisdom first surrounded the soul-spirit with heavenly essentiality, with heavenly divine flesh; and the Holy Spirit gave the heavenly **tincture**, which produced heavenly blood and water, as was reported at length in our third book. Thus the inner man stood in heaven, and his essences were Paradise; his radiance in his inner eyes...

And the outer spirit, as air, with the entire outer principle—with stars and elements—clung to the inner one; and the outer spirit breathed its life into him at the same time as the soul, through the nose into the heart—into the outer heart, into the earthly flesh, which yet was not truly "earthly" in our sense, for it had become corporeal out of the Matrix <note>original: "Matrice"; the divine womb or source-material of creation.</note> out of the labor <note>original: "Sucht"; Böhme often uses this to mean a longing or the "birth-pang" of creation.</note> from which the earth was formed.

And the soul burned out of the heart-blood like a light from a candle, and it passed through all three principles like a king over his land. 24. Qu. Does man then have three souls?

**Answer:** Just as the Triune GOD is revealed according to three principles—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—and remains one single true GOD, highly praised in eternity, so also is this three-fold breath of life. Namely: the dark fire-soul in the property of the Father; the light-soul or the spirit in the property of the Son; and the air-spirit in the property of the Holy Spirit, which proceeds from all three principles. It is only one single spirit and one single soul. It has, however, in its power a three-fold qualification: to live as an angel of GOD, or as a devil, or as a beast. Wherever it directs its **imagination** <note>The spiritual power to shape one's inner reality.</note>, that specific life is awakened within it. Thus when Moses says: *GOD breathed into man the living breath, and there man became a living soul*, this refers to a living, speaking, and understanding spirit drawn from all three principles: from the inner fire-world (which is revealed through the dark world), from the holy light-world, and from the outer air-world. That is the soul. The inner fire-breath is the true, eternal, creaturely soul; and the light-breath is the true, understanding spirit of the soul, in which it is an angel; and the outer air-breath is the rational soul in the growing animal life, by which man rules over all creatures of this world. This is one single soul in three principles, according to the likeness of GOD.

Just as the single understanding of the unfathomable Godhead has revealed itself with three principles, so He has also [revealed] the same...

GOD spoke this again into this unique image to be a ruler of the body and all other creatures—or, as the German text in Moses [Genesis] says, "breathed."

The third realm or world is the outer starry and elemental one, as the air with its ruling stars, in which all five outer stars rule, as the higher and the lower of the four elements, from which the five senses <note>original: "Sensus"</note> take their origin, in which the growing and the rational life stands. ### 3. Part / Chapter 8.

...[God] breathed the living breath into man. What do you understand by this? Do you understand it to be only the air? That is not **GOD’S** breath alone: for the air was breathed into his nose, as *Moses* says. But **GOD’S** breath cannot be blown in from the outside; for **GOD** is Himself the fullness of all things and is already present when the outermost part arrives. Now, so that you may be correctly, thoroughly, and truly informed, look at what we mentioned earlier: how **GOD** longed for His own likeness according to the visible essence, and how the image of the Virgin <note>Böhme refers to the "Heavenly Virgin" or "Sophia," representing Divine Wisdom and the mirror in which God sees His own wonders.</note>, in whom His wonders stood, caused one imagination to receive the other. Though **GOD** is without essence and desire—for His desire is only majesty and freedom—the Center of Nature <term>Center of Nature</term> <note>original: *Centrum Naturae*. This is the inner "workshop" or driving force of reality where the dark and light forces of existence are generated.</note> upon the Cross of Wonders <note>A symbolic reference to the intersection of the eternal and temporal worlds, often depicted by Böhme as a cross-like structure within the divine manifestation.</note> lusted after the image seen in the Virgin, where the Spirit of **God** goes forth into Wisdom, and where Wisdom causes essence. See, such was **GOD’S** breathing-in: The Spirit of **God** hovered upon the waters and traveled upon the wings of the wind, as the Scripture says. He had grasped the spirit—the governance of this world—with the *Word "Let there be"* <note>original: *Verbo Fiat*</note> and breathed it into Adam’s nose. Now the Spirit breathed the air in from the outside, and Himself from the inside out into the center of the heart: for He dwells not in the outward, but in the Center of Nature, and goes from the inside out of the Godhead into the outside, opening an image according to Himself—understand this as being according to the Center of Nature.

We told you before how the wheel of outward nature winds itself inward as far as the Sun, and onward through the fire into the freedom of **GOD**, wherein it also maintains its existence. And the inner desire of the eternal center penetrates with the Spirit of **GOD** out into the Heart of the Sun <note>original: *Herze Solis*</note>, which is the great life and fire that melts stones and earth, wherein the eternal Tincture <term>Tincture</term> <note>A term from alchemy used here to mean the spiritual essence or "color" that transforms and enlivens base matter into spiritual gold.</note> is recognized

<column-break/>

in the ninth number <note>In Böhme’s mystical numerology, the "ninth number" represents the transition into the divine kingdom or the "Tincture" of light.</note>. Thus you must also understand the breathing-in: the outward governance of the spirit of this world, which reaches as far as the Sun, was breathed into him from the outside as an outward life. And the inward governance from the inward fire in the eighth number was breathed into him from the inside out into the heart: for that was from the eternal fire, which reaches toward the cross into the ninth number according to its own Tincture, which goes toward the Trinity—that is, into eternal freedom. There man became a living soul, with spirit and soul: for the soul originates one degree deeper than the Sun, out of the eternal fire that burns in the eternal will, which will is to birth the Heart of **God** and to exalt the luster of majesty into the wonders.

There the Spirit of **God** awakened the soul and led it from the inside out into the Tincture of the outward spirit, into the heart’s blood, through Himself. That is the soul. It should not turn back into the spirit of this world, into the fire of the "offgrowth" <note>The temporal, corrupted world that "grew out" of the eternal fall.</note>, but into the fire of the Trinity, into the *Holy Ternary* <note>original: *Ternarium Sanctum*</note>.

Now you understand what you are, and what you were before the Fall: for you could rule over the sun and stars; everything was in your power. Fire, air, and water, along with the earth, could not tame you. No outward fire burned you, no water drowned you, no air suffocated you.

**25. Question:** How then is the threefold soul united in and with the body?

**Answer:** Regarding this question, much strife and quarreling has been carried out in the schools <note>Referring to the academic universities and traditional theological institutions of the 17th century.</note> until now; various opinions have also been brought forth, but little underlying truth has been experienced. This is because reason grasps the true quality and nature of neither the body nor the soul, nor does it distinguish between their powers. The soul of man is united with the body just as fire is with wood, or another oily fuel and substance: as the substance is, within which the soul burns and qualifies <term>qualifies</term><note>In Böhme’s vocabulary, "to qualify" means to operate, interact, or take on a specific character or "quality."</note>, so also is the soul’s revelation and character. Just as a fire cannot persist without substance, so too the soul cannot persist without a body. If the soul has no balm, oil, or substance in which it can burn, shine, qualify, and reveal itself, then it consumes itself and becomes, as it were, a gnawing worm that does not die. If it leads its fire-hunger and desire into **God’s** Holy Element, and through the sinking-down of its fire-power reaches the balm and the oil of Divine gentleness and love, then it burns in this Holy Spirit-Water as a flame of the **Lord**; but if the fire-soul grasps an earthly, coarse, unstable, stinking sulfur <note>original: *Sulphur*. In alchemy, sulfur represents the active, combustible principle of the soul’s desire.</note>, then it likewise burns therein and characterizes an earthly life.

Now Adam had all three properties within himself, but with the fire-soul qualifying and burning in the heavenly essence, he had an angelic life; and the property of the dark world, as well as the property of the visible world, were held as if swallowed up in the Light-Principle.

Every essence of the body <note>original: *Corporis*</note> accepted the spirit according to its own property: thus the outer flesh took in the outer air with its stars, for a rational and grow-

<column-break/>

ing life for the revelation of the wonders of **GOD**; and the light-body, or the heavenly essence, took in the breath of light, of the great Divine powers: which breath is called the Holy Spirit.

Thus the light penetrated the darkness, such as the dark fire-breath, and also the outer air-breath in its constellation, and took away the power of all [harsh] properties, so that the anguish of the fire-breath in the inner soul-property—as well as heat and cold, and all other properties of the outer constellation—could not and might not be manifest. The properties of all three worlds in soul and body stood in equal concordance <note>original: *Concordantz*, meaning a state of perfect harmony or balance.</note> and weight: The inner Holy ruled through the outer, as through the external powers of the outer life, the outer constellation, and the four elements. And that was the holy Paradise; thus man stood in Heaven and also in the outer world, and was a lord of all creatures of this world; nothing could have broken him.

For the earth was also like this, until the curse of **GOD**. The holy property of the spiritual world also bloomed through the earth and bore Holy Paradisiacal fruits; these man could eat in such a magical Paradisiacal way, and he required no teeth nor intestines in his body: For just as the light swallows the darkness, and the fire the water, and yet does not become full from it—such a center <note>original: *Centrum*</note> man had in his mouth, after the manner of eternity. And in such a magical way he could also give birth to his like from himself, without the tearing or opening of his body and spirit. Just as **God** gave birth to the outer world and yet did not tear Himself apart, but rather in His desire, as in the "Let there be" Word <note>original: *Verbo Fiat*</note>, grasped the property and made it qualitative, and revealed it out of the "Let there be" Word, and introduced it into a figure according to the eternal spiritual birth: thus man was also such an image and likeness, created according to time and eternity out of time and eternity.
