**26. Question:** But how exactly is the spirit of man understood?

**Answer:** Just as a fire has a substance <note>original: *Wesen*</note>, so too is the flame and the air that rises from the fire. If we place noble balsam upon the fire, it gives off a lovely scent; but if we place a coarse, foul, stinking, and poisonous substance upon the fire, it gives off a dark, stinking smoke and odor that ruins the eyes and affects the nose unpleasantly. Thus, as the soul burns in a substance, a spirit rises out of the soul and out of that substance, in which all the qualities of the soul and the substance are contained. As long as man placed his imagination <note>In Böhme’s thought, "Imagination" is the creative power of the mind to focus on and manifest a specific reality.</note> into the heart of God, and operated within the light of God according to the qualities of humility and gentleness, his soul-spirit was also light, loving, gentle, friendly, and humbly disposed. He possessed the tincture-spirit <term>tincture</term><note>A "tincture" is a vital, transformative essence or spiritual power that gives life and color to a being.</note> of the fire and the tincture-spirit of the water within himself; he loved himself and God in and through himself, and united himself with God, wherein he found his highest clarity, love, joy, and pleasure, as was reported in detail above.

**27. Question:** What then was the actual purpose for which God created man in His image, and what was man to do in this world?

**Answer:** The text of Moses says, firstly, they should bring forth fruit, multiply, and fill the earth. Secondly, they should subject the earth and all its creatures and rule over them. Thirdly, they should eat what God had ordained for them as food.

**28. Question:** Why and in what manner was man to bring forth fruit, become many, and fill the earth?

**Answer:** The purpose for which man was to fill the earth with the image of God was none other than this: because Lucifer and his angels had corrupted their kingdom, and God had separated this visible world out of the wrath <note>original: *Grimm*; refers to the "dark fire" or fierce quality of God's nature that becomes "wrath" when separated from His light.</note> and destruction, He also willed that this world should be filled with a human host as large as the host of fallen angels had been. This was so that they might withstand the wrath of God with humility and gentleness, and prevent Lucifer from re-awakening and igniting the anger of God in the world. However, the manner in which this multiplication and fruit-bearing was to occur in

<column-break/>

the state of perfection has remained very hidden until now. Reason imagined that God had created man in the beginning as a male, and afterwards assigned a woman to this man for such procreation, so that man could not have multiplied otherwise than by mixing with his wife in an animalistic way, casting his seed into the woman through animal members, just as the animalistic man still does in the state of his corruption. Whoever thinks thus knows neither God nor man created in the image of God. Our highly-enlightened author <note>Referring to Jacob Böhme (1575–1624), the German mystic whose works this text summarizes.</note> has opened this otherwise locked gate and excellently demonstrated this high mystery to us.

> I know, he says, that the sophist <note>A term Böhme used for traditional scholars or theologians who rely on logic rather than spiritual revelation.</note> will blame me here and cry out that it is an impossible knowledge, because I was not there and did not see it myself. To him let it be said that in the essence of my soul and body, when I was not yet the "I" but was Adam’s essence, I was indeed there, and I myself squandered my glory in Adam. But because Christ has brought it back to me, I see in the spirit of Christ what I was in Paradise, what I became in sin, and what I shall become again. And no one should cry out that we are ignorant; for although I may not know it, Christ knows it in me, and from this knowledge I shall write.

Adam was a man and also a woman, and yet neither of them, but a virgin, full of chastity, modesty, and purity, as the image of God. He had both tinctures—of fire and light—within himself, in which conjunction his own love stood as the virginal center <note>original: *Centrum*</note>, like the beautiful Paradisiacal rose-garden and garden of pleasure, wherein he loved himself. For we shall be like this in the resurrection of the dead, as Christ tells us in Matthew 13 and 22: that we shall neither marry nor be given in marriage, but are like the angels of God.

Such a man, as Adam was before his Eve, shall rise again and [inhabit] Paradise...

**31. Question:** It is well understood / that man in the state of his perfection had a great power / for procreation : But how was he to rule?

**Answer:** The dominion of man is firstly over himself / and secondly over the creatures outside of himself. No principle surpassed the other / there was an equal Concordance / the Divine light tempered all properties / so that they all stood with one another in a play of love <note>original: "Liebe-Spiel".</note>. In such Concordance man was to constantly maintain the properties of the three principles in himself / and for this man had the power / for he was a part <note>original: "Particular" — an individual expression or piece of the whole.</note> of the Omnipotence of GOD, and of the Essence of all Essences / where all powers gathered themselves through the *Fiat* / and revealed themselves in one image / for this he had the kingdom of holy powers in the light of GOD within himself / to tame all desires, affects, and rising fire-powers.

### Part 3 / Chapter 8

32. **Question:** However, does Holy Scripture not speak of such a dominion, but only of how man should rule over the birds of the heavens and the fish of the sea, which are creatures of this visible world?

**Answer:** Holy Scripture speaks of dominion over the earth in general, but specifically mentions fish and birds because they possess the greatest natural freedom; ruling them requires a magical and spiritual power rather than a merely physical and earthly force. For whoever wishes to command fish and birds must have authority within the vast sea and the open air—to say nothing of the mighty wonders of GOD in the ocean and on the earth, such as the Leviathan <note>A primordial sea monster mentioned in the Old Testament, representing the untamed forces of nature.</note> and Behemoth. 

That man was intended to rule over the invisible worlds—Heaven and Hell—is evident from the fact that Christ, the God-man, and His members <note>The "members" refers to the body of believers or the "limbs" of the spiritual body of Christ.</note> have retaken possession of what Adam lost. This occurred when GOD raised Him from the dead and seated Him at His right hand over all things in heaven, above all principality and power, might and dominion, and every name that is known. (Ephesians 1:20-21; Colossians 1:16; 2:15).

Man, being the noblest spirit and the most excellent being drawn from all three principles <note>In Böhme’s thought, the "Three Principles" are: 1. The dark fire-world (the Father), 2. The light world (the Son), and 3. The outer material world.</note>, held power over all three. He possessed the keys to Hell and Death; he could enter the palace of the "strong armed one" <note>A reference to the devil or the power of death.</note> and take the prey from the roaring lion through the small spring-well of Divine gentleness welling up within him. With his indwelling Light, he could dispel the power of darkness in his kingdom, soothe the ignited anger and wrath of GOD within nature, and rule the entire world in light, love, and gentleness as a sovereign lord.

33. **Question:** What, then, was the food of man?

**Answer:** GOD gave to man every seed-bearing herb and tree-fruit for food. To understand how man’s eating is to be interpreted, we must investigate three things: first, Adam’s hunger; second, the food itself; and third, the manner in which he ate.

Regarding hunger: every life desires the "mother" from which it originated. Thus, hunger is actually nothing other than an outgoing desire from the fire-source <note>original: 'Feuer-Quall' - Böhme uses this to describe the intense, driving energy or 'quality' at the root of existence.</note> toward nourishment and being, according to its kind. When the source-spirits <note>The 'Seven Source-Spirits' (Quell-Geister) are the fundamental qualities or forces that constitute Böhme’s divine and natural architecture.</note> of nature are at work, their working is

<column-break/>

nothing other than an awakened hunger and desire, each following the other until reaching the seventh source-spirit, which satisfies and fulfills them all—each with what it desires. Thus, every hunger is an outward pressure followed by a firm inward pulling. In this way, from two things—namely, the hunger and that which the hunger desires—a "being" or substance is formed.

The first hunger in the Center before the fire is a spiritual hunger; it creates the dark world. The hunger of free desire creates the light world. Both of these are purely Spirit until they pass together through the ignition of the fire; then they "die" to the spirit and become a likeness of the first Spirit—a revelation of the ungraspable Spirit, whom we call GOD in Love and Wrath. The temporal spirit-hunger creates a temporal body, and the eternal spirit-hunger creates an eternal body. These two are within one another, yet neither is the other. The seven forms <note>The seven properties of nature.</note> create a body for themselves according to their hunger from their own self-quality; therefore, everything that the spirit possesses in all its qualities lies within the body.

->*The Signature of All Things*, 4:12, 14.<-

Thus, the inner spirit creates a body, and the body nourishes and increases the spirit. Man possesses such a threefold hunger. The dark fire-soul <term>Fire-soul: The aspect of the human soul that originates in the eternal, "fiery" energy of God’s power.</term> is nothing other than a very rigorous magical hunger-fire, which GOD breathed out from eternal nature. This hunger drives through all six source-spirits toward the seventh, which is its body and substance. Whichever source-spirit holds the upper hand determines the nature of the hunger, and as the hunger is, so is the food. If the six source-spirits are in concordance <note>In a state of harmony or "Symphony."</note>, they are all satisfied by a single food. If the hunger follows the quality of the light-world, then the Holy Element and its fruits are a holy food, and this food strengthens the six source-spirits to live according to the will of GOD. But where the soul possesses a "foreign image" and a false desire for foreign food, it attracts that food through such false desire, and the food begins to qualify <note>To take on or impart a specific quality or nature.</note> in that foreign property, awakening a foreign life—be it earthly and fleshly, or fiery and wrathful.

Now, concerning man’s eating in particular: if Adam had remained in innocence, he would have eaten the fruit of Paradise.

### Part 3 / Chapter 8.

32. **Q.** But does Holy Scripture not speak of such dominion, but only of how man should rule over the birds of the heavens and the fish of the sea, which are creatures of this visible world?

**Ans.** Holy Scripture speaks of dominion in general over the earth, but specifically mentions fish and birds, which otherwise possess the greatest freedom and require a magical and spiritual power rather than a physical and earthly one to be mastered. For whoever wishes to rule fish and birds must have authority in the wide sea and in the open air—to say nothing of the mighty wonders of GOD in the sea and on earth, such as Leviathan and Behemoth <note>Biblical monsters from the Book of Job representing the untamable forces of nature.</note>. But that man was intended to rule over the invisible worlds, Heaven and Hell, is seen from the fact that Christ, the God-Man, and His members <note>Referring to the collective body of believers or the Church.</note> have repossessed what Adam lost, since GOD raised Him from the dead and set Him at His right hand over the things that are in Heaven, above all authority and power, strength and dominion, and above every name that is known.

<margin>Ephesians 1:20-21. Colossians 1:16. chapter 2:15.</margin>
Man, as the noblest spirit and the noblest being from all three principles <note>In Böhme’s system, the "three principles" are the dark fire-world, the light-world, and the visible/outer world.</note>, had the power in all three principles; he had the keys of hell and death; he could step into the palace of the "strong man armed" <note>A reference to the devil or the power of darkness (Luke 11:21).</note> and take the prey from the roaring lion through the little fountain of Divine Gentleness welling up within him. With his indwelling light, he could dispel the power of darkness in his kingdom, soothe the kindled wrath and grimness of GOD in nature, and as a sovereign lord, rule the whole world in light, love, and gentleness.

33. **Q.** But what was man's food?

**Ans.** GOD gave man for food every seed-bearing herb and tree-fruit. How man's eating is to be understood, however, we wish to investigate: first, Adam's hunger; secondly, the food; thirdly, how he ate.

Regarding hunger, every life desires its mother from which it originates; thus hunger is essentially nothing other than an outgoing desire from the fire-source <note>original: "Feuer-Quall." In Böhme's philosophy, this is the driving, agonizing root of existence that seeks satisfaction.</note> toward its nourishment and essence according to its kind. When the source-spirits <note>original: "Quell-Geister." These are the seven fundamental qualities or forces that make up all of creation in Böhme’s cosmology.</note> of nature are at work, their working is

<column-break/>

nothing other than an awakened hunger and desire, one after the other, up to the seventh source-spirit, which satisfies and fills them all, each with what it desires; thus every hunger is pressing outward and then drawing hard into itself. Thus, from two—namely, from the hunger and from that which the hunger desires—a being is formed.

The first hunger in the Center before the fire is a spiritual hunger; it creates the dark world; and the hunger for free delight creates the light-world. These both are only spirit until they pass through the ignition of the fire together; then they die to the spirit and are a likeness of the first spirit—as a revelation of the ungraspable spirit, which is called GOD in love and wrath. The temporal spirit-hunger creates a temporal body, and the eternal spirit-hunger an eternal body; these are both within each other, and neither is the other. The seven forms <note>Another term for the seven source-spirits or properties of nature.</note> make for themselves a body according to their hunger out of their own property; therefore, everything that the spirit has in all its properties lies within the body.

<margin>The Signature of All Things 4:12, 14.</margin>
Thus the inner spirit makes a body, the body nourishes and increases the spirit, and man has such a threefold hunger. The dark fire-soul <note>The core of the human soul which Böhme associates with divine fire; it requires the "light" to become holy.</note> is nothing other than a very rigorous magical hunger-fire, which GOD breathed out from eternal nature. This hunger drives through all six source-spirits to the seventh, as its body and essence: according to whichever source-spirit has the upper hand, so it has a hunger; and as it has a hunger, so it also has a food. If the six source-spirits are in harmony <note>original: "Concordantz."</note>, they are all satisfied by one food. If the hunger is according to the property of the light-world, then the holy element and its fruits are a holy food, and this food strengthens the six source-spirits to live according to the will of GOD. But where the soul has an alien image and a false desire for alien food, it draws the food to itself in such false desire, and the food begins to qualify <note>original: "qualificiren." This means to interact with and take on the specific characteristics or qualities of that thing.</note> in an alien property, and awakens an alien life, whether it be earthly and fleshly, or fiery and grim.

As for man's eating in particular: if Adam had remained in innocence, he would have eaten Paradise-fruit...

# Of the Revelation of GOD in the Creation of Man.

...be born again / so was the fruit of Paradise born out of the <term>Wrath</term> <note>original: "Zorn" – the harsh or fiery quality of nature</note> back into heavenly essence: Or as we see / that a good sweet herb grows out of the bitter earth / which the sun qualifies differently / than the earth has qualified it: So the holy man qualified the fruit of Paradise in his mouth / so that the earthliness was swallowed up / as a nothingness / and did not trouble the man: Or / as we recognize / that the earth will be swallowed up in the end / and no longer be a tangible <term>Body</term> <note>original: "Corpus"</note>.

Thus also was the outward eating of man / he ate the fruit into his mouth / and needed no teeth for it / for there was the separation of power: There were two <term>Centers</term> <note>original: "Centra"</note> of power in Adam’s mouth / each took its own: The earthly was transformed into heavenly quality / just as we recognize / that according to our bodies we shall be transformed and placed into a heavenly body of power: So too was the transformation in the mouth / and the body received the power / for the kingdom of GOD stands in power: So indeed man stood in the kingdom of GOD / for he was immortal / and a child of GOD; But had he been meant to eat into the intestines / and have such a stench in his body / as we have now / then I will ask Reason / whether this is Paradise / and whether GOD's Spirit dwells in that / when GOD's Spirit was supposed to dwell in Adam / as in GOD's creature.

# The IX. Chapter.
## Of the Revelation of GOD in the Completion of Heaven and Earth / as the true Sabbath and the Rest of GOD.

->Text. Gen. 2. V. 1. 2. 3.<-

AND the heavens and the earth were completed, and all the host of them, and GOD completed on the seventh day his work, which he had made, and he rested on the seventh day, from all the work, which he had made, and GOD blessed the seventh day, and hallowed the same, because in it he rested from his works, which GOD had made.

->1. Question.<-
Why does the rest of GOD on the seventh day follow the creation of man on the sixth day?

->Answer.<-
WHEN we speak of the rest of GOD, it is to be understood as nothing other than how God has introduced himself into nature and creature. GOD in himself needs no rest / for he has worked from eternity / and is a pure <note>original: "eitle" – in this context meaning "pure" or "nothing but"</note> active power / therefore the understanding lies hidden here in the word. For Moses says / GOD commanded the seventh day to be for rest; The seventh day was the true Paradise / understand it spiritually / as the <term>Tincture</term> <note>original: "Tinctur" – in Boehme's thought, a spiritual or alchemical essence that "tinges" or transforms matter into a higher state</note> of Divine Power / which is a <term>Temperament</term> <note>original: "Temperament" – a state of perfect balance where no single quality dominates another</note>, which has penetrated through all qualities / and worked in the seventh of all other beings. The Tincture has penetrated through the earth and all elements / and tinged everything; there was Paradise on earth / and in 

<column-break/>

man / for evil was hidden / just as night is hidden in the day.
<margin>The Key, 94. 95.</margin>

->2. Q. Could GOD then not complete his work before the creation of man, and why was Paradise only revealed in this visible world after man's creation?<-

Answer. Before the fall of Lucifer and his angels, this whole world was like an angelic kingdom in its highest perfection, and stood as a lovely Paradise, in the highest balance of qualities, which reached their perfect pleasure in the seventh [day], as in the essence, so that the revelation of GOD in this throne would have been an eternal Sabbath, wherein God's life and essence would have been transfigured and made manifest in the highest name. But when Lucifer placed his <term>Imagination</term> <note>original: "Imagination" – the creative, shaping power of the will</note> into the power of fire, and awakened the fire-source <note>original: "Feuer-Quall"</note> in himself and his kingdom beyond its limit, the speaking Word of GOD became manifest and active throughout this whole kingdom in the distinction of the <term>Source-Spirits</term> <note>original: "Quell-Geister" – the fundamental spiritual forces that "well up" to create reality</note>, which moved out of the balance, and each sought to rule over the other...

# Of the Revelation of GOD on the seventh day.

thoroughly knew the hour of the sixth day, in which the creation was completed, then we would present to you the year and day—understand this as the **Last Day** <note>Also known as the Day of Judgment.</note>—for not a single minute passes beyond it; it has its goal, which stands hidden in the **inner circle** <note>In Böhme’s mysticism, the "inner circle" refers to the eternal, spiritual realm that governs the "outer circle" of physical time.</note>. Therefore, know for certain that the time is near; for in the sixth day, after midday, the fires of the eternal day began, and GOD therefore established the Sabbath of the seventh day as a rest and an everlasting memorial. And just as on the sixth day the rest began toward evening, so did the entrance into the revelation of the work of creation, where the end has again taken up the beginning; and thus the six days have stood in a circle as a wonder. Know this also: you were created into Paradise, but you have entered out of it into the **spirit of wrath** <note>original: *Geist der Grimmigkeit*. For Paradise has been reborn; speaking here in the manner of reason and not [merely] in GOD: but you do not escape mortality, nor the wrath in the flesh, but in the mind and in the soul Paradise now stands open to the children of GOD, and they have the true taste of the Power. And no cunning nor power may hold this back; no cunning may dampen it, and no devil break it; for the end has found the beginning; there is no stopping it, the power and falsehood break apart, and there is now only a waiting for the **Bridegroom** <note>A traditional Christian metaphor for Christ returning to his people.</note>, for the children of GOD shall be found in Paradise when the **Turba** <note>original Latin: *Turba*. # Of the Revelation of GOD on the Seventh Day.

DDD 3

If we thoroughly knew the hour of the sixth day in which the **Creation** was completed, then we would wish to present to you the year and day—understand, of the Last Day <note>The Day of Judgment or the end of the current world cycle.</note>; for not a single minute passes beyond it; it has its goal, which stands hidden in the inner circle. Therefore, know for certain that the time is near; for in the afternoon of the sixth day, the fires of the eternal day began, and **GOD** therefore established the Sabbath of the seventh day as a rest and an everlasting memorial. And just as rest began toward the evening of the sixth day, along with the entrance of the revelation of the work of creation—where the end again took up the beginning, and thus the six days stood in a circle as a wonder—so you must know this: you were created for Paradise, but you entered out of it into the spirit of wrath <note>German: *Grimmigkeit*; the quality of harshness or fire in Böhme’s system.</note>, into death, which has now worked its wonders in you for five and a half thousand years <note>original: *sechste-halb Tausend Jahr*; an archaic way of saying 5,500 years.</note>.

Now the end has found the beginning again, and you shall see, also feel and find, what Paradise once was—all those who are born in **GOD**. For Paradise has been reborn; speaking here in the manner of reason and not in **GOD** <note>Böhme distinguishes between human logical reasoning and divine understanding.</note>. But you do not escape mortality, nor the wrath in the flesh; however, in the mind and in the soul, Paradise now stands open to the children of **GOD**, and they have the true taste of its power. And no cunning or might can stop this; no cunning can dampen it, and no devil can break it. There is no stopping it; power and falsehood are breaking, and now there is only a waiting for the Bridegroom, for the children of **GOD** shall be found in Paradise when the Turba <note>The *Turba* is a technical term in Böhme's work referring to the "disturber" or the spirit of confusion and divine wrath that destroys things that are out of harmony.</note> is swallowed up in wrath; we speak dearly of what we recognize and know for certain in the wonder.

For the six spirits must pour out their influence, whatever is in their seals, and they are not recognized before they have poured out the vials of their power in the Principle <note>original: *Principio*; one of the three fundamental realms of reality (darkness, light, or the physical world).</note> of this world, which brings humans and creatures to their essence and work, like a building for **GOD'S** eternal act of wonder. And when this is completed, the hidden spirits of **GOD** under the seals go back into the Ether <note>original: *Æther*; the subtle, spiritual substance of the heavens.</note>, as into their center, and then the time of the seventh seal begins, in the presence of **GOD**, and the mystery of the Kingdom of **GOD** is completed, as the Revelation of Jesus Christ testifies, and as we have recognized in the Holy Ternary <note>original: *Ternario Sancto*; the three-fold manifestation of God.</note>.

Remember the Sabbath day, that you keep it holy, etc. For in six days the **LORD** made heaven and earth, and the sea, and all that is in them, and rested on the seventh day.

Dear **GOD**! this commandment reminds me of my inward, true, divine rest in your love and power: that my will should rest in you from its own gratification of self-will; and you, eternal **GOD**, would work with your power in my will. You are the true Sabbath, in which all my powers should work in an eternal rest, and be and remain holy in you.

O alas! it was Paradise, into which you placed our first parents, so that they should hallow your Sabbath as your indwelling, active power—that is: to love rightly, and to let no strange lust of false desire...

# Chapter X.
## Concerning Paradise, or the Revelation of GOD in Man in the State of His Perfection.

1. Question.
-> What does the blessed author actually call Paradise? <-

Answer.
That state of perfection where all the six Source-Spirits <note>In the author's mystical system, these are the seven foundational qualities or "fountains" of nature—such as desire, mobility, and perception—through which God manifests his power.</note> of the active Word of GOD have reached their fulfillment, rest, and complete satisfaction in the seventh; working in perfect temperature <note>meaning a balanced, harmonious mixture of qualities</note> and union for total delight. It is, therefore, nothing other than a perfect revelation of the Triune GOD within the creature, and especially within man, in which all three Principles <note>The three "Principles" refer to the dark fire-world, the light-world of love, and the external physical world.</note> and their properties interact in the highest harmony and glorify God within man. Thus, the Greek word <term>Paradise</term> <note>original: *παράδεισος*</note> according to its true meaning signifies such a revelation, demonstration, transfiguration, and confirmation. Our blessed author has discovered the true significance of this word better than the great masters who boast and brag so much of the original languages, even though all their science is based on nothing but vain word-books and uncertain lexicons.

2. Question. How may a person arrive at a thorough knowledge of Paradise?

Answer. No goods nor money, neither art nor power, will bring you to the eternal rest of the eternal gentleness of Paradise. Only the noble knowledge—into which you can wrap your soul—is the pearl that no moth eats and no thief steals; therefore seek that, and you will find a noble treasure. Our knowledge and wisdom have slipped away from us so harshly that we no longer have any knowledge of Paradise, unless we be born anew through water and the Holy Spirit. Otherwise, the veil of Moses always lies before our eyes when we read his writings, and we imagine that the Garden of Eden was Paradise, of which Moses says: God placed Adam in the

<column-break/>

Garden of Eden, which he had planted, so that he might cultivate it. My dear person, that was not Paradise, and Moses does not say so either; rather, it was the Garden in Eden where they were tempted. Paradise is the divine delight, which was within their own mind while they were in God’s love. Paradise has a different Principle, for it is the divine and angelic delight; but it is not outside the location <note>original: *Loco*</note> of this world. Yet the spirit of this world cannot grasp it at all, much less any creature of it, for it does not stand in the anxious birth <note>a reference to the restless, struggling cycle of material existence</note>. Even though it received its origin there, it stands in pure perfection, in pure love, joy, and delight, where there is no fear, nor death, nor torment; no devil can touch it, no animal reaches it.

However, when we wish to speak of the source and joy of Paradise, and of its highest essence and what that may be, we have no likeness in this world. We would need the tongues of angels for that, and angelic knowledge; and even if we had them, we could not speak of it with these tongues. In the mind, when the soul travels upon the Paradisiacal bridal-chariot, it is well understood, but with the tongue we cannot exalt it. Nevertheless, we will not throw away the A-B-C’s, and will speak with the children for a while, until another mouth is given to us to speak.

When GOD had created the animals, he brought them to Adam so that he might give them names, to each according to its essence and the way it was constituted. Now Adam was in the Garden of Eden in Hebron <note>Hebron is often cited in mystical traditions as the geographic center of the earthly world and the site of Adam's creation or burial.</note> and also at the same time in Paradise. But no animal can go into Paradise, for it is the divine and angelic delight, wherein nothing un-

The Garden of Eden was a place on earth where man was tested, but Paradise was in Heaven, and yet it was also within the Garden of Eden. But in Paradise, the essence of the Divine world permeated the essence of time, just as the sun’s power permeates a fruit on a tree and qualifies it into a sweetness, so that it is lovely to look at and good to eat: This is how we are likewise to understand the Garden in Eden.

All the high schools <note>A term for universities or academic theological faculties.</note> wrangle over this and do not understand it; for they wish to seek and grasp the internal within the external, and thus it remains silent before them. Man was created out of all three <term>Principles: in Böhme's philosophy, these are the three realms of existence—the dark fire-world (source of power), the light-world (divine love), and the outer world (nature/matter).</term> according to both body and soul, and was set within the properties of the internal and external worlds in equal number, measure, and weight. No principle outweighed the other; there was a perfect concordance <note>original: "Concordantz"</note>. The Divine tempered all properties so that they all stood together in a play of love. The fiery, dark world rejoiced in the holy Light-world, and the Light-world rejoiced in the outer world as its own revelation. In return, the outer world rejoiced in both internal worlds as its own life, and between them there was nothing but pure goodwill and pleasant taste. **Mercury** <term>Mercurius: here referring to the active, vibrating life-force or the "voice" of the divine in nature</term>, as the sounding, hearing, and feeling life, as the revelation of the Divine Word in the **Fiat** <note>The creative command "Let there be."</note>, was in a state of entirely joy-filled property, penetrating all essence. The property or essence of all three worlds reached with desire toward the Light, and in the Light, the spoken Word was holy. This same Holiness gave its power to the sound of the internal, dark fire-world, as well as to the sound of the outer elemental world—acting as the internal fiery word or life, and also as the outer earthly life. Thus, the Holy Divine Word governed through all three principles of human property; there was an equal concordance, and no enmity or resistance was manifest between the principles. Instead, there was only goodwill, pleasant tasting, pleasant hearing, pleasant smelling, friendly and lovely seeing, and soft feeling and well-doing. For man was captured on the sixth day in the sixth revelation of the seven properties of Divine revelation in

<column-break/>

[page-num 722]

-># Concerning Paradise.<-

the spoken power (which had led itself forth and revealed itself through the fifth property—the fiery desire of love). He was created as a Divine likeness and image. The center of his true life was the fifth property of eternal nature: the fiery desire of love, which held the fire and the darkness hidden within itself and used them for the fullness of joy.

<margin>Great Mystery <note>original: "Myst. Mag." referring to Böhme’s work *Mysterium Magnum*</note> 17. 10. 21.</margin> From this we see clearly that as the hunger was, so it awakened in the tree such a *qualification* <note>The way a thing functions or its internal character.</note>, and according to such a qualification, the fruit grew for him. As long as man placed his will neither into the wrath nor into the third principle (to live or function therein), but rather his inclination was in the Heart of GOD, he ate of the Word of the Lord <note>original: "Verbo Domini"</note> in all the fruits of this world. Particularly, the fruits of the inner element grew for him on the Tree of Life. But as soon as he placed his **imagination** and will into the third principle, he awakened the fruits of this world, and the Tree of Knowledge became manifest, functioning according to the manner of this world, in Good and Evil.

To properly distinguish this tree and its fruits, we must see, first, what the author understands by it. Secondly, how this tree grew in Adam’s garden. Thirdly, the tree’s qualification for temptation. Just as the Tree of Life is understood to be the *new creature* <note>The spiritually reborn person.</note>, which functions entirely according to the property of the Light-world in the highest **Temperature** <term>Temperature: a state of perfect balance where no single quality dominates others</term> of the source-spirits; so by the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil is understood that creature according to the property of this visible world, where the source-spirits have departed from the Temperature and stand in "partedness," in conflict and wrestling—functioning as *evil* according to the dark-world’s property, and as *good* according to the light-world’s property. This tree grew from the earth and certainly possessed the nature of the earth, just as all earthly trees do today; it was no different, neither better nor worse. Within it stood fragility, just as the earth—as the mother—is fragile and will eventually pass away. All other trees in the garden bore Paradisiacal fruits; but this tree alone, among all the trees that stood in the Garden of Eden, bore earthly fruit, in which there was fragility, **putrefaction** <note>Rotting or decay.</note>, and corruption.

Although it is perhaps not good for us that we must know the severe, earnest, and most original birth (into which knowledge and recognition, as well as feeling and tangibility, our first parents brought us through the Devil’s infection and deceit): yet this knowledge is now highly necessary for us, so that we may learn to know the Devil, who lives in the most severe birth, and our own enemy, whom our first parents awakened and bequeathed to us, whom we carry within us, and who we now are ourselves.

Although I now write as if it takes a beginning in the eternal birth, it is not so; rather, the eternal Nature gives birth to itself without beginning. My writing should not be understood as creaturely <note>That is, referring to finite, created beings limited by time.</note>, like the birth of a human (who is the **likeness of GOD**): although it is indeed so in the eternal Essence, but without beginning or end. And my writing arrives only at the end that a person should learn to know themselves, what they are, what they were in the beginning—what a magnificent, holy, and eternal person who would never have known the gate of the severe birth in eternity if they had not let themselves lust after it through the Devil's infection, and had not eaten of that same fruit of which they should not. Thereby they became such a naked and bare human with a beast's form, and lost the heavenly garment of divine power, and now live in the infected **Salniter** <term>Salniter: a term Böhme uses to describe the "divine saltpeter," the fundamental, explosive, and creative "sap" of nature. Here it refers to the corrupted state of this vital force.</term> in the Devil's kingdom, and eat of infected food. It is now necessary for us that we learn to know ourselves, what we are, and how we might be redeemed from the earnest and severe birth, and be born anew

to live as a new human, who is similar to the first man before the Fall, in **Christ** our Re-generator. For if I speak and write for a long time about our first Fall, and then also about the rebirth in Christ, and do not come to the purpose and ground of what the Fall was, and with what we have been corrupted, what the power is for which GOD has a loathing, and how that happened against GOD’S prohibition and will: what do I understand of it? Nothing. How then shall I flee from that which I do not know? Or how shall I prepare myself for the new birth and surrender myself to it, if I do not know how, or where, or with what? Yet the world is filled with books and speeches about the Fall and the new rebirth. But in the books of the theologians, for the most part, only the history <note>original: "Historia"</note> is described—that it happened once, and that we should be born anew in Christ. Our theologians resist with hands and feet, yes, with their whole capacity, with persecution and reviling, [insisting] that one should not search into the deep ground of what GOD is, one should not brood and search into the Godhead—to speak plainly <note>original: "deutsch davon reden", literally 'to speak German,' an idiom meaning to speak bluntly or clearly.</note>—but what is it? It is dung and filth that they hide the Devil, and cover up the infected malice of the Devil in man, so that one knows neither the Devil, nor the wrath of GOD, nor the unruly, evil beast <note>original: "Bestia"</note> within man. But where is it more necessary for him to defend than at the gap where the enemy might break in? He covers the hearts, senses, and minds of the theologians, leads them into greed, pride, and unchastity, so that they themselves are terrified of the light of GOD, fear it, and...

To recognize the true foundation of the Fall, it is necessary for us to investigate: first, man's temptation to fall; and second, the Fall itself. To know the temptation well, we must research: first, who it was that was tempted. Second, how the temptation arose within the human being. Third, what the temptation actually consisted of. Fourth, how the human being behaved during the temptation.

First, the one who was tempted is Adam, the first man. This man was created in the place of the cast-out Lucifer—understand this as the inner spiritual man. He was created in the same Heaven according to the inner soul-man, and was intended to possess the *hierarchy* <note>original: "Hierarchiam"; referring to the rank or spiritual order of angels</note> which Lucifer had lost; from this

the Devil's envy against man arose. But because **GOD** well recognized that the Devil would attack him and begrudge him such honors, the deepest love of **GOD** (as the high name **JESUS** out of **Jehovah** <note>In Böhme’s theology, the name "Jesus" is seen as the "sweetened" or love-centered manifestation of the sterner name "Jehovah."</note>) consented to this: to give birth anew to this *hierarchy* which Lucifer had defiled, to purge it through fire, and to lead His highest love into it; and to overcome the wrath <note>original: "Grimm"; the fierce, dark quality of nature</note> that Lucifer had awakened with love, and to *transmute* <note>original: "transmutiren"</note> it into Divine joy, as if back into a holy heaven, in which place the Last Judgment stands. And it is here that *St. Paul* says: **Man was chosen in Christ JESUS before the foundation of the world was laid.** And to that end, **GOD** created man out of three *principles* <note>Böhme’s "three principles" are: 1. The dark fire-world (the Father), 2. The light world (the Son), and 3. The external world (Nature/Earth).</note> into one, so that he did not live entirely in the *place* of Lucifer, so that He might help him. For **GOD** saw very well, according to the property of His wrath, that man would fall; so He wanted to lead him back into the Royal Kingdom from which Lucifer had fallen, through and in the name of **JESUS**, by way of the death of fragility. In this place, the Man Christ—**GOD** and man in one person, as a *hierarch* and High Priest or Grand Prince of men—was to sit in the name and power of **JESUS**, out of **Jehovah**.

Therefore, we must here rightly consider the Fall of man: how he stood in the Paradise of **GOD** and was tempted, and what Paradise was. Man stood in three *principles*, which indeed stood in equal *concordance* <note>original: "Concordantz"; a state of perfect harmony or agreement</note> within the man himself, such as in body and soul, but not outside of him. For the dark world has a different desire than the light world, and the outer world also has a different desire than the dark and light worlds. Thus the image of **GOD** stood between three *principles*, all three of which directed their desire toward this image: each one wanted to be manifest in Adam and to have him as the ruler in its dominion.

8. Question: But how did the desire for separateness <note>original: "Schiedlichkeit," meaning the state of being divided or diverse</note> arise in man, since he was created in such harmony and equality?

Answer: The first beginning—or as the <term>theologians</term> call it, the <term>initial impulses</term> <note>original: "Motus primo primi"</note>—as the first lust and desire for sin, takes its origin from the fall of Lucifer, who ignited his kingdom with **GOD'S** wrath and infected the <term>salitter</term> <note>Böhme's term for the divine "sap" or fundamental substance of a realm</note> of the earth with fierce envy. For Prince Lucifer sat, before the time of the created earth, in the heavenly <term>essence</term> <note>original: "Ente"</note>, in the angelic world, in the place <note>original: "Loco"</note> of this world, wherein the essence of the earth was seized in the "Let there be" <note>original: "Fiat"</note> and led into a compaction. His false imagination made the <term>clay</term> <note>original: "Limum," referring to the "dust of the ground" from Genesis</note> sickly before the compaction; it was the place of his hierarchies. Now, the outer body of man was seized from the clay of the earth in the Word of the "Let there be," and formed according to the property of human life, which was in the Word. The Word formed the essence or clay from the earth, according to the shape of the human soul-life that was in the Word, through the "Let there be." And because **GOD** had, through His Word, appointed Himself as judge over the false sickness and desire of the devil, to judge him and his ignited being, the sword of judgment was already in the clay of the earth from which Adam was made.

For when **GOD** created the earth, He established its time, when He intended to hold judgment and separate the Evil from the Good, and to give the Evil to the apostate prince as a dwelling. But because the Good in the enclosed earth was without heavenly creatures (since its prince had been cast out), **GOD** created Adam as another <term>hierarch</term> <note>a spiritual ruler or governor</note> from this good essence to be the ruler of this place; and from this came the devil’s envy against man and all good creatures of this world.

# Of Paradise.

A saying of Paul: **GOD** recognized that this essence <term>Ens: a philosophical term for "being" or "spiritual substance"</term>, from which Adam was to be created, was already somewhat prone to sickness from the desire introduced by the Devil. Therefore, **GOD** foresaw this clay <term>Limum: the "dust of the ground" or slime from which man was formed</term> in Christ **JESUS** before the foundation of the world, from which He wished to make man, so that He would lead him through the judgment of the fiery sword, through death, and through fire, and entirely burn away the false sickness; and in His highest love, in His Word, in **Jehovah**—that is, revealed out of **Jehovah**—birth him anew in **JESUS**, introducing a new essence <note>original: "Ens"</note> into the sickly one, and together lead them through the judgment of the fiery sword and prove them entirely pure. And here also stands Christ’s descent into Hell, where the love of **GOD** in Christ entered into this fiery sword and transformed the wrath into love; He also broke the sting of death which was within the clay of the earth, from which Adam was created according to his outer humanity. And in the corruption of **Lucifer**, this fiery sword has its awakened original source <note>original: "Urstand"</note>.

For although Adam was created in one part from heavenly essence—which was attached to the Word of human life that was breathed into his outer and inner clay—nevertheless, this fiery sword lay like a smoldering decay <note>original: "Moder"</note> in secret within the earthly clay of the outer body. This sword also pressured Adam, so that he lusted against **GOD’S** commandment and the Kingdom of Heaven; in which decay the Devil also introduced his desire into him and incited him to apostasy. Because **GOD** well recognized that the poor human being would not be able to endure, He ordained for him a helper in Christ, who should lead him, into whose holy essence he should be introduced as into the true Sabbath and eternal rest. Adam was indeed placed in equal harmony <note>original: "Concordantz"</note>, entirely perfect, and introduced into Paradise, provided that the soul might have been able to overcome the decay. And therefore the Tree of Temptation was set before him, to see if it were possible that

<column-break/>

the soul could overcome this sickness and remain entirely in equality. And as it now stood firm in Christ, the newly introduced heavenly essence broke the sword in the death of Christ’s outer body, and led the outer body—which He had taken on in Mary from her seed—through this sword of the wrath of **GOD** into the holy essence; and in that same power, the outer body rose from death and triumphed over death and this fiery sword. He took the fiery sword into His power, with which He will sweep His threshing floor <note>A biblical metaphor for the final judgment</note> at the end of the world as a judge over devils and men, as well as the earth. For the fiery sword was the central issue, because King **Lucifer** had transformed it for himself from the bright light into fire, wanting to rule with it as a god. But **GOD** sent him another Prince and King who took it from him and thrust him away from this throne; and He was to transform this sword in the essence of the earth back into Divine property and cast out and judge the Devil with this sword. And it is not such a simple thing as people have understood the fiery sword to be until now; although it has been hidden by **GOD’S** counsel, we should now lift up our eyes and consider what it means for such a thing to become revealed—that the judgment itself indicates this sword, and that He is coming who carries it in His mouth. It is also a messenger that **Babel** <note>In this context, Babel refers to the "confused" or false institutional church</note> shall take its end through this sword and be given to the sword to be devoured.

8. **Question:** But how did the desire for multiplicity <note>original: "Schiedlichkeit" — the state of being divided or distinguished from the whole</note> arise in man, since he was created in such concord and equality?

**Answer:** The first beginning—or as the theologians call it, the <term>Motus primo primi: the very first impulses of the mind</term>—namely, the first lust and desire for sin, takes its origin from the fall of Lucifer, who ignited his kingdom with **GOD’S** wrath and infected the <term>Salitter: a Böhmean term for the "divine saltpeter" or the fundamental substance of the world</term> of the earth with fierce envy. For Prince Lucifer, before the time the earth was created, sat in the heavenly <term>Ente: being or essence</term>, in the angelic world, in the very place of this world where the <term>Ens: spiritual substance</term> of the earth was seized by the <term>Fiat: the "Let it be" or creative word</term> and led into compaction. His false imagination made the <term>Limum: clay or slime</term> sickly before it was even compacted; it was the location of his hierarchies. Now, the outer body of man was seized from the <term>Limo</term> of the earth by the Word <term>Fiat</term> and formed according to the property of human life which was in the Word. The Word formed the <term>Ens</term> or <term>Limum</term> out of the earth according to the shape of the human soul-life that was in the Word, through the <term>Fiat</term>. And because **GOD** had set Himself as Judge through His Word over the false sickness and desire of the Devil—to judge him and his ignited being—the Sword of Judgment was already in the <term>Limo</term> of the earth from which Adam was made.

For when **GOD** created the earth, He established its time for when He wished to hold judgment and separate the Evil from the Good, and give the Evil to the apostate Prince as a dwelling. But because the Good was in the locked earth without heavenly creatures (since its Prince had been cast out), **GOD** created Adam as another Hierarch <note>A sacred ruler or governor</note> from this good <term>Ente</term> to be the ruler of this place; and from this came the Devil’s envy against man and all the good creatures of this world.

# Of Paradise.

A saying of Paul: **GOD** recognized that this **essence** <note>original: "Ens" — a philosophical term for the fundamental "being" or "stuff" of a thing</note> out of which Adam was to be created was already somewhat prone to falsity because of the desire introduced by the Devil. Therefore, **GOD** foresaw this **clay** <note>original: "Limum" — Latin for the mud or slime from which Adam was formed in Genesis 2:7</note> in **Jesus CHRIST** before the foundation of the world, out of which He wanted to make man; He intended to lead him through the judgment of the **fiery sword**, through death and through fire, and to entirely burn away the false craving. In His highest love, within His Word, within **Jehovah**—that is, revealed out of **Jehovah**—He intended to give him a new birth in **JESUS**. He would introduce a new **clay** [original: *Limum*] into the craving one, lead them together through the judgment of the **fiery sword**, and prove them entirely pure. And here also stands **Christ’s** descent into Hell, where the love of **GOD** in **Christ** entered into this fiery sword and transformed the wrath into love; He also broke the sting of death which was within the **clay** [original: *Limo*] of the earth, from which Adam was created according to his outward humanity. And in the corruption of **Lucifer**, this fiery sword has its awakened origin.

For although Adam was created in part from heavenly essence <note>original: "Wesenheit"</note>, which was attached to the Word of human life that was breathed into his outward and inward **clay** [original: *Limum*], yet this **fiery sword** lay like a smoldering decay <note>original: "Moder" — can refer to mold, rot, or the smoldering embers of a fire</note> in secret within the earthly **clay** [original: *Limo*] of the outward body. This also pressured Adam so that he lusted against **God’s** commandment and the kingdom of heaven; into this decay, the Devil also introduced his desire and enticed him to apostasy. Because **God** recognized this well—that the poor human being would not be able to stand—He ordained a helper for him in **Christ**, who was to lead him, and into whose holy essence he was to be led as into the true Sabbath and eternal rest. Adam was indeed placed in equal **concordance** <note>original: "Concordantz" — a state of perfect harmony between conflicting spiritual properties</note>, entirely perfect, and introduced into Paradise, provided the soul could have overcome the decay. ### Part 3 / Chapter 10.

Earth? <note>This continues a rhetorical question about whether God created evil before the world began.</note> Yes, dear Reason; here you have hit upon it. The Word was an echoing-out from the spiritual Fire-world and Light-world. According to the Fire, God calls Himself a strong, jealous, and angry God; and according to the Light, He calls Himself a merciful, dear God. Now, if God had abolished the first **principle** <note>original: "Principium"</note>—the "fire-source" within the essence of the Earth from which it was created—where would the Light get its power? Especially the ignited **essence** <note>original: "Ens"</note> within the solidification? Only God’s love could do it.

Now, how can a creature, such as a "fire-soul" or an angel, enter into a created form if the fire-source were not specifically mobile? For "sameness" would only remain within sameness. # Of Paradise.

<margin>Ggg</margin>

<meta>Catchword: He</meta>

...was created. And because he was an extract <note>original: *Auszug* — an epitome or summary of all things</note> from the eternal mind, from all the essences of all three principles; therefore he had to be tested, to see if he could persist in Paradise. For the heart of **GOD** willed that he should remain in Paradise. Now, he could not remain in Paradise unless he ate Paradisiacal fruit, and thus his heart should have been entirely inclined toward **GOD**. In this way, he would have lived in the Divine Center, and **GOD** would have worked within him. Now, who then was against him, or who drew him from Paradise into disobedience, so that he entered into another image?

See, you child of man: there was a threefold struggle in Adam; outside of Adam, and in everything that Adam looked upon. You ask: What was it? It was the three *Principles* <note>The author's term for the three fundamental layers of reality: 1. The dark "fire-world" or wrath, 2. The light "love-world" or Paradise, and 3. The physical "outer-world" of the elements</note>: the Kingdom of Hell, as the power of fierceness <note>original: *Grimmigkeit* — a term used to describe the harsh, stern, or wrathful quality of the first principle</note> for one; and then the kingdom of this world, as the stars and elements, for the second; and thirdly, the Kingdom of Paradise, which also wanted to have him.

Now the three kingdoms were within Adam and also outside of Adam, and there was a mighty struggle within the essences. Everything pulled at Adam, both within and without, and wanted to possess Adam, for he was a great Lord, taken from all the powers of nature. The heart of **GOD** wanted to have him in Paradise and dwell in him. For it said: "He is my image and likeness." And the Kingdom of Fierceness wanted to have him too, for it said: "He is mine and has come out of my fountain, out of the eternal mind of darkness; I will be in him, and he shall live in my power, for he is born out of me; I will demonstrate strong and great power through him." And the kingdom of this world said: "He is mine, for he carries my image and lives in me, and I in him. He must be obedient to me; I will restrain and tame him. I have all my members in him, and he in me. I am greater than he. He shall be my steward; I will demonstrate my beauty, wonders, and power in him; he shall reveal my power and wonders; he

<column-break/>

shall guard and tend my flock. I will clothe him with my beautiful glory," as is now clearly evident before our eyes. But when the Kingdom of Fierceness, of wrath, death, and hell, saw this—that it had lost and could not maintain the man—it said: "I am Death <note>original: *Mors*</note>, and a worm, and my power is in him, and I will break him and crush him, and his spirit must live in me. And though you, World, think he is yours because he carries your image, yet his spirit is mine, born out of my kingdom; therefore take from him what is yours, but I shall keep my own."

Now, what did the power in Adam do regarding this struggle? It flattered <note>original: *heuchelte* — played the hypocrite or compromised</note> all three. To the heart of **GOD** it said: "I will remain in Paradise, and you shall dwell in me. I will be yours, for you are my Creator and have thus extracted and created me from all three principles; your delight is lovely, and you are my bridegroom; from your fullness I have received, therefore I am pregnant and will give birth to a virgin <note>This refers to the "Heavenly Sophia" or the spiritual humanity that the author believes Adam was meant to generate</note> so that my kingdom may become great and you may have pure joy in me; I will eat of your growth, and my spirit shall eat of your power, and your name within me shall be called *Emmanuel* <note>original: *Emmanuel* — Hebrew for "God with us"</note>, **GOD** with us." And when the spirit of this world perceived this, it said: "Why will you alone eat of that which you cannot grasp, and drink of that which you cannot feel? You are not merely a spirit; you have every kind of tangibility from me upon you. See, the tangible fruit is sweet and good, and the tangible drink is mighty and strong. Eat and drink in me, and you will obtain all my power and beauty; you can be mighty in me over all creatures; the kingdom of this world will become your property, and you will be a lord on earth." And the power in Adam said: "I am on earth and dwell in the world, and the world is mine; I will use it according to my desire."

### 3rd Part / Chapter 10.

11. **Qu.** The question is: was it then not the absolute will of **GOD** that Adam had to be tempted and fall?

**Ans.** It is highly recognizable to us what **GOD** and Nature are, as well as the Ground and the Unground <note>original: *Grund und Ungrund* — Böhme’s terms for the foundation of existence and the "abyss" or "groundless" void preceding it</note>, and also the depth of eternity. We thus recognize that the eternal fire is magical, and is born in the desiring will, as has been explained in the second or third part of these books. Now, if the eternal "Ungroundable" is magical, then that which is born from the Eternal is also magical; for all things have come into being out of desire. Heaven and earth are magical, as is the mind with its senses, if we would only know ourselves.

What then can this light be, which catches and swallows the fire, when the thing caught by the fire is also magical? If it then has a life and the power and understanding of the light, why does it then run into the fire? Was not the Devil an angel, and Adam an image of **GOD**? They both had the fire and the light, and additionally, Divine knowledge within them. Why did the Devil imagine <note>original: *imaginirte* — to direct the creative power of the mind or will toward a specific goal</note> into the fire, and Adam toward the earth, when they were both free? The light and power of **GOD** did not pull the Devil into the fire, but rather the fierceness <note>original: *Grimm* — the harsh, wrathful quality of the first principle of nature</note> of nature did. Why did the spirit consent? Whatever their *Magic* <note>original: *Magia* — Böhme uses this to describe the process of the will becoming a tangible reality or "essence"</note> made for them, that is what they had: the Devil made hell for himself, and he had it; Adam made himself earthly, and that is what he is. For **GOD** is not a creature, nor a maker, but a spirit and an opener. When the creation occurred, we are to contemplate and recognize it thus: the fire and light awakened together in delight, and desired a mirror or image according to eternity. Thus we know in true recognition that the fierceness, as the nature of the fire, is not a maker; it has made nothing out of itself that would be essential, for that cannot be; rather, it has made spirit and torment. But no creature stands merely in the *Essence* alone. If a

<column-break/>

creature is to exist, it must be made of substance <note>original: *Wesen* — being, substance, or reality</note>, as if out of power or *Sulphur* <term>Sulphur: Böhme uses this alchemical term to represent the "burning" or "desiring" power of life</term>. It must consist of a spiritual *Salt* <term>Sal: Salt represents the "compacting" or "shaping" principle that gives a spirit form</term>, so that out of the fire-torment a *Mercury* <term>Mercurius: Mercury represents the "movement" or "living spirit" that acts as a bridge between fire and light</term> and a truly essential life is formed; additionally, it must have brilliance if understanding or recognition is to be within it.

Thus we know that every creature stands in the spiritual *Sulphur*, *Mercury*, and *Salt*, and yet the spirit does not do it alone; there must be *Sulphur* in which the *Fiat* <note>original: *Fiat* — the Latin command "Let there be," referring here to the creative word of God that pulls spirit into form</note> stands, as the harsh *Matrix* <note>original: *Matrix* — the "womb" or origin-point of nature</note> to the *Center of Nature*, in which the spirit is preserved. That is, there must be substance; for where there is no substance, there is no creation. While a creaturely spirit is not a tangible substance, it must draw substance into itself through its *Imagination*, otherwise it would not persist. Since the Devil then drew fierceness into his spirit, and man drew earthliness, how could the love of the essence of **GOD** be to blame? For the love and gentleness of **GOD** were offered to the Devil as well as to man. Who will accuse **GOD**? If the fierce *Essence* in the Devil was too strong, so that it overcame the love-*Essence*, how is **GOD** responsible for that? If a good branch is planted but withers, how is the earth responsible? Does it not give it sap and power? Why does the branch not draw it into itself? You might say: its *Essences* are too weak. But how is the earth, or the one who planted the branch, responsible for that? His will is only that he wants to raise a good tree for his pleasure, and wants to enjoy its fruit; had he known the branch would wither, he never would have planted it.

Thus we are to recognize that the angels were created not like someone who plants a good tree, but by the movement of **GOD**, with both *Principles*, such as light and darkness, in which the fire lay hidden. Yet the fire did not burn in the creation and in the movement, just as it still does not burn today; for it has its own principle...

12. **Question:** Did Adam then have free will, so that he could have withstood the temptation if he had wanted to?

**Answer:** Understand it correctly. He led his false desire into Adam, by which Adam's free will in the fiery **Scientz** was infected, just as a poison enters the body and begins to **qualify** <note>original: *qualificiren* — to take on a specific quality or to interact with other forces</note>, from which an initial will toward one's own pleasure arose. Then it was all over for the **Temperature** <note>original: *Temperatur* — the perfect, balanced state where all conflicting qualities of nature are in harmony</note>, for the properties of **Creation**, which all lay in Adam in the **Temperature**, each woke up in its own specificity and pulled the free will into themselves, wanting to be manifested. Also, the **Spirit of the World** <note>original: *Spiritus Mundi*</note> of the external world pulled the **Temperature**—the part of the external world in Adam—into itself, and wanted to rule in Adam; **Likewise**, the realm of **Fantasy** also reached for Adam and wanted to be manifested in the Image of God, as well as the Fierceness of Nature <note>original: *Grimm der Natur*</note>, namely God's wrath in the devil's envy; everything pulled at Adam. 14. **Question:** But because man had a free will, wherefore was the command or prohibition given to him, not to eat of the tree?

**Answer:** Man was created entirely free without any law / except the natural law / that he should not mix one principle into the other / the inner man should let nothing earthly into himself / but should rule freely over the outer principle / so no death nor dying would have come into him / the outer elements could not have touched him / neither heat nor frost would have affected him: For as the noble image must endure in the fire / so also should that same noble image rule through the whole man through all three principles / govern everything / and fill it with the Paradise-source-activity.

<margin>Of the Incarnation p. 3. cap. 6. §. 7.</margin>

to it / and lies in conflict with the other. Now the law follows for it / that it should enter again into that which it was in its original state / and be one / not two; for a thing should lead only one government / and not two: Man was created in the government of love and gentleness / as in God’s being / therein he should remain. But because he has awakened another government in himself / namely the wrath <note>original: *Grimm* — the harsh, fierce, or "dark fire" quality of nature</note> / now he is in conflict / and has laws / that he should kill and leave the wrath / and be in his government again; since both governments have become powerful in him / and the government of wrath has overwhelmed love / he must break apart entirely in his being / and be born anew out of the first root / therefore he has laws in this twofold being / how he should behave / and give birth to a will-spirit for the eternal government.

<margin>Six Points 9. 24. 25.</margin>

15. **Question:** Why did God threaten man with death, if he should eat of the forbidden fruit?

**Answer:** Death is not so much a threatened punishment, as an unavoidable consequence of eating from the Tree of Knowledge; For when Adam ate of it, with his imagination, the source-spirits then immediately went out of the balance <note>original: *Temperatur*</note>, from which the heavenly tincture <term>Tincture: a spiritual life-force or "essence" that permeates and gives divine quality to matter</term> faded, which stood in a fiery love, and the earthly [property] woke up in the outer soul-quality, whereby the heavenly image was darkened, so he died to the Kingdom of God, and woke up in the kingdom of this world, as follows hereafter.

-> ### Part 3 / Chapter 18. <-

Who commanded man to live within laws? It was GOD the Father from His Center <note>original: *Centro*; the source-point of divine manifestation</note>; therefore, it occurred with fire and thunder, for in the Heart of God <note>representing the Son or the Principle of Love</note> there is no fire and thunder, but only gracious love.

Now Reason speaks: Is God the Father not then one single being with the Son? Yes, they are one being and one will. By what means, then, did He give the Law? Through the spirit of the great world <note>the macrocosm or the physical universe</note>, because Adam (after the Fall) and all humanity lived within it. Thus, it was tested whether man could live within it while trusting in GOD. Therefore, He confirmed this with great wonders and gave him clarity—as can be seen in Moses, who possessed a transfigured face. And when He had chosen this people for Himself, He destroyed the children of unbelief and led them out into the wilderness with wonders and deeds; there it was tested whether man could live in perfect obedience under this clarity.

What happened there? Moses was called by GOD from among the children of Israel up to Mount Sinai and remained there for forty days. There, He wished to test this people, to see if it were possible for them to place their trust in GOD, so that they might be fed with heavenly bread and come to perfection. But then the people were tested, for Moses—along with the pillar of cloud and fire—withdrew from them and delayed for forty days. There, the mind of the spirit of the great world <note>original: *Majoris Mundi*</note> stood once more in conflict against the eternal mind of GOD. To this end, the people chose a belly-god <note>a god serving physical appetites</note> for themselves, a golden calf, so that they might live freely without laws. Here you see once again how the three Principles <note>original: *drey Principia*; Böhme’s system of the dark fire-world, the light love-world, and the outward physical world</note> struggled with one another over humanity. The Law that was with Adam in the Garden of Eden broke forth again and demanded obedience; so

the spirit of grimness <note>wrath or severity</note> also broke forth again, with false fruit and lust, seeking the fragile life of the flesh. But when they had fallen from GOD, Moses came with Joshua and saw the apostasy; he broke the tablets into pieces and led them into the wilderness, where they all had to die, except for Joshua and Caleb. For the clarity of the Father in the fire—in the first Principle—could not lead them into the Promised Land; and even though they ate Manna, no amount of testing helped. Only Joshua—and finally JESUS—could accomplish it.

And when the time finally came for the true Hero to return from Paradise and become the Virgin’s Child <note>Christ</note>, the struggle of the three Principles returned once more. There, the struggle lasted again for forty days and forty nights—as long as the struggle with Adam in Paradise had lasted, and not an hour longer—and so the Hero overcame. Therefore, open your eyes wide and look rightly upon the Scripture; though it may be brief and obscure <note>original: *dunckel*; "dark" or hidden</note>, it is nonetheless true. You do not find in the books of Moses that Adam was driven out of Paradise on the first day; the testing of Israel and of Christ proves something very different to us. For the temptation of Christ is exactly parallel to the temptation of Adam in every circumstance. Had he done so, GOD would have given him (to his body) the heavenly Limbo <term>Limbo: a spiritual substance or "divine soil" that provides holy nourishment</term> to eat, so that he might eat with his mouth and not into a digestive body. 18. **Question:** How then did Adam endure in such a powerful trial, and what was Adam’s state of mind during such a temptation?

**Answer:** What Adam’s state of mind was during such a temptation, the author presents in a beautiful parable. Great and powerful are the mysteries, and whoever seeks and finds them has pure joy therein; for they are truly **Heavenly Bread** for the soul. If we remember and receive the knowledge of the **heavenly Tincture** <note>original: *Tinctur*; a spiritual essence or transformative power that "colors" or gives quality to the soul</note>, then the knowledge of the **Joyful Kingdom of God** rises within us, making us wish to be free from vanity and to live in such a birth—which, however, cannot yet be, for we must finish our daily work. **Reason** says: "Oh, if only Adam had not allowed himself to feel such desire, he would not have fallen asleep! If I were in his place, I would stand firm and remain in **Paradise**." Yes, dear Reason, you hit the mark well; you claim much for yourself! I will show you your strength and the gate; only think how firmly you might stand if you were standing before the **Tree of Temptation** as Adam did. See, I give you a fair parable: whether you be a youth or a maiden—since Adam was both in one person—how do you think you would stand? I propose, therefore, a male youth of good **complexion** <note>original: *Complexion*; referring to the balance of the four temperaments/humors</note>, with a beautiful form and virtue: and then

a beautiful, well-formed, modest maiden placed opposite one another. Then command them that neither shall burn with lust or love for the other in any thought, nor allow any personal inclination to escape from them—much less any kind of **infection** <note>original: *Inficirung*; used here to mean the tainting of the pure will with earthly desire</note> of the will. Let them be together for forty days and nights, walking with one another in pure joy. And command them further that their will and mind remain steady, never to grasp a single thought of desiring or "infecting" one another with any **essence** <note>original: *Essentia*</note> or property, but rather that their will and inclination remain so steady and firm in my command. And the youth must be resolved in his will never and eternally to mingle with this or any other maiden, and likewise the maiden on the other hand, etc. How do you think, you miserable Reason, full of lack and infirmity, that you would endure here? Would you not promise as Adam did, yet be able to keep nothing?
Thus, my dear Reason, I have placed a mirror before you; and so it was with Adam. **GOD** had created all His work wisely and well, and drawn one out of the other. The first Ground was **He**, out of which He had created this world, and out of the world, **Man**. To him He gave His Spirit and commanded him to live in Him without wavering or having any other will, entirely and perfectly. Now Man also had the **spirit of the world**, for he was from the world and lived in the world. So Adam was the modest maiden—understand, the Spirit that was breathed into him by **GOD**—and the spirit which he had inherited from nature and the world was the youth. These two were now together and rested in one arm.
