### Part 3 / Chapter 10

...[if I] then lose my companion, whom I had chosen for myself as a bridegroom with whom I wished to have joy, then my pearl and beauty will have no playmate. (Isaiah 5, Matthew 21, of which Isaiah and also Christ speak in parables, saying that he also gladly wished to eat of the noble grapes from the vine, Micah 7, Mark 12.) "I had joined myself to you for the sake of my joy, and you do not wish to enjoy my beauty; stay then in my adornment and virtue, and dwell with me in joys; I will clothe you eternally." And the Youth spoke: "Your jewelry is already mine; I use you according to my will. As you say: 'I shall break,' yet my **worm** <term>Worm: referring to the 'worm that never dies,' the restless, consuming hunger of the soul's dark center when separated from God</term> is eternal; with it I will rule. In you, however, I will dwell and clothe you with my garment." Then the Virgin turned to the Heart of God and spoke: "My Heart and my Love, you are my strength; from you I am bright; from your root I am born from eternity. Deliver me from the worm of darkness that infects and tempts my bridegroom; let me not be darkened in the gloom. Am I not your adornment, come here so that you might have joy in me? Why then should I stand in the dark with my bridegroom?" And the Divine Answer spoke: "The seed of the woman shall tread upon the head of the serpent—the worm—and she shall sting him in the heel." <note>original: "Des Weibes Saamen soll der Schlangen... den Kopff zutreten." This refers to the Protevangelium or 'First Gospel' in Genesis 3:15.</note>

See, dear soul, herein lies the **heavenly tincture** <term>Tincture: a mystical, alchemical term for the spiritual power that transforms and 'colors' the soul with divine light</term>, which we must place in a parable and cannot speak of anywhere with words. Yes, if we had the tongues of angels, we would speak rightly of what the mind perceives; but the pearl is clothed with the dark garment. The Virgin constantly calls to the Heart of God that He might deliver her playmate from the dark worm. But the Divine Answer says: "The seed of the woman shall tread upon the serpent's head," that is, the serpent's darkness shall be separated from your bridegroom.

<column-break/>

"The dark garment with which the serpent has clothed your bridegroom and darkened your pearl and beautiful crown shall break and become earth; and you shall rejoice in me with your bridegroom. That was my eternal will, which must stand." But it was the Virgin's law and will that, just as God rules over all things and imagines Himself into everything and gives power and life to all, yet the thing does not grasp Him even though He is right there—so also should the soul stand still, and the Virgin's form should rule in the soul and crown the soul with the light of God. The soul was meant to be the beautiful Youth who was created, and the power of God was to be the beautiful Virgin and the light of God the beautiful **pearl-crown** <note>The 'pearl' or 'crown' represents the restored image of God within the human soul</note> with which the Virgin wished to adorn the Youth. But the Youth wanted to have the Virgin as his own possession, though she was one degree higher in birth than he, and it could not be. For the Virgin was from eternity, and the bridegroom was given to her so that she might have joy and delight in God with him.

But since the Youth could not obtain this from the Virgin, he reached back toward the worm in his **center** <term>Centro: the 'center' or 'source-wheel' of a being's existence, where its fundamental desires are born</term>. For the form of this world pressed so hard upon him—which was also in the soul—and would have liked to have the Virgin as a possession and to make a "wife" out of her, as indeed happened in the Fall. But not from the pearl, but from the spirit of this world, the "wife" is made. For the nature of this world still constantly agonizes to be rid of vanity <note>original: "Eitelkeit"; in this context, it refers to the temporary, fleeting, and empty nature of the physical world</note> through the Virgin and thinks to **commingle** <note>original: "inqualiren"; a term used by Böhme to describe how different qualities or powers work together or permeate one another</note> with the Virgin. But it cannot be, for the Virgin is higher born. And even when this world eventually breaks and becomes free of the vanity of the worm, it still does not attain the Virgin, but remains without spirit and worm under her shadow, in beautiful and gentle rest, without any child—

### 21. Question: What then are the actual names that man gave to the animals?

**Answer:** The spirit of man gives names to each thing according to how it stands within itself in its birth, and as it formed itself in the beginning of creation, so our mouth also forms it. The living, speaking Word, through which everything was made that is made, was in man; through it, he could rule everything and form everything, for this various compaction of the properties of **Salt** <term>Salis: Salt, representing the physical or "contracting" principle in alchemy</term>, **Sulphur** <term>Sulphuris: Sulphur, representing the "flaming" or soul-like principle</term>, and **Mercury** <term>Mercurii: Mercury, representing the "flowing" or communicative principle</term> were in his power.

<column-break/>

He was the central foundation of the entire creation; he had the sharp fire-desire of all creatures in his power, and he recognized the mind of God. From this, it is easy enough to understand how powerful, friendly, and lovely his words were, and how profound and full of meaning the names are that he gave to the animals, and how the animals themselves are meaningful **signs** <note>original: "Characteres," referring to the alchemical 'signatures' or outward physical signs of an inner spiritual reality</note> which allow us to recognize the secrets of Divine Wisdom.

### 22. Question: Could Adam then have found no help among the animals, so that he might help himself?

**Answer:** Although Adam searched through the entire animal kingdom, he found no help that was suitable for him; instead, his lust and desire were further ignited in the animal kingdom, and vanity awoke within him. The appetite for the Tree of Life faded, the **source-spirits** <term>Quell-Geister: the seven fundamental qualities or "fountain-spirits" that drive all existence</term> of fire and light left their **balance** <note>original: "Temperatur," the state of perfect harmony between opposing forces</note>, and each began to drive in its own selfhood. His **imagination** <term>Imagination: the soul's power of creative desire</term> was captured in the kingdom of this world; all three **Principles** began to pull and press upon him, so that he did not know which way to turn. Each wanted to have him and reveal itself in him. The **heavenly Virgin** <note>Sophia, or Divine Wisdom, the spiritual counterpart to the soul</note> withdrew; the light-tincture became faint and weak, while on the other hand, the rough spirit of the stars and elements became active, and the animal-like outer man became fierce and restless. Just as before, the spirit of man rose up according to the property of the light-world from the quality of the **angelic life** <gloss>the life of the angels</gloss> like a lovely scent, applying itself in the most unified union, love, and joy with God and all holy angels: so now the spirit rose up very weak and faint according to the property of light, but according to the quality of the stars, it was somewhat coarse, bitter, harsh, driving, and hot. Thus man could not remain standing, but was forced, as one overcome, to fall asleep.

### 23. Question: Would Adam then never have slept in Paradise?

**Answer:** It is quite easy for an understanding person to establish and know that in Adam, when he was in God's image, there was no sleep, nor should there have been; for Adam was such an image as we will be in the resurrection from death. Sleep is nothing other than an overcoming; for the sun and the stars are always in a powerful struggle with the elements, and the element is

# Chapter XL.
## On the Creation of Woman / the fleshly, wretched, and dark gate.

-> 1. Question. <-

**How did GOD make for Adam a helpmate in his sleep, who would be around him?**

-> Answer. <-

The author reports how this came to pass.
Out of displeasure I can hardly bear to write of it; but since it cannot be otherwise, we will meanwhile wear the woman's garment, but live in the life of the Virgin <note>Böhme refers to the "Heavenly Sophia" or Divine Wisdom, which he identifies as the spiritual, virginal half of the original androgynous Adam.</note>; and though we receive much tribulation in the woman, yet the Virgin shall go well with us. We must thus drag ourselves along with the woman until we send her to the grave; then she shall be a shadow and a figure, and the Virgin shall be our bride and worthy crown, who will give us her pearl and beautiful crown, and clothe us with her finery. Therefore, we will venture it for the sake of the lilies <note>The "Lily" is Böhme’s symbol for the future flowering of true spiritual life and the reformation of the world.</note>, even if we should stir up a great storm; and though the Anti-Christ should tear the woman away from us, yet the Virgin must remain with us, for we are wedded to her. Let each take only what is his, and what is mine remains mine.

Now as Adam walked in the Garden of Eden, so that the three **Principles** <term>Principles: In Böhme's system, these are the three realms of reality: the dark fire-world (First), the light-world of God (Second), and the visible, material world (Third).</term> in Adam carried out such a struggle, his **Tincture** <term>Tincture: A vitalizing, spiritual life-force or "inner light" that gives quality and power to a being.</term> became entirely weary and the Virgin withdrew; for the spirit of desire of this world in Adam had overcome him. Therefore, he sank down into sleep. At this hour, his heavenly body became flesh and blood, and his strong power became bones. Then the Virgin went into her **Ether** and shadow, but into the heavenly Ether into the Principle of power, and waits there for all of Adam's children, to see if anyone will receive her again as a bride through the new birth.

But what was GOD to do? He had created Adam out of His eternal will; since it could not be that Adam would have born the Virgin in a Paradisiacal way out of

### 3. Part / Chapter 10.

...as if they performed the work in the spirit, painting also in the spirit that which are dreams and prefigurations.

Thus it is for us to recognize: When earthliness <term>Irrdigkeit: The quality of being earthly or worldly, as opposed to heavenly or spiritual.</term> wrestled with Adam, and his imagination turned toward it, he was immediately infected by it. He became dark and harsh in his mind, for earthliness began to operate <note>Original: "qualificiren," a technical term in Böhme's writing meaning the active qualities, powers, or "flavors" working within a being.</note> like water that begins to boil from fire; the torment of the stars became active and was now the master of the body. So Moses says quite rightly: **GOD** let him fall into a deep sleep. That is because his spirit of will imagined toward earthliness, so **GOD** let him fall away; for through his imagination, he brought earthliness into the heavenly essence, and the Spirit of **GOD**—which is a Spirit of Light—did not want to have that. For Adam’s spirit was a creature and proceeded from God’s Spirit of Love; thus He did not let go of him willingly, but earthliness had already captured him. And when He let him go, he sank down into a swoon and fell prey to the **third principle** <term>Third Principle: In Böhme's cosmology, this is the visible, material world governed by the stars and the four elements, existing outside the pure light-world of God.</term>, namely the stars and the four elements. 

Thus he lay in the earthly magic <note>Original: "Magia," referring to the creative or formative power of the will.</note> and yet did not become entirely earthly; he lay hidden in the Mystery between God’s kingdom and the kingdom of this world, where both "Fiats"—the divine and the earthly—were active within him. The two kingdoms, **GOD'S** and this world’s, were now for the first time in conflict over humanity. If the precious name **JESUS** had not been formed within Adam—even before his creation, within the essence of **GOD** where the Wisdom of **GOD** stood and from which Adam was created—he would likely still be sleeping and remain in earthly death.

<margin>On the Incarnation of Christ, Part I, Chapter 6, Sections 1 & 2.</margin>

**24. Question: How long did Adam sleep?**
**Answer:** Adam fell asleep in the temperament <note>The "Temperament" refers to the perfect, harmonious balance of all qualities in the divine world before they were split by the fall.</note>—meaning the Divine World. From 

<column-break/>

this sleep, **Christ** must awaken him, or he can no longer see **GOD** within the creature. For this falling asleep was nothing other than losing **GOD’S** light in love—losing the fire of love. That light was extinguished in the *ens* <term>Ens: The essential spiritual substance or "being-ness" of a creature.</term> of the heavenly world-essence; thus he was already half dead. 

So, Christ later had to rest in Adam's death for forty hours to awaken Adam within Him—who had slept for forty hours in Paradise. Meditate on this, and you will learn to understand the entire ground of the **Process of Christ**. Just place Christ in Adam’s stead, and you will find the whole foundation of the Old and New Testaments. Place Adam in the formed word of **Creation**, and let him be the image of the outer and inner eternal nature of all three principles. Then place Christ in the eternally speaking Word, according to the true Divine quality, in which no evil can arise, but only the birth of love in Divine revelation according to the Kingdom of Glory. Lead Adam into Christ, so that Christ may give birth to Adam anew within Himself and tincture <term>Tincture: A spiritual essence or "dye" that transforms, heals, and vivifies a substance.</term> him with love, so that he wakes from his deep sleep. Thus you have the entire process of Adam and Christ. For Adam is the spoken, formed Word, and Christ is the holy, eternally speaking Word; thus you will lead time into eternity and see more than you could ever learn from all the books of men.

<margin>On the Election of Grace, 6. 42, 45. On the Signature of All Things, II. 80, 82.</margin>

**25. Question: What then did GOD do with Adam during his sleep?**
**Answer:** When the tincture within Adam was almost earthly and powerless, and the spirit of the great world had overcome him so that he fell into sleep, heavenly procreation was finished. Magical birth without the tearing of his body was also impossible; the virginal heavenly tincture had faded. Then, while he slept, **GOD** made him a helpmate to be before him.

# Chapter XI.
## On the Creation of the Woman / the fleshly, miserable, and dark gateway.

---

-> 1. Question. <-

-> How did GOD make a helper for Adam in his sleep, to be around him? <-

-> Answer. <-

The author reports how this came to pass.
I hardly wish to write of it out of displeasure <note>Böhme often expresses a mystical reluctance to describe the "fall" into physical, sexual reality, which he views as a step away from divine perfection.</note>, but because it cannot be otherwise, we shall for the time being wear the woman’s garment, yet live in the life of the virgin; and although we have received much tribulation in the woman, the virgin shall surely delight us: we must therefore drag ourselves along with the woman until we send her to the grave; then she shall be a shadow and a figure, and the virgin shall be our bride and worthy crown. She will give us her pearl and beautiful crown, and clothe us with her finery; therefore we will venture it for the sake of the lilies, even if we should stir up a great storm; and though the Anti-Christ should tear the woman away from us, yet the virgin must remain with us, for we are wedded to her. Let each take only what is his, so that what is mine remains with me.

As Adam now walked in the Garden of Eden, so that the three principles <term>Principia: The three fundamental realms of existence in Böhme’s thought: the dark fire-world, the light world of God’s love, and the visible material world.</term> in Adam waged such a struggle, his tincture <term>Tinctur: In alchemical and mystical terms, a vital spiritual essence or "life-oil" that animates and ennobles matter.</term> became entirely weary and the virgin <note>Reference to the "Heavenly Sophia" or Divine Wisdom, which Böhme believes was Adam's original spiritual "spouse" before the fall into gendered existence.</note> withdrew, for the spirit of desire of this world in Adam had overcome; therefore he sank down into sleep. At this hour, his heavenly body became flesh and blood, and his strong power became bones. Then the virgin went into her ether and shadow, but into the heavenly ether into the principle of power, and waits there for all of Adam’s children, to see if anyone will receive her again as a bride through the new birth.

But what was GOD to do? He had created Adam out of His eternal will; since it could not be that Adam would have born the virgin in a Paradisiacal manner out of

<column-break/>

himself, GOD placed the Fiat <term>Fiat: The creative "let it be" or the formative power of God that shapes reality.</term> of the great world in the midst; for Adam had now fallen back into the power of the Fiat as a half-broken person, because he was half-killed through his desire and imagination. If he were now to live, GOD had to advise him again: if he were to bear a kingdom, there must now be a woman, just like all other animals with reproduction. The angelic kingdom in Adam was gone; it must now become a kingdom of this world.

What then did GOD do with Adam? Moses says: When Adam fell asleep, He took one of his ribs and built a woman from it (from the rib which He took from the man) and closed up the place with flesh. Now, Moses wrote quite rightly, but who here would understand him? If I did not know the first Adam in his virgin-like form in Paradise, I would remain stuck there and know nothing else but that Adam had been made into flesh and blood from a lump of earth, and Eve <note>Original: "Heva"</note> his wife from his rib and hard bone. This often looked strange to me in the past when I read the commentaries on Moses, that such highly-learned men have written thus: some even want to speak of a pit in the East <note>Original: "Morgen-Land," referring to the traditional location of Eden.</note> where Adam was taken out and made, as a potter makes a jar or a pot. I would have thought so too, had I not considered the Scripture which says: *That which is born of the flesh is flesh.* Item: *Flesh and blood shall not inherit the kingdom of heaven.* Item: *No one goes to heaven except the Son of Man, who came from heaven (as the pure virgin) and who is in heaven.* To this end, it helped me greatly that the Virgin’s Child <note>Jesus Christ.</note> was the Angel of Restoration for what was lost in Adam. 3. Part / Cap. 11.

...women in their virginal body would restore the Virgin Child, whom Adam was meant to bring forth. If I had not considered the text in Moses, where GOD spoke: "It is not good that man should be alone; we will make him a helper," I would still be stuck in the will of the woman <note>Meaning he would still be thinking from a purely physical, gendered perspective.</note>. But that same text says: GOD looked at everything he had made, and behold, it was all very good. Now, if it was good during the creation, then it must truly have become evil for GOD to say: "It is not good that man should be alone." Had GOD wanted them to be like all the animals with beast-like reproduction, he would surely have made a man and a woman right away; but that GOD felt a disgust toward it is well proven by the first child of the woman, Cain the brother-murderer, and the curse upon the earth proves it as well. Oh, why should I spend space on this testimony? The proof will follow clearly, and it is not only to be confirmed from the Scripture (which admittedly wears a veil), but in all things, if we would take the space and not spend our labor on vain things.

Now Reason <note>Reason (Vernunfft) is often personified by Böhme as the limited, logical mind that cannot grasp divine mysteries without spiritual illumination.</note> asks: What then are Moses' words regarding the woman? To this we say: Moses wrote correctly, but after I lived in the woman <note>Likely referring to his own state of being trapped in physical, fallen nature.</note>, I did not understand it correctly. Moses certainly had a glorified countenance, but he had to hang a veil over it so that one could not look into his face. But when the Virgin's Son, as the Virgin, came, he looked into his face and took away the veil. So Reason asks: What was the rib for the woman taken out of Adam?

<margin>Princ. 13. 7. <note>original: "Drei Prinzipien" (Three Principles of Divine Essence), Chapter 13, verse 7.</note></margin>
So that we may grasp this fundamentally, we wish to investigate:

1. The Creator and Maker of this helper.
2. The *Materia* <note>original: "Materia" (material/substance)</note>, out of which she was made.
3. The Form and the Image, according to which she is made.
4. The Purpose for which she was created.

<column-break/>

Concerning the Creator, one should not think that it was something external over Adam that made his Eve out of him, or that formed them both for the external natural life, other than simply the *Verbum Fiat* <term>Verbum Fiat: The Latin phrase for the creative command "Word, let it be," which Böhme views as an internal force of manifestation.</term> within them—their own possession, and nothing foreign outside of them. Just as the first creation of Adam and all species occurred: the *Verbum Fiat* coagulated every *Ens* <term>Ens: A philosophical term for "being" or "essence."</term>, and the revealed Word decided itself within the *Ens* according to its own property. It formed the creature according to its star and species; therein, in every *Ens*, the *Matrix* <term>Matrix: The "womb" or generative source of a particular form of life.</term> separated from the *Limbo* <term>Limbus: A term Böhme uses for the "spiritual earth" or the concentrated essence of the world from which Adam was made.</term> and formed into a male and a female. The "painter-work"—as when one paints GOD as a man who makes Adam, and then stands over Adam as he sleeps and makes a woman out of him—is more idolatrous than truthful. GOD strictly forbade this in Moses, to make any likeness of the one GOD; for He is no image except only in creatures, according to the spoken, formed Word, both in eternal and temporal creatures. He is not a "Maker" <note>In the sense of a physical craftsman.</note> but only a "Former" of properties—a Creator and not a Maker. The first Creator, who moved Himself and entered into a creature, left the power within all creatures for self-multiplication, increase, procreation, and making, and embodied the *Fiat* within them as a "maker" for their own possession.

<margin>Myst. Mag. 19. 26. 27. 28. <note>Refers to Böhme's "Mysterium Magnum," Chapter 19, verses 26–28.</note></margin>

# Concerning the Creation of the Woman.
Iii 2

...we will make him a helper/ and the **"Let there be"** <note>original: "Fiat"; the divine command of creation.</note> stood in the Center, and separated the **Womb** <note>original: "Matrix"; the feminine, receptive principle in nature.</note> from the **spiritual seed** <note>original: "Limbo"; the essential masculine or creative matter of the earth.</note>, and the **"Let there be"** seized a rib in the midst of Adam from his right side/ and created the woman from it. Now you must clearly understand/ that when the **"Let there be"** was at work for the creation within Adam/ while he slept/ his body had not yet become such entirely hard bone and marrow. Oh no/ that only happened when Mother Eve bit into the apple/ and gave some to Adam as well. However, the infection and earthly death were already present within him through the longing and deadly sickness/ the bones and ribs were still strength and power/ and Eve was created from the strength or power/ out of which the rib was to become. But you must understand deeply/ she was not drawn out like a spirit/ but entirely in essence. One must say/ that Adam received a rift; and the woman carries Adam’s spirit, flesh, and bone: But in the spirit, it is somewhat distinct. For the woman carries the **Womb**, and Adam the **spiritual seed**, or man/ and the two are one flesh/ undivided in nature/ for both must again give birth to a human being/ which previously one alone could do.

->A lovely Gate.<-

For the text in Moses says rightly: God closed the place with flesh. But now the fury of the serpent has brought it about/ that Adam fell into lust/ and yet the purpose of God must stand. For Adam must rise again entirely unbroken on the Last Day in the first image/ as he was created. But now, even though the serpent and the devil brought it about/ that such a rift occurred in him/ so the Spirit

<column-break/>

testifies to us/ that/ just as little as the worm or soul-spirit could have been helped/ unless the Virgin came and then went into death/ into the worm/ into the abyss of the soul-spirit/ which in its abyss reaches the gates of Hell and the fierce wrath of God/ and teaches him (Adam) anew toward a new creature of the first image/ which happened in the Virgin’s Son in Christ. Just as little could Adam’s rib and hollow side/ where it once stood/ have been brought to its perfection/ unless the second Adam <note>Refers to Christ, who restores the perfection lost by the first Adam.</note> allowed himself to be wounded in this same place in the Virgin/ so that his precious blood might come to the aid of the first Adam again/ and heal his broken side. Let us speak deeply according to our knowledge/ which/ when we write of the suffering and death of Christ/ the Virgin’s Son/ we shall explain in such a way/ that the thirsty soul shall find a spring-well/ which will be of little use to the devil.

->Further concerning the Woman.<-

Reason <note>As in previous pages, "Reason" represents the limited, worldly intellect.</note> says: If Eve was created merely from a single rib of Adam/ must she then be much lesser than Adam? No, dear Reason/ that is not so; the **"Let there be"**, acting as a sharp attraction/ took from all essences and properties from Adam, from every power/ but it took no more members from him in essence/ for the image was meant to be a man in the **spiritual seed** in a masculine way/ yet not with this current deformity. Understand it correctly at the root/ he was meant to be/ and was indeed a man/ and had a virginal heart/ entirely chaste in the **Womb**. But because Eve was certainly created from all of Adam’s essences/ and thus Adam received a great rift/ and yet the woman also came to her full perfection in the image of God/ the great mystery <note>original: "Mysterium"</note> proves to me once again/ where the Virgin testifies most dearly/ that not only...

3. Question: In what kind of shape and form did GOD create Eve through His Word?

# On the Creation of the Woman.

From Adam’s flesh and bones, nothing more went to the woman than the rib in his side and the half-cross in the head, which was the birth-cross of life, upon which Christ broke death. The <term>Matrix</term> <note>original: "Matrix"; in this context, it refers to the creative or "mother" principle through which life is shaped.</note> of the heavenly part in Adam was magical—that is, it hovered in the <term>essence</term> <note>original: "Essentz"; the spiritual substance or "flavor" of a being.</note>. But the outer part of the external world was enfleshed, and both were bound together, just as time is bound with eternity. The holy part was in heaven, and was heaven itself, and the outer enfleshed part was in the external world, in the <term>Matrix of the World</term> <note>original: "Matrice Mundi".</note>. Thus, the female property was drawn out of Adam from his essence through the <term>Fiat</term> <note>Latin for "let it be done"; the creative word of God.</note>, as his beloved rose-garden; and he retained the <term>Limbus</term> <note>The "extract" or spiritual soil from which the human form was drawn.</note>, both heavenly and earthly, according to the revealed property of the eternal Father, as the property of the fire-soul’s <term>Matrix</term>. And the woman received the part of the spirit of the soul’s property: the woman had, in her faded part of the soul-like property, the <term>Center</term> of the angelic world, as the revealed Word of Love, the fifth form of eternal nature. And the man had in his <term>Limbus</term> the Divine Fire-World, as the <term>Center</term> of the Light-World, the <term>Center</term> of all beings. The man’s <term>Limbus</term>, which he retained when the woman was made from him, was the Father’s property according to all being; and the woman was made from the man according to the Son’s property, according to all being—understand this as the heavenly part. Therefore, Christ was a man in the woman’s part and led the man’s part back into the holy <term>Matrix</term>, so that the <term>Limbus</term> and the female Matrix were once again one image, as a male virgin over and in all three <term>Principles</term>, as a creaturely-formed God in whom the eternal unformed God dwelt with total fullness, simultaneously within the formed and outside the formed. For so was Adam before his Eve, and so we must also become in Christ, if we wish to be the image and temple of God.

Reason will object and say to me: God created Adam in the beginning as a man, and with all the members just as he is now; yet reason cannot prove this. For the soul is ashamed of this animal property. Also, I will ask "Reason" itself: if such an Adam had been created for eternal life without lack, and without need or death, why would he have been created so miserable, naked, and bare into this animal life? ### Part 3, Chapter 11

What use is this birth? The new birth <note>Refers to the spiritual rebirth or regeneration of the soul.</note> maintains this right: that the angelic image which **GOD** had created in Adam should be born again. **GOD** formed Adam in the image of **God**; and although He well knew that Adam would not endure, He ordained for him the Savior, who should lead him back into the first image and confirm him in Himself for eternity.

That Adam stood in **God's** image and not in an animal image is found in this: that he knew the properties of all creatures and gave names to all creatures based on their *essence*, form, and property. He understood the language of nature <note>original: "Natur-Sprache"; the idea that names perfectly reflect the inner spiritual reality of a thing.</note> as the revealed and formed Word in all *essence*, for from this the name of every creature arose. Since he knew how the Word of power stood in the form of every creature, we cannot consider him animal-like; he must have been angelic. For no other person shall rise again except such a one as Adam was before his Eve: **GOD** created him perfect, but he did not withstand the trial. Following this, **GOD** allowed him to fall into external *magic* <note>original: "Magiam"; here meaning the power of the external, material world's influence.</note> and appointed him to the image of this world in natural life, characterized by fragility and the need for new birth. For in heaven there is neither man nor woman, but all are one gender with their own love, without further procreation, in an eternal confirmation. This also shows us that Adam died in Paradise, just as **GOD** said to him: "When you eat of the tree, you shall die." He died to the holy image and lived to the awakened animal image. For when Adam now woke from sleep, he was indeed still in Paradise, for the vanity in flesh and soul did not yet qualify <note>original: "qualificirte"; meaning to manifest its specific qualities or effects.</note> him; it was still mute, non-weaving, and unfeeling until they bit into the forbidden fruit. Then the earthly dominion began; then vanity woke up, as all the forms of life, each in its

own selfhood, and they separated from their state of equality. Immediately, heat and cold fell upon them, for the outer now interacted with the inner; and the heavenly image completely faded, which had still lived in Adam’s sleep and also in his waking, both in Adam and Eve, but almost dark and powerless.

Adam, in his perfection, became infatuated with the animals. Because he was man and woman and had the magical conception within himself, he introduced himself into animal lust, both for animal eating and birthing. Thus the *Fiat* <note>Latin: "let it be done"; the creative power of God's word.</note> also found him in that same lust and formed him in his sleep according to that lust. And every member was formed in its place for the *conjunction* <note>original: "Conjunction"; a technical term for the union or joining of two things, here referring to sexual union.</note> of beastly mixing, for every desire received its mouth for revelation. Thus the image of **GOD** had formed itself through the *Word of the Fiat* into such an animal as we still are today; and the human's own *Fiat*, as the first form of nature—which is the desire for Divine revelation—did this, and no other maker outside of him.

# On the Creation of the Woman.

The Cross in the head—which is the character <note>In Böhme's mysticism, a "character" is a spiritual seal or signature of a divine truth.</note> of the Holy Trinity—is marked with the Word of Life, as if with the heavy Name of **GOD**. This carries such a character that the **T** signifies the Cross of Christ, upon which He was to suffer death, to give Adam a new birth, and to lead him in the Name of **JESUS** into the Holy Ternary <note>original: "Ternarium Sanctum"; refers to the three-fold manifestation of God’s glory or the "holy kingdom."</note>. The **Fiat** <term>Fiat: The creative "Let there be" of God; a spiritual power that shapes spirit into matter.</term> took all of this into itself with all the essences of human property, including the property of the soul-fire, though in the Tincture of Venus <note>original: "Veneris Tinctur"; in Böhme's alchemy, Venus represents the principle of love, desire, and gentle attraction.</note>, not according to the power of the Center, and it divided itself into the entire form of the human being.

Thus the woman was built with all the limbs and female properties that they still possess. For the Spirit of the Greater World <note>original: "Majoris Mundi"; the macrocosm or the outer universe.</note> now held the strongest **Fiat**, and it figured the woman according to such a shape as was possible within its power; for the angelic form was gone. Now, humans had to be born in an animal-like way. Therefore, because Adam had fallen victim to earthly magic <note>original: "Magiæ"; Böhme uses this to mean the power of desire and imagination that binds the spirit to the material world.</note>, he was also given the animal form and shape of the male members. Adam’s procreation was given over to the **Fiat**, which made an image like him and out of him. Had he remained heavenly-minded, he would have given birth in a heavenly way himself; instead, the earthly **Fiat** acted, and his outer body became an animal, and he also lost the heavenly knowledge and the power of omnipotence.

Therefore, dear reader, you should know that the second Adam, Christ, did not allow Himself to be crucified in vain, nor did He have His side pierced with a spear and His blood shed in vain. Here lies the key: Adam’s side was broken open at the rib to create the woman; into that same side, Longinus’ spear <note>Referring to the Roman soldier who, according to tradition, pierced the side of Jesus on the cross.</note> had to come with God's wrath. For that wrath had entered into Adam, and through Mary’s earthliness, it also entered the side of Christ. Christ’s blood had to drown that wrath and take it away from the first Adam. For the second Adam also has heavenly blood, which had to drown the earthly Turba <term>Turba: A chaotic, disturbing force or "uproar" within nature, often associated with God's judgment and the potential for destruction.</term>

<column-break/>

so that the first Adam might be made whole again.

Let this be told to you, children of men, for it has been recognized in the Holy Ternary <note>original: "Ternario Sancto"</note>, and not in mere opinion or fancy; it costs you soul and body. See to it what you do.

Thus human procreation began in an animal-like way; for Adam kept the Limbus <term>Limbus: The vital, masculine seed or extract of the earth’s substance.</term>, and his Eve kept the Matrix of Venus <term>Matrix: The feminine "womb" or receptive principle in nature.</term>, for the Tinctures <note>A "Tincture" is a spiritual essence or "coloring" that gives life and quality to matter.</note> were separated. Now, every Tincture is a complete Magic, like a longing addiction in which the Center of Nature is born, and this happens in **Sulfur** <note>original: "Sulphur"; in alchemical terms, this represents the combustible, substantial, and physical aspect of a thing.</note>. Then, in the Sulfur, there is again the longing Magic with the Tincture, and yet it cannot come to life unless the fire’s Tincture enters the Tincture of Venus. And the Tincture of Venus cannot awaken any fire; she is too weak. Since this cannot happen within itself, and yet both Tinctures long for life, now the intense Imagination of the man and woman begins. One desires to mix with the other, because the power of the essences wants to be alive; the Tincture drives toward this and desires it. For the Tincture is from eternal life, but it is enclosed within the physical essence; thus it wants to live as it has done from eternity. Therefore, the man yearns for the woman’s Matrix, and the woman for the man’s Limbus. The woman has a watery Tincture, and the man a fiery one. The man sows the soul, and the woman the spirit; and both sow flesh, as Sulfur. Therefore, man and woman are one body, and both make one child. For this reason, both should stay together once they have mixed, for they have become one body. But whoever mixes with others, or separates, breaks the order of nature and resembles a beast; he does not consider that the eternal Tincture lies in his seed, in which the Divine Essence lies enclosed, and which will one day be awakened in the Part of Wrath <note>Referring to the day of judgment or the spiritual consequences of misusing the creative power.</note>...

The "Let it be" <note>original: "*Fiat*"; the divine command of creation.</note> went in, to remain there forever and always: Now the **tincture** <term>Tincture: A spiritual essence or "pigment" that gives life, quality, and character to a being.</term> in **Adam** had not yet vanished; rather, **Adam’s** soul still sat quite powerfully and mightily in the tincture. You must understand this correctly: **Eve** did not receive **Adam’s** soul, nor **Adam’s** body, only a rib. Yet the **Creative Word** had already formed her into a woman—not uncreated, but quite lovely. 7. Question: How did it then go for Adam with his Eve in Paradise?

The serpent was likewise formed; however, it did not become so through its own self-elevation, but rather when **God** spoke: "Let all kinds of animals come forth, each according to its kind." Thus, from every property of nature—as it became manifest in the separation when **God** moved toward creation—animals came forth. For the devil wished to rule over the love and gentleness of **God**, and he placed his desire also into wrath—that is, into the strict power where the life of poison <note>original: "Gifft-Leben"</note> has its origin. From this form have come adders, snakes, toads, and other poisonous crawling things. This is not because the devil made them—he cannot do that—but rather as the desire was in the "impression" <note>The contracting, forming force of nature.</note> of the **Fiat** <note>original: "Fiat" — Latin for "Let it be," referring to God's creative command.</note>, so also the creature was formed in both Evil and Good. For in the impression of the **Fiat** at the primordial origin of the outer **Mercury** <term>Mercury: in this context, the active, moving spirit of life</term>—as the life that becomes manifest within itself—there was the separation where **God** and the world divide; **God** being in Himself, and the world being out of Himself, as a likeness of the **Abyss** <note>original: "Ungrundes" — Böhme's term for the "Groundless" or the nothingness before creation.</note>, or a mirror of eternity. There, the inner wrath—because of which **God** calls Himself a jealous, angry **God** and a consuming fire—manifested itself in outer figures as a likeness of the inner birth in the **Center** <note>original: "Centro"</note>. This occurred just as the eternal longing, which He Himself is, awakens and causes the desire for the nature of eternal revelation, giving itself into that desire and turning the wrath of the desire into a kingdom of joy.

It is the same with the serpent’s poison: in the highest **Mercury** is the highest, sharpest trial <note>original: "Proba"</note> of all things. The more poisonous a thing is, the more sharply it tests a thing; for the sharpest taste and smell exist in the greatest poison, as if in a dying torment. the light also becomes a desire out of the fire’s torment and property. This is the desire of Divine Love and the kingdom of joy. In this desire, **Mercury** is rightly considered and named the **Eternal Word**, or the primordial origin of eternity or the **Godhead**. And this "going out" from the fire (understand this as the eternal, magical spirit-fire) is a bringing forth, such as the Word of power, colors, and virtues. And this same desire of that **Mercury** or **Word** also takes the power into itself and makes it essential <note>Meaning, it gives it "essence" or "substance."</note>. This is the gentleness and the love which extinguishes the wrath of the eternal Father—as the desire of eternal nature—with love, and transforms it into a kingdom of joy, where the Name of **God** has its origin from eternity. This contained essence gives two properties: one is "oily" <note>original: "Olitätische" — Refers to a spiritual, heavenly "oil" that fuels the light of the spirit.</note>, which is a heavenly being and a cause of the light’s shine; and one is powerful, from the movement of the eternal impression or the Father’s desire for the birth of the Son. From this, the Divine Air—as the power through the shine of the light—goes out from that same fire of love, which is the **Spirit of God**.

Likewise, know this: that eternal love (understand this as the essence or the heavenly substance) has entered into the creation with the **Word "Let there be"** <note>original: "Verbo Fiat"</note>, to place the Father’s wrath—as the form of eternal nature—into the highest kingdom of joy, and to represent likenesses of the eternal birth. 9. **Question:** From this, I see how the devil became the serpent; but tell me, was the serpent that tempted Adam not a literal, created serpent?

**Answer:** We do not doubt that the hellish serpent, through dark magic <note>original: "Magiam"</note>, embodied itself into a literal serpent and infected its essence <note>original: "Ens"</note>, from which its great cunning arose.

As we now write of the serpent’s cunning, of its adorned art and false virtue, understand our very sharp and revealed meaning from **GOD’s** counsel thus: The serpent’s essence and origin was once a heavenly virgin of heavenly pomp, a queen

**10. Question:** Did the serpent in the Garden of Eden not have such a figure and bodily shape as it has now?

**Answer:** Whether its outward form was such that it had to eat the dust of the earth and go upon its belly, as it did after the curse, is not to be believed. You, as physicians <note>original: "Medici"</note>, will no doubt also well know the secret of the serpent: what it carries hidden beneath its poison. If one takes that from it or tests it correctly, you have a tincture against poison such as no other can be. Every sin is born from a foreign **Essence** <term>Essence: Translated from "Ens," referring to the inner spiritual substance or "being" of a thing</term>, whenever the free will departs from the essence in which **GOD** created it. The sin that is conceived in the free will through false longing, and brought into substance within the essence of the will—so that the person would gladly do wrong if they only had the opportunity—is also great before **GOD**. But if it enters into an active or spoken reality and offends other people, it is doubled; for it is formed in its own essence and also forms itself within the person into whom it introduces the false word—provided that the false word finds a place of rest in that person’s own speaking where it can take effect. And therefore, the Holy Word shall judge the false; just as at the end of this time, the Holy Word will cast out from itself all false formation and everything that has been formed in the serpent’s essence, and give it over to the dark world.

All those who grasp the Word within themselves in their devilish and serpent-essence, and direct it against **GOD’S** children (in whom the holy essence is manifest), also awaken an offense in the children of **GOD**. This causes the free will in those children to also grasp itself in the serpent’s essence—such as in wrath and ill-will—whereupon the holy essence always reacts, and the Spirit of Zeal goes forth. These same false initiators and causes of sin all sin against the Holy Spirit. For they provoke Him, so that He must pass through the wrath of the children of **GOD**, by which He is sharpened; sometimes He goes out in the **Great Turmoil** <term>Great Turmoil: Translated from "Turba Magna," referring to the destructive awakening of God's wrath within a creature's essence</term> of the children of **GOD** and comes down upon the neck of the godless. This is seen in the cases of Elijah and Moses, and also with *Elisha* <note>original: "Eliseo"</note>, who cursed the boys so that bears tore them apart, and with Elijah, when fire consumed the two captains and their fifties. For thus the sword

<column-break/>

of **GOD** goes through the mouth of the holy children when the Holy Spirit is provoked to zeal; thus he awakens the *Great Turmoil* <note>original: "Turbam Magnam"</note>, which wields the sword over a godless people and devours them.

Therefore, understand it well enough: Man has **GOD’S** Word within himself, which created him. Understand this: the Word enclosed and formed itself within the creation, both in its holiness and also in its wrath, and also from the outer world. For the **Slime** <term>Slime: Translated from "Limus," the biblical material (clay or dust) from which the first human was formed</term> of the earth—or the earth itself—was grasped and compacted through the Word. It is the formed Word which took its beginning in Divine Desire, as in the **Let It Be** <note>original: "Fiat," the creative command</note>, a breathed-out breath from the Spirit of **GOD** out of love and wrath. Therefore, the earth is both evil and good, but the evil was hidden and entirely swallowed up in the light, just as the day swallows the night.

But the sin-desire in *Lucifer* and *Adam* awakened the wrath, so that it became substantially manifest. Now the gate of the formed Word—both in love and in wrath—is manifest in the earth, and also in the *Slime* of the earth (which is man), as well as in the free will of man. Whatever a person now forms and grasps in their free will, that they have made, whether it be good or evil. Now, however, the evil shall be separated from the good in **God’s** judgment; and in whichever part the human understanding (the soul) is found, into that part it must enter, as into its own self-made dwelling-house. And therefore *Christ* says: "Their works follow them, and shall be proven through the fire." Likewise: "At the end, when the books of the essence are opened, they shall be judged according to their works." For the work—whether evil or good—encompasses the soul, unless the soul departs from it entirely and breaks it apart again through reconciliation with its offended brother, drowning that substance in the blood and death of **CHRIST**; otherwise, there is no other counsel.

And even if it should only be a jest, the serpent’s essence has nonetheless attached itself to what is good and has merged with the Word. Therefore, Christ says: *You shall not swear: Your speech shall be Yes, Yes; No, No; whatever is more than this is of evil,* <note>Matthew 5:34-37</note> that is, it is born out of the serpent’s essence. All who curse and swear have introduced their free will—as the poor soul—into the vanity of the serpent’s essence; they form their oaths and curses along with all the decadent speech that occurs in the serpent’s essence, and they sow into **GOD’S** wrath. Dear brothers, Adam and Eve bequeathed such a state to us. And this is the reason why the body must die and completely decay, and must enter again into its first essence; for the serpent’s essence must be entirely removed, as it cannot inherit the Kingdom of **GOD**.

### 14. How then did the serpent persuade Eve?

**Answer:** The Devil spoke in the serpent to Eve: that the fruit would not harm her, but rather the eyes of her sharp understanding would be opened, and she would be like **GOD**. This seemed good to Eve—that she might be a goddess—and she consented to it entirely. In this consent, she fell away from the Divine Harmony, from **Resignation** <term>Resignation: Translated from "Gelassenheit," a central concept in German mysticism meaning a state of yieldedness or letting go of one’s own self-will to God.</term> in **GOD**, and entered with her own desire into the

<column-break/>

serpent’s and the Devil’s cunning, addiction, and vanity. At that point, the Devil’s desire completely possessed Eve’s will and led it into a serpent-like substance. There, Eve became monstrous in her own essence, according to the serpent’s essence; and here, the Devil built his castle and fortress within the human essence. Here is the death of the heavenly essence, that is, of the heavenly being. Here, the Holy Spirit of **GOD** withdrew from Eve’s heavenly essence. Thus, at this point, the heavenly part of man faded—the **heavenly clay** <term>Clay: Translated from "Limus," referring to the substance or "slime" of the earth from which Adam was formed (Genesis 2:7), which Böhme believes had a heavenly counterpart before the Fall.</term> in the flesh. And this is why **GOD** said: *In the day that you eat of it, you shall surely die.* <note>Genesis 2:17</note> When Eve introduced her will out of obedience to **GOD** and into the serpent’s cunning, the power of heavenly gentleness and humility faded in the heavenly substance—not that she had entirely taken the essence of the dark world into her own essence. No; but as **GOD** said to her: *You will die,* which means to die or fade away from the Kingdom of Heaven. For the Kingdom of Heaven admits no true death; rather, when the light of the Divine Principle is extinguished, that same being in which it burned and shone out becomes mute and as if dead, without feeling or understanding, like a nothingness. It is just as when a candle burns in a dark place, making an entire room light; if it is extinguished, there is no trace of it left behind. Its power goes into nothingness, in the same way that **GOD** made all things out of nothing. This is not to be understood as if the heavenly essence of man became a literal nothing; it remained in man. But to man in his life, it was as a nothing, for it stood hidden in **GOD** and was incomprehensible to man, being without life. In **GOD** nothing dies, but in the human life, the holy essence faded.

# Of the Fall of Man.

...Angelic? Does he have an angelic source? Is his source found in love, humility, and gentleness? Is it found in obedience to GOD, in the light of joys? O, you blind mind with your power and pomp, full of the malice and wrath of the devil; you are among all the devils in the abyss of hell, unless you turn back and walk in the angelic footsteps through earnest regret and repentance for your abomination. This turn allows the Savior and **Serpent-Treader** <note>A traditional reference to the Messiah (Christ) who, according to Genesis 3:15, would "crush the head" of the serpent.</note> of wrath, anger, malice, lying, and deception—and your innate pride and spirit—to meet you and take you into his arms. He births you anew in himself and places you in the lap of the **chaste virgins** <note>A reference to Divine Wisdom or Sophia, often personified as a pure maiden in Böhme's theology.</note>, so that you may become an angel. Otherwise, you belong to eternal death in eternal darkness and will never reach the Kingdom of GOD.

->**The Three Principles, Chapter 17, Verses 36–44.**<-

If we now wish to look deeply into the Fall of Man for our own humbling, we must investigate:
1. What kind of life it was that man died to.
2. What kind of life it was that man woke up to again.

**Question 2:** What then was that life to which man had died, and how did this come about?

**Answer:** He died to the Divine and Paradisiacal life, which we mentioned above. As long as a branch lives on the tree, it shares the tree's will, life, and property. But as soon as it is torn from the tree and grafted into another tree, it dies to the life of the first tree and lives for the second. Understand this: Man was a branch on the **Tree of Life**; his will, imagination, and desire were set in GOD'S will and heart. But as soon as Adam turned his will away from GOD'S heart and placed his imagination into the kingdom of this world, leading it into the **Tree of Knowledge**, he died to the life that is from GOD. He then functioned according to the properties of the kingdom of this world, eating from the fruits of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil. Thus, it is understood regarding the Fall that all properties in the 

<column-break/>

**Spirit of the World** <note>original: *Spiritu Mundi*—the animating force or "soul" of the physical cosmos.</note> revealed themselves within man; all fiery **active forces** <term>Scientz: In Böhme's writing, this refers to an indwelling power or "science" of nature—the way a thing operates based on its inner makeup.</term> according to heat and cold, as well as all other qualities in particular. Likewise, the properties of the whole of nature were revealed in him according to both Evil and Good. For as soon as they ate the earthly fruit into the body, the **balanced state** <note>original: *Temperatur*—the perfect harmony of elements that existed before the Fall.</note> fell apart, and the body became manifest according to all the properties in the Spirit of the World. Then heat and cold fell upon him and pressed into him. Likewise, all the properties of nature, in which the foundation of the creature stands, pressed themselves into him in a state of conflict, from which sickness and the "death of breaking" <note>Referring to the physical decomposition and fragmentation of the once-unified body.</note> arose for him. And in this bite, he died to GOD's kingdom and woke up to the kingdom of nature; he was moved from a state of being **beyond suffering** to a state of **vulnerability** <note>original: *Unleidlichkeit* into *Leidlichkeit*—transitioning from a state where nothing can harm or affect the spirit to a state of physical and emotional suffering.</note>. Regarding the outer body, he became a "beast of all beasts," as the animalistic image of God, wherein the Word of God revealed itself in an earthly likeness. Thus, man became a master and prince of all animals regarding the outer body, and yet was himself only an animal—though possessed of a nobler **inner power** <term>Scientz</term> than a beast—yet he nonetheless had a beast within his nature.

And at this hour, a gate of the dark world was opened in man within GOD'S wrath, namely hell, or the "throat of the devil"; likewise, the kingdom of **fantasy** <note>In Böhme’s view, "fantasy" is a self-centered, illusory world created by the mind when it is separated from God.</note> was revealed in him. The "angry GOD" (so called according to the kingdom of darkness) was revealed in him and captured him according to the soul's **inner power** <term>Scientz</term> within the creature. It is not that the foundation of the soul's power can be destroyed, but the creature is made of the three first principles: **Salt**, **Sulfur**, and **Mercury** <term>Sale, Sulphure, and Mercurio: The three "Paracelsian" principles representing stability (Salt), expansion/combustion (Sulfur), and movement/spirit (Mercury).</term>, as the eternal nature, as well as the temporal nature in the Spirit of the World. The temporal nature was placed into the earthly property, and the eternal nature into the wrath of the dark world, as a neighbor to the devil.

### Part 3 / Chapter 12.

**Question 3:** Since the human soul is immortal, how could man have died to the spiritual life?

**Answer:** The soul, in its created nature, did not die; that could not be. For whatever originates from the eternal does not admit death. Instead, the "Image of GOD," which had formed itself within the created soul as the divine <term>Ens</term> <note>original: "Ens"; refers to a spiritual substance or "being" that acts as the seed of divine life within the soul.</note>, faded away when the <term>Fire-Wrath</term> <note>original: "Feuer-Grimm"; the harsh, energetic, and dark foundation of existence that, without God’s light, becomes a consuming fire.</note> awoke. In GOD, there is no dying, but only a separation of the principles. We can understand this by looking at how the night swallows the day, and the day swallows the night; thus, one is as if "dead" within the other, for it can no longer reveal itself. 

To understand this through a likeness: if the sun were to vanish, the <term>Spirit of the World</term> <note>original: "Spiritus Mundi"; the animating breath or soul of the physical universe.</note> would become a vain, harsh hostility and a perpetual night. In such a state, the four elements—in their current properties—could not function, no fruit would grow, and no creature could live within them. In the same way, Adam and his Eve died to the kingdom of the Divine Sun-Power—that is, to the Divine Essence and Will—and woke up to the fierce nature within their souls, and also externally, in their animal-like properties.

The soul’s <term>Scientz</term> <note>original: "Scientz"; from the Latin *scientia*, here meaning an active, internal "knowledge-power" or the root of consciousness that drives the will.</note> from the <term>Abyssal Will</term> <note>original: "ungründlicher Wille"; the "groundless" or bottomless will of God that precedes all created things.</note> in which GOD brings forth life did not die, for nothing can break it; it remains eternally a free will. But its "creaturely form"—the soul as an image shaped by the Spirit of GOD from eternal nature—lost that holy <term>Ens</term> in which God’s light and fire of love once burned. It is not that this <term>Ens</term> became "nothing." To the created soul, it did indeed become a "nothing" in the sense of being imperceptible. Rather, the holy power—the Spirit of GOD, which was the active life within it—hid itself. This was not by God’s own decree, but because the eternal <term>Scientz</term> (the unfathomable will toward the soul-creature) turned from 

<column-break/>

the Will of Love and entered into its own thorny "self-property" of the soul’s nature. GOD did not withdraw Himself from the soul; rather, the <term>Scientz</term> of the free will withdrew itself from GOD. Just as the sun does not withdraw from the thistle, yet the thistle withdraws its thorny <term>Scientz</term> from the sun and directs it into its own prickly being. The more the sun shines upon it, the thornier and stronger the <term>Scientz</term> of its working will becomes. This is how we must understand the soul. GOD dwells through everything, even through the darkness and through the devils, but the darkness does not grasp Him; likewise, the devil and the godless soul do not grasp Him. You may ask: "Why is that?" Because the creaturely will to true, surrendered humility (to submit under GOD’S obedience) is dead, and only a "thistle-and-thorn-will" remains within the life of the creature. Thus, the thorn-will keeps the noble <term>Scientz</term> of the fathomless eternal will of the <term>Ungrund</term> <note>original: "Ungrund"; the "Groundless" or the infinite void of the Divine from which all light and darkness emerge.</note> imprisoned or covered within itself; they exist within one another like day and night.

The created soul became night. The <term>Spirit of the World</term>, which in the beginning stood in "balance" <note>original: "Temperatur"; a state where all qualities are in perfect harmony.</note> within the body, now stood in both evil and good, just as all temporal things do. But the devil’s thistle-seed had entered into it, within which lay temporal death; thus, man was to be understood as nothing other than an "animal of all animals." The likeness of the "formed, spoken Word" stood in hostility and opposition. The angelic image was entirely destroyed, both in the mind and the senses. As we still see today, the senses always grasp for the animalistic will of self-love; they find it very difficult to love GOD and his Likeness. Instead, they always strive upward, wanting to possess everything for themselves alone, wanting to be the "fairest child in the house"—from which arise <term>Pride</term>, <term>Greed</term>, <term>Envy</term>, and <term>Hatred</term>. All of this is the <term>Ens</term> of the Serpent and the property introduced by the devil,

**Question 4:** It is very difficult for Reason to grasp how such a terrifying misery and wretchedness could have arisen from a single bite of an apple?

**Answer:** To GOD, it was not about a single apple; the sin is not actually in the outward action, but the sin is in the lust and the false fire-desire of the soul, through which the Wrath of GOD is ignited within the soul. This soul-fire inflames the whole person, so that all qualities depart from their <term>Temperature</term> <note>original: "Temperatur"; the state of perfect balance where all inner forces work in harmony.</note>, and all the source-spirits fall into a mighty conflict. Thus, the root and source of sin is the evil lust and fiery desire of the soul, through which GOD became active in the soul as an angry, jealous GOD. For as soon as the soul broke its will away from GOD and led its desire into the <term>Vulcan of Mercury</term> <note>original: "Vulcanum des Mercurii"; "Vulcan" represents the raw, forging fire of nature, and "Mercury" represents the restless, driving spirit of life. Together they signify the soul turning toward its own autonomous power.</note>, there arose in it at once the lust to eat of the knowledge of evil and good; it reached for the fruit of the knowledge of good and evil and ate of it. Then there arose a lust for **Pride**: to be great, mighty, and powerful; to subdue everything under oneself and to rule with violence; wanting to be one's own master and to be equal to nothing; to despise humility and equality; to consider oneself alone as clever and witty, and to hold everything as foolish that did not match this wit.

### 5. Question: Is there then no difference between the Devil and the fallen Fire-Soul?

**Answer.** Regarding the inner nature and root of the <term>Fire-Soul</term> <note>original: "Feuer-Seele"; the soul in its state of burning desire or "fire," stripped of the cooling light of God.</note> and the fallen angels, there is little difference between them. But as for the Fall, Lucifer—out of his own inner impulse, without any external temptation—turned his will away from the heart of GOD and placed his desire into the fire-power beyond its proper limit. Thus, the magical constellation of the <term>Great Mystery</term> <note>original: "grossen Mysterii"; the *Mysterium Magnum*, the vast spiritual chaos or "chaos-source" from which all things originate.</note>

<column-break/>

of the dark world seized him. He has now become the <term>Calefactor</term> <note>original: "Calefactor"; Latin for "one who heats" or "stoker." In this context, it refers to one who stokes the fires of divine wrath.</note> in the dark fire-world, where he continually and eternally blows upon the wrath of GOD in nature and creation. Through this "blowing," the fire-desire also arose in the soul, so that man turned his will away from GOD. However, at first, he was not cast back into the dark world like Lucifer, but into the <term>Third Principle</term> <note>original: "dritte Principium"; in the author's system, this refers to the visible, material world of time and space.</note> which was attached to him. In this realm, the soul lives in an animalistic way as long as this world remains within him. If the soul—which has retained the possibility of restoration—does not turn back and incline its fire-desire toward God through abstinence, it will finally become a devil.

Therefore, it was not without reason that GOD breathed the outer spirit, as the outer life, into Adam's nostrils. There was danger in this image; GOD knew what had happened with Lucifer and what the great eternal <term>Magia</term> <note>original: "Magia"; the spiritual power of will and desire to manifest reality.</note> is capable of. Adam could also have become a devil if the outer life did not prevent it. For where there is water, it extinguishes the fire so that the soul does not catch fire entirely. How many a person is so fierce, poisonous, and evil that they would like to murder everything? But their fire still has water; otherwise, it would have happened. This can be seen in the bile, which is a "fire-poison," but it is mixed with water so that the "fire-glory" is restrained from lashing out against the <term>gentleness of GOD</term> <note>original: "Sanfft-muth GOTTES"; the cooling, loving aspect of the divine nature that balances the fiery wrath.</note>.

...[longing] entered in: this hunger now impressed itself with a hard pull into the **essence** <term>essence: translated from "Essentz," the fundamental spiritual substance or "stuff" of a being</term> of the being, and thus drew the kingdom of this world to itself, so that the spirit of this world became **qualifying** <note>In Böhme’s terminology, this means the worldly spirit began to determine or "flavor" the soul's nature.</note>. For we know that the soul dwells in the heart: Its own essence is the **Center of Nature** <note>original: "Centrum der sieben Geister der Natur"</note> made of the seven spirits. **5th Question:** Is there then no difference between the Devil and the fallen Fire-Soul?

**Answer:** As far as the inner nature and root of the Fire-Soul and the fallen angels are concerned, there is little difference between them. But as for the Fall itself, Lucifer, out of his own inner impulse and without any external temptation, turned his will away from the heart of GOD and set his desire into the **fire-power** beyond the goal; thus, the magical constellation of the **Great Mystery** <note>original: "grossen Mysterii"; Böhme uses this term to describe the fundamental chaotic potential of all being.</note>

of the dark world seized him. He has now become the **Stoker** <note>original Latin: "Calefactor"; literally one who fans the heat or tends a furnace.</note> in the dark fire-world, where he constantly and eternally fans the wrath of GOD in nature and in the creature. Through this fanning, the fire-desire also arose in the soul, so that man turned his will away from GOD. However, for a time, he was not cast back into the dark world like Lucifer, but remained in the **Third Principle** <term>Third Principle: Böhme’s term for the physical, material world we inhabit</term> which clung to him. Therein the soul also lives in a beastly way as long as this world lasts within him; then the soul—which has retained the possibility for restoration—finally becomes a devil if she does not turn back and incline her fire-desire toward GOD through restraint.

Therefore, it did not happen without reason that GOD breathed the external spirit, as the external life, into Adam's nostrils. There was danger in this image; GOD knew how it had gone with Lucifer and what the great eternal **Magia** <term>Magia: the spiritual "will" or power that brings thoughts into substance</term> is capable of. How many a person is so fierce, poisonous, and evil that he would like to murder everything! But his fire still has water; otherwise, it would have happened. This can be seen in the gall, which is a fire-poison, but it is mixed with water so that the fire-glory is restrained from breaking out over the **gentleness of GOD**.

Since then, we unfortunately find—and must lament with great pain—how our father Adam introduced this evil, poisonous, earthly rule <note>The German *Regiment* refers to a governing order or system of control.</note> to us. Thus, the poor soul is entirely imprisoned by the spirit of this world, which wells up and works powerfully within the soul's government. Because of this, the malice of the abyss breaks forth from our soul’s words often and hourly; the devil mixes himself into this and possesses our hearts in the outer realm, and even in the very innermost part—namely, in the first four forms of nature. He turns us away from **God’s** will into all the vices and malice that are within him. And as he now sees how a person is naturally inclined—specifically, which spirit is master according to the outer rule of their body—he always looks for that and drives such great villainy with the soul that no mouth can describe it. For there are also seven forms in the outer rule, just like the seven planets which govern the outer man; these reach into the soul unless she resists without ceasing and rejects the evil influences. In this, the devil has a powerful access to the soul. However, he does not have the same rule or full power therein unless the Great Turmoil <note>original: "Turba magna." In Böhme's philosophy, this is the "awakened wrath" or a state of severe spiritual disruption where the divine order is broken.</note> is ignited in the wrath of **GOD**; in such a case, he acts as a Stern Executioner. But he does possess the inner rule of the four forms of the fire-life; as often as the soul immerses herself in them, he can possess her. If he catches her there, oh, how he holds her! He wants to pull her entirely into his kingdom, for it is his realm, and he marks us as a precious prize.

The four forms contain the original state of nature: first, in the desiring will, darkness enters into the desire through attraction. Then the desire becomes severe, harsh, hard, and cold; this desire creates a pulling and a stirring within that severe harshness, which are two forms. And the third form is the great

<column-break/>

anxiety, where the desire wants to be free, which awakens the anxious wheel of nature and finally the fire-flash of the fourth form, as was reported at length previously. Now, that same harsh attraction in the desire of the will creates a great greed in the outer nature of this world; the mind <note>original: "Gemüthe," referring to the seat of emotions, thoughts, and disposition.</note> wants to pull everything to itself and possess it alone. Even if it cannot consume it, it still wants to own it, and does not like to leave or grant anything to anyone else. This is a root of the abyss of hell, in which the devil fiercely attacks the soul so that she shall not go out and come to the light of **GOD**.

The second root is the bitterness of nature; this is a hostile sting within the harshness and will not allow itself to be tamed. The more sharply one resists it, the greater the sting becomes. This is the second form, which creates a hostile, stinging, envious, and bitter mind in the outer nature. The devil wraps himself into this as well and infects the soul's words with a sharp-witted, stinging, and envious essence, so that the will always burns in envy and never speaks anything good, but only vain flippancy which serves the devil. From this come the liars, slanderers, misinterpreters, and false hearts. **GOD** be lamented for our great misery into which we are immersed!

The third root is the anxious wheel of the mind, from which the senses arise and are born. This contains primarily the miserable house of mourning, and yet it is also the house of life's rising. This is primarily the devil’s seat; he sits himself therein—it is his throne—and he always awakens that same house of mourning so that the soul becomes faint-hearted and doubts **GOD'S** grace and the light of eternal life. He always throws the first two forms—namely greed and envy—into it, and turns the wheel of the mind with that same poison, creating a confusion in the essences of the thoughts. He constantly mixes greed and envy together, so that he may keep his seat.

Fourthly, the fourth generation is **Wrath**, which is the son of Envy; what he cannot achieve with an evil will, he ignites in the wrath-fire, and breaks it with violence, inciting war and murder; he wants to break everything—this generation wants to subdue everything with force.

These are thus the four elements of the devil, all four of which are within one another as one; one proceeds from the other, and each one gives birth to the other; they originate from the dark nature, such as from **Harshness**, **Bitterness**, **Anguish**, and **Fire**.

# On the Fall of Man.

**GOD’S** Splendor, and in the heart, the Devil’s power and poison. This one is king on Earth and governs two kingdoms: the first is called Perdition <note>original: *Verderbnis*, meaning destruction or the state of being spiritually lost</note>; the other, Babel, which is a Confusion. For the kingdom of Perdition, this king has put on strength and power; that is the garment of that kingdom. For the other kingdom, namely Babel, he has put on a white, glittering garment; this must serve him in **GOD’S** stead, with which the king on Earth rules as if he were **God**. And the nations worship this same garment, and beneath the garment is the man of Falsehood and Deceit; he has his mother, the four elements <term>four elements: in Böhme’s theology, these are not physical earth, air, water, and fire, but the spiritual roots of sin: Pride, Greed, Envy, and Wrath</term>, within himself.

Thus the four elements of the devil rule under a shimmering coat, and people fight over that same coat; everyone wants to put it on, but whoever puts it on, puts on Hell and **GOD’s** wrath. Such a coat is honored in **GOD’s** stead; it is the coat that the wrath of **GOD** put upon Adam and Eve when the devil deceived them, so that they fell from **GOD’s** obedience. <note>This refers to the "coats of skins" in Genesis 3:21, which Böhme interprets as the mortal, earthly nature that covers the lost spiritual body.</note> And it is the very same little coat <note>original: *Röcklein*. When we put it on, we take the devil into our lodging and must do what he wants, for he is the host in that same house and rests in that same little coat. Since he is a prisoner of **GOD**, he dresses us in his little coat and sends us with it toward Babel into his service, where we must mock **GOD**; for we wear **GOD’S** little coat <note>The outward appearance of a human being created in God's image</note> and have the devil lodged underneath as a guest. Thus the tongue gives **God** good words, but the heart has the spirit of the four elements of wrath; and so **God** is mocked by the devil, so that **God** must see that he, the devil, is lord and king over mankind, and regards **GOD’S** sovereignty in man as nothing more than a glittering coat, within which he, the devil, is the man,

and has caught the human in his arm. He covers the human with the little coat and allows the human to be called **GOD’s** child, but the human only does the devil's will in this coat. All that the devil cannot or may not do in his own kingdom, the human does for him in his service. The devil may kill no one, but the human does it gladly to please him. Also, the devil cannot use **GOD’s** creatures, but the human gladly misuses them to please him, thereby mocking **GOD**. He practices pride and greed, as well as falsehood and malice, and accomplishes everything with them that the devil wants; he even glitters with them as if he were **God**. Therefore, the outer kingdom has become a constant murder-pit for the devil; and the false, supposed human—who calls himself a human but is not—carries out the murder and increases **GOD’S** wrath, setting fire to the dark world within this outer one, so that **GOD’S** wrath burns forever in this world.

Thus **GOD’S** kingdom is hindered, and the devil’s will is done, and the devil remains a prince on earth; where he would otherwise have no way to accomplish anything on earth, the supposed human is in his service and carries out his will. Thus, two generations of humans dwell together on earth: one are true humans, who serve **GOD** in the coat of humility and misery; the devil mocks them and plagues them by means of the other generation, performing all his wonders upon them through those who serve him.

The other generation also calls itself human and walks in human form, but they are evil beasts; they put on their king's garment, which is called Falsehood, and live in the power of their king's four elements: pride, greed, envy, and wrath. Pride is the first virtue <note>Böhme uses "virtue" ironically here to describe the primary driving force of the fallen nature.</note>; it tears the bread out of the mouth of the true human and forces the wretched to satisfy its desires. The third virtue <note>The author uses "virtue" ironically here to describe the dominant characteristics or "powers" of the devil's kingdom.</note> is Envy, found in the four elements of the devil, in the kingdom of falsehood; it is a sting, a rager and raver, like an evil poison.
