It is the mouth of Greed, a constant liar and slanderer; it stabs into its neighbor's heart and wounds it, devours itself with poisonous hunger, and yet is never satisfied. It creates unrest without end or measure; it is the greatest poison and the eye of hell; the devil uses it to look into the soul and body of man. Nothing is equal to it; it is not fire, but the sting of fire. It causes all evil and yet finds no rest; the more it drives, the more insane it becomes. It is a parched poison; it requires no substance, and yet rages within substance; it makes a person more than insane, so that he desires to rage and rave against **GOD**. It is the essence of hell and of wrath; it turns the greatest friendship into enmity; it grudges no one anything, and is itself a starving nothing. This is the will-spirit of the devil; whichever person takes it in as a guest, takes in the devil along with **GOD’s** wrath, for it carries the hellish torture and woe. It is the eternal, hostile plague and unrest, and it destroys the noble image of **GOD**, for it is the enemy of **GOD** and of all creatures.

The fourth virtue in the four elements in the kingdom of the devil’s falsehood is Wrath, or Malice; this is the true hellish fire. For Wrath is born between Greed and Envy; it is the fire and life of Envy. What Envy cannot accomplish, Wrath completes; Wrath takes body and soul together and runs like a raging devil, wanting to murder and break everything; it runs against walls and castles, and even if it should burst 

<column-break/>

While literally meaning gout, the author uses it here as a metaphor for a crippling, agonizing disease of the world.</note> of the world; when Pride in her glittering little coat cannot obtain power through cunning and falsehood, then the fourth virtue must carry it out; it strikes with fists and starts wars. Oh, how joyful is the devil when his four elements rule in this way; then he still imagines he is the lord on earth. Even though he is a prisoner, the animal-men perform his office well for him, and he only mocks humans in this way, seeing that they are worse and do more than he himself can do.

7. Question: How then are the senses, such as sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch, corrupted in the outward nature?

Answer: The corruption of the senses lies especially in the fact that they are turned away from the heavenly being and are turned out and scattered into the kingdom of this world. For the senses are, as it were, the wagon with which the fire-soul <note>A mystical term for the core of the human soul, which seeks the "light" but can be trapped in "fire" or desire.</note> drives in and out of the kingdom of this world and attaches itself to everything. For the senses enter into everything; they test, search, and seek everything because of the soul's insatiable fire-hunger. The eye is never satisfied with seeing, and the ear is never satisfied with hearing; what they seize, they bring to the understanding. What agrees with the soul's lust and the impression of its hunger, the understanding calls "good," and what does not harmonize, it calls "evil"; the former was accepted, the latter rejected. To this also belongs that power of the mind called <term>Phantasia</term> <note>Imagination or the power of forming mental images.</note>, which is nothing other than the water-mirror of the third <term>Principle</term> <note>original: "Principii." In this cosmology, the Third Principle refers to the physical, material world.</note>. Just as the fire-soul has an impression and an image of its desire, so there is a reflection in the Phantasia, as if all kinds of <term>monstrosities</term> <note>original: "Monstra."</note> of images were figured in the Phantasia of man, according to which man's fire-desire forms its lust. Man has such an internal form: one person like a snake, full of wicked cunning and poisonous malice; another has the quality of a toad; many have the quality of a dog, a cat, a basilisk, a lion, a bear, a wolf, or even the quality of a good animal.

8. **Question:** But how was it possible that the fire-soul, through its monstrous image, could also corrupt the excellent likeness of **GOD** in the body and make such a monster out of it?

From this, the flesh became coarse, hard, raw, thick, and tangible, surrounded by a tough, thick skin, and even overgrown with hair and a beard, just like the animals.

# On the Fall of Man.
### N n n 3

...that the will of the **Groundless** <note>original: *Ungrund*; Böhme’s term for the absolute, unmanifested divine abyss before creation</note> has introduced itself into the desire and **Imagination** <term>Imagination: here meaning the "magical" or spiritual power of the mind to form and manifest substance</term> of itself, from which nature and the creature have their origin. From this also natural life has its origin, which now, out of that same differentiation of the exhaled will, possesses its own will and its own **Imagination**, to shape and form itself according to its lust and craving: just as one sees such transformation in nature, how nature forms itself into so many kinds and properties, and how each of those formed properties craves its own likeness again.

Because the soul now—as the inner ground of man—has, in **Adam** the first man, turned away with its lust and craving from its first mother (from its origin), namely from the Divine Word and Will, and turned into the influence of the stars and the elements, and formed itself into that same influence, and practiced a foreign **Imagination**; thereby the Divine food, namely the substantial **Wisdom** of **GOD**, was withdrawn from it, from which it broke itself off with its lustful craving. Thus it became entirely blind to **GOD**, and its first Divine essence, into which **GOD** created it, faded away. Because the soul led its **Imagination** out of that essence and into earthly and astral properties, its body <note>original: *Corpus*</note>, in which the threefold spirit works, also became entirely earthly, coarse, and beast-like. For into whatever the **Imagination** of the spirit introduces itself, such a body also becomes through the impression of spiritual craving; as we then see in man, that he has received a coarse-earthly body, in which the **Principles** <note>original: *Principia*; the fundamental spiritual realms of Light, Darkness, and the World</note> now stand in pure conflict, adversity, and enmity: from which pain, as well as fragility and death, have arisen for him. Yet **GOD** forbade this to him in **Paradise**, while he still stood therein, that he should not eat with his **Imagination** from the knowledge of evil and good, or he would fall into such distress and death, and to the kingdom of heaven

<column-break/>

die away, Genesis 2:17, as has also happened. When the soul introduced itself into earthly **Imagination**, it led itself into earthly formation and lost the heavenly formation. Where it should have imagined itself into the substantial **Wisdom**, as into the holy substantial Word, and taken its nourishment therefrom, it instead formed itself into the outer **Astrum** <term>Astrum: the "astral" or starry influence that governs the physical and seasonal world</term>, and into the craving of the serpent and the devil: whereby in its noble image it became a **Ghostly Husk** <note>original: *Larva*; suggesting a hollow mask or a fallen, shadowy shell of its former self</note> and a **Monster** <note>original: *Monstrum*; meaning something unnatural or a distortion of the divine order</note> before **GOD**, and lost the angelic form it once had, as well as **Paradise** and the kingdom of heaven. Now, with its ground, it stood within the impression of darkness, in **GOD’S** wrath, and would have had to remain eternally in such a ghostly image, had not the great love of **GOD** come to its aid again.

Man, in his first **Paradisiacal** image, was neither man nor woman, but a virgin <note>Böhme uses "virgin" here to describe a spiritually pure, androgynous state</note>, without animal form: he had no shame and no breasts, nor did he need them. Just as they have all been redeemed by one man from eternal death and the torment of hell, those who come to the one **Chief Shepherd** <note>original: *Erz-Hirten*; referring to Christ</note> to his rest.

### Part 3 / Chapter 12.

...man co-qualifies <note>original: *inqualiret*; Böhme’s term for acting or existing within a specific quality or property</note>, and sin first became manifest in the element of the mind in **Adam** and **Eve**; then fear and terror fell into the essences of the soul. For the first **Principle** <note>In Böhme’s system, the "First Principle" refers to the dark, fiery, and harsh foundation of nature, which is divine wrath when separated from God's light</note> in the wrathfulness was stirred; it received, as one might say, wood for a fire-source, and rose up inflammably in the counter-will within the essences, where each form went against the other. 

Just as harshness and cold, through their attraction, awakened the bitter stinging and aching in the essences of the **Tincture** <note>The *Tincture* is the vital, spiritual essence or "light-water" that gives life and beauty to the soul and body</note> of the blood in the spirit, so too the bitter raging and rising up awakened the fire. And instead of Paradisiacal joy and delight, there arose a mere **Sulfur-Spirit** <note>original: *Schwefel-Geist*; an alchemical term for the combustible, anxious, and suffering quality of physical life</note>, which stands in the anguish and trembling of its own fragmentation, and which ignites the **Tincture** of the blood. Within this, tearing, stinging, torture, and woe occur; and if the fire in the **Sulfur-Spirit** ignites too much, it burns up the **Tincture**, so that the light of life is extinguished: thus the body falls down as a dead carcass. 

If the harshness then ignites with its hard attraction, the **Tincture** becomes hard, dark, and cold from the pulling and holding; then also the light of life is extinguished, and the body perishes. Likewise with the water: if the **Tincture** ignites in the gentleness, it becomes fatty, thick, and swollen, entirely sickly, as well as dark and dim, within which the lightning of life moves like a stinging thorn. 

And thus human life is surrounded everywhere by enemies, and the poor soul is always held in a heavy prison, bound with many chains, and always fears that when the body breaks, it might fall home to the executioner—the devil—into his kingdom. 

Thus there arose in **Adam** and **Eve** in the Garden of Eden, after the **Apple-Bite**, the first fruit in the gates of the deep, where the soul stands before **GOD** and co-qualifies with the Father’s righteous will. This will sets itself before the fragmentation of the darkness, leading into the light of gentleness, and 

<column-break/>

[the Father] always brings forth his dear Heart and Son, in the power of the gentleness of the will, as his eternal Word, from eternity. So too the angelic man should have set his will before him into the shattered gates of darkness, through the Father’s will—with which the soul co-qualifies—into the gentleness of **God’s** heart. Had he done so, the torment of darkness in the wrath would not have stirred him, but he would have remained a victorious prince in the triumph of Paradise, over the kingdom of hell and this world.

But when he set his **Imagination** <term>Imagination: the "magical" power of the mind to focus on and manifest a particular reality</term> into the kingdom of this world, the swollen kingdom of the "outgrowth" pulled his bright and pure soul-will into itself. Thus the pure Paradisiacal soul became dark, and the element of the body received the mixture or mass <note>original: *Mesch* or *Massa*; referring to the coarse, material substance of the physical body</note>, which pulled the will of the soul and the mind into the element. Thus, a fleshly man was formed, and he received the wrath of the first **Principle**, which transformed the strong "breakthroughs" toward **God** (which existed in the gates of the deep) into hard bones and limbs. 

And this is for us to recognize excellently and highly: For it is seen in the light of life that the marrow in the bones has the noblest and highest **Tincture**, wherein the spirit is sweetest and the light brightest. This can be recognized in fire, even if you are otherwise blind with contradiction. It is clearly seen that these passages, where hard bones are now, were once "wonder-power" which shattered the gates of darkness, and in which the angelic man stood in the light.

9. **Question:** All of this is well understood, especially since the soul stood in such an inflammation within a powerful <term>Magia</term> <note>The supernatural or spiritual willpower that shapes reality</note> and fire-power. What then followed upon such a sorrowful state for man?

### 14. Question: Did GOD then not mean the literal, natural serpent here?

**Answer:** GOD primarily meant the old serpent here, the Devil, who now held his dominion in the fire-soul <note>The "fire-soul" refers to the primal, energetic, and often wrathful foundation of human life when separated from God's light</note>, and the fleshly, animalistic desire and lustful addiction of mankind. **Moses** writes here as if the serpent had deceived **Eve**. For **GOD** cursed it so that it should eat the earth and go upon its belly. But **Moses** here places a veil before the eyes <note>An allusion to Moses veiling his face; here it means the true spiritual meaning is hidden behind a literal story</note> so that one does not look him in the face. For all prophecy stands in obscure words, so that the Devil does not recognize it and learn the timing, lest he sow his false seed beforehand, before the wonders of **GOD** appear: as can be seen in all the prophets who prophesy of the **Serpent-Crusher** <note>original: *Schlangen-Treter*; a messianic title referring to the one who will tread upon or crush the head of the serpent</note>.

It is clear to us that the Devil crept into the serpent and spoke out of the serpent; for **GOD** did not mean that the **Serpent-Crusher** should crush the head of the animalistic serpent, but rather the Devil, and destroy the abyss of hell. Yet it was the punishment of the animalistic serpent that it should remain a poisonous worm, without feet, and eat the earth and have fellowship with the Devil. For in this way, all evil spirits also appear in hell in their own form, according to their torment, as serpents, dragons, hideous worms, and evil beasts. The Devil did not understand this at the time, because **GOD** spoke of the serpent and cursed it to be a terrible worm; he thought it did not concern him. He still does not know his own judgment, except for what he learns from man, who interprets in the **Spirit of GOD**—although the **Spirit of God** does not fully indicate his judgment to him, but keeps everything at a great distance in the depths,

<column-break/>
<page-num>860</page-num>

so that he does not entirely understand it. For to the enlightened person, all prophecies—even those regarding the wickedness of mankind—are given in such a way that he must not present them clearly, so that the Devil does not fully learn the counsel of **GOD** and sprinkle his sugar into it <note>A metaphor for the Devil corrupting or tainting God's plans with deceptive sweetness or false doctrines</note>. Although very excellent things are written in this place which must not be revealed to the world—for they remain for the judgment of **GOD**—so that the Devil does not introduce new sects and lead man into doubt; thus it shall be passed over until the **Time of the Lily** <note>The "Time of the Lily" is Böhme’s term for a future age of spiritual purity, peace, and the full revelation of divine knowledge</note>.

<margin>Principles 17. 103. 105.</margin>

### 15. Question: What then does GOD’S curse upon the serpent mean, that it must eat dust, etc.?

**Answer:** **GOD’S** curse signifies a permanent separation and flight of the serpent from **GOD’S** holy communion of love. For **GOD’S** cursing is to drive into flight; whatever **GOD** curses is eternally driven away from **GOD’S** communion and shuts itself up in a contrary torment of wrath. It is condemned, for the maintenance of its poisonous torment, to eat dust and to devour the waste <note>original: *Egest*; likely referring to the foul results or "excrement" of sinful desire</note> it generates within man—namely, the torment of hell which the Devil ignited in man, thereby defiling the image of **GOD**. Thus, animalistic lust and fleshly desire eat nothing but dust and filth, from which they are born and into which they have placed their will. To this the Spirit points when it condemns the serpent to crawl on its belly; this belly-crawling is a great loathing before the pure eyes of **GOD**, through which the serpent exercises great power in man and miserably defiles many hearts, until finally, through the earnest struggle of repentance and faith, the **Serpent-Crusher** enters into their conflict. He carries out the curse in power, treads upon the serpent’s head, and sets the precious name **JESUS** as a boundary-mark where its proud power lies defeated, according to the promise:

> The seed of the woman shall crush the serpent's head, and you, as the serpent, will sting him in the heel; that is, in **GOD’S** wrath you will kill him, but he will grow green again out of death and crush your head—that is, take your power and the wrath...

16. **Q.** But how were Adam and Eve able to grasp the Word of the **Serpent-Crusher** / after the heavenly world-property <note>The "heavenly world-property" refers to the spiritual, divine nature that Adam possessed before the Fall, which became "clogged" or dormant after his sin.</note> was blocked within them?

**A.** Just as the Devil's word had spoken itself into the soul / (and awakened the hellish **Ens** <note>original: *Ens*; a philosophical term meaning "essence" or "being." In Böhme’s thought, it is the spiritual substance that makes up a person.</note> in the soul / and the hearing according to the torment of wrath / ) so came the Word of GOD’S love / and spoke itself again into the faded **Ens** / to indicate / that it was a goal of an eternal Covenant of Grace / wherein GOD’S love in the name of JESUS would destroy his works / and intended to reintroduce the living holy **Ens** in the name of JESUS / into this speaking-in / or the spoken Word / which happens in Christ’s incarnation. For the single root of the **Ens** out of Divine Love / namely the heavenly world-essence / faded in Adam / as the true image of GOD / according to the property of Divine Holiness / and into that same single image / which faded in Adam in GOD / GOD had incorporated the goal of His eternal holy will / in Christ. Into that same image GOD’S holy Word spoke / when the poor creaturely soul had now become blind to GOD: *The seed of the woman shall crush the serpent's head.* And in that same spoken voice / the poor soul received Divine Breath and Life again. And that same spoken voice / was planted within human life (as a figure of the true image / in this goal of the Covenant of GOD / which He had seen in the Divine **Ens** before the foundation of the world) continuously from person to person / as a Covenant of Grace.

<column-break/>

For the speaking-in of the Devil / from which an evil will arose / happened first in Adam / when he was man and woman / and yet neither of them / but rather an image of GOD / and it pressed from Adam into Eve / who began the sin. So now also came the speaking-in of GOD / and pressed into Eve / as the mother of all humans / and through Eve / set itself against the beginning torment of sin in Adam. For in Eve lay the **Tincture** <note>original: *Tinctur*; in alchemy and Böhme's theology, a "tincture" is a spiritual force or "dye" that gives a substance its quality—here, the "light" or "love" quality of the soul.</note> of Light / and of spiritual water / and into this the holy **Tincture** in the Word embodied itself / in the name of JESUS / so that it would break the animalistic <term>Matrix</term> <note>original: *Matricem*; Latin for "womb" or "mother-source." Böhme uses it to describe the formative spiritual mold from which life emerges.</note> / and transform it into a holy one. For it should not happen through Adam’s fire-**Tincture** <note>Adam's "fire-tincture" represents the harsh, masculine, and wrathful aspect of the soul that needs the "light-tincture" of the woman to be balanced.</note> / but through / and in the part of the Adamitic light-**Tincture** / in which the love burned / which was separated into the woman / as the mother of all humans / therein GOD’S voice promised / to reintroduce the living holy **Ens** from heaven / and to give new birth to the faded image of GOD / which stood therein / in Divine Power.
In the third [chapter] of John, Christ says: *He is come from heaven*; by this one understands essence / for the Word needs no coming / it is already there / and only needs to move. Now all humans lay in the seed of Adam according to the corrupted soul-property: And conversely all humans lay in the <term>Matrix of Venus</term> <note>original: *Veneris Matrice*; Venus here refers to the spiritual quality of love and desire, which Böhme associates with the feminine principle and the potential for redemption.</note> / as in the feminine property / in Eve; and in Eve / as in the <term>Matrix</term> of the love of the heavenly world-essence / which faded in Adam and Eve / as in the part of the Kingdom of GOD / GOD placed His Covenant / and led His Word into it / so that the woman's seed (understand the heavenly seed / which the Word would reintroduce / in which GOD and man should again be one person / ) should crush the head of the serpent’s refuse <note>original: *Egeßt*; referring to the "excrement" or the base, fallen matter produced by the serpent/devil.</note> / and the power of the Devil’s will / and destroy the Devil’s works / which he would work in soul and body.

16. **Question:** But how were Adam and Eve able to grasp the Word of the "Crusher of the Serpent" <note>This refers to the "Seed of the Woman" in Genesis 3:15, who is promised to crush the serpent’s head.</note>, after the heavenly world-quality in them had been blocked?

**Answer:** Just as the Devil’s word had spoken itself into the soul / (and awakened the hellish <term>essence</term> <note>original: *Ens*; a Latin term Böhme uses to describe the "inner being" or "spiritual substance" of a thing.</note> in the soul, and the hearing according to the source-torment of wrath,) so also came the Word of GOD’S love / and spoke itself back into the faded essence / to signify / that there was a goal of an eternal Covenant of Grace / in which GOD’S love in the name of JESUS would destroy his [the Devil’s] works / and intended to lead the living holy essence in the name of JESUS / back into this "speaking-in" / or "spoken-in" Word / which happens in Christ’s incarnation. For the single root of the essence <note>original: *Entis*, the genitive form of *Ens*.</note> out of Divine Love / namely the heavenly world-substance / faded in Adam / as the true image of GOD / according to the quality of Divine Holiness / and into that same single image / which faded in Adam in GOD / GOD had incorporated the goal of his eternal holy will / in Christ. Into that same image, GOD’S holy Word spoke / when the poor creaturely soul had now become blind to GOD: *The seed of the woman shall crush the serpent’s head.* And in that same spoken-in voice, the poor soul received Divine Breath and life again. And this same spoken-in voice / was planted further from person to person in human life / (as a figure of the true image / in this goal of the Covenant of GOD / which he had foreseen in the Divine essence before the foundation of the world) / as a Covenant of Grace.

For the "speaking-in" of the Devil / from which an evil will arose / occurred first in Adam / when he was man and woman / and yet neither of them / but rather an image of GOD / and it forced its way from Adam into Eve / who began the sin. For in Eve lay the <term>tincture</term> <note>original: *Tinctur*; in Böhme’s thought, a spiritual "dye" or "vibration" that gives a being its specific quality, such as Light or Fire.</note> of the light / and of the spiritual water / and into this, the holy tincture in the Word / in the name of JESUS / embodied itself / so that it might break the animal <term>matrix</term> <note>original: *Matricem*; the Latin word for "womb," used here to mean the formative power or "source-mold" of a being.</note> / and transform it into a holy one. For it was not to happen through Adam’s fire-tincture / but through / and in that part of the Adam-like light-tincture / in which love burned / which was separated into the woman / as the bearer of all humans / into which GOD’S voice promised / to lead the living holy essence from heaven again / and to give new birth in Divine power to the faded image of GOD / which stood therein.

In the third chapter of John, Christ says: *He is come from heaven* ; here one understands "substance" / for the Word requires no "coming" / it is already there / and only needs to move itself. Now all humans lay, according to the corrupted soul-quality, in the seed of Adam: And on the other hand, all humans lay in the <term>Matrix of Venus</term> <note>original: *Veneris Matrice*; Venus here represents the quality of love and the female principle in Böhme’s astrological-spiritual system.</note> / as in the feminine quality / in Eve / and in Eve / as into the matrix of the love of the heavenly world-substance / which faded in Adam and Eve / as into the part of the Kingdom of GOD / GOD placed his Covenant / and led His Word into it / so that the woman’s seed (meaning the heavenly seed / which the Word wanted to introduce again / in which GOD and man should again be one person /) should crush the serpent’s <term>outflow</term> <note>original: *Egest*; from the Latin *egestio*, referring to the waste or poisonous discharge of the serpent's will.</note> / and the head of the Devil's will and power / and destroy the Devil’s works / which he would work in soul and body.

### 17. Question: Which are the two parties between whom GOD has set enmity?

**Answer:** They are the serpent and the woman, the serpent’s seed, and the woman’s seed. What is to be understood by the serpent, we have sufficiently revealed above: GOD did not mean so much the creaturely animal serpent here, but rather the false fire-desire of the soul, and the monstrous fleshly lust, which had imagined itself into Adam and Eve; and thus the seed of the serpent is all kinds of powers, both of hell, and of the flesh, along with its lusts and desires.

### 18. Question: In what does the enmity actually consist?

**Answer:** In a great struggle, and irreconcilable hatred and ill-will; the flesh against the spirit, and the spirit against the flesh. This struggle is expressed when Moses says: **The seed of the woman shall crush the serpent’s head, and it shall sting him in the heel.**

The "crushing of the head" is nothing other / than to break the serpent’s disgust / to take his power through a true desire for faith / and through such powerful imagination of faith in the promised Word / to grasp that same Word / and introduce it into the serpent’s substance / and thereby destroy the Devil’s fortress of plunder / the matrix <note>original: *Matricem*; the "womb" or "generative source."</note> of the harlot...

# On the Fall of Man.

The property of Fire, as it entered into the *Fiat* <term>Fiat</term> <note>Latin for "let it be done"; the creative command of God that forms reality.</note>, took hold of him and introduced the serpent-*essence* <term>Ens</term> <note>Latin for "being" or "essence"; the fundamental spiritual substance of a person.</note> with the desire of the *Fiat* into the earthly *clay* <term>Limus</term> <note>Latin for "mud" or "slime"; referring to the biblical "dust of the ground" from which man was made.</note>; from this, the four elements became manifest in man instead of the single element. Therefore, the virginal *essence* from the single element must now crush the head of the introduced serpent-*essence* in the four elements, and man must die to the four elements and decay. Then, on the Last Day, he must return as the first man in a single element—where everything lies within in an equal balance—surrounded by the virginal *essence*. For that same virginal *essence*, reborn anew in the Spirit of **Christ**, does not die anymore, even though the four-elemental man dies as the image of this world. Instead, he lives in **GOD’S** Kingdom and, in the resurrection of the dead, will encompass and put on the *clay* of the earth as the third *Principle* <term>Principle</term> <note>Böhme's term for the three realms of reality: the dark fire-world, the light holy-world, and this visible world.</note>, like a garment of **GOD’S** wonder-work. But the serpent-*essence* remains in the earth and shall be burned away from the pure *clay* of the earth by fire on the Last Day; then the dark world, along with all its workings, shall swallow it up.

Thus we clearly understand here how **GOD**, out of great love, promised the Crusher of the Serpent to fallen man and wedded Him into the virginal, faded Center, giving Him as a helper and companion. For when they had fallen away from **GOD** and had made themselves monstrous, the image from the *clay* of the earth had become entirely beastly and lived in adversity, in sickness, and also in heat and cold, like all other animals.

That I say / however / that the being out of **JEHOVAH** had faded in the fall / that is true / and is precisely the death / in which Adam and Eva died. # Of the Fall of Man.

Will / against the nature of the love-fire.

Now, however, it is not as if some foreign will of a wrath-fire enters into the natural soul to take it over; rather, it is the soul's own fire, of which the soul is a fundamental essence. The wrath of its own nature becomes hardened by the contraction of its own bitterness <note>Original: *Eckels*. In Böhme's vocabulary, this refers to a sharp, contracting, or repulsive quality in the first stages of nature.</note> in the three first origins of nature—namely **Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury** <term>Sale, Sulphure, Mercurio</term> <note>These are the three alchemical principles (Tria Prima). Here, Böhme uses them metaphorically to describe the soul's inner "chemistry": Salt is contraction, Sulfur is friction/fire, and Mercury is the restless movement or "spirit" of the two.</note>—as in the quality of the dark world, which becomes manifest in the false desire, and then also from outward accidents, which the false lust from the fiery desire takes into itself. Just as Adam and Eve became hardened and poisoned by the introduced serpent-venom <note>Original: *Schlangensucht*. This refers to the "serpent’s sickness" or "longing" injected by the Fall.</note>, so that immediately this same introduced poison also began to hunger for a quality like itself. Then one bitterness gave birth to another, as the Apostle Paul says of it: That it is not he in the Spirit of Christ who wills and works sin, but sin in the flesh—that is, the sin which is in nature as the manifest wrath of eternal and temporal nature—and that which introduces bestial lust into the flesh, that is what does it.

So understand me rightly now: The most inward ground in man is **Christ**, not according to the nature of man, but according to the Divine quality in the heavenly essence, which He has newly born; and the second ground of nature is the **Soul**—understand the eternal nature, in which Christ manifested Himself and which He took upon Himself; and the third ground is the **Created Man** made from the mud of the earth <term>Limo der Erden</term> <note>Latin *limus*, meaning the slime, mud, or clay from which Adam was formed.</note>, with the stars and the four elements.

In the first ground, which is **Christ**, is the working life in Divine love. And in the second ground is the natural fire-life of the creaturely soul, wherein **GOD** calls Himself a "jealous God." And in the third ground lies the creation of all qualities, which in Adam stood in the "temperature" <note>In Böhme’s writing, "temperature" refers to a state of perfect balance where no single element or "quality" dominates another.</note> but fell apart during the Fall.

<column-break/>

In the first ground is **GOD JEHOVAH**; He gave the people—who in the beginning were His—to the name and manifest power of **JESUS**, as Christ says in John 17: *Father, the people were yours, and you have given them to me, and I give them eternal life.* Originally they stood in **JEHOVAH**, in the Father's quality; now they stand in the Son's quality, according to the inward ground of the Kingdom of Heaven. For the inward ground is the inner Heaven; it is the **Sabbath**, which is Christ, whom we should hallow—that is, rest from our own will and works, so that the Sabbath of Christ may work in us.

The other ground is now the kingdom of eternal nature, according to the Father's quality, wherein **GOD'S** wrath and the dark world are understood, over which **GOD** has set His Son as Judge. For Christ says in Matthew 28: *All power in heaven and on earth has been given to me by my Father*; in those words, the judgment of all things is also comprised.

20. **Question:** We have heard the judgment upon the serpent so far; but what judgment did GOD speak over the woman?

**Answer:** To the woman He said: **"I will create much pain for you when you become pregnant; you shall bear children with pain, and your will shall be subject to your husband, and he shall be your master."** We have revealed above how man would have propagated before the Fall, and how the **magical birth** <note>Böhme uses 'magical' to mean a spiritual, non-physical process of the will and spirit.</note> would have occurred: namely, not through a separate exit from Adam’s body as it happens now, but just as the sun shines through water without tearing it. In that way, the spiritual body would have gone forth as the birth, and in going forth would have become substantial without effort or distress. It would have happened in a great richness of joy and well-being, in the same way that the two seeds of man and woman receive a joyful sight in their **union** <term>Conjunction</term>.

The magical pregnancy and birth would have been like that: a virginal image, entirely perfect like the first. But because the **Womb of Venus** <term>Veneris Matrix</term> <note>Böhme uses this alchemical/astrological term to describe the feminine creative principle or the "mother" of physical form.</note> was later taken from Adam and formed into a woman, birth now must happen through anxiety, pain, woe, and distress.

21. **Question:** But why should her will be subject to the man?

**Answer:** Because she sprouted from the man's will; Eve was the half of Adam, acting as the part in which Adam was meant to love and propagate <note>The original German *schwängern* usually means to impregnate, but in Böhme's mystical biology, it refers to the original human's ability to bring forth life from within themselves before the division into two sexes.</note> himself. That part was taken from him in his sleep when he failed to withstand the trial, and it was formed into a woman. Therefore, when Adam saw her, he said: "She shall be called Woman <note>Original: *Männin*, a feminine form of 'Man,' reflecting the Hebrew *Ish* and *Ishah*.</note>, because she was taken out of Man." Adam possessed the **Tincture** <term>Tincture</term> <note>In Böhme’s alchemy, a 'Tincture' is the essential spiritual "dye" or quality of a being; the fire-tincture represents the active, testing force of the soul.</note> of fire, serving as the sharp testing of all beings. And the woman has the watery **Tincture**; her **Matrix** <term>Matrix</term> <note>The 'Matrix' refers to the feminine creative principle or womb of nature.</note> is like the Moon. Just as the Moon longs for the Sun, so the woman longs for the man and his heart. The woman's blood could not have reconciled the wrath of GOD; only the man's blood could do so, for the woman belongs within the man, and in the Kingdom of GOD, she will be a **Masculine Virgin** <note>This refers to the "Androgyne," the restored state of humanity where the male and female spiritual principles are perfectly united, as Böhme believed Adam was before the Fall.</note>, just as Adam was. There will be no "woman" there; the woman finds salvation within the covenant of the man, for the covenant was made for the sake of the man—that is, for the sake of the **Masculine Virgin**—so that she might be reconciled again.

Therefore, Paul says: *The woman is saved through childbearing, if she remains in faith, love, and holiness, with modesty.* And not only through that, but also within the man's covenant, for she is a part taken from Adam. For this reason, every woman should be subject to the man, and he shall be the master.

GOD also gives the man **Virginal Wisdom**; he is to govern the woman, not as a tyrant, but as his own life. He should love his wife as his own body, for she is his flesh and body, an image formed from him, his helper, and his rose-garden. Although she may be earthly and weak, he must know that he himself is the cause of this, and he must bear with her in patience, never allowing his wrath to turn into violence or destruction. Likewise, the woman should know that she finds salvation in the man’s covenant and blood, and that she is Adam's and the man's rib and

<column-break/>

**Tincture**, belonging to the man. She should be humble, serving the man as a limb serves the body; thus the woman should serve the man and love him as herself. Her love should be cast entirely into him, for in this way she attains the heavenly Virgin with Divine Wit <note>Original: *Witze*, meaning spiritual understanding or wisdom.</note> and the Spirit of the Covenant. But to the living virgins and men without wives, as well as to widows, it was said that they have the Covenant of Christ as their spouse. Before Him, they should be modest and humble, for Christ is the man's bride—His modest Virgin, whom Adam lost—and He is also the bridegroom of the single virgins and widows. For His manhood is their manhood, so that they may appear before GOD as a **Masculine Virgin**. For our true image is now born in the will and in faith; wherever our heart and will are, there also is our treasure and our true image.

Therefore, guard yourselves against fornication and false love, for the true image is destroyed by them. Fornication is the greatest vice that a person works within themselves. Other sins pass out of the person into a figure; but the "harlot" <note>Referring to the spiritual stain of promiscuity.</note> remains standing within him, for he works a false image in which the image of GOD is not recognized, but rather a beastly one. Let this be told to you, O Man: such a great abomination lies behind this that Heaven itself recoils from it with its **Imagination** <term>Imagination</term> <note>To Böhme, 'Imagination' is the creative power of the mind to "form" spiritual reality.</note>. Heaven does not easily enter into a beastly imagination, and this is why so many beastly people are born.

Because man had entered into the inequality of properties with his desire—which had also taken hold of him in such a beastly, hard, tangible, and sensitive essence of enmity within the **Phantasia** <term>Phantasia</term> <note>The realm of shadows, delusions, or the false "imagination" of the fallen world that replaces the true divine image.</note>—as in the four-elemental coarseness of heat and cold, and also into the **poison-torment** <note>Original: *Gifft-Quaal*. For the **Temperature** of the single Holy Element does not belong to inequality; rather, the four elements belong to it. Therefore, the curse is the boundary of separation, so that the impure may not enter into the pure; for the curse is nothing other than a fleeing of the Good, such that the single Element withdraws into itself and has hidden itself from the essence of wickedness.

...or a hellish or beastly one; all of this shall be tested in the fire of GOD. And as the **Essence** <term>Ens</term> <note>Original: *Ens*. And just as mercury evaporates in the fire, so too does all the godless work of the Serpent and the Devil, which has been impressed into us from the dark world and the devil’s desire. If a person during this time, through earnest faith and Divine desire, has impressed the Divine **Essence** <term>Ens</term> into themselves (meaning, through the holy man of the soul) and introduced it into the mortal part from the **Earthly Clay** <term>Limus</term> <note>Original: *Limo der Erden*. So too shall be the dissolution of man’s body from the earth.

Thus we now understand here the body of sickness, and also the Physician. For when the heavenly essence faded and was captured by the earthly, like gold in lead, the outer **Constellation** <term>Geſtirn</term> <note>Original: *Geſtirn*. Böhme uses this term to describe the complex of astral and cosmic forces that govern the physical world and the fallen human mind.</note> awoke in the body. Refers to the seat of the emotions, will, and thoughts—the 'disposition' of the soul.</note> (which is also a magical constellation) is governed, as is the body. It is thereby led into foreign desire and lust, from which it becomes sick and plagued; and each introduced essence—both through food and thoughts or grief—torments or sickens the other. As is plain to see, man torments and sickens himself most of all in the astral mind with desire, and plagues himself for that which he cannot obtain, which is not revealed in his constellation, and which his constellation cannot

grasp or accept. Over this very thing, the false, introduced desire from the foreign constellation plagues itself and sickens itself day and night. From this arises great Greed, because man desires such things and introduces into his constellation that which is a harmful poison and plague to him; and yet, with foreign matter, he can create nothing fixed or permanent within himself that may endure in eternity. Everything that one’s own constellation (as the true constellation of life) impresses into itself from a foreign constellation is false and an aversion, from which Enmity (as the great Envy in Nature) arises, so that the human mind seeks to rule over a foreign essence. And if this cannot be achieved, then that same foreign, introduced essence burns within him in the manner of a spirit, like a poisonous, hungry fire of envy, which begrudges another that which it wishes to possess itself. And if it happens that he may draw it to himself or possess it through the **Serpent’s Cunning** <term>Schlangen-Liſt</term> <note>Original: *Schlangen-Liſt*. The deceptive, ego-driven cleverness that replaced divine wisdom after the Fall.</note>, it still has no fundamental seat in his true constellation of life, for he is not capable of it. The false desire, however, sets it up above itself as a king and parades with it like its own god, who has taken foreign power and sits upon foreign authority. From this arises the pride of wealth and self-attained honors and power; and all of this, in its ground and origin, has arisen from the Devil (through the Serpent’s essence), who also entered into foreign desire with his free will from his own essence. Thereby, he introduced and awakened within himself hellish torment and sickness (with foreign essence), so that his constellation of life was pulled apart, departed from **Equality** <note>Original: *Gleichheit*. A state of perfect, divine balance where no single quality dominates another.</note>, and entered into a magical property. The same happens to fallen man.

# Chapter XIII.
## How GOD cast Man out of Paradise. And how GOD guards Paradise.

### 1. Question.
### What then did GOD do with poor fallen man?
### Answer.

When GOD the Lord had pronounced the judgment upon Adam and Eve because of their earthly misery—as well as the toil, sorrow, and heavy burdens they would have to bear—and had confirmed them as husband and wife, binding them in marriage duty to cling to one another as one body, and to love and help each other as members of a single body, they were then entirely naked and bare. They stood and were ashamed of their earthly image, and especially of their shameful members, and also of the exit of earthly food from their bodies. For they saw that, according to the outer body, their whole being was of a **beastly nature**; heat and cold also fell upon them, and the virtuous image of GOD was extinguished; they were now to procreate in the manner of beasts. Then GOD the Lord, through the **Spirit of this world** <note>Original: *Geist dieser Welt*. In Böhme's thought, this is the *Spiritus Mundi*, the astral and elemental soul of the physical universe that governs all mortal life.</note>, made them garments of animal skins and clothed them through the Spirit of this world, so that they might see that according to this world they were beasts. He taught them how they should seek and reveal the wonders within the Spirit of this world and clothe themselves from those wonders. And here one sees quite clearly how man is not at home in this world, but has entered it as a guest. He did not bring his clothing with him, as do all other creatures who are at home in this world; rather, he must borrow his clothing from the children of the stars and elements. He must cover himself with a foreign garment that he did not bring with him when he entered into the Spirit of this world. With this he now parades like

<column-break/>

a proud bride, thinking himself beautiful therein, yet it is only borrowed from the Spirit of this world, which in its own time takes it back and consumes it; it lends it to him only for a while, then devours it again. And this happens to this end: because the Spirit of this world always seeks the **noble Virgin of the Wisdom of GOD** <note>The "Virgin of Wisdom" or *Sophia* represents the divine image and mirror of God that man lost at the Fall, which the physical world yearns to be reunited with.</note> and knows that she is within man, so that man should seek the great wonders that are within him and bring them to the light. The Spirit always intends to bring the noble **Tincture** <term>Tinctur</term> <note>Original: *Tinctur*. An alchemical term used by Böhme to describe the spiritual life-force or "dye" that can transform base matter into gold, or the soul into a divine state.</note> to light through man, so that Paradise might appear and the Spirit might be rid of earthly vanity. For the holy element always longs to be rid of the vanity of the four elements through those same four elements, and also to be rid of the influence of the **fierce stars** <note>Original: *grimmen Sterne*. Refers to the harsh, conflicting astral forces that cause suffering and strife in the material world.</note>. Therefore, it leads man to seek in such a wondrous form, so that the eternal wonders of GOD may be revealed, all of which will remain as figures in the shadows after the breaking of the world.

Therefore, all arts and wisdom are revealed by GOD through the Star-Spirit of this world in man, so that they may appear in wonder. And to that end GOD created this world: that His wonders might be made manifest. To that end, GOD permitted man to enter into the Spirit of this world, so that He might reveal His wonders through him. But He does not wish for man to misuse this world, but rather to enter back into Him from this world. He wants man to be where He is. Therefore, He immediately showed Adam and Eve their monstrous shape with the beastly clothing, which He put on them through the **Spirit of the greater world** <note>Original: *Geist majoris Mundi*. The Macrocosm or the collective spirit of the universe.</note>. Had Adam only remained in—

# Of the Expulsion from Paradise.

...remain in Paradise; he could have nonetheless revealed the wonders—indeed, even better: for they [men] would have been closer to the angelic form, and such sin and shame would not have been committed as now happens.

But the Spirit of Wrath <note>Original: *Grimmigkeit*. In the author's mystical system, this refers to the harsh, fiery side of God's nature that becomes "wrath" when separated from Love.</note> in the eternal torment <note>Original: *Quaal*. A technical term in this context meaning both a "source-spring" of energy and a painful quality.</note> also wished to be manifest and reveal its wonders, about which not much is to be written; for it is a <term>Mystery [Mysterium] (a hidden spiritual truth)</term> that it is not fitting for us to reveal, even if we recognize it; It remains for the **Time of the Lily**, when the **Rose** blooms, so that the thorns in **Babel** <note>Babel refers to the state of spiritual confusion and the corrupt institutional churches of the time.</note> do not prick us.

When the driver’s <note>Original: *Treiber*. Referring to the taskmaster of this world or the spirit of legalism and oppression.</note> chain breaks, and the thorn-bush burns, one walks more safely from the sting of burning; then may this Mystery well stand in the light, for it is great and wonderful, and reaches into the gates of God the Father. The Rose-branch in the wonder will understand us well, but Babel is not worthy of it; she seeks only thorns and wishes to prick: Therefore we will give the driver no cause, and rather let these Mysteries stand for the children in the **Lily-Rose**; they are white and have the noble <term>Tincture [Tinctur] (the spiritual essence or life-force that transforms matter)</term> in the light; the driver’s brilliance will no longer be so dear, for the guests of the world have it in hand.

->2. Question: Why did GOD cast man<-
->out of Paradise?<-

**Answer.** When GOD had cursed the serpent along with the earth, the **beast-man** was no longer of any use in Paradise, for he could no longer enjoy the fruits of Paradise; so He laid upon him the labor and toil of the world, and drove him out of the garden, and stationed the **Cherub** with the **fiery sword** of judgment before it; so that, when the new-born **Virgin-child** from the woman’s seed should return and enter into Paradise, this Angel with the fiery sword should

<column-break/>

cut off the serpent-beast from it and no longer let it into Paradise.

<margin>Mysterium Magnum 25: 1</margin>
Thus the Fall of Adam is sufficiently recognizable to us, as well as why he could not remain in Paradise, and what Paradise was—which still exists today. It no longer bears Paradisiacal fruit, and we do not have Paradisiacal qualities <note>Original: *Quaal*. See note above regarding "source-springing."</note> and eyes; we do not see it, for GOD cursed the earth for man's sake, so that Paradise no longer greens through the earth; for it has become a Mystery to us, and yet it is still always there, and into that same Mystery the souls of the saints depart when the earthly body separates from the soul. It is in this world, and is also outside of this world, for the torment of this world does not touch it; the whole world would be Paradisiacal if Adam had remained in innocence; but when GOD pronounced the curse, Paradise withdrew; for **GOD’S cursing is a fleeing**: His fleeing is not a moving away, but an entering into another <term>Principle [Principium] (one of the foundational realms of existence: the dark fire, the light, or the physical world)</term>, namely into Himself. The Spirit of God goes out from GOD into the **Essence** <note>Original: *Wesenheit*. The spiritual substance of reality.</note>; but when this essence became earthly and the devil dwelt therein—who was an enemy of GOD—the Spirit of God entered into His own Principle, namely into **Love**, and withdrew from the earthliness: There He now stands opposite man as the **Light of Life**. Whoever now desires to enter into God's Love, he enters with his will-spirit into Paradise; there Paradise greens again in his will-spirit, and his image begins to receive heavenly Essence again, in which the Holy Spirit rules.

Let this be a **pearl** to you, children of men, for it is the true foundation. Whoever seeks and finds it has pure joy in it. It is the **pearl** lying in the field, for which one sold all his goods and bought the pearl, of which Christ speaks.

### Part 3 / Chapter 13.

Thus, the **Cherub** who drove Adam and Eve out of Paradise is also to be recognized by us as the **stern Angel**; he signifies the one who severs the earthly life from Paradise, where body and soul must eventually part.

It is indeed recognizable to us that Adam and Eve were driven away from the place where the **Tree of Temptation** stood, for Paradisal fruit was there, which they were no longer to see or eat; for that which is heavenly does not belong within that which is earthly. The animals were also driven away because of the "evil tree," for otherwise they could not have enjoyed the Paradisal fruit; but from this tree, every animal could eat, for it was earthly. Thus, they had to leave Paradise, for God—through the **Spirit of the Great World** <note>The "Spirit of the Great World" (Spiritus Mundi) refers to the soul of the physical universe or macrocosm, which governs the material realm.</note>—had clothed them in animal skins in place of the heavenly "garment of clarity" <note>Original: *Klarheit*. This refers to the translucent, radiant light-body the author believes humans possessed before the Fall.</note>. He had pronounced the sentence upon them, declaring what their conduct and life in this world should be, what they were henceforth to eat, and how they should nourish themselves in sorrow and misery until they returned to the earth, from which one part of them had been drawn.

<margin>The Incarnation of Christ, Part 1, chapters 6, 17, 20.</margin>
Therefore, the expulsion from Paradise is not to be understood as moving from one physical location to another; rather, the "departure" from Paradise is the **change of their state**, wherein man passed from an angelic and Paradisal life into a foreign, devilish, and earthly life.

**3. Question: How then did God guard the entrance to Paradise?**

**Answer:** When God had thus provided Adam and Eve with an animal-like garment so that their shame was covered and they could defend themselves against the frost, He let them out of the garden and placed the Cherub before it with a naked, hewing sword to guard the way to the **Tree of Life**; and man was now to till the field. Understanding in us poor children of Adam and Eve is so completely sunken that we barely achieve a small glimpse of this at the very end of our final age—of the lamentable

<column-break/>

Fall of Adam and Eve—though we must seek such things very deeply in the **Center of the Light of Life**. For it is a wonderful thing that Moses says: God placed the Cherub before the garden to guard the way to the Tree of Life. Who would understand this if God did not open our eyes? We would merely speak of a guard with a sword, and human reason sees nothing else.

But the **noble Virgin** <note>Referring to "Lady Wisdom" or Sophia, the divine mirror and bride of the soul in the author’s mystical theology.</note> shows us the gates: how we must enter Paradise again through the sharpness of the sword. However, the sword cuts the earthly body cleanly away from the **holy element**; then the "new man" may enter Paradise on the path of life. And the sword is nothing other than the realm or the **Gate of Wrath** <note>Original: *Grimmigkeit*. This is the harsh, fiery "dark" side of nature that exists when not tempered by divine light.</note> in the anger of God, through which man must penetrate—through fierce death and through the **Center**—into the "other principle," into the Paradise of the holy element before God. There, fierce death cuts away the earthly body (as the four elements) from the holy element. And the guardian of the garden is the Cherub, the "cutter-off" of the **starry-torment** <note>Original: *Sternen-Quall*. In the author's unique vocabulary, *Qual* can mean both "source-spring" and "torment." It refers to the conflicting influences of the stars and planets on the human soul.</note>, who preserves the four elements for a time and then breaks them, severing them from the soul with his bitter sharpness, and then he himself passes away with his sword. He stands here in the way so that we cannot reach the Tree of Eternal Life; he is in the middle and does not let us into Paradise. The "closed garden of Eden" is our **earthly flesh**—that is the fence around the garden.

Now, if anyone wishes to be in the garden, he must penetrate through the sword of death. Although **Christ** has broken the sword, so that we can now enter much more easily with our souls, there is still a sword before it. But for the one who finds the way, it does not cut very much, for it is blunt and is bent aside; as soon as the soul enters the gates into the Center, it is already helped by the noble Knight, Christ.

This book had seven seals of the seven spirits of the birth of GOD; he took it and opened it, while the elders fell down before him and worshipped the slain Lamb, giving praise and honor to him who sat upon the throne, because the **Hero of the house of Israel** had overcome. The seven golden candlesticks are his humanity; the seven stars are his divinity, for the Divine Birth exists within itself in a sevenfold form, as was mentioned in the beginning in the first four chapters of this book.

Thus, **Moses** has a veil <note>Original: *Deckel*. This refers to the veil Moses wore to hide the radiance of his face from the Israelites (Exodus 34).</note> before his eyes. If you wish to look him in the face, you must only place **Christ**, your Knight, before you, so that he may lift the veil for him. Then you will see that Moses does not have horns <note>A reference to a common historical mistranslation of the Hebrew word for "radiant" as "horned" in the Latin Vulgate Bible.</note>, but is a patient lamb, firmly bound to the death of Christ. You will see that his veil was the closed book, so that we might not recover until the Hero came and broke its seven seals through his entrance into death. Then the veil was taken away, and in the book stood the **Holy Gospel** of the Kingdom of GOD: may the dear Knight **JESUS Christ** read that to us.

Namely: the Angel with the sword is the true **Exterminating Angel**, who carries death and life in his sword; he has GOD’S love and wrath within it. When a person dies in this world, they come before the gates of Paradise, before this Angel; there the soul must pass through this judgment. If the soul is captured in GOD’S wrath, it cannot pass through this judgment. But if it is a **Child of the Virgin**, born of the **Woman’s Seed** <note>The "Woman's Seed" refers to the promise in Genesis 3:15, interpreted here as the spiritual nature of Christ born within the believer.</note>

In Böhme's vocabulary, *Ente* refers to the inner essence or being.</note>. Thus, the soul is then an Angel of GOD and serves him in his temple, in Paradise, and waits for the Day of Judgment—the resurrection of the external body. When this Angel with the fiery sword separates the earth from the curse, then the true human body will return, for it must also pass through this sword, and the sword will cut away its "animal," so that it may be a human alone, and no longer an animal.

To the earthly man, the words of Moses regarding this mystery are entirely hidden. # Chapter XIV.
## Concerning the Procreation of Humanity after the Fall.

**1. Question.**
We have seen from all of this so far: Firstly, what man was before his Fall : Secondly, what he became through the Fall : Thirdly, how he lives as a poor stranger outside of Paradise between Heaven and Hell in anxiety and distress : Fourthly, how he is on the one hand poisoned by sin and the ruin arising from it, but on the other hand is called back to fellowship with GOD by the working Word of promise through a true change of mind and living faith. It follows now to investigate how man procreated himself in such a state, both according to sin and according to the Word of promise?

**Answer.**
**T**he procreation and multiplication of humanity in general is spoken of

<column-break/>

<page-num>898</page-num>
appeared in the fiery sword of flames within the bush / and who led Israel out of Egypt / and went before them in a pillar of fire / and by day in a pillar of cloud; Who gave them the Law in fire / and finally, with Joshua—as the fire-image of him who was to be born out of the fiery sword—led them into the land of Israel.

This Fire-Angel turned his inner light outward / and revealed himself in Christ’s person in humanity / whereby Christ / as the holy anointing oil of the deepest hidden love / transformed the Fiery Sword of the Angel into a Sword of Love / and a holy government. And that is the true Cherub / who drove the false Adam out of Paradise / and who leads back the **Virgin-Child** <note>In Böhme’s theology, this represents the "new man" or the spiritual soul born of grace.</note> newly born from Adam in Christ; and there is no other foundation or understanding for it.

### 2. Question. What then is sin, properly speaking?

**Answer.** Nobody knows what night is who has never seen any daylight; likewise, nobody knows what sin is who does not have grace within themselves, and nobody knows what grace is who does not feel what sin is. If we were to call to mind the horror and great sins before GOD within man—which we have inherited from our first parents—we might well never be joyful again in this world, if the spirit of this world did not plunge us into a foolish **shadow-boxing joy** <note>Original: *Spiegelfechter-Freude*, referring to a deceptive, illusory joy or "tilting at mirrors."</note> in our prison: or else, if **rebirth** <note>Original: *Wiedergeburt*, the process of spiritual renewal.</note> did not so often greatly gladden us by setting us free from this prison. For indeed, in this life we find nothing but vain horror, sin, distress, and death, and we hardly attain a glimpse of eternal joy in this life.

Now the **mind** <term>Gemüthe: In Böhme's thought, the "Gemüthe" is the deep seat of the soul's will, desire, and consciousness.</term> says: What then is sin? Or how is it sin? Why does GOD have a loathing for the being that He has created? See, you child of man, before GOD there is no sin in heaven; sin is in you alone, and sins separate us and our GOD from one another. Otherwise, everything is **stable** <term>fix: Derived from the Latin "fixus," meaning established or consistent within its own nature.</term> and good in its own essence. The kingdom of the hells and of the wrath is good in itself according to its own region; it does not inflict any martyrdom or woe upon itself, but rather its woe is its own birth and the rising up of its torment; it desires nothing else. Likewise, the kingdom of this world is also **stable** <term>fix</term> and good for itself; it also inflicts no woe upon itself, but rather the rising up of the elements—such as the igniting, the heat, cold, air, and water—is its growth and flourishing, and does nothing painful to itself within itself: It also has no trembling or fear within itself.

Only man, who has proceeded from another **principle** <term>Principio: A foundational realm of existence or source of being.</term>, has in

<column-break/>

these two **principles** <term>Principien</term> woe, distress, lamentation, and trembling; for he is not in his fatherland, and these two **principles** <term>Principia</term> can never reach his fatherland. Therefore, the poor soul must so squeeze and press itself that it may reach back into its fatherland; it must go again through the gates of the deep anguish of death; it must burst through two kingdoms, and here it is stuck between the door and the hinge, and is always **infected** <note>Original: *inficiret*, meaning tainted or corrupted.</note> with those things that hold it back and squeeze it greatly; it is stuck as if in a press. If it presses toward GOD, the devil holds it on one side by a bond, and the world on the other side by a bond, and they strike at it; the devil ignites it with grimness and wrath—that is a torment and sin that cannot reach the kingdom of GOD. And the world leads it into pride, greed, and fleshly lust, so that the soul's **essences** <term>Essentien: The inner vital powers or spiritual "substances" of the soul.</term> become full of the fleshly will. For the will of the mind draws these things into the soul; thus the soul becomes entirely impure, swollen, and dark from that which has been drawn in, and cannot reach the light of GOD. Its **essences**, which it should adapt into GOD, cannot do so, for they are too coarse and cannot enter the light. It does not ignite therein. Only when the gates of the deep have been burst asunder do the **essences** press out into freedom, out of the darkness. But if the mind is filled, it cannot do this; then terror, fear, trembling, and despairing of the kingdom of GOD begin, and make for the soul a vain torment.

Also, you should know how it is sin before GOD: you have within you the **element** <note>Böhme refers to the "Pure Element," the spiritual substance of the heavenly world.</note>, which is a delight before GOD. Now, when you rage and storm so with the torment of hell, you touch the **element** and awaken the wrath to go forth; it is just as the devil did when he stirred up and ignited the wrath in the **Fiat** <term>Fiat: The Latin "Let it be," referring to God's creative command.</term>, from which the wrath gave birth to the earth and stones. You sin all the way into heaven before GOD. Concerning this, the prophets lamented in many places that the

the disobedient people offended their GOD; although it does not cause Him pain within Himself, His wrath—according to the **first Principle** <term>Principle: In Böhme's cosmology, the "First Principle" refers to the dark, fiery source of strength and wrath, which must be overcome by the Light of the Second Principle.</term>—is ignited in the **gates of the deep** <note>Original: *Thoren der Tieffe*, referring to the fundamental spiritual dimensions or "centers" where the soul resides.</note> where the soul stands, and it is a sheer abomination before Him.

See, everything that you let into your **mind** <term>Gemüthe: The deep seat of the soul's will and desires.</term>, if your soul is not united in GOD so that it stands in faith and confidence upon Him, then everything you do is sin to you; for you lead an earthly mind into the gates of the deep, where the Spirit of GOD moves, and you unite with the **Element** <note>Meaning the pure, spiritual "Fifth Element" or heavenly substance that exists before God.</note> which is before GOD.

<margin>Principle 17. 72 ----- 78. <note>Refers to Böhme's work "The Three Principles of Divine Essence," Chapter 17, paragraphs 72 to 78.</note></margin>
From this it is easy to judge that the cause of why this or that is sin is not to be sought in GOD; for in GOD, in and for Himself, nothing is sin. But when something is sin, it becomes sin in man, who introduces himself into a **foreign image** <note>The "foreign image" is the distorted, earthly identity taken on after the Fall, replacing the divine image.</note> through evil desire, and thus turns away from the communion of GOD through a perverted mind. A thing that is "One" has neither commandment nor law; and where there is no law, there is no sin, for sin originates from a **contrary will**.

Thus we must consider the enmity against GOD; GOD is one and good, outside of all **anguish** <term>Quaal: Often translated as "torment" or "pang," Böhme uses this to describe the restless, driving force of existence or "source-spirits."</term>, and even though all anguish is in Him, it is nonetheless not **manifest** <note>Original: *offenbar*. In Böhme's thought, God contains all possibilities, but in His "Goodness," the harsh or dark qualities remain hidden or "swallowed up."</note>. For the Good has swallowed up the evil or the contrary and holds it in check within the Good, as if it were a prisoner, where the evil must be a cause of life and light, but not manifest; rather, the Good "dies away" to the evil, so that it may live in itself within the evil without anguish or sensation. Love and enmity are but one thing, but each dwells in itself, which makes two things: Death is the boundary-mark between them, and yet it is no death, except that the Good dies away to the evil, just as the light of a fire has "died" to the **anguish of the fire** <note>The light comes *from* the fire but does not feel the fire's heat or pain; it is a different "state."</note> and feels the fire no longer.

Thus we are now to fathom sin in human life. For life is one and good, but if a different anguish than the "good"

<column-break/>

is within it, then it is an enmity against GOD; for GOD dwells in the highest life of man. Thus, nothing "ungrounded" can dwell in a "grounded" thing: For as soon as the right life awakens anguish within itself, it is no longer like the **Abyss** <term>Ungrund: The "Groundless" or "Abyss"—the absolute, nothingness-like freedom of God before any creation or manifestation.</term> in which there is no anguish; immediately the one separates from the other. For the Good or the Light is as a "Nothing"; but if "Something" enters into it, then that same "Something" is different from the "Nothing," for the "Something" dwells in itself, in anguish; for wherever "Something" is, there must be an anguish which makes and holds that "Something."

Thus we must consider love and enmity. Love has only one anguish and will: it desires only its own kind, and not many things. For the Good is only one, but the anguish is manifold; and whichever human will desires "much," that will introduces the **anguish of multiplicity** into the "One" (wherein GOD dwells). For the "Something" is dark and obscures the light of life; and the "One" is light, for it loves itself, and there is no desire for anything more.

Therefore, the will of life must be directed into the "One" (as into the Good), so it remains in one anguish. But if it **imagines** <note>Original: *imaginiret*. To Böhme, "imagination" is the soul's power to "image" or form itself into a specific desire or state of being.</note> into another anguish, then it becomes pregnant with the thing for which it lusts. And if that same thing is without an eternal ground, in a fragile root, then it seeks a root for its preservation so that it may remain; for all life stands in **magical fire**, and so every fire must have **substance** <note>Original: *Wesen*. The "fuel" or being that allows the spiritual fire to burn.</note> in which it burns. Now, it must make for itself a substance according to its desire, so that its fire has something to consume. Thus, no fire-anguish can subsist in the "free fire," for it cannot reach that, as it is only a "self-thing" <note>An "Eigenes" or a thing of self-will, separated from the universal whole.</note>.

Everything that is to subsist in GOD must be rid of its own will; it must have no "self-fire" burning within itself, but GOD's fire must be its fire. Its will must be united in GOD, so that GOD's and man's will and spirit are only **One**.

...whoever is one <note>Original: *nes ist*, completing the word *wer-nes* or similar from the previous page's catchword *wer*.</note>. For that which is **One** does not oppose itself, because it has only one will; wherever that will goes, or whatever it does, it is one with itself. A single will has only one **imagination** <term>Imagination: In Böhme's thought, this is not just "fantasy" but the creative power of the soul to form itself into what it desires.</term>; therefore, the imagination only creates or desires that which is like itself. We must also understand the **contrary-will** <note>Original: *Wider-Willen*, the state of a will that has turned against the divine unity.</note> in this way. God dwells in all things, and nothing perceives Him unless it is one with Him. But if something goes out from the **One**, then it goes out from God into itself, and becomes something other than God, thereby separating itself. There, the **Law** arises—the requirement that it must either go out of itself again and return to the One, or remain separated from the One.

In this way, it can be known what sin is, or how it becomes sin: namely, when the human will separates itself from God into a **selfhood** <note>Original: *Eigenes*, meaning a state of selfish independence or "own-ness."</note> and awakens its own fire. When it burns in its own **torment** <term>Quaal: Often used by Böhme to describe the agonizing "restlessness" of the soul when it is focused only on itself.</term>, that same self-centered fire is not capable of receiving the Divine Fire. For whatever the will enters into and wishes to possess as its own, that is a foreign thing within the one will of God; for all belongs to GOD, and nothing belongs to the human self-will. But if man is in GOD, then all is also his.

Thus we recognize that **desire** is sin; for it lusts to move from the One into the many, and leads the many into the One. It wishes to possess, and yet it ought to be **will-less** <note>Meaning a state of "Gelassenheit" or yieldedness, where one has no selfish desires.</note>. Through desire, a "being" or substance is sought, and within that substance, the desire ignites the fire. Now, every fire burns according to the quality of its substance. Thus separation and enmity are born, for Christ says:

> He who is not with me is against me, and he who does not gather with me scatters. <note>Original: Quote from Matthew 12:30.</note>

For such a person gathers outside of Christ, and whatever is not with Him is outside of GOD.

Thus we see that **avarice** is sin, for it is a desire outside of GOD. And we also see that **pride** is sin, for it wishes to be its own master and separates itself from GOD as the One. For whatever

<column-break/>

wishes to be in GOD must walk in Him within a single will. Since we are only **One** in GOD, though in many members, it is an act against GOD when one member withdraws from another and makes a lord of itself, as pride does. Pride wishes to be lord, and GOD alone is LORD. Now there are two lords, and one separates from the other. Therefore, everything is sin and a **contrary-will** that the desire possesses for its own, whether it be food or drink; if the will **imagines** <note>Directs its inner focus and longing.</note> into these things, it fills itself with them and ignites their fire. Then another fire burns within the first, which is a contrary-will and an error. Therefore, a **new will** must grow out of the contrary-will, which yields itself back into the single unity; and the contrary-will must be broken and killed. 

And here we must consider the **Word of GOD** that became man; if man places his desire into that Word, he departs from the torment of his own fire and is **born anew** in the Word. Thus the outgoing will dwells in GOD, while the first will remains in desire, in error, and in multiplicity. Therefore, the multiplicity must break apart with the body and die to the outgoing will; then the outgoing will is recognized as a **new birth**. For it takes everything back into itself within the One—but not with selfish desire, but with its own love, which is united in GOD, so that GOD may be **All in All**, and His will may be the will of all things; for in GOD there exists an eternal will.

Thus we find that evil must serve life for the sake of the good, provided the will departs from evil and enters into good again; for the **wrath** <term>Grimm: The fierce, dark energy of the first principle of nature, which provides the "fuel" for the light.</term> must be the fire of life. But the will of life must be directed in struggle against itself, for it must flee from the wrath and not desire it. It must not want the desire, which nevertheless desires its fire and must have it. This same will, which flees from earthly desire, does not arise from the earthly fire. No! It is the soul-fire-will, which is imprisoned and covered by earthly desire; it does not want to remain in earthly desire but wants to go into its **One**, into GOD, from whom it originally sprang. But if it is held captive in earthly desire, it is locked in death and suffers **torment** <term>Quaal: Often used by Böhme to describe the agonizing "restlessness" or "birth-pangs" of the soul when it is focused only on itself.</term>; this is how sin is to be understood.

### Six Points, page 82. § 2...32.

When the soul imagines into the **complexion** <term>Complexion: In the 17th century, this referred to a person’s temperament or the balance of their bodily humors.</term> and eats from it (that is, accepts all impressions just as they come to it through the complexion) and turns away from God’s will, it acts according to the nature of the complexion; it accepts everything that the spirit of the Great World <note>Original: *Geist der grossen Welt*, referring to the Macrocosm or the external universe.</note> introduces into the complexion through its imagination; it gazes foolishly in the desire of the complexion at all external beings, at all that the world does, in words and works; the desire of the complexion carries such things into the soul-fire, and there the soul-fire burns.
