### Complexions § 20. 21.

As for the third point, namely the word of promise in the sower—that is, in man and woman—we have just briefly revealed it. Man, now consisting of body and soul, has within himself active sin and the word of grace, both in his body and in his soul; he sows according to these two active powers, not in a magical or paradisiacal way, but in a beast-like way, through the loathsome organs of reproduction. The man has the **fire-tincture** <term>Tincture: An alchemical term used by Böhme to describe a spiritual essence or life-force that "colors" or animates matter.</term>, in which the soul stands, in his seed; and the woman has the spirit of this world, as the **tincture of Venus** <note>In Böhme’s cosmology, Venus represents the watery, loving, or receptive principle.</note> within her in her **matrix** <note>The womb.</note>. Thus they both sow; neither can sow without the other, for they must both unite again into one body and have one will, pleasure, and desire, just as they were once one; therefore, each desires the other so intensely for mingling. The fire-mother seeks in the water-mother, and the water-mother seeks in the fire-mother; one seeks the child of love in the other, and yet neither finds it without the other.

The conjunction of desire between women and men comes from the two mothers—from the division of Adam, from the two tinctures, from fire and light. These are in themselves much nobler and purer than the flesh, or the **Mercury** <term>Mercurius: The alchemical principle of movement, spirit, and transformation.</term> in the **Sulphur** <term>Sulphur: The alchemical principle of substance, structure, and "burning" desire.</term> of the flesh. They are separated and do not have the true life in themselves, but are the fiery desire for the true life. But if they come together again into one, into being, they awaken the true life in the Mercury; their intense desire is for life. They want to be again what they were in the image of GOD, when Adam was both man and woman; from this arises the intense imagination in the Sulphur and Mercury in the flesh.

3. **Question:** Does the intense drive for procreation then proceed solely from the outer body of the human being?

**Answer:** Man is a Great Mystery <note>original: "gros Mysterium"</note>, in whom all "Centers" reside. When a person is ignited for procreation, the desire proceeds from all three Centers of the will. In the **first Center**, there arises between the parents of the child the attraction and animal desire to mix; this is the outer elemental Center, which is fixed for itself. Secondly, in the **other Center**, there arises the attraction and love for union; even if they were otherwise displeased by the sight of one another, in the act of union the Center of love arises alone for the sake of mixing, for one pure Tincture catches the other, and in the union, the physical mass <note>original: "Massa"</note> receives both.

(Therefore, if only one party feels a loathing for the work, and the Center of love remains closed during the act, then neither pleasure nor fruit can be awakened.) The **third Center** is the powerful fire-strength of the soul, acting as the fire-desire and the Vulcanus <term>Vulcanus: Named after the Roman god of fire; here it represents the internal "blacksmith" or energetic force that sparks life and drives transformation.</term> who awakens both other centers. Each center now sows according to its own property and its own pleasure of "selfhood."

<margin>See The Principles <note>original: "Princ." refers to Böhme's work "The Three Principles of Divine Essence."</note> 15. 30.</margin>

4. **Question:** What then is actually the seed that is sown?

**Answer:** The seed is a Quintessence <term>Quintessence: The "fifth essence" or the purest, most concentrated spiritual core of a substance.</term>, a concentrated power drawn from the whole human being—from both body and soul. This seed possesses a twofold property, both masculine and feminine, and in each of them, all three Principles are at work.

The Principle of Love "in-qualifies" <term>In-qualify: Böhme's term for how different qualities or spirits intermingle and influence one another from within.</term> with the inner Element, and the Element with Paradise, and Paradise is of GOD. The outer seed has its essences which in-qualify with the outer elements and the stars; these in turn in-qualify with the outer Fierceness <term>Fierceness: "Grimmigkeit" in German; the harsh, wrathful, or ego-driven aspect of nature that exists apart from God's light.</term>, and this Fierceness in-qualifies with the abyss of Hell, and the abyss in-qualifies with the devils. Thus, through this mixing, the kingdom of darkness and of the devil is sown along with it, and there arises the third center of great heat <note>original: "Brunst," meaning burning lust or heat.</note>, from which the Fierceness and the "house of flesh" are born. For pure love, which reaches the Element and further into Paradise, has a truly chaste and modest Center and is fixed within itself.

I give you this as a righteous example for diligent and high contemplation: Behold two young people who have now reached the "flower" of the noble Tincture in the Matrix and the Limbus, such that it is ignited. See what heartfelt loyalty and pure love they carry toward each other, where one grants their heart to the other in love, wishing to share it if it could be done without need or death. This is the true Paradisiacal flower, and this flower reaches and in-qualifies with the Element and Paradise. But as soon as they take one another and mix, they infect each other with their "heat," which is born from the outer elements and stars and reaches the abyss; thus, they sometimes become "spider-hostile" <note>original: "Spinnen-feind," a German idiom meaning to be bitter enemies.</note> toward one another. Even if their temperaments <note>original: "Complexion"</note> were noble enough that some love remains, it is nevertheless not as pure and faithful as the first love was before the mixing—which is fiery—while the love in the heat of lust is earthly and cold. For that first love must hold true because it cannot be otherwise, as is seen with many...

And although he did eat, and thus corrupted us, it now happens to him like a thief who was in a pleasure-garden and went out of it to steal; he now returns and wants to go back into the garden, but the gardener <note>The gardener likely represents the Cherub or God's justice guarding the gates of Eden.</note> does not let him in; he must reach into the garden with one hand for the fruit, but the gardener comes and tears the fruit out of his hand, and he must go away in his heat and wrath, and does not return to the garden; and his longing heat for the fruit remains. That is what he received instead of the Paradisiacal fruit; of that we must now eat, and live in the women.

Thus I give you clearly to recognize what a human being is, and what man sows, and what grows in the seed as **three realms**, as mentioned above. If then the three realms are sown in this way, they are first before the Tree of Temptation, where quarreling and great strife begin: There the three realms stand within one another and carry great desire and longing for each other. The element in Paradise wants to keep the pure mind and will, which stands in love in the Tincture of the seed. And the outer elements, as the outgrowth of the Element <note>Böhme distinguishes between the single "Pure Element" of Heaven and the four "outer elements" of our world.</note>, want to have the Element and mix with it; thus comes the external **wrath of the stars**, drawing it together with the external **Fiat** <term>Fiat: The creative "Let there be" of God; for Böhme, it acts as a shaping, magnetic force.</term>, and sets itself therein; thus the internal will in love is darkened with the element and Paradise, and the love goes into Paradise into its **Ether**, and is extinguished in the Tincture of the seed, and goes beneath the heav-

**Answer:** Just as in the depths of this world, through the ignition of the stars, a seed is born out of the body of the dark deep, similar to the creaturely body; so also in like manner, a seed is born in the **flesh-house** <note>The physical body.</note> of man, according to the eternal birth-right of the seven **Source-Spirits** <term>Source-Spirits: The seven fundamental qualities or "forces" (like attraction, expansion, and circulation) that Böhme believes constitute both God and nature.</term>. **First**, there is the whole body of the human being, which is a dark house and has no mobility outside of the qualification of the seven spirits, but is a dark valley, just like the body of the depths of this world. Now in the dark body of man, there is also such a government with the seven spirits, just as in the body of the deep. When the seven spirits qualify according to the birth-right of the Godhead, a seed is born from the wrestling of the seven spirits according to their kind. This same seed has, **firstly**, a mother, which is the dark chamber of the flesh-house; **secondly**, it has a mother, which is the wheel of the seven spirits, after the manner of the seven planets; **thirdly**, it has a mother, who is born in the circle of the seven spirits, in the middle, and is the **heart** of the seven spirits.

This is now the **mother of the soul**, which shines through the seven spirits and makes them alive; and at this place, the seed co-qualifies with the **Heart of GOD**; but only that one in which the light is ignited; but in which the **wrath-fire** burns, there this third mother remains in the...

### The Secret Gate of Women.

Here I must show the foundation to the seeker, for the **Doctor** [of medicine] cannot show it with his **anatomy**, even if he slaughtered a thousand people; he still would not find it. She is as subtle as the tincture, but she has a life, whereas the tincture has none; rather, the tincture is only a rising, joy-filled, and powerful will—a housing for the **soul** and a lovely **Paradise** of the soul, which is the soul's own property as long as the soul clings to **GOD** with its imagination and will.

However, if the soul becomes false, so that her **essences** <term>Essences (Essenitien): The fundamental spiritual "substances" or qualities that make up the soul's inner being.</term> play the hypocrite with the **Spirit of the Great World** and desire the world’s fullness—such as much wealth in "harshness," or much gluttony and drunkenness, always filling oneself—then it goes astray. And in "bitterness," she desires great power: to rise high, to rule mightily, to exalt herself above all things and be seen like a proud bride. And in the "Fire-Source," she desires grim power, igniting the fire and believing herself to be beautiful in this glare, taking a self-satisfaction in herself. 

Then comes the flatterer and liar, the **Devil**, and he enters into the Spirit of the Great World, just as he did in the Garden of Eden. He leads the soul into greed, into gluttony and drunkenness, and always says: "You will not have enough; pull things toward yourself wherever you can get them, so that you always have plenty." And in the bitter form, he says: "You are rich and have much; rise up, exalt yourself, you are greater than other people; the lowly person is not your equal." And in the power of the fire, he says: "Ignite your mind, make it rigid, and bow before no one; terrify the weak so that you are feared, and your power remains; then you can do whatever you want, and everything you desire will fall to your lot. Is that not a glory for you? You are indeed a lord on earth."

**7. Question:** How then is the **seed** generated from the outer man?

**Answer:** The seed from the outer man is generated first from the **animal soul**, in which the earthly tincture resides, according to the "quality" <note>original: "Quall" — Böhme uses this term to describe both a "source-spring" and the internal "torment" or "vibration" of a specific elemental force.</note> of the stars and elements. The animal soul is a powerful hunger, in which the **Fiat** <note>original: "Fiat" — The divine creative command ("Let there be"). In Böhme's view, this force acts as a "spiritual magnet" that pulls form out of chaos.</note> of the third principle resides. This soul, in its ignition, pulls from the whole body—and all its large and small parts—a **Limum** <term>Limum: Literally "slime" or "clay," referring to the biblical "dust of the earth" from which Adam was made, but here meant as a concentrated physical extract.</term> in which lies the whole of humanity, according to all properties and forms of all three principles: in the male seed according to the property of **Fire**, and in the female according to the property of **Light**.

**8. Question:** What then is the **field** into which the man and woman sow the seed?

**Answer:** The field is none other than the **Paradisiacal Rose Garden**, which formerly stood in full bloom when Adam, in the state of his innocence and perfection, directed his fire-desire into the **Divine Virgin**. But when he turned his love-desire away from her and directed his **imagination** into the kingdom of this world, this Rose Garden was taken from Adam and transplanted into the woman, where it has become a field of thistles and thorns. There, Adam sows his corrupted seed and propagates himself according to the flesh in much misery, sin, and malice. Now, this garden is altogether according to the property of the seed and possesses the essences and attractive powers of all three principles within itself: whichever principle's property predominates in the seed, that is what is accepted by the female **matrix** <term>Matrix: The womb, or more broadly, the creative "mold" or "mother-source" that gives shape to a living thing.</term>; and the matrix is awakened and becomes active according to the property of the seed. For within the matrix is every "magical star" of property from both the visible and invisible worlds, and within it are also the properties of both the animal and vegeta-

-ble kingdoms; for this field is a **little world** <note>original: "kleine Welt" — The microcosm, the idea that the human being contains the entire universe in miniature.</note>. Whichever property is awakened within it by the ignition of the fire, the seed becomes "constellated" according to that same property, and the growth rises up in such a property. Thus, it is not only the sower who sows, but the field also contributes its own essences to the process.

**9. Question:** How then is this seed sown into the field?

**Answer:** The seed is sown through the mingling of man and woman, in the same manner and fashion as all animals are accustomed to do. When Adam directed his fire-desire in purity of heart and chastity of mind into the **heavenly Virgin** and was holily wedded to her, it was called a **Union**, for Adam became one spirit with **Sophia**. But as soon as man wished to multiply himself in an animal-like way, it is now rightly called a **Mingling** <note>original: "Vermischung" — A term Böhme uses to contrast the "pure union" of the spirit with the "messy mixture" of fallen physical sexuality.</note>, which is a loathsome abomination before GOD; because in the conjunction of both tinctures according to all three principles, a violent strife arises. This strife already begins in the seed: while it still lies locked within both sexes, in man and woman, the **Turba** <term>Turba: The "Disturber" or "Awakener of Wrath"; the force that disrupts harmony and leads to decay or internal conflict.</term> is already stirred up, as the essence of the seed drives toward a false desire. And even if the spirit tames the body, the imagination still wanders; this causes the **Turba** in the seed. No man can deny this—that many a person is an enemy to their own imagination and wishes it were banished.

These two **tinctures** thus immediately marry into one within the **Sulphur** of the seed and awaken **Mercury**, as the **Master-Builder** of life, so that he may work in the seed and awaken the forms of life in the **Sulphur**. And if the **Mercury** is not powerful enough, he draws the mother’s **menstruum** <note>original: "Menstruum" — In early modern medicine and alchemy, this refers to the nourishing blood of the womb used to "clothe" the spiritual seed with flesh.</note> to himself, leads it into the seed of the **conjunction**, and turns the seed into flesh within the **menstruum**, in which there is nevertheless an evil, mercurial poison and the greatest loathing against holiness and purity—as is sufficiently understood by all lovers of truth regarding what poison lies in the **menstruum**, which even destroys a tender plant of the earth, as is undeniable. So the Spirit of the Great World <note>The "Great World" refers to the Macrocosm — the physical universe and its astrological influences.</note> bows down / and thinks: "The child is mine / I will rule in the **Virgin**" <term>Virgin: For Böhme, this refers to the "Heavenly Sophia" or Divine Wisdom, a spiritual mirror-image that humans lost at the Fall.</term> / and it continually pours in the elements, whereby the **Tincture** becomes full / quite thick; Then the **Tincture** feels a loathing for this fullness / for it is bright / and the **Fiat** with the elements is thickly swollen / of which women can well speak / when they become pregnant / how many feel a loathing for food and drink / and always want something strange to eat. For the **Tincture** feels a loathing for the filling-up of the Spirit of this world with its elements / and wants something else. For this **Virgin** does not taste right to it / and regret <note>original: "Reuel" — likely a variation of "Reue" (regret/remorse).</note> begins within it / and it does not like this / and goes into its **Aether** <note>The subtle, spiritual atmosphere.</note>, and does not return. 
So then the Spirit of the sun / stars, and elements of this world thinks: "Now you are right / the child is yours / the foundation is laid / you shall tend to it: The **Virgin** must be yours / you shall live within her / and have your joy in her / her adornment must become yours" / and so it draws in its great lust through the **Fiat**, which does not yield in eternity / continually to itself / and believes / it possesses the **Virgin**. Then the mother’s blood is drawn into the seed / in which the mother’s **Tincture** resides. And when it now tastes the harsh **Fiat**, seeing that it is sweeter than its own **Essence**, it imagines itself therein with great longing / and becomes strong in the **Tincture** / and wants to create an Adam / and distinguishes the **Matter** / so the spirit of the stars and elements is in the middle / and rules mightily in the **Fiat**.

<column-break/>

Thus the **Matter** is determined according to the Wheel of the Stars / as they stand at that time in their order / understand here the **Planets** / and whichever one is the **Primary** <note>original: "Primas" — the dominant astrological influence at the moment of conception.</note> / that one figures the **Matter** most strongly through the **Fiat** / and the child receives a form of its kind. Thus the **Matter** is divided into limbs through the **Fiat**. 
And when the **Fiat** now draws the mother's blood into the **Matter** in this way / it suffocates / so the **Tincture** of the blood becomes false and quite anxious. For the harsh **Essence**, acting as the **Fiat**, is startled / and all joy departs / which the harsh **Fiat** had gained in the **Tincture** of the blood / and the **Fiat** begins to tremble in the fright <note>original: "Schreck" — a pivotal concept for Böhme where a sudden "fright" or "shock" causes spiritual forces to contract into physical form.</note> within the harsh **Essence**, and the fright departs like a flash of lightning / and wants to flee out of the **Essence** / and escape / but is held fast by the **Fiat**. It is now hard / and tough from the **Essence** / for the **Essence** makes it tough in its harshness / this now encloses the child / that is the skin of the child / and the **Tincture** suddenly flies upward in the fright / and wants to retreat / and yet cannot. For it stands in the fruit of the **Essences** / but stretches itself quickly upward in the fright / and takes the power of all **Essences** with it / there the spirit of the stars and elements is also imagined / and fills itself therein in its flight / and thinks / it has the **Virgin** / and wants to travel along / and the **Fiat** seizes everything and holds it / and thinks / it is the **Word of the Lord** <note>original: "Verbum Domini" — the divine creative command.</note> there in that commotion / it shall create Adam / and strengthens itself in the strong power of the fright / and creates again the higher body, such as the head / and from the hard fright / which is always in the soft / and yet cannot escape / comes the skull / which encloses the upper center / and from the soft (out of the **Essences** of the **Tincture** with the fright into the upper center) the veins and neck are formed / thus out of the body into the head into the upper center. 
Also, all veins in the whole body are formed from the fright of suffocation / when the fright goes out of all **Essences** / and wants to retreat / and the **Fiat** holds it with its strong power.

rough essences [become] angelic <note>original: "Englisch" — in this context, Böhme uses the word to mean "angel-like" (from *Engel*), not the English language.</note> and full of joy / and then her rough essences serve her well / and are more useful and better to her / than if they were all sweet in the original source / in which there would be no strength or power / as there is in the harsh, bitter, and fiery ones. For the fire in the **Essence** <term>Essence (Essentia): The fundamental spiritual substance or "being-ness" of a thing.</term> becomes a gentle light / and is only a burning ignition in the **Tincture** <term>Tincture (Tinctur): A spiritual life-force or "quintessence" that transforms and vitalizes the soul, acting as the medium between the spirit and the body.</term>, and the harsh essence ensures / that she can draw the **Divine Power** to herself / and taste it / for in the essence is the taste in nature; So the bitter essence serves her, for the movable, ascending joys / and good smell and growth / and out of these forms the **Tincture** goes forth, and is the **soul's house** / just as the **Holy Spirit** [goes forth] from the Father and Son / so also the **Tincture** goes forth from the light of the fiery soul / and then from its powerful essences / and compares itself to the **Holy Spirit** / but the **Holy Spirit of GOD** is a degree higher / for he goes forth from the **Light-Center**, entirely in the **fifth form** out of the **Heart of GOD** / at nature's end. Unless / the soul steps into the source of **Harshness** <term>Harshness (Herbigkeit): Also translated as "astringency," this is the first quality of nature—a cold, contracting force.</term> and malice / then there is a whole birth between them / for the harshness stands in the fourth form of darkness / and the bitterness in the fire between the fourth and fifth form.

**14. Question: Can a soul reach the Light of GOD in the gentle spring of Divine Love by its own power?**

**Answer:** Because the soul has now introduced itself, in and with **Adam**, into the spirit of the great world, and set its imagination therein, it has just such a craving in its propagation, so that although there is a secret longing in the soul for the 

<column-break/>

**Virgin**, the soul may not reach the freedom and the light, unless / the **Crusher of the Serpent** <note>A traditional title for Christ, referring to Genesis 3:15.</note> with his virgin-like, tender love blows upon her tinder, and leads the fire-desire away from the earthly state, and draws her into the **little fountain of salvation** [of] **Gentleness** <term>Gentleness (Sanfftmuth): Also translated as "meekness," the soft, yielding quality of divine love that overcomes the harshness of nature.</term>.

For the chamber of the building stands in very great anxiety. And we must remember the original source of the **Being of all Beings** / the eternal birth and root of all things / that in the house of anxiety there is first a single being / and that same being is the mixture of all beings / and has first a will to bring forth the light / and that same will is attractive. For the desire is the attraction of that / which the will desires / and that same will is at first pure / neither dark nor light / for it dwells in itself and is the very gate of **Divine Power** which fills all things. Now the attraction fills the will with the thing / that the will desires / and even though it is pure / and desires only the light / yet there is no light in the dark anxiety / that it could attract / but rather it draws into itself the spirit / or the essences of the stars and elements. Thereby the will is filled with **Divine Power** / and that is all rough and dark. Thus the will is placed into the darkness / this happens in the heart.

Then, when the will stands in the dark anxiety / it conceives for itself again another will to flee from the anxiety / and to bring forth the light. And that same second will is the **Mind** <term>Mind (Gemüthe): The seat of thoughts and disposition, which Böhme sees as arising from the soul's inner tension.</term> / from which the senses go out / not to remain in this anxiety / and the will beholds itself in the essences of **Harshness** / as in the fierce hardness of death / and the **Flash** breaks through the essences of the harsh hardness like a swift flash of lightning / and sharpens itself in the harsh hardness / so that it becomes polished and bright.

carries with it those properties and powers that are internally active in a thing. Thus, the spirit of man takes its origin from the **Fire-Soul**, in the fire-flash of the fourth form, as the point of separation between the first and second **Principles** <note>original: "Principii"</note>, where the light is born. According to the impression the Fire-Soul receives, so it imagines; and as it imagines, so it introduces itself into a substance wherein it qualifies and connects itself with that substance, just as a fire connects itself with wood. Now, according to the nature of this qualifying, so the spirit goes out from that qualification like a flame, containing air, light, smell, etc. If the soul sets its imagination back into the dark **Principle** <note>original: "Principium"</note> of its fierce nature, its ascent is the spirit: harsh, bitter, fierce, and fiery; but if it leads its desire into the kingdom of this world, then the spirit of this world rises up: reason, etc.

When the light shines in all three **Principles**, the noble **Tincture** <term>Tincture (Tinctur): A vital, transformative spiritual essence or "life-blood" that reveals the inner qualities of a being.</term> of all three Principles goes out. It is highly important to note that the Middle-Principle accepts no light from nature; rather, as soon as the darkness is shattered, it appears in high, joy-filled delight—and the noble **Virgin** <term>Virgin (Jungfrau): Divine Wisdom or Sophia, the pure spiritual reflection of God.</term> dwells in that delight, as if living within that very Tincture. The Deity appears to us within man very highly and greatly, for we find it in nothing else in such a way, no matter what thing we observe.

In the first **Principle** <note>original: "Principio"</note> is the fire-flash, and its Tincture is the terrifying light of the Sun, which originates from the eternal foundation, from the first Principle with its root, out of the **Fifth Essence** <term>Fifth Essence (Quinta Essentia): The pure, spiritual quintessence from which the four physical elements are born.</term> through the element most sharply. This could be explained in another place, but is too long for here: It also wishes to remain hidden; he who knows it keeps silent about it, just as with the rising of the stars and planets. For the "crowned little hat" <note>This refers to academic or scholarly pride, specifically those who wear doctoral caps but lack spiritual insight.</note> wants to be right in its schools, though it understands the least in the light of nature. It remains so until the **Lily-Time** <term>Lily-Time (Lilien-Zeit): Böhme's term for a predicted future age of peace and spiritual clarity.</term>; then everything stands open, and the Tincture is the light of the world.

# Of the Propagation of Mankind.

...brings with it those properties and powers that are inwardly active in a thing. Thus, the spirit of man takes its origin from the **Fire-Soul** <note>original: "Feuer-Seele" — in Böhme's thought, the first, fundamental aspect of the soul rooted in divine wrath and energy</note>, in the **Fire-Flash** of the fourth form, acting as the boundary-mark between the first and second **Principles** <note>original: "Principii" — the fundamental planes of existence: darkness/fire and light/love</note>, where the Light is born. Depending on the impression the Fire-Soul receives, so it **imagines** <note>original: "imaginiret" — here used in the sense of "forming an internal image" or "desiring into a form"</note>; and as it imagines, so it leads itself into a being, wherein it **qualifies** <note>interacts with and takes on specific characteristics</note>, and clothes itself with that being, just as a fire clothes itself with wood. Now, according to this qualifying, the spirit goes forth from that interaction like a flame, containing within it the air, the light, the scent, and so on. If the soul sets its **imagination** back into the dark **Principle** of its fierce nature, then its ascending spirit is harsh, bitter, fierce, and fiery; but if it leads its desire into the kingdom of this world, then the spirit of this world—Reason—ascends, and so forth.

When the light shines in all three **Principles**, then the noble **Tincture** <note>original: "Tinctur" — a spiritual life-force or "dye" that gives quality and vitality to matter</note> of all three Principles goes forth. It is highly important to note that the middle **Principle** <note>the realm of Divine Light and Love</note> receives no light from nature; rather, as soon as the darkness is shattered, it appears in high, joy-filled delight, and the noble **Virgin** <note>Divine Wisdom or Sophia</note> dwells within that delight, as if in that very Tincture. The Godhead appears to us in man very highly and greatly, for we find it nowhere else in such a way, no matter what we contemplate.

In the first **Principle** is the **Fire-Flash**, and its **Tincture** is the terrifying light of the Sun, which manifests itself very sharply through the **Element** from the eternal foundation—from the first **Principle** with its root—out of the **Fifth Essence** <note>original: "Quinta Essentia" — the spiritual core behind the four physical elements</note>. This could be explained further in another place, but it is too long for here. It also wishes to remain hidden; he who knows it remains silent, just as with the rising of the stars and planets. For the "capped little hat" <note>original: "gekrönete Hütlein" — a mocking reference to academic or clerical scholars who pride themselves on titles but lack true spiritual insight</note> wants to be right in its schools, though it understands very little in the Light of Nature. It remains so until the **Lily-Time** <note>original: "Lilien-Zeit" — a predicted future era of spiritual peace and enlightenment</note>, when everything shall stand open, and the Tincture shall be the light of the world.

And one sees quite clearly here how the third **Principle** <note>the physical, visible world</note> aligns itself with the first, as they have almost one will. For they proceed from one another; and if the second

<column-break/>

**Principle** were not in the middle, then everything would be one thing. But since we are speaking here of the **Tincture** in life, we wish to draw the true ground from the Light of Nature regarding all three births.

The noble **Tincture** is the dwelling-house of the spirit and has three forms: One form is eternal and unbreakable; the second is changeable, remaining eternal with the saints, but in the ungodly it is changeable and flows into the **Ether** <note>original: "Aether" — the subtle spiritual atmosphere</note>; the third is breakable, as in death.

The first **Tincture** of the first **Principle** is properly the delight in the **Fire-Flash**; that is the source in the **Bile** <note>original: "Galle" — associated with bitterness and the energetic "fire" of the body</note>. This creates a dwelling-house for the **Sulfur-Spirit** <note>original: "Schwefel-Geiste" — Böhme's term for the active, burning principle of the soul's desire</note> (which is the indissoluble **Worm of the Soul** that rules powerfully in the sharp **Essences** <note>original: "Essentien"</note> and moves and carries the body wherever the mind in the other center wishes to go). Its **Tincture** is like the stern and sharp power of GOD; it ignites the whole body so that it is warm and does not freeze, and it maintains the "Wheel in the Terror-Shock" <note>original: "Rad im Schracke" — the dynamic, circular motion of the spiritual qualities as they interact</note> within the **Essences**, from which hearing arises. It is sharp and tests the scent of all things in the **Essences**; it creates hearing, though it is not hearing or scent itself, but rather the **Gate** which lets in good and evil—just like the tongue and the ear. All this is caused because its **Tincture** is grounded in the first **Principle**, and the ignition of life happens in the sharpness, in the breaking-through, through the gates of eternal darkness.

Therefore, the **Essences** of the soul-spirit become so sharp and fiery, and such a sharp, fiery **Tincture** goes forth from the **Essences**. Within this now stand the five senses: 1. Seeing, 2. ### Part 3 / Chapter 14

...heart and also in the head, so that it might everywhere defend and steer the soul. 
We must further consider that when the Terror <note>original: "Schreck" — in Böhme’s system, this is the sudden, vibrating shock or "crack" that occurs when the dark, tense will of the soul is struck by the light of God, leading to the birth of the spirit</note> made its dwelling-place in its strong breakthrough out of the gates of the anxious darkness—at the time when the tongue [spoke]—the Terror had not yet beheld the Virgin <note>original: "Jungfrau" — referring to the Divine Wisdom or Sophia</note>. However, when it looked back into the heart, into the opened darkness, and found it so full of Bliss <note>original: "Wonnesam"</note>, then for the first time did Joy, Bliss, and Loveliness arise within it, and it became Paradise. It did not wish to return to the tongue, but rather into the head, to establish its region there from the source-spring <note>original: "Quall" — a Böhmean term implying both a source (Quelle) and a throbbing, quality-giving movement</note> of the heart.

Therefore, one must not believe everything the tongue says, for it does not reside in the heavenly region like the blissful, lovely Power; rather, it has its region in the Terror and the Flash <note>original: "Blitz" — the sudden ignition of light from the fire of the soul</note>. For the Flash is as near to the hellish region as the Terror, because they are both born in the strict sharpness, within the essences. The tongue speaks lies and truth, whichever spirit arms it, so it "rides": it also frequently speaks lies in high-ranking men; when it is armed by the essences, it rides in Terror, like a rider in his pride.

Since the life's power and spirit of the second Principle <note>original: "andern Principii" — the realm of Divine Light and Love</note> is born in the first origin of the first Principle <note>original: "ersten Principii" — the realm of darkness and fire-energy</note>, as in the gates of the deep darkness—which the will of the Virgin's power shattered in the strict, earnest glance of God's stern might, placing itself in the lovely Bliss—so the essences of the stars and elements immediately pressed in at the glance of life's rising. Yet this happened only after the building of the lovely Bliss. For Bliss is the Element, and the power of the inner Element is the Love of Paradise; the outer elements—those born from the Element—desire to have this from their mother, and the sharp *Fiat* <note>Latin: "Let it be done" — the creative Word of God</note> brings them into the Bliss. There, the light of life is truly kindled, and all essences live in the Bliss,

and the sun of the stars rises in Bliss, for in the beginning of life, each Principle captures its own light.

The first Principle, as the darkness, captures the fierce and swift Fire-Flash <note>original: "Feuer-Blitz"</note> when the re-captured will beholds itself in the harshness of the first will of the attracted darkness, and shatters the darkness in that glance. Thus, the Fire-Flash remains in the first will of the harsh darkness and stands above the heart in the gall, kindling fire in the essences of the heart.

And the second Principle keeps its light for itself, which is the lovely Bliss that appears where the darkness is shattered, within which the gracious power and loveliness arise. From this, the Terror in the strong power becomes so joy-filled and lays down its great "tearing" <note>violent movement</note> into a joy-filled trembling; to this, the Fire-Flash of the first Principle then clings, making it tremble. Thus its source-spring <note>original: "Quall"</note> is loveliness and joy; one simply cannot write it down—blessed is he who experiences it.

And the third Principle <note>the material world</note> keeps the light entirely for itself, which—when the light of life rises—penetrates through the soul’s Tincture <note>the spiritual life-force</note> to the Element, and reaches for the Element. However, it receives nothing more than the solar light, which has gone forth from the *Quinta Essentia* <note>Latin: "Quintessence" — the pure, fifth essence that is the spiritual core of all matter</note> out of the Element. Thus the stars and elements rule in their solar light and power, and qualify <note>interact and co-operate</note> with the soul, bringing many vices and also sickness into the essences, from which gout, racking pains, swelling, and infirmity arise within them, and finally their breaking apart and death.

The gaze goes through wood and stone / through marrow and bone / and nothing can hold it / for it bursts through any kind of thing without tearing the body / everywhere the darkness / and the will is its riding-horse / upon which it rides. (Here one must remain largely silent / because of the devilish **incantation** <note>original: "Incantation" — a reference to the power of the word in magic or spells.</note>: otherwise we would open up much more here / for it is here that the **Necromancer** <note>original: "Nigromanticus" — a practitioner of black magic who manipulates the hidden forces of nature.</note> is born.)

But now the first will in the Mind is from the severe **Anxiety** <note>original: "Aengstlichkeit" — a technical term in Böhme’s system for the contraction and tension within the first principle of nature, before it breaks through into light.</note> / and its gaze in the original source is the bitter / severe fire-flash / in its sharpness / that creates the stir and the sound / and the seeing in the luster of the flash's sharpness / so that the gathered gazes in the thoughts have a light within them / by which they see / when they run like a flash. To this first will in the Mind, it is now not proper to look backward into the **Abyss of Wrath** / in which is the

<column-break/>

severe malice / but rather forward into the **Center of Bursting Forth** from the darkness into the light / for in the light is pure gentleness and humility / and goodwill and friendly desire / also going out from itself with the gathered will / and opening itself with its precious treasury. For in the gathered will toward the birth of light there is no torment of anxiety / but pure desire for love. For the gaze rises up out of the darkness into itself / and desires the light / and the desire draws the light into itself. Thus, out of the anxiety comes an uplifting joy / within it a humble laughter / of a gentle delight / for the gathered will in the light is pregnant / and its fruit in the womb is power / which the will desires to bring forth and to live within / and the desire brings the fruit from the pregnant will before the will / and the will beholds itself in the fruit in an infinite **Love-Number** <note>original: "Liebe-Zahl" — likely referring to a harmonious spiritual proportion or the infinite variety of ways love manifests.</note>: there goes out in the love-number in the beheld will the high **Blessing** <note>original: "Benedeyung" — from "benediction."</note> / wishing well / being friendly / lovely appropriation / the taste of joys / the well-doing of gentleness / and that which my pen cannot write / much rather would the Mind be free from vanity / and live without wavering therein.

These are now two gates within one another: the lower goes into the abyss / and the upper into Paradise / to this now comes the third from the elements with its four outlets / and pushes itself in / with fire / air / water and earth / and its kingdom is the sun and stars / which **co-qualify** <term>inqualiren: a term Böhme uses to describe how external forces or qualities "work into" or interact with the internal spirit of a being.</term> with the first will / and their desire is to fill themselves / to become swollen and great: They draw to themselves / and fill the chambers of the deep / the free and naked will in the Mind: They bring the gazes of the stars into the gates of the Mind / and **co-qualify** with the sharpness of the gaze; the shattered gates of darkness they fill with flesh / and struggle constantly with the first will / from which they have gone out into this region / and surrender themselves to the first will...

### 16. Question: But how does it happen / that so few men reach the Light of GOD and his birth / and thus actually attain the Spirit of GOD?

Answer: Because the **First** and **Third Principle** have the greatest power in man / and man by nature has no other craving for the property of the **Light-World** within himself / than what comes to him from the Third Principle and its government; on the other hand, the wrath in the **Fire-Soul** / and also in the outward part is so much more powerful. Thus man has the qualification according to the property of the dark world as a **Natural Right** / and on the other hand has the light more in possibility than in working / which it cannot reach otherwise / unless it be / that such is blown upon from the light-flaming Heart of GOD / and the spirit rising therefrom / through the mighty **Word of Grace**. Nevertheless, it remains a truth / that one man has a greater possibility / also a greater desire in his soul for the Light of GOD than another / just as one man has more natural understanding than another / which has its ground partly from the qualification of the parents / partly from the stars / and the form of the **Spirit of the World** <note>original: "Spiritus Mundi" — the astral spirit that governs the physical world and human temperament.</note>. For as the great world stood in a birth at the time of the **mixture** <note>Refers to the moment of conception/mingling of seeds.</note> / so it also breathed out a spirit / which breath the essences drew to themselves / and thereafter also shaped the Mind,

Or perhaps you save it until the end, wanting to become a heavenly birth then, even though you have grown throughout the entire time of your life in the wrath of God and in the abyss of hell. No, that is a deception; you are deceiving yourself.

17. <term>Question:</term> Until now, we have considered how the inner core and the marrow of humanity is generated and propagated, both according to the root of the plant—which is the dark fire-soul with its harsh, bitter, fierce, and hot qualities—and according to the inner driving tincture <note>original: *Tinctur* — an alchemical term used here to describe the vitalizing spiritual essence or life-force.</note>, color, figure, essence, and quality. Now it follows that we must also consider the plant according to its external qualification, quality, figure, and growth. Namely, the external man, consisting of an animal soul and a beast-like body, as well as its external life. How then is such an animal soul, and through that soul such a beast-like life, ignited within a human being?

<term>Answer:</term> During the time of the external body, the soul has three mirrors or eyes of all three

<column-break/>

worlds, into which mirrors the soul centers <gloss>centers itself</gloss> itself, and from which it looks out. Into whichever world the soul now leads its will, in that same world it also receives its being as a spiritual body. For that same being becomes food or matter for the burning of the soul-fire. This is why God led the soul into flesh and blood: so that it might easily become free from the essence of the wrath <note>original: *Grimm* — the fierce, raging quality of the dark fire-world.</note>. Thus, for a time, it has its joy in the Sun-mirror and rejoices in the sidereal essence <note>original: *Siderischer Essentz* — the influence or substance of the stars and the cosmic arrangement.</note>. And first, the Light-world stands against it in its right fire, as in the first Principle <note>original: *primo Principio* — Latin for "First Principle," the fiery foundation of nature.</note>. Second, the dark world stands against it in the fire-root; and third, the external elementary world stands in the "star-wheel" <note>original: *Sternen-Rad* — the rotating cycle of the stars and constellations that governs physical time and nature.</note>. There, in between, hovers the great mystery <note>original: *Mysterium*</note> of the soul-fire. To whichever world the soul now attaches and surrenders itself, from that world it receives its being through its imagination. However, because the soul turned itself with Adam into this world and led its imagination into it, its highest desire now stands in the source of the sun and stars. It constantly draws the spirit of the external world—with its essence of the four elements—into itself, and has its greatest joy therein, in which it is a guest in a strange inn; for the abyss stands beneath it, and it is in great danger.

Now external Reason speaks: "But did God not create the soul into flesh and blood, into the external world? How can that harm it?" This external Reason knows no more of the soul's origin than a cow knows of a new stable door; the cow looks at it and it seems strange to her. In the same way, the inner world seems strange to external Reason. It perceives itself only in the external world and strives after that which is...

->Six Points 7. 18. 26.<-

Now because man has become qualifying in such an animalistic life / he has also, as mentioned, reproduced himself in such an animalistic craving, in an animal-like manner. 18. **Question:** What kind of governance is this then?

**Answer:** It is the **governance of the Mind** <term>original: *Regiment des Gemüths* — The internal order of thoughts, dispositions, and the seat of the soul's will.</term>, the senses, and speech; namely, how the inner soul and the mind govern the outer man through the senses and speech. For in the aforementioned rising of earthly life, the "starry quality" in the mother's womb arises just as it does in every animal. Every animal takes its beginning in exactly this way, and its spirit also lives from the stars and elements, and they have their sight from the glare of the sun. In this regard, there is no difference between humans and animals; for an animal eats and drinks, smells, hears, sees, and feels just as well as a human. And yet, there is no **Understanding** <note>original: *Verstand* — In Böhme's terminology, this is higher spiritual reason/intellect, which animals lack.</note> in it, except for that which concerns nourishment and reproduction.

As for what concerns the sensory life in man: see, what are your five senses? In what power do they stand, or how do they come into the life of man? From where does your seeing come, such that you see in the light of the sun and nowhere else? Consider this deeply, if you wish...

### Of the Propagation of Mankind.
#### Xxx 2
<meta>catchword: 19. Fr.</meta>

You may be a naturalist <note>original: *Natur-kündiger* — a scholar of the natural world</note> and boast of the light of nature, but you cannot say that you see by the sun alone. There must also be something within that catches the sun’s light and has an infection <note>original: *Inficirung* — here meaning a reciprocal influence or blending</note> with the sun’s light; only then is the "star" in your eyes. This internal star is not the sun itself, but it stands in fire and water, and its radiance—which catches the sun's light—is a flash <note>original: *Blitz*</note> that testifies from the fiery, harsh, and bitter gall, while the water makes it gentle. Now, here you perceive only the outward aspect, the **third Principle** <note>original: *Principium* — In Böhme’s cosmology, the third principle is the visible, material world governed by the stars and elements.</note>, in which the sun, stars, and **elements** exist; this is the same in all **creatures** in this world. Now, what then creates the sense of hearing, so that you hear what sounds and moves? Would you say it comes from the sound of outward things that ring out? No; there must also be something that catches the sound and **interacts** <note>original: *inqualiret* — to work together with the qualities of another thing</note> with it, distinguishing the tone—whether it is whistled or sung. The outward alone cannot do this; the inward must catch and distinguish the sound. Look, here you find the uprising of life and the **Tincture** <note>original: *Tinctur* — a spiritual "dye" or vitalizing force that transmits qualities between the physical and spiritual realms</note> in which life stands. For the **Tincture** of the "shriek" <note>original: *Schreck* — the sudden "crack" or ignition of life at the moment fire meets light</note>, in the uprising of life and the bursting of the dark gates, exists in sound. It has its gates open next to the fire-flash <note>original: *Feuer-Blitz* — the spark of consciousness or vital energy</note> beside the eyes and catches every sound that rings. For the outward sounding **interacts** with the inward and is decided through the **essences**, and the **Tincture** accepts everything, be it evil or good. In doing so, it testifies that its **essences**, which it brings forth, are not born of the **Godhead**; otherwise, the **Tincture** would not let evil and falsehood into the **essences** of the soul. Thus, we must consider that the sound in the human **Tincture** is higher than that in animals; for the human testifies to and decides all things that sound, and knows where they come from and how they manifest. No animal can do this; it merely gapes at it and does not know what it is. By this, one understands how humanity’s

<column-break/>

origin is from the Eternal: that man can distinguish the thing that has come to be in the out-birth <note>The physical world produced from the spiritual realm.</note> from the Eternal. And from this it is testified that—because all things are set from the eternal Nothing into a "Something" that is graspable—even though it is not a "nothing" but a **source-quality** <note>original: *Quall* — a pun on *Qual* (torment/labor) and *Quelle* (source/wellspring)</note>, it shall stand in its eternal figure after the breaking of the **body** <note>original: *Corporis*</note>, though not in the spirit, since it is not from the eternal spirit. Otherwise, if it were from the spirit, it would also testify to the beginning of all things, just like man, who catches and distinguishes all things in his sound. Thus, the housing of man’s sound, in which the understanding resides, must be from eternity—even though, in the **Fall of Adam**, he placed himself into fragility and great lack of understanding, as will follow. In the same case, we also find this regarding smell <note>original: *Ruche*</note>. For if the spirit did not stand in the sound, no smell of any thing would penetrate the **essences**, for the spirit would be entirely closed off and swollen. But because it stands in the gate of the burst darkness, in the shriek and the sound, all the power of all things penetrates those same gates and **proves** itself against one another. Whatever the **essences** of the spirit’s body desire, it craves and draws into the **Tincture**; then the mouth and hands reach for it and put it into the stomach, into the forecourt of the four **elements**, from which the earthly **essences** of the stars and **elements** eat. Thus, taste is the very same thing: a proving and drawing of the **Tincture** into the **essences** of the spirit; and feeling is the same. If the spirit of man with its **essences** did not stand in the sound, there would be no feeling. For when the harsh **essence** draws to itself, it excites the bitter sting in the fire-flash, which stirs itself—whether by grasping, pushing, or hitting—and so in every touch, the bitter sting in the fire-flash is awakened, and therein lies the stirring, as if in the **Tincture**.

### 19. Question: But from where does speech come to man in his outward life?

**Answer:** Speech, which man possesses and by which he is distinguished from all animals in his outward life, arises from the birth of Mercury <note>original: *Mercurius* — in Böhme’s thought, this refers to the dynamic, expressive power of nature and the "word" that puts things into motion</note>, according to the sixth form of the qualification of the fire-soul. When the mind <note>original: *Gemüthe* — the seat of thoughts, emotions, and the soul's disposition</note> stands in free will, the will looks toward what the "regions" <note>spheres of spiritual or natural influence</note> have introduced into the essences, whether it be evil or good, whether it be fit for the kingdom of heaven or the kingdom of hell. Whatever the "glance" of the mind seizes, it introduces into the will of the mind. Within the mind stands the King, and this King is the light of the entire body. He has five counselors who all sit in the resonance <note>original: *Schall*</note> of the Tincture <note>the spiritual life-force</note>, and each one tests whatever the glance has brought into the will through its "infection" <note>original: *Inficirung* — a blending or reciprocal influence</note>, to see whether it be good or evil. These counselors are the five senses.

First, the King gives it (1.) to the eyes to see whether it is evil or good. Then the eyes give it (2.) to the ears to hear from whence it comes—whether it comes from a right region or a false one, and whether it be a lie or the truth. Then the ears give it (3.) to the nose, to the sense of smell, which must smell that which has been introduced and stands before the King, to see if it comes from good essences or false ones. Then the nose gives it (4.) to the taste, which shall thoroughly test it to see if it is pure or false. For this reason, the taste has the tongue, so that it may spit it out if it is false. But if it is a thought intended for a word, then the lips are the gatekeepers; they must lock tight and not let the tongue out with it. Instead, they should lead the thought into the region of the air, into the bladder <note>meaning the lungs or vocal cavity</note>, and not into the heart, stifling it there so that it is dead. And when the taste has tested it and finds that it does well for the soul’s essences, it then gives it (5.) to the feeling <note>the sense of touch or internal sensation</note>, which shall test what quality it is: whether it be hot or cold, hard or soft, thick or thin. And if it is tolerable, the feeling gives it into the heart before the glance of life, and before the King of the Life-Light. Then the will of the mind looks

<column-break/>

further into the thing, into a great depth <note>original: *Tieffe* — partially cropped</note>, and sees what is within it, and how much of that thing he <note>the will</note> wishes to accept and let in. When it is enough, the will then gives it to the spirit of the soul, as the eternal authority <note>original: *Obrigkeit*</note>, who leads it out from the heart with his strong and powerful resonance <note>original: *Schall*</note> upon the tongue under the palate. There the spirit divides <note>original: *zerscheidet*</note> it according to the senses, as the will has envisioned it, and the tongue distinguishes it in the sound. For the region of the air must here carry out the work through the throat, where the veins <note>or vessels</note> go throughout the whole body and come together, bringing the power of the noble Tincture there. They mix it with the word, to which all three regions of the mind come and mingle themselves with the distinguishing of the word; therein is a wondrous form. For every region wants to distinguish the word according to its own essences. For the sound goes out from the heart, out of all three Principles <note>original: *Principia* — the three foundational realms of Böhme's cosmos: the dark fire-world, the light love-world, and the outward material world</note>.

The first Principle wants to adorn it according to its own severe power and magnificence, and mixes into it thorny grimness, wrath, and malice. But the second Principle, where the Virgin <note>Wisdom or Sophia</note> stands in the center, shoots rays of dear gentleness into it and restrains the first. And if the spirit is ignited in this gentleness, then the word is soft, friendly, and humble, and turns itself toward the love of one’s neighbor. It desires to attack no one with the proud sting of the first Principle, but rather displaces the sting of wrath. It shapes the word out of purity and arms the tongue with righteousness and truth, sending its rays forth in the will of the heart. And when the will receives the lovely, gracious rays of love, it ignites the whole mind with love, righteousness, and the chastity of the Virgin, and the truth of things as they are approved on the tongue by all regions. Thus the tongue, with the five senses, makes it pure, and the precious image of GOD appears.

Likewise, in art and wisdom / and conversely in folly and foolishness.

For according to how the stars—at the time of the child's <term>incarnation</term> <note>original: *Menschwerdung* — the process of the child becoming human or taking on flesh</note>—look upon one another in their present wheel / when the housing of the four elements / and the star-house in the head, in the brain, is built by the <note>original: *Fiat* — Latin for 'let it be'; the creative Word of God</note>, according to that same power is the strength in the brain / as well as in the heart / gall / lung and liver / and according to that, the region of the air adapts itself / and a <term>tincture</term> <note>original: *Tinctur* — a spiritual life-essence or "dye" that gives life its specific quality</note> also rises up to the dwelling of life. form no man / that would be a likeness of **GOD** or figured in the image of **GOD** / but rather an animal in will, custom, and sense: It also has no power or understanding / to be able to figure a likeness of **GOD** / and even if it raises itself to the highest degree in its will according to the likeness of **GOD** / it still only gives birth to a friendly and cunning animal / and nothing more / in man as well as in other creatures. Only the eternal <term>essences</term> <note>original: *Essentien* — the fundamental spiritual building blocks of the soul</note> inherited from Adam upon all men / remain standing with the hidden element in man / wherein the image stands / but entirely hidden / except for the rebirth in water and the Holy Spirit of **GOD**.

All according to how the stars stood in their strength of the quintessence in the wrestling wheel during his incarnation / thus is the star-mind figured in its region; although the hour of a man’s birth changes much / and puts a stop to the first influence / of which I will write hereafter in its place / concerning the birth of man.

### Part 3 / Chapter 14.

Now, as the vision from this mind—whether from this form or others not named here—looks out through the eyes, it begins to project its own form onto every object, according to how its <term>starry region</term> <note>original: *Sternen-Region* — the specific astrological influences dominant in a person's makeup</note> is most powerful at any given time in the heavens, whether for good or evil, in falsehood or truth. This vision is brought before the King; there, the <term>five counselors</term> <note>original: *fünff Räthe* — the five senses: sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch</note> are meant to test it. Yet these counselors are themselves unjust rogues, infected by the stars and elements and stationed within their own worldly region; they now desire nothing more than the kingdom of this world. Whichever way the "starry house" of the brain and heart is most sharply inclined, the five counselors give their advice accordingly and demand it: whether it be for splendor and pride, for wealth, beauty, or high living; **likewise** <note>original: *item*</note> for the art and virtue of earthly things—and no sense desires the <term>poor Lazarus</term> <note>A reference to the biblical parable of the beggar Lazarus and the rich man, symbolizing spiritual humility and the rejection of worldly excess.</note>. In this, the counselors are quickly in agreement. For in their own form, all five are unjust before **GOD**, but according to the region of this world, they are fixed. Thus they advise the King, and the King gives the command to the soul-spirit, which gathers up the essences and reaches out with hands and mouth.

If these are words, he brings them to the palate; there the five counselors divide them according to the will of the mind, and then, upon the tongue, the senses divide them further within the vision. There, the <term>three Principles</term> <note>Böhme’s theological framework: 1. The dark fire-world (wrath), 2. The light-world (divine love), and 3. The outer world (nature/the stars).</note> stand in conflict. The first Principle, as the kingdom of <term>fierceness</term> <note>original: *Grimmigkeit* — the wrathful, consuming aspect of existence</note>, says: "Out with it through strong fire-power, it must be so!" Then the second Principle speaks in the mind: "Stop and look at it; **GOD** is here with the <term>Virgin</term> <note>original: *Jungfrau* — Sophia, or Divine Wisdom, who acts as a moral guide within the soul</note>; fear the abyss of hell." It seizes the region of the air as its spirit, and travels out through the mouth, maintaining the distinctions according to the kingdom of this world.

falsehood, and mere cunning to exalt oneself: one person acts in fire-power, through strength and anger; another in the art and virtue of this world, who is nonetheless a hypocrite and a rogue before **GOD**, holding on until he gets the upper hand; another in the form of a simple and tame beast, quite craftily drawing things to himself under a good appearance; another in pride and the physical beauty of the body and gestures—who is a true devilish **beast** <note>original: *Bestia*</note>. Everything that does not resemble him, he despises, exalting himself alone above all gentleness and humility, above the image of **GOD**. There is not one who is righteous according to the spirit of this world; we are altogether children of deceit and falsehood. According to this image which we have received from the spirit of this world, we belong in eternal death and not in Paradise.

This remains the case unless we are born anew from the <term>Center</term> <note>original: *Centro*</note> of the precious Virgin, who with her rays restrains the mind from the ungodly way of sin and wickedness. For no more than two Principles remain eternally; the third, in which man lives here, passes away. If he now [chooses] the other...

# The Gate of Distinction between Humans and Animals.

My dear and beloved **Reason**, stretch out your five senses and behold yourself now in the things mentioned above—what you are, how you were created as an image of **GOD**, and how in **Adam** you allowed the spirit of this world to occupy your **Paradise** through the Devil's infection; it now sits in the place of Paradise. If you now wish to say that you were created for this world in **Adam** at the beginning, then look at yourself and consider: in your mind and speech, you will find another likeness. Every animal has a mind of one will, and within it the five senses, so that it can distinguish therein what is good or evil for it. But where do the senses in the will remain out of the gates of the deep, where the will beholds itself as infinite in the **first principle** <note>Böhme’s "First Principle" refers to the dark, fiery source of all existence from which light and matter emerge.</note>, from which the understanding proceeds? Through this, a human can look into the **essences** <term>essences</term> <note>original: *Essentien* — the fundamental spiritual energies or "inner being" of physical things.</note> of all things, seeing how highly each is graded, from which the distinction on the tongue follows. If an animal had this, it could also speak and distinguish the sound, and tell of the things that exist in being, and find their ground in the original source. And for the reason that it is not from the Eternal, it has no understanding in the light of nature; however cunning and swift it may be, its strength and power do not help it to rise in understanding; it is all in vain. Humans alone have understanding, and their senses grasp into the essences and qualities of the stars and elements, and

<column-break/>

search out the ground of all things in the region of the stars and elements. This now manifests itself in humans within the **eternal element**, showing that he is created from that element and not merely from the **outgrowth** <note>original: *Ausgeburt* — the external, physical manifestation or "offspring" of spiritual forces.</note> of the four elements. Therefore, eternity stands within the initial outgrowth in fragility, and the beginning within the outgrowth cannot see into eternity. For understanding originates from eternity, from the eternal mind. But the fact that man is so blind and lacking in understanding is because he lies imprisoned under the rule of the stars and elements, which often shape a wild beast—a **lion**, **wolf**, **dog**, **fox**, **snake**, and the like—within the human mind. Although the human does not receive such a body, he nevertheless has such a mind, of which **Christ** speaks to the **Jews**, calling some of them wolves, foxes, vipers, and snakes. **John the Baptist** also said such things to the **Pharisees**, and it is clearly proven by how many a person lives almost entirely like a beast out of his beastly mind, yet is so bold as to judge the one who lives in the image of **GOD** and tames his body. However, if he now speaks and judges something good, he does not speak from the animalistic image of the mind in which he lives; rather, he speaks from the **hidden man** <note>The "inner" or "spiritual" self that remains connected to the divine despite the fallen state of the physical body.</note> who is concealed within the beastly one, and he judges against his own beastly life. For the hidden law of eternal nature stands concealed within the beastly nature, and is in a great prison, and it judges against the malice of the fleshly mind.

Thus, there are **Three** in man who struggle against one another: first, the **Eternal**, Proud, Malicious, and Angry one, from the source of the mind. And secondly, the **Eternal**, Holy, Modest, and Humble one, who is born from the eternal source. And thirdly, the **Fragile**, Animalistic, and entirely **Beastly** one, born of the stars and elements, which the whole...

But if he yields himself to another swinish and bestial nature, such as living in mere bestial lust, in gluttonous and mad gorging, drinking, unchastity, stealing, robbing, murdering, lying, and deceiving, then the eternal mind also shapes for him such an image, like an irrational, hideous beast or worm. And here in this life, he must remain caught "between the door and the hinge" <note>An idiom meaning to be in a state of constant pressure or a narrow, difficult passage.</note>, between the kingdoms of Hell and this world, and must allow the noble image to be well squeezed. Therefore, the children of **GOD** are cross-bearers in this world, in this evil earthly image.

### Part 3, Chapter 14.

The essence <term>Ens: The essential spiritual "seed" or substance of a thing.</term> of the body arose from this, within which the first free will of the inhaled soul moved, and accepted the lust of the body; and it introduced that same lust into a desire for substance. And from that same substance, another new, private will arose, like a **bastard child**, a false **serpent-child**; and Adam bequeathed this same bastard child to his Eve, and Eve to her son Cain, and so one human has bequeathed it to the next. Thus, we now have in this earthly flesh that same false will from the serpent's substance, into which the devil introduces his desire, and sifts us, and constantly makes us lustful according to the devilish nature, so that his desire, which he introduces into us—into that false bastard child—might become substance and being. From this, such a bastard child and the devil's serpent-seed is continually fathered; and from that same false essence <note>original: "Ente"</note> comes a devilish will. Thus the devil rides in and over man, in and over body and soul.

<margin>Mysterium Magnum 26. 64–68. <note>A reference to Böhme’s commentary on Genesis.</note></margin>
We do not wish to involve ourselves in explaining this extensively; daily experience teaches it to us more than enough. Just to consider one thing, namely our language and our words: we see with great misery how it goes for us. Even if the sensible word forms itself in the inner essence <note>original: "Ente"</note> and wishes to reveal the truth, as soon as the awakened vanity in the earthly clay <note>original: "Limo," referring to the biblical 'limus terrae' or dust of the ground.</note> of the body catches it, it qualifies it into its own nature. Thus the word of human understanding echoes out as lies, malice, falsehood, and subtle frivolity. In this echo, the devil's desire mingles and makes it a substance of sin, which is caught by the kingdom of **GOD'S** wrath. For in whatever quality each word in the human echo forms and reveals itself during the speaking—either in **GOD'S** love, as in the holy essence, or in **GOD'S** wrath-essence—it is, in turn, taken in when it

<column-break/>

is spoken. The false word from a false essence <note>original: "Ens"</note> is infected by the devil, and sealed for destruction, and also taken into the mystery <term>Mysterium: A hidden spiritual reality or treasury of qualities.</term> of wrath, as into the nature of the dark world. Every thing returns with its essence into that from which it originated.

Since the spoken word is a divine revelation, by which the eternal Word of **GOD** has revealed itself, and since He breathed that same spoken word into man, we must now remember what man reveals with this spoken word. Understand it thus: if human lust and desire (which is the *Fiat* <note>The 'Fiat' is the creative power—the 'Let there be'—that Böhme believes also acts within the human soul to 'form' spiritual matter.</note> or the creating of the human word) grasps the form of the word in the holy essence, as in the heavenly part of humanity, then the word echoes from holy power, and the mouth speaks the truth. But where it comes from vanity, from the serpent’s cunning (which Eve impressed into herself, thereby awakening her cleverness), the word echoes from the essence of the dark world, as from the center of the fire-word; and it enters back into its essence when it departs from its form, namely from the mouth. And wherever it goes now, it works fruit. If it enters into another person in whom the hunger for cunning and vanity stands open in desire, into his housing of clay or hearing, it is immediately taken in as if into a fertile field. It takes root and bears such evil fruit, from which such sharp words and prickly thorns of the devil are hatched in a devilish essence. But if it goes out empty, only in false imagination, then it climbs into the will of the mind and settles in the mind into a substance, a seat for the devil's desire, a robber's castle that he holds within man. But if the false word goes out against a holy person in scorn and blasphemy, and the holy person does not wish to let it in, nor awaken themselves in the evil part of their nature with a similar evil word...

Fire and water are at enmity; for while fire is life, water is its death. You see this clearly: when one pours water into fire, the anguish <note>original: "Quaal." And yet, the fire is the sole cause of there being a vibration within the Light's gentleness; for the Light arises from the fire’s luster and contains within itself the fire’s vibration.

But when the grimness is so sharpened and ignited into fire, the will enters into a great anguish, like a dying, and sinks into itself away from the grimness into the eternal freedom. Yet it is not a death; rather, in this way, another world is made out of the first. For the will now sprouts in the other world as a sharpness out of the fire, but without such torment of anguish, out of the eternal freedom. It is a weaving, a driving, a recognizing of the nature of the anguish; it possesses all the essences that are born in the anguish of the first sharp fire-world, but they are like one who goes from fire into water—the anguish of the fire remains [quenched] in the water.

Understand us thus: This life is the soul’s spirit-life; the soul is the *Center of Nature* <note>original: "Centrum Naturæ."</note>, and the spirit is the precious, noble Image that **GOD** created in His likeness.

# Chapter XV.
## Concerning the Election of Grace / or the so-called absolute eternal Decree of GOD / both for eternal Salvation / and for eternal Damnation.

**1. Question.**
Why do you bring the doctrine of the Election of Grace to this place, after the doctrine of Propagation?

**Answer.**
We handle this doctrine in this place, partly on account of the children of Adam, such as Cain and Abel, who are the first example that those who argue for Election <note>The "Gnaden-Wähler," referring to theologians who believe God chooses certain individuals for salvation regardless of their actions.</note> cite to maintain their doctrine; but also because the <term>Predestinarians: Followers of the doctrine that God has unchangeably determined every person's eternal fate from the beginning.</term> themselves are not yet in agreement as to which place in theology they should bring this dogma, since some introduce it before the Fall and others after the Fall of man: for in every place where they arrange it, it corrupts the coherence and connection of Divine truths, because in a healthy theology it gives neither place nor any true concept. We would also not have touched upon this error, had the Author <note>Jacob Böhme.</note> not refuted this doctrine in all places with such great earnestness and wisdom—indeed, in an entire treatise—doubtless because much occasion was given to him for it, and this doctrine was mightily pushed in his time. Because it seems that the time has been born in our days for this most dangerous error of reason to be recognized and rejected by all true Christians, we wish to refute this doctrine with the Author's reasons. In order that we may find the proper ground of the matter herein, we wish to investigate: Firstly, what is understood by Predestination or the Election of Grace: Secondly, how and with what reasons this doctrine is refuted and rejected.

**2. Qu.** What then is actually understood by Predestination or the Election of Grace?

**Answer.** It is understood to be such an unchangeable decree of **GOD**, through which

<column-break/>

**GOD** from eternity has chosen a few from among [men] to eternal salvation, so that He might show to them the great power and the rich[es] of His mercy, goodness, and love; whereas [the] greatest part of the human race has been v[on]—from eternity—ordained to an eternally-lasting d[estruction], so that in them, as vessels of H[is] wrath, He might reveal His eternal justice and j[udgment].
