In order that we may summarize the blessed author's extensive refutation in the shortest possible way, we wish to investigate: First, from where such an error arises: Second, whether such a decree is in accordance with GOD and His nature: Third, whether, and what kind of decree and purpose GOD has, both in view of the whole world, and particularly in view of mankind: Fourth, we wish to answer from the author’s writings how reason seeks to maintain this error.

### 4. Question: From where does such a highly dangerous error arise?

**Answer:** From Reason. When **Reason hears talk of GOD, what He is according to His Being and Will:**

<column-break/>

then it imagines to itself, as if GOD were something distant and foreign, who dwells far from the place of this world, high above the stars, and thus rules with His Spirit, with an omnipresent power in the locality <note>original: "Loco," from the Latin *locus*, meaning place or space.</note> of this world, but His Majesty in Trinity dwells specifically in Heaven, outside the locality of this world.

And from this, Reason also falls into a creaturely delusion <note>A "creaturely delusion" refers to the mistake of thinking about God as if He were a finite, created thing subject to human logic and spatial limits.</note>, as if GOD were something foreign, and had, before the time of the creation of the creatures and of this world, held a counsel within Himself in His Trinity, through Wisdom, regarding what He wished to make, and what the purpose of all being should be; and had thus conceived a purpose within Himself, as to where He wished to ordain each thing.

From which the contentious delusion has arisen regarding the decree over mankind, as if GOD, by His purpose, had chosen one part of mankind for the Kingdom of Heaven in His holy delight; and the other part for eternal damnation: in those He wished to reveal His wrath: and conversely, in the other Elect, His grace. And thus, by His purpose, He made a distinction to show His power, His love, and His wrath; and therefore all things must necessarily happen in this way / and the portion of wrath, by GOD’S purpose, becomes so hardened and rejected, that there is no longer any possibility for GOD’S favor; whereas in the others, there is no possibility of damnation.

And although Holy Scripture speaks with almost similar sayings, and creaturely reason also agrees, which does not understand what GOD is: yet, on the contrary, Scripture speaks much more the opposite, that GOD wills nothing evil, or from His purpose...

If we as creatures wish to speak of the decree of **GOD**, we should ground ourselves no deeper than in **GOD** as He has introduced Himself into nature and creature, and therein conceived a decree and purpose. ->### Part 3 / Chapter 15.<-

The will of the Groundless <term>Ungrund</term> <note>original: *Ungrund*; Böhme’s term for the absolute, undifferentiated primal state of God before creation—a "groundless" depth or abyss.</note> is as a single one, and desires nothing in itself but the Good. Therefore, he is himself that same willing Good; for the Good that he wills is the birth of his power, as his Son. God wills to reveal nothing in himself but his Goodness, which he himself is. This could not happen if the single good Power did not introduce itself, through its breathing-out, into a desire for nature and into distinctness. For if the Good remained a single unity, there would be no knowledge <note>original: *Wissenschafft*; here meaning conscious awareness or experiential knowledge.</note>. Now, however, the Good (as God in himself) does not make itself distinct; rather, the Science <term>Scientz</term> <note>original: *Scientz*; from the Latin *scientia*. In Böhme's vocabulary, this is the formative, "attracting" power of the mind or the "Fiat" that brings things into being.</note>, as the <term>Fiat</term> <note>Latin: "Let it be." The creative command of God.</note> or the desire for distinctness, introduces itself into nature and creature. From this Science (or the attracting desire in nature and creature), evil and good originate—and not from God, or in God in his Trinity <note>original: *Dreyheit*.</note>. In God there is no decree <note>original: *Decret*.</note>; for if there were a counsel within him, there would also have to be a cause for that counsel, and then a cause for that cause in turn. Something would have to exist before or after God about which he would deliberate. But he himself is the Groundless and the One; he is a single will, which is himself, and that [will] alone is good. For a single thing cannot be contrary to itself, because it is only one and has nothing to struggle against. Therefore, it is a folly of Reason to speak of the "compulsion of inevitability," and it does not understand the Great Mystery <term>Mysterium Magnum</term> <note>Latin: "The Great Mystery." A term Böhme uses for the chaos or the potentiality from which the world was created.</note>. Nor does it understand when it says that God, by his own purpose, wills the evil will which he has hardened, and refuses to touch it with his grace. To this blind Reason, I point to a thistle, which the sun shines upon for a whole day, giving it light and power—yet it remains a thistle. So it is also with the godless will: the Divine Sun shines upon it all the days of its life, but its ground is the essence <term>Ens</term> of a thistle.

<margin>Great Mystery 61. 61. 67.</margin>
From this we see that God properly has no counsel in himself. For if he had ever held a counsel within himself so to re-

<column-break/>

veal himself, then his revelation would not be from eternity, beyond mind and place. Such a counsel would also have to have taken a beginning at some point, and there would have to have been a cause for the Godhead for which God, in his Trinity, would have deliberated. Thoughts would then have to be in God, which modeled him into a form according to how he wished to encounter a thing.

Now, he himself is the One, and the ground of all things, and the eye of all beings, and the cause of all essence. Nature and creature arise from his properties. With whom, then, would he deliberate? No enemy is before him, and He alone is everything himself: the willing, the doing, and the power. Therefore, if we wish to speak solely of God's unchangeable being—what he wills, or what he has willed and always wills—we should not speak of his "counsel," for there is no counsel in him. He is the eye of all seeing and the ground of all beings. He wills and does only one thing in himself forever: He births himself into Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, into the Wisdom of his revelation. Otherwise, the single, groundless God wills nothing in himself, nor does he have any counsel for anything more. For if He willed anything more in himself, He would not be Almighty enough in that willing to accomplish it. Thus, he can will nothing more in himself than to will himself. For whatever He has ever willed from eternity, that He is himself; thus He is alone One, and nothing more. So, too, a single thing cannot become contentious with him, from which a counsel would arise to distinguish the conflicts.

### 7. Question: Did GOD then for himself, outside of nature and creature, not see from eternity beforehand that Lucifer and his angels, as well as man and his race, would fall?

**Answer:** Reason runs into vain imagery, after a creaturely fashion, and thinks that GOD consulted with himself in his Trinity regarding what he wanted to make and how things must and should go. Therefore, Reason wants to conclude the Fall of Lucifer and Adam within a certain fixed goal, as if GOD had ordained it so in his purpose. But such reason-thinking is not the Ground. GOD does not need to consult about anything, for he is himself the Counsel. The high, out-flowing names of the powers are the Counsel of GOD, as the **miracle-working Word**.

There is also no "purpose" of any single thing; rather, the origin of all things, and how they can happen, lies in the **Idea** <term>Idea</term> <note>The eternal "mirror" or "image" in which God sees all possibilities before they are manifested.</note>, in eternal formation—not as something already formed, but in constant-enduring formation, where GOD’s Love and Wrath, as the two central fires, stand in constant wrestling. The wrath of GOD in nature knew it well, for it is its craving <note>original: *Sucht*; a drive or sickness/craving.</note>. But no such imagination enters into his Love. Not a single spark of the Devil or the darkness is revealed in his Love; rather, it is a pure desire for love. Thus, GOD calls himself a GOD according to love and gentleness. In hell there is hellish science, in heaven heavenly, and in this world siderial <term>siderische</term> <note>original: *siderische*; relating to the stars or the astral influences of the physical universe.</note>.
->See Apology against Tilken 478.<-

->8. Question: What then is actually the Counsel or Purpose of GOD in general over all creatures?<-

**Answer:** The Counsel of GOD in the creature is none other than that very active Will of GOD which goes forth to sustain, to enliven, and to continually <gloss>the</gloss> bring forth all things, just as this same Will created and made all things. Therefore, the author calls this Counsel, or conceived active Will of GOD, a **Purpose**, because the Will of GOD continues the work of creation incessantly and never withdraws it.

GOD’S sole Purpose is His eternal speaking Word, which He speaks forth through Wisdom from His power in the Science <term>Scientz</term>, into distinctness <term>Schiedlichkeit</term> <note>original: *Schiedlichkeit*; the capacity for things to be separate, diverse, or distinct from one another.</note> for His manifestation. He has no other Purpose in Himself anymore, nor can it be that He has more purposes; for if that were so, then there would have to be something before Him from which He took cause for a purpose. Thus, the speaking of His power for His Self-manifestation is the sole Divine Purpose—not a beginning purpose, but a **begetting** purpose. And the Purpose of the Word is the Science of distinctness and formality of the sole Divine Power; which distinctness and formality the one GOD in His Trinity has spoken forth from eternity into a beginning through the Word, as into an essence <term>Ens</term> of all properties of distinctness. Thus all distinct things lie within one another, and that which is Spoken is the **Great Mystery** <term>Mysterium Magnum</term> <note>Böhme’s term for the chaos or "Great Mystery" from which all things—both light and dark—are manifested.</note>, and a true, sole Purpose of the Word. The Word desires nothing more than only to manifest its Holy Power through distinctness, and in the Word, the Deity becomes manifest in distinctness through fire and light. Thus the two—the Word and the Great Mystery—are in one another, like soul and body: For the Great Mystery is the essence of the Word, in which and through which the invisible GOD in His Trinity is manifest, and is manifest from eternity to eternity; for that which the Word is in power and sound, the Mystery is in essence.

A Great Being; it is the eternal essential Word of GOD.

The working Being within the properties—with Light and Darkness, in which the entire Creation is comprised—is now the single Purpose of GOD’S Word: namely, that He should bring forth Life and Creatures, and lead the spoken Word into a formal image <note>original: *Bildlichkeit*; the state of having a form or image</note>. Thus, every power stands in the Science <term>Scientz</term> <note>original: *Scientz*; for Böhme, this is the "attraction" or "knowing" that gives form to a spirit's desire.</note> of distinctness, within a life and an image, according both to the property of the Light-power of the holy Word and the properties of the Fire-power. The Light, however, is given to all things for a Temperament <note>original: *Temperatur*; a state of balance between opposing qualities</note>, not so that the Light alone should shine upon the essence from the outside, but rather it is co-active within every Being <note>original: *Enti*; from the Latin *ens*, meaning a thing that exists</note> in all that lives and grows. Therefore, no creature has cause to complain against its Creator, claiming He created it for evil; rather, the Wrath in nature is what hardens a thing and hinders the power of the Light. Furthermore, the curse hinders it, so that the holy Tincture <term>Tincture</term> <note>original: *Tinctur*; the spiritual essence or "dye" that imparts quality and life to a thing.</note> of the holy ground of the speaking Word in the eternal Light has withdrawn into itself (because of the vanity of the Devil, as well as that of Man and the creatures). It gives itself only to that which enters into an image of the Light-power, and which does not wish to work with the Science that gives itself over to the Wrath of the darkness. For this is the cause: otherwise, the darkness seizes the holy power and leads it into its own wickedness. As it says in the Scriptures, *Psalm 18*: **With the perverse you are perverse, and with the holy you are holy.** <note>original: *Bey den Verkehrten bist du verkehrt / und bey den Heiligen bist du heilig.*</note> Just as the sun must suffer the thistle to swallow its good essence into its prickly nature and use it for its thorns, so the highest Tincture will not give itself into the falsehood of the Science where the eternal groundless will has transformed itself into an image of the dark world’s property.

<margin>Election of Grace, 8. 29. 30.</margin>
Thus, GOD, in and of Himself, has no purpose to make this or that creature in such a way—

<column-break/>

to make one for a life of joy and the other for a life of poison, one as a lily and the other as a thistle; rather, He gives Himself into each one as it is and for what it is.

The groundless <term>Ungrund</term> <note>original: *ungründliche*; referring to the "Ungrund," the fathomless abyss or nothingness that precedes all creation.</note> will of GOD is nothing other than that GOD wills to beget GOD, and to reveal Himself in Nature and Creature. There is no other purpose in GOD than this eternal birth. But the creature that departs from the will of GOD and wishes to be its own self, shuts itself into its own will as into a painful and hostile life. That same hostile life is the cause of the Fall; for it has given itself over to the Fantasy <term>Phantasey</term> <note>original: *Phantasey*; here, it refers to the mirror-play or "imagination" of nature’s working powers, rather than just a mental dream.</note> of nature (or the play of generation) and has made itself the leader or master of that same Fantastical nature. The Fantasy has taken that same life into itself and given itself entirely to that life. Now, the Fantasy and the life have become one thing and possess the will of the Abyss <note>original: *Ungrundes*</note> (as the Divine Science, wherein GOD begets GOD in Himself). But in this enclosed Science, GOD does not beget Himself. He may indeed beget Himself within it, but He does not become manifest in the Science as far as nature seizes and grasps it. GOD is immovable and non-active within it. He does not beget therein a Father, Son, Holy Spirit, and Wisdom, but rather a Fantasy according to the property of the dark world. GOD is indeed a GOD within it, but dwelling only in Himself—not in the creature—but in the Abyss outside of the movement, and outside of the will of the creature, and outside of the life of the creature. So, when the creature does something, it is not GOD who does it in the will of the Abyss (which is also in the creature), but rather the life and the essence of the life in the creature do it.

<margin>Election of Grace, 4. 43. 44.</margin>

### 11th Question: Is there then actually in GOD no absolute decree to make some people blessed and to damn others?

**Answer:** In **GOD** Himself—so far as He is called and is **GOD**—there is no decree for evil, or for anything else, for He is the only Good, and has no other capacity in Himself but only Himself. He seeks nothing but only to give birth to Himself in all things, to reveal Himself, and to fill all in all with Himself.

When man stood in the state of perfection in the <term>Temperament</term> <note>original: *Temperatur*; in Böhme's philosophy, this is the state of perfect balance where all spiritual properties exist in harmony without conflict.</note>, God’s will also worked in that balance, and **GOD** revealed Himself as a single **GOD**, in a single name, as the highest Good and Love. But after man fell from that balance into the divisibility of properties, and finally into sin, **GOD** became manifest to him in good and evil, and finally as an angry, jealous **GOD**, and as a consuming fire. **GOD** did not withdraw Himself from the soul; rather, the <term>Science</term> <note>original: *Scientz*; from the Latin *scientia*, referring here to the active, formative power or "knowledge-seed" of the free will.</note> of the free will withdrew itself from **GOD**. Just as the sun does not withdraw itself from the thistle; but the thistle withdraws its own property from the sun into a prickly nature; the more the sun shines upon it, the sharper and pricklier the attractive desire of its will becomes: the same is to be understood regarding the soul.

The soul-driven will must turn itself toward the promised grace; then the Divine Sun will appear in its will and shatter the hatred of malice; then the soul reaches for the Sun of Grace, and so the work of repentance begins in the power of grace; then the wrath of **GOD** in the soul gives up its strict justice to the Spirit of Christ; then Christ says to His Father: *I have lost none of those whom You have given Me.* Scripture says: **GOD** wills that all men be helped [saved]; and Christ has come to seek and to make blessed that which

<column-break/>

was lost, and has no pleasure in the death of the sinner. Thus Reason speaks: If **GOD** then wills that all men be helped, and does not will evil, can He not then help them all? Why then do they remain hardened, if He does not will their hardening?

**Response:** The soul stands in the bottomless <note>original: *ungründlichen*; referring to the *Ungrund*, the primal divine abyss.</note> will of **GOD** in the eternally-speaking Word: It is a spark from the Divine Speaking, where the <term>Abyss</term> <note>original: *Ungrund*; the "groundless" or "abyss," the primal nothingness out of which the divine nature and all existence emerge.</note>, as the eternal One, speaks itself out into <term>Science</term>, understanding, and the knowledge of diversity; the soul has come into nature and creaturely existence through this speaking, and now has the power to "speak back out" again, as an image of itself. It also speaks out through its knowledge the wonders of the Divine power in good and evil; it speaks itself out of its essential speaking, out of the eternal Science itself into malice: where it should speak "**GOD**," it speaks within itself "**Distress**"; where it should speak into the eternal One through its Science—into **GOD’S** love and wisdom—it speaks itself into divisibility, into multiplicity. It leads the Science of its power, which stands within the eternal speaking Word, out of the <term>Temperament</term> into a self-will, which breaks away from the single will of **GOD** and enters into a "Selfhood." Therefore, it transforms the eternal will of unity within itself into the center of divisibility, wherein the single **GOD** introduces His single will—through the speaking of the Word into nature and painfulness—toward Divine perceptibility and feeling, as into an essential spiritual fire, and out of that fire into a light, through which the Abyss becomes majestic and active. Thus the false soul speaks itself only into a <term>Fire-Torment</term> <note>original: *Feuer-Quaal*; the state of the soul when it experiences the divine energy as burning pain because it has cut itself off from the Light.</note>. For its will for speaking, which stands in **GOD** in the Abyss, and which introduced itself through desire into the "fire-speaking" (as into properties), does not go back again into the Abyss, into the eternal One: But if it were to go back,

12. **Question:** Does man then, even after his Fall, still have a free will to grasp GOD’S working Word for his conversion and salvation, or for his hardening and damnation?

**Answer:** That man had a free will before the Fall has been sufficiently proven; however, after man turned his will away from GOD and placed it into vanity, he became captured therein. But GOD, according to His great love, spoke His Word of Grace into man, which awakens his will toward freedom; so that just as he may grasp God's Word for damnation according to the property of wrath, he may also grasp GOD’S Word in an earnest desire for his improvement.

Man in this life is threefold, and a threefold spirit clings to him and is born within him, and he cannot be rid of it unless he breaks apart. Truly, of the **Para-** <note>Catchword for "Paradise" (Paradies), continued on the next page.</note>

<header>3. Part / Cap. 15.</header>

He can lose Paradise if his spirit <term>imagines</term> <note>original: *imaginiret*; in Böhme’s thought, "imagination" is a creative, formative power of the soul that shapes its reality.</note> itself into <term>wrath</term> <note>original: *Grimmigkeit*; refers to the harsh, fierce, and dark quality of the first principle of nature.</note> and falsehood and gives itself over to it, desiring to live in pride above gentleness and righteousness within himself as a master—just as **Lucifer** did. Thus, Paradise falls away and is shut, and he loses the first image, which exists in the hidden element within Paradise. For the Adamic man can nonetheless live in Paradise according to the inner element, which stands open in the <term>mind</term> <note>original: *Gemüthe*; the disposition of the soul, combining will, emotion, and intellect.</note>, if he resists wickedness and gives himself entirely with all his might into the heart of **GOD**. Then the <term>Virgin</term> <note>original: *Jungfrau*; referring to the Virgin of Wisdom or Sophia, the mirror of God’s glory.</note> stays with him in the inner element in Paradise and enlightens his mind so that he can tame the Adamic body. For these three births are born within every person in the mother’s womb, and no one should say: "I am not chosen." That is a lie that denies the very element in which the person lives; furthermore, the Virgin of Wisdom—whom **God** gives to everyone who seeks her with earnestness and humility—testifies against it. So the possibility of seeking is also within everyone, born within them through the all-powerful, hidden element. And there is no other cause for the ruin of man than there was for **Lucifer**, whose will stood free. He was meant to reach into **God**, into humility, purity, and gentleness—not into the dark mind, into the rising wickedness and wrath, which in its own source does not desire to raise itself above **GOD**, but only appropriates for itself power over gentleness in the <term>fire-flash</term> <note>original: *Feuer-Blitz*; the sudden manifestation or "lightning strike" of life and light from the dark nature-source.</note> in the rigorous rebirth. But the devils, as creatures, wanted to be masters above and alone. This is how it also goes for man here.

To be sure, the pride of nature manifests more strongly in one person than in another; however, it forces no one to be proud. And even if there is a compulsion, the person willfully lets the devil into the eternal <term>essences</term> <note>original: *Essentien*; the fundamental spiritual substances of the soul.</note> for the sake of temporary honor and pleasure. The devil soon sees how the person is

<column-break/>

inclined toward the spirit of this world, and so he seeks him out as well. If the person lets him in, he is a difficult guest to evict. Yet it is indeed possible, if the person completely and firmly intends to turn back and to live in the will of **GOD**, that the Virgin will help him even while he is on the path. It is certainly a hard struggle when the noble <term>grain of mustard seed</term> <note>A biblical reference to the small beginnings of the Kingdom of God within the soul.</note> is to be sown, for the devil defends himself powerfully. But whoever perseveres will experience what is written in this book. And even if he cannot rid himself of the drive of the outward elements' virtues, the seed remains for him in the <term>Limbo of GOD</term> <note>original: *Limbo GOTTES*; here meaning the divine reservoir or spiritual sphere of potentiality.</note>, which sprouts and grows, and finally becomes a tree that does not taste good to the devil. Instead, the devil goes around the tree like a fawning dog that urinates on the tree; he also throws all misfortune from his servants at him, and even tears many a person out of his house through his pack, though it does him no more harm; but it happens for the best, and he arrives in the Land of the Living.

-> Principles. 15. 19 to 23. <-

Thus **GOD** knows the free will into which man has entered; if he has entered into wickedness and selfhood, then **GOD’S** wrath confirms him in his choice of damnation. But where he enters into the Word of the Image, then **GOD** confirms him as a child of Heaven. It is said here: *I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and whom I will harden, I will harden.* <note>original: *Welche ich gnädig bin, dem bin ich gnädig; und welchen ich verstocke, den verstocke ich*; a reference to Romans 9:15-18.</note> **God** knows His children even while they are still in the mother’s womb. Why should He give His <term>little pearl</term> <note>original: *Perlein*; a common metaphor for the hidden divine spark or the Kingdom of Heaven within the soul.</note> to one whom He well knows will turn away from Him? The ground of the little pearl certainly lies within him, but it is locked away; however, if he leads his will into the little pearl, it will open itself within him.

All people come from one and the same seed, but in one, the holy fire glimmers, and in another, it lies as if locked away and cannot emerge because of the moisture of the <term>serpents</term> <note>original: *Schlangen*; symbolic of the ego and the devilish nature.</note>. Say...

# On the Election of Grace.

You say: "Is the serpent's <term>essence</term> <note>original Latin: *Ens*; here meaning the spiritual 'being' or 'substance' of the soul's fallen nature.</note> then mightier than **GOD’S** love?" I have told you above that Love and Wrath are in conflict. Whichever the <term>essence</term> joins itself to, by that it is seized and confirmed; yet in such a way that the will remains free to go from evil to good, and from good to evil. And because the person lives on earth, both doors stand open to them: for the free will is not bound. If it were bound, no judgment could pass over it with justice. The human has laws and teachings, which are not given to them for death, but for life; but if they transgress these and persist in the transgression, then judgment passes over them—for every judgment arises from the transgression of the commandment. 

So you say: "He cannot keep it; he is being pulled [by sin]." Yes, quite right; yet the Truth rebukes him to his face as a faithless one who allows himself to be pulled toward evil. The law to do right stands in the Light of Life as a constant mirror: He sees it and knows that he is a liar and runs on the devil’s path. It shows him the way of Truth, but the free will rejects it; now he is <term>predestined</term> <note>original: *prædestiniret*</note> to damnation. However, this is so that the will remains free while it is in this "hut" <note>A common 17th-century metaphor for the physical body.</note>. But the heavy bond of **GOD'S** wrath, pulling in the devil's desire, drags many to the damnation of death. 

Reason says: "If man has a free will, then **GOD** is not Almighty over him, to do with him what He wills." [But] the free will has no beginning; it is not contained in any foundation <note>original: *Grund*</note> nor shaped by anything. It is its own <term>original source</term> <note>original: *Urstand*; refers to the primordial state of being before manifestation.</note> out of the Word of Divine Power, out of **GOD's** Love and Wrath. It forms for itself, in its own will, a <term>center</term> <note>original: *Centrum*</note> for its seat; it gives birth to itself in the first <term>principle</term> <note>original: *Principio*</note> toward fire and light. Its true origin is in the Nothing, where the Nothing—as the ∆ <note>A symbol for the Trinity or the heart of God.</note> or as one might unfold it: A. O. V. <note>These letters represent the breathing out of the Divine Name: Alpha, Omega, and the *Viatum* or Word.</note>—introduces itself into a delight for contemplation; and this delight leads

<column-break/>

itself into a will, and the will into a desire, and the desire into a being. 

Now the eternal Understanding, which is **GOD**, is a judge over the being. If the delight (having deviated from Him) has introduced itself into an evil being, then He judges that being in its <term>principle</term> <note>original: *Principium*</note>, into whatever torment and quality—or into whatever <term>essence</term>—the delight from the deviated ∆ has introduced itself into a principle. Therein it is confirmed by the universal, eternal, free will, which is the <term>Abyss</term> <note>original: *Ungrund*; Böhme’s term for the "groundless" or "bottomless" nothingness that precedes God's self-manifestation.</note> and the cause of all foundations. That which is without foundation judges that which introduces itself into a foundation; it separates the good (which introduces itself into a good essence) into the Good, as into Divine Love; and the evil (which has introduced itself into an evil essence and placed and shaped itself into a center as an evil spirit and will) into His fierceness and wrath. 

For how can He judge a thing that does not belong to Him? How would **GOD** judge the will of the creature if it had not originated from Him? Or how could a judgment pass over a thing that is bound, and not free in its willing and doing? The human and angelic will arose from the movement of the <term>Abyss</term> <note>original: *Ungrund*</note> (when the Deity moved itself in its contemplation and perceptibility, and with that movement introduced itself into a beginning of spirits). Since it arose from that same beginning, every beginning now goes toward its end; and the end is that which was before the beginning. There is the "test" of the beginning: into what the beginning has introduced itself. 

Thus **GOD** is before and outside of all beginnings, and from Him comes every beginning; likewise, He is the end of all beginnings. So the middle of all things that have begun stands between the beginning and the end; for with its beginning, it must enter again through the end into that from which it originated. 

Because **GOD** is then a jealous **GOD** and a consuming fire, and also a dear, merciful **GOD**, now to every free will, with its introduced <term>center</term>...

# Part 3 / Chapter 15

...master, his judge born within himself / either Divine Love / or Divine Wrath. For when a thing begins / it enters into a time / but when that same time is seized by the end / as by eternity / then it is in its own Eternal / from which it has introduced itself into a <term>compaction</term> <note>original: *Compaction*; in this context, it refers to the process where spiritual desires solidify into a fixed, permanent state of being.</note> / and thus confirmed into eternity. Therefore, the free will has its own judgment / for good or evil within itself / it has **GOD’S** love and wrath within itself / whatever it grasps and desires / that it forms within itself / and thus only forms itself in its own lust into a <term>center</term> <note>original: *Centrum*; the inner point of origin for a person’s spiritual identity.</note>.

->*Mysterium Magnum* 26. 41::::60.<-

**13. Question:** But sin is so powerful in man that the good will cannot emerge?

**Answer:** This is the understanding of the Scripture / that the earthly Adam / in the kingdom of corrupted nature / in his own will / does not find repentance / nor can he find it / for there is no power within it for the Good / but the <term>ingrafted grace</term> <note>original: *eingeleibte Gnade*; the idea that a spark of God's favor is biologically or spiritually "woven" into the human essence despite the Fall.</note> in him awakens it / when the will turns toward it. For if the own will could perform repentance / and become godly / then it would have no need of grace. The <term>decrees of Scripture</term> <note>original: *Decreta der Schrifft*; the formal theological laws or pronouncements found in the Bible.</note> concern only the two kingdoms / just as <term>hardening</term> <note>original: *Verstockung*; a state where the heart becomes stubborn and unreachable, similar to the biblical account of Pharaoh.</note> concerns the false will / the false will hardens itself; **GOD’S** wrath / in the will's own essence / hardens it / not by entering from the outside / but by manifesting within the will’s own essence. The will is from **GOD** / and that same **GOD** in the will leads himself into hardening / in the same manner as he leads himself into hell / into darkness and pain: Thus it is also to be understood regarding the kingdom of grace. **GOD** wants only good in man within the kingdom of His grace / where the free will surrenders itself into grace / there **GOD** wants good in the will through grace.

But to say / that man cannot turn his will toward the Good / as toward grace / that is an

<column-break/>

untruth <note>original: *Ungrund*; literally "without ground," meaning a baseless or false claim.</note>: For grace stands in the ground of the creature / in all godless people / and the will only needs to stand still from human working / so it begins to arise from the abyss of its own will. For that which stands still / stands still with the eternal One / and becomes one being with the One / for it enters into its Nothingness. If the false will must stand still from wrong works for the sake of worldly laws / out of fear of punishment / why can it not also do so for the sake of **GOD’S** commandment? If he can obey his worldly lord and stand still at a place where he wants him to be / why not also **GOD**? To whom the "ability" is immediately given / as soon as he merely leads the will to standing still.

But that the entirely false, godless will does not stand still / and turn itself toward grace / the cause is / that it is already a "born thistle" / in which grace lies too deep within / and the grimness of **GOD** is too strong in its nature. Grace draws it / and shows it its falsehood / but it despises grace / and works like a thistle in the power of the sun. This is a terrible smell to **GOD** for the damnation of death in hell / so that grace might be distinguished from the false will. But the <term>logical conclusions</term> <note>original: *Vernunfft-Schlüsse*; the rationalistic arguments used by contemporary theologians to argue for predestination.</note> / which state / that **GOD** in himself / insofar as he is called **GOD** / has decreed / that a part of humanity / and indeed the greatest multitude / shall and must be damned / and that he hardens them out of his own proposed will / is false; and has a basis neither in Scripture / nor in the light of nature / if one considers the Scripture rightly / and does not look at it blindly.

->*Mysterium Magnum* 61. 54::::61.<-

# On Election by Grace

...you emerge only in water and a handful of blood / and yet you act so proud? What then is your beauty / your splendor / honor and wealth? Consider yourself / seek yourself / and find yourself; depart from this dangerous life / from the vipers and snakes / into an eternal one / for you have this in your full power: Whoever teaches and speaks otherwise / speaks from the Devil / who does not want to admit / that man has the power to become a child of **GOD**; even though the Scripture says: **GOD** has given man power in Christ to become children of **GOD**: And **GOD** wills that all people be helped <note>In this context, "helped" (geholffen) means to be saved or brought to salvation.</note>. For through the will **GOD** created heaven and earth: And such a mighty will is also hidden in the soul / though it now swims there in misery / in great weakness / in the sinking of death / it is tied down / and allows itself to be led / as a poor imprisoned creature / from one mire into another. Now the Devil leads her into this pool / soon into another / and she looks like a stained cloth / full of impurity: All the stars pour their poison into the body / and soil the poor soul: She must allow herself to be soiled by all animals / the body devours the animals' flesh / with which the poor soul is clothed.

### Part 3, Chapter 15

an entry into the Wrath, the mirror of His covenant is presented to the soul as the **Virgin of Divine Wisdom**, so that she might behold herself therein. Wisdom always speaks: "Come!" But the Devil speaks from behind her also, "Come!" Wherever the soul then turns, there she is chosen as a child.

**GOD** does not allow the light of any soul who possesses **GOD’S** light to be extinguished by His own purpose <note>original: "Fürsaß," referring to God's eternal decree or intended plan.</note>; rather, the free will extinguishes it. The Devil presents himself to the soul in the form of an angel, so that she *imagines* in both evil and good. Thus her *imagination* then eats of evil and good; and so the soul becomes blind and captured in her own imagination <term>Imagination: in this mystical context, it refers to the soul's "inward shaping" or the creative power of its desires to form its own reality.</term>. Otherwise, if **GOD** hardened someone out of His own purpose and allowed His light to be extinguished by His own decree, then what David says in his fifth Psalm would not be true: *You are not a **GOD** who wills evil.* To be sure, He allows it to happen that a godly person becomes evil: when the will turns itself toward evil, He allows His light to be extinguished. But this is not out of His own purpose, as if He did not desire to have that person; for He accepts him if he returns. As long as man lives in this hut <note>A common metaphorical reference to the physical body.</note>, he has the power to become **GOD’S** child. For the Apostle also says: *He has given us power to become children of **GOD**.*

Understand: this is not out of the will of the flesh, which belongs to the outer world and does not belong in **GOD’S** kingdom, but out of the will of the soul-spirit, which is born in **GOD**. For **GOD’S** purpose is that the true Divine will be ever born out of the soul. This happens when the soul enters into Christ's incarnation; therein she is born again as **GOD’S** child. For the soul-fire is led into Christ's death and "greens" <note>The author uses the image of a plant blooming (grünet) to describe the soul's spiritual rebirth.</note> again with a new and beautiful flower out of Christ's death, in the divine freedom, within the angelic world. That same flower, or spiritual will, is **GOD’S** will; and in that same spirit of the will, the soul is an angel, for it

<column-break/>

possesses the second principle <note>original: "Principium." In this theological system, the Second Principle represents the world of Light, Love, and Majesty.</note> as **GOD’S** Majesty. It leads divine essence into the soul—as Christ’s flesh, which fills the heavens—so that the soul eats of Christ's flesh and drinks His blood from the water of meekness, of eternal life. John 6.

Therefore I say with foundation: it is not **GOD’S** purposeful will that even a single person be lost; rather, it is the will of His fury and wrath, and of the dark world, and of the Devil. Therefore, he is a false judge and an advocate of **GOD’S** wrath who wishes to judge and blame **GOD**, yet does not know the distinction of what **GOD** is in love and in wrath. He does not know from where an evil and a good will originate <note>original: "urständet," meaning the primal rising or "grounding" of a state of being.</note>, and yet he wants to be a judge; he always cries "God, God!"

The Prophets and Apostles have often called the whole of **GOD**—according to love and wrath, as well as according to all three principles—by a single word. But one must use a distinction and a right understanding between **GOD’S** love-will and His wrath-will. We see well enough in man that he wills both evil and good. He always wants to be an angel, yet also wants pride in greed and the power of this world. One must search out from where each will takes its origin and not always say: "**GOD**, **GOD**, **GOD** wills this." He wills only His own likeness. His love, as the true name of **GOD**, wills only that we love **GOD** and our neighbor, and remain in His desire and will. He wills nothing more than that all people turn to Him and depart from the fury into the love; for the love of **GOD** and neighbor is the whole law and the prophets. Conversely, His fury and wrath, which is a root of the outer world, also wants only its own likeness: a fire, and pride. # Of the Election of Grace.

...does he then walk in the **Mirror of Wrath** <note>The "Mirror of Wrath" is a Böhmean term for the dark, fire-principle of God's nature, which becomes a reality for the soul that turns away from love.</note> and let the Devil rock him to sleep? Does **GOD** not send prophets and teachers according to His purpose, who reveal and announce His wrath to the world? Why does man follow sin? It would be a strange thing if **GOD** had someone called, bidding him to come to Him, and yet also willed to harden his will so that he could not! If that were so, **GOD** would be unjust. The lust of the flesh and of the Devil hardens the soul and holds it captive. If **GOD** had willed evil or the fall of man, He would not have forbidden Adam the **Tree of Good and Evil**, which represents the lust of this world. But since He did forbid it, if He had also hardened Adam so that he could not have done **GOD’S** will, who then would be righteous: **GOD** or man?

-><margin>Apology against Tilke, pages 549, 570.</margin><-

*15th Question: How can it be possible that it stands within man’s free will to attain salvation, since all men would gladly be saved, and yet so few become saved, especially although **GOD** calls them?*

Answer: Would **GOD** then call someone to salvation whom He did not want to make whole and have saved? Rather, it is and remains an irrefutable truth: **GOD** wills that all men be helped and that all men be saved; the failure lies with man himself, in that he will not allow himself to be helped.
Here the **Door of Grace** stands open to man: there is no sinner so great that, if he turns back and works the genuine fruits of repentance, he may not be born anew out of his malice. But if someone willfully throws his root into the Devil’s fire and despairs of his own blossoming, who can help the one who does not want it himself? However, when he turns his will toward **GOD**, then **GOD** wants to have him: for whoever wants to be in **GOD’S** wrath, him **GOD’S** wrath wants to have; but whoever wants to be in Love, him **GOD’S** love wants to have.
Paul says: *To whomsoever you yield yourselves as servants in obedience, whether of sin unto death, or of obedience to **GOD** unto righteousness, his servants you are.* The

<column-break/>

godless man is a sweet fragrance to **GOD** in His wrath, and the saint is a sweet fragrance to **GOD** in His love. A man may make of himself what he will; he has both before him: fire and light. If he wishes to be an angel in the light, then **GOD’S** Spirit helps him in **Christ** toward the angelic host. If he wishes instead to be a devil in the fire, then **GOD’S** wrath and grimness help him and draw him into the abyss to become a devil. Also <note>original: "Item"</note>, he receives his **Ascendant** <term>Ascendant: Borrowed from astrology, Böhme uses this to mean the dominant spiritual influence or "ruling star" that a soul aligns with through its own desires.</term> according to what he has a lust for. If he breaks his first lust and enters into another, he receives another **Ascendant**; but the first one clings to him greatly and always wants him back. Therefore, the noble little grain of seed must often stand in a great squeeze; it must allow itself to be pricked by thorns, for the serpent always stings the woman's seed—the **Virgin-Child** <note>The "Virgin-Child" or "Maiden-Child" refers to the new, spiritual man born within the soul through Christ.</note>—in the heel. The serpent’s sting is lodged in the **Old Adam**, which is always stinging the **Virgin-Child** in the mother’s womb in the heel. Therefore, this life in this world is a **Vale of Tears** for us poor imprisoned men, full of anguish, cross, misery, tribulation, martyrdom, and pain. We are foreign guests here and are on the pilgrim’s path; we must wander through great, desolate, wild wildernesses and are surrounded by evil beasts—by adders and snakes, wolves and nothing but gruesome animals—and the most evil beast of all we carry in our own bosom: our beautiful young maiden <note>Referring to the soul's pure, divine spark.</note> stays in that same evil, desolate cattle-stall as her lodging.

**15. Question:** How can it be possible that it remains within man’s free will to attain salvation, since all people would like to be saved, and yet so few are, especially although God calls them?

**Answer:** Would God then call someone to salvation whom He did not wish to save or have in a state of bliss? Rather, it is and remains an irrefutable truth: God wills that all people be helped, and that all people be saved; it is the fault of the person themselves that they will not let themselves be helped.

Here, the Door of Grace stands open to man: there is no sinner so great that, if he turns back and produces the righteous fruits of repentance, he may not be born anew out of his wickedness. But he who willfully throws his root into the Devil's fire and despairs of his own blossoming—who can help him who does not want it himself? But when he turns his will toward God, then God wants him: for he who wants to be in God's wrath, God's wrath will have him; but he who wants to be in Love, God's love will have him. Paul says: *To whom you yield yourselves as servants in obedience, whether of sin unto death, or of obedience to God unto righteousness, his servants you are.* <note>Original Latin/German context: Romans 6:16. Böhme emphasizes that our "service" is a matter of choice.</note> The

<column-break/>

ungodly is a "sweet-smelling savor" to God in His wrath, and the holy is a "sweet-smelling savor" to God in His love. Let a man make of himself what he will; he has both before him: Fire and Light. If he wants to be an angel in the Light, then God's Spirit helps him in Christ toward the angelic host. If he then wants to be a devil in the fire, then God's wrath and grimness help him and pull him into the abyss to the devil. Likewise, he receives his <term>Ascendant</term> <note>An astrological term used here metaphorically to describe the spiritual "disposition" or "ruling influence" that a person chooses for themselves through their desires.</note> according to what he has a lust for. But if he breaks his first lust and enters into another, he receives another Ascendant; yet the first clings to him mightily and always wants him back. Therefore, the "noble grain" <note>The "noble grain" or "precious seed" refers to the divine spark or the potential for the "new man" to be born within the soul.</note> must often stand in a great press; it must allow itself to be pricked by thorns, for the serpent always stings the woman’s seed—the "Virgin-Child"—in the heel. The serpent’s sting sits in the "Old Adam," and it always stings the Virgin-Child in the mother’s womb in the heel. Therefore, this life in this world with us poor, captive humans is a Vale of Sorrows, full of anxiety, crosses, misery, tribulation, martyrdom, and pain. Here we are foreign guests and are on a pilgrim’s path; we must walk through great, desolate, wild wildernesses and are surrounded by evil beasts—by adders and serpents, wolves and nothing but hideous beasts—and the most evil beast of all we carry in our own bosom: our beautiful "Maiden" <note>The "Maiden" or "Virgin" represents the Divine Wisdom or the pure, heavenly image of the soul that is currently "lodging" in the animalistic human body.</note> stands in that same evil, desolate cattle-stall as her lodging.

Concerning such people, the Scripture says in Psalm 69:24: *Make their way into a snare and a fall.* Also: *He lets their light be extinguished in the midst of darkness and hardens them in their own delusion, for their ways are harmful.* The Election <note>meaning the "selection" or "choosing" process of God</note> passes over these people, for they were called at the beginning and are still called at all times, but they will not come. Thus Christ says: *We have piped for you, and you have not danced.* Also: *O Jerusalem, how often I have wanted to gather your children together, as a clucking hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you yourself would not.* You were seized in the Call of God, but you turned yourself away from it by your own will.

Reason then says: "They were not able to come."
Answer: Why were they not able, since they were called? He who is not in the Call cannot come; but who can say who that might be? The Devil within them does not want to; he tears the Word from their hearts so that they do not believe or be saved, as Christ says. Therefore, they are rejected in the **Election**. So it is also with man. Many a soul is a good little grain, but the Devil's weeds ruin it.

You might say: "That cannot be, since Christ says in John 10: *My sheep are in my hands; no one can pluck them out of my hand.*"

Christ is then crucified and killed in His members, and the Temple of the Holy Spirit is turned into a temple of harlotry—understand this in regards to the soul. Not that Christ Himself can be killed, but rather His temple, which is His member. For here is the separation in the Election.

The Election is the Spirit of Christ, which then passes such a soul by, for His voice is no longer in the soul; she no longer has a Divine hearing because she is outside of GOD. Therefore Christ says: *He who is of GOD hears GOD’s word; therefore you do not hear, because you are not of GOD.* They have lost the Divine voice within them and have taken in the Devil's voice in the <term>Turba Magna</term>. <note>Turba Magna: Latin for "Great Disturbance." In Böhme's philosophy, this represents the chaotic, wrathful, and destructive element in nature that breaks things apart.</note>

### Part 3 / Chapter 15.

the Earth would not be able to ignite the **essence** <note>original: "Ens," a term Böhme uses to describe the inner vital substance or "being" of a thing</note> within the core or seed, in which the **three first principles** (Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury) <note>Böhme adopts these Paracelsian terms to describe the fundamental forces of nature: Salt (stability/contraction), Sulfur (fire/growth), and Mercury (motion/communication).</note> reveal themselves, if the Sun, as the Light, did not first ignite them. For these three first principles lie locked within the Earth in a "cold fire"; but when the Sun ignites them, the "hot fire" unfolds itself, from which the **Light of Nature** <note>The inherent intelligence or divine spark within the natural world.</note> originates—that is, it unfolds within it. In this same unfolding, the seed is taken up; the power of the Earth then receives its dear Son in the seed, who is born from her, and accepts him with joy. For, according to his essence, he is more noble than his mother.

Now we must consider the ground of the Earth, namely: whether the three first principles in a place where the seed is sown are similar in their active, manifest **essence** to the quality of the seed. Where this is the case, they receive the seed as a dear son with joy. Likewise, the essence of the seed yields itself with great desire into its mother, the Earth, for it finds its true mother from whose property it was born. Thus, the essence of the Earth also finds a true and very dear son in the essence of the seed; they rejoice in one another, and the growth begins. But if the essence of the Earth in that place is unlike the essence of the seed, then the Earth may well receive it, but only as a **step-son**. She does not pour her joy and desire into it; instead, she leaves the step-son standing. He must then suck essence out of his true mother, who is hidden very deep in that place; due to this hiddenness, many a seed decays before it can reach the true mother of its own property. And even if it does take on essence from that which is mismatched, it remains in great danger before it can transform its own essence into the foreign essence; it will never become as good or strong a tree as it would have been had the seed been sown into its true mother. For the contrary

<column-break/>

**essence** <note>original: "Ens"</note> is always opposed to it, and the **vital powers** <note>original: "Essentien"</note> remain in conflict. Because of this, the tree becomes gnarled and crooked, and yields little, and often (if an external **constellation** <note>The alignment of the stars, which Böhme believed influenced the "spirit" of the natural world.</note> falls upon it) it bears evil fruit, or even withers and dies. For when the essence of the Earth mixes with a contrary constellation and takes it in, the Earth rejoices in the property of that constellation because they are of one will in that same property. In their union, they wish to give birth to a new son; then the tree is abandoned by the essence of the Earth and perishes, or brings forth evil, meager, or false fruit. 

If we now consider the growth of this tree, we find first the hidden ground of all secrets. First, it takes the essence of the step-mother into itself, and it gives its own essence to the step-mother, who also receives the seed's essence, but not with such joy as if it were a matching essence. She does indeed draw the essence of the seed to herself, in which the root originates; but there is soon a reluctance in the three first principles of the mother, which causes the root to become knotty and deformed. In this conflict, the fire now ignites in the essence of the seed through the power of the Sun, in which ignition the **Great Mystery** <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum," the source of all manifestation</note> becomes manifest in the **Spirit of the World** <note>original: "Spiritu Mundi," the animating soul of the physical universe</note>. The essence of the Sun seizes this and rejoices in it, for the power of the Sun becomes substantial within it and draws the essence of the seed from the root upward into the heights, so that a fruit may be born within it. The Sun gives itself with its power into it without distinction; it loves every fruit and plant, and withdraws itself from no thing. It desires nothing else than to raise up every herb, or whatever it may be, into a good fruit. It accepts them all, whether they be evil or good, and gives them its "Will of Love," for it can do no other; it is a servant of all beings, providing what it has within itself. is also a poison to the evil, and a good to the good; for in their power the growing soul arises, and in their authority it also perishes. Understand it thus: if the properties of nature in the **three first principles** <note>Böhme refers to the Paracelsian triad of Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury—the foundational forces of all matter and spirit.</note>—at the root of the tree within the Mother Earth—are of a single will, then the Earth gives her power and sap to the root with great desire. Then the power of the Sun rejoices within it and hastens its growth. But if the Earth and the root are contrary to one another, then the power and sap of the Earth are withheld from the root. If the Sun then ignites the root and the tree with its rays of light, the **three first principles** within ignite in their own malice; they burn up the **essence** <note>original: "Ens," the vital inner substance.</note> of the Sun and dry up the water, so that the trunk or the branches wither away. However, when the **three first principles** are able to receive the sap of the Earth, they remain in **equality** <note>original: "Gleichheit," meaning a state of balance or harmony.</note> and do not awaken in conflict; instead, they harmonize with the rays of the Sun's light. We see this also in the **Mystery** <note>original: "Mysterio"</note> of the **Spirit of the World** <note>original: "Spiritu Mundi"; the animating spirit that permeates the physical universe.</note>: when the fiery property winds itself upward so that it can ignite the Sun, a parching heat arises that beats down the herbs and the grass.

Furthermore, we see in this figure how it happens in the growth of the branches: when the trunk rises, the conflict in nature rises with it. For when nature is ignited in its **temperature** <note>original: "Temperatur," meaning the perfect balance of opposing qualities.</note>, it stands incessantly in the distinctiveness of the Sun's power. It always seeks to cast off the malice of the **three first principles**, and these also hasten in their own will. From this separating and moving apart, the branches break out from the trunk. In winter, the cold shuts them in with their conflict; but when spring comes and they can finally reach the heat, they enter into the conflict once more. Then the conflict pushes out again into the limbs and branches, as one can see in the annual growth of every tree. But now we must consider the inner ground of 

<column-break/>

this driving out of the branches. For we see that one branch grows large and bears fruit, while another withers. We understand this through the distinctiveness of nature in the **Spirit of the World** <note>original: "Spiritum Mundi"</note>: where the properties each want to seize a particularity for themselves within the **essence** of the tree and thus abandon **equality**. This particularity, which breaks out of equality and into the power of fire through its **pride** <note>original: "Hoffart," a central concept for Böhme where a part of nature tries to exalt itself above the whole.</note> over the others, refuses to remain in the Sun’s will within the **temperature** (which nourishes it); consequently, it is stifled once it has pushed out from the trunk. For that same **inner consciousness** <note>original: "Scientz"; in Böhme’s terminology, this refers to a self-aware power or "knowing" within nature.</note> in that property has led itself into its own will; it wished to break out in pride sooner than the others who remained in equality, and it lacked sufficient power. When a strong constellation of the stars then penetrates these proud branches from the outside, sifting and testing whether they are from the **equality**, they become poisoned and wither. They are apostate branches, and the heat of the Sun in the **Spirit of the World** dries them out. But the other branches come from the **temperature** and from the powerful drawing-out of the Sun; the Sun rejoices in their properties, tempers them, and draws itself out within them. The Sun raises these same branches in its power, for their properties stand within its will. We see further how the properties of nature in the branches, as they grow, are corrupted by outward accidents—such as the stars or the impure air where the Sun’s rays cannot reach—so that they become knotty, crooked, and hunched; many a branch is thereby stunted and cast off to wither. And just as it happens with the understanding and growth of a tree, so it happens with the origin and growth of man.

The constellations in the clockwork pull them together, but most are pulled together through their own will, where the human will—which is from the eternal ground—constellates itself, whereby the external constellation is broken. We see this in how the rich constellate with the rich; likewise, the noble with the noble; otherwise, if the **Spirit of the World’s** <note>original: "Spiritu Mundi"; the animating spirit of the physical universe.</note> constellation were not broken, many a poor servant girl would be joined to a nobleman, for they constellate with one another externally in the **Spirit of the World**. But the self-made human soul-constellation, coming from the high ground, is more powerful than the constellation in the **Spirit of the World**. Therefore, it happens often and for the most part according to the soul's constellation, which surpasses the outer world in power and highness, just as it depends on the sower where he sows his grain, even if another field might be better suited for it. # On the Election of Grace.

The constellation in the **Spirit of the World** <note>original: "Spiritu Mundi"; the animating spirit of the physical universe.</note>, in the true order of the formed, spoken Word, is embittered; for it does not stand in a joyful state within the great clockwork of nature. Instead, it immediately shoots out its enemy-rays from the **Great Turba** <note>original: "Turba Magna"; the "Great Disturbance" or source of chaos and destruction in nature.</note> into the formation of the creature, whereby many a fruit is spoiled before it even receives life. What kind of effect there may be here in the **Center of Nature** <note>original: "Centro der Natur"</note> regarding life, I leave to Reason to contemplate, as well as how nature hardens itself in its adversity. What kind of soul-fire it awakens and gives birth to within itself is easy to imagine, of which the Scripture says: **GOD'S** wrath hardens them, so that they do not come to the true holy light. For whichever quality the soully fire possesses, such a light also originates from it, and life now stands in that soully light; therefore the Scripture says: *With the holy you are holy, and with the perverse you are perverse;* <note>Psalm 18:25-26</note> whatever a people is like, they have such a **GOD** accordingly.

The Light of Nature—in which the voice of **GOD** in Paradise has again embodied itself in the woman's seed (in which Christ is conceived and born)—now stands in the innermost ground and is meant to reveal itself through the kindled soul-fire, entering into and working within the creature. The soul should stand still before the Spirit of Christ, so that He may work within it; but the soul (meaning the soully quality) in which the soul-fire burns and becomes living, is in the wrath of conflict. Here now is the "pulling" in the wrath, and also the pulling of Christ through the Light of Nature; and here it is rightly said: wherever the **Science** <note>original: "Scientz"; Böhme uses this to mean an active, creative spark of knowledge or the "will-spark" that directs a being's essence.</note> of the groundless <note>original: "ungründlichen"; referring to the *Ungrund*, the absolute, abyssal source of all being before it takes form.</note> will directs itself from the ground of eternal nature into the soully property, and gives itself up as a servant in obedience, it becomes the servant of that thing: either to the wrath of **GOD** in the fury of eternal nature, or to the life of Christ in grace, as **St. Paul** says in Romans 6.

<column-break/>

Thus Reason speaks: "The soully **essence** <note>original: "Essentz"</note> cannot do otherwise; it must suffer what **GOD** does with it, especially since it is corrupted and inclined toward wrath?" Answer: Yes, in its own selfhood it cannot. But Christ, when He took on the soully quality, shattered the wrath and the **Turba** <note>the "Disturbance" or chaotic disruption.</note> of the false will with love, and introduced His love into the created Word, giving it to the soully **Ens** <note>original: "Enti" from Latin *ens*; the essential being or core substance of the soul.</note> as a helper. It depends entirely on which quality surpasses the other: either the Light-fiery or the Wrath-fiery; **GOD'S** love or His wrath. For the **Ens** of the soul has as yet no understanding, but it has the ground of the will from the groundless eternal will, for the purpose of bringing forth the "Place of God," where the Father's groundless will gives birth to the Son as the power. The soul's **Ens** stands in this groundless will, and **GOD** wants to have it from him; it should give birth to Divine power. And since the soul cannot do this by its own ability after its fall, He has embodied the Kingdom of His Grace within it and revealed it in the name of **JESUS**.

If the soully groundless will now adopts the Spirit of Christ in its innermost ground, then Christ seizes it and draws it up into Himself. There, the "ability" originates; for the essence of wrath is shattered by the embodied voice of Divine love, and the Spirit of Christ penetrates the Light of Nature in the soully quality and works within it—just as the light of nature in the earth works in the seed to become a tree, pressing itself in so that the seed may take root. And this "pressing-in" of the Spirit of Christ into the **Ens** of the soul is the Divine **Calling** <note>original: "Beruff"</note>, of which the Scripture says: *Many are called, etc.* For thus they are called in the soully ground before the soul even has life.

Question: But why does the Scripture say "Many" and not "All"? Answer: Christ stands before all and calls them all; for

### Part 3 / Chapter 15.

The Scripture says: **GOD** wills that all people be helped (1 Timothy 2:4). But they are not all capable of hearing the Call, for many an **essence** <note>original: "Ens"; in Böhme’s philosophy, this refers to the fundamental spiritual substance or "being" of a thing.</note> is more devilish than human; the same has been overwhelmed and hardened by the Wrath. In such a person, the light shines in itself within the darkness, but the dark essence of the soul has not grasped it. The Call passes by this soulish essence, for the soulish property is gripped in darkness. The light certainly penetrates it, but it finds no **essence** of love within it where it might ignite itself. Therefore, the essence of the creaturely soul remains outside of **GOD**, dwelling within itself, and **Christ** also remains dwelling within himself, and yet they are near to one another. But a **Principle** <note>original: "Principium"; Böhme uses this to describe the different "realms" or "dimensions" of existence (Darkness, Light, and the Physical World).</note> separates them, like the great chasm between the rich man and poor Lazarus, for they stand against one another like life and death.

By this, it is understood that **GOD** makes known His wrath and hardens them—but not out of some foreign or Divine will or purpose, but rather out of the way He has introduced His Word into nature and **differentiation** <note>original: "Schiedlichkeit"; the quality of being distinct or diverse within the divine unity.</note>. It is not the holy will of **GOD** that withdraws from them so that they must remain hardened, as Reason erroneously thinks here. For He is within them and would gladly have them and reveal Himself in them, as in the **Image of GOD**. But the Fury in the **Center of Nature**—where the will of the **Unground** <note>original: "Ungrund"; the "Abyss" or the primal, groundless void from which the Divine Will originates.</note> separates itself into the darkness—has seized them, and filled the shattered gates of Divine Love with the abominations of inherited sins.

To this, the contrary **constellation** <note>The spiritual and astrological alignment of qualities at the moment of conception.</note> of inequality contributes, where the husband and the wife, in both their wills, sow against each other only hatred, cursing, and a sheer will for death. They capture their life-**tincture** <note>original: "Tinctur"; the spiritual life-force or "inner quality" that animates the soul.</note> in a hostile will and come together only in the mixing of their seed in beastly lust; no will is faithful to the other, and they intend only poison and death, cursing one another at all hours and living together like dogs and

<column-break/>

cats. Just as their life and constant **conduct** <note>clipped: "L[auf]"</note> is, so also is their soulish **tincture in the** <note>clipped: "Tinctu[r im]"</note> seed. Therefore **Christ** says: A **bad** <note>clipped: "bö[ser]"</note> tree cannot bear good **fruit** <note>clipped: "Früchte trag[en]"</note> (Matthew 7:18). For in the tincture of the seed, the hardening is **already present**; what can **GOD** <note>clipped: "GO[TT]"</note> do about it, if they plant a thistle? One might then **ask** <note>clipped: "[spricht]"</note>: what can the child do about it? **Answer** <note>clipped: "Antw[ort]"</note>: The child and the parents are one **tree** <note>clipped: "Bau[m]"</note>; the child is a branch on that same tree. **Therefore** <note>clipped: "D[arum]"</note> listen, Reason: When does the **sun** change a branch on a sour tree so that **it** <note>clipped: "sie"</note> becomes sweet? Should **GOD** then act against **the** <note>clipped: "sein[em]"</note> purpose of His spoken Word **and** <note>clipped: "und"</note> Will for the sake of a thistle? Yet the kingdom of darkness also **needs** <note>clipped: "au[ch]"</note> creatures; they are all useful to **GOD**. To the **ungodly**, **GOD** is a savor **unto** <note>clipped: "z[um]"</note> death, and to the holy, a savor **unto** <note>clipped: "z[um]"</note> life (2 Corinthians 2:15-16). Therefore, the **will** toward destruction **originates** <note>clipped: "urstän[det]"</note> in the essence of the **creature** <note>clipped: "C[reatur]"</note>: and the will toward holy life **originates** from **GOD** in **Christ**, and **they** <note>clipped: "d[iese]"</note> are both within one another as one thing, but **understood** as two Principles. Because they **are** <note>clipped: "werd[en]"</note> both the working of the creature, **they** <note>clipped: "sie"</note> are also drawn by both. But if it **is** <note>clipped: "ist es aber / d[aß]"</note> that **Christ** can find no place of His **rest** <note>clipped: "find[en]"</note>, then the devil possesses the place where **Christ** should work.

-> Election of Grace 8. 48–64. <-

Thus every child born from **man’s** and woman’s seed has this **gift of grace** <note>clipped: "G[naden-Geschenck]"</note> standing opposite the light of life in its inner ground; it offers itself to **every** soul and stretches its **desire** out toward the soul through the whole time of a person's life, calling to her: "Come here **to** me, and go out from the earthly **imagery** <note>clipped: "Bildlichke[it]"</note> in the Fury and from the **Phantasy** <note>original: "Phantasia"; the false, self-centered imagination.</note>." **Opposing** this, as soon as **its** <note>clipped: "i[hr]"</note> life begins, there stands in every soul the fierce, awakened **wrath** <note>clipped: "Zor[n]"</note> of **GOD** in the essence of **differentiation**, within which also lies the introduced **serpent's poison** together with the devil’s desire.

# Of the Election of Grace.

Thirdly, every seed of the body, according to the outer world, stands under the authority of the **Spirit of the World** <term>Spiritus Mundi</term> <note>The vital force or soul of the physical universe that governs natural processes.</note>, within the **Constellation** <term>Conſtellation</term> <note>The astrological alignment of the stars and planets at the moment of birth.</note>. Just as the great **Clockwork** <term>Uhrwerck</term> <note>Böhme frequently uses the image of a clockwork to describe the mechanical, predestined movements of the natural and celestial worlds.</note> stands in its figure at that time, the **Spirit of the World** also gives the person such a figure in the property of their outer life; it models such an "animal" into their outer property. For the spirit of the outer world, drawn from the elements, can give nothing other than an animal. Such an animal arises because the entire Creation lies within man, and because—through the Fall—he led himself out of the **Temperature** <term>Temperatur</term> <note>The state of perfect balance between opposing spiritual forces; the Fall disrupted this harmony.</note> into earthly desire and imagery, such that the **Spirit of the World** became manifest within him in all its **differentiation** <note>original: "Schiedlichkeit"; the quality of being divided into distinct, often conflicting, parts.</note>. 

And so, this spirit still divides itself into such a figure at the beginning of every child's life. As the stars stand in their wheel, so he makes such an image in that property out of the **clay** <term>Limo</term> <note>original: "Limo"; Latin for mud or slime, referring to the "dust of the ground" from which Adam was formed.</note> of the earth, that is, into the four elements. Because of this, many a person from their mother’s womb—according to the outer man—possesses the nature of an evil, poisonous serpent, a wolf, a dog, a toad, a sly fox, a proud lion, a filthy sow, or a vain peacock. Likewise, some have the nature of a courageous horse or other good, tame animals; all according to the figure as it exists in the **Spirit of the World**. Thus, that same **constellation**, from the outer purpose of the formed Word, instills in one person good reason and senses, along with honor and worldly luck, while in another it instills misery, misfortune, folly, malice, roguery, and a bad will toward all kinds of vices. Consequently, if such a person does not continually kill the implanted earthly animal and break that evil will with the gift of Divine Grace, they will fall into the hands of the executioner.

Now behold, O Man! This is what the outer purpose of the formed and spoken Word brings to you, wherein both Evil and Good lie, and where the **formative science** <term>Scientz</term> <note>original: "Scientz"; in Böhme’s usage, this is not "science" in the modern sense, but a formative, "knowing" power or seed-essence that seeks to manifest itself.</note> of the seed divides itself into a specific property at the beginning of life. And herein lies the pull from the Father’s property toward the Evil or the Good,

<column-break/>

and into whatever **essence** <term>Ens</term> <note>original: "Ens"; the fundamental "being" or spiritual substance of a thing.</note> the life has aligned itself according to the stars. That same **constellation** then pulls itself into its own likeness; it always desires to dwell with and in its own kind. For instance: a pious man gladly dwells with the pious, and a mocker with mockers, a thief with thieves, a glutton, a drunkard, a gambler, a whoremonger, and the like, also dwell with their own kind. Their nature pulls them there out of the property of **GOD’S** wrath. So too, the actual sins of the parents enter into this property, for every child is born from the seed of the parents; whatever the parents are, the child is also. However, the **constellation** often changes this with force and compels the nature into its own power, if it be strong.

Now see, this is the "pull" of the outer life, where **GOD** says: *Whom I harden, I harden* (Romans 9:18). Thus is man hardened, and also drawn, whether piously and sensibly toward humility, or toward pride. This is now **GOD’S** purpose according to His wrath, which man has awakened in himself; for man is the outer, birthing Word of **GOD**, through which **GOD** acts with the outer creature just as He grasps it within His **Clockwork**. Through this **Clockwork**, He also reveals His glory, both according to fire and light, according to understanding and folly, so that one may be made manifest and recognized in the other, to show what is good. 

But this **Clockwork** of the spoken Word is not **GOD** Himself; rather, it is only an image of Him—namely, the outward, substantial Word into which He has enclosed the Creation and out of which He created it. For no creature can come from the purely Divine property, because that has no foundation or beginning; therefore, a creature can form itself into no other beginning than through the Word of Power, through **differentiation**, and out of the distinctness of the "Speaking"—where the Speaking must introduce itself into Nature, otherwise the Word would not be made manifest. The inner property of the soul now lies in the first created **constellation**,
