 of Divine power moved / and **essentially** <note>original: *essentialiter*</note> took on our human flesh and blood together with the soul / and made the faded heavenly **substance** <note>original: *Ens* - refers to the spiritual essence or "being" that was lost when Adam fell.</note> in the seed of Mary on our behalf alive / which revelation also penetrated into Mary’s heavenly being / so that her own heavenly virginity / which had faded in Eve / became alive: and in this living virginity / as in Adam’s heavenly **womb** <note>original: *Matrice* - The spiritual matrix or "mother-source" of life.</note> / GOD became man.

The Word and the soul are not one single being / rather the Word and the soul stand alongside each other as two persons; the Word penetrates the soul / and out of the Word shines **Majesty** / as the Light of Life / and the soul is free for itself / for it is a **creature**. I give this earthly comparison: look at a glowing iron / which is in itself dark and black / and the fire penetrates the iron / so that it all shines / yet nothing happens to the iron / it remains iron / and the property of the fire keeps its own right / it does not take the iron into itself / but it penetrates the iron / and the iron is at once as

14. **Question:** We have examined what the difference is between the eternal Word and the soul that has assumed the eternal Word; now I would also like to know if there is no difference at all between our soul and the soul of **Christ**?

**Answer:** When the Word came into the flesh / it became heavenly / just as it had become earthly in Adam. For the flesh of **Christ** was led into the Word / into the eternal will / so that the flesh and the Word became one inseparable person: Now, it was a matter of the eternal will / from which Adam had departed / and **GOD** led us back into that same will in **Christ's** soul. **GOD** is not such a clumsy body / but a body in power and heavenly flesh and blood / where our will is / there is also our heart: **GOD** is in us: When we enter into his will / then we put on his Wisdom / and in that Wisdom, **Christ** is a man / thus we enter into his humanity / and become a new man in the life of **Christ** / in the soul of **Christ** / in the flesh of **Christ** / in the tincture <term>original: *Tinctur*—A term from alchemy used by Böhme to describe the spiritual essence or "life-dye" that transforms and vitalizes matter.</term> of **Christ** / in the Majesty of **Christ** / and **Christ** is in his Father / and his Father is eternity and the end of nature. Where will you go further / you poor human? Do not let the Devil and the Anti-Christ make a fool of you.

...[we understand] that this new image had to be led through death and the wrath of fire back into the heavenly Divine essence in the <term>Holy Ternary <note>original: Ternarium Sanctum; in this context, it refers to the holy realm or "body" of the Trinity where the divine essence is manifested.</note></term>. Since the Word of eternal life has moved again within our cold love and virginity, which were locked in death, and took upon itself our corrupted virginity, and became an inner and outer human, and led the center—as our soul-fire—into its love: So we recognize His love and virginity, introduced into us, as our own virginity. For His love and virginity have wedded themselves with our cold love and virginity, and surrendered into it, so that **GOD** and man shall eternally be one person. Now Reason <note>The author uses 'Reason' (Vernunfft) to represent the limited, earthly intellect that struggles to grasp spiritual mysteries.</note> speaks: "That happened in **Mary**, as in only one person; but where do I stand? **Christ** was not also born in me." Oh, our great misery and blindness, that we do not want to understand anything! How completely the earthly, tangible addiction has blinded us, and how the devil has thoroughly seduced us with the abominable Anti-Christ in **Babylon** <note>original: Babel; symbolic of the state of spiritual confusion and the false, worldly church.</note>, so that we wish to have no spiritual senses at all! Look now, you miserable and wretched Reason, what are you? Nothing else than a whorish woman toward **GOD**: How else should I name you, since you are broken and perjured regarding the pure virginity toward **GOD**! Do you not have **Adam’s** flesh, soul, and spirit, and have you not come from **Adam**? Have you not sprung from **Adam’s** water and fire? You are indeed **Adam’s** child: Do as you will, you must stand still: You swim in **Adam’s** <term>Mystery <note>original: Mysterio; the hidden spiritual foundation or source-reality of a being.</note></term>, both in life and in death. Now Reason speaks: "How does it happen then, since I am **Christ’s** member and **GOD’S** child, that I do not feel Him, nor sense Him?" Answer: Yes, here is where it lies, dear soiled little piece of wood—smell your own bosom! What do you stink of? Of devilish addiction, such as temporal lust, greed, honor, and power. Listen, that is the devil’s garment: take off this fur coat and throw it away! Place your desire into **Christ’s** life, spirit, flesh, and blood; imagine into it <note>This refers to the spiritual practice of "imagining"—forming one's inner will and focus—upon the divine reality until it becomes part of one's nature.</note>, just as you have imagined into earthly addiction, then you will put on **Christ** in your body, in your flesh and blood; you will become **Christ**; His incarnation will manifest itself in you at once, and you will be born anew in **Christ**. For the Deity or the Word, which stirred in **Mary** and became human, also became human at the same time in all deceased humans from **Adam** onward, who had surrendered and entrusted their spirit to **GOD**, or to the promised **Messiah**; and it also extended to all those who were yet to be born from the corrupted **Adam**, who would only allow that same Word to be awakened within them; for the first human also encompasses the last. **Adam** is the trunk, we are all his branches: but **Christ** has become our sap, power, and life. When Christ hung on the Cross and died, we hung there with Him and in Him, and died in Him; we also rose from death in Him and live eternally in Him, as a member of the body. And thus the "Seed of the Woman" has crushed the serpent’s head; Christ has done it in us, and we have done it in Christ. The divine and human essence did it. Now, it all depends on us following Him, etc.

<margin>On the Incarnation, Part 1, Chapter 12.</margin>
This, herewith, is the ground of truth, and also the fruit and benefit of the Incarnation of JESUS Christ; all of which the author summarizes in the following:

<margin>On the Incarnation, Part 1, Chapter 14, Section 12.</margin>
Thus we will now speak with the ground of truth concerning the Incarnation or humanity, and say with clear, dry, uncovered words—not from delusion or opinion, but from our own true knowledge, in the enlightenment given to us by God:

I. That the new, born-again man, who lies hidden in the old like gold in the stone, has a heavenly **tincture** <note>A spiritual essence or "alchemical" force that transforms and perfects nature.</note>, and carries divine, heavenly flesh and blood, and that the spirit of that same flesh is no foreign spirit, but his own, born out of his own essence.

II. We confess and say that the Word, which became man in the Virgin Mary, is the first ground for the beginning **tincture** in the **Sulphur** <note>In Böhme’s terminology, Sulphur represents the soul’s inner fire or the vital, formative principle of life.</note>, and we confess Christ's Spirit, which fills heaven at all ends, to be dwelling in that same tincture.

III. We confess this heavenly flesh to be Christ’s flesh, in which the Holy Trinity dwells inseparably.

# Chapter II.
## Regarding the Circumcision, Childhood, and Baptism of **JESUS Christ**.
### Also: Regarding His Temptation, Ministry, Miracles, and Holy Conduct.

---

**1. Question.**
Why did *Christ*, the Son of **God**, have to be circumcised in His flesh on the eighth day after His birth, since He was born of a Virgin?

**Answer.**
**Christ** allowed Himself to be circumcised as a Jew, and allowed Himself to be baptized as a Christian, to demonstrate this: that He had revealed the Fire-Baptism <note>The "Fire-Baptism" refers to the Old Covenant's strict law and the "burning" wrath of the Father, which is transformed into the "Water-Baptism" of the Son’s gentleness.</note> in His revealed love, within humanity in the water, as if in great gentleness and endurance, and had transformed the two into one. Among the Jews, the Essence <term>Essence: original "Ens" or "Ente"; the spiritual "being" or "seed" of faith.</term> of faith had not yet become flesh;

<column-break/>

therefore **GOD** gave them the sign of inward circumcision through the outward circumcision of the foreskin, so that they might have a sign that the Holy Spirit, in the essence of faith, would cut away their sinful birth through the Covenant, so that they might be children of grace in the essence of faith. Now, to confirm this, *Christ* was circumcised—not because any sinful birth clung to Him, but because He came in the form of sinful flesh. Thus, in that same form, He confirmed the Covenant of **GOD** with the outward circumcision of the foreskin of His flesh, as a benefit of the Covenant according to the flesh, and thereby abolished the Covenant of Circumcision because He fulfilled the sign with living truth—about which more will be said below.

# Of the Baptism of JESUS Christ.

2. Q. How does it happen that Christ, in the twelfth year of his age, remained in Jerusalem against the knowledge of his parents, and was sought by his mother with such sorrow?

Ans. In this figure <note>The author uses "figure" to mean a symbolic representation of a deeper spiritual truth.</note> we see the will of the inner and outer worlds—how they exist within one another, against one another, and yet are one. Just as two kingdoms were manifest in Christ: one worked in **GOD’S** will and broke the will of the outer world of his parents, in that Christ remained behind against his parents' will, over which they were troubled (which the Divine will in Christ well knew). The other kingdom, as his parents' will, broke the Divine will, so that he went home with them and was subject to them according to their will.

Signat. 7. 63. <note>This likely refers to Jacob Böhme’s work *De Signatura Rerum* (The Signature of All Things), chapter 7, paragraph 63.</note>

3. Q. What must we consider regarding the Baptism of Christ?

Ans. By whom he was baptized, where and when he was baptized, and then to what purpose and end this occurred. Christ was baptized by John the Baptist. When **GOD** established the testament of his holy Covenant of Grace in Paradise <note>The "Covenant of Grace" refers to the promise of salvation given after the Fall of Man.</note>—arising from the prefigurement, the sacrifices, and the circumcision—He wished to ordain it into Water-Baptism. Thus, He brought forth a branch from His covenant in human manifestation and began the Water-Baptism through him. This is clearly seen in John the Baptist, who was announced by the angelic message and came from the High-Priestly lineage. His incarnation did not come from the will of the flesh, for his father Zacharias and his mother Elizabeth were old, advanced in years, and their "fleshly seed" <term>Seed: Translated from the German *Sperma*, which in this historical context refers to the vital procreative power or life-force.</term> had already died away, as human capacity was already gone. The seed of Zacharias and Elizabeth was awakened by the movement of the Holy Spirit from the Paradisiacal Covenant of Grace within their now-faded "spermatic" 

<column-break/>

property. Truly, he came from a human ground, but not from human power; for the anointing in the Covenant awakened him, so that their "seed" was opened above the course and power of nature's own ability. For the Holy Spirit awakened a seed in them from human "sperm" and chose him for that purpose from his beginning. But the anointing of John occurred at the greeting of Mary, when she came to the aged Elizabeth, and the Divine anointing from Christ's incarnation moved within her (meaning within Mary). When Mary, full of this anointing, greeted Elizabeth, the incarnation of Christ "dipped" <note>This is a mystical interpretation of baptism as an immersion or "dipping" into the spirit.</note> into John in his mother’s womb with the anointing through Mary’s greeting. And not only into John, but also into his mother Elizabeth, so that she became full of this anointing, and both mothers prophesied in the spirit of this anointing.

And this is the Baptism of John: that he was anointed out of Christ with the incarnation of Christ, and received the Baptism of the Holy Spirit from the Covenant in his mother's womb. Thus, he was to be a forerunner and proclaimer, showing that the time of anointing and the fulfillment of **GOD’S** Covenant was at hand; that **GOD** had introduced His Covenant of the Grace-Anointing into humanity, and that the Covenant had become a man. Now, **GOD** wished to pour out the anointing through the humanity of Christ, through an elemental medium (which no longer stands in fire, as in the Old Testament, but in the love and meekness of water). The time of Grace is here, since **GOD** has given His anointing into humanity. And then we see that **GOD** did not begin a new Covenant there, but only a new order; for John was circumcised, as was Christ. John took the authority and calling from the Covenant of Circumcision, from the sacrifices of fire, and led it by **GOD’S** command into the

For sin should now no longer be extinguished through fire / but through the love / which **GOD** revealed in the Covenant through Christ / it should be drowned and transformed through **GOD’S** gentleness.

Therefore, **GOD** also ordained such a means for the purging of sin through Water-Baptism / to indicate / that sin should be drowned in the blood of Christ in his love and grace / and that man should henceforth have an open gate of grace in love and gentleness toward **GOD** / so that he might enter into grace through such a gate only with repentance for his sins / and with the remission of sins.

For flesh and blood / without this anointing / cannot baptize / because this power does not reside in human authority / but in Christ’s authority.

## 4. Q. When was Christ baptized?

Ans. Christ was baptized / when he was thirty years old / when he reached his proper manhood / and his humanity stood in full vigor / like a plant / that has now reached its perfection / and pushes forth toward bloom and fruit / just as all ages in the Lineage of the Covenant / point toward the movement and revelation of the Covenant: So Christ’s thirty-year age signifies the highest perfection and maturity / as the manhood of the Covenant of **GOD**. Furthermore / when Christ was to be tempted by the devil / what did Christ do / when he was to endure this struggle of testing / when the human essence <term>essence (Essentz)<note>In theosophical writing, "essence" refers to the fundamental spiritual substance or inner nature of a being, which must be transformed or "tinctured" by the Divine.</note></term> should enter back into the Godhead with its desire / and eat of **GOD’S** Bread / that is / of Divine Being? He went to the Jordan / and let himself be baptized by John. With what? With water in the Jordan / and with water in the Word of Life / as with Divine Essence / which had to tincture <term>tincture (tingiren)<note>To "tincture" is a term borrowed from alchemy, meaning to permeate, color, or transform a substance through a spiritual or medicinal agent.</note></term> our mortal essence in the outer humanity of Christ / from which the Divine hunger arose in the human essence / so that he desired to eat **GOD’S** Bread. Therefore the Spirit of **GOD** took him / and led him into the wilderness / there the Father’s property in the Wrath <note>Original: *Grimm*. 5. **Question:** But why did **Christ** allow himself to be baptized, since he already possessed within himself the true baptism of the Holy Spirit?

**Answer:** When we look upon the baptism of **Christ** / and then his temptation immediately following the baptism / we will find our own new rebirth / and see in which kingdom we lie imprisoned; and it rejoices us deeply in this knowledge / that **GOD** has become man. If we then wish to grasp this / we will place the baptism of **Christ** at the beginning / and then the temptation / so that they stand in the proper order.

As we know / that through **Adam’s** fall we fell into **GOD'S** wrath / in that the spirit or soul of **Adam** turned away from the heart of **GOD** and toward the spirit of this world / whereby the holy, heavenly image was immediately extinguished / and wrath held the poor soul captive in darkness. There, the devil immediately gained his entrance and dwelling-place in the wrath of the human soul / and if the **Crusher of the Serpent** <note>original: *Schlangen-Treter*; a reference to the Messianic prophecy in Genesis 3:15 where the "seed of the woman" shall bruise the serpent's head.</note> had not immediately entered into the dividing-goal / into the **Center** <term>Centrum: the core or generative source of life's light</term> / then wrath would have swallowed us up / and we would have remained eternal companions of all devils. But because the **Crusher of the Serpent** stepped into the middle / though not yet in full humanity / but into the **Center** of the Light of Life / the poor captive souls / who turned back again to **GOD** / were thus bound again to the **Godhead** in that **Center** / until the Hero entered into humanity / where he took up the whole of man again in his conception and humanity. And we see this clearly in his baptism. For there stood a person / who was **God** and man: He had both the heavenly and also the earthly body. Now, however, the baptism was not intended or established for the sake of

the earthly, perishable body / which belongs to the earth / nor for the sake of the heavenly body / which was already pure and without blemish / but for the sake of the poor soul / because the heavenly man in **Christ** had taken our natural soul into his heavenly humanity within **Mary’s** womb / and at the same time the earthly part still clung to the soul; thus **GOD** the Holy Trinity, through human hands, took the water of eternal life in the pure element <note>The "pure element" refers to the spiritual substance of the heavenly world, distinct from the four physical elements of the fallen world.</note> / and dipped or baptized the soul into it / as I might say.

See / you dear soul / you had gone out from **GOD** / but his love caught you again / and bound you to his thread / with the promise. Now the fulfillment of the promise has come / and put another new body upon you: Now, however, you can receive no other soul / for yours was already out of eternity. Now, just as the Holy Spirit overshadowed and filled **Mary**; so the water from the heavenly **Matrix** <term>Matrix: the divine womb or generative source of all things</term> / which has its beginning from the **Trinity** / overshadowed and filled the soul of **Christ** / and the souls of all **Christians** / in the baptism in the **Jordan**; and thus it **renewed** <note>original: *renoviret*</note> and beautifully washed the earthly water of the **offspring** <term>Ausgeburt: that which is birthed or manifested out of a source</term> within the soul / so that in the new body it may be a pure angel for itself / which may eat of the heavenly fruit / and that is the cause of baptism.

### Part 4, Chapter 2.

Maria, his Mother, in her essence or seed, had moved; and into the dead soulful essence, He had introduced the glance of God’s eye in love, and had revealed love in death. Here began the struggle which Adam was meant to have endured in Paradise. For on one side, God’s love-desire, which had revealed itself in the soul, pressed hard upon the soulful and bodily property, and introduced its desire into the soulful property; the soul was to eat of it and give Manna to the body. And on the other side, the Devil, within God’s fierce property, pressed upon the soul’s property and led his **imagination** into the property of the first **Principle**, into the **Center** of the dark world, which is the soul’s fire-life.

Now the struggle was over the image of GOD: whether it wished to live in God’s love or wrath, in the fire or the light. For the property of the soul, according to its fire-life, was the Father’s property according to the fire-world. Just as the soul in Adam

<column-break/>

had extinguished the light-world, so the light-world was again embodied into it with the name **JESUS**, which occurred in the conception of **Mary**. Now it was at stake in the temptation: in which property did the human wish to live? In the Father’s in the fire, or the Son’s in the light of love? Thus, the entire property of the person of *Christ* was tempted. The Devil spoke, just as he had spoken to Adam: "Eat of evil and good; do you not have bread? Make bread out of stones; why do you hunger so long in your self-property?" But the Divine desire spoke: "Man does not live by bread alone." Thus, the property of the fiery soul, with its desire, yielded itself into the love, as into the property of the Speaking Word, and the fire-desire ate Manna within the love-desire.

O you **philosophers**, mark this well, for as this occurred, love **transmutated** <note>original: "transmutirte"; Böhme uses alchemical language to describe the spiritual transformation of the soul from a state of wrath to a state of love.</note> the fiery property into its own love-property. Here the Father gave the fire-soul to the Son—understand this as the fiery property of the spoken **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurius"; in Böhme’s system, Mercury represents the active, vibrating power of life and speech.</note> being given to the speaking **Mercury** in the light. For *Christ* also spoke thus afterward: "Father, the people were yours, and you have given them to me, and I give them eternal life." Here, God’s love was given to corrupted humanity as the eternal love-life; the love has yielded itself entirely into the fire-fierceness and has **transmutated** the fierceness of the soul into a love of the joyful kingdom.

But if the soulful and bodily property had followed the Devil into God’s fierceness, and had made and eaten bread from the "locked Mercury," then the will would have entered back into <term>I-hood</term> <note>original: "Ichheit"; referring to the ego, self-will, or the state of being separated from God.</note> and could not have been **transmutated**. But because he entered into <term>resignation</term> <note>original: "Gelassenheit"; a central term in German mysticism meaning a state of yieldedness or letting go of the self-will to God.</note>, into the Speaking Word of GOD, whatever that might then do with him, the will sank out of its "I-hood" through the fierce death of the wrath of God (as out of the Spoken Word, which the Devil had corrupted with his **imagination**)...

<summary>This page describes Christ's temptation as an alchemical-spiritual "transmutation" where the soul's fiery, wrathful nature (the Father's property) is yielded to Divine love (the Son's property). By refusing to create bread from stones, Christ rejects "I-hood" (self-will) and restores the divine image that Adam lost.</summary>

<meta>This page follows the account of Christ’s temptations in the desert. Having triumphed over the Devil's final offer of worldly power, Christ now transitions from his private testing to his public ministry. This section outlines the theological framework of his mission through the "Threefold Office" (Prophet, Priest, and King), a standard concept in Reformation theology that the author imbues with mystical significance.</meta>

<header>1177 Of the Threefold Mediatorial Office of JESUS Christ. 1178</header>

### Chapter III.

# Of the threefold Mediatorial Office / and the great Work of Redemption of JESUS Christ / of his Suffering / Death and Resurrection / of his Ascension / Sitting at the Right Hand of GOD / etc.

**1. Question.**
**What did Christ do after the baptism of John, and after he had been tempted by the Devil in the wilderness?**

**Answer.**
HE stepped forward, as the Emissary of **GOD**, toward the great work of the redemption of the human race. As the great **Prophet**, he taught the way of salvation and redemption, and confirmed his teaching with great power, deeds, and miraculous signs, as one who had the authority. As a **High Priest**, he offered himself through his eternal Spirit to **GOD** his heavenly Father. As a **sovereign King**, he ruled and triumphed over all his enemies, and led a new government in righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit. For he is the crown and the ultimate goal of the Covenant, who—as the promised <term>Crusher of the Serpent</term> <note>original: "Schlangen-Treter"; a reference to the prophecy in Genesis 3:15 that the offspring of the woman would crush the serpent's head.</note>—was hitherto embodied in the Patriarchs and pressed toward manifestation; but now, in the fullness of time, was perfectly manifested in the flesh. He is like the blossomed <term>Lily</term> <note>In this mystical tradition, the lily represents the spiritual rebirth and the blossoming of the soul in divine light.</note> from the plant and the Root of David, in whom the enclosed Covenant of the Promise of Grace has opened. With his color, power, and virtue, he has unlocked the entire Kingdom of Heaven, and with his lovely fragrance, he has awakened all of humanity—which hitherto lay imprisoned in death—to a new life.

**2. Question. How then did Christ administer his Prophetic Office?**

**Answer.** He administered it partly with powerful teaching, and partly with signs and wonders. The teaching did not consist of unnecessary dogmas and vain <term>opinions</term> <note>original: "Meinungen"; the author uses this to describe sectarian disputes or human theories that lack spiritual life.</note>; rather, the teaching of Christ consists of a powerful conviction of the heart, leading to a joyful and voluntary obedience of faith, to the killing of the "old man" and the resurrection of the "new man," as a true rebirth from the Spirit. Christ pursued this teaching as the open mouth of the Kingdom of **GOD** in the days of his flesh with external words and testimonies; but now he pursues it from within, through his internal Word and Spirit, upon all the consciences and souls of men.

<column-break/>

Christ’s light and power arise in his children in the inward ground / and shine through them throughout the entire course of their lives / and in that same well-fountain of light is the Kingdom of **GOD** within man. If he does not have this / let him bicker however he wishes / he will not bring it in with any "opinion." But if he has it / then nothing but streams of love will flow from that same well-fountain. There is no need for "opinions" / let him only see to it that Christ’s Kingdom be born in him / that Christ becomes man in him; otherwise he is no Christian / let him hold whatever opinion he likes / he must stand upon the Vine of Christ as a branch. <note>original: "Joh. 15"; referring to John 15:5, "I am the vine, you are the branches."</note> Opinion helps him nothing / but rather true faith / which is active through the breaking-forth of love / and works good works. <note>original: "Gal. 5, 6"; referring to Galatians 5:6, "faith working through love."</note> If he has not the works of love / then he also has no faith. Opinion does not create salvation, but <term>Babel</term> <note>original: "Babel"; used here to mean a state of spiritual confusion, sectarianism, and the "tower" of human intellect built apart from God.</note> / a confusion of the tongues of the one Love. No one is a Christian unless he loves his neighbor and desires to do him good.

Christ has bequeathed his kingdom to us in his Testaments / whoever wishes to receive it must become his child / otherwise there is no inheritance. To work repentance is better than to desire to know much. If knowledge is not given to someone by **GOD** / he will not understand the ground of Divine Mystery; but if it is given to him / he needs no image. To remain in the humility and simplicity of Christ / and to cling to his love and grace without despising anyone / is good Christianity. Everything that speaks of itself is Babel. In Christ we are all members / and only One. Amen.

<header>4. Part / Chapter 3.</header>

**3. Question.**
**Why did Christ teach in parables and proverbs, and not freely and openly?**

**Answer.**
Christ taught the things that are unavoidably necessary for a person's salvation in a very simple and clear manner, so that no doubt remains. For he who accepts it in simplicity <note>The German *Einfalt* (simplicity) here refers to a "single-hearted" or "uncomplicated" faith, rather than a lack of intelligence.</note> requires no further explanation other than how the Spirit inwardly confirms it to the person's conscience; this can be seen in Matthew 5, 6, and 7 <note>The Sermon on the Mount, which the author views as the core, simple essence of Christ’s teaching.</note>. These testimonies convince Jews, Turks <note>In the 17th and 18th centuries, "Turks" was the standard term used to refer to Muslims.</note>, Heathens, and all people of the pure truth, provided they are accepted in simplicity. 

Therefore, I say: everything is Babel <note>A common term in mystical writing for the "confusion" of organized, sectarian religious denominations that fight over doctrine.</note> that bites at one another and wrangles over the "letters" <note>The "letter" refers to a literalist or legalistic interpretation of scripture without spiritual insight.</note>. The letters all stand in one root, which is the Spirit of **GOD**. Just as various flowers all stand in the earth and grow alongside one another: none bites the other over their colors, scent, or taste; they let the earth and sun, as well as rain and wind, heat and cold, do with them what they will; yet each grows in its own essence and property. 

So it is also with the children of **GOD**: they have various gifts and knowledge, but all from one Spirit. They rejoice alongside one another in the great wonders of **GOD**, and thank the Most High in His wisdom. Why should they wrangle long about Him in whom they live and are, and whose essence they themselves are? It is the greatest folly in Babel that the Devil has made the world wrangle over religion, so that they fight over self-made opinions and over the letters; yet the Kingdom of **GOD** stands in no opinion, but in power and love. 

Christ also said, and left it finally to his disciples: they should love one another, by which everyone would recognize that they were his disciples, just as he had loved them. If people sought after love and righteousness as much as they do after opinions, there would be no strife at all on earth: we would live as children in our Father, and would need no law nor order. For **GOD** is served with no law, only with obedience;

<column-break/>

Laws exist because of the wicked, not for the sake of love and righteousness; the wicked are driven and coerced by laws. We all have only one single life-path <note>The original text is fragmented: "L- den". In this context of "keeping still," it likely refers to a "charge" or "burden" (Laden) or "suffering" (Leiden) that leads to spiritual peace.</note>, which is that we keep still before the **LORD** of all beings, and surrender our will to Him, and let His Spirit work, play, and do in us what He wills. And what He works and manifests in us, that we give back to Him as His fruit. 

If we did not wrangle over the various fruits, gifts, and knowledge, but instead recognized one another as children of the Spirit of **GOD**, what would there be to judge us? After all, the Kingdom of **GOD** lies not in our knowledge and suppositions, but in the power. If we did not know half as much and were much more childlike, but had only a brotherly will toward one another and lived as children of one mother, or like the branches on a tree that all take sap from one root, we would be much holier. 

Knowledge is only for this purpose: that we learn it because we have lost the Divine power in Adam, and are now inclined toward evil, so that we may learn to recognize that we have evil properties within us and that doing evil does not please **GOD**. Thus, through knowledge, we learn to do right. But if we have the power of **GOD** within us and desire with all our strength to do right and live right, then knowledge is merely our play <note>The author uses "play" (*Spiel*) to describe the joyful, non-legalistic expression of divine wisdom in the soul.</note> in which we rejoice. 

For true knowledge is the revelation of the Spirit of **GOD** through eternal wisdom: He knows in His children what He wills; He pours out His wisdom and wonders through His children just as the earth pours out various flowers. If we now dwelt alongside one another in the Spirit of Christ as humble children, and if each rejoiced in the other’s gifts and knowledge, who would judge us? Who judges the birds in the forest, who praise the **LORD** of all beings with various voices, each in its own essence? Does the... <note>The sentence ends abruptly; the catchword for the next page is "the."</note>

### 4. Question: How then did Christ perform His miracles?

**Answer:** Christ prayed to His Father; His human soul pressed into the **Word of the Lord** <note>original: *Verbum Domini*</note>, into the seven golden candlesticks, which are the burning Spirit of Love of God’s heart in the Father, in the still eternity. There, Christ worked great miracles here on earth in the Father's <term>working power</term> <note>The original German uses *Quall*, a term specific to the author Jacob Böhme, referring to the "source-springing" or "quality" of a divine force.</note>: For He opened the seals of hiddenness and drove the unclean spirits out of the fierce torment of the souls, and resounded with His word in the **center** <note>original: *Centro*</note> of the poor imprisoned soul, so that all the seals were moved and pressed into the life of Christ toward **GOD**.

<margin>The Threefold Life, ch. 3, 72.</margin>

### 5. Question: Why could Christ, if He was **GOD’S** Son, not perform miracles in all places?

**Answer:** Christ performed no miracles unless the faith of those who desired the miracle awakened His eternally-speaking Word and affected and quickened His mighty <term>Mercury</term> <note>In Böhme’s alchemy-influenced theology, "Mercury" (*Mercurius*) represents the active, moving, and expressive power of the divine Word within nature and humanity.</note> in His humanity. Faith must be present. For Christ also testified that He could perform few miracles in Capernaum, besides healing a few sick people; for the faith of the people of Capernaum would not enter into the Divine Mercury of Christ. Thus we see there that the person of Christ, as the creaturely human, could not work miracles by His own power, but rather the **Mercury**, as the living speaking Word within Him. For the person also called into **GOD** as the speaking Word and placed His desire therein, as can be seen on the Mount of Olives, that He prayed until He sweated bloody sweat, and with Lazarus, when

**6. Question: What miracles did Christ then perform?**

**Answer:** He worked miracles according to all seven properties of nature. For instance, according to **Saturn**, or the harsh, stern property, he raised the dead and redeemed souls from greed <note>In Böhme’s system, Saturn represents contraction, coldness, and the "grip" of material or spiritual avarice.</note>; he unlocked the prisons and all bonds, even **Hell** <note original: "Tartarum">The Greek term for the deepest abyss of the underworld.</note> itself. In **Jupiter** <note original: "Jove">Jupiter/Jove represents the property of wisdom and light in the soul.</note>, Christ made the immature, the unlearned, and the weak to be knowing and understanding; out of poor fishermen and carpenters he made Apostles and messengers of **GOD**. In **Mars**, as the third property of the mother of all beings—that is, in the ignition of the fire—Christ drove the devils out of the possessed. In the **Sun** <note original: "Sole">The fourth property, representing the balance between fire and light.</note>, as the fourth form, namely the property of fire and light, he made the blind to see, both physically and spiritually. In **Venus**, he opened the highest fountain of love; he loved his brothers even unto death and gave his life for his brothers in the property of wrath <note>Venus represents the sweet, yielding power of love that overcomes the "grimness" or wrath of the fire.</note>. In **Mercury**, or the sixth form, Christ made the deaf to hear, the speechless to speak, and cleansed the lepers from the poison of Mercury. In the seventh form, as the **Moon** <note original: "Luna">The Moon represents "Wesenheit" or substantiality—the physical manifestation of the spiritual.</note> or substantiality, Christ fed five thousand men with five barley loaves and turned water into wine, etc.

**7. Question: How did Christ become a High Priest?**

**Answer:** Paul says:
> Every high priest taken from among men is appointed for men in matters pertaining to God; and no one takes this honor for himself, but he who is called by God, just as Aaron was.

<column-break/>

Thus Christ is a High Priest, not according to the flesh from the tribe of Levi, nor extracted from one people for one people alone; rather, according to his humanity, he is an extract from the peoples, lineages, and tribes of the Earth. According to his heavenly humanity, he is an extract of Paradise, as well as of all the angelic hierarchies, kingdoms, and principalities. According to his Divine nature, he is the Heart and the Son of the eternal Godhead; for from him, through him, and in him, all things are—both those in heaven and on earth, and those under the earth. Now, just as every priest is appointed as a servant of the holy and true **tabernacles** <note original: "Hütten">A reference to the biblical Tabernacle, used here as a metaphor for the spiritual dwelling of God.</note>, to offer gifts and sacrifices: so Christ is appointed a High Priest for the service of future goods. He entered the sanctuary once and for all through a greater and more perfect tabernacle, which is not made with hands and is not of this creation, nor through the blood of goats and calves, but through his own blood, and has found an eternal redemption, offering himself to **GOD** through his eternal Spirit as one without blemish. In this single sacrifice, he fulfilled everything that was prefigured through the Aaronic priesthood and the Mosaic sacrificial service. Thus, when the time was fulfilled that this Covenant of Grace was manifested and took on humanity in soul and body, the prefiguration ceased. For **GOD’S** **Wrath-fire** <term>Zorn-Feuer: The aspect of God's nature that acts as a consuming, judging fire when not balanced by love.</term> in the soul was quenched, and in its place the **Holy Fire** burned in the heavenly humanity, and the true sacrifice of atonement became manifest in this holy fire within humanity. For the soul, according to the Father's property, had become a pure fire of wrath. The Father led this fire of wrath into the Son’s **Love-fire** <term>Liebe-Feuer: The cooling, light-giving essence of the Son that transforms the Father's wrath into joy.</term>, so that the Love-fire of the Son swallowed the Wrath-fire of the Father, and such fire now became a single fire. To this fire, the heavenly humanity gave itself as food, in the manner that one gives a lovely, oily balm to a fierce, dark, smoldering fire, so that the fire...

**8. Question: How then did Christ, the High Priest, offer the great atonement sacrifice to his heavenly Father?**

**Answer:** Through his bitter suffering and death on the trunk of the Cross, so that his whole life was nothing else, outwardly and inwardly, than a ceaseless struggle of suffering and death; but he especially offered himself solemnly <note original: "solenniter">Latin: in a formal or ritualistic manner.</note> to **GOD** his heavenly Father in his High-Priestly struggle on the Mount of Olives, where he wrestled with the wrath of **GOD**, and gave himself up in humble gelassenheit <note>A key term in German mysticism meaning "yieldedness" or "letting go" to God's will.</note> into the fierce wrath of the Father.

Now it was a matter of wrestling with one another / from which also came the temptation of Christ / and when the Divine World was victorious / there followed the great wonders through the outer human world. ### 9. Question: How then did Christ suffer inwardly in His soul?

**Answer:** During the time of earthly life, the human soul is bound by three cruel chains. First is **GOD’S** severe wrath, the abyss and dark world, which is the *center* <note original: "Centrum">The core or internal origin point of the soul's being.</note> and creaturely life of the soul. Furthermore, it is the soul's own life-birth, whose innermost

<column-break/>

root is poison and fierceness. Since the soul is from the eternal source of torment <note original: "Quall">Böhme uses this term to describe both a "wellspring" (Quelle) and "torment" (Qual), signifying the restless, aching nature of eternal existence without God's light.</note> and manifests itself out of eternity, no one can redeem it from behind in its own root of eternity, or lead it out of the wrath, unless someone comes who is Love itself and is born into the soul's own self-birth, so that he may place it out of the wrath into Love within himself—as happened in *Christ*. The second gate and chain is the Devil's desire toward the soul; for he constantly sifts and tempts the soul, and without ceasing wants to turn it from **God's** truth into unbridled arrogance <note original: "Geilheit">In this context, it refers to a wild, unruly rankness of spirit, including pride and greed, rather than modern sexual lust.</note>—such as pride, greed, envy, and wrath. With his desire, he constantly inflates and ignites these same evil properties within the soul, whereby the soul's will turns away from **GOD** and enters into selfhood. The third and most dangerous chain to which the poor soul stands bound is the corrupted and entirely dead, earthly, mortal flesh and blood, full of evil desire and inclination; and it is the *Stellar Region* <note original: "Sternen-Region">The sphere of astral and planetary influences that Böhme believed governed the physical body and lower mind.</note> in which the soul swims as in a great sea, through which the soul is constantly infected, so that it becomes ignited.

We know well of these three chains in our deep knowledge, which we see in the ground of the original record <note original: "Urkund">The fundamental testimony or "charter" of creation's nature.</note> and truly recognize that we could not be released from them unless the Deity entered into the soul and birthed the soul's will again out of the fierceness into itself—into the light of gentleness. For the root of life must remain, otherwise the entire creature would break apart. Since, however, the soul stood with its innermost root in the abyss of hell, and according to the kingdom of this world in hard death—so that if it left the flesh and blood, as well as the *Stellar Region*, it would still have to remain in an external hardness where there was no torment, yet it would stand in its own torment within itself, only in the wrath of the original record, in great misery: it was necessary not only that **GOD** came into the soul and birthed it to the light, for

**9. Question:** How then did Christ suffer inwardly in His soul?

**Answer:** During the time of earthly life, the human soul is bound to three cruel chains. First is **GOD’S** strict **Wrath**, the abyss and the dark world, which is the center and creaturely life of the soul. Furthermore, there is its own life-birth, whose innermost

<column-break/>

root is poison and fierceness. Since the soul is from the eternal **Source-Torment** <note original: "Quall">Böhme often uses this term to describe the "laboring" or "pulsing" source of life which can feel like torment (Qual) or a fountain (Quelle).</note> and manifests from eternity, it cannot redeem anyone beneath itself in its own root of eternity, or lead them out of the wrath, unless one comes who *is* that very soul and is born in its own self-birth, so that He may place it out of the wrath and into Love within Himself, as happened in Christ. The second gate and chain is the **Devil’s** desire against the soul; for he constantly sifts and tempts the soul, incessantly trying to provoke it from **God’s** truth into vanity—such as pride, greed, envy, and wrath—and with his desire, he constantly stirs up and ignites those same evil qualities in the soul, whereby the soul's will turns away from **GOD** and enters into **Selfhood**. The third and most harmful chain to which the poor soul stands bound is the corrupted and entirely vain, earthly, mortal flesh and blood, full of evil desires and inclinations; and this is the **Star-Region** <note>The "sidereal" or "astral" realm, which Böhme believed exerted a constant, often distracting, influence on human desires and moods.</note> in which it swims, as if in a great sea, whereby the soul is daily infected and ignited.

Of such three chains we know only through our deep knowledge, which we see in the ground of the **Original Source** <note original: "Urkunde">The primal testimony or foundation of being.</note> and recognize quite specifically: that we could not be released unless the **Godhead** entered into the soul and bore the soul’s will again out of the fierceness and into itself, toward the light of gentleness. For the "life-corner" <note>The fundamental structural "angle" or "point" that allows a creature to exist as an individual entity.</note> must remain, otherwise the whole creature would break apart. However, because the soul stood with its innermost root in the abyss of hell, and according to the kingdom of this world, in harsh death—so that if it left the flesh and blood (as well as the Star-Region), it would then have to remain externally in a hardness where there was no torment, and yet stand in its own torment within itself, only in the fierceness of the **Original Source**, in great misery. It was not enough that **GOD** came into the soul and bore it into the light, for...

### On the Threefold Mediatorial Office of JESUS Christ.

There was a danger that the soul might again depart from the Light through its own **Imagination** <note>In Böhme’s thought, "Imagination" refers to the soul’s creative power to focus its will and shape its internal reality, for better or worse.</note>; therefore, **GOD** also assumed a human soul—from our soul—and put upon that soul a new heavenly body, drawn from the first glorious body that existed before the Fall. This was attached to the old earthly body, not merely as a garment, but as something participating in the very **Essences** <note>Spiritual substances or fundamental qualities.</note>. Thus, a creature stood forth who was the whole **GOD**, containing all three **Principles** <note>The "Three Principles" describe the structure of reality: the Dark World (God’s wrath), the Light World (God’s love), and the Outer World (the physical universe).</note>. And since each must be separated from the other—such as the kingdom of this world, which is a root or a "puffer-up" of the root of **Wrath** <note>original: "Grimm"</note>—it was necessary that **GOD**, with the new body, enter into the division of that root and the kingdom of this world, even into the death of **Wrath**. He broke death in two and, by His own power, surged through death like a flower springing from the earth; thus He held the innermost **Wrath** captive within the power of His own new body. This is how we understand **Christ**: He truly entered therein, took the fierce anger and the devils within it captive, and now flourishes with His holy heavenly body through death. He has shattered death so that eternal life sprouts through it. Thus, death has been captured by the new eternal body and has become an eternal prison; in this way, an eternal life has grown within death. This new body steps upon the head of death and **Wrath**, for their torment now remains confined within the prison of the new eternal life. So stands the **Woman** <note>A reference to the "Woman clothed with the sun" from Revelation 12, representing the redeemed soul or the Church.</note>, in whom the new life flourishes, upon the earthly **Moon** and despises all that is earthly; for the earthly passes away, leaving only the hardness of death behind. Thus, God's Word entered death like a living spring and birthed the soul within itself, sprouting out of the soul through death like a new flower—and this flower is the new body in Christ.

So you understand, firstly, how Christ shattered death, because the eternal

<column-break/>

life in the Godhead flourishes through death. And secondly, you understand how the new body in **GOD’S** Love holds the eternal **Wrath-Torment** captive: for Love is the prison. The **Wrath-Torment** cannot enter into Love, but remains separate by itself, just as it has been from eternity; and therein the devils are imprisoned. For the Light of **GOD** strikes them down; they cannot, nor may they, behold it for all eternity, as a **Principle** <note>A fundamental boundary of existence.</note> remains between them. For Love flourishes in the **Center of the Soul**, and therein the **Holy Trinity** appears. Thus, we have received a Prince of eternal life and need do nothing more than penetrate into Him with strong confidence and faith. Then our soul receives His love and flourishes with Him through death; it stands upon the earthly—upon flesh and blood—as a growth in God's kingdom within the body of **JESUS Christ**, and triumphs over the **Wrath**. For Love holds the **Wrath** captive and mocks death, as St. Paul says: *Death, where is your sting? Hell, where is your victory? Thanks and praise be to GOD, who has given us the victory through our LORD JESUS CHRIST!*

->Princ. 25. §. 17.<-

Now, although Christ in His soul calmed the fierce torment through **GOD’S** Love and was Himself free from such bonds and chains of darkness, the **Wrath of GOD** nevertheless remained ignited in humanity—especially in the Jewish people, and most of all in the high priests and scribes. Through their **Imagination**, they channeled their ignited **Wrath** into the meek and patient Lamb; they sought to ignite the **Fire-Soul** of Christ with anger and to awaken it into **Wrath**. There, the terrifying battle and struggle began against the power of darkness and hell. Because the soul has its **Origin** <note>original: "Urstand"</note> in the **fourth form** <note>In Böhme’s seven qualities of nature, the fourth form is the 'Cross' or the flash where fire and light originate; it is the point of tension between darkness and light.</note>—that is, in the **Wrath-Torment**—all the **Essences** of that fourth form pricked at the soul. When this form was stirred into action, it agitated all the forms in nature; they all became sharp and bitter. Because of this, the person of Christ sweated blood from His body in the Garden, when He cried out: *My Father, if it is...*

For when **Adam** first departed from his **Angelic Form** and entered into **Fierceness** <note>original: "Grimmigkeit," referring to the wrathful, dark quality of nature.</note> and the **Serpent-form**, the devils mocked him. And fourthly: just as Adam’s **Essences** were broken after his entry into the spirit of this world—when the woman was made from him and a rib was broken from his side for the woman—so too had **Christ’s blood** to flow from all His essences during His scourging. His side had to be opened with a spear, so that we might see the "broken man" within us, whom the Devil had mocked; thus this Christ had to bear such mockery on His body for us again.

And sixthly: just as Adam, out of his own **presumption** in his will to become highly wise like **GOD** Himself, entered into this world in the spirit of fierce torment: so too did all mockery, martyrdom, and pain have to happen to Christ, the **Second Adam**, at the hands of the "clever" **Scribes**. This shows us that in our greatest "art" <note>Here meaning worldly skill, cleverness, or academic learning.</note>—which we think we possess according to the schools of this world—we are fools, for such wisdom is foolishness before **GOD**. Thus also, when we fall away from **GOD** onto our own reason, we are fools. How then do you **Anti-Christian** fools want to bind us to your "art," asking us to look away from **God’s heart** toward your fabricated trifles? For you are merely the **fools of this world**, just as Adam became when he turned his spirit away from the **heart of GOD**.

10. Question: Some circumstances, especially his words on the cross, are still to be taken to heart: when JESUS said: *Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do?*

Answer: When JESUS broke through the death of humanity and took away the "selfhood" <note>original: "Selbstheit," the ego-centric nature that separates man from God</note>, he did not throw away the human quality in which death and the wrath of GOD resided; rather, he truly accepted it for the first time. Understand: he truly took the outer kingdom into the inner. For the outer kingdom is a wonder born out of eternal wisdom in the speaking Word, and spoken into a form as a revelation of the Godhead in love and wrath, in good and evil. Thus, Jesus did not want the outer image of wonders—the likeness of God—to perish. Instead, the "fierceness" <note>original: "Grimm," the harsh, wrathful quality of nature</note> which had overwhelmed love in man was to be forgiven; that is, it was to be yielded into nothingness, as if into freedom, so that it would not be manifest in its own self-quality. It was to become a servant, and only a cause for fiery love and a kingdom of joy. Nothing in man was to perish, for GOD created him in His image.

His mother is the Christian Church on earth, wherein the children of God are born according to the Spirit; he shall care for her, and lead and guide her, until the number of humanity from the flesh is completed. Then the spiritual body shall begin, and shall be tested in Christ’s death—in his entry into wrath, where he transmuted wrath into love—and the kingdom shall be separated from him along with the torment of darkness. But during this time, although the spirit is transmuted in Divine power and is inwardly baptized with the Virginal Baptism <note>A reference to the "Heavenly Virgin Sophia" or divine wisdom, a central concept in Böhme’s theology representing the pure, spiritual element of humanity</note> and puts on the image of Christ inwardly, as the body of Venus in love <note>In Böhme’s cosmological system, Venus represents the power of love, desire for the light, and spiritual sweetness</note>: yet the Adam within is not capable of this until he also enters into the transmutation of Christ, which happens in dying. So, in the meantime, John, as the teacher of Christ in Christ's stead, shall take care of the external mother according to the external man, and pasture and teach Christ’s sheep with Christ’s Spirit.

<column-break/>

And he shows us clearly how the external human being is not God’s mother; for Christ separates himself from his external mother and gave her to John. He had put off the eternal nature <note>original: "ewige Natur," referring to the ground of existence from which the soul is birthed</note> as the Father of the eternal birth. Therefore, those do wrong who honor and worship the external mother of Christ as the Mother of GOD. The entire true Christendom is Christ’s mother, which gives birth to Christ within itself; and John, as the servant of Christ, is her foster-nurse, who cares for the mother of Christ as John did. He immediately took care of Christ’s mother and tended to her as her son, not as her lord; for Christ also spoke to him: *Behold, that is your mother.* Thus all disciples and teachers of Christ should do, and care for poor Christendom as sons, with great humility toward the mother, serving her with earnestness and diligence, tending to her modestly and humbly, pasturing and comforting her with Christ’s Spirit. Not as the priests of Babel <note>A common term in Reformation-era radical theology for the corrupted, institutionalized church structures</note> do, who, as fat, rich lords, ride over her and wish to be lords over the mother, and only seek honor and fat bellies in lust, and live in strife. All of these together, whatever name they may bear, are not "Johannites" <note>Followers of the spirit of John the Apostle</note>, but are the poisonous mercurial <term>mercurial: referring to Mercury as a principle of restlessness, pain, and "stinging" conflict when not balanced by light</term> Pharisees, in whom is nothing but anxiety, martyrdom, and torment, where one property always torments and is hostile toward the other, holding it for false. And yet they are all from one root and all have one will, only that one color does not shine like the other.

->Signat. 11. 53 === 59.<-

12. **Q.** For what did JESUS thirst on the cross?

**Ans.** He thirsted for the members of human property <note>In this context, "property" (Eigenschaft) refers to the essential nature or characteristics of a person</note> and desired human salvation as the health of his members—understand this as his children, who were to be born in him. And the Jews gave his humanity gall and vinegar to drink, and when he tasted it, he would not drink it.

# Part 4 / Chapter 3

Here is once again the external image of how things occurred within the internal. The name JESUS, as the Love of GOD—which had entered into humanity and wedded itself to it—thirsted in its longing of love for corrupted humanity. It desired to taste the pure water of humanity within itself. However, the fierce Wrath of GOD, which was ignited within the human property, entered into this thirst of love-longing along with the human property. And when the love-longing tasted it, it did not wish to drink it, but rather sank down into it, as if entirely surrendered or released, and appropriated itself entirely *essentially* <note>original: "essentialiter"</note> into the Wrath of GOD, as a total obedience, surrendered in complete and peculiar freedom. 

This was now a terror-shock <term>terror-shock: "Schrack," a pivotal moment in Böhme’s philosophy where one quality is suddenly transformed into another, like a lightning flash</term> of the fury, that Love entered into it; because of this, the earth trembled and the rocks were rent asunder, for Death was thus terrified before Life. And here, the property of the awakened fury separated itself into the Center <note>original: "Centrum"</note>, into the first Principle <note>original: "Principium"</note>, into the fire-root; and out of the Center in the human property, there now arose the hunger for Rebirth. From the hunger for death, there became a hunger for life: for Love tinctured <term>tinctured: an alchemical term meaning to permeate and transform the inner nature of a substance</term> the Wrath, so that from the fire-longing for dark impression, there became a longing for life.

Understand this rightly: GOD the Father, who had given his beloved Heart into humanity to help them, thirsted for humanity as for his Heart or the Word of Power. And the Godhead in humanity, as the Father’s Heart, thirsted for the Father; and the essence of Light and Love thirsted for the essence of Fire. For in Adam, the essence of the fire or the soul—which had stood within the being of Love and Paradise—had gone out into its own selfhood and had become disobedient to GOD. Therefore, the essence and being of Light and Love died away in the "greening"—that is, in the vegetable life <note>the vital, growing force of the spirit</note> or the heavenly greening and feeling of the Paradisiacal torment—and woke up to the earthly world.

<column-break/>

Here the Father led the soul, which had entered into his fury and revealed itself in his wrath, back into Love, as into the faded image of Paradise. And here the dark world trembled in the terror of death before the fire-terror, which rose up in Love within death as a terror-shock of joy. This joy-shock entered into the deceased bodies of those who hoped for Israel <note>the patriarchs and prophets of the Old Testament</note> as a resonance of the power of GOD, and awakened them from death. 

This shock tore the curtain in the Temple, which is the Veil of Moses <note>a reference to spiritual blindness or the separation between man and the direct presence of God</note> that hung before the clear face of GOD, so that man could not see GOD. Because of this, man had to serve Him with a sacrifice and a prefigurement of this final sight, in which GOD revealed Himself in humanity. This shock broke the prefigurement in the sacrifice and revealed the clear face of GOD, uniting human time with eternity. Everything that the Jews did to JESUS from the outside was a prefigurement of the internal: how things proceeded between GOD and humanity, or between eternity and time. 

The Jews gave JESUS gall and vinegar in his thirst. These two properties are Mercury in the Sulfur of Saturn <note>original: "Mercurius im Sulphur Saturni"; these are alchemical metaphors for the soul's bitter, contracted state of suffering</note>, within the "Impression" <term>impression: the spiritual force of contraction or hardening that creates material density</term>. This is exactly the image of the soul's property as it is in itself alone, outside of the other form of Love. GOD gave this property of the soul back into his Love, death into life. The faded being of Love—which the Word of GOD took upon itself in Mary’s essence and seed—was made alive in the property of wrath, within the soul’s essence, as into the Center of the fire-world and dark-world. From this, the soulish fire-and-dark-world became a high kingdom of joy and Paradisiacal life. And here the Knight <note>the conquering Christ</note> mocked death and hell, as the dark world in the soul, and said: *Death, where is your sting now in man? Hell, where is now your victory in the fury of the poisonous torment in the spoken word or...*

# On the Threefold Mediatorial Office of JESUS Christ.

the light closed off the <term>Principle<note>In Böhme’s system, a "Principle" (Principium) is a fundamental realm of existence. The first is the dark world of fire/wrath, the second is the light world of love, and the third is the visible world.</note></term> of Hell; this is to be understood such that no devil dare look into it; he is blind within it, and it is his terror and shame. Thus, you should not think that Christ’s soul had traveled far away from his body, for all three Principles were present on the Cross—why then not also in the grave? At the very moment when Christ let go of the kingdom of this world, Christ’s soul penetrated into death and into the wrath of GOD; and in that same moment, the wrath was reconciled in love within the light, and became Paradise; and the devils were captured within themselves in the wrath, along with all godless souls. And immediately, life flourished through death; there, death was shattered and became a mockery. To the godless, who remain in wrath, death is a death; but to the saints in Christ, it is a life. Thus, the soul of Christ rested for forty hours in the grave within the Father, present with its body: For the celestial body was not dead, but rather the earthly one. The soul flourished in the celestial body through death, and stood for forty hours in rest. These were the forty hours that Adam had stood in sleep when his wife was made from him; likewise the forty days of temptation with Moses on the mountain, to see if it were possible to live in the Father’s power in the kingdom of heaven. But because it was found to be impossible, the people immediately fell away from the Law of the Father (as Nature) and honored a crafted calf as GOD, and Moses broke the tablets of the Law. And GOD spoke further in fire with Israel, so that they might see it was not possible to enter the promised land of Paradise until the right Joshua or JESUS came, who would lead them through death into life.

<margin>Principles 25. 76. 82.</margin>

In such a monstrous, masked image, it would have had to stand eternally before GOD, had not the great love of GOD come to its aid again: so that the Divine Word, as its first Mother (its first origin), spoke grace into it once more. That same Word wished to give itself again into the ground of the soul as a new source-well, joining with the innermost hiddenness and love, and introducing a new nourishment into the soul’s life. Through this, its natural, fiery, and painful property would be transformed back into the image of GOD. This great Divine Love wished to become a death to the rebellion, as well as to the venom of the serpent and the devil, and to kill the monstrous image with its false imagination, introducing the first image back into a new life. He broke [the devil's] will and desire, and with His love, He brought the false qualities back into the <term>Temperamentum<note>The perfect, harmonious balance of all spiritual qualities, which Böhme believed was lost when man fell into the conflicting "dark" and "light" properties.</note></term>. And He became a death to the Death that held us captive, so that Death's <term>wrath<note>Original: 'Grimm.' A key term for Böhme describing the harsh, fiery quality of God's judgment or the dark side of nature.</note></term> and fragility must die away within this introduced Love; and through Him, human life might blossom anew in such love, through a new will and eternal life. This newly introduced Love and Grace entered into the breaking of human life—that is, into the dying of man—in the person of Christ. It introduced the assumed human self-will into death and broke it. And the human image—which the self-will, through its imagination and desire for selfhood, had made so coarse, bringing it from its first angelic form into such a monster—He allowed to hang upon the <term>+<note>The cross symbol, used here as a shorthand for the Crucifixion.</note></term> and be mocked there. Thus, He bore upon the <term>+<note>The Cross.</note></term> the eternal mockery that man would have had to bear, and there publicly demonstrated before all angels and spirits how this great Grace-Love intended to break the devil's introduced desire as well as death itself. And with this newly introduced Love, He would blossom out through death and lead human life through death, transforming the fury of GOD’s wrath into love, making a light out of the darkness, and through this newly introduced love, transform and <term>transmute<note>To change the very nature or substance of something; a term borrowed from alchemy.</note></term> the coarse (earthly) human image back into a heavenly one.

In His resurrection, He displayed them all as conquered within the human soul and body, as a victor over them.

And it is now rightly said here, as Christ said in John 17: <note>original: "Vater, die Menschen waren dein, aber du hast sie mir gegeben..."</note> "Father, the people were yours, but you have given them to me, and I now give them this victory, as the new life introduced into death, which also breaks death within them, so that in my power they can go through death, and in my power also be thus transmuted, and through my resurrection come back to you."

19. **Question:** How long did Christ lie in His grave?

**Answer:** Just as Adam entered from the Light of God into the dark kingdom of this world, and Adam’s soul stood between two <term>Principles<note>In Böhme’s system, 'Principles' are the fundamental realms of existence: the dark fire-world (wrath), the light-world (love), and the external physical world.</note></term>, flourishing between death and hell within the body—so too did Christ wish to rise from death in His flourishing <note>Original: 'grünenden.' Literally 'greening.' Böhme uses this to describe spiritual life blooming or sprouting like a plant from a hidden source.</note> body at midnight. He wished to turn the night in His Holy Body into an eternal, bright day, where no night would ever enter again, but rather the light of God the Father and the Lamb would shine. And you should not think that the soul of Christ was in any other place during these forty hours than in the Father and in His body; there it flourished in great gentleness amid the persecution, like a little rose or a beautiful flower from the earth. Then our...

<column-break/>

...souls also flourish in our rest within the body of Jesus Christ, until the Last Day. In the passing away of this world, the new creature will break forth from the old, and meanwhile, the soul flourishes in the Holy Element within the body of Christ in quiet, gentle rest, until our forty hours are also over—and not an hour longer than the appointed time. Thus, the body of Christ rose again through the power of the Father by means of the soul and came forth, and had within it the eternal light of the Trinity.

There was no need for the stone to be rolled away, except as a sign for the blind Jews <note>A typical 17th-century theological polemic regarding those who refused to recognize Christ's divinity.</note>, so that they might see that all their actions were foolishness in trying to hold God back; also for the sake of the disciples' weak reason, so that they might see He had certainly risen, for thus they could go into the grave and see for themselves. Also, the angel appeared to them there and comforted them. In the same way, Christ wishes to comfort His afflicted ones who are saddened for His sake; yes, He is with them, as with Mary Magdalene and the two disciples on the way to Emmaus. You should know that Christ’s body cannot be held or contained by any rock or stone; He passes through all things and yet breaks nothing. He contains this world, yet the world does not contain Him. He suffers no torment from anything; in Him is the entire fullness of the Godhead, and yet He is not imprisoned. He appears as a creature in our human form, as large as our bodies, and yet His body has no end. He is the entire princely throne of the whole Principle. When He was here on earth in the earthly man, His outer man was measurable, like our bodies, but the inner man was immeasurable. For in the resurrection, we too are immeasurable in the body of Jesus Christ, yet visible and tangible in heavenly flesh and blood, like the Prince of Life Himself. In the heavenly form, we can be large or small, and yet nothing of us is broken; it requires no compression.

-># On the Triple Office of Mediation of JESUS Christ.<-

20. **Question:** How has Christ, through his heavenly humanity, raised his and our humanity again?

**Answer:** If my soul was not with Christ in death—since it existed in the Father from eternity in the Divine Essence—then I have no part in Christ's death. I know that Jesus Christ, through the power of the heavenly <term>tincture<note>In Böhme’s thought, a 'tincture' is a transformative spiritual force or quality that changes the state of a substance, much like an alchemical agent.</note>, has ignited the fire which was dark in the soul’s essence. He did this with his precious heavenly blood—which became blood from the Divine Essence within the corrupted seed of the human image. In that same hour, that soul-fire began to burn in white, bright, majestic power, light, and radiance. There, God’s wrath in the soul's essence was extinguished and turned into love. This was called Christ’s <term>Descent into Hell<note>Original: 'Höllenfahrt'. This refers to the theological concept of Christ descending into the realm of the dead after his crucifixion to liberate souls.</note>, as God’s love—by the power of the living Word, in the heavenly essence, with Christ’s blood—entered the center of the soul, as if into the Father’s wrath, and overcame and extinguished it with gentleness. This was the <term>smoke-hole<note>Original: 'Rauch-Loch'. A mystical term for the vent or entry point of spiritual darkness and evil influences.</note> where the devil and the seed of the serpent ruled. Now, that same hell was stormed, and the devil's kingdom in the soul was taken away. And it was said: just as sin came from one upon all and pressed from one upon all, so also grace and eternal life came from one upon all and pressed upon all. Whoever will not accept this but waits for a "special election" <note>A critique of strict Calvinist predestination, suggesting salvation is open to all who accept it through their own will.</note>, let him stay there, whether he comes or not. It is written: "We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we called you, and you did not come to us." <note>A reference to Matthew 11:17.</note>

It fell away entirely from the will of the outer world (which is both evil and good), so that it no longer lived for the world or the stars in the boiling heat of the four elements, but for the nature of the eternal Father in the boiling heat of the pure <term>Divine Element<note>A spiritual substance or environment that exists beyond the four physical elements of our world.</note>. 4. Part / Chapter 3.

Christ’s death with: The name JESUS was in Christ—in Adam’s humanity—the **Serpent-Crusher**: Christ entered into the image of the first Adam, so that the first Adam, within Christ’s humanity, became that same Christ and Serpent-Crusher; certainly not in the same individual creature, but in the same qualities of soul and body.

The first Adam fell down into sleep—as if into the faintness of the Divine world—and died in the <term>death of death<note>A common theological expression referring to the spiritual state of being dead to God, which Christ overcomes by entering it himself.</note>. The second Adam entered into the death of death and took the death of death into himself as a prisoner within Adam’s humanity. He became a death to Death and led Life out of death into eternal freedom. He arose in Divine omnipotence in the essence of the first Adam: God’s Spirit, in the speaking eternal Word, led Adam out of death within Christ’s humanity. Adam arose in Christ’s humanity, and all children of Adam who become partakers of Christ’s kingdom all rise in Christ—all in Christ’s flesh and blood, soul and spirit—but each in his own creaturely form that he held here and which died in Christ’s death. Each is a particular branch, but there is only one single tree; that is Christ in Adam, and Adam in Christ—only one, not two—only **One Christ** in all Christians. Thus I may say: Since I have died to the world in Christ, I am that same Christ, as a branch on the same tree. However, because I still live in my <term>selfhood<note>Original: 'Ichheit'. In Böhme's thought, this refers to the ego or the "I-ness" that seeks its own will instead of God's.</note> in the outer man, I must also die in Christ’s death with the outer man and arise and live in him. So I live now with the will of faith in the mind in Christ, and am a Christian in the will of the mind in the desire of faith; I take Christ into my will with his humanity and cast my will into his death. Thus my inward man has died with him in Christ’s death and no longer lives for selfhood, but is surrendered in him and lies buried in his death. But because he has arisen in GOD-

<column-break/>

-S will, I live in his resurrection in him. But my <term>earthliness<note>Original: 'Jrrdigkeit'. Refers to the physical, fallen nature that belongs to the temporal world.</note> in its selfhood lives for the earthly world until it also dies to selfhood and enters entirely into <term>resignation<note>Original: 'Gelassenheit'. A key mystical term for a state of yieldedness or letting go of one's own self-will to allow God to act through the soul.</note> and <term>decay<note>Original: 'Verwesenheit'. While this often means corruption/decomposition, in Böhme's context, it refers to the passing away of the old, fallen self-nature.</note>. Then Christ will awaken it through my inner man, who now lives in him. Just as he has arisen from the dead, so also shall I—who must die to earthliness in him—arise in him, as in my first father Adam, in the name of JESUS, as a Christian in Christ.

My branch on the tree, which had withered in sins, shall receive power and sap for life in the name of JESUS; in him, as in my trunk—which has become a heart and power in my father Adam—I shall and will grow green with my humanity and bring forth fruits to the praise of God. My will-spirit, which is now in Christ’s humanity and lives in Christ’s spirit, shall give sap to the dry tree in Christ’s power, so that on the Last Day, at the sound of the trumpets of the Divine resonance in Christ’s voice—which is also my voice in his resonance—it may rise again and grow green in the tree of Christ, as in Paradise. Paradise will be within me; everything that God the Father has and is shall appear in me as a form or image of the Divine essences. All the colors, power, and virtues of his eternal Wisdom shall be manifest in and upon me as his image. I shall be the revelation of the spiritual Divine world and an instrument of the Spirit of God, wherein he plays with himself, with this resonance—which I myself am—as with his <term>signature<note>Original: 'Signatur'. Böhme's concept that the inner essence of a thing is revealed through its outer form or "sign."</note>. I shall be his instrument and the **string-music** of his spoken Word and resonance; and not only I, but all my fellow members in the gloriously prepared instrument of GOD. We are all strings in his play of joy; it is the Spirit of his mouth that strikes our strings to his voice. And therefore is GOD-
