# On the Threefold Mediatorial Office of JESUS Christ.

...became man, so that he might restore his glorious <term>instrument<note>Jacob Böhme frequently uses the metaphor of a musical instrument (like a lute or harp) to describe the human soul, which must be "tuned" by God to sound the right notes of love.</note>, which he made for his praise and which had been ruined—refusing to sound according to his desire for joy and love—and so that he might reintroduce the true sound of love into the strings. Yes, that sound which rings before him, he has reintroduced into us as his instrument. He became what I am, and has made me what he is. Thus I may say: in my <term>yieldedness<note>Original: 'Gelassenheit'. A central term in German mysticism referring to a state of complete surrender, letting go of the self-will to let God act through the person.</note> in him, I am his trumpet and the voice of his instrument and Divine sound. In this I now rejoice in all my fellow-strings and voices which, alongside me, are directed toward the praise of GOD as an eternal work.

So know this now, my dear fellow-voices in the praise of GOD: upon and within your sound, I ring out with my string, struck in the Spirit, and so I echo in you. For everything that JESUS has done through the Christ—as through his and my humanity—he still does today in me and in all my fellow-members. He died to his "I-ness" in his death, and I also die to my <term>selfhood<note>Original: 'Ichheit'. The ego-driven nature that seeks its own power rather than God's will.</note> in his death. He gave himself up to his yieldedness in GOD his Father, and GOD his Father awakened him in himself with the breath of his mouth, and presented him as the Royal Image according to the Holy Trinity, through and with which GOD will judge all things in the <term>sphere<note>Original: 'Loco' (Latin). Referring to the place or dimension of this material world.</note> of this world. Thus also has GOD awakened my spirit and soul through his Spirit in the great name of JESUS, in the Christ, within him. Therefore, in my yieldedness in him, I do not need to die, for he has died to me and for me; his death, in which he is risen from death, has become my eternal life. So I live now in his death as one who is dying, yet there is no more death in him; rather, I die to my selfhood and sins in him. Since my desire and will penetrate from my selfhood into him, I die 

<column-break/>

daily to my selfhood, until I shall one day reach the goal of my selfhood and my selfhood—along with the earthly will and desire of the "I"—completely dies away. Then shall my selfhood, and everything in me that seeks and loves itself, fall into the death of Christ as into the <term>first mother<note>The original divine source or "ground" from which humanity was first created before the fall.</note> from which GOD created me. My selfhood shall become a Nothing; then my selfhood lies in Christ's death in yieldedness as a <term>tool<note>Original: 'Werck-Zeug'. Literally "work-thing," meaning an instrument or implement used by God.</note> of GOD, who may then make an instrument out of it as he wills.

But because my soul and spirit now live in his resurrection, and his sound is in me according to my yieldedness in him—as St. Paul says: **Our citizenship is in heaven, from whence we look for the Savior JESUS Christ;**—so also shall his sound, which is in me (since I am no longer myself according to my selfhood, but he alone), also awaken my dead body, which I leave in him, and place it into its first image for which he created it. Thus I live now in God, and my selfhood does not know it; for it lives not in GOD, but in itself. GOD is indeed in it, but it does not grasp him, and it covers the <term>pearl<note>The 'Perlein' (Little Pearl) is Böhme's famous symbol for the spark of divine light or Christ-nature hidden within the soul.</note> that I am in Christ: not I, but he in his humanity, in my creaturely self within him. And thus I speak and write of the great <term>mystery<note>Original: 'Mysterio' (Latin). The hidden spiritual reality underlying all of existence.</note> of all beings—not that I have grasped it in my selfhood, but he strikes my <term>signature<note>Original: 'Signatur'. The inner essence or "spiritual blueprint" of a person that God plays upon like a musician.</note> in my desire, which penetrates into him as he wills. I am known to myself, but not in my selfhood; rather, in his mirror, which he places in me out of grace, thereby to lure my selfhood into him as into yieldedness. And so it is presented to you again, dear brothers, from his mirror, which he has presented to you through my understanding in him as his instrument.

# 1223 Fourth Part / Chapter 3. 1224

### 21. Question: How then did Christ live here on Earth immediately after his Resurrection?

Answer: As we speak of Christ’s true Resurrection, we also point you toward his conduct during the forty days after his Resurrection and before his Ascension. Since we know that he has become a true **LORD** over Heaven, Hell, and Earth, we show you this: that the kingdom of this world, with all its <term>essences<note>Original: 'Essentien'. In Böhme's thought, these are the fundamental spiritual forces or "being-ness" underlying physical matter.</note> and qualities, had to be subject to him. And although he did not always walk visibly among his disciples, he nevertheless showed himself to them many times in a visible, tangible, and persistent way. This was according to the kingdom of this world and according to the body he had here, which the New Man had swallowed up; he had to present that body once again. For **GOD** is **LORD** of all beings, and everything must transform as He wills, so that He could show his disciples his true body with his nail-marks. These marks remain in the holy Christ, in his Holy Body for eternity, as a sign of victory, and they are more beautiful than the morning stars. He strengthened his weak-believing disciples with this, and thereby indicated that he is also a **LORD** over the outward kingdom of this world. Everything that we sow, build, plant, eat, and drink, he holds in full omnipotence; he can bless and multiply everything, and is not separated from us in that way. Instead, just as a flower grows green out of the earth, so too does his Word, Spirit, and Power green within all things. And if our mind is inclined toward him, then we are blessed in body and soul by him; but where it is not, there is the curse and **GOD’S** wrath in all things, and we eat of death in every fruit. Therefore we pray—and it is right to do so—that **GOD** will bless our food and drink, as well as our body and soul, in Christ.

Secondly, we point out to you that Christ walked upon the Earth for forty days after his Resurrection—understand this as being in the kingdom

<column-break/>

of this world, even though he was simultaneously in Heaven. However, he bore the image without external radiance before the eyes of men, and he possessed entirely the body—with all its being—that hung on the Cross, except that he did not have the <term>torment of the Principle<note>Original: 'Quaal des Principii'. Böhme uses 'Qual' (torment/source) to describe the driving, often painful, forces of nature and the dark fire-world. Here, it means Christ was free from the fallen, suffering state of material existence.</note>. Otherwise, he had all the characteristics of flesh and blood, even though the outward flesh stood under the power of the heavenly. We see this in how he entered to his disciples through locked doors and led his body through wood and stone. Thus you understand that this world is as a nothingness before him, and he is powerful over everything. And then we add for you that these forty days are the days of Adam in Paradise before his sleep, before the woman was made from him, when he stood in the Paradisiacal trial and was still pure and heavenly. Thus, this Christ also had to stand for forty days in Paradisiacal <term>trial<note>Original: 'Quaal'. In this context, Böhme uses the word to mean both a state of tension/testing and the fundamental source of life.</note> and temptation, to see if the body would remain Paradisiacal before it was glorified. Therefore, he ate and drank before his disciples and with them in a Paradisiacal manner—just as Adam was also supposed to do: in the mouth and not in the body, for the consumption consisted in the power. Here it was truly tested whether the body would live in Divine might and power, just as Adam was supposed to do when he was in this world in Paradise. Adam was indeed meant to be in this world, but not to live in the "torment" of this world; rather, he was to live in a Paradisiacal way over this world, and also over the fierce wrath of Hell. He was meant to live within that trial in love, humility, gentleness, and mercy, in the friendly will of **GOD**. Thus he would have ruled over the stars and elements, and there would have been no death or decay within him.

Therefore, you Turks and other unbelieving peoples should take note and rightly understand why Christ gave us such laws, such as that we should not be vengeful. If someone strikes us on one cheek, we should offer him the other, and so forth: we should bless those who curse us.

Böhme argues that Christ's resurrected body was physical yet transcendent, proving his mastery over material nature and the "wrath" of the world.</summary>

<header>Of the Triple Mediatorial Office of JESUS Christ.</header>

...and do good to those who hate and offend us: do you understand this? Look, a true Christian, who lives in the Spirit of Christ, should also walk in Christ’s path; he should not go about in the fierce, vengeful spirit of this world. Just as Christ lived and walked in this world after his Resurrection, and yet did not live and walk in this world’s torment <note>Original: 'Quaal'. Böhme uses this term to describe the painful, agitated state of nature or the soul when it is separated from God’s light.</note>; and although it is not fully possible for us, because we live in this world's torment, it is nonetheless possible in the "New Man" in Christ, whom the devil covers. If we live in gentleness, we overcome the world in Christ: if we do good for evil, we testify that Christ’s Spirit is in us. Thus, we are dead to the spirit of this world for the sake of Christ’s Spirit, which is in us; and even though we are in this world, this world only clings to us as it clung to Christ after his Resurrection, while he yet lived in the Father in Heaven; so it is with us also, if we are born in Christ.

Therefore let it be told to you, you **Jews, Turks <note>In the 17th century, "Turks" was a common collective term for the Islamic world.</note>, and Peoples**, you need wait for no other; no other time is at hand but the time of the **Lilies** <note>The "Time of the Lilies" is Böhme's prophetic term for a coming age of peace and spiritual purity on earth.</note>, and his sign is the sign of **Elijah**; therefore see to it in what spirit you live, so that the **fire of wrath** does not swallow and consume you. It is now time that **Jezebel** with her harlotry be hunted out of the house, so that you do not receive the harlot's reward, and as you flay one another, so also devour one another. Truly, if it is not soon resisted, the fire will burn out over **Babel** <note>Babel (Babylon) represents the fragmented, warring, and worldly institutional churches that Böhme criticized.</note>, and then there is no counsel until the wrath devours everything that has grown within it.

Therefore let each man go into himself and not speak of others and hold them to be false, but rather let him convert himself, and see that he is not found in the wrath of the devourer; otherwise, if he cries out: "Aha! **Babel** is burning!" he must also burn, for he is capable of that same fire. If you feel a

<column-break/>

thought within you that desires after wrath, then it is from **Babel**.

Therefore it is difficult to recognize **Babel**; everyone thinks he does not stand within it, and yet the Spirit shows me that **Babel** encompasses the whole **circle of the earth**. Therefore let everyone take heed of his own affairs for himself, and do not hunt after the [worldly] spirit, for the driver breaks it, and the stormer devours it. No man's wise counsel helps anymore. All the wisdom of this world stands in folly, for the fire is from **GOD’S** wrath; your cleverness will turn to your own harm and mockery.

->Principles 25. 97========106.<- <note>This is a reference to Böhme's earlier work, "The Three Principles of the Divine Essence," Chapter 25, paragraphs 97–106.</note>

22. **Question:** Why did Christ not ascend to Heaven sooner than forty days after his Resurrection?

**Answer:** We know that Adam lived forty days in Paradise; then he entered into the spirit of this world when he should have entered into the Holy Trinity; for he stood in the time of temptation, and if he had withstood these forty days, he would have stood completely with his soul in the Light of **GOD**, and his body in the **Holy Ternary** <note>Original: 'Ternario Sancto'. This refers to the divine substantiality or "heavenly materiality" that Böhme believed was the original state of the human body.</note>, like this Christ. Then, after Christ had walked forty days in this world in the **trial** <note>Original: 'Proba'. A period of testing or verification to prove the restoration of the human state.</note> after his Resurrection, he went up a mountain, where he appointed his disciples, and visibly ascended into the heights with his own body, which he had sacrificed on the Cross, until a cloud came and hid him; as a certain sign that he was their brother and that he would not leave them in this earthly form; just as he then said to them: "Lo, I am with you always, even unto the end of the world."

Now Reason speaks: Where has Christ gone? Has he traveled out of this world high above the stars into another heaven? Listen, my dear Reason, incline your mind into Christ, and see, I will tell you; for we see and know it—not I. For when I say "We,"

1227 4. Part / Chap. 3. 1228

...you must not understand my earthly person alone, for the Spirit that drives this pen is named along with it: therefore I write and say, when I wish to speak of myself as the author, **"We."** For I would know nothing if the Spirit did not breathe the science <note>In Böhme’s time, "science" or *Wissenschaft* referred to deep, divinely-inspired knowledge or "knowing-ness" rather than just modern empirical study.</note> into me; and nothing could have been found except in such a manner. The Spirit would not have it otherwise, but hid itself, while my soul showed itself within me as completely restless, with a great longing for the Spirit, until I learned how it was.

See, this is not the foundation that the ancients have imagined and measured—calculating how many hundred thousand miles it might be to the Heaven where Christ has ascended. They did this to the end that they wanted to be God on Earth, as their imaginary kingdom shows, which stands more in **Babel** <note>Böhme uses "Babel" to describe the confusion and pride of organized worldly religions and academic systems that lack true spiritual insight.</note>. When we speak of the **Thrones**, it is much different, and one finds only their blindness and ignorance. Although there is also a spirit in their knowledge which one should not simply cast aside, it is not from the *Ternario Sancto* <note>Original Latin: *Ternario Sancto*. This refers to the "Holy Ternary," the divine, spiritual substance or "heavenly body" of God’s kingdom.</note>, out of the Body of **Jesus Christ**; rather, it is from the high eternity that passes over the Thrones, of which mention may be made in another place.

We must remain in the Throne; what do the other Thrones concern me, which belong to the Angelic Princes? Yet they are, for all that, our friends and dear faithful ones in the service of **God**, (Hebrews 1:14). We must look upon *our* Throne, in which we were created as creatures, and upon our Throne-Prince in **God**. The first Prince of **God**, as He created us and beheld us in the eternal bond, must remain. This Throne belonged to **Lucifer** with his legions; but when he fell, he was cast out into the **first Principle** <note>Böhme’s "First Principle" is the dark, fiery source of nature—God’s "wrath" or potential energy without the "light" of his love.</note>. Thus the Throne stood empty in the **second Principle** <note>The "Second Principle" is the world of light, love, and the "Holy Ternary."</note>, in which **God** created man; he was meant to remain therein and was tested to see if it were possible. Therefore **God** created the **third Principle** in the *Loco* <note>Original Latin: *Loco*, meaning "place" or "location."</note> of this world, so that

<column-break/>

man, in the event of a fall, would not also become a devil, but might still be helped. Therefore, the enmity of the devil is against **Christ**, because Christ sits upon his [the devil's] royal chair and still holds him captive with His Principle. Thus, the "place" of this world, according to the heavenly Principle, is our **Christ's** Throne and His own Body; and everything that is in this world in the third Principle is His own. And the devil, who dwells in this place in the first Principle, is our **Christ's** prisoner. For all Thrones are in **God the Father**, and outside of Him is nothing; He is the Bond of Eternity. But His love in the Body of Christ, as in His Throne, holds the wrath in the Bond of Eternity—along with the devils—captive.

And you understand how everything is thus "creaturely" <note>By "creaturely," Böhme means that even spiritual realities have a form or "body" appropriate to their nature.</note>—His love and also His wrath—and is only one birth (as mentioned before). The difference is such that one cannot say the devils dwell far from Christ. No, they are near, but in all eternity they cannot reach Him. For they cannot see the clear **Godhead** in the Light, but are blinded by it. And we also shall not see or feel them in eternity, just as we do not see them now because they are in a different Principle; so that same Principle remains.

Therefore, my dear mind <note>The "mind" or *Gemüthe* refers to the inner seat of the soul's desires and thoughts.</note>, know that the creature of Christ is the center of this Throne, from which all life (understand that which is heavenly) goes forth. For in that center is the **Holy Trinity**; and not only in this center, but in all Angelic Thrones, and also in the holy souls of men. However, we must speak in this way to make you understand. So the Body—understand the creature, the Man Christ—is seated in the midst of this Throne, and thus stands in Heaven (understand in His Principle), sitting with His Throne at the **Right Hand of God the Father**. The Right Hand of **God** is where love extinguishes wrath and brings forth Paradise; that is rightly called the "Right Hand," where the angry Father is called **God** in love.

He identifies the physical world as Christ's rightful throne, where the devil is held prisoner within a different spiritual dimension (the first Principle) despite being locally 'near.'</summary>

**23. Q[uestion]. How is the Body of Christ glorified in Heaven, and what does it possess in such quality and virtue?**

**Answ[er].** Since we wish to speak of Christ’s transfiguration / and of his Body / which he led into the heights visibly / and in the form / as he had walked on Earth / so we must speak of the form / how the Love of the Heart of GOD has reconciled the Wrath of the Father / and holds it as if imprisoned / within itself / so also has the *Ternarius Sanctus* <note>original: "Ternarius Sanctus." <column-break/>

For in his Divine glorified form we could not behold him before our transfiguration / especially the godless. But thus all generations shall see and recognize him / and the unbelievers shall howl and weep over it / that they have thus departed from their flesh and blood into another torment / and whereas they should and could have put on GOD in their own essences / they instead put on the grim kingdom of the Wrath of GOD with the Devil / and let the same into their essences of the soul / and corrupted themselves. Thus we say / that in the soul of Christ in its essences is grasped the clear Deity / as the Light of GOD / which has extinguished the Wrath in the torment of the soul. Thus the Light transfigures the soul / and through the power of the outgoing from the soul the *Tincture* <term>Tincture: in Böhme’s alchemy-influenced theology, this is the spiritual life-force or "inner fire" that transforms and beautifies matter</term> is always born, and the *Fiat* <note>original: "Fiat." Latin for "Let it be," referring to the creative word of God.</note> in the essences makes it tangible and graspable. And that is the *Ternarius Sanctus* / or the Holy Earth / that is / the Holy Flesh. For GOD illuminates All in All in this Body. Thus is his earthly body swallowed up in GOD / although he never had a completely earthly body like us. For he was not of man’s seed: But we speak only of the tangibility and visibility in our eyes / according to which he is our brother. And he will [reveal] himself in our fleshly form in Divine power on the [Last Day]...

### Part 4 / Chapter 3

...present himself again on the Last Day as a **LORD over All**. For all powers are subject to him in heaven and in this world, and he is a Judge over all, a Prince of Life and **LORD of death**. Thus the Kingdom of Heaven of his own body and the entire Princely Throne of his *Principle* <note>original: "Principii"; in the author's mystical system, this refers to one of the three fundamental realms or "births" of existence—the dark fire-world, the light holy-world, or the outer material world.</note> is a Paradise, wherein the gracious fruit rises in the power of **GOD**. For the Holy Spirit is the power of the growth, like the air in this world. Thus the Holy Spirit is the air and spirit of the souls in Christ and all his children, for there is no other air in heaven in the body of Christ, and **GOD** the Father is All in All. Thus we all live and are in Christ, all in the Father, and no soul searches the depths <note>meaning: the soul does not need to anxiously investigate the mysteries of the Godhead because it lives within them</note>, but we all live in simplicity, in great humility and love toward one another, and rejoice like children before their parents; and for this purpose **GOD** has also created us.

Therefore, my dear soul, seek and align yourself in Christ, so you shall receive the Holy Spirit, who will give your soul a new birth, and enlighten, lead, and guide you, and will reveal Christ to you. Just let go of all human trifles and inventions <note>original: "Menschen-Tand und Fündlein"; referring to worldly distractions or man-made religious ceremonies that lack spiritual substance.</note>, for the Kingdom of **God** is near to you (yes, it is within you, as Christ himself says, Luke 17), and only your own unbelief and your evil works—such as greed, pride, envy, wrath, and falsehood—keep you outside of **GOD**. For you put these on, and thus you stand in the Devil's garment outside of **GOD**. But if you lay these aside and enter with your heart's desire into the mercy of Christ, then you enter into heaven, into **GOD** the Father, and walk in the body of Christ in the pure element <note>the "pure element" is a spiritual substance that Böhme describes as the "quiet residence" of God, distinct from the four conflicting elements of the material world.</note>, and the Holy Spirit proceeds from your soul and leads you into all truth; and the old, corrupt man only clings to you. You shall break that old man in death, and with your love in Christ, you shall still the Father's wrath in your soul, and overcome it, and take it captive; and you shall sprout through

<column-break/>

death with your new man, and come forth on the Last Day.

-> *The Threefold Life, Chapter 26, verse 12* <note>original: "Princ. 26. v. 12."; referencing Jacob Böhme's work 'The Threefold Life of Man'.</note> <-

**24. Quest.** How then does Christ rule as a King, sitting at the Right Hand of **GOD**, over all principality, power, might, and everything that may be named?

**Ans.** We have indicated above how the heaven, wherein **GOD** dwells and Christ sits at the Right Hand of **GOD**, is everywhere in this world, like the day is in the night. The inner ground of the world, from which the four elements have sprung, is the heaven and a spiritual world: In that same inner power, Christ, true **GOD** and Man, rules through the outer world. For as Christ says in Matthew 28:18, 20: *All power is given to me in heaven and on earth.* Also: *I am with you always, even unto the end of the world.* Also: *He shall reign over all his enemies, until all his enemies be made his footstool*, 1 Corinthians 15:25, Psalm 110:1. This is to be understood of his inner kingdom, where he rules in the inner power over the outer, earthly, as well as the hellish realm. For the outer world has sprung from the inner, spiritual world, as if from Light and Darkness. This activity <note>original: "Gewürcke"; the dynamic, weaving process of creation.</note>, before Christ's office, stood in the office of the eternal Creator, who in eternity worked Light and Darkness as the spiritual world. That same activity has flowed out and become visible, and was brought by **GOD** into a creaturely state, wherein Light and Darkness, as Good and Evil, rule with and in one another. In the outflow of eternal darkness is hell and pain, and in the outflow of light is the Light of Nature; and in that realm where Evil and Good rule simultaneously, the Kingdom of Nature is understood with heat and cold and all other properties. This mixture **GOD** has given to the office of Christ, so that he, as true **GOD** and Man at once, [rules] over all selfhood and self-will of this kingdom, where Evil and Go...

rules and governs within one another. Just as the sun in the visible world rules over both evil and good, and is present everywhere with its light and power and all that it is—penetrating all beings and yet not tearing itself apart in its reflected form through its outflowing, but rather giving itself entirely into all beings while remaining whole and losing nothing of its essence—so it is also to be understood regarding Christ's Person and Office. He rules visibly in the inner, spiritual world, and invisibly in the outer world, penetrating the soul, spirit, and heart of faithful people. 25. **Q.** Should Christ then, according to his human nature, be able to be present everywhere?

**A.** Listen, dear Reason: when the Word of **GOD** became man in Mary’s womb, was it not also at that time high above the stars? When it was at Nazareth, was it not also at Jerusalem, and everywhere in all thrones? Or do you think that when **GOD** became man, he was so squeezed <note>original: "eingepresset"; suggesting the error of thinking the infinite God could be physically compressed or trapped within a single human body.</note> and stuck into humanity that he was not everywhere else? Do you think the Godhead split itself apart in Christ’s incarnation? Oh no; he never departed from his seat; that cannot be. Now, if he has become man, then his humanity must have been everywhere his Godhead was. For you cannot

<column-break/>

say that there is any place in heaven or in this world where **GOD** is not. Now, where the Father is, there also is his Heart <note>In this mystical tradition, "the Heart" is a frequent title for the Son, representing the center of Divine love and light.</note> within him, and there also is the Holy Spirit within him. Now his Heart has become man and is in the humanity of Christ. If you were to think that Christ’s body is far away in heaven, you would also have to say that the Heart of **GOD** is only in him there. Would you then say, when you say **GOD** the Father is present here, that his Heart is not also present in him here? Or do you want to divide God’s Heart, and have one spark in Christ’s body and the rest entirely everywhere? What are you doing? Stop; I will show you the true ground, truthfully and properly. Behold, **GOD** the Father is everywhere, and his Heart and Light are everywhere in the Father. For from eternity it is always born everywhere in the Father, and its birth has no beginning or end. It is still born today, always from the Father. And even when it was in Mary’s womb, it still stood in the birth of the Father and was always being born of the Father. And the Holy Spirit has from eternity always proceeded from the Father through his Heart; for the entire birth of the Godhead is nothing else and can do nothing else. Now the Father is greater than everything, and his mercy is also greater than everything, and the Son in him is also greater than everything. And the Element stands in his mercy and is as great as **GOD**, except that it is born of **GOD**, and is substantial, and is under **GOD**. And within it is the <term>Holy Ternary</term> <note>original: "Ternarius Sanctus"; a term for the "holy earth" or the heavenly manifestation of the Trinity in a spiritual substance.</note>, with **GOD’s** Wisdom in the wonders; for all wonders are revealed therein. And that is Christ’s heavenly body, with our assumed soul within it, and the entire fullness of the Godhead in the center within it. Thus the soul is surrounded by the Godhead and eats of **GOD**, for it is spirit. Therefore, my dear soul, if you are born again in Christ, you put on the body of Christ from the holy element.

# On the Work of Redemption in General.

Now follows an investigation into how **JESUS** Christ actually applies the dearly won right of human redemption in deed and power, and how He truly redeems us poor humans, imprisoned in sin and death, making us truly whole and blessed. To fundamentally recognize this right, we will investigate: first, who performs the great work of redemption and what right He has to do so. Second, by what means and how He does it. Third, humans and their conditions before they are redeemed. Fourth, the work of redemption itself.

### 1. Question.

->Who is he then, who accomplishes the great work of redemption?<-

->Answer.<-

**JESUS** Christ, the true Son of **GOD**, who, as the great High Priest of the entire human race and of all creatures, overcomes sin, death, devil, and hell through His Spirit and Word. He introduces into humanity all the righteousness that He earned in His own person, so that He also assumes our human nature and introduces His heavenly humanity into us. He crucifies and slays the old man <note>The "old man" refers to the fallen, sinful nature of Adam within every person.</note> along with its lusts and desires, awakens the new man to a new life, and exalts him together with Himself into eternal blessedness, joy, and glory. This new life is the New Testament, which is confirmed through His blood and death, and is now actually carried out and applied through His Holy Spirit and living Word.

### 2. Qu. How then is this work of redemption carried out and actually applied through the Holy Spirit?

**Answer.** As soon as a fire or life is ignited in any being, an air or spirit goes out from such fire or life. There is no herb so small, and no blade of grass so lowly, that it does not expire a spirit which carries within itself all the qualities of the plant, the root, the heart, and the like. Thus, the Spirit rises out of Christ as if from the ignition of the Divine and heavenly life. In this Spirit reside all the powers of the suffering, death, resurrection, and ascension of **JESUS** Christ. This Spirit of **God** in **JESUS** Christ is a Divine <term>magical longing</term> <note>original: "magische Sucht"; Böhme uses "Sucht" or "Sehnsucht" to describe an intense, attractive spiritual hunger or desire that pulls one reality into another.</note>, through which **God** desires humanity; for humanity is **God’s** Paradise, temple, and dwelling-house, His own image in which He wishes to dwell, to see, and to recognize Himself. The outgoing Spirit of **JESUS** Christ is a very sharp and attractive desire toward the entire human race; and wherever it applies itself, it works until it has ignited the life of **JESUS** Christ in a soul. And once it has awakened that same life in the soul, it drives the life of **JESUS** Christ forward from the Incarnation unto the complete crown and to the revelation of

<column-break/>

the perfect glory of **JESUS** Christ. Thus, this Spirit carries out the entire <term>process</term> <note>original: "Proceß"; In theosophical terms, this refers to the lived, sequential journey of Christ's life—from birth to crucifixion to resurrection—replicated within the believer's own soul.</note> of **JESUS** Christ within the human being and makes those people who allow the Spirit to work within them into kings and priests before **GOD**, from having been poor sinners. Thus, the Godhead moves not only in Christ’s person, but through Christ in all those who receive Him with true faith, just as He moved in Christ; for **GOD** is not divisible, but is entirely everywhere. He is the fullness of all things; where He reveals Himself, He reveals Himself entirely. So He is also not measurable; no place is found for Him unless He first makes a place for Himself within a creature; yet He is also for Himself outside of the creature. Such is also the Spirit of Christ. Just as a fire cannot exist without essence and <term>matter</term> <note>original: "Materia"; the physical or spiritual substance that acts as fuel.</note> in which it burns, just as little can He exist and manifest His qualities without and outside of humanity. For as the Word moved toward the opening of life, it opened itself in the Divine Essence as in the water of eternal life. It entered in and became <term>Sulphur</term> <note>original: "Sulphur"; In alchemical theology, Sulfur represents the active, fiery, and constructive principle of substance.</note>, which is flesh and blood; it produced the heavenly <term>Tinctur</term> <note>original: "Tinctur"; The "Tincture" is the spiritualizing power or "essence" that transforms and ennobles base matter into a divine state.</note> which encloses and fills the Godhead, wherein the wisdom of **GOD** stands eternally with the Divine <term>Magia</term> <note>original: "Magia"; Böhme uses this to mean the creative will or the "magic" of God's power to manifest thought into being.</note>. In this <term>Magia</term>, the Spirit of **GOD** always longs to become flesh and blood even more, and to ignite the Divine life in humanity. Through this ignition of life, sin in the flesh is condemned, and the flesh is purified from the poisonous, coarse <term>Sulphur</term>, so that **God**, as the highest good, light, and love, becomes active and burning within it.

> This is what **Christ** says: I have
> come to ignite a fire, and
> would to **GOD** it were already burning. Also:
> It is good for you that I go away, for
> if I did not go, the Com-
> forter, the Holy Spirit, would not come
> to you.

For before Christ led our humanity into death and died on the stem of the Cross...

there were still the harsh elements in his outer humanity, and the Holy Spirit went forth with greater sharpness and severity because he still stood under the Law, and the properties of the Father were active in his outer humanity. However, after he had perfectly reconciled the wrath of **GOD**, perfectly satisfied His justice, and fully unlocked the center of **GOD'S** love, then the Spirit of **GOD** went forth according to the property of love, in a friendly, joyful, gentle, and heartfelt desire of love. Every birth or ignition of life is active according to the seven forms of nature. <term>The "seven forms of nature" is a foundational concept in the thought of Jacob Böhme, describing the seven stages through which all life and spirit evolve from darkness into light.</term> Likewise, the Spirit of **JESUS** is active according to the seven forms of the Divine World of Love and Light. Namely: according to the first form, seeking, desiring, attracting, and inclining; according to the second, driving and working toward freedom, in order to make the soul free from all images and bonds; thirdly, he takes hold of the soul and works within it to ignite life—he draws and awakens the fire-desires and inclines them out of the dark fire-life of vanity and wrath, in which they are imprisoned, into the Divine Principle of Love. He pacifies the wrathful power of the fire and opens the little wellspring of the sweet water-source through humble sinking; he leads the light out of the darkness and awakens the love-desire to attract the Holy Element and the pure virginal humanity. Within this, the soul becomes burning, like a fire burning in a precious balsam; he rises from the deep center of the Heart of **GOD** as a virgin and awakens her bridegroom in the fire-soul, in the center of the natural fire-life. There, the two lovers come together again and become one heart and one soul once more. The soul’s grim hunger of fire enters into the Divine food, into the fullness of Him who fills all in all. **JESUS**, who has thirsted for the soul for so long, enters with his love-desire into the opened wellspring of life, and the soul leads its thirst and fire-desire into the Heart of **GOD**. Here there is nothing but a friendly meeting <note>original: "Beneveniren," from the Latin for coming together or welcoming.</note>, a desiring of love, goodwill, each seeking the other, desiring, fulfilling, entering into pleasure, uniting, and eternally enjoying.

### 3. Question. How, then, does the Spirit of **JESUS** Christ enter into humans?

**Answer.** Just as **GOD** is present everywhere, so also is the Spirit of **JESUS** Christ in all places. As the air fills everything, so this Spirit fills everything. As soon as a fire ignites, the heat, the power, the air, and the radiance go forth. Likewise, wherever a soul inclines its desire toward **JESUS**, it takes hold of the Spirit of **JESUS**,

<column-break/>

and the Spirit joins itself to the soul, fans the fire, and becomes active in igniting the new life.

However, when we speak of the Temple of Christ and of the river from Zion, we do not mean a single place in one land alone, for the Temple of Christ is everywhere. We understand it to be among all tongues and languages, even though the tongues may be raised higher in one place than another, according to the character of the people and according to how the Spirit is within the person. For the Temple of Christ is within us; we must teach ourselves to hear Christ within us. If Christ does not teach within us, then the external clamor of the mouth is in vain and spoken into the air. Therefore, let no one think that it will happen such that people will come who will teach or force the Holy Spirit into humans by violence. No, it is said:
> Today, if you hear the **LORD'S** voice, do not harden your ears and hearts.
Do not wait for another time, for this is the time of your visitation. Devote your ears and hearts to the Temple of Christ within you; cast away your abomination and false will, and lead your will earnestly through Christ into the Father. Resolve to no longer enter into malice, such as pride, greed, envy, anger, and falsehood. Leave behind the high things of this world and humble yourselves into the hand of the **LORD** and into love toward the needy.

Regard yourselves as the foolish simplicity in Christ; count your art <note>In this context, "art" refers to human cleverness, intellectual vanity, or worldly academic learning.</note> as nothing, for it only leads away from Christ. Desire to know nothing more than what the Holy Spirit in Christ wants to know in you, so that He alone may be your knowledge and will. For through no searching of reason will the source in Zion be found; Zion is not first born from the outside, but from within. We must seek and find ourselves within ourselves. No one needs to run after another place.

### Of the Work of Redemption in General.

He must only enter into himself, and seek and call upon the Holy Spirit within him, for within himself is the place where **GOD** dwells in His Heaven and takes possession of the soul’s will with its desire. Where would the soul soar off to for so long, when it is itself the source of eternity? Within it stands the Principle of the world of light and the world of darkness: it is all three worlds. It is only a matter of this: that just as the soul—through the **Imagination** <note>In this context, "Imagination" refers to the soul's power to focus its desire and "form" its internal reality, not merely "make-believe."</note> in Adam—led itself into the earthly world (which essentially stands within the dark world), whereby its omnipotence and capability were broken and locked in death; so now, in the Spirit of Christ, who shattered that same death, it must wind itself back into the light and into omnipotence. <meta>This page continues the exploration of how the Holy Spirit operates within the human soul. # 4. Part / Chapter 4.

...rather, he awakens: This Divine Mercury <note>original: "Göttlicher Mercurius." In this mystical context, Mercury refers to the active, animating power of the spirit that stirs all other qualities into motion.</note> worked before Christ’s suffering and death according to the justice of **GOD** and the properties of fire—harsh, severe, and sharp. It affected the soul through fear, anxiety, darkness, and the accusations of the conscience. However, after the wrath of **GOD** was reconciled through Christ’s death, and the power of the fire was soothed by his blood, and the requirements of the law were fulfilled, the Holy Spirit then went forth through Christ’s wounds, blood, and death in the highest mercy. Now, it affects mankind with the greatest gentleness, friendliness, humility, and love.

<margin>Grace 12. 20.</margin>
Whoever is now born from Christ, and lives and walks in him, and takes him up in his suffering, death, and resurrection according to his inner man, that person is a member of his body. From him alone flow streams of living water through the powerful Word of **JESUS Christ**. This Word becomes human within him in the inner ground of his being, and expresses itself through him by means of the creature in the *Spirit of the World* <note>original: "Spiritu Mundi." The breath or spirit that governs the physical, external world.</note> of the outer man. For within the human being lies the essential Word of the power of **GOD**, spanning both time and eternity. If he is then **GOD’S** image and the Divine Life is kindled within him, then the living Word expresses itself through him. But where there is a false image and a false ground for speaking—where the hellish or animalistic life dominates—there can be no good willing or expression. For the kind of word that expresses itself from a person’s powers depends entirely on the quality of the *Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterium." The hidden, internal potential or spiritual source within a person.</note> that is awakened within them. Therefore, those who are true teachers are the ones whose internal Mystery is opened by **GOD**, and in whom the ground of Divine Life is kindled. From this ground follows a good willing, desiring, driving, life, light, love, and word, of which more will be said below.

### 5. Question: What then is the difference between the Spirit and the Word of JESUS Christ?

**Answer:** The Spirit kindles the life of **JESUS Christ** internally within the soul; the Word, however, reveals that kindling of life and provides a profound understanding of what the Spirit is working internally.

<column-break/>

<page-num>1246</page-num>

We have now revealed how and by what means **JESUS** Christ works internally and kindles the Divine Life; now it follows to investigate who those are whom the Spirit of **JESUS Christ** awakens and kindles to a new life.

### 6. Question: Which ones are they?

**Answer:** They are all human beings together—all peoples, nations, and tongues, Jews and Gentiles—who were all estranged in and with Adam from the true life that is from **GOD**, and who lie captive in sin and in the death of sins. Even while they still lay in Eve in the *Mystery* <note>The author suggests that the potential for redemption was placed in humanity at the very beginning, even before individuals were born.</note>, **God’s** mercy spoke the word of promise into them. The Spirit of **JESUS Christ** desires all of these, in order to awaken the life of **JESUS Christ** within them. For if the Spirit of **JESUS Christ** does not penetrate the soul and blow upon the Divine Life to fan it into flame, the soul-fire cannot reach the life of **GOD**. And if the soul did not already have the "spoken-in" work of grace within itself, the Spirit of **JESUS Christ** would not be able to awaken that life.

### 7. Question: Can all people then attain the life of JESUS Christ?

**Answer:** The possibility lies in all people, but the awakening to life and the making of a child of **GOD** now belongs to the Holy *Fiat* <note>The divine "Let it be." The creative command of God’s desire that brings new life into being.</note> as the working desire of the newly-introduced Word. For it does not depend on anyone’s own willing, running, or striving, but on **God’s** mercy. Every person has Christ, the new Creator, within himself; but his own will does not take hold of him, for he does not want to die to his *Selfhood* <note>original: "Selbstheit." The ego-driven, independent will that separates the individual from God.</note> so that he might enter into Christ’s death. For in the Holy Spirit and the voice of Christ, all poor sinners who turn themselves to **GOD** are born of a new will and life; and in the death of Christ, they die to the self-will of Selfhood through the birth of a child, fading away in the voice of Christ. For Christ died to human Selfhood in the Father’s wrath, and was buried with the will of Selfhood into eternal death, and rose again in his Father’s will...

<sig>Pppp 3</sig>
<meta>catchword: ...again</meta>

# Concerning the Work of Redemption in General.

...to be / for the indwelling Word <note>original: "eingesprochene Wort" — literally the "spoken-into" Word, referring to the divine breath or promise implanted in the soul at creation.</note> lies within him / like gold in lead. Just as gold was once lead <note>This is an alchemical metaphor: lead was often seen as "sick" or "unripe" gold.</note> before Lucifer corrupted the **Salitter** <term>Salitter: A term unique to the mystic Jacob Boehme, referring to the divine "saltpeter" or the essential, crystalline substance of the heavenly world.</term> / so has it retained the possibility of taking on the properties of gold again: In the same way, man was once heavenly / and though he has become earthly and hellish / he has nonetheless retained the possibility of becoming heavenly once more.

### 9. Question: Now follows the work of redemption itself / namely, how **JESUS Christ**, through his Holy Spirit and living Word, brings the possibility of a new life in a natural man <note>into action; that is / awakened to working and driving?</note> <note>original Latin: "ad actum gebracht." This refers to moving from a state of potential (possibility) to actual activity.</note>

**Answer:** Regarding the work of redemption / as the kindling of the new life / we wish to speak / first / in general / and thereafter specifically from one degree of the new birth to another / until the highest perfection. The Word of promise / or the possibility of the new birth / lies there like an unsubstantial faith / which is like a smoldering fire or damp rot in a wetness / that would gladly burn / but has no proper **essence** <term>original: "Ens." A philosophical term for the "being" or "substance" that gives a thing its reality.</term> for it; but when a proper **essence** is given to it / then the tiny spark of fire increases / from which a beautiful light arises / that shines around itself: It then becomes manifest / how such a fire and beautiful light lay hidden within the wood / which was not recognized before. This is also to be understood in a child of **GOD** / because the poor soul is wrapped in the **Fierceness** <note>original: "Grimm" — often translated as "Wrath," referring to the dark, consuming fire of God's justice.</note> of **GOD** / it is like a smoldering little wick / that would gladly burn / but cannot because of the vanity of sins and the wrath of **GOD**: But when the soul / as the tiny spark of Divine fire / receives **Christ’s** Love-**Essence** <term>original: "Ens." Here referring to the spiritual substance of Christ's nature.</term> / as **Christ’s** flesh and blood / then the tiny spark begins to become a great fire and light / which shines and glows around itself with beautiful virtues and good works / and lives in great patience under the vanity of this world / yet grows forth like a beautiful flower out of the wild earth. # Part 4 / Chapter 4.

...the Divine Sun in the Divine Star-system <note>original: "Gestirne" — referring here to the celestial or spiritual influences/constellations of divine power.</note> of the powers of the Word of GOD in the temple of JESUS Christ / so that he is a branch on the vine of Christ / and brings forth good grapes / which the Divine Sun ripens / so that GOD’s children / as his dear fellow-members / may eat / from which they also sprout forth in and with him; which grapes are good teaching / life / and deeds. It helps nothing to tickle / comfort / nor to boast of a faith / unless that faith becomes a God-formed child in essence and will / which bears Divine fruit.

A good tree always bears good fruit / and even if it must suffer / so that the wind often strikes off its branches and fruit / and the sun dries them out / or that / when they have become ripe / the sows eat them / or they are trampled / yet it always works toward other good fruit. Thus also a true Christian can will nothing else in Christ / but what Christ wills in him / even if he must suffer / so that often from his evil flesh and blood / as well as from the devil’s wind / and the world's malice / his good fruits / which sprout and grow from the inner man / are trampled and spoiled / yet the tree of the new growth remains standing in the life of Christ / and sprouts forth through the outer mortal man / without any stopping / just as eternity sprouts through time / and gives life and power to time. And as the day sprouts forth through the night / and transforms the night into day / and yet the night remains within itself / but is not recognized in the day: So also the Divine day sprouts forth through our eternal night within us / and transforms the night—as GOD’S wrath / hell / death / anguish and eternal destruction—into the Divine day of the kingdom of joy / even if

A good tree bears good fruit for everyone; and even though it must suffer, that the wind often strikes off its branches and fruit, and the sun parches them, and also that when they have become ripe, the swine eat them or they are trampled underfoot, it still works constantly toward other good fruit. In the same way, a true Christian in Christ can want nothing other than what Christ wants in him, even though he must suffer that often—by his own evil flesh and blood, as well as by the devil’s wind and the world's malice—his good fruits, which sprout and grow from the inner man, are trampled and spoiled; yet the tree of the new growth remains standing in the life of Christ, and sprouts through the outer mortal man without any stopping, just as eternity sprouts through time, giving life and power to time. Although in this matter it tends to go differently for one person than for another, according to each one’s <term>Complexion<gloss>In the 17th century, "complexion" referred to a person’s temperament or constitutional makeup (the balance of the four humors).</gloss></term> and form, and also according to whether the purpose is earnest or great; for the Spirit of GOD is unbound, and tends to hold many kinds of processes, as He knows each person. 2. **Question.** *Is it necessary for a person, in such a struggle of repentance, to confess all his committed sins, piece by piece, before GOD?*

**Answer.** Where a person is truly earnest, and the fire has properly ignited within, his conscience will present all his sins to him, and the devil himself will make even the smallest faults so large that he will not know where to turn. In such a case, there is nothing better for a person to do than simply not to dispute much with him because of the multitude of his sins, but rather to gather all sins into a single heap—even if there were as many as the sand by the sea—and throw them onto the devil’s own neck, saying in his heart: "Go away, devil, you are the cause of all this evil; I offer the sin to you, but GOD’S mercy and the death of Christ to myself; in these will I wrap myself; if you can, then devour me."

<column-break/>

And only look steadily upon Christ’s promise, and set the storm entirely within Christ’s death and wounds, and suffering, and into His love: do not dispute much further with sin, for the devil only entangles himself in it and stirs up the sin so that you should despair. Try it thus; you will soon see and feel another person, with another mind and will. We speak as we know and have ourselves experienced, and not in imaginings or opinions, or from historical accounts, but from that which we have a grounding in; and a soldier knows what it is like in war; but he who has not experienced it and was not there, he always thinks otherwise. Such things we report for teaching and instruction out of love, as a spirit that speaks of how it happened to him, as an example to others; if someone wishes to follow after us, he will experience whether it be true.

<margin>The Threefold Life, 9, 30, 31.</margin>
3. **Question.** *Is it then enough that a person has such a heartfelt regret and sorrow for his committed sins?*

**Answer.** As soon as a person becomes perceptibly aware of the abomination of his sins, and regrets them with true earnestness and feeling, he will immediately be intent on how he may be rid of the loathsome malice. To him who is now in right earnest, we tell our own process: that as soon as he becomes aware of these <term>beasts<gloss>A metaphor for the sinful, worldly, or "animal" impulses that Böhme believes inhabit the fallen human soul.</gloss></term>, he should in that very hour and minute so take hold of himself in the soul, and enter into a will, that he wishes to go out from the **Animal Will** and turn to GOD through true repentance. And although he is not able nor can do this in his own strength, let him take Christ’s promise into himself, where CHRIST said: *Seek, and you shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.* No son asks the father for bread, who offers him a stone in its place; or for an egg, who offers him a scorpion. If you, who are evil, can give good gifts to your children; how much more will my Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him for it.

Let him <term>form<gloss>In the mysticism of this period, 'forming' or 'imaging' (Einbildung) refers to the internal process of shaping one’s will and spirit toward a specific spiritual reality.</gloss></term> this promise into his heart: For it is the poison and death of the devil, and of all inherited and molded-in beasts. The earthly, natural will certainly desired them, but the soul wished to leave them and desired to die to all temporal pleasure and joy, longing only for her **first fatherland** <note>The soul's original home in the divine light before the fall into material existence.</note> from which she had originally come; but she found herself far from it, in great abandonment and misery, and knew not what she should do. She thought to go into herself and awaken herself even more, and to pray more vehemently,

but the Devil resisted her and held her back, so that she might not enter into greater movement and repentance. Part 4 / Chapter 5.

### 5. Question. Is the work of the new birth then completed through such a process?

**Answer.** With this process, the work of redemption and rebirth is only just truly begun. Just as a seed works to become a child in the mother's womb / and grows amidst many struggles of nature and outward accidents / until the child receives its life in the mother's womb: So it also happens here. The more a person goes out from themselves and away from their "images" <note>original: "Bilder" — refers to the worldly attachments, mental idols, or ego-driven concepts that distract the soul from God.</note>, the more they enter into **GOD**: until at last Christ becomes living in the indwelling grace; this occurs through the great earnestness of one's purpose. Then the marriage with Virgin Sophia <note>Sophia is the personification of Divine Wisdom, often described by Böhme as the soul's celestial bride and the "mirror" of God.</note> begins immediately, where the two lovers receive each other in joy / and with very inward desire penetrate together into the most sweet love of **GOD**: There, in a short time, the Marriage of the Lamb is prepared, where Virgin Sophia (as the worthy humanity of Christ) is wedded to the soul. And what happens there / and what joys are held there / joy over the converted sinner / which occurs in heaven / for this we have neither pen nor words to write or speak / what the sweet grace of **GOD** in Christ’s humanity may be / and what happens to those / who worthily come to the Marriage of the Lamb / which we have experienced ourselves in our own process / and we know / that we have a true foundation for our writing: Which we would most heartily wish to share with our brothers in the love of Christ: If it were possible / that they would believe our faithful, childlike advice / they would experience within themselves / from where this simple hand understands and knows these great mysteries.

->On Repentance §. 16. 17.<- <note>original: "Poenit." — short for De Poenitentia, the Latin title of Böhme's treatise "On True Repentance."</note>

### 6. Question. How then may a person, who is truly earnest in their repentance, arrive at a right, heartfelt, and burning prayer, through which they feel God's grace so powerfully within them, that they may conquer and overcome the devil and sin within themselves?

**Answer.** When a fire ignites, the spirit and the power go out from the fire, acting as a

<column-break/>

longing and hunger for such a substance from which the fire burns: As soon as the Spirit of **JESUS** Christ has ignited the new life in the soul, the spirit goes out from that ignition, as a longing and hunger for the Divine Being; with this, the fire-hunger attaches itself, and finds satisfaction therein. This ascending spirit and hunger we call prayer; the entering, taking, eating, and filling, we call faith.

Thus prayer has two things within it: One is the earnest will / which presses out from the miserable "smoky house" <note>The "smoky house" of the heart is a metaphor for the earthly human condition, filled with the "smoke" of pride, anger, and worldly desires.</note> of the heart out of the soul in great humility / and yields itself into the Heart of **GOD** / who became man / as into the Tree of Life. And then the will eats of the Divine power / that is called faith. For the soul's will grasps and holds it with the "tongue against the teeth" / if you understand this in the Language of Nature <note>The "Language of Nature" (Natursprache) is Böhme's concept that the very sounds and mechanics of speech reveal the hidden spiritual essence of the things being named.</note> / and yet lets the Holy Spirit go out from the power / which the will brings into the soul / out of the power / which the soul has grasped: As it then goes out powerfully from the heart through the grasped power through the teeth: For in **GOD’S** power there is nothing consumable: The more the will grasps and the soul eats / the more power there is / and the more powerful and joyful is **GOD’S** body / that is / Christ’s body: Not that it is one time larger than the other / No / for it is larger than everything; only the power rises up in great wonders of joy from eternity to eternity.

Therefore, understand us most dearly: When we pray / we do not merely speak before **GOD**: Indeed the will bows before **GOD** / but it enters into **GOD** / there it becomes filled with **GOD’S** power / and that it brings to the soul: The soul eats at **GOD’S** table. This is what Christ says: **Man lives by every word of GOD.**

->The Threefold Life 16. 47. 48.<- <note>original: "Dreyfach Leb." — refers to Böhme's work "The Threefold Life of Man."</note>

Thus the actual ground of prayer is nothing other than a strong, persistent fire-desire and hunger of the soul for the Being of **GOD** — and for the spirit-water of the holy, pure Element, wherein the fire-soul reaches the light, the love, and the life of **GOD**.

### Part 4 / Chapter 5.

You go and seek your abominations, and see the Devil’s and the world’s husks <note>original: "Treber" – the spent grain or husks fed to swine, a direct reference to the Parable of the Prodigal Son in Luke 15:16.</note> which you have eaten for a long time; and you remember **GOD** and His mercy. If so, do not return again to the pigsty, and do not say: "I am ashamed before my pious old Father, I dare not look him in the eye because of my great mockery and abomination, for I was a magnificent son and am now a naked pig-herd." Rather, think that your Father is just as concerned for you (as for His lost son) as you are for His favor and love, which you have willfully gambled away. Just grasp a friendly, humble, submissive, and obedient will—and come! Go out from the pigs, leave the husks of the world behind, let the pigs eat them and pasture themselves. Go into yourself and knock on your evil heart; break in through doors and gates, and even if all the pigs and devils howl for their herdsman, come to the Father with such gestures and words that you do not need to adorn <note>The author suggests that sincere, raw prayer is better than rehearsed or "fancy" religious language.</note> to make them as they "should" be. And even if you had no more than the words of the poor tax collector <note>A reference to Luke 18:13: "God, be merciful to me a sinner."</note>, it matters not. Only be earnest and constant without ceasing. And though hell should burst and body and soul pass away, stand still and do not go back out of the Father’s door. As soon as you open the door in your soul and walk out of the filth toward the old Father so that He may recognize you as His son and see that you are turned toward Him, He says: "This is my lost son, for whom my heart has been troubled; I entered into humanity in this world and sought him, and now I have found him." Then He sends the Holy Spirit to meet him, falls lovingly around his neck, and receives him with joy. As a sign of His love, He places the seal and the ring of the Holy Trinity—through the suffering and death of **CHRIST**—onto the hand of the soul. Then He brings the gracious Virgin of His Wisdom, the new angelic garment, which is the 

<column-break/>

flesh of **CHRIST**, and puts it on the soul. Then all the servants of **GOD**, the Holy Angels, must rejoice in the Father’s house and be merry with the lost son. Then the old Father slaughters a good calf and feeds the son at His table of heavenly essence with the power and the flesh of His obedient Son **CHRIST**, and gives him to drink of the water of eternal life in the blood of **CHRIST**, in the first Mother <note>This refers to the original spiritual essence or "divine womb" from which the soul was first created before the fall.</note> from which the soul was created. And there is joy in heaven before ninety-nine angels or holy souls who are with **GOD**, that yet another dear brother has come into their company. And even if one’s own work-holiness <term>Werck-Heiligkeit: the belief that one is made holy through outward religious acts or "good works" rather than inner spiritual rebirth</term>, acting as the elder son who has always walked about in the Anti-Christian house, grumbles and snorts against it, boasting of his obedience and the toil and labor he spent in hypocrisy <term>Gleißnerey: a 17th-century term for religious hypocrisy or "shining" with a false, outward piety</term>—the Father does not ask about that. The new son pleases Him better than the one in the house, for the one in the house is envious and does not want to have heavenly joy with his lost brother. He thinks he alone holds the inheritance, that the Kingdom of Heaven is his, that he has earned it and never left the house, and that the key to the treasure belongs to him while the other is but a pig-herd. This does not disturb the Father; He is merry with His servants, the angels and holy souls, and lets the angry one—who will not share heavenly joy with his brother—go into the wrath-pit of the Devil. He remains merry with His child. But because the hypocrite is angry and despises the Father’s supper <note>original: "Abendmahl" – referring both to the parable’s feast and the Holy Communion.</note>, he also does not enjoy the heavenly joy.

->Threefold Life, ch. 16. 13–16.<-

**Answer:** It is not without reason; this commonly happens to earnest fighters in their first zeal, and is...

# Of the Repentance of Man.

...is permitted by **GOD** <note>original: "zugelaſſen" – Böhme often argues that God allows doubt or "reason" to challenge the believer to strengthen their resolve.</note> to test man, to see if his will is clothed in right earnestness and sincerity. Therefore, if anyone wishes to pray rightly, he must turn his will away from every creature <note>original: "Creatur" – referring to all created, worldly things as opposed to the Creator.</note> and step purely with his mind before **GOD**. There must be such a resolution and earnestness as with the poor tax collector in the temple and the prodigal son <note>References to the parables of humility and return in Luke 18 and Luke 15.</note>, who come to **GOD** in this way. You cannot come before **GOD** with your desire, for you receive no power within yourself?" Do not let any of this lead you astray; the power is in the inner ground, in the desire of the will, and it works with **GOD**. Only stand still and wait for the **LORD**; it will surely break through at last, so that you will feel it in your heart and thank **GOD**.

<margin>Borr. regarding Prayer, §. 19.</margin>

8. **Question:** In what, then, does the answering of prayer actually consist, and how can one be assured of having been heard by **GOD**?

**Answer:** The ears that hear it are neither the senses, thoughts, nor *imagination* <note>original: "Phantaſia"</note>, nor any natural power of the soul; rather, it is the Divine hearing that hears the prayer, not outside, but within the soul—namely, that power of grace which **GOD** spoke back into us in the name of **JESUS** <note>Böhme refers to the "Ingoing" of the Word (the "re-speaking") into the human heart through the incarnation of Christ.</note>, opening a gate for us through which we may hear **GOD** speak, as He speaks His Word in us from the *Principle* <note>original: "Principio" – Böhme's term for the fundamental states of being (light, dark, and the material world).</note> of His love, and through which we assure ourselves that **GOD** also hears us in ourselves when we speak His Word into Him. One should not think as if **GOD** sat in some remote place above the clouds and heard what people down here wished and desired, sharing it with them from above. No! Rather, when we pray to **GOD**, **GOD** hears our soul within ourselves in the *Center* <note>original: "Centro"</note>—that is, the soul penetrates with its

<column-break/>

penitent will out of the *Center* <note>original: "Centro"</note> of anguish, out of the abyss of hell, and out of the spirit of this world, into the other *Principle* <note>original: "Principium"</note> in **GOD**, which is also the soul's own; for all three *Principles* <note>original: "Principia"</note> are in the soul: two eternal ones <note>The "Dark World" of fire/will and the "Light World" of love.</note>, and then the fragile one which causes the death of this world. The Word that created our soul and became man—that has the Holy Spirit within it, and it proceeds from the Father in the Word and meets the calling mind and will, and opens itself from within the soul. For the outer animal body is not worthy of the Holy Spirit to open itself within it, though it happens at times to the saints that it goes out from the soul into the outer *Principle* <note>original: "Principium"</note>, where the body triumphs and knows not what is happening to it for joy. But in the soul's new body in **Christ**, when she receives **Christ's** body, there the Holy Spirit dwells within as in a holy temple, and therein the prayer is performed when the soul leads its <term>fire-desire: Böhme’s term for the soul’s primary, burning hunger for God's light</term> into it; therein also the prayer is heard when the Holy Spirit moves and goes out in the power of the essence and satisfies the fire-desire.

<margin>See *Threefold Life*, Ch. 16, §§. 10, 12.</margin>

9. **Question:** Can a person reach such a high degree of perfection that they no longer need to pray?

**Answer:** Just as little as a fire can be without heat, a light without radiance, or a life without spirit and hunger, so little can a soul be in a state of the ignition of the new life without having a hunger and desire for the origin from which it was ignited, and for the essence in which it became burning. However, a soul may well reach a point where its desire is swallowed up in the essence, its hunger in the fullness, and its fire in the light; then its prayer is changed and made manifest in praise and thanksgiving.

<header>Part 4 / Chapter 6.</header>

# Chapter VI.
## Concerning True Faith.

After we have considered how the kindling of the new life gives rise to the fire-desire <note>original: "Feuer-Begierde" — In Böhme’s mystical philosophy, this refers to the soul’s primal, burning hunger for God's light, which acts as the "fuel" for spiritual transformation.</note>, which is prayer, we must now investigate how the new man satisfies his fire-desire, hunger, and thirst. This is done through true, living faith, which leads the fire-desire into the true food of the soul, eating and embracing it, thereby strengthening and maintaining the new life within.

Therefore, dear brothers, watch yourselves carefully in this world, for you are being led upon hypocritical paths. There is much boasting about faith, yet people are led into a historical faith <note>original: "Hiſtoriſchen Glauben" — A common term in 17th-century mysticism for an intellectual belief in the facts of the Bible that lacks personal, spiritual experience.</note>, which is merely a form of science or scholarly knowledge. You are taught this "science," and whoever does not cling to it is considered a heretic. Oh, how dead is the faith of today! It remains stuck in mere knowledge. People think that if they know how to speak much about **GOD**, and about Christ’s merit, suffering, and death for the human race, and take comfort in that, then that is the way to eternal life. Oh no, it does not help you at all that you simply know it and tickle yourself with the thought of it. Right faith in Christ is quite another thing; it does not lie merely in history and in the letter <note>A reference to 2 Corinthians 3:6: "the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life."</note>. The letter is not the Word; it is only a ladder and an instruction toward the Word. The Word is living and possesses Spirit. True faith is the right will that enters into the living Word. If you comfort yourself for a long time with Christ's suffering, yet your will remains a rogue, then the spirit that comes out of your will is a thief and a murderer. You teach one thing but do another. **GOD** desires no hypocrite, but rather an earnest will that enters into obedience to Him; that is faith in the Holy Spirit. Only there do the Word and the death of Christ become fruitful. Christ says: You must turn back and become as children who know nothing of falsehood, and you must be born in Christ through Christ’s death and out of his flesh and blood, if you wish to see the kingdom of heaven. For whoever does not eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood has no part in him <note>A reference to the Gospel of John 6:53-56.</note>.

Dear brothers, this does not reside solely in the Host <note>original: "Hoſtia" — the bread used in the Eucharist or Holy Communion.</note> that you distribute, nor in that same chalice. No; rather, when the soul turns around, tames the body, and gives itself entirely in obedience to **GOD**, into His will, and desires Christ’s entrance to the Father, then it departs from the life of this world and goes with Christ into the Father. He gives the soul Christ’s flesh and blood, for it eats from the Word of the Lord <note>original: "Verbo Domini"</note> at **GOD’S** table, receiving Christ’s flesh for a body and Christ’s blood for a delight. For the soul dwells in the heart and burns out of the heart’s blood like a kindled light, and it holds its princely governance in the head, in the brain. There it has five open gates <note>The five senses, which Böhme views as the portals through which the soul interacts with both the physical and spiritual worlds.</note> where it governs with its spirit-life. Now, if the <term>tincture</term> <note>original: "Tinctur" — An alchemical term used by Böhme to describe a spiritual essence or transformative power that can change "base" nature into "divine" gold.</note> in the soul has entered into Christ’s will within the heart’s blood, then that same will also governs the spirit of the soul in the head. Although it faces many obstacles from the earthly, bestial spirit—as well as from the Devil, who infects the earthly spirit whenever the soul is merely secure <note>In this context, "secure" implies being spiritually careless or complacent.</note> and leads it into the lusts of the flesh—nonetheless, as long as the soul rejects those earthly, bestial thoughts and influences, it remains in Christ. For it is a hard morsel for the Devil to overcome the body of Christ which the soul wears; but it is a much harder morsel for the soul to turn itself away from the spirit of this world and enter into obedience to **GOD**.

<header>Of True Faith.</header>

Dear brothers, it takes more than a handful of historical faith <note>original: "Historisches Glaubens" — Böhme uses this to describe an intellectual or scholarly belief in biblical history that lacks a personal, transformative experience of God.</note>, where one merely places the merit of Christ <note>The theological idea that Christ’s suffering and death "earned" salvation for humanity.</note> at the forefront. It must be a matter of earnestness; you must enter with earnestness into the merit of Christ, passing through death, the devil, and hell. You must overcome the spirit of this world. Your will, with all its reason and senses, must entwine itself entirely into **GOD’S** will; then you will clearly see what the "history of knowledge" actually accomplishes. If you do not drive the devil out of your heart, he will not let you enter into **God’s** will. If you keep the rogue of falsehood in your heart, and try to fight him only with Christ’s merit, you will surely be overtaken, for the devil sets himself violently against it. He strives with the soul as much as he can; he does not let her go unless she leaves all earthly things upon his neck <note>An idiom meaning to leave the devil behind with all the worldly burdens he claims as his own.</note> and departs from him. When she does this, she leaves his territory, and thus he is overcome. 

But Oh, how he always holds those things before her again! Like a fowler <note>A bird-catcher or hunter.</note>, he is always following after her. If he is able, he pulls the earthly garment back onto her. What a heavy struggle the poor soul must endure with the devil! In such a time, Christ's merit, suffering, and death are good—when the devil has captured the poor soul again and will not let her go, but drives her down into the abyss of despair. There, the soul must seize Christ’s suffering and death, and with the devil, walk through hell into the death of Christ, and from Christ’s death, bloom forth again with Christ in **GOD**. This is a lily that the devil does not like to smell. But that you wish to hang onto history, and thus claim Christ's merit, suffering, and death for yourself while keeping the false devil as a guest in your soul—that is a disgrace to Christ.

-> The Threefold Life, chapter 14, verses 6, 8. <-

### 1. Question.
### What, then, is true faith properly called?
### Answer.

Faith is nothing else than turning one’s will and desire away from all selfhood <note>original: "Selbstheit" — The state of being self-centered or focused on the ego rather than God.</note> and all created things, and leaning into the true, living **God**. It is to take His will, Word, and power into one's own will, and to unite one's will with **GOD**, so that these two wills—**God’s** will and man’s will—become one substance and essence. In this way, **God’s** desiring, attracting will finds its pleasure and fulfillment in the new essence of man, and man’s hunger and desire also attain their perfect fullness in **GOD**.

Thus, faith is not a historical science <note>In the 17th century, "science" referred to any organized body of knowledge or scholarship.</note> where a person creates articles [of dogma] and clings to them alone, forcing his mind into the works of his reason; rather, it is one spirit with **GOD**.

<column-break/>

For the Holy Spirit moves within the spirit of faith. True faith is a power of **GOD**, one spirit with **GOD**. It works in **GOD** and with **GOD**; it is free and bound to no article of belief except to right love. Within that love, it draws the power and strength of its life, and it cares nothing for human opinions. For just as **God** is free from all accountability—doing what He wills and needing to give no account for it—so too is the right, true faith free in the Spirit of **GOD**. It has no inclination other than toward the love and mercy of **GOD**, such that it throws its will into **God’s** will and departs from sidereal and elemental reason <note>original: "siderischen und elementischen Vernunfft" — This refers to the intellect influenced by the stars (astrology) and the physical world (elements), which Böhme considers inferior to spiritual intuition.</note>. It does not seek itself in the reason of the flesh, but in **God’s** love; and when it finds itself there, it finds itself in **GOD**, and works with **GOD**—not according to what the reason wants, but in **GOD**, according to what **God’s** Spirit wants.
