He surrenders himself in humility to the will of **GOD**, and through his reason he sinks into death, but blossoms with **God’s** Spirit in the life of **God**. He is as if he were Nothing, and yet is all in **God**; he is an ornament and crown of the Godhead, a wonder in the Divine Magic <term>Magia / Divine Magic: Böhme uses this term not to mean sorcery, but the spiritual "creative power" by which God brings the hidden internal essence into visible, external form.</term>. It is a companion and friend of the Divine Virgin, the Wisdom of **GOD** <note>original: "Göttlichen Jungfrauen / der Weißheit GOttes" — refers to Sophia, the personification of Divine Wisdom who acts as a mirror to God's glory.</note>; within it stand the great wonders of **GOD**, and yet it is free from everything, just as light is free from fire, even though it is always born from the fire, and the torment of the fire cannot seize or rebuke it.

Likewise, we give you to understand that faith is born from the Spirit of Life, as if from an ever-burning fire, and shines within that same fire; it fills the fire of life and yet is never consumed or seized by it. But if it *is* seized, then it has entered into reason as if into a prison, and is no longer in **God**, in His freedom, but has entered into torment. It plagues itself, even though it could well be free. In reason, it works wonders in the fire of nature; but in freedom, it works the wonders of **God** in love.

->2. Question: How is faith born and what is its origin?<-

**Answer:** Faith does not originate at all from knowledge, or the intellectual part of the soul, but faith takes its origin entirely from the **will**. Just as the will becomes active and driving according to the seven forms of nature <note>Böhme’s complex system of seven "Source-Spirits" or properties that govern all existence, from harsh contraction to the "kingdom of glory."</note>, where in the fourth form the kindling of life is born and the lightning-flash rises to the light: so also the will works toward the kindling of the new life, and from such a kindling of life, the fire-desire goes out as the lightning-flash. Now, no flash is born except out of anguish; so too faith rises in no other way than out of the press of anguish <note>original: "Angst-Presse" — literally "the pressure of anxiety." Böhme sees spiritual labor as a mechanical-like pressure that must reach a breaking point to produce light.</note> in the soul. The greater the anguish, the sharper and more powerful the faith becomes. Thus, faith is indeed no mere science or image of reason, but it is **God’s** image, **God’s** likeness, and in its origin it is purely a **will**. And that same will is a **seed**; the fire-spirit (which is the soul) must sow this seed into the freedom of **GOD**. Then a tree grows from that same seed, from which the soul eats and soothes its fire-life, so that it becomes powerful and gives its strength to the root of the tree. From this, the tree grows in the Spirit of **GOD**, reaching into the wonders of the Majesty of **GOD**, and blossoms in the Paradise of **GOD**. And although it is true that with this description we might seem mute or misunderstood—for reason wants to grasp and see everything with the physical eyes—

First, an animal life, in which **Reason** <term>Vernunfft / Reason: For Böhme, this is the earthly, logical intellect that belongs to the stars and elements, useful for worldly things but blind to divine mysteries.</term>—as a reflection of the stars and elements—ignites itself with all its essences and pulling powers to nourish and increase itself in the external, animal life. Accordingly, there is in man a desire and craving for a higher, better, and eternal life, where no torment <note>original: "Quaal"</note> exists. And though **Reason** neither grasps nor sees such a desire, there is nonetheless a hidden sighing, longing, and yearning for something higher than the kingdom of this world. This **Magical** craving lies in man before the new life, as it were, as a **Mystery** <term>Mysterium / Mystery: The hidden spiritual potential or divine seed within the soul.</term>, which Mystery is hidden in the fire within the anguish-torment, and opens itself through the anguish of the will. There we find how that same Mystery is held captive by the spirit of this world, and how the external life-reason has a power to enter therein and destroy it, so that the Mystery does not come to the light; it covers it so that the mother <note>The "mother" here refers to the soul's creative capacity to give birth to the light.</note> may not give birth, and thus it remains hidden in the Mystery. And so, if the body breaks <note>i.e., at death</note>, the will has no one left to open the Mystery; thus the fire-spirit or soul-spirit remains in darkness, and the Mystery stands eternally hidden within him, just as in another **Principle** <term>Principio / Principle: One of the three fundamental realms of existence in Böhme’s cosmology (Darkness, Light, or the Material World).</term>. Therefore we recognize the Mystery as **God’s** Kingdom, which stands hidden in the soul, and which gives the soul a delight and desire to imagine into that same Mystery; then, in a magical way, she becomes pregnant in that same Mystery, from which the will arises to go out from the fire-life into the Mystery of **GOD**. And when it happens that she raises the will and from herself into the Myste-

->3. Question: How then is faith proven, that<-
->it is of the right kind?<-

**Answer:** If we wish to properly describe the tree of Christian life, we say: its root stands in the **Mystery of Hope**; its growth stands in **Love**; and its body in the **Comprehension of Faith**. That is, when the Image <note>The "Image" refers to the divine likeness or "Sophia" within the soul.</note> with its earnest desire penetrates into God’s Love and grasps God’s Essence as **Christ’s Body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note>. That is now the **Body** in which the tree stands, grows, turns green, and brings forth fruits in patience. These belong to the **Angelic World** <term>Engliſche Welt / Angelic World: Böhme uses "Engliſche" to mean "pertaining to angels" (Engel), referring to the heavenly or divine realm rather than the country of England.</term>, and they are the soul’s food, from which it eats and refreshes its fiery life, so that it is transformed into the light of **Gentleness** <term>Sanfftmuth / Gentleness: In Böhme’s system, this is the "sweet" divine light that quenches the soul's natural fire.</term>. Thus the tree grows in the Paradise of God, which the outer man does not know and no Reason grasps, but which is very well known to the noble Image; this tree then becomes manifest when the outer life breaks apart, and all

his works follow him into the Mystery of Hope into which he has sown.

In contrast, the good tree of Faith arises and greens out of death into Paradise, where it bears much nobler fruits. We must be born of Christ’s flesh if we wish to see the Kingdom of God. It is not such an easy thing to be a true Christian; rather, it is the most difficult thing of all. The Will must become a **Knight** and fight against the corrupted will; it must sink itself out of earthly Reason into the death of Christ, into God’s wrath, and—as a precious knight—break the power of the earthly will, and venture so boldly that it is willing to stake its earthly life upon it, and not give up until it has broken the earthly will. **5. Question:** But if Faith is such a great power of God, how does it happen that believers must endure so much adversity, crosses, and tribulation?

**Answer:** Just as no fire ignites except in **anguish** <note>original: "Angst." In Böhme’s thought, "Angst" refers to the spiritual tension or "contraction" necessary to produce the "flash" of life and light.</note>, and no life is born except from the ignition of fire; so it is impossible for the **Tree of Faith** to grow except in storms, temptation, crosses, and adversity. It takes its life from dying and turns green out of death. The more powerful the anguish-torment, the more powerful the ignition of fire and life becomes, and the stronger the fire-flash. It is as impossible to have true faith in good days, wealth, honor, lust of the flesh, health, and the like, as it is for earthly fire to burn in earthly water.

Therefore, dear soul, if you wish to become God’s child, prepare yourself for temptation and tribulation. It is not easy or gentle to enter into the **Child-life** <note>The state of being a child of God.</note>, especially since **Reason** lies captive in the earthly kingdom. Reason must be broken, and the Will must go out from Reason; it must sow itself into God’s Kingdom in humble obedience, just as a grain is sown into the field. It must make itself as if dead within Reason and surrender to God; thus the new fruit grows in God...

### Of the True Faith.

...God's Kingdom. Therefore, man stands in a threefold life, and everything belongs to GOD. The internal fiery **essences** <term>essences / Essentien: The fundamental spiritual properties or "substances" that make up a being’s nature.</term> of the first **Principle** <note>original: "Principii"</note> <term>Principle / Principium: A foundational source or realm of reality; here referring to the spiritual foundation of fire and energy.</term> are incorporated with the new body in Christ, so that they well up in Christ’s flesh and blood out of GOD’S will. Their fire is GOD’S fire, from which love, gentleness, and humility burn, as the Holy Spirit goes forth and helps them to withstand the struggle against earthly **Reason** <term>Reason / Vernunfft: The worldly, analytical mind that lacks spiritual insight and often opposes divine truth.</term>, as well as against the will of the corrupted flesh and the Devil. His yoke of the earthly will becomes lighter for him, but he must remain in the struggle in this world. For nourishment belongs to the earthly life; man must seek it, and yet he must not set his will and heart therein or hang upon it. He must trust GOD. His earthly reason always enters into doubt that he will lack what he needs; it always wants to behold GOD and yet cannot, for GOD does not dwell in the earthly kingdom, but in Himself.

Thus, because **Reason** cannot behold GOD, it must be constrained into hope. There, doubt runs against faith and seeks to destroy hope. Then the earnest will, with the right **image** <term>image / Bildnis: The true spiritual form or "new man" restored in the believer through Christ.</term>, must struggle against earthly reason. This causes pain and often proceeds sadly, especially when reason beholds the course of this world and recognizes its own "will-spirit" as being, as it were, foolish compared to the course of this world. Then it is said: *Be sober, watch, fast, and pray* <note>A reference to 1 Peter 5:8 and Matthew 26:41.</note>, so that you may deaden the earthly reason and make it as if dead, so that GOD’S Spirit may find a place in you. When that Spirit appears, He soon overcomes the earthly reason and gazes upon the will in its anxiety with His love and sweetness. Then, every time, a beautiful little branch is born from the **Tree of Faith**, and all tribulation and temptation serve the children of GOD for the very best. For as often as GOD ordains that His children

<column-break/>

are led into anxiety and tribulation, they always stand in the birth of a new little branch from the **Tree of Faith**. When the Spirit of GOD appears again, He always brings forth a new growth, in which the noble **image** rejoices greatly. It is only a matter of the first storm, where the earthly tree must be overcome and the noble grain sown in GOD’S field, so that man may learn to recognize the earthly man. For when the will receives GOD’S light, the mirror sees itself; one **essence** in the light sees the other. Thus the whole man finds himself within himself and recognizes what he is, which he cannot recognize in earthly reason.

Therefore, no one should think that the tree of the Christian faith is seen or recognized in the kingdom of this world; external reason does not know it. And even if the beautiful tree already stands in the inner man, earthly reason still doubts, for the Spirit of GOD is like foolishness to it; reason cannot grasp it. Although it may happen that the Holy Spirit opens Himself in the external mirror, so that the external life rejoices greatly therein and becomes trembling with great joy, thinking: "Now I have attained the worthy Guest, now I will believe it," there is still no perfect stability in it. For the Spirit of GOD does not remain forever in the earthly **torment** <note>original: "Quaal"</note>; He desires a pure vessel. And when He withdraws into His **Principle** <note>original: "Principium"</note>, into the right **image**, then the external life becomes faint-hearted and timid. Therefore, the noble **image** must always be in struggle against the external life of reason; and the more it struggles, the larger the beautiful tree grows, for it works with God. For just as an earthly tree grows in wind, rain, cold, and heat, so also does the tree of GOD’S **image** grow under the cross and tribulation, in anxiety and torment, in mockery and contempt; it greens forth in GOD’S Kingdom and brings forth fruit in patience.

### Part 4 / Chapter 6.

**Patience.** Since we know this, we should work toward it and allow no fear or terror to stop us; for we shall enjoy its benefits eternally and reap what we have sown here in anxiety and toil, which will comfort us forever.

6. **Question:** What is the actual difference between **Faith** and **Yieldedness** <term>Yieldedness / Gelassenheit: A central concept in German mysticism referring to the state of letting go of one’s own will to become a vessel for God. Often translated as "resignation" or "equanimity."</term>?

**Answer:** **Faith** is an active, effective power of GOD, but **Yieldedness** is a passive, suffering <note>In the sense of "submitting" or "undergoing" rather than just feeling pain.</note> power of GOD. Just as Faith rises out of the ignition of the fire in a lightning-flash and drives toward freedom, so **Yieldedness** descends and sinks into the power of its own fire in humility. Faith is the life-source of the **New Man**, and **Yieldedness** is the dying and fading away of the **Old Man**.

All sins arise from **Selfhood** <term>Selfhood / Selbstheit: The ego-driven state of being focused on one's own desires and separation from God.</term>; for **Selfhood** swings itself with its desire into its own, turning into greed and envy. It draws foreign essences into its self-desire and makes the owners of those foreign essences into enemies against itself; thus, sin is worked with sin, and loathing with loathing, and everything runs into and under one another as a vain abomination of the **Eternal Mother** <note>In Böhme’s thought, the "Eternal Mother" refers to the spiritual nature or the "Womb" of reality from which all things are birthed.</note>. We must think similarly of the **reborn will**, which enters back into **Yieldedness** out of its "I-hood" or **Selfhood**; it also becomes an enemy and a loathing to **Selfhood**. Just as sickness is an enemy to health, and health in turn is an enemy to sickness, so the **yielded will** and the **own-will** <note>The "own-will" is the stubborn, selfish will of the individual.</note> are in constant enmity, an everlasting war and struggle. The own-will seeks only what serves its **Selfhood**, but the yielded will cares for nothing, but leads its desire solely and alone into its Eternal Mother,

<column-break/>

that it may be one with her; it wishes to be nothing, so that the Mother may be everything in it alone. The **own-will** says to the **yielded will**: "You are foolish to give yourself up to death, when you could live magnificently in me." But the **yielded will** speaks: "You are my loathing, my pain, and my opposition; you lead me out of eternity into time, into nothing but sorrow and misery. You afflict me for a time, then you give my body to the earth and my soul to hell."

Right and true **Yieldedness** is the dying of the loathing against God. Whoever entirely leaves their **Selfhood** and gives themselves over with mind and desire, senses and will, into God's mercy—into the death of JESUS Christ—is dead to the earthly world in their will. Such a person is a **twofold man**, where the loathing within works only toward death, but the **yielded will** lives in Christ’s death and stands up forever in Christ’s resurrection in GOD. And though the **own-desire** sins—which indeed cannot do otherwise than sin—the **yielded will** does not live in sin; for it has died to the desire for sin and lives through Christ in God, in the Land of the Living. But **Selfhood** lives in the Land of Death, in a state of "ever-dying" and "ever-enmity" against GOD.

<margin>The Signature of All Things [Signatura Rerum], Chapter 15, Paragraphs 12–15.</margin>
Thus, **Faith** and **Yieldedness** are always together; the former is the working of the new life, the latter is the fainting of the old life. The former is the heavenly, paradisiacal greening—an impulse of the **Divine Tincture** <term>Tincture / Tinctur: An alchemical term used here to mean a spiritual essence or "dye" that transforms and perfects the soul.</term> in the spirit of JESUS Christ—but the latter is a withering and weakening, a drying up of the earthly **tincture** in the flesh.

Of the Forgiveness of Sins.

# Chapter VII.
## On the Forgiveness of Sins and the Righteousness Imputed to Us in Christ Through Faith.

**1. Question.**
**What then does faith in JESUS Christ effect?**

->Answer<-

When the repentant soul puts on JESUS Christ and His precious merit through true faith, the life of JESUS Christ immediately becomes effective within the soul, leading to an actual forgiveness of sins and the true imputation of the righteousness of JESUS Christ.

Holy Scripture testifies in all places that we are justified from sins through faith in Christ, not through the works of our merits, but through the blood and death of Christ. While this is indeed taught by many, it is understood by few among those who teach it. We are taught well enough about "imputed grace," but as to what faith is, how it is born, what its essence and being are, and how it grasps the merit of Christ with grace—there, the majority are mute and blind. They remain stuck in a **historical faith** <note>original: "Historischen Glauben"</note> (James 2), which is merely a form of knowledge. With this, a person toys <note>original: "kügelt"; a metaphor for playing idly or comforting oneself with a trifle</note> and comforts themselves regarding sin and death, flattering themselves through such imagination and calling themselves a Christian. Yet they are not yet capable or worthy of this high title; they are only a "title-Christian," covered from the outside with Christ’s purple cloak. Of these, the Prophet says: *With their lips they draw near to me, but their heart is far from me*, and Christ says: *Not all who say, LORD, LORD, shall therefore enter into the kingdom of heaven, but those who do the will of my Father in heaven.*

->Epistle 4:28, 29<-

<column-break/>

**2. Q. In what then does the forgiveness of sins actually consist?**

**Answer.** The forgiveness of sins and the adoption into grace consist in the justification through the blood and death of Christ. It is where Christ’s heavenly blood **tinged** <term>tingirte: From the Latin "tingere," meaning to dye or permeate. In this mystical context, it refers to a spiritual substance "coloring" or transforming the soul's nature.</term> us and overcame the wrath of GOD in our souls and in our inward Divine ground (which comes from the essence of eternity). This was done with the highest love of the Godhead, in the name of JESUS, and **transmuted** <term>transmutirte: An alchemical term for changing one substance into another; here, changing the soul's wrathful state into a loving one.</term> us back into Divine humility and obedience. At that point, the shattered **temperature** <term>temperature / Temperatur: A state of perfect balance between the conflicting "qualities" or "properties" of a person's nature.</term> of our human property—our obedience and goodwill—entered again into the equality and unity of these properties. There, the Father's wrath, which had awakened in our life-properties and made itself the ruler of our soul and body (whereby we had died to the kingdom of heaven and become children of wrath), was changed back into the single love and equality of GOD. Our human self-will died in the death of Christ to its "I-ness" and self-willing, and the first human will, which GOD breathed from His Spirit into Adam, blossomed again through the overcoming sweetness of God in Christ’s heavenly blood. There, the devil and hell, who held man captive, were put to shame; for that was the meaning of **Aaron’s dry rod** <note>A reference to Numbers 17, where the rod of Aaron miraculously sprouted and bore almonds, symbolizing God's chosen life arising from death.</note>, which blossomed in a single night and bore sweet almonds.

Now, just as sin came from one man and pressed from that one upon all: so also did the sweet grace and victory in Christ press from one upon all. It was in the single Adamic soul that the de—

### Concerning the Forgiveness of Sins.

...not through a one-time, external spoken word, as a lord in this world grants life to a murderer through an external, imputed grace <note>This refers to the "extra nos" or "forensic" justification debated during the Reformation; Böhme argues that God's grace must actually change the person's nature, not just be a legal declaration.</note>: No, that does not hold before **GOD**. There is no grace by which we may attain to childhood except purely in the blood and death of **Christ**. **GOD** alone has presented Him as a Throne of Grace <note>original: "Gnaden-Thron"</note> in His own love, which He introduced into Him out of **JEHOVAH** in the sweet name of **JESUS**. He is the only Sacrifice that **GOD** accepts, which can reconcile His wrath. But if that same sacrifice is to benefit me, it must happen *within* me. The Father must beget or infuse His Son into my desire of faith, so that my hunger of faith grasps Him; and as my soul's hunger of faith grasps Him, as in His promised Word, so I put Him on—in His entire process of justification—within my inner ground. Immediately, the killing of wrath, the devil, death, and hell begins within me through the death of Christ. For I can do nothing; I am dead to myself, but Christ in me does it. When He rises within me, then I am dead to myself according to the old man, and He is my life; and what I then live, I live in Him, and not for the sake of fallen humanity <note>original: "Menschheit," referring here to the corrupted nature of Adam.</note>, for grace kills my will and seats itself as Lord in place of my **Selfhood** <note>original: "Ichheit," a term Böhme uses to describe the ego-driven, self-centered nature of the fallen human soul.</note>, so that I may be a work of **GOD**, who does with it what He wills.

->Epistle 46. 12:23<-

**3. Q.** Who is it, then, who actually forgives sin?

**Ans.** **Christ** is the Lamb of **GOD**, who takes away the sins of the world. If **Christ** is not in the soul, there is no grace or forgiveness of sins, for **Christ** Himself is the forgiveness of sins. He transmutes <note>original: "transmutiret," an alchemical term used here to describe the spiritual transformation of the soul’s "lead-like" wrath into "golden" divine love.</note> the abominations introduced into **GOD'S** wrath within the soul with His blood, and changes them into the Divine

<column-break/>

Fire; just as He said to the Pharisees concerning the paralytic <note>original: "Gichtbrüchtigen," referring to the man "sick of the palsy" in the Gospels (e.g., Matthew 9:2).</note> when He spoke: *Thy sins are forgiven thee.* This happened when he caught **Christ's** voice in his soul; then the living Word within him forgave his sin—that is, it overpowered the sins and trod upon the head of the serpent's introduced abomination <note>A reference to the "protoevangelium" of Genesis 3:15, where the Savior's victory is described as crushing the head of the serpent.</note> with the fire of love. Thus, no one can forgive sin except **Christ** in the human being; where **Christ** lives in the human, there is Absolution. For when **Christ** said: *Receive the Holy Spirit; whosoever's sins you remit, they are remitted; and whosoever's sins you retain, they are retained:* this applies to the true Apostles and their righteous successors, who have taken the Holy Spirit from **Christ**, and who themselves live and are in **Christ**, having **Christ's** voice within them. These have the power to speak the living Word of **Christ**—which dwells within them—into the hungry soul. No other person has this power, no matter how they name themselves or shine with outward show; they must be **Christ's** Apostles if they wish to administer His office; otherwise, they are only Pharisees and wolves. For the forgiveness of sins does not rest with humans (as we shall prove further below with more evidence), but it rests in the power of the Word of **Christ** that dwells in the human. It is not the human's speaking that forgives sin, but **GOD'S** speaking in the human's word. Therefore, the soul must open its hungry mouth toward the in-speaking <note>original: "Einsprechen," referring to the mystical act where God's Word is spoken directly into the essence of the listener's soul.</note>, otherwise the Word does not enter into it.

->On Grace 13. §. 10–13<-

### 5. Question: Can a person in this lifetime reach a point where they no longer sin, and no longer feel the lusts of sin within themselves?

**Answer:** How far a person may or may not reach in the redemption from sin is not to be discussed here; it is our duty to strive after it with all earnestness, so that through **Christ** we might reach the point where we no longer sin. Whoever thinks to accomplish something perfect and good, in which they hope to rejoice eternally and to enjoy it, let them go out from **Selfhood** <note>original: "Selbstheit"</note>—as one's own desire—and enter into <term>Gelassenheit</term> <note>A central concept in German mysticism, often translated as "yieldedness," "resignation," or "letting-be." it describes a state of surrendering the individual ego to the will of God.</note> in **GOD’s** will, and work with **GOD**. Even if the earthly desire of the selfhood still clings to the flesh and blood, as long as it does not take hold of the soul's will, the selfhood can produce no work; for the yielded will constantly breaks the essence of the selfhood again, so that it cannot reach **GOD’s** wrath. And if it should reach it, it nevertheless leads its power upward within it again.

When the mind <note>original: "Gemüthe," referring to the seat of emotions and disposition.</note> stands captive in its own desire for the earthly life, then it

<column-break/>

cannot grasp **GOD’s** will; it only runs in <term>Selfhood</term> <note>original: "Selbstheit"; the state of being focused on the "I" or ego rather than God.</note>, from one path to another, and yet finds no rest: for its own desire always introduces unrest. But when it sinks itself entirely into **GOD’s** mercy, and desires to die to its selfhood, and desires **GOD’s** will as its leader and understanding—so that it recognizes and holds itself as a Nothing that wills nothing except what **GOD** wills—then, even if the desire of wrath moves through the earthly flesh with the devil’s <term>Imagination</term> <note>In Böhme’s vocabulary, "Imagination" is the creative or "imaging" power of the soul that gives form to its desires.</note> and strikes against the soul, the yielded desire cries out to **GOD**:
> Abba <note>Aramaic: "Father," used as an intimate address to God.</note>, dear Father, deliver me from evil,
and it works then (even if it happens that the earthly will becomes too strong in the fury of **GOD** through the devil’s craving) only within itself, as St. Paul also says:
> If I now sin, it is not I who do it, but the sin that dwells in the flesh. <note>Refers to Romans 7:17.</note>
Likewise:
> So then, with the mind I serve the law of **GOD**, but with the flesh the law of sin. <note>Refers to Romans 7:25.</note>
Paul does not mean that the mind should consent to the will of the flesh; rather, sin in the flesh is as strong as the awakened wrath of **GOD** in the selfhood, such that it is often led into lust by force—through a false hatred from godless people, or through a sight of worldly vanity—so that it completely deafens the yielded will and rules it as if by force. And when sin has been worked in the flesh in this way, the wrath wants to delight in it and reaches also for the yielded will; then the yielded will cries to **GOD** for deliverance from the evil, that **GOD** would hand the sin away from it and lead it into the <term>Centrum</term> <note>original: "Centrum," the "Center." In this context, it refers to the inward point of transformation or the "dark world" where the old nature must die.</note>, as into death, so that it may die. And St. Paul speaks further:
> There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in **Christ JESUS**, who are called according to his purpose, <note>Refers to Romans 8:1.</note>
that is, those who are called back into that same call in the purpose of **GOD** in which **GOD** originally called man, so that they

# On the Forgiveness of Sins.

...they stand once more in God's purpose, in which He created humanity in His likeness and as an image of Himself. As long as one's own will remains in <term>Selfhood <note>The German *Selbstheit* refers to the ego-driven state of living for oneself rather than for God.</note></term>, it does not stand in the purpose and call of God; it is not "called," for it has departed from its proper <note>original: "Loco," Latin for "place" or "position"</note> place. However, when the mind turns back into the "Calling"—that is, into <term>Resignation <note>The German *Gelassenheit* is a central concept for Böhme, meaning a state of yieldedness, surrender, or "letting go" of the self-will to allow God to work through the person.</note></term>—then the will is within God’s calling, in the very place where God first created it. Thus, it has the power to become God’s child, as it is written: *He gave us power to become the children of God.* This power which He has given us is His purpose, according to which He created humanity in His image; God has brought this power back into humanity through Christ. He has given that same power a strength to trample the head of sin in the flesh—that is, the serpent’s will and desire. This means that the resigned will in Christ steps upon the head of the sinful serpent-will's desire and kills the committed sin: this granted power becomes a death to death, and a power of life for the living.

<margin>Resignation <note>original: "Gelassenheit"</note> chapter 2. §. 16. 21.</margin>

Therefore, reflect, dear children, and enter through the right door: it is not called "forgiving" alone, but "being born"; only then is it forgiven. That is to say, sin is then merely a husk; the new man grows out of it and casts the husk away—that is what God’s forgiveness is called. God forgives by moving the evil away from the new man; He puts it away from him. It is not taken out of the physical body, but the sin is cast into the <term>Center <note>In Böhme’s cosmology, the "Center" refers to the foundational "fire-principle" of existence, which can either be a source of torment or the necessary fuel for the light of God's love.</note></term> as if it were firewood, and it must thus serve as a cause for the "Fire-Principle," out of which the light shines. It must serve for the benefit of the holy person, as St. Paul says: *To those who love God, all things must work together for the best, even sin.* 

What shall we say then: Shall we sin, so that our salvation may be born? Far be it! How could I enter back into the "counter-will" to which I have died?

<column-break/>

Should I go out from the light and back into the darkness? But it must be so, that nothing of God’s holy ones is lost; everything must serve them. What is a sting of death to the sinner is a power of life to the holy. Thus speaks outward Reason: "Then I must indeed sin, so that my salvation may become great!" But we know that whoever departs from the light enters into the darkness; let him take care that he does not remain in the darkness, for he sins intentionally against the Holy Spirit. Do not be deceived; God is not mocked. By His love, we have become righteous again after our Fall through His entry into our flesh. But whoever intentionally enters into sin despises and slanders the Incarnation of Christ and takes a heavy burden into himself; he may well see whether he can escape from intentional sin more easily than one to whom the way of God has not yet been revealed. Therefore, it is good to avoid and flee from evil, to turn one's eyes away from falsehood so that the senses do not enter into what is false and later bring it to the heart. From this, lust arises, which the desire imagines; it then leads it into the mind, whereby the noble image is destroyed and becomes an abomination before God.

### 6. Question: What is actually understood by the "Righteousness of Jesus Christ," which God attributes to the sinner?

This new man in Christ is a true child and heir of God, who has the hereditary right in Christ to all the goods of the House of God. Thus, there is no other way to true righteousness and the right of the children of God...

For, if the eye of the soul is light, then the whole body is light in all its members. For no fire is without light. If God’s fire is in the mind, it will certainly shine forth and do that which God wants to have.

7. Question: How then is the **Imputation of Righteousness** of Jesus Christ to be understood, of which Holy Scripture, and especially Paul, speaks so much in Romans 3, 4, and 5?

# Of the Forgiveness of Sins #

...sufficiently done and paid, and earned for him the righteousness that counts before God, as if he himself had in his own person fully satisfied God's justice. But we understand that God reckons the perfect satisfaction and righteousness of Jesus Christ to the sinner in such a way that, just as sin entered the world through one man and permeated all people and became effective unto death and damnation—not through a mere reckoning <note>i.e., not just a legal attribution</note>, but through inheritance; not accepted from the outside, but internal, powerful, effective, even dominant—so also the righteousness of Jesus Christ, the second Adam, is reckoned through faith so that this righteousness and satisfaction works powerfully within to eradicate sin, to kill the old man, and to awaken the new life internally, so that the grace, the Word, and the Spirit of Jesus Christ may hold dominion within the person.

<margin>See above, *Of Election by Grace* [Gnaden-Wahl] chapter 10, section 37.</margin>

But as to how God introduces the righteousness of Jesus Christ into the sinner essentially and actually, so that the righteousness of Jesus Christ becomes as powerfully effective internally for the new life as sin became effective for death and damnation: understand, we are all dead and perished in sin by nature, and nothing remains to us except a possibility to receive God's grace and the power of His promise. Now, as previously mentioned, the heart of God introduced itself into the human essence, which lay locked in death, and entered into the Chamber of Anguish <note>original: *Angst-Kammer*; refers to the soul's state of separation from God</note> of our misery. He drew a soul from our essence to Himself, took our mortal life upon Himself, and led the soul through death—through the earnest fire of God the Father—into the **Light-World** [Licht-Welt]. He broke death, which held us captive, and unlocked life.

Now it may and can be no other way: whoever wishes to possess the Light-World must enter through the same path that He made. He must enter into Christ's death, and in Christ's resurrection, he enters into the Light-World. Just as we recognize that the eternal Word of the Father, which is the Father's heart from eternity to eternity, is born out of the wrath of the death of darkness through the Father's fire, and is in itself the true **Center of Nature** (*Centrum Naturæ*) <term>Center of Nature: In Böhme's thought, the foundational point where the dark, fiery power of nature is transformed into the light and love of God.</term> of the Holy Trinity...

<column-break/>

...is, and of itself, with the proceeding Holy Spirit, is the light-flaming Majesty or Light-World: So too, in like manner and quality, we must—in our heart, mind, and soul—depart from the bitter, harsh, and evil worldliness within ourselves, away from the corrupt Adamic man, and break and kill him with our earnest will and deed.

We must take the cross of the old Adam, which clings to us while we live, upon ourselves; we must go onto and into the cross, into the *Center of Nature*, into the **Triangle** [Drey-Angel] <note>A geometric symbol Böhme uses for the Trinity</note>, and be born again out of the **Wheel of Anguish** [Angst-Rad] <term>Wheel of Anguish: The restless, circular motion of the natural soul's desires and fears before it finds rest in God's light.</term>, if we wish to be angels and live eternally in God. Because we were not capable of this, Christ surrendered Himself into that same center of wrath, broke the wrath, and extinguished it with His love. For He brought heavenly, Divine essence into that same wrath, into the center of the Chamber of Anguish, and extinguished the soul's fire of anguish—as the wrath of the Father of the fiery world in the soul—so that we now no longer fall prey to the wrath. Instead, when we give ourselves into Christ's death and depart from our own evil Adam, we fall into Christ's death, into the path He made for us; we fall into **Abraham's Bosom** [Schooß Abrahā], that is, into Christ's arms, who receives us into Himself. For Abraham’s Bosom is the unlocked Light-World in Christ's death; it is the Paradise into which God created us. And it now depends on this: not that we be **Mouth-Christians** [Mund-Christen] <note>Hypocrites who speak of faith but do not live it</note>, merely picturing Christ's death to ourselves while remaining rogues in heart, spirit, and soul, but that we quite earnestly—with mind and soul, with will and deed—depart from the evil **attachment** [Anneiglichkeit] <note>The soul's tendency to lean toward or "attach" itself to worldly vanity</note> and struggle against it. Although it still clings to us, we must yet daily and hourly kill the will and deeds of that same evil Adam. We must do what we do not want to do; we must deny our own earthly evil life, and Christ's...

#### Part 4 / Chapter 7. ####

...drawing life into ourselves; then "the kingdom of heaven suffers violence, and those who take it by force pull it to themselves," <note>original: "das Himmelreich Gewalt leidet" — a reference to Matthew 11:12</note> as Christ says. Thus we become pregnant with the kingdom of heaven and enter into Christ's death while still in our living bodies, receiving the body of Christ as the **Divine Essence**; we carry the kingdom of heaven within us. So we are Christ's children, members, and heirs in God's kingdom, and the image of the Holy Divine World, which is God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, and the essence of that same Holy Trinity. Everything born and revealed out of **Wisdom** <note>Sophia, the divine mirror of God's ideas</note> is our paradise, and nothing in us dies except the dead Adam—the earthly, evil nature whose will we have already broken and to whom we have become enemies. Our enemy simply departs from us; he must go into the fire—understand, into the **essential** fire, into the four elements, and into the **Mystery** <term>Mysterium: the hidden spiritual foundation of the physical world</term>—and at the end of this time, he must be preserved through God’s fire and must present our wonders and works back to us. Whatever the earthly **Mystery** has swallowed up must be returned in God's fire—not as something evil, for God's fire consumes the evil, but it gives us back what we sought in our anxious searching. Just as fire consumes substance but gives back spirit in place of substance, so our works are presented to us in the spirit and in heavenly joys out of God's fire, like a bright mirror, resembling the wonder of God’s Wisdom. Let this be revealed to you, dear children, for it has been recognized as highly precious. Do not let yourselves be tickled <note>i.e., superficially comforted or flattered</note> by Christ’s death, imagining it as a finished work that is enough for us if we only know and believe it happened for us. What good does it do me to know where a treasure lies if I do not dig it out? It is no use to comfort oneself, to play the hypocrite, and to speak good words with the mouth while keeping the rogue in the soul—

<column-break/>

—Christ says: "You must be born again, or you will not see the kingdom of God." We must turn around and become like a child in the mother's womb, born of the **Divine Essence**. We must put a new garment on our souls, namely the robe of Christ—the humanity of Christ. Otherwise, all hypocrisy is useless; everything the "mouth-shouting" says is a lie when it paints Christ before our eyes as if He did everything for us so that we only need to take comfort in it while still walking in the old Adam, in greed, pride, and falsehood, and in the desires of wickedness. This is the **Antichristian deception** of the false clergy, against whom the Revelation warns us. It is of no use to play the hypocrite and tickle ourselves with Christ's suffering and death; we must enter into it and become like His image. Only then are Christ's suffering and death useful to us. We must take His cross upon us, follow Him, and dampen and kill evil lusts, always desiring to do good. Then we will clearly see what Christ's footsteps are, when we fight against the devil, the old Adam, and the evil world—against earthly reason, which desires only temporary pleasure. There, Christ’s cross is truly laid upon us; for it is the devil, the world, and our evil Adam who are our enemies. There, the new man must stand like a knight and fight in Christ's footsteps. O, how many countless enemies he will awaken there, who will all strike at him! There, it is a matter of fighting for the thorny "knight’s wreath" <note>The crown of thorns, reimagined as a victor's laurel</note> of Christ like a soldier, yet always being despised as one who is not worthy of the earth. There, one must stand in war and faith, where outward reason says a loud "No." There, it is good to place Christ's suffering and death at the forefront, presenting them to the devil, the world, and death alongside earthly reason, and not despair. For here, it is a matter of an **angel's crown**—of being either an angel or a devil. We must enter into

...only believe / and so we are made righteous. You teach one thing and do another, and thus you testify that GOD’s judgment over you is just. Or what pleasure does GOD take in your knowledge while you remain a scoundrel <note>original: "Schalck"—a rogue or unregenerate person</note>? You must constantly crucify the **old Adam** <note>the sinful, fallen nature of humanity inherited from the first man</note> and always hang upon Christ’s cross, and you must become an obedient child who always hears what the Father says and always desires to do the same. ### Part 4 / Chapter 7. ###

...only believe / then we are made righteous. I must enter into that same path and walk in that same street as a **pilgrim** who walks out of death into life.

### The VIII. Chapter.

->Concerning True Rebirth, and its internal<-
->powerful effects, as well as its genuine fruits<-
->and identifying signs.<-

The entire teaching and main foundation of the **Gospel** <note>original: "Evangelii"</note> consists, firstly, in the great work of redemption from sin and the indescribable misery that arose from it. Secondly, it consists in true rebirth and the restoration of the pure, virginal image of **GOD**. The first is carried out by **JESUS Christ** in the soul through the great power of His suffering and death; this power works in us true repentance, earnest prayer, living faith, active love, obedience, patience, suffering, and finally a complete redemption into the death of the old man, which we have discussed until now. Now follows the second part, namely, how **JESUS Christ**, through the great power of His resurrection, awakens us to a new life and births us anew through His Holy Spirit.

To recognize this fundamentally, we wish to investigate: Firstly, what true rebirth is and what it consists of. Secondly, how a person is born again. Thirdly, how the new birth grows in a new life until the full maturity of Christ, and eternally marries the heavenly **Wisdom** <note>original: "Sophia"—the personification of Divine Wisdom, often described by Böhme as the soul's spiritual bride.</note>, and how it works, acts, and completes its sanctification in Christ as a prophet, priest, and king.

1. Question.
What does true rebirth actually consist of?

Answer.
True rebirth consists purely in this: that we enter with our will into **GOD’S** will, and surrender and commit ourselves entirely to Him. This is called faith; for the word "faith" is not merely historical <note>Böhme frequently warns against "historical faith," which is mere intellectual belief without spiritual transformation.</note>, but it is a taking from **GOD’S** being, an eating of **GOD’S** being, introducing **GOD’S** being into the soul-fire through the **imagination** <term>Imagination: In Böhme’s thought, this is the soul's creative focus or "imaging" power that shapes its inner reality.</term>, quieting its hunger therewith, and thus putting on **GOD’S** being—not as a garment, but as a body for the soul. The soul must have **GOD’S** being within its fire; it must eat of **GOD’S** bread.

<column-break/>

2. Question. What then must we do on our part so that we may be born again?

Answer. We have taught above how the word of the promise of the **Serpent-Crusher** <note>original: "Schlangen-Treter"—referring to the prophecy in Genesis 3:15 that the seed of the woman would crush the serpent's head.</note> is embodied in all people; also how **JESUS Christ**, after He seated Himself at the right hand of the Majesty of **GOD**, constantly pours out and speaks His Spirit and living Word, unceasingly knocking and persisting at the person’s door so that they might open the door to Him. Thus, on the human side, there is nothing more to do than that we enter with our will and spirit through Him into **GOD’S** being. In this way, our will is born anew into **GOD’S** will and receives Divine power. And so the image of God is awakened again through this power out of the death into which it was led by Adam and held captive by sin; and thus the life of **JESUS** sprouts <note>original: "hervorgruͤnt"—literally "greens forth," a favorite metaphor of Böhme's for organic spiritual growth.</note> within us once more.

<summary>This page defines true rebirth as the active merging of the human will with the Divine will, moving beyond mere intellectual belief to a literal "feeding" on God's essence. It frames this process as the restoration of the divine image within man, catalyzed by Christ's resurrection power.</summary>
<keywords>rebirth, regeneration, Divine Will, Sophia, Serpent-Crusher, Imagination, Jacob Böhme, spiritual growth, Gospel foundation</keywords>

outer reason; how can it be that

becomes a tree. Thus the new birth is an
impulse of the Spirit of JESUS Christ in the soul, in
which the seed of the Word lies.

# 4. Part / Chapter 8.

4. Question: By what may one recognize that the seed of the new birth has been unlocked in the soul, and that the Spirit of JESUS Christ is driving and active within that growth?

Answer: As soon as the Light of GOD ignites the essences of the fire-soul <note>original: "Feuer-Seele"—the soul in its primary, energetic state before being illuminated by grace.</note> with the love-pang <term>Qual</term> <note>original: "Liebes-Quaal"—a technical term in Böhme’s writing where "Qual" implies both a "tormenting" desire and a "quality" or "source" of being.</note>, they give forth a growth from within themselves in the quality of the Spirit. This appears as a friendly will, good habits, virtue, piety, patience in suffering, and the hope of being delivered from evil. It manifests as a desire to always speak, ring out, and sing of GOD’S wondrous deeds, and to rejoice in the works and wonders of GOD; to always wish to do good, to resist evil and malice, and to always gladly draw one's neighbor into the light-world <note>original: "Licht-Welt"—the divine realm of peace and clarity.</note> with love. It is seen in fleeing from the wicked and always suppressing evil affections with patience, in the hope of being redeemed; in rejoicing in the hope of that which the eyes do not see and outer reason does not know; in always striving to break out of evil and to lead the desire into the Divine Being; always wishing to eat of GOD’S Bread. These qualities are carried by the new man who is born again from the light-world; these are his fruits, which the light-world thus generates quite hiddenly within the old Adam <note>original: "alten Adams"—the fallen, earthly nature of humanity.</note>. It continually kills the old Adam of this world and lies always in conflict with him. The old Adam must follow the new man, though like a lazy donkey that must carry the sack while its master constantly whips it. Thus the new man does to the old; he forces him to do what he does not want to do. Whatever concerns the joy of this world would be preferred by the old donkey, but he must remain a servant. Secondly, this principle <note>original: "Principium"—one of the three fundamental levels of reality in Böhme's philosophy.</note> has its growth and gives its fruit into the third principle in general—that is, into the spirit of the great world—so that the outer and inner <term>Turba</term> <note>original: "Turbæ"—the Latin term for "distress" or "disturbance," used by Böhme to describe the chaotic, wrathful element in nature that leads to destruction.</note> is restrained. It breaks through and yields fruitfulness; it resists the wrath of the stars and breaks the constellation of spirits, and also of the firmamental heaven; it resists the

<column-break/>

wrath of the devil and the plots of wicked people, provided that saints are found who are worthy of it.

By this, everyone should learn to know themselves; one need only search after one's own quality, to see where the will constantly drives. In that kingdom one stands, and is not a "human" in the way one considers and presents oneself, but rather a creature of the dark world—such as a greedy dog, a proud bird, an unchaste beast, a fierce serpent, or an envious toad full of poison, etc. All these qualities well up within him and are his "wood" from which his fire burns. When the outer wood—the essence of the four elements—leaves him at his death, then only the inner, poisonous, evil pang <note>original: "Quall"—referring again to the source-quality of the soul.</note> remains. What kind of figure shall stand in such a quality? None other than the one which was the strongest among these qualities; that one will be shaped into its form by the hellish <term>Fiat</term> <note>original: "höllischen Fiat"—the "let it be" or creative command, here acting within the realm of darkness to fix the soul's shape.</note>. Such as a poisonous serpent, a dog, or something similar, or another beast, etc. Into whatever quality the spirit of the will has surrendered itself, that same quality is hereafter the image of the soul; and this is one part of it. Furthermore, a person should test themselves in their desire; for every person has these evil qualities within them: Does he also find a constant desire in himself to kill this poison and malice? Is he an enemy to this poison? Or does he have his joy therein, to always put the false poison into action—such as in pride, greed, envy, unchastity, or in lying and deceiving? If he finds within himself that he takes joy in it and always wishes to put it into practice, then he is no human being, as he esteems himself, but the devil in a foreign form. It deceives him so that he thinks he is a man; but he carries not GOD’S image, but the image of the serpent <note>original: "Schlangen Bildnis"—representing the fallen, deceptive nature.</note>, and is only in the outer realm a likeness of a human image, so long as he remains in this quality and this quality is the master. **5. Question.** Can it then not easily happen that such a delicate plant dies, and the new light of life goes out again?

**Answer.** So long as the fire-soul <term>Feuer-Seele</term> <note>In this theology, the soul is viewed as a "fire" that must be transformed by Divine light to reach a state of peace.</note> is still tied to the bond of vanity in this outer realm during this time, and must breathe and work within this earthly life, the little tree stands in great danger. For the Devil does not rest from blowing up the hellish source <term>Höllen Quall</term> <note>The original term "Quall" implies both a "fountain/source" and "torment," describing the turbulent energy of spiritual suffering.</note> in the fire-soul, whereby flesh and blood are inflamed by the grimness of **GOD’S** wrath and sin, through which the branch in many people is spoiled or broken, and the poor soul is made earthly.

The same thing happens to the poor sinner when he repents but afterwards becomes an evil person again; it happens to him as it happened to Adam. Adam was a beautiful, glorious image, created by **GOD** and highly enlightened; but when he allowed lust to overcome him, he became earthly, and his beautiful image was captured in the earthly torment within the wrath of **GOD**. This is how it still happens today. But we say this—as we have received enlightenment through the grace of **GOD** and have wrestled for a long time over this "little crown" <note>likely referring to the prize of spiritual victory</note>—that for one who remains steadfast in earnestness until his branch becomes a little tree, his branch may not easily be broken in one or more storms. For that which is weak also has a weak life. We do not speak this into the Godhead <note>i.e., we are not describing God's internal nature</note>, rather this is natural, and yet everything happens naturally, for the Eternal also has its own nature, and one thing simply proceeds from another. Thus the Devil gains his power because the outer dominion is born out of the inner, and since he dwells in the inner, he slips from the inner into the outer and ignites the outer mind; from this arises the false addiction and evil lust. So it is that two dominions fight against the soul's dominion, and the 

<column-break/>

poor soul is in the middle between the dominion of this world and the dominion of hellish torment; there she stands before the Gates of Heaven in great danger. Her root is **GOD’S** wrath and the hellish fire, and her superior spirit is the dominion of this world; there she stands in the middle of the fire’s tincture <term>Tincktur</term> <note>An alchemical term referring to the essential spiritual quality or "dye" that colors the soul’s existence.</note>. Whichever way she reaches out, she enters into it: if it is into the lust of this world, she stands within it and is captured by the Devil; but if she reaches inward into **God**, then the Devil strikes at her, for she is now in his territory. But when she receives Christ’s flesh as a new body, she is no longer in his territory. That is a tree to him which is his poison and death; therefore he is hateful and does not like to touch it, but he incites his servants against the outer body, which must bear shame and mockery, so that he may indeed cover up this tree so that it is not recognized; otherwise, it might produce more little branches, and eventually hell might become too narrow for him. Therefore he resists as much as he can. Now, when the poor soul breaks away from him and turns with her dear bridegroom Christ toward **GOD’S** love—entering into the will of **GOD** through earnest repentance and turning inward—the Devil still has seven snares with which he holds her before he lets her go. She must wind herself loose through all seven and leave his ropes entirely behind. At the eighth <note>referring to the eighth stage or level of spiritual progression</note>, she must go through the fire; that is the earnest trial <term>Proba</term> <note>original: "Proba" — Latin for "test" or "proof."</note>, and when she comes through it, she attains the heavenly tincture in the ninth number; and in the tenth number upon the Cross, she attains Christ’s body, so that she is an angel in Heaven and a guest on Earth in this valley of tabernacles <term>Hütten-Thal</term> <note>A poetic reference to the temporary nature of earthly life, often compared to living in a fragile tent or hut.</note>. The seven ropes with which the soul is tied are the seven spirits of outer nature, belonging to the dominion of this world; she must wind through them and break through them, casting them all behind her. And in the eighth number stands Moses with his Law, where the soul is first read...

What joy there is before the angels of GOD, and what joy the soul attains there, we have no pen to write, nor do we have any mouth in this world to speak of it. We only wish for the reader and all people that they might experience it for themselves, for which reason we occupy ourselves with this writing through much effort and deep labor. For we write what we ourselves have recognized and seen with spiritual eyes. We do not say this for our own glory, but so that the reader may know what to expect if he wishes to follow us—since he otherwise sees that the world views the children of GOD only as an owl <note>A German idiom: the owl is a bird that is mocked and pecked at by other birds during the day; thus, a person who is an object of scorn.</note>. But we will surely enjoy ourselves after this short life; this little crown is dearer to us than the whole world, even if it is sometimes hidden from us. It does not die. For just as the harsh winter covers the green earth, where reason says "all is dead," but when spring returns it begins to go green and bloom again—so it is with the noble and beautiful crown of Christ. When it turns green again, then

it brings forth lilies without number, and every spring—whenever the mind is renewed in Christ—it increases tenfold.

<margin>Threefold Life, 14. 34–37.</margin>
But where the soul goes backward and sets its will either into the grimness of GOD'S wrath or into the lust, honor, wealth, and joy of this world, so that it defiles itself with the filth of this world, the noble image is darkened. For the more vain the outer man becomes, the darker the inner man becomes, until he fades away entirely. Then it is over for the beautiful little Tree of Paradise, and it will be difficult to regain it. Especially if the outer soul becomes a hypocrite <term>Schein-Gleißner</term> <note>Literally a "shining-pretender," referring to someone who maintains a pious exterior while their inner spiritual life has perished.</note> and considers itself godly even though the pearl is gone. Although the gate of grace still stands open, the false light of the outer "reason-soul" keeps them away, making them think they have the pearl while they only live for the vanity of this world and dance to the Devil's pipe.

Even though we have mentioned this once before, we present it here again so that those who formerly denied the world and its lusts, but now return and defile themselves worse than before, might take it to heart.

Even Lucifer and Adam fell, though they were in a much more glorious state than we can reach in this time. 7. **Question:** Can a person then not reach the point where the Divine and heavenly birth swallows up the outer man, just as the day swallows the night, so that one might see and recognize the glory and majesty of GOD in him?

**Answer:** Just as little as gold can shine through a stone, just as little can the new man so shine through the earthly, four-elemental man <note>The "four-elemental man" is the physical body composed of the four elements of the material world.</note> that he may be recognized with earthly eyes. For now, however, we recognize the new man no better than in the Center—namely, in the desire, sense, and mind. When we find that our desire is entirely toward

<column-break/>

and toward GOD, our senses constantly run in GOD’S will, and the mind yields itself entirely in obedience to GOD’S will, so that the imagination catches hold of GOD’S power—then we may surely know that the noble **lily-branch** <note>The lily is Böhme’s primary symbol for the blossoming of the new spiritual life out of the "dark earth" of the soul.</note> is born, that the Image of GOD is in essence, and that GOD has become man in this likeness. Here it is necessary and vital to preserve the noble image, and to allow the **old Adam** <note>The "Old Adam" represents the fallen, sinful human nature inherited from the first man.</note> with his lusts no room to exalt himself or take pleasure therein, but always to kill him <note>To "kill the old Adam" is the process of mortification, or denying one's selfish impulses.</note>, so that the new man may grow large and be adorned with the wonders of Wisdom.

<margin>See *The Incarnation of Jesus Christ*, part 2, chapter 10, section 3.</margin>

The old stock, or husk—meaning the body, which Adam introduced to us with his imagination into earthliness, out of earthly and Devilish essence, as a contrary torment—that is not what "greens" or grows; rather, it is the faded image of GOD (understand: given to Adam from the Divine essence, as from the second Principle <term>Principio</term> <note>The "Second Principle" is the world of Light, Love, and Heaven.</note>, out of the Kingdom of Heaven, which died with the earthly introduction, or as I might put it: was closed again into the eternal silence, as into the **Nothing** <note>The "Nothing" or *Ungrund* is the absolute, undifferentiated source of all being in Böhme’s thought.</note>, where it lost its right Divine life). It is into this [faded image] that the eternal Word became man, and introduced living essence again with his entrance and opening, and bore eternal life out of death. That same Divine—and then also in death enclosed—human essence or flesh, became a man to whom the earthly husk only clung, and who held the earthly burning death captive within himself.

Holy Scripture also does not speak of an entirely new flesh, as if the old flesh were received entirely anew in Divine essence and born in GOD: Otherwise, it would have to follow that the evil, introduced animal flesh, with its animal property, would have been exalted in the power of Majesty.

## Of the Wedding and Marriage of the Human Soul with Sophia, the Highly-Blessed Virgin.

->1. Question.<-

What then is the degree of the perfect rebirth of man?

->Answer.<-

As soon as Jesus CHRIST gains a true form in the soul, and the little sacred wellspring of Divine gentleness is unlocked, so that the masculine fire of the soul reaches the Virginal light of heavenly character; then immediately begins the marriage of the soul with Virgin Sophia <note>Sophia is the Greek word for Wisdom. There, Virgin Sophia—as the worthy humanity of Christ—is married to the soul.

Concerning this high mystery, many holy men have written from living experience, but generally only of the sweetness, sensation, effect, and the fruits: of the root, the ground, and the first source of such a marriage, and its drive, no one has given such an explanation as our highly enlightened Author <note>The "Author" refers to Jacob Böhme (1575–1624), the German mystic whose complex terminology this text is explaining.</note>.

all three births, much less the kingdom of this world of stars and elements, which is the source-quality, life, and governance of the outer man.

We cannot deny that, let a man be as holy as he will, the spirit of the outer world is still the spirit, life, and guide of his outer flesh; and we see clearly how the outer man stands in a constellation of the stars; when that constellation leaves him, he falls away and decays.

2. Fr. What does the Author actually understand by the marriage or union of the soul with Sophia, the noble Virgin?

Answer. Our Author speaks very much and in various ways about this high mystery, which is misunderstood by many, and also poorly applied and abused. The Author understands by this nothing other than the highest bloom and the perfect growth of the new humanity, when the Spirit of Jesus Christ, and the Virginal Fire- and Light-Tincture <term>Tincture</term> <note>In alchemy and Böhme's philosophy, a "Tincture" is a transformative essence that changes the quality of a substance; here it refers to the spiritual power that transforms the soul.</note> in the blood of the new man, has driven the new growth of the new creature to its flower and crown, so that it is now Virginal and mature. Just as in Christ Jesus, man and woman are not separated, but Christ Jesus in the state of His glorification in His Divine life has both the Light- and Fire-Tincture, and is as much a masculine Virgin as a Virginal Man: so also is every reborn person in Christ such a new creature, and has in themselves both tinctures of Fire and Light, in Virginal virtue and character. As soon as the Spirit of Jesus Christ settles in the soul, it cleanses the Fire-power of the soul, which hitherto has burned in the unclean sulfur of the flesh, in lusts and desires; the Spirit of Jesus kills this unclean, fleshly, animal life, and burns out all impurity; in return, He inclines

# Of the Marriage of the Soul with Sophia.

the soul’s fire and its hunger into the heavenly pure sulfur and balsam of humanity, and the body and blood of JESUS Christ; He blows upon the fire so that from the fire there goes forth the **fire-tincture** <note>In this context, a "tincture" refers to a spiritual essence or "coloring" that transforms the nature of a substance, much like a dye or an alchemical catalyst.</note>, as a pure Divine longing, hunger, desire, and awakened **Magia** <note>Magia refers to a spiritual "will" or "desire" that has the power to manifest or create reality.</note>. The sharper, mightier, and purer the fire-tincture becomes, the more strongly it drives to reach the **light-tincture**, and where this fire-tincture exerts its vigor and reaches maturity, the new creature becomes masculine, and drives toward marriage and union with **Sophia**, as with the light-source of the light-soul of JESUS Christ in His person; and where the fire-tincture, as a magical longing, perceives the masculine virgin in its pure scent and spirit as a noble flower in a member of JESUS Christ or a reborn child of GOD.

The new creature, now at such a high degree—both in the purification of the soul-fire, or the *Limbus* <note>The "Limbus" here refers to the spiritual "matrix" or reservoir of formative substance.</note>, and in the noble, pure, Divine, paradisiacal driving of the tincture of the soul-fire—the Author calls the **Youth, Bridegroom, the Virginal Man**, etc. Likewise, where the Spirit of JESUS Christ applies itself to a person and purifies the fire-soul, the Spirit of JESUS opens, through His Virginal Magnet, the lovely sweet wellspring of Divine love and gentleness, which was previously dried up and locked away in the bitter, fierce soul-fire, like water in a stone. 

Then, as soon as the soul-fire is purified and its bitter, fierce fire-power is soothed and tempered through the gentle, lovely, sweetening effect of the Spirit of JESUS Christ—when the Spirit of JESUS Christ is taken in and swallowed into the soul-fire like a little spiritual water—He opens the **light-center** in the soul and the so-greatly-sealed fountain. Then the fire-flash rises in the temperament <note>The "temperament" refers to the balanced state where the conflicting qualities of fire and light are harmonized.</note> of the properties. In the ignition of the fire-flash of the new life, both tinctures are present: the masculine fire-tincture rises above itself in the **property of Mars** <note>Mars represents the fiery, energetic, and sometimes "wrathful" aspect of the soul's nature.</note>, yet pure, clean, not poisonous, fierce, squinting, or false; and the Virginal light-tincture in the **heavenly property of Venus** <note>Venus represents the soft, loving, and gentle aspect of the Divine nature.</note> sinks beneath itself—not earthly, fleshly, impure, or dim, but as a pure, clear, transparent crystalline fountain. Where this source now becomes active in a soul, the noble Virginal light-tincture rises; this drives in the new growth toward the flower of Virginal perfection and maturity, where the flower blossoms out and, in its colors, scent, and form, presents itself as a noble lily: the virtue and property of its root and the whole growth. Just as the fire-tincture is a driving longing, hunger, and *Magia* for

<column-break/>

the light, so is the light-tincture a yearning drive, a self-appropriation, a self-surrender into the fire-tincture—an ineffable love—where these two enter into one another and embrace one another in virginal discipline. 

This spiritual marriage is twofold, as every new creature has two centers, namely **fire** and **light**; also, each center has its own tincture. The fire-soul together with the fire-tincture is called the **Man**, both in the person of Christ and in His members and brothers. Where this tincture comes to the maturity of manhood, it becomes driving and active to awaken and ignite a pure Virginal life. Christ the Virginal Man—both in His highly-blessed person and His members <note>Note well</note> who grow into such perfect greatness of manhood and in whom the tincture reaches its maturity—is the **Bridegroom**. Likewise, Christ and His members in whom the flower of Divine virginity reaches its breakout and full opening are the **Bride, Sophia**, and the Divine delight of love; just as in the **Song of Solomon**, JESUS Christ and the newly-born enlightened soul are alternately called and compared to the Bridegroom and the Bride. 

The pen is not to be trusted further here, for the sake of the corrupted, defiled **old Adam** and his lusting Eves. We have presented it so clearly for no other reason than to earnestly warn everyone not to easily exalt themselves into this state of marriage and chatter about Sophia, but rather to remain in humility and to green as a **lily in the valley**, until this noble flower rises of itself and proves the maturity of the tinctures with its virtue and scent. From this, one will easily recognize what the Author means when he speaks so much loveliness to us of Sophia, especially when he says:

->But the fire-soul of man must persist in the fire of GOD / and thus be as pure as clear gold / then <note>Note well</note> he is the **husband of the noble Sophia**, from the seed of the woman: she is the tincture of the fire / and Sophia the tincture of the light. Where the tincture of the fire is entirely pure / then Sophia is given into it / so Adam receives his most noble bride / who was taken from him in his first sleep / back into his arms / and henceforth is neither man nor woman / but a branch on **Christ’s Tree of Life** / which stands in the Paradise of GOD / for which we here require the tongue of an angel.<-

3. **Question:** But how may a soul reach such a precise union with the heavenly Virgin?

**Answer:** Dear soul, this requires **Earnestness** <note>In Böhme’s vocabulary, "Earnestness" (*Ernst*) implies a total, life-altering commitment to the spiritual struggle.</note>; for if the soul wishes to obtain Christ's **Knightly Wreath** from the noble Sophia, it must woo her with a great desire of love. It must pray to her by her most holy name and step before her in very great, modest humility—not as a lustful bull or a lewd Venus. All who are such should not even desire it from her; so long as they remain in that state, they shall not obtain it. And even if a glimpse were obtained in this time, it would be to such people only a **mere glint** <note>original: "Glast" — a fleeting reflection or superficial glimmer rather than the true light.</note>.

4. **Question:** How is the noble Virgin first revealed to her Bridegroom?

**Answer:** This happens first in the **earnest struggle of repentance** <note>original: "ernsten Buß-Kampff" — Böhme describes repentance as a literal battle against the ego and the devil.</note>, about which we have dealt above with more detail. When the dark **Fire-soul** hungers for its salvation through the "drawing of the Father," the Father strikes the spark of His Divine Omnipotence into the faded essence of the heavenly image—which died in Adam. Then the spark begins to glow; at first it is as small as a mustard seed, as Christ says. If the soul persists and constantly leads its will and hunger into the glowing wick, it blows upon the holy fire through its desire until it glows brightly, from which it develops a great hunger. If the soul now ventures away from its **Selfhood** <note>original: "Selbstheit" — the ego-driven state of being separate from God.</note> and desires to cast the Falsehood of the devil entirely 

<column-break/>

away, and enters into the **Fire of Love** through earnest struggle, prayer, and **surrender** <note>original: "Einergebung" — a key term in German mysticism meaning total yielding of the self-will to God.</note>, then the Love-fire seizes the soul's desire, and one fire is ignited within the other. For the soul is the Father’s fire, and the sown love is the Son’s fire. Now the "Prodigal Son" returns to the Father’s love, and there is great joy in heaven, such that His angels rejoice more than over ninety-nine righteous ones who need no repentance. When the Virgin’s Spirit enters into the Soul-fire from the Love-fire, he ignites the Soul-fire as well, so that the Virgin's light shines in the light of her Bridegroom (the soul). Thus, understand it well: the **fire** signifies the soul when it is ignited in God's light; the **light and radiance** signify the holy fire of love from the Virgin; but the power of the light is the **Pearl-Wreath**. The Virgin does not give this to the Fire-soul as its own property, but she places it upon him and presses it into his heart as long as the soul leads its Fire-desire into the Virgin Sophia and its earnest will remains set in God's light. Yet the Fire-soul does not *become* the Light-soul; the Fire is the Father, the Light is the Son. Each retains its own **source-quality** <note>original: "Quall" — Böhme uses this term to describe the fundamental vibration or character of a spiritual principle.</note> as two **Principles** within one another. The creature does not become God; it remains eternally beneath God. God, however, glows through the creature with His desire of the Love-fire, as with His light and radiance.

->*Apologia* against Stiefel 310-313.<-

6. Question: But how is it that the noble Virgin <note>Böhme frequently uses "the noble Virgin" as another title for Sophia or Divine Wisdom.</note> departs so soon from her bridegroom and leaves him in so much anxiety and adversity?

Answer: The noble Virgin was deceived by Adam in such a way that she does not easily entrust herself to the fire-soul <note>The "fire-soul" represents the human will and primary life-force, which Böhme characterizes as a spiritual fire that needs the "light" of Sophia to be balanced.</note> as its own possession, unless the fire-soul is found to be purified and proven from all false lust and desire. Why do you not strive after temporal honors, after pleasure and riches, so that it might go well for you in this world? Why do you make yourself the world's fool and become everyone's owl <note>To be the "world's owl" meant to be an object of mockery or an outcast, as the owl is chased by other birds in daylight.</note> and foot-rag? Why do you let

<column-break/>

those who are less and know less than you despise you? Could you not also trot along with the hypocrite? Then you would be beloved, and no harm would come to you; you would be more secure in your body and goods than on this path, where you are only the world's owl and fool." But my dear Virgin says: "You, my dear beloved <note>original: *Buhle*. In the 1600s, this was a term for a sweetheart or one dearly loved, carrying no negative connotation.</note>, whom I have chosen, walk with me. In my kingdom there is nothing but joy, honor, and glory; no taskmaster is within it. I will adorn you with God’s glory and put my beautiful jewelry upon you. I will make you a lord in heaven and a judge over this world. You shall help judge the oppressor in his wickedness; he shall lie as a stool for your feet. He shall not open his maw against you but shall be eternally locked within his grim gates. You shall eat from my table; there shall be no envy or lack. My fruit is sweeter and lovelier than the fruit of this world; it will never cause you pain. All your bearing shall consist of friendly laughter and gracious conversation; before you shall appear nothing but humility in great love.
