# Of the Outer Visible Church.

He claims to have and lead **GOD'S** Word and Christ’s teaching / yet he strongly believes he has grasped the Word: But it is a shadow-fencing <note>original: "spiegel-fechten"; meaning fighting an imaginary opponent or engaging in empty, performative debate</note>; his shouting and calling is mere jugglery. If you do not have a right hammer / you cannot strike the bell / that awakens the poor imprisoned soul. Heaven and Earth with all their essence lie within man. You must only use a right hammer / if you wish to strike his hour / and awaken him from his sleep. Your great shouting does not do it / you do not shout the Divine sound into him / if you do not have it yourself; But where the right hammer is / that awakens him. Therefore all teachers without **GOD'S** hammer are only jugglers / Belly-hammers / Ear-hammers / and not Soul-hammers <note>Böhme invents these compounds to distinguish between preachers who satisfy physical needs (belly) or intellectual curiosity (ears) versus those who strike the heart (soul)</note>. The soul does not dwell in the outer spirit. Indeed, the outer spirit has woven itself into the soul / like a rogue / but he does not have the *Principle* within / where the soul dwells / he is only her cover and hindrance: So also is the Anti-Christ only a hindrance to poor souls. If the soul were not bound so tightly to the shouting in the ears / she would go into herself and seek herself / she would strive after abstinence <note>meaning renunciation of the worldly self</note>: Instead she thinks / that it is holiness / that enters into her ears / and yet there is often filth and mockery against love and unity within it. What should one say / for everything is blinded and full of hypocrisy / everyone strives only after the belly / the shepherd with the sheep / the superior and the inferior: The Spirit of **GOD** is very precious / and yet people boast so much of the Spirit / and it is only dissimulation / of which the heart knows little or nothing / it is a scraped-together entity without spirit.

O you worthy Christendom / look at yourself! O Europe, Asia and Africa, open your eyes / and behold your own self! Every man must seek himself / or things will not become good. A serious bow is drawn: Fall into the archer's arm / and return / and find yourself / or you will be shot

<column-break/>

away: Do not let yourself be treated like a child / walk on your own feet. It is time, the sleep is over, the angel has sounded the trumpet, delay no longer. Think / what the Revelation of **JESUS CHRIST** says / that those / who hang upon the Whore of Babylon <note>A biblical figure from Revelation often used by Reformers to symbolize the corrupted institutional church</note> / shall go with her into the pit / that burns with fire and sulfur. For the Whore will not convert / for she shall drink down the measure / that she has poured out. Therefore let everyone open their own eyes / for great is **GOD** / who will judge them. She will persist in her sins / and finally despair. She cries "Murder!" <note>original: "Mordio", a traditional cry for help</note>, yet it is nothing / but her own evil plaging her / as the hypocrisy of her holiness / her pride and greed: She has wolves / that bite her; But they are wolves / and do not go among the sheep. Therefore it is necessary to wake up / not in much searching / but to seek oneself. For much searching / without the turning away of evil / is a mockery upon this path. And if you read this a thousand times / and yet remain only in the unturned state of your will / then you understand as much of it / as the donkey understands the Psalter <note>A common German proverb meaning to have zero comprehension of a holy or complex text</note>.

So it also goes with the Order of the Belly, the Anti-Christ. Do you think / it is an easy thing / to set a donkey upon a Royal throne? How then will the Belly-donkey stand before **GOD** / who seats himself with a donkey's heart in Christ’s throne / which is the place of the Holy Spirit / only for the sake of money and honor / and is only a Historical-shouter <note>original: "Historisch-Schreyer"; one who preaches the Bible as mere history or dead facts without spiritual life</note> / without any knowledge / and might well be full of vice? Or do you think / you are skilled enough to sit in Christ's throne / when you know arts and foreign languages? Yes, "Smell-Fritz" <note>original: "riech Friz"; a derogatory colloquialism for a pedantic or pretentious person</note>, look at **GOD'S** choice / look at Abraham and the Patriarchs / as well as Moses the shepherd / also the prophets and apostles / then you will soon see / whom **GOD** chooses / whether He chooses art or Spirit. Therefore let everyone take heed of the station / in which he sits: One who works there / he works **GOD'S** work...

# Chapter XLIII.
## Concerning the true and false worship; the right administration and use of the Holy Sacraments, as well as the false administration and abuse of the same.

->Connection.<-

In previous chapters, we have taught what the true and false church is, and what kind of teachers and teachings the true church of Christ has; likewise, what kind of apostles, servants, and ministry the false church has. Since the service of the so-called external churches of all sects consists in the administration of the Word—as their articles and dogmas—as well as in the administration of ceremonies and church customs, but especially of the Holy Sacraments; and since we have spoken of the former administration, namely of the external Word, it follows that we should now also examine the administration of church customs, and primarily the Holy Sacraments, or as our author calls them along with the Scripture, Testaments <note>original: "Testamente"; Böhme emphasizes the Sacraments as the "Last Will and Testament" or living covenant of Christ</note>.

### I. Question.
What is required for a right understanding of the teaching concerning the mysteries of the Sacraments?

->Answer.<-

<column-break/>

No disputing is required for this, but only an earnest, repentant person who has faith understands the Testamentary institution and partaking <term>Niessung|The spiritual "consumption" or internalizing of the Sacrament</term> in the power of Christ. But to the natural man, it is foolishness, and he cannot grasp it (1 Corinthians 2:14). A much different kind of earnestness belongs to true understanding,

which is not grasped by human reason, and is understood correctly by no person unless the Spirit of Christ opens it within their heart. A firm seal lies upon it, which no reason nor human art <note>The term "art" (Kunst) here refers to intellectual cleverness or academic skill.</note> can unlock, except for the slain Lamb of the house of Israel, who has the Key of David, Revelation 3, verse 7. To reason without divine light, Christ's Testaments <note>original: "Christi Testamenta"; likely referring to the Sacraments or the New Covenant.</note> are a closed book, but to the true children of God and Christ, they are an open book. To unlock such a book requires no great art or scholarship, but only childlike simplicity and humility. The peasant is as close to this as the doctor; they must all enter into the simplicity of Christ in obedience, and come like the prodigal son and the tax collector in the temple. There is no other way to it. It requires no great speculating, nor does it matter with what elegant words or gestures one wishes to approach; we must come only as children who surrender themselves to the Father’s rod <note>A metaphor for accepting divine discipline or guidance.</note> and plead for grace. He who has learned much and knows how to conduct himself is no more pleasing to God than he who knows nothing, but turns to Him with his whole heart and soul in repentance for his sins, possessing a faith in grace and a right, earnest intention to become a new creature.

<margin>Preface to the Testaments 2. ss. 24. 25.</margin>
**2. Question:** If these mysteries are so easy for a simple, earnest mind to grasp, how is it that so much strife has arisen over this matter?

**Answer:** Christ's Testaments are nothing other than a covenant between God and man—a member-like union <note>A "member-like union" refers to the parts of a body working together as one organism in Christ.</note> of the children of men, where God has again bound Himself

<column-break/>

with humanity through the humanity of Christ after the Fall, to be their dear God. Everything that now babbles about delusions and opinions or wrangles over scholarship outside of such a member-like covenant of love, departs into selfhood <note>original: "Eigenheit"; a Böhmean term for the ego or self-will that separates itself from God.</note> outside of Christ. There is no true understanding in any such person, for no one knows Christ except the Father, and those to whom the Father wills to reveal Him, Matthew 11:27. If Christ is manifest with and in a person, that person has no bickering or strife with anyone over knowledge and scholarship. Instead, he is humble and considers himself unworthy of all such knowledge. He does not revile anyone for having different gifts, but loves himself in all others, leaves every man to his own, and gives to his neighbor only for the sake of love; he thinks only of how he may be a member of Christ and of his brothers and sisters. But when people run into so many opinions, and strive and wrangle within them, and revile, despise, and hand one another over to the Devil for the sake of the letter <note>Focusing on the literal text rather than the spiritual meaning.</note>, the simple Christian should know that in all such strife there is no true understanding. Rather, it is vain pride and an Antichristian essence <term>Antichristian essence|Anti-Christisches Wesen: A state of being that opposes the spirit of Christ through sectarianism and intellectual pride</term>—a wretched confusion of the words of Christ, from which nothing arises but disunity, calamity, and enmity. Here, nothing is accomplished but the will of the Devil.

And that is why they set themselves up as teachers of the Kingdom of Christ, yet are neither sent nor recognized by God. They take their entire matter from others and merely trade words and letters. They wrangle over the "art"—how one can artistically assemble letters—and create opinions on which composition is the most artistic, forcing consciences into this art; yet they themselves do not understand what they do. Their knowledge sticks merely to the letter, and yet they do not have the living Word, Christ, within themselves, who gives witness to the literal word. If they had Him...

# Of True and False Worship

[If] they possessed Christ within themselves in love, they would share only that same love, and point people toward the Christ within them, walking in such a way that others could see they were *Christ's* children. But because they only quarrel, and do not wish to live and love in this way themselves, their worship is false—nothing but a glistening outward appearance. To see that this is true, one only needs to look at the delusions they fight over. One group claims: Christ is substantially present under the bread and wine. Also: Bread and wine are transformed into the *Testament* <note>original: "Testament"; here referring to the Sacrament of the Altar or the New Covenant.</note> of *Christ*, being a literal transformation of bread and wine; thus they want to take Christ into the mortal person, though He is of no use to such a person in holiness.

The second party says: It is only a sign and a symbol of the body of *Christ*, indicating that He was broken or died for us. They deny the present, substantial partaking <note>original: "wesentliche Niessung"; the actual spiritual or physical consumption of Christ's essence.</note> and understand nothing of the human being—what and how he is, or what he lacks and needs in order to regain **God’s** favor.

The third party thinks they have hit the mark best, and they stick to the words of the institution, but they say: Christ is partaken of with and under bread and wine; that is, *Christ's* flesh and blood are eaten and drunk under bread and wine. Yet, they have no understanding of how this happens, or what is within a human being that is capable of receiving such a gift. They wish to know nothing of the inner ground <note>A central concept in German mysticism referring to the deepest part of the soul where God dwells.</note> or the right *Adamic* humanity; furthermore, they deny the substantial indwelling of *Christ*. They are as far from understanding as the others. They want to know nothing of how the partaking occurs, but instead hang purely on the dead letter; they strike out and thunder all around them with scolding, reviling, accusations of heresy, and blasphemy. Each party fights only for a literal image, wanting to bind Christ to their own conceptual opinion, and wants to be the patron

<column-break/>

of that same image; this happens for no other reason than the desire for fame, honor, and high standing. This can be recognized by the fact that they all disgrace and revile one another, so that each might maintain his own conceptual opinion and be called and respected as a master over the mysteries of *Christ*. Yet, in the ground of their hearts, nothing sits there but the wandering *Lucifer* <note>original: "irrige Lucifer"; referring here to pride and the fallen intellect.</note> with worldly honors and self-will, wanting to be worshipped in place of Christ. Each party demands that people worship their "image"—their own manufactured, literal opinion. They distinguish their various "images" by their different interpretations of *Christ's* *Testaments*, creating a following for themselves and crying out: "Here is the Church of *Christ*! There is heresy and deception! Follow me, Christ is here!" In doing so, they embitter the hearts of princes and kings, as well as the minds of the common people, so that one brother despises, disgraces, reviles, and blasphemes another for the sake of a conceptual opinion, crying out and regarding him as devilish. Thus, war, bloodshed, and the devastation of land and people are brought about for the sake of such idols <note>original: "Götzen-Bilder"; literally "idols," but used here to describe the rigid mental constructs or doctrines people worship instead of God.</note>.

<margin>*Testam.* 2. c. 5. 2......11.</margin>

**3. Question:** Why does the author explain this teaching so extensively?

**Answer:** This foundation is laid out so deeply only so that those who quarrel over it may see the true inward ground, cease their strife, and surrender themselves to the simplicity and love of **JESUS** *Christ*. By this, Satan’s power would immediately be diminished, and the nations would see that Christians were truly **God’s** children if they walked in love. It is for the sake of this purpose that this little book has been written.

4. Question: Since, as previously stated, true Christianity consists neither in words nor in outward gestures, but solely in a person dying to their own selfhood <note>original: "Selbstheit"; referring to the ego or self-will that separates one from God.</note> and allowing the new life in Christ **JESUS** to be awakened within them through Christ's Spirit and the living, inward, powerful, and active Word;
->Dear friend, why then are such ceremonies and Sacraments necessary for this?<-

Answer: (We here present to the kind reader the enlightened author's meaning and opinion regarding the Sacraments in faithfulness and simplicity, without involving ourselves in any way in dispute or accountability; let everyone see to it how and what they judge.) The author holds that the Holy Sacraments are necessary because faith—as a spark of fire and a flash from the ignition of the new life—must necessarily have a tinder and an essence <note>original: "Wesen"; here meaning a substantial or material basis.</note> in which it can catch, and maintain its holy fire of the desire for faith and love. When one wishes to light a fire, one must have a substance for it that is capable of fire. It must be a substance in which there is oil and sulfur, or it will not burn; for even if one throws a stone into the fire, it does not burn so as to become a shining light. The same is to be understood regarding the poor soul: when she broke her desire away from **God’s** essence of love and gentleness—which essence was in her at the beginning, like a spiritual oil and water, while she herself was like a spiritual sulfur in which the light of **God** burned—she led herself into her own desire. Through this, she became enclosed like a hard stone and lost all her love and gentleness, becoming like a burning sulfurous spirit that could not be helped unless the oil of Divine Gentleness and Love were infused into her again. For such an infusion into human nature, there had to be a subject <note>original: "Subjectum"; a medium or vessel.</note> as a means or a "counter-likeness" through which it might happen, into which a person's faith could enter and receive power through a medium. In the Old Testament, such a medium is circumcision, along with the sacrifices; and in the New Testament, it is Holy Baptism and the Lord's

<column-break/>

Supper of Christ, along with the heard Word. Through these, Divine Love and Gentleness—as the true anointing oil of Divine Power—is infused into faith once again. Thus, the soul’s closed mouth is enclosed in **GOD'S** covenant and opened again through sweet grace, so that she may once more eat of the heavenly Manna.
->Explanation of the Testaments, Book 2, Paragraphs 1–3.<-

5. Question: What then are the Testaments of Christ actually called?

Answer: **CHRIST'S** Testaments <note>The author uses "Testaments" to refer to the Sacraments, viewing them as the legal and spiritual legacy left by Christ to His followers.</note> are a seal of the firm, eternal covenant of **GOD**, by which **GOD** has accepted humanity back into grace after the terrible Fall, and has sealed them with the outflow of His love through His blood and death. This is so that we might believe His word and promise—which He revealed to us in Holy Scripture concerning His Son and the redemption from sin, and which was previously announced by the prophets. This **WORD** came into our humanity in the outflow of His love, taking on a human soul as well as flesh and blood, and confirmed such a covenant with His blood and death. And He now gives such a Testament to His believers as their bounty <note>original: "Ausbeute"; the spiritual profit or inheritance.</note>, making them branches on the grapevine of His flesh and blood, so that they are incorporated into Him and made into His true children. In these children, He Himself wishes to dwell with His flesh and blood through such a Testamentary bounty. Thus, through this, with joyful confidence and in true childlike humility, they may ask the Father in the name of His Son **JESUS** Christ, and He will give them such grace. John 16:23.
->Preface to the Testaments, Sections 5 & 6.<-

### Of the True and False Worship of God.

6. Question: What does it mean that **GOD** offers such spiritual and heavenly treasures through visible, bodily, and tangible means?

Answer: We have recently noted how faith must have a substance <note>original: "Wesen"; meaning a substantial or essential reality.</note> in which the fire may take hold and into which the imagination may enter. For the first people before the time of Christ—before Christ revealed himself in the incarnate Covenant of Grace and became man—were enclosed in the living Word of **GOD**, as if in grace, through such faith. Then the human introduced will, which clung to error, was purified in the holy fire through the sacrifices; and they were ransomed from their sins toward the future fulfillment, until Christ fulfilled this prototype and rose from the dead. Thus, he also arose and became manifest with his life and essence within them—in the inward ground of their heavenly part, which had withered in Adam. They have "put on" Christ in soul and spirit. Therefore, only their body—formed from the <term>slime</term> <note>original: "Limo"; referring to the biblical dust or "mud" of the earth from which Adam was created.</note> of the earth as the third <term>principle</term> <note>original: "Principium"; in the author's system, this refers to the physical, visible world.</note> of the visible world's property—awaits the formed, spoken, substantial Word of the resurrection on the Last Day. This is also how it is to be understood regarding Christians.

<margin>Treatise on the Testaments, part 1, 2, § 19.</margin>

7. Question: Why did Christ ordain two Testaments <note>The author uses "Testaments" to refer to the two Sacraments of Baptism and the Lord's Supper.</note>, since faith could have grasped enough in one?

Answer: Just as the soul exists in two things, fire and water, from which a twofold life arises: a fire-soul-life, which <term>predominates</term> <note>original: "prædominiret".</note> in men, and a water-spirit-life, which has the upper hand in women. Both of these soul-lives were corrupted in Adam: the fire-life was seized by **GOD’S** wrath, and the spirit- or water-life was captured by the <term>spirit of the greater world</term> <note>original: "Geist Majoris Mundi"; the macrocosm or the astral influences of the physical universe.</note>. Both were imprisoned by the devil, had the <term>Word of the Lord</term> <note>original: "Verbum Domini".</note> not stepped in between. Therefore, **GOD** established two Testaments through Christ: one for little children in the Holy Spirit, who performs the office—holding the high office in Baptism—and creates in the soul water,

<column-break/>

a water of life in His power. And then one for the old, poor sinners who understand, in the Word of Life—as in flesh and blood. There the Word, as the Heart of **GOD**, holds the high office and feeds us with His body and gives us His blood to drink. The Testament of food and blood belongs to the <term>tincture</term> <note>original: "Tinctur"; an alchemical term for the spiritual "dye" or essence that transforms and ennobles a substance.</note> of the fire-life (the soul), and the Testament of water belongs to the spirit-life, or the other <term>tincture</term>. And yet there is but one human being; however, before Christ’s birth, the devil played great mischief with humanity by possessing them spiritually. But here his trade was put to an end, for Christ prepares for the children a bath of rebirth in the Holy Spirit. For a child does not yet have faith, and many a person learns little of faith; thus, one Testament might sustain the poor, uncomprehending person. It is not the Holy Spirit alone who baptizes; He holds the high office and takes the power from the <term>Trinity</term> <note>original: "Drey-Zahl", literally "Three-Number".</note> with which He baptizes. When the baptizer says: "I baptize you in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit," the Holy Spirit takes hold in the Trinity and baptizes in the soul’s water—the water of life which is in the blood of the tincture, which sustains the spirit-life as the second <term>center of nature</term> <note>original: "Centrum Naturæ".</note>. The soul-spirit receives the power and office of the Holy Spirit, and herein lies the <term>Great Mystery</term> <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum".</note>.

<margin>The Threefold Life, 13. 24. 26.</margin>

### 9. Question: Why was circumcision and the entire Mosaic worship maintained during the baptism of John, but everything was abolished during the baptism of Christ?

Answer: John baptized with water for repentance, and in his time the blood of the New Covenant was not yet shed, and the great sacrifice of atonement was not yet accomplished; therefore, the law of circumcision and the service of sacrifice in blood and fire—according to the property of the Father—could not be abolished. To be sure, the **Love-fire** in the Word of promise stood opposed to the **Wrath-fire** in the sacrifice and circumcision; however, the **Wrath-fire** was more powerful, so that it consumed the sacrifices. But when the blood of the Covenant was shed, the consuming fire of GOD'S wrath was appeased, and the **Love-fire** was kindled in the life of JESUS Christ; and the fire now burned in the holy and incombustible oil in the blood of Christ, and awakened also our faded heavenly essence. Our faded essence, locked in death, was like the withered **rod of Aaron** <note>A biblical reference to Numbers 17, where Aaron’s dry wooden staff miraculously sprouted leaves and fruit as a sign of God's choice.</note> / signifying / which essence in such awakening and introduction of the heavenly / living Love-essence flourished / when GOD'S essence became man / in whom the holy fire could burn: For the Divine <term>Ens</term> <note>original: "Ens"; a philosophical term for the fundamental substance or "being" of a thing.</note> and the <term>Ens</term> that faded in Adam / which was also heavenly / and which flourished again with such kindling / was a food for this **Love-fire** / like a spiritual

<column-break/>

holy oil / in which the **Love-fire** could kindle itself and burn. And that same burning of Love was the new life of **Rebirth**. But because such a supernatural kindling was not to happen in other people through a special movement of GOD—meaning that all other people were to be kindled by this holy fire from Christ—the Covenant entered through the water-baptism with the outflowing grace first into the heavenly <term>Ens</term> of man / as into the faded essence / wherein the embodied **Paradise-Covenant** with the **Crusher of the Serpent** <note>original: "Schlangen-Treter"; a traditional name for Christ, referencing the prophecy in Genesis 3:15 that the offspring of the woman would crush the head of the serpent.</note> remained / and it pressed into that same Covenant. But because the human <term>essence</term> / which had become earthly / was to go along in such a penetration / there also had to be such a medium for it / into which the human essence could take hold : For into GOD’S holiness it could not take hold / because the will was separated from it; So it had to be merely a likeness / in which the <term>Imagination</term> <note>original: "Imagination"; here meaning the creative, formative power of the soul's desire or will.</note> of human nature took hold. For Christ also had taken this likeness / as the <term>Elements</term> <note>original: "Elementa"; the basic physical components of the world.</note> / from us humans / so that the Divine <term>Imagination</term> might take hold in the water: So that thus the Divine and human <term>Imagination</term> together might awaken and kindle the embodied **Paradise-Covenant** / in the manner / that a glimmering fire comes into wood and glimmers. So in such a way / through baptism / a holy and Divine glimmering fire was introduced / which canceled and broke sin and death in man’s inwardness / as in the faded heavenly <term>Ens</term> / from which the dry / withered tree of the inward ground received a life again / as a spiritual oil: In which new spiritual oil / by the power of Divine light / the **Love-fire** / as the new life / should burn. This is now the water-baptism / where the Holy Spirit in the inward ground is the hand for it / who with the outflow of Divine love from Christ’s suffering / death and resurrection with His victory...

# Of True and False Worship.

...connection <note>Completing the word "Verbindung" from the previous page.</note> baptizes; that is: He immerses Christ’s humanity, suffering, death, and resurrection into the inward ground, and ignites the incorporated **Paradise-Covenant** with this fire, so that the dry **rod of Aaron** <note>A biblical reference to Numbers 17:8, where Aaron's staff miraculously sprouted, symbolizing life coming from death.</note> becomes green. 10. **Question:** Is it then certain that water-baptism was instituted in place of circumcision?

**Answer:** Christian baptism and Jewish circumcision hold exactly the same right. Among the Jews, circumcision occurred in the **Word of Power**; the Holy Spirit baptized them with the baptism of Holy Fire—meaning their true humanity which had been corrupted in Adam (and which was transformed in this baptism) was treated as the essence of faith. For the **essence of faith** was the baptism of the Jews, wherein the Holy Spirit baptized into Christ's humanity. But because that same Word of faith (as that same essence of faith) has now taken on humanity and made it alive within itself, the same Spirit now baptizes with water. This signifies the humanity of Christ; for the water of eternal life—the substance of the heavenly world—had faded in Adam. In Christ’s introduced heavenly essence, as well as in the water of heavenly powers, it became living again in our humanity (which He assumed). Therefore, the humanity of Christ was the **first-**

<column-break/>

**born from the dead.** And with that same heavenly water (which God’s Word and Power introduced from heaven into Christ’s humanity—understand this as being from the **holy spiritual world**, or the **Second Principle** <term>Second Principle</term> <note>The author divides reality into three "Principles": 1. The dark fire-world (wrath), 2. The light world (love/heaven), and 3. This visible world.</note>), the Holy Spirit in Christ baptizes Christians in their water-baptism. This outward act is only a sign of the inward seal, in which seal the Holy Spirit baptizes. And therefore, Christ ordered the seal of circumcision into a water-baptism, because the **Fire-Baptism** (of the Covenant) has been revealed in humanity, in the Water of Life—meaning that same Fire-Baptism, as the fiery Word of Love, has become flesh. Therefore, Christ says in John 3: *We must now be born anew through water and spirit, otherwise we cannot see God.* For in the water—wherein the fiery Word of Love in the essence of the Covenant has revealed itself in our heavenly, faded water (which has become flesh)—all children of Christ must be born anew. They must grasp that same water in their desire for faith, in which water the eternal fiery Word of God’s Covenant has incorporated itself. That same water baptizes the inner man (who faded in Adam) toward a new Rebirth, and the earthly, animalistic, half-serpentine and devilish man <note>A reference to the corrupt nature inherited after the Fall, often described by the author as "serpentine."</note> toward death and dying. It circumcises the imprisoned soul and puts upon it the Covenant and the humanity of Christ in the inner, spiritual man that had faded away from the Kingdom of Heaven.

Understand it then, you Jews and Christians: you have one and the same baptism. The Jew is circumcised in the essence of the Covenant inwardly in the soul and in the faded essence of the true heavenly humanity; just as the "serpentine essence" is cut off from the heavenly essence by the power of the Word, and the fiery Spirit of Love in the essence of the Word transforms the true humanity and baptizes it in the essence of the established faith.

### 11. Question: What does the baptism of JESUS Christ actually mean?

**Answer:** Baptism is nothing other than a marriage or covenant with **GOD**, based upon **Christ’s** blood and death, where **Christ** binds himself to man with his victory and resurrection, and places man into it. In baptism, man surrenders his Adamish, turned-away will to the death of **Christ**, and desires to die to his own self-will in the death of **Christ**, and through **Christ’s** resurrection, to rise out of **Christ’s** death with and in **Christ** as a new will, and to live and will with **Christ**. For through baptism, we are planted anew into the Word of **GOD** by **Christ’s** victory. For man is the spoken, formed Word of **GOD**, which in Adam introduced its will from **GOD’s** speaking into a self-willing and self-speaking, and became unfaithful to the Word of **GOD**; and with baptism, the formed word betroths and incorporates itself again with the eternal speaking of **GOD**, so that it wants to will and speak with **GOD**, as **GOD’s** righteousness and truth.

Baptism is an oath that man swears in **GOD**, wherein he renounces the devil and his kingdom, and surrenders himself to **GOD** as his own property, as a temple of **GOD**.

->**1st Testament 4. 23. 25.**<-

Thus, baptism does not consist in a mere outward sprinkling or immersion with water, but in a living, inwardly-working power

**12. Ques. Who baptizes, and who is baptized here internally?**

Ans. The internal Baptizer is the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, **GOD** revealed in the flesh; the one who is baptized is the threefold human, who had fallen according to all three principles; thus the whole human required baptism / all three principles, as the properties of all three worlds / had to be baptized in the human. The first principle is the eternal nature / the <term>Mysterium Magnum</term> <note>Latin: "Great Mystery"; in this context, the vast, hidden potentiality or the eternal source from which all nature arises.</note>, from which the visible world sprouted / a ground of the true eternal soul / which came into the body through **GOD’S** breathing-in. The second principle is the true eternal spirit / as the Holy Light-Power / (which power I call in this booklet the heavenly <term>Ens</term> <note>Latin: "being" or "essence"; refers to the spiritual substance of the soul that was lost in the Fall.</note>, or essence, that faded in Adam /) which faded in Adam with the Fall / when the soulish will went out from it into wandering / and broke its will away from it. The third principle is the human being from the essence of the visible world / as the <term>astral soul</term> <note>The "star-soul" or the psychological/emotional nature influenced by the physical cosmos.</note> with its body from the <term>limus</term> <note>Latin: "limo"; the "slime" or "dust" of the earth mentioned in Genesis.</note> of the earth / which stands in the four elements. This threefold human was entirely fallen; for as soon as the light in the spirit of the second principle was extinguished / he was completely blind to **GOD** / and dead to Paradise. Into this, a Divine Love-<term>Ens</term> had to be dipped or imprinted again / in which the Divine fire and light might ignite for a new life. And therefore the Holy Fire of the great love of **GOD** revealed itself in the covenant in the humanity of **Christ** / so that **God’s** Spirit might baptize us out of / with / and through this threefold humanity: That each principle in us would be baptized with its likeness / for the Holy Spirit baptized through **Christ** for the forgiveness of sins.

### How does the baptism by the Holy Spirit occur?

To which ground **Christ** afterwards gives his holy spiritual flesh and food / in which the true image of **GOD** stands. Divine love and sweetness in the Holy Fire baptize this spirit / for it is an <term>Ens</term> of the Holy Fire / in which it burns or lives; And the first principle, as the fiery soul from Divine <term>Scientz</term> <note>original: "Scientz"; referring to a living, formative knowledge or the "science" of the eternal Word's articulation.</note>, of the distinct / eternally-speaking Word / from the Father’s fiery essence, is baptized with the fiery spirit of the Father’s property / as with the fire-burning love.

The Father’s property in the fire first attacks the soul with the law of nature / as with His strict justice of the eternal birth of the fire-ground / through this, the hard, impressed, dead soul becomes movable in that same dipping-in of the fire of Divine life / and its hard impression of the false magnetic desire is shattered and opened up / in the way that one strikes a fire / thus a new fire of **GOD** is ignited / which shattering is also the ground of repentance.

**14. Question.** Who may worthily administer the outer water-baptism?

**Answer.** No other person is worthy to baptize into this new Covenant of Grace than one who has also previously been anointed with this grace, like John, who was anointed in his mother’s womb. For flesh and blood without this anointing cannot baptize; for this power does not stand in human authority, but in Christ’s authority. A Christian, in whom the anointing of Christ resides, baptizes with the anointing of Christ; for the Holy Trinity baptizes with the Covenant of Grace of the anointing, with Christ’s incarnation, suffering, death, and overcoming. If a person wishes to baptize, he must not only baptize with the hand and water, but also with the faith of the anointing. An unbelieving baptizer does no more in this high work of baptism than the baptismal stone <note>The stone baptismal font.</note> does, which holds the water. For even if he pours the water and uses the words of Christ, he does not work with them, but is silent in the effect; rather, the Covenant of Christ works and baptizes, while he is only a means—like an unworthy vessel—that does not itself work within this Covenant, but only performs the outward task, in which task **GOD** works because of his Covenant. This is not to be understood as if the work were therefore entirely powerless in an unworthy hand; no, the Covenant of **GOD** does not separate itself for the sake of the unworthy hand, which is only a means.

And if a person is now converted and turns to it as a human being and not a beast, then the Holy Spirit baptizes the inner ground as His temple, which He Himself possesses as the true eternal Spirit, together with the eternal soul. And the anointing of Christ, from His humanity accepted for us, anoints and baptizes in us the true man first created in Adam from the clay <note>original: "Limo"; referring to the Latin *limus*, the slime or dust of the earth from which Adam was formed in Genesis.</note> of the earth, together with the mortal soul (provided that one understands the inner ground here), which shall arise and live eternally. This happens through Christ’s suffering, death, and resurrection, in His bloody struggle; for the victory of His death is the hand which baptizes.

<margin>1. Testament 3. 22-26.</margin>
**Note.** The right man is baptized unto life, and the snake-like, gross-earthly man <note>Böhme uses terms like "snake-monster" to describe the corrupted, selfish nature humans inherited after the Fall in Eden.</note> is baptized with Christ’s death and dying, so that he should die, and leave all his evil lusts and desires to the death of Christ, so that He may kill them and bring forth a new will out of Christ’s death, from soul and body. The evil Adam, as the snake-monster, is taken with this baptism (when the hand of God, as His speaking Word itself, takes hold and baptizes) and is buried with Christ into His death and displaced into hell, into which Christ entered in His dying, cast into the darkness of God’s wrath as into the abyss of humanity. And this anointing in baptism binds itself with the true first Adamical body, which was before the Fall of Adam, and through Christ’s victory gives birth to a new will in soul and body, which obeys God.

<column-break/>

14. **Question:** Who may worthily administer the outward water-baptism?

**Answer:** No other person is worthy to baptize with this new Covenant of Grace than he who has previously been anointed with this grace, like John, who was anointed in his mother's womb. For flesh and blood without this anointing cannot baptize; for this power does not stand in human authority, but in Christ's authority. A Christian in whom the anointing of Christ dwells is the one who baptizes with the anointing of Christ; for the Holy Trinity baptizes with the Covenant of Grace of the anointing through Christ’s incarnation, suffering, death, and victory. If a person wishes to baptize, he must not only baptize with the hand and water, but also with the faith of the anointing. An unbelieving baptizer does nothing more in this high work of baptism than the baptismal stone <note>The baptismal font.</note> does, which holds the water. For even though he pours the water and uses the words of Christ, he does not work with them, but is mute in the spiritual effect; rather, the Covenant of Christ works and baptizes, while he is only a means, like an inactive being that does not itself work in this Covenant, but only performs the outward deed—in which deed God works because of His Covenant. This is not to be understood as if the work were entirely powerless because of an unworthy hand; no, the Covenant of God does not separate itself for the sake of the unworthy hand, which is only a tool.

<margin>1. Testament 4. 10-13.</margin>
The living Word in the Covenant, which baptizes there, does not originate from the power of the godless mouth, but from the decree in the Covenant. The godless mouth carries the outward literal word as a servant of the same, but the Covenant carries the living Word in power. However, if the baptism is to be powerful in all circumstances, the baptizer should be an anointed Christian and step toward such a work through the gates of Christ, or he is only a piece of wood or a block, acting as an instru- <note>The text cuts off here, likely intending "instrument."</note>

### 16. Question: May young, infant children also be baptized?

Answer: Christ says: "Let the little children come to me, for of such is the kingdom of God." Do not say: "What good is baptism for a child? It does not understand it." It does not depend on our understanding; we are all together without understanding regarding the Kingdom of God. If the child is your little branch, grown on your tree, and you stand in the Covenant, why do you not also bring your little branch into the Covenant? Your faith is its faith, and your confidence in the Covenant with God is its confidence; they are indeed your essences, and born of your

<column-break/>

soul. And you should know for a certainty: if you are a true Christian in the Covenant of Jesus Christ, your child also enters the Covenant of Christ at the ignition of its life <note>original: "Lebens Anzündung"; Böhme’s term for the moment life is sparked or conceived.</note>. Even if it should die in the mother's womb, it is found within the Covenant of Christ. For the Godhead stands in the Center of the Light of Life <note>original: "Centro des Lebens-Lichts"; a central concept in Böhme's mysticism where the divine presence illuminates the core of existence.</note>. So, if the tree stands in the Covenant, its little branches rightfully do as well.

<margin>Principles 23. 39.</margin>

For believing parents, who stand in the anointing <term>Salbung (Anointing): The spiritual "oil" or grace of the Holy Spirit that permeates the believer's soul.</term> of this Covenant and have "put on" the Covenant, also have the anointing in their seed and beget children out of their own bodily and soulful quality. If they are enriched in soul and body and have put on the anointing of Christ, why then should the heir of the body not also have it? If they are temples of the Holy Spirit who dwells in them, and eat Christ’s flesh and drink his blood, so that Christ is in them and they are in Christ—

<margin>John 6:56.</margin>

Christ indeed says (Matthew 7:18): "A [good] tree cannot bring forth bad fruit; an evil tree cannot bring forth good fruit." If the eye of the spirit is light, the whole body is light. If the first portion is holy, then the whole batch is holy <note>original: "Ist der Anbruch heilig / so ist der ganze Teig heilig"; referencing Romans 11:16. "Anbruch" refers to the firstfruits/root, and "Teig" (dough/batch) refers to the whole community or offspring.</note>. (Matthew; Romans 11).

John [the Baptist] was baptized in the mother’s womb by the Spirit of Christ through Mary’s voice, as was his mother Elizabeth. There we see exactly how it happened; for when Elizabeth heard the spirit of Mary, the Holy Spirit moved within her and in her fruit <note>The unborn child.</note> at the same time. They received the baptism of Christ from his humanity together, the mother with the son. Why then not also now in holy parents, in whom the anointing is present? For to whom the tree belongs, to him also belongs its fruit.

<margin>1st Testament 4. 13. 14.</margin>

17. Question: Why then is it necessary that the children of godly parents be baptized, who already belong to the <term>Covenant</term> <note>The "Covenant" (German: *Bund*) refers to the theological agreement between God and humanity, specifically the "Covenant of Grace" established through Christ.</note> of God and His congregation?

Answer: Even though a child is born of holy parents and already stands in such a Covenant while in the mother's womb, it should nevertheless put on such a Covenant in its own independent person and by its own will for living. The reason for this is that sin and impurity are inherited within the flesh; therefore, the child itself must put on the Covenant. For it must now, by itself, with the Covenant of Grace, crush the head of the serpent <note>A reference to Genesis 3:15, interpreted here as the spiritual victory over the "poison" of original sin inherited through the flesh.</note> in the flesh. For this reason, it must also personally put on Christ and His victory. For Christ now offers Himself to the child; it is to receive Him in its own power with its own will and, in return, give its own will to Him.
<margin>Testament 4. 22.</margin>

18. Question: But can a small child not understand what is being done there?

Answer: Even if a child does not understand it, the baptizer, as well as the parents and godparents, should understand it and introduce their faith into the child's will. Thus, with their introduced will joined to the child's will, they sink themselves with such an oath into God's Covenant through the words of Christ, at His command, into the water-baptism. They grasp the command of Christ within themselves as their faith, and so, with the child's lack of understanding joined to their own understanding, they enter into the Covenant. In the place of and with the child's will, they vow such a thing to God within their own will. Parents can and should primarily do this because the child has sprouted from their life and essence, like a branch from the trunk; thus, they also have the power to enclose the child's will within their own will of faith, and with the child's will, surrender and bind themselves to God. It does not stand in the choice of Christians to do this or leave it; rather, if they wish to be Christians, they

<column-break/>

shall do that, or else they despise His <term>Testament</term> <note>In this context, "Testament" refers to the legacy or sacred ordinance left by Christ, specifically the sacraments.</note> and do not wish to come to Him.
<margin>1. Testament 4. 26.</margin>

19. Question: But if a child dies before baptism, may it nonetheless be saved?

Answer: It is not to be understood that if a child of godly and anointed parents, having received life, should die before baptism, it would not be within the <term>anointing of Christ</term> <note>The "anointing" (German: *Salbung*) refers to the spiritual grace or "Christ-essence" passed down through the spiritual lineage of faithful parents.</note>. It has indeed put on the parents' anointing, for it has arisen from their essence—from their baptized soul-and-body essence. If it lives, it needs only to enter into the image of the visible Covenant as an independent life, and with its own will, surrender itself into that which it has inherited from its parents.
<margin>1. Testament 4. 16.</margin>

20. Question: May the children of the ungodly also be baptized?

Answer: It cannot be otherwise: where there are godless parents without faith, they also beget godless children. For as the trunk is, so is the fruit. If they do not turn around and incorporate their fruit into Christ through true, earnest repentance, and send them to this Covenant with faith—and if they even request such godless godparents without faith for the task, and there is also a godless baptizer—who is supposed to baptize here? Shall God's love in the Covenant of Grace baptize? It may not happen. As *St. Paul* says of the Lord's Supper, that the godless receive it to judgment? <note>original: "daß es der Gottlose zum Gericht empfahe?" Referring to 1 Corinthians 11:29, warning that taking the sacrament unworthily brings judgment upon oneself.</note> If one only mocks the Covenant, how then shall God's honor appear among the mockers? There it is rightly said: *With the holy You are holy, and with the perverse You are perverse.* <note>original: "Bey den Heiligen bist du heilig / und bey den Verkehrten bist du verkehrt." A quote from Psalm 18:26.</note> If the seed is false, even if one sows it on a good field, an evil fruit still grows; for it draws from the good field only an <term>Ens</term> <note>A Latin term for "being" or "essence" used frequently by Böhme to describe the internal spiritual substance of a thing.</note> according to its own likeness. How then can things proceed there, where a child springs from entirely godless parents, and also only godless godparents...

### 21. Question: What can the child do about being born of unbelieving parents?

### 22. Question: What is the actual purpose of the so-called witnesses or godparents in this act?

**Answer:** Those present should turn to this Covenant with great humility and submission to GOD with earnest prayer, and well consider what they intend to do there: that they are stepping before the revealed face of GOD for the Covenant of the Holy Trinity, and are dealing with GOD and men, and they should clearly imagine the bitter suffering and death of **JESUS** Christ. Also, for the child being baptized, they are participating witnesses according to faith; they should not step before this Covenant like a harlot before a mirror, with a proud gait, as if it were only a worldly honor because they were needed for it. Such people, who have neither understanding nor faith for it and only approach with a proud heart, are of no use to this Covenant, but are a hindrance; they hinder others who gape at their pride and meanwhile forget the earnestness of the matter. Although baptism may be performed without such persons through the earnestness and prayer of the parents and the baptizer, the Christian Church has nonetheless ordered it so that living witnesses should be present to attend such an earnest occasion with their prayer. This was well-ordered, but it has fallen into such misuse that it would sometimes be better if such children of unbelief were not there, for the devil does not belong to this work. If, however, the devil has the rule in a person, of what use is such a person there? As mentioned above, the baptismal font <term>Tauff-Stein</term> <note>Literally "Baptism-Stone."</note> and the unbelieving witness are one and the same, except that the proud person is a hindrance to others.

<margin>1. Testament c. 4. 51-53.</margin>

# Part 4 / Chapter 13.

There are three witnesses to this <term>Covenant</term> <note>The "Covenant" (German: *Bund*) refers to the sacred agreement between God and the believer initiated at baptism.</note> of Baptism: one is named GOD the Father, the other GOD the Son, and the third GOD the Holy Spirit. These are the Master-Builders who perform the office, who carry out the baptizing. Thus, if you come parading in, you filthy harlot of vanity, and bring the poor soul to the Covenant of Christ, standing there only for show, understanding nothing of Baptism and failing to offer even one "Our Father" to GOD—what do you think of how you stand before this Covenant, before the Holy Trinity? Like a sow before a mirror. Or should I remain silent? I must speak it, for I see it; do what you will, it is true. You carry away a newly-washed soul from the baptismal font, but you yourself are a besmirched sow, dwelling in the kingdom of all devils. The <term>Bath of Rebirth</term> <note>The "Bath of Rebirth" refers to the ritual of baptism as a spiritual cleansing.</note> does not take hold in you, for you are like a beast and far from the Kingdom of GOD; yet it remains firm in the Covenant of Christ.

<margin>Principles 23. §. 41 = 44.</margin>
But I say this according to my understanding, and not by command: if the parents are ungodly—even dwelling in the kingdom of the devil—and have conceived their fruit out of their false essences, having no faith but only a false, hypocritical appearance, seeking to be regarded as Christians only for the sake of mockery; and just as the devil often disguises himself as an angel of light, they also send their children before the Covenant of Christ with such adorned, false "angels" <note>This likely refers to godparents or sponsors who are outwardly fine but inwardly lacks faith.</note>—this is quite dangerous, as is soon revealed in the growth of the tree. The Covenant certainly remains, but there must be an earnest desire to flee from the devil. It may well be that some are baptized in the wrath of GOD because the Covenant is merely despised, and sometimes there are godless, drunken priests involved who stand in hellish fire up to their heads. Therefore, the Covenant of Grace stands as a witness over the heap of the ungodly; and that which they see and know, yet do not perform in earnest, shall judge them.

<column-break/>

23. Question: Be that as it may, this is a very hard word to hear, especially since living examples teach us how often the most ungodly parents have godly children, and often godly parents have ungodly children. It is therefore further asked: when a person who was baptized in their youth and entered into a Covenant with GOD through baptism later enters into the wickedness of this world in their adult years, defiling themselves with all manner of sin and vice, and thus profanes their baptismal Covenant—can such a person return to grace?

Answer: If such a soul enters into the wickedness of this world and allows the devil to pull them along, they depart from the Covenant and abandon GOD and the Kingdom of Heaven. Yet there stands the noble <term>Virgin of GOD</term> <note>The "Virgin of GOD" or "Sophia" is a central concept in Böhme’s theology, representing Divine Wisdom and the spiritual companion of the soul that guides it back to the Light.</note> in the center of the Life-Light. At the very entrance of life, she moves into the center of the Life-Light to be a guide to the soul, a dear companion, and she warns the soul against the ungodly path, urging it to turn back and re-enter the Covenant. If not, and the soul remains in the devil’s kingdom, she remains standing in the center of the holy Paradise; she is a Virgin for herself, but the soul has grieved her. Thus they are separated, unless the soul returns in true regret and <term>Repentance</term> <note>The German *Buße* implies both the inward feeling of remorse and the outward change of life.</note>; then it is received by its Virgin with great honor and joy. For this reason, Christ established two <term>Testaments</term> <note>The "two Testaments" here refer to the two sacraments of the Lutheran tradition: Baptism (the water of life) and the Lord's Supper (His true body and blood).</note>: one in the water of eternal life, and the other in His true body and blood. So if the poor soul should ever be defiled by the devil, it can yet enter into Christ’s body again through the other. And if it turns back with regret over its committed sins and places its trust once more in the mercy of GOD, it re-enters the first Covenant; thus it may come to the second Testament and draw near to GOD. # On True and False Worship.

24. **Qu.** What then is to be thought of those who are not outwardly baptized, such as Jews, Turks <note>In the 17th century, "Turks" was a common collective term for Muslims.</note>, and Heathens? Can these also truly be saved without Baptism?

**Ans.** To say that those who do not have the outward Baptism—such as the Jews, Turks, and other nations who lack this knowledge and do not have the "Lampstand"—are all cast off by God, even though they otherwise press into the love of God through their teaching, life, and deeds, is a fantasy and spoken in the manner of <term>Babel</term> <note>The author uses "Babel" or "Babylonic" to refer to the confusion and corruption of institutionalized religious denominations.</note>, without true understanding. Salvation does not lie in the outward Word alone, but in the Power. Who would cast out one who enters into God? Is it not Babel that has confused the whole world? That the nations have divided themselves into opinions, yet in their will follow only one path—who is the cause of this, if not the <term>Anti-Christ</term>? For he pulled the Kingdom of GOD into his own power and made a trifle out of the <term>Rebirth</term>; when the day truly dawns, even the children will be ashamed of this. One can rightly say that the Anti-Christ's teaching is a "shadow-fight" and a serpent-like falsehood that always deceives Eve.

->40. Qu. 14. 11=13.<-

25. **Qu.** We have heard, firstly, what Baptism is in general; secondly, what a true baptizer must be like, and what parents and godparents do therein; and also who should and may be baptized. Now there remains the most eminent point, over which the greatest strife and quarreling is conducted in Babel: namely, whether the water in Baptism is a pure sign <note>The German *Kenn-Zeichen* refers to a symbolic marker or token.</note> and has no power in itself, or whether the blood and the Spirit of JESUS Christ are in, with, and under the water and active there, or whether the water is substantially transformed into the blood and the Spirit of JESUS Christ through the priest's blessing?

**Ans.** The outward elemental water is not the ground of Baptism, but rather the spiritual water, which is in covenant with the Word and bound with faith;

<column-break/>

for the Word pours itself out into the water-source of life, into humility and love, and faith <unclear>grasps</unclear> such a promised Word of grace in the <unclear>Covenant.</unclear> This grace in the spiritual water joins with the elemental water, in the same manner as the invisible Word made itself visible through the substance of this world, as if through the elements; and just as the invisible being of GOD works through the visible, and as the visible being of the elements shall again enter into the invisible. Thus, in the baptismal Covenant, the invisible element (as the heavenly substance) unites with the visible element of the human body (as the substance of time). The eternally-speaking Word of Divine Love unites with the spoken word of humanity; for the Element according to the holy spiritual world—from which the four elements sprang—is that which baptizes through the four elements of the human body. The true human being created in Adam, who is stuck in the coarse substance of the four elements, is baptized into eternal life; for the pure Element dips itself again into the faded image of Man (which image was also from the pure Element, but became mortal in Adam).

->1st Testament 4. 43=45.<-

In a word, the outer man is baptized with outer elemental water, but the inner man is baptized with the Spirit-Water in the holy pure Element; there, the pure oil of the Holy Spirit is poured into the nature-fire of the soul, so that the Light of GOD rises and the human being is renewed in the image of GOD.

# Chapter 14.
## Concerning the Holy Supper.
### Connection.

We have considered the first testament that Christ established in the New Covenant; it now follows to consider the second, namely, the Holy Supper. Through Baptism, the new life of **JESUS** Christ is awakened and ignited in the soul, but through the Holy Supper, it is sustained, as if by food and drink. Baptism awakens the spirit, and the Supper brings about the body of the new man. For when the soul thus enters into the Majestic Light, as previously mentioned, and receives the light of **GOD**, it becomes entirely longing and desiring, and in its desire, it always draws **GOD’S** power into itself—which is **GOD’S** Body—and the Holy Spirit is the Spirit of **GOD’S** power. Thus, the soul receives **GOD’S** Body and Spirit and eats at **GOD’S** table. For what the Father has belongs to His Son; and everything the Son has belongs to His image <note>Referring to the soul restored in the likeness of Christ.</note>. It eats **GOD’S** flesh, Christ’s body, and from such eating, **GOD’S** body also grows within it, so that it thus possesses **GOD’S** body and is **GOD’S** child—not merely a likeness, but a child, born from **GOD’S** <term>Essence</term> <note>original: "Essentz"; the underlying spiritual substance of a being.</note>, born of **GOD**, and living in **GOD**. When the soul hears of **GOD’S** Word, or rather, hears **GOD’S** Word teaching and speaking—just as in this world—it catches it and eats it. The outer man eats earthly bread, and the soul eats **GOD’S** bread, of which Christ said that He gives us His body as food. And His testaments are nothing else; we do not eat spirit without a body, for the soul is already spirit and desires to have a body; thus, it receives body and spirit at once.

2. **Question:** Since the soul of man must indeed have an external bodily nature from which it enjoys the heavenly nature, why did Christ institute the Supper with bread and wine, and not retain the use of the Passover Lamb?

**Answer:** With the institution of the New Testament, Christ did not wish to ordain anything foreign or new / but only to fulfill the Old Testament / and to enter into the covenant of the Old Testament Himself with the <term>substantial Grace</term> <note>original: "wesentlichen Gnade"; grace that is not just a concept, but has a real, spiritual "substance" or presence.</note> / which had become man in His soul and flesh / and to be the fulfillment Himself / as the Passover Lamb / and the holy bread and flesh / through which our true <term>Adamic</term> <note>Referring to the original nature of humanity as created in Adam before the Fall.</note> man would be blessed. For He first ate the Passover Lamb with His disciples / and incorporated Himself with them into the covenant of the Old Testament / and washed their feet. Afterward, He took the bread, gave thanks, and broke it, and gave it to them, and said: Take and eat, **THIS IS MY BODY**, which is given for you. Likewise, He also took the cup after the supper, and gave thanks, gave it to them and said: Drink all of it,

<column-break/>

**THIS IS MY BLOOD OF THE NEW TESTAMENT**, which is shed for many, for the forgiveness of sins. I say to you, I will not drink from this fruit of the vine from now on, until the day when I drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom. (Matthew 26. Mark 14. 1 Corinthians 11:23.)

This is now the true ground / and indicates / firstly / how the sweetest grace of the Covenant of **GOD** has entered into our humanity; secondly / how the same Covenant of Grace / which in the Old Testament entered into Israel as a blessing under the food of the sacrifices and the Passover Lamb / now gives itself to mankind with the assumed humanity / also under a medium / namely under bread and wine / to eat and to drink; and thirdly / how He did not want to abolish the first covenant / and start something new / but how He Himself is that same Covenant of Grace / and now presents Himself as a man / and now gives Himself to mankind in a Divine and human way / so that / just as they had previously enjoyed Him with His grace in the covenant through the sacrifices in a spiritual way in power through a medium / so they should also now enjoy Him in a bodily and spiritual way / through the medium of bread and wine / and essentially enjoy that same incorporated grace in the covenant. 3. **Question:** But since Christ has died and risen again, and no longer administers the Supper externally Himself, tell me: what must the person be like who wishes to worthily administer the Holy Supper in the name of **JESUS** Christ?

**Answer:** He must have actually "put on" <note>This refers to the Pauline concept of "putting on Christ" like a garment, meaning to embody His nature.</note> the **LORD JESUS** Christ and the power of His death and resurrection within himself. He must have surrendered his <term>old man</term> <note>original: "alten Menschen"; the sinful, fallen nature of humanity before spiritual rebirth.</note> along with its lusts and desires unto death, and lead the <term>new man</term> <note>original: "neuen Menschen"; the spiritually reborn self that lives in Christ.</note> out of death into life, so that he may be essentially fed with Christ’s body and blood. In such power of **JESUS** Christ, he must also possess a heartfelt love, sacrificing himself and all that he is and has for the service and salvation of his brothers, being ready even to lay down his life for them.

->Dear brothers, both teachers and listeners, you who lay hold of the covenant of Christ: see to what you do; there is a great earnestness in this, lest you become guilty of the death of Christ.<-

4. **Question:** But when a godless priest administers the office, and a believing communicant enjoys the mystery from the hand of that godless one, does the Supper nonetheless retain its power, or can such a man hinder that power?

**Answer:** A godless priest, in whom the Spirit of Christ does not dwell, cannot absolve or receive the communicant; rather, the <term>Office</term> <note>original: "Amt"; the divinely instituted role or authority of the ministry, which exists independently of the person holding it.</note> of Christ, through the words of His promise, receives him. A false priest is merely an external, ineffective tool in himself; he does nothing more than a godless priest does at a water-baptism, who only pours the water and speaks the words without the co-working of the Spirit. But the Spirit of the Office does not look upon the unworthy servant of that office, but upon those who come to the ministry with faith. He absolves them through His office and receives them into the community with the Bride of Christ <note>A traditional metaphor for the Church or the collective body of believers.</note> in which He works—and not precisely through a godless

<column-break/>

Pharisee, who is himself incapable of the office and only sits there like an idol to be worshiped, being himself only a devil full of falsehood, promising others what he himself does not possess. One must handle such an office of **GOD’s** power with earnestness, or Christ is merely mocked therein.

Therefore, no person should rely solely on the <term>ordinance</term> <note>original: "Ordnung"; the formal, established religious rite or ceremony.</note> and think that the ordinance itself absolves him, or that he receives Christ's Testament simply for the sake of the ritual and institution. If one wishes to receive Christ as a guest within oneself, then he must bring the Temple of Christ (wherein Christ absolves him) into the ordinance with him. The absolution is merely an acceptance into the fellowship of the members of Christ; the priest accepts him externally with the congregation, and Christ accepts him in faith and actually unites with him—which cannot happen without faith and an earnest turning toward **GOD**. And just as Christ now works inwardly in him, so also the congregation, as the Bride of Christ, works as a fellow member in him through their prayers; and in Christ, they are all but one.

<margin>2nd Testament [Chapter] 4. [Sections] 19. 22.</margin>
5. **Question:** What must the person be like who wishes to enjoy the Holy Supper worthily?

**Answer:** He must be a worthy table-companion, a true disciple of Christ in whom **JESUS** Christ is active toward the killing of the "old man" and his works, and toward the awakening of the new life; he must also be ready to go into death in and with Christ, and to give his life for his brothers. A Christian must be one spirit in us with Christ, and must will and work in Christ's power. It is a living, active, and real grace in a Christian—a constantly burning fire, a perceptible power. For if one is a Christian, he will hate the will of the flesh and be grieved by it; he will be an enemy to his own evil fleshly lusts, and will constantly accuse himself, and consider himself unwor-

# Part 4 / Chapter 14

<margin>2 Samuel 6:6–7; 1 Chronicles 14:9–10 <note>These verses refer to Uzzah touching the Ark of the Covenant improperly and being struck down; the author uses this to warn against approaching the sacrament unworthily.</note></margin>
...which a godless person should take good note of: that he must not touch this Testament without repentance for his sins; otherwise, he lays his hands with a false disposition upon **Christ’s** wounds, martyrdom, and death, and will finally receive Judas's reward for it.

It is not to be understood as if the godless person, who joins himself to this covenant of **Christ’s** Testament, receives nothing (just as is to be understood regarding Baptism). For the Testament stands firm and the institution remains in force, because unbelief does not abolish the covenant and its power. The covenant extends to everyone through such partaking and use; but as the "mouth" is <note>The "mouth" here refers to the spiritual capacity or faith of the recipient.</note>, so also is the partaking. **GOD’s** great love and grace—as the essential love—does not give itself into the godless soul. However, the <term>Process of Christ</term> <note>original: "Process Christi"; the sequence of Christ's life, suffering, death, and resurrection viewed as a spiritual path for the believer.</note> with His martyrdom, anguish, mockery, and death, does indeed enter the godless soul. For within that soul, the human devil—the godless heart—stabs **Christ** in His wounds and makes itself guilty of **Christ’s** death. The godless person indeed partakes of **Christ’s** descent into hell, His anguish, and His death; but he is not capable of His Resurrection, where **Christ** rules over death and hell. For his godless will does not desire to die to its false nature in **Christ’s** death; rather, it only desires to rise and live in **Christ’s** Spirit while remaining in sin. He wants to rule in **Christ’s** Resurrection with his earthly Lucifer <note>A reference to the sin of pride.</note>; therefore, he tramples the death of **Christ** with the feet of his false desires and does exactly what the Pharisees did to **Christ**. Therefore, it would be better for him if he did not boast of being a Christian and did not touch **Christ’s** Testament.

For **Christ** said: *He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood remains in me, and I in him* (John 6:56). **Thirteenth:** whether he finds in his mind that the stream of living water of Divine Love flows from him, so that he loves his **GOD**, and his brother and neighbor as himself? **Fourteenth:** whether he wishes his enemy well, and...

-> 2. Testament 4. 30. ::::: 38. <-

8. **Q.** We have considered who may worthily administer and enjoy the Supper; it follows now to investigate the ground of the Supper itself: How Christ instituted it, and what He intended to assure through it?

**Ans.** Because, as mentioned above, much strife and bickering has arisen in Christendom because one party wants to maintain this and the other something else from the words and letters of the institution, we will first search for the ground of the matter: namely, how Christ and His disciples, as well as the Apostles and the first Christians, held the memorial of the death of JESUS Christ? 

<column-break/>

When they (the first Christians) came together and proclaimed the LORD’s wonders and thus sat together with a fervent spirit: they distributed the LORD’s Last Supper according to the admonition, as He had commanded them; they took the bread and broke it and ate it, and thereby and herewith proclaimed the death of the LORD; likewise they took the cup and drank from it and proclaimed His blood-shedding, and each said to the other: "Take and eat the body of the LORD, which was given for us on the tree of the cross"; likewise they also did with the cup, took it in their hand and drank from it; for the leader of the congregation began this and spoke to the others: "Take the cup and drink the blood of Christ our LORD, which He shed for us on the tree of the cross for the forgiveness of sins, and proclaim His death and blood-shedding until He comes again for judgment and brings us to Himself." This, dear Christians, was the right Apostolic custom, and Christ's Last Supper was also thus; for when Christ had instructed and taught His disciples, He began—after the evening meal, when they had eaten the <term>Passover Lamb</term> <note>The Jewish Pesach meal, which the author views as a precursor or "shadow" of the Christian Eucharist.</note>—the true eating of the Passover Lamb, and gave them the Passover Lamb to eat, of which the first (instituted by Moses) was only a figure and shadow: for He gave them His heavenly body to eat and His heavenly blood to drink, which He had brought into Mary’s body into the eternal, unbeginning <term>Heavenly Virgin of God</term> <note>original: "himmlische Jungfrau GOTTES"; in this mystical tradition, this refers to Divine Wisdom or Sophia, the spiritual mirror of God through which the Incarnation was mediated.</note>, into the pure, chaste essence without blemish, and had taken on from His mother, the earthly Mary.

You must understand this profoundly: He did not give His disciples the earthly substance—that which merely clung to Christ’s body, in which He suffered death, and which was mocked, spat upon, scourged, and killed. With that, He would have given them mortal flesh. Rather, He gave them His holy body, His holy flesh, which hung on the wood of the Cross within that mortal substance. And He gave His holy blood, which was shed along with the mortal blood, as an immortal flesh and blood that the disciples received into their own bodies. This was put on by the soul as a new body from Christ’s body; thereby the disciples of Christ became capable and were members of His body. You should not understand this to mean that the disciples of Christ received a piece of Christ’s outer body—as if from His earthly body—and took it into their mouths, chewing and biting it with their outer earthly teeth and swallowing it into the belly. No, the text shows that He sat with them at the table and did not tear apart His outer body. Just as the Godhead <note>original: "GÖttheit"</note> in His will conceived the Image that GOD created in His Virgin <note>In Böhme’s theology, the "Virgin" refers to Divine Wisdom (Sophia), a spiritual mirror or presence through which God manifests.</note> of His wonders and wisdom, and led that flesh and blood with the eternal **Tincture** <term>Tincture: A spiritual life-force or transformative essence that permeates and animates matter.</term>, in which the soul lives as the eternal fire—which reaches into the Godhead according to the essence of Majesty, and is softened, filled, and strengthened by it—entering from Mary into the Virgin, into the **Holy Ternary** <term>Ternarium Sanctum: The spiritual or "angelic" materiality that constitutes the manifestation of the Trinity.</term>; into this the Word yielded itself as a life, into the Tincture of Eternity, and became the spirit, life, and power of that same flesh (which arose from the Tincture of that same soul-fire-source). For the Spirit was in the Word, and the Word was the power, and from the power shone the Light of Majesty. And the kingdom with the power of this world clung to Him as His own property, which had been born out of the Virgin of His wonders and wisdom from the eternal **Center of Nature** <term>Centro Naturæ: The foundational point or "heart" from which all natural and spiritual forces originate.</term>, and Mary also stood within it with the out-

<column-break/>

er power and life, with the outer flesh and blood; so, in such a manner, has Christ—GOD’s true Son and our brother—given His disciples His body and blood to eat and drink. Just as GOD, in His heavenly Virgin (from whom the heavenly essence is perceived and receives its being in the Fire-Tincture), is a Being; which Being GOD conceived with the Word and Heart, encompassing the Tincture from Mary’s blood in which the soul dwelt, with the **Word "Let it be"** <note>original: "Verbo Fiat"; the creative command used by God in Genesis.</note>, as if with the eternal, sharp **Matrix** <term>Matrix: A generative, mother-like vessel or medium of creation.</term>, and allowed them to become flesh and blood together, after the human manner. Understand: Just as the earthly substance, together with Wisdom as the eternal virginity, entered into the corrupted Tincture and **Matrix** of Mary—in which the promised Word resided, which entered into the corrupted Tincture along with the eternal essence, and thus became a new Man who was foreign and unknown to earthly nature—so also has this same new body of Christ (understand: the *inner* Christ, whom the outer man, who was mortal, covered) given itself under bread and wine as under an earthly substance, into the soul-tincture of the Apostles. He became man within the Apostles in their soul-tincture, and that is the new body which Christ brought to us from heaven. So, when we surrender ourselves entirely to His will in obedience, and go out of ourselves with our old will into His will, and come into the community of Christ, desiring His flesh and blood with all His benefits, He gives us this body and blood to eat and to drink. The inner man, born of GOD, receives this. For that same body of Christ is all-essential and omnipresent; it occupies the second **Principle** <term>Principium: One of the three foundational realms of reality described by Böhme (the dark fire-world, the light holy-world, and the outer world).</term>. For if you wished to say that Christ feeds the soul with spirit without a body, that is not true; the Holy Spirit does not make a **Principle**, but rather the eternal essence in which the Spirit dwells.
