->9. Question: How may a simple person distinguish the body of JESUS Christ?<-

**Answer.** This the author teaches very clearly in *The Second Testament*, Chapter 3. Christ did not give his disciples his formed, created, outward, comprehensible, fleshly humanity, as if he gave them a piece of it: No, that is not the case, for he sat with them at the table and did not tear apart the formed being of his body. Instead, he gave them his spiritual humanity, as the power of his body and blood, his own **mummy** <term>Mumia: In the alchemical tradition of Paracelsus followed by Böhme, this refers to the vital, spiritual life-force or "balsam" inherent in a living body.</term> <note>original: "Mumiam"</note>, in which the Divine and human power is understood. This **mummy** is a true human being of flesh and blood and is a spiritual flesh, out of which the visible image grows, and it is entirely one with the visible image. 

Consider a likeness in the sun: it remains in its place, yet it penetrates with its radiance, power, and entire being—with all that it is in **essence** <note>original: "Essentz"</note>, power, and being—out of itself into the whole world. It gives itself to all elements, beings, and creatures, to all herbs and trees, and also to all created life, and it works in everything that will but receive it. Yet the sun does not tear itself apart when it goes out of itself and gives itself into the creatures; it remains forever whole, and nothing of its being is diminished. 

The Supper of Christ is to be understood in this same way, just as we see in the likeness of a herb of the earth: the herb does nothing, nor can it do anything, without the power of the sun. It only opens its palate of **essence** <note>original: "Essentz"</note> toward the sun's power; that is, it only hungers for it. Into that same hunger the sun shines and ignites the **spirit** <note>original: "Spiritum"</note>, acting as the sul-

<column-break/>

-fur, salt, and oil of the herb. As soon as this happens—so that the sun's power finds itself or is felt in the sulfur, salt, and oil of the herb—it becomes [active] therein. From this, the herb receives a perceptible warmth, and it encloses and presses the sun's power into itself, so that the sun's power becomes substantial in the herb and grows with it. The sun **tinctures** <term>Tingiret (Tinctures): To permeate or transform the inner nature of a substance through a spiritual essence.</term> the herb and transforms it into corporeality, so that the herb becomes sun-like and works toward producing fruit.

In the same way, we are to understand Christ’s Testament, for he is the sun of life and the light of the world (John 8:12). According to his Godhead, he is the eternally-speaking Word, as the power of the Godhead and the power of the Divine light. According to his humanity, he is the formed, spoken word, which is entirely one with the eternally-speaking Word. Therefore, he has unified our assumed humanity in the eternal Word, turning the outward inward (as the essence of time) and the inward outward (as the essence of eternity). Through our human essence, which he assumed from us, he has become out-pressing with the Divine essence, just as the sun presses out from itself and gives itself; thus the Divine essence gives itself through the human.

<margin>NB. †</margin>
The Divine essence carries the human with it as it goes out, for the Divine desire goes out toward the human **essence** <note>original: "Essentz"</note>, and the human essence goes inward toward the Divine out-pressing delight.

<margin>NB. †</margin>
But when the Divine power meets the human, the human is carried out with it by Divine force, so that the human power also gives itself along with the Divine, through the Divine force. For the human power is the Divine's perceptibility, or "findability" <note>original: "Findlichkeit"; Böhme's term for the state where the infinite God becomes "findable" or manifest in a specific form</note>, in which the Divine finds itself in something, as in the formed being of the Word of power, wherein the Divine power loves itself, as in its...

# Of the Holy Supper.

...sensitive being / just as the soul loves itself in its own body.

*NB.* † And thus God has infused his love through a human being—in the humanity of Christ—into the disciples of Christ with a human being. This happened in the same way that the sun’s power in the *Spirit of the World* <note>original: "Spiritu Mundi"; the vital spirit or breath of the macrocosm</note>—as an outflow of the stars' powers—mingles with the spiritual **sulfur**, **salt**, and **oil** <term>Sulfur, Salt, and Oil: The "Tria Prima" or three primary principles in alchemical thought, representing the soul, body, and spirit of all matter.</term> in the upper elements. The sun's power captures those powers into its own radiance and gives itself into them, and they (those powers) give themselves into the sun’s power and work together. Through this, the "light of nature" is unlocked and, through such working, gives itself into the earth, herbs, trees, and all creatures, so that in a herb or tree, a power arises from which the growth or the breaking-forth of the creatures originates. In such growth or life, one always understands, first, an elemental, substantial power, and then, secondly, a supra-elemental, solar, and stellar power, where the solar and stellar powers break forth with their strong authority alongside the elemental power.

*NB.* † Now we see in the herbs and all living things growing from the earth that when they capture and eat such power from the sun and stars, they do not tear themselves apart or create or use a special physical mouth for it. Rather, the **essence** of their desire—(acting as the natural sulfur, salt, and oil within the herb)—is the "mouth" that captures the influence of the upper elements, the sun, and the stars. The same is to be understood regarding Christ’s disciples and all other people; they have eaten and drunk Christ’s flesh and blood under bread and wine, as through a medium, with the essential, desiring mouth of faith. This is not done with a circumscribed, creaturely concept <note>i.e., not a physical, limited understanding</note>, but with the desire of faith.

<column-break/>

*NB.* † However, let this be understood rightly. First, the outer mouth with its physical grasp takes hold of the outer elemental being: the bread and wine. The mortal, perishable being of man—the coarse flesh which cannot and shall not inherit the Kingdom of God (*John 6:63; 1 Corinthians 15:50*)—grasps and eats the bread and wine, for bread and wine are also an earthly, perishable being that enters the belly and is cast out again, like all natural food (*Matthew 15:17*). And secondly, the right, true human being, who was created in Adam—who, before the animal coarseness, was a true human and an image of the visible world according to its inward spiritual ground—that same person eats Christ’s spiritual, essential flesh with the essential desire.

*NB.* † Understand: this is the flesh that he took on in Mary as our human flesh, but not the outer ground of the physical four elements. Rather, it is the inner holy element, which is the "ground" from which the four elements proceed. Not fire, air, water, and earth, but the eternal, pure element, which is a substance of Paradise hidden within the four elements—understand it as the substance of Eternity from which Time has proceeded into a visible being.

This same flesh is a spiritual **mummy** <term>Mumia: The vital, spiritual essence or life-force of a body.</term> <note>original: "Mumiam"</note>, from which the human being (according to the visible body) took its origin in the *Word FIAT* <note>original: "Verbo FIAT"; the creative 'Let there be' of God</note>. This essence became blind to the Kingdom of Heaven in Adam when he entered into the four-fold elemental coarseness with his desire. This fleshy essence was filled with heavenly, living substance and made alive again in Christ’s incarnation. This is what the right Adamic human—who sticks hidden within the coarse shells of the four elements—eats (*NB.*). And in that same essence, the true human eats Christ’s suffering, dying, and death. Through his victory, Christ's death has become an eternal life, which life, having arisen from the death of Christ...

### Part 4, Chapter 14.

...originated / breaks our earthly evil will / and has become a death to our death / which the outer nature considers to be a life.

*NB. NB.* † And here the suffering and death of Christ is shown to man quite *essentially* <note>original: "essentialiter"; meaning substantially or in reality, rather than just symbolically</note>, effectively—not merely imputed or credited to us as something that happened once in the past—but as an effective reality. This "life-death" of Christ swallows up our death. Within this, the body rests when it dies here according to its four-elemental nature / and the four-elemental part turns to dust and ashes. That same power of true humanity rests in its *Principle* <term>Principle: In Böhme's thought, a "Principle" (Principium) is one of the three fundamental realms of existence: the dark fire-world, the light-world, and the outer material world.</term> until the return of the corporeal being. The soul, however / which is a spiritual fire / eats in its desire—as if with the true mouth of faith—the supernatural, substantial love of the name **JESUS**. This name has become a substantial power / acting as the supernatural Wisdom of God / wherein the entire Godhead is effectively understood to be present.

The "soul-mouth" eats this holy being / whereby the soul is transformed into a burning fire of love / for the love of Christ gives *Ens* <term>Ens: A philosophical term for the "being" or "essence" of a thing—the spiritual substance that gives it reality.</term> and being to the soul-fire. The fiery life of the soul takes the essence of this love into its own essence. Through such a burning of love, the temple of **SOPH-IAH** <note>original: "Soph-IAH"; referring to Sophia, the personification of Divine Wisdom</note> is unlocked once again / acting as the substantial, holy power-light / the true spirit that faded away in Adam. Just as a light shines out from a fire / so another Principle goes forth through the soul-fire / as the property of Divine power. In this same outgoing power dwells the supernatural, un-substantial **GOD** in Trinity. For this is the Divine Principle / where God dwells, works, and wills within man / wherein the Divine light is understood / which penetrates through the true humanity / like a fire through iron.

*NB.* Therefore, understand it correctly: man stands in three *Principles* / as in three beginnings. The visible man is the visible...

<column-break/>

...world / which exists outwardly and inwardly / as a perishable and an imperishable thing / as the pure element / and the four-fold path / as the four elements. But the foundation of the soul is the element / it is grounded in the eternal Word / where the fiery Word of the Father’s property breathed itself into the created image / as another Principle of the eternal nature. 

The third supernatural foundation of man is now the true angel—understand this as the substantial light / the substantial Wisdom / which came into man with the breathing-in of the soul. However / when the soul led itself away from the breathing Word by its own will and into the visible being with its desire / this light faded. For the soul-fire-life, arising from the Father’s property, could no longer reach it; therefore, this foundation of the creature faded / and was no longer in **GOD** / but remained only as the creaturely soul. And as this holy foundation became hidden from the soul and the body / the soul and body became a dark valley / full of pain and torment / for **GOD** was hidden from him. Immediately, the Principles began to *operate* <note>original: "qualificiren"; to manifest or act according to their specific qualities</note> according to their own properties: The soul operated according to the wrath-property of **GOD** the Father / which was hidden as light within her; and the outer body began to operate in the four elements / such as in heat and cold / and in all other properties of the star-powers. Each awakened property impressed itself into a being / from which the body became coarse, hard, and bestial / and the true image of **GOD** became a mask and a monster. And that is sin / for the sake of which the power of **GOD** entered into humanity again / took on humanity / and again manifested his Divine power through and in true humanity...

This "substantial faith" in man is Christ himself, who remains in man, and who is man’s life and light. This is the temple of the Holy Spirit who dwells in us, as St. Paul says: 

> Do you not know that you are the temple of **GOD**, and that the Spirit of **GOD** dwells in you?

This same substantial faith is also the branch on Christ’s vine; its power penetrates the whole man (just as the sun penetrates a plant) and kills the lusts and works of the flesh. It is not the mortal flesh that is the substantial faith. The flesh does not grasp Christ’s flesh and blood, but it *suffers* it <note>In this context, "suffers" means to undergo or receive the influence of something, like a material being transformed by a chemical process.</note>, just as a coarse stone suffers the <term>Tinctur: In alchemy and Böhme’s thought, a "tincture" is a transformative spiritual essence that can change the quality of a substance, much like a dye or a catalyst.</term> of gold. And just as beautiful gold lies and grows within a coarse stone, so the body of Christ grows in man’s true life and penetrates that life like a fire penetrates iron. 

It is not that such power lies within the human life itself, as if it could take **GOD’S** essence by its own strength; no, it is given to him out of grace, just as the sun gives itself to the plant by its own will. O little children, it is a great mystery!

We should bind ourselves together in love and remember that we are members of one body in Christ, and that in Christ we are all only one. 

Just as the one Christ gives himself to us all in common as one life, and loves us all in his one humanity—offering that same humanity with his great love and grace to us all in common under the bread and wine, and binding himself to us in this shared participation—so we also, in such a gathering and partaking, should bind ourselves in true love and faithfulness as members of one body. We must truly think that in such participation we are all only one in Christ. For we all partake of the one Christ and become, in that same Christ, only a single body—which is Christ in his members.

O little children, what a depth of mystery this is, if we only reflect on it rightly! Satan, through God’s wrath, has made us divided and scattered us, so that we have opposing minds. # Of the Holy Supper. #

...[must] be rooted in Him, and all live from His power and essence, standing in one single trunk, which is He Himself. Therefore, we should contemplate this correctly, and not approach such a communion with unworthy hearts and mouths, thinking it enough that we consume bread and wine. No, it is a brotherly, organic alliance; we bind ourselves through it in Christ into one single Man, and that same single Man is every individual in Christ Himself.

Therefore, our intention at such a gathering should be that we—as members of one body—wish to bind ourselves firmly through this partaking, to renounce Satan and his ill-will, and to love one another heartily, just as Christ loved us and gave His life for us unto death. To this end, this Testament of partaking under bread and wine was ordained. **NB.** This is not to be understood as if it were a special kind of partaking that a Christian could not participate in outside of this practice; for if we are in Christ, and He Himself is in us, and is our life and light, and we are thus rooted in Him in the "substantial faith" (of which faith He Himself is the essence), why should that same desire for life not be able to eat of Him at all times, whenever it turns toward Him? This ordinance is simply a communal love-alliance, so that we may remember what Christ did for us until He comes again visibly in His assumed human form, and remains eternally with and in us as our true High Priest.

<margin>2. Testament, chapters 3, 35–54.</margin>

10. **Question:** Despite all this, a doubt remains for me: how can Christ, who is at the right hand of the Father, give us His body and blood to eat?

**Answer:** For a clearer explanation, consider that just as the Right Hand of **GOD** is everywhere and cannot be excluded or locked away from any place, so also Christ’s body is not excluded or locked away from any place. Rather, He is in all things and through all things, but especially in His believers.

<column-break/>

Now you might say: What did Christ give His disciples at the Last Supper when He sat with them at the table? See, the Godhead is incomprehensible <note>In this context, "incomprehensible" means that God cannot be physically contained or limited by space.</note>, and the holy body of Christ is also not measurable; it is indeed <term>creaturely: relating to the nature of a created being, having a specific form or identity.</term>, but not measurable. He gave them His holy heavenly body and His holy heavenly blood to eat and drink, as His own words state in Matthew 26:26–28. You ask: How can that be? Tell me, how can it be that the "holy element" <note>The "holy element" refers to the spiritual substance or "quintessence" that Böhme believes underlies the physical world.</note> has put on this world, and has another <term>Principle: a distinct realm or level of reality (Böhme describes three: the dark world, the light world, and the physical world).</term> within the body of this world, and that this holy element is Christ’s heavenly body? Thus, Christ gave His disciples external bread and external wine in the kingdom of this world, and beneath it, His holy heavenly body in the other Principle (which sustains the outer world) and His holy heavenly blood, in which the heavenly <term>Tincture: a spiritual life-essence or "soul-fluid" that transmits power and transformation.</term> and the holy life exist. Then Reason says: "That would be a foreign body in foreign blood, and would not be the body of His creaturely self." Dear Reason, tell me how that can be a foreign body? It is indeed in another Principle, but it is from no other creature. Did Christ not say, "I am not of this world"? Yet He was truly of this world according to the outward man. Or do you understand this only of His Godhead? If so, where would His eternal humanity remain, according to which He was a King of the Promise on the Throne of David?

Christ had to overcome the devil not so much according to His Godhead, but primarily according to His humanity; and indeed, not just here or there, but in all places and ends. He had to bring forth life out of death, love out of wrath, and blessing out of the curse—not only in Himself, but in all people, at all times, and in all places. Thus, the inner element which sustains the whole body of this world has become Christ’s eternal body. For the entire Godhead entered therein and wedded itself to it, to remain therein for eternity; and that same Godhead became a creature—a creature that [can be] everywhere...

This is the temple of the Holy Spirit who dwells in us, as St. Paul says: 

> Do you not know that you are the temple of **GOD**, and that the Spirit of **GOD** dwells in you? <note>1 Corinthians 3:16</note>

Also: The temple of Christ is holy, which you are, *1 Corinthians 6:19.* <note>The original text cites 16, 17, likely a scribal error for 6:19 or 3:17</note> Also: 

> Should we, who belong to Christ, still be sinners? Far be it! For then Christ would be a servant of sin in us, *Galatians 2:17.* 

That same substantial faith is also the branch on Christ’s vine, which power penetrates the whole man (just as the sun penetrates a plant) and kills the lusts and business of the flesh. It is not the mortal flesh that is the substantial faith. The flesh does not grasp Christ’s flesh and blood; rather, it endures it, just as a coarse stone endures the tincture of gold <note>An alchemical metaphor: a "tincture" was a substance believed to be able to permeate and transform base matter into gold</note>, and just as a beautiful gold lies and grows within the coarse stone, so the body of Christ grows in man’s true life and penetrates that life like fire penetrates iron. Not that such power lies within man’s life, that it could take **GOD’S** essence by its own strength; no, it is given to him out of grace, just as the sun gives itself to the plant by its own will. For the plant cannot say: "I am the sun," simply because the sun works within it. So too, man cannot say: "I am Christ," simply because Christ

<column-break/>

dwells and works in him; rather, the creature is the recipient <note>original: *Leidende*, literally the "passive" or "suffering" party</note> in whom the Creator dwells and works. We are members of Christ according to his humanity, and are called Christians because Christ dwells and works in us, so that in our life we are his limbs and branches in which he bears fruit through his power. O little children, it is a great mystery!

**Note well. Note well.** The use of this Testament <note>The Holy Supper or Communion</note>, where we are specifically meant to partake of Christ’s flesh and blood under bread and wine, is ordained so that we should come together and eat of one bread and drink of one cup, and receive Christ therein; so that we should constantly remember what he has done for us, and proclaim his suffering, death, and blood-shedding among one another, and teach such things to our children. We should bind ourselves together in love and remember that we are members of one body in Christ, and that in Christ we are all but one. Just as the one Christ gives himself to us all in common as a life, and loves us all in his one humanity, and reaches out that same one humanity with his great love and grace to us all in common under one bread and wine, and binds himself with us in one kind of partaking; so should we also, in such a gathering and partaking, bind ourselves as members of one body in true love and faithfulness, and indeed think that in such partaking we are all but one in Christ. For we all partake of the one Christ, and in that same one Christ we become only one single body, which is Christ in his members.

O little children, what a depth of mystery this is, if we only consider it rightly! Satan, in God’s wrath, has made us disunited and divided us, so that we have conflicting minds. Here Christ comes with his love and makes of everyone a single man again within himself, who is he himself in us; so that we all together become branches of his tree, which he himself is.

# Chapter 15.
## On the Threefold State and Way of Life of the Members of the Visible Church, namely: On the Defending, Nourishing, and Multiplying Estates.

### Connection.

In the external, visible church, we have examined, first, the true and false office of teaching. Secondly, the true and false doctrine. Thirdly, the true and false worship of God. Now it follows that we also investigate where the difference lies between a true and a false Christian regarding their external way of life and external conduct. This generally consists of four main estates, known as the **Teaching, Defending, Multiplying, and Nourishing Estates**. <note>These "Four Estates" were a common early modern way of dividing society: the clergy (Teaching), the nobility/military (Defending), the married/family life (Multiplying), and the laborers/farmers (Nourishing).</note> It will be most necessary to distinguish such states of a Christian’s external life clearly, because the author’s <note>Referring to Jacob Böhme.</note> testimonies can be misused in various ways by the inexperienced. We have briefly spoken of the **Teaching Estate**; it follows now to investigate the **Estate of Authority** <note>The "Obrigkeit," or secular government.</note>. Therefore, the question is asked:

#### 1st Question.
Where does the **Estate of Authority**, such as: Emperors, Kings, Princes, Potentates, and whatever belongs to them, have its first origin?

#### Answer.
The office of secular authority here on Earth has its original source in the **Angelic Kingdom** <note>The original German "Englischen" refers to "Angelic," not the nation of England.</note>, which Lucifer once ruled with his throne-princes. But when he devastated this, his Angelic Kingdom, and corrupted it with his fierce power of fire and tyranny, God cast him from his throne and set another King in his place, who was to ascend Lucifer’s throne and inhabit the kingdom with a new Angelic host. However, after this King <note>Adam</note> also fell from his governance into the servitude of sin, and the fierce qualities of nature gained the upper hand in corrupted humanity, they introduced themselves through their struggle into a structured governance. Thus, the royal and princely government of this world has its origin; because it has its own **Principle** <note>A "Principle" in Böhme’s thought is a fundamental realm of reality or source of existence.</note>, it possesses all the forms of the heavens. Even if the hypocrites of the high clergy, as they call themselves (who exalt themselves above kings and princes), do not want to believe this, it is nonetheless true. For the strict power of the **Principle** carries out its order according to a heavenly form. Now, although the strict spirits of the hidden seals pour out their bowls of wrath herein,

<column-break/>

and the Devil gains a great deal of plunder in this, what does that have to do with the Order itself? We have both life and death before us, and we may reach for whichever we want: Who will accuse God? Let everyone go where they wish; to whomsoever he yields himself as a servant in obedience, he is that one's servant, and in that kingdom he will remain eternally, whether he be prince or servant. Even if one is a superior and a leader in this **Principle**, he still has no Divine power of his own; rather, he is thus a steward of the **Principle** and is under the seals which bring their wonders to light under his governance. A prince sits just as much in obedience to wait upon the Devil as does a wretched shepherd; there is no difference here except for the office that he bears; that office he bears for God and not for himself. For in the courts of princes and kings, the bowls of wrath of the hidden seals or spirits are poured out, from which come thunder, lightning, and strife on earth. These are always blown up with their trumpets by the hypocrites of the **Great Whore of Babylon** <note>A common Reformation-era term for what was perceived as the corrupt or false institutional church.</note>, who ride upon the beast of the princes’ power like a god. Princes should guard themselves against her, if they do not wish to go with the Whore into the sulfurous pit of God’s wrath, as is to be seen in the **Apocalypse** <note>original: "Apocalypsi", the Book of Revelation</note>.

Therefore, when man entered into the Spirit of this World and now contained all gates within him—both the Kingdom of Heaven and the kingdom of this world—he was forced to live in the "press" <note>German: *Quetsche*; a metaphor for the agonizing tension of being caught between spiritual and worldly realities.</note> between Heaven and this world. In Böhme's thought, this refers to the physical world as a manifestation of God's power, containing both good and evil qualities.</note>, in both evil and good. When God wanted to prefigure a worldly estate in His love, He placed livestock shepherds into it, or indeed low, poor, despised, and unremarkable people. Look at Abel, Seth, Enos, Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Moses, David; likewise, the prophets and apostles, and all the saints through whom God has ever revealed Himself—there you will see that before Him no highness counts for anything; it is only a mirror of the wonders in evil and good, at once a play of God’s love and wrath, a prefiguration of the angelic dominions in light and darkness, in Heaven and Hell.

<margin>
*Mysterium Magnum*, Chapter 73, Sections 36, 44.
</margin>

2. Question: But since Christ, the second Adam, has contested for royal dignity and glory, and has ascended the throne of God, and is crowned as a King of all kings, has He therefore not abolished the office of authority <note>German: *Obrigkeitliche Amt*, referring to the secular government or magistracy.</note> in the New Testament?

Answer: The kingdom of Jesus Christ is not of this world, nor are His throne-princes any visible worldly kings and potentates; rather, Christ is a heavenly King, He leads a spiritual government <term>spiritual government: *geistlich Regiment*, the inner rule of Christ over the soul as opposed to external laws</term>. His servants are not raised to government by their own power, but through the power of His Spirit; they stand in no outward glory and do not rule with outward gestures, nor with outward words, statutes, and orders, but in power. He does not protect His subjects with carnal weapons, but through His almighty Word. He kills the members that are on earth, and His subjects conduct their lives in Heaven through His power; but as long as they still live in flesh and blood, they also bow with all obedience, as is proper, under authorities who have power over them, for they are ordained by God for the punishment of the wicked and the protection of the pious, until the appointed time.

<column-break/>

3. Question: But may a Christian well administer an office of authority, especially if he is born into it and perhaps attains it through inheritance?

Answer: If someone wishes to become a Christian, let him beware above all things that he does not strive for highness; but if he stands in a government and office, let him go out from selfhood <note>German: *Selbstheit*, the ego-driven state of being turned away from God.</note> into humility and self-denial above all things, so that his heart remains free. For the outward conduct remains in this world, but what the heart grasps, that we take with us. Therefore it is necessary for us to strive for something good, in which the soul can spend its eternal play and have joy; for the works of our souls follow after us, and the works of our hands and of the outward spirit remain in this world. For the soul is in eternity; that stands forever before it—unless it breaks itself apart again, then it is like a broken work, in which no seeking satisfies it anymore, because it has departed from it. Therefore, the eternal carves an eternal model, and the fragile and beginning carves a fragile model, for all things in this time shall each stand in its model; for what the eternal will grasps, that receives an unbreakable form, provided it does not break it itself. Therefore it is good for man that he choose the best for himself in this life, in which he may have eternal joy. For even if you wanted to choose beauty and honor for yourself, or wealth, you are nonetheless unworthy of your brother and sister who are in the misery of this world; for the beauty of this world despises the simple, and wealth wrings sweat from the wretched, and great power presses and oppresses the low and wretched, great honor despises the simple, and does not liken itself to the needy. If then in that life many simple, wretched, and in this world despised, poor, and troubled souls are found, then in their forms will be enclosed much highness, beauty, and desire for power and honor; for those souls have only [spent themselves] in this vale of tears <note>German: *Jammerthal*, a traditional term for the suffering of earthly life.</note>...

### Part 4 / Chapter 15.

4. **Question:** May a Christian also rightly go into war and strife against the enemies of his earthly fatherland, when the authority requires it of him, or may he rightly defend himself against his enemy if he is attacked?

**Answer:** Through Adam's Fall <note>The biblical event of the first man's disobedience, which Böhme views as a cosmic disaster affecting human nature.</note> we are plunged into such great misery that our life-spirit is like a poisonous, fiery dragon, and the soul is a fiery source of poison. As soon as even a little is struck upon his <term>martial</term> <note>Referring to Mars, the planet and archetypal force of war and fire.</note> fiery quality, <term>signature</term> <note>The outward expression or character of an inner spiritual reality.</note>, or the form of his prepared instrument, then his evil, poisonous, fiery quality comes forward and sets the body on fire, so that it trembles with the poison of wrath. It always wants to enter into the same ignited source of poison in the one who awakened and ignited it, and to <term>inter-qualify</term> <note>original: *inqualiren*; a term used by Böhme to describe how different forces or qualities work together or blend into one another.</note> in its malice with the malice of the awakener, and to wrestle in the rights of the poisonous quality. Thus, the body must then take hold as a servant and fulfill the will of the poison, and scuffle and strike with its opposite, and also let itself be struck—whether it happens with physical grips or with words, it is all within such a quality and desire of the poisonous <term>Mercury</term> <note>In Böhme's alchemy-based theology, Mercury represents the active, vital, and "speaking" principle of life that can be either heavenly or poisonous.</note>. From this arises all war and strife: namely, from the government of **GOD’S** Wrath in the corrupted and ignited Mercury of the "expressed word" <note>The "expressed word" refers to the physical, created world as spoken into existence.</note>; this Mercury thus has its joyful play in man within the quality of the poison's wrath and the dark world. Therefore, the warrior is a servant of **GOD’S** Wrath: he is the axe with which the angry farmer cuts down the thornbush on his field; he is the driving work of the fierce Wrath of **GOD**. The Wrath of **GOD**, according to its fire-quality, desires it—and not His Love. Whoever now lets himself be used for this serves the Wrath of **GOD** according to the desire and quality of the dark and fire-world, which revealed itself in human nature during the heavy Fall of Adam, and led man, as the **Angelic Image**, into a half-devillish <term>mask</term> <note>original: *Larvam*; suggesting a false or monstrous outward appearance that hides the true spiritual self.</note> and

<column-break/>

image. In this quality and the image of his will within the expressed, creaturely Mercury or Word of Life, he cannot possess **GOD’S** Kingdom. Instead, he must be born anew with and in **Christ**, in His Mercury and Will, in **GOD’S** Love—as in the holy, speaking Mercury and Word of Life—so that a new, obedient will, entirely surrendered to **GOD’S** Love, may go forth from his creaturely Mercury. This new will should want or do nothing except what the will of the speaking Divine Mercury wants; it is as if dead in its "I-ness" and "selfhood" <note>Böhme emphasizes the death of the "ego" or "self-will" as the path to spiritual rebirth.</note> in its own will, so that it may be the instrument of the great **GOD**, with which He works and does what and how He wills. Then **GOD** is All in All in him—the will and the doing—and he is a branch on the whole Tree, which draws its sap, power, and life from the Tree of **GOD**, grows in Him, lives, and bears its fruit. Then the Mercury of human life is a born-out or expressed fruit that grows, echoes, and sounds upon the Paradise-Tree of **GOD**, and strikes the <term>signature</term> in the speaking Word of **GOD**, as **GOD’S** harp and lute-play in His praise. For this end was man created: not that he should strike as an instrument of wrath and death and the Devil's will. The Devil has committed himself to that same lute-striking, and helps to drive the play in fierceness and in darkness. He is the conductor and the lute-player in the wrath of eternal nature, which has its fulfillment there; so too must the godless man do, as St. Paul says of it: The Saint is to **GOD** a good fragrance of life unto life, and the godless a good fragrance unto death <note>A paraphrase of 2 Corinthians 2:15-16.</note>.

## On Secular Authority.

5. **Question:** Yet did not holy men in the Old Testament lead great and heavy wars, such as Abraham, Joshua, David, etc.?

**Answer:** We must clearly distinguish and understand how the children of the Saints led war against the hoards of the godless and drove them out; they acted within the **property of wrath**, which wields its sword through them to exterminate the heathens and those of the <term>nature of Ham</term> <note>original: "Hams-Art." This refers to the biblical Ham, son of Noah, traditionally viewed in this era as the ancestor of those outside of God's grace or those destined for servitude and worldly struggle.</note>. For Abraham went out with his whole house and people against the heathens who had taken his brother's son, Lot, captive and led him away; he struck down the heathens and delivered his brother. This happened in the **zeal of God**, who thus rescues His children through the power of His wrath. For what results in destruction for the godless, results in life and a rescue for the Saints.

But that those who wish to be called Christians—who should be dead to the anger and fury of God in the death of Christ—wage wars, they do this not as Christians, but as heathens. No Christian wars; for if he is a Christian, he is dead to the <term>four elements</term> <note>The physical and spiritual components of the material world which Böhme believes are currently in a state of conflict or "wrath."</note> of the wrath of God in his <term>selfhood</term> <note>original: "Selbstheit." A central concept in Böhme’s theology referring to the ego-driven, fallen state of man that seeks its own will over God's.</note> through and in Christ's death. He is born in Christ's spirit of love as a new man, who lives in righteousness, love, and patience—living not for himself, but for God in Christ. For a true Christian conducts his <term>conduct</term> <note>original: "Wandel," often translated in older Bibles as "conversation" or "citizenship," meaning one's entire way of being and acting.</note> and will in heaven, in the life and spirit of Christ, as St. Paul says: *Our citizenship is in heaven.*

That Christians do war, they do so out of their **heathen property**, and not out of Christ’s property. For a Christian is not of this world; his kingdom is in heaven, and he in Christ is dead to the world according to the new spiritual man within him. The heathen—as the half-devilish man who has his kingdom in this world—desires to war and murder within the Christian. Such a one has 

<column-break/>

no room anywhere on earth, living instead in the four elements of God's wrath: namely in **pride, greed, envy, and wrath.** St. Paul says: *Give your members as weapons of righteousness.* For why does one wage war? For the sake of the kingdom of this world. And yet Christ says His kingdom is not of this world; thus, the kingdom of His children in Him is also not of this world.

If we now surrender our body and soul to be weapons of God's wrath, and thereby seek only our **selfhood**, murdering one another for the kingdom of this world: I truly believe we are Christians here only with the mouth, but the heart and soul are heathen, and not born of Christ's spirit. Abraham, when he struck the heathens, desired nothing from the goods he took; instead, he gave back to the King of Sodom what the heathens had taken from him. He acted solely in the zeal of the Lord. He did not war for land and kingdoms, but to rescue his brother; that was indeed a righteous zeal which the Lord drove within him. He did not rise up and war for a land or a city; and even when he obtained it, he desired none of it, but moved back to his own place.

<margin>Mysterium Magnum 38. 15 :: 18.</margin>
If we then walk in God's power, all our doing is well-pleasing to God. For when one defends himself against the necessity of his enemy without any other desire, it is not contrary to God. For if his house is on fire, he extinguishes it: He did, after all, allow Israel to defend itself. But he who starts and causes a war is the **Devil's steward**. For God's wrath drives all wars, and the Devil dwells therein. God has instituted no war, for He created us in love, that we should be together in Paradise in friendly love as dear children; but the Devil begrudged us this and led us into the spirit of this world, which awakens wars and all evil in the wrath of God, so that we become enemies to ourselves and murder one another.

### Part 4 / Chapter 15.

Since we are surrounded by enemies in this **valley of sorrows** <note>original: "Jammerthal." A traditional term for the earthly world as a place of trial and suffering.</note> and grow amidst mere thorns and thistles, we may well take heed of ourselves: for we must also guard against the enemy we carry in our own bosom—who is the worst of all—namely our **disposition and senses**. The Devil also has his **robber-castle** <note>original: "Raub-Schloß." A metaphor common in Böhme’s writing for the ego or the heart when it is occupied by selfish or demonic influences.</note> within them, and it requires great effort to drive him out. He often slips into our mind and leads us upon a glistering path, so that we think we are in **GOD** and that our way is right; therefore, we should always have the **touchstone** with us—that is, the gracious love toward **GOD** and mankind.
->The Threefold Life, 12. 40. 41.<-

6. **Question:** So much for the estate of secular authority. Concerning the **estate of marriage**, we have already seen enough from the testimonies of our blessed author in Chapter 14, especially § 10; furthermore, daily experience testifies to every conscience that the estate of marriage is subject to many hindrances to a true Christian life—which consists in the living communion with **GOD** through Christ, and in the true **rebirth** and renewal of the spirit. Specifically, the **fleshly mingling** <note>original: "fleischliche Vermischung." A 17th-century term for sexual intercourse.</note> practiced therein is such an abomination <note>original: "Eckel," literally "disgust" or "loathing."</note> before God’s holiness; thus, it is rightly asked: is a Christian even permitted to enter the estate of marriage, and can he live and persist within it as a Christian?

**Answer:** Both the Holy Scripture and the countless examples of the Fathers, the Apostles, and the first Christians—indeed, the experience of our author himself—testify how **GOD’S** immeasurable grace and mercy do not leave themselves without witness to marriage-partners who desire salvation, even in this estate. And though some, according to their own opinion, wish to exclude such people from the **right of the first-born in Christ**, and do not recognize the grace of **GOD** to attain true rebirth and a new life within this estate, nevertheless the Spirit of **JESUS** Christ does not cease to carry on His work in God-fearing married people, and to lead their struggle through all the many and great temptations toward their sanctification and redemption.

The testimonies of Holy Scripture and the examples of countless believers of the Old and New Testaments, as well as the first Christians, have been thoroughly presented in other writings by others; here, we hold to the testimonies of our blessed

<column-break/>

author, who—after he had been illuminated by **GOD** for the first time in an extraordinary way during his tender youth—entered into the estate of marriage in his twentieth year of age. He lived in it for thirty years and fathered four children, during which time he was seized by **GOD** for the second and third time and drawn into His communion; also, through the assistance of the Holy Spirit, he suffered many a hard battle and struggle **in this** estate. Now, concerning the fact that the blessed author presents the so-called marital **mingling**—that is, physical intercourse—as an **abomination before** **GOD’S** holiness, this is not done **to** cast a noose around anyone’s neck <note>To "cast a noose" means to trap someone's conscience or create a legalistic burden.</note>, but **rather** to refute the highly dangerous error of Esaias Stiefel and Ezechiel Meth <note>Two contemporary heterodox spiritualists who claimed that their physical actions were divinely sanctified and sinless.</note>, who **falsely** taught: that through the **union** <note>original Latin: "junction."</note> or mingling of man **and** woman in their lustful desire, the evil **qualities** and lust of the flesh are **separated**, and entirely sanctified in the spirit of CHRIST; that Christ’s spirit of love enters into their **imagination** <note>original: "Imagination." In Böhme's philosophy, this is the soul's creative power to form itself into a specific likeness.</note> and drives out all abomination, and works such lust of man and **woman** **in the** imagination, and sanctifies the imagination **and the** seed, whereby sin dies away **and** an entirely holy child is conceived—even **a** little Christ-child who is without the blemish **of** sin, and who is **GOD** and **man** from within and without. **Et cetera.** In short, the **entire** content and **meaning** of this Stiefel’s [system] was that it was no longer he who **willed**, acted, spoke, thought, or **felt**, but rather it was only **GOD** in Christ **in** everything—the willing, acting, speaking, **thinking**, meditating, fathering of children, **eating**, drinking, sleeping, waking, **etc.**
->Apology against Stiefel, § 407. //// 414.<-

This dangerous error—whereby the flesh is given a **completely free rein** and a wide gate is opened to **sin**, under the **appearance** of holiness and a Christian **freedom** to practice shame—is refuted by our **illuminated** author. He proves that it is impossible **that** pious married people may mingle **without stain**, and that they therefore cannot **beget children** who are entirely pure and without sin; **he shows**, therefore, what in the marital work is **stained** and an abomination before **GOD**, yet **in turn** [is] good and according to **GOD’S** ordinance.

# On Secular Authority.

He says: One must distinguish the external from the internal. The marital act <note>original: "Eheliche Werck." A common 17th-century term for sexual intercourse within marriage.</note> is not sinful in itself—if it occurs within the proper order—for it is driven by **GOD’S** steward of nature and borne under Divine patience. **GOD** presents to him [the person] the incarnation of **Christ** His Son, just as with the Jews the sacrifices, which **GOD** presented in the Covenant through the future humanity of **Christ** and was reconciled in the Covenant, so that His wrath was not ignited in human loathing <note>original: "Eckel." This suggests the natural revulsion or "shame" felt regarding the fallen state of the flesh.</note>. Thus also in our marital act, **GOD** presents the true image—which lies locked within our seed—in **Christ** His Son, and enters through the working power into the essence of that same image of heavenly being, like a glimmering mother <note>original: "Moder." In this mystical context, it refers to the "matrix" or the primal material/womb of a quality.</note> of Divine property. Herein lies the holiness of the children of holy married people; however, in the external flesh—as well as in the soul and the fire-spirit—the loathing of sin clings to them, and no child is born into the world without sin. One must distinguish the will toward the external act of mingling from the will of Divine holiness and from the will of one's own lust. Nature desires the heat of passion, as the mingling; **GOD’S** holiness desires the conjunction of the pure tinctures <note>original: "Tincturen." In Böhmean thought, "tinctures" are the subtle spiritual energies (male and female) that must be harmonized.</note>. In which conjunction the Divine center <note>original: "Göttliche Centrum."</note>, as a holy spark of fire, incorporates itself into the essence of the heavenly image in the Word of power, and does not "inflesh" itself in the external flesh. §. 409. 410. 411. From this it can clearly be seen what is holy or unholy in the marital act: that, while on one hand human passion and animal fleshly lust may not be considered a sanctuary, on the other hand, **Christ** is also present with holy, God-fearing married people, provided they begin all things in His name. He governs and blesses them as they remain earnestly in Him, and all their work in right marital duty is pleasing to Him, as He who has come to destroy the work of the Devil.

->Regarding this, read § 330 in the Apology against Stiefel.<- <note>Refers to Jacob Böhme’s "Apologia contra Esaiam Stiefel," a polemical work against a contemporary religious leader.</note>

Since **Christ** also dwells and works in God-fearing, believing married people, and there-

<column-break/>

-fore permits a Christian to enter into marriage, the question arises: how should a youth or maiden, wishing to enter the estate of marriage, undertake this according to **GOD’S** will? Youths and maidens should take care, in their first zeal and the impulse of awakening grace, that they make no vows <note>original: "Gelübde." Likely referring to vows of celibacy or perpetual virginity.</note> not to marry, nor help to condemn others who do so with lack of understanding and premature judgment. For such people are commonly tempted all the more powerfully afterward, and if they do enter marriage, they must often undergo great anguish and many difficult trials because of it. But if someone has the gift of grace of continence from **GOD**, let him recognize such a gift as a grace of **GOD** in humility, and not exalt himself because of it, lest he bring temptation and trial upon himself, as has already happened to many. Furthermore, let him be cautious in the choice of a marriage partner, discerning well whether it is a pure impulse of nature and a longing of the external birth and its sidereal tincture <note>original: "Syderischen Tinctur." This refers to the influence of the stars or the "astral" body on human attraction.</note>—lest he be blinded by the lust of the eyes, driven by the longing of the changeable stars, and coupled by nature—or whether he is led by a higher hand and the tincture is driven from a deeper ground. The former is inconstant, coarse, and false, soon causing one to become an object of loathing and offense to the other; but the latter, which flows from a purer ground and is directed by a higher hand, dispels the loathing that often arises in nature. For when the tincture in flesh and blood has exhausted its passionate impulse and longing, and the <term>Turba</term> <note>original: "Turba." A Latin term used by Böhme to describe the "awakened wrath" or the spirit of disruption and destruction that arises when harmony is lost.</note> wakes up within, and the power of darkness covers the mind with great loathing and shame before **GOD**, then the inner tincture in holy, God-fearing married people opens up and, with its faithful love and inclination, soothes the heart that was ignited and distressed by wrath once again. Therefore, the Holy Spirit in the Old and New Testament warns so earnestly that the children of **GOD** should not mingle fleshly with the children of men, but that believers should marry in the **LORD**. For when the children of **GOD** looked upon the daughters of men, how beautiful they were, and took as wives whomever they wanted, and mingled in fleshly lust with fleshly women—introducing the seed of the holy <term>being</term> <note>original: "Entis." Latin genitive of "Ens," meaning essence or being.</note> into such animal vessels, and thus corrupting the holy <term>essence</term> <note>original: "Ens." Latin for "being" or "essence."</note> in the Covenant in which **GOD** had incorporated Himself—then were born such tyrants and fleshly-minded people who would not allow the Spirit of **GOD** to rebuke them. From this, the Deluge <note>original: "Sünd-Fluth," literally "Sin-Flood."</note> subsequently arose, in which these mixed peoples were rooted out.

### Part 4 / Chapter 15.

Therefore, take note: the Woman is the field, and the Man has the grain <note>original: "Korn." In this context, it refers to the seed of life.</note> that is sown to become a human tree. Here, Reason says: **GOD** joins them together however He wishes to have them. Answer: Yes, rightly so; but it happens through His purpose, which He has framed into a governance within the Word through the great clockwork of nature. The *Constellations* <note>original: "Constellationes." These refer to the spiritual and astrological alignments of qualities or "stars" within a person.</note> in this clockwork draw them together; but most are drawn together through their own will, where the human will—which originates from the eternal ground—*aligns* <note>original: "constelliret." This refers to the act of positioning oneself within a spiritual or planetary influence.</note> itself. In such cases, the external *constellation* is broken, as we see when the rich *align* themselves with the rich; *likewise*, the noble with the noble. Otherwise, if the *Spirit of the World* <note>original: "Spiritu Mundi." The universal life-force or atmospheric spirit of the physical world.</note> were not interrupted in its *constellation*, many a poor servant girl would be joined to a nobleman, for they would *align* with one another externally within the *Spirit of the World*. But the self-made, human *constellation* of the soul, coming from a higher ground, is more powerful than the *constellation* in the *Spirit of the World*; therefore, things often and mostly follow the *constellation* of the soul, which surpasses the outer world in power and majesty. It is just like the sower: it depends on him where he sows his grain, even if another field might be better suited for it. If, however, the soul surrenders its will to **GOD** and does not *align* itself by its own choice in this order, but instead commits itself to the purpose of **GOD**, then the male and female *Tinctures* <note>original: "Tinctur." In alchemical and mystical terms, this is the inner spiritual essence or life-force that gives a being its specific quality.</note> are encompassed within the Word. They are *aligned* in the right Divine order: according to the soul in the *Great Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterio Magno." The source of all things, the "chaos" or womb from which all manifestation arises.</note>, and according to the body in the *Spirit of the World*. There, a love is awakened within them according to the true equality of their qualities. And if the person then follows this love, and does not look at wealth, nobility, or beauty and cleverness, then his own *constellation* which he has by nature attains the true, right equality, and he becomes a field that is like and pleasing to the grain. Thus, strife does not easily or quickly arise in the fruit <note>i.e., the children born of the union.</note>, for they

stand with one another in equality, and the inner and outer Sun can assist in *aligning* the fruit. But one sees how it goes in the world: even when nature brings people together and binds two young people in the highest love (which happens out of the great purpose of the true *constellation* in the formed Word of the *Spirit of the World*), parents and friends break this bond for the sake of poverty or status. Then **GOD** says to Noah: "Humanity will not let itself be drawn by My spirit," and they enter into marriages and sleep with the daughters of men according to how they are beautiful, rich, and noble—all of which is merely a human fabrication. From this, there arise the Mighty and the Tyrants, against whom **GOD** sets the Flood <note>original: "Sünd-Fluth." Literally "Sin-Flood."</note> of His wrath in their perverse *constellation*, hardening their own will. For many people are forced or coupled together because of rank or wealth, though they are enemies to one another; all their lives, they wish for death and separation in their minds. Now, these two are supposed to introduce their *Tinctures* together into a *Conjunction* <note>original: "Conjunction." A union or joining, often used in alchemy to describe the marriage of opposites.</note> for the human life of a child; these two *Tinctures* should enter into each other and change into one. In the female and male seed, the *Essence* <note>original: "Ens." The vital, spiritual substance or "being" within the seed.</note> should lead itself into a joy-filled equality, yet they are unequal to one another in spirit. The field—that is, the woman—then treats the grain like a step-son; she must indeed accept the grain, for it enters into her and draws the *Essence* from the field into itself; but the field does not give its good will. Thus, the *Essence* of the seed must seek its equality in the female seed, but it then lies buried too deep in the *constellation* and can hardly reach it. From this arises infertility and the loathing of nature. And if it does happen that the female *Tincture* of the field is received...

->7. *Question:* So much for the so-called worldly state of marriage. Now the question concerns external labor: namely, whether and how a Christian must also work with his hands?<-

*Answer:* Labor in and of itself is neither helpful nor a hindrance to a Christian regarding the Kingdom of GOD. Rather, it is a necessity for the external man, who is a guest here in a foreign inn where he requires food and nourishment. But where a person enters into the things of this world with his mind and desire, seeking his trust in his own ability to become rich, to fill his belly, and worries in unbelief—"What shall we eat? What shall we drink? With what shall we be clothed?"—this hinders the life of **JESUS Christ**.

Therefore, dear children, if we step entirely out of our own reason and surrender into the will of GOD, so that He may do with us as He wills; when we place our trust in Him, we enter into a true Father and are His children. And just as a father cares for his children, so GOD our Father will care for us, as **Christ** faithfully teaches us: "Seek first the Kingdom of GOD and His righteousness, and all these other things shall be added unto you." Likewise: "Behold the birds of the heaven; they neither sow nor spin, nor do they gather into barns, yet your heavenly Father feeds them; are you not much better than they?" O you of little faith! A soul knows that this garment of her flesh and blood is a foreign garment <note>original: "fremdes Kleid." Böhme often describes the physical body as a "covering" or "garment" that masks the soul’s true spiritual nature.</note>, of which she is heartily ashamed before GOD'S wrath. Therefore, she also doubts GOD'S grace when she contemplates it, always thinking: the sins are too many, they cannot honor GOD'S Majesty. The Devil also inflicts such torture...

Indeed, this is the case for those who build and trust in themselves; for the soul thinks that when it is stuck in **Reason** <term>Reason (Vernunfft): Böhme often distinguishes between "Vernunft" (earthly, limited human intellect) and "Verstand" or "Weisheit" (divine understanding or wisdom).</term> outside of **GOD**, it must accomplish everything with its own worries, that there is no other way, that it must be so, and that the hands alone must do it—or even through cunning, from which a great deal of evil arises.

Dear children, let yourselves be rightly instructed: the outer earthly life has fallen to the spirit of this world. The belly requires earthly food, the body requires earthly clothes, and a hut for a dwelling. The outer spirit must strive for these; it should work and walk, for in the sweat of his face shall the earthly man eat his bread until he becomes earth again, from which he was taken—so says **GOD** in Moses <note>A reference to Genesis 3:19.</note>. For the body was taken from the **Earth's Matrix** <term>Matrix: From the Latin for "womb," referring to the primal material or mother-substance from which the physical world was formed.</term>, and it imagined into the earth, and the earth captured it again so that it ate earthly fruit; there it became the earth from which it was taken.

For **GOD** took him from the earth; that is, a human or "Red-Earth" <note>original: "Roth-Erde." A reference to the Hebrew name 'Adam,' which is traditionally associated with 'adamah' (red ground/earth).</note>, from the **Fire-Center** and from the **Water-Center**, as if from both mothers of nature, and breathed into him the breath from the outside through the spirit of the great world, and the soul from within, from the other **Principle** <note>In Böhme’s cosmology, the "Second Principle" is the world of Light and Divine Love.</note> into the heart. The soul does not dwell in the outer in this way, yet it is captured by the outer. Its will has entered into the outer; there it has become pregnant in its will with the outer government, and thus the outer government has come into the soul—which **GOD** forbade man, telling him not to let himself lust after earthly fruit and power. And he would not have needed it out of necessity, for

<column-break/>

he was in **Paradise**, and had **Paradisical** food without need or death. Just as **God** dwells even in the earth, and yet the earth does not know Him and does not grasp Him; so also man could have dwelt in the **Earth's Matrix** and yet remained with the soul in **GOD**, and the soul’s will would have brought the soul Divine food.

But since he has now turned around, the soul eats from the **Center of Nature** <note>original: "Centro Naturæ." The source of natural life, which in its fallen state is driven by hunger and desire.</note>, and the outer spirit eats from the earth. However, if the soul converts and goes with its will into **GOD’S Love**, then it eats of **GOD’S Word**, and the outer body eats of **GOD’S blessing**. For when the soul is blessed, **GOD** also blesses the body, because the soul carries a heavenly body within the old Adam-like one. Thus his food and drink are blessed, and everything that the whole man does and has.

He attains a wonderful blessing which his **Reason** does not grasp; he must work and earn, for he was created into this outer life for the purpose of revealing **GOD’S wonders** with his art and trade. All states <note>original: "Stände." Referring to social classes, vocations, or professions.</note> are **GOD’S order**; each one works **GOD’S wonders**, and as long as the soul stands in **GOD’S hand** in His love, the body is in **GOD’S wonder-working**, and **GOD** has no displeasure in his being, whatever he then does to gather food.

Whatever man now trusts **GOD** and sets his heart entirely within his **Reason**, he always has the Spirit of **GOD** as his **Creator**. He has the **Word "Let it be"** <note>original: "Verbum Fiat." The creative command of God.</note> and creates continually; He blesses him in body and soul, in the field, in the house, in his handicraft and trade. Whatever he then does, the Spirit of **GOD** is within it and works—how could it be otherwise? The soul has its body; how then would He desert the outer body which is meant to reveal His wonders? He is well off in all things, provided they are not false and do not run against the love of **GOD** and man: And

### Of the Threefold Life, Chapter 17, §§ 1, 7.

8. **Q.** Is it then not all the same what kind of external calling or manual labor a man—and especially a believer—has?

**Ans.** It is not all the same. A Christian must have a calling that he can perform without cunning, falsehood, or deceit, and without harm or disadvantage to others, but rather in simplicity for the service of his neighbor, as our author has sufficiently proven in the testimony cited above. The simpler, more honest, and more necessary his work is, the more blessing and freedom of mind a man finds in his labor. The more subtle, sharp-witted <note>original: "spitzfündiger" - implying overly complex or deceptive ingenuity.</note>, and unnecessary a work is, the more it is subject to the curse, and it causes nothing in the mind but disorder, reproach, anxiety, and confusion.

<column-break/>

9. **Q.** How, then, should a Christian behave so that his mind is not disturbed in the inner ground of the workings of Divine Grace by external labor?

**Ans.** Behold, you dear soul: if you wish to have **GOD’S** light and see with God's eye, and yet also wish to have this world-light, nourish your body, and seek the wonders of **GOD**, then do as **GOD** Himself does. You have two eyes in your soul <note>The "two eyes of the soul" is a classic mystical concept: one eye looks toward the eternal and divine, while the other looks toward the temporal and material world.</note> which are set against one another: one looks into eternity, and the other looks behind itself into time. This latter eye always moves forward, seeking desires and establishing one foundation after another—let it go on so, if **GOD** wills it. But do not turn the other eye back into time. Instead, use the right eye <note>The eye of eternity.</note> to pull the left eye back toward you. Do not let the eye that is turned toward freedom <note>Divine freedom/eternity.</note> be pulled away from you by the will of the wonders <note>The marvels of the physical world.</note>; rather, draw its opened and created wonders toward yourself. Let your eye give food to the earthly life, but do not let the eye enter into the food as if it were the food itself. Rather, hold it back firmly. Let the hands work and seek food, and let the eye draw in the wonders—but let it draw in no matter <term>Matter (Materia): Physical substance or worldly concerns that weigh down the spirit.</term>. Otherwise, a darkness will dwell within that which has been drawn in, and the devil will rustle behind you before the left eye. He cannot enter unless you close the eye so that it takes in matter. Thus, when your earthly body breaks apart, you will see all the wonders with your right eye that you sought and found here with the left. And when the earthly life falls away, your left eye will also be free from the nature of wrath <term>Nature of Wrath (Natur des Grimmes): In Böhme's theology, the "grim" or "wrathful" quality of nature that exists apart from God's light.</term>—even if it possesses nature—for it is nature that awakens and holds the wonders. Yet it shall then retain them with the wonders of eternal freedom, because it let in no matter, and thus it is free. And...

...work within them so powerfully that they themselves become unfit for any external labor. He who is powerfully moved in prayer and intercession today may stand dry and empty tomorrow. He who at one time overflows like a spring of Divine blessing will at another time be like a hunted deer languishing in the parched desert, panting for the little fountain of Divine mercy. For this is how Wisdom is accustomed to exercise her children in full obedience and releasement <note>The original term "Gelassenheit" refers to a core mystical concept of surrendering one's self-will to God's will.</note>, so that the self may not introduce itself into anything, but that the soul may stand holy and naked before the will of **GOD** in all things. As can be seen in Abraham, when he sacrificed his son Isaac to the will of God in the figure of Christ <note>A "figure" is a person or event in the Old Testament seen as a prophetic symbol or "type" of something in the New Testament—here, Abraham's sacrifice foreshadows Christ's sacrifice.</note>, which was the most magnificent sacrifice and service of God in the Old Testament, and for which reason Abraham, as a father of all believers, attained the highest blessing; the text reports:

> **So Abraham returned to his young men, and they rose up and went together to Beersheba, and dwelt there. Gen. 22.**

From this, our author <note>Likely referring to Jacob Böhme, the mystic whose work is being interpreted here.</note> shows us how, in this figure, it may again be seen how **GOD** has not rejected the realm of nature within man, but rather that He wishes to redeem it in Christ out of its anguish and resistance. He shows that a person should and must remain standing within the realm of nature, just as Abraham, after he had performed this sacrifice, went again with his son and two young men to Beersheba and dwelt there. By this, the Spirit of Moses indicates that once Abraham had performed his station before the **LORD** in the figure of Christ, he returned—Note Well—into his natural business, as into the workings of this world's essence. He went to Beersheba, which is to say, into the toil into which Adam has led us, where a child of **GOD**, amidst the shattering of nature as if in Beersheba, must work in **GOD** with teaching and praying, and also with manual labor to nourish the outer man. They must drive the wonders of the outer world in the formed word, and help to form and reveal them in figures for the contemplation of **GOD’S** Wisdom, and also to signify,

<column-break/>

that a child of **GOD** in this world's essence does not stand every day and hour in the operation of the spiritual figure, so that his spirit might see and recognize it. Rather, he also stands in the natural state, where the Spirit of **GOD** works along with the labor of nature and reveals Himself in another quality within him. This is seen in Abraham and all the saints: at one moment **GOD** reveals Himself in them in the figure of Christ, and at another moment in the cross and toil, in the temptation and adversity of the corrupt Adam. They lived in weakness and infirmity like all of Adam's children. We should regard and contemplate the figure of Abraham in all that the Spirit of Moses and Ezra wrote as nothing other than a prefiguration of Christ and Adam—as the Kingdom of Christ and the Kingdom of Nature—and how **GOD** presented to him the figure of Christ and His Christendom to show how He would again redeem man from his great toil. Alongside this, the Kingdom of Darkness is also constantly presented in pain and torment, showing how it too reaches for man, and how man stands and grows here in a field where sometimes the Sun of Divine Love shines over him, and sometimes **GOD’S** fury and wrath. It shows how man must be tested and refined; and this is the most principal part: how man must resign himself to **GOD** in faith and total trust, and keep still, letting Him work within him, and how he should learn to tame his own nature and lead it before **GOD**, so that in all things it desires to be **GOD’S** instrument and servant, and wishes to work nothing else except what belongs to the Divine Revelation in the wonders of nature for the contemplation of Divine Wisdom, and conversely, to reject the Devil’s self-will and all desire for selfhood.

<meta>This page continues the theme of balancing spiritual heights with worldly duties. While the previous page used Abraham’s return from the mountain to illustrate this, this page expands on the physical and spiritual "work" of mystical experience and moves into a discussion of whether a Christian can rightly possess worldly wealth.</meta>

### Part 4 / Chapter 15.

A Christian should not make a grand display of high contemplation <note>The original term "Beschauung" refers to the mystical practice of gazing upon Divine truths, often leading to ecstasy.</note>, priesthood, sanctuary, or other high degrees of divine service, nor should they attempt to establish themselves therein as if in a permanent fiefdom <note>A "fiefdom" (Erb-Lehn) refers to land held in a feudal system; the author warns against treating spiritual gifts as something one "owns" by right.</note>. Instead, one should always recognize themselves in all these high graces as a pure instrument of the Spirit of **JESUS** Christ. Even if one were led into such states for many years and a long time, they should not exalt themselves as if it were their own property, but remain composed in humility, ready to undertake the lowliest exercises—even physical and menial labor—whenever the **LORD** leads them back down from the mountain. In this sense, one should not judge unfairly anyone who, during the time of such powerful workings of grace (whether they last a short or long time), abstains from external labor and their vocation to offer themselves to the **LORD** in body and soul. For, aside from the fact that the **LORD** alone has the power to use His instrument as He pleases, the vital spirits <term>Vital spirits: in early modern medicine, these were believed to be subtle fluids that carried life and sensation through the body.</term> are often led from the outer man into the inner man by the mighty impulses of grace. This causes the body, and especially the head, to become powerfully weak, as the sensory powers are drawn inward. And truly, such people perform a difficult labor, for the curse of nature often lies upon them like great mountains, and the wrath of **GOD** burns within like a consuming fire—not to mention the mighty struggle with the Prince of Darkness and the god of this world—until the little spring of Divine love and gentleness breaks forth from within. Then the fire dissolves into pure and holy oil and balsam, the darkness is driven away, and the heart is thus strengthened, whereby even the outer body regains its strength and is refreshed. Just as everyone must take care not to claim such honor for themselves before the world in vain glory, either in writing or by word of mouth—much less seek nothing but an unjustifiable idleness under the appearance of such high grace, becoming a burden to others for their own benefit—so also should a modest soul take care not to sin against such people with a perverse judgment. Rather, one should either let it be, or if it concerns them, carefully test all such things before **GOD** in the light of grace and report it in simplicity.

11. **Question.** One more thing will be necessary to investigate here: namely, whether a Christian may possess the goods of this world with a good conscience, and if **GOD** allows them to come to him, how is he
->to behave regarding them?<-

**Answer.** The goods of this world are in and of themselves neither good nor evil; for apart from human

<column-break/>

addiction and desire, they lie there as something dead. But if a person turns their heart away from **GOD** and directs their desire into them, then it is not the goods that become evil, but the person who makes themselves evil within those goods. Thus, depending on how the goods of this world are used, they are to the one who uses them either a blessing or a curse. When Christ says that it will be difficult for a rich man to enter the Kingdom of **GOD**, this is not meant to refer to the wealth itself, but to the self-willed, proud, and greedy life, where one consumes the sweat of the needy in pride and forgets **GOD**. Oh, how difficult it is for a rich and proud person to humble themselves before **GOD** and men; yet the Kingdom of Heaven stands solely in the power of humility. Yet one sees how several "fat ones" <note>The "fat ones" is a biblical metaphor for the wealthy or prosperous.</note> approached Christ; it is to be seen that the Kingdom of Heaven consists not only in misery, but in joy, in the Holy Spirit. And no one should esteem himself holy just because he is poor and miserable; for if he is unbelieving and godless, he nonetheless belongs to the kingdom of the devil. <meta>This page continues the discourse by introducing Chapter 16, which shifts focus from the critiques of social and church corruption (found in the previous page's discussion of *The Threefold Life*) to the specific prophetic gifts of the "highly enlightened author"—Jakob Böhme.
