### Part 4, Chapter 17.

**rebirth** <note>original: "dergeburt," likely "Wiedergeburt"</note>, in which Paradise, power, and wonders arise. And your worldly splendor and glory, beauty and wealth, will not exalt you before **GOD** as you think; nor will the office you held here, whether you were king or priest; you must be born anew through the **Savior**. If you wish to be beautiful in Heaven, you must lead toward righteousness, then you will shine with your office before **GOD** like the radiance of the Heavens, and your works will follow you. O human, consider yourself in this! But what shall I write of you, you earthly **Babylon**? I must nevertheless show you the foundation, so that your **hypocrisy** <note>original: "Gleißnerey," referring to a false, shining outward appearance of piety</note> may be brought to light, and the devil may not stand there in the form of an angel, being a god within man in the lustful kingdom of this world—as that is his highest ambition.

See, you call yourself a **Christian**, and boast of being a child of **GOD**; you indeed confess this with your mouth, but your heart is a murderer and a thief; you strive only for worldly honor and wealth, and your conscience does not ask how you might obtain them. You may indeed carry a will to enter into **earnest repentance** <note>original: "ernste Busse"</note> at some point, but the devil holds you so that you cannot; you say: "Tomorrow," and that lasts forever; and you think: "If only I had my coffers full, I would afterwards become a pious person, if only I first had enough so that I would not suffer want later." You carry on this way until your end, which the devil paints as still being far off.

Meanwhile, you consume the sweat and blood of the **wretched** <note>original: "Elenden," referring to the poor or oppressed</note> and collect all their misery and lamentation into your soul; you take their sweat and practice pride with it, and your conduct must be held as holy. You offend the wretched man, so that through you and your conduct, he also becomes frivolous and does what is wrong before **GOD**. He curses you and ruins himself thereby, and so abomination is born out of abomination—but you are the first cause. And though you may present yourself so elegantly

<column-break/>

and wisely, the **Deceiver** is nevertheless before you, and you are the very manifestation of sin <note>original: "Werck-Sünden"</note>.

Even if you pray, you wear the dark garment that is defiled with vain [lust], with usury, greed, pride, [unrighteousness], whoredom, anger, envy, and theft; it is beastly, envious, and malicious. You cry to **GOD** that He should hear you, and yet you will not take off this [pelt] <note>original: "Pelz," a metaphor for the thick, animalistic layer of sin</note>. Do you think such a devil enters into **GOD**, that He would let such a coarse devil into Himself? Your mind stands in the form of a snake, or a wolf, a lion, a dragon, or a toad. If you dress yourself up more elegantly, you are at best a cunning fox. As the heart's will and torment are, so is your figure; your soul possesses such a shape. Do you think you will lead such a **little beast** into the Kingdom of **GOD**? No, it does not belong in the Kingdom of **GOD** unless you are born anew, so that your soul appears in the **Image of GOD**. And so **GOD'S** mercy is over us, and the suffering of **Christ** covers all your sins; but if you persist in your beastly form until the end, and then stand there and give **GOD** good words, asking Him to take your soul into Heaven—when yet no faith is in you, but your faith is merely a **historical knowledge** <term>historical knowledge: an intellectual belief in the facts of the Bible without a living, spiritual transformation</term> of **GOD**, which the devil also knows well—then you are not tied to the bond of **JESUS Christ**. Your soul remains a worm and a beast and does not bear the Divine Image; when it departs from the body, it remains in the fire and does not reach the **gates of the breakthrough** <note>original: "Thoren der Durchbrechung," a mystical term for the soul breaking through the darkness into the light of God</note>.

# On Temporal and Bodily Death.

**GOD's** wrath has been so fiercely ignited in the sins they brought upon themselves; yet one soul experiences this less than another, depending on whether they entered into repentance and perhaps performed some good works. The souls who must thus wait for the **Last Day** for their bodies, they remain with their bodies in quiet rest, without sensible torment, until the **Last Day**, but in a different **Principle** <note>original: "Principio"; in Böhme's thought, a "Principle" refers to a fundamental realm of existence—here, the state of the soul after death but before the final judgment</note>. In the earth, they have no darkness, nor any majesty; rather, they are in the one quiet freedom, in rest without torment, without the touch of the body. But they see their **wonders** <note>the spiritual manifestations of their life's actions</note>; however, they accomplish nothing within them, for they wait upon **GOD** and are in humility; for they have sunk through death and are in another world. But there is still a "chasm" between them and the holy souls in **Christ's** flesh and blood—not exactly a different **Principle**, for they are in one **Principle**, but a spirit without a body does not have the power of one in a body. Therefore they are at rest; they are "under **GOD's** altar." When the **Last Day** comes, then they shall come forth and eat of **GOD's** bread, and put on **GOD's** body, as is mentioned in the **Revelation of John**, where the souls in white robes under the altar say: "**LORD**, when will you avenge our blood?" And it is told to them that they should rest yet a little while, until their brothers also come, who shall be murdered for the sake of **Christ's** testimony.

40. Fr. 21. §. 10. 13.

9. **Question:** What happens, however, to the souls of good, natural people, who were neither great sinners nor great saints, but here followed the impulse of their nature and concerned themselves more with temporal nourishment than with their salvation, yet did no one wrong or harm, but lived honorably, morally, and civilly, and additionally believed whatever the **Priest of Babel** <note>a derogatory term for institutional clergy who teach "historical" faith without inner spiritual rebirth</note> babbled to them?

**Answer:** When the simple person is about to die, he does not know where he should give his soul; he clings to his works and to his "opinion," and leaves the will of **GOD**, and thus remains outside of **GOD**.

<column-break/>

Where do you think the poor soul remains when it is outside of **GOD's** will? See, we wish to tell you, for we recognize this with certainty, because the Spirit of our Mother <note>referring to Divine Wisdom or Sophia</note> opens this to us, so that we see it as if with both eyes.

See, **Christ** says: "Where your treasure is, there is also your heart." See, the soul is wrapped in its "opinion" <note>human-made dogma or personal notions of God</note>, and thus runs with it to the patron who taught it so, and seeks him; and if it does not find him, it becomes sorrowful and has no rest. It hovers thus between Heaven and Hell and would gladly escape the devil. This is why it has often happened that poor souls have appeared again in the congregation, or else in houses, in fields, or in churches, and have called upon the congregation for help with their prayers, and entered into the religious orders, thinking thus to receive relief—from which **Purgatory** <note>original: "Feg-Feuer," literally "cleansing fire"</note> was fashioned. For the soul truly has **Purgatory** if it cannot reach **GOD's** will; and in such a fervent surrender to its "opinions," it has sunk through those opinions and yet entered into the quiet eternity. But we understand these souls to be those who, in their opinions, have **imagined** <note>the term "imagination" in this context refers to the soul's power to form its internal reality</note> toward the Kingdom of **GOD**, and not the souls of the **Deceiver**, who sought their own profit and lust therein. These latter are all "whoring" with the **Anti-Christ**, for they are bound to him by oaths; and though they sit with him in hellish fire to whore, they still flatter him and blaspheme **GOD**, as if He were doing them an injustice.

For whatever the soul does here in this time, that which it entangles itself in and takes into its will, that same thing it takes with it in its will; and after the change of the body, it cannot be rid of it, for it has nothing more afterward than that very thing. And even if it enters into that thing and ignites it and seeks with diligence, it is only an unfolding of that same essence, and the poor soul must be content with that. Alone...

For whatever is recognized in that same opinion by many, or whatever many of them (or they alone) know within that opinion, that is what the soul knows alone. For here, the soul is one body with all those who are of the same opinion, and they have one heart in many members, where each carries out its business. This remains so until the Judgment of GOD, who will thereafter separate it, at which time all the tribes of the earth shall howl and weep before him, when they shall recognize that very Judge whom they despised here.

10. **Question:** But can a soul not be ransomed <note>original: "ranzioniret"</note> from Purgatory <note>original: "Feg-Feuer," literally "cleansing fire"</note> through human intercession?

**Answer:** The Anti-Christ <note>Böhme uses "Anti-Christ" to refer to institutional religious systems he viewed as spiritually hollow or corrupt</note> has played much jugglery with this and built his kingdom upon it; but I will show you the aim as it is highly recognized in the light of nature. Human intercession reaches as far as the soul still hangs upon the thread of the New Birth <note>term: "New Birth" (Wiedergeburt); the process of spiritual transformation and alignment with God's light</note>, and is not entirely a worm or a beast—that is, if it still penetrates toward GOD with desire. If those interceding are true Christians who earnestly stand in the New Birth, and their soul-spirit penetrates toward GOD on the thread of the bond of the poor soul, joined with the poor soul in their fervent love for it, then they indeed help the poor captive soul to struggle and to burst the chains of the devil. This is especially effective when it happens before the departure of the poor soul from the

<column-break/>

**Right Column:**

body, and particularly by parents, or children, or siblings, or blood-friends <note>relatives</note>. In these, their tinctures <note>term: "Tincture" (Tinctur); in Böhme's alchemy-influenced theology, this refers to the fundamental spiritual essence or "life-oil" of a person</note> interact, as they are born of one blood; their spirit enters much more willingly into this great struggle and conquers more easily and powerfully than strangers do—provided they only stand in the New Birth. But without this, nothing is obtained; no devil breaks another. But if the soul of the dying is entirely loosed from the bond of JESUS Christ, and does not itself achieve the power to penetrate through with its own will, then the intercession of those standing around helps nothing. Rather, it happens to them as Christ said to his seventy disciples in Matthew 10, 12, whom he sent out: "When you go into a house, greet it; if a Son of Peace is in such a house, then your greeting of peace shall rest upon him; if not, your greeting of peace shall return to you again." Thus, your heartfelt root of love and your earnest penetration toward GOD remains with the believers who so heartily take up the cause of their friend's soul.

But as for the priest-fiction <note>original: "Pfaffen-Gedicht"</note> of the Soul-Mass <note>the Requiem Mass for the dead</note>, which they perform without devotion, without a heartfelt penetration to GOD, and for the sake of money—that is all false and stands in Babel <note>term: "Babel"; Böhme's term for the "confusion" of outward, worldly, and hypocritical church structures</note>. It helps the soul little or nothing. There must be an earnestness to fight with the devil; you must be armed, for you are drawing against a Prince in the storm. See to it that you yourself are not struck down in your "rough little coat" <note>an idiom for one's humble or perhaps unprotected spiritual state</note>. I do not say that a true believer in the New Birth cannot come to the aid of a soul hovering in the door of the deep, between heaven and hell, with his earnest spiritual warfare <note>original: "Ritterschafft," literally "knighthood"</note>. But he must himself be armed, for he has to do with Princes and Powers; otherwise, they will mock him. This is certainly what happens when a priest, with his white or glistering garment, full of lust, steps between heaven and hell and wishes to fight with the devil.

O listen, priest! <note>The German "Pfaffe" is a derogatory term for a priest, used here to criticize those Böhme viewed as spiritually corrupt.</note> Neither money nor goods are required for this, nor any self-chosen holiness; it is a very precious knight who stands by the poor soul. You take money and hold masses for everyone, whether they are in Heaven or Hell; you ask nothing about it, and you are entirely uncertain of it yourself, except that you appear as a constant liar before GOD.

A heartfelt prayer and wish can come to their aid, penetrating with full earnestness into the torment of the poor captive soul. For such a soul is not in Hell, nor is it in Heaven, but in the gate, in the midst of the torment of the Principle <note>original: "Principium." It is held by its Turba <note>original: "Turba," a Latin term Böhme uses to describe the "disturber" or the wrathful, destructive power of the first principle that seeks to dissolve a soul.</note>, which always seeks the fire; thus, that tiny grasped branch of weak faith sinks down and presses toward GOD’S mercy, yielding itself patiently into the death of sinking away from the anguish. It sinks out of the torment and into the gentleness of Heaven. And even if some souls are held for a considerable time, the wrath still cannot swallow that small faith, and must finally let it go.

But in its glorification <note>The final state of heavenly bliss</note>, a brother can help the soul no further, for that must shine forth from the soul's own essence and will. 11. **Question:** Do the souls of the deceased also have some connection and communion with the souls of their friends, relatives, and good acquaintances during this time, so that they reveal themselves to them?

**Answer:** You ask a lofty question / I do not understand it [by my own reason]; for if I were to grasp it / I would have to be inside the departed souls / and would have to exist within the soul's spirit and knowledge. Well then! Because we are one body in Christ / and all have Christ’s Spirit / we see in Christ all from one Spirit / and have His knowledge / for He was born as a man within us / and the souls of all saints are our members / all generated from one / and all have one will in Christ / in the true bosom of Abraham <note>A biblical expression for the place of rest for the dead.</note>.

Now we have received power / to reveal to you the hidden thing in Christ; for our soul sees into their soul / not that they thus press toward us / but we press toward them / for they are in perfection / and we are in "piecemeal" <note>original: "Stück-werck." A reference to 1 Corinthians 13:9, "For we know in part [piecemeal]."</note>. Now we can answer you / not from the reason of the outer world / but from the image in Christ / and from His and our Spirit. You ask / whether the departed soul concerns itself with human affairs / and sees them, both the just and the unjust? This is to be understood in three ways regarding three kinds of souls / as there are three distinctions.

> “Firstly, concerning those souls / who have not yet reached Heaven / who thus remain stuck in torment in the Principle <note>original: "Principio." This refers to the fundamental spiritual realms; here, it likely refers to the "dark world" or the state of purification where the soul is still transitioning.</note>, in the birth [process] / these still have the human essence with its works attached to them / they certainly search for the cause of their condition.
> “Therefore, many a soul returns with the star-spirit <note>original: "Stern-Geiste." In Böhme's system, this is the "sidereal" or astral spirit, the intermediary between the eternal soul and the physical body that lingers for a time after death.</note> / and wanders about in its house and place / lets itself be seen in human form / desires this or that / and often worries about a testament [will] / thinking thus to obtain the blessing of the saints for its rest. And as long as earthly happenings still stick within it / it concerns itself indeed with children and friends / this lasts so long / until they sink into their rest / so that their star-spirit is consumed / then everything is gone with all sorrow and care / and it has no more knowledge of it / except merely / that it sees it as a wonder in the Magic <note>original: "Magia." For Böhme, this is the divine "working power" or "imagination" that creates and sees all things in their essence.</note>. But it is not moved by mercy, nor does it seek / what is in this world / for it has escaped the Turba <note>original: "Turbæ." The Latin term for "disturber," representing the wrathful, chaotic power that dissolves forms.</note> once and for all through death / it desires it no more / it notices nothing further / for in sorrow the Turba is active; for the soul’s will must enter into earthly things with its spirit / and it refrains from that / it has already escaped the wagon / it will not invite the earthly will upon itself again.

This is a report of the one part / and we say freely with truth / that this part—after it has come to grace—no longer concerns itself out of its own purpose with human earthly affairs / but with heavenly affairs / which come to it through the human spirit / these it sees / and has its joy therein.

But there is one thing more behind this: A living person has such power / that he may reach with his spirit into Heaven to the departed souls / and indeed awaken them / often in questions / or heartfelt desire; but it must be earnest / faith is required for it / to break through a Principle <note>original: "Principium."</note>. We see such a thing also in Samuel / the prophet / whom the King of Israel [Saul] stirred up / so that he revealed his will to him; although some look upon it differently / we say: they are blind without knowledge / and speak their "school-chatter" <note>original: "Schulen-Tand." Böhme's term for empty academic or theological trivia that lacks spiritual insight.</note> / and make a show of understanding / when they know nothing of it in the spirit / and that is Babylon. And then for the second / there is the second [category of soul]...

### Part 4, Chapter 17. ###

Even though it is now taught to the contrary, it is not recognized among them; however, it has a different **alphabet** <note>original: "A, B, C." Referring to the basic fundamentals or rudiments of spiritual understanding.</note> than both parties understand.

One faith captures another; the faith of the living has captured the faith of the deceased saints, and that faith has worked wonders. Is it not so powerful that it overturns mountains? Should the pure faith of the saints then be able to achieve nothing within the faith of the living? It could certainly break the world apart if GOD permitted it, just as GOD permitted the heathens to be converted through such means when they saw that such wonders occurred at the burials of the saints.

Should a soul in heaven not wish to lend its faith to GOD’S honor and wonder-working? It happened in the Holy Spirit, who worked the wonders through the faith of both parties; it is simply the wonder of GOD and His children. But that this path is now completely struck down, and there is now a learned school that despises all of GOD’S wonders—that is **Babel** <note>Böhme uses "Babel" to describe the prideful, fragmented, and spiritually blind institutional churches of his time.</note> and not Spirit; it is envious pride, where men stand and shout: "Follow me, here is **Christ** <note>original: "Christus"</note>, here is the **Gospel** <note>original: "Evangelium"</note>!" Indeed, it is pride, greed, ambition, self-will, and an exaltation of proud Babel.

->40. Question 26. §. 30.<-

12. Question: Do the souls of the deceased also know hidden arts, concerning Divine, Angelic, or earthly things?

**Answer:** Since you wish to ask about arts, whether they know them: they know all arts, as deeply as they are founded. But they may not awaken them so that they appear in the spirit, for the arts are born in the **Center of Nature** <note>original: "Centro Naturæ." In Böhme's philosophy, this is the foundational point where spiritual forces manifest into form.</note> from the **Essences** <note>original: "Essentien." The fundamental spiritual qualities or "being" of a thing.</note> in which the wonders stand. These they sought in this world, as much as was 

<column-break/>

revealed to them in the **Mystery** <note>original: "Mysterio." The "Great Mystery" or the hidden spiritual reality of the universe.</note>. A soul without GOD’S body does not enter into the Mystery in search of art; she stands still in her rest, she fears the **Turba** <note>original: "Turbæ." The spirit of wrath or destructive "uproar" that breaks things apart.</note>, and she gives GOD the glory. But the highly-enlightened souls, who carry heavenly being in their spirit, have the knowledge of heaven and everything that lies in the Mystery—especially those who dealt with the Mystery while here. Others do not usually ground themselves in the Mystery; for each remains in her calling, in what she loved while here. Even if it is such work, they still have joy in it, for in heaven there is a simple, humble child-life. Why would one ask for art? The entire Mystery of GOD stands open. GOD fills all in all; it is a life of pure wonders, all within the Wonder, and all are GOD’S art. They all have great knowledge, but within a paradisical, simple child-life.

Concerning Divine and Angelic knowledge, she [the soul] certainly has much more, for she is in the **Principle** <note>original: "Principio." The fundamental spiritual realm or source-light of God.</note> of GOD. For the son sees what the father does in the house; so too the soul sees what is in heaven. Their knowledge is varied, for the highest knowledge is recognized in the **Majesty**; there, most souls must wait until the Last Day, when they will receive their new bodies. But the highly-enlightened holy souls in GOD’S body and power have exceeding knowledge and recognition of GOD as well as of angels, for they are in the images of GOD, until they also present their wonder-works.

The souls without bodies are in heaven like GOD, in a **magical** way; they awaken no wonders but are under GOD’S altar and await the wonders on the Day of Manifestation. 13. **Question:** We have previously examined the condition of both the saints and the departed souls who still take hold of **Christ** at their final end. Now it follows that we also investigate the condition of the souls of the godless and the damned: is there then truly an eternal damnation?

**Answer:** Every human being has an immortal soul as their own property, like a **fire-spark** from **GOD’S** omnipotence. Just as this fire-spark has an essence, so it becomes manifest in such a life. If the will has nothing of the power of humility, there is no "sinking" down into oneself—passing through death into life—but rather it is like an anxious, maddening wheel that always wants to go upward and yet falls downward on the other side. It is of a fiery nature, yet has no fire-burning; for the **Turba** <term>Turba: Böhme’s term for the "disturber" or the source of wrath and chaos that breaks things apart when they fall away from God's light.</term> is the utterly severe harshness and bitterness, where the bitterness always seeks the fire and wants to strike it up, while the harshness holds it captive. This results in nothing but a terrifying anguish, moving always like a wheel within itself. It imagines, but it finds nothing but itself; it draws itself into itself and becomes pregnant with itself; it devours itself, and is itself its own essence. It has no other essence than this which the soul-spirit always created during its outward life: such as greed, or pride, cursing, swearing, skinning <note>i.e., exploiting others</note>, backbiting, slandering, envy, hatred, grimness, wrath, and falsehood. This is its food and pastime, its way of passing time, for the **Turba** carries the essence along in the will; "their works follow after them." And even if it had done something "good," it happened only in a mirror and outward show, out of a boastful mind; thus, it also remains hereafter in a state of constant climbing and exalting itself. It always wants to rise above gentleness, yet does not recognize it and does not see it; it is a constant exalting of itself above **GOD**, and yet 

<column-break/>

only an eternal sinking. It seeks a foundation, and there is none; that is its life. But if, in its will, it has still seized something pure from **Love**—as many do who finally convert at the very end—it nonetheless sinks into itself through the anguish. Then the humble little spark goes downward through death into life, where indeed the soul’s torment finds an end; but it is a small twig, turning green in **GOD’S** kingdom. And what kind of **Purgatory** <note>original: "Feg-Feuer," literally "cleansing fire."</note> the soul must endure before it is able to enter into itself with that little spark is more than can be written; how it is then held and plagued by the **Devil**, which the "clever world" does not want to believe. This world is too clever, and also far too blind; it does not understand and constantly hangs upon the literal letter. Oh, would to **GOD** that no one had to experience it; we would gladly remain silent. We speak, however, of no foreign torment, but only of that which is within the **Turba**, and of no other power of the **Devil** over the poor soul than his terror and hideous presentation, so that the soul’s **Imagination** is tormented enough therein.

<margin>40 Questions, 18. 15–19.</margin>

With whatever the soul is clothed, that is what it grasps and holds. If it is the treasure, pleasure, power, honor, wealth, malice, wrath, lies, or falsehood of this world, then the severe power of the **essences** from the **First Principle** <term>First Principle: In Böhme's thought, the dark, fiery source of all existence which becomes a "hell" if not tempered by the Light of the Second Principle.</term> seizes these things through the **sidereal spirit** <term>sidereal spirit: the "astral" or star-influenced spirit that links the eternal soul to the physical body and the world.</term> and holds them, and torments the soul with them according to the region of the stars. But the soul-spirit cannot bring these things into its own true shape; rather, it passes its "phantom-play" with them. Since there is no rest in its **worm** <note>Referring to the "worm that never dies," a biblical metaphor for the gnawing of a guilty conscience or the core of the soul's desire.</note>, the soul-worm hangs onto its treasure, as **Christ** says: "Where your treasure is, there is your heart also."

Therefore, it often happens that one sees the spirit of a deceased person wandering about, even riding, often in a completely fiery form, or in other restlessness—all according to how the soul was clothed during the time of its body; thus—

14. **Question:** Is it then not possible for such a soul to reach **GOD’S** grace and mercy in eternity and turn back to **GOD** again?

**Answer:** A thing that enters into an eternal entrance is also at an eternal end. Who can give something to one who is far away, and not present where it might be given? Only that which is in the place where he is can be given to him. A thing that goes out of itself by its own will can take

<column-break/>

nothing into itself, for it does not desire itself. Thus the godless person is judged in this world; by his own will, he has gone out of himself into greed, into pride and luxury, into vice, gluttony, drunkenness, whoring, and banqueting. His will has constantly stepped into contempt for the miserable, into mocking and despising, into plaguing the righteous and suppressing him with force. He has mixed justice with lies and bribes, and has perpetually drunk down injustice as a cow drinks water. His "going out" was bitter envy, yet he held that for his power. His will was wantonness; he did whatever he lusted after. He was a prisoner of the Devil, dancing to his fiddle, entering only into his own greed. He regarded his gold and goods as his treasure, and his will was always directed toward them. He never entered into himself, and into the love of **Jesus** much less humility. To him, the wretched person was regarded as nothing more than a foot-rag, whom he oppressed beyond measure. He considered it art and wit when he could subdue the simple and take their labor. He thought he was establishing "good policy" <note>i.e., good governance or social order.</note> by maintaining such a state of affairs, so that he could do as he pleased, believing it was clever and showed great wisdom.

All this, and much more, he has grasped within his will, and with it, the image of the soul-spirit has been filled. It all stands in his figure, and as soon as the body falls away, the **Turba** <term>Turba: The spirit of wrath or the "disturber" that breaks down the soul's harmony and leads to destruction.</term> in the spirit has grasped all of this. And though the spirit might wish to go into itself, the **Turba** goes with it and seeks the "ground" as the soul's root; thus, the fire is only kindled further. And we give you to know that the souls of the godless have no relief; their best relief and joy is when they rise up in their will within the essence they had here, and desire to do the same even more. They only regret it when they have not tormented a godly person enough. Their will—

But know this: the Wrath has swung its throat wide open and pulls mightily, wanting to swallow everything, for it is the greed and pride that stands against humility. Likewise, Love and Humility have also opened their throat wide and pull with all their strength, wanting to draw man into Love and into Heaven. Here in this life, the soul is in the balance, upon the hinge <note>Original: "im Angel" — This refers to a pivot point or the hinge of a door, symbolizing the soul's capacity to swing toward either light or darkness while still in the body.</note>, and can—even if it has been evil—be born again in Love. When the hinge breaks, then it is gone; thereafter it is in its own land, in its own Principle <note>Original: "Principio" — Böhme's term for the fundamental spiritual realm or "starting point" (Love, Wrath, or the physical world) that governs a being's existence.</note>. Who shall break that which is eternal, where no "breaker" can be found? For the soul is its own maker;

And so that you may see that **GOD** does not will evil, He allows His will to be proclaimed to you; He sends you prophets and teachers and gives them His Spirit to warn you. If you will not listen, then you have allowed the Wrath to hold you; that is also your reward and your kingdom. It pains you that you must be torn away from your own will—from your lustful, proud, and decadent life. Very well: the hellish dregs <note>Original: "Grund-Suppe" — literally "bottom-soup," referring to the foulest sediment or dregs of a liquid.</note> will surely taste good to you hereafter.

We teach you the Cross, and the devil teaches you lust. Now you may reach for whichever you want; that you shall also have, whether Love or Wrath. We labor for you, and you despise us; what more should we do for you? And we are, furthermore, your bodily servants. If you truly do not want it, then go your way and take what is yours, and we shall take what is is ours, and we are parted in eternity.

15. Question: Do the souls of the damned then have no more pain than that which is within themselves? Or are they also tormented by the devils?

Answer: The pain of the damned souls until the Judgment Day is like that of a captured criminal who is always listening whenever something moves, wondering if the Executioner <note>Original: "Scharff-Richter" — the "Sharp-Judge" or beheader; the official who carries out a death sentence.</note> is coming to execute the law and give him his "reward"; so it is with them. They have a false conscience that gnaws at them; they also see their works magically; they see all their injustice, their frivolity, their immoderate finery and pride. They see the distress of the wretched, and their own mockery and arrogance; their false confidence and hollow worship flee from them. But those which are highly damned souls are daring; they renounce **GOD**, curse Him, and are His—

If eternal nature died in the fire, then **GOD’S** Majesty would also be extinguished, and the Eternal Good would turn back into an eternal Nothing. That cannot be; what is from eternity, remains.

The false soul can awaken no other source-spring but this one, which has stood from eternity in the "Wrath-Eye," as if in the <term>Center of Nature</term> <note>Original: "Centro Naturæ."</note>. 2. **Question:** What assurance do we have, however, that the dead shall rise, and that there will be a Last Judgment?

**Answer:** We know / firstly / that Christ has taught us / that a judgment shall be held / not only for the punishment of those who despise GOD / and for the rewarding of the good / but also for the sake of the creature and nature / so that they might be liberated from vanity. And we know / secondly / that the essence of this world must pass away with its torment: Sun, moon, and stars, as well as the four elements, must pass away in such torment / and everything be brought back again; then life will flourish through death / and the figure of every being shall stand eternally before GOD / for the purpose for which it was originally created. Also, we know / thirdly / that our souls

<column-break/>

are immortal / born from the eternal band. So when this world passes away / its essence also passes / whatever is born from it / and yet the *Tincture* <note>Original: "Tinctur" — a spiritual essence or life-force that gives quality and color to existence.</note> remains in the spirit.
Therefore / O man! consider yourself well in this world / in which you stand in the field! You are sown as a small grain / and a tree grows out of you / so look now / in which field you stand / so that you might be found as wood for the great building of GOD in His City / and not as wood for a bridge / which people walk upon with their feet / or wood which is worthless / which is used for the fire / where only its ashes remain / and it becomes earth. It is told to you / that the "wood" of your soul will burn in the last fire / and your soul will remain as ash in the fire / and your body will appear as black soot. Why then do you wish to stand in a desert / even upon a rock / where there is no water? How then will your tree become green?
Oh, the great misery / that we are ignorant / of the field in which we grow / and what essences we draw into ourselves! Yet our fruit will be viewed and tasted / and that which is lovely / shall stand upon GOD'S table; the other shall be thrown to the Devil’s swine. Therefore let us consider / and see to it / that you grow in the field of CHRIST / and bring forth fruit / such as is used at GOD'S table / which never decays / but always wells up / and the more one eats of it / the lovelier it shall be. Then you will rejoice in the LORD!

3. **Question:** Who will awaken the dead, and by what power will they rise?

# On the Resurrection of the Dead.

...say: "Arise, you dead, and come before the judgment." This voice is the original eternal Spirit that holds all life and has always ruled in all **three principles** <note>Original: "dreyen Principien" — Böhme's term for the three realms: the dark fire-world, the light-world of God, and the physical world we inhabit.</note>; for it is the Spirit from which all life has arisen, and in which it stands for eternity, which has been the life and movement of all things, in which the beginning of every life has stood, as well as its end, and eternity; for he is from eternity, and the **Creator** <note>Original: "Schöpffer"</note> of all things.

He has two eternal beginnings, namely in fire and in light, and the third beginning was a mirror of the Eternal, namely the spirit of this world: He has been in this world as a wonder, and through him the wonders have become manifest: and he is the one who possesses the last judgment; his movement is the final one. For in creation he moved the Father, and in the incarnation of the **Word** <note>Original: "Wortes"</note> the Son; and now the last movement and the judgment is his: He will lead every thing home into the eternal place; and this occurs through the voice of the **Word** from the mouth of Christ.

For the Spirit goes out into two principles in **GOD** <note>Original: "GOTT"</note>; as in wrath, as in fire he goes out as the earnest fury of the fire-life; and in the light of love he goes out as a flame of the Divine Majesty; and in the spirit of this world as a wonder of life, just as all such things are undeniable.

And because this same Spirit has the **Word of Making** <note>Original: "Verbum Fiat" — Latin for "The Word: Let it be," the creative command from Genesis.</note>, as GOD’s word with the **Center of Nature** <note>Original: "Centro Naturæ"</note>, from which it originates from eternity, and as the Spirit of the Center goes out in two ways—one in the fire, the origin of the **essences** <note>Original: "Essentien"</note> of life, the ground of the soul's origin, and then the other in the light of the fire, as in the other quality which greens through death and is called GOD's kingdom, where he is the flame of love in the light, and the flame of wrath in the fire. Thus he will also stir the gates of death, for he awakens death and

<column-break/>

has the **Word of Making** <note>Original: "Verbum Fiat"</note> upon himself, and that same **Fiat** is also in the soul and also in the body; and even if it—the body—has long since decayed, the **Turba** <note>Original: "Turba" — the spirit of disruption or wrath that breaks things down and leads to destruction</note> with the body's wonders has remained in the **Fiat**.

Now the **elements** <note>Original: "Elementa"</note> must give back the essence they have swallowed to the **FIAT**, for the word of the Lord is within it, but in its own principle: each must give what it has received: namely, the earth the body, as the **Phur** <note>Original: "Phur" — likely derived from the latter part of "Sulphur," Böhme uses this to refer to the material or earthly substance of the body.</note>; and the water also its essences; the air the sound of the voice of the words; and the fire the essences of the souls; for everything shall be judged.

All words that the mouth has spoken, which the air has taken into itself and served the Word in its making, the air shall present again, for it is the mirror of the eternal Spirit: the Spirit sees this in the mirror.

Now man shall be tested and judged according to heart, mind, and thoughts; for the **Turba** stands in all malice that is against love; there will not be much excusing, for everyone accuses themselves—their **Turba** convicts them.

And thus—understand us—this same Spirit, who is All in All, will awaken all life that was immortal, and with the **Fiat** give it to the body: for the **Fiat** pulls the body to the soul with all its deeds and wonders, with all that he has done here with words and works; everything that has reached the abyss of the soul must come forth.

6. Question: Will the bodies of the righteous then have a different matter <note>Original: "Materiam."</note> in the Resurrection than the bodies of the godless?

Answer: The final judgment is an igniting of the fire according to **GOD’S** Love and Wrath. Within it, the matter of all beings passes away, and each fire will pull its own—the essence of its own likeness—into itself. Whatever is born in **GOD’S** Love draws the Love-fire of **GOD** into itself, wherein it shall also burn according to the nature of Love and give itself over to that very essence. But whatever was worked in **GOD’S** Wrath according to the darkness draws the pain <note>Original: "Peinlichkeit." In Böhme's vocabulary, this refers to the agonizing friction or "sting" of the dark nature.</note> into itself and consumes the false essence; then, only the painful will remains in its own formation and shape.

The Disciple spoke: In what matter or form shall our bodies arise?

The Master spoke: A natural, coarse, and elementary body is sown, which in this time is equal to the outward elements; and in this same coarse body is the subtle power—just as there is a subtle, good power in the earth which compares and unites itself with the Sun, and which also sprang from Divine power at the beginning of time, from which the good power of the body was also taken. This good power of the mortal body shall return in a beautiful, transparent, crystalline, material quality, in spiritual flesh and blood, and live eternally. Just as the good power of the earth—for then the earth

<column-break/>

will also be crystalline, and the Divine Light will shine in all essence. And just as the coarse earth shall pass away and not return, so too shall the coarse flesh of man pass away and not live eternally. But before the judgment, everything must be separated—and in the judgment, through the fire—both the earth and the ashes of the human body. Then, when **GOD** shall move the spiritual world once more, every spirit draws its spiritual essence back to itself; just as a good spirit and soul draws its good essence to itself, and an evil one its evil. One must understand this only as an essential, material power, where the essence is pure power, like a material tincture <note>Original: "Tinctur." An alchemical term used by Böhme for the spiritual essence or life-force of a substance.</note>, where the coarseness passes away from all things. So, shall we not rise with visible bodies and live in them eternally?

The Master spoke: When the visible world passes away, everything that was outward and came from it also passes away; from the world, only the heavenly crystalline nature and form remains. Thus also from man, only the spiritual earth remains; for man will be entirely like the spiritual world, which is now still hidden.

<margin>
Of the Supersensual Life §. 46. 49.
</margin>

Thus we tell you that we shall have a body in flesh and blood, a body such as Christ has; for through His incarnation, Christ is also born as man within us. # On the Resurrection of the Dead.

The <term>Verbum Fiat</term> <note>Original Latin: "Verbum Fiat," meaning "The Word 'Let it be'." In Jacob Böhme’s theology, this is the creative power of God that speaks all things into existence and restores them.</note> clothes the soul-spirit in the true Adamic image once again; for the pure image has stood hidden in **GOD**, in the Word that became Man. Now, as the soul stands at its goal, it receives that image back, along with the beautiful Virgin of the Wisdom of **GOD** <note>This refers to "Sophia," the divine wisdom often personified in mystical literature as a celestial bride or the mirror of God’s glory.</note>; for the image was destroyed in Adam when the woman was made from him, so that he kept only the fire-tincture, and the woman the spirit-tincture <note>Böhme uses "tinctures" to describe the fundamental energies of being—the "fire" (masculine, strength) and the "light/spirit" (feminine, beauty). In the resurrection, these are reunited.</note>. Now it all comes home to each person completely. For the woman shall receive the fire-tincture in the fire of **GOD**, so that she will also be like Adam: neither woman nor man, but a virtuous virgin, without female or male form or members. And here it will never again be: "you are my husband" or "you are my wife," but rather brothers. In the divine magical wonders, something of this will be recognized, but no human regards it; instead, they are altogether only **GOD’S** children in a life of childhood and a game of love.

->40. Questions 30. 59=62.<-

Now behold, you child of man, this is what you have to expect after the breaking of your body; because you are an eternal spirit, you will become either an Angel of **GOD**, or a hideous, misshapen worm, beast, or dragon—all according to how you have committed yourself here in this life. With that very image which you have carried here in your mind, you shall appear in eternity.

->Principles 16. 42.<-

### 9. Question: What follows after the general resurrection of the dead?

**Answer:** Following this is the Last Judgment, consisting:
1. In the separation of the pious and the godless.
2. In the sentence and judgment of the same.
3. In the execution or fulfillment.

The last judgment belongs to the Judge Christ with the Holy Spirit; for here the center of the eternal spirit will move itself,

<column-break/>

which has also divided itself into three <term>Principia</term> <note>Original Latin: "Principles." These are the three realms of reality: the Dark World (wrath), the Light World (love), and the Outward World (nature).</note>: as One in the spirit of wrath, and One in the spirit of divine love, and One in the spirit of the air of the outer world. The last movement belongs to Him; according to the Deity, He is in Christ’s mouth; and according to the wrath, He is in the hellish torment of anguish; and according to the wonders, He is in the spirit of this world.

He was the master-craftsman of all beings, so He is also the one who will give each work its eternal dwelling and gather each into its barn. For He has many helpers, namely the Angels, who shall divide and separate everything. The Judge, Christ, will appear upon the bow of the Three-foldness, like a rainbow; for according to the <term>Principle</term> of this world it is a natural rainbow, but according to the <term>Principle</term> of **GOD** it is the Three-foldness, the Cross with a double rainbow, where one part stands turned toward the inner <term>Principle</term>, into the abyss of wrath. There He sits upon **GOD’S** wrath, which the devils and all godless people shall see; for that same bow is enclosed in all three <term>Principles</term>, and this Judge Christ sits upon it, and in the omnipotence of eternity, over everything that is called "being."

->40. Questions 30. 11. 14. 27.<-

### 10. Question: By what power, and in what manner, will Christ judge all creatures?

**Answer:** Through the Word of **GOD**, from which, through which, and to which all things are. This Word will move itself in all humans and creatures, and exclude all things, and separate everything according to the properties of the <term>Principles</term>, in old forms in love and wrath. For the <term>Verbum Fiat</term> has enclosed this world within itself as a model and established the goal; when all the wonders—which have happened from eternity in the Wisdom, in **GOD’S** <term>Magia</term> <note>Böhme’s "Magia" (Magic) refers to the divine power of manifestation, the process by which spiritual desire becomes substantial reality.</note>—have been revealed and come into being, then the goal is at hand, and no more time [remains].

### Part 4 / Chapter 18.

Seek no further, for it is finished; the Beginning has found the End again, and through the Middle, the End returns to the Beginning as it was from eternity, with all its revealed wonders—with all humans and angels in their being, as well as all creatures, forms, and everything that has ever become *substantial* <note>Original: "essentialisch." This refers to the spiritual substance or "essentials" that underlie physical matter.</note>. The earth with its metals, stones, and all material beings, as well as trees, herbs, and grass—all of this stands in its figure, in the Middle and in the Wonder, but without such *essences* <note>In this context, "essences" refers to the physical life-force or biological function.</note> and life. For no animal returns [to life], but its figure remains standing in *Magic* <note>Original: "Magia." In Böhme's work, this is the spiritual power of imagination or the divine "workshop" where forms are held in eternity.</note>, for it originated from the eternal mirror. Thus, when the outer earthly mirror breaks, it must also remain standing eternally in the eternal mirror as a wonder to the honor and glory of **GOD**. And these same beings all belong to Paradise, for it shall be the holy Paradise where the heavenly elements will bear substantial, tangible fruit. And just as we here in this earthly life regard the fruits of the earth according to their *essence* as dead things without understanding, so too will the animalistic and earthly likeness of this world appear as a dead being; as with all other creatures' beings, it shall stand as a shadow. But Paradise has and bears fruit from the eternal power of life, as from **GOD’S** *essences*.

All of this, which is now mostly hidden from us, is enclosed in the Word "Let it be" <note>Original: "Verbum Fiat." The creative command of God.</note>, in the Beginning and the End, and lies therein as a great *Mystery*. Now the Spirit of the first creation of all three *Principles* <note>Böhme's "Three Principles" are the Dark World (fire/wrath), the Light World (love/majesty), and the Outer World (nature).</note> will move, and before this happens, the Word of **GOD** joins with that same Spirit, like an elevation or revelation of the Deity. Then the Spirit stirs the *Turmoil* <note>Original: "Turbam." The "Turba" is Böhme's term for the awakening of God's wrath or the disturbing element that brings about the destruction of the old world.</note> of all beings in all three *Principles*; then, in a single hour, everything that is in Heaven, Hell, and in this world shall become manifest.
<margin>40. Questions 30. 18 = 26.</margin>

11. Question: In what does the Judgment actually consist?

Answer: The eternal Word of **GOD**, which will move within all creatures, brings all creatures before the Judgment of Christ. Through such movement of the Word, life becomes manifest in all its works, and every person will see and feel their judgment and sentence within themselves. Through such a powerful pull, where Love and Wrath will be in a mighty tugging and driving, each person will be drawn into their eternal entrance and container; for the Word will make manifest everything hidden in all life and being.
<margin>Description of Life 52.</margin>

There, the wretched terror of all devils and godless people will arise, and they will howl, tremble, shriek, and cry out; but the Eye of Wrath of the Judge grips them in their heart, through spirit and flesh, through marrow and bone. For the soul is in the *Turmoil* <gloss>Turba</gloss> with the movement of **GOD**, stirred in the wrath; there they will fall to the earth in agony and bite through part of their blasphemies. The proud will say: "Oh, you mountains, fall upon us! And you hills, cover us from this Eye of Wrath!" They will crawl into caves, into the rocky cliffs, and bury themselves in the mountains; they will want to kill themselves, but death is no longer there. They use weapons to take their own lives, but there is no dying there, only wrath and fury. In this terror, all the buildings of the world will collapse, for the earth will tremble like thunder, and the terror will be in every life, each according to its own torment. The animal has no such torment as the soul, only fear because of the *Turmoil* <gloss>Turba</gloss>, and in this earthquake, all waters rise high above all mountains, so that there is no refreshment on earth, and in all elements, there will be nothing but anguish. All high mountains and rocks burst and fall over; the stars fall down—

The earth, with its severe power—and all of this will happen over different days—just as the world was created, so too shall it come to an end. The earth’s craving <note>Original: "Sucht." In Böhme’s writing, this implies a compulsive, hungry desire or a diseased longing.</note> will, in its distress, draw the stars to itself, as it has always done during this time; and in the awakening of the great **Turba** <note>The "Turba" is a central concept in Böhme’s philosophy, representing the "disturber" or the principle of wrath and destruction that breaks down the harmony of creation.</note>, it will become so thirsty and hungry that it will pull the stars into itself; such an agony will be upon the earth. But the children of **GOD** will lift up their eyes with folded hands toward Christ and rejoice that the day of their redemption is coming, for this agony does not touch them.

And in those same days (which are hidden in **GOD**, as to how many of them belong to this process; for in six days the world was created with its host, which now remains hidden from us), the water will be found again and fill all the depths, even more than there was before.

For now, death comes along, and in that same hour all creatures die except for humanity; and all people who have crawled away into the rocks and mountains will come forth again, but with the agony of their conscience—even though the **Turba** has now subsided, so that the terror stands in death—for the falling of the waters seizes the **Turba**.

Then the **Turba** of every person will say what their nature was: for now, everything will stand before them in its figure <note>The "figure" refers to the eternal spiritual form or "blueprint" of a person's life and deeds, which becomes visible at the judgment.</note>, both within them and outside of them, so that there will be no denying it. For the Spirit tests the soul, spirit, and flesh with the **Turba**; here, everything is revealed.

There, everyone shall give an account of their station: whether they forced themselves into it out of greed and pride and made themselves a lord, or whether their government was ordained by **GOD**.

Look to it, you rulers of the world, you powerful ones, whether you are in **GOD’S** order, whether you are in the right Divine order.

For Moses and Elijah hold the fire-sword, alongside all the highly-esteemed teachers of the Law and promoters of **GOD'S** justice, while those on the right hold **GOD'S** mercy.

# Of the Resurrection of the Dead.

...a hundred years will be as a newborn child, and they shall live in pure love-delight. Everything that is joy will be sought, and wherever one can bring joy to another, there his will is inclined. We will lead a holy, priestly life, and all shall speak of **GOD’S** wisdom and eternal wonders; for the Divine Magic <term>Magia: Here meaning the creative, spiritual power of God's will that brings all things into being.</term> has wonders without number—the more one seeks, the more there is to find, and that is the increase of the will of **GOD**. To that end, **GOD** created Himself in an image—as in angels and humans—so that He might have joy in Himself and eternally rejoice with the essences of His life. Hallelujah.

**14. Question.** It will yet be necessary to explain one thing: namely, whether any memory will remain with us in eternal life of our parents, children, blood-relatives, or other remarkable circumstances of this world?

**Answer.** This world will be thought of no more, for we now lead a new, Paradisiacal child-life. All earthly knowledge and thoughts remain in the Turba <term>Turba: A term used by Jacob Böhme to describe the "disturbance" or "wrathful turmoil" of the physical world that consumes and destroys earthly things.</term> of the earthly body in the fire; we know nothing more of our parents, children, or friends who are in hell. We will all know one another and know each other by name, although the earthly name also remains with the Turba; instead, we have a name from our first name according to the language of angels, which we do not understand here. We understand something of it in the Language of Nature <note>original: "Natur-Sprache." The idea that there is a primal language where the sound of a word perfectly reveals the inner essence of the thing named.</note>, but we have no tongue here to speak it.

No one says to another: "You are man," "you are woman," "you are son," "daughter," "servant," or "maid." Everything is equal; we are all children—neither man nor woman, child nor servant nor maid—but rather

<column-break/>

all are free. Each person is everything; there is only one gender, like heavenly virgins, full of discipline, chastity, and purity. We are all **GOD’S** wife; He is our husband. He sows His power into us, and we bear Him praise and honor. There are likewise round-dances and singing, just as children are accustomed to doing, who hold onto one another and sing in a circle.

All [earthly] art is not esteemed; but know this: those who carried the Mystery <term>Mysterium: The hidden spiritual reality or the "Great Secret" of God's nature that a person can experience internally.</term> within them here, and had it opened within them, will also have great wisdom and wit above others and will lead the others. This is not through compulsion or teaching, but their wisdom begins all sorts of exercises from the heavenly Mystery, so that joy is established. For just as when children run together and one starts a game, so it is also here. The little children are our schoolmasters; before wickedness touches them so that they catch the Great Turba <note>original: "Turbam Magnam." The great disturbance or the awakening of the spirit of this world’s vanity.</note>, they bring their play with them from the mother’s womb—that is still a piece of Paradise. Otherwise, all is gone until we shall attain it again.

A king is worth no more there than a beggar. If he ruled well, his virtues follow him, and he will have his fame in the Majesty; for he attains a beautiful glorification, like a shepherd of his little sheep. But if he was evil, yet finally converted and entered [heaven] by a thread <note>A metaphor for barely escaping damnation at the last moment.</note>, his royal works remain in the fire, and he will be or be valued as nothing more than a beggar here who was pious—and even then, not so beautiful. In the works of each person, one will recognize what each was, when they display their "wares" <note>original: "Kram." Literally "stuff" or "merchandise," suggesting the collection of one's life's actions and spiritual growth.</note> in the heavenly Magic, as children do in their play.

Yet know that it will not exactly be a kingdom of play, for one will speak of **GOD’S** wonders and wisdom—

### 4. Part / Chap. 18.

...regarding the great mysteries of heavenly *Magic* <note>original: *Magiæ*; here meaning the spiritual power of God's creative will</note>; the song of the driver <note>A reference to the end of earthly labor and oppression</note> will remain for the devil's mockery, and for the praise of **GOD**.

One will indeed know something of Hell, but see nothing of it, except through *Magic* within the *Mystery* <note>original: *Mysterio*; referring to the hidden inner workings of spiritual reality</note>; for the devils must dwell in the darkness. The fierce fire within them is their light; they have eyes of fire with which they see, otherwise all other fire is gone, because the Majesty of God has sunken it all away so that it burns only in love. Although there is fire in the Center <note>original: *Centro*</note>, from which the Majesty originates, that same fire is not granted to the devils; they are cast out into the darkness, where there is wailing and gnashing of teeth, where there is more frost than heat.

<margin>40. Question 32. 5. 15.</margin>
**15. Question.** Will the damned then be cast out to some specific place called Hell?

**Answer.** Hell remains in the space of this world at all ends, but it is hidden from the Kingdom of Heaven, just as the night is hidden within the day. The light shall shine eternally into the darkness, and the darkness cannot comprehend it. Thus, the light is the Kingdom of Christ, and the darkness is Hell, wherein the devils and the godless dwell. In this way, they are suppressed by the Kingdom of Christ and placed as a footstool—as a mockery.

<margin>Of the Supersensual Life. §. 51.</margin>
**16. Question.** What will the damned and the cursed do in such a state?

**Answer.** This has been almost sufficiently reported above; for **GOD’S** wrath is their dwelling in the darkness. Their light shines from their fiery eyes, which glitters like a flash of lightning; otherwise they have no light,

<column-break/>

for they dwell at the very outermost edge, and so they ride out in pride over the thrones like powerful knights—and yet each one is different from the other, all according to what kind of spirit they are.

For a dog produces a dog-like nature, a wolf a wolf-like one, and so too a horse, bird, toad, or serpent; but they are all severed and flying, like thoughts. They still have their joy in abominations, and that is their greatest joy: that they mock **GOD**, that they are fire-spirits while **GOD** is a light-spirit. Their glory is always in their strong fire-power; like a dragon that spits fire, so also are they. They seek destruction and find abominations. Fruits also grow for them out of their Principle <note>original: *Principio*; Böhme’s term for one of the fundamental realms of existence—in this case, the "Dark World" of wrath</note>, all according to the abominations of their will. They have a game like fools do who spit fire from rockets; juggling and tomfoolery is their pastime—though there is no time—and even after the Last Judgment Day there is no more fear concerning their torment, but rather their entire life is an eternal fear, an eternal terror and lamentation. Each one has his works in the figure <note>A "figure" refers to the spiritual form or "shadow" of one's earthly actions</note> of what he did here; there he awakens the Turba <term>Turba: The source of wrath or "disturbance" that destroys and torments</term> and rides in the fire. The soul would have no feeling, for it is without the fire; but the Turba, with the introduced abominations, plagues it. There is an eternal despair within them; therefore they are also **GOD’S** enemies.

As for blaspheming **GOD**, that is their greatest strength. They eat hellish sulfur and abominations, for their fruits are such materials—beautiful on the outside, but inside nothing but wrath. Just as they were such hypocrites <note>original: *Gleißner*; literally "shiners" or those who put on a false front</note> on earth, so now their heaven gives them such bread to eat. They are free, enclosed in nothing; they may travel as deep as they wish, for the abyss and the darkness are everywhere—and yet they remain in the same place. The deeper they desire to swing themselves, the deeper they fall.

# Of the Resurrection of the Dead.

...them, and yet they are nowhere at an end or a foundation. Their number is no human number; their joy is a stench of fire and sulfur, because of their vices—that they were once angels and are now devils. When they contemplate themselves, then the gnawing worm <note>A biblical reference to the "worm that dieth not," representing eternal remorse or a consuming conscience</note> first arises, which eats and torments them. Why should one even write of their vices? They are unchaste, evil beasts; everything they pursued on earth follows after them, and they wish to do the same there, drinking down abominations and vices without measure. One can recognize their governance no better than by the *Anti-Christian* horse <note>original: *Anti-Christischen*; likely a reference to the corrupt spiritual and political structures Böhme called "Babel"</note> and by those vice-ridden people who are mad with wickedness; though this is only a mirror compared to the hellish abominations, we do not wish to name them further, for they are not worthy of it.

->40. Question 34. In the 7th<- <note>A reference to Böhme’s work *Forty Questions on the Soul*</note>

**17. Question.** The final point follows, namely concerning the end of the world: It is asked, then, how this world, along with everything within it, shall pass away?

**Answer.** We have already quite clearly revealed this in part in what has been cited: nothing of this world will pass away except for the outward shape of the four elements and the coarse palpability <note>The physical, heavy materiality of the world</note>.

For the outward world was conceived and born out of the inward world, within the inward desire, and was created into a form through the *Fiat* <note>original: *Fiat*; the Latin creative command "let there be"</note>—not entirely as a perishable being, for it was to be renovated in the fire and stand there once again as a wondrous deed of **GOD**. It will not be four *Elements* <note>original: *Elementa*</note>, but One, within which the four lie hidden. For the outward world shall not rule, but rather the inward Divine world shall rule through everything. When the coarse material being—such as the four elements, the sun, moon, and stars—passes away, then the inward spiritual world will become entirely visible and manifest.

<column-break/>

**18. Question.** But when the sun, moon, and stars pass away, what kind of light will then shine in this world?

**Answer.** **GOD** will be the light, and the Lamb <note>A reference to Revelation 21:23, "And the city had no need of the sun... for the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof"</note>; for it is well to know that the governance of the seven spirits of **GOD**, which became parched in the house of this world through Lucifer’s wrath <note>original: *Grimm*; Böhme uses this to describe the harsh, fiery quality of nature separated from God's light</note>, shall again become manifest. For the clear Godhead stands everywhere in a circle, hidden in the heart of the entire Deep <note>The "Deep" or "Abyss" refers to the infinite space of spiritual reality</note>, and the seven spirits stand in the body of the Deep in anxiety and great longing, and are continually ignited by the planets and stars, from which movement and birth in the whole Deep arise. But because the heart of the Godhead hides itself in the body of this world in the outermost birth—which is corporeality—this corporeality is a dark house. Everything stands in great anxiety and requires a light to shine in the chamber of darkness, which is the sun, until the heart of **GOD** moves again within the seven spirits of **GOD** in the house of this world and ignites the seven spirits.

Then the sun and the stars will return to their original place <note>original: *Locum*</note> and pass away in that form; for the heart or light of **GOD** will shine once again in corporeality—that is, in the body of this world—and fulfill all things.

At that time, the anxiety <note>Böhme’s technical term for the restless tension of natural forces seeking the light</note> ceases; for when the anxiety in the governance of birth tastes the sweetness of the light of **GOD**, so that the heart of **GOD** triumphs in the midst of the governance of birth, then everything is full of joy, and the entire body triumphs. This cannot be so in this current time in the house of this world because of the fierce, imprisoned devils who keep house in the outermost birth in the body of this world until the judgment of **GOD**.

# Introduction.

**W**hen we are to speak here of the *Signature of Things* <note>original Latin: *Signatura Rerum*; the mystical belief that the outward appearance of every creature reveals its inner spiritual character</note>, as of the various formations, shapes, and moldings of creatures, of their *Physiognomy* <note>original: *Viſionomia*; the practice of assessing a person's character or fortune from their outer appearance, especially the face</note>, colors, features, sounds, and tones; of the image of man, his inner *Constitution*, *Temperament* <note>original: *Complexion*; referring to the four humors or bodily dispositions</note>, and outward bodily form, appearance, witness, and language; likewise, of the origin of diseases; of the true *Physicians* <note>original Latin: *Medici*</note>; of the highest *Tincture*; of the *Philosophers' Stone*; of the *Universal* <note>The "Universal Medicine," a legendary alchemical substance capable of curing all illness and perfecting all matter</note>; of the metals and their inclinations, etc., no one should think that we will describe these high mysteries so clearly and extensively that everyone will be able to grasp and understand them. For—to say nothing of the fact that such a thing is not fitting for the true wisdom of an experienced man—it is also a work that exceeds our understanding as much as our ability; for there is hardly a blade of grass, or a little worm, yes, hardly a grain of sand on the earth, about whose birth, shape, way of life, and use one would not have to write a large book. We remain within the bounds of our purpose: namely, to gather what our late *Author* <note>Jacob Böhme (1575–1624), the German mystic and shoemaker whose writings form the basis of this text</note> has reported here and there in his writings on this subject—which we could not include in the preceding *Treatise* <note>original: *Tractat*</note> in order to maintain a *Connection* <note>original: *Connexion*</note>—and to present it in a suitable order to the reader for better understanding. If
<margin>//</margin>anyone has a serious urge and pull in their heart from **GOD** to investigate these things somewhat more closely,
<margin>//</margin>and to search out **GOD'S** great mysteries in nature, let them first test their own heart
<margin>Mz</margin>and open their inner self to Him who has the keys to everything that is hidden. Let them cleanse their under-
<margin>//</margin>standing of prejudices, and their will of self-love; thus they will have a key within themselves
<margin>//</margin>to unlock all *Centers* <note>original Latin: *Centra*</note> of light and darkness, of heaven and hell, of life and death. It was also the *Author's* purpose to do nothing else than to give the loving, God-fearing reader and seeker of **GOD'S** wisdom a reason to be moved or brought into a desire—as if into a hunger—for the noble *Little Pearl* <note>A common metaphor in Böhme’s writing for the divine spark or the Kingdom of God within the soul, referencing the "pearl of great price" from the Gospels</note>, which is more precious than the outer world. Through this, first, the wonders of **GOD** may be revealed in us; second, His holy name may be praised and recognized in us and by us; third, the kingdom of *Satan* may also be made manifest and hindered; and fourth, so that man might learn to recognize **GOD'S** will toward him. Also, that man may depart from the useless strife from which brotherly disunity arises, so that the loving will of **GOD** toward us—which is dragged into mere conflict—may be recognized and revealed. For strife is a hollow and highly damaging thing, originating not in **GOD'S** will, but in the devil’s will and desire; from this, the noble image of **GOD** departs, and enters into the true knowledge of **GOD**, His will, and His essence. Now, although reason only cries out: "Bring here the Scripture and the letter!" yet the outward letter alone is not enough for knowledge—even though it is the guide to the foundation. The living letter, which is **GOD'S** self-existent, spoken Word and Essence, must also be opened and read within the guide of the spoken word in man himself, in which the Holy Spirit is the reader and the revealer Himself. Therefore, my intention is to write down the true ground of all beings according to my knowledge and gifts, as the spirit of understanding has opened it within myself, and to keep it as a *Brief Memorial* and exercise. Thus, if anyone should lust to investigate, they may find and experience such benefit within themselves. It is not, however, my intention to lead man into misunderstood, useless arts for which he is neither called nor gifted by **GOD**, since I myself do not lead or engage in them in *Practice* <note>original Latin: *Praxi*</note>. Rather, I only announce the possibility of all things alongside the *Practice* of the New Birth, and give guidance to the outward things to those gifted by **GOD** for it. Since, indeed, the time for the opening of all secrets approaches and dawns: but should anyone give themselves over to curiosity and enter into calamity themselves before they are fit for it and have reached true understanding alongside the Divine will, let them blame themselves for not wanting to follow our faithful counsel contained herein.

Appendix / Ch. 1. On the Signature of Things in General.

# The 1st Chapter.
## On the Signature of Things <note>original Latin: *Rerum*</note> in General.

-> 1st Question. <-
-> What is and what is actually called the Signature of Things <note>original Latin: *Signatura Rerum*</note>? <-
-> Answer. <-

A visible image and meaning of the inner form, desire, impulse, qualification <note>original: *Qualificirung*; refers to the specific qualities or properties that make a thing what it is</note>, and way of life of a creature.
The entire external visible world with all its essence is a designation or figure of the inner spiritual world; everything that is in the interior / and how it operates / so it also has its character <note>original: *Character*</note> externally; just as the spirit of every creature <note>original: *Creatur*</note> represents and reveals its inner birth-form with its body: so also the eternal essence. The essence of all essences is a wrestling power / for the Kingdom of GOD stands in power / and also the external world / and it stands primarily in seven forms / where each one causes and creates the other / none is the first nor the last / but it is the eternal bond: Therefore GOD also ordained six days of work for man / and the seventh day is the perfection / in which the six rest: It is the center <note>original Latin: *Centrum*</note>, toward which the six run with their desire: Therefore GOD called it the Sabbath <note>original: *Sabbath*</note> or day of rest; for therein the six forms of the working power rest. It is the Divine resonance in the power / or the kingdom of joy / in which the other forms all become manifest / for it is the composed Word / or the divine corporality / through which all things are born into essence and arrive. That same composed Word has revealed itself through the movement of all forms with this visible world / as with a visible likeness / so that the spiritual essence might stand revealed in a bodily, comprehensible way; as the desire of the inner form

<column-break/>

has made itself external / and the internal stands in the external / the internal holds the external before itself as a mirror / in which it beholds itself in the quality of the birthing of all forms; the external is its signature. Thus also every thing / that has been born from the internal / has its signature. The uppermost form / which is the highest in the spirit of operation in the power / that designates the body <note>original Latin: *Corpus*</note> the most / and the other forms hang upon it / as one sees in all living creatures <note>original: *Creaturen*</note> / in the shape of the body / and in manners and gestures; likewise <note>original: *Item*</note>, in the resonance, voices, and languages / as well as in trees and herbs / in stones and metals; just as the wrestling is in the power of the spirit / so also stands the figure of the body / and so also is its will / as long as the seething in the spirit-life thus active.

<margin>Signature 9, sections 1–4.</margin>
Thus there is nothing in nature / that is created or born / that does not reveal its inner form also externally / for the internal works constantly toward revelation. Therefore, in the signature lies the greatest understanding / wherein man / as the image of the greatest virtue / not only learns to know himself / but he may also therein learn to know the essence of all essences / for by the external form of all creatures / by their impulse and desire / likewise <note>original: *Item*</note>, by their outgoing resonance, voice, and language / one knows the hidden spirit / for nature has given every thing its language according to its form and essence <note>original: *Essentz*</note> / for out of the essence originates the language / or the resonance / and the *Fiat* <note>original Latin: *Fiat*; the creative command "let there be"</note> of that same essence forms the quality of the essence / in the outgoing resonance or power / the living quality in the resonance / and the essential <note>original: *essentialischen*</note> quality in the scent, power, and form. Every thing has its mouth to—
