It emphasizes that the book is a compilation of the author's (Jacob Böhme's) scattered writings, intended for spiritual edification rather than just intellectual or alchemical instruction.</meta>

# Introduction.

When we are to speak here of the *Signature of All Things* <note>original Latin: *Signatura Rerum*</note>—as in the various formation, shape, and fashioning of creatures, their *Physiognomy* <note>original: *Visionomia*, the practice of discerning character from outward appearance</note>, colors, features, sound, and tone; of the image of man, his inner *constitution*, *temperament* <note>original Latin: *complexion*, referring to the balance of the four humors</note>, and outer physical form, appearance, attire, and speech; *Likewise*, of the origin of diseases; of true *medicine*; of the highest *tincture* <note>an alchemical substance capable of transmuting or healing</note>; of the *philosopher's stone*; of the *universal* <note>likely the *Universal Medicine* or a primary spiritual substance</note>; of metals and their inclinations, etc.—no one should think that we will describe these high secrets so clearly and circumstantially that everyone will be able to grasp and comprehend them. For, not to mention that such a thing is not fitting for the true wisdom of an experienced man, it is also a work that exceeds both our understanding and our ability. For there is hardly a blade of grass, or a little worm, indeed hardly a grain of sand on the earth, about whose birth, form, way of life, and utility one could not write a large book. We remain within the bounds of our purpose: namely, to bring together what our late *author* has mentioned here and there in his writings—which, to maintain a *connection*, we could not include in the preceding *treatise*—and to present it in a fitting order for the reader's better understanding. If someone feels an earnest urge and pull from *GOD* in their heart to investigate these things more closely and to search out *GOD’S* great secrets in nature, let him first examine his own heart, 
<margin>Note Well</margin> and open his inward self to the one who holds the keys to all that is hidden. Let him cleanse his understanding of prejudices and his will of self-love; thus he will have within himself a key to unlock all the *centers* of light and darkness, of heaven and hell, of life and death.

It was also the *author's* purpose nothing other than to give the loving, God-fearing reader and seeker of *GOD'S* wisdom a cause, whether he might thereby be moved or brought into desire—as into a hunger for the noble pearl, which is more precious than the external world. Through this, firstly, the wonders of *GOD* might be revealed in us; secondly, His holy name might be praised and known in and by us; thirdly, that *Satan's* kingdom might also be made manifest and hindered; so that fourthly, man might learn to recognize *GOD'S* will toward him and depart from the useless strife from which brotherly discord arises. Thus, the loving-will of *GOD* toward us, which is dragged into vain conflict, might be recognized and revealed: showing that strife is a void and highly harmful thing, originating not in *GOD'S* will but in the devil's will and desire. From such strife the noble image of *GOD* departs, but through this understanding, it enters into the true knowledge of *GOD*, His will, and His essence.

Though reason may only cry out, "Bring forth the Scripture and the letter!", the outer letter alone is not enough for knowledge, even though it is a guide to the foundation. The living letter—which is *GOD'S* independent, spoken Word and essence—must also be opened and read within the guide of the spoken word in man himself, where the Holy Spirit is the reader and revealer. 

Therefore, my intention is to write down the true foundation of all beings according to my knowledge and gifts, as the spirit of understanding has opened it within me, in its specific properties; I do this to keep a brief *memorial* <note>a record or reminder</note> and exercise, so that if anyone desires to investigate, they may find and experience such utility within themselves. However, it is not my intention to lead man into misunderstood, useless arts for which he is neither called nor gifted by *GOD*, since I myself do not engage in or practice them. Rather, I only announce the possibility of all things alongside the *practice* of the new birth, and give guidance regarding external things to those gifted by *GOD* for that purpose. For indeed, the time for the opening of all secrets draws near and dawns. But if anyone should surrender to curiosity and enter into calamity before they are ready and have attained true understanding along with the Divine will, let them blame themselves for not following our faithful advice contained herein.

->Signature [of Things], Preface, sections 3, 6.<-

Appendix / Chapter 1. Concerning the Signature of Things in General.

# The First Chapter.
## Concerning the Signature of Things <note>original Latin: *Signatura Rerum*</note> in General.

->1. Question.<-
->**What is, and what is specifically meant by, the Signature of Things?**<-
->Answer.<-

It is a visible image and a representation of the internal form, desire, impulse, character, and way of life of a creature. The entire external, visible world with all its being is a designation or a figure of the internal spiritual world; everything that exists in the interior, and however it exists in its operation, also possesses its character externally. Just as the spirit of every creature displays and reveals its internal birth-form through its body, so it is with the eternal being. The essence of all essences is a wrestling power—for the Kingdom of **GOD** consists in power—as does the external world. It exists primarily in seven forms <note>the seven "qualities" or "source-spirits" in Böhme's cosmology</note>, where each causes and creates the other; none is the first nor the last, but rather it is an eternal bond. Therefore, **GOD** ordered six days of work for mankind, and the seventh day is perfection, in which the six rest: It is the center <note>original Latin: *Centrum*</note> toward which the six run with their desire. Therefore **GOD** called it the Sabbath or day of rest; for within it, the six forms of the working power rest. It is the divine resonance in the power, or the realm of joy, in which the other forms all become manifest; for it is the enclosed Word, or the divine corporeality, through which all things are raised into being and arrive there. This same enclosed Word has revealed itself through the movement of all forms within this visible world, as if with a visible likeness, so that the spiritual being might stand revealed in a bodily, comprehensible form. Just as the desire of the internal form

<column-break/>

has made itself external, so the internal stands within the external. The internal holds the external before itself as a mirror, in which it beholds itself in the quality of the procreation of all form; the external is its signature. Thus, every thing that has been born from the internal also has its signature. The highest form, which is the supreme one in the spirit of operation within the power, is what characterizes the body <note>original Latin: *Corpus*</note> the most, and the other forms cling to it—as one sees in all living creatures, in the shape of the body, and in customs and gestures. *Likewise* <note>original Latin: *Item*</note>, it is seen in the resonance, voices, and languages, as well as in trees and herbs, in stones and metals; as the wrestling is within the power of the spirit, so the figure of the body appears, and so also is its will, as long as the ferment in the spirit-life continues to boil.

<margin>Signature [Chapter] 9, Sections 1–4.</margin>
Thus, there is nothing in nature that is created or born that does not reveal its internal form externally as well, for the internal constantly works toward revelation. Therefore, the greatest understanding is found in the "signature," wherein man—as the image of the greatest virtue—not only learns to know himself, but may also learn to recognize the essence of all essences. For by the external form of all creatures, by their impulse and desire, *likewise* by their outgoing resonance, voice, and language, one recognizes the hidden spirit. Nature has given each thing its language according to its form and essence <note>original Latin: *Essentz*</note>; for language or resonance originates from the essence, and the *Let it be* <note>original Latin: *Fiat*, the creative command</note> of that same essence shapes the quality of the essence in the outgoing resonance or power—the living quality in the resonance, and the essential quality in the scent, power, and form. Every thing has its mouth for

->Sign. 1. 16. 17.<-

2. **Qu.** But what basis and **principle** <note>original Latin: *Principium*</note> does this high knowledge have, from which I can conclude and argue that this or that creature has such or such a **physiognomy** <note>original: *Visionomia*; the art of judging character from outward appearance</note>: **Therefore** <note>original Latin: *Ergò*</note> **GOD** has revealed Himself in it in such and such a way?

**Ans.** The true **principle** and the infallible basis of such high knowledge is the thorough knowledge of oneself; for man is **GOD’S** image, in whom **GOD** has revealed Himself according to all three principles. The key to revealing the internal form of all creatures lies in man himself; for as he unlocks himself, so he also unlocks all of nature and every creature. From his own internal signature, form, ring, and sound, he can infallibly notice, test, and taste another's signature, according to the internal taste, smell, and feeling.

Everything that is spoken, written, or taught about **GOD** without the knowledge of the signature is mute and without understanding; for it comes only from a historical delusion, from another's mouth, in which the spirit is mute without knowledge. But if the Spirit opens the signature to him, then he understands the other's mouth, and further understands how the Spirit has revealed itself from the essence through the **principle** in the resonance of the voice. For merely seeing that someone speaks, teaches, preaches, and writes about **GOD**, and hearing or reading the same, is not enough for me to understand it; but if his resonance and his spirit enter from his signature and form into my own form, and mark his form into mine, then I may understand him in the true foundation—whether spoken or written—provided he has the hammer that can strike my bells.

By this we recognize that all human properties come from one, and that they have only

<column-break/>

one single root and mother; otherwise, one human being could not understand another in speech. For with the resonance or language, the form marks itself into another's form; a similar sound catches and moves the other, and in the resonance, the spirit marks its own form, which it has drawn from the essence, and has brought to form in the **principle**—so that one can understand in the word where the spirit has drawn itself from, whether in evil or good. And with that same designation, it enters into another human's form and awakens such a form in that other's signature as well, so that both forms **interact** <term>original: *inqualiren*; a technical term used by Böhme to describe how different qualities or spirits blend, resonate, and work together</term> with one another in one form; then there is one concept, one will, one spirit, and thus one understanding.

And then, secondly, we understand that the signature or form is not a spirit, but rather the container or case of the spirit, within which it lies. For the signature stands in the **essence** <note>original: *Essentz*</note> and is just like a lute that stands still; it is indeed mute and misunderstood, but if one strikes it, then one understands the form—in what shape and preparation it stands, and according to which voice it is tuned. Thus, the designation of nature in its form is also a mute being; it is like a prepared lute-play upon which the will-spirit strikes; whichever strings it hits, they sound according to their property. Within the human mind <note>original: *Gemüthe*</note> lies the signature, quite artistically prepared according to the essence of all essences; and man lacks nothing more than the artistic Master who can strike his instrument—that is the true Spirit of the high power of eternity. But if that same Spirit is awakened in man, so that it becomes active in the **center** <note>original: *Centro*</note> of the mind, then it strikes the instrument of the human form; then the form goes out from the mouth with resonance in words. Just as his instrument was tuned during the time of his **formation** <note>original: *Menschwerdung*; literally "becoming human" or incarnation</note>, so it sounds; and such is his know-

3. **Qu.** But it seems as if this science stands upon a **Spinozistic** <note>original: *Spinositischen*; referring to Baruch Spinoza, whose philosophy was often viewed as reducing God to the mechanical laws of nature</note> basis, where everything is viewed merely as a clockwork in which nature is active, without **GOD** effecting, enlivening, preserving, and directing everything through a special influence?

**Ans.** Our author understands "Nature" not as a being separated from **GOD** that is active and exists in itself; rather, he understands by it the very acting, birthing, creating, and preserving of **GOD** in all creatures.

"At this point," he says, "reflect, and leave me unreproached; I do not say that Nature is **GOD**, much less the fruit of the earth; but I say: **GOD** gives power to all life, be it evil or good, to each

according to its desire. He grants His power to all His beings and works, and each thing accepts His power according to its own property. One takes darkness, the other light; every hunger desires its own property, and yet the entire being is all **GOD'S**, whether it be evil or good. For from Him and through Him is everything; whatever is not of His Love, that is of His Wrath."

The Light-World has one signature, Hell another, and this visible world yet another. From the outward signature, we learn to recognize the signature of the spiritual worlds and their creatures. The entire **Creation** is nothing other than a revelation of the all-essential, groundless **GOD**. Everything that He is in His eternal, beginningless birthing and government—of that also is the creation; yet not in the same omnipotence and power, but just as an apple grows on the tree: it is not the tree itself, but grows from the power of the tree. Thus all things have sprung from Divine desire and were created into a being, where in the beginning no being was present for it, but only that same **Mystery** <note>original Latin: *Mysterium*</note> of eternal birthing, in which an eternal perfection existed. For **GOD** did not bring forth the **Creation** so that He might thereby become perfect, but for His own self-revelation, as a great joy and glory. # Chapter II.
## Concerning the Signature of the Creatures of this Visible World / particularly of the Stars / Herbs / Minerals / and Animals.

->Question 1.<-

From what was stated above, it is to be seen how the inner spiritual world—both the angelic Light-World and the dark Wrath-World <note>original: *Zorn-Welt*; in this context, the "dark" or "fierce" side of nature’s foundational forces</note>—is the ground of all Signatures, shapes, and images of the creatures of this world. Thus, this world is nothing but an image and a mirror for the revelation of that which is born out of the dark essence of fierceness, and out of the origin of the clear essence, which is Light; out of love and wrath, good and evil. Now the question arises: how many and of what kinds are the signatures of the creatures of this visible world?

->Answer.<-

Considering the innumerable creatures of this visible world, the signatures are beyond description. The sidereal <note>original: *syderische*; relating to the stars and the influence of the heavens</note> creatures, such as the stars in the firmament, have their signature in their brilliance, glow, color, and size. The vegetable life forms have their signature in their shape, size, color, smell, taste, and form. Mineral things have their signature in their color, weight, in certain lineaments <note>distinctive lines or features</note>, and also in their tone, resonance, and sound. The animal life forms have their signature in the stature of their body, in the form, the features of the face—especially in the flash of the eyes—and in their tongues, resonance, and sound. Each kind of these signatures is distinguished according to the seven forms of nature <note>A reference to the seven "Qualities" or planetary spirits that the author believes govern all existence</note>; whichever one has the upper hand makes an impression, and according to that impression, the inner spirit of life draws and drives, and shapes the entire body. No single form alone can make an image or signature without the others; however, whichever holds the upper hand in the constellation <note>The specific arrangement of spiritual forces at the moment of a thing's beginning</note> imprints its character and image into the desire—as if into Saturn—and according to that image, Saturn becomes active.

As the quality of each thing is in its interior, so it marks itself on the exterior, both in living and growing things; you shall see this in a herb, as well as in trees, in animals, and even in humans. If the Saturnine quality <note>referring to the influence of the planet Saturn, associated here with contraction, hardness, and darkness</note> is powerful and primary <note>original: *Primas*</note> in a thing, then it is black or grayish in color, hard and coarse, sharp, sour, or salty in

<column-break/>

taste; it receives a long, lean body, gray eyes, and likewise a dark flower; it is quite plain in the body, but hard to the touch. Though the quality of Saturn is rarely powerful in a thing alone, for with its hard impression it soon awakens Mars <note>associated with heat, fire, and conflict</note>, who makes its quality hooked and hunched, entirely gnarled, and prevents the body from growing long; instead it becomes branchy and wild, as is to be seen in oak trees and the like. But if Venus <note>associated with sweetness and beauty</note> is in a certain place in the boiling <note>original: *Sude*; an alchemical term for the seething process of growth or refinement</note> of the earth nearest to Saturn, then the boiling in the Sulfur of Saturn <note>Sulfur here refers to the active, "burning" principle in a substance</note> gives a long, strong body; for she gives her sweetness into Saturn’s impression, from which Saturn becomes quite joyful. And if Venus is not hindered by Mars, it becomes a large, long, plain tree, herb, animal, or human, whatever it may be. But if it happens that Jupiter <note>associated with wisdom and benevolence</note> is nearest to him in the quality of Venus, so that Jupiter is stronger in Saturn than Venus, and Mars is beneath Venus, then it becomes a precious body, full of virtue and power, and also of good taste. Its eyes are blue and somewhat whitish, of a humble quality, yet quite powerful. If it happens that Mercury <note>associated with communication and movement</note> is positioned between Venus and Jupiter, and Mars is at the bottom, then this quality in Saturn is refined to the highest degree, with all power and virtue, in words and works, and with great understanding. If this occurs in herbs, they become long, of a medium body, very well-shaped, with beautiful flowers, white or blue. But where the Sun also pushes in with its quality, the color often leans toward yellow because of the Sun. If it is unhindered by Mars, then the universal <note>original: *Universal*; a term often used for a sovereign medicine or a perfect, divine quality</note> is quite magnificent in this thing, whether it be a human or some other...

<term>Answer</term> <note>original: *Antw.*, abbreviation for *Antwort*</note>. Mark this well: in the earth, there is a constant wrestling and driving of light and darkness and their properties. Now, when Mercury receives the **tincture** <term>Tincture: A spiritualizing essence or light-power that transforms matter</term> or clarity of heaven into its hunger, it becomes joy-rich and uplifting, making that same free delight bodily within itself—that is, gold and silver alongside other metals and good herbs. In this description, it should be well noted that the author, by mentioning **Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sol, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon**, does not only mean the planets in the firmament, but the seven forms of nature. These act as working constellations within every creature, even in the smallest blade of grass or herb, and are ignited by the stars in the firmament.

As for the animals, each has a figure and outward form according to the likeness of its inner life-spirit. For just as **Mercury** took on a figure and image within an element, so too a life was ignited within that same element; the seven forms became active according to that likeness. The ignition of life possesses a certain hunger; as the hunger is, so is the drive; and as the drive is, so the entire body is formed. The inner spirit creates a mouth according to its desire and appetite, and hands, feet, wings, and feathers according to its drive. It looks out through the eyes; it sounds and echoes according to its inner lust, desire, and quality. Those who qualify <note>Function or vibrate according to a specific nature</note> according to the dark fire-world are armed for prey: greedy, fierce, predatory, poisonous, wrathful, and fiery. Those according to the light-world quality are lovely, friendly, tame, useful, and communal. We could make a long description here of the animals, birds, fish, four-footed and creeping beasts—how the eyes, nose, mouth, face, and form of each reveal its inner qualities. But we shall stay with our author, who speaks of this matter only in general; and if a serious seeker is able to break the sealed signs of nature and see through to the ground and cause of inner birthing through a living knowledge, he will easily perceive such a **Signature**.

Just as the form was shaped at the time of the *Fiat* <note>original: "Fiat"; Latin for "let it be," referring to the divine command of creation</note> in the incarnation, so also is his natural spirit; for it originates from the essence of all **three principles** <term>Three Principles: Böhme’s concept of the three realms of existence: the dark fire-world, the light world of God, and the external visible world</term>, and it carries out a will according to its own quality. Now, however, that will may be broken; for when a stronger force comes over him and awakens his inner form with its own introduced resonance and willing-spirit, then his chief governance loses its right and power. We see this in the power of the sun, how it qualifies a bitter and sour fruit into sweetness and loveliness with its might. Likewise, just as a good person might be corrupted among a wicked crowd, or as a good herb on a poor field cannot sufficiently demonstrate its true virtue; for in the good person, the hidden evil instrument is awakened, and in the herb, a contrary essence from the earth is stirred, so that often good is transformed into evil, and evil into good. And as it stands within the power of the quality, so it marks itself externally in its outward form and shape—both in a person's speech, will, and manners, and also in the form of the limbs, which he possesses and must use according to that same shape. His inner form also marks him in the shape of his face; likewise an animal, likewise an herb and even trees. Each thing, as it is within itself, is also marked externally. For even if it happens that a thing often transforms from evil to good, and from good to evil, it still retains its external character, so that one recognizes the good or evil—that is, the transformation. For a person is known here by his daily practice, likewise by his conduct and words; for the primary instrument is always struck, whichever is most strongly drawn.

**2. Q.** What kind of **Signature** <term>Signature: The external physical expression or "sign" that reveals the internal spiritual essence of a being</term> did man have in his state of perfection?

**Ans.** Man was entirely perfect internally according to soul and spirit, in righteous justice and holiness; externally, he presented the majesty, radiance, wisdom, justice, and holiness of GOD, as an image and likeness of the Godhead in which GOD dwells. He was the very same essence of what GOD is according to eternity and according to time in all three worlds—yet a creature with a beginning according to the nature of a creature.
Since the fire-soul was then as if swallowed up in the light-soul, and qualified rightly according to the Godhead, the inner light shone through the outer man, so that the majesty, radiance, and glory of GOD radiated from his eyes and his whole face, just as with Moses when he came back from the mountain. But when man turned his desire away from gentleness and turned away from the inner delight of freedom into the "outgrowth" <note>Referring to the physical manifestation or "falling out" from spiritual unity</note>—into the divisibility of the planetary qualities, out of the pure Divine element into the four elements—then the Divine clarity and glory faded, and the character of the majesty of GOD became entirely faded and unrecognizable. In contrast, the stars and the four elements gained governance within him; the soul-fire burned in earthly **Sulphur** <term>Sulphur: In alchemical terms, the active, combustible principle associated with the soul's inner fire</term>, and the light was extinguished. Man then had to help himself with the light of the sun; in contrast, his face was formed and his body shaped according to his impression and desire, so that one can now clearly see what kind of quality holds governance within him.

**3. Q.** How many kinds of **Signature** must we observe in man?

**Ans.** Two kinds: one internal, called **Constitution** <note>original: "Complexion"; referring to the balance of the four humors and the spiritual temperament</note>; the other external. The internal reveals itself with certain characters in the external as well. The external, however, is again of two kinds: one is called **Physiognomy** <note>original: "Visionomia"; the art of judging character from facial features</note> and consists in the flash of the eyes and the features of the face and the whole body. The second is in the tongue, speech, and tone, or resonance.

**4. Q.** What does the author actually understand by the **Constitution**?

**Ans.** The Constitution is actually nothing other than a certain form, figure, and quality, according to which the fire-soul [acts] in the animal or outer soul, in the spirit of this world, and in the **Sulphur**...

In this description, it should be well noted that the author, by **Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury,** and **Moon**, does not only mean the planets in the sky, but the seven forms of nature. These act as working constellations within every creature, even in the smallest blade of grass or little herb, and are ignited by the stars in the sky.

As for the animals, each has such a figure and outward form as the inner spirit of life has an image; for just as **Mercury** had a figure and image in an element, so a life was ignited in that same element. The seven forms became active according to that image, and the ignition of life has such a hunger; as the hunger is, so is the urge; as the urge is, so is the entire body formed. The inner spirit makes for itself a mouth according to its desire and appetite, hands, feet, wings, feathers, according to its urge. It flashes from the eyes; it resounds and echoes according to its inner pleasure, desire, and quality. Those qualifying according to the dark fire-world are armed for prey, greedy, fierce, predatory, poisonous, angry, fiery; those according to the light-world quality are lovely, friendly, tame, useful, social. We could make a long description here of the animals, birds, fish, four-footed and crawling creatures, how each one's eyes, nose, mouth, face, and form reveal its inner qualities. However, we remain with our author, who speaks of this matter only in general; and if an earnest seeker is able to break the sealed locks of nature and perceive the ground and cause through a living knowledge of the inner birth, he will easily notice such a **Signature**.

# On the Complexion of Man.

Just as the form was figured in the time of the *Fiat* <note>original: "Fiat"; the divine command "let there be," signifying the moment of creation</note> during the becoming of man, so too is his natural spirit; for it originates from the essence of all three principles, and it carries out such a will from its own property. Now, however, that will may be broken; for when a stronger force comes over him and awakens his inner form with its introduced resonance and spirit of will, his superior governance loses its right and power. We see this in the power of the sun: how it, with its might, qualifies <note>transforms the quality of</note> a bitter and sour fruit into sweetness and loveliness. Similarly, just as a good person may be corrupted among a wicked crowd, or a good herb in a bad field cannot sufficiently manifest its true virtue—for the hidden evil instrument is awakened in the good person, and a contrary essence from the earth is awakened in the herb—so that often the good is transformed into an evil, and the evil into a good. And as it now stands in the power of that quality, so it marks itself externally in its outward form and shape; this is true of man in his speech, will, and customs, as well as the form of his limbs, which he possesses and must use according to that same shape. His inner form also marks him in the shape of his face; likewise an animal, an herb, and also trees. Every thing, as it is within itself, is also marked outwardly. For even if it happens that a thing often transforms from evil to good, or from good to evil, it still retains its external **Character**, so that one may know the good or the evil—that is, the transformation. For a person is known by his daily practice, as well as by his conduct and words; for the upper instrument is always struck, whichever is most strongly drawn.

2. **Question:** What kind of signature did man have in the state of his perfection?

**Answer:** Man was entirely perfect internally according to the soul and spirit, in upright righteousness and holiness. Outwardly, he presented the majesty, radiance, wisdom, justice, and holiness of **GOD**, as an image and likeness of the Godhead in which **GOD** dwells. He was the very essence of what **GOD** is according to eternity and time in all three worlds, yet he was a creature with a beginning, according to the nature of a creature.

Since the **Fire-Soul** <note>the primary, energetic aspect of the soul</note> was then as if swallowed up in the **Light-Soul**, and was rightly qualified according to the Godhead, the inner light shone through the outer man, so that the majesty, radiance, and glory of **GOD** beamed out from his eyes and his whole face, just as with Moses when he came back from the mountain. But when man turned his desire away from gentleness and turned away from the inner delight of freedom into the "Out-birth" <note>the external, material manifestation of reality</note>—into the divisibility of the planetary properties, out of the pure divine element into the four elements—then the divine clarity and glory faded, and the **Character** of the majesty of **GOD** became entirely faded and unrecognizable. In its place, the stars and the four elements took over the governance within him; the soul-fire burned in the earthly **Sulfur** <note>the alchemical principle of substance and combustibility</note>, and the light was extinguished. Man then had to help himself with the light of the sun; in contrast, his face was formed and his body shaped according to his impression and desire, so that one can now clearly see what kind of property holds the governance within him.

3. **Question:** How many kinds of signatures must we notice in man?

**Answer:** Two kinds: one internal, called **Complexion** <term>Complexion: here meaning the "temperament" or the specific mixture of the four humors/elements that defines a person's nature</term>; the other external. The internal reveals itself with certain characters in the external as well. The external is again of two kinds: one is called **Physiognomy** <note>original: "Visionomia"</note> and consists of the flash of the eyes and the features of the face and the whole body. The second is in the tongue, speech, and tone, or resonance.

4. **Question:** What does the author actually understand by the **Complexion**?

**Answer:** The **Complexion** is actually nothing other than a certain form, figure, and property according to which the **Fire-Soul** acts in the animal or outer soul, in the spirit of this world, and in the **Sulfur**...

### Appendix / Chapter 3.

The **Sulphur** <note>In alchemical terms, "Sulphur" represents the active, combustible, and vital principle within a substance.</note> of the blood works, burns, lives, and qualifies; the soul is within the **Complexion** <note>The "Complexion" refers to the four humors or temperaments (choleric, sanguine, phlegmatic, melancholic) that were believed to govern a person's nature.</note> as if in a form, figure, model, and dwelling-house—almost as if imprisoned, bound, and enclosed. Understand this: the soul is not the complexion itself, and though one dwells within the other, one cannot grasp the other in its essential essence.

Know further: The soul, in its substance, is a **magical fire-source** <note>original: "Feuer-Quall"; a term used by Jacob Böhme to describe a vibrating, energetic source of life that can be both a "wellspring" and a state of "agony" or "longing."</note> from the nature of **GOD** the Father; it is a great desire for the Light, just as **GOD** the Father, in great desire from eternity, desires His Heart as the center of the Light, and in His desiring will, generates from the property of fire, just as light is born from fire. But now, no fire can exist unless the root of the fire is also present—the center or the form of nature. The soul also has this within itself and burns out of the forms of nature, as if out of the dark world, which drives itself in its torment or desire until it reaches the fire; for it desires freedom, which is the Light, as has been explained in the book *Of the Threefold Life*.

Since the soul is a hungry, magical spirit-fire, it desires spiritual essence as a power by which it may maintain its fire-life and soothe the fire’s torment. Now it is well known how, in Adam, the soul turned itself through disobedience into the spirit of this world and ate from the spirit of the external world; therefore, Christ became a man in our essence so that He might turn it back through the center and through the fire of **GOD** into the Light—into the world of **meekness**—which has now occurred in the person of Christ. But because our soul, from the mother's womb, stands thus turned only into the spirit of the great world within the complexions, it immediately eats from the mother's womb (indeed, while still within the mother) from the spirit of this world.

The soul eats spiritual food, namely from the spirit of the form of the complexions—not entirely of that same essence, but magically; it is the soul's fire-ignition. The com-

<column-break/>

-plexion becomes "soul-like" within the soul-fire. It is like wood and fire toward one another (understand the wood as the complexion and the fire as the soul), for the fire must have wood—that is, either the external complexion or a divine essence from **GOD'S** being. It must eat from one of these or it perishes—though no perishing is actually possible for it, because it is a desire. But wherever a desire exists, there is also essence; the desire creates its own essence.

Now we understand why there is such a difference among people in their will and actions. For whatever the soul eats, and whatever its fire-life is ignited by, that is what governs the life of the soul. If the soul turns from its complexion into **GOD'S** love-fire and into heavenly essence—which is Christ's corporeality according to the angelic world of light—then it eats of Christ's flesh (meaning the heavenly essence), as His eternal essence of the meekness from the light of Majesty. In this essence, the fire of **GOD** the Father creates a **Tincture** <note>term: Tincture; in this context, a spiritualizing or transformative power that "colors" or changes the quality of a substance from base to divine.</note> within the radiance, in that same essence, as in the water-source of eternal life, of which Christ said: *He would give us such water to drink.* The soul-fire eats of this as a divine, heavenly essence, which is transformed in the Tincture into heavenly blood (to be understood spiritually). From this, the soul receives a divine will and leads the body by force to do what it does not like to do according to its own form and the spirit of this world. In such a person, the complexion must not rule in the soul, but stands only in the essence of the flesh and carries out the fleshly governance concerning the outward body. Such a person asks for **GOD'S** Word and has a constant longing for **GOD**; his desire is always to speak of **GOD** and would always gladly taste more of **GOD'S** sweetness, but he is oppressed and hindered by the complexion, so that a constant struggle remains within him.

# Of the Signature of Man.

The soul struggles against the temperament <note>original: "Complexion"; referring to the four humors (choleric, sanguine, phlegmatic, melancholic) that govern a person's nature</note>, for they are now bound together; the temperament struggles against the soul, as it always wishes to enter the soul-fire and ignite itself so that it might truly live. For when the soul eats of God’s Word, the temperament becomes faint and as if imprisoned in regard to the outward life, even though it lives within itself. But the soul is so faithful—especially when God’s Love, which alone comes to the aid of its essence, leads it (whenever it eats of God’s Love-essence)—that it often carries a triumph and a divine taste into the temperament. From this, the temperament becomes trembling and highly joyful, awakening the entire body as if Paradise were now present. However, this does not always last; the soul is soon covered by something else (which falls into the temperament and introduces the outward imagination of the spirit of the great world <note>original: "Geist der grossen Welt"; the *Spiritus Mundi* or macrocosmic influence</note> into the temperament). From this, the soul receives a mirror and begins to imagine into it; thus it departs from the Spirit of God and is often felt to be in the mud, unless it calls again to the Virgin of Divine Wisdom <note>Sophia, the mystical personification of God's wisdom and the soul’s spiritual mirror</note> to return, who is placed before the soul as a mirror.

When the soul imagines into the temperament and eats of it, turning away from God’s Word and Will, it behaves according to the property of the temperament. It accepts everything thrown into the temperament by the stars—everything that the spirit of the great world introduces into the temperament with its imagination. Through the desire in the temperament, the soul forgets itself in all external matters—in everything the world does, in words and works. This carries the desire of the temperament into the soul-fire, and there the soul-fire burns.

Here one finds how all evil deeds and works burn in the fire of God the Father (in which the soul stands); that which is not similar to the Love of God cannot be caught by Love. Here one finds

<column-break/>

what sin is and how it is, and how God is angered when such abominations—as man commits—are introduced into His soul-burning or life. These things keep the soul away from God's Love and make the soul-fire stone-blind to God's Wisdom and Light. For God’s Spirit does not enter into the fire-burning or the life of abomination until the soul departs from it again and bathes itself once more in the water of eternal life. This happens through earnest repentance; then the soul is renovated again in the fire of God’s gentleness and in the Holy Spirit, like a new child, and begins again to drink from that same water and lives with God.

->Temperaments <note>original abbreviation "Compl." for *Complexionibus*</note> 11:::22.<-

From this clear testimony of the author, we see what is actually to be understood by the temperament, and how the soul works within the temperament. Namely, just as fire burns in an oil: if the oil is subtle, pure, spirit-rich <note>original: "Geist-reich"</note>, and heavenly, it gives a magnificent, shining, and glancing light. But if the oil is coarse, earthly, thick, watery, and muddy—like the sulfur of this world—then the light is also weak, pale, and dark, etc. It also produces a source-vibration <note>original: "Quall"; a term for the energetic quality or "bubbling" nature of a thing</note>, spirit, odor, and smoke, which the wise man distinguishes through the inner eyes, smell, and taste.

### 5. Question: How many temperaments are there actually?

**Answer:** Our blessed author speaks of four temperaments, according to the four forms of nature, working toward the ignition of life—namely: harsh, bitter, anxiety, and fire—and according to the four elements: fire, air, water, and earth. However, it is well to note, firstly, that just as no property of nature can work for itself alone without the others, and no element exists without the other, so also is no temperament without the others; but one has the governance over the others. Secondly, just as the properties and elements stand in a constant wrestling match and always give birth to a third through their struggle, so also the temperaments in their constellation always give birth to a third. For example, if two married people come together, and the man is choleric and the woman is phlegmatic <note>Choleric: fiery/irascible; Phlegmatic: watery/calm</note>, they give birth to a third, such as a choleric-phlegmatic child, etc. Thus, just as countless types of life are ignited from the four forms of nature, and countless types of bodies are born from the four elements;

Thus, the constitutions <note>original: "Complexionen"; referring to the theory of the four humors which dictated a person's physical and mental nature</note> of men are, in a precise sense, innumerable. For just as among a thousand people one can hardly find two who have one and the same physiognomy <note>original: "Visionomia"; the practice of judging character from facial features</note>, one also finds few people who are of exactly the same constitution in all things, etc. All these species of constitutions have four main categories <note>original: "Genera"</note>, namely: *Choleric* / *Sanguine* / *Phlegmatic* / and *Melancholic*.

6. Q. What does the author call the Choleric constitution?

Answer. Choleric is the natural property of Fire; it gives strong courage, sudden anger, the rising of pride, stubbornness, and a disregard for others. In the outward world, this form appears in a fire-light; it works according to the power of the Sun and always desires to be the master. If the soul-life is surrounded by this constitution, it is fiery, fierce, rising, and consuming; it also produces such a body that is lean, malicious, fierce, and angry. If the soul imagines <note>in the sense of "focusing the will or imagination into something"</note> into it, she ignites the constitutions even more, for she too is fiery. Then there arises in the human being anger, pride, a desire to rise in power and splendor, to suppress everything beneath oneself, to be a mocker of the miserable, a ruler over bowed knees, regarding nothing even if someone dies in their anger—unless the stars prevent it, which often intervene with a union of constitutions and hinder much.

There is great danger in this constitution if the soul lives in the outward temperament; it has a hard bond when one fire-source <note>original: "Feuer-Quall"; a Böhmean term for a source-fountain or surging quality</note> is bound to another. The fierce Devil has a powerful access to it, for the property of fire serves him; he is also proud and envious, and so is this constitution. O, how difficult it is for the soul to get loose when she is truly ignited in this property! The Devil does not even need to tempt her; she follows his tune <note>original: "nach seiner Geigen"; literally "to his fiddle"</note> quite willingly. She does not easily become sad, for she has a fire-light in her constitution, and she always believes it is GOD-

TES light <note>The word "GOTTES" (God's) is split across the column break</note> and that she is on a good path. Yet, it is a proud, envious, angry, powerful, and oppressive will and spirit as long as the soul avails itself only of the constitution. O, she loves to give a glistening appearance in her splendor, out of her fire-constitution and shine; in her great pride and arrogance, she also wants to be praised as holy. O Devil in an angel’s form, how dark you are when the constitution breaks in death!

7. Q. How then should a person who stands in this constitution behave?

Answer. The person who has their best treasure, the noble soul, in a Choleric house, should above all things practice humility, or they stand in great danger. They may well pour water into the fire so that their noble image <note>the divine image within the soul</note> is not ignited; for the constitution produces great pride, stubbornness, sudden anger, and is loved almost to the point of hard-heartedness. Unless the Water of GOD—namely, noble humility—comes into the fire, then it becomes lovable and gives the first true light. For this "chamber" has its own shine in outward nature; it is certainly not naturally humble, unless it has Jupiter in the sign of life, or Venus; yet even under Venus, it has its devil who plagues it day and night with unchastity. And I say as a warning that there is great danger in this constitution, much greater than in the Melancholic; for here the Devil comes in the form of an angel of light in a fire-glance. He tickles the poor soul so that she makes use of the fire-shine and becomes high-minded; everything is presented to her as easy, and she bites very easily at sin. Swearing, cursing, and light-minded speech that runs against GOD’S name and profanes the soul are not rare in this chamber. The fierce essence of the fire holds the mind...

### 8. Q. What is the Sanguine temperament?

**Answer.** Sanguine, according to the element of Air, is subtle, friendly, and cheerful, yet not of strong courage; it is changeable and easily moved from one thing to another. It naturally receives the quality and wit of the stars <note>original: "Gestirns"; the astrological influence of the planets and constellations</note> into its essence; it is modest and pure, and carries great secrets in its knowledge. If the soul is surrounded by this temperament and focuses its imagination into it, desiring to live within it, then it shows itself to be friendly and cunning; it wants to experience much and succeeds in doing so. Everything that the stars produce, it experiences within the temperament: It is joyful, yet soon loses heart before the power of fire (as if before the "big shots" <note>original: "grossen Hansen"; a colloquialism for powerful or intimidating people</note>), but within itself, it is powerful in its own mind, without needing advice. Through the temperament, it possesses sharp reason according to the outward spirit; it does not easily do anything harmful in anger; it is sometimes uplifting and magnanimous, and then again falling, like the air. It must be careful; the devil is its enemy and cannot do much to it within the temperament, so he would like to confuse it so that it might harbor many different thoughts, preventing it from imagining toward God’s kingdom. He throws strange things before it to pass its time, as it likes to study many things; for the stars cast their imagination into the air, from which it receives many strange, far-reaching thoughts.

->Temperament §. 27.<-

The person leads a weak life, common to everyone, pious and simple; but the devil pushes his enemies against him excellently; he must suffer much, but passes through it easily, just as air passes through something. He is rarely very sad, for he does not carry a fiery heart, nor does terror burn harshly within him; yet he should guard himself against unchastity and idolatry, for in those things, the devil has an entry into the temperament.

### Appendix / Chapter 3.

9. Question: What should the soul do in this temperament <note>original: "Complexion"; referring here to the Sanguine temperament, associated with the element of Air</note>?

Answer: You should also arrange your life accordingly, and in this noble temperament, do not act as a hypocrite to yourself. With your talkativeness <note>original: "Weitschweiffigkeit"; a tendency toward being expansive or wordy, typical of the Sanguine type</note> you discover much; see to it that you do not bring stubble and straw into the Sanguine chamber and think it is the Holy Spirit. For you also have a deceptive light in this temperament; it is indeed human, but take care not to introduce error into it. To live soberly is good for you; beware of drunkenness, otherwise you will fall into the enemy's arms; for you love much, beware that you do not love unchastity and pride. And although you are humble by nature, pride can easily be brought into you: For you carry the house of all stars, like the air and the upper waters. If you enter into the fear of God and conduct yourself rightly within it, you may well find the Great Mystery <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"; in Böhme’s theology, the divine source or "Great Mystery" from which all creation proceeds</note>; but not of yourself, but through GOD; only you have an open chamber for it. Therefore see to what you give your soul for food. For nothing is so good that it may not become evil if something evil enters it. As for people despising you, let that pass, and trust in GOD; it happens to you frequently because of your simple appearance <note>or guileless nature</note>. Just keep what you have and do not use many foreign wits <note>intellectualisms or cleverness borrowed from others</note>, so that you do not lead a foreign spirit into your noble house. It is better to suffer mockery here than distress after this life. If you torment yourself with drunkenness, the devil will introduce much evil and misfortune into the delicate house; for he is hostile to it and has no seat of his own within it, except through the introduction of sin. A lonely, quiet life would be good for you; but you are too talkative and find much, and you also give it away for nothing, like the air. Watch what you let in and what you give out, that it may not be a discovery of the stars <note>merely astrological or worldly influence</note>, but born of GOD; otherwise you will be deceived and will deceive others.

<column-break/>

10. Question: What does Phlegmatic mean?

Answer: Phlegmatic is, according to the nature and property of water, fleshly, coarse, and soft; of a feminine will <note>referring to a passive or receptive nature in the gendered language of the period</note>, of moderate comprehension, but it holds fast to what it receives. Art <note>skill or knowledge</note> must be brought into it through sound and teaching; it does not discover it from its own root. It lets everything be as it is, does not create melancholy for itself, and has a glow from the light; it is neither sad nor highly joyful, but everything is easy and common. If the soul is surrounded by this temperament and blows up its life from it, it is a thick, swollen life, clumsy, almost snowy and slighting, of a coarse body, and poor reason; yet through teaching, everything is brought into one's being. If the power of the moon is not added, it is a very coarse block, and therein almost unjust through the power of the moon. One can carve all sorts of things out of this temperament; the water-spirit takes on everything—now evil, now good—and likes to give itself the appearance of a holy hypocrite, ascribing to itself a pious, righteous life, but it is mixed. Water is deceptive; the soul also does not easily perceive God's wrath and the dark world (which is in its center), but bites greedily at the abominations of the world and covers them under the water-shimmer, thinking it is God’s radiance. The devil can introduce all vices (which he knows in hell) into this temperament where the stars do not prevent it and the soul permits it; he gains as much here as in the fire of the Fire-temperament <note>the Choleric type discussed on the previous page</note>; for sin is lightly regarded here, as a stream of water flows away. He also has the power to attack it with sadness here if it wants to escape him. For he darkens the shimmer of the water with the sins he has introduced and encloses the soul so that it remains back from GOD. But in the storm of the soul, if it wants to escape him by force from the house of mourning <note>original: "Trauer-Hause"; a state of spiritual depression or spiritual captivity</note>, he cannot withstand it here; the temperament is too weak; he can hold on better in the fire.

# On the Temperaments of Man.

11. Question: How should a person conduct themselves in this temperament <note>The Phlegmatic temperament, associated with the element of Water.</note>?

Answer: Just as water takes everything into itself—be it evil or good—and holds it, becoming darkened and troubled by it, so it goes with this temperament. It absorbs the poisonous rays of all the stars and presents them to the poor soul as a mirror. The soul then bites into this and carries out in the body's actions what is merely a magical mirror within the temperament. O, what good, sweet words—like sweet water—are offered without cost, yet they are full of bitter gall mixed in by the stars! There is almost no limit to the deceit; lies are the cloak of hypocrisy, used to present oneself in a looking-glass. Wherever "good Christians" dwell in Babylon <note>original: "Babel"; Böhme uses this to refer to the corrupted, outward church system focused on ritual rather than inner spirit</note>, it is and wants to be counted as divine service. You do not realize that you are doing wrong, but if a tiny spark comes too close to you, it is immediately reflected in your mirror. It would be well to advise you to recognize how you are an ever-sinful human being. You should truly enter into a right repentance and ask GOD for the governance of His Holy Spirit, so that the evil affects <note>original: "Affecten"; the emotional or astrological impulses that drive a person's behavior</note> of the stars may be broken and kept in check, so that the poor soul does not embrace them and thus become a fool.

Truth and justice would be a noble medicine within you; for otherwise, you are gladly full of lies and care little for what you give out or take in. You, poor soul, have a dangerous path to walk through the sea of misery in this temperament; you are constantly defiled by the vices of words and deeds. A sober life will also be healthy for you—always waking and praying, and constantly dwelling in the fear of God. This turns away everything evil from the stars; for whoever lives according to the stars lives just like a beast. But when one impresses the fear of God into the heart, the soul becomes a master over the outward life and forces it into obedience. If this does not happen, then the temperament becomes the soul’s—

<column-break/>

master and guide. Although the soul cannot govern itself by its own power, the temperament presents its elemental mirror to the soul, in which the soul gazes foolishly and allows itself to be captured. Therefore, a human should be a human and not a beast; he should rule humanely with the soul and not with the desire of the temperament; thus he may attain the highest and eternal Good, no matter which temperament he is under.
Temperaments <note>original: "Complex."</note> 116. 122.

12. Question: What is the melancholic temperament?

Answer: Melancholic is the nature and property of the Earth. Just as the Earth is cold, rigid, dark, and sad, so the melancholic nature is dark and dry. It gives little essence <note>original: "Wesenheit"; substance or vital reality</note>; it consumes itself and always remains in the house of mourning. Even when the sun shines within it, it is still sad in itself, though it does receive some refreshment from the sun’s radiance. But in the darkness, it is always in fear and terror of GOD’S judgment. It grants a moderate understanding, yet one that is somewhat deeply meditative. This temperament may grasp much, provided that melancholy <note>original: "Schwermuth"; literally "heavy spirit" or depression</note> does not hinder it. If the soul is surrounded by this temperament so that it eats from it, its fire-burning <note>The soul’s inner spiritual energy, often described by Böhme as a fire.</note> becomes almost dark and very sad. It pays little heed to worldly luxury; through the temperament, it is always melancholic and fearful like the Earth. The Devil attacks it harshly, for he would gladly plunge it entirely into the darkness of his kingdom.

13. Question: How does it happen that the Devil attacks this soul so strongly?

Answer: Wherever it is dark, he gladly enters. He creates phantoms <note>original: "Fürbilde"; mental images or representations</note> for the soul and terrifies it with his malice, so that it shall despair of GOD’S grace; for the soul in this chamber of melancholy otherwise does not provide much that is useful to him—unless it should turn away from GOD’S grace and become completely frivolous; then the—

# On the Temperament of Man.

14. **Question:** How should an afflicted soul behave within this <term>temperament [Complexion]<note>The 'Complexion' refers to the four humors (Sanguine, Choleric, Phlegmatic, Melancholic). Here, the author treats it as the physical "house" the soul must inhabit while on earth.</note></term>?

**Answer:** A soul in this temperament must distinguish well whether she is being afflicted by her own dark nature, or by the devil. Not all afflictions come from the devil (especially among melancholic people); most sadness comes from the soul’s own <term>imagination<note>For Böhme, the 'imagination' is the soul's ability to "clothe" itself in thoughts, which can either lead to light or darkness.</note></term>. When the soul must stay in a melancholic lodging-house, she easily becomes sad and thinks that GOD has forgotten her or does not want her. For the melancholic temperament is dark and has no light of its own, unlike the others. However, this temperament does not belong to the essence of the soul; during this time of outer life, it is merely the soul’s dwelling-house. Thus, the soul’s holiness and righteousness do not reside in the temperament, but in heaven with GOD; for St. Paul says (Philippians 3): *Our citizenship is in heaven.* This heaven where GOD dwells is not manifest within the temperament, but within itself in the <term>other Principle<note>The 'Second Principle' in Böhme’s theology is the World of Light/Love, distinct from the 'First Principle' (Fire/Wrath) and the 'Third Principle' (the physical world).</note></term>. <note>original: "andern Principio"</note>
Compl. §. 64.

15. **Question:** What if the affliction in the temperament were from the devil?

**Answer:** The devil is a proud, haughty spirit. One cannot cause him more pain—so that he retreats sooner—than to take up a fresh courage against him, being completely defiant and high-minded, not being terrified of him. For he has not the power of a single straw; one should only mock him and throw his own fall in his face—how he was once such a beautiful angel and has now become a black devil.

Secondly, one should by no means dispute with him when he brings the **Register of Sins** and asserts his power, claiming he has access to you. Give him no answer to all his accusations. Instead, when he comes and strikes the soul with his imagination, throwing in evil thoughts and wanting to terrify you with your sins, then take up a defiant courage and mock him. If he wants to reproach you, saying you have sinned intentionally and well knew that it was wrong,

<column-break/>

and that you now want to justify yourself with GOD’S grace even though GOD’S wrath is already ignited within you and you now belong to the devil—this is how it enters the poor soul through the devil’s imagination, so that she becomes afraid and thinks: "You are a great sinner; GOD has abandoned you because of your sins; now the devil will cast you down and finish you off," so that she begins to be terrified of him.

When he comes in this way, take courage once more from Christ against him and say: "I have something else for you, devil, so that you can become an angel again; take this in," and say: ***The blood of JESUS Christ makes us clean from all our sins.*** <note>1 John 1:7</note>
Likewise: ***The Son of Man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.*** <note>Luke 19:10</note>
"What would you give, devil, for God to have become man in you? I have an open door of grace forever, but you do not. You are only a liar; be gone! You have no claim on me. Even if I am a sinner, you are to blame for it; you worked the sin in me through your deceit. Now take what is yours—the sin is yours—but the suffering and death of our LORD JESUS Christ is mine. He became a man for the very purpose of delivering us from sins. You worked the sin in me; you keep that for yourself. And my LORD JESUS Christ worked the righteousness in me that counts before GOD; I will keep that for myself. His suffering and death for sin is mine; He died for my sin which I have committed, and He rose again in His righteousness, and has gathered my soul into His satisfaction. Christ is in me, and I am in Him, and my sin is in you, and you are in hell."

You executioner’s servant! Take my sin away in...

**16. Question:** How is it, however, that in temptations the soul can often defend itself against the devil with certain passages from the Scripture, but at other times such a thing will not work?

**Answer:** This usually happens because the Spirit of Grace often thrusts out one passage or another of Holy Scripture with living power against the devil, and then he must retreat. But often the soul wants to defend itself in its own self-will with the <term>bare letter<note>The 'bare letter' refers to intellectual knowledge of the Bible without the inner, living power of the Holy Spirit.</note></term> and dispute with him from the Holy Scripture; yet that only makes the trouble worse. Let your mind hold no kind of dispute with him; he is not worthy of it. Simply impress this one little verse upon yourself—you have enough in it, and you need no more comfort in your terror:
> **The blood of JESUS Christ, the Son of GOD, cleanses us from all our sins.**

Wrap all your

<column-break/>

senses in this; let no other thought leave you. Let the devil suggest to you whatever he wants through his <term>imagination<note>For Böhme, the devil works by projecting dark images into the soul's 'imagination' to lead it into despair.</note></term>; just think: everything the devil says is a lie. But this verse is true; hold the verse as your own, and let him suggest whatever he wishes. Do not seek many verses in a moment of terror; he is too cunning for you, and he will snatch the first and best one out of your heart so that you forget it or doubt it. Simply wrap the soul in this one; it is strong enough to resist him. You may (while you wrap your soul in it) truly mock him; he cannot touch you and will not wait long. If you only do not yield to him, he will become a laughingstock before his other servants in man, and even before the holy angels; then he flees from all things before you can even mock him. Repeat the verse, take it into your heart, and draw a defiant courage against him. The Spirit that stays within the verse will surely stand by you. Though the soul trembles before him, stand in wrath against him as if you were risking your life; nothing will happen to you. He may not apply <note>Possible misprint for "anlegen" (to apply/exert power).</note> any power, nor does he have any, while man lives in this time; he may do nothing to him. 

For Christ has opened the Door of Grace, which stands open to the poor sinner while he lives on earth; that same Door of Grace is open in the human soul. Christ has burst the firm lock (which was shut within GOD’S wrath) in his soul. Now all souls <term>in-qualify [inqualiren]<note>A Böhme-specific term meaning to work, resonate, or operate together within a shared essence or quality.</note></term> as one; they all come from one, and are all together only a single tree with many branches. His shattering [of the lock] has gone out upon all souls, from him to Adam and to the last human being. The Door of Grace stands open to all; GOD has barred it to no one except the one who does not want it. The sign of his entrance into humanity is manifest to all souls, just as was sufficiently proven above.

# Concerning the Temperament of Man.

**17. Question:** How should those souls behave who are not so much tempted by the Devil, but by the melancholic temperament <note>Original: "Complexion." In the 17th century, this referred to the four humors—Sanguine, Choleric, Phlegmatic, and Melancholic—which were believed to determine a person's physical and mental health.</note>?

**Answer:** If the Devil does not come with the terror of fear, then he is not there; rather, it is the soul’s own dread before the dark abyss, which recoils in terror before GOD’S wrath. It often happens that the most holy souls become thus obscured and saddened; GOD also frequently permits it so that they might be tested, to wrestle for the noble little wreath of the knight. For when the soul attains the little wreath of the Holy Spirit with storming and great steadfastness in the struggle, it is much more noble and beautiful than if it were placed upon the soul only after the death of the body; for the Revelation of JESUS Christ says: *To him who overcomes, I will give to sit with me on my throne, as I have overcome, and have sat with my Father on his throne.* <note>Reference to Revelation 3:21.</note> Likewise: *To him who overcomes, I will give to eat of the hidden manna, and will give him a good testimony, and with the testimony a new name written, which no one knows except him who receives it.* <note>Reference to Revelation 2:17.</note> Often the stars have an evil conjunction <note>A term from astrology meaning two celestial bodies appearing in the same area of the sky, believed to exert a combined influence.</note> or meeting, often an eclipse of the Sun and Moon; then, if Mars <note>In this context, Mars represents the fiery, aggressive, or "poisonous" spiritual quality in the cosmos.</note> throws its poison-rays into it, and the conjunction happens in an earthly sign in the melancholic chamber, it mightily terrifies those souls who are surrounded by a melancholic temperament; they constantly think it is the fierce wrath of GOD, or the Devil, coming to fetch the soul. For the soul feels the poison-rays of Mars within the temperament, and seeing that she is in a dark lodging, she thinks GOD has rejected her and wants nothing to do with her—especially when she imagines <note>In the author's philosophy, "imagination" is a creative power of the will that "shapes" the soul's internal reality.</note> herself into that temperament and searches so deeply that she eats of the poison of Mars, blowing up her fire-life with it; then there is great bitter anxiety and fear of the De-

<column-break/>

-vil and GOD'S wrath within her. Then she speculates and thinks that GOD has not predestined her in Christ for eternal life; she is so anxious that she does not like to lift her face to GOD, thinking always that she is one of the greatest of sinners and that the door of grace is shut. Yet in truth, it is nothing other than a fantasy of the stars within the temperament, wherein the soul torments itself. When the Devil sees this, he shoots his imagination into it, tormenting the poor soul even more; but he has no power, for only the torment of anxiety is the torment of his life; he likes to be near it, for he is anyway an enemy of the human race.

Therefore, no one who is tempted by sadness should imagine, when this assails him through his temperament, that it is due to GOD’S disfavor and wrath; it is a fantasy of the temperament and the stars. ->§. 64 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ 103.<-

Thus much regarding what our author has written about the **temperaments** <term>Complexions: The four humors or constitutional types (Choleric, Sanguine, Phlegmatic, Melancholic) thought to determine human character.</term>; as mentioned above, every temperament has seven properties: for instance, **Choler** <note>The "Choleric" temperament, associated with fire and bile.</note> is either **Saturnine**, **Jovial**, **Martial**, **Venereal**, **Mercurial**, or **Lunar**; each of these properties creates a distinct kind of Choler. Likewise, the **Sanguine** and **Phlegmatic** temperaments, as well as **Melancholy**, are either **Saturnine**, **Jovial**, **Martial**, etc. Each of these types of Choler, Phlegm, and Melancholy has its own constellation and gives birth to a third. And as the properties of nature stand in a constant struggle, so too does a person rarely have the same temperament as another, and the temperaments themselves change within the person. For just as the air is easily bound by **Saturn** and becomes water, and water can be contracted and become earth, so too can a Sanguine temperament become Phlegmatic, and a Phlegmatic temperament become Choleric. Thus, Choler especially—where it is **Mercurial** and **Saturn** enters into the drive—can degenerate into Melancholy.

Just as every person has an inner constellation, and as the soul stands within a temperament, so also does the Grace of GOD work within it,

<column-break/>

from which that one effective Grace is revealed in so many kinds of gifts of Grace; the **heavenly Magus** <note>A term for a spiritually enlightened person or Christ acting as the master of divine mysteries.</note> distinguishes all of these, rejoicing inwardly in them as part of GOD’S order, and holily praises GOD’S manifold wisdom. But he who does not have the spirit of discernment, but wishes to judge everything according to his own urge and **quality** <term>Quall: A term used in mystical writing to describe the "source-spring" or the inherent driving nature of a being.</term>, is called the **Whore of Babylon** <note>original: "Hure zu Babel." A symbolic reference to the false, prideful, and divisive spirit of the world or the corrupted church.</note>.

Does one herb, flower, or tree say to another: "You are sour and dark; I do not wish to stand beside you"? Do they not all have one mother from which they grow? So also are all souls from One, and all men from One. Why do we boast of being children of GOD, when we are yet more foolish than the flowers and the herbs of the field? Is it not also thus with us, that GOD reveals His wisdom in us? Just as He reveals the **tincture** <note>A spiritual essence or "hidden light" within nature.</note> of hiddenness in the earth through the earth with beautiful plants, so He does also in us humans; we should rather rejoice in this and love one another heartily, that GOD reveals His *wisdom* in us in such manifold ways. But he who judges and condemns in a godless way, running only in pride to make himself seen, he is the driver of **Babylon**, a turning wheel that only puffs up strife.

# Chapter IV.
## Concerning the external Signature of Man, such as Physiognomy, and Lineaments in general.

---

->1. Question.<-

We have considered the inner condition of the soul and the external temperament in which the soul is active, as if contained in a mold; now follows: how is each property of the soul formed through the temperament into the external body?

->Answer.<-

This external image and **signature** <term>Signatur: The belief that the inner spiritual essence of a thing is "signed" or marked upon its outward physical form.</term> is, as mentioned, of two kinds; one is **Physiognomy** <note>original: "Visionomia." The practice of assessing a person's character from their outer appearance, especially the face.</note>, the second is the tongue and speech of

<column-break/>

man. As far as **Physiognomy** is concerned, it is found either in the entire posture of the person, or in the flash of the eyes, or in the **lineaments** (the shape and image of the forehead, the nose, the mouth, the chin, and the remaining parts of the face), as well as in the inner drawing of the lines in the hollow of the hand—the knowledge of which signature is called **Palmistry** <note>original: "Chiromantia."</note>. It is not our intention here to interpret and point out all these lineaments and signatures according to their circumstances; so many books have already been written about this that the world can hardly carry them, yet most of it is miserably abused,

and

## On the Origin of Human Diseases / and their
## Various Kinds.

Having considered the various complexions, forms, signatures, **Visionomia**, and speech, it is fitting to investigate here what our blessed author has reported here and there concerning the origin and basis of diseases / of their kinds, forms, and types; of the necessary qualities of a physician, of proper medicines and their preparation; accordingly, the question is asked:

->1. Question.<-

From where have all diseases in the human body arisen?

->Answer.<-

When Adam was created in Paradise / he had the **heavenly Mercury** <note>In the alchemical philosophy of Jacob Böhme, Mercury represents the vital spirit or the "Word" that animates the body.</note> as his guide / his life burned in a pure **Oil** <note>Likened to a "divine fuel" or the "radical moisture" that sustains life without consuming it.</note> / therefore his eyes were heavenly / and his understanding surpassed nature / for his light shone in the Oil of the **Divine Essence**; the external watery quality was not manifest in his Oil / he was **iliastric** <term>Iliastric: A term used by Paracelsus and Böhme to describe things that are eternal, celestial, and not subject to decay.</term> / that is, angelic / and in the Fall he became **cagastric** <term>Cagastric: A term for things that are corruptible, subject to the "star" of mortality and decay.</term> / that is / the watery quality in the deadly property became manifest in its Oil / and broke through; Thus the **Mercury** in him became an **anguish-poison**, which previously in his Oil was an exaltation of the kingdom of joy. Thus in Mercury the death-poison began to **qualify** <note>In this context, to "qualify" means to take on an active, specific property or power.</note> / and the **wrath-torment** became burning in the eternal **Mars** <note>Original: "Marte." In alchemical terms, Mars represents the fierce, burning fire of nature.</note> / and the dark **Impression** of the eternal property of nature took hold of him / his body, in the dark Impression and in the poison of the ignited Mercury, became as earth / and its enmity against

<column-break/>

GOD / it was all over for him / and there was no counsel for any creature / neither in heaven / nor in this world / grim death had captured him in soul and body.

All properties awoke in the grimness and poison-torment in the essence of the body / each one affected the body according to its ignited selfhood / from this arose hostility and adversity in the essence of the body / so that one property is against the other / one taste against the other; everything departed from the **Temperament** <term>Temperament: Here used in the sense of a perfect balance (temperature) where all qualities are harmonized.</term> / and from this arose pain, sickness, and death.

**4. Question: How many kinds of diseases have then become manifest in the human body?**
**Answer:** After man turned his will away from **Unity**, and introduced it into the divisibility of properties, his evil lusts and desires, and consequently his diseases, became innumerable. These innumerable diseases are conveniently divided into two parts: namely, into **Heat** and **Cold**. Our author calls the latter **Saturnine** <note>Associated with the planet Saturn, representing coldness, contraction, and melancholy.</note>; the physicians call them **tartaric** <note>original: "tartarische." The former are **mercurial**, **martial** <note>Associated with Mars: fiery, aggressive, or inflammatory.</note>, and **venereal** <note>Associated with Venus: relating to desire or the blood.</note> diseases, arising from a superfluous, overly sharp **acid** <note>original: "Acido."</note>, or a sharp, stinging, fierce quality—a gnawing, eating, biting **corrosive** <note>original: "Corrosiv."</note>. Understand every disease and ache / as a property of death / for **Mercury** has ignited and burnt itself too much either in heat or cold / whereby the essence or flesh / which he drew to himself in his desire / as in his mother in the **Sulphur** <note>original: "Sulphur." In this context, Sulfur represents the "mother" or the combustible, substantial ground of the body.</note> / has been burnt / whereby the earthliness arises / both in water and flesh. Just as the matter of the earth and the stones / as the coarseness of the same / is nothing other than a burnt **Sulphur** and water in the property of **Mercury** / where the **nitre** <note>original: "Salniter." A reference to saltpeter, which Böhme uses to symbolize a sudden, explosive, or "lightning-like" spiritual force.</note> in the **terror** <note>original: "Schracke." A sudden flash or shock that causes matter to "freeze" or "frighten" into a specific form.</note> of the mercurial wheel / from which the various salts arise / was burnt / there-

This is why **GOD** cursed the earth / for from the mercurial wheel its good (namely the desire of love / which arises in eternal freedom / and reveals itself through this mercurial wheel through cold and heat / and goes out through the fire / and makes a shine of light / ) was withdrawn / and the curse was introduced into it / that is, a fleeing of the desire of love.
