## Of a Righteous Physician / and the True Cure, along with the Foundation of Medicines and Healing Agents.

We have seen the true origin of diseases, and their many types. It follows now to investigate the foundation of a **righteous physician**, what is required for such a role, as well as the necessary cure and the properties of a true medicine.

-> What exactly is a righteous physician? <-

This refers to a state of balance or "temperament" where no single property dominates the others.</note>. # ->Of a Righteous Physician.<-

You must become a merciful Samaritan; otherwise, you cannot heal that which is wounded and broken. For the body that you are meant to heal is half-dead and severely wounded; furthermore, its proper clothing has been stripped off, so that you would hardly recognize the man you are meant to heal unless you possessed the Samaritan’s eyes and will—seeking nothing else through them but to restore the damage of the wounded person.

Consider this: the eternal Word revealed itself in Adam with Divine living essence, with the heavenly **Mercury** <note>original: *Mercurio*. In Böhme's alchemy, Mercury represents the active, moving spirit or "word" within a substance.</note>. However, when the soul-fire in Adam—through the Devil's infection—poisoned the spirit of the will and led it into earthly, deadly lust through the nature of the Serpent, the heavenly Mercury withdrew from the heavenly essence. That is to say, the soul's will departed from it with its desire and led its hunger into the earthly, deadly essence, into the property of the **cold Mercury** which had created stones and earth. Adam’s spirit wanted to test this and possess the knowledge of Good and Evil; but he was seized by the properties of the night, by the cold, deadly Mercury. This now ruled within him, just as it does in the earth since **GOD** cursed it.

If you now wish to be a **Magus** <note>A "Magus" is a wise practitioner who understands the hidden spiritual forces of nature and can work with them.</note>, you must have the understanding of how you can transmute the night back into day. For the night, as the torment of darkness, is the anguish-torment of death; and the day, as the torment of light, is life and a radiance within life. This radiance **Christ** has rekindled in humanity and has made man alive within himself again. If you now wish to **tinge** <note>original: *tingiren*. To "tinge" is to apply a <term>Tincture</term>, a concentrated spiritual essence that transforms a base or diseased substance into a perfected, healthy state.</note>, you must transmute that which lies locked in the death of night back into the day; for the day is the **Tincture**, and yet day and night lie within one another as one single being.

<note>Signat. 7. §. 40-43.</note>

<column-break/>

Accordingly, it is necessary for the **Physician** <note>original: *Medico*</note> to take note and learn to recognize the distinction of which property is the strongest in every thing with which he wishes to cure. If he does not know this, he will often give death to his patient. It is also necessary for him to know the patient’s property, and in what manner the Mercury within the **Sulphur** <note>Sulphur represents the soul-principle or the combustible, oily essence of a thing.</note> exists among the seven forms of nature; for it is such a thing that creates a **Salt** <note>Salt represents the physical, contracting principle that gives a thing its body.</note>. Now, if the Physician gives him a contrary Salt, the Mercury will only be further angered by it and become more poisonous. But if he can receive his own Salt according to his property (for which he hungers), then he rejoices and lets his poison-torment sink into **Mars's fire** <note>Mars represents the fiery, energetic, and sometimes aggressive aspect of nature.</note>. 

But the true Physician has another cure: he leads his Mercury—with which he intends to cure—out of the death-anguish into freedom beforehand. Such a man may cure; the other way is dangerous and uncertain. If he succeeds, it is a matter of luck and a fleeting thing, and he cannot drive a sickness out from its foundation. For the outer Mercury is locked up; it can reach no further than into the four elements, into the deadly essence; it has no power in the sidereal <note>Refers to the "astral" or star-influenced body that mediates between the physical and the spiritual.</note> body. But if it is turned around and led into Love, then it attacks the root and the foundation and renovates even unto the Divine power, unto the other **Principle**.

<note>Signat. 8. 14. 15.</note>

Thus it belongs to the Physician to know how to deal with medicines in **Equality** <note>The principle of *Homeopathy* or "like cures like."</note>, so that he does not also anger them and lead them into another property. For they are in their property just like a human life; he must see that they remain in their **degree** <note>original: *Gradu*. The specific level of intensity or "potency" of a natural property.</note> as they were originally born in their mother; for no thing is able to rise higher than it is in the **Center of its origin** <note>original: *Centro seines Urstandes*</note> according to its hiddenness. etc.

<note>Signat. 13. §. 56.</note>

### Appendix / Chapter 6.

Therefore, if you dear lords and brothers wish to be called Doctor and Master, you must also know how you may **transmute** <term>transmutiren: to transform the inner nature of a substance or spirit from one state to another</term> the ignited, poisonous **Mercury** <term>Mercurium: in Böhme's thought, the active, moving life-force or "word" within all things</term> in all things—according to all its properties—into Love. This must be done so that it is released from the torment of anguish and placed into a state rich in joy, just as the earthly is changed into a heavenly thing, and death into a life. This is your doctorate in the true understanding, and not through the **Magistrate** <note>original: *Amtmann*. Böhme uses this term to represent "Reason," which acts like a worldly official—useful for external order but blind to internal spiritual mysteries.</note> of Reason alone. **GOD** has set man over the Magistrate and ordered him into the Understanding as his own dominion; he has the power to transmute nature and to set the Evil into a Good, provided he has first transmuted himself; otherwise, he cannot. As long as he is dead in his Understanding, he remains the servant and minister of the Magistrate (Reason); but when he becomes alive in **GOD**, then the Magistrate becomes his servant. You proud little huts <note>A metaphorical jab at scholars who take pride in their physical bodies or limited intellectual structures.</note>, let it be told to you: pride and self-honor, as well as earthly fleshly lust, lie in your way, so that you are not Masters in the mysteries, but rather blind children. You do not wish to lay your hands upon the coals, but you take money from the wretched and give to many that which it would be better they had never bought; for this, you shall give a heavy account.
<margin>Signat. 8. 27. 29. <note>References to Böhme’s work "De Signatura Rerum."</note></margin>

3. Question: Does a human being also have so much power in nature that he may transmute the wrath into love, and overcome and subdue the ignited wickedness within the creatures?

Answer: The power of the Most High has given a fixed perfection to all and every thing according to its property; for as Moses says: "Everything was very good." However, with the Curse, the **Turba** <term>Turba: the "turmoil" or "interruption"—the source of strife and decay that entered nature after the Fall</term> was introduced, so that the properties stand in the strife of the **Mercury**. But in every property, in every herb, or whatever it may be that ever grows or arises from the seething of the four elements, there is also a

<column-break/>

**Fixed** <note>In alchemy, a "fixed" substance is stable and resists the fire, representing the eternal, perfected state.</note> thing hidden within. For all things that are in the four elements have originally sprung from the eternal element, in which there is no strife, neither heat nor cold, but rather an equal weight of all properties in a play of love, just as it is in Paradise; and that same Paradise bloomed in the beginning of this world through the earth before the Curse. Thus, it is still hidden in all things and may yet be opened through understanding and art, so that the first virtue overcomes the ignited wickedness. Although we humans may not have the full authority to proceed by our own power, it nevertheless happens by **GOD's** permission, He who has turned His mercy back toward us and has reopened Paradise and its concept within man. If **GOD** has given us power to become His children and to rule over the world, why not also over the curse of the earth? No one should consider it impossible; it requires only a Divine understanding and knowledge. This shall bloom in the **Time of the Lilies** <note>A prophetic term used by Böhme to describe a coming age of spiritual enlightenment and peace.</note>, and not in **Babylon** <note>original: *Babel*. Refers to the "confused" and prideful systems of false scholars and churches.</note>, for whom we have written nothing.
<margin>Signat. 13. 60. 61.</margin>

4. Question: We have heard what is required of a righteous **Physician** <note>original: *Medico*</note>; it follows now to investigate: what is the cure or recovery from diseases?

Answer: Firstly, for the actual cure of a disease, a good **Medicine** <note>original: *Artzney*</note> is required; secondly, a wise and well-ordered application of that medicine. Medicine is generally nothing other than a means by which the ignition of the **Mercury** or the life-spirit—whether it be from heat or cold—is soothed and placed into a state of equality. Therefore, the medicine must be of that same equality; but it must first be released from the cold (as from the ignited cold wrath) and brought into gentleness. Then it also stills the hunger of the cold desire in the sickness of the body. For if one gives ignited heat to the ignited cold, the cold is terrified by the...

### 6th Question: How many kinds of medicine are then necessary for a cure?

**Answer:** Not many kinds are necessary for this, but one single **medicine**. For everything—white and thin, sweet and sour, cold and warm—originates from Unity. One must seek that which is nearest to Unity, wherein the most noble ground of Divine Revelation lies in power and effect within the fiery hardness, being a "dry unity" as a **Temperamentum** <term>Temperamentum: A balanced state where all opposing qualities (hot, cold, wet, dry) are in perfect harmony or "tempered"</term>, in which the suitability of all powers resides again. For where the powers do not reside in the unity of one will, there the will is divided, and no great power is to be understood in that thing. This is well for physicians to note: that they should not look upon the coarse spirits of strong **scent** <term>Ruch: An archaic term for scent or "Ruach" (spirit/breath), referring here to volatile essential oils or the "soul" of the plant</term> and take it for the right **Balm** <term>Balsam: A healing, soothing spiritual essence</term>; for although it is within there, the **Tincture** <term>Tinctur: The highest spiritual essence or "color" of a substance that can transform others</term> within is very mobile and prone to flying away.

The spirits of strong power in the **scent** must be brought into the **Temperamentum**, as if into Unity, and not fly away from it. Otherwise, one seeks to cure with the salt as if with the sharpness of fire, and gives the patient "soul without spirit." The soul of such balms is divided in its properties; each gives itself particularly in its great joy, and yet in that division they are too antagonistic. They do not unify the enmity and division of life, but rather ignite the division of life even more. Close them up, and make them a...

### 7. Question: What then are the metals exactly?

**Answer.** The metals are in themselves nothing other than a water and oil / they are held by

<column-break/>

the fierce properties / such as by the harsh, severe desire / or Saturnine <note>Referring to the cold, restrictive influence of the planet Saturn</note>, Martial <note>Referring to the fiery, aggressive influence of the planet Mars</note>, fiery properties in the compaction of **Sulfur** and **Mercury**, so that it is a **body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note>; but if I completely destroy the body / and divide each into its property / then I find the first creation clearly within it.

<margin>Mysterium Magnum 10. §. 27.</margin>
We want to search / which is the first ground and the **Radical Moisture** <term>Humidum Radicale: The fundamental life-fluid or "oil" that sustains the living spirit within a body</term>, or the innermost birth of all metals in general, thereafter how this first ground becomes **Salt, Sulfur, Mercury**, distinctly in their conjunction according to the three properties (harsh, bitter, fire), and thus various minerals grow, which in the ground are only one.

### 8. Question: Which is then exactly the subtlest ground / and the purest, initial root-essence for the birth of metals?

**Answer.** This is nothing else / than the pure little spirit-water / flowing out like a dew of heaven / from the **temperature** <note>The state of perfect balance</note> of fire and light / the innermost birth / which is there in the outer heaven / like the kernel in a shell; The author calls it <note>Aurora 1. §. 4.</note> the light / or the heart of the heat. This / he says / is in itself a lovely, joy-rich sight / a power of life / a fountain of the heavenly kingdom of joy / for it makes everything in this world living and moving / all flesh / as well as trees, foliage, and grass / grows in this world in the power of light / and has its life therein. If this light were not / then the elements would be motionless / everything would be a harsh, severe property / quite rough and cold. But because the light is a cause of all stirring, moving, and life / so all life desires the light's power / as the unlocked point / which / if it did not stand open / then the kingdom of darkness would be manifest in the **place** <note>original: "Loco"</note> of this world / and everything like a dark hell.

This little spirit-water, or clarity of heaven, is in and of itself pure, virginal, without form, universal, neither dry nor wet, neither hard nor soft, thick nor thin, for it is a weaving spirit in the loveliest temperament <term>Temperatur: The state of perfect balance between qualities, where no single element dominates</term> of properties. Understand, therefore, that when this light, as the joy of freedom, enters into a being, whether it be wet or dry, it immediately ignites a life and growth with its love-desire, according to the drive and property of its source-spirits, and pushes to become free from its enclosure, as a joy of freedom. But three properties especially become active in such an ignition of life; namely Astringency, which is called the salt-spirit; Bitterness, which is called **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurius"</note>; and Anguish, which is called the sulfur-spirit; according to the property of the fire, the fire is ignited, and according to the property of the light, the light-life is ignited; whichever property predominates, that same one generates the being.

The salt-spirit is nothing other than the harsh, attracting, binding, coagulating, drying, contracting, working property in nature; when the light or the free joy sinks into the earth, it ignites the matrix, or nature in the earth, with its joy-desire, and the earth, or the being, becomes desiring, thirsting, to grasp such loveliness, and thereby the free joy, which is otherwise pure

Thus the author understands by **Salt**, **Saturn** <note>original: "Saturnus"</note>, etc. the salt-spirit / or that which is the first / namely the harsh desire of the **Let it be** <note>original: "Fiat," the creative command of God</note>.

### Appendix / Chapter 6.

The first beginning of Nature—serving as the innermost ground—is where the self-risen will introduces itself into an **acceptability** <note>original: "Annehmligkeit"; the state of being received or taking on form</note> toward **Selfhood** <term>Ichtheit: A central term in Jacob Boehme’s philosophy referring to the drive of the individual will to exist as a separate "I."</term>, acting as a natural working. For Nature is merely an instrument of GOD, through which GOD’S power works; yet it possesses its own mobility derived from the outflowing will of GOD. It is the **Center**, the point or ground of that acceptance of **Selfhood**, from which something comes into being, and from which the seven properties originate.

<margin>Key 24. <note>original: "Clav. 24."; referring to Boehme's work 'Clavis'</note></margin>
Just as there is a Center in eternal nature, there is also a Center in temporal nature. From this Center of visible nature, one understands the ground of the invisible. This **Little Spirit-Water**, or clarity of heaven, is in and of itself pure, virginal, without form, universal—neither dry nor wet, neither hard nor soft, thick nor thin—for it is a weaving spirit in the loveliest **balance** <note>original: "Temperatur"</note> of properties. Now, where the drive within the Light-property (in this clarity and light-spirit, or the upward-flowing ray of the innermost birth) is gently bound by the harsh property and sinks down, it becomes a weaving spirit-water, like the purest air; it falls into the earth like dew and impregnates the **Womb** <note>original: "Matrix"</note> of the earth. In whatever place the earth is pure and its fundamental moisture is not infected by the **wrath** <note>original: "Grimm"; the fierce, dark side of nature</note>, this clarity sinks into it. Such water is then called a **Radical Moisture** <note>original: "Humidum Radicale"; the fundamental fluid that sustains life</note>, and such earth is the **purity of Nature** <note>original: "purum Naturae"</note>, the **Prime Matter** <note>original: "prima Materia"</note> of the philosophers.

Understand, therefore, that when this light—as the delight of freedom—enters into a being, whether it be wet or dry, it immediately ignites a life and growth with its love-desire, according to the drive and property of its source-spirits. It drives outward to become free from its enclosure, as a longing for freedom. Specifically, however, three properties are stirred in the ignition of such life: **Harshness**, which is called the **Salt-Spirit**; **Bitterness**, which is called **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurius"</note>; and **Anguish**, which is called the **Sulfur-Spirit** <note>original: "Schwefel-Geist"</note>. According to the property of the fire, the fire-life is ignited, and according to the property of the light, the light-life is ignited; whichever property **predominates** <note>original: "prædominiret"</note>, that same property generates the being.

The **Salt-Spirit** is nothing other than the harsh, attracting, binding, coagulating, drying, and contracting property in nature. When the light or the free delight sinks into the earth, it ignites the **Womb** <note>original: "Matricem"</note> or nature in the earth with its desire for delight, and the earth (or the being) becomes desiring and thirsty to grasp such loveliness. Through this, the free delight—which is otherwise pure

<column-break/>

spirit—becomes essential, substantial, and perceptible. If the fierce, strict harshness is awakened according to the property of the dark world, it swallows the heavenly delight and loveliness into its fierce, harsh hunger; then the light is enclosed in darkness, and life is bolted and sealed within death. Through this awakened Salt-Spirit, in the ignition of the **Wrath-Fire**, the hard stones and bones, the dark earth, and similar things are born. This is the ground of the sour, bitter, fiery salts in herbs, metals, and other beings. Thus, the author understands by **Salt, Saturn** <note>original: "Sal, Saturnus"</note>, etc., the Salt-Spirit, or the first property: namely, the harsh desire of the **Command of Creation** <note>original: "Fiat"</note>. According to the property of the dark world, we find in metals and in the earth, first, a hardness and cold; further, a deadly, stinking water (where **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurius"</note> is caught, poisonous and fierce, in death) from the harsh impression; and thirdly, in this stinking water, a deadened earth or **mute salt**; fourthly, a sharpness like the salt of the harsh law. And this is commonly the stony, coarse essence of the earth and metals.

<margin>Great Mystery 10. §. 18. <note>original: "Myst. Mag. 10. §. 18."; referring to Boehme's 'Mysterium Magnum'</note></margin>
But where the harsh property in nature remains in its balance and gentleness, the Salt-Spirit dries and binds the spirit-water in its womb very gently. It gives a lovely, sweet, flavorful, and pleasant sharpness to a being, which holds the being together very softly and preserves the **Body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note>, so that the delight of freedom—the life—does not become volatile and flee.

Since the very best is often caught and bound within the very worst, the **Physician** <note>original: "Medicus"</note> needs, above all things, to dissolve the bonds of death and separate the evil from the good. He must ensure he does not further awaken the patient's own inflamed, harsh Salt-Spirit by using a wrathful, harsh, or poisonous salt, thereby hastening their death. Every herb, plant, metal, or whatever one may use for medicine has a twofold salt: one according to the harsh, fierce, poisonous torment, and the other according to the Light-torment—gentle, lovely, and drying. Also, the salts exist according to the seven properties of nature; such as: there is a **Saturnine**, **Jovial**, **Martial**, **Veneric**, **Mercurial**, and **Lunar** salt, among which the **Solar** is the noblest. The author names three of the most prominent salts that one may use for a cure, which belong to the vegetable life (under which he sometimes also understands the mineral life). These are **Jupiter**, **Mars**, and **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurius"</note>; these are the working life, in which the **Sun** is the right spirit.

The latter, however, in its heavenly, lovely, joy-filled quality <note>original: "Quaal"; in Boehme's usage, this often refers to the "source-spring" or "vibration" of an essence rather than just pain.</note>, is an awakener and strengthener of life, which soothes the poisonous **Mercury** and kills its poisonous torment, treading on the head of the serpent in earthly nature.

Thus, the **Physician** must know this: that in the strongest **Mercury**, which is the most poisonous, lies the highest **Tincture**. But it is not for **Mercury’s** own self-property; that must be broken. For its self-property, from its **center** outward, is the anxious poisonous life. Yet it has another property within itself, like an oil of light, from which it is so strong and powerful—that is its food and preservation. If that same oil can be separated from it, it is a **tincturing** and a powerful ignition of all dark lives—that is, of all diseases. For in that same oil lies the joy-filled life, and there is a hunger for life, namely, to ignite the weak and lead it on high. One will find the highest **Tincture** in a toad, or an adder, or similar poisonous worms or animals, if one brings them into an **oily essence** <note>original: "olitätisches Wesen"</note> and separates the wrath of **Mercury** from them. ### Of Sulfur.

9. Question: What does our author actually mean by **Sulfur**?

Answer: He understands by it the third **Principle** <note>original: "Principium"</note> or quality of a being, or that spirit through which, in the third form of nature, **Sulfur** <note>original: "Sulphur"</note> is raised up—that is, the brimstone, the oil, the balsam. This occurs in eternal nature in a spiritual way, and in external nature in an external way. The external **Sulfur** is an image and birth of the internal, and the internal is the foundation of the external. Just as the torment of anguish takes its origin from the harsh and bitter quality, so also the **Sulfur-spirit** arises from the salt-spirit and from **Mercury**. Specifically, when the noble desire for freedom or the clarity of heaven is bound by the harsh quality and becomes driving and active in the bitterness, it turns like a wheel and gives birth to anguish or constriction within its enclosure; in such anguish, the free desire becomes a **Sulfur-spirit** or **Sulfur**. This **Sulfur-spirit** is now the active cause in nature, which in its anguish gives birth to the sulfur, oil, and balsam. In this anguish, known as the "sulfur-torment," stands the division of qualities or powers: fire and light. For according to the fierce quality, the fire is awakened into life, and this awakened fire is called "the Terror" <note>original: "der Schreck," the sudden flash or turning point between darkness and light</note>; this is the goal of the dark world. Now, where the Terror in the lightning-flash reaches freedom—the second quality—through the balanced temperature, there the free desire opens itself again in the form of a lovely oil. This is sweeter than any sugar could be, provided it can be separated from the other qualities. This is the first heavenly holy essence, which took its origin from the free desire; it is beautiful and translucent. If the fire-torment could be separated from it

<column-break/>

(though it is not possible to separate them entirely, for the bond of the great kingdom of joy stands therein), then it would be whiter than any thing in nature could be. But because of the fire, it remains ruby-red, which the light transforms into yellow, then toward red and white, because of the earthly quality and the power of the sun. But if the artist is able to dissolve it and make it free from the fire of wrath and the other qualities, then he possesses the **Pearl of the whole world**—understand this as the **Tincture** <note>original: "Tinctur," the spiritualizing essence or "philosopher's stone" that perfects matter</note>; for Lady Venus <note>the principle of love and desire</note> has her treasure-chest lying there; it is the Virgin with her beautiful little wreath. Oh, you earthly man, if only you still had that! Lucifer and Adam gambled it away here. Oh man, if you knew what lay here, how you would strive for it! But it belongs only to those whom GOD has chosen for it. Oh noble pearl, how sweet you are in the new rebirth, how beautiful is your radiance!

Because two **Principles** lie within one **Sulfur**, namely fire and light, the author calls it **Sulphur** in this way: **Sul** he calls the free desire, the clarity of heaven, the soul, the first beginning of the free will out of the "Nothing" into "Something," in the freedom outside of nature. **Phur** is as much as fire: the sharpness and rigorous attraction of the will, the harsh desire which captures the **Sul**, as the soul, into a being. That same being is rigorous because of the attraction, and introduces itself into three forms, as mentioned above, and further into the fourth form, as if out of fire. In the **Phur**, the origin of both eternal and external nature is understood, for hardness is a mother of the sharpness of all beings and a sustainer of all existence. Out of the **Sul**, as from the desire for freedom, the dark anguish becomes a shining light. In the third **Principle**, the external kingdom, the **Sul** is the oil of nature, in which the life burns and everything grows. ### Concerning the metals in particular—namely gold, silver, iron, copper, tin, and lead—what they consist of, and what medicines can be prepared from them.

# Concerning the Metals in Particular.

...how the <term>Salitter</term> <note>original: "Salitter"; Böhme uses this to describe the "divine sap" or fundamental substance of the spiritual world, akin to a celestial saltpeter.</note> in the natural heaven was primary in its ascent into the light of love. For every <term>source-spirit</term> <note>original: "Quell-Geist"; these are the seven fundamental qualities or forces that flow through all of creation.</note> in the heavenly nature possesses the kind and quality of all other source-spirits within itself, for it is always being influenced by the others; from this, Life and the unfathomable birth of GOD arises. But according to its own power, it is primary, and that is its own "body" from which it takes its name.

Now, every source-spirit has the quality of all of nature and its workings. During the time of the "ignition of the wrath," these were incorporated into death, and from the workings of each spirit, earth, stones, ore, and water were formed. Therefore, you find ore, stones, water, and earth within the ground according to the quality of each spirit. This is why the earth has so many and such varied qualities—all according to how each source-spirit, with its inherent birth, was primary during the time of the ignition <note>The "ignition" refers to the fall or the moment divine harmony was disrupted by "wrathful" or harsh qualities.</note>.

This crystalline water, in which Salt, Mercury, and especially the pure heavenly Sulfur reside, the author calls **Venus**. By this, he understands nothing other than the heavenly Salitter, the pure heavenly body within the metals. **Venus** in **Sol** <note>Sun/Gold</note> is a golden Venus; in **Luna** <note>Moon/Silver</note> a silver one; **Mars** <note>Iron/Force</note> in **Venus** is copper; **Venus** in **Mars** is iron; **Jupiter** <note>Tin/Justice</note> in **Venus** is tin; **Saturnus** <note>Lead/Contraction</note> in **Venus** is lead; **Mercurius** <note>Quicksilver/Motion</note> in **Venus** is quicksilver. Without **Venus**, there is no metal, neither among the "fixed" <note>stable metals like gold</note> nor the minerals.

### Of Gold.

2. Question: What does the author understand by **Sol**?

Answer: By this, he sometimes understands the Divine Sun, sometimes the heavenly sun, sometimes the sidereal <note>pertaining to the stars</note> sun, and sometimes **Gold**, or the very purest metal, in which Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury exist and are bound together in the highest "temperature" <note>balance or harmonious mixture</note> of fire and light. By this, he does not mean common gold, but the noblest and best kernel of the Salitter,

<column-break/>

in which the light and the clarity of heaven are most abundant, and which is least infected by the "wrath." This kernel is more present and purer in our common gold than in all other metals. The coarse body of gold is not the gold itself; rather, it is only its container and dwelling-house. Its coarseness does not produce the gold; rather, the <term>Tincture of the Sun</term> <note>original: "Tinctura Solis"; the spiritual essence or "soul" of the sun that gives gold its value and power.</note> produces it within the coarse stone. But the coarse stone is the Mother, and **Sol** is the Father, for **Sol** impregnates the coarse stone because it possesses the <term>Center of Nature</term> <note>original: "Centrum Naturæ"</note> from which **Sol** has its origin.

<margin>On the Incarnation of Christ, part 1, chapter 14, section 4.</margin>

The Philosophers <note>Alchemists</note> call it "theirs," namely **Philosophic Gold**. In this gold resides the most noble <term>Universal Medicine</term> <note>original: "Medicina Universalis"; the legendary panacea or "Philosopher's Stone" capable of curing all illness.</note>. This is clearly recognized because mankind loves gold so much and directs such sharp desire toward it. For the noblest and best kernel is within it—something that sick and weak humans lack in their own bodies, which are inflamed by the "fury of the wrath." But the human only fumbles for and grabs at the outer chest; the treasure lying within he cannot obtain unless he has the right key to the chest and has himself put on the noble kernel—the true magnet—namely the clarity of heaven through the **New Birth**.

<margin>See Aurora 18. §. 18. 19. 20.</margin>

We must perceive the inner kernel from the outer shells, then exclude the shells and take the kernel from them. Note, therefore: the quality of the "free delight" gives birth to the essence in the three forms: as **Salt** in **Saturn**, as **Mercury** in **Mercurius**, and as **Sulfur** in **Mars** (the "anxiety-torment"). These three qualities—Saturn, Mercury, and Mars—are nothing other than certain forms of hunger and desire, and they form an essence for food according to their appetite. For example: in the Saturnine quality, the desire for "free delight" according to the first principle...

### Appendix / Chapter 7

[In the principle of] Lead, following the <term>Mercurial</term> <note>Referring to Mercury, the principle of movement, volatility, and transformation in alchemy.</note> watery sharp Salt, also hard stones and earths.

But according to Freedom, or the property of Light, in which it gives itself over to <term>Saturn</term> <note>Saturn is associated with Lead, contraction, coldness, and the "desire" of the material world.</note> as the "Desire," it produces Gold within Saturn, according to the Desire of the Light. There, the spirit and the body part; the spirit of its desire is **Sol** <note>original: "Sol"; the Sun or the spiritual essence of Gold.</note>, and the body is Gold. Understand this: the golden body is within Saturn according to the property of "free desire" and not according to Saturn’s own property. His own property within himself is Lead, Salt, and Earth, but he holds the golden child locked within himself like a **black raven**—not in his gray form, but in a dark glass. He is a great lord, but his lordship, because of the golden child he carries in his belly, is not within his own power. He is not the father of the child; rather, <term>Mercurius</term> is the one who works the child. But Saturn wraps his "mourning-cloak" around it so that he cannot have joy with the golden child. Yet he makes the beautiful child bodily, for he is its <term>Fiat</term> <note>original: "Fiat"; the divine "Let there be" or creative command that gives form to spirit.</note> or creator, and keeps it covered and hidden under his cloak. He cannot give the child a body out of his own property, for it is the essence of free desire in the highest degree of corporality within "fixed death"—though it is not truly death, but an enclosure, and a representation, by way of parable, of the divine heavenly essence.

Mercury is the master-craftsman of this child which Saturn covers. When Mercury receives this into his "hunger," he throws away the black cloak in a "strange fire"—and yet it is not strange—and rejoices in the child. But Mercury is too malicious in the "fire-wrath"; he swallows the child and turns it entirely into his own property. When he is most hungry in the fire, one must give him **Sol** (who is his wife) so that his hunger is stilled. Then, when he is satisfied, he works in the matter of the

<column-break/>

child with his own hunger or fire, and fulfills his satisfied desire from the property of **Sol**, which he had previously eaten. He nourishes the child until it takes on all four elements along with the stars, and he becomes "heavy with child." Then it belongs in a "strange fire"—and yet not strange, for it is an earnest fire. Thus the Father gives it the Soul, as the fire-spirit; and its first Mother (whom Mercury ate in his hunger, and who was fixed and perfect) gives the spirit of the soul as the "light-life." Then "Death" arises (which is the <term>Tincture</term> <note>The spiritual essence or "medicine" that transforms lower metals into gold or heals the body.</note> that colors the body), and the child is born. Hereafter, it is its own being, a child of freedom, and it asks nothing more of its master-craftsman. It is better than its father, but no better than its mother, in whose seed it lay before the father worked within it. It treads upon the head of the fiery essence of its father (as if upon the Serpent) and walks free through death in the fire. If you understand nothing here, you were not born into the highest knowledge of <term>Spagirey</term> <note>original: "Spagirey"; the art of spagyrics or alchemy, specifically the separation and recombination of natural substances.</note>.

You have an example of this in gold and silver; you cannot make them pure so that they are pure silver and gold until they have been melted seven times in the fire. When that happens, the metal remains sitting in the "middle seat," in the Heart of Nature (which is the Water), in its own quality and color. First, the harsh quality, which [holds] the <term>Salitter</term> <note>original: "Salitter"; Böhme's term for the divine "sap" or fundamental substance of the spiritual world.</note> in the hard clay...

Thirdly, the **bitter** [quality], which arises in the ignition of the water within the flash of fire, is smelted away; for that same quality is a rager, a ranter, and a breaker, and neither silver nor gold can endure if it has not yet been killed; for it makes everything brittle and manifests itself in many kinds of colors, for it rides through all the spirits and takes on the colors of all spirits. In this sixth smelting, I believe, lies the greatest danger for the alchemists with their making of silver and gold. When it is now smelted for the seventh time, an even more subtle fire is required; for there the life rises up and rejoices in love, and desires to manifest itself in the infinite, as it did in heaven before the time of wrath. And through this, the body receives its greatest strength and power, and the body colors itself with the highest degree, and receives its true beauty and virtue. Through its <term>tincture</term>, which stands in the balance of fire and light, it soothes everything that is ignited by heat or cold; just as the sun shines through everything with its power, so the core of the gold shines through the whole body and awakens its life-spirits, opens the foundational fluids, cleanses the blood, rejuvenates the body, and protects it from all evil accidents; therefore, <term>physicians</term> <note>original: "Medici"</note> should, through prayer and labor,

The world is greedy and boastful, especially those who wish to be masters of the arts and say they know gold, yet they are blind people; why do you not seek it? He brings forth manifold fruit; there you have an angel who is free from the wrath, for he is entirely pure. Seek him, and you shall find him. ->**Concerning Silver.**<-

**5th Question: What does the author understand by Silver?**

**Answer:** By silver, the author generally understands the clarity of heaven, or the light—the heavenly <term>tincture</term> in its <term>lunar</term> <note>original: "Lunarischer"; relating to the moon's influence.</note> property. He calls it the <term>Moon</term> <note>original: "Lunam"</note>, whether it be in trees, herbs, animals, but especially in silver. For just as gold has the color of the sun and the clarity of heaven found in the <term>purity of nature</term> <note>original: "puro Naturæ"</note>, or <term>salitter</term> <note>A term Böhme uses for the divine force or "saltpeter" of the earth.</note>—a <term>solar</term> <note>original: "Solarische"; relating to the sun's influence.</note> property—so silver has the color of the water or the moon, because the <term>salitter</term>, into which the clarity of heaven entered in that same place, became <term>lunar</term> in its property. It has exactly the property of gold in its core, but its outer shell of mortal graspability is infected by <term>Venus</term> <note>In alchemy, Venus represents the metal copper and its associated spiritual qualities, here described as a "leprosy" or impurity affecting silver.</note> with her poisonous leprosy. Thus, that same <term>medicine</term> is to be obtained from silver when it is cleansed of its infected water and leprosy, as was mentioned above regarding gold.

## Of Copper.

Next to silver is copper, whose inner essence is closely related to gold and is called <term>Venus</term> <note>In alchemy, Venus is the name and symbol for the metal copper.</note> by the Author; by Venus, the Author understands the fifth form of nature, according to the property of Light. Thus, copper is generated, as far as its core is concerned, when the clarity of heaven falls into <term>Salitter</term> <note>original: "Salitter"; Böhme's term for the divine-natural essence or "celestial saltpeter" from which all physical matter is born.</note>, wherein this property lies hidden, being awakened into movement by the heavenly <term>tincture</term> <note>A spiritual essence or "dye" capable of transforming matter.</note>, which then arrives and defines such a tincture. But because <term>Mars</term> <note>The alchemical name for iron, representing the fiery and severe force of nature.</note> is also ignited where Venus rises, the outer shell or physical tangibility is infected and scorched by the <term>wrath</term> <note>original: "Grimm"; the harsh, contractive force of nature that Böhme often contrasts with divine love.</note> of Mars, and thus the Salitter of this coarse tangibility is iron-like. The birth of Venus, or copper, is described by the Author in *The Signature of All Things* <note>original: "Signat. c. 4. §. 35-39."</note>.

Love proceeds from wrath and is a humility or a sinking; thus it has also stepped into an order in the Creation. Therefore, Venus stands on the wheel at the lines of Mars beneath the <term>Sun</term> <note>original: "Sonne" or "Solis"; representing the spiritual source of light and the metal gold.</note>; for such is the separation in nature, and thus one thing proceeds from the other. Its metal is copper. The origin is this: that love is a desire, and yet it desires only light and joy. Then the matter becomes a property of desire; but if the love-desire is to become physical in its <term>impression</term> <note>The process by which spiritual forces condense into physical form.</note>, it must surrender itself to the wrathful <term>Fiat</term> <note>The creative "let there be" command of God, acting here through the desire of Mars.</note>, as the desire of Mars in fire, or in the fiery property; for the <term>Saturnine</term> <note>Related to Saturn, the principle of contraction, coldness, and lead.</note> property takes everything into its power and makes it physical. Therefore, the metal of Venus is closely related to gold because of its self-property from freedom; but Mars makes it too wrathful and too brittle. Because it separates itself from the fire of Mars, it retains a large portion of Mars's property within itself.

The metal of Mars is iron, for he is the wrath in the <term>Sulphur</term> <note>In alchemical thought, Sulphur represents the "soul" or the active, combustible principle of a substance.</note>, in which the fire ignites and takes its origin. His origin with matter is in the severity of desire. Copper separates itself from iron during the process of birth; for it originates

<column-break/>

from the will of Venus, and there is a distinction between them like that of body and soul. For Mars is the "fire-soul" of Venus and causes Venus to become physical; otherwise, Venus, according to her own property in the "mortification" <note>An alchemical term for the breakdown or "death" of a substance before its rebirth.</note> within the "salnitric terror," would yield only water. For her fire is only a smile or a love-fire, which she is alone without other influences. Therefore, by her own power, she can give birth to no physical being that would be hard or tough; she is only the mother to her child, without a natural soul. Mars is her soul, and Saturn makes her body. The spirit of <term>Sol</term> <note>The Sun or the spiritual principle of Gold.</note> may <term>tinge</term> <note>original: "tingiren"; to spiritually transform or refine the essence of a metal.</note> Mars and Venus and transform them into the highest metallic perfection—that is, into gold. This cannot happen as easily with silver unless it is first brought back into the "first matter" <note>original: "erſte Materia"; the primal, undifferentiated substance before it takes a specific form.</note>, where Saturn, Mars, and Mercury are joined together in the Sulphur; then it can be. Venus receives her toughness from Saturn and her redness from Mars, as if from fire.

Yet now, the desire of Venus is only intense for Sol, as for her first mother, from whom she springs in her birth in her first origin. For love springs from GOD; thus it is also in the figure of the outward birth. The desire of Venus goes into Sol, into the sun, and receives the property of the sun in her desire, and shines from Sol. She has a unique shine above all planets and stars, which she takes from her mother; and in her mother’s power stands her joy, like the laughter she has within her. She is, in her self-property—what she is purely alone without the property of the other planets—a true daughter of the Sun (understand this within the Sulphur) where everything is joined together. Therefore she stands closest beneath the sun, as a child of the sun; not that the sun has physically given birth to the star, for it was also created with the rest, but in the Sulphur, outside of the creation, in the birth process alone, it is so.

# Concerning Metals in Particular.

### On Copper.

Next to silver is copper, whose inner essence is closely related to gold and is called *Venus* <note>original: "Venus"</note> by the author; by *Venus*, the author understands the fifth form of nature, according to the property of light. Thus, copper is generated—as far as its kernel is concerned—when the clarity of heaven falls into <term>Salitter</term> <note>original: "Salitter"; a term used by Jacob Böhme to describe the divine "sap" or the spiritual matter of the celestial world from which all things grow.</note>, wherein this property lies, since it is awakened into motion by the heavenly <term>Tincture</term> <note>original: "Tinctur"; a spiritualizing force or essence that can transform and perfect matter.</note>, and it then arrives and terminates such a Tincture accordingly. But because *Mars* <note>original: "Mars"; associated with iron, fire, and the "wrath" or "fierceness" of nature.</note> is ignited wherever *Venus* arises, the outer shell or tangibility is infected and scorched by the <term>Wrath</term> <note>original: "Grimm"; the harsh, fiery, and dark quality of nature that provides energy but requires tempering by light.</note> of Mars, and thus the Salitter of coarse tangibility is iron-like. The birth of *Venus*, or copper, is described by the author in *The Signature of All Things*, chapter 4, paragraphs 35–39.

### 6. Question: How is a good medicine prepared from copper?

**Answer:** Copper possesses a sharp acidity; now, in all things there is a twofold acidity or sharpness: one according to the fierce property, which the philosophers call <term>cursed acid</term> <note>original: "acidum maledictum"</note>, and one according to the property of light, which is called <term>blessed acid</term> <note>original: "acidum benedictum"</note>; the author speaks of both these acids or sournesses in *Aurora*, chapter 1, § 23.

The sour quality is the opposite of the bitter and the sweet / and tempers everything finely / a refreshment and a quenching / whenever the bitter and sweet qualities rise too high / it is a craving in the taste / a joy of life / a welling joy in all things / a desire / a longing and a delight of the kingdom of joy / a quiet bliss of the spirit / such things it tempers in all living and welling things; however, it also has within it a source of evil and perdition / for if it rises too high / or wells up too much in a thing / so that it ignites / then it begets sadness, <term>melancholy</term> <note>original: "Melancholia"</note>, a foul and brittle stench in the water / an oblivion of all that is good / a sadness of life / a house of death / a beginning of sorrow / and an end of joys.

When the artist has not properly separated that acidity which has its origin in the evil property of Lucifer's wrath, and if the lovely acidity, the <term>blessed acid</term> <note>original: "Acidum benedictum"</note>, is not

<column-break/>

freed from the curse without any infection, so that a sweet, lovely, and pleasant sharpness [becomes active] and does not turn sour again, then copper can provide <unclear>no</unclear> safe or useful medicine, because the <term>cursed acid</term> <note>original: "Acidum maledictum"</note> is a terrible poison from which [illness] arises; for if, according to the opinion of today's physicians, all diseases are born from an acidity, it would not be at all useful to give the body even more acidity, and thereby sharpen the acidity of the stomach and the blood.

Accordingly, in the decomposition of metals—and especially in copper—one finds a volatile, corrosive acid, and if one could take such acid from it, one would have found a great treasure in medicine. But it is not enough that one separates the coarse, external sourness from the copper and sweetens it, for copper also has a coarse, loathsome sweetness in itself, which becomes as sour and sharp in the stomach and blood as a vitriol <note>A metallic sulfate, often highly acidic and corrosive.</note>; rather, what is meant is a sweetness which cannot become sour again, and which is born from the root and source of the <term>acid</term> or the sharpness; everything else, however beautiful the names may sound, is uncertain and dangerous.

### Concerning Iron, Mars. ♂.

When our author speaks of Mars, he commonly understands by it the birth of fire in the anguish-torment <note>original: "Angst-Quaal"; a Böhmean term for the transformative tension or "contraction" in nature that precedes the flash of light or fire.</note> of both temporal and eternal nature. Just as the planet Mars has a birth and qualification in the sidereal sphere, iron also has a birth in the mineral kingdom; in this regard, we refer to what we cited above in the third part from the author concerning Mars. We now report only this, according to the principles of our author: namely, that the clarity of heaven, or the delight of freedom—the Tincture of the innermost birth—falling into the <term>Salitter</term> <note>The divine "sap" or spiritual substance of the earth.</note> of the earth (where the anguish-torment lay in the potential for heat and ignition), awakened the same, and like a fire-shock, rose up into the wrath, and in its boiling prepared and cooked the Salitter into an iron; thus Mars, considered as a spirit, is the shaper and cause of iron. Now iron has two kinds of properties within it: one according to the property of the dark world—according to its spirit, it is fiery, hot, stinging, breaking, a raging, raving source of poison, a fierce <term>mercury</term> <note>original: "Mercurius"; here referring to the active, transformative spirit.</note>. Its body and outer shell is a burnt, hard, impure, unrefined earth. The corrosive, gnawing spirit must have something to consume, and if it has nothing, it eats and gnaws its own body; it takes with great [force]...

From this, one sees what a noble Tincture is in Mars, if it can be separated from the fierce fire; it cannot be used for any medicine unless its own leprosy—the corrosive fire and the cursed acid <note>original: "Acidum maledictum"</note>—is taken from it, and its outer hard shell from the hard impression is unlocked, and its inner red core is turned outward. Here again, the philosophers do not lack for beautiful names with which they title their lyes <note>liquid extracts</note> from the outer shell of Mars and their rust: such as <term>Tincture of Mars</term> <note>original: "Tinctura Martis"</note>, <term>Essence of Mars</term> <note>original: "Essentia Martis"</note>, <term>Aperitive Saffron of Mars</term> <note>original: "Crocus Martis aperitivus"</note>, etc. But the effects prove that these are nothing but names and titles.

## Of Tin or ♃ Jupiter.

By Jupiter, the author understands—both in eternal and temporal nature—such a property that stands in the middle between heat and cold (or Saturn and Mars). In this, Mercury predominates, but is very volatile and unstable. Now, when the heavenly Tincture sinks into a <term>Salitter</term> <note>A term used by Böhme for a divine or cosmic substance, often likened to saltpeter, but representing the active forces of nature</note> of such property and ignites that same source-spirit, Tin is born. This has a birth in the mineral kingdom just like the planet Jupiter in the sidereal <note>pertaining to the stars</note> kingdom, of which we spoke above. Its inner core is a sweet, gentle water, but it is unstable in fire because there is little of the pure Salt within it. Therefore, the philosophers work little in this Salt. It has, however, a very beautiful shining Tincture and is used more by potters for glazing than by physicians for medicine; and because it holds fast, it is a sign that a noble Salt still resides within, if only someone wished to seek it.

### Of the Universal.

...with their **Philosopher's Stone** <term>Stone Philosophorum</term> <note>The legendary "Philosopher's Stone," a substance capable of turning base metals into gold and granting eternal life; here used as a metaphor for spiritual perfection.</note>; there is no point of difference between them / for everything has its origin in the eternal birth / and everything must have a restoration in the same manner.

Therefore / if the **Magus** <term>Magus</term> <note>A practitioner of "Magia," which in this context refers to divine wisdom and the understanding of the hidden workings of nature.</note> wishes to seek and find Paradise again within the curse of the earth / he must first walk in the person of Christ / **GOD** must be manifest in him / understand: in the inner man / so that he has the magical vision / he must proceed with his undertaking / just as the world did with Christ / then he can find Paradise / wherein no death exists. But if he is not himself in that same birth of restoration / and does not himself walk in the way / upon which Christ walked on Earth / so that he proceeds in Christ's spirit and will / then let him simply cease his searching / he finds nothing / but only death and the curse of **GOD** / I tell him faithfully / for the little pearl / of which I write / is Paradisiacal / which **GOD** does not throw before swine / but gives to his children for a game of love.

And although much might be stated in this place / so that reason might receive open eyes / it is nevertheless not to be done / for the godless would only become worse / and more haughty thereby; Therefore / because he is not worthy of Paradise / nor can he enter therein / no heavenly jewel shall be given to him / and therefore **GOD** hides it / nor does He permit anything to be spoken of it / except magically / to him to whom He reveals it / therefore no one attains it / unless he himself becomes a Magus in Christ / so that Paradise is manifest in him / in the inner man / then he may find it / provided he is born for it and chosen by **GOD**.

and found himself in the quality of clear gold; This process is also thus / and not a tiny spark different / for man / and the earth / with their secrets / lie locked in the same curse and death / and require the same restoration.

But this is said to the seeker / and he should be faithfully warned / as his temporal and eternal welfare is dear to him / that he does not set out on the path to try the earth / and to bring **Mercury** <term>Mercurium</term> <note>In alchemy, Mercury represents the fluid, transformative principle; spiritually, it relates to the Word of God or the life-force.</note> back out of that which is locked / unless he himself is first reborn out of the curse and death through the Divine Mercury / and possesses the Divine Rebirth in full knowledge / otherwise all is in vain / and no amount of learning helps; for that which he seeks / lies in death / in the wrath of **GOD** / locked in the curse / if he wishes to make it living / and place it into its First state / then that same life must first be manifest in him: Then he may say to the mountain / lift yourself from there / and cast yourself into the sea / and to the fig tree / let no fruit grow upon you henceforth / and it will come to pass.

life is **air** / thus you work in the body in vain; But if you now seize the spirit of the **tincture** <term>Tinctur</term> / then you indeed walk upon a path / on which many have found the **Sun** <term>Solem</term>. But they followed the path / all the way to the heart of the Sun / where the spirit of the heavenly tincture captured them / and led them into freedom and majesty; There they then recognized the noble stone / the **Philosopher's Stone** <term>Lapidem Philosophorum</term> / and were immediately terrified by human blindness / and saw the wasted labor.

If you wish to find the noble stone / look / we will show it to you well enough / if you are a **Magus** <term>Magus</term>, and worthy of it / otherwise you shall surely remain blind: So tackle it thus / for it has nothing more than three numbers. From one to ten is one number / and you have power only over the number **nine** / before the **tenth** you shall stand still / for it is the end of nature; It does not befit the creature to search there / as long as it remains under the cross / it remains in the body of the apprehended **will of GOD** <term>Willens GOTTES</term>. And then it has ten times ten / which is a hundred / and then ten times a hundred / which is a thousand: There lies the stone without great effort / for it is pure / and never defiled by earthly nature.

Do it thus / as I have written above concerning the **Center** <term>Centro</term> of all beings: Exchange the planets around the wheel / and take them / one masculine and then one feminine / one for the soul-spirit / and one for the air-spirit. You need not worry about the body / for every planet makes for itself its own **body** <term>Corpus</term>, whatever its desire is / quite by itself. Start with **Saturn** <term>Saturno</term> / for he is the first in the fire-life to the noble tincture; And then travel around the wheel to the **Moon** <term>Luna</term>, for you must always take one planet for the tincture-life / and then one for the air-spirit / for neither exists without the other / otherwise you get spirit without a body/

# Concerning the Universal.

[A] body / [has] a fire-spirit / which burns in a lamp / like a kindled fire / but it gives nothing; It is only a pride / wishing to be without a body. Travel then around the wheel until the **Sun** <term>Solem</term> <note>original: "Solem." In Böhme's cosmology, the Sun represents the fourth property of nature, the point of transformation where fire becomes light.</note>, that is the Seven-Fold Number in the first number; and when you arrive there / you think / you have the **Stone** <note>The Philosopher's Stone, which Böhme interprets as a spiritual transformation rather than just a physical one.</note> / but it does not endure / **Mars** breaks it. Travel further through the fire of the **Sun** / which is the eighth number; And when you come through / then seize the **Eternity** through the **Tincture** <term>Tinctur</term> <note>The spiritualizing essence that heals and transforms both metals and the human soul.</note> / which is the ninth number / and lead it upon the **Cross** / to the tenth number / that is the end of Nature. There reach out / and take the **Stone** / as much as you want / it will not break in any fire / it is free from the **wrath** <note>original: "Grimmigkeit." A technical term for the harsh, consuming fire of the first principle of nature before it is softened by light.</note> and its offspring; Its radiance and light stand in the power of Majesty; Its **Body** <term>Corpus</term> is out of the eternal essence; Its number is a hundred upon the Cross / and a thousand in the Majesty.

This we give to the seekers / for no one finds the **Stone** in the **Moon** <term>Luna</term> / unless he then comes upon the Cross into the tenth number. If it then further pleases him / to seek this world / and he would gladly have the radiance of this world / and desires the **Stone** of this world / as in metals / let him then go from the Inner into the Outer; Let him go into the **Moon** / and melt it into a thousand parts / and give it a little of the **Sun** <term>Solis</term>; But if his spirit is great / then let him give it the seventh part of the **Sun** / and it is already done.

For all planets and stars run toward the **Heart** / each one takes power from the heart / and makes for itself its own body; For the **Moon** is made of all six planets / and has also the **Sun** <term>☉</term> / but not the Heart / for it has the **Sun** <note>original: "Solem"</note> only in desire / as you see / that it shines with the **Sun** / and not with its own luster; Therefore the spirit of the Heart must be added to it / which is pure from the beginning; then all the planets run toward it / each one desires the pure child / and builds its house within it.

You keep the black **Saturn** <term>Saturnum</term> with the heat of **Mars** <term>Martis</term> / so finally the kind **Jupiter** will appear to you / who is friendly / and has the Upper-House / the house of the spirit / of the **Tincture**, when he comes out of the black **Saturn** / he is the **Metallic Stone** <term>Metallische Stein</term>.

### Appendix / Chapter 8.

7. Question: Now, once a person has the **Matter** <term>Materia</term>,
->tell me, how must he handle the same?<-

Answer: When the Matter is known and has been properly dealt with, the Matter is placed into the fire in a **Philosophical Furnace**; however, both the furnace and the fire are to be understood as being both external and internal, bodily and spiritual. The external fire is the fire of the four elements, and its furnace is made of clay, as is well known to chemists; as soon as the external fire begins to work, it awakens and kindles the **internal fire**. This internal fire, however, is two-fold: according to the first and then according to the second **Principle** <note>In Böhme’s system, the First Principle is the "dark fire-world" or "wrath," and the Second Principle is the "light-world" or "love."</note>. The latter would not arise if the former did not first come into drive and action. Therefore the Author says: Two **Central Fires** are required for it, within which the power of all things resides, and which are very easy to come by if a person is properly suited for it. The reader should not, therefore, trouble himself with gold or minerals in the manner suggested; it is all false. The very best in Heaven and in the world must be used for it—from that which is Above and that which is Below, which is both near and far. The place where it is to be found is everywhere, but not everyone is fit for it. It also costs no money at all, except what goes toward the time and nourishment of the body; otherwise, one could prepare it with 2 Florins <note>An old German currency; the author emphasizes that the spiritual "Stone" is not a commodity bought with wealth.</note>, or even less. The world must become Heaven, and Heaven must become the world. It is not of the earth, stones, or metals, and yet it is from the foundation of all metals; it is a spiritual essence which is surrounded by the four elements, and which also transforms the four elements into one: a **Double Mercury** <term>Mercurius</term>, yet not quicksilver, nor any other mineral or metal.

<margin>Epistle 28. §. 13.</margin>
Thus the true fire with which the Stone is cooked is a two-fold **Central-Fire**, a double Mercury; if these two fires are not awakened centrally, and both do not drive in the proper temperature, then all external blowing of the bellows is in vain.

<column-break/>

1792

8. Question: When the two central fires are awakened in the **Matter**—one in the seed and kernel as the ignition of the root and life, and the other for growth and the becoming of a body—what should the Artist do next?

Answer: The Author presents the entire process of the **Philosophical Work** in the image of the suffering and death of Christ, and in the parable of the **Planetary Wheel**. Regarding the latter, we have spoken briefly; the former, however, the Author opens up in the treatise concerning the **Signature of All Things** <term>Signatura Rerum</term> <note>One of Jacob Böhme’s most famous works, explaining how the internal essence of things is revealed through their external form.</note>, point by point, piece by piece. We wish to include the most important parts here.

Just as in the seed of man there lie two central fires—one for the fire-life, and therein the **wrath** <note>original: "Grimm." The harsh, consuming power of nature before it is softened by divine light.</note> of God's anger in potential, and the other for the light-life, and therein the Word of the promise of the **Crusher of the Serpent** <note>A reference to Christ, who "crushes the head of the serpent."</note>. Now, where these two central fires are to be awakened, they must come into a proper **Womb** <term>Matricem</term>, in which these two properties also lie, according to all the forms of the seed. Likewise, in the true Matter, there is a two-fold central fire in **potential** <term>potentia</term>; this fire cannot come **into action** <term>ad actum</term> and be kindled unless it comes into its proper **Matrix**.

The Mother of all beings is **Sulfur** <term>Sulphur</term>. **Mercury** <term>Mercurius</term> is her life; **Mars** is her feeling; **Venus** is the love; **Jupiter** is the understanding; **Luna** (the Moon) is her bodily being; **Saturn** is the man (understand this as the structuring of the becoming-body). You must therefore reconcile the man with the woman; for the man is angry, so his dear bride gives herself into his arms. But see to it that the bride is a **Virgin**, entirely modest and pure. For the woman’s seed shall crush the head of the serpent (that is, the man’s wrath). The Virgin must be in true love without any falsehood—a Virgin who has not yet touched any man in wrath according to his manhood. For the clear Godhead in pure love likewise marries itself with humanity; and when Mary said: *Let it be to me as you have said, for I am the servant of the LORD,* then humanity took in the Godhead, and likewise the Godhead took in humanity.

# Concerning the Universal.

The clear Deity signifies the chaste **Virgin** <note>In this mystical context, the "Virgin" refers to Divine Wisdom or Sophia, the mirror of God's glory.</note> in the Philosophical Work. Humanity is **Mercury**, **Sulphur**, and **Salt**, <note>The *Tria Prima* (Three Primaries) of alchemy: spirit/fluidity, fire/soul, and body/solidity.</note> both heavenly and earthly. The heavenly part has faded and is as nothing; that which was dead in **Wrath** <note>Original: *Grimm*—the harsh, bitter quality of fallen nature.</note> has awakened and lives for the fury. In these qualities of wrath, humanity was tempted in Adam and also in Christ. Now you ask: With what? With a corresponding opposition in the wrath—with such a devil who possessed all these qualities within himself as a prince.

The quality in **Sulphur** <term>Sulphur</term> <note>The vital, flammable principle of the soul.</note> was tempted by its own likeness; the temptation came within or from the sulphuric quality, and there were three forms. One was in the **Impression** <note>The force of contraction or "hardening" into matter.</note>, which the Philosopher calls **Saturn**. The human spirit or will was meant to open this in the quality of **Venus** <note>The quality of love, light, and desire.</note> and thereby still or feed its hunger, which is the **Fire**.

The second quality was that he should live in his own awakened and opened Venus, arising from the quality of **Saturn**, and fly within his own will.

The third quality was that he should lead his will, through the awakened desire for love, back into the **Center**, as if back into the **Sulphuric Mother**, which arises within the Impression in anguish. But he would not do this. However, the first Adam had done [the opposite]; therefore **GOD**, when He wished to help him, tested him in Sulphur—as the first Mother of humanity—and allowed a fierce devil, who was ignited in Sulphur, to tempt him with his ignited malice. Do you not understand this? What more then should I tell you? Sulphur is the **Mother's womb**; we must enter into it if we wish to be born again.

Thus, the **Artist** <note>The alchemist or spiritual seeker performing the work.</note> must seek the "evil child" who fled from his mother and entered the Center of selfhood, finding him in **Saturn**; for the **Wrath of GOD** has enclosed him in the chamber of death with His Impression.

<column-break/>

This child the Artist shall take and lead back into the Mother’s womb, and there send the Angel with the message to **Mary**, announcing to her that she shall bear a son, and she shall call his name **JESUS**. And if the Mother consents to this and receives the name JESUS, then the **new humanity** will begin with the new child within the old apostate, who was held captive in the Mother by the **Wrath of God**. First, the name JESUS will give itself into the dead child who lay captive in Saturn, entreating the will of the evil, dead child. This is the **beautiful Bride** <note>Divine Wisdom/Sophia.</note> who offers her pearl wreath to her apostate bridegroom, asking only that he receive her again, and she will return her love to him. If the apostate youth, locked in death, accepts her again, then the Artist is prepared and deemed worthy by **GOD** for his undertaking. Now the Bride will love the bridegroom, and a **Virgin** shall bear a son at which all the world wonders; the woman will encompass the man, but he is a man and not a woman, and he has the heart of a Virgin. Now he must be tested to see if he will live in Virginly discipline and in a will resigned to **GOD**. For he must become a **Knight** and destroy the devil's "robbery-castle," which he holds within his Mother across seven kingdoms <note>The seven properties of nature or planetary spirits.</note>. So, let the devil set his Mother's house on fire with his wrath and tempt him; he will now surely protect himself from the devil with Christ. This shall happen: when the tempter comes and attacks him, the youth, together with the Virginly heart, will surrender himself entirely into the Mother. The Mother will completely swallow him up through the devil's wrath. He gives himself up entirely, moving from his own will into **Nothingness**. At this, the Artist thinks: "Now I have lost," for he has lost heaven; for he sees nothing and does not consider that a...

In the fourth kingdom of the mother of all beings / which is the **Mercurial** <term>Mercurialische</term> <note>Associated with the element Mercury, representing the fluid, communicative, and transformative principle in both the soul and the laboratory matter.</note> on the wheel of the nature of life / Christ made the deaf to hear / the mute to speak / and the lepers clean from the poison of Mercury. In the fifth kingdom of the mother of all beings / namely in **Mars** / or in the property of **Wrath** / Christ drove the devils out from those who were possessed / and made those afflicted with the "falling sickness" <note>original: "Taub-süchtigen"; likely referring to epilepsy or fits associated with the "deaf and dumb" spirits in the Gospels.</note> healthy in this form and property. In the sixth kingdom of the mother of all beings / on the wheel of life / called **Venus** / Christ loved his brothers and sisters according to humanity / and washed his disciples' feet / and loved them even unto the highest humility / and gave his life in the property of **Wrath** for them into death / and revealed himself among them / that he was Christ / and when they perceived / that the King had come / who

# 1795 Appendix / Chapter 8. 1796

A virgin has born anew; but he should have patience. What is impossible for the **Artist** <term>Artista</term> <note>The alchemist or practitioner of the Great Work.</note> is possible for Nature; after the night, day comes. When the tempter has finished all his temptations, then comes the sign of the angels; then the devil, who tempted him, must yield. The **Artist** should note this well, and dismiss the devil, and lay the youth with his virginal heart in his bed, and let him eat his former food. For he is now a physician to his siblings in his mother's house; he will perform great wonders in all seven kingdoms of his mother, which are the seven forms of life, just as **Christ** <note>original: "Christus"</note> has done.

As in **Saturn** <term>Saturno</term> <note>The planetary principle of contraction, coldness, and the "lead" of material existence.</note> he will raise the dead; understand this: in his previous prison, he will awaken the dead essence that held him captive. For he shall make the earth into heaven. Just as the Virgin awakened his will out of wrath into love and made him a wonder-worker; so shall he, with his will—which is united in the Virgin's heart—awaken the forms in his mother's womb, from which she bore him and all her children. He shall ignite them with the Virgin's and his own love-desire. This happens in the **Sulfur of Saturn** <term>Sulphure Saturni</term> <note>The inner, active fire or "soul" hidden within the cold, dark matter of Saturn.</note>, the youth's own bodily property, and in his mother. For before the marriage of the Virgin, the heavenly essence of the youth lies locked in death; for when **GOD** <note>original: "GOTT"</note> cursed the earth, the heavenly paradisical body faded, and the **Impression of Saturn** <term>Impression Saturni</term> <note>The force that solidifies spirit into hard, heavy matter.</note> took it over until the restoration, when **GOD** will bring back that which is hidden, so that Paradise greens again in the spoken Word, or the **Artist** opens such in a partial work through **GOD'S** permission.

In the second kingdom of the mother, as of the **Moon** <term>Lunæ</term>, he shall also work wonders; for **JESUS** feeds five thousand men with five barley loaves; that is the working in the

<column-break/>

essence or corporeality. He turned water into wine. This and the like all belong to the Lunar property, where the Knight with his Virgin opens Paradise and feeds the body where there is nothing—where the outer **Mercury** <term>Mercurius</term> worked nothing. Thus shall the forms in the Lunar property open themselves as if they were paradisical. Then the **Artist** thinks, "I am close to it," but he still has far to go until the end.

In the third kingdom of the mother, as in **Jupiter** <term>Jove</term>, **Christ** made the simple and uncomprehending—those who were dull and almost ignorant—knowing and understanding. As from poor fishermen and carpenters and the like, he made apostles and the most understanding of men; likewise from poor, unsightly people, from women and simple folk, he made faithful, **God-like** <note>original: "GOttförmige"</note> dear children, who grasped the **Universal** <note>The totality of divine wisdom or the "Universal Medicine" of the alchemists.</note> within themselves without academic art. 

So it also happens in the **Philosophical Work**; the essence that had faded in death, where the **Mercury** is entirely earthly, cold, and powerless, rises up in power, as if the whole being were a new life. The **Artist** marvels at this—what it might be or how it happens—and also rejoices greatly that he sees the Divine power greening before him in a half-dead being, even while under the curse of **GOD**. He sees all four **Elements** <term>Elementa</term>, each one individually, and sees how the Wisdom of **GOD** mirrors itself therein as a play of joy; and he sees all colors and the rainbow—upon which **Christ** sits in judgment—in the spoken **Mercury** <term>Mercurio</term>. 

The nature of this appearance arises from the **Impression of Saturn**; the benevolent **Jupiter** thus lets himself be seen in a certain way, just as **GOD** will change the world and transmute it back into **Paradise** <note>original: "Paradiess"</note>. For that is the understanding in the spoken Word; just as **Christ** made simple, uncomprehending people understanding in the Divine, right, heavenly **Jovial** <note>original: "Jovialischer"; referring to the qualities of Jupiter: wisdom, expansion, and joy.</note> understanding.
