-># Of the Universal.<-

In the fourth kingdom of the Mother of all Beings—which is the **Mercurial** <term>Mercurialische</term> <note>Representing the principle of movement, communication, and the "vital spirit" in both the body and the alchemical flask.</note> realm on the wheel of the nature of life—**Christ** <note>original: "Christus"</note> made the deaf hear, the speechless speak, and the lepers clean from the poison of **Mercury** <term>Mercurii</term>. All palsy and gout, such as the **French disease** <note>original: "Frankosen"; a historical term for syphilis.</note> and poisonous rashes, arise from the **Saturnine** water in Mercury, which is called **Phlegm** <term>Phlegma</term> <note>One of the four humors, here associated with the cold, damp, and "dead" residue of Saturn.</note>; all of this Christ healed in the form of the Youth and the Virgin; for eternal virginity had wedded itself to the Youth, as if to humanity. This also happens in the **Philosophical Work**; the **Artist** <term>Artista</term> will see how the heaven separates from the earth, and how the heaven sinks back into the earth, and transforms the earth into a heavenly color; he will see how Mercury purifies the **Matter** <term>Materiam</term>, how the purified colors will appear in their own property within the **Antimony** <term>Antimonio</term> <note>A metallic element used in the purification of gold, often symbolizing the transition to a higher state.</note>, and how the wonder continues.

In the fifth kingdom of the Mother of all Beings—that is, in **Mars**, or in the property of **Wrath** <note>original: "Grimmes"; a central term in Böhme’s thought describing the harsh, consuming fire of nature before it is lightened by love.</note>—Christ drove out the devils from the possessed and healed the epileptics in this form and property. The Artist will also see this in the Philosophical Work: how **Jupiter** in Mercury will drive a black, squinting fire-vapor up out of the Matter, which settles like **soot**; for this is a hunger of the poison in Mercury, and it is rightly compared to the devil, for it is of his property.

In the sixth kingdom of the Mother of all Beings—on the wheel of life called **Venus**—Christ loved his brothers and sisters according to his humanity, and washed his disciples' feet, and loved them even unto the deepest humility; and he gave his life into the property of Wrath for them, unto death, and revealed himself among them, that he was Christ. And when they perceived that the King had come who

<column-break/>

was to take the power from their self-will and break the devil’s kingdom, they cried out and said: "We have no king but the Emperor." They took him into their power in the dark night and bound him, and led him before their council, mocked him, scourged him, and struck him, and stripped off his clothes, and hung him on the cross.

The Artist will see this magnificently in the Philosophical Work; for as soon as the dark fire-vapor departs from the Matter—acting as the **Matter’s Devil**—then **Lady Venus** <note>original: "Frau Venus"</note> appears in her virginity, most magnificent and beautiful. This signifies Christ's love, which humbled itself and revealed its love in our humanity. At that point, the Artist thinks he has the **Philosophical Child**, that he has "caught the prize" <note>original: "den Braten"; literally "the roast meat," an idiom meaning one has succeeded or secured the win.</note>; but he is dancing with the Jews, who, when they had captured Christ, thought: "Now we have him, we shall certainly hold him." In the same way, the Artist thinks: "It is finished," and he accepts the child; but when he examines it in the **Proof** <term>Proba</term> <note>The technical test to see if the alchemical transmutation is permanent and genuine.</note>, he finds he has Venus, a mere woman, and not the Virgin with the **Fire- and Light-Tincture** <term>Tinctur</term>, and he has allowed himself to be deceived by the woman.

Now look closely: what do the properties of **Saturn**, **Mars**, and **Mercury** do? When they see the Child as the Knight in royal color, and find that he carries no outward kingdom with power and violence as they do, but wishes only to rule with love within their poisonous fire-power—him they will not endure. For **Saturn** signifies worldly rule, and **Mercury** signifies spiritual rule (like the **Pharisees**), and **Mars** signifies the devil. These three would not suffer Christ among them, for he said: He was a King of Love and the Son of God, and had come to save his people from sins. Then the devil thought: "That sounds bad; you will lose your kingdom"; and the worldly...

The authorities thought: If this one is a king and *GOD'S* son, he will abolish our power; that does not taste well to us. And the mercurial priests thought: This one is far too little for us; we want a **Messiah** <note>original: "Messiam"</note> who leads us into worldly glory, who makes us high and rich in the world, so that we alone possess the honor of the world; we do not want to accept him, for he is much too poor; we might lose the favor of the worldly authorities and would have to pay the price for him; we would much rather remain in our honors and power and abolish the beggar-king with his kingdom of love. Just as they are still so minded today, and do the same to the messengers he sends.

So it also happens in the **Philosophical Work**; when **Venus** <term>Venus</term> <note>In Böhme's system, Venus represents the "soft" water of love and the light-essence that must transform the harsh base metals.</note> reveals herself in the three fierce forms—namely in **Saturn** <note>original: "Saturno"</note>, **Mars** <note>original: "Marte"</note>, and **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurio"</note>—with Love in her own form, they cannot bear it, for it is entirely against their harsh, dark fire-power, especially against the poison of **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurii"</note>; they flash at Venus, shooting their beam, like the mercurial poison-beam, at her, just as the **Pharisees** <note>original: "Pharisäer"</note> did to **Christ** <note>original: "Christum"</note>.

Meanwhile **Jupiter** and **Luna** stand by **Venus**, and give their power to Venus; for in **Jupiter's** <note>original: "Jovis"</note> power, Venus now stands there. The Pharisees laugh at this and think: we are already wise, why do we need understanding? We want power and honor. And **Luna** <term>Luna</term> <note>The Moon, representing the soul of the world or the common people, easily influenced by the shifting of the higher powers.</note> signifies the crowd of laypeople who clung to Christ while things went well for him. So also in the Philosophical Work, **Luna** clings to **Venus** in her brilliance because **Saturn**, **Mercury**, and **Mars** do not yet attack her; but when the violence of the **Wrath** <note>original: "Grimmes"; the harsh, judgmental quality of nature.</note> comes, **Luna** changes her will like her color, looks on, stands up, and joins in shouting "**Crucify him!**" <note>original: "Crucifige"</note>. The **Artist** <term>Artista</term> <note>The practitioner of alchemy.</note> will see this, if he is chosen by **GOD** for the work and is worthy of it.

In this mighty struggle between death and life, heaven and hell, the Youth will sweat his blood-sweat. The angry Mercury wants to lock the child of Venus into death, and for that reason he awakens **Saturn** <note>original: "Saturnum"</note>.

# Appendix / Chapter 8.

The secular authorities thought: "If this one is a king and **GOD’S** son, he will overthrow our power, and that does not suit us." And the mercurial priests <note>In Böhme’s thought, "mercurial" people are those driven by restless intellect and self-interest, often associated with the volatile nature of the planet Mercury.</note> thought: "This one is far too lowly for us; we want a Messiah who will lead us into worldly glory, who will make us great and rich in the world, so that we alone possess the world's honor. We would much rather remain in our own honor and power and do away with this beggar-king and his kingdom of love." Indeed, they are still of this mind today and treat the messengers he sends in the same way.

It happens exactly the same way in the Philosophical Work <term>Philosophisches Werck</term> <note>The alchemical process of creating the Philosopher’s Stone.</note>. When **Venus** <note>original: "Venus"</note>—as love in her own form—reveals herself within the three wrathful qualities of **Saturn**, **Mars**, and **Mercury**, they cannot bear it. They flash at **Venus** and shoot their rays at her—like mercurial rays of poison—just as the Pharisees did to **Christ**.

Meanwhile, **Jupiter** and the **Moon** <note>original: "Luna"</note> stand by **Venus** and give their strength to her; for **Venus** now stands there in the power of **Jupiter**. The Pharisees mock this and think: "We are already wise; what do we need with more understanding? We want power and honor." And the **Moon** signifies the crowd of laypeople who clung to **Christ** while things went well for him. Similarly, in the Philosophical Work, the **Moon** holds to **Venus** in her brilliance as long as **Saturn**, **Mercury**, and **Mars** do not attack her. But as soon as the power of the **Wrath** <term>Grimm</term> <note>A technical term for the harsh, consuming, and un-tempered force of nature.</note> arrives, the **Moon** changes her will—as she changes her color—and looks on, stands up, and joins in the cry of **"Crucify him!"** <note>original: "Crucifige"</note>. The **Artist** <term>Artista</term> <note>The alchemist performing the work.</note> will see this, if he is chosen by **GOD** for the Work and is worthy of it.

If it did so, it would be like the Sun and would be a master over the **Sulfur of Mars** <note>original: "Sulphur Martis"</note> and of **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurii"</note>, but only a master of the external world's essence, a ruler in wrath—just as the **Sun** is such a ruler.

But **Saturn**, because it is not of his property, gives it to the soldiers among the murderers to be crucified. The Jews <note>In this context, Böhme uses "the Jews" as an allegory for the harsh, legalistic, or wrathful properties of the human mind.</note> seize it in their false, poisonous, and angry desire; they pierce and murder it with three nails or awls—namely, with the properties of **Saturn**, **Mercury**, and **Mars** belonging to the dark world. When this is separated from coarseness through the opening of all properties of nature, it is truly spiritual; then the **Solar Spirit** <note>the spirit of the Sun</note> takes no other property into itself but this one, which it may reach in the opened forms within their sensual soul. For the Sun takes nothing into itself but its own likeness; it takes its heaven from the earth—if you wish to understand me rightly—for it is its food. From this, it brings forth a young son within itself, who is also called **Sun**, but he is a **Body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note>. Therefore I say to you: keep yourself diligently and closely to her; you will surely be gladdened. May God let you live so long, provided you have the right Father, whom I have contemplated and in whom I have found great delight. This is well known to me, for I have recently seen something at which I not only marvel but also rejoice, wherein much has been revealed to me. And although I would like to write more extensively about it, it is not necessary for you in this process; also, the pen is not to be trusted. It can happen another time. I ask you to keep this letter secret and in confidence; if I come to you, I might well entrust you with something that I have recently received and seen. However, I shall go only as far as I am permitted.

<column-break/>

<margin>Epistle 15. §. 10. 20.</margin>

Thus, this is a **Universal** <term>Universal: A master medicine or spiritual tincture believed to cure all diseases and perfect all matter.</term> which also transmutes the "counter-will" of all diseases in the human body into a single Will, so that the raging and stinging—being the seven properties of life—become unified in their enmity. Then the "hunger" of the disease ceases. The process for the Universal is as was previously stated; it is not my intention to provide a clearer indication, for it is clear enough. Whoever does not wish to seek a new man born in God through this, and to prepare himself for it, should leave my writings in peace. I have written nothing for such a seeker; he cannot fully grasp our meaning. No matter how much he practices, unless he enters into **Resignation** <term>Gelassenheit: the mystical practice of yielding one's self-will to God</term> in Christ, where he may grasp the Spirit of the Universal, all is in vain. We wish to warn the over-curious mind not to be deceived; he will achieve nothing at all on this path unless he enters into it himself. Then it will become manifest to him without much searching, for the way is like that of a child.

<margin>Signatura Rerum 12. §. 37. 38.</margin>

Thus, dear and inclined reader, we have set before you a selection from the writings of the highly enlightened man of God’s wonders, **JACOB BÖHME**. As you are a seeker, so shall you find. If you seek God, He will make Himself known to you. If you seek gold, then see how and where you find it, and how you use what is found. The time of finding is near; the winter will soon pass; the time of the **Lily** becoming a **Rose** will bloom in May. Blessed is he who has eyes to see and ears to hear. God be with us all, Amen.

Böhme concludes with a prophetic promise that those who seek God will find Him as the spiritual "winter" ends.</summary>

# Notice
## To the Kind Reader.

We inform the kind reader that, as it is the common lot of such writings in this world to have to work their way through many difficulties and opposition before they come to light, this work has also experienced the same; so much so that if the first impulse for its publication had not been driven from the root of the Divine Will, it would have been smothered often under these hindrances. Although, beyond our expectation and inquiry, some <term>lovers</term><note>Interested supporters or patrons of the author's work</note> appeared of their own accord to promote it with a sufficient <term>advancement</term><note>Financial backing or pre-payment for printing costs</note>, it could not come to light without passing through many <term>fates</term><note>original: "Fata," referring to the trials and tribulations of the publishing process</note>. It was already handed over to the press in a certain place two years ago, but from there, for significant reasons, it was referred further; since it finally came to a distant place, to a location where it could not be proofread in time either by ourselves or by someone knowledgeable about the work; therefore it might not turn out as exact and correct as we would have wished. Moreover, since in some places gross printing errors have occurred, which the kind reader—before he reads this work earnestly—is requested to correct according to the attached list; so particularly the distinction between the author’s and our own words has not been sufficiently observed through the change of smaller and larger type, but has been confused <note>original: "confundiret"</note> in one place or another; Although we ourselves with our words

seeking nothing else but to present the author’s meaning impartially, we have nevertheless wished to inform the gracious reader of this; requesting that, if such a distinction is especially important to him, he might note the difference himself according to the attached first index. For the rest, may he receive this well-intentioned work—as well as it has turned out—in the blessing of **GOD** with a simple heart. But should any, as men of our time, elder brothers, fathers, masters <note>original: "Magistri"</note>, or doctors <note>original: "Doctores"</note> (whose dignities we gladly grant to everyone before **GOD** and men), contrary to our expectations, wish to set upon us, we inform them in childlike simplicity that we do not represent ourselves here as anything higher than an ABC-student <note>A common metaphor in this period for a humble beginner or someone still learning the basics of spiritual truth.</note>, just as the author himself describes his writing as no more than that of a student. Let no one come to us with higher arguments or the pretense of some special revelations <note>The editor is likely defending against critics who claimed direct, private divine authority to contradict the text.</note> other than those customary in our class and ABC-school—where the highest and the elders sit at the bottom—and which press the true brotherly ABC into the conscience and convince all reason toward humility. Thus, in **GOD’S** grace, we shall meet everyone with due modesty, love, and friendship, both in spirit and in word.

<meta>This page concludes the introductory remarks and continues the detailed errata list, picking up from the catchword on page 595. It maintains the humble tone of the editors, who position themselves as mere "students" of the author’s difficult "ABC-school" of spiritual wisdom.</meta>

...having sought nothing other than to impartially present the Author's intended meaning, we nevertheless wish to advise the kind reader of this: if such distinctions are of particular importance to him, he should note the differences himself according to the first index provided. For the rest, we ask that this well-intentioned work—as good as it has turned out—be received with a simple heart in the blessing of GOD. 

Should any, however—as men of our time, elder brothers, fathers, Masters, or Doctors (whose dignities we gladly leave to each before GOD and men)—wish to set upon us contrary to our expectations, we answer them in childlike simplicity. We do not represent ourselves here as anything higher than an ABC-student <note>original: "A, b, c.-Schüler." This is a common metaphor in 17th-century pietism and theosophy, suggesting a humble beginner in the school of the Holy Spirit.</note>, just as the Author himself gives out his writing as nothing more than that of a student. Let no one approach us with loftier arguments or the pretext of some "Special Revelations" <note>original: "Special-Offenbarungen." The editors are wary of radical visionaries who claim private authority outside of the established "school" of this wisdom.</note> other than those customary in our class and ABC-school—where the highest and the eldest sit at the bottom. These truths press the true Brother-ABC into the conscience and convince all reason to practice humility. Thus, in GOD’S grace, we shall meet everyone with due modesty, love, and friendship, both in spirit and in word.

having sought nothing other than to present the author's meaning impartially, we nevertheless wished to inform the kind reader of this: asking that, if such a distinction is particularly important to him, he might note the difference himself according to the attached first index. For the rest, may you receive this well-intentioned work, as well as it has turned out, with a simple heart in the blessing of GOD. Thus, in GOD'S grace, we shall meet everyone with due modesty, love, and friendship, both in spirit and in word.
